kapotaromā parjanyaścandrasenaḥ parāntakaḥ .. 22 ..
meaning:
महोत्साहो वीतभयो निरमित्रः प्रभाकरः ..
कपोतरोमा पर्जन्यश्चन्द्रसेनः परान्तकः .. 22 ..
text_mt: Mahotsāha, Vītabhaya, Niramitra, Prabhākara, / Kapotaromā, Parjanya, Candrasena, Parāntaka,

sanskrit_iast:
bhīmaseno dṛḍharathaḥ kuśanābhaḥ prabhadrakaḥ ..
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ pūrvajanmani keśavam .. 23 ..
meaning:
भीमसेनो दृढरथः कुशनाभः प्रभद्रकः ..
एते चान्ये च बहवः पूर्वजन्मनि केशवम् .. 23 ..
text_mt: Bhīmasena, Dṛḍharatha, Kuśanābha, and Prabhadraka— / these and many others, having worshipped Keśava in a previous birth,

sanskrit_iast:
pūjayitvā kṣitāvasyāṃ prāpū rājyamakaṇṭakam ..
yakṣatvamatha devatvaṃ gandharvatvaṃ tathaiva ca .. 24 ..
meaning:
पूजयित्वा क्षितावस्यां प्रापू राज्यमकण्टकम् ..
यक्षत्वमथ देवत्वं गन्धर्वत्वं तथैव च .. 24 ..
text_mt: obtained on this earth an unobstructed kingdom. / The state of a yakṣa, or the state of a god, and likewise the state of a gandharva,

sanskrit_iast:
vidyādharatvaṃ nāgatvaṃ ye gatā manujottama ..
bahutvātte kathaṃ śakyā mayā vaktuṃ tavānagha .. 25 ..
meaning:
विद्याधरत्वं नागत्वं ये गता मनुजोत्तम ..
बहुत्वात्ते कथं शक्या मया वक्तुं तवानघ .. 25 ..
text_mt: the state of a vidyādhara, the state of a nāga—those who reached them, O best of men, / because of their multitude, how can they be told by me to you, O sinless one?

sanskrit_iast: tasmādyatnaḥ sadā kāryaḥ puruṣaiḥ kusumārcane ..26..
meaning: तस्माद्यत्नः सदा कार्यः पुरुषैः कुसुमार्चने ..26..
text_mt: Therefore, effort should always be made by men in worshipping with blossoms.

sanskrit_iast:
araṇyajātaiḥ kusumaiḥ sadaiva saṃpūjayitvā svayamāhṛtaistu ..
sarveśvaratvaṃ phalamāpnuvanti rājendra tadvarṇayituṃ na śakyam .. 27 ..
meaning:
अरण्यजातैः कुसुमैः सदैव संपूजयित्वा स्वयमाहृतैस्तु ..
सर्वेश्वरत्वं फलमाप्नुवन्ति राजेन्द्र तद्वर्णयितुं न शक्यम् .. 27 ..
text_mt: Having constantly worshipped with blossoms born in the forest and gathered by oneself, / they obtain the fruit of sovereign lordship over all, O king of kings; it cannot be described.

sanskrit_iast:
vajra uvāca ..
aṭavyo dāruṇā brahmansiṃhavyāghraniṣevitāḥ ..
taskarācaritā ghorāḥ sarīsṛpavimiśritāḥ .. 1 ..
meaning:
वज्र उवाच ..
अटव्यो दारुणा ब्रह्मन्सिंहव्याघ्रनिषेविताः ..
तस्कराचरिता घोराः सरीसृपविमिश्रिताः .. 1 ..
text_mt: Vajra said: / The forests are terrible, O brahmin, frequented by lions and tigers, / traversed by thieves, frightful, and filled with crawling beasts;
title: Upalepanaphalapraśaṃsanaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
nityotthitasya cādhvānaṃ dāhakṣayakaraṃ param ..
ataḥ svalpataraṃ karma brūhi me keśavārcane .. 2 ..
meaning:
नित्योत्थितस्य चाध्वानं दाहक्षयकरं परम् ..
अतः स्वल्पतरं कर्म ब्रूहि मे केशवार्चने .. 2 ..
text_mt: and for one constantly set out, travel brings extreme exhaustion and decay. / Therefore, tell me of an even lesser work in the worship of Keśava.

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ataḥ svalpataraṃ rājandevaveśmānulepanam ..
mahāphalaṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇairvedapāragaiḥ .. 3 ..
meaning:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
अतः स्वल्पतरं राजन्देववेश्मानुलेपनम् ..
महाफलं विनिर्दिष्टं ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः .. 3 ..
text_mt: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / An even lesser [work] than this, O king, is the smearing of the deity's temple; / it is declared as having great fruit by brahmins who have mastered the Vedas.

sanskrit_iast:
sammārjanaṃ tu yaḥ kuryātpuruṣaḥ keśavālaye ..
rajastamobhyāṃ nirmuktaḥ sa bhavennātra saṃśayaḥ .. 4 ..
meaning:
सम्मार्जनं तु यः कुर्यात्पुरुषः केशवालये ..
रजस्तमोभ्यां निर्मुक्तः स भवेन्नात्र संशयः .. 4 ..
text_mt: The man who would perform sweeping in the temple of Keśava / becomes freed from passion and darkness; there is no doubt about this.

sanskrit_iast:
pāṃsūnāṃ yāvatāṃ rājankuryātsammārjanaṃ naraḥ ..
tāvantyabdāni sa sukhī nākamāsādya modate ..5 ..
meaning:
पांसूनां यावतां राजन्कुर्यात्सम्मार्जनं नरः ..
तावन्त्यब्दानि स सुखी नाकमासाद्य मोदते ..5 ..
text_mt: As many particles of dust as a man sweeps away, O king, / for that many years, happy, having reached heaven, he rejoices.

sanskrit_iast:
abhyukṣaṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryātpānīyena surālaye..
sa śāntapāpo bhavati nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..6..
meaning:
अभ्युक्षणं तु यः कुर्यात्पानीयेन सुरालये..
स शान्तपापो भवति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..6..
text_mt: One who performs sprinkling with water in the temple of the god / has his sins stilled; there should be no doubt about this.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvopalepanaṃ viṣṇornarastvāyatane sadā ..
gomayena śubhām̐llokānayatnādeva gacchati .. 7 ..
meaning:
कृत्वोपलेपनं विष्णोर्नरस्त्वायतने सदा ..
गोमयेन शुभाम्̐ल्लोकानयत्नादेव गच्छति .. 7 ..
text_mt: Having always performed the smearing of Viṣṇu's temple / with cow dung, a man goes to auspicious worlds without any effort.

sanskrit_iast:
hastapramāṇaṃ bhūbhāgamupalipya narādhipa ..
devarāmāśataṃ nākaṃ labheta satataṃ naraḥ .. 8 ..
meaning:
हस्तप्रमाणं भूभागमुपलिप्य नराधिप ..
देवरामाशतं नाकं लभेत सततं नरः .. 8 ..
text_mt: Having smeared a plot of ground measuring a cubit, O ruler of men, / a man would continually obtain heaven with a hundred divine maidens.

sanskrit_iast:
tato'nusāreṇa phalaṃ vistṛtāyāṃ kṣitau smṛtam ..
nityāsamarthastu tathā devaveśmopalepane .. 9 ..
meaning:
ततोऽनुसारेण फलं विस्तृतायां क्षितौ स्मृतम् ..
नित्यासमर्थस्तु तथा देववेश्मोपलेपने .. 9 ..
text_mt: In accordance with that, the fruit on an expanded ground is recorded. / But one incapable of daily [action] in smearing the temple of the god

sanskrit_iast:
triḥ pakṣasya tu kurvīta devaveśmopalepanam ..
pañcamīṃ daśamīṃ caiva tathā pañcadaśīṃ nṛpa .. 1.169.10 ..
meaning:
त्रिः पक्षस्य तु कुर्वीत देववेश्मोपलेपनम् ..
पञ्चमीं दशमीं चैव तथा पञ्चदशीं नृप .. 1.169.10 ..
text_mt: should perform the smearing of the deity's temple three times in a fortnight: / on the fifth, the tenth, and the fifteenth [lunar day], O king.

sanskrit_iast:
triḥ pakṣasya sadā kṛtvā devaveśmopalepanam ..
saṃvatsarāttadāpnoti yatphalaṃ tannibodha me ..11 ..
meaning:
त्रिः पक्षस्य सदा कृत्वा देववेश्मोपलेपनम् ..
संवत्सरात्तदाप्नोति यत्फलं तन्निबोध मे ..11 ..
text_mt: Hear from me the fruit which one obtains after a year, / having constantly smeared the temple of the god three times a fortnight.

sanskrit_iast:
janmāntaramathāsādya gṛhaṃ prāpnotyanuttamam ..
sarvopabhogasaṃyuktaṃ gṛhaprāsādasaṅkulam ..12..
meaning:
जन्मान्तरमथासाद्य गृहं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ..
सर्वोपभोगसंयुक्तं गृहप्रासादसङ्कुलम् ..12..
text_mt: Attaining another birth, he gains an unsurpassed house, / endowed with every enjoyment, crowded with chambers and mansions,

sanskrit_iast:
vṛkṣodyānalatāgulmatoyavāpīvibhūṣitam ..
gavāśvadhanadhānyāḍhyaṃ sarvopakaraṇairyutam .. 13 ..
meaning:
वृक्षोद्यानलतागुल्मतोयवापीविभूषितम् ..
गवाश्वधनधान्याढ्यं सर्वोपकरणैर्युतम् .. 13 ..
text_mt: adorned with trees, gardens, creepers, shrubs, and water-reservoirs, / rich in cattle, horses, wealth, and grain, equipped with every implement,

sanskrit_iast:
priyaṃvadābhirhṛdyābhiḥ svarūpābhiśca pārthiva ..
vṛtaṃ ca bahubhiḥ strībhiścāruvaṃśābhireva ca .. 14 ..
meaning:
प्रियंवदाभिर्हृद्याभिः स्वरूपाभिश्च पार्थिव ..
वृतं च बहुभिः स्त्रीभिश्चारुवंशाभिरेव च .. 14 ..
text_mt: and surrounded by many women of charming lineage, O king, / sweet-spoken, delightful, and beautiful.

sanskrit_iast:
gārhasthyaṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ tatra sa cāpnoti mahītale ..
na ca pracyavanaṃ tasmājjīvannāpnoti karhicit .. 15 ..
meaning:
गार्हस्थ्यं च दृढं तत्र स चाप्नोति महीतले ..
न च प्रच्यवनं तस्माज्जीवन्नाप्नोति कर्हिचित् .. 15 ..
text_mt: And there on the earth he attains a steadfast householder's life, / and while alive he never suffers a fall from it.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya ye bāndhavāstatra sarve te dīrghajīvinaḥ ..
bhavanti na bhavantyasya ādhayo vyādhayastathā ..16..
meaning:
तस्य ये बान्धवास्तत्र सर्वे ते दीर्घजीविनः ..
भवन्ति न भवन्त्यस्य आधयो व्याधयस्तथा ..16..
text_mt: All his kinsmen there become long-lived; / mental anxieties and bodily diseases do not come to him.

sanskrit_iast:
na tasya mṛtaniṣkrāntirgṛhe bhavati karhicit..
yāvajjīvatyasau tatra gṛhe śrīmānmudā yutaḥ .. 17 ..
meaning:
न तस्य मृतनिष्क्रान्तिर्गृहे भवति कर्हिचित्..
यावज्जीवत्यसौ तत्र गृहे श्रीमान्मुदा युतः .. 17 ..
text_mt: A corpse is never carried out of his house / as long as he lives there, prosperous and full of joy.

sanskrit_iast:
caurajaṃ na bhayaṃ tasya na ca vyādhikṛtaṃ bhayam ..
vyālabhūpālajaṃ vāpi na ca tasya phalaṃ bhavet .. 18 ..
meaning:
चौरजं न भयं तस्य न च व्याधिकृतं भयम् ..
व्यालभूपालजं वापि न च तस्य फलं भवेत् .. 18 ..
text_mt: He has no fear arising from thieves, nor fear caused by disease, / nor fear arising from snakes or kings, nor does that bear fruit against him.

sanskrit_iast:
svarūpaḥ sarvasiddhārtho dīrghāyurvyādhivarjitaḥ ..
ājñāvidheyabhṛtyaśca dhruvaṃ syānmanujeśvara .. 19 ..
meaning:
स्वरूपः सर्वसिद्धार्थो दीर्घायुर्व्याधिवर्जितः ..
आज्ञाविधेयभृत्यश्च ध्रुवं स्यान्मनुजेश्वर .. 19 ..
text_mt: He is handsome, has accomplished all his aims, is long-lived, free from disease, / and has servants obedient to his command, O lord of men.

sanskrit_iast:
bhuñjāno yaḥ sadā kuryāttasyaitatkathitaṃ phalam ..
naktabhojī tathā kṛtvā dviguṇaṃ phalamāpnuyāt .. 1.169.20 ..
meaning:
भुञ्जानो यः सदा कुर्यात्तस्यैतत्कथितं फलम् ..
नक्तभोजी तथा कृत्वा द्विगुणं फलमाप्नुयात् .. 1.169.20 ..
text_mt: This fruit is proclaimed for him who, while eating [normally], always performs it; / eating only at night, having done so, he would obtain twice that fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
upoṣitastu riktāsu pūrṇāsu tu harergṛhe ..
kṛtvopalepanaṃ nityaṃ cānantyaṃ phalamaśnute .. 21 ..
meaning:
उपोषितस्तु रिक्तासु पूर्णासु तु हरेर्गृहे ..
कृत्वोपलेपनं नित्यं चानन्त्यं फलमश्नुते .. 21 ..
text_mt: Fasting on empty lunar days and on full ones, having continually performed / smearing in the house of Hari, he enjoys endless fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
upalepanakṛdyastu kṛṣṇasyāyatane bhavet ..
pāpasaṃmārjanaṃ tasya śīghrameva bhaviṣyati .. 22 ..
meaning:
उपलेपनकृद्यस्तु कृष्णस्यायतने भवेत् ..
पापसंमार्जनं तस्य शीघ्रमेव भविष्यति .. 22 ..
text_mt: One who performs the smearing in the abode of Kṛṣṇa / will quickly have his sins wiped away.

sanskrit_iast:
niṣpādyametatsasukhaṃ narendra ārādhanaṃ devavarasya viṣṇoḥ ..
proktaṃ mayā te dhanavarjitānāṃ dhanānvitānāṃ saphalaṃ viśeṣam .. 23 ..
meaning:
निष्पाद्यमेतत्ससुखं नरेन्द्र आराधनं देववरस्य विष्णोः ..
प्रोक्तं मया ते धनवर्जितानां धनान्वितानां सफलं विशेषम् .. 23 ..
text_mt: This worship of Viṣṇu, the best of gods, is to be performed with ease, O king; / it has been proclaimed by me to you for those devoid of wealth, and especially fruitful for those endowed with wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam ..
phalamāsādya yadgītaṃ devaveśmopalepane .. 1 ..
meaning:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ..
फलमासाद्य यद्गीतं देववेश्मोपलेपने .. 1 ..
text_mt: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Here too they cite this ancient narrative / which was sung upon obtaining the fruit of smearing the house of the god.
title: Māndhātrupākhyānam

sanskrit_iast:
babhūva śūdrajātīyaḥ kaścidbhāgyavivarjitaḥ ..
kṛtavānsa tu vāṇijyaṃ dhanaśeṣeṇa kenacit .. 2 ..
meaning:
बभूव शूद्रजातीयः कश्चिद्भाग्यविवर्जितः ..
कृतवान्स तु वाणिज्यं धनशेषेण केनचित् .. 2 ..
text_mt: There was a certain man of the śūdra caste, devoid of fortune; / he engaged in trade with the remainder of some wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
tasminvipanne sa kṛṣiṃ cakāra nṛpasattama ..
tasyāmapi vipannāyāṃ cakre sevāṃ punaḥpunaḥ .. 3 ..
meaning:
तस्मिन्विपन्ने स कृषिं चकार नृपसत्तम ..
तस्यामपि विपन्नायां चक्रे सेवां पुनःपुनः .. 3 ..
text_mt: When that failed, he undertook agriculture, O best of kings; / when that too failed, he repeatedly performed service.

sanskrit_iast:
tato'pyanāsādya phalaṃ siddhiṃ tīramupāśritaḥ ..
gaṅgāyāḥ saptamo bhāgaḥ sindhurnaranarottama .. 4 ..
meaning:
ततोऽप्यनासाद्य फलं सिद्धिं तीरमुपाश्रितः ..
गङ्गायाः सप्तमो भागः सिन्धुर्नरनरोत्तम .. 4 ..
text_mt: Failing to obtain success or fruit even from that, he resorted to the bank / of the Sindhu, the seventh part of the Gaṅgā, O best of men,

sanskrit_iast:
śītalāmalapānīyaḥ svargalokapradāyakaḥ ..
yatra snātvā gatiṃ yānti brāhmaṇāśca tapasvinaḥ ..5..
meaning:
शीतलामलपानीयः स्वर्गलोकप्रदायकः ..
यत्र स्नात्वा गतिं यान्ति ब्राह्मणाश्च तपस्विनः ..5..
text_mt: having cool and pure water, bestowing the heavenly world, / where, having bathed, brahmins and ascetics go to their goal.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya tīre varāhārcā purāṇarṣivinirmitā ..
tāṃ samāsādya śūdrastu nityaṃ bhaikṣyaparāyaṇaḥ .. 6 ..
meaning:
तस्य तीरे वराहार्चा पुराणर्षिविनिर्मिता ..
तां समासाद्य शूद्रस्तु नित्यं भैक्ष्यपरायणः .. 6 ..
text_mt: On its bank was an image of Varāha fashioned by an ancient sage; / reaching it, the śūdra, constantly devoted to begging for alms,

sanskrit_iast:
nityopalepanaparastadarcādevaveśmani ..
uvāsa bhāryayā sārdhaṃ tatra nityānuraktayā .. 7 ..
meaning:
नित्योपलेपनपरस्तदर्चादेववेश्मनि ..
उवास भार्यया सार्धं तत्र नित्यानुरक्तया .. 7 ..
text_mt: constantly intent on smearing [the ground] in the divine temple of that image, / lived there together with his wife, who was constantly devoted to him.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminneva kāle tu varāhārcādidṛkṣayā ..
sauvīrarājaḥ samprāptastaṃ deśaṃ citravāhanaḥ .. 8 ..
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु वराहार्चादिदृक्षया ..
सौवीरराजः सम्प्राप्तस्तं देशं चित्रवाहनः .. 8 ..
text_mt: At that very time, wishing to see the image of Varāha, / Citravāhana, the king of Sauvīra, arrived in that region.

sanskrit_iast:
sindhau snānaṃ samāsādya pūjayitvā jagatpatim ..
sabhāryaḥ pṛthivīpālaḥ prāyādrājanyathāgataḥ .. 9 ..
meaning:
सिन्धौ स्नानं समासाद्य पूजयित्वा जगत्पतिम् ..
सभार्यः पृथिवीपालः प्रायाद्राजन्यथागतः .. 9 ..
text_mt: Having bathed in the Sindhu and worshipped the Lord of the world, / the ruler of the earth, accompanied by his wife, departed as he had come, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
śriyaṃ tasya tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sa śūdro bhāryayā saha ..
bhūpālatvaspṛhāṃ kṛtvā kālātkālavaśaṅgataḥ .. 1.170.10 ..
meaning:
श्रियं तस्य तु तां दृष्ट्वा स शूद्रो भार्यया सह ..
भूपालत्वस्पृहां कृत्वा कालात्कालवशङ्गतः .. 1.170.10 ..
text_mt: Seeing his splendour, that śūdra, together with his wife, / conceived a desire for kingship, and in the course of time fell subject to Time.

sanskrit_iast:
vanātkāṣṭhānyupāhatya kṛtvā bhartustataścitim ..
anvāruroha taṃ bhāryā śūdraṃ pañcatvamāgatam .. 11 ..
meaning:
वनात्काष्ठान्युपाहत्य कृत्वा भर्तुस्ततश्चितिम् ..
अन्वारुरोह तं भार्या शूद्रं पञ्चत्वमागतम् .. 11 ..
text_mt: Bringing wood from the forest and then making a pyre for her husband, / the wife ascended [the pyre] after that śūdra who had met his demise.

sanskrit_iast:
sa śūdro bhāryayā sārdhaṃ nākapṛṣṭhamito gataḥ ..
satataṃ dharmaśīlastu devaveśmopalepanāt .. 12 ..
meaning:
स शूद्रो भार्यया सार्धं नाकपृष्ठमितो गतः ..
सततं धर्मशीलस्तु देववेश्मोपलेपनात् .. 12 ..
text_mt: That śūdra, together with his wife, went from here to the vault of heaven, / being constantly of righteous conduct because of smearing the house of the god.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminneva kāle tu yuvanāśvo mahīpatiḥ ..
viṣṇuṃ sampūjayāmāsa putrīyeṇa vratena tu .. 13 ..
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु युवनाश्वो महीपतिः ..
विष्णुं सम्पूजयामास पुत्रीयेण व्रतेन तु .. 13 ..
text_mt: At that very time, King Yuvanāśva / worshipped Viṣṇu with a vow to obtain a son.

sanskrit_iast:
rājñastasya vratasyānte svapne prāha janārdanaḥ ..
bhārgavaṃ cyavanaṃ gaccha tataḥ putramavāpsyasi .. 14 ..
meaning:
राज्ञस्तस्य व्रतस्यान्ते स्वप्ने प्राह जनार्दनः ..
भार्गवं च्यवनं गच्छ ततः पुत्रमवाप्स्यसि .. 14 ..
text_mt: At the conclusion of the vow, Janārdana said to that king in a dream: / 'Go to Cyavana, the descendant of Bhṛgu; from him you will obtain a son.'

sanskrit_iast:
yuvanāśvastathoktastu svapne devena cakriṇā ..
prātaḥ padbhyāṃ yayau tasya cyavanasyāśramaṃ śubham .. 15 ..
meaning:
युवनाश्वस्तथोक्तस्तु स्वप्ने देवेन चक्रिणा ..
प्रातः पद्भ्यां ययौ तस्य च्यवनस्याश्रमं शुभम् .. 15 ..
text_mt: Yuvanāśva, thus addressed in a dream by the discus-bearing god, / went on foot in the morning to the auspicious hermitage of that Cyavana.

sanskrit_iast:
sampūjayitvā cyavanaṃ cyavanena ca pūjitaḥ ..
vratasvapnāvubhau tasya jagāda nṛpasattamaḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
सम्पूजयित्वा च्यवनं च्यवनेन च पूजितः ..
व्रतस्वप्नावुभौ तस्य जगाद नृपसत्तमः .. 16 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped Cyavana and being honoured by Cyavana, / the best of kings related to him both the vow and the dream.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣisaṅghānupādāya cyavano'pi mahātapāḥ ..
avijñātaṃ narendreṇa putrīyaṃ kṛtavāñjalam .. 17 ..
meaning:
ऋषिसङ्घानुपादाय च्यवनोऽपि महातपाः ..
अविज्ञातं नरेन्द्रेण पुत्रीयं कृतवाञ्जलम् .. 17 ..
text_mt: Cyavana too, of great austerities, having gathered hosts of sages, / prepared water that produces a son, unbeknownst to the ruler of men.

sanskrit_iast:
kalaśasthaṃ jalaṃ tacca sthāpayāmāsa bhārgavaḥ ..
tato niśīthe saṃprāpte tṛṣārtaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
कलशस्थं जलं तच्च स्थापयामास भार्गवः ..
ततो निशीथे संप्राप्ते तृषार्तः स महीपतिः .. 18 ..
text_mt: And the descendant of Bhṛgu placed that water in a pot; / then, when midnight arrived, that ruler of the earth, afflicted with thirst,

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣimadhye tu sa suptānṛṣīnvākyamathā'bravīt ..
tṛṣārto'smi bhṛśaṃ viprāḥ pānīyaṃ me prayacchata ..19 ..
meaning:
ऋषिमध्ये तु स सुप्तानृषीन्वाक्यमथाऽब्रवीत् ..
तृषार्तोऽस्मि भृशं विप्राः पानीयं मे प्रयच्छत ..19 ..
text_mt: spoke these words to the sages who were asleep among the sages: / 'I am exceedingly afflicted with thirst, O brahmins! Give me water!'

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣistasya na śuśrāva kaścidbhāvyarthacoditaḥ ..
tataḥ khinno mahīpālaḥ kalaśasthaṃ jalaṃ papau .. 1.170.20 ..
meaning:
ऋषिस्तस्य न शुश्राव कश्चिद्भाव्यर्थचोदितः ..
ततः खिन्नो महीपालः कलशस्थं जलं पपौ .. 1.170.20 ..
text_mt: Impelled by destiny, not one sage heard him; / then, distressed, the ruler of the earth drank the water in the pot.

sanskrit_iast:
pītvā suṣvāpa ṛṣayaḥ prātaḥ sarve samutthitāḥ ..
apaśyamānāḥ kalaśaṃ papracchuste para sparam .. 21 ..
meaning:
पीत्वा सुष्वाप ऋषयः प्रातः सर्वे समुत्थिताः ..
अपश्यमानाः कलशं पप्रच्छुस्ते पर स्परम् .. 21 ..
text_mt: Having drunk, he slept; in the morning, all the sages arose; / not seeing the pot, they asked one another:

sanskrit_iast:
putrīyaṃ kalaśaṃ rājñaḥ kṛtaṃ yattadgataṃ kva nu ..
tadovāca sa rājendrastānṛṣīnsaṃśitavratān .. 22 ..
meaning:
पुत्रीयं कलशं राज्ञः कृतं यत्तद्गतं क्व नु ..
तदोवाच स राजेन्द्रस्तानृषीन्संशितव्रतान् .. 22 ..
text_mt: 'Where has the pot prepared for the king to obtain a son gone?' / Then that best of kings said to those sages of strict vows:

sanskrit_iast:
tṛṣārtena mayā pītaḥ kalaśastvapavāhitaḥ ..
te hocustaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ bhāvyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ tvayā .. 23 ..
meaning:
तृषार्तेन मया पीतः कलशस्त्वपवाहितः ..
ते होचुस्तं नृपश्रेष्ठं भाव्यं कर्म कृतं त्वया .. 23 ..
text_mt: 'Afflicted with thirst, I drank [it] and removed the pot.' / And they said to that best of kings: 'You have done an act that was fated.'

sanskrit_iast:
bhāryā pītvaiva tattoyaṃ putraṃ te janayiṣyati ..
ityevaṃ mantrakalaśaḥ so'smābhirbhūpate kṛtaḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
भार्या पीत्वैव तत्तोयं पुत्रं ते जनयिष्यति ..
इत्येवं मन्त्रकलशः सोऽस्माभिर्भूपते कृतः .. 24 ..
text_mt: 'Having drunk that water, your wife would give birth to a son'— / thus that consecrated pot of water was prepared by us, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
putrīyamudakaṃ tacca tvayā pītamabuddhinā ..
tasmāttvameva tanayaṃ svakukṣau janayiṣyasi .. 25 ..
meaning:
पुत्रीयमुदकं तच्च त्वया पीतमबुद्धिना ..
तस्मात्त्वमेव तनयं स्वकुक्षौ जनयिष्यसि .. 25 ..
text_mt: And that water that produces a son was drunk by you without thought; / therefore, you yourself will give birth to a son in your own belly.

sanskrit_iast:
nāvāpsyasi tathā mṛtyuṃ varadānāddvijanmanām ..
evamuktastu sampūjya brāhmaṇānsvagṛhaṅgataḥ .. 26 ..
meaning:
नावाप्स्यसि तथा मृत्युं वरदानाद्द्विजन्मनाम् ..
एवमुक्तस्तु सम्पूज्य ब्राह्मणान्स्वगृहङ्गतः .. 26 ..
text_mt: And you will not meet death, due to the granting of a boon by the twice-born.' / Thus addressed, having worshipped the brahmins, he went to his own home.

sanskrit_iast:
rājñaḥ kukṣiṃ vinirbhidya jajñe bālārkasannibhaḥ ..
punaḥ putravatāṃ śreṣṭha śūdro'sau nākavicyutaḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
राज्ञः कुक्षिं विनिर्भिद्य जज्ञे बालार्कसन्निभः ..
पुनः पुत्रवतां श्रेष्ठ शूद्रोऽसौ नाकविच्युतः .. 27 ..
text_mt: Bursting open the belly of the king, that śūdra, fallen from heaven, / was born, resembling the rising sun, O best of those who have sons.

sanskrit_iast:
jātamātrasya tasyendro dadau prādeśinīṃ mukhe ..
āsādya yāṃ sa bālatvaṃ śiśustatyāja tatkṣaṇāt .. 28 .....
meaning:
जातमात्रस्य तस्येन्द्रो ददौ प्रादेशिनीं मुखे ..
आसाद्य यां स बालत्वं शिशुस्तत्याज तत्क्षणात् .. 28 .....
text_mt: As soon as he was born, Indra placed his forefinger in his mouth; / reaching it, the infant abandoned infancy that very moment.

sanskrit_iast:
kukṣiṃ pasparśa rājñastu rājasiṃhaśatakratuḥ ..
rājā śakrakarāmṛṣṭo vijvaraścāvraṇo'bhavat .. 29 ..
meaning:
कुक्षिं पस्पर्श राज्ञस्तु राजसिंहशतक्रतुः ..
राजा शक्रकरामृष्टो विज्वरश्चाव्रणोऽभवत् .. 29 ..
text_mt: Śatakratu, a lion among kings, touched the belly of the king; / touched by the hand of Śakra, the king became free from fever and unblemished.

sanskrit_iast:
yuvanāśvaḥ sa tasyāpi nāma cakre śatakratuḥ ...
māṃ dhāsyatīti māndhātā khyātiṃ tribhuvane gataḥ ..1.170.30 ..
meaning:
युवनाश्वः स तस्यापि नाम चक्रे शतक्रतुः ...
मां धास्यतीति मान्धाता ख्यातिं त्रिभुवने गतः ..1.170.30 ..
text_mt: And Śatakratu gave that son of Yuvanāśva a name: / thinking 'he will suckle me' (māṃ dhāsyati), he became known as Māndhātṛ throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
tamāviveśa bhagavāṃstejasā svena mādhavaḥ ..
sāpi svargacyutā bhāryā tasya śūdrasya yādava .. 31 ..
meaning:
तमाविवेश भगवांस्तेजसा स्वेन माधवः ..
सापि स्वर्गच्युता भार्या तस्य शूद्रस्य यादव .. 31 ..
text_mt: The blessed Mādhava entered him with his own splendor. / And that fallen-from-heaven wife of that śūdra, O descendant of Yadu,

sanskrit_iast:
kāśirājasutā jātā bhīmavegasya mānada ..
nāmnā prabhāvatī subhrūstryailokyasyaikasundarī .. 32 ..
meaning:
काशिराजसुता जाता भीमवेगस्य मानद ..
नाम्ना प्रभावती सुभ्रूस्त्र्यैलोक्यस्यैकसुन्दरी .. 32 ..
text_mt: was born as the daughter of the king of Kāśi, Bhīmavega, O granter of honor, / named Prabhāvatī, fair-browed, the singular beauty of the three worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
yuvanāśvastu tāṃ vavre māndhāturlakṣaṇānvitām ..
sa rājā pradadau tāṃ tu māndhātuścitravāhanaḥ .. 33 ..
meaning:
युवनाश्वस्तु तां वव्रे मान्धातुर्लक्षणान्विताम् ..
स राजा प्रददौ तां तु मान्धातुश्चित्रवाहनः .. 33 ..
text_mt: Yuvanāśva chose her, endowed with auspicious marks, for Māndhātṛ; / and that king, Citravāhana, gave her to Māndhātṛ.

sanskrit_iast:
ekaiva bhāryā sā tasya babhūvātyantasundarī ..
rūpayauvanasampannā prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī ..
kṛtvodvāhamayodhyāyāmabhiṣicya sa taṃ nṛpam .. 34 ..
meaning:
एकैव भार्या सा तस्य बभूवात्यन्तसुन्दरी ..
रूपयौवनसम्पन्ना प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी ..
कृत्वोद्वाहमयोध्यायामभिषिच्य स तं नृपम् .. 34 ..
text_mt: She was his only wife, exceedingly beautiful, / endowed with beauty and youth, dearer to him than his own breaths. / Having performed the wedding in Ayodhyā and consecrated that king,

sanskrit_iast:
yuvanāśvo vanaṃ prāyādvanādapi triviṣṭapam ..
rājyastho'pi sa māndhātā trailokyaṃ saptabhirdinaiḥ .. 35 ..
meaning:
युवनाश्वो वनं प्रायाद्वनादपि त्रिविष्टपम् ..
राज्यस्थोऽपि स मान्धाता त्रैलोक्यं सप्तभिर्दिनैः .. 35 ..
text_mt: Yuvanāśva departed to the forest, and from the forest to heaven. / Established in his kingdom, that Māndhātṛ, within seven days,

sanskrit_iast:
rathenaikena vaśagaṃ cakāra khaḍgadarpitaḥ ..
pātāle gagane śaile samudre ca mahātmanaḥ .. 36 ..
meaning:
रथेनैकेन वशगं चकार खड्गदर्पितः ..
पाताले गगने शैले समुद्रे च महात्मनः .. 36 ..
text_mt: brought the three worlds under his control with a single chariot, proud of his sword. / In the underworld, in the sky, on mountains, and in the ocean,

sanskrit_iast:
āsīttasyāpratihatā gatiścakrasya pārthiva ..
cakravartī sa dharmātmā vaiṣṇavaśca tathā'bhavat .. 37 ..
meaning:
आसीत्तस्याप्रतिहता गतिश्चक्रस्य पार्थिव ..
चक्रवर्ती स धर्मात्मा वैष्णवश्च तथाऽभवत् .. 37 ..
text_mt: the progress of that great-souled one's chariot was unobstructed, O king. / He became a righteous universal monarch and a Vaiṣṇava.

sanskrit_iast:
samāyutānāṃ bubhuje sa rājyaṃ daśa mānada ..
brahmāṇḍamaṇḍapaṃ yāvatsūryastapati raśmibhiḥ ..
tāvatkṣetraṃ mahībharturyuvanāśvasya kīrtyate .. 38 ..
meaning:
समायुतानां बुभुजे स राज्यं दश मानद ..
ब्रह्माण्डमण्डपं यावत्सूर्यस्तपति रश्मिभिः ..
तावत्क्षेत्रं महीभर्तुर्युवनाश्वस्य कीर्त्यते .. 38 ..
text_mt: He enjoyed the kingdom for ten myriad years, O granter of honor. / As far as the sun warms the pavilion of the universe with its rays, / that whole territory is renowned as belonging to Yuvanāśva's son, the lord of the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ sa rājā vijitāripakṣo devājirālepanakṛdbabhūva ...
bhāryā ca sā tasya babhūva bhāryā loke variṣṭhā pramadāvarābhyaḥ .. 39 ..
meaning:
एवं स राजा विजितारिपक्षो देवाजिरालेपनकृद्बभूव ...
भार्या च सा तस्य बभूव भार्या लोके वरिष्ठा प्रमदावराभ्यः .. 39 ..
text_mt: Thus that king, having conquered his adversaries, smeared the courtyards of the gods [with his offerings]; / and that wife of his was the foremost wife in the world among excellent women.

sanskrit_iast:
1.171
.. vajra uvāca .. ..
sa tu rājā mayā brahmanmāṃdhātā bhuvaneśvaraḥ ..
māheśvareṇa śūlena lavaṇena hataḥ śrutaḥ .. 1 ..
meaning:
1.171
.. वज्र उवाच .. ..
स तु राजा मया ब्रह्मन्मांधाता भुवनेश्वरः ..
माहेश्वरेण शूलेन लवणेन हतः श्रुतः .. 1 ..
text_mt:
1.171
Vajra said: / But that king Māndhātṛ, the lord of the world, O brahmin, / has been heard by me to have been slain by Lavaṇa with the trident of Maheśvara.
title: Svarūpavarṇanam

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ajeyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tejastatra nityaṃ ca jantuṣu ..
nāśamāyānti te sarve hīnā vaiṣṇava tejasā ..2 ..
meaning:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
अजेयं वैष्णवं तेजस्तत्र नित्यं च जन्तुषु ..
नाशमायान्ति ते सर्वे हीना वैष्णव तेजसा ..2 ..
text_mt: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The splendor of Viṣṇu is unconquerable and eternal among living beings there; / all of them go to destruction when deprived of the splendor of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
avināśi jagatyasminna kiñcidatha vidyate ..
ṛte tu mahatastasmāttejaso nṛpa vaiṣṇavāt .. 3 ..
meaning:
अविनाशि जगत्यस्मिन्न किञ्चिदथ विद्यते ..
ऋते तु महतस्तस्मात्तेजसो नृप वैष्णवात् .. 3 ..
text_mt: Nothing whatsoever in this world is imperishable, / except indeed for that great splendor of Viṣṇu, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
tejastasya sudurvāhyaṃ dehibhirnapa sarvadā ..
tasmāttena vihīnāste kṣayaṃ gacchanti mānada .. 4 ..
meaning:
तेजस्तस्य सुदुर्वाह्यं देहिभिर्नप सर्वदा ..
तस्मात्तेन विहीनास्ते क्षयं गच्छन्ति मानद .. 4 ..
text_mt: His splendor is always exceedingly difficult to bear for embodied beings, O king; / therefore, abandoned by it, they go to ruin, O granter of honor.

sanskrit_iast:
matsyaḥ kūrmo varāhaśca narasiṃho'tha vāmanaḥ ..
brahmā śambhustathaivārkaścandramāśca śatakratuḥ .. 5 ..
meaning:
मत्स्यः कूर्मो वराहश्च नरसिंहोऽथ वामनः ..
ब्रह्मा शम्भुस्तथैवार्कश्चन्द्रमाश्च शतक्रतुः .. 5 ..
text_mt: The Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, Narasiṃha, and the Dwarf, / Brahmā, Śambhu, as well as the Sun, the Moon, and Śatakratu—

sanskrit_iast:
evamādyāstathaivānye yuktā vaiṣṇavatejasā ..
gajacchāyānumānena viyujyante ca tejasā .. 6 ..
meaning:
एवमाद्यास्तथैवान्ये युक्ता वैष्णवतेजसा ..
गजच्छायानुमानेन वियुज्यन्ते च तेजसा .. 6 ..
text_mt: these and other [beings] endowed with the splendor of Viṣṇu / are separated from that splendor according to the measure of an elephant's shadow.

sanskrit_iast:
vitejasaśca te sarve pañcatvamupayānti ca ..
pañcabhūtātmakaṃ sthūlaṃ yatkiñcijjagatīgatam .. 7 ..
meaning:
वितेजसश्च ते सर्वे पञ्चत्वमुपयान्ति च ..
पञ्चभूतात्मकं स्थूलं यत्किञ्चिज्जगतीगतम् .. 7 ..
text_mt: And bereft of that splendor, all of them meet dissolution. / Whatever gross thing exists in the world, composed of the five elements,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvaṃ vināśi tajjñeyaṃ tvayā pārthivasattama ..
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena viśvamidaṃ tatam .. 8 ..
meaning:
सर्वं विनाशि तज्ज्ञेयं त्वया पार्थिवसत्तम ..
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन विश्वमिदं ततम् .. 8 ..
text_mt: you must understand all of that to be perishable, O best of kings. / But know that to be imperishable by which this entire universe is pervaded:

sanskrit_iast:
yattu gandhaguṇairhīnaṃ rūpasparśavivarjitam ..
śabdahīnaṃ ca virasaṃ sarveśaṃ sarvagaṃ ca yat .. 9 ..
meaning:
यत्तु गन्धगुणैर्हीनं रूपस्पर्शविवर्जितम् ..
शब्दहीनं च विरसं सर्वेशं सर्वगं च यत् .. 9 ..
text_mt: that which is devoid of the quality of smell, devoid of form and touch, / free of sound, devoid of taste, the ruler of all, and omnipresent;

sanskrit_iast:
nirguṇaṃ tadguṇātītamantikasthaṃ ca dūragam ..
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam .. 1.171.10 ..
meaning:
निर्गुणं तद्गुणातीतमन्तिकस्थं च दूरगम् ..
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् .. 1.171.10 ..
text_mt: quality-less, beyond qualities, situated near and far away, / appearing through the qualities of all senses, yet devoid of all senses;

sanskrit_iast:
sarvataḥ pāṇipādāntaṃ sarvato'kṣiśiromukham ..
sarvendriyaguṇaṃ devaṃ sarvataḥ parameśvaram ..11..
meaning:
सर्वतः पाणिपादान्तं सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् ..
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणं देवं सर्वतः परमेश्वरम् ..11..
text_mt: having hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, / the god possessing the qualities of all senses, the supreme lord everywhere.

sanskrit_iast:
avināśi tadevaikaṃ yasyodaragataṃ jagat ..
sadāśiveti taṃ kecidāhurdevaṃ jagatpatim ..12..
meaning:
अविनाशि तदेवैकं यस्योदरगतं जगत् ..
सदाशिवेति तं केचिदाहुर्देवं जगत्पतिम् ..12..
text_mt: That alone is imperishable, in whose belly rests the universe. / Some call that god, the lord of the universe, Sadāśiva;

sanskrit_iast:
vāsudeveti cāpyanye kālamityeva cāpare..
devamityapare taṃ ca svabhāvamiti cāpare .. 13 ..
meaning:
वासुदेवेति चाप्यन्ये कालमित्येव चापरे..
देवमित्यपरे तं च स्वभावमिति चापरे .. 13 ..
text_mt: and others call him Vāsudeva, while others call him Time; / others call him God, and others call him Nature;

sanskrit_iast:
karmeti cāpare prāhuḥ puruṣeti tathā pare ..
praṇavākhyaṃ tathā taṃ ca vidurvedavido janāḥ .. 14 ..
meaning:
कर्मेति चापरे प्राहुः पुरुषेति तथा परे ..
प्रणवाख्यं तथा तं च विदुर्वेदविदो जनाः .. 14 ..
text_mt: others call him Action, and others likewise call him the Cosmic Person; / and people who know the Vedas know him by the name of Praṇava.

sanskrit_iast:
tadekamajamavyaktamavināśaṃ narādhipa ..
ṛte tamekamīśānamaṃtavatsakalaṃ jagat .. 15 ..
meaning:
तदेकमजमव्यक्तमविनाशं नराधिप ..
ऋते तमेकमीशानमंतवत्सकलं जगत् .. 15 ..
text_mt: That alone is unborn, unmanifest, and imperishable, O ruler of men; / except for that single ruler, the entire universe has an end.

sanskrit_iast:
etattavoktaṃ bhuvanasya patyurmayā svarūpaṃ yaduvaṃśacandra ..
bhaktiṃ vinā buddhimatāpi yasya śakyaṃ na vaktuṃ grahaṇaṃ nareṇa .. 16 ..
1.172
.. vajra uvāca ..
prādurbhāvā varāhādyāḥ sarveśasyāmitātmanaḥ ..
mahābhūtacayāḥ sarve janmamṛtyuyutāśca ye .. 1 ..
yadyevaṃ prāṇibhisteṣāṃ ko viśeṣo bhṛgūttama ..
etattvaṃ saṃśayaṃ chindhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 2 ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sarve jīvā mahīpāla karmabandhanibandhanāḥ ..
jāyante ca mriyante ca paratantrāḥ sadaiva ca .. 3 ..
īśvarapreritairnityaṃ karmabandhaiḥ śubhāśubhaiḥ ..
janmāntarakṛtairbhūpa sukhaduḥkhasamanvitāḥ .. 4 ..
vāsudevastu dharmātmā prādurbhāveṣu yādava ..
ātmanaḥ svecchayā janma vidhatte maraṇaṃ tathā .. 5 ..
karmāṇi na ca limpanti prādurbhāveṣvapi prabhum ..
karmasvapi sadā saktaṃ padmapatramivāmbhasā .. 6 ..
meaning:
एतत्तवोक्तं भुवनस्य पत्युर्मया स्वरूपं यदुवंशचन्द्र ..
भक्तिं विना बुद्धिमतापि यस्य शक्यं न वक्तुं ग्रहणं नरेण .. 16 ..
1.172
.. वज्र उवाच ..
प्रादुर्भावा वराहाद्याः सर्वेशस्यामितात्मनः ..
महाभूतचयाः सर्वे जन्ममृत्युयुताश्च ये .. 1 ..
यद्येवं प्राणिभिस्तेषां को विशेषो भृगूत्तम ..
एतत्त्वं संशयं छिन्धि परं कौतूहलं हि मे .. 2 ..
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
सर्वे जीवा महीपाल कर्मबन्धनिबन्धनाः ..
जायन्ते च म्रियन्ते च परतन्त्राः सदैव च .. 3 ..
ईश्वरप्रेरितैर्नित्यं कर्मबन्धैः शुभाशुभैः ..
जन्मान्तरकृतैर्भूप सुखदुःखसमन्विताः .. 4 ..
वासुदेवस्तु धर्मात्मा प्रादुर्भावेषु यादव ..
आत्मनः स्वेच्छया जन्म विधत्ते मरणं तथा .. 5 ..
कर्माणि न च लिम्पन्ति प्रादुर्भावेष्वपि प्रभुम् ..
कर्मस्वपि सदा सक्तं पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा .. 6 ..
text_mt:
Thus the true nature of the lord of the world has been told to you by me, O moon of the Yadu dynasty, / the comprehension of which cannot be expressed by man, even if intelligent, without devotion.
1.172
Vajra said: / The manifestations beginning with the Boar belonging to the ruler of all, the boundless soul, / and all the aggregates of elements are accompanied by birth and death.
If so, what is their difference from ordinary living beings, O foremost of the Bhṛgus? / Dispel this doubt of mine, for great indeed is my curiosity.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / All individual souls, O ruler of earth, are tied by the bonds of karma; / they are born and they die, always dependent on others,
constantly driven by the Lord through auspicious and inauspicious bonds of karma / performed in other births, O king, accompanied by happiness and sorrow.
Vāsudeva, however, the righteous soul, in his manifestations, O descendant of Yadu, / ordains his own birth and death by his own will.
And actions do not cling to the Lord even in his manifestations, / even while always engaged in actions, just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf.

sanskrit_iast:
phalānāṃ karmajātānāṃ bhogaṃ tatrāpi yādava ..
nṛṇāṃ darśayate mithyā maryādābhedabhīrnṛpa .. 7 ..
yadāyadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati yādava ..
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjatyasau .. 8 ..
devatiryaṅmanuṣyeṣu gandharvoragapakṣiṣu ..
yoniṣvanyeṣvapi tathā buddhvā kāryabalābalam .. 9 ..
yasyāṃ yasyāṃ yadā yonau prādurbhavati kāraṇāt ..
tadyonisadṛśaṃ tatsa tadā loke viceṣṭate .. 1.172.10 ..
saṃhartuṃ jagadīśānaḥ samartho'pi tadā nṛpa ..
tadyonisadṛśopāyairvadhyānhiṃsati yādava .. 11 ..
hārdaṃ tamastathā naiśaṃ mūrtaṃ ca puruṣottamaḥ ..
eka eva sa lokānāṃ nāśayatyamaladyutiḥ .. 12 ..
hārdaṃ dhvastaṃ tamastena jagato devamūrtinā ..
jyotīrūpeṇa ca dhvastaṃ tamo naiśaṃ sudāruṇam .. 13 ..
tamo nāśayituṃ mūrtaṃ prādurbhāvagataḥ sadā ..
mūrtaṃ tamaśca rājendra daityadānavarākṣasāḥ .. 14 ..
meaning:
फलानां कर्मजातानां भोगं तत्रापि यादव ..
नृणां दर्शयते मिथ्या मर्यादाभेदभीर्नृप .. 7 ..
यदायदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति यादव ..
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजत्यसौ .. 8 ..
देवतिर्यङ्मनुष्येषु गन्धर्वोरगपक्षिषु ..
योनिष्वन्येष्वपि तथा बुद्ध्वा कार्यबलाबलम् .. 9 ..
यस्यां यस्यां यदा योनौ प्रादुर्भवति कारणात् ..
तद्योनिसदृशं तत्स तदा लोके विचेष्टते .. 1.172.10 ..
संहर्तुं जगदीशानः समर्थोऽपि तदा नृप ..
तद्योनिसदृशोपायैर्वध्यान्हिंसति यादव .. 11 ..
हार्दं तमस्तथा नैशं मूर्तं च पुरुषोत्तमः ..
एक एव स लोकानां नाशयत्यमलद्युतिः .. 12 ..
हार्दं ध्वस्तं तमस्तेन जगतो देवमूर्तिना ..
ज्योतीरूपेण च ध्वस्तं तमो नैशं सुदारुणम् .. 13 ..
तमो नाशयितुं मूर्तं प्रादुर्भावगतः सदा ..
मूर्तं तमश्च राजेन्द्र दैत्यदानवराक्षसाः .. 14 ..
text_mt:
Even there, O descendant of Yadu, fearing the rupture of righteous order, / he falsely displays to men the experience of the fruits born of karma, O king.
For whenever there is a decline of dharma, O descendant of Yadu, / and an uprising of adharma, then he projects himself.
Among gods, animals, and humans, among gandharvas, serpents, and birds, / and in other wombs as well, having considered the relative weight of the task,
in whatever womb he manifests on any occasion due to a specific cause, / he acts in the world in a manner appropriate to that womb.
Though capable of destroying [all at once], the ruler of the universe then, O king, / destroys those who deserve to be slain through means appropriate to that womb, O descendant of Yadu.
The darkness of the heart, the darkness of night, and embodied darkness— / Puruṣottama, of spotless splendor, destroys all three for the worlds entirely alone.
The darkness of the heart of the world was dispelled by him in the form of a deity; / and the terrible darkness of night was dispelled by him in the form of light.
To destroy embodied darkness, he continually assumes manifestations; / and embodied darkness, O king of kings, consists of daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas.

sanskrit_iast:
vandhyānāmapi daityānāṃ dehastho'pi janārdanaḥ ..
na vimuñcati dehāni yuktyā tāṃśca jighāṃsati .. 15 ..
daivatānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca dvijānāṃ ca gurupriyaḥ ..
śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā bhavatyārādhane rataḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
वन्ध्यानामपि दैत्यानां देहस्थोऽपि जनार्दनः ..
न विमुञ्चति देहानि युक्त्या तांश्च जिघांसति .. 15 ..
दैवतानां गुरूणां च द्विजानां च गुरुप्रियः ..
शास्त्रदृष्टेन विधिना भवत्याराधने रतः .. 16 ..
text_mt:
Even when dwelling in the bodies of demons who cannot be slain,
Janārdana does not abandon their bodies, and by skilful means he seeks to slay them.
Affectionate toward elders, he is devoted to the worship
of gods, elders, and twice-born men according to the rule set forth in scripture.

sanskrit_iast:
na ca tasyāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana ..
naivānāptamavāptavyaṃ vartate'tha ca karmasu .. 17 ..
meaning:
न च तस्यास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन ..
नैवानाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्ततेऽथ च कर्मसु .. 17 ..
text_mt:
There is nothing for him to do in the three worlds,
nor is there anything unattained to be attained, yet he engages in actions.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī ca sarvaśaktirapi prabhuḥ ..
tathāpyadhīte yajate tapastapyati pārthiva .. 18 ..
meaning:
सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च सर्वशक्तिरपि प्रभुः ..
तथाप्यधीते यजते तपस्तप्यति पार्थिव .. 18 ..
text_mt:
Though all-knowing, all-seeing, all-powerful, and sovereign,
he nevertheless studies, offers sacrifices, and performs austerities, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
maryādāsthāpanārthāya jagato hitakāmyayā ..
karoti rājankarmāṇi kīnāśa iva durbalaḥ .. 19 ..
meaning:
मर्यादास्थापनार्थाय जगतो हितकाम्यया ..
करोति राजन्कर्माणि कीनाश इव दुर्बलः .. 19 ..
text_mt:
For the sake of establishing limits, out of a desire for the welfare of the world,
he performs actions, O king, like a feeble laborer.

sanskrit_iast:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ ..
sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanu vartate .. 1.172.20 ..
meaning:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ..
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनु वर्तते .. 1.172.20 ..
text_mt:
Whatever an exemplary person does, other people do as well;
whatever standard he sets, the world follows after it.

sanskrit_iast:
etatkāraṇamāsthāya sadā karmasu vartate ..
prādurbhāvakṛto viṣṇuryathānyaḥ prākṛtastathā .. 21 ..
meaning:
एतत्कारणमास्थाय सदा कर्मसु वर्तते ..
प्रादुर्भावकृतो विष्णुर्यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा .. 21 ..
text_mt:
Taking recourse to this reason, Viṣṇu manifested [as an incarnation]
always engages in actions, like any ordinary person.

sanskrit_iast:
devebhyaśca ṛṣibhyaśca varānprārthayate sadā ..
varāṃśca varadasteṣāṃ mānayatyapi pāṇḍava .. 22 ..
meaning:
देवेभ्यश्च ऋषिभ्यश्च वरान्प्रार्थयते सदा ..
वरांश्च वरदस्तेषां मानयत्यपि पाण्डव .. 22 ..
text_mt:
He always requests boons from the gods and the ṛṣis;
and though he is the grantor of boons, he honors their boons, O descendant of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit_iast:
prādurbhāvaratastasmātparo'yamiti mānavāḥ ..
puruṣaṃ nādhigacchanti mohitāstasya māyayā .. 23 ..
meaning:
प्रादुर्भावरतस्तस्मात्परोऽयमिति मानवाः ..
पुरुषं नाधिगच्छन्ति मोहितास्तस्य मायया .. 23 ..
text_mt:
Deluded by his māyā, human beings do not recognize the supreme Person,
[thinking,] 'He is merely engaged in an incarnation.'

sanskrit_iast:
prādurbhāvaṃ gato'pyevaṃ saṃhatya sa carācaram ..
nimeṣāntaramāttreṇa śaktimāñjagataḥ prabhuḥ ..24 ..
meaning:
प्रादुर्भावं गतोऽप्येवं संहत्य स चराचरम् ..
निमेषान्तरमात्त्रेण शक्तिमाञ्जगतः प्रभुः ..24 ..
text_mt:
Even when he has entered upon an incarnation, having drawn together all moving and unmoving beings,
that capable sovereign of the world [can dissolve them] in the mere span of a blink.

sanskrit_iast:
prādurbhāvagatasyāpi tasya sarvagatā smṛtā ..
svatantratā ca sarvatra nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 25 ..
meaning:
प्रादुर्भावगतस्यापि तस्य सर्वगता स्मृता ..
स्वतन्त्रता च सर्वत्र नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 25 ..
text_mt:
Even when he has assumed an incarnation, his omnipresence is remembered,
as is his absolute autonomy everywhere; in this matter no doubt is to be entertained.

sanskrit_iast:
mahadviśeṣametatte prāṇibhiḥ prāṇināṃ pateḥ ..
mayoktaṃ tasya devasya sarvagasya svayambhuvaḥ .. 26 ..
meaning:
महद्विशेषमेतत्ते प्राणिभिः प्राणिनां पतेः ..
मयोक्तं तस्य देवस्य सर्वगस्य स्वयम्भुवः .. 26 ..
text_mt:
This great distinction of the Lord of living beings from living beings
has been explained to you by me, regarding that self-existent, omnipresent deity.

sanskrit_iast:
ākṣiptāḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyaiḥ kaiścidyaduvarottama ..
teṣāmāviśate devastejasā tena sarvaśaḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
आक्षिप्ताः कर्मभिः पुण्यैः कैश्चिद्यदुवरोत्तम ..
तेषामाविशते देवस्तेजसा तेन सर्वशः .. 27 ..
text_mt:
Impelled by some meritorious deeds, O best of the Yadus,
the god enters into them entirely by means of that power.

sanskrit_iast:
āviṣṭāstejasā tena devena parameṣṭhinā ..
tadvatkarmāṇi kurvanti pūjyamānā maharṣibhiḥ .. 28 ..
meaning:
आविष्टास्तेजसा तेन देवेन परमेष्ठिना ..
तद्वत्कर्माणि कुर्वन्ति पूज्यमाना महर्षिभिः .. 28 ..
text_mt:
Possessed by that power by the god Parameṣṭhin,
they perform deeds in that manner, honored by great ṛṣis.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā tu kāle saṃnyastāstena vaiṣṇavatejasā ..
diṣṭāntavaśamāyānti tasyaiva rucitaṃ yathā .. 29 ..
meaning:
तथा तु काले संन्यस्तास्तेन वैष्णवतेजसा ..
दिष्टान्तवशमायान्ति तस्यैव रुचितं यथा .. 29 ..
text_mt:
Then, at the [appointed] time, abandoned by that Vaiṣṇava power,
they come under the sway of their ordained end, just as it pleases him.

sanskrit_iast:
ye ca kecana loke'smindṛśyante tejasānvitāḥ ..
teṣāṃ tadvaiṣṇavaṃ tejastvayā jñeyaṃ mahīpate .. 1.172.30 ..
meaning:
ये च केचन लोकेऽस्मिन्दृश्यन्ते तेजसान्विताः ..
तेषां तद्वैष्णवं तेजस्त्वया ज्ञेयं महीपते .. 1.172.30 ..
text_mt:
And whatever beings in this world are seen endowed with splendor,
their splendor is to be understood by you as Vaiṣṇava, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
yaccandramasi yaccāgnau yacca sūrye jagatpatau ..
tejaḥ paśyati tatsarvaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ viddhi pārthiva .. 31 ..
meaning:
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ यच्च सूर्ये जगत्पतौ ..
तेजः पश्यति तत्सर्वं वैष्णवं विद्धि पार्थिव .. 31 ..
text_mt:
What splendor one sees in the moon, in fire, and in the sun, the lord of the world,
know all that to be Vaiṣṇava, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
agastyapramukhānāṃ ca yā ca śaktiratīndriyā ..
tatsthasya rājansā jñeyā tvayā vaiṣṇavatejasā .. 32 ..
meaning:
अगस्त्यप्रमुखानां च या च शक्तिरतीन्द्रिया ..
तत्स्थस्य राजन्सा ज्ञेया त्वया वैष्णवतेजसा .. 32 ..
text_mt:
And the power beyond the senses of Agastya and other [sages]—
you should know that it belongs to him abiding within it through Vaiṣṇava power, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā ..
tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ yuktaṃ vaiṣṇavatejasā .. 33 ..
meaning:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा ..
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं युक्तं वैष्णवतेजसा .. 33 ..
text_mt:
Whatever being possesses majesty, prosperity, or great energy,
understand that every such being is endowed with Vaiṣṇava power.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇānāṃ surāṇāṃ ca sādhvīnāṃ ca tathā gavām ..
jagatāṃ dhāriṇīṃ śaktiṃ viddhi tāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ vibho ..34..
meaning:
ब्राह्मणानां सुराणां च साध्वीनां च तथा गवाम् ..
जगतां धारिणीं शक्तिं विद्धि तां वैष्णवीं विभो ..34..
text_mt:
The power of brahmins, gods, virtuous women, and cattle
that sustains the worlds—know that to be the power of Viṣṇu, O mighty lord.

sanskrit_iast:
rājānastejasā yuktā vaiṣṇavena vasundharām ..
pālayanti mahīpāla vīryodagrā yaśasvinaḥ .. 35 ..
meaning:
राजानस्तेजसा युक्ता वैष्णवेन वसुन्धराम् ..
पालयन्ति महीपाल वीर्योदग्रा यशस्विनः .. 35 ..
text_mt:
Kings endowed with Vaiṣṇava power protect the earth,
O protector of the earth, exalted in valour and renowned.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣayaśca tathā viprā vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ ..
pālayanti jagatkṛtsnaṃ yuktā vaiṣṇavatejasā ..36..
meaning:
ऋषयश्च तथा विप्रा वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः ..
पालयन्ति जगत्कृत्स्नं युक्ता वैष्णवतेजसा ..36..
text_mt:
And the ṛṣis and the twice-born who have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas
protect the entire world, endowed with Vaiṣṇava power.

sanskrit_iast:
tretāyugādau ye kecijjāyante cakravartinaḥ ..
guruṇā viddhi tānsarvānsaṃyuktānviṣṇutejasā ..37..
meaning:
त्रेतायुगादौ ये केचिज्जायन्ते चक्रवर्तिनः ..
गुरुणा विद्धि तान्सर्वान्संयुक्तान्विष्णुतेजसा ..37..
text_mt:
Whatever universal monarchs are born at the beginning of the Tretā age,
know them all to be endowed with the mighty power of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
ājānubāhavaḥ sarve nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalāḥ ..
jihvayā sakalaṃ vaktraṃ parimārjanti te tathā ..38..
meaning:
आजानुबाहवः सर्वे न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलाः ..
जिह्वया सकलं वक्त्रं परिमार्जन्ति ते तथा ..38..
text_mt:
All of them have arms reaching down to their knees and the proportions of a banyan tree;
they can wipe their entire face with their tongue;

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṣṭyā dantaiśca saṃyuktā daṃṣṭrābhiśca tathāṣṭabhiḥ ..
aurṇeyaṃ ca śubhaṃ teṣāṃ bhavatyantarbhruvornṛpa..39..
meaning:
षष्ट्या दन्तैश्च संयुक्ता दंष्ट्राभिश्च तथाष्टभिः ..
और्णेयं च शुभं तेषां भवत्यन्तर्भ्रुवोर्नृप..39..
text_mt:
they are endowed with sixty teeth and eight canine teeth;
and they have an auspicious whorl of hair between their eyebrows, O king;

sanskrit_iast:
cakrāṅkitaiḥ pādatalaiḥ karaiścāpi śarāṅkitaiḥ ..
jālapādakarāścaiva tathā turagamehanāḥ ..1.172.40..
meaning:
चक्राङ्कितैः पादतलैः करैश्चापि शराङ्कितैः ..
जालपादकराश्चैव तथा तुरगमेहनाः ..1.172.40..
text_mt:
their soles are marked with wheels and their hands with arrows;
they have webbed hands and feet, and equine privities;

sanskrit_iast:
rūpavantaḥ prabhāvanto vapuṣmantaśca yādava ..
atīndriyajñānabalāḥ pṛthivyāṃ cakravartinaḥ..41..
meaning:
रूपवन्तः प्रभावन्तो वपुष्मन्तश्च यादव ..
अतीन्द्रियज्ञानबलाः पृथिव्यां चक्रवर्तिनः..41..
text_mt:
they are handsome, majestic, magnificent, O Yādava,
possessing knowledge and strength that transcend the senses—the universal monarchs on earth.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāṃ tu sapta ratnāni bhavantīha mahītale..
hastyaśvaratharatnāni bhāryāratnaṃ tathaiva ca ..42..
meaning:
तेषां तु सप्त रत्नानि भवन्तीह महीतले..
हस्त्यश्वरथरत्नानि भार्यारत्नं तथैव च ..42..
text_mt:
And seven jewels belong to them here on the surface of the earth:
the jewels of an elephant, a horse, a chariot, and likewise the jewel of a wife,

sanskrit_iast:
tathaivāyudharatnaṃ ca maṇiratnanidhistathā ..
catasraścāpratihatāsteṣāṃ tu gatayastathā..43..
meaning:
तथैवायुधरत्नं च मणिरत्ननिधिस्तथा ..
चतस्रश्चाप्रतिहतास्तेषां तु गतयस्तथा..43..
text_mt:
and likewise the jewel of a weapon, the jewel of a gem, and a treasure.
And four unimpeded courses belong to them:

sanskrit_iast:
pātāle gagane śaile samudre ca mahīpate..
samudraḥ stambhitajalaḥ prayāṇe cakravartinām .. 44 ..
meaning:
पाताले गगने शैले समुद्रे च महीपते..
समुद्रः स्तम्भितजलः प्रयाणे चक्रवर्तिनाम् .. 44 ..
text_mt:
in the underworld, in the sky, upon a mountain, and upon the ocean, O lord of the earth;
the ocean has its waters stilled during the march of the universal monarchs,

sanskrit_iast:
bhūsamāśca tathā śailā mārge teṣāṃ bhavanti tu ..
bhūmirdadāti vivaraṃ pātālamupayāsyatām .. 45 ..
meaning:
भूसमाश्च तथा शैला मार्गे तेषां भवन्ति तु ..
भूमिर्ददाति विवरं पातालमुपयास्यताम् .. 45 ..
text_mt:
and mountains become level with the ground in their path;
the earth opens a fissure for those about to enter the underworld;

sanskrit_iast:
na viṣīdanti gagane tathā teṣāṃ turaṅgamāḥ ..
śrutena tapasā yajñairvīryeṇāstrabalena ca .. 46 ..
meaning:
न विषीदन्ति गगने तथा तेषां तुरङ्गमाः ..
श्रुतेन तपसा यज्ञैर्वीर्येणास्त्रबलेन च .. 46 ..
text_mt:
nor do their horses falter in the sky.
By sacred learning, austerity, sacrifices, valour, and mastery of weapons,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvebhyaste'tiricyante prāṇibhyo manujeśvara ..
ārādhitajagannāthāḥ prāpnuvantīha tatpadam .. 47 ..
meaning:

1.173
Vajra said:
I wish to hear about that son-yielding observance which was performed by King Yuvanāśva,
out of a desire for the welfare of mankind.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I shall explain to you the son-yielding observance, O best of kings,
called the Anantavrata, which grants the birth of a son to those who practice it.
Month by month, when the asterism marked by the name of that month arrives, / fasting, best of men, one should worship the God.
Particularly, one limb after another of the God should be worshipped each month, / restrained and pure; listen to my sequence of the limbs.
Beginning from Mārgaśīrṣa, one should undertake this observance: / In Mārgaśīrṣa, one should worship the left knee of the God.
And in the month of Pauṣa, one should worship the left portion of the waist; / in Māgha, under Maghā, one should worship the left arm of the God.

text_mt:
Under the asterism Uttarāphalguni, one should worship the left shoulder. / In these four left [phases], one should perform bathing with cow urine.
The worship of the God of gods should be performed with red flowers and other offerings; / the fire offering should be made with clarified butter, and a gift of sesame seeds to the twice-born.
And likewise a gift of copper; then the drinking of cow urine, / and then the wise person should take food consisting of sacrificial fare.
In Caitra under Citrā, one should worship the right shoulder of the God; / and in Vaiśākha under Viśākhā, the right arm of the God.
In Jyeṣṭha under Jyeṣṭhā, one should worship the right portion of the waist; / and in Āṣāḍha under Vaiśvadeva, the right knee.
In these four months, bathing with milk is prescribed, / and worship with yellow flowers and the like for the discus-bearing God of gods.
One should make the fire offering with śāli rice; barley should be given to the twice-born, / and silver should also be given, just as food is taken.
So it should be done, lord of men. Then, in Śrāvaṇa under Śravaṇa, / one should worship first the feet of Him whose whole world this is.

text_mt:
In the month of Bhādrapada, the private parts; then in Āśvina, the heart; / and in Kārtika under Kṛttikā, the worship of the head should be done.
In these four months, bathing with curds is prescribed, / and worship of the God of gods with white flowers and the like.
The fire offering should be made with milk; clarified butter should be given to the twice-born, / and gold likewise, O King; eating should be done with curds.
The name of Ananta should be chanted in all months, O King; / with that very name, one should perform the fire-offering rites for the God.
At the conclusion of the observance, food should be given to brahmins; / and gifts should be given according to one's capacity to brahmins, O ruler of men.
After a year, one attains all wishes whatsoever. / It should be observed by those desiring sons, those desiring a livelihood, those seeking servants, wives, and wealth,
and by those praying for strength, health, and prosperity. / This observance, great king, is auspicious and brings supreme well-being.

It is called the Anantavrata, destroying all defilements. / Having performed this observance in the past, King Yuvanāśva
obtained a son, Māndhātṛ, a universal sovereign king; / and likewise, O foremost of kings, Śīladharā, the wife of Kṛtavīrya,
by means of this observance obtained a thousand-armed son, / named Kārtavīryārjuna, a universal sovereign king,
whom the blessed Mādhava entered with His own splendor: / 'Homage to you, Kārtavīrya, the great-souled Arjuna,
and the sovereign over the earth with its seven continents and oceans!' / By that much merit, it equals [the gift of] a prastha measure of sesame seeds,
duly given, O King, to a self-controlled brahmin. / At whose very birth an auspicious wind blew,
the sky became dustless, and the entire world experienced joy; / seeking refuge with the king, Daityas entered human form

At night, one should eat the offered food, restrained in speech and well-composed; / restrained, one should spend that night lying on the bare ground.
One should do so again until Kṛttikā in Kārtika; / there, having worshipped the Lord of gods according to the initial rule, O King,
a vessel filled with clarified butter, along with gold, should be given to a twice-born, / and a feast should especially be provided for brahmins.
Having performed this observance for a year, the best of men, / having attained his abode, rejoices, and likewise a woman, O descendant of Yadu.
It produces lasting fortune, a mind set on dharma, strength, good fortune, vitality, and steadfast courage, / and a very long stay in heaven; this observance for human beings brings immense merit.

"This accomplished female ascetic knows, the renowned Śāmbarāyaṇī."
Having been addressed thus, Śakra, the slayer of Bala, asked [her].
And she narrated to Śakra the great deeds of earlier Indras,
of the past Śakras by the hundreds and thousands.
She related their deeds in other aeons as well, O lord.
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
All the cousin-kinsmen of every one of the Śakras
were destroyed by that mighty Viṣṇu;
likewise, all the Śakras were endowed with that Vaiṣṇava splendour.
Therefore, their abundance of virtues surpassed [all] beings,
through generosity, sacrifices, heroism, austerity, and strength,
through sacred learning and righteousness, [surpassing] gods, Daityas, and great serpents.

Caitra, Kaviruta, Kṛtānta, Vidyuta, Ravi,
Bṛhadgraha, Nabha, of great strength and valour.
His [sages were] Ūrja, Prāṇa, Ṛṣabha, Niścala,
Dantobhi, and Śākvarīvat; [these] are proclaimed as the seven sages.
Twelve are spoken of as the Bhūṣitas, and likewise those [called] Pārāvatas;
their Indra was the high-souled Vipaścit, world-renowned.
At that time, fierce Asuras were his cousin-kinsmen;
their king then was Purukutsa, superior in strength.
Intent upon doing disservice to Śakra, he went to the forest to hunt;
resorting to great prowess, he destroyed rutting elephants.
An elephant [form], the king's companion, killed the lions in the forest.

he violently killed that foremost Daitya who could not be slain in battles by gods or Asuras.

Learn from me the sons of Auttama, the third Manu:
Aja, Paraśu, Devadeva, Vṛdha, Naya,
Devāvṛdha, Apratima, Mahotsāha, Gaja,
Vinīta, Suketu, Sumitra, Subala, and Śuci.
Hereafter I shall proclaim the seven sages at that time:
Rajobāhu, Ūrdhvabāhu, Savana, and Anagha,
Sutapas, and Śakti—these are declared as the seven sages.
The Vaśavartins, the Svadhāsans, the Vaśas, the Satyahās, and the Matārdanas—
these five classes of gods are declared, and each consists of twelve.
Their Śakra was Sucitti by name, conqueror of enemies' citadels.
At that time, fierce Asuras were his cousin-kinsmen,
whose mighty king was Pralamba by name.

Intent upon doing disservice to Śakra, carrying the waters of the ocean,
Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a fish, swallowed that exceedingly powerful one.
Resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution, an enemy in foreign lands, [Viṣṇu] moving through the worlds in the form of a fish,
slew him, who was as large as a mountain peak and unsatisfied by autumn, in the midst of the ocean.

Learn from me the sons of Tāmasa, the fourth Manu:
Jānujaṅgha, Śāntabhaya, Nara, Khyāti, and Nara.
Priyabhṛtya, indeed Avikṣit, Prasthila, and Dṛḍheṣudhi, / and Kṛta and Kṛtagandha are the sons of Manu Tāmasa.
The sage Vana, Kaṭhīyān indeed, Gātra, Caitra, and Agni, / Jyotirvāsas, Pṛthu, and Kāvya are proclaimed the seven sages.
The Satyas, Supādas, Surihas, and Haras are proclaimed / as these four groups of deities, consisting of twenty-five each.
Of the Satyas, two divisions are proclaimed: the Satyas and the Viśvas; / twelve are designated as Satyas, and thirteen are declared as Viśvas.

Their Indra was the valorous Śibi of great splendour. / At that time there were terrible asuras, kinsmen sharing inheritance with him,
whose master was the king Bhīmaratha of great splendour, / by whom, having propitiated Brahmā, invulnerability on dry land was chosen [as a boon].
From then on, that evil-minded one avoided water. / In the desert he saw a tortoise looking like a mountain.
Filled with curiosity, the foolish-minded one mounted upon it. / Lord Hari, taking that enormous-bodied one who had mounted [him],
bearing the form of a tortoise, swiftly entered the waters of the netherworld. / Having brought him to the waters of the netherworld and submerged him, he killed him, / having overwhelmed that huge body with his immense tortoise form.
Thus, that foremost of all asuras, the enemy of the peerless lord of the gods, / was forcibly struck down in the water with a tortoise [form] by that peerless Lord of All.
Śāmbarāyaṇī said: / Learn from me the sons of the fifth Manu, Raivata: / Mahāpurāṇa, Sambhāvya, Pratyaṅga, Parahan, Śuci,

Calabindu, Nirāmitra, Ketuśṛṅga, and Dṛḍhavrata / are the sons of Manu Raivata; I tell you his sages:
Vedaśruti, Vedabāhu, Ūrdhvabāhu, and Yajus, / Hiraṇyaroman, Parjanya, and likewise Satyanetra.
The Ābhūtarajasas and likewise the Sumedhas gods, / the Vaikuṇṭhas and the Amṛtas are the four groups of deities.
Fourteen gods are declared in each single group. / Their Indra, renowned for valour in the world, was named Vibhu.
At that time there were terrible asuras, kinsmen sharing inheritance with him; / among them was a great lord of great splendour named Śambhu,
by whom death [only] through the world of Brahmā was chosen [as a boon] from the Grandfather. / Once, upon seeing an enormous swan moving in the waters of the ocean,
the evil-minded one seized it and mounted it. / As soon as he mounted, taking him, it went to the world of Brahmā; / right there, Lord Hari in the form of a swan killed him.

Ikṣvāku, then Nābhāga, Viṣṇu, and Śaryāti, / Avṛdhyatu, as well as Prāṃśu, and the great-spirited Diṣṭa,
Karūṣa, Pṛthudhra, and Sudyumna are the sons of the Manu. / Atri, the venerable Vasiṣṭha, Jamadagni, Kaśyapa,

the two Aśvins are designated, as well as the ten Viśvedevas, / and ten are the Āṅgirasa gods; thus there are nine groups of gods,

all composed of twenty divine beings of great soul; / their future Indra will be Bali, the best of the Dānavas,
the lord of the gods who was bound by the God of gods for your sake. / He shall have no heirs or kinsmen, O Vāsava.
The role of Indra, free from thorns, is to be held by him throughout that manvantara. / That great Asura made a gift placed in the hands of the God of gods;
he will become the king of the three worlds during the period of Manu Sāvarṇa. / When that manvantara arrives, a mighty,
evil-doing rākṣasa named Nānola, residing in the Snowy Mountains, / having obtained a boon from Brahmā, terrifying and intent on destroying the three worlds, will arise.
Viṣṇu, whose vehicle is Garuḍa, the righteous-souled one, / will slay him with his hundred-edged discus, desiring the welfare of the worlds.
Tearing apart with his discus that [demon] terrible with fangs, monstrous and dreadful in guise, / shining like dark collyrium and striking terror in the three worlds, the god will make the whole world free from fear.

Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Hear now of the sons of the ninth Manu, the son of Brahmā: / Dhṛtiketu, Dīptiketu, Pañcahasta, Nirākṛti,
Pṛthuśravas, Bṛhaddyumna, Ṛcīka, and Bṛhatgaṇa. / Those are the sons of the son of Brahmā; and hear from me the sages:
Medhātithi, Dyuti, Savana, and Vasu, / Jyotiṣmat, Havya, and Satya are proclaimed as the sages.
The Pāras, the Marīcigarbhas, and the Svadharmans—these three / classes of gods are declared to consist of twelve each; and their Indra will be
the mighty Vibhu of great splendor, lord of all the gods. / His righteous kinsmen and heirs who will arise
will have a king known as Kālakākṣa. / In that manvantara, there will be a king named Vasunābha;
his son, by his disposition, will be King Vāsudeva, / an emperor of great splendor, known as Padmanābha.

In the war between the gods and the Asuras, the mighty Padmanābha / will slay Kālakākṣa, fierce in battle, who could only be killed by a man.
Having slain with a gold-adorned arrow charged with the weapon of Brahmā / that demon fierce in battle and possessing the might of Death, that king will dispel the fear of the world.
1.185
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Hear now of the sons of the tenth Manu, the son of Dharma: / Sukṣetra, Uttamaujas, and the heroic Bhūriśoṇa,
Śatānīka, Nimi, Mitra, Vṛṣasena, Jayadratha, / Bhūridyumna, and Suvarman—the sons of Manu, the son of Dharma.
Āpomūrti, Haviṣmat, Sṛtiki, and the changeless one, / Nābhāga, Pramita, and Saurabha are the sages;
and the classes of deities, numbering a hundred, are named Prāṇas. / His glorious Indra will be Śānti.
His heirs and kinsmen, who will be Asuras, / will have a king, a great Asura named Bālī.

Viṣṇu will strike him down with his mace of terrible speed / in the war between the gods and the Asuras, desiring the welfare of the gods.
When that lord of the Asuras of great strength is struck down by the blow of the mace by that foremost of gods, / this entire threefold world will be free of fault, enjoyed by gods and brahmins.

With the lustre of a blue lotus, the colour of molten gold, his own form having beautifully rounded pairs of knees and thighs, / having made a most beautiful female form, that slayer of foes will suddenly [slay] that fierce enemy of the gods.
1.187
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Hear from me the sons of the twelfth Manu, the son of Dakṣa: / Devavān, Upadeva, Devaśreṣṭha, Vidūratha,
Mitravān, Mitradeva, and the powerful Mitrasena, / Mitrabāhu, and Suvarcas—these are the sons of Manu, the son of Dakṣa.
Sattama, Dyaus, Dyuti, Tapana, Sutapas, / Taporati, and Tapasvin are proclaimed as the seven sages.
The Suśarmans, the Sutapases, the Haritas, the Rohitas, / and those called the Sutāras are the five classes [of gods], each having a group of ten.
And their Indra will be the righteous, majestic Ṛtadhāman. / Those who will be his heirs, kinsmen, and the asuras—
of them there will be a king named Naraka by name; / and by the granting of a boon by the Self-born, he cannot be slain by female or male beings.
Hari, having assumed a neuter form, will then cause him to be slain.

Having slain that destroyer of gods, that great asura of power equal to Death, with a eunuch body, / that exalted, noble Lord will make this entire world free from fear.
1.188
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Learn from me the sons of the thirteenth Manu, Raucya: / Citrasena, Vicitra, Naya, Dharmabhṛt, Dhṛti,
Sunetra, Vṛkṣavṛddhi, Sunaya, Dharmaya, and Dṛḍha. / These are the sons of the Manu Raucya; hear my sages [of this period]:
Dhṛtimān, Avyaya, Niḥprakopa, Nirutsuka, / Nirmāṇa, Tattvadarśin, and Davayāyata are proclaimed.
The Sutrāmāṇas, the Sudharmāṇas, and the Śubhakarmāṇas— / these, O Śakra, are then declared to be the three classes of deities.
In each class there are then eleven auspicious gods; / and their lord of gods then will be Bṛhaspati.
Those who will be his heirs and kinsmen, O Vāsava— / of them, an evil-minded one named Ṭiṭṭibha will be king.

text_mt:
Endowed with an expansive plumage, crested, magnificent, with a neck lovely as a blossoming blue lotus, / having forcibly slain that dānava there in battle, he will surely make the three worlds joyful.
1.189
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Hear the sons of the fourteenth Manu, Bhautya, from me: / Taraṅga, Bhedabhid, Budhnya, Tarasvān, and Ugra,
Abhimānin, Pravīra, Jiṣṇu, and Saṃkrandana, / Tejasvin, and Sulabha—these are the sons of Manu Bhautya.
Agnīdhra, Atibāhu, Māgadha, Śuci, / Ajita, Yuktaga, and Śakya are proclaimed as the seven sages.
The Cākṣuṣas, the Kaniṣṭhas, the Pavitras, and the Bhajiras, / and the Vayovṛddhas are declared to be the five classes of gods, each of seven.
Their Indra will be named Śuci; and those who will be his heirs and kinsmen— / of them, Mahāsukha will be king.
A war between the gods and asuras, lasting a thousand divine years, / will then take place, extremely terrible; at its end, Keśava will slay that great asura

त्रैलोक्यमेतद्विरुजं समन्तात्तदा भविष्यत्यमलप्रतापम् .. 9 ..

शक्र उवाच ..

सम्भवस्त्रिदशश्रेष्ठ गन्धर्वाणां तथा स्मृतः .. 4 ..
text_mt:
who relies on dark illusory power, / having mounted a divine elephant resembling a moving mountain.
Resembling an uprooted mountain, Madhusūdana with his discus / will slay that evil-minded great daitya who stands upon a chariot.
When that enemy of the gods and of Vāsava, possessing great strength and splendour equal to Death, is slain, / this threefold world will then become free from distress on all sides, with spotless radiance.
1.190
Śakra said:
O gentle lady, the origin of Garuḍa in this manvantara / has been witnessed by me; in the past ones, how, having Garuḍa as his mount,
did he slay the asuras, and likewise in future ones, / having mounted Garuḍa, how will he slay [them]? Tell me that.
Since the destruction of all is declared to occur at the end of a manvantara, / therefore explain this to me, for you are skilled and righteous.
Śāmbarāyaṇī said:
Just as the origin of the gods and the asuras takes place in each manvantara, / O best of the thirty [gods], so is recorded that of the gandharvas,

text_mt:
of the nāgas, of the rākṣasas, of the yakṣas, and then of the birds, / and of the suparṇas, O Śakra, and of living creatures entirely without exception.
The foremost of the suparṇas in that manvantara at that time, / always becomes Garuḍa, O king, best among the winged ones.
In the same way, he attains the status of vehicle to that lord of gods. / Just as the manifestations of Viṣṇu have been declared by me to you,
so also are those of the noble Garuḍa to be known. / But the gods whose duties are accomplished, O Śakra, at the end of a manvantara,
relinquishing their offices, depart from here to the other world, O Lord; / and so do the mantras bearing their marks along with those very gods.
And the collection of mantras is a deity worshipped by the thirty [gods];
embodied in the abode of Brahmā, it is proclaimed to be eternal.

sanskrit_iast:

As long as Brahmā, bowed to by all the worlds, lives,
so long does Brahmā take refuge in the Cosmic Person, the god of gods.

Having cast off his body, the god too attains the Cosmic Person.
The Cosmic Person also [effects] the great creation, as well as the host of primary elements.

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ ..

sanskrit_iast:

text_mt:

no one is able to effect the destruction of this imperishable [reality].

sanskrit_iast:

प्रादुर्भावसहस्राणि समतीतान्यनेकशः .. 16 ..

Just as in this auspicious Vaivasvata manvantara, O lord of gods,

manifestations of that great-souled one were seen by me:
the Boar, the Dwarf, and likewise Trivikrama, O Śakra,

they will occur by the hundreds and by the thousands in future ones.
And coming to each and every manvantara for you,

even in hundreds of years here?

I know the course of future manvantaras in the same way.
Having attained human birth, worship of the months and lunar mansions

pratimāsaṃ kṛtaṃ viṣṇoryāvajjīvaṃ sureśvara ..
tena karmavipākena tridive vasatiściram ..

1.192
Vajra said:
I have heard from you as you declared the fruit of plastering the temple of a god, O knower of dharma;
O brahmin, I wish to hear further.
Tell me that action which yields the fruit of heaven even [more than] plastering,
and how it does so; you are all-knowing, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Praise of him is easier even than plastering, O Yādava,
and is declared to bear much fruit; perform it if you wish.
For those who praise the great god who holds the conch, discus, and mace,
nothing is difficult to obtain in this world or in the next.
Praising Vāsudeva, a mortal casts off all sin
and attains endless heaven; no doubt should be entertained on this matter.
One seeking dharma obtains dharma; one seeking wealth obtains wealth;
one who has desires obtains desires; one seeking offspring obtains offspring.

one who is afraid is freed from fear; one in calamity is freed from calamity.
Praising Puruṣottama, a man quickly crosses over difficulties,
O tiger among men; no doubt should be entertained on this matter.
Therefore, with all effort, with divine hymns composed by seers
and well-spoken words, O king, one should constantly praise the god of gods.
Having taken refuge in Hari, who has auspicious and spotless eyes like lotus petals, who slays enemies and possesses unfathomable valour, / men afflicted by great fear on earth become free from fear.
1.193
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Concerning this, they also cite this ancient narrative,
namely, what was done for the king of elephants by the God of gods when he was praised.
Formerly, O mighty-armed Vajra, the two Gandharvas who were Hāhā and Hūhū
engaged in a contest with one another in singing, O scorcher of foes.
Vying with each other, O king, they then asked one another:
'Who in this world will be a proper arbiter for the two of us?'

text_mt:
Then the Gandharvas said to them, 'This Devala will be [the arbiter].'
Having been spoken to thus, the two, however, did not want the sage Devala.
'This one does not know the nuances of song,' thus deluded [they thought].
Greatly enraged, Devala, endowed with very great ascetic power, cursed the two of them:
'Because contempt was shown by you two to me who do indeed understand,
therefore I shall bestow a curse upon you both, O singers of the gods!
Hāhā shall become an elephant; Hūhū shall become a crocodile.
And the Lord of the gods of gods, to the crocodile intent on dragging the elephant,
being praised by the elephant, will cut in two with his discus. Then you two,
O singers, both shall regain your own form at the end of the curse.'
Then by his curse the two were born as told by me to you, O lion among kings.
And by that Janārdana the elephant [and crocodile], the two of them were completely released from the curse of the foremost of twice-borns.

1.194
Vajra said:
O blessed one, I wish to hear of the liberation of the king of elephants
in detail, O highly fortunate one, and of both from the curse of the crocodile.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In this Jambūdvīpa there is a principal mountain named Śṛṅgavān,
endowed with sky-scraping peaks abundant with great minerals,
whose three central peaks shine conspicuously, O king,
abodes of Brahmā, the Sun, and the Moon, captivating the mind and reaching heaven.
Of them, one is of gold, another great one of silver,
and one middle one, the abode of Brahmā, is made of all kinds of gems;
the golden one is the abode of the Sun, the silver one the abode of the Moon.
[This mountain is] Trikūṭa, resembling the king of mountains, endowed with jewel-winged trees.
The ungrateful do not see it, nor the cruel, nor the unbelievers,
nor any whose austerities are unperformed, nor people who commit sins.

unfathomable in the middle, driving away with its waves, like proud doorkeepers,
the [debris] arising from trees thrown by the wind on its four [banks];
as if gazing at that great height of the mountain's peaks
with its eyes that were white water-lily blossoms with bees nestled inside;
where the water is extremely cool, light, sweet, and resembling nectar.
Another charming peak echoed with the humming of bees.
In that lake the evil-minded Hūhū, misshapen, lying beneath the water,
attained the state of a crocodile through the curse of Devala.
On that very mountain, Hāhā, the best of Gandharvas,
became an elephant, the leader of a herd, resembling a moving mountain.
Then one day the leader of the elephant herd, whose body was radiant with tusks,
came to the lake with full-blown lotuses, O protector of the earth,
surrounded by young calves [slender] as bamboo canes and by female elephants,
perfuming that Trikūṭa mountain with the scent of his rut.

text_mt:
That elephant, resembling collyrium, his eyes contracted with rut,
playfully roaming amidst the herd in the cluster of lotuses,
was seized by that fierce crocodile of indistinct form,
while the whole herd watched and cried out most piteously.
He made a mighty effort for his own liberation;
the great crocodile also made an effort to drag the elephant.
Even the crocodile was unable to pull the powerful elephant [completely] into the deep water,
nor was the elephant able to free himself.
Having struggled with all his might and having uttered great roars,
afflicted and deprived of effort, he reached his final state.
Then that glorious, foremost of elephants, devoted to Nārāyaṇa,
took refuge in Viṣṇu and praised him, O scorcher of foes.
Taking with the tip of his trunk an excellent lotus from the lake,
and offering it with devotion to Kṛṣṇa, the elephant uttered a hymn of praise.

text_mt:
The elephant said:
Homage, homage to the causal Dwarf, to Nārāyaṇa, the tearer of asuras,
to the bearer of the auspicious Śārṅga bow, discus, sword, and mace; homage be to that Puruṣottama!
To the primordial one, the abode of the Vedas, the great serpent, the lion, the destroyer of daityas, the four-armed one,
praised by Brahmā, Indra, Rudra, sages, and cāraṇas, the highest of gods, the giver of boons, homage to Acyuta!
To him who dearly loves the coils of the king of serpents as bed and seat, who resembles cow's milk, gold, a parrot, and a dark blue cloud,
clad in yellow garments, the destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, dear to his devotees, with his excellent, blazing Sudarśana!
To the one who has the four-faced [Brahmā] seated on the lotus sprung from his navel, who bears fame with his dwelling on the ocean of milk, / who is adorned with various wondrous crowns and armlets, the Lord of all, victorious, the excellent one—obeisance!
To the soul of the universe, the cause of the supreme cause, whose wide and long eyes are like blooming lotuses, / whose virility was tested by the imagination of the king of gods, the Lord of yogins, victorious, the excellent one—obeisance!

text_mt:
To the refuge of the worlds, the refuge of the gods, the refuge of Brahmā, the refuge of his own attributes, / the refuge of dharma, the refuge of the lone person, to the Great Boar, I am always bowed.
To Nārāyaṇa, the primeval deity, the cause, unthinkable, unmanifest, of endless form, / the ancient Cosmic Person remaining at the end of the aeon, to that Vāsudeva I fly for refuge.
Whom the great sages call invisible, indivisible, without beginning or middle, the treasure of the Veda, the Lord of gods, / indeed the eternal Cosmic Person—to that Vāsudeva I fly for refuge.
Whom they call the imperishable Brahman, all-pervading, having heard of whom one is released from the jaws of death, / to that Lord, exalted by unexcelled qualities, the supreme goal, eternal Viṣṇu, one attains.
To the cause, action, and effect, immeasurable, whose navel is golden, who holds a golden lotus, / of great strength, the treasure of the Vedas, foremost of the gods—to Viṣṇu Janārdana I go for refuge.
To Keśava, with wondrous armlets and a precious gold ornament, whose entire body is adorned with excellent jewels, / clad in yellow garments patterned with gold designs, bearing a garland, I draw near.

text_mt:
To the origin of existence, the best among knowers of the Veda, the best among those of disciplined mind and knowers of Sāṅkhya, / possessing the splendour of the Ādityas, Moon, Aśvins, and Vasus, to the sovereign, Acyuta, who has become the Self, I surrender.
To the great deity marked with the Śrīvatsa, the secret of the Vedas, the unexcelled, / subtle, immovable, who grants fearlessness to his devotees, I surrender.
To the origin of all worlds, free from qualities yet the soul of qualities, / the supreme goal of ascetics whose attachments are cast off, I surrender.
To the Blessed One, overseer of the gods, imperishable, lotus-eyed, / the refuge worthy of refuge, dear to brahmins, I surrender with devotion.
To the authority for Brahmā, Lord of the three worlds, the primeval, the one, free from affliction, / the inner self of all beings, the Great Soul, Madhusūdana, I surrender.
To the Knower of the Field, the Cosmic Person, Viṣṇu, beyond the three guṇas, imperishable, / Nārāyaṇa, most subtle, to Hari I go for refuge.
To the one, the ruler of the universe, the Supreme Self beyond the beyond, / to the thousand-headed, infinite Great Soul, obeisance!

text_mt:
To the desirable, sinless deity whom all the sages who have crossed to the far shore of the Veda / praise as unborn—to that eternal one I surrender.
Obeisance to you, O lotus-eyed one, granter of fearlessness to devotees! / O friend of the brahmins, obeisance be to you! Protect me who have come for refuge!
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Considering the devotion of that elephant and his unfailing hymn of praise, / the Bearer of the discus and mace, O king, instantly felt delight.
Mādhava made his presence felt, struck the crocodile with his discus, / and released the elephant who had come to him for refuge from his bonds.
For through the curse of Devala he, Hāhā, the best of gandharvas, / had become an elephant; casting [that form] off and attaining liberation, he went to heaven.
Released from the crocodile, the elephant at once attained the state of a gandharva; / and the crocodile, who was struck down by Kṛṣṇa, attained the state of a gandharva.
Upon him too the fault of a curse had been laid of old by Devala. / When pleased, Viṣṇu instantly rescues [one] from the ocean of worldly existence.

Even when angry, slaying his enemies, he grants them godhead. / Both of them, having regained their own respective forms and bowed down to Janārdana,
the two gandharva chieftains quickly attained supreme bliss. / And of old, O mighty-armed one, the god spoke this very thing,
the Blessed Lord Madhusūdana, having seen the elephant and the crocodile released: / "Whoever remembers the one who seized the king of elephants, and me who am full of intent meditation,
and this lake, and the liberation of you two, / as well as the thicket of whistling bamboos and this excellent mountain,
the sacred fig tree, the Sun, the Gaṅgā, and the Naimiṣa forest, / Prayāga, the Brahmatīrtha, and the Daṇḍaka forest—
those mortals who remember these, and also those who hear them properly, / will not suffer the evil of bad dreams, through my acceptance [of them].
They will be freed from all sins and will become partakers of auspicious things; / and so these mortals will attain a holy destination.

as well as the Man-Lion, which bring about creation and dissolution— / those men who, having risen in the morning, remember these [forms],
purified of all sins, will go to the supreme goal." / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, O king of kings, the god of gods, Janārdana,
touched the elephant-gandharva and the crocodile-gandharva. / Touched by him, both of them immediately endowed with divine garlands and garments
and having boarded a chariot of their desire, went to the abode of the gods. / There the lord of gods, Kṛṣṇa, having released the excellent elephant,
being praised by sages with esoteric words and syllables of the Veda, / that Blessed Lord Viṣṇu, the all-pervading one whose ways are difficult to fathom, departed.
Having witnessed the liberation of the lord of elephants, all, led by Indra, / placed the brahmins at their head and folded their hands in reverence.

text_mt:
Reciting the holy "Liberation of the Lord of Elephants", which releases one from all sins, / upon rising in the morning, one is freed from all sins.
Indeed, O best of the Yadus, through faith, when it is remembered and narrated, / through this "Liberation of the Lord of Elephants" alone, one attains a long life.
By me this divine, purifying, sin-destroying [account] has been told to you; / recite it, O mighty-armed one, for it destroys severe nightmares,
and listen with devotion when it is recited by brahmins as it was told.
The foremost knowers of Brahman praised the supreme, adorable Nārāyaṇa, whose navel is a supreme lotus, who holds the treasure of lotuses, the lord of gods, / that secret of the gods, the primeval Cosmic Person.
This holy [account], O best of Yadus, of men who have committed sins, / having heard it upon seeing a terrible nightmare, one is freed from sin.
Devoted to the lotus-eyed [Lord], the elephant was delivered from misery. / Likewise you too, O king of kings, having sought refuge in Hari,
freed from all sins, will attain the supreme goal.
