text_mt:
Vajra said: / O Lord, what kind of protective rite did that best of twice-born perform, / by which that night-wanderer was rendered powerless and helpless?
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / With mind focused solely on Govinda, murmuring his [mantra] and devoted to him, / he entered the Armor of Viṣṇu, which quells all evil.
Vajra said: / I wish to hear about the Armor of Viṣṇu, O best of the upholders of dharma, / which may always be the supreme protection against all fears.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Formerly, for Śaṅkara when he was slaying Tripura, the Armor of Viṣṇu / was prescribed by Brahmā, O best of Yadus, for his protection;
and by the Lord of Speech for Śakra when he was marching to destroy Bala. / I shall tell you its nature; listen to it, O ruler of the earth.
Viṣṇu bearing the discus stands in the east; Viṣṇu bearing the mace is to the south; / Viṣṇu wielding the bow Śārṅga is in the west; Viṣṇu bearing the sword is to my north.
Hṛṣīkeśa is in the intermediate directions; Janārdana is in the gaps between them; / Hari in the form of a boar is on the ground to slay the deceased and the night-wanderers.

text_mt:
And this mace, blazing with a thousand rays, vomiting fierce fire, / destroys rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, and ḍākinīs.
And may the twang of Vāsudeva's bow Śārṅga utterly slay my enemies: / animals, men, kūṣmāṇḍas, the deceased, and the rest.
Those who, being focused, are cleansed by the pure moonlight of the sword-blade, / may they instantly become benign, like serpents before Garuḍa.
Whatever kūṣmāṇḍas and yakṣas, whatever daityas, whatever night-wanderers, / deceased spirits, cruel vināyakas, men, jackals, birds,
lions and other beasts, biting reptiles, and serpents— / may they all become benign, struck down by the sound of Kṛṣṇa's bow Śārṅga.
Those people who steal my mental faculties, who rob my memory, / who destroy strength and vitality, and who cause my shadow to fade,
and those who take away my enjoyments, and who destroy my auspicious marks— / may those kūṣmāṇḍas perish, struck by the speed of Viṣṇu's discus.

Health of intellect, health of mind, and likewise health of the senses, / may they be mine through the chanting of Vāsudeva, god of gods.
Behind me, in front of me, to my right and left, and in the intermediate directions, may Janārdana Hari be present. / Having bowed down to that Janārdana, the praiseworthy lord of infinite stride, one does not perish.
Just as Hari is the supreme Brahman, so too Keśava himself is the supreme reality of the world; / by that truth, through the chanting of Acyuta's name, may my threefold misfortune come to destruction.

text_mt:
These blades of kuśa grass originate from the body of Viṣṇu, and I, Janārdana, have come in person. / All his wickedness has been slain by me; let this man be healthy, according to the word of Hari.
1.197 / Vajra said: / In the context of the creation of the universe, the birth of Urvaśī / was told by you, O fortunate one, and in that context others,
and delightful stories joined with dharma were told, O brahmin, / endowed with the majesty of Viṣṇu, removing all sins and fears.
The wife of Kaśyapa, who was mentioned by you by the name of Khaśā, / whose two high-souled sons were stated to be the yakṣa and the rākṣasa—
I wish to hear their origin and likewise their lineage; / relate the ongoing creation of the universe in its entirety.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / In the morning twilight, that Khaśā gave birth to the rākṣasa, / whose face was terrifying with fangs, whose eyes were tawny and prominent,
with a mouth torn open to the ears, huge and fierce at the tip of the nose, / dishevelled, monstrously arrogant, spike-eared, and terrifying.

text_mt:
In the same way, at the other twilight, that very same woman gave birth to a yakṣa, / of the very same form as that of the rākṣasa.
Agitated, the yakṣa said to her, "I am destroying [my] mother." / But the rākṣasa said to the yakṣa, "Protect [our] mother!"
From protecting (rakṣaṇa) he is called a rākṣasa; from destroying (kṣaṇa) the other is called a yakṣa. / The wife of the yakṣa was the divine courtesan Kṛtasthalā.
The yakṣa named Rājatanābha is remembered as her and his son. / His wife, O king, was a guhyaka woman, the daughter of Anuhlāda.
Heroic Maṇicara and also Vīrabhadra— / her two sons are famed, wise and equal to gods.
Their wives, O lord of men, were two daughters of Kakutstha. / O king, the first had Puṇyajanī as her name;
likewise the second was named Devajanī, O Yādava. / From her came the Puṇyajana yakṣas, and likewise the Devajana [yakṣas], / said to be many thousands, endowed with great strength and valour.

Through auspicious marriages with yakṣa lineages, O king, yakṣas were born endowed with noble conduct, / established in dharma, dedicated to truth, modest, of great dignity, granters of boons, and pre-eminent.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Aja and Ṣaṇḍa were two piśācas, O protector of the earth, sons of Kapiśā. / A piśācī named Brahmadhānā is considered to be the daughter of Aja there;
the piśācī named Yātudhānā is considered to be the daughter of Ṣaṇḍa. / Both Aja and Ṣaṇḍa, O king, were hungry at midnight.
Accompanied by their servants outside, O lord of men, they saw / a rākṣasa of hungry appearance, descending in the night, famished.
When that powerful one was seized by the two hungry piśācas, / he was questioned with care by the two, having observed his strength then.
He told the cause of birth of both, O best of rulers of the earth. / Having heard his birth and deed, those two flesh-eaters
gave their two maiden daughters to that man-eating rākṣasa. / Two lineages from the two wives of the rākṣasa are celebrated:

In the lineage of Brahmadhānā were his Brahmadhāna night-wanderers; / in the lineage of Yātudhānā were his Yātudhānas proclaimed.
First I shall speak of the rākṣasas born in the lineage of Brahmadhānā: / Yajñahā, Nirdhanikṣepā, Brahmapūta, then Nighnavān,
Śvānakṛt, Kuntala, and Sarpa are remembered as the sons of Brahmadhānā. / Those born in their lineage, by the hundreds and thousands,
dwelling in the Śleṣmātaka forest, are proclaimed as brahmarākṣasas. / Heti, Praheti, Ugra, Pauruṣāda, and Vadha,
Vidyutsphūrja, Vāta, Nasa, Vyāghra, / Susakṛt, and Karāla—these are the ten sons of Yātudhānā.
These are indeed the followers of Sūrya, wandering together with him. / The Yātudhānas born in their lineage are proclaimed.
I shall speak to you of the two lineages of Heti and Praheti, O Yādava. / The son of Heti is remembered as Laṅku, whose [wife] was Sālakaṭaṅkaṭā;

she is remembered as the wife, the daughter of Sandhyā, and Sukeśa is remembered as their son. / Mālī, Sumālī, and the very powerful Mālyavān—

Mālyavān, aged with years, still lives there today, O Yādava; / by him his two brothers, eager for war with the gods, had formerly been made to hear
beneficial, righteous, and auspicious words, but they did not act upon his [words]. / Therefore those two rākṣasas met destruction in two battles.

Likewise was that Rāvaṇa made to hear words by him at the time of hostility; / disregarding his words, though established in dharma and of incomparable power, he met with destruction.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The son of Praheti, O king, was renowned by the name Puloman, / who was quickly destroyed by Cyavana with a wrathful glance.
Vajra said: / For what reason was the rākṣasa Puloman killed by Cyavana, / and how, O tiger among the Bhṛgus? Explain that to me as I ask.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Two daughters of Puloman, the lord of the dānavas, were renowned on earth: / Pulomā was given to Bhṛgu, and Śacī was given to Vāsava.
Once, when she was crying in her maidenhood, O delight of the Yadus, / Puloman, the lord of the dānavas, said to Pulomā, O king:
"Hey rakṣas, seize by force this maiden who is crying!" / At that very time, in the courtyard of Puloman's palace,
that wicked Puloman stood, looking for an opportunity; / and having approached, he seized that lovely-eyed maiden.

Having rebuked that wicked one, Puloman, the best of the dānavas, / in time gave that slender-waisted maiden to Bhṛgu.
Seeing that blameless woman pregnant and alone, separated from Bhṛgu, / when she had gone to the agnihotra, Puloman then spoke to Agni:
"If she is Paulomī, previously mine, declare this to me, O Fire!" / Agni said to him, "She is the auspicious wife of Bhṛgu."
Having thus heard from Agni of Bhṛgu, that rākṣasa carried her off. / While she was being taken, the foetus fell from her womb then;
from falling (cyavana) he became named Cyavana, of great ascetic power. / No sooner was he seen by him than that Puloman was reduced to ashes.
From the falling of Pulomā's tears, the river Vadhūsaras was born, / and fire came to be the devourer of all through the curse of Bhṛgu.
Then the fire, having received the curse from that foremost of the twice-born, became enraged; / Brahmā, devoted to the welfare of the worlds, himself spoke these words:

"O Fire, everything touched by your flames shall become pure; / having thus become pure, it will thereafter undoubtedly be consumed."
Thus the birth of Cyavana has been told to you, as well as the destruction of that foremost rākṣasa, / and the purity of fire and of its flames; now learn, O king, the lineage of Puloman.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Puloman had an illustrious son, a night-roamer named Madhu; / the bull-bannered [Śiva], pulling a trident from his own trident, gave it to him,
pleased by the asceticism of that great-souled one along with his son. / When Rāvaṇa was bent upon the conquest of the three worlds, O best of kings,
and Meghanāda was consecrated [for ritual] and had gone to Nikumbhilā, / and the heroic Vibhīṣaṇa was immersed within the waters,
and Kumbhakarṇa, the enemy of the gods, had fallen under the power of sleep, O king, / Rāvaṇa's sister, the daughter of Mālinī, was carried off by him—
the highly fortunate Kumbhīnasī, endowed with beauty and wealth; / in her, a son was born to him, a rākṣasa named Lavaṇa,

With ten thousand living beings, beginning with humans, O king, / the daily meal of that glutton was made.
By Rāma's command, the younger brother of Rāma, endowed with noble courage, became his death, O king— / the hero named Śatrughna, who was the immeasurable Hari residing within another form.

text_mt:
By the matchless curse of that extremely mighty king of the gandharvas, O king, / Bharata, who was the immeasurable Hari residing in another body, became their death in battle.
Vajra said: / How were the gandharvas, the sons of Śailūṣa, slain by Bharata? / And for what reason, O highly fortunate one? Explain that to me as I ask.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / While Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, was in unconquerable Ayodhyā, / the glorious ruler of the Kaikeyas, a king named Yudhājit,
Bharata's maternal uncle, sent an envoy to Rāma— / his aged family priest, the descendant of Garga; hear for what purpose:
"On both banks of the Sindhu, O Rāma, is a charming land; / having killed the lords of men in battle, it has been settled by gandharvas.
And those gandharvas, O best of kings, are doing displeasures to kings. / Either Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, or Śatrughna, O king,
having dispatched, destroy those gandharvas, O descendant of Raghu, / so that kings may be free from fear, and that land may become yours."

wearing fine garments, adorned with all ornaments,
resembling the sun in radiance and the moon in beauty.

Having consecrated your two sons in those two cities, my dear child, / and having entrusted them to Yudhājit, you must return quickly.
Without you, tiger among men, I have no desire to live; / placing the duty of a kṣatriya foremost, you are sent there by me.
Go, therefore, fortunate one; let there be no delay for you. / May there be welfare for you as you travel, from airborne and earthly beings,
and from divine beings, and likewise in battle, sinless one!

As he, the scion of Raghu who was eager for battle, lay asleep, / there passed that auspicious night of resolute nature in the month of Jyeṣṭha, adorned with the full moon, renowned.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / But when the night had dawned, O great king, / the loud-sounding marching kettledrum of Bharata was struck.
Awakened by its great sound, the people in the camp, / having performed the necessary duties, filled with haste, O king,
hastening for the march, calling out to one another, / began to strike down the charming cloth-tents.
Large and very pleasing, made of spun wool, / they made them easily portable without effort, O best of kings.

baggage of various kinds, soft beds, / excellent seats, and whatever utensils were in the kitchen,

filled with scum, mud, and flies; / leaving it behind, all the soldiers of Bharata departed.
During the march of that army, [the drivers] with great effort made the bullocks, / overcome with exhaustion, and the seated elephants rise up.
The best of men loaded baggage again on those [beasts] / that had been frightened by camels and thrown down by a donkey.
At river-crossings, people beat the buffaloes, / scorched by the sun's rays, that had sat down along with their loads.
Some, O king, carefully seized by the reins the mules / on which women were mounted, frightened by the trumpeting sounds of elephants.
Some men were thrown to the ground by horses terrified of elephants, / their feet resting on the horse's neck to rest their knees.
And riders whose shields had slipped swiftly overtook and seized / the horses that were then running wild, O Yādava.
Some men rested in the shade of trees, / while others took their meal on the banks of waters.

śreṇī cakrustathaivānye kaṭacchāyāsu pārthiva ..
vitānādhastathā kecitsthāpayāñcakrire hayān .. 49 ..
hayebhyo yavasaṃ dattvā kecidbubhujire janāḥ ..
kaṭacchāyāśca nāgānāṃ cakruścānye sahasraśaḥ ..1.205.50 ..
vitānāni ca mukhyāni sūryatāpapraśāntaye ..
snātāñjalāśaye nāgām̐llabdhatoyāñjanādhipa .. 51..
sacchannānsvaparīdhānakumbhānninyuḥ svamālayam ..
kaṭakāddūrataścakrurālānaṃ nṛpadantinām.. 52..
meaning:
ददृशे बहुसाहस्रं कटके भरतस्य तु ..
रथेभ्यस्तुरगानन्ये विमुच्य हयकोविदाः .. 46 ..
अवरोपितभाण्डानि सान्त्वयाञ्चक्रिरे शनैः ..
समुत्थाय रजो भौमं तुरङ्गपरिवर्तनैः .. 47 ..
खमारुरोह राजेन्द्र कपोतारुणपाण्डुरम् ..
स्थापयाञ्चक्रिरे चान्ये जलस्थाने च वाजिनः .. 48 ..
श्रेणी चक्रुस्तथैवान्ये कटच्छायासु पार्थिव ..
वितानाधस्तथा केचित्स्थापयाञ्चक्रिरे हयान् .. 49 ..
हयेभ्यो यवसं दत्त्वा केचिद्बुभुजिरे जनाः ..
कटच्छायाश्च नागानां चक्रुश्चान्ये सहस्रशः ..1.205.50 ..
वितानानि च मुख्यानि सूर्यतापप्रशान्तये ..
स्नाताञ्जलाशये नागाम्̐ल्लब्धतोयाञ्जनाधिप .. 51..
सच्छन्नान्स्वपरीधानकुम्भान्निन्युः स्वमालयम् ..
कटकाद्दूरतश्चक्रुरालानं नृपदन्तिनाम्.. 52..
text_mt:
Many thousands [of them] were seen in the camp of Bharata. / But others, skilled with horses, unyoked the steeds from the chariots,
unloaded their gear, and gently soothed them. / Dust from the earth, rising up from the horses rolling over,
ascended to the sky, O best of kings, grayish-red and pale like a pigeon. / Others stationed the steeds at the watering place,
and others arranged them in rows in the shade of straw mats, O king. / Some stationed the horses under awnings.
Having given grass to the horses, some people ate. / Others made shades of straw mats by the thousands for the elephants,
and excellent awnings to relieve the heat of the sun. / The elephants bathed in the water reservoir, and having received water, O lord of men,
they brought them to their quarters, their frontal lobes covered with their own garments. / Far from the camp they set up tethering posts for the king's elephants.

sanskrit_iast:
ālānāni mahārāja mahāvṛkṣeṣu mānavāḥ ..
ādāya gopinastatra kaṭakācca vidūrataḥ .. 53 ..
meaning:
आलानानि महाराज महावृक्षेषु मानवाः ..
आदाय गोपिनस्तत्र कटकाच्च विदूरतः .. 53 ..
text_mt: Men [made] tethering posts on large trees, O great king. / Taking [their animals] far from the camp, the cowherds there

sanskrit_iast:
gosaṅghānmahiṣīsaṅghāṃścakrurvyastānyathāsukham ..
kaṭake ca tathā ninyurgorasāni narādhipa .. 54 ..
meaning:
गोसङ्घान्महिषीसङ्घांश्चक्रुर्व्यस्तान्यथासुखम् ..
कटके च तथा निन्युर्गोरसानि नराधिप .. 54 ..
text_mt: comfortably dispersed the herds of cows and herds of buffaloes. / And likewise, O lord of men, they brought milk products into the camp.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭakāpaṇyavīthīṃ ca sarvapaṇyavibhūṣitām ..
dadṛśuḥ puruṣāstatra ayodhyāmiva cāparām .. 55 ..
meaning:
कटकापण्यवीथीं च सर्वपण्यविभूषिताम् ..
ददृशुः पुरुषास्तत्र अयोध्यामिव चापराम् .. 55 ..
text_mt: And the people there saw the market street of the camp, adorned with all wares, / as if it were a second Ayodhyā.

sanskrit_iast:
sthānāni sarvavaidyānāṃsadhvajāni narādhipa..
sāgadāni ca dṛśyante kaṭake bharatasya tu..56..
meaning:
स्थानानि सर्ववैद्यानांसध्वजानि नराधिप..
सागदानि च दृश्यन्ते कटके भरतस्य तु..56..
text_mt: The stations of all the physicians, furnished with banners and with medicines, / were seen, O lord of men, in the camp of Bharata.

sanskrit_iast:
senādhyakṣeṇa vīreṇa vijayena mahātmanā..
kṛtaṃ śāstrānusāreṇa skandhāvāraniveśanam .. 57 ..
meaning:
सेनाध्यक्षेण वीरेण विजयेन महात्मना..
कृतं शास्त्रानुसारेण स्कन्धावारनिवेशनम् .. 57 ..
text_mt: By the heroic commander-in-chief, the great-souled Vijaya, / the layout of the encampment was executed according to the treatises.

sanskrit_iast:
viveśa bharataḥ śrīmāṃścaturaṅgabalānvitaḥ ..
anvīyamāno vīrābhyāṃ putrābhyāṃ yadunandana .. 58 ..
meaning:
विवेश भरतः श्रीमांश्चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः ..
अन्वीयमानो वीराभ्यां पुत्राभ्यां यदुनन्दन .. 58 ..
text_mt: The glorious Bharata, accompanied by the fourfold army, entered, / followed by his two heroic sons, O delight of the Yadus,

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkareṇa ca vīreṇa takṣeṇa sumahātmanā ..
balamukhyaistathaivānyaiḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ .. 59 ..
meaning:
पुष्करेण च वीरेण तक्षेण सुमहात्मना ..
बलमुख्यैस्तथैवान्यैः सूतमागधबन्दिभिः .. 59 ..
text_mt: by the heroic Puṣkara and the very great-souled Takṣa, / as well as by other army commanders, and by bards, chroniclers, and heralds.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṅkhavāditraśabdena paṭahānāṃ svanena ca ..
bharatasya gṛhadvāratoraṇāntikamāgatāḥ .. 1.205.60..
meaning:
शङ्खवादित्रशब्देन पटहानां स्वनेन च ..
भरतस्य गृहद्वारतोरणान्तिकमागताः .. 1.205.60..
text_mt: With the sound of conch-shell instruments and the beat of kettle-drums, / they arrived near the gateway arch of Bharata's dwelling.

sanskrit_iast:
babhūburbalamukhyāste dikṣu ye yadunandana ..
santyajya madhyamāṃ vīthīṃ praveśāya mahāmanāḥ .. 61 ..
meaning:
बभूबुर्बलमुख्यास्ते दिक्षु ये यदुनन्दन ..
सन्त्यज्य मध्यमां वीथीं प्रवेशाय महामनाः .. 61 ..
text_mt: Those army commanders who were in the various quarters, O delight of the Yadus, / left the middle avenue for his entry, being magnanimous.

sanskrit_iast:
bandibhiḥ khyāpyamānāṃstānnāmakarmāvadānataḥ ..
śiraḥkampena bharataḥ prairayatsvānniveśanān .. 62 ..
meaning:
बन्दिभिः ख्याप्यमानांस्तान्नामकर्मावदानतः ..
शिरःकम्पेन भरतः प्रैरयत्स्वान्निवेशनान् .. 62 ..
text_mt: As they were being proclaimed by the heralds according to their names, deeds, and heroic exploits, / Bharata dismissed them to their own quarters with a nod of his head.

sanskrit_iast:
balamukhyānviveśātha svagṛhaṃ sarvaṛddhimat ..
dviyojanādhvanā śrāntā bharatasya tu sainikāḥ .. 63 ..
meaning:
बलमुख्यान्विवेशाथ स्वगृहं सर्वऋद्धिमत् ..
द्वियोजनाध्वना श्रान्ता भरतस्य तु सैनिकाः .. 63 ..
text_mt: [Dismissing] the army commanders, he then entered his own house, endowed with all prosperity. / The soldiers of Bharata, wearied by a journey of two yojanas,

sanskrit_iast:
viviśurbhavanānsvānsvānbhejire śayanāni ca ..
praviśya veśmapravaraṃ bharato'pi yathāsukham ... .. 64 ..
meaning:
विविशुर्भवनान्स्वान्स्वान्भेजिरे शयनानि च ..
प्रविश्य वेश्मप्रवरं भरतोऽपि यथासुखम् ... .. 64 ..
text_mt: entered their respective dwellings and resorted to their beds. / Having entered his excellent dwelling, Bharata, too, as he pleased,

sanskrit_iast:
vijahāra mahārāja devarājasamadyutiḥ ..
krameṇānena dharmātmā bhūmipāla dinedine ..
āsasāda vrajanneva gaṅgāṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm .. 65 ..
meaning:
विजहार महाराज देवराजसमद्युतिः ..
क्रमेणानेन धर्मात्मा भूमिपाल दिनेदिने ..
आससाद व्रजन्नेव गङ्गां त्रिपथगां नदीम् .. 65 ..
text_mt: diverted himself, O great king, equal in radiance to the king of the gods. / In this manner, day by day, the righteous ruler of the earth, / proceeding on his way, reached the river Gaṅgā that flows through the three worlds,

sanskrit_iast:
surāṅganāpīnapayodharasthasaccandanakṣālanalabdhalakṣmīm ..
grīṣmārkatāpādvigalattuṣāravivṛddhaśītodapaṭottarīyām .. 66 ..
bharata-śailūṣākhyānopari ṭippaṇī
meaning:
सुराङ्गनापीनपयोधरस्थसच्चन्दनक्षालनलब्धलक्ष्मीम् ..
ग्रीष्मार्कतापाद्विगलत्तुषारविवृद्धशीतोदपटोत्तरीयाम् .. 66 ..
भरत-शैलूषाख्यानोपरि टिप्पणी
text_mt:
which possessed beauty gained from washing away the pure sandalwood paste resting on the plump breasts of divine maidens, / and whose upper garment of cloth was the cool water increased by snow melting from the heat of the summer sun.
Note on the narrative of Bharata and Śailūṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
1.206
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
niveśamakarodrājan gaṅgātīre sa rāghavaḥ ..
bharatasya tadā cakrurgaṅgāyāṃ jalamaṇḍapān .. 1 ..
meaning:
1.206
.. मार्कण्डेय उवाच .. ..
निवेशमकरोद्राजन् गङ्गातीरे स राघवः ..
भरतस्य तदा चक्रुर्गङ्गायां जलमण्डपान् .. 1 ..
text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
That descendant of Raghu made his encampment on the bank of the Gaṅgā, O king. / Then they built water-pavilions in the Gaṅgā for Bharata,
title: Gandharvasabhākṣobhavarṇanaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
tathaiva balamukhyānāṃ prādhānyena narādhipa ..
sainikaśca janastasya prāpya tāṃ suranimnagām .. 2 ..
meaning:
तथैव बलमुख्यानां प्राधान्येन नराधिप ..
सैनिकश्च जनस्तस्य प्राप्य तां सुरनिम्नगाम् .. 2 ..
text_mt: and likewise for the principal army commanders, O lord of men. / And his soldiering folk, having reached that river of the gods,

sanskrit_iast:
sāphalyaṃ janmano mene tatyāja ca tathā klamam ..
sasnau papau payaḥ kāmaṃ harṣeṇa mahatā yutaḥ .. 3 ...
meaning:
साफल्यं जन्मनो मेने तत्याज च तथा क्लमम् ..
सस्नौ पपौ पयः कामं हर्षेण महता युतः .. 3 ...
text_mt: considered their birth fruitful and cast off their fatigue. / They bathed and drank water to their heart's content, filled with great joy.

sanskrit_iast:
snāpayāñcakrire tatra turagāṃsturagapriyāḥ ..
kuñjarānsnāpayamāsurmahāmātrāstathaiva ca .. 4 ..
meaning:
स्नापयाञ्चक्रिरे तत्र तुरगांस्तुरगप्रियाः ..
कुञ्जरान्स्नापयमासुर्महामात्रास्तथैव च .. 4 ..
text_mt: There, those fond of horses bathed their steeds, / and the mahouts likewise bathed their elephants.

sanskrit_iast:
majjadbhirbahusāhasraiḥ kuñjarairjāhnavī nadī ..
kirātaviṣayaiḥ saiva virarāja yathopalaiḥ .. 5 ..
meaning:
मज्जद्भिर्बहुसाहस्रैः कुञ्जरैर्जाह्नवी नदी ..
किरातविषयैः सैव विरराज यथोपलैः .. 5 ..
text_mt: With many thousands of plunging elephants, the river Jāhnavī / shone as if with boulders in the realm of the Kirātas.

sanskrit_iast:
samutthitamahāmātrāndṛṣṭvābhyukṣaṇachadmanā ..
cikrīḍurdṛtibhiḥ kecidviviśurbāhubhistathā .. 6 ..
meaning:
समुत्थितमहामात्रान्दृष्ट्वाभ्युक्षणछद्मना ..
चिक्रीडुर्दृतिभिः केचिद्विविशुर्बाहुभिस्तथा .. 6 ..
text_mt: Seeing the mahouts who had stood up, some played with leather water-bags / under the guise of sprinkling, and others entered [the river swimming] with their arms.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṅgāmāsādya saṃhṛṣṭā bharatasya tu sainikāḥ ..
bharato'pi tathā snātaḥ kṛtadaivatapūjanaḥ ..7..
meaning:
गङ्गामासाद्य संहृष्टा भरतस्य तु सैनिकाः ..
भरतोऽपि तथा स्नातः कृतदैवतपूजनः ..7..
text_mt: Having reached the Gaṅgā, Bharata's soldiers were overjoyed. / Bharata too, having bathed and performed worship of the deities,

sanskrit_iast:
śrāddhaṃ cakre mahātejā dadau dānaṃ tathaiva ca ..
dattvā tatra mahādānānājñāpayati yādava ..8..
meaning:
श्राद्धं चक्रे महातेजा ददौ दानं तथैव च ..
दत्त्वा तत्र महादानानाज्ञापयति यादव ..8..
text_mt: the greatly radiant one performed a śrāddha and likewise gave gifts. / Having given great gifts there, O descendant of Yadu, he commanded:

sanskrit_iast:
śilpino mama kurvantu kūṭāgārānmanoramān ..
rātrau dīpaniveśārthaṃ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..9..
meaning:
शिल्पिनो मम कुर्वन्तु कूटागारान्मनोरमान् ..
रात्रौ दीपनिवेशार्थं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ..9..
text_mt: 'Let my artisans construct charming floating pavilions / by hundreds and thousands, for the placement of lamps at night.

sanskrit_iast:
ānīyantāṃ tathā nāvaḥ sainyasya taraṇāya me ..
kriyantāṃ carmanāvaśca plavāśca śataśastathā ..1.206.10..
meaning:
आनीयन्तां तथा नावः सैन्यस्य तरणाय मे ..
क्रियन्तां चर्मनावश्च प्लवाश्च शतशस्तथा ..1.206.10..
text_mt: Let boats also be brought for the crossing of my army, / and let leather boats and rafts be made by the hundreds.

sanskrit_iast:
uttaraṃ pāramāsādya niveśaḥ kriyatāṃ tathā ..
paraṃ pāraṃ janā yāntu udayāstamayāntare ..11..
meaning:
उत्तरं पारमासाद्य निवेशः क्रियतां तथा ..
परं पारं जना यान्तु उदयास्तमयान्तरे ..11..
text_mt: Having reached the northern shore, let an encampment be made there as well. / Let the people go to the further shore between sunrise and sunset.'

sanskrit_iast:
evamājñāya bharato vijahāra yathāsukham ..
prasāritakaro rājansarvatraiva divākaraḥ .. 12 ..
meaning:
एवमाज्ञाय भरतो विजहार यथासुखम् ..
प्रसारितकरो राजन्सर्वत्रैव दिवाकरः .. 12 ..
text_mt: Having commanded thus, Bharata diverted himself as he pleased. / The sun, having stretched out its rays everywhere, O king,

sanskrit_iast:
yayāvadarśanaṃ tatra bharatasyaiva lajjayā ..
padmapatradalāgrābhā pratīcī cābhavatkṣaṇāt ..13..
meaning:
ययावदर्शनं तत्र भरतस्यैव लज्जया ..
पद्मपत्रदलाग्राभा प्रतीची चाभवत्क्षणात् ..13..
text_mt: went out of sight there, as if out of bashfulness before Bharata; / and the western quarter instantly became radiant like the tip of a lotus petal.

sanskrit_iast:
ādityestamanuprāpte sandhyārāgānurañjitā ..
tatastu tamasā vyāpte na prājñāyata kiñcana .. 14 ..
meaning:
आदित्येस्तमनुप्राप्ते सन्ध्यारागानुरञ्जिता ..
ततस्तु तमसा व्याप्ते न प्राज्ञायत किञ्चन .. 14 ..
text_mt: When the sun reached its setting, [the west] was tinted with the glow of twilight. / Then, when it was pervaded by darkness, nothing could be discerned.

sanskrit_iast:
bharatājñākṛtānpūrvaṃ kūṭāgārānsadīpakān ..
dhvajamālāparikṣiptāṃścikṣipurjāhnavījale ..15..
meaning:
भरताज्ञाकृतान्पूर्वं कूटागारान्सदीपकान् ..
ध्वजमालापरिक्षिप्तांश्चिक्षिपुर्जाह्नवीजले ..15..
text_mt: They cast into the water of the Jāhnavī the floating pavilions equipped with lamps / and surrounded by garlands of banners, which had previously been made at Bharata's command.

sanskrit_iast:
sainikaiśca tathā mukhyairbharatasya pṛthakpṛthak .
gaṅgāmbhasi parikṣiptā dīpavṛkṣāḥ sahasraśaḥ ..16..
meaning:
सैनिकैश्च तथा मुख्यैर्भरतस्य पृथक्पृथक् .
गङ्गाम्भसि परिक्षिप्ता दीपवृक्षाः सहस्रशः ..16..
text_mt: And likewise, by the chief soldiers of Bharata, individually, / lamp-trees were cast into the water of the Gaṅgā by the thousands.

sanskrit_iast:
sā dīpamālinī gaṅgā tīradyotitavigrahī ..
jahāsa phenahāsena jihveva gaganapriyā .. 17 ..
meaning:
सा दीपमालिनी गङ्गा तीरद्योतितविग्रही ..
जहास फेनहासेन जिह्वेव गगनप्रिया .. 17 ..
text_mt: Garlanded with lamps, her body illuminated along the bank, / the Gaṅgā laughed with the laughter of foam, like a tongue beloved of the sky.

sanskrit_iast:
jalāntarāgatai rdīpairdīpavṛkṣairmanoharaiḥ ..
tathā kallolasaṃkrāntairgaṅgā dīpteva lakṣyate .. 18 ..
meaning:
जलान्तरागतै र्दीपैर्दीपवृक्षैर्मनोहरैः ..
तथा कल्लोलसंक्रान्तैर्गङ्गा दीप्तेव लक्ष्यते .. 18 ..
text_mt: With the lamps that had moved into the water, with the delightful lamp-trees, / and with [reflections] transferred onto the billows, the Gaṅgā appeared as if ablaze.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ hi krīḍatāṃ tatra gaṅgātīre tathā nṛṇām ..
rātrāvevāñjasā jagmurnāvo bahuvidhā nṛpa .. 19 ..
meaning:
एवं हि क्रीडतां तत्र गङ्गातीरे तथा नृणाम् ..
रात्रावेवाञ्जसा जग्मुर्नावो बहुविधा नृप .. 19 ..
text_mt: While the men were thus sporting on the bank of the Gaṅgā, / various kinds of boats went swiftly across that very night, O king.

text_mt:
King Bharata, whose might was equal to Śakra, having crossed that goddess / who rests on the crags of Mahādeva’s matted locks and whose cool waters are enhanced by contact with the moon, / brought [the crossing] to completion.
1.207 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When Bharata had crossed the Gaṅgā, the sky’s girdle, / another Kaurava king entered his camp, O king,
accompanied by a fourfold army resembling an ocean, / and the ruler of the Kirātas, the king named Damana.
He appeared with forces comprising many thousands of scent-elephants; / having honoured him appropriately, Bharata, who loved dharma,
reached the Yamunā, the daughter of the sun who destroys sins, / the holy sister of Yama, a lovely dark garland.
Indeed, having performed a śrāddha anywhere in that river, O lord of men, / one obtains imperishable reward and rejoices in the heights of heaven.
Bathed [in it] on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight and having worshipped the daughter of the sun, / one is freed from all sins and goes to the heavenly realm.

text_mt:
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha, before sunrise, / he who has bathed in it and worshipped Dharmarāja with water and sesame seeds
does not fall into a bad rebirth and redeems his family; / indeed, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha, in whatever river
he has bathed, in all river waters, he is freed from sins; / but in the Yamunā especially, because she is the sister of Yama.
Having bathed in the Yamunā's water and gratified the ancestors and gods, / he does not go to a bad rebirth and goes to the realm of heaven.
Having reached that Yamunā, just as [he had done with] the water of the Gaṅgā, / sporting thus, Bharata crossed the great river.
When the great-souled Bharata had crossed the Yamunā, / Suratha, king of the Matsyas, then entered his camp,
and Gorasena of the Sālvas, and Prabhadraka of the Śibis; / with those rulers of men, he approached Kurukṣetra,
concerning which this ancient verse circulates in the world: / “Even the dust of Kurukṣetra stirred up by the wind

all reach heaven and shine in the sky like gods; / where, O best of kings, is the sacred place Sannīti, famous throughout the three worlds.
It is celebrated as Sannīti precisely because of bringing together the holy places; / all the holy places and lakes on earth down to the ocean

"There is a glorious Bhārgava brahmin renowned as Dadhīca. / Let an excellent weapon be made for the lord of the gods from his bones.
Entering [the weapon] there, O gods, I will slay Vṛtra beyond doubt." / Addressed in this way, all the gods went to the hermitage of Dadhīca.
They saw the illustrious Dadhīca, a treasury of austerities. / Having worshipped that illustrious one, the assembled gods said to him:
"With your bones we will make the vajra that destroys the daityas, / as well as other divine weapons for the accomplishment of the purpose of the gods.
Therefore, O twice-born, consent to renunciation for the purpose of the gods." / Addressed in this way, Dadhīca replied to those gods:
"A pilgrimage has been vowed by me to all sacred bathing places. / Having made that [pilgrimage], O best of gods, I will lay down my body."

The gods said: / "You are capable of summoning all the sacred bathing places, O bull among the twice-born. / May all the sacred bathing places come here this very day for you, O sinless one,
by your splendor, O Bhārgava, and likewise by ours." / Ghaṭodara said: / Addressed in this way by all the gods, the sacred bathing places, as well as the rivers,
the lakes, and the oceans came there, O ruler of men, / through their great affection, O king, and through his supreme yoga.
And perceiving their presence, the best of the twice-born bathed there; / and having performed the water-offering to the gods along with the ancestors,
he spoke these meaningful words to the gods standing there: / Dadhīca said: / "From this day forward, at the end of each month, O gods, continuously,
presence must be maintained here by you and by the sacred bathing places as they have arrived." / Ghaṭodara said: / When addressed in this way, having been answered, "So be it," by the gods and by the sacred bathing places, he then,
having abandoned his body, Dadhīca went to heaven through his own splendor. / And Viśvakarman then fashioned the vajra from portions of his bones,

all residences empty, their occupants drawn away to the royal road, / and the mansions along the royal road occupied by crowds of women.

women abandoned their household chores and went to the windows: / some with their limbs only half-anointed, some with collyrium applied to only one eye,

the women rushed hastily, with leather sandals on the second; / likewise, others pushed aside those who had previously occupied the windows.
While others were proceeding, some swift women / quickly went from window to window, casting off their leather sandals.
The women made those windows fair-faced with their own faces, / their hands resembling lotus buds with fine conch bracelets half-inserted.

They went with hands occupied in viewing their other hand, / their minds confused by the loosening of the knot of their skirts.
Others went there holding their skirts with their hands; / some, carrying a shower of flowers on their heads,
hurried to the windows with their long garments trailing. / By the charming dark-and-white [glances] of the beautiful women, the descendant of Raghu
passed by, as though being coloured by the falling of their glances, like the sun. / Then, with the rays of their eyes that fell upon him,
that descendant of Raghu, as he went, seemed to seize and draw away their hearts. / But whenever he passed beyond the range of their sight,
they were unaware of any action, as if depicted in a painting. / Even when Bharata had gone far away, some remained motionless;
pulled by their companions, they went down to the ground. / Born from a portion of Pradyumna, appearing like Pradyumna,
having taken their hearts, he swiftly went to the elephant stable. / In that Rājagṛha, O king, the descendant of Raghu reached the royal palace,

and leading sūtas, māgadhas, and bards, O lord of men. / They praised the heroic, highly intelligent Bharata who was sleeping happily:
"Good morning! Arise! The auspicious night has dawned. / The eastern quarter, O tiger among the Raghus, is coloured red by the dawn.
Surely at this hour Mātali awakens the lord of the gods, / the lord of the worlds, for the happiness [of all], O king of kings.
When you are asleep, the world is asleep; and when you are awake, it is endowed with happiness. / Therefore arise, O delighter of the Raghus, for the welfare of the worlds!
For you are the delight of all virtues, just like King Rāma; / the world has indeed been delighted by you with virtues resembling the rays of the moon."
It is a great wonder, O strong-armed one, that through your exceedingly white fame / the faces of the hosts of your enemies are made dark.
Seeing the water that is the edge of your sword, your enemy host, / out of fear, quickly has its home reddened merely by thirst.
You are unshakeable, exceedingly deep, and likewise a mine of jewels; / yet since you cannot be grasped, you do not seem to us equal to the ocean.

text_mt:
Gentle, endowed with the arts, fortunate, delighting the eyes— / there is no comparison for you, O king of men, with the moon, which is a source of blemishes and wanes.
Vast, to be enjoyed by your arm, furnishing refuge to all, and firm, / your earth bears no proper comparison to the shaking Vindhya.
Whatever you possess, you certainly give away, O slayer of foes; / whence then was non-existent fear bestowed by you upon the host of enemies?
He who is looked upon by you with sidelong glances for even a moment, / is looked upon constantly by the glances of Fortune with her full gaze.
With his discus whose edge is sharp as a razor, Janārdana, the god of gods, / carries away in battle the heads of your enemy host.
Wearing a garland of skulls, bearing a skull-topped staff, adorned with the moon, / his left half having the form of his beloved—may Śaṅkara bring you welfare!
Seated on a lotus, born from a lotus, the grandfather of all the worlds— / may he grant you prosperity, intelligence, resolve, fortune, and strength!
Moving through the sky, born of water, a god filling the hands of the maidens that are the directions, / a lamp in the pavilion of the universe—may he bring you an auspicious dawn!

May Śiva, the lord of Yakṣas, the lord of gods, the lord of the dead, and the night-roaming spirits, / along with all the hosts of gods, grant you an auspicious dawn!
May the sages, rivers, mountains, oceans, the ten directions, / and the divisions of time grant you an auspicious dawn!
Hearing this holy speech of these chanters of benedictions, / accompanied by the loud chant of an auspicious day, he then arose from his bed.
He listened to the income and expenditure together with the scribes and accountants; / then, having discharged the bodily urges, he went to the auspicious bath-chamber.
Then, having first cleansed his teeth, he began his bath; / he was then rubbed down with an astringent paste by strong men.
Seated comfortably on an auspicious seat, wearing a fine garment, the lord / bathed with various pure waters born of rivers and oceans,
With more than a hundred jars, O great king, made of gold, clay, / copper, and silver, accompanied by all kinds of medicinal herbs,

Filled with sandalwood extract, consecrated with the mantras of twice-born [priests]. / He wore a beautiful garment drenched with the abundance of bath-water,
Like the full disc of the moon veiled by thin clouds, / to the sound of musical instruments and the chant of an auspicious day, and likewise to the sound of songs.
Having bathed, having sipped water according to rule, collected in mind at the morning twilight, / he then looked at his handsome face in a mirror and in clarified butter,
And in gold, O great king, consecrated by the astrologer. / Then the descendant of Raghu listened to the [ruling] deity of the day, the lunar day, and the lunar mansion,
Uttered from the mouth of the astrologer, which destroys the bad dreams of the Kali age. / Then he performed the worship of the discus-bearing god of gods,
With an abundance of perfumes, garlands, obeisance, incense, lamps, and food, / with hymns of praise, offerings, and the sound of songs and musical instruments.
Having worshipped the god, the lord of gods, he entered the auspicious fire-chamber; / there he approached the fire previously offered into by the family priest.

text_mt:
The wise royal priest had already performed for him beforehand / the rite that destroys bad dreams and bestows accomplishment, prosperity, and victory.
Then, with a pleased mind, in the domestic fire, Bharata, / restrained, then made oblations reciting the Śrīsūkta and the Pauruṣasūkta,
With clarified butter purified by mantras according to rule, fully concentrated; / having offered the final oblation into the fire, the highly intelligent one, having performed his silent recitation,
Performed the worship of the gods together with the ancestors using water. / Then Bharata went out from that fire-chamber.
Having stepped out, he then honored the brahmins with wealth, / with cows, horses, and gold, accompanied by curds, flowers, and fruits,

Then the glorious Bharata dismissed the rulers of men,
presented by the doorkeeper, after giving them betel with his own hand.
Then, rising up, he went to a second, supreme chamber.
There he held counsel with his maternal uncle Yudhājit,
and with his priest Gārgya, as well as with his astrologer.
Yudhājit said:
"You have arrived at the desired time, wishing to slay the Gandharvas.
Therefore, as long as those Gandharvas do not know of your arrival,
slay them tonight by a surprise attack, O Lord.
Their destruction will easily take place by means of a surprise attack."
The astrologer said:
"Against one asleep, careless, trusting, and likewise, O King, exhausted,
or when the army has disembarked and is crossing a flowing river,
or is worn out by staying awake at night—covert warfare is prescribed.

उत्सारितस्तथा पदभ्यां धावद्भिः कुशलैर्जनैः ..83..
text_mt:
and likewise in hand-to-hand combat, O best of the Yadus,
and was challenged on foot by skilled runners.

sanskrit_iast:
snātaiḥ saṃpūjito viṣṇurvidhivatsāttvatottamaiḥ ..
namaskṛtya tathaivāgniṃ hutaṃ suṣṭhu purodhasā .. 84 ..
meaning:
स्नातैः संपूजितो विष्णुर्विधिवत्सात्त्वतोत्तमैः ..
नमस्कृत्य तथैवाग्निं हुतं सुष्ठु पुरोधसा .. 84 ..
text_mt:
Having bathed, Viṣṇu was properly worshipped by the foremost Sātvatas;
and having bowed to the fire, an oblation was well poured by the priest.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā bhuktavatāṃ śrutvā pūjitānāṃ dvijanmanām ..
puṇyāhaghoṣaṃ vittena bhūmipāla visarjya tān .. 85 ..
meaning:
तथा भुक्तवतां श्रुत्वा पूजितानां द्विजन्मनाम् ..
पुण्याहघोषं वित्तेन भूमिपाल विसर्ज्य तान् .. 85 ..
text_mt:
Then, having heard the proclamation of an auspicious day by the twice-born who had dined and been honored,
and having dismissed them with wealth, O protector of the earth,

sanskrit_iast:
parārdhyacandanāktāṅgastanucārusitāmbaraḥ ..
sarvālaṅkaraṇopetaḥ sragvī dhūpena dhūpitaḥ .. 86 ..
meaning:
परार्ध्यचन्दनाक्ताङ्गस्तनुचारुसिताम्बरः ..
सर्वालङ्करणोपेतः स्रग्वी धूपेन धूपितः .. 86 ..
text_mt:
his body anointed with supreme sandalwood, clad in fine and beautiful white garments,
adorned with all ornaments, wearing garlands, and perfumed with incense,

sanskrit_iast:
āsīnastvāsane divye bubhuje svajanairyutaḥ ..
mātulasya mahārghāṇi śucīni guṇavanti ca .. 87 ..
meaning:
आसीनस्त्वासने दिव्ये बुभुजे स्वजनैर्युतः ..
मातुलस्य महार्घाणि शुचीनि गुणवन्ति च .. 87 ..
text_mt:
seated on a heavenly seat together with his kin, he partook
of his maternal uncle's costly, pure, and wholesome [food],

sanskrit_iast:
aparīkṣitapūrvāṇi puruṣairāptakāribhiḥ ..
narapakṣimṛgāṇāntu liṅgairvahnau tathaiva ca .. 88 ..
meaning:
अपरीक्षितपूर्वाणि पुरुषैराप्तकारिभिः ..
नरपक्षिमृगाणान्तु लिङ्गैर्वह्नौ तथैव च .. 88 ..
text_mt:
previously tested by trustworthy men
by means of signs on humans, birds, and deer, and likewise in fire:

sanskrit_iast:
bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca peyaṃ coṣyaṃ tathaiva ca ..
pātreṣu rukmaraupyeṣu tathā maṇimayeṣu ca .. 69 ..
meaning:
भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च लेह्यं च पेयं चोष्यं तथैव च ..
पात्रेषु रुक्मरौप्येषु तथा मणिमयेषु च .. 69 ..
text_mt:
food to be chewed, food to be eaten, licked, drunk, and sucked,
served in vessels of gold, silver, and crystal.

sanskrit_iast:
bhuktvānnaṃ gītaśabdena cāptaiḥ katipayaiḥ saha ..
tathopaspṛśya dharmātmā dantadhāvanapūrvakam .. 1.209.90 ..
meaning:
भुक्त्वान्नं गीतशब्देन चाप्तैः कतिपयैः सह ..
तथोपस्पृश्य धर्मात्मा दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् .. 1.209.90 ..
text_mt:
Having eaten the meal to the sound of song along with a few trusted companions,
and then having performed ablutions preceded by cleansing his teeth,

sanskrit_iast:
cakrasya śayanaṃ bheje vāmapārśvena śatruhā ..
itihāsaṃ sa śuśrāva tatrasthaḥ puruṣottamaḥ .. 91 ..
meaning:
चक्रस्य शयनं भेजे वामपार्श्वेन शत्रुहा ..
इतिहासं स शुश्राव तत्रस्थः पुरुषोत्तमः .. 91 ..
text_mt:
that slayer of foes, the righteous-minded Puruṣottama,
retired to the couch of the discus on his left side and listened to historical lore while lying there.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa śayanaṃ tyaktvā śāstrābhyāsaṃ mahāyaśāḥ ..
cakāra raghuśārdūlaḥ satāṃ mārgamanuvrajan .. 92 ..
meaning:
ततः स शयनं त्यक्त्वा शास्त्राभ्यासं महायशाः ..
चकार रघुशार्दूलः सतां मार्गमनुव्रजन् .. 92 ..
text_mt:
Then, rising from his bed, that tiger of the Raghus of great renown,
following the path of the virtuous, engaged in the study of the scriptures.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminneva kāle tu saha gārgyo yudhājitā ..
viveśa bharataṃ draṣṭuṃ rathareṇupariplutaḥ .. 93 ..
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सह गार्ग्यो युधाजिता ..
विवेश भरतं द्रष्टुं रथरेणुपरिप्लुतः .. 93 ..
text_mt:
At that very time Gārgya, covered with chariot dust,
entered along with Yudhājit to see Bharata.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhāsīnaśca bharataṃ vākyametattato'bravīt ..
gārgya uvāca ..
tato vākyāni sarvāṇi śailūṣaḥ śrāvito mayā .. 94 ..
meaning:
सुखासीनश्च भरतं वाक्यमेतत्ततोऽब्रवीत् ..
गार्ग्य उवाच ..
ततो वाक्यानि सर्वाणि शैलूषः श्रावितो मया .. 94 ..
text_mt:
And sitting comfortably, he then addressed these words to Bharata.
Gārgya said:
"Thereupon all those words were made to be heard by Śailūṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
na tāni tasya rocante saṃgrāmastasya rocate ..
bharatena samāgamya śvobhūte dvijapuṅgava .. 95 ..
meaning:
न तानि तस्य रोचन्ते संग्रामस्तस्य रोचते ..
भरतेन समागम्य श्वोभूते द्विजपुङ्गव .. 95 ..
text_mt:
They do not please him; battle pleases him.
[He said:] 'Having encountered Bharata tomorrow, O bull among the twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
bharataṃ nāśayiṣyāmi nīhāraṃ candramā yathā ..
ityuktvā sa tu māṃ rājā preṣayāmāsa satvaraḥ .. 96 ..
meaning:
भरतं नाशयिष्यामि नीहारं चन्द्रमा यथा ..
इत्युक्त्वा स तु मां राजा प्रेषयामास सत्वरः .. 96 ..
text_mt:
I shall destroy Bharata as the moon destroys the mist.'
Having spoken thus, that king sent me away in haste.

sanskrit_iast:
āhvānadundubhistatra niṣkrānte mayi cāhataḥ ..
etajjñātvā sa yuddhāya prātaḥ sajjo bhavettava .. 97 ..
meaning:
आह्वानदुन्दुभिस्तत्र निष्क्रान्ते मयि चाहतः ..
एतज्ज्ञात्वा स युद्धाय प्रातः सज्जो भवेत्तव .. 97 ..
text_mt:
And as I went forth, the drum of summons was beaten there.
Knowing this, let your army be ready for battle in the morning."

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
iti gārgyavacaḥ śrutvā bharato gārgyamabravīt..
gaccha śīghraṃ gṛhaṃ brahmañchrānto rathabalādhvataḥ ..98..
meaning:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
इति गार्ग्यवचः श्रुत्वा भरतो गार्ग्यमब्रवीत्..
गच्छ शीघ्रं गृहं ब्रह्मञ्छ्रान्तो रथबलाध्वतः ..98..
text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having heard these words of Gārgya, Bharata said to Gārgya:
“Go home quickly, O brahmin; you are exhausted from the journey by chariot and army.

sanskrit_iast:
ahamājñāpayiṣyāmi sarvaṃ sāṃgrāmikaṃ vidhim ..
etāvaduktvā vijayaṃ senādhyakṣamathā'bravīt..99..
meaning:
अहमाज्ञापयिष्यामि सर्वं सांग्रामिकं विधिम् ..
एतावदुक्त्वा विजयं सेनाध्यक्षमथाऽब्रवीत्..99..
text_mt:
I will order all the preparations for battle.”
Having said this much, he then addressed Vijaya, the commander of the army:

sanskrit_iast:
mamoṣṭravāhibhiḥ śīghraṃ śibireṣu mahīkṣitām ..
yodhānājñāpayatvadya śvobhūtāya raṇāya vai .. 1.209.100 ..
meaning:
ममोष्ट्रवाहिभिः शीघ्रं शिबिरेषु महीक्षिताम् ..
योधानाज्ञापयत्वद्य श्वोभूताय रणाय वै .. 1.209.100 ..
text_mt:
“Let my camel-riders quickly order the warriors
in the camps of the kings for battle tomorrow.

sanskrit_iast:
yuddhāvadhānikaṃ sarvaṃ kartavyaṃ ca tathā tvayā ..
evamājñāpya nāgānāṃ turagāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 101 ..
meaning:
युद्धावधानिकं सर्वं कर्तव्यं च तथा त्वया ..
एवमाज्ञाप्य नागानां तुरगाणां तथैव च .. 101 ..
text_mt:
And you must likewise attend to everything required for the fight.”
Having given this command, he inspected the elephants and horses,

sanskrit_iast:
pratyāvekṣāṃ tataḥ kṛtvā sandhyāmanvāsya paścimām ..
rahogataḥ sa śuśrāva narāṇāṃ mūḍhabhāṣitam ..102 ..
meaning:
प्रत्यावेक्षां ततः कृत्वा सन्ध्यामन्वास्य पश्चिमाम् ..
रहोगतः स शुश्राव नराणां मूढभाषितम् ..102 ..
text_mt:
and then, having performed the review and attended to the evening twilight devotion,
he retired to seclusion and heard the confused chatter of the men.

sanskrit_iast:
āruroha tadā śrutvā prāsādaṃ himapāṇḍuram ..
kailāsaśikharākāraṃ nirvātaṃ rajanīmukhe .. .. 103 ..
meaning:
आरुरोह तदा श्रुत्वा प्रासादं हिमपाण्डुरम् ..
कैलासशिखराकारं निर्वातं रजनीमुखे .. .. 103 ..
text_mt:
Hearing it, he then ascended at nightfall to a palace white as snow,
shaped like the peak of Mount Kailāsa and sheltered from the wind.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu sainikaḥ kaścicchibire bharatasya tu ..
talaṃ talenābhyahanatpavanārthaṃ yadṛcchayā .. 104 ..
meaning:
ततस्तु सैनिकः कश्चिच्छिबिरे भरतस्य तु ..
तलं तलेनाभ्यहनत्पवनार्थं यदृच्छया .. 104 ..
text_mt:
Then a certain soldier in Bharata’s camp
struck palm against palm at will to create a breeze.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu sainikaiḥ sarvaistalatālairmahāsvanam ..
cakrire puruṣavyāghra tasminkāle divaṃ gatam .. 105 ..
meaning:
ततस्तु सैनिकैः सर्वैस्तलतालैर्महास्वनम् ..
चक्रिरे पुरुषव्याघ्र तस्मिन्काले दिवं गतम् .. 105 ..
text_mt:
Thereupon, O tiger among men, all the soldiers with the clapping of their hands
made a great sound at that moment that reached up to the sky.

sanskrit_iast:
pravavau ca tadānīto vāyurmanujapuṅgava ..
etasminneva kāle tu madrarājastadāṃśumān .. 106 ..
meaning:
प्रववौ च तदानीतो वायुर्मनुजपुङ्गव ..
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मद्रराजस्तदांशुमान् .. 106 ..
text_mt:
And the wind, brought forth thereby, blew, O best of men.
At that very time, the radiant king of the Madras,

sanskrit_iast:
prāsādavaramārūḍho jñātavānbharataṃ tadā ..
dīpālokena lakṣmyā ca prāsādasya vivṛddhayā .. 107 ...
meaning:
प्रासादवरमारूढो ज्ञातवान्भरतं तदा ..
दीपालोकेन लक्ष्म्या च प्रासादस्य विवृद्धया .. 107 ...
text_mt:
having climbed to the top of his excellent palace, noticed Bharata
by the light of lamps and the elevated splendour of the palace.

sanskrit_iast:
sa jagāma tadā rājā prahasansainikaṃ janam ..
bharatasya pradāsyāmi yuktyaiva baladarśanam .. 108 ..
meaning:
स जगाम तदा राजा प्रहसन्सैनिकं जनम् ..
भरतस्य प्रदास्यामि युक्त्यैव बलदर्शनम् .. 108 ..
text_mt:
Then that king went, laughing, to his soldiers:
“By a clever device I will show our strength to Bharata.

sanskrit_iast:
tṛṇamuṣṭimupādīpya sarvo'pi kaṭake janaḥ ..
pāṇāvādāya muditaḥ kṣveḍāśabdaṃ karotu vai .. 109 ..
meaning:
तृणमुष्टिमुपादीप्य सर्वोऽपि कटके जनः ..
पाणावादाय मुदितः क्ष्वेडाशब्दं करोतु वै .. 109 ..
text_mt:
Let every single person in the camp light a handful of grass,
take it in his hand, and joyfully raise a war-cry.”

sanskrit_iast:
pārthivenaivamukte tu kaṭake tasya dhīmataḥ ..
solkāhasto janaḥ sarvaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata .. .. 1.209.110 ..
meaning:
पार्थिवेनैवमुक्ते तु कटके तस्य धीमतः ..
सोल्काहस्तो जनः सर्वः क्षणेन समपद्यत .. .. 1.209.110 ..
text_mt:
When the wise ruler had spoken thus in his camp,
all the men in an instant stood with torches in their hands.

sanskrit_iast:
śibiraṃ madrarājñastu dvitīyamiva cāmbaram ..
babhūva tārakācitramulkāhastaistadā naraiḥ .. 111 ..
meaning:
शिबिरं मद्रराज्ञस्तु द्वितीयमिव चाम्बरम् ..
बभूव तारकाचित्रमुल्काहस्तैस्तदा नरैः .. 111 ..
text_mt:
The camp of the king of the Madras then became like a second sky,
variegated with stars, by means of those men holding torches in their hands.

sanskrit_iast:
tadbalaughamaparyantaṃ solkāhastairjanairvṛtam ..
dṛṣṭvā jagāma dharmātmā parāṃ prītiṃ raghūdvahaḥ .. 112 ..
meaning:
तद्बलौघमपर्यन्तं सोल्काहस्तैर्जनैर्वृतम् ..
दृष्ट्वा जगाम धर्मात्मा परां प्रीतिं रघूद्वहः .. 112 ..
text_mt:
Seeing that boundless flood of an army surrounded by men holding torches,
the righteous-minded descendant of Raghu experienced supreme delight.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāścaiva śrutvā harṣamupāgataḥ ..
tasminpraśānte jvalane mandībhūte ca nisvane .. 113 ..
meaning:
क्ष्वेडाः किलकिलाश्चैव श्रुत्वा हर्षमुपागतः ..
तस्मिन्प्रशान्ते ज्वलने मन्दीभूते च निस्वने .. 113 ..
text_mt:
Hearing the war-cries and shouts of joy, he was filled with gladness.
When that blaze subsided and the noise diminished,

sanskrit_iast:
abhyahanyanta bhūpānāṃ śibireṣu pṛthakpṛthak ..
saṃjñātūryāṇi ramyāṇi nānāliṅgāni cāpyatha .. 114 ..
meaning:
अभ्यहन्यन्त भूपानां शिबिरेषु पृथक्पृथक् ..
संज्ञातूर्याणि रम्याणि नानालिङ्गानि चाप्यथ .. 114 ..
text_mt:
the charming signal-trumpets of various descriptions
were sounded individually in the camps of the kings.

sanskrit_iast:
subahūni mahārāja tena kolāhalaṃ mahat ..
babhūva prītijananaṃ bharatasya mahātmanaḥ .. 115 ..
meaning:
सुबहूनि महाराज तेन कोलाहलं महत् ..
बभूव प्रीतिजननं भरतस्य महात्मनः .. 115 ..
text_mt:
Very many they were, O great king, and from them arose a great clamour
that produced delight for the high-souled Bharata.

sanskrit_iast:
mantrayitvā tataḥ śrīmānkṣaṇamātraṃ yudhājitā..
tenaiva saha bhuktvā ca suṣvāpa śayanottame ..
madhureṇa sugītena vīṇāveṇuraveṇa ca .. 116 ..
meaning:
मन्त्रयित्वा ततः श्रीमान्क्षणमात्रं युधाजिता..
तेनैव सह भुक्त्वा च सुष्वाप शयनोत्तमे ..
मधुरेण सुगीतेन वीणावेणुरवेण च .. 116 ..
text_mt:
Then the glorious one, having conferred for a mere moment with Yudhājit
and dined with him, went to sleep on an excellent bed
to the sweet sound of singing and the melody of lutes and flutes.

sanskrit_iast:
himāvadāte varamālyacitre vitānakādhovihite manojñe ..
suṣvāpa rātriṃ sa mahānubhāvo bhogīndrabhoge madhujidyathaiva .. 117 ..
1.210
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
āhvānadundubhiṃ śrutvā śailūṣatanayāstataḥ ..
āseduḥ pārthivaṃ sarve śailūṣaṃ taṃ samāgatāḥ .. 1 ..
namuciḥ kāmapālaśca gaveṣaṇasudarśanau ..
vīrabāhuḥ subāhuśca vāyuvegasuvarcasau ..2..
nikumbhaḥ kumbhanāmā ca balāko balakastathā ..
harikeśo mahojāśca sūryaraśmiprabhaṅkaraḥ .. 3 ..
vṛndārako jyautiṣiko dṛḍhasyuraparājitaḥ ..
kumudaḥ kumudāpīḍo vasunāthaḥ sulocanaḥ .. 4 ..
candrāpīḍo gadī maulī kinnaro'jagaro ruhaḥ ..
kesarī varavāṇaśca bhānurāgāvaho rayiḥ ..5..
ekalavyo viśālaśca kalaviṅkaḥ kalāpriyaḥ ..
bhīmanādo mahānādo vāsukiḥ panaso gadaḥ .. 6 ..
meaning:
हिमावदाते वरमाल्यचित्रे वितानकाधोविहिते मनोज्ञे ..
सुष्वाप रात्रिं स महानुभावो भोगीन्द्रभोगे मधुजिद्यथैव .. 117 ..
1.210
.. मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
आह्वानदुन्दुभिं श्रुत्वा शैलूषतनयास्ततः ..
आसेदुः पार्थिवं सर्वे शैलूषं तं समागताः .. 1 ..
नमुचिः कामपालश्च गवेषणसुदर्शनौ ..
वीरबाहुः सुबाहुश्च वायुवेगसुवर्चसौ ..2..
निकुम्भः कुम्भनामा च बलाको बलकस्तथा ..
हरिकेशो महोजाश्च सूर्यरश्मिप्रभङ्करः .. 3 ..
वृन्दारको ज्यौतिषिको दृढस्युरपराजितः ..
कुमुदः कुमुदापीडो वसुनाथः सुलोचनः .. 4 ..
चन्द्रापीडो गदी मौली किन्नरोऽजगरो रुहः ..
केसरी वरवाणश्च भानुरागावहो रयिः ..5..
एकलव्यो विशालश्च कलविङ्कः कलाप्रियः ..

text_mt:

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Hearing the war-drum of challenge, all the sons of Śailūṣa
then assembled and approached the king, that Śailūṣa:
Namuci, Kāmapāla, Gaveṣaṇa, Sudarśana,

Bhīmanāda, Mahānāda, Vāsuki, Panasa, Gada,

text_mt:
Candravarmā, Mahāvarmā, Vasuṣeṇa, and Agrajāraka—
these and other Gandharvas were sons of the powerful Śailūṣa.
Wearing celestial garlands and garments, adorned with celestial sandalwood paste,
they then entered the assembly hall and sat upon costly seats.
Protected by Śailūṣa’s sons, that assembly hall, adorned with jewels,
shone, O king, like an autumn night variegated with stars.
When they were seated, Śailūṣa then told them
everything Gārgya had said, as well as his own assessment.
Hearing then of the assault from mortals, O lord of men,
their minds enraged, they made various gestures in fury.
Those sons of the Gandharva king, shedding tears of wrath,
resembled clouds at the end of an aeon, their eyes flashing like lightning.
Namuci wore a face flushed with the red of rage,
like the northern quarter during a forest fire foretelling a great battle.
The three-pointed knit of Kāmapāla’s brows on his forehead shone
like the Gaṅgā falling upon the Himalayas in three cascades.

text_mt:
Kumudāpīḍa’s eyes, black with white edges
and tinged with the red of rage, became coppery like twilight.
With his body overcome by anger, Kumuda, who had the splendour of a white lotus,
turned into the likeness of a red water-lily in an instant.
Candrāpīḍa’s handsome face, darkened with the smoke of anger,
assumed the appearance of the moon shrouded by thin clouds.
The face of Bhānu, veiled by the smoke of his angry breaths,
became like the sun during an eclipse, O best of the Yadus.
With his face and limbs darkened by the smoke born from wringing his hands,
Sudarśana, “Fair to Behold,” at that time gained an irony in his name.
By Gaveṣaṇa’s violent fury, blazing as if with fire within,
the destruction of kings was portended, just as by a shower of meteors.
By the dust of crushed jewels struck by the arms of Vīrabāhu,
an eruption occurred in the hall, as if wrath had assumed an embodied form.
The clash of Subāhu’s arms made a sound like a thunderbolt,
deep as an atmospheric crash portending the death of kings.

text_mt:
The ground, scraped by the feet of Vāyuvega with great speed,
tore open, O protector of the earth, proclaiming the terror of destruction.
Suvarcas bore the expanse of his forehead,
adorned with the sprouting of bristling hair and perspiration born of exertion.
Tawny from the golden pillars reflected on his sweating limbs,
Kumbhanābha, indeed, was like wrath embodied.
Garlanded with manes of flames from the fire of his bristling hair that burst forth,
he imitated Hari of the form of Nṛsiṃha through his brilliance.
With the entire circle of Gandharvas reflected on his sweating body,
Maula laughed aloud at Janārdana bearing the universal form.
O king, all those sons of the Gandharva king
were then especially seized in their minds by fury.
Seeing thus the anger of his sons and recalling the words of the royal priest,
that king, whose terrible mouth bit his lip, gave way completely to fury.

kavidattakarālambā kīrtiryātu divaṃ tava .. 15 ..
meaning:
..महाधर्म उवाच ..
शत्रुमस्तकविन्यस्तपदक्रमविलासिनी ..
कविदत्तकरालम्बा कीर्तिर्यातु दिवं तव .. 15 ..
text_mt:
Mahādharma said:
Delighting in placing its steps on the heads of enemies,
supported by the hand given by a poet, may your fame go to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
.. vāsukiruvāca ..
māyānihatamātaṅgamadhyadvīpavidāritām ..
kṣitiṃ bhittvāviśatkanyā kīrtito vasudhātalam .. 16..
meaning:
.. वासुकिरुवाच ..
मायानिहतमातङ्गमध्यद्वीपविदारिताम् ..
क्षितिं भित्त्वाविशत्कन्या कीर्तितो वसुधातलम् .. 16..
text_mt:
Vāsuki said:
Splitting the earth torn in the middle island where elephants were slain by magical illusion,
the maiden of your fame has entered the surface of the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
.. panasa uvāca ..
hatārilakṣmīsaṃyogavikasadvadanasya te ..
prayātu tvaritā kīrtiḥ krodhaneva diśo daśa ..17..
meaning:
.. पनस उवाच ..
हतारिलक्ष्मीसंयोगविकसद्वदनस्य ते ..
प्रयातु त्वरिता कीर्तिः क्रोधनेव दिशो दश ..17..
text_mt:
Panasa said:
May your fame, swift as if angry,
go to the ten directions for you whose face blossoms from union with the fortune of slain enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
gada uvāca...
satoyatoyadākārairnāgairdānapravarṣibhiḥ ..
ākrāntadiṅmukhe yuddhe vidyuttvamme karotvasiḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
गद उवाच...
सतोयतोयदाकारैर्नागैर्दानप्रवर्षिभिः ..
आक्रान्तदिङ्मुखे युद्धे विद्युत्त्वम्मे करोत्वसिः .. 18 ..
text_mt:
Gada said:
In battle where the faces of the directions are overtaken by elephants like rain clouds pouring rut-fluid,
let my sword act as lightning.

sanskrit_iast:
mahānāda uvāca ..
madīyasiṃhanādena vitrāsitagajākulam ..
balaṃ nipātayārīṇāṃ śaraiḥ sannataparvabhiḥ .. 19 ..
meaning:
महानाद उवाच ..
मदीयसिंहनादेन वित्रासितगजाकुलम् ..
बलं निपातयारीणां शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः .. 19 ..
text_mt:
Mahānāda said:
Cast down with arrows of straight joints the army of the enemies,
which is agitated with elephants terrified by my lion-roar.

sanskrit_iast:
vasuruvāca ..
gajāśvarathapādātacaraṇollikhitaṃ rajaḥ ..
draṣṭāsi praśamaṃ yātaṃ paritastvariśoṇitaiḥ .. 1.211.20 ..
meaning:
वसुरुवाच ..
गजाश्वरथपादातचरणोल्लिखितं रजः ..
द्रष्टासि प्रशमं यातं परितस्त्वरिशोणितैः .. 1.211.20 ..
text_mt:
Vasu said:
You will see the dust kicked up by the feet of elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers
quickly completely settled by the blood of enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛndāraka uvāca ..
gajakumbhasamudrasthamuktāphalavikāsiṣu ..
tiṣṭhatsu rājankhaḍgeṣu kaḥ saheta parābhavam .. 21 ..
meaning:
वृन्दारक उवाच ..
गजकुम्भसमुद्रस्थमुक्ताफलविकासिषु ..
तिष्ठत्सु राजन्खड्गेषु कः सहेत पराभवम् .. 21 ..
text_mt:
Vṛndāraka said:
While swords stand shining with pearls from the ocean of elephants' frontal globes,
O king, who would tolerate defeat?

sanskrit_iast:
.. jyotiṣika uvāca ..
kāpiśabhrūlatābhaṅgakuṭiladvayakoṭiṣu ..
vidyamāneṣu cāpeṣu kaḥ saheta parābhavam .. 22 ..
meaning:
.. ज्योतिषिक उवाच ..
कापिशभ्रूलताभङ्गकुटिलद्वयकोटिषु ..
विद्यमानेषु चापेषु कः सहेत पराभवम् .. 22 ..
text_mt:
Jyotiṣika said:
While bows exist whose two ends are curved like the bending of brown creepers of eyebrows,
who would tolerate defeat?

sanskrit_iast:
dṛḍhasyuruvāca ..
rājaṃstīkṣṇāḥ santi yasya viśikhāḥ pañca māninaḥ ..
kimanyaistasya kartavyaṃ pakṣapātibhirāhave .. 23 ..
meaning:
दृढस्युरुवाच ..
राजंस्तीक्ष्णाः सन्ति यस्य विशिखाः पञ्च मानिनः ..
किमन्यैस्तस्य कर्तव्यं पक्षपातिभिराहवे .. 23 ..
text_mt:
Dṛḍhasyu said:
O king, for a proud man who has five sharp arrows,
what need is there of others who take sides in battle?

sanskrit_iast:
candrāpīḍa uvāca ..
kimāyudhaiḥ sattvavatāṃ cārudordaṇḍa śālinām ..
sadyaḥ sañjātamanyūnāṃ yuddhavyākṣepakārakaiḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
चन्द्रापीड उवाच ..
किमायुधैः सत्त्ववतां चारुदोर्दण्ड शालिनाम् ..
सद्यः सञ्जातमन्यूनां युद्धव्याक्षेपकारकैः .. 24 ..
text_mt:
Candrāpīḍa said:
What need is there of weapons that delay the fight
for resolute men possessing beautiful staff-like arms, whose fury has just arisen?

sanskrit_iast:
gadyuruvāca ..
khaḍgāstiṣṭhantu me tucchā bhuktabhaṅgāṭṭahāsinaḥ ..
ekadordaṇḍaśeṣo'pi kaḥ saheta parābhavam .. 25 ..
meaning:
गद्युरुवाच ..
खड्गास्तिष्ठन्तु मे तुच्छा भुक्तभङ्गाट्टहासिनः ..
एकदोर्दण्डशेषोऽपि कः सहेत पराभवम् .. 25 ..

sanskrit_iast:
kalaviṅka uvāca ..
madbāhumandarakṣubdhavairisainyamahārṇavāt ..
bhuṅkṣva lakṣmīṃ samutpannāṃ cirāya jagatīpate .. 26 ..
meaning:
कलविङ्क उवाच ..
मद्बाहुमन्दरक्षुब्धवैरिसैन्यमहार्णवात् ..
भुङ्क्ष्व लक्ष्मीं समुत्पन्नां चिराय जगतीपते .. 26 ..
text_mt:
Kalaviṅka said:
Enjoy for a long time, O ruler of the earth, the fortune produced
from the great ocean of the enemy army churned by my arm like Mount Mandara.

sanskrit_iast:
.. gaja uvāca ..
kimāyudhaiḥ sattvavatāṃ kupuṃsāṃ ca kimāyudhaiḥ ..
arātiśastrāṇyekeṣāmanyeṣāmaphalāni hi .. 27 ..
meaning:
.. गज उवाच ..
किमायुधैः सत्त्ववतां कुपुंसां च किमायुधैः ..
अरातिशस्त्राण्येकेषामन्येषामफलानि हि .. 27 ..
text_mt:
Gaja said:
What use are weapons to resolute men, and what use are weapons to cowards?
To the former, the weapons of enemies [are enough]; to the latter, indeed, they are useless.

sanskrit_iast:
balaka uvāca ..
durbalotkhāta śakrebhadaśanābhihate harau ..
mayādya surarāḍastu bhavāṃstribhuvaneśvaraḥ .. 28 .. ..
meaning:
बलक उवाच ..
दुर्बलोत्खात शक्रेभदशनाभिहते हरौ ..
मयाद्य सुरराडस्तु भवांस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरः .. 28 .. ..
text_mt:
Balaka said:
When Śakra's elephant has its tusks torn out by the weak, and Hari is struck down,
may you become the king of the gods today, and ruler of the three worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
pranaṣṭadevatāpūjaṃ balihīnaṃ sudurdaśam ..
mayā kṛtamathādyāstu trailokyamapi suprabho .. 29 ..
meaning:
प्रनष्टदेवतापूजं बलिहीनं सुदुर्दशम् ..
मया कृतमथाद्यास्तु त्रैलोक्यमपि सुप्रभो .. 29 ..
text_mt:
O radiant lord, let even the three worlds be made by me today
free of worship to gods, devoid of offerings, and reduced to a wretched state.

sanskrit_iast:
harika uvāca ..
kīnāśamahiṣeṇādya harasya vṛṣabheṇa tu ..
ayodhyāṃ vāhayiṣyāmi śeṣāherlāṅgalena ca .. 1.211.30 ..
meaning:
हरिक उवाच ..
कीनाशमहिषेणाद्य हरस्य वृषभेण तु ..
अयोध्यां वाहयिष्यामि शेषाहेर्लाङ्गलेन च .. 1.211.30 ..
text_mt:
Harika said:
Today, with the buffalo of Yama and the bull of Hara,
and with the serpent Śeṣa as a plow, I will cultivate Ayodhyā.

sanskrit_iast:
mahodara uvāca ..
nirastamayamārtaṇḍe mayā loke carācare ..
yamasya mahiṣaṃ paśya kramantaṃ sūryavājiṣu .. 31 ..
meaning:
महोदर उवाच ..
निरस्तमयमार्तण्डे मया लोके चराचरे ..
यमस्य महिषं पश्य क्रमन्तं सूर्यवाजिषु .. 31 ..
text_mt:
Mahodara said:
When the moving and unmoving world has had its sun cast into night by me,
behold the buffalo of Yama trampling the horses of the sun.

sanskrit_iast:
sūrya uvāca ..
niḥśeṣadevatāsaṃghe mayā lokatraye kṛte ..
durgāsiṃhavinirbhinnaṃ paśyādya maghavadgajam .. 32 ..
meaning:
सूर्य उवाच ..
निःशेषदेवतासंघे मया लोकत्रये कृते ..
दुर्गासिंहविनिर्भिन्नं पश्याद्य मघवद्गजम् .. 32 ..
text_mt:
Sūrya said:
When the three worlds have been emptied by me of all hosts of deities,
behold today the elephant of Indra torn apart by the lion of Durgā.

sanskrit_iast:
prabhasa uvāca ..

praṇamantu tavādyaiva devasaṃghā hatatviṣaḥ .. 33 ..
meaning:
प्रभस उवाच ..
निरस्ताम्बुपिपासेन समाकृष्ट धनेश्वराः ..
प्रणमन्तु तवाद्यैव देवसंघा हतत्विषः .. 33 ..
text_mt:
Prabhasa said:
Drawn out by me, whose thirst for water is quenched, let the hosts of gods, their radiance destroyed, / bow before you this very day, O lord of wealth!

sanskrit_iast:
bhadraka uvāca ..

śikhī saṃbhakṣayatvadya śarvābharaṇapannagān .. 34 ..
meaning:
भद्रक उवाच ..
स्कन्दशङ्करशून्येऽस्मिन्मया त्रिभुवने कृते ..
शिखी संभक्षयत्वद्य शर्वाभरणपन्नगान् .. 34 ..
text_mt:
Bhadraka said:
When I have emptied these three worlds of Skanda and Śaṅkara, / let the peacock eat Śarva's ornament-snakes today!

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
krodhāndhakārakaluṣīkṛtacāruvaktrāngandharvarājatanayānprasamīkṣamāṇaḥ ..
jagāda rājānamadīna sattvo nāḍāyanākhyastu tadā purodhāḥ .. 35 ..
1.212
.. nāḍāyana uvāca .. ..
ekayā dve viniścitya trīṃścaturbhirvaśīkuru ..
pañca jitvā vijitvā ṣaṭ sapta hitvā sukhī bhava .. 1 ..
ekayā prajñayā rājankāryākāryadvayaṃ naraḥ ..
viniścitya tu yaḥ kuryātkāryaṃ tatra sa paṇḍitaḥ .. 2 ..
madhyasthaṃ yadi vā mitraṃ śatruṃ vā kāryagauravāt ..
jñātvā deśaṃ ca kālaṃ ca hyupāyairabhyupakramet .. 3 ..
sāmabhedapradānāśca upāyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
upāyaśca caturtho 'tra daṇḍastvagatikā gatiḥ .. 4 ..
pañcendriyajayo yena kṛta ādau jigīṣuṇā ..
trilokavijayaṃ tasya na dūre pratibhāti me .. 5 ..
pañcendriya jayaṃ kṛtvā guṇaṣaṭkamupāśrayet ..
buddhvā balābalaṃ samyagātmanaścāparasya ca .. 6 ..
meaning:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
क्रोधान्धकारकलुषीकृतचारुवक्त्रान्गन्धर्वराजतनयान्प्रसमीक्षमाणः ..
जगाद राजानमदीन सत्त्वो नाडायनाख्यस्तु तदा पुरोधाः .. 35 ..
1.212
.. नाडायन उवाच .. ..
एकया द्वे विनिश्चित्य त्रींश्चतुर्भिर्वशीकुरु ..
पञ्च जित्वा विजित्वा षट् सप्त हित्वा सुखी भव .. 1 ..
एकया प्रज्ञया राजन्कार्याकार्यद्वयं नरः ..
विनिश्चित्य तु यः कुर्यात्कार्यं तत्र स पण्डितः .. 2 ..
मध्यस्थं यदि वा मित्रं शत्रुं वा कार्यगौरवात् ..
ज्ञात्वा देशं च कालं च ह्युपायैरभ्युपक्रमेत् .. 3 ..
सामभेदप्रदानाश्च उपायाः परिकीर्तिताः ..
उपायश्च चतुर्थो ऽत्र दण्डस्त्वगतिका गतिः .. 4 ..
पञ्चेन्द्रियजयो येन कृत आदौ जिगीषुणा ..
त्रिलोकविजयं तस्य न दूरे प्रतिभाति मे .. 5 ..
पञ्चेन्द्रिय जयं कृत्वा गुणषट्कमुपाश्रयेत् ..
बुद्ध्वा बलाबलं सम्यगात्मनश्चापरस्य च .. 6 ..
text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Seeing the sons of the king of the Gandharvas, their handsome faces darkened by the gloom of rage, / the royal priest named Nāḍāyana, whose spirit was undaunted, then spoke to the king:
1.212
Nāḍāyana said:
Determining the two through the one, master the three through the four; / conquering the five and overcoming the six, abandoning the seven, be happy!
By means of the one discernment, O king, a man determines the two—what should and should not be done; / and he who performs what should be done is a wise man in this regard.
Whether one be neutral, a friend, or an enemy, because of the gravity of the task, / having considered both place and time, one should proceed by means of the [four] expedients.
Conciliation, sowing dissension, and gift are declared as the expedients; / and the fourth expedient here, force, is the recourse when there is no other recourse.
By him who, desiring victory, has first conquered the five senses, / the conquest of the three worlds, it seems to me, is not far off.
Having achieved the conquest of the five senses, one should resort to the six royal policies, / having correctly understood the strengths and weaknesses of both oneself and the other.

sanskrit_iast:
rājadoṣāḥ parityaktā yena sapta narādhipa ..
siddhiṃ tasya samāyānti yathākālaṃ guṇā nṛpa .. 7 ..
mṛgayāyānamukhyāśca striyaśca puruṣā giraḥ ..
arthasandūṣaṇaṃ caiva daṇḍapāruṣyameva ca .. 8 ..
rājadoṣaiḥ parityaktā rāghavāstatra pārthiva ..
guṇāśrayavibhāgajñā vigrahastairna rocate .. 9 ..
bharatena vayaṃ sāmnā bale mahati tiṣṭhatā ..
prathamaṃ samupākrāntaṃ tadeva tava rocatām .. 1.212.10 ..
bharatasya vayaṃ sāmnā yadi gacchema parvatam ..
hitaṃ tatsyānmahābhāga sakulasya tavā'nagha .. 11 ..
tvayā kṛtvā samucchedaṃ rājñāṃ jananivāsinām ..
akāraṇānmahadvairaṃ kṛtaṃ bhūpatibhiḥ saha .. 12 ..
jane nivāsādasmākaṃ kevalaṃ laghutā bhavet ..
mānuṣaiḥ saṃgamaścaiva vigrahaśca punaḥpunaḥ .. 13 ..
meaning:
राजदोषाः परित्यक्ता येन सप्त नराधिप ..
सिद्धिं तस्य समायान्ति यथाकालं गुणा नृप .. 7 ..
मृगयायानमुख्याश्च स्त्रियश्च पुरुषा गिरः ..
अर्थसन्दूषणं चैव दण्डपारुष्यमेव च .. 8 ..
राजदोषैः परित्यक्ता राघवास्तत्र पार्थिव ..
गुणाश्रयविभागज्ञा विग्रहस्तैर्न रोचते .. 9 ..
भरतेन वयं साम्ना बले महति तिष्ठता ..
प्रथमं समुपाक्रान्तं तदेव तव रोचताम् .. 1.212.10 ..
भरतस्य वयं साम्ना यदि गच्छेम पर्वतम् ..
हितं तत्स्यान्महाभाग सकुलस्य तवाऽनघ .. 11 ..
त्वया कृत्वा समुच्छेदं राज्ञां जननिवासिनाम् ..
अकारणान्महद्वैरं कृतं भूपतिभिः सह .. 12 ..
जने निवासादस्माकं केवलं लघुता भवेत् ..
मानुषैः संगमश्चैव विग्रहश्च पुनःपुनः .. 13 ..
text_mt:
By whom the seven royal vices have been abandoned, O lord of men, / to him accomplishments come in due time, O king.
Hunting, travel [or gambling], women, harsh words, / squandering of wealth, and harshness of punishment—
the descendants of Raghu, O earth-ruler, are free from these royal vices; / knowing the proper classification of the six policies, conflict with them is not advisable.
We were first approached peacefully by Bharata, who possesses a vast army; / let that very [peace] be pleasing to you.
If we were to go to the mountain peacefully with Bharata, / that would be beneficial, O illustrious and sinless one, to you along with your kin.
By bringing about the destruction of the kings who dwell among the people, / you have made great enmity with the rulers of the earth without cause.
From living among humans, only diminishment would be ours, / as well as contact and repeated conflict with mortals.

न कृषिर्न च वाणिज्यं जनोऽस्माकं प्रयोजनम् ..
ते वयं सजनां भूमिं त्यक्त्वा यामः शिलोच्चयम् .. 14 ..

Neither agriculture nor trade among the people is our concern; / let us abandon this inhabited land and go to the mountain.
Considering place and time, peace and war, / and discerning the result, he who acts, O king, is a wise man.
Land, gold, and an ally are the threefold grounds of conflict; / whereas our own possession is Meru, the golden mountain.
Then, O slayer of foes, we have no need for gold; / since we have no agriculture, land is of no use to us.
Therefore, O ruler of men, seek out Bharata as an ally through conciliation; / having made the family of Raghu an ally, our dwelling shall be on the Himācala.
Unseen by divine armies, enjoy happiness for a long time! / You should not consider Bharata as merely human.
For the restraint of the wicked, Janārdana of four forms / was born in the family of Raghu, O king, as the son of Daśaratha.

As a portion of Vāsudeva, the renowned Rāma was born; / and as a portion of Saṃkarṣaṇa, Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of enemy warriors.
Likewise, as a portion of Pradyumna, Bharata, who loves dharma, was born; / and as a portion of Aniruddha, Śatrughna of immense strength.
There, by Rāma, the lion of the Raghus, whose deeds are effortless, / Rāvaṇa, who caused terror to all living beings, was slain in battle.
Meghanāda was cast down in battle by Lakṣmaṇa, / and by Śatrughna, the wicked rākṣasa Lavaṇa was destroyed.
I consider the nature of the great-souled Bharata to be superior, / by whom previously Mālī, that rākṣasa dwelling in Laṅkā, was slain.
This Bharata is Viṣṇu, who is marching to battle against you.
Who constantly abides in the welfare of the gods, his mind resolved upon the destruction of the lords of the Daityas— / make peace swiftly, O illustrious one, with that immeasurable Janārdana!

Śailūṣa said:
How was Sumālī formerly struck down in battle by Viṣṇu? / Dispel this doubt of mine; he is heard of as one of mighty strength.
Nāḍāyana said:
This tale, O tiger among kings, was told long ago by the wise Agastya / to Rāma, O hero; listen to it as I relate it.
Formerly, when Vṛtra was slain, the Daityas, deprived of their leader, / made the ocean their water-fortress and slaughtered the creatures at night.
When all the gods assembled, since their destruction could not be achieved by other means, / Agastya was then urged to drink the ocean waters.
Delighted by the work of the gods, the sage Agastya then, O king, / drank it, O best of kings, and made the reservoir of water dry.
And the Daityas were slain by the gods in that waterless reservoir of water. / Then, once upon a time, the Vindhya mountain addressed the sun and the moon:
"O illustrious ones, leaving Meru aside, circumambulate me!" / Those two then said to the Vindhya: "O mountain, it is not in our power.

Having spoken thus, the Blessed One vanished right there.
Agastya too, of great ascetic power, reached that abode,
he by whom sacrifices were offered with hundreds of rites, and by whom great austerity was performed.
By his own ascetic power was created the sweet-speaking Lopāmudrā,
the daughter of the king of Vidarbha, as his lawful wife.
His son was Dṛḍhasyu, an ascetic of great austerity;
Pramucu, Mumucu, and Tanmucu of great austerity,
and the learned Svastyātreya was the disciple of that great-souled one.
Impenetrable armor was given [by him], as well as two inexhaustible great quivers,
and two exceedingly strong bows to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa;
and he was endowed with fierce Vaiṣṇava splendour.
Even in hundreds of years, a man is not able to recount
the deeds of him who could not tolerate Rāvaṇa’s uncontrolled power.

about the slaying of Mālī by Viṣṇu; hear what was spoken by him to him.

which the great-souled sage, whose splendor was equal to the moon, sun, and fire, told to the delight of the Raghus.
Agastya said:
O king of kings, Mālī, Sumālī, and Mālyavān, fierce in battle,
having reached the fortress of Laṅkā, dwelt [there], conversing wonderfully with one another.
Mālī and Sumālī were of wicked conduct, tormenting the deities,
even though always restrained by that Mālyavān, O king.
Terrified of the two, Brahmā was informed by the gods along with their purpose.
Having gone together with Brahmā, the destroyer of Tripura was informed.
Accompanied by Brahmā and Īśa, the gods, having taken refuge in Viṣṇu,
went to make their petition to Acyuta residing in the salt-water ocean.
And they saw, O best of the Raghus, the ocean of water that was drunk,
as if leaping with the wind through dancing swarms of waves,

Reaching that ocean resembling the firmament, whose quarters were bewildered by a vast garland of restless waves,

Agastya said:
Pleased by the gods through their ascetic penance, Janārdana, the god of gods,
left his abode in the great waters and showed himself to the deities.

And with joy, their knees, hands, and foreheads dusty from falling to the earth,
they bowed to Hari, the slayer of the enemies of the gods,
and praised [him] with hymns, and then declared their purpose:
for the slaying of the sons of Sukeśa, to the god of gods.
Then the divine Hari promised them the slaying of Māli:
“O foremost of gods, you are capable of the destruction of Sumāli.
Mālyavān too is not to be slain, for he is ever devoted to dharma.”
Having spoken thus, Keśava then summoned Tārkṣya.
The Universal Self mounted the golden son of Vinatā;
Madhusūdana, marked with conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
dark as an atasī blossom, seated upon the golden bird,
borne the splendor of a raincloud laden with water, accompanied by lightning.
Wearing a diadem and the Kaustubha, adorned with exquisite ornaments,
mounted upon the foremost of birds, the dwellers of heaven followed him.
Difficult to behold because of his mass of matted locks, Brahmā followed him
on swans with noble wings white as nectar, flying across the wide sky.

text_mt:
Hara went, rending the sky with the blazing light of his third eye,
possessing a hump of compact limbs resembling the rays of the moon.
With a peacock that obstructed [sight] with the display of its plumage resembling the eyes of Mahendra,
the six-faced Skanda then followed him.
Intending to render the lords of the rākṣasas leaderless, Vināyaka,
mounted upon the realm of wind, set out behind Mādhava.
On a lion whose mane was like a mass of blazing clusters of fire,
the goddess Bhadrakālī followed Janārdana.
Seated on the back of Airāvaṇa, whose frontal globes resembled the breasts of a lovely woman,
the diadem-wearing lord of the thirty [gods] followed him with thunderbolt in hand.
Fire followed the god upon a vehicle of parrots, O king,
shining like a grassy plot strewn with swarms of indragopa beetles.
Vaivasvata also, mounting a buffalo that resembled a mountain peak
and had its head adorned with horns, followed Hari.
With peg-like ears and a huge neck, seated upon the shoulder of an excellent elephant,
the mighty Virūpākṣa followed behind the god.

text_mt:
Varuṇa, resembling smooth cat's-eye gem, followed behind
in a splendid, magnificent carriage swift as the mind and the wind.
The god Vāyu, moving as swiftly as thought, standing in the midst of his sphere of wind,
followed behind with his auspicious garments filled with wind.
Dhanada, upon a human-borne chariot brilliant with every jewel,
accompanied Govinda, endowed with supreme splendor.
Mounted upon a single-wheeled chariot with seven horses, the Sun,
difficult to behold with his orb of radiance, likewise followed the god.
And the Moon, with terrifying force and brilliance, followed Hari
with ten foremost horses and with a chariot swift as thought.
Mounted upon an excellent steed, his form resembling the sun,
the fierce son of the Sun then followed him, O king.
Quickly mounting a chariot yoked with four elephants,
the goddess Earth followed the god worshipped by the thirty [gods].
Mounted on a chariot of resolve, preceded by determination,
even Kāmadeva followed Keśava upon the chariot of his desire,

text_mt:
even he of flower-arrows whose command the entire universe obeys;
and mounting diligence, the goddess Sarasvatī [followed].
She followed the lotus-eyed one who is affectionate to those who seek refuge.
Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Rāhu, Ketu, and Saturn,
with chariots yoked with horses, swiftly followed Puruṣottama.
And the gods, the forty-nine Maruts of beautiful circles,
the gods situated in the sphere of the wind, followed Kṛṣṇa.
The Ādityas followed him in chariots of bright gold.
The Vasus, the Aṅgirases, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, and the two Aśvins,
and the Bhṛgus followed that god in chariots joined with horses.
And the Rudras followed the god upon bulls prominent in strength;
likewise other gods fierce in strength, who followed the god,
upon donkeys, porpoises, large camels, buffaloes, serpents,
lions, tigers, hyenas, bears, elephants, monkeys, and baboons,

text_mt:
upon yaks, antelopes, monitor lizards, cats, and porcupines,
and upon various bird-mounts, they followed Janārdana.
Along the path of the perfected ones, the Siddhas and sages also proceeded,
praising the lotus-eyed one who removes the fear of the hosts of gods.
Serving Janārdana with exceedingly sweet songs and instrumental music,
troops of gandharvas and apsarases went thither rejoicing.
Austerity, truth, forbearance, charity, and various vows,
all limbs of the sacrifice, and the divisions of time,
years, months, the two fortnights along with the karaṇas,
ages, solstices, muhūrtas, and various sacred scriptures,
and the embodied divine missiles and weapons of the Lord of the Universe,
and the personified forms of the ocean paths, its islands, and its trees [followed].
