text_mt:
In the northern quarter of the Himālayas, when the two armies stood in the sky, those two men, foremost heroes, / with their bows raised for victory, of undaunted spirit, joined battle.
Agastya said: / Then the battle commenced between those two armies stationed in the sky, / whose arms were upraised with varied striking weapons, wishing for victory.
Then, when the sky was covered with army-clouds, lit by the lightning of swords, / at that very moment the sun became devoid of light, O king.
From that body illuminated by the lightning-flashes of moving sword-blades, / from that cloud-like army, a rain of blood fell upon the earth.
Then, as the surface of the earth was being drenched with the shower of blood, / there was a great shower of stones, by which the ground was covered.
Inundated by floods of blood, the earth became impassable, / resembling a menstruating young woman at that time, O lord of men.
Arms smeared with sandalwood paste were seen quivering, / fallen under sword-blows like five-headed serpents.

text_mt:
Faces filled with teeth and covered in blood / shone like pomegranates bursting open upon ripening.
With falling parasols, chowries, and fans, / and with the severed limbs of mounts, the sky was utterly congested.
With diadems, earrings, necklaces, upper-arm bracelets, and armlets / being cast down, the sky was resplendent with masses of rays.
Severed by crescent-shaped arrows on the blood-soaked earth, / elephants' trunks, resembling the coils of serpents, rolled about.
Not seeing their heads fallen here upon the surface of the earth, / having struck down the lineages, their life-breaths departed into the sky as if in search of them.
With their bodies they reached the surface of the earth, and with their souls they reached heaven; / fixed in the sky, wishing to conquer the three worlds, / the severed heads of the rakshasas, from which drops of blood dripped, / fell down from above, their entrails having been carried off by falcons.

text_mt:
Beholding the head of the lord of night-wanderers, adorned with earrings and a beautiful crest, / struck down upon the earth, the wives of the foremost gods became filled with joy.
Agastya said: / When Mālī was slain, that king of birds, consoled by the Lord, / turned back and swept away the army of the rakshasas with the wind of his wings.
Like a heap of dry leaves driven by the wind of Tārkṣya's wings, / those tigers among rakshasas then fled in all ten directions, O Rāma.
Finding no peace, afflicted by fear of Vāsudeva, / they all went separately to the lower regions of Pātāla.
Having consoled the thirty gods, Viṣṇu, worshipped by the thirty gods, / vanished right there while all of them were watching.
Even Laṅkā became deserted, O best of kings, and was given to Vaiśravaṇa; / having belonged to Viśravas himself, it was taken by force by Rāvaṇa.
Having slain Rāvaṇa, it was given to Vibhīṣaṇa by you. / O Rāma, you are Viṣṇu born here for the destruction of the rakshasas.

text_mt:
Indeed, by you alone were slain in battle those who were a danger through their maternal uncles; / those who were the Paulastya rakshasas have been slain by you as acknowledged.
There is no slayer of the rakshasas other than Keśava, O Rāma. / "I have seen and spoken [with you]," saying this, he departed as he had come.
Nāḍāyana said: / Having spoken thus, Agastya then departed as he had come, O subduer of foes. / Therefore, O king, battle today does not please me for you.
Rāghava is endowed with the power of energy and the power of counsel; / he is likewise possessed of the power of majesty and of divine power.
What wise man would wage war over matters that can be accomplished through conciliation, / resorting solely to anger—a war that brings ruin to a king?
He by whom desire and anger are conquered, by him the self is conquered; / he by whom the self is conquered, by him this earth is conquered.
For a king whose mind is unconquered, whence can come victory over enemy forces? / One whose senses are unconquered cannot achieve the conquest of anyone.

text_mt:
Contempt must not be shown to anyone, whether weak or highly esteemed; / for in this world, stronger persons are always seen than the strong.
Men of wise intellect desire to act according to their ability and act according to their ability; / they hold no one in contempt.
These two are sharp thorns that dry up the body: / he who, being penniless, desires, and he who, being powerless, becomes angry.
These two men in this world stand above heaven: / a master endowed with forbearance, and a poor man who is generous.
Who would direct anger toward a weak person who is subdued by his very nature? / And toward a strong person, what man would direct anger that destroys his own life?
Anger toward one engaged in seizing [what is right] is called spiritedness; / therefore, anger has been subdued by the wise by becoming angry at anger.
Threefold is this gate of hell that brings ruin to the self: / desire, anger, and greed; therefore, one should abandon these three.

Considering the consequence and the fruition of deeds, / as well as one's own enterprise, one should then undertake action.
One should not behave [carelessly] merely thinking that kingship has been acquired; / for lack of discipline destroys fortune, just as old age destroys excellent beauty.
Leaving your dwelling among the inhabited lands, go, O king, to the Himālayas. / Having slain Rāvaṇa, the most unbearable one who made the worlds weep, / see the lord of wealth, who abandoned Laṅkā and took refuge on Kailāsa.
That Rāvaṇa, afflicted by the arrows of Rāghava, abandoned his royal fortune and perished, O lord of the earth; / while the lord of wealth, whose fame is vast, even today rules over the night-wanderers.
1.219
Śailūṣa said:
How was Laṅkā given of old to Vaiśravaṇa, O best of the twice-born? / And how was it wrested from him by the high-souled Rāvaṇa?
I wish to hear truly the life of Rāvaṇa, / by whom the three worlds were conquered through his ascetic power and manly strength.

text_mt:
Nāḍāyana said:
Pulastya is known as the mind-born son of Brahmā; / his son was Viśravas, renowned throughout the three worlds.
Bṛhaspati's granddaughter and Bharadvāja's auspicious daughter / became his wife, O ruler of kings, named indeed Devavarṇinī.
Upon her he fathered a lordly son, Vaiśravaṇa. / Propitiated by his excellent austerities, the Grandfather granted him
the lordship over the Yakṣas, the lordship over wealth, and guardianship of the world, / as well as the Puṣpaka aerial car, which moves at will and changes its shape at will.
To his son who had obtained the boons, O king, Viśravas spoke: / 'Constructed by Viśvakarman on Trikūṭa, the foremost of mountains,
was the delightful city named Laṅkā, built of old for the sake of the king of the gods. / Having stolen it of old from the king of the gods, the sons of Sukeśa
caused distress [to the gods], O great king; but after Vāsudeva / struck down Mālin, the eldest among them, they were put to flight from there.
Having taken refuge in the netherworld, they live here free from fear. 1.219.10

Let your mind be set on dharma in every condition at all times. / From dharma arise wealth and pleasure; this world is rooted in dharma.'
Hearing his father's words, the lord of wealth, whose courage was undaunted, reached Laṅkā, / and delighting the world with dharma, he ruled over the night-wanderers.
1.220
Nāḍāyana said:
At that very time, Sumālī roamed the surface of the earth, / taking with him his daughter, Kaikasī by name.
As he wandered over the thriving earth, he saw the ruler of men / mounted on the Puṣpaka car, endowed with supreme splendour.
Seeing him, the night-wanderer spoke these words to Kaikasī: / 'Daughter, the time has come to give you away, yet no one chooses you from me.
Nor do I offer you unasked, for fear of rejection and insult, / for your sake, O large-eyed girl of excellent complexion.

Painful indeed is fatherhood of a daughter for men who desire honour; / fatherhood of a daughter is certainly a humiliation even for Śakra.
The mother's family, the father's family, and that to which the maiden is given— / a maiden stands here placing all three families in jeopardy.
Therefore I shall not give you away; go yourself, O auspicious one, / and swiftly choose as your husband the sage, the powerful Viśravas.
Since this lord of wealth is endowed with supreme splendour, / you will bear from him a son of such a kind, O beautiful lady.'
Kaikasī then went, O king, to the sage Viśravas / at a dreadful hour, when twilight had arrived, O best of kings.
Having paid homage to the feet of that sage Viśravas, / the slender woman stood before him, as if ashamed with modesty. 1.220.10
The sage spoke to that Kaikasī, who was bowed low and had a charming smile: / 'Your intention has been understood by me today, O fair-complexioned one.

You have come to my presence for the sake of a son, O blameless lady; / as you have approached at a dreadful time, such a son shall you bring forth.'
Told 'So be it,' she then dwelt there happily. / Then, in time, that beautiful woman gave birth to a son:
ten-faced, twenty-armed, with a single body, exceedingly strong. / His wise father gave him the name Daśagrīva.
Then she brought forth a second son, possessing a massive body; / his father gave him the name Kumbhakarṇa at that time.
Then she also gave birth to a daughter, Śūrpaṇakhā. / Thereafter, at one time, Kaikasī said to her eldest son,
pointing out the lord of wealth, as if with bashfulness, O scorcher of foes: / 'Behold the splendour of your elder brother, O ten-faced one.
Therefore, exert yourself and become equal to Vaiśravaṇa.' / Thus addressed, he departed for Gokarṇa along with his brothers.
Subsisting on fallen leaves, he performed very severe asceticism there. / When a thousand years were completed, the ten-faced one, cutting off a head,

sacrificed them one by one into the fire, emaciated by austerities, O highly fortunate one. / Kumbhakarṇa also practised austerities, exposing himself to the five fires in summer, sleeping in the open in the rains,
and wearing wet clothes in winter. / Then Vibhīṣaṇa ate fruit only at every sixth mealtime.
Their sister Śūrpaṇakhā attended upon them then. / Then, at the end of ten thousand years, when the ten-faced one
wished to sacrifice his tenth head into the fire, O lord, / Brahmā, arriving at that place, spoke these words:

Nāḍāyana said:
The rākṣasa enumerated all beings beginning with the gods, / completely without exception, leaving out only human beings.
Having named them, he asked for invulnerability against them, O ruler of the earth, / and dominion over the three worlds; and the Lord granted that to him.

Then, having gratified the night-roamer Daśagrīva with a boon, / [and] having placed Sarasvatī in the mouth of the rakshasa Kumbhakarṇa,
he came and gratified Vibhīṣaṇa with a boon. / He chose an eternal mind ever set on dharma.
Pleased with that, the Lord then gave him immortality. / Having gratified them with boons, Brahmā went to his own abode.
Knowing that Daśagrīva had obtained a boon, the hosts of rakshasas then / emerged from Pātāla and consecrated him in the great sovereignty.
Having obtained the kingdom, he then sent the rakshasas, / [and] then an envoy named Prahasta to Kubera:
‘This Laṅkā was constructed in the past as the dwelling of the rakshasas. / Relinquish it through peaceful conciliation alone to me, O superintendent of wealth, without delay!’

sanskrit_iast:
rāghaveṇa mahārāja rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā ..
laṅkāṃ tyaktvā dhanādhyakṣaḥ kailāse parvatottame .. 38 ..
meaning:
राघवेण महाराज रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ..
लङ्कां त्यक्त्वा धनाध्यक्षः कैलासे पर्वतोत्तमे .. 38 ..
text_mt: by the descendant of Raghu, Rāma of untiring deeds, O great king. / Having abandoned Laṅkā, the superintendent of wealth, on Kailāsa, the foremost of mountains,

sanskrit_iast:
adyāpi pālayannāste rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam..
tasmāttvamapi rājendra tyaktvā deśamimaṃ svayam..
himavantamathāsādya vasa vaiśravaṇopamaḥ ..39..
meaning:
अद्यापि पालयन्नास्ते राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्..
तस्मात्त्वमपि राजेन्द्र त्यक्त्वा देशमिमं स्वयम्..
हिमवन्तमथासाद्य वस वैश्रवणोपमः ..39..
text_mt: dwells even today protecting his kingdom, its thorns removed. / Therefore, O king of kings, you too should personally abandon this region, / and reaching the Himavat, dwell like Vaiśravaṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmānna kāryaṃ bharatena vairaṃ mahābalāstrā raghavaḥ pratītāḥ..
prasīda jīvantu saputrapautrāḥ putrāstaveme tuhinādrisaṃsthāḥ ..1.220.40..
meaning:
तस्मान्न कार्यं भरतेन वैरं महाबलास्त्रा रघवः प्रतीताः..
प्रसीद जीवन्तु सपुत्रपौत्राः पुत्रास्तवेमे तुहिनाद्रिसंस्थाः ..1.220.40..
text_mt: Therefore enmity should not be made with Bharata; the descendants of Raghu are famed for weapons of great might. / Be gracious! Let these sons of yours, dwelling on the snow-mountain, live with their sons and grandsons!’

sanskrit_iast:
śailūṣa uvāca ..
śrotumicchāmyahaṃ tasya daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ ..
trilokavijayaṃ brahmaṃstatra me saṃśayo mahān .. 1 ..
meaning:
शैलूष उवाच ..
श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं तस्य दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः ..
त्रिलोकविजयं ब्रह्मंस्तत्र मे संशयो महान् .. 1 ..
text_mt: Śailūṣa said: / ‘I wish to hear of the conquest of the three worlds by that rakshasa Daśagrīva, / O holy one; regarding that, I have a great doubt.’
title: Bhūrlokavijayam

sanskrit_iast:
nāḍāyana uvāca ..
varapradānātsaṃmatto daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ ..
devagandharvadaityānāṃ nāgendroragarakṣamām..2..
meaning:
नाडायन उवाच ..
वरप्रदानात्संमत्तो दशग्रीवो निशाचरः ..
देवगन्धर्वदैत्यानां नागेन्द्रोरगरक्षमाम्..2..
text_mt: Nāḍāyana said: / ‘Maddened by the grant of boons, the night-roamer Daśagrīva / [attacked] the gods, gandharvas, daityas, lords of nāgas, uragas, and rakshasas.

sanskrit_iast:
ākramyā'kramya ratnāni sa jahāra tadā balāt ..
patnyaśca rājaśārdūla tadā duhitaraḥ śubhāḥ.. 3 ..
meaning:
आक्रम्याऽक्रम्य रत्नानि स जहार तदा बलात् ..
पत्न्यश्च राजशार्दूल तदा दुहितरः शुभाः.. 3 ..
text_mt: Attacking again and again, he then seized their jewels by force, / and their wives, O tiger among kings, and their lovely daughters.

sanskrit_iast:
narendrāndharmasaṃsaktānbrāhmaṇāṃśca jighāṃsati ..
ayodhyāvāsinaṃ vīramanaraṇyaṃ ca jaghnivān .. 4 ..
meaning:
नरेन्द्रान्धर्मसंसक्तान्ब्राह्मणांश्च जिघांसति ..
अयोध्यावासिनं वीरमनरण्यं च जघ्निवान् .. 4 ..
text_mt: He sought to kill kings devoted to dharma, and brahmins; / and he slew the heroic Anaraṇya, who dwelt in Ayodhyā.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃgrāme nihatastena daśagrīvaṃ sa śaptavān ..
utpatsyati kule nīca puruṣo mama vīryavān .. 5 ..
meaning:
संग्रामे निहतस्तेन दशग्रीवं स शप्तवान् ..
उत्पत्स्यति कुले नीच पुरुषो मम वीर्यवान् .. 5 ..
text_mt: Slain by him in battle, he cursed Daśagrīva: / ‘A mighty man will be born in my lineage, O vile one,

sanskrit_iast:
yastavādāsyati prāṇānsamare samarapriya ..
yuyudhe ca tathā rājñā māṃdhātrā raṇaśālinā .. 6 ..
meaning:
यस्तवादास्यति प्राणान्समरे समरप्रिय ..
युयुधे च तथा राज्ञा मांधात्रा रणशालिना .. 6 ..
text_mt: who will take your life in battle, O you who delight in war!’ / And he likewise fought with King Māndhātṛ, who was distinguished in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
tatrainaṃ vārayāmāsa nārado munisattamaḥ ..
mayūrasya tato yajñe bhakṣayāmāsa vai dvijān .. 7 ..
meaning:
तत्रैनं वारयामास नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ..
मयूरस्य ततो यज्ञे भक्षयामास वै द्विजान् .. 7 ..
text_mt: There Nārada, the best of sages, checked him. / Then, at the sacrifice of Marutta, he devoured the twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
indro mayūrarūpeṇa tasmādyajñādapākramat ..
mayūrasya varaṃ prādānmeghe varṣati sarvadā .. 8 ..
meaning:
इन्द्रो मयूररूपेण तस्माद्यज्ञादपाक्रमत् ..
मयूरस्य वरं प्रादान्मेघे वर्षति सर्वदा .. 8 ..
text_mt: Indra slipped away from that sacrifice in the form of a peacock; / he granted a boon to the peacock: ‘Whenever a cloud rains,

sanskrit_iast:
gamiṣyasyatulāṃ prītiṃ mama netragaṇākṛtim ..
dhārayiṣyasi loke'sminkalāpaṃ sumanoharam .. 9 ..
meaning:
गमिष्यस्यतुलां प्रीतिं मम नेत्रगणाकृतिम् ..
धारयिष्यसि लोकेऽस्मिन्कलापं सुमनोहरम् .. 9 ..
text_mt: you will experience peerless joy; / you will bear in this world a very captivating tail-plumage in the likeness of my multitude of eyes.’

sanskrit_iast:
kṛkalāsasya rūpeṇa dhanādhyakṣo vyapākramat ..
varṇaṃ tasya suvarṇābhaṃ sadravyaṃ ca tathā śiraḥ .. 1.221.10 ..
meaning:
कृकलासस्य रूपेण धनाध्यक्षो व्यपाक्रमत् ..
वर्णं तस्य सुवर्णाभं सद्रव्यं च तथा शिरः .. 1.221.10 ..
text_mt: The superintendent of wealth slipped away in the form of a chameleon; / he granted him a colour like gold and a head endowed with treasure;

sanskrit_iast:
prādāddvayamameyātmā rājarājena dānava ..
varuṇaśca tadā rājanhaṃsarūpeṇa nirgataḥ .. 11 ..
meaning:
प्रादाद्द्वयममेयात्मा राजराजेन दानव ..
वरुणश्च तदा राजन्हंसरूपेण निर्गतः .. 11 ..
text_mt: the king of kings of immeasurable soul granted both, O Danu's son. / And Varuṇa, O king, then departed in the form of a swan.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsasya ca varaṃ prādāttoye ratimavāpsyasi ..
varṇataścandraraśmyābho bhaviṣyasi tathaiva ca .. 12 ..
meaning:
हंसस्य च वरं प्रादात्तोये रतिमवाप्स्यसि ..
वर्णतश्चन्द्ररश्म्याभो भविष्यसि तथैव च .. 12 ..
text_mt: And he granted a boon to the swan: ‘You will find pleasure in the water, / and likewise your colour will resemble the rays of the moon.’

sanskrit_iast:
yamo vāyasarūpeṇa tasyādyajñādapākamat ..
vāyasasya varaṃ prādādamaratvaṃ vinā vadhāt.. 13..
meaning:
यमो वायसरूपेण तस्याद्यज्ञादपाकमत् ..
वायसस्य वरं प्रादादमरत्वं विना वधात्.. 13..
text_mt: Yama slipped away from that sacrifice in the form of a crow; / he granted a boon to the crow: ‘Immortality except by slaughter.

sanskrit_iast:
yuṣmaddattena cānnena ghorā madviṣaye sthitāḥ ..
parāṃ tṛptiṃ gamiṣyanti tadā puṇyena yokṣyase .. 14 ..
meaning:
युष्मद्दत्तेन चान्नेन घोरा मद्विषये स्थिताः ..
परां तृप्तिं गमिष्यन्ति तदा पुण्येन योक्ष्यसे .. 14 ..
text_mt: And by means of the food offered by you, the terrifying [spirits] stationed in my realm / will attain supreme satisfaction, and you will then be endowed with merit.

sanskrit_iast:
vakṣyadhvaṃ balidātṝṇāṃ digdeśagataceṣṭitaiḥ ..
śubhāśubhaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tatrātithyaṃ bhaviṣyati ..15..
meaning:
वक्ष्यध्वं बलिदातॄणां दिग्देशगतचेष्टितैः ..
शुभाशुभं मनुष्याणां तत्रातिथ्यं भविष्यति ..15..
text_mt: You will foretell the good and bad fortune of men who offer oblations, / by your movements directed to the quarters and regions; hospitality will be shown to you there.

sanskrit_iast:
vajratuṇḍāśca ye kākā ghorā madviṣaye sthitāḥ ..
balipiṇḍām̐śca dātṝṇāṃ bhaviṣyanti tataḥ śivam .. 16 ..
meaning:
वज्रतुण्डाश्च ये काका घोरा मद्विषये स्थिताः ..
बलिपिण्डाम्̐श्च दातॄणां भविष्यन्ति ततः शिवम् .. 16 ..
text_mt: And the terrifying crows with diamond beaks that abide in my realm / will [partake of] the oblation-balls of the givers, and good fortune will follow from that.’

sanskrit_iast:
maruttayajñe vitrāsaṃ janayitvā divaukasām ..
babhrāma vasudhāṃ rājā rākṣasānāṃ pratāpavān .. 17 ..
meaning:
मरुत्तयज्ञे वित्रासं जनयित्वा दिवौकसाम् ..
बभ्राम वसुधां राजा राक्षसानां प्रतापवान् .. 17 ..
text_mt: Having produced terror among the celestials at the sacrifice of Marutta, / the powerful king of the rakshasas roamed over the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
dadarśa sa tadā kanyāṃ tapasyantīṃ mahattapaḥ ..
rūpeṇāpratimāṃ loke yauvane prathame sthitām..18..
meaning:
ददर्श स तदा कन्यां तपस्यन्तीं महत्तपः ..
रूपेणाप्रतिमां लोके यौवने प्रथमे स्थिताम्..18..
text_mt: He then saw a maiden performing severe asceticism, / peerless in beauty in the world, in the first flush of youth.

sanskrit_iast:
daśagrīvaḥ sa papraccha tāṃ kanyāṃ lokasundarīm..
kā tvaṃ kimarthaṃ suśroṇi cāsthitā yauvane tapaḥ..19 ..
meaning:
दशग्रीवः स पप्रच्छ तां कन्यां लोकसुन्दरीम्..
का त्वं किमर्थं सुश्रोणि चास्थिता यौवने तपः..19 ..
text_mt: Daśagrīva questioned that maiden of worldly beauty: / ‘Who are you, and why, O fair-hipped one, have you undertaken asceticism in youth?’

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvā tasya tu sā kanyā satyaṃ vacanamabravīt ..
bṛhaspatisuto vidvānpitā mama kuśadhvajaḥ ..1.221.20..
meaning:
श्रुत्वा तस्य तु सा कन्या सत्यं वचनमब्रवीत् ..
बृहस्पतिसुतो विद्वान्पिता मम कुशध्वजः ..1.221.20..
text_mt: Hearing him, that maiden spoke true words: / ‘The wise Kuśadhvaja, son of Bṛhaspati, is my father.

sanskrit_iast:
vedābhyāsapravṛttasya tasyāhaṃ nṛpabāndhavā..
sutāparā samutpannā tatpatnyā viditā tathā .. 21 ..
meaning:
वेदाभ्यासप्रवृत्तस्य तस्याहं नृपबान्धवा..
सुतापरा समुत्पन्ना तत्पत्न्या विदिता तथा .. 21 ..
text_mt: Of him engaged in the study of the Vedas, O kin of kings, / I was born as another daughter, likewise acknowledged by his wife,

sanskrit_iast:
nāmnā vedavatītyevaṃ khyātā lokeṣu rākṣasa ..
viṣṇormayeyaṃ dātavyā tasyāsīnme piturmatiḥ .. 22 ..
meaning:
नाम्ना वेदवतीत्येवं ख्याता लोकेषु राक्षस ..
विष्णोर्मयेयं दातव्या तस्यासीन्मे पितुर्मतिः .. 22 ..
text_mt: known by the name Vedavatī in the worlds, O rakshasa. / “She should be given by me to Viṣṇu”—such was my father’s intention.

sanskrit_iast:
madyācanā nirastena daityanāthena śambhunā ..
pitā mama hato rātrau tamāliṅgya vibhāvasum .. 23 ..
meaning:
मद्याचना निरस्तेन दैत्यनाथेन शम्भुना ..
पिता मम हतो रात्रौ तमालिङ्ग्य विभावसुम् .. 23 ..
text_mt: Rebuffed in his suit for me, the daitya king Śambhu / killed my father at night; embracing the sacrificial fire,

sanskrit_iast:
praviṣṭā janayitrī me yathāhaṃ vidhṛtā ciram ..
svargasthasya pituḥ kāmaṃ sāhaṃ satyamabhīpsatī .. 24 ..
meaning:
प्रविष्टा जनयित्री मे यथाहं विधृता चिरम् ..
स्वर्गस्थस्य पितुः कामं साहं सत्यमभीप्सती .. 24 ..
text_mt: my mother entered [the flames] as I was held back for a long time. / Wishing to fulfill the true desire of my father residing in heaven,

sanskrit_iast:
ārādhayāmi tapasā patyarthaṃ madhusūdanam ..
tatastāmabravīdrakṣo mā tvaṃ kleśe matiṃ kṛthāḥ ..25 ..
meaning:
आराधयामि तपसा पत्यर्थं मधुसूदनम् ..
ततस्तामब्रवीद्रक्षो मा त्वं क्लेशे मतिं कृथाः ..25 ..
text_mt: I worship Madhusūdana with asceticism to have him as my husband.’ / Then the rakshasa said to her: ‘Do not set your mind on distress!

sanskrit_iast:
bhavasva me varārohe bhāryā trailokyasundarī ..
rūpasya vayasaścaiva nānurūpaṃ tapastava .. 26 ..
meaning:
भवस्व मे वरारोहे भार्या त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी ..
रूपस्य वयसश्चैव नानुरूपं तपस्तव .. 26 ..
text_mt: Become my wife, O woman of lovely hips, beauty of the three worlds! / Your asceticism is not suited to your beauty and youth.

sanskrit_iast:
tvāṃ kṛtvoparato manye rūpaṃ kṛtvā sa viśvakṛt ..
na hi rūpopamā tvanyā tathāsti sadṛśī yataḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
त्वां कृत्वोपरतो मन्ये रूपं कृत्वा स विश्वकृत् ..
न हि रूपोपमा त्वन्या तथास्ति सदृशी यतः .. 27 ..
text_mt: I think that the creator of all, having made your form, has ceased; / for there is no other counterpart equal to your beauty.’

sanskrit_iast:
saṃpūrṇakāntimatsaumyaṃ vadanaṃ te varānane ..
sakalaṃkena candreṇa kathamopamyamarhati .. ..28..
meaning:
संपूर्णकान्तिमत्सौम्यं वदनं ते वरानने ..
सकलंकेन चन्द्रेण कथमोपम्यमर्हति .. ..28..
text_mt: Your gentle face possessed of full radiance, O fair-faced woman, / how does it deserve comparison with the moon, which bears a blemish?

sanskrit_iast:
bhava bhūṣaṇajātānāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ tvaṃ śucismite ..
vṛṇuṣva māṃ varārohe patitve varavarṇini .. 29..
meaning:
भव भूषणजातानां भूषणं त्वं शुचिस्मिते ..
वृणुष्व मां वरारोहे पतित्वे वरवर्णिनि .. 29..
text_mt: Be the ornament of all kinds of ornaments, O woman of pure smiles! / Choose me, O woman of lovely hips, as your husband, O fair-complexioned one!

sanskrit_iast:
ākramyākramya lokasya pradhānā yā mayā hṛtāḥ..
striyaḥ kuruṣva sarvāsāṃ tāsāṃ svāmyamanindite ..1.221.30..
meaning:
आक्रम्याक्रम्य लोकस्य प्रधाना या मया हृताः..
स्त्रियः कुरुष्व सर्वासां तासां स्वाम्यमनिन्दिते ..1.221.30..
text_mt: The foremost women of the world whom I have abducted after repeatedly attacking, / exercise lordship over all of them, O blameless one!

sanskrit_iast:
jaṭāmālājinadharī tvamevaṃ rativardhinī ..
na jāne maṇḍanāṃ prāpya kathaṃ bhīru bhavi ṣyasi .. 31 ..
meaning:
जटामालाजिनधरी त्वमेवं रतिवर्धिनी ..
न जाने मण्डनां प्राप्य कथं भीरु भवि ष्यसि .. 31 ..
text_mt: Wearing a garland of matted locks and an antelope skin, you increase [my] longing in this way; / I do not know, O timid one, how you will be once you have attained adornments.

sanskrit_iast:
rūpeṇa vayasā lakṣmyā tathaiva guṇasampadā ..
vikrame me varārohe na samo hi janārdanaḥ .. 32 ..
meaning:
रूपेण वयसा लक्ष्म्या तथैव गुणसम्पदा ..
विक्रमे मे वरारोहे न समो हि जनार्दनः .. 32 ..
text_mt: In beauty, in youth, in fortune, and likewise in wealth of virtues, / indeed Janārdana is not my equal in valour, O woman of lovely hips.

sanskrit_iast:
janma tasya na jānanti parebhyo ye pare janāḥ ..
tena tvamakulīnena kiṅkariṣyasi sundari .. 33 ..
meaning:
जन्म तस्य न जानन्ति परेभ्यो ये परे जनाः ..
तेन त्वमकुलीनेन किङ्करिष्यसि सुन्दरि .. 33 ..
text_mt: People whose origins are higher than the highest do not know his birth; / with him who has no noble lineage, what will you do, O beautiful woman?

sanskrit_iast:
anindraṃ lokamicchantī surāṇāṃ hitakāmyayā ..
hatā yenānuvṛttena yoṣitkāvyā raṇiḥ purā .. 34 ..
meaning:
अनिन्द्रं लोकमिच्छन्ती सुराणां हितकाम्यया ..
हता येनानुवृत्तेन योषित्काव्या रणिः पुरा .. 34 ..
text_mt: By him, wishing for the welfare of the gods, longing for a world without Indra, / the woman Kāvī was formerly killed in battle through [mere] conformity [to duty].

sanskrit_iast:
purāṇā ye jagatyasmim̐stebhyaḥ pūrvatarāśca ye ..
tebhyo'pyati purāṇaṃ taṃ bhartāraṃ kathamicchasi .. 35 ..
meaning:
पुराणा ये जगत्यस्मिम्̐स्तेभ्यः पूर्वतराश्च ये ..
तेभ्योऽप्यति पुराणं तं भर्तारं कथमिच्छसि .. 35 ..
text_mt: Those who are ancient in this world, and those who are even earlier than they— / how do you desire as a husband him who is exceedingly ancient even compared to them?

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaṇo varadānena yastvavadhyo divaukasām ..
te daityanāthāḥ sabalāśchadmanā tena ghātitāḥ .. 36 ..
meaning:
ब्रह्मणो वरदानेन यस्त्ववध्यो दिवौकसाम् ..
ते दैत्यनाथाः सबलाश्छद्मना तेन घातिताः .. 36 ..
text_mt: By him, through deceit, were slain those lords of Daityas together with their armies, / who were invulnerable to the sky-dwellers by the boon of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
tatpratāpa?niviṣṭena cetasā rakṣasāṃ śriyam ..
yo bibhartyapi tāṃ tena kiṃ kariṣyati bhāmini .. 37 ..
meaning:
तत्प्रताप?निविष्टेन चेतसा रक्षसां श्रियम् ..
यो बिभर्त्यपि तां तेन किं करिष्यति भामिनि .. 37 ..
text_mt: He who maintains the fortune of the Rākṣasas with a mind focused on its splendour— / what will he do with that [fortune], O passionate woman?

sanskrit_iast:
vṛddhebhyo na śrutaṃ tasya tvayā rūpamanindite ..
viditaṃ sarvalokānāṃ viśvarūpadharastvasau .. 38 ..
meaning:
वृद्धेभ्यो न श्रुतं तस्य त्वया रूपमनिन्दिते ..
विदितं सर्वलोकानां विश्वरूपधरस्त्वसौ .. 38 ..
text_mt: Have you not heard from the elders of his form, O blameless one? / It is known to all the worlds; indeed, he bears a universal form.

sanskrit_iast:
śeṣāhibhogaparyaṅke tena tvaṃ śayitā saha ..
saviṣairbhoganiśvāsaiḥ parāṃ glānimupaiṣyasi .. 31...
meaning:
शेषाहिभोगपर्यङ्के तेन त्वं शयिता सह ..
सविषैर्भोगनिश्वासैः परां ग्लानिमुपैष्यसि .. 31...
text_mt: Sleeping with him upon the couch of the coils of the serpent Śeṣa, / you will come to extreme exhaustion through the venomous exhalations of the coils.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṇṭhagraheṇa nihatau yena tau madhukaiṭabhau ..
kathaṃ kaṇṭhagrahaṃ tasya samupaiṣyasi sundari .. 1.221.40 ..
meaning:
कण्ठग्रहेण निहतौ येन तौ मधुकैटभौ ..
कथं कण्ठग्रहं तस्य समुपैष्यसि सुन्दरि .. 1.221.40 ..
text_mt: By him those two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, were slain by seizing their throats; / how will you approach his embrace of your throat, O beautiful woman?

sanskrit_iast:
hiraṇyakaśipuryena nakhairutkāntajīvitaḥ ..
kathaṃ ratyantare tasya nakhāghātaṃ sahiṣyasi .. 41 ..
meaning:
हिरण्यकशिपुर्येन नखैरुत्कान्तजीवितः ..
कथं रत्यन्तरे तस्य नखाघातं सहिष्यसि .. 41 ..
text_mt: By whom Hiraṇyakaśipu was deprived of life with claws; / how will you endure his claw-wounds in the midst of lovemaking?

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādbhāvaṃ samutsṛjya cārugātri janārdane ..
bhajasva bhajamānaṃ māṃ ciraṃ prītimavāpnuhi .. 42 .. ..
meaning:
तस्माद्भावं समुत्सृज्य चारुगात्रि जनार्दने ..
भजस्व भजमानं मां चिरं प्रीतिमवाप्नुहि .. 42 .. ..
text_mt: Therefore, abandoning [your] affection for Janārdana, O woman of lovely limbs, / devote yourself to me who am devoted to you, and obtain delight for a long time!

sanskrit_iast:
vedavatyuvāca ..
guṇā eva sureśasya doṣāste rajanīcara ..
jagatprakāśakā bhānorulūkasyeva raśmayaḥ .. 43 ..
meaning:
वेदवत्युवाच ..
गुणा एव सुरेशस्य दोषास्ते रजनीचर ..
जगत्प्रकाशका भानोरुलूकस्येव रश्मयः .. 43 ..
text_mt: Vedavatī said: / The very virtues of the lord of the gods appear as faults to you, O night-wanderer, / just as the rays of the sun, which illuminate the world, [are dark] to an owl.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ tvayā saha vādena varaṇīyaḥ sa me prabhuḥ ..
yādṛśastādṛśo vāpi patitve rajanīcara .. 44 ..
meaning:
किं त्वया सह वादेन वरणीयः स मे प्रभुः ..
यादृशस्तादृशो वापि पतित्वे रजनीचर .. 44 ..
text_mt: What is the use of disputing with you? He is my lord to be chosen, / of whatever nature he may be, as my husband, O night-wanderer.

sanskrit_iast:
iti vedavatīvākyaṃ śrutvā kopasamanvitaḥ ..
kāmena rākṣasendrantāṃ keśapāśe parāmṛśata .. 45 ..
meaning:
इति वेदवतीवाक्यं श्रुत्वा कोपसमन्वितः ..
कामेन राक्षसेन्द्रन्तां केशपाशे परामृशत .. 45 ..
text_mt: Having heard this speech of Vedavatī, filled with rage / and overcome by desire, the lord of the Rākṣasas touched her braid of hair.

sanskrit_iast:
tvayā saṃdharṣitā pāpa pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam ..
ayonijā bhaviṣyāmi vadhārthaṃ na tathā tava .. 45 ..
meaning:
त्वया संधर्षिता पाप प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम् ..
अयोनिजा भविष्यामि वधार्थं न तथा तव .. 45 ..
text_mt: "Assaulted by you, O wicked one, I shall enter the sacrificial fire; / I shall be born without a womb for your destruction, not otherwise."

sanskrit_iast:
evamuktvā citāṃ kṛtvā praviṣṭā jātavedasam..
bhūya sītā samutpannā janakasya mahātmanaḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
एवमुक्त्वा चितां कृत्वा प्रविष्टा जातवेदसम्..
भूय सीता समुत्पन्ना जनकस्य महात्मनः .. 47 ..
text_mt: Having spoken thus and constructed a funeral pyre, she entered the fire; / she was born again as Sītā, [daughter] of the great-souled Janaka,

sanskrit_iast:
ayonijā mahābhāgā karṣato yajñamedinīm ..
bhartāraṃ tapasā viṣṇuṃ rāmaṃ labdhavatī yathā .. 48 ..
meaning:
अयोनिजा महाभागा कर्षतो यज्ञमेदिनीम् ..
भर्तारं तपसा विष्णुं रामं लब्धवती यथा .. 48 ..
text_mt: not born from a womb, highly fortunate, as he was ploughing the sacrificial ground; / as one who attained Viṣṇu, Rāma, as her husband by means of austerity,

sanskrit_iast:
yasyā arthe sa rāmeṇa daśagrīvo hato raṇe ..
lokāpavādabhītena daśagrīvagṛhoṣitā .. 49 ..
meaning:
यस्या अर्थे स रामेण दशग्रीवो हतो रणे ..
लोकापवादभीतेन दशग्रीवगृहोषिता .. 49 ..
text_mt: for whose sake the ten-necked [Rāvaṇa] was slain in battle by Rāma. / Because she had dwelt in the house of the ten-necked one, frightened of public slander,

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ patnī parityaktā sītā bhūyo janeśvara ..
vālmīkerāśrame sā tu prasūtā dārakadvayam .. 1.221.50 ..
meaning:
अतः पत्नी परित्यक्ता सीता भूयो जनेश्वर ..
वाल्मीकेराश्रमे सा तु प्रसूता दारकद्वयम् .. 1.221.50 ..
text_mt: his wife Sītā was subsequently abandoned, O lord of men. / But in the hermitage of Vālmīki she gave birth to a pair of sons,

sanskrit_iast:
kuśaṃ lavaṃ ca vikrāntau yayoḥ sarvāḥ kriyāḥ kṛtāḥ ..
vālmīkinā mahābhāgau vedamadhyāpitā yathā .. 51 ..
meaning:
कुशं लवं च विक्रान्तौ ययोः सर्वाः क्रियाः कृताः ..
वाल्मीकिना महाभागौ वेदमध्यापिता यथा .. 51 ..
text_mt: Kuśa and Lava, both valiant, for whom all sacraments were performed / by Vālmīki, both highly fortunate, and whom he taught the Veda.

sanskrit_iast:
prakarṣaṃ ca dhanurvede pāraṃ nītā tu tau śiśū ..
vālmīkinā tathā kṛtvā rāmasya caritaṃ śubhama .. 52 ..
meaning:
प्रकर्षं च धनुर्वेदे पारं नीता तु तौ शिशू ..
वाल्मीकिना तथा कृत्वा रामस्य चरितं शुभम .. 52 ..
text_mt: Both children were brought to excellence and mastery in the science of archery; / and having composed the auspicious life-story of Rāma,

sanskrit_iast:
adhyāpito viśālākṣau dārakau priyadarśanau ..
agāyatāṃ tatastau tu rāmayaje kumāgkā .. 53 ..
meaning:
अध्यापितो विशालाक्षौ दारकौ प्रियदर्शनौ ..
अगायतां ततस्तौ तु रामयजे कुमाग्का .. 53 ..
text_mt: Vālmīki taught the two large-eyed, handsome boys. / Then those two youths sang at the sacrifice of Rāma

sanskrit_iast:
rāmasya caritaṃ kṛtsnaṃ rāmasya purataḥ sthitau ..
tasmātkāvyāttu vijñāya putrau tau priyadarśanau .. 54 ..
meaning:
रामस्य चरितं कृत्स्नं रामस्य पुरतः स्थितौ ..
तस्मात्काव्यात्तु विज्ञाय पुत्रौ तौ प्रियदर्शनौ .. 54 ..
text_mt: the entire life-story of Rāma, standing in the presence of Rāma. / Having recognised from that poem those two handsome boys as his sons,

sanskrit_iast:
yajñe tāṃ ca tathābhūtāmānayāmāma satvaraḥ ..
uvāca ca varārohāṃ pratyayaṃ kuru me śubhe .. 55 ..
meaning:
यज्ञे तां च तथाभूतामानयामाम सत्वरः ..
उवाच च वरारोहां प्रत्ययं कुरु मे शुभे .. 55 ..
text_mt: he quickly had her brought to the sacrifice in that condition, / and said to that woman of lovely hips: "Give me proof, O auspicious one!"

sanskrit_iast:
rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā sītā vacanamabravīta ..
yathā'haṃ rāghavādanyaṃ manasāpi na kāmaye .. 56 ..
meaning:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सीता वचनमब्रवीत ..
यथाऽहं राघवादन्यं मनसापि न कामये .. 56 ..
text_mt: Having heard the words of Rāma, Sītā spoke these words: / "As I do not desire anyone other than the descendant of Raghu even in my mind,

sanskrit_iast:
tena satyena me devī vivaraṃ saṃprayacchatu ..
etasminneva kāle tu bhuvaṃ bhittvā samutthitam .. 57 ..
meaning:
तेन सत्येन मे देवी विवरं संप्रयच्छतु ..
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भुवं भित्त्वा समुत्थितम् .. 57 ..
text_mt: by that truth let the goddess [Earth] grant me an opening." / At that very time, bursting through the earth, there arose

sanskrit_iast:
dhṛtaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ nāgaistatraināmupaveśayat ..
svayaṃ vasumatī devī pātālaṃ sā tato gatā .. 58 ..
meaning:
धृतं सिंहासनं नागैस्तत्रैनामुपवेशयत् ..
स्वयं वसुमती देवी पातालं सा ततो गता .. 58 ..
text_mt: a lion-throne held up by serpent-deities; on it the goddess Vasumatī herself / seated her, and she then went to the netherworld,

sanskrit_iast:
avicchinnena patatā puṣpavarṇena pārthiva ..
tasyāṃ bhūmipraviṣṭāyāṃ rāghavaṃ krodhasaṃyutam .. 59 ..
meaning:
अविच्छिन्नेन पतता पुष्पवर्णेन पार्थिव ..
तस्यां भूमिप्रविष्टायां राघवं क्रोधसंयुतम् .. 59 ..
text_mt: amidst a continuous falling rain of flowers, O king. / When she had entered the earth, the descendant of Raghu, filled with anger,

sanskrit_iast:
sāntvayāmāsa vai brahmā sarvalokanamasrkṛtaḥ ..
rāmo'pi kṛtvā sauvarṇīṃ sītāṃ patnīṃ yaśasvinīm .. 1.221.60 ..
meaning:
सान्त्वयामास वै ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकनमस्र्कृतः ..
रामोऽपि कृत्वा सौवर्णीं सीतां पत्नीं यशस्विनीम् .. 1.221.60 ..
text_mt: was consoled by Brahmā, who is revered by all the worlds. / Rāma, too, having made a golden [image of] Sītā, his renowned wife,

sanskrit_iast:
īje yajñairbahuvidhaiḥ saha bhātṛbhiracyutaḥ ..
nāpadbhayaṃ na vidhavā na ca vyālakṛtaṃ bhayama .. 61 ..
meaning:
ईजे यज्ञैर्बहुविधैः सह भातृभिरच्युतः ..
नापद्भयं न विधवा न च व्यालकृतं भयम .. 61 ..
text_mt: the imperishable one sacrificed with various sacrifices along with his brothers. / There was no fear of calamity, no widow, and no fear caused by wild beasts,

sanskrit_iast:
na ca vyādhikṛtaṃ kiñcidrāme rājyaṃ praśāsati ..
ājānubāhurdharmātmā siṃhaskandho nareśvaraḥ .. 62 ..
meaning:
न च व्याधिकृतं किञ्चिद्रामे राज्यं प्रशासति ..
आजानुबाहुर्धर्मात्मा सिंहस्कन्धो नरेश्वरः .. 62 ..
text_mt: nor was there anything caused by disease, while Rāma was ruling the kingdom. / His arms reaching to his knees, righteous in soul, lion-shouldered, a lord of men,

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthvī sasāgarāṃ rāmo dharmeṇānvaśipatprabhuḥ ..
devāśca ṛṣayaścaiva gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 63 ..
meaning:
पृथ्वी ससागरां रामो धर्मेणान्वशिपत्प्रभुः ..
देवाश्च ऋषयश्चैव गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः .. 63 ..
text_mt: the lord Rāma governed the earth along with the oceans in accordance with dharma. / And the gods and the ṛṣis, and the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases,

sanskrit_iast:
yakṣāśca bhūtāni tathā kinnarāścaiva rākṣasāḥ ..
mānuṣyāṇāṃ darśanaṃ te saumyāḥ santo yayussadā .. 64 ..
meaning:
यक्षाश्च भूतानि तथा किन्नराश्चैव राक्षसाः ..
मानुष्याणां दर्शनं ते सौम्याः सन्तो ययुस्सदा .. 64 ..
text_mt: the Yakṣas, spirits, and likewise the Kinnaras and Rākṣasas, / being gentle, continually came into the sight of humans.

sanskrit_iast:
yadarthameṣā carati gāthā loke purātanī ..
ājānubāhuḥ siṃhāsyaḥ kambugrīvo mahābalaḥ .. 65 ..
meaning:
यदर्थमेषा चरति गाथा लोके पुरातनी ..
आजानुबाहुः सिंहास्यः कम्बुग्रीवो महाबलः .. 65 ..
text_mt: For which reason this ancient verse circulates in the world: / "Arms reaching to his knees, lion-faced, conch-necked, of great strength,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvabhūtaśaraṇyaśca viṣṇurmānuṣyatāṃ gataḥ ..
satyavānanṛśaṃsaśca jāto bhaktajanapriyaḥ .. 66 ..
meaning:
सर्वभूतशरण्यश्च विष्णुर्मानुष्यतां गतः ..
सत्यवाननृशंसश्च जातो भक्तजनप्रियः .. 66 ..
text_mt: a refuge for all beings, Viṣṇu attained human state; / truthful, not cruel, he was born dear to his devoted people,

sanskrit_iast:
dhṛtiyukto dayāśīlo dharmayukto jitendriyaḥ ..
mitavāgapi kāryeṣu vaktā vācaspateḥ samaḥ .. 67 ..
meaning:
धृतियुक्तो दयाशीलो धर्मयुक्तो जितेन्द्रियः ..
मितवागपि कार्येषु वक्ता वाचस्पतेः समः .. 67 ..
text_mt: endowed with fortitude, compassionate in nature, endowed with dharma, self-controlled, / of measured speech, yet in affairs an orator equal to Bṛhaspati,

sanskrit_iast:
vīryavānna ca vīryeṇa mahatā tena vismitaḥ ..
tejasā bhāskagsamaḥ kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ .. 68 ..
meaning:
वीर्यवान्न च वीर्येण महता तेन विस्मितः ..
तेजसा भास्कग्समः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः .. 68 ..
text_mt: heroic, yet not astonished at that great heroism, / equal to the sun in splendour, equal to the earth in patience,

sanskrit_iast:
maheśvarasamaḥ krodhe nītāvuśanasā samaḥ ..
evaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu guṇairdāśarathirbabhau .. 69 ..
meaning:
महेश्वरसमः क्रोधे नीतावुशनसा समः ..
एवं सर्वेषु भूतेषु गुणैर्दाशरथिर्बभौ .. 69 ..
text_mt: equal to Maheśvara in anger, equal to Uśanas in statecraft." / Thus among all beings the son of Daśaratha shone with virtues.

sanskrit_iast:
varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca na sāṅkaryaṃ nṛpottame ..
dharmiṣṭhāśca janāḥ sarve rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati .. 1.221.70 ..
meaning:
वर्णानामाश्रमाणां च न साङ्कर्यं नृपोत्तमे ..
धर्मिष्ठाश्च जनाः सर्वे रामे राज्यं प्रशासति .. 1.221.70 ..
text_mt: There was no intermixture of the social classes and the stages of life under that foremost of kings; / and all the people were exceedingly righteous while Rāma was ruling the kingdom.

sanskrit_iast:
nirdasyurabhavalloko nānarthaḥ kiñcidaspṛśata ..
nākālavarṣī parjanyaḥ sarvasasyadharā dharā ..
janānurāgaśca mahānrāmasya viditātmanaḥ ..71..
meaning:
निर्दस्युरभवल्लोको नानर्थः किञ्चिदस्पृशत ..
नाकालवर्षी पर्जन्यः सर्वसस्यधरा धरा ..
जनानुरागश्च महान्रामस्य विदितात्मनः ..71..
text_mt: The world was free of thieves, no misfortune touched anyone, / Parjanya did not rain out of season, the earth bore all crops, / and great was the affection of the people for Rāma of realised soul.

sanskrit_iast:
na te kṣamaṃ tena narendracandra vairaṃ mahātmā sa tu lokapūjyaḥ ..
tasyāstravegasya raṇe ca vegaṃ soḍhuṃ na śaktāstridaśāḥ saśakrāḥ ..72 ..
1.222
śailūṣa uvāca ..
vahnipraviṣṭāṃ saṃprekṣya tadā vedavatīṃ dvija ..
kiṃ cakāra mahātejā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān..1..
nāḍāyana uvāca..
jagāma sa tadā laṅkāṃ pūjyamāno niśācaraiḥ ..
tatrasthaṃ prerayāmāsa dūtaṃ dhanapatiḥ svayam .. 2 ..
akāryādvinivartasva suraiste cintyate vadhaḥ ..
dūtasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dūtaṃ hatvā niśācaraḥ ..3..
gatvā vijigye dhanadaṃ vijahārā'sya puṣpakam ..
puṣpakeṇa vimānena kailāsaṃ sa tadā yayau .. 4 ..
puṣpakasya gatiṃ ruddhāṃ tatra vīkṣya niśācaraḥ ..
dadarśa śailaśṛṅgasthaṃ nandinaṃ vānarākṛtim .. 5 ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā mumuce hāsaṃ nandī taṃ śaptavāṃstataḥ ..
girāvasmindaśagrīva svayaṃ krīḍati śaṅkaraḥ ..6..
meaning:
न ते क्षमं तेन नरेन्द्रचन्द्र वैरं महात्मा स तु लोकपूज्यः ..
तस्यास्त्रवेगस्य रणे च वेगं सोढुं न शक्तास्त्रिदशाः सशक्राः ..72 ..
1.222
शैलूष उवाच ..

Śailūṣa said:
Seeing Vedavatī entering the fire at that time, O twice-born,
what did the ten-necked, glorious, majestic [Rāvaṇa] do?
Nāḍāyana said:
He then went to Laṅkā, honoured by the night-wanderers.
The Lord of Wealth himself dispatched a messenger to him residing there:
"Turn back from what should not be done! Your slaying is being plotted by the gods."
Having heard the messenger's words and having killed the messenger, the night-wanderer,
having gone, conquered the Giver of Wealth and carried off his Puṣpaka [chariot].
In that Puṣpaka aerial chariot he then went to Kailāsa.
Seeing the passage of the Puṣpaka blocked there, the night-wanderer
saw Nandin, who had the form of a monkey, stationed on the peak of the mountain.
Having seen him, he burst into laughter. Thereupon Nandin cursed him:
"On this mountain, O ten-necked one, Śaṅkara himself sports.

Since you approach his presence with an aerial chariot
and mock me, therefore I shall curse you:
Ferocious monkeys resembling my face, terrible [and born] in the lineage
of the progenitor Pulaha, will arise for your destruction."
Hearing these words of Nandin, and wishing then to carry off
[mount] Kailāsa together with the Three-Eyed [Śiva] to Laṅkā, he thrust his arms under the mountain.
Her seat shaken on Kailāsa as it was agitated by the arms of Pulastya's descendant,
Umā then seized the Destroyer of Tripura tightly by the neck.
Then roaring, Mahādeva, Hara, the foremost of the gods,
pressed down that mountain with his big toe in sport.
By that rākṣasa, out of rage and also out of the agony in his arms,
a tremendous cry was let out, by which the three worlds were made to scream.
His ministers thought the gnashing of his mouths to be the destruction of the world-age.
The gods headed by Śakra were shaken from their seats.
Terrified exceedingly by that sound, the daughter of the mountain,
her eyes restless with fear, embraced Hara intensely.

Attaining then the delight born from her spontaneous embrace,
and releasing his arms, O king, Hara addressed the ten-faced one:
"I am pleased with your valour and your prowess, O ten-faced one!
Because a terrifying cry, not of a rākṣasa, was emitted by you,
therefore you will be known by the name 'Rāvaṇa' in the three worlds."
From then on, O ruler of kings, [he was called] Rāvaṇa, who makes the worlds cry out.
A liṅga made of gold of the god of gods, the bearer of the trident,
he worships, O ruler of kings, always filled with faith.
Wherever and however he goes, O protector of the earth,
the golden liṅga of that god is carried along after him.
Then King Rāvaṇa went to the city of Saṃyamanī.
He fought with Death and with the snares of Time [and Yama's] sacrifices.
Having conquered the hosts of ancestors and freed the inhabitants of hell,
he fought with Yama. Then the son of Vivasvat out of anger,

desiring to slay the night-wanderer with the weapon of the staff, O protector of the earth,
was stopped by Brahmā, who indeed spoke these words:
"Infallible is this staff of yours, and Rāvaṇa cannot be slain.
If even one [of these conditions] were violated, I would become a speaker of falsehood."
Hearing the words of the Grandfather, that god then vanished.
Rāvaṇa, together with his army, went to Mount Kailāsa.
He dwelt there for the night, desiring to fight with the dwellers of heaven.
At moonrise in the night, [the celestial nymph] who was going to an assignation with his brother's son,
he saw—Rambhā, radiant like a streak of lightning in a cloud.
Afflicted by lust, having violated the celestial woman who was unwilling,
[he was cursed by Nalakūbara:] "From this day forth your head will split into a hundred pieces!"
Going at daybreak to the abode of the gods, that rākṣasa,
accompanied by Meghanāda and the rākṣasa Kumbhakarṇa,
wrought the slaughter of the gods, along with other foremost rākṣasas.
In the thick of that battle, the fierce Sumālī, child of Rāvaṇa's [mother's family],
was forcefully struck down then in combat by the son of Savitṛ, O sinless one.

Knowing the rākṣasas to be invincible, a dānava named Pulomā
[took] his own grandson Jayanta, Indra's son, from the battlefield,
and, illustrious, led him to his own home on the surface of the earth for his protection.
[Seeing] Śakra bewildered in mind, not seeing his son,
Meghanāda, who had obtained a boon from Brahmā, bound him slowly
and brought him thus to Laṅkā. Then the divine Grandfather,
having gone, released that Śakra, the lord of the three worlds.
And to Meghanāda [he granted] weapons and diverse magical powers,
and then gave him immortality, except in the interval of a fire ritual.
He then gave him a name: "You shall be Śakrajit [Conqueror of Śakra]."
Having consoled Meghanāda and having released the one of a hundred sacrifices,
the blessed Brahmā addressed the god of a thousand eyes:
"When the dear wife of Gautama, fashioned by me through the mind,
incomparable in beauty, O Śakra, was violated by you,

Nāḍāyana said:
Having been thus praised by Śaṃkara, the glorious Vināyaka
brought the three cities together in one place without hindrance. / Once the three cities were united, Viṣṇu, situated on the tip of the arrow and released from the bow, / propelled swiftly by Śaṃkara, reduced them to ashes.
When the three cities were destroyed by that foremost of gods, great joy arose in the worlds. / The hosts of gods, overjoyed, then returned to their own abodes, O king of kings.

text_mt: Yet from that blood of the Andhakas, they [more Andhakas] arose again in great numbers, even though [the Mothers were] satisfied; / and by them Mahādeva was afflicted with tridents, clubs, and spears.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa śaṅkaro devastvandhakairvyākulīkṛtaḥ ..
jagāma śaraṇaṃ devaṃ vāsudevamajaṃ vibhum .. 32 ..
meaning:
ततः स शङ्करो देवस्त्वन्धकैर्व्याकुलीकृतः ..
जगाम शरणं देवं वासुदेवमजं विभुम् .. 32 ..
text_mt: Then the god Śaṅkara, distressed by the Andhakas, / went for refuge to the god Vāsudeva, the unborn and all-pervading lord.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu bhagavānviṣṇuḥ sṛṣṭavāñchuṣkarevatīm ..
sā papau satvaraṃ teṣāmandhakānāmasṛkkṣaṇāt .. 33 ..
meaning:
ततस्तु भगवान्विष्णुः सृष्टवाञ्छुष्करेवतीम् ..
सा पपौ सत्वरं तेषामन्धकानामसृक्क्षणात् .. 33 ..
text_mt: Thereupon the blessed Lord Viṣṇu created Śuṣkarevatī. / In an instant, she quickly drank the blood of those Andhakas.

sanskrit_iast:
yathāyathā ca rudhiraṃ pibatyandhakasambhavam ..
tathā tathā'dhikaṃ devī saṃśuṣyati janādhipa .. 34 ..
meaning:
यथायथा च रुधिरं पिबत्यन्धकसम्भवम् ..
तथा तथाऽधिकं देवी संशुष्यति जनाधिप .. 34 ..
text_mt: And the more she drank the blood arising from the Andhakas, / all the more, O ruler of men, the goddess dried up.

sanskrit_iast:
pīyamāne tadā teṣāmandhakānāṃ tathāsṛji ..
andhakāstu kṣayaṃ nītā sarve te tripurāriṇā .. 35 ..
meaning:
पीयमाने तदा तेषामन्धकानां तथासृजि ..
अन्धकास्तु क्षयं नीता सर्वे ते त्रिपुरारिणा .. 35 ..
text_mt: As the blood of those Andhakas was being drunk, / all those Andhakas were brought to destruction by the enemy of Tripura.

sanskrit_iast:
mūlāndhakaṃ tu vikramya tadā sarvatra lokakṛt ..
cakāra vegāñchūlāgre tadā tuṣṭāva śaṅkaram .. 36 ..
meaning:
मूलान्धकं तु विक्रम्य तदा सर्वत्र लोककृत् ..
चकार वेगाञ्छूलाग्रे तदा तुष्टाव शङ्करम् .. 36 ..
text_mt: Then, striding over the original Andhaka everywhere, the creator of the world / swiftly impaled him on the tip of his trident; and he [Andhaka] then praised Śaṅkara.

sanskrit_iast:
andhakaḥ sumahāvīryaḥ tasya tuṣṭo'bhavadbhavaḥ ..
sāmīpyaṃ pradadau nityaṃ gaṇeśatvaṃ tathaiva ca .. 37 ..
meaning:
अन्धकः सुमहावीर्यः तस्य तुष्टोऽभवद्भवः ..
सामीप्यं प्रददौ नित्यं गणेशत्वं तथैव च .. 37 ..
text_mt: Andhaka possessed exceedingly great valor. Bhava was pleased with him; / he granted him eternal proximity and likewise the leadership of the gaṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
tato mātṛgaṇāḥ sarve śaṅkaraṃ vākyamabruvan ..
bhagavan bhakṣayiṣyāmaḥ sadevāsuramānuṣam .. 38 ..
meaning:
ततो मातृगणाः सर्वे शङ्करं वाक्यमब्रुवन् ..
भगवन् भक्षयिष्यामः सदेवासुरमानुषम् .. 38 ..
text_mt: Then all the troops of Mothers said to Śaṅkara: / "O Blessed Lord, we wish to consume the gods, asuras, and human beings.

sanskrit_iast:
tvatprasādājjagatsarvaṃ tadanujñātumarhasi ..
śaṅkara uvāca ..
bhavatībhiḥ prajāḥ sarvā rakṣaṇīyā na saṃśayaḥ .. 39 ..
meaning:
त्वत्प्रसादाज्जगत्सर्वं तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ..
शङ्कर उवाच ..
भवतीभिः प्रजाः सर्वा रक्षणीया न संशयः .. 39 ..
text_mt: By your favor, you should allow [us to consume] the entire universe." / Śaṅkara said: / "All creatures must be protected by you, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādghorādabhiprāyānmanaḥ śīghraṃ nivartyatām ..
nāḍāyana uvāca ..
ityevaṃ śaṅkareṇoktaṃ tvanādṛtya vacastu tāḥ .. 1.226.40 ..
meaning:
तस्माद्घोरादभिप्रायान्मनः शीघ्रं निवर्त्यताम् ..
नाडायन उवाच ..
इत्येवं शङ्करेणोक्तं त्वनादृत्य वचस्तु ताः .. 1.226.40 ..
text_mt: Therefore let your minds be quickly turned away from that terrible intention." / Nāḍāyana said: / But disregarding the words spoken thus by Śaṅkara, they, 1.226.40

sanskrit_iast:
kṣobhayāmāsu'vyagrāstrailokyaṃ sacarācaram . .
trailokye bhakṣyamāṇe tu tadā mātṛgaṇairnavaiḥ .. 41 ..
meaning:
क्षोभयामासुऽव्यग्रास्त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् . .
त्रैलोक्ये भक्ष्यमाणे तु तदा मातृगणैर्नवैः .. 41 ..
text_mt: undismayed, agitated the three worlds, both moving and unmoving. / While the three worlds were being devoured by the newly-arisen troops of Mothers, 41

sanskrit_iast:
nṛsiṃhamūrtiṃ devaṃ ca pradadhyau bhagavāñchivaḥ ..
anādinidhanaṃ devaṃ sarvalokabhavodbhavama .. 42 ..
meaning:
नृसिंहमूर्तिं देवं च प्रदध्यौ भगवाञ्छिवः ..
अनादिनिधनं देवं सर्वलोकभवोद्भवम .. 42 ..
text_mt: the blessed Lord Śiva meditated upon the god in his Nṛsiṃha form, / the god without beginning or end, the source of the existence of all worlds, 42

sanskrit_iast:
daityendravakṣorudhiraprokṣitorumahānakhama ..
vidyujjihvaṃ mahādaṃṣṭraṃ sphuṭakesarasaṅkaṭam .. 43 ..
meaning:
दैत्येन्द्रवक्षोरुधिरप्रोक्षितोरुमहानखम ..
विद्युज्जिह्वं महादंष्ट्रं स्फुटकेसरसङ्कटम् .. 43 ..
text_mt: whose great claws were sprinkled with the blood of the demon king's chest, / with a tongue like lightning, huge fangs, and thick with bristling manes, 43

sanskrit_iast:
kalpāntamārutakṣubdhasaptārṇava mahāsvanama ..
vajrāgratīkṣṇanakharamākarṇāddāritānanam.. 44 ..
meaning:
कल्पान्तमारुतक्षुब्धसप्तार्णव महास्वनम ..
वज्राग्रतीक्ष्णनखरमाकर्णाद्दारिताननम्.. 44 ..
text_mt: making a mighty roar like the seven oceans stirred by the wind at the end of the aeon, / whose claws were as sharp as the point of a vajra, his mouth torn open to the ears, 44

sanskrit_iast:
maruśailapratīkāśamudayārkasamekṣaṇama ..
himādriśikharākāraṃ cārudaṃṣṭrojjvalānanam .. 45 ..
meaning:
मरुशैलप्रतीकाशमुदयार्कसमेक्षणम ..
हिमाद्रिशिखराकारं चारुदंष्ट्रोज्ज्वलाननम् .. 45 ..
text_mt: resembling the desert mountain, his gaze like the rising sun, / having the appearance of a peak of the Himalaya, his radiant face lovely with fangs, 45

sanskrit_iast:
khavinissṛtaromāgniṃ jvālākesaramālinam ..
baddhāṅgadaṃ sumukuṭaṃ cārukeyūrabhūṣaṇama .. 46 ..
meaning:
खविनिस्सृतरोमाग्निं ज्वालाकेसरमालिनम् ..
बद्धाङ्गदं सुमुकुटं चारुकेयूरभूषणम .. 46 ..
text_mt: with fires of bodily hair issuing into the sky, garlanded with manes of flames, / wearing armlets, an excellent crown, and adorned with beautiful bracelets, 46

sanskrit_iast:
śroṇīsūtreṇa mahatā kāñcanena virājitama ..
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaṃ vāmoyugavibhūṣitama .. 47 ..
meaning:
श्रोणीसूत्रेण महता काञ्चनेन विराजितम ..
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामं वामोयुगविभूषितम .. 47 ..
text_mt: resplendent with a large golden girdle, / dark like the petal of a blue lotus, adorned with a pair of garments, 47

sanskrit_iast:
tejasākrāntasakalaṃ brahmāṇḍāntaramaṃḍapama ..
sādarabhrāmyamāṇānāṃ hutahavya ghanārciṣām .. 48 ..
meaning:
तेजसाक्रान्तसकलं ब्रह्माण्डान्तरमंडपम ..
सादरभ्राम्यमाणानां हुतहव्य घनार्चिषाम् .. 48 ..
text_mt: pervading the entire pavilion within the cosmic egg with his splendour, / with body-hairs resembling spirals / of thick flames of offered oblations being reverently whirled about, 48

sanskrit_iast:
āvarttaiḥ sadṛśākāraiḥ saṃyuktaṃ daihalomajaiḥ ..
sarvapuppavicitrāṃ ca dhārayānaṃ mahāsrajama .. 49 ..
meaning:
आवर्त्तैः सदृशाकारैः संयुक्तं दैहलोमजैः ..
सर्वपुप्पविचित्रां च धारयानं महास्रजम .. 49 ..
text_mt: and wearing a great garland variegated with all kinds of flowers. 49

sanskrit_iast:
sa dhyātamātro bhagavānpradadau tasya darśanam ..
yādṛśenaiva rūpeṇa yāto rudreṇa bhaktitaḥ .. 1.226.50 ..
meaning:
स ध्यातमात्रो भगवान्प्रददौ तस्य दर्शनम् ..
यादृशेनैव रूपेण यातो रुद्रेण भक्तितः .. 1.226.50 ..
text_mt: As soon as he was meditated upon, the Blessed Lord granted him a vision, / in that very form in which Rudra, through devotion, had approached [him], 1.226.50

sanskrit_iast:
tādṛśenaiva rūpeṇa durnirīkṣyeṇa daivataiḥ ..
praṇipatya tu deveśaṃ tadā tuṣṭāva śaṅkaraḥ .. 51 ..
meaning:
तादृशेनैव रूपेण दुर्निरीक्ष्येण दैवतैः ..
प्रणिपत्य तु देवेशं तदा तुष्टाव शङ्करः .. 51 ..
text_mt: in that very form which was hard to behold even by the gods. / Having bowed down to the lord of gods, Śaṅkara then praised [him]: 51

sanskrit_iast:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
namastestu jagannātha narasiṃhavapurdharaḥ ..
daityanāthāsthisaṃpūrṇa nakhaśuktivirājita .. 52 ..
meaning:
शङ्कर उवाच ..
नमस्तेस्तु जगन्नाथ नरसिंहवपुर्धरः ..
दैत्यनाथास्थिसंपूर्ण नखशुक्तिविराजित .. 52 ..
text_mt: Śaṅkara said: / "Obeisance to you, Lord of the universe, bearer of the Narasiṃha body, / resplendent with claws like oyster shells filled with the bones of the demon king, 52

sanskrit_iast:
tadasrakaṇasaṃlagnahemapiṅgalavigrahaṃ ..
meroḥ sapadmarāgasya śobhāṃ dhatse jagadguro .. 53 ..
meaning:
तदस्रकणसंलग्नहेमपिङ्गलविग्रहं ..
मेरोः सपद्मरागस्य शोभां धत्से जगद्गुरो .. 53 ..
text_mt: your reddish-gold body touched with droplets of his blood! / O teacher of the universe, you bear the beauty of Mount Meru adorned with rubies, 53

sanskrit_iast:
kalpāntāmbhodanirghoṣa sūryakoṭisamaprabha ..
sahasrayama saṃkrodha sahasrendraparākrama .. 54 ..
meaning:
कल्पान्ताम्भोदनिर्घोष सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभ ..
सहस्रयम संक्रोध सहस्रेन्द्रपराक्रम .. 54 ..
text_mt: thundering like clouds at the end of the aeon, equal in splendour to ten million suns, / having the fury of a thousand Yamas, the prowess of a thousand Indras, 54

sanskrit_iast:
sahasradhanadasphīta sahasravaruṇātmaka..
sahasrakālacarita sahasraniyatendriya..55..
meaning:
सहस्रधनदस्फीत सहस्रवरुणात्मक..
सहस्रकालचरित सहस्रनियतेन्द्रिय..55..
text_mt: abundant like a thousand Dhanadas, having the nature of a thousand Varuṇas, / acting like a thousand Kālās, having the self-control of a thousand restrained [sages], 55

sanskrit_iast:
sahasrabhūmisaddhairya sahasrānantamūrttimat ..
sahasracandrapratima sahasraharivikrama .. 56 ..
meaning:
सहस्रभूमिसद्धैर्य सहस्रानन्तमूर्त्तिमत् ..
सहस्रचन्द्रप्रतिम सहस्रहरिविक्रम .. 56 ..
text_mt: having the true steadfastness of a thousand earths, having the forms of a thousand Anantas, / resembling a thousand moons, having the strides of a thousand Haris, 56

sanskrit_iast:
sahasrarudratejaska sahasrabrahmasaṃstuta..
sahasravāyuvegogra sahasrajyotirīṣaṇa..57..
meaning:
सहस्ररुद्रतेजस्क सहस्रब्रह्मसंस्तुत..
सहस्रवायुवेगोग्र सहस्रज्योतिरीषण..57..
text_mt: possessing the splendour of a thousand Rudras, praised by a thousand Brahmās, / fierce with the speed of a thousand winds, with the gaze of a thousand lights, 57

sanskrit_iast:
sahasrayantramathana sahasrābādhamocana ..
andhakasya vināśāya sṛṣṭā yā mātaro mayā .. 58 ..
meaning:
सहस्रयन्त्रमथन सहस्राबाधमोचन ..
अन्धकस्य विनाशाय सृष्टा या मातरो मया .. 58 ..
text_mt: crusher of a thousand snares, deliverer from a thousand afflictions! / The Mothers who were created by me for the destruction of Andhaka, 58

sanskrit_iast:
anādṛtya tu madvākyaṃ bhakṣayaṃtyaśca tāḥ prajāḥ ..
kṛtvā tāśca na śakto'haṃ saṃhantumaparājita..59..
meaning:
अनादृत्य तु मद्वाक्यं भक्षयंत्यश्च ताः प्रजाः ..
कृत्वा ताश्च न शक्तोऽहं संहन्तुमपराजित..59..
text_mt: disregarding my command, are devouring the creatures. / Having created them, I am unable to destroy them, O unconquered one! 59

sanskrit_iast:
svayaṃ kṛtvā kathaṃ tāsāṃ vināśamapi rocaye ..
nāḍāyana uvāca ..
evamuktaḥ sa rudreṇa nārasiṃha vapurdharaḥ .. 1.226.60 ..
meaning:
स्वयं कृत्वा कथं तासां विनाशमपि रोचये ..
नाडायन उवाच ..
एवमुक्तः स रुद्रेण नारसिंह वपुर्धरः .. 1.226.60 ..
text_mt: Having created [them] myself, how could I even wish for their destruction?" / Nāḍāyana said: / Being addressed in this way by Rudra, he who bore the Nārasiṃha body 1.226.60

sanskrit_iast:
sasarja devīṃ jihvātaḥ tadā vāgīśvarīṃ hariḥ ..
hṛdayācca tathā māyāṃ guhyācca bhagamālinīm .. 61 ..
meaning:
ससर्ज देवीं जिह्वातः तदा वागीश्वरीं हरिः ..
हृदयाच्च तथा मायां गुह्याच्च भगमालिनीम् .. 61 ..
text_mt: then created from his tongue the goddess Vāgīśvarī, Hari [created] Māyā / from his heart, and from his secret part Bhagamālinī. 61

sanskrit_iast:
asthibhyaśca tathā kālī sṛṣṭā pūrvaṃ mahātmanā ..
yayā tadrudhiraṃ pītamandhakānāṃ mahātmanām .. 62 ..
meaning:
अस्थिभ्यश्च तथा काली सृष्टा पूर्वं महात्मना ..
यया तद्रुधिरं पीतमन्धकानां महात्मनाम् .. 62 ..
text_mt: And Kālī had been created earlier from his bones by the Great Soul, / by whom that blood of the mighty Andhakas was drunk, 62

sanskrit_iast:
yā tvasminkathitā loke nāmataḥ śuṣkarevatī ..
dvātriṃśanmātaraḥ sṛṣṭā gātrebhyaścakriṇā tataḥ .. 63 ..
meaning:
या त्वस्मिन्कथिता लोके नामतः शुष्करेवती ..
द्वात्रिंशन्मातरः सृष्टा गात्रेभ्यश्चक्रिणा ततः .. 63 ..
text_mt: she who is spoken of by name in this world as Śuṣkarevatī. / Then thirty-two Mothers were created from his limbs by the Bearer of the Discus. 63

sanskrit_iast:
tāsāṃ nāmāni vakṣyāmi tāni me gadataḥ śṛṇu ..
sarvakliṣṭā mahābhāgā kaṇṭhakarṇī tathaiva ca .. 64..
meaning:
तासां नामानि वक्ष्यामि तानि मे गदतः शृणु ..
सर्वक्लिष्टा महाभागा कण्ठकर्णी तथैव च .. 64..
text_mt: I shall state their names; hear them from me as I speak: / the illustrious Sarvakliṣṭā, and likewise Kaṇṭhakarṇī, 64

sanskrit_iast:
trailokya mohinī puṇyā sarvasattvavaśaṅkarī ..
tathā ca cakrahṛdayā pañcamā vyomacāriṇī ..65..
meaning:
त्रैलोक्य मोहिनी पुण्या सर्वसत्त्ववशङ्करी ..
तथा च चक्रहृदया पञ्चमा व्योमचारिणी ..65..
text_mt: Trailokyamohinī, holy, Sarvasattvavaśaṅkarī, / and Cakrahṛdayā, the fifth Vyomacāriṇī, 65

sanskrit_iast:
śaṃkhinī lekhinī caiva kālasaṅkarṣiṇī tathā ..
iti devyaṣṭakaṃ rājanvāgīśyanucaraṃ smṛtam .. 66 ..
meaning:
शंखिनी लेखिनी चैव कालसङ्कर्षिणी तथा ..
इति देव्यष्टकं राजन्वागीश्यनुचरं स्मृतम् .. 66 ..
text_mt: Śaṅkhinī, Lekhinī, and likewise Kālasaṅkarṣiṇī: / this group of eight goddesses, O king, is considered the retinue of Vāgīśī. 66

sanskrit_iast:
ajitā sūkṣmahṛdayā vṛkṣāveśāśmadarśanā ..
nṛsiṃhabhairavā cillā garutpakṣahṛdānayā .. 67 ..
meaning:
अजिता सूक्ष्महृदया वृक्षावेशाश्मदर्शना ..
नृसिंहभैरवा चिल्ला गरुत्पक्षहृदानया .. 67 ..
text_mt: Ajitā, Sūkṣmahṛdayā, Vṛkṣāveśā, Aśmadarśanā, / Nṛsiṃhabhairavā, Cillā, Garutpakṣahṛdānayā: 67

sanskrit_iast:
bhagamālinya 'nucarā ityaṣṭau nṛpa mātaraḥ ..
ākarṣiṇī ca bhārūṭī tathaivottaramālikā .. 68 ..
meaning:
भगमालिन्य ऽनुचरा इत्यष्टौ नृप मातरः ..
आकर्षिणी च भारूटी तथैवोत्तरमालिका .. 68 ..
text_mt: these eight Mothers, O king, are the attendants of Bhagamālinī. / Ākarṣiṇī, Bhārūṭī, and likewise Uttaramālikā, 68

sanskrit_iast:
jvālāmukhī bhīṣaṇikā kāmadhenuśca bālikā ..
tathā padmakarā rājanrevatyanucarāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 69 ..

vacā, kuṣṭha, mustā, vālaka, the two rajanīs,
sandalwood, saffron, nāgadāna, and rocanā:

This bath is to be employed to destroy the afflictions caused by the Mothers.
With flowers of five colours, and incense made from resins,
with delightful saffron, agallochum, camphor, and sandalwood,
with lamps, edible delicacies, milk, sour gruel, ollopikās, and jaggery,
with pāyasa mixed with honey, with meat, and with cooked rice,
an offering duly performed destroys the afflictions caused by the Mothers, O king.
Sprouts of dūrvā grass, mañjiṣṭhā, ginger, nāgakeśara,
rocanā, saffron, sandalwood, and likewise vacā:
this is the supreme ointment that destroys the afflictions caused by the Mothers.
Claws of an elephant, horse, monkey, and boar, and also ghee:
this is declared the supreme incense that destroys the afflictions caused by the Mothers.
Those who consume consecrated ghee and aged pañcagavya, O king, / will never suffer any fear born of the Mothers, nor one arising from planetary seizures.

1.228
Nāḍāyana said:
Hear further power of that God of gods,
as it is being told by me, O king, which destroys all impurities.
Śaṅkara and Pārvatī, competing with one another,
engaged in sexual union, O king, for fully a hundred years, it is said.
When there was no defeat of either of the two,
then the deities, distressed, spoke to one another:
'The embryo that will be born from this—the three worlds with all their moving and unmoving beings
will without doubt be bewitched by its splendour.
Therefore, O God of gods, consumer of oblations, enter into them.'
Addressed thus, the fire entered the best of gods.
Seeing him, the three-eyed god arose in agitation;
agitated by splendours, [his seed] then entered into the mouth of the fire.
The goddess Pārvatī cursed the gods: 'Upon your own wives,
defiled by my anger, you shall obtain no sons at all!'

The consumer of oblations, burning indeed from the splendour of Śarva,
deposited the embryo in the Gaṅgā, and she too after some time,
deposited on the White Mountain the embryo resembling fire in splendour.
Because it was born there, the White Mountain turned golden.
By the splendour of that Śaṅkara whose seed was gold,
the Kṛttikās beheld the boy abandoned there by the Gaṅgā.
Out of compassion, O best of kings, they offered their breasts to him.
Becoming six-faced, he then drank the breast of all six.
Grown through their milk, righteous in nature and of lovely splendour,
he granted a boon to the Kṛttikās, which I shall tell you, O king.
Nāḍāyana said:
'When you enter into conjunction with the moon, O fair-faced ones,
then whatever men will perform worship of you,
and of Fire, of the Moon, of Varuṇa, and of me,

I shall grant a favor to you, O river of the gods:
on the third day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha, O fair-faced one,
you descended to the human realm; then you will receive worship.
Whoever on that day performs a bath in you, O auspicious one,
he will attain the fruit of a Rājasūya and an Aśvamedha sacrifice. / Whoever, situated anywhere at all, on that day [performs] worship,
with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, offerings and the like, incense, lamps, and food, / [and] is an actor [of rituals] toward you, O fortunate one, the fruit born of bathing in your water
he will surely attain, O knower of dharma; there should be no doubt about this. / Whatever one gives on that day, endowed with faith,
that fruit of his will be inexhaustible; there is no doubt. / That lunar day is to be known as inexhaustible (Akṣayā); if joined with the Kṛttikās,
it will be, O highly fortunate one, exceptionally fruitful.
Those who, on that day, O lady of lovely limbs, will perform your worship as described before, / having dwelt for a very long time in heaven, will go to the worlds of the lord of waters.

1.230 / Nāḍāyana said: / Then Viśvāmitra performed the birth rites and other rituals / for that great-souled one, and likewise auspicious ceremonies.
At that very time, [messengers] reported to the thunderbolt-wielder, the lord of the gods, / about the child of blazing splendour born on the white mountain.
Then Purandara set his mind on his destruction. / Together with the gods, ancestors, sacrifices, and the powerful Dānavas and Rākṣasas,
and with the Bhūtas, Nāgas, Piśācas, ancestors, Gandharvas, and humans, / having deliberated on his destruction, he created great seizing spirits (grahāḥ):
terrible seizing spirits of gods and Daityas, ancestors, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, / of Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Nāgas, and flesh-eating mortals.
Those seizing spirits, many thousands in number, raising various weapons, / approached the white mountain with the desire to slay Kumāra.
Those seizing spirits were many thousands, and the auspicious Skanda / created seizing spirits by the hundreds, night-wanderers who were earlier spirits,
possessing great strength and great valour, moving at will, changing form at will, / many hundreds of thousands, in various garbs, swift as thought.

नदीकूलाद्रिशिखररुचिः प्रासादमेव च ..
शुचिशील समाचारो ज्ञेयो देवग्रहार्द्दितः .. 1.231.30 ..
text_mt: Fond of riverbanks, mountain peaks, and temples, / pure in character and conduct—he is to be known as afflicted by a divine spirit.

sanskrit_iast:
devānāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya puṣpadhūpaphalākṣataiḥ ..
gandhadīpapradānaiśca vahnisantarpaṇaistathā .. 31 ..
meaning:
देवानां पूजनं तस्य पुष्पधूपफलाक्षतैः ..
गन्धदीपप्रदानैश्च वह्निसन्तर्पणैस्तथा .. 31 ..
text_mt: Worship of the gods for him with flowers, incense, fruits, and unbroken grains, / with gifts of perfume and lamps, and likewise with offerings to the fire,

sanskrit_iast:
gorasaiśca sa śālyannairbrāhmaṇaiḥ svastivācanaiḥ ..
karttavyaṃ viduṣā nityaṃ tataḥ saṃpadyate sukhī .. 32 ..
meaning:
गोरसैश्च स शाल्यन्नैर्ब्राह्मणैः स्वस्तिवाचनैः ..
कर्त्तव्यं विदुषा नित्यं ततः संपद्यते सुखी .. 32 ..
text_mt: and with milk products, rice preparations, and benedictions recited by brahmins / should constantly be performed by the wise man; then he becomes happy.

sanskrit_iast:
ucchiṣṭānbhairavānrāvānvirasaṃ kurute'dhikam ..
tasmiṃstathotsavānyakṣānvratānadhyayanāni ca .. 33 ..
meaning:
उच्छिष्टान्भैरवान्रावान्विरसं कुरुतेऽधिकम् ..
तस्मिंस्तथोत्सवान्यक्षान्व्रतानध्ययनानि च .. 33 ..
text_mt: He emits impure, terrible roars, excessively harsh; / he [despises] festivals, yakṣas, vows, and recitations of sacred texts;

sanskrit_iast:
bahuśo vaṭucāśnāti vastraṃ pāṭayati svakam ..
asuragrahaduṣṭasya rūpametadvinirddiśet .. 34 ..
meaning:
बहुशो वटुचाश्नाति वस्त्रं पाटयति स्वकम् ..
असुरग्रहदुष्टस्य रूपमेतद्विनिर्द्दिशेत् .. 34 ..
text_mt: he eats frequently and voraciously, and tears his own garment— / one should declare this to be the appearance of one afflicted by an asura spirit.

sanskrit_iast:
daityasaṃpūjanaṃ tasya kāryaṃ māṃsasurāsavaiḥ ..
raktaiḥ puṣpairdhūpadīpaistathā bījasamudbhavaiḥ .. 35 ..
meaning:
दैत्यसंपूजनं तस्य कार्यं मांससुरासवैः ..
रक्तैः पुष्पैर्धूपदीपैस्तथा बीजसमुद्भवैः .. 35 ..
text_mt: Worship of the daityas must be performed for him with meat, wine, and liquor, / with red flowers, incense, lamps, and things produced from seeds.

sanskrit_iast:
gandharvavādyanirghoṣaṃ śrutvā hṛṣṭaḥ pranṛtyati ..
tīrthodyānanadītīragandhamālyādisevanāt .. 36 ..
meaning:
गन्धर्ववाद्यनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा हृष्टः प्रनृत्यति ..
तीर्थोद्याननदीतीरगन्धमाल्यादिसेवनात् .. 36 ..
text_mt: Hearing the sound of gandharva musical instruments, he rejoices and dances; / from frequenting sacred bathing places, gardens, riverbanks, perfumes, and garlands,

sanskrit_iast:
yathākāmaṃ vicarati gandharvonmādito naraḥ ..
gandhairmālyaiśca vividhairgītavādyaistathaiva ca .. 37 ..
meaning:
यथाकामं विचरति गन्धर्वोन्मादितो नरः ..
गन्धैर्माल्यैश्च विविधैर्गीतवाद्यैस्तथैव च .. 37 ..
text_mt: the man maddened by a gandharva roams about at will. / With various perfumes and garlands, and likewise with songs and musical instruments,

sanskrit_iast:
gandharvapūjanaṃ kāryaṃ tena saṃpadyate sukhī ..
nidrāluralaso duṣṭo darvīvatkurute karau .. 38 ..
meaning:
गन्धर्वपूजनं कार्यं तेन संपद्यते सुखी ..
निद्रालुरलसो दुष्टो दर्वीवत्कुरुते करौ .. 38 ..
text_mt: worship of the gandharvas must be performed; thereby he becomes happy. / Sleepy, sluggish, corrupt, he makes his hands like a snake's hood;

sanskrit_iast:
garbhavāsaguhāsevī naronmattaṃ vidurbudhāḥ ..
nāgānāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya kāryaṃ kulmāṣaparpaṭaiḥ .. 39 ..
meaning:
गर्भवासगुहासेवी नरोन्मत्तं विदुर्बुधाः ..
नागानां पूजनं तस्य कार्यं कुल्माषपर्पटैः .. 39 ..
text_mt: resorting to the inner chambers and caves, the wise know the man to be mad. / Worship of the nāgas must be performed for him with boiled sour pulses and crisps,

sanskrit_iast:
pāyasollopikāpūpaiḥ padmotpalabisaistathā ..
amatsarī mṛdurvīraḥ priyavāgbahubhojanaḥ .. 1.231.40 ..
meaning:
पायसोल्लोपिकापूपैः पद्मोत्पलबिसैस्तथा ..
अमत्सरी मृदुर्वीरः प्रियवाग्बहुभोजनः .. 1.231.40 ..
text_mt: with rice boiled in milk, sweetmeats, cakes, and lotus roots. / Free from envy, gentle, valiant, speaking pleasant words, eating much,

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthuvihvalatāmrākṣaḥ tathā vai gorasapriyaḥ ..
bhūtonmādasamāviṣṭo liṅgairetairvinirdiśet .. 41 ..
meaning:
पृथुविह्वलताम्राक्षः तथा वै गोरसप्रियः ..
भूतोन्मादसमाविष्टो लिङ्गैरेतैर्विनिर्दिशेत् .. 41 ..
text_mt: with broad, rolling, copper-colored eyes, and fond indeed of milk products— / one should designate one possessed by spirit-madness by these signs.

sanskrit_iast:
kusumairbahuvarṇaiśca gorasairvividhaistathā ..
bhūtapūjā tu karttavyā tena sampadyate sukhī .. 42 ..
meaning:
कुसुमैर्बहुवर्णैश्च गोरसैर्विविधैस्तथा ..
भूतपूजा तु कर्त्तव्या तेन सम्पद्यते सुखी .. 42 ..
text_mt: With many-colored blossoms and likewise with various milk products, / worship of the spirits must be performed; thereby he becomes happy.

sanskrit_iast:
śūnyāgāraśmaśānādricatuṣpathaniṣevakaḥ ..
rātrau carati yocchiṣṭaḥ piśāconmādito naraḥ .. 43 ..
meaning:
शून्यागारश्मशानाद्रिचतुष्पथनिषेवकः ..
रात्रौ चरति योच्छिष्टः पिशाचोन्मादितो नरः .. 43 ..
text_mt: Frequenting empty houses, cremation grounds, mountains, and crossroads, / a man driven mad by a piśāca roams about at night while polluted by leftover food.

sanskrit_iast:
piśācayajanaṃ tasya karttavyaṃ palalāmiṣaiḥ ..
kaṇṭakīsambhavaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaistathaiva ca .. 44 ..
meaning:
पिशाचयजनं तस्य कर्त्तव्यं पललामिषैः ..
कण्टकीसम्भवैः पुष्पैः कृष्णवर्णैस्तथैव च .. 44 ..
text_mt: A sacrifice to the piśācas must be performed for him with ground sesame, flesh, / flowers from thorny plants, and black-colored [offerings].

sanskrit_iast:
avyaktabhāṣī raktākṣo hāsye coccasvarastathā ..
raudraṃ nirīkṣate'tyarthaṃ yakṣenonmādito naraḥ ..45..
meaning:
अव्यक्तभाषी रक्ताक्षो हास्ये चोच्चस्वरस्तथा ..
रौद्रं निरीक्षतेऽत्यर्थं यक्षेनोन्मादितो नरः ..45..
text_mt: Speaking incoherently, red-eyed, laughing with a loud voice, / a man driven mad by a yakṣa glares terribly.

sanskrit_iast:
kulmāṣaghṛtapiṇyākapalalollopikāguḍaiḥ ..
yakṣāṇāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ doṣaśāntaye .. 46 ..
meaning:
कुल्माषघृतपिण्याकपललोल्लोपिकागुडैः ..
यक्षाणां पूजनं तस्य कर्तव्यं दोषशान्तये .. 46 ..
text_mt: Worship of the yakṣas must be performed for him with sour gruel, clarified butter, oil-cake, ground sesame, cakes, and molasses, / for the pacification of the affliction.

sanskrit_iast:
udvignacetāḥ śītaśca nātiśokaparāyaṇaḥ ..
rākṣasena gṛhītaśca bhavatyoṣṭhavilehakaḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
उद्विग्नचेताः शीतश्च नातिशोकपरायणः ..
राक्षसेन गृहीतश्च भवत्योष्ठविलेहकः .. 47 ..
text_mt: His mind agitated, feeling cold, not excessively prone to grief, / he who is seized by a rākṣasa constantly licks his lips.

sanskrit_iast:
pakvāmiṣeṇa māṃsena rudhireṇa tathaiva ca ..
rākṣasānāṃ baliḥ kāryastasya doṣapraśāntaye .. 48 ..
meaning:
पक्वामिषेण मांसेन रुधिरेण तथैव च ..
राक्षसानां बलिः कार्यस्तस्य दोषप्रशान्तये .. 48 ..
text_mt: An oblation must be made to the rākṣasas with cooked meat, raw flesh, / and blood, for the pacification of his affliction.

sanskrit_iast:
bhasmapāṃśurajodhvasto malino malināmbaraḥ ..
pretagṛhīto bhavati vikṛto dhvastamastakaḥ .. 49 ..
meaning:
भस्मपांशुरजोध्वस्तो मलिनो मलिनाम्बरः ..
प्रेतगृहीतो भवति विकृतो ध्वस्तमस्तकः .. 49 ..
text_mt: Covered in ash, dust, and grime, filthy, wearing dirty clothes, / he who is seized by a deceased spirit is deformed, with his head covered [in dust].

sanskrit_iast: odanaṃ madhupānīyaṃ sarpiḥ kṣīrasamanvitam .. 1.231.50 ..
meaning: ओदनं मधुपानीयं सर्पिः क्षीरसमन्वितम् .. 1.231.50 ..
text_mt: Boiled rice, honey-water, clarified butter mixed with milk,

sanskrit_iast:
pretānāṃ tatra dātavyaṃ tena saṃpadyate sukhī ..
śuciḥ śucisamācāraḥ sandhyācārī tilapriyaḥ .. 51 ..
meaning:
प्रेतानां तत्र दातव्यं तेन संपद्यते सुखी ..
शुचिः शुचिसमाचारः सन्ध्याचारी तिलप्रियः .. 51 ..
text_mt: must be given there to the deceased spirits; thereby he becomes happy. / Pure, pure in conduct, moving about at twilight, fond of sesame,

sanskrit_iast:
pitṛgrahagṛhītasya rūpametadvinirdiśeta ..
tilagorasapuṣpānnamadhumūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 52 ..
meaning:
पितृग्रहगृहीतस्य रूपमेतद्विनिर्दिशेत ..
तिलगोरसपुष्पान्नमधुमूलफलैः शुभैः .. 52 ..
text_mt: this is declared to be the appearance of one seized by the seizure of the ancestors. / With sesame, dairy products, flowers, food, honey, roots, and auspicious fruits,

sanskrit_iast:
dīpairdānaistathā nityaṃ praṇipātena cājñayā ..
pitṝṇāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya karttavyaṃ doṣaśāntaye .. 53 ..
meaning:
दीपैर्दानैस्तथा नित्यं प्रणिपातेन चाज्ञया ..
पितॄणां पूजनं तस्य कर्त्तव्यं दोषशान्तये .. 53 ..
text_mt: with lamps, gifts constantly, prostration, and obedience, / worship of the ancestors must be performed for him to pacify the affliction.

sanskrit_iast:
adhīte japate caiva śucistiṣṭhati cāpyatha ..
yogāsaktastathārṣeṇa gṛhīto mānavo bhavet .. 54 ..
meaning:
अधीते जपते चैव शुचिस्तिष्ठति चाप्यथ ..
योगासक्तस्तथार्षेण गृहीतो मानवो भवेत् .. 54 ..
text_mt: Reciting, muttering prayers, remaining pure, / and attached to yoga—a man seized by a seer [spirit] becomes such.

sanskrit_iast:
havirgorasapuṣpādyaistathā'dhyayanasaṃstavaiḥ ..
ṛṣīṇāṃ pūjanaṃ kāryaṃ tasya doṣapraśānnaye .. 55 ..
meaning:
हविर्गोरसपुष्पाद्यैस्तथाऽध्ययनसंस्तवैः ..
ऋषीणां पूजनं कार्यं तस्य दोषप्रशान्नये .. 55 ..
text_mt: Worship of the seers must be performed for him with sacrificial offerings, dairy products, flowers and the like, / as well as recitation and eulogies, for the pacification of his affliction.

sanskrit_iast:
karmaprasakto bhavati na nidrāṃ bhajate divā ..
pauruṣeṇa gṛhītasya lakṣaṇaṃ samudāhṛtama .. 56 ..
meaning:
कर्मप्रसक्तो भवति न निद्रां भजते दिवा ..
पौरुषेण गृहीतस्य लक्षणं समुदाहृतम .. 56 ..
text_mt: Constantly attached to activity, he does not take sleep by day— / this is declared to be the characteristic of one seized by a human [spirit].

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇānbhojayettatra miṣṭamannaṃ susaṃskṛtam ..
gandhamālyojvalānrājaṃstasya doṣapraśāntaye .. 57 ..
meaning:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्तत्र मिष्टमन्नं सुसंस्कृतम् ..
गन्धमाल्योज्वलान्राजंस्तस्य दोषप्रशान्तये .. 57 ..
text_mt: One should feed brahmins there with sweet, well-prepared food, / radiant with perfumes and garlands, O king, for the pacification of his affliction.

sanskrit_iast:
skandagrahagṛhītānāṃ bālānāṃ śṛṇu lakṣaṇama ..
roditi stanati dhyāti bhūmau svapiti cāsakṛt .. 58 ..
meaning:
स्कन्दग्रहगृहीतानां बालानां शृणु लक्षणम ..
रोदिति स्तनति ध्याति भूमौ स्वपिति चासकृत् .. 58 ..
text_mt: Hear the symptom of children seized by the seizure of Skanda: / he weeps, groans, broods, and sleeps repeatedly on the ground,

sanskrit_iast:
asambaddhapralāpī vā jñeyaḥ skandagrahārdditaḥ ..
raktaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalairmūlaiḥ bālakrīḍanakaistathā .. 59 ..
meaning:
असम्बद्धप्रलापी वा ज्ञेयः स्कन्दग्रहार्द्दितः ..
रक्तैः पुष्पैः फलैर्मूलैः बालक्रीडनकैस्तथा .. 59 ..
text_mt: or prattles incoherently—he is to be known as afflicted by the seizure of Skanda. / With red flowers, fruits, roots, and children’s toys,

sanskrit_iast:
ghaṇṭā ca kukkuṭaiḥ pūjā balinā vividhena ca ..
patākābhiśca karttavyā kumārasya mahātmanaḥ .. 1.231.60 ..
meaning:
घण्टा च कुक्कुटैः पूजा बलिना विविधेन च ..
पताकाभिश्च कर्त्तव्या कुमारस्य महात्मनः .. 1.231.60 ..
text_mt: and a bell, cocks, worship with diverse oblations, / and banners, [the rite] should be performed for the great-souled Kumāra.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ paraṃ lokahitaṃ tavādya sarvagrahaghnānnipuṇānprayogān ..
vakṣyāmi yeṣāṃ hi niṣevaṇena grahairvimucyanti narā narendrān .. 61 ..
1.232
.. nāḍāyana uvāca ..
abhyaṅgotsādanaṃ snānaṃ dhūpo rakṣābalirghṛtama ..
netrāñjanaṃ pradhavanaṃ navagrahaharāḥ kriyāḥ .. 1 ..
sarpagandhā vacā kuṣṭhamustākṣepaṇacandanaiḥ ..
sakṣīramūtrairvipacettailaṃ sarvagrahāpaham .. 2 ..
bilvamadhyaṃ brahmadatta gavākṣībṛhatīphalam ..
utsādanamidaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ ślakṣṇapiṣṭaṃ jalena tu .. 3 ..
uśīrakuṣṭhamañjiṣṭhādevadārumanaḥśilāḥ ..
śrīveṣṭakastathā kauntī haritālailavāluke .. 4 ..
etaccūrṇīkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ pañcagavyāṃśamiśritam ..
sarvagrahapraśamanaṃ snānamāyuṣyamuttamam ..5..
sarṣapāśca khuraṃ kuṣṭaṃ ghṛtaṃ bhallātakaṃ vacā..
pūtīkamajamodā ca dhūpaḥ sarvagrahāpahaḥ ..6..
meaning:
अतः परं लोकहितं तवाद्य सर्वग्रहघ्नान्निपुणान्प्रयोगान् ..
वक्ष्यामि येषां हि निषेवणेन ग्रहैर्विमुच्यन्ति नरा नरेन्द्रान् .. 61 ..
1.232
.. नाडायन उवाच ..
अभ्यङ्गोत्सादनं स्नानं धूपो रक्षाबलिर्घृतम ..
नेत्राञ्जनं प्रधवनं नवग्रहहराः क्रियाः .. 1 ..
सर्पगन्धा वचा कुष्ठमुस्ताक्षेपणचन्दनैः ..
सक्षीरमूत्रैर्विपचेत्तैलं सर्वग्रहापहम् .. 2 ..
बिल्वमध्यं ब्रह्मदत्त गवाक्षीबृहतीफलम् ..
उत्सादनमिदं श्रेष्ठं श्लक्ष्णपिष्टं जलेन तु .. 3 ..
उशीरकुष्ठमञ्जिष्ठादेवदारुमनःशिलाः ..
श्रीवेष्टकस्तथा कौन्ती हरितालैलवालुके .. 4 ..
एतच्चूर्णीकृतं सर्वं पञ्चगव्यांशमिश्रितम् ..
सर्वग्रहप्रशमनं स्नानमायुष्यमुत्तमम् ..5..
सर्षपाश्च खुरं कुष्टं घृतं भल्लातकं वचा..
पूतीकमजमोदा च धूपः सर्वग्रहापहः ..6..
text_mt:
Hereafter, for the welfare of the world, I shall tell you today skillful remedies destroying all seizures, / through the application of which men are freed from seizures, O best of kings.
1.232 / Nāḍāyana said: / Anointing, rubbing with paste, bathing, incense, protective oblation, clarified butter, / collyrium for the eyes, and fumigation are the rites that remove the nine seizures.
With sarpagandhā, sweet flag, costus, nut grass, akṣepaṇa, and sandalwood, / one should boil oil with milk and urine; it removes all seizures.
Bael pulp, brahmadatta, colocynth, and nightshade fruit— / this is an excellent paste for rubbing when finely ground with water.
Khus grass, costus, Indian madder, deodar cedar, realgar, / turpentine resin, kauntī, orpiment, and elavāluka—
all this powdered and mixed with a portion of the five products of the cow / is an excellent bath that pacifies all seizures and promotes longevity.
Mustard seeds, hoof, costus, clarified butter, marking nut, sweet flag, / pūtīka, and bishop's weed are an incense that removes all seizures.

śastraṃ vā rocanaṃ śastaṃ suvarṇaṃ maṇimauktikam ..
viṣaṃ savatsāṃ dhenuṃ ca mattaṃ chāgaṃ tathaiva ca .. 7 ..
pūrṇakumbhaṃ ca maṃtrāśca vīṇā candanameva ca ..
mayūrapakṣānrajataṃ samārgaṇaguṇaṃ dhanuḥ .. 8 ..
bhallātakāni sarpiśca rakṣārthaṃ dhārayedgṛhe ..
puṣpairdhūpaistathā gandhairbhakṣyairnānāvidhaistathā .. 9 ..
pūrṇakumbhaiḥ sakulmāṣairgorasaiścandanena ca ..

It is named Mahāpaiśācaka, warding off all seizures. / Extract of Indian barberry, the three pungents, Indian madder, and realgar—
having ground equal parts with goat's urine, one should fashion a wick; / drying it in the shade, one should prepare that collyrium which destroys seizures.
White jyotiṣmatī and the three pungents wrapped in a cloth thread / and dried in the shade, then ground again, should be known as a wholesome pacifier.
For those who have the worship of the gods, guru, and twice-born, and supreme devotion to the Wielder of the Discus and Mace, / the blazing fires arising from seizures do not prevail, O foremost of kings.
1.233 / Śailūṣa said: / Having heard of the seizures that took refuge with Skanda, what Śatakratu / did, O illustrious one, tell that to me who am asking.
Nāḍāyana said: / Having heard of those who had taken refuge with Skanda, Śatamakhu went / together with the hosts of gods to where Skanda was stationed.
