They all collapsed onto the floor of their chariots, unconscious, / and were all carried away from the battle by their charioteers.
Then Bharata, enraged, with four arrows, / rendered [Śailūṣa's] horses lifeless in the combat, O Yādava,
and with flights of arrows he thwarted his prowess. / Then, checking the force of the high-souled [Bharata's] arrows with steadfastness,
[Śailūṣa], mighty and well-armoured, quickly mounted [another] chariot. / Having mounted the chariot, he deeply pierced Bharata in the chest
with a straight-jointed arrow, and, struck [by it], Bharata swooned. / At that moment, a cry of dismay was raised by gods and Asuras,
the one [side] despondent and the other overjoyed, as the descendant of Raghu was stupefied. / Through that loud cry of dismay, that descendant of Raghu regained his senses;
drawing his bow forcefully, he cut the great bow of Śailūṣa / into two pieces, O best of kings, and struck Śailūṣa severely.
His bow severed, swiftly taking up a mace with speed, / he hurled it, O knower of dharma, at the high-souled Bharata.

sa mohayitvā bharataṃ mokṣayāmāsa pārthiva ..
mokṣayitvā ca rājānaṃ gate'staṃ ravimaṇḍale ..19..
kṛtvāvahāraṃ tu gataḥ śibirāya narādhipaḥ ..1.265.20..
hatvā rathe nāgarathāśvayodhānsaṃprāpya madhye niśitaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ ..
raghupravīro'pi gṛhāya yātaḥ saṃpūjyamāno bhuvi mānavendraiḥ .. 21 ..
meaning:
आपतन्तीं गदां दृष्ट्वा भरतो रणमूर्धनि ..
द्विधा चकार चक्रेण सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः .. 14 ..
ततः स परिघं शीघ्रं चिक्षेप भरतं प्रति ..
तमापतन्तं चिच्छेद चतुर्भिः सायकैर्दृढम् .. 15 ..
ततोऽन्यद्धनुरादाय सायकानेकविंशतिम् ..
चिक्षेप स महाराज भरतस्य रथं प्रति.. 16 ..
छित्त्वा तान्भरतः सर्वान्नवधीत्तस्य सारथिम् ..
तथा च चतुरो वाहाननयद्यमसादनम् .. 17 ..
शैलूषं विरथं दृष्ट्वा गन्धर्वाणां महाचमूः ..
ववर्षायुधवर्षेण मेघो वृष्ट्येव पर्वतम् .. 18 ..
स मोहयित्वा भरतं मोक्षयामास पार्थिव ..
मोक्षयित्वा च राजानं गतेऽस्तं रविमण्डले ..19..
कृत्वावहारं तु गतः शिबिराय नराधिपः ..1.265.20..
हत्वा रथे नागरथाश्वयोधान्संप्राप्य मध्ये निशितैः पृषत्कैः ..
रघुप्रवीरोऽपि गृहाय यातः संपूज्यमानो भुवि मानवेन्द्रैः .. 21 ..
text_mt:
Seeing the mace flying towards him at the front of the battle, / Bharata cut it in two with a discus, before the eyes of the entire army.
Then he swiftly hurled an iron club towards Bharata; / as it was flying toward him, he firmly severed it with four arrows.
Then, seizing another bow, O great king, / he hurled twenty-one arrows towards Bharata's chariot.
Splitting all of them, Bharata killed his charioteer, / and likewise sent his four horses to the abode of Yama.
Seeing Śailūṣa deprived of his chariot, the great army of the Gandharvas / rained down a shower of weapons, like a cloud [raining] water upon a mountain.
Bewildering Bharata, it rescued [him], O king; / and having rescued the king, when the disc of the sun had set,
having sounded the retreat, the lord of men went to his camp.
Having slain the warriors on elephants, chariots, and horses in their midst with sharp arrows from his chariot, / the foremost hero of the Raghus also went to his dwelling, praised on earth by the lords of men.

sanskrit_iast:
1.266
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
tatastu saptame prāpte divase yuddhadurmadau ..
samīyaturmahātmānau śailūṣabharatāvubhau .. 1 ..
meaning:
1.266
.. मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
ततस्तु सप्तमे प्राप्ते दिवसे युद्धदुर्मदौ ..
समीयतुर्महात्मानौ शैलूषभरतावुभौ .. 1 ..
text_mt: 1.266 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, when the seventh day arrived, the two high-souled warriors, / both Śailūṣa and Bharata, passionate for battle, met.
title: Śailūṣavadhaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu bharataḥ prāha śailūṣaṃ yuddhadurmadam ..
āvayoḥ prastutaṃ sainyaṃ kimetaissainikairmṛtaiḥ .. 2 ..
meaning:
ततस्तु भरतः प्राह शैलूषं युद्धदुर्मदम् ..
आवयोः प्रस्तुतं सैन्यं किमेतैस्सैनिकैर्मृतैः .. 2 ..
text_mt: Then Bharata spoke to Śailūṣa, who was passionate for battle: / 'Our army is prepared; what is the use of these dead soldiers?

sanskrit_iast:
nivārayasva sainyaṃ svaṃ vārayiṣyāmyahaṃ svakam ..
āvayordvairathaṃ yuddhaṃ paśyantu vasudhādhipāḥ .. 3 ..
meaning:
निवारयस्व सैन्यं स्वं वारयिष्याम्यहं स्वकम् ..
आवयोर्द्वैरथं युद्धं पश्यन्तु वसुधाधिपाः .. 3 ..
text_mt: Restrain your own army, and I shall restrain mine; / let the rulers of the earth watch a duel of single chariots between the two of us,

sanskrit_iast:
tvadīyāḥ sainikā ye ca suranāthāḥ sahāmaraiḥ ..
hate mayi madīyanta sainyaṃ kāmaṃ prayudhyatām .. 4 ..
meaning:
त्वदीयाः सैनिका ये च सुरनाथाः सहामरैः ..
हते मयि मदीयन्त सैन्यं कामं प्रयुध्यताम् .. 4 ..
text_mt: as well as your soldiers, and the lords of the gods together with the immortals. / If I am slain, let my army fight at will,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃgrāmaṃ vā karotvājau tvadīyantu hate tvayi ..
evamuktastathetyuktvā vārayāmāsa sainikān .. 5 ..
meaning:
संग्रामं वा करोत्वाजौ त्वदीयन्तु हते त्वयि ..
एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा वारयामास सैनिकान् .. 5 ..
text_mt: or let yours do battle in the field if you are slain.' / Being addressed thus, he said, 'So be it,' and restrained his soldiers,

sanskrit_iast:
gandharvarāṭ sa śailūṣo bharato'pi tathā svakān ..
tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tayordevāsuropamam .. 6 ..
meaning:
गन्धर्वराट् स शैलूषो भरतोऽपि तथा स्वकान् ..
ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तयोर्देवासुरोपमम् .. 6 ..
text_mt: that king of the Gandharvas, Śailūṣa, and Bharata likewise his own. / Then a battle began between the two of them, like that of the gods and asuras,

sanskrit_iast:
paśyatāṃ sarva sainyānāṃ devānāmapi paśyatām ..
śarajālena mahatā chāditārkakare raṇe .. 7 ..
meaning:
पश्यतां सर्व सैन्यानां देवानामपि पश्यताम् ..
शरजालेन महता छादितार्ककरे रणे .. 7 ..
text_mt: while all the armies looked on, and even while the gods looked on, / in a conflict where the rays of the sun were covered by a great net of arrows.

sanskrit_iast:
tatakṣatustāvanyo'nyaṃ śaraiḥ sannataparvabhiḥ ..
parasparaśarāghāta visaracchoṇitokṣitau .. 8 ..
meaning:
ततक्षतुस्तावन्योऽन्यं शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ..
परस्परशराघात विसरच्छोणितोक्षितौ .. 8 ..
text_mt: The two slashed each other with straight-jointed arrows; / sprayed with blood flowing from the strikes of each other's arrows,

sanskrit_iast:
virejatustau rājendra puṣpitāviva kiṃśukau ..
ubhau mahārathau vīrau cobhau viśrutapauruṣau .. 9 ..
meaning:
विरेजतुस्तौ राजेन्द्र पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ ..
उभौ महारथौ वीरौ चोभौ विश्रुतपौरुषौ .. 9 ..
text_mt: the two shone, O best of kings, like two blossoming kiṃśuka trees. / Both were great chariot-warriors, heroes, and both of renowned prowess,

sanskrit_iast:
tathobhau varadhānuṣkau cobhau samaradurmadau ..
kāñcanāṅgarathasthau tau cobhau saddhvajaśobhitau .. 1.266.10 ..
meaning:
तथोभौ वरधानुष्कौ चोभौ समरदुर्मदौ ..
काञ्चनाङ्गरथस्थौ तौ चोभौ सद्ध्वजशोभितौ .. 1.266.10 ..
text_mt: and both were excellent archers, and both passionate in battle; / mounted on chariots with gold fittings, both were adorned with noble standards,

sanskrit_iast:
vījyamānau tathaivobhau yodhābhyāṃ varacāmaraiḥ ..
chatrayostau tadādhastācchuśubhāte mahārathau .. 11 ..
meaning:
वीज्यमानौ तथैवोभौ योधाभ्यां वरचामरैः ..
छत्रयोस्तौ तदाधस्ताच्छुशुभाते महारथौ .. 11 ..
text_mt: and both were likewise fanned by warriors with excellent chowries; / beneath their two parasols, the two great chariot-warriors shone at that time.

sanskrit_iast:
ubhāvastrapratāpena cakratustumulaṃ raṇam ..
astrayuddhaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā śarayuddhaṃ pracakratuḥ .. 12 ..
meaning:
उभावस्त्रप्रतापेन चक्रतुस्तुमुलं रणम् ..
अस्त्रयुद्धं चिरं कृत्वा शरयुद्धं प्रचक्रतुः .. 12 ..
text_mt: Both engaged in a tumultuous fight with the power of divine weapons; / having fought for a long time with divine weapons, they waged a battle of arrows.

sanskrit_iast:
śarayuddhe vyatikrānte astrayuddhaṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..
evaṃ tau divasaṃ kṛtvā yuddhaṃ saṃśrāntavāhanau .. 13 ..
meaning:
शरयुद्धे व्यतिक्रान्ते अस्त्रयुद्धं पुनःपुनः ..
एवं तौ दिवसं कृत्वा युद्धं संश्रान्तवाहनौ .. 13 ..
text_mt: When the battle of arrows had passed, [they fought] again and again with divine weapons; / having fought in this way for a day, their steeds exhausted,

sanskrit_iast:
ropayantau śramaṃ rājansamareṣu jitaśramau ..
tato gandharvarājastu lambamāne divākare .. 14 ..
meaning:
रोपयन्तौ श्रमं राजन्समरेषु जितश्रमौ ..
ततो गन्धर्वराजस्तु लम्बमाने दिवाकरे .. 14 ..
text_mt: healing their weariness, O king, having overcome exhaustion in battles; / then, as the sun was setting, the king of the Gandharvas

sanskrit_iast:
cakāra tāmasīṃ māyāṃ yayāndhamabhavajjagat ..
andhakāre tato jāte vāco'śrūyanta dāruṇāḥ .. .. 15 ..
meaning:
चकार तामसीं मायां ययान्धमभवज्जगत् ..
अन्धकारे ततो जाते वाचोऽश्रूयन्त दारुणाः .. .. 15 ..
text_mt: created an illusion of darkness by which the world became blind; / then, when darkness had arisen, dreadful voices were heard:

sanskrit_iast:
bharato hanyatāṃ śīghraṃ bhakṣyatāṃ pātyatāṃ tathā ..
abhyavartanta bharataṃ sarpavṛścikakarkaṭāḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
भरतो हन्यतां शीघ्रं भक्ष्यतां पात्यतां तथा ..
अभ्यवर्तन्त भरतं सर्पवृश्चिककर्कटाः .. 16 ..
text_mt: 'Let Bharata be quickly slain! Let him be devoured! And let him be struck down!' / Serpents, scorpions, and crabs advanced against Bharata,

sanskrit_iast:
markaṭā vānarā ghorāḥ sṛgālā dvīpinastathā ..
siṃhavyāghravarāhāśca kravyādā ye ca jātayaḥ .. 17 ..
meaning:
मर्कटा वानरा घोराः सृगाला द्वीपिनस्तथा ..
सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाश्च क्रव्यादा ये च जातयः .. 17 ..
text_mt: as did monkeys, terrible apes, jackals, and leopards, / lions, tigers, boars, and whatever kinds of carnivorous beasts [there are].

sanskrit_iast:
ardyamānaḥ sa dharmātmā bharatastaiḥ sudurmukhaiḥ ..
saureṇāstreṇa tāṃ māyāṃ babhañja paravīrahā .. 18 ..
meaning:
अर्द्यमानः स धर्मात्मा भरतस्तैः सुदुर्मुखैः ..
सौरेणास्त्रेण तां मायां बभञ्ज परवीरहा .. 18 ..
text_mt: Tormented by those fierce-faced creatures, that righteous / Bharata, slayer of enemy heroes, shattered that illusion with the weapon of the Sun.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu mahatīṃ māyāṃ sa cakāra mahābhujaḥ ..
uttasthau sumahānmeghaśchādayitvā nabhastalam..19..
meaning:
ततस्तु महतीं मायां स चकार महाभुजः ..
उत्तस्थौ सुमहान्मेघश्छादयित्वा नभस्तलम्..19..
text_mt: Then that mighty-armed one created a great illusion: / a colossal cloud arose, covering the vault of the sky,

sanskrit_iast:
pravavarṣa ca ghorāṇi śastrajālānyanekaśaḥ ..
nārācānardhanārācām̐stathaiva caṣakānanān .. 1.266.20 ..
meaning:
प्रववर्ष च घोराणि शस्त्रजालान्यनेकशः ..
नाराचानर्धनाराचाम्̐स्तथैव चषकाननान् .. 1.266.20 ..
text_mt: and rained down manifold terrible masses of weapons: / iron arrows, half-iron shafts, and likewise cup-mouthed arrows,

sanskrit_iast:
vatsadantām̐stathā vallānkarṇinālīkagomukhān ..
kṣuraprānardhacandrāṃśca varāhavadanāṃstathā .. 21 ..
meaning:
वत्सदन्ताम्̐स्तथा वल्लान्कर्णिनालीकगोमुखान् ..
क्षुरप्रानर्धचन्द्रांश्च वराहवदनांस्तथा .. 21 ..
text_mt: calf-toothed arrows, vallas, barbed arrows, tubular arrows, ox-faced arrows, / razor-faced arrows, crescent-headed shafts, and boar-faced arrows,

sanskrit_iast:
gadābhuśuṇḍīḥ prāsāṃśca bhiṇḍipālānparaśvadhān ..
huḍānguḍānsalaguḍām̐ścakrakhaḍgāṃstathā parān . .. 22 ..
meaning:
गदाभुशुण्डीः प्रासांश्च भिण्डिपालान्परश्वधान् ..
हुडान्गुडान्सलगुडाम्̐श्चक्रखड्गांस्तथा परान् . .. 22 ..
text_mt: clubs, bhuśuṇḍīs, darts, javelins, axes, / huḍas, guḍas together with bludgeons, discuses, swords, and others.

sanskrit_iast:
etānanyāṃśca vividhānvavarṣa paramāyudhān..
patadbhirāyudhairghorairvādhyamānaḥ sa rāghavaḥ .. 23 ..
meaning:
एतानन्यांश्च विविधान्ववर्ष परमायुधान्..
पतद्भिरायुधैर्घोरैर्वाध्यमानः स राघवः .. 23 ..
text_mt: These and various other supreme weapons he showered down. / Being afflicted by the terrible falling weapons, that descendant of Raghu

sanskrit_iast:
vāyavyāstreṇa tāṃ māyāṃ nāśayāmāsa śatruhā ..
tato babhūva rājendra gandharvaḥ parvato mahān .. 24 ..
meaning:
वायव्यास्त्रेण तां मायां नाशयामास शत्रुहा ..
ततो बभूव राजेन्द्र गन्धर्वः पर्वतो महान् .. 24 ..
text_mt: destroyed that illusion with the weapon of the Wind, that slayer of foes. / Then, O best of kings, the Gandharva became a great mountain,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣaratprasravaṇo ghoraḥ śikharaiśca samucchritaiḥ ..
māyāṃ tāṃ pārvatīṃ śrīmānvajrāstreṇa raghūdvahaḥ .. 25 ..
meaning:
क्षरत्प्रस्रवणो घोरः शिखरैश्च समुच्छ्रितैः ..
मायां तां पार्वतीं श्रीमान्वज्रास्त्रेण रघूद्वहः .. 25 ..
text_mt: dreadful with flowing torrents and lofty peaks. / With the weapon of the Thunderbolt, the glorious scion of Raghu

sanskrit_iast:
nāśayāmāsa rājendra sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ ..
hanyamānāsu māyāsu rūpām̐ścakre sudāruṇān .. 26 ..
meaning:
नाशयामास राजेन्द्र सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः ..
हन्यमानासु मायासु रूपाम्̐श्चक्रे सुदारुणान् .. 26 ..
text_mt: destroyed that mountainous illusion, O best of kings, while all the army looked on. / As his illusions were being destroyed, he assumed exceedingly terrible forms

sanskrit_iast:
yakṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca piśācānāṃ patattriṇām ..
siṃhavyāghratarakṣūṇāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 27 ..
meaning:
यक्षाणां राक्षसानां च पिशाचानां पतत्त्रिणाम् ..
सिंहव्याघ्रतरक्षूणां कुञ्जराणां तथैव च .. 27 ..
text_mt: of yakṣas, rākṣasas, piśācas, and birds, / and likewise of lions, tigers, hyenas, and elephants.

sanskrit_iast:
babhañja tasya māyāstā divyāstrairbharato ruṣā ..
hanyamānāsu māyāsu lāghavādbharataṃ raṇe .. 28 ..
meaning:
बभञ्ज तस्य मायास्ता दिव्यास्त्रैर्भरतो रुषा ..
हन्यमानासु मायासु लाघवाद्भरतं रणे .. 28 ..
text_mt: Bharata angrily shattered those illusions of his with divine weapons. / While his illusions were being destroyed, in the battle, through his agility,

sanskrit_iast:
mohayāmāsa rājendra śailūṣo raṇadarpitaḥ ..
bharato'pi dhanuṣkoṭyāṃ śarāgre ca nilīyate..29..
meaning:
मोहयामास राजेन्द्र शैलूषो रणदर्पितः ..
भरतोऽपि धनुष्कोट्यां शराग्रे च निलीयते..29..
text_mt: Śailūṣa, proud in battle, bewildered Bharata, O best of kings. / And Bharata concealed himself on the tip of the bow and on the point of the arrow,

sanskrit_iast:
dhvajāgre ca rathāgre ca turagāgre punaḥ punaḥ ..
sāyakānbhāratāñśaighryāddhvaṃsayāmāsa yādava .. 1.266.30..
meaning:
ध्वजाग्रे च रथाग्रे च तुरगाग्रे पुनः पुनः ..
सायकान्भारताञ्शैघ्र्याद्ध्वंसयामास यादव .. 1.266.30..
text_mt: and on the tip of the standard, the front of the chariot, and the head of the horse repeatedly; / with swiftness, O descendant of Yadu, he destroyed Bharata's arrows.

sanskrit_iast:
rāghavāstutuṣustasya devadaityāśca saṃghaśaḥ ..
asurā mumucurghoramaṭṭahāsaṃ sudāruṇama ..31..
meaning:
राघवास्तुतुषुस्तस्य देवदैत्याश्च संघशः ..
असुरा मुमुचुर्घोरमट्टहासं सुदारुणम ..31..
text_mt: The descendants of Raghu were pleased with him, as were the gods and daityas in crowds; / the asuras released a terrible, exceedingly dreadful roar of laughter.

sanskrit_iast:
daityānāmaṭṭahāsena bharataḥ kupito bhṛśam ..
nārāyaṇāstraṃ saṃyojya śareṇānataparvaṇā..32..
meaning:
दैत्यानामट्टहासेन भरतः कुपितो भृशम् ..
नारायणास्त्रं संयोज्य शरेणानतपर्वणा..32..
text_mt: At the loud laughter of the daityas, Bharata was greatly enraged; / having fitted the weapon of Nārāyaṇa with a straight-jointed arrow,

sanskrit_iast:
iyeṣa hantuṃ taṃ krodhādgandharvaṃ raṇagarvitam ..
astraṃ tatsaṃhṛtaṃ jñātvā jagāma svaṃ rathaṃ tvaran ..33..
meaning:
इयेष हन्तुं तं क्रोधाद्गन्धर्वं रणगर्वितम् ..
अस्त्रं तत्संहृतं ज्ञात्वा जगाम स्वं रथं त्वरन् ..33..
text_mt: he wished in fury to slay that Gandharva proud in battle. / Knowing that weapon to be withdrawn, he went swiftly to his own chariot.

sanskrit_iast:
iyeṣa hantuṃ taṃ cāstraṃ rudrāstreṇa tu dāruṇam..
etasminneva kāle tu mumoca bharataḥ śaram..34..
meaning:
इयेष हन्तुं तं चास्त्रं रुद्रास्त्रेण तु दारुणम्..
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मुमोच भरतः शरम्..34..
text_mt: And he wished to slay that dreadful weapon with the weapon of Rudra; / and at that very moment Bharata released an arrow,

sanskrit_iast:
kālānalasamaprakhyaṃ sapuṅkhaṃ saphalaṃ tathā ..
rājitaṃ vainateyasya pakṣaiḥ śatruvināśanam .. 35 ..
meaning:
कालानलसमप्रख्यं सपुङ्खं सफलं तथा ..
राजितं वैनतेयस्य पक्षैः शत्रुविनाशनम् .. 35 ..
text_mt: resembling the fire of destruction, with shaft and point, / shining with the feathers of Vainateya, destroying foes.

sanskrit_iast:
hatvā rudrāstravegantu rathasthasya mahīpateḥ ..
bibheda hṛdayaṃ rājanvarma bhittvātha kāñcanam .. 36 ..
meaning:
हत्वा रुद्रास्त्रवेगन्तु रथस्थस्य महीपतेः ..
बिभेद हृदयं राजन्वर्म भित्त्वाथ काञ्चनम् .. 36 ..
text_mt:
Destroying the force of the Rudra-weapon, it pierced the golden armour
and then the heart, O king, of the lord of the earth standing in his chariot.

sanskrit_iast:
rājñaśca hadayaṃ bhittvā bhittvā ca vasudhātalam ..
snātvā rasātalāmbhaḥsu tūṇaṃ punarupāgamat ..37..
meaning:
राज्ञश्च हदयं भित्त्वा भित्त्वा च वसुधातलम् ..
स्नात्वा रसातलाम्भःसु तूणं पुनरुपागमत् ..37..
text_mt:
And having pierced the king's heart and split the surface of the earth,
it bathed in the waters of the netherworld and returned swiftly to the quiver.

sanskrit_iast:
gandharvarājo'bhihataḥ śareṇā nataparvaṇā ..
rathanīḍe dhanustyaktvā mamāra paravīrahā .. 38 ..
meaning:
गन्धर्वराजोऽभिहतः शरेणा नतपर्वणा ..
रथनीडे धनुस्त्यक्त्वा ममार परवीरहा .. 38 ..
text_mt:
Struck down by that straight-jointed arrow, the king of the Gandharvas,
slayer of enemy heroes, dropped his bow in the chariot-box and died.

sanskrit_iast:
pitaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā śailūṣatanayā raṇe ..
krodhaduḥkhaparītānte bharataṃ raṇakarkaśam .. .. 39 ..
meaning:
पितरं निहतं दृष्ट्वा शैलूषतनया रणे ..
क्रोधदुःखपरीतान्ते भरतं रणकर्कशम् .. .. 39 ..
text_mt:
Seeing their father slain in battle, the sons of Śailūṣa,
filled with wrath and sorrow, [surrounded] Bharata, who was fierce in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
vivyadhurbhūpatiśreṣṭha bāṇairāśīviṣopamaiḥ ..
āyudhairvividhākāraistadā te vai raṇājire .. 1.266.40 ..
meaning:
विव्यधुर्भूपतिश्रेष्ठ बाणैराशीविषोपमैः ..
आयुधैर्विविधाकारैस्तदा ते वै रणाजिरे .. 1.266.40 ..
text_mt:
They pierced him, O best of kings, with arrows resembling venomous serpents,
and then with weapons of diverse forms on the field of battle.

sanskrit_iast:
māyāśca vividhāścakrurbharatasya vipattaye ..
antarikṣaṃ ca tairvyāptaṃ nānāhetipravarṣibhiḥ .. 41 ..
meaning:
मायाश्च विविधाश्चक्रुर्भरतस्य विपत्तये ..
अन्तरिक्षं च तैर्व्याप्तं नानाहेतिप्रवर्षिभिः .. 41 ..
text_mt:
They also wrought diverse illusions for Bharata's destruction,
and the sky was filled by them raining down various missiles.

sanskrit_iast:
astraiśca kecidbharataṃ pravavarṣurmahārathāḥ ..
bhūribhāvātsa yodhānāṃ mahāstrāṇāṃ mahābalāt .. 42 ..
meaning:
अस्त्रैश्च केचिद्भरतं प्रववर्षुर्महारथाः ..
भूरिभावात्स योधानां महास्त्राणां महाबलात् .. 42 ..
text_mt:
And some great chariot-warriors showered Bharata with divine weapons.
Because of the vast multitude of warriors and the great might of their supreme weapons,

sanskrit_iast:
pratāpādastrajālānāṃ saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ ..
kālāstramatha sāṃvartaṃ mumoca bharatastadā .. 43 ..
meaning:
प्रतापादस्त्रजालानां संशयं परमं गताः ..
कालास्त्रमथ सांवर्तं मुमोच भरतस्तदा .. 43 ..
text_mt:
and the fiery power of the nets of weapons, they fell into the greatest peril.
Then Bharata released the Kālāstra, the weapon of cosmic dissolution.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādastrātsahasrāṇi śastrāṇāṃ niryayustadā ..
gandharvasainyaṃ sakalamastraistaiḥ pratyahanyata .. 44 ..
meaning:
तस्मादस्त्रात्सहस्राणि शस्त्राणां निर्ययुस्तदा ..
गन्धर्वसैन्यं सकलमस्त्रैस्तैः प्रत्यहन्यत .. 44 ..
text_mt:
From that weapon thousands of blades then issued forth;
by those weapons the entire army of the Gandharvas was struck down.

sanskrit_iast:
śastraiḥ kecidviśirasaḥ kṛtvā gandharvasattamāḥ ..
vivāhāśca kṛtāḥ kaicitkecidrājandvidhā kṛtāḥ .. 45 ..
meaning:
शस्त्रैः केचिद्विशिरसः कृत्वा गन्धर्वसत्तमाः ..
विवाहाश्च कृताः कैचित्केचिद्राजन्द्विधा कृताः .. 45 ..
text_mt:
Some of the foremost Gandharvas were made headless by the blades;
some were severed of arms, and some, O king, were cut in two.

sanskrit_iast:
kecidvivāhavaścaiva kecidvyaṅgāśca yādava ..
gandharvāṇāṃ ca tāḥ koṭyastisraḥ saṃgrāmaśālinām .. 46 ..
meaning:
केचिद्विवाहवश्चैव केचिद्व्यङ्गाश्च यादव ..
गन्धर्वाणां च ताः कोट्यस्तिस्रः संग्रामशालिनाम् .. 46 ..
text_mt:
Some were deprived of their arms, and some were mutilated of limbs, O Yādava.
And those three hundred million Gandharvas, renowned in battle,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣaṇenāstraprapātena bharatena nipā titāḥ ..
gandharvasainye nihate pravavurmārutāḥ śivāḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
क्षणेनास्त्रप्रपातेन भरतेन निपा तिताः ..
गन्धर्वसैन्ये निहते प्रववुर्मारुताः शिवाः .. 47 ..
text_mt:
were struck down in an instant by the fall of Bharata's weapon.
When the army of the Gandharvas was slain, auspicious winds blew.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpavarṣaṃ papātātha bharatasya tu mūrdhani ..
diśaśca nirmalībhūtā devānāṃ vigataṃ bhayam .. 48 ..
meaning:
पुष्पवर्षं पपाताथ भरतस्य तु मूर्धनि ..
दिशश्च निर्मलीभूता देवानां विगतं भयम् .. 48 ..
text_mt:
A shower of flowers then fell upon Bharata's head;
the quarters became clear, and the fear of the gods departed.

sanskrit_iast:
tato devaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sarvaiḥ suragaṇaiḥ samam ..
vimānastho babhāṣedaṃ bharataṃ dharmavatsalam .. 49 ..
meaning:
ततो देवः सहस्राक्षः सर्वैः सुरगणैः समम् ..
विमानस्थो बभाषेदं भरतं धर्मवत्सलम् .. 49 ..
text_mt:
Then the thousand-eyed god, along with all the hosts of gods,
situated in his celestial chariot, spoke thus to Bharata, who was devoted to dharma:

sanskrit_iast:
indra uvāca .. ..
pitāmahavarodrekādavadhyaṃ devatāgaṇaiḥ ..
hatavānasi śailūṣaṃ devabrāhmaṇakaṇṭakam .. 1.266.50 ..
meaning:
इन्द्र उवाच .. ..
पितामहवरोद्रेकादवध्यं देवतागणैः ..
हतवानसि शैलूषं देवब्राह्मणकण्टकम् .. 1.266.50 ..

sanskrit_iast:
yasmāttasmādvaraṃ matto gṛhāṇa raghunandana ..
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
śatakratorniśamyaitadbharato vākyamabravīt .. 51 ..
meaning:
यस्मात्तस्माद्वरं मत्तो गृहाण रघुनन्दन ..
.. मार्कण्डेय उवाच .. ..
शतक्रतोर्निशम्यैतद्भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत् .. 51 ..
text_mt:
Therefore, receive a boon from me, O descendant of Raghu.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having heard this speech of Śatakratu, Bharata said:

sanskrit_iast:
.. bharata uvāca .. ..
tvamīśaḥ sarvadevānāṃ tavedaṃ sakalaṃ jagat ..
acireṇaiva maraṇaṃ tvadājñābhaṅgakāraṇāma .. 52 ..
meaning:
.. भरत उवाच .. ..
त्वमीशः सर्वदेवानां तवेदं सकलं जगत् ..
अचिरेणैव मरणं त्वदाज्ञाभङ्गकारणाम .. 52 ..
text_mt:
Bharata said:
You are the lord of all the gods; this entire world belongs to you.
Death comes before long because of disobedience to your command.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavaṃtīha sadā loke nimittaṃ madvidho janaḥ ..
prajāpatikṛtaṃ bhedaṃ ko moktuṃ jagati kṣamaḥ .. 53 ..
meaning:
भवंतीह सदा लोके निमित्तं मद्विधो जनः ..
प्रजापतिकृतं भेदं को मोक्तुं जगति क्षमः .. 53 ..
text_mt:
People like me in this world are always merely an instrument;
who in the world is able to set aside the distinction ordained by Prajāpati?

sanskrit_iast:
varaśca yadi me deyastvayā deva pradīyatāma ..
sindhorubhayakūleṣu kariṣyāmi puradvayam .. 54 ..
meaning:
वरश्च यदि मे देयस्त्वया देव प्रदीयताम ..
सिन्धोरुभयकूलेषु करिष्यामि पुरद्वयम् .. 54 ..
text_mt:
And if a boon is to be given to me by you, O god, let it be granted:
I shall build two cities on both banks of the Indus,

sanskrit_iast:
gaṃdharvarakṣite deśe putrayorubhayoḥ kṛte ..
nirveśaṃ tadavāpnotu prasādena śatakrato .. 55 ..
meaning:
गंधर्वरक्षिते देशे पुत्रयोरुभयोः कृते ..
निर्वेशं तदवाप्नोतु प्रसादेन शतक्रतो .. 55 ..
text_mt:
in the realm guarded by the Gandharvas, for my two sons;
by your grace, O Śatakratu, may it find peace and settlement.

sanskrit_iast:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
evamastvityathoktvaiva svarlokaṃ vāsavo yayau ..
vāsave tu gate nākaṃ rājā citrarathastataḥ .. 56 ..
meaning:
.. मार्कण्डेय उवाच .. ..
एवमस्त्वित्यथोक्त्वैव स्वर्लोकं वासवो ययौ ..
वासवे तु गते नाकं राजा चित्ररथस्ततः .. 56 ..
text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Saying 'So be it,' Vāsava then departed for the celestial world.
When Vāsava had gone to heaven, King Citraratha then,

sanskrit_iast:
gaṃdharvāṇāṃ mahātejā bharataṃ vākyamabravīt ..
.. citraratha uvāca .. ..
gaṃdharvā nihatā vīrā madājñābhaṅgakāriṇaḥ .. 57 ..
meaning:
गंधर्वाणां महातेजा भरतं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ..
.. चित्ररथ उवाच .. ..
गंधर्वा निहता वीरा मदाज्ञाभङ्गकारिणः .. 57 ..
text_mt:
the immensely resplendent [king] of the Gandharvas, spoke these words to Bharata.
Citraratha said:
The heroic Gandharvas, who disobeyed my command,

sanskrit_iast:
tvayā te dharmanityena devabrāhmaṇakaṇṭakāḥ ..
tanme samuddhṛtaṃ śalyaṃ devānāñca priyaṃ kṛtam .. 58 ..
meaning:
त्वया ते धर्मनित्येन देवब्राह्मणकण्टकाः ..
तन्मे समुद्धृतं शल्यं देवानाञ्च प्रियं कृतम् .. 58 ..
text_mt:
and were thorns in the side of gods and brahmins, have been slain by you, who are constant in dharma.
Thereby that dart of mine has been removed, and what is pleasing to the gods has been accomplished.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmātsabhājayitvā tvāṃ yāsyāmi tridivaṃ punaḥ ..
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
bharatastamuvācātha gandharvā nihatā mayā .. 59 ..
meaning:
तस्मात्सभाजयित्वा त्वां यास्यामि त्रिदिवं पुनः ..
.. मार्कण्डेय उवाच .. ..
भरतस्तमुवाचाथ गन्धर्वा निहता मया .. 59 ..

sanskrit_iast:
tata enaṃ janaṃ teṣāṃ striyaśca paripālaya ..
gandharvāḥ paripālyāste teṣāṃ tvaṃ paripālakaḥ .. 1.266.60 ..
meaning:
तत एनं जनं तेषां स्त्रियश्च परिपालय ..
गन्धर्वाः परिपाल्यास्ते तेषां त्वं परिपालकः .. 1.266.60 ..
text_mt:
therefore, protect this people of theirs and their women.
The Gandharvas are to be protected by you; you are their protector.

sanskrit_iast:
madīyenānurodhena viśeṣātkartumarhasi ..
sarveṣāñca tathā sthānaṃ parvate gandhamādane .. 61 ..
meaning:
मदीयेनानुरोधेन विशेषात्कर्तुमर्हसि ..
सर्वेषाञ्च तथा स्थानं पर्वते गन्धमादने .. 61 ..
text_mt:
You ought especially to do this at my request.
And likewise, the dwelling of all of them is on Mount Gandhamādana;

sanskrit_iast:
prayātāstava tatrasthāḥ pālayiṣyanti śāsanam ..
evaṃ kariṣya ityuktvā pariṣvajya ca pīḍitam .. 62 ..
meaning:
प्रयातास्तव तत्रस्थाः पालयिष्यन्ति शासनम् ..
एवं करिष्य इत्युक्त्वा परिष्वज्य च पीडितम् .. 62 ..
text_mt:
going thither and dwelling there, they will obey your command.'
Saying 'I shall do so,' and embracing closely

sanskrit_iast: sarvajñaṃ bharataṃ śrīmāngandharvastridivaṃ yayau .. 63 ..
meaning: सर्वज्ञं भरतं श्रीमान्गन्धर्वस्त्रिदिवं ययौ .. 63 ..
text_mt: the all-knowing Bharata, the glorious Gandharva departed for heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
raghupravīro'pi raṇe maghonaḥ śatrūnnihatvā varadānayuktama ..
virājamāno yaśasā pareṇa jagāma rājansvapuraṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ ..64..
1.267
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
āditye'stamanuprāpte sandhyākāle sudāruṇe ..
nivartayāmāsa rathaṃ yudhājidbharatasya ca .. 1 ..
nivartayānaśca rathaṃ bharataṃ vākyamabravīt ..
saṃgrāmamedinīṃ paśya svakṛtāṃ raghunandana .. 2 ..
gandharvāṅgasamākīrṇāṃ hatakuñjarabhūṣaṇāma ..
turaṅgamagaṇākīrṇāṃ varāyudhadharāṃ dharām .. 3 ..
saṃpūrṇacandrapratimairdaṣṭoṣṭhai ścārukuṇḍalaiḥ ..
bhṛkuṭītaṭaduṣprekṣyairmastakairbhāti medinī .. 4 ..
pañcaśīrṣoragākārairvarāṅgadavibhūṣaṇaiḥ ..
bāhubhirbhāti śūrāṇāṃ vasudhā vasudhādhipa .. 5 ..
padmapatradalākārairgendharvāṇāṃ tathā karaiḥ ..

meaning:
रघुप्रवीरोऽपि रणे मघोनः शत्रून्निहत्वा वरदानयुक्तम ..
विराजमानो यशसा परेण जगाम राजन्स्वपुरं प्रहृष्टः ..64..
1.267
.. मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
आदित्येऽस्तमनुप्राप्ते सन्ध्याकाले सुदारुणे ..
निवर्तयामास रथं युधाजिद्भरतस्य च .. 1 ..
निवर्तयानश्च रथं भरतं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ..
संग्राममेदिनीं पश्य स्वकृतां रघुनन्दन .. 2 ..
गन्धर्वाङ्गसमाकीर्णां हतकुञ्जरभूषणाम ..
तुरङ्गमगणाकीर्णां वरायुधधरां धराम् .. 3 ..
संपूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमैर्दष्टोष्ठै श्चारुकुण्डलैः ..
भृकुटीतटदुष्प्रेक्ष्यैर्मस्तकैर्भाति मेदिनी .. 4 ..

पद्मपत्रदलाकारैर्गेन्धर्वाणां तथा करैः ..
भाति सायकविच्छिन्नैः सपद्मेव वसुन्धरा .. 6 ..
text_mt:
That foremost hero of Raghu's race as well, having slain the enemies of Maghavan in battle and received the granting of boons,
shining with supreme renown, O king, went to his own city in great joy.
1.267
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When the sun had set, at the dreadful twilight hour,
Yudhājit caused Bharata's chariot to turn back.
And turning the chariot back, he addressed Bharata with these words:
'Look upon the field of battle made by yourself, O descendant of Raghu,
strewn with the limbs of Gandharvas, decorated with slain elephants,
covered with herds of horses, and bearing excellent weapons upon the earth.
The earth shines with severed heads resembling full moons, their lips bitten,
adorned with beautiful earrings, dreadful to behold with knitted brows.
The earth shines, O lord of the earth, with the arms of heroes,
resembling five-headed serpents, adorned with excellent armlets.
And with the hands of the Gandharvas resembling lotus petals,
severed by arrows, the earth shines as though covered in lotuses.

udbhrāntajīvitaiḥ paśya vinikīrṇadharātalam .. 8 ..
āviṣkṛtaradaiścāśvairvivṛtākṣaistathaiva ca ..
patitairāvṛtā paśya turaṅgairmedinī raṇe .. 9 ..
ātapatreḥ śaśāṅkābhaiścāmaraiśca virājitām..

text_mt:
The earth, strewn with the arms of the Gandharvas,
which resemble the trunks of elephants and are adorned with choice sandalwood, shines resplendent.
Look upon the earth's surface strewn with elephants resembling massive boulders,
pierced by your single arrow, their lives fled.
Behold the earth in battle covered with fallen steeds,
their teeth bared and their eyes wide open,
adorned with parasols shining like the moon and with chowries,
with straps, bits, saddles, housings, and conches,
with hair, clubs, bows, spears, swords, battle-axes,
and with various kinds of auspicious arrows marked with diverse names,
and adorned with diadems, armlets, necklaces, and earrings.
Behold the earth, O lord of the Raghus, charming even in its pathos!'
And behold the Gandharvas being eaten by carnivorous beasts and birds, / their every limb handsome, adorned with all kinds of ornaments.

text_mt:
Being dragged into hollows like corpses in battle by the flesh-eaters, / with their limbs moving, they seem as if alive, O ruler of the earth.
The lotus-like hand, familiar to the warriors, has fled [and is severed], / scarred from holding the bow, eaten by birds.
With faces half-eaten and fully devoured, / behold the wicked Gandharvas, as if [struck down] by a curse of the kings of the earth.
What the Gandharvas previously did to innocent kings, / you have done once more in battle to the Gandharvas. / Behold, O Rāghava, the Gandharvas [lying] on the battlefield for the Piśācas,
and for the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas by the hundreds and thousands, / who crave the flesh of Gandharvas and continually feed on blood.
Flesh-eaters [from as far as] the sea coasts have arrived, exceedingly hungry; / by you their highest gratification has been made today at the front of battle.
Behold the various forms of the flesh-eaters in battle: / some are fat, some lean, some tall, and others short.

With faces resembling various kinds of creatures, / wearing diverse garbs, fierce, and of various grotesque appearances,
clothed in lion skins and clothed in tiger skins; / some are summoned, others bite, and others carry off the excellent blood.
Others, hoisting flesh and blood onto their shoulders, marched off; / they sport as they please in the rivers of blood created by you.
Others bathe [one another] in blood, and others make [their companions] drink blood, / pouring blood into skulls and placing it again and again in their laps.
Others drink blood in battle along with their wives; / likewise others, [their] women, make [their companions] drink, O younger brother of Rāma.
Others drink blood from skulls held in the hands of their wives; / other fierce ones drink blood from elephant skulls.

text_mt:
Having placed their children upon their shoulders, others, satisfied, dance; / taking the hand of their wives, others dance likewise.
Others dance, others laugh with grotesque voices; / others sing, others sleep, and others quarrel.
Others drop corpses on the ground; / they desire to seize others, and grasp yet others.
Vile beings quarrel over corpses; / tearing off flesh, some eat, adorned with severed limbs.
And having eaten, some chew on bones and marrow, O Rāghava; / and others say, “We are satisfied by the grace of Bharata!”
And having attained supreme joy, they speak to one another: / “May there always be war, enmity, and cruelty among kings,
and strength, allies, and nourishment, whereby we are satisfied!” / Speaking thus, they sang with diverse voices.

Likewise, others, extremely hideous to look upon, gaze affectionately at your chariot. / Thus glorious Bharata, having been shown [the field] by his maternal uncle,
beholding the battlefield, went again toward Rājagṛha. / Near the city, he saw, bewildered by the Vāyavya missile,
that army of the foremost of kings. Seeing Bharata, sprinkled with the dust of battle, / returning from the battle,
the kings cheered the hero victorious in combat. / Having met with the illustrious kings and embraced them, / and having consoled them, the righteous one dismissed them to their camps.
Then the lord of Raghu's line entered by night that capital of his maternal uncle, / delightful with rejoiced warriors and noble folk, being praised with hymns by lions among men.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When that night had passed, the people from the Gandharva city, / the sons and wives of the Gandharvas, and likewise the wives of the king,

Some fell upon their husbands, others embraced them; / others wept, O king, crying out with sweet voices.
As they were weeping thus, the king's wives, deeply distressed, / with dishevelled hair, wept piteously, O king:
“Ah, beloved! Ah, great king! Ah, darling of the populace! / Ah, crusher of the pride of the lord of gods! Ah, moon-faced one!

[having embraced] the earth with your loving arms, are you not ashamed in the assembly? / Why do you lie before us, especially [upon one who is] stained with dust?
Though you were a sky-wanderer, O king, the earth was ever dear to you.

We are tormented by your unforeseen departure; / comfort us, O slayer of foes, with merely a word.

text_mt:
As the surface of the earth was overwhelmed by the sound of their weeping, / the learned twice-born Nāḍāyana offered them consolation.
At that very time, the undefeated lord of the Gandharvas / came to that region, urged by Bharata.
Having arrived at that place, King Citraratha then / gradually consoled all the people according to rule.
He caused funeral honours to be rendered to Śailūṣa along with his sons. / Urged then by King Citraratha, those Gandharvas
built a pyre for the king with many well-dried pieces of wood at that time, / and for all of his sons, and for the warriors without exception, / with logs of sandalwood, agallochum, and kālīyaka.
Having ignited the pyres with perfumes, oils, and ghee, / and having performed the last rites for them all, they set out for the city.
Then, at the word of the king of the Gandharvas, all the people, / placing Nāḍāyana at their head, went to Mount Gandhamādana.

text_mt:
He made a settlement there on the slope of Mount Rāma. / Having made a settlement there, they all, by order of Citraratha, / lived happily, O great king, protected by that noble-souled one.
There too, O king, the grandson of Śailūṣa became the chief of the people in the city, / and the king of the Gandharvas protected him according to the word of the foremost of the Raghus.
1.269
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then, at the end of the bright fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha,
the five-day festival of the chiefs of the gods was completed.
Lying upon Śeṣa in the Ocean of Milk, the blessed Madhusūdana
then entered into yogic sleep, wishing for the welfare of the worlds.
Bharata too, having celebrated the festival, worshipped Janārdana,
and likewise made gifts of land, eating only at night for five days.
And when the four-month vow of abstaining from honey and meat was concluded,
he honoured the kings and dismissed them from his home.
Addressing them with various soothing words, embracing them tightly,
and distributing the hoards of wealth acquired from the city of the Gandharvas,

text_mt:
and having honoured his own soldiers during the rainy season,
he consulted with them and sent them away, yearning for their beloved kin.
Having sent the people off, with a small remainder of his soldiers,
Bharata went and dwelt at his maternal uncle's house, like the king of the gods.
The best of the Raghus dwelt [there] with pleasure for four months.
Then, at the beginning of the month of Kārttika, ending with the bright fortnight,
when the five days arrived, he celebrated a great festival
for the awakening of the God of gods, amid the great festival of the gods.
Having bestowed great gifts on those [days], and especially on the full moon of Kārttika,
and having worshipped the Lord of the world, who bears the conch, discus, and mace,
on an auspicious day, under a favourable lunar mansion, having honoured the best of the twice-born,
and having placed the astrologer and the master-builders in the lead, that scion of Raghu
founded two cities on both banks of the Sindhu:
Puṣkara in Puṣkarāvatī, and Takṣa in Takṣaśilā.

text_mt:
Having commenced [the building of] the two cities, and having duly consecrated both sons
in the two cities, O great king, he gave lavish sacrificial fees,
installing his son Puṣkara in Puṣkara and Takṣa [in Takṣaśilā], O Yādava.
When the two cities were crowded with merchants as well as brahmins,
and with craftsmen, O great king, who lived by various crafts,
crowded with clusters of houses, and adorned with temples of the gods,
and when the kingdom was thus established for his two sons, Bharata then
divided wealth, jewels, horses, and elephants between both his sons.
Having entrusted them to Yudhājit, when a year had elapsed,
and the month of Kārttika had passed, under an auspicious lunar mansion,
the glorious Bharata went to see Rāma, O king of men,
the hero followed by his sons and by his maternal uncle Yudhājit.
On the border of his own realm, he dismissed both his sons
and his maternal uncle Yudhājit to their homes, embracing them tightly.
His eyes full of tears, Bharata set out with a small
fourfold army and on a chariot of gold.

text_mt:
Turning back from the chariot, with downcast minds
and somewhat bewildered, they watched Bharata departing.
Bharata departed, turning back again and again with great difficulty.
Ceasing to look at each other, they departed in haste.
Bharata too, passing through countries, lakes, rivers,
and gatherings of villages and towns, went on to the city.
Then he reached Ayodhyā after his long sojourn abroad,
and entered the city, which was filled with banners and flags,
its mansions white with plaster, sprinkled with sandalwood water,
all arranged by Rāma's command, with the children of the gods worshipped.
By Rāma's command, the intensely radiant Lakṣmaṇa came forth
to meet him, accompanied by a fourfold army and with the citizens.
Seeing Bharata after his long stay abroad,
Lakṣmaṇa greeted him with affection, placing his head on the ground.
Bharata smelled his crown, embraced him tightly,
and duly inquired after his well-being in every respect.

text_mt:
He honoured the townspeople according to their rank,
addressing them with smiles while exchanging inquiries of well-being.
Honoured repeatedly by that multitude of people,
the glorious Bharata entered the city mounted on the neck of an elephant.
Gazed upon with yearning by the women
standing at the windows of celestial cars, mansions, and palaces,
the intensely radiant one reached the wide royal gate.
There arose a great sound of musical instruments and a vast tumult.
Then, having reached the royal gate, he dismounted from the excellent elephant,
and taking Lakṣmaṇa by the hand, entered the assembly hall.
There he saw the mighty-armed Rāma seated upon the lion-throne,
his limbs anointed with sandalwood and adorned with all ornaments,
with a face like the full moon and eyes like blue lotus petals.
As soon as he saw Rāma, Bharata placed his head upon the ground;
the intensely radiant one fell prostrate, and Lakṣmaṇa likewise.
Rāma too, seeing Bharata, raised up the mighty-armed one,

clasped him tightly by the neck, smelled his head again and again,
and, inquiring after his imperishable welfare, offered him a seat.
Having presented the foremost jewels of the Gandharvas
to Rāma, who is constant in dharma, that scion of Raghu took the excellent seat.
Questioned by Rāma, that hero among men reported the events as they had occurred;
and dismissed by him, he went to his house and then worshipped Viṣṇu.
In peace the hero, invincible in battles, dwelt attending Rāma's feet;
and Rāma, having utterly crushed his adversaries, ruled the kingdom together with him.
Then, in the fourth year, Rāma heard of the glory of the two cities
established by the two sons of Bharata, and he, exceedingly pleased, attained supreme joy in Viṣṇu.
Thus has been recounted by me today the victory of the son of Raghu on the field of battle;
this, delightful with knowledge, dharma, wealth, and fame, should be listened to by a man with regular observance.

sanskrit_iast: 18 sagaranṛpavisṛṣṭāśvamedhīyaturagamapahṛtya kapilena svāśrame pātāle tanni rodhaḥ; tadanveṣaṇavyāpṛtaṣaṣṭisahasrasagarasutānāṃ svanikhātasāgaramārgeṇa pātālagamanaṃ kapilaśāpena bhasmībhavanañca, tadanveṣaṇapravṛttāṃśumatā santoṣitakapilatastvatpautro bhagīrathastaduddhārārthaṃ svargaṅgāmāneṣyatīti varaprāptiḥ ...

sanskrit_iast: 19 pitryuddhārakāmabhagīrathasya sahasravarṣatapohaṣṭagaṅgādeśānusāraṃ viyatastanni- pātavegasahanakṣamaśaṅkarārādhanānte tatkaparde gaṅgānipātaḥ, aho prakhara- vegāyā mama sahanaṃ kathaṃ maheśvaraḥ soḍhetyavaliptāyāstasyā hareṇa sajaṭājūṭe tirodhānam, tadanu ciratapaḥkliṣṭabhagīrathānukampayā tasyāstyāgaḥ prācyādiṣu saptadhā tadgatiśca ...

text_mt: 19. Bhagīratha, desiring the deliverance of his ancestors, according to the instruction of Gaṅgā who was delighted by a thousand years of austerity, propitiates Śaṅkara who is able to bear the momentum of her fall from the sky; the Gaṅgā falls into his matted locks; filled with conceit—'Ah, how can Maheśvara endure me who have such a fierce torrent?'—she is hidden away by Hara in his mass of matted locks; thereafter, out of compassion for Bhagīratha who had suffered long austerities, he releases her, and she courses in seven streams toward the east and other quarters.

sanskrit_iast: 20 kānyakubje yajñadīkṣitasya jahnorāśramaplāvanāttena yogabalena gaṅgāyāḥ pānaṃ munyanunayena karṇatastyāgo duhitṛtve kalpanañca ( ata eva jāhnavītvam) ...

text_mt: 20. Jahnu, consecrated for a sacrifice in Kānyakubja, has his hermitage flooded, and drinks up the Gaṅgā by the power of yoga; upon the sage being placated, she is released through his ear and is reckoned as his daughter (hence her status as Jāhnavī).

sanskrit_iast: 21 svāyambhuve'ntare bāṣkali (bali) rājena viśvabhugindrapadamapahṛtam, punarindrasya svārājyalabdhaye'dbhutavāmanarūpamugdhabāṣkalinendraprārthanayā vāmanāya tripadabhūmidānapratijñāne taddakṣiṇacaraṇākramaṇena śakrasya svarājyalābho viṣṇupadāgrakṣatāṇḍapraviṣṭapavitrajalasya viṣṇupadītvam

text_mt: 21. In the Svāyambhuva manvantara, King Bāṣkali (Bali) usurped the status of Indra Viśvabhuk; then, so that Indra might regain his sovereignty, Bāṣkali, enchanted by the wondrous Vāmana form, upon Indra's request pledged to give three paces of land to Vāmana; through the stride of his right foot Śakra regained his sovereignty, and the holy water that entered the cosmic egg pierced by the tip of Viṣṇu's foot became the Viṣṇupadī.

sanskrit_iast: 22 brahmāṇḍādvinirgatya viṣṇutapomaharlokacandramaṇḍalasarvavarṣadvīpasaptapātālāni vyāpya gaṅgāyā bhūyo brahmāṇḍapraveśaḥ
meaning: 22 ब्रह्माण्डाद्विनिर्गत्य विष्णुतपोमहर्लोकचन्द्रमण्डलसर्ववर्षद्वीपसप्तपातालानि व्याप्य गङ्गाया भूयो ब्रह्माण्डप्रवेशः
text_mt: 22. The Gaṅgā issuing forth from the cosmic egg, pervading the world of Viṣṇu, Tapas, Mahas, the lunar sphere, all the realms, the continents, and the seven subterranean regions, and re-entering the cosmic egg.

sanskrit_iast: 23 bhagīrathasya rājarṣervaṃśyānuvarṇanapurassaraṅkārttavīryyasya viśeṣataḥ pauruṣavarṇanam
meaning: 23 भगीरथस्य राजर्षेर्वंश्यानुवर्णनपुरस्सरङ्कार्त्तवीर्य्यस्य विशेषतः पौरुषवर्णनम्
text_mt: 23. Description of the lineage of the royal sage Bhagīratha, followed by a particular description of the prowess of Kārttavīrya.

sanskrit_iast: 24 vṛttrāsuraviśvarūpa ( brahma )hatyābhītavāsavasya mānase sarasi bisatantau līnatvānnahuṣasyendratā, śacīkāmukamunivāhyāśibikārūḍhasya tasyā- gastyaśāpātsarpatā, bhāviyudhiṣṭhirasākṣātkāre śāpavimokṣaḥ, devarājā- bhāve dharmaviplavānmarakādyupadravācca pralīnasvāhāsvadhāvaṣaṭakāre trida- śaprārthitaharyanugrahādindrasya punaḥ svārājyalābhe sarvalokaśāntiḥ
meaning: 24 वृत्त्रासुरविश्वरूप ( ब्रह्म )हत्याभीतवासवस्य मानसे सरसि बिसतन्तौ लीनत्वान्नहुषस्येन्द्रता, शचीकामुकमुनिवाह्याशिबिकारूढस्य तस्या- गस्त्यशापात्सर्पता, भावियुधिष्ठिरसाक्षात्कारे शापविमोक्षः, देवराजा- भावे धर्मविप्लवान्मरकाद्युपद्रवाच्च प्रलीनस्वाहास्वधावषटकारे त्रिद- शप्रार्थितहर्यनुग्रहादिन्द्रस्य पुनः स्वाराज्यलाभे सर्वलोकशान्तिः
text_mt: 24. Vāsava, terrified of the murder of a brahmin in the slaying of the demon Vṛtra and Viśvarūpa, conceals himself in a lotus fiber in the Mānasa lake, whereupon Nahuṣa obtains the status of Indra; lusting after Śacī and mounted on a palanquin borne by sages, he becomes a serpent by the curse of Agastya, his liberation from the curse to occur upon meeting Yudhiṣṭhira in the future; in the absence of the king of gods, because of the subversion of dharma and plagues of pestilence and the like, the utterances of svāhā, svadhā, and vaṣaṭ vanish; upon Indra regaining his sovereignty through the grace of Hari requested by the thirty gods, peace is restored to all the worlds.

sanskrit_iast: 25 hariharāvatreḥ putrībhūya dattātreyadurvāsorūpeṇāvatīrṇau, tatra dattātreyeṇa vedādhyayanayajñādivinaṣṭadharmyakriyāṇāmuddharaṇaṃ kārtavīryasya daśasahasra- varṣaparyyantaṃ tapaścaraṇācchiṣyīkaraṇaṃ pracchannadaityatadāśritanṛpapīḍita- dharāyāḥ śakrasamīpagamanañca
meaning: 25 हरिहरावत्रेः पुत्रीभूय दत्तात्रेयदुर्वासोरूपेणावतीर्णौ, तत्र दत्तात्रेयेण वेदाध्ययनयज्ञादिविनष्टधर्म्यक्रियाणामुद्धरणं कार्तवीर्यस्य दशसहस्र- वर्षपर्य्यन्तं तपश्चरणाच्छिष्यीकरणं प्रच्छन्नदैत्यतदाश्रितनृपपीडित- धरायाः शक्रसमीपगमनञ्च
text_mt: 25. Hari and Hara, becoming sons of Atri, descend in the forms of Dattātreya and Durvāsas; therein Dattātreya restores the destroyed righteous rites such as Vedic recitation and sacrifice; he accepts Kārtavīrya as a disciple following his practice of austerity for ten thousand years; and the earth, oppressed by disguised Daityas and the kings dependent upon them, approaches Śakra.

sanskrit_iast: 26 nāke bhūmyā viṣṇudarśanaṃ śakraṃ prati svaduḥkhanivedanaṃ, śakreṇa tatkaṣṭa- nivāraṇārthaṃ brahmasadogamanam ...
meaning: 26 नाके भूम्या विष्णुदर्शनं शक्रं प्रति स्वदुःखनिवेदनं, शक्रेण तत्कष्ट- निवारणार्थं ब्रह्मसदोगमनम् ...
text_mt: 26. The vision of Viṣṇu in heaven by the earth; her report of her suffering to Śakra; and Śakra's journey to the assembly of Brahmā to remove that distress.

sanskrit_iast: 27 duṣṭakṣatriyapīḍitabhūbhāraharaṇārthaṃ bṛhaspatisahitaśakreṇa pitāmahastavanaṃ śaṃkaro vo duḥkhaṃ nivārayiṣyati tatsamīpe gacchateti tasyottaram
meaning: 27 दुष्टक्षत्रियपीडितभूभारहरणार्थं बृहस्पतिसहितशक्रेण पितामहस्तवनं शंकरो वो दुःखं निवारयिष्यति तत्समीपे गच्छतेति तस्योत्तरम्
text_mt: 27. Praise of the Grandfather by Śakra accompanied by Bṛhaspati to remove the burden of the earth oppressed by wicked kṣatriyas; his reply: 'Śaṅkara will remove your suffering; go to him.'

sanskrit_iast: 28 śaṃkaradarśanastutī...
meaning: 28 शंकरदर्शनस्तुती...
text_mt: 28. The vision of Śaṃkara and the hymn of praise to him.

sanskrit_iast: 29 śaṃkarakṛtacandrastuticandramaṇḍalamānādi ...
meaning: 29 शंकरकृतचन्द्रस्तुतिचन्द्रमण्डलमानादि ...
text_mt: 29. The hymn of praise to the moon uttered by Śaṃkara, the dimensions of the lunar disc, and the like.

sanskrit_iast: 30 sūryadarśanatanmaṇḍalapramāṇatatpraśaṃsāpurastaraṃ rudraṃ prati sūryeṇa kārtavīryā- nugapracchannāsurakṣattriyādināśakaraṇaprativacanam
meaning: 30 सूर्यदर्शनतन्मण्डलप्रमाणतत्प्रशंसापुरस्तरं रुद्रं प्रति सूर्येण कार्तवीर्या- नुगप्रच्छन्नासुरक्षत्त्रियादिनाशकरणप्रतिवचनम्
text_mt: 30. The vision of the sun, the measurement of his disc, and praise of him, followed by the sun's promise to Rudra to destroy the disguised asuras, kṣatriyas, and others who followed Kārtavīrya.

sanskrit_iast: 31 dvijaveśadhārisūryasya bhojanārthaṃ kārtikeyasakāśagamane tadanumatena sthāvarībhūtāsurāṇāṃ raviraśmiprajvalaccharaiḥ sarvadrumadāhe vaśiṣṭhāśramasyāpi dāhādbrāhmaṇo'valiptasyate (paraśurāmaḥ) bāhūṃśchetsyatīti śāpaḥ
meaning: 31 द्विजवेशधारिसूर्यस्य भोजनार्थं कार्तिकेयसकाशगमने तदनुमतेन स्थावरीभूतासुराणां रविरश्मिप्रज्वलच्छरैः सर्वद्रुमदाहे वशिष्ठाश्रमस्यापि दाहाद्ब्राह्मणोऽवलिप्तस्यते (परशुरामः) बाहूंश्छेत्स्यतीति शापः
text_mt: 31. The sun in the guise of a twice-born goes to Kārtikeya to receive food; with his consent, as the asuras turned into trees are burnt along with all other trees by the flaming arrows of the sun's rays, the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha is also burnt, whereupon the curse is uttered: 'A brahmin (Paraśurāma) will cut off your arms, you arrogant one!'

sanskrit_iast: 32 bhṛguvaṃśe jamadagrivaḍavāgnyādyutpatiḥ
meaning: 32 भृगुवंशे जमदग्रिवडवाग्न्याद्युत्पतिः
text_mt: 32. The origin of Jamadagni, the submarine fire, and others in the lineage of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast: 33 svaparicaryāhṛṣṭapatyṛcīkalabdhavarayā satyavatyā svamātre balavattare svasyai ca brahmavarcasvidharmajñe putre vṛte svamātṛprārthanayā tayā caruviparyāsakaraṇādgarbhayorviruddhadharmatā
meaning: 33 स्वपरिचर्याहृष्टपत्यृचीकलब्धवरया सत्यवत्या स्वमात्रे बलवत्तरे स्वस्यै च ब्रह्मवर्चस्विधर्मज्ञे पुत्रे वृते स्वमातृप्रार्थनया तया चरुविपर्यासकरणाद्गर्भयोर्विरुद्धधर्मता
text_mt: 33. Satyavatī, having obtained a boon from her husband Ṛcīka who was pleased by her devotion, chooses for her mother a son possessed of great strength and for herself a son endowed with brahma-splendour and knowledge of dharma; at her mother's request she exchanges the sacrificial messes, resulting in the contrary natures of the two embryos.

sanskrit_iast: 34 cyavanamunikṛpayā viśvāmitrasya bhāvibrāhmaṇyam
meaning: 34 च्यवनमुनिकृपया विश्वामित्रस्य भाविब्राह्मण्यम्
text_mt: 34. The future status of Viśvāmitra as a brahmin through the grace of the sage Cyavana.

sanskrit_iast: 35. satyavatī jamadagnivātsyādiśataputrān, gādherbhāryā ca viśvāmitramasūta. madhyandine bane śarakrīḍāsaktajamadagniṃ patiṃ reṇukā bāṇānayanādinā paryacarat, sūryakarasantaptāṃ cirāgatāṃ tāmavalokya jamadagnau śaraiḥ sūryaṃ hantumudyukte vipramūrtidharo ravistatputratāṃ svīkṛtyacchatropānadbhayāntāmanujagrāha. sā ca sūryāṃśaputrotpatyanantaraṃ rāmaputramajījanat
meaning: 35. सत्यवती जमदग्निवात्स्यादिशतपुत्रान्, गाधेर्भार्या च विश्वामित्रमसूत. मध्यन्दिने बने शरक्रीडासक्तजमदग्निं पतिं रेणुका बाणानयनादिना पर्यचरत्, सूर्यकरसन्तप्तां चिरागतां तामवलोक्य जमदग्नौ शरैः सूर्यं हन्तुमुद्युक्ते विप्रमूर्तिधरो रविस्तत्पुत्रतां स्वीकृत्यच्छत्रोपानद्भयान्तामनुजग्राह. सा च सूर्यांशपुत्रोत्पत्यनन्तरं रामपुत्रमजीजनत्
text_mt: 35. Satyavatī gave birth to a hundred sons, including Jamadagni and Vātsya, and the wife of Gādhi gave birth to Viśvāmitra. At midday, as her husband Jamadagni was engaged in archery practice in the forest, Reṇukā served him by fetching arrows and doing other tasks. Seeing her arrive late, scorched by the sun's rays, when Jamadagni prepared to slay the sun with his arrows, the Sun, assuming the form of a brahmin, accepted becoming his son and bestowed his grace upon her, who was relieved of fear, by means of an umbrella and shoes. And she, after the birth of the son who was a portion of the Sun, gave birth to the son Rāma.

sanskrit_iast: 36 vanavihārāgatacitrāṃgarājamicchantīṃ svamātaraṃ pitrājñayā paraśurāmo'vadhīt svājñāpālanatuṣṭajamadagnistasmā icchāmaraṇavaraṃ dāśarāthirāmasākṣātkārāvadhi śastradhāritvañca vitīrya tadanurodhena tanmātaraṃ bhrātṝṃścojjīvayāmāsa, rāmaśca pitṛnideśācchaṃkaramārādhya tadanujñayā devapīḍakasaiṃhikeyānhantumiyeṣa
meaning: 36 वनविहारागतचित्रांगराजमिच्छन्तीं स्वमातरं पित्राज्ञया परशुरामोऽवधीत् स्वाज्ञापालनतुष्टजमदग्निस्तस्मा इच्छामरणवरं दाशराथिरामसाक्षात्कारावधि शस्त्रधारित्वञ्च वितीर्य तदनुरोधेन तन्मातरं भ्रातॄंश्चोज्जीवयामास, रामश्च पितृनिदेशाच्छंकरमाराध्य तदनुज्ञया देवपीडकसैंहिकेयान्हन्तुमियेष
text_mt: 36. At his father's command, Paraśurāma slew his own mother, who had desired King Citrāṅga as he came strolling in the forest. Jamadagni, pleased by his obedience to his command, granted him the boon of dying when he wished, and of bearing arms until he saw Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, face to face; and at his entreaty he brought his mother and brothers back to life. Then Rāma, worshipping Śaṃkara at his father's instruction, desired by his permission to slay the Saiṃhikeyas, the tormentors of the gods.

sanskrit_iast: 37 seṃhikeyaniveśane vividhotpātavarṇanam . . .
meaning: 37 सेंहिकेयनिवेशने विविधोत्पातवर्णनम् . . .
text_mt: 37. Description of various portents in the abode of the Saiṃhikeyas...

sanskrit_iast: 38 utpātakāraṇajijñāsayā pṛṣṭaśukreṇa saiṃhikekāya paraśurāmarūpiviṣṇunā naratiryagdevādiyonāvavatīrya surapatapakṣapātinā sadā daityavināśinā yuddhaṃ vihāya pātāle gantavyamiti hita upadiṣṭe saiṃhikeyena yuddhanirdhāraṇam
meaning: 38 उत्पातकारणजिज्ञासया पृष्टशुक्रेण सैंहिकेकाय परशुरामरूपिविष्णुना नरतिर्यग्देवादियोनाववतीर्य सुरपतपक्षपातिना सदा दैत्यविनाशिना युद्धं विहाय पाताले गन्तव्यमिति हित उपदिष्टे सैंहिकेयेन युद्धनिर्धारणम्
text_mt: 38. When questioned by the Saiṃhikeya out of a desire to know the cause of the portents, Śukra gave beneficial counsel: 'Viṣṇu, who has assumed the form of Paraśurāma, takes descent in the wombs of men, animals, gods, and other beings, always sides with the lord of the gods, and ever destroys the Daityas; you must abandon the fight and go to the nether world.' Thereupon, the Saiṃhikeya resolved upon war.

sanskrit_iast: 39 śukranayasamarthakaduḥsvapnasūcitadānavānvayātyayāśaṃki gaviṣṭhamatamanādṛtya viṣṇuhastena maraṇaṃ śreya iti saiṃhikeyena niścitam
meaning: 39 शुक्रनयसमर्थकदुःस्वप्नसूचितदानवान्वयात्ययाशंकि गविष्ठमतमनादृत्य विष्णुहस्तेन मरणं श्रेय इति सैंहिकेयेन निश्चितम्
text_mt: 39. Disregarding the opinion of Gaviṣṭha, who feared the destruction of the lineage of the Dānavas indicated by bad dreams that supported Śukra's policy, the Saiṃhikeya decided that death at the hand of Viṣṇu was preferable.

sanskrit_iast: 40 viṣṇunā vaireṇālamiti rāhuṇopadiṣṭe kṣīrodamathanalakṣmyādiratnotpattivarṇanam
meaning: 40 विष्णुना वैरेणालमिति राहुणोपदिष्टे क्षीरोदमथनलक्ष्म्यादिरत्नोत्पत्तिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 40. When Rāhu counselled that there should be an end to enmity with Viṣṇu, there is the description of the churning of the ocean of milk and the emergence of gems such as Lakṣmī.

sanskrit_iast: 41 lakṣmīnivāsasthānāni viṣṇuvallakṣmyā vyāpakatā svāyambhuvādyantare bhṛgvāditastasyā utpattiśca
meaning: 41 लक्ष्मीनिवासस्थानानि विष्णुवल्लक्ष्म्या व्यापकता स्वायम्भुवाद्यन्तरे भृग्वादितस्तस्या उत्पत्तिश्च
text_mt: 41. The dwelling places of Lakṣmī, the all-pervasiveness of Lakṣmī like that of Viṣṇu, and her birth from Bhṛgu and others in the intervals such as that of Svāyambhuva.

sanskrit_iast: 42 viṣṇunā'dṛṣṭapūrvāṃ kāminītanuṃ nirmāya daityebhyo'mṛtakalaśamādāya prahlādāya brahmadinamitamāyuṣyaṃ vitīrya ca devebhyastasya dānaṃ devapaṃktyuṣpaviṣṭasūryarūpirāhuṇā tasya pānaṃ tatsūcitaviṣṇunā tacchira:kartenapurassaraṃ tasmai grahatvalokapūjyatvādivaradānam
meaning: 42 विष्णुनाऽदृष्टपूर्वां कामिनीतनुं निर्माय दैत्येभ्योऽमृतकलशमादाय प्रह्लादाय ब्रह्मदिनमितमायुष्यं वितीर्य च देवेभ्यस्तस्य दानं देवपंक्त्युष्पविष्टसूर्यरूपिराहुणा तस्य पानं तत्सूचितविष्णुना तच्छिर:कर्तेनपुरस्सरं तस्मै ग्रहत्वलोकपूज्यत्वादिवरदानम्
text_mt: 42. Viṣṇu fashioned the body of a lovely woman never seen before, took the pitcher of nectar from the Daityas, granted Prahlāda a lifespan measured by a day of Brahmā, and gave it to the gods. When Rāhu, assuming the form of the Sun, sat in the row of gods and drank it, Viṣṇu, informed of this, first cut off his head, and then granted him boons such as becoming a planet and being worthy of worship by the world.

sanskrit_iast: 43 viṣṇukartṛkarāhuśiraśchedakruddhadaityānāṃ devaissaha samare teṣāṃ parājayaḥ
meaning: 43 विष्णुकर्तृकराहुशिरश्छेदक्रुद्धदैत्यानां देवैस्सह समरे तेषां पराजयः
text_mt: 43. The defeat of the Daityas, who were enraged by Viṣṇu's decapitation of Rāhu, in battle with the gods.

sanskrit_iast: 44 viṣṇunā yuddhe hate nidhanamāpyāpi svargarājye susiddha evaiti niścityāgrajarāhumatamanādṛtya sālvasya yuddhasthirīkaraṇam .
meaning: 44 विष्णुना युद्धे हते निधनमाप्यापि स्वर्गराज्ये सुसिद्ध एवैति निश्चित्याग्रजराहुमतमनादृत्य साल्वस्य युद्धस्थिरीकरणम् .
text_mt: 44. Sālva's determination to fight, disregarding the opinion of his elder brother Rāhu, having resolved: 'Even if I meet my death being slain by Viṣṇu in battle, [my place] in the kingdom of heaven is indeed well assured.'

sanskrit_iast: 45 paraśurāmeṇa yuddhayārthaṃ sālvasamīpe akṛtavraṇasya preṣaṇaṃ, nāhaṃ rāmeṇa yotsye kintu tadguruśaṃkareṇa samprahariṣya ityakṛtavraṇaṃ visṛjya sālvasya yuddhārthaṃ prayāṇamū
meaning: 45 परशुरामेण युद्धयार्थं साल्वसमीपे अकृतव्रणस्य प्रेषणं, नाहं रामेण योत्स्ये किन्तु तद्गुरुशंकरेण सम्प्रहरिष्य इत्यकृतव्रणं विसृज्य साल्वस्य युद्धार्थं प्रयाणमू
text_mt: 45. Paraśurāma sent Akṛtavraṇa to Sālva for the purpose of battle. Saying, 'I will not fight with Rāma, but I will strike his guru Śaṃkara,' Sālva dismissed Akṛtavraṇa and set forth for battle.

sanskrit_iast: 46 sālvacamūyātrāyāṃ durnimittavarṇanam ... ....
meaning: 46 साल्वचमूयात्रायां दुर्निमित्तवर्णनम् ... ....
text_mt: 46. Description of ill omens during the march of Sālva's army...

sanskrit_iast: 47 yuddhabhūmau bhārgavāgamanamū. . . .
meaning: 47 युद्धभूमौ भार्गवागमनमू. . . .
text_mt: 47. The arrival of the Bhārgava on the battlefield...

sanskrit_iast: 48ājau sakṛtparaśupātena rāmeṇāsam̐khyaśālvacamūhananam
meaning: 48आजौ सकृत्परशुपातेन रामेणासम्̐ख्यशाल्वचमूहननम्
text_mt: 48. The slaughter of Sālva's countless army by Rāma with a single fall of his battle-axe in the fight.

sanskrit_iast: 49 paraśurāmakṛtasālvavadhatuṣṭamahendrapramukhadevānāṃ raṇabhūmāvāgatya paraśurāmakarmapraśaṃsanaṃ śaṃkareṇa tadgātrasammārjanapūrvamanuttamaśastragrāmasya pradānamarātiṃ hatvā paraśoḥ punastaddhastagamanasya ca
meaning: 49 परशुरामकृतसाल्ववधतुष्टमहेन्द्रप्रमुखदेवानां रणभूमावागत्य परशुरामकर्मप्रशंसनं शंकरेण तद्गात्रसम्मार्जनपूर्वमनुत्तमशस्त्रग्रामस्य प्रदानमरातिं हत्वा परशोः पुनस्तद्धस्तगमनस्य च
text_mt: 49. The gods, headed by Mahendra, pleased with the slaying of Sālva accomplished by Paraśurāma, came to the battlefield and praised Paraśurāma's deed; and Śaṃkara, having wiped his limbs, bestowed upon him a host of unsurpassed weapons, and [granted] that his battle-axe, having slain the enemy, would return again to his hand.

sanskrit_iast: 50 brāhmavaiṣṇavaraudrāgneyādyastrapradānapurassaraṃ śaṃkareṇa rāmāya saprayogarahasyasaṃhāramanekāstravitaraṇam
meaning: 50 ब्राह्मवैष्णवरौद्राग्नेयाद्यस्त्रप्रदानपुरस्सरं शंकरेण रामाय सप्रयोगरहस्यसंहारमनेकास्त्रवितरणम्
text_mt: 50. Śaṃkara bestowed many divine missiles on Rāma, along with their secret methods of discharge and withdrawal, beginning with the gift of the Brahmā, Vaiṣṇava, Raudra, and Āgneya missiles.

sanskrit_iast: 51 sarvadevavariṣṭho'pi bhavāṃścetasi kaṃ smaratīti śaṃkaraṃ prati paraśurāmapraśnaḥ
meaning: 51 सर्वदेववरिष्ठोऽपि भवांश्चेतसि कं स्मरतीति शंकरं प्रति परशुरामप्रश्नः
text_mt: 51. Paraśurāma's question to Śaṃkara: 'Though you are the foremost among all the gods, whom do you remember in your heart?'

sanskrit_iast: .. atha śaṃkaragītā ..
meaning: .. अथ शंकरगीता ..
text_mt: Now begins the Śaṃkaragītā.

sanskrit_iast: 52 śaṃkaragītāsu dhyeyanirdeśaḥ ... .
meaning: 52 शंकरगीतासु ध्येयनिर्देशः ... .
text_mt: 52. Indication of the object of meditation in the Śaṃkaragītā...

sanskrit_iast: 53 prajāpatiḥ kaśyapasyāditidityorbhāryayoḥ śakrahiraṇyākṣaputrayoḥ svargapātālarājye pradattavān,ekadā giriṣūtpatiteṣu dharācalanātpātāle'rṇavajalamagne devakṛtopadravaṃ śaṃkamāno hiraṇyākṣaḥ śakraṃ vijitya svārājyaṃ lebhe, hṛtasvargatridaśaprārthanayā viṣṇurnṛvarāhavapuṣānekadaityasahita hiraṇyākṣaṃ hatvā śakrāya tallokamarpitavān sa ca parvatapakṣām̐ścakarta ....
meaning: 53 प्रजापतिः कश्यपस्यादितिदित्योर्भार्ययोः शक्रहिरण्याक्षपुत्रयोः स्वर्गपातालराज्ये प्रदत्तवान्,एकदा गिरिषूत्पतितेषु धराचलनात्पातालेऽर्णवजलमग्ने देवकृतोपद्रवं शंकमानो हिरण्याक्षः शक्रं विजित्य स्वाराज्यं लेभे, हृतस्वर्गत्रिदशप्रार्थनया विष्णुर्नृवराहवपुषानेकदैत्यसहित हिरण्याक्षं हत्वा शक्राय तल्लोकमर्पितवान् स च पर्वतपक्षाम्̐श्चकर्त ....
text_mt: 53. The Prajāpati Kaśyapa gave the kingdoms of heaven and the nether world to Śakra and Hiraṇyākṣa, his sons by his two wives Aditi and Diti. Once, when the mountains flew up and the nether world was submerged in the waters of the ocean due to the shaking of the earth, Hiraṇyākṣa, suspecting an affliction caused by the gods, conquered Śakra and obtained sovereignty over heaven. At the entreaty of the thirty gods who were deprived of heaven, Viṣṇu, in the form of a man-boar, slew Hiraṇyākṣa along with many Daityas and restored that world to Śakra; and he [Śakra] cut off the wings of the mountains...

sanskrit_iast: 54mahogratapastuṣṭaprajāpatinā hiraṇyakaśipave devatiryaṅnarādyavadhyavare datte tadadhamasvabhāvaśaṃkitadevaprārthanayā viṣṇostasya vadhe ca sūcite devapīḍanānte nṛsihavapuṣā viṣṇunā tadvadhaḥ .
meaning: 54महोग्रतपस्तुष्टप्रजापतिना हिरण्यकशिपवे देवतिर्यङ्नराद्यवध्यवरे दत्ते तदधमस्वभावशंकितदेवप्रार्थनया विष्णोस्तस्य वधे च सूचिते देवपीडनान्ते नृसिहवपुषा विष्णुना तद्वधः .
text_mt: 54. When the Prajāpati, pleased by the fierce asceticism [of Hiraṇyakaśipu], granted Hiraṇyakaśipu the boon of invulnerability to gods, beasts, men, and others, Viṣṇu, at the prayer of the gods who feared his base nature, indicated his death; and at the end of his torment of the gods, Viṣṇu slew him in the form of Narasiṃha.

sanskrit_iast:
55 balinogratapasā prajāpateḥ surāsurāvadhyatvavare labdhe, prāptāyāśca daityaḥ rājatāyāṃ svargādindraprabhṛtidevanissārṇam, śakreṇa kaśyapabrahmabhyāṃ saha viṣṇave svaduḥkhaṃ nivedya vāmanarūpiṇā tena balimakhe tripādabhū
miprāptyā sumeruparyantaṃ pādadvayabhūmilābhādavaśiṣṭabhūmerabhāvādbalaye sutale sthānadānaṃ dvitīye manvantare śakratvaprāptiṃ sadā ca sutale svasannidhānādivarānadadāt
meaning:
55 बलिनोग्रतपसा प्रजापतेः सुरासुरावध्यत्ववरे लब्धे, प्राप्तायाश्च दैत्यः राजतायां स्वर्गादिन्द्रप्रभृतिदेवनिस्सार्णम्, शक्रेण कश्यपब्रह्मभ्यां सह विष्णवे स्वदुःखं निवेद्य वामनरूपिणा तेन बलिमखे त्रिपादभू
मिप्राप्त्या सुमेरुपर्यन्तं पादद्वयभूमिलाभादवशिष्टभूमेरभावाद्बलये सुतले स्थानदानं द्वितीये मन्वन्तरे शक्रत्वप्राप्तिं सदा च सुतले स्वसन्निधानादिवरानददात्
text_mt: 55. When Bali obtained from the Prajāpati, by his fierce asceticism, the boon of invulnerability to gods and asuras, and the sovereignty of the Daityas was established, Indra and the other gods were expelled from heaven. Śakra reported his distress to Viṣṇu together with Kaśyapa and Brahmā. Viṣṇu, in the form of a dwarf, received three paces of land at Bali's sacrifice. Since he acquired land extending up to Mount Sumeru with two paces and there was no remaining land, he gave Bali an abode in Sutala, and granted boons such as his attaining the status of Śakra in the second Manu-interval and his own constant presence in Sutala.

sanskrit_iast: 56 viṣṇordivyavibhūtivarṇanam
meaning: 56 विष्णोर्दिव्यविभूतिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 56. Description of the divine manifestations of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: 57 viṣṇvārādhanatassakalārthasādhanam
meaning: 57 विष्ण्वाराधनतस्सकलार्थसाधनम्
text_mt: 57. Accomplishment of all goals through the worship of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: 58 keśavatuṣṭikaranānākarmakathanam
meaning: 58 केशवतुष्टिकरनानाकर्मकथनम्
text_mt: 58. Account of various acts that produce the pleasure of Keśava.

sanskrit_iast: 59 vāranakṣatratithiṣūpavāsakaraṇaphalam
meaning: 59 वारनक्षत्रतिथिषूपवासकरणफलम्
text_mt: 59. The fruit of observing fasts on weekdays, lunar mansions, and lunar days.

sanskrit_iast: 60 śravaṇadvādaśītryahaspṛktithimahāpūrṇamāsīṣūpavāsadānādiphalam
meaning: 60 श्रवणद्वादशीत्र्यहस्पृक्तिथिमहापूर्णमासीषूपवासदानादिफलम्
text_mt: 60. The fruit of fasting, giving gifts, and other rites on the twelfth day conjoined with Śravaṇa, on the lunar day touching three days, and on great full-moon days.

sanskrit_iast: 61 prātaḥkālika (abhigama) pūjāyāmitikartavyatā ..
meaning: 61 प्रातःकालिक (अभिगम) पूजायामितिकर्तव्यता ..
text_mt: 61. What is to be done in the morning worship (approaching the deity)...

sanskrit_iast: 62 upādānavidhiḥ . . . . .
text_mt: 62. The rule for gathering materials...

sanskrit_iast: 63 ijyāsamayavidhimātrāmadhuparkādīnāṃ nirvacanam . ..
meaning: 63 इज्यासमयविधिमात्रामधुपर्कादीनां निर्वचनम् . ..
text_mt: 63. The rule for the time of sacrificial worship, and the definition of the measures of the honey-mixture and the rest...

sanskrit_iast: 64 svādhyāyakālānukīrtanamū .
meaning: 64 स्वाध्यायकालानुकीर्तनमू .
text_mt: 64. Recitation of the time for scriptural study...

sanskrit_iast: 65 svastikādyāsanapavanajayasthūladharācintanapurassaraṃ bhūmyādipañcabhūtamanobuddhyātmāvyaktapuruṣayogādikathanam
meaning: 65 स्वस्तिकाद्यासनपवनजयस्थूलधराचिन्तनपुरस्सरं भूम्यादिपञ्चभूतमनोबुद्ध्यात्माव्यक्तपुरुषयोगादिकथनम्
text_mt: 65. Account of the yoga of the five elements beginning with earth, mind, intellect, self, the unmanifest, and the Cosmic Person, preceded by postures such as the svastika, breath control, and contemplation of the gross earth.

sanskrit_iast: .. iti śaṅkaragītā ..
meaning: .. इति शङ्करगीता ..
text_mt: Thus ends the Śaṃkaragītā.

sanskrit_iast:
66 śakraprārthanayā śaṃkareṇa pātālasthanaravadhyadevaśatruhananārthaṃ vaiṣṇavadhanurakṣayasāyakatūṇavitaraṇapurassaramasurajayānantarandāśarathirāmahetoragastyāya
tadarpaṇopadeśaśca
meaning:
66 शक्रप्रार्थनया शंकरेण पातालस्थनरवध्यदेवशत्रुहननार्थं वैष्णवधनुरक्षयसायकतूणवितरणपुरस्सरमसुरजयानन्तरन्दाशरथिरामहेतोरगस्त्याय
तदर्पणोपदेशश्च
text_mt: 66. At the entreaty of Śakra, Śaṃkara, for the sake of slaying the enemies of the gods dwelling in the nether world who were to be slain by a man, gave a Vaiṣṇava bow and quivers with inexhaustible arrows, and instructed that after the victory over the asuras, it should be given to Agastya for the sake of Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit_iast: 67 viṣṇuśivayoḥ kaḥ śreṣṭha iti devapraśne viṣṇuśivayorabhedaprakaṭanapurassaraṃ madīyacāparatnaṃ bhārgavanandanāya ṛcīkaputrāya ṛcīkaputraḥ svaputrāya rāmāya dāsyati sa daityānhatvā tadrādyavāya so'pi varuṇāya so'rjunāya sa janakāya dāsyatīti vaiṣṇavadhanuṣaḥ sampradānavarṇanam
meaning: 67 विष्णुशिवयोः कः श्रेष्ठ इति देवप्रश्ने विष्णुशिवयोरभेदप्रकटनपुरस्सरं मदीयचापरत्नं भार्गवनन्दनाय ऋचीकपुत्राय ऋचीकपुत्रः स्वपुत्राय रामाय दास्यति स दैत्यान्हत्वा तद्राद्यवाय सोऽपि वरुणाय सोऽर्जुनाय स जनकाय दास्यतीति वैष्णवधनुषः सम्प्रदानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 67. Upon the gods asking, 'Between Viṣṇu and Śiva, who is superior?', Śiva revealed the non-difference of Viṣṇu and Śiva, and described the transmission of the Vaiṣṇava bow: 'The jewel of my bow will be given to the son of Ṛcīka, the delight of the Bhārgavas; the son of Ṛcīka will give it to his own son Rāma; he, having slain the Daityas, will give it to Rādhyava; he will give it to Varuṇa; he to Arjuna; and he will give it to Janaka.'

sanskrit_iast: 68 kailāsādrāmasya svapitrāśrame pitrādīnabhivādya varuṇālayasyāśmakanagarasya darśanam ...
meaning: 68 कैलासाद्रामस्य स्वपित्राश्रमे पित्रादीनभिवाद्य वरुणालयस्याश्मकनगरस्य दर्शनम् ...
text_mt: 68 Rāma's departure from Kailāsa to his father's hermitage, saluting his father and others, and seeing the city of Aśmaka, the abode of Varuṇa...

sanskrit_iast:
69 varuṇapurasamṛddhivarṇanapurassaraṃ savigrahagaṃgādinadīsevitasya tasya rāmakartṛkavandanānantaraṃ varuṇakṛtarāmapūjā, tato mahādevasandeśaśravaṇāvasāne varuṇena daityebhyo samarāya dūtapreṣaṇam
.
70 vividhāstraśastraprahāridānavacamūvīrānnihatyāyaḥśaṅko rāmadvārā hananam
meaning:
69 वरुणपुरसमृद्धिवर्णनपुरस्सरं सविग्रहगंगादिनदीसेवितस्य तस्य रामकर्तृकवन्दनानन्तरं वरुणकृतरामपूजा, ततो महादेवसन्देशश्रवणावसाने वरुणेन दैत्येभ्यो समराय दूतप्रेषणम्
.
70 विविधास्त्रशस्त्रप्रहारिदानवचमूवीरान्निहत्यायःशङ्को रामद्वारा हननम्
text_mt: 69 After describing the prosperity of Varuṇa's city, his worship of Rāma following Rāma's salutation to him who was attended by rivers such as the Gaṅgā in embodied form; then, after hearing the message of Mahādeva, Varuṇa sends a messenger to the Daityas for battle. / 70 After slaying the warriors of the Dānavas' army striking with diverse missiles and weapons, the slaying of Ayaḥśaṅka by Rāma.

sanskrit_iast: 71 paraśurāmakṛtastutyanantaraṃ bhavatkṛtasarvapraśanottarāndāsyāmīti varuṇoktiḥ
meaning: 71 परशुरामकृतस्तुत्यनन्तरं भवत्कृतसर्वप्रशनोत्तरान्दास्यामीति वरुणोक्तिः
text_mt: 71 Following the praise offered by Paraśurāma, Varuṇa says, "I will answer all the questions asked by you."

sanskrit_iast: 72 rudrātmakakālasyātisūkṣmatve'pi grahagatyanusāreṇa māsavarṣādi varṇanam.
meaning: 72 रुद्रात्मककालस्यातिसूक्ष्मत्वेऽपि ग्रहगत्यनुसारेण मासवर्षादि वर्णनम्.
text_mt: 72 Description of months, years, and so on according to the motion of the planets, despite the extreme subtlety of Time which is of the nature of Rudra.

sanskrit_iast: 73 nimeṣādyārabhya yugaparyantaṃ kālāvayavavarṇanapurassaraṃ tatratatra ( yuge2) manuṣyāyuḥpramāṇadharmavṛddhihrāsādivedavibhāgabrahmāyurvarṇanam .. ...
meaning: 73 निमेषाद्यारभ्य युगपर्यन्तं कालावयववर्णनपुरस्सरं तत्रतत्र ( युगे2) मनुष्यायुःप्रमाणधर्मवृद्धिह्रासादिवेदविभागब्रह्मायुर्वर्णनम् .. ...
text_mt: 73 Description of the divisions of Time beginning with the twinkling of an eye and ending with the age, along with the lifespan of human beings, the increase and decrease of dharma, the division of the Vedas, and the lifespan of Brahmā in each respective [age]...

sanskrit_iast: 74 purā kṛtādiyugānteṣu kṣatriyādibhirbrāhmaṇāditrivarṇādinipātane dvijarājādinirdiṣṭaviṣṇvavatārapramitiviprādidvārā tattadbrahmakṣatriyādināśapurassaraṃ pārāśaravyāsaprakāśitacaturvargapradīpabhūtamahābhāratasya vaiśampāyanena parīkṣinnṛpāyākhyānaṃ vedānvyasya pailajaiminyādiśiṣyāṇā madhyāpanaṃ vālmīkinirmitarāmākhyānaṃ viṣṇuyaśasaḥ kalkyudbhavatatkartavyādi ca.
meaning: 74 पुरा कृतादियुगान्तेषु क्षत्रियादिभिर्ब्राह्मणादित्रिवर्णादिनिपातने द्विजराजादिनिर्दिष्टविष्ण्ववतारप्रमितिविप्रादिद्वारा तत्तद्ब्रह्मक्षत्रियादिनाशपुरस्सरं पाराशरव्यासप्रकाशितचतुर्वर्गप्रदीपभूतमहाभारतस्य वैशम्पायनेन परीक्षिन्नृपायाख्यानं वेदान्व्यस्य पैलजैमिन्यादिशिष्याणा मध्यापनं वाल्मीकिनिर्मितरामाख्यानं विष्णुयशसः कल्क्युद्भवतत्कर्तव्यादि च.
text_mt: 74 In ancient times at the ends of the Kṛta and other ages, when the three classes beginning with the brahmins were brought low by the kṣatriyas and others, the destruction of those various brahmins, kṣatriyas, and others through the avatars of Viṣṇu indicated by the lord of the twice-born and others; the narration of the Mahābhārata, the lamp of the four aims of life revealed by Vyāsa, son of Parāśara, by Vaiśampāyana to King Parīkṣit; the division of the Vedas and teaching them to disciples such as Paila and Jaimini; the story of Rāma composed by Vālmīki; and the origin of Kalki from Viṣṇuyaśas, his duties, and so on.

sanskrit_iast:
75 kṣīṇe manvantare manvantareśvarāṇāṃ maharloke manuśakradevasaptarṣīṇāṃ brahmaloke nivāsaḥ, kulaparvatavarjyaṃ bhūlokasya nāśaḥ, naukārūpeṇa dharitryāḥ sarvabījarakṣaṇaṃ bhaviṣyanmanunā saha saptarṣīṇāṃ tatra nivāsaḥ, .
matsyarūpiśṛṃgiviṣṇornaukārakṣaṇaṃ munīnāṃ tatstavanaṃ nāvi himaśiśikharaṃ nītāyāṃ viṣṇorantardhānaṃ kṛtayugaprādurbhāvaśca.
meaning:
75 क्षीणे मन्वन्तरे मन्वन्तरेश्वराणां महर्लोके मनुशक्रदेवसप्तर्षीणां ब्रह्मलोके निवासः, कुलपर्वतवर्ज्यं भूलोकस्य नाशः, नौकारूपेण धरित्र्याः सर्वबीजरक्षणं भविष्यन्मनुना सह सप्तर्षीणां तत्र निवासः, .
मत्स्यरूपिशृंगिविष्णोर्नौकारक्षणं मुनीनां तत्स्तवनं नावि हिमशिशिखरं नीतायां विष्णोरन्तर्धानं कृतयुगप्रादुर्भावश्च.
text_mt: 75 When a manvantara has waned, the lords of the manvantara dwell in Maharloka, and the Manu, Śakra, the gods, and the seven seers dwell in Brahmaloka; the destruction of the earthly world except for the principal mountain ranges; the preservation of all seeds by the earth in the form of a boat, the dwelling there of the seven seers together with the future Manu; / the preservation of the boat by Viṣṇu with a horn in the form of a fish, the seers' praise of him, the disappearance of Viṣṇu when the boat is led to the peak of the Himalayas, and the manifestation of the Kṛta age.

sanskrit_iast: 76 jalaprāyabhūtale saptasūryadagdhajīvānāṃ janaloke sthitiḥ, raudratejasā'rka nāśe mahāraudraghanāvāripūrṇajagati svaśarīre vāyuṣmādāya yugasahasraparyantamarṇave pitāmahaḥ svapiti vibuddhaśca sṛjati jagaditi pratikalpakramaḥ ... ...
meaning: 76 जलप्रायभूतले सप्तसूर्यदग्धजीवानां जनलोके स्थितिः, रौद्रतेजसाऽर्क नाशे महारौद्रघनावारिपूर्णजगति स्वशरीरे वायुष्मादाय युगसहस्रपर्यन्तमर्णवे पितामहः स्वपिति विबुद्धश्च सृजति जगदिति प्रतिकल्पक्रमः ... ...
text_mt: 76 On the earth which is mostly water, the living beings burnt by the seven suns abide in Janaloka; when the sun is destroyed by the fiery energy of Rudra, the world being filled with the waters of the terrible clouds of Rudra, the Grandfather gathers the breath into his own body and sleeps in the ocean for a thousand ages, and on waking creates the world: such is the order of every aeon...

sanskrit_iast: 77 kalpānte jagadasvathāvarṇanam
meaning: 77 कल्पान्ते जगदस्वथावर्णनम्
text_mt: 77 Description of the unstable state of the world at the end of the aeon.

sanskrit_iast: 78 ekārṇave bhūmitale vaṭaśākhini paryaṃṅkasthabhagavadudare brahmā trilokīdarśanāntaraṃ yugasahasramuṣitvāpyantaṃ nāpa.
meaning: 78 एकार्णवे भूमितले वटशाखिनि पर्यंङ्कस्थभगवदुदरे ब्रह्मा त्रिलोकीदर्शनान्तरं युगसहस्रमुषित्वाप्यन्तं नाप.
text_mt: 78 In the single vast ocean on the surface of the earth, within the belly of the Lord reclining on a couch under the branch of a banyan tree, Brahmā, even after residing for a thousand ages seeing the three worlds, did not find the end.

sanskrit_iast: 79 kalpānte bālarūpiviṣṇoraniruddhatā tannābhikamalādbrahmāvirbhāvaḥ .
meaning: 79 कल्पान्ते बालरूपिविष्णोरनिरुद्धता तन्नाभिकमलाद्ब्रह्माविर्भावः .
text_mt: 79 At the end of the aeon, Viṣṇu in the form of a child is Aniruddha; Brahmā's emergence from his lotus-navel.

sanskrit_iast: 80 brahmotpatimārabhya kālagatipūrvakaṃ vajraparīkṣijjanamejayācalavajrāṇāṃ bhāvyetadavanirakṣaṇamabhidhāya dhanañjayānantaraṃ rākṣasaiḥ sudharmasabhāyā himācale nayanam
meaning: 80 ब्रह्मोत्पतिमारभ्य कालगतिपूर्वकं वज्रपरीक्षिज्जनमेजयाचलवज्राणां भाव्येतदवनिरक्षणमभिधाय धनञ्जयानन्तरं राक्षसैः सुधर्मसभाया हिमाचले नयनम्
text_mt: 80 Beginning from the origin of Brahmā, proceeding with the passage of time, stating the future protection of this earth by Vajra, Parīkṣit, Janamejaya, and Acalavajra, the abduction of the Sudharmā assembly to the Himālaya mountains by the rākṣasas after Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit_iast: 81 ahorātrakalpādyātmakakālasya daivatādikathanapurassaraṃ manvantarasādṛśyakathanam
meaning: 81 अहोरात्रकल्पाद्यात्मककालस्य दैवतादिकथनपुरस्सरं मन्वन्तरसादृश्यकथनम्
text_mt: 81 Stating the deities and other attributes of Time consisting of day, night, the aeon, and so forth, and describing the similarity of the manvantaras.

sanskrit_iast: 82 kṛtādiyugadevaṣaṣṭyabdanāma tatkālagurucārasambhūtadvādaśābdādhipa tatphalasaumyabārhaspatyanākṣatrādivarṣatatphalasaṃvatsarādhipagrahādivarṇanam ...
meaning: 82 कृतादियुगदेवषष्ट्यब्दनाम तत्कालगुरुचारसम्भूतद्वादशाब्दाधिप तत्फलसौम्यबार्हस्पत्यनाक्षत्रादिवर्षतत्फलसंवत्सराधिपग्रहादिवर्णनम् ...
text_mt: 82 The deities of the Kṛta and other ages, the names of the sixty years, the rulers of the twelve-year cycles arising from the transit of Jupiter at that time, their fruits, the gentle years, the Bārhaspatya years, the lunar-mansion years, their fruits, the planets presiding over the years, and so on...

sanskrit_iast: 83 sadevatākā'yanamāsagrahanakṣatratithikaraṇāni, karaṇānayanaprakāraviṣṭihorākulikādivelāmuhūrtatatsvāmivarṇanaṃ yathāsamayakṛtārcāyāḥ phalādhikyañca
meaning: 83 सदेवताकाऽयनमासग्रहनक्षत्रतिथिकरणानि, करणानयनप्रकारविष्टिहोराकुलिकादिवेलामुहूर्ततत्स्वामिवर्णनं यथासमयकृतार्चायाः फलाधिक्यञ्च
text_mt: 83 The half-years, months, planets, lunar mansions, lunar days, and karaṇas along with their deities; the method of calculating karaṇas, viṣṭi, planetary hours, kulika periods, Muhūrtas and their lords, and the greater fruit of worship performed at the proper time.

sanskrit_iast: 84 lagnataddevatāhorādreṣkāṇanavāṃśarāśīśvaratriṃśāṃśakathanam .........
meaning: 84 लग्नतद्देवताहोराद्रेष्काणनवांशराशीश्वरत्रिंशांशकथनम् .........
text_mt: 84 Description of the ascendants, their deities, horās, dreṣkāṇas, navāṃśas, lords of the zodiacal signs, and triṃśāṃśas...

sanskrit_iast: 85 grahanakṣatrādivaśācchubhāśubhaparijñānam .
meaning: 85 ग्रहनक्षत्रादिवशाच्छुभाशुभपरिज्ञानम् .
text_mt: 85 Knowledge of the auspicious and inauspicious by means of the planets, lunar mansions, and so on.

sanskrit_iast: 86 pīḍitagrahanakṣatrāṇāṃ tattaddikpīḍākaratvaṃ yuddhe vidhvastaparājitanīcapitṛgṛhasthānāmapi svasvadikpīḍanam .........
meaning: 86 पीडितग्रहनक्षत्राणां तत्तद्दिक्पीडाकरत्वं युद्धे विध्वस्तपराजितनीचपितृगृहस्थानामपि स्वस्वदिक्पीडनम् .........
text_mt: 86 Afflicted planets and lunar mansions bring affliction to their respective directions; even those destroyed, defeated in planetary war, debilitated, or situated in the ancestral house afflict their own respective directions...

sanskrit_iast: 87 janmādyāśritacandrādinakṣatranavaṣaṭtrinakṣatrādiśubhāśubhakathanam
meaning: 87 जन्माद्याश्रितचन्द्रादिनक्षत्रनवषट्त्रिनक्षत्रादिशुभाशुभकथनम्
text_mt: 87 Statement of the auspicious and inauspicious effects of the nine, six, three, and other lunar mansions relative to the moon's lunar mansion and others occupied at birth.

sanskrit_iast: 88 aśvinyādinakṣatratārāsaṃkhyāgrahanakṣatramaṇḍalādivarṇanam .
meaning: 88 अश्विन्यादिनक्षत्रतारासंख्याग्रहनक्षत्रमण्डलादिवर्णनम् .
text_mt: 88 The number of stars in the lunar mansions beginning with Aśvinī, the spheres of planets and lunar mansions, and so on.

sanskrit_iast: 89 janmakarmasāṅghātikasāmudāyikavaināśikābhiṣekarkṣadeśanakṣatreṣu pīḍiteṣu gomūtrādyabhiṣekapurassaraṃ tattadgrahapūjādi
meaning: 89 जन्मकर्मसाङ्घातिकसामुदायिकवैनाशिकाभिषेकर्क्षदेशनक्षत्रेषु पीडितेषु गोमूत्राद्यभिषेकपुरस्सरं तत्तद्ग्रहपूजादि
text_mt: 89 When the natal, action, collective, communal, destructive, consecration, and country lunar mansions are afflicted, worship of the respective planets preceded by lustrations with cow urine and other substances.

sanskrit_iast: 90 graharkṣapūjāvidhivarṇanam
meaning: 90 ग्रहर्क्षपूजाविधिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 90 Description of the ritual of worship for planets and lunar mansions.

sanskrit_iast: 91 tattaddravyairgraharkṣasnānavidhivarṇanam
meaning: 91 तत्तद्द्रव्यैर्ग्रहर्क्षस्नानविधिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 91 Description of the bath ritual for planets and lunar mansions with respective substances.

sanskrit_iast: 92 bhūmyuddhāravedinirmāṇatatsaṃskārādyagnikārye prāktanakathanapurassaraṃ homāṃte mahākalpādideyādhipatīnāṃ vaidikamantrairhavanakarmasamāptirūpottaratantrakathanam
meaning: 92 भूम्युद्धारवेदिनिर्माणतत्संस्काराद्यग्निकार्ये प्राक्तनकथनपुरस्सरं होमांते महाकल्पादिदेयाधिपतीनां वैदिकमन्त्रैर्हवनकर्मसमाप्तिरूपोत्तरतन्त्रकथनम्
text_mt: 92 After previously setting forth the preparation of the ground, construction of the altar, and its consecration in the fire ritual, description of the concluding ritual consisting of the completion of the fire-offering with Vedic mantras to the lords of the great aeon and other presiding deities at the end of the oblation.

sanskrit_iast: 93 pañcagavyena maṇḍalaśaucādi vidhāya jīvāvāhanagrahapūjādikathanam
meaning: 93 पञ्चगव्येन मण्डलशौचादि विधाय जीवावाहनग्रहपूजादिकथनम्
text_mt: 93 Having performed purification of the sacred diagram with the five products of the cow, the invocation of life, the worship of the planets, and so forth are described.

sanskrit_iast: 94 sarvagrahayajane maṇḍalavidhiṃ vidhāya madhye sadhruvakoṣṭhakadvādaśakoṣṭhabhagaṇe prācyādito meṣādikalpatvā''kāśadhruvadigbhāgādimaṇḍaleṣu tattaddevatāmaṇḍaleṣu ca tattannyāsakaraṇam
meaning: 94 सर्वग्रहयजने मण्डलविधिं विधाय मध्ये सध्रुवकोष्ठकद्वादशकोष्ठभगणे प्राच्यादितो मेषादिकल्पत्वा'ऽकाशध्रुवदिग्भागादिमण्डलेषु तत्तद्देवतामण्डलेषु च तत्तन्न्यासकरणम्
