text_mt: 94 Having prescribed the diagram ritual in the worship of all planets, in the zodiac of twelve divisions having Dhruva's division in the centre, the performance of the respective ritual placements in the diagrams of the sky, Dhruva, and the directional portions beginning with the east as the Aries-cycle, and in the diagrams of the respective deities.

sanskrit_iast: 95 dhruvākāśānantagrahanakṣatrādyāvāhanam
meaning: 95 ध्रुवाकाशानन्तग्रहनक्षत्राद्यावाहनम्
text_mt: 95 Invocation of Dhruva, the sky, Ananta, the planets, lunar mansions, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 96 tattaddevatānulepanavarṇanam ... . . . .
meaning: 96 तत्तद्देवतानुलेपनवर्णनम् ... . . . .
text_mt: 96 Description of the anointings of the respective deities...

sanskrit_iast: 97 graharkṣadigdevatādīnāṃ tattadvarṇavastrapatākābhūṣaṇaratnapuṣpādidānam
meaning: 97 ग्रहर्क्षदिग्देवतादीनां तत्तद्वर्णवस्त्रपताकाभूषणरत्नपुष्पादिदानम्
text_mt: 97 Presentation of garments of the respective colours, banners, ornaments, jewels, flowers, and so on to the planets, lunar mansions, and directional deities.

sanskrit_iast: 98 tattaddevānāṃ tattaddravyadhūpadīpādi
meaning: 98 तत्तद्देवानां तत्तद्द्रव्यधूपदीपादि
text_mt: 98 Incense, lamps, and so on of the respective substances for the respective deities.

sanskrit_iast: 99 dhuvasthānaniviṣṭadevānāṃ naivedyapadārthāḥ ...
meaning: 99 धुवस्थाननिविष्टदेवानां नैवेद्यपदार्थाः ...
text_mt: 99 Food offerings for the deities situated in the place of Dhruva...

sanskrit_iast: 100 tathā pānapadārthāḥ
meaning: 100 तथा पानपदार्थाः
text_mt: 100 Likewise the drink offerings.

sanskrit_iast: 101 tattaddevatāhomapadārthakathanam
meaning: 101 तत्तद्देवताहोमपदार्थकथनम्
text_mt: 101 Description of the oblation substances for the respective deities.

sanskrit_iast: 102 dhruvadigbrahmagraharkṣāṇāṃ homamantrāḥ
meaning: 102 ध्रुवदिग्ब्रह्मग्रहर्क्षाणां होममन्त्राः
text_mt: 102 Oblation mantras for Dhruva, the directions, Brahmā, the planets, and the lunar mansions.

sanskrit_iast: 103 tattaddevatādakṣiṇānirdeśaḥ
meaning: 103 तत्तद्देवतादक्षिणानिर्देशः
text_mt: 103 Direction regarding the sacrificial fees for the respective deities.

sanskrit_iast: 104 śāntyavasāne yājakakartṛkayajamānakare pratisarabandhanamāśīrvādaśca
meaning: 104 शान्त्यवसाने याजककर्तृकयजमानकरे प्रतिसरबन्धनमाशीर्वादश्च
text_mt: 104 At the conclusion of the propitiation, the tying of the protective cord on the hand of the patron of the sacrifice by the officiating priest, and the blessing.

sanskrit_iast: 105 grahaśāntiphalābhidhānam
meaning: 105 ग्रहशान्तिफलाभिधानम्
text_mt: 105 Statement of the fruit of the propitiation of the planets.

sanskrit_iast: 106 graharkṣameḍhībhūtadhuvasthitacaturdaśatārakānāmanirdeśapūrvakaṃ śiśumāracakranibaddhatārakājñānataddarśanādimāhātmyakathanamū, auttānapādidhruvasya viṣṇurūpatā tannibaddhamarujjyotirgaṇasya bhramaṇam, tadadhaḥ krameṇasaptarṣimaṇḍala-bhacakra-śanaiścara-kuja-sūrya-śuka-budha-candrāṇāṃ sthitiḥ, prāgdakṣiṇagatijyotiścakrañca . navagrahāṇāñjanmavṛttam, tatra sūryatejo'sahamānāyāḥ saṃjñāyā manuyamayamunotpattyanucchāyātaḥ sāvarṇaśanaiścarotpattiḥ, uttarakuruṣu vaḍavārūpeṇa carantyāḥ saṃjñāyā kheḥ sakāśādāśvineyaraivantotpattiḥ,raivantapūjayā'śvasampatkathanañca
meaning: 106 ग्रहर्क्षमेढीभूतधुवस्थितचतुर्दशतारकानामनिर्देशपूर्वकं शिशुमारचक्रनिबद्धतारकाज्ञानतद्दर्शनादिमाहात्म्यकथनमू, औत्तानपादिध्रुवस्य विष्णुरूपता तन्निबद्धमरुज्ज्योतिर्गणस्य भ्रमणम्, तदधः क्रमेणसप्तर्षिमण्डल-भचक्र-शनैश्चर-कुज-सूर्य-शुक-बुध-चन्द्राणां स्थितिः, प्राग्दक्षिणगतिज्योतिश्चक्रञ्च . नवग्रहाणाञ्जन्मवृत्तम्, तत्र सूर्यतेजोऽसहमानायाः संज्ञाया मनुयमयमुनोत्पत्त्यनुच्छायातः सावर्णशनैश्चरोत्पत्तिः, उत्तरकुरुषु वडवारूपेण चरन्त्याः संज्ञाया खेः सकाशादाश्विनेयरैवन्तोत्पत्तिः,रैवन्तपूजयाऽश्वसम्पत्कथनञ्च
text_mt: 106 With reference to the fourteen stars located at Dhruva, who serves as the central pivot for the planets and lunar mansions, an explanation of the knowledge of the stars bound to the celestial dolphin-wheel and the greatness of viewing it; the nature of Dhruva, the son of Uttānapāda, as an embodiment of Viṣṇu, and the revolution of the host of luminaries and winds bound to him; below him, in order, the position of the constellation of the seven seers, the zodiacal circle, Saturn, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon; and the eastward-southward motion of the wheel of luminaries; the account of the birth of the nine planets: therein, of Saṃjñā unable to endure the Sun's brilliance, the birth of Manu, Yama, and Yamunā, followed by the birth of Sāvarṇi and Saturn from Chāyā; of Saṃjñā wandering in the northern Kurus in the form of a mare, the birth of the two Aśvins and Revanta from the Sun; and statement of the acquisition of horses through the worship of Revanta.

sanskrit_iast: 107 asurasurapitṛdvijādiśabdārthasandhyopāsanahetu manuṣyarākṣasagandharvādivividhasṛṣṭikathanapurassaraṃ svadharmasthitadvijānāṃ svargādyuttamalokavāsaḥ prajāpatyaṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ dakṣatatpatnīprādurbhāvatatprasūtivistāradakṣayajñe'nāhūtasatyanādaraprayuktatanutyāgena manuṣyo bhaveti dakṣāya śivaśāpādyākhyānam
meaning: 107 असुरसुरपितृद्विजादिशब्दार्थसन्ध्योपासनहेतु मनुष्यराक्षसगन्धर्वादिविविधसृष्टिकथनपुरस्सरं स्वधर्मस्थितद्विजानां स्वर्गाद्युत्तमलोकवासः प्रजापत्यंगुष्ठाभ्यां दक्षतत्पत्नीप्रादुर्भावतत्प्रसूतिविस्तारदक्षयज्ञेऽनाहूतसत्यनादरप्रयुक्ततनुत्यागेन मनुष्यो भवेति दक्षाय शिवशापाद्याख्यानम्
text_mt: 107 The meaning of the terms asura, sura, ancestor, twice-born, and so forth; the reason for twilight worship; following the account of the diverse creations of humans, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and others, the residence of twice-borns steadfast in their own dharma in heaven and other supreme worlds; the manifestation of Dakṣa and his wife from the thumbs of the lord of creatures; the expansion of his offspring; and, on account of the casting off of her body out of disrespect for Satī when uninvited to Dakṣa's sacrifice, the curse given by Śiva to Dakṣa: "Become a human."

sanskrit_iast: 108 dhuvavaṃśyakathane venasyātikāntamaryādatvādadharmanivārakahitopadeṣṭṛmunivacassvanādarācca devadattaprajñayā mantrapūtajalena taistasyāsubhirvirahīkaraṇam, punarmantrapūtakuśodakena tadūrumanthanānniṣādapṛthū utpedāte
meaning: 108 धुववंश्यकथने वेनस्यातिकान्तमर्यादत्वादधर्मनिवारकहितोपदेष्टृमुनिवचस्स्वनादराच्च देवदत्तप्रज्ञया मन्त्रपूतजलेन तैस्तस्यासुभिर्विरहीकरणम्, पुनर्मन्त्रपूतकुशोदकेन तदूरुमन्थनान्निषादपृथू उत्पेदाते
text_mt: 108 In the account of the lineage of Dhruva, because Vena transgressed limits and showed disrespect toward the words of the sages who prevented adharma and offered beneficial counsel, their depriving him of his life-breaths with water consecrated by mantras using intelligence bestowed by the gods; then, from the churning of his thigh with water and kuśa grass consecrated by mantras, the arising of the Niṣāda and of Pṛthu.

sanskrit_iast: 109 brahmaviṣṇādidevakṛtapṛthurājyābhiṣeke devadattahayagajacchatracāmarādibhi statprabhāvardhanānte sūtamāgadhastavanahṛṣṭasya tasya tābhyāmanūpamāgadhagrāmadānam, vṛttyarthiprajāprārthanayā pṛthvītaḥ sasyādyānayanaṃ svāyambhuva manusomādivatsadohanātsasyasudhāpayoviṣāṣādyutpattiḥ,pitṛviraktaprajānāṃ tenānurañjanam
meaning: 109 ब्रह्मविष्णादिदेवकृतपृथुराज्याभिषेके देवदत्तहयगजच्छत्रचामरादिभि स्तत्प्रभावर्धनान्ते सूतमागधस्तवनहृष्टस्य तस्य ताभ्यामनूपमागधग्रामदानम्, वृत्त्यर्थिप्रजाप्रार्थनया पृथ्वीतः सस्याद्यानयनं स्वायम्भुव मनुसोमादिवत्सदोहनात्सस्यसुधापयोविषाषाद्युत्पत्तिः,पितृविरक्तप्रजानां तेनानुरञ्जनम्
text_mt: 109 In Pṛthu's royal consecration performed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and other gods, after the enhancement of his majesty through horses, elephants, parasols, chowries, and the like bestowed by the gods, his granting of marshland and the Magadha village to the bard and the herald, delighted by their praise; at the request of his subjects seeking livelihood, the drawing forth of grain and other produce from the earth; from the milking [of the earth] as Svāyambhuva Manu, Soma, and others [acted as calves], the emergence of grain, nectar, milk, poison, and so forth; and his winning the affection of the subjects who had become alienated under his father.

sanskrit_iast: 110 pṛthuputraprācīnabarhitanujānāṃ daśaprācīnabarhiṣāṃ daśavarṣaparyantaṃ tapaścaraṇena vṛkṣavṛddhayā prajākṣaye sati sammilitapracetomukhasamutthāgninā drumakṣaye somarājaprārthanayā vṛkṣarājakanyāyā māriṣayā vṛkṣāṇāṃ patnītvena grahaṇe dakṣaprajāpatijanma, tataśca haraśāpāttanmānasīsṛṣṭyuparodhe vīraṇaprajāpatikanyāyāṃ vīriṇyāṃ putrasahasrotpattiḥ, nāradopadeśanaṣṭeṣu putreṣu dakṣaśāpānnāradasya kaśyapasutatvena janma, haradvārā dakṣasyāśdhamedhabhaṅgo dakṣeṇāpi yajñe śivaṃ na yakṣyantīti śāpadānaṃ dakṣaprasūtivarṇanañca
meaning: 110 पृथुपुत्रप्राचीनबर्हितनुजानां दशप्राचीनबर्हिषां दशवर्षपर्यन्तं तपश्चरणेन वृक्षवृद्धया प्रजाक्षये सति सम्मिलितप्रचेतोमुखसमुत्थाग्निना द्रुमक्षये सोमराजप्रार्थनया वृक्षराजकन्याया मारिषया वृक्षाणां पत्नीत्वेन ग्रहणे दक्षप्रजापतिजन्म, ततश्च हरशापात्तन्मानसीसृष्ट्युपरोधे वीरणप्रजापतिकन्यायां वीरिण्यां पुत्रसहस्रोत्पत्तिः, नारदोपदेशनष्टेषु पुत्रेषु दक्षशापान्नारदस्य कश्यपसुतत्वेन जन्म, हरद्वारा दक्षस्याश्धमेधभङ्गो दक्षेणापि यज्ञे शिवं न यक्ष्यन्तीति शापदानं दक्षप्रसूतिवर्णनञ्च
text_mt: 110 Because the ten Prācīnabarhis sons, offspring of Pṛthu's son Prācīnabarhis, practiced austerities for ten years, there was a destruction of living beings due to the growth of trees; when the trees were being destroyed by the fire that arose from the mouths of the gathered Pracetases, upon the plea of King Soma, their taking of Māriṣā, the daughter of the king of trees, as their wife; the birth of the lord of creatures Dakṣa; then, when his mental creation was obstructed due to the curse of Hara, the birth of a thousand sons in Vīriṇī, the daughter of the lord of creatures Vīraṇa; when those sons were lost through Nārada's instruction, Nārada's birth as the son of Kaśyapa due to Dakṣa's curse; the disruption of Dakṣa's horse-sacrifice by Hara; the pronouncement of a curse by Dakṣa too, saying, "They shall not sacrifice to Śiva in the ritual"; and the description of Dakṣa's offspring.

sanskrit_iast: 111 svāyambhuve'ntare śivaśaptamunīnāṃ vaivasvate'ntare sambhavaḥ, bhṛgvaṅgiraḥprabhṛtimunīnāmutpattipravarasaṃkhyā'vaivāhyatā
meaning: 111 स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे शिवशप्तमुनीनां वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे सम्भवः, भृग्वङ्गिरःप्रभृतिमुनीनामुत्पत्तिप्रवरसंख्याऽवैवाह्यता
text_mt: 111 The birth in the Vaivasvata interval of the sages who were cursed by Śiva in the Svāyambhuva interval; the origin, the number of pravaras, and the prohibition of intermarriage among the sages beginning with Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras.

sanskrit_iast: 112 aṅgiraso vaṃśānuvarṇanaṃ tadvaṃśyānāṃ mitho'vaivāhyatā . .... ....
meaning: 112 अङ्गिरसो वंशानुवर्णनं तद्वंश्यानां मिथोऽवैवाह्यता . .... ....
text_mt: 112 The description of the lineage of Aṅgiras and the prohibition of intermarriage among the members of his lineage.

sanskrit_iast: 113 atrivaṃśyagotrakāramuniśākhānirdeśapurassaramatriputrikāputravarṇanaṃ mitho'vaivāhyatā ca
meaning: 113 अत्रिवंश्यगोत्रकारमुनिशाखानिर्देशपुरस्सरमत्रिपुत्रिकापुत्रवर्णनं मिथोऽवैवाह्यता च
text_mt: 113 Following the specification of the sage-branches that founded clans descended from Atri, the description of the sons of Atri's daughter and their mutual prohibition of intermarriage.

sanskrit_iast: 114 atreraparavaṃśavarṇane tapasā viśvāmitrasya brāhmaṇyamāptistripravarāṇāṃ tadvaṃśyānāṃ mitho'vivāhyatā ca ..
meaning: 114 अत्रेरपरवंशवर्णने तपसा विश्वामित्रस्य ब्राह्मण्यमाप्तिस्त्रिप्रवराणां तद्वंश्यानां मिथोऽविवाह्यता च ..
text_mt: 114 In the description of the other lineage of Atri, Viśvāmitra's attainment of brahminhood through austerity, and the mutual prohibition of intermarriage among his descendants who have three pravaras.

sanskrit_iast: 115 mārīcakaśyapakule gotrakāramunināmapravarasaṃkhyādvyāmuṣyāyaṇagotraādi varṇanam 116 vaśiṣṭhavaṃśīyaikarṣipravarādivarṇanam....
meaning: 115 मारीचकश्यपकुले गोत्रकारमुनिनामप्रवरसंख्याद्व्यामुष्यायणगोत्रआदि वर्णनम् 116 वशिष्ठवंशीयैकर्षिप्रवरादिवर्णनम्....
text_mt: 115 In the family of Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, the description of the names of the clan-founding sages, the number of their pravaras, the clans of double descent, and so forth. 116 The description of the single-seer pravaras and others belonging to the lineage of Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit_iast: 117 nimipūrvapurohitavaśiṣṭhe tasyānavaratayājanaśrānte kiñcidviśramya yājayiṣya ityuttavatyapi dharmācaraṇe kālayāpanaṃ na śreya iti dvitīyapurohitadvārā yiyakṣamāṇaṃ videho bhaveti nirmi śaśāpa vaśiṣṭhaḥ; nimirapyanucitakāriṇaṃ taṃ videho bhaveti śaśāpa, brahmavaradānānmanuṣyapakṣmasu nimervāsaḥ, vaśiṣṭhajīvasya mitrāvaruṇaputratā, nāradabhaginyā'rundhatyā vaśiṣṭhasyodvāhaḥ, tasyāṃ śakterjanma, tatsutaḥ parāśaraḥ; tatputro dvaipāyanaḥ, tasya kṛṣṇanīlaraktaśvetagauradhūmraparāśarāsteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ tryārṣeyāḥ pravarāḥ ( parāśaraśaktivaśiṣṭhāḥ ) teṣāṃ mitho'vaivāhyam ....
meaning: 117 निमिपूर्वपुरोहितवशिष्ठे तस्यानवरतयाजनश्रान्ते किञ्चिद्विश्रम्य याजयिष्य इत्युत्तवत्यपि धर्माचरणे कालयापनं न श्रेय इति द्वितीयपुरोहितद्वारा यियक्षमाणं विदेहो भवेति निर्मि शशाप वशिष्ठः; निमिरप्यनुचितकारिणं तं विदेहो भवेति शशाप, ब्रह्मवरदानान्मनुष्यपक्ष्मसु निमेर्वासः, वशिष्ठजीवस्य मित्रावरुणपुत्रता, नारदभगिन्याऽरुन्धत्या वशिष्ठस्योद्वाहः, तस्यां शक्तेर्जन्म, तत्सुतः पराशरः; तत्पुत्रो द्वैपायनः, तस्य कृष्णनीलरक्तश्वेतगौरधूम्रपराशरास्तेषां सर्वेषां त्र्यार्षेयाः प्रवराः ( पराशरशक्तिवशिष्ठाः ) तेषां मिथोऽवैवाह्यम् ....
text_mt: 117 When Nimi's former family priest, Vasiṣṭha, who was exhausted from continuously performing sacrifices for him, said, "Having rested a little, I will officiate for you," Vasiṣṭha cursed Nimi, who was seeking to sacrifice through a second family priest because delaying the performance of dharma is not beneficial: "Become bodiless"; Nimi too cursed him who had acted improperly: "Become bodiless"; by the boon of Brahmā, Nimi's residence in the eyelashes of human beings; the soul of Vasiṣṭha becoming the son of Mitra and Varuṇa; Vasiṣṭha's marriage to Arundhatī, the sister of Nārada; the birth of Śakti in her; his son Parāśara; his son Dvaipāyana; his [clans], the black, blue, red, white, fair, and smoky Parāśaras; all of them have three-seer pravaras (Parāśara, Śakti, and Vasiṣṭha); their mutual prohibition of intermarriage.

sanskrit_iast: 118 agastyavaṃśapravarakathanaprasaṅge pulastyapulahakratvagastyānāmekavaṃśatā
meaning: 118 अगस्त्यवंशप्रवरकथनप्रसङ्गे पुलस्त्यपुलहक्रत्वगस्त्यानामेकवंशता
text_mt: 118 In the context of stating the lineage and pravaras of Agastya, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Agastya belonging to a single lineage.

sanskrit_iast: 119 arundhatīprasūtivarṇanam
meaning: 119 अरुन्धतीप्रसूतिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 119 The description of the offspring of Arundhatī.

sanskrit_iast: 120 kaśyapavaṃśavarṇanaṃ, ādityotpattiḥ . . . .
meaning: 120 कश्यपवंशवर्णनं, आदित्योत्पत्तिः . . . .
text_mt: 120 The description of Kaśyapa's lineage; the birth of the Ādityas.

sanskrit_iast: 121 hiraṇyākṣādīnnṛvarāhadirūpeṇa hatvā baliñca chalayitvā bāṇāsurayuddhe sakārtikeyarudraṃ kṛṣṇo vijigye .
meaning: 121 हिरण्याक्षादीन्नृवराहदिरूपेण हत्वा बलिञ्च छलयित्वा बाणासुरयुद्धे सकार्तिकेयरुद्रं कृष्णो विजिग्ये .
text_mt: 121 Having slain Hiraṇyākṣa and others in the form of the man-boar and other [avatāras], and having deceived Bali, Kṛṣṇa conquered Rudra along with Kārttikeya in the battle with the asura Bāṇa.

sanskrit_iast: 122 mayatārapramukhadaityaparājitadevānāṃ devācāryasaṃnidhigamane tatkṛtāgnistutiprītavahninā tadūrīkaraṇam .
meaning: 122 मयतारप्रमुखदैत्यपराजितदेवानां देवाचार्यसंनिधिगमने तत्कृताग्निस्तुतिप्रीतवह्निना तदूरीकरणम् .
text_mt: 122 When the gods, defeated by the daityas led by Maya and Tāra, approached the preceptor of the gods, the removal [of the daityas] by Fire, pleased by the hymn to Agni composed by him.

sanskrit_iast: 123 agrisāhāyyārthaṃ devācāryakṛtavāyustavanam .
meaning: 123 अग्रिसाहाय्यार्थं देवाचार्यकृतवायुस्तवनम् .
text_mt: 123 The hymn to Vāyu composed by the preceptor of the gods to assist Agni.

sanskrit_iast: 124 agnivāyuparājitadaityānāṃ pātāle gamanamū, kālanemino devānparājitya trailokyeśvaratvaṃ vaiṣṇavapadecchayā viṣṇudarśanañca ...
meaning: 124 अग्निवायुपराजितदैत्यानां पाताले गमनमू, कालनेमिनो देवान्पराजित्य त्रैलोक्येश्वरत्वं वैष्णवपदेच्छया विष्णुदर्शनञ्च ...
text_mt: 124 The going of the daityas, defeated by Agni and Vāyu, to the netherworld; Kālanemi's defeat of the gods, his sovereignty over the three worlds, and his vision of Viṣṇu out of a desire for the abode of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: 125 kālanemiṃ nipātya brahmastuto viṣṇurlokapālānyathāpurā tattatsthāneṣu yojayitvā devānyajñabhujaścakāra .
meaning: 125 कालनेमिं निपात्य ब्रह्मस्तुतो विष्णुर्लोकपालान्यथापुरा तत्तत्स्थानेषु योजयित्वा देवान्यज्ञभुजश्चकार .
text_mt: 125 Having struck down Kālanemi, Viṣṇu, praised by Brahmā, appointed the guardians of the worlds to their respective posts as before and made the gods partakers of the sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: 126 balibandhanakruddhadaityatāḍitabhūsuratyaktayajñe bhūtale bubhukṣitadevapreritabrahmaprārthitavarāhurūpiviṣṇunā dhvastaduṣṭadaitye pātāle kṛte sati sa hariḥ svabhaktaprahlādāyābhūtasaṃplavamāyurdaityarājatāṃ tatputravirocanāya kalpāyuṣṭvaṃ pradāya baleḥ sāvarṇikamanvantare śakratvaṃ svīkṛtya tatputraṃ bāṇaṃ svavipriyakāriṇamapi nāsubhirviyokṣya ityanucakampe
meaning: 126 बलिबन्धनक्रुद्धदैत्यताडितभूसुरत्यक्तयज्ञे भूतले बुभुक्षितदेवप्रेरितब्रह्मप्रार्थितवराहुरूपिविष्णुना ध्वस्तदुष्टदैत्ये पाताले कृते सति स हरिः स्वभक्तप्रह्लादायाभूतसंप्लवमायुर्दैत्यराजतां तत्पुत्रविरोचनाय कल्पायुष्ट्वं प्रदाय बलेः सावर्णिकमन्वन्तरे शक्रत्वं स्वीकृत्य तत्पुत्रं बाणं स्वविप्रियकारिणमपि नासुभिर्वियोक्ष्य इत्यनुचकम्पे
text_mt: 126 When the brahmins on earth, beaten by the daityas who were enraged at the binding of Bali, had abandoned the sacrifice, and the evil daityas had been driven into the netherworld by Viṣṇu in the form of a boar, entreated by Brahmā who was urged by the hungry gods, that Hari, having granted an lifespan lasting until the cosmic dissolution and the kingship of the daityas to his devotee Prahlāda, and a lifespan of an aeon to his son Virocana, and having accepted Indrahood for Bali in the Sāvarṇika manvantara, felt compassion for his son Bāṇa, thinking: "Though he has acted against my wishes, I shall not deprive him of his life-breaths."

sanskrit_iast: 127 śakrahantāraṃ putraṃ me prayaccheti ditiprārthitaḥ kaśyapo rajanīṃ tayā sahoṣitvā śucitayā varṣasahasraṃ sthāsyasi cedevaṃ bhaviṣyatītyuktvā tapase jagāma, śakrastu tāṃ chalayitvā sevitumājagāma, abdaśeṣe kāle divā suptāyāstasyā udaraṃ praviśya vajreṇa saptadhā garbhaṃ vidārya punaḥ saptadhā kṛtvonapaṃcāśanmaruto nirmitavān, ditiprārthanayā teṣāṃ sthānāni nāmāni ca cakre
meaning: 127 शक्रहन्तारं पुत्रं मे प्रयच्छेति दितिप्रार्थितः कश्यपो रजनीं तया सहोषित्वा शुचितया वर्षसहस्रं स्थास्यसि चेदेवं भविष्यतीत्युक्त्वा तपसे जगाम, शक्रस्तु तां छलयित्वा सेवितुमाजगाम, अब्दशेषे काले दिवा सुप्तायास्तस्या उदरं प्रविश्य वज्रेण सप्तधा गर्भं विदार्य पुनः सप्तधा कृत्वोनपंचाशन्मरुतो निर्मितवान्, दितिप्रार्थनया तेषां स्थानानि नामानि च चक्रे
text_mt: 127 Entreated by Diti, "Grant me a son who will slay Śakra," Kaśyapa, having dwelt with her for a night, said, "If you remain in purity for a thousand years, it will be so," and went away for austerities; Śakra, however, came to serve her with deception; when a year remained, entering the belly of her who was asleep during the day, he cleaved the fetus into seven parts with his thunderbolt and then made each into seven parts, producing the forty-nine Maruts; at Diti's request, he assigned their abodes and names.

sanskrit_iast: 128 danusiṃhikāprajotpattiprasaṃge gandharvāpsarasāṃ nāmāni tajjanma kadrū santatiḥ, ahalyānirmāṇaṃ tatkāmukaśakrasya nirvṛṣaṇatādi ca
meaning: 128 दनुसिंहिकाप्रजोत्पत्तिप्रसंगे गन्धर्वाप्सरसां नामानि तज्जन्म कद्रू सन्ततिः, अहल्यानिर्माणं तत्कामुकशक्रस्य निर्वृषणतादि च
text_mt: 128 In the context of the emergence of the offspring of Danu and Siṃhikā, the names and birth of the gandharvas and apsarases; the offspring of Kadrū; the creation of Ahalyā; and the castration and other fates of Śakra who desired her.

sanskrit_iast: 129 badaryām̐ tapasyantau naranārāyaṇau pralobhayitumāgatā daśa mauneyāpsaraso lajjayituṃ nārāyaṇena svorvoradbhutarūpasaundaryaśālinanyurvaśī nirmame
meaning: 129 बदर्याम्̐ तपस्यन्तौ नरनारायणौ प्रलोभयितुमागता दश मौनेयाप्सरसो लज्जयितुं नारायणेन स्वोर्वोरद्भुतरूपसौन्दर्यशालिनन्युर्वशी निर्ममे
text_mt: 129 In order to put to shame the ten Mauneya apsarases who had come to tempt Nara and Nārāyaṇa as they practiced austerities at Badarī, Nārāyaṇa created Urvaśī from his own thighs, endowed with marvelous form and beauty.

sanskrit_iast: 130 vaivasvatasya manordvāpare yuge devāsurayuddhaprasaṃgena svargatapurūravanṛpāsaktorvaśyā raṃbhayā sakhyā saha saṃvādaḥ
meaning: 130 वैवस्वतस्य मनोर्द्वापरे युगे देवासुरयुद्धप्रसंगेन स्वर्गतपुरूरवनृपासक्तोर्वश्या रंभया सख्या सह संवादः
text_mt: 130 In the Dvāpara age of Vaivasvata Manu, in the context of the war between gods and asuras, the dialogue of Urvaśī, who was in love with King Purūravas who had gone to heaven, with her friend Rambhā.

sanskrit_iast: 131 rambhayā sahorveśyā ākāśamārgeṇa pratiṣṭhānapurārthagamane nāradadarśanaṃ, tena ca purūravaso gṛhe vāse urvaśīputrīkṛtameṣadvayasya sadā śayanāgāre sthāpanaṃ, ghṛtamātrāhāreṇa vartanaṃ, kadācidapi nagnasya rājño'navalokanamakāmāyāstasyāḥ purūravasā ratyakaraṇam, samayeṣveṣu kasyāpi bhaṃge urvaśyāḥ śilābhāvaḥ, sarvapratijñāhāniśceti, pratiṣṭhānapurasamṛddhivarṇanam 132 kiñcidavaśiṣṭadivasabhāgaṃ yāpayituṃ rambhorvaśīṃ purūravasa ākrīḍaśobhāvarṇanamiṣeṇa vinodayāmāsa
meaning: 131 रम्भया सहोर्वेश्या आकाशमार्गेण प्रतिष्ठानपुरार्थगमने नारददर्शनं, तेन च पुरूरवसो गृहे वासे उर्वशीपुत्रीकृतमेषद्वयस्य सदा शयनागारे स्थापनं, घृतमात्राहारेण वर्तनं, कदाचिदपि नग्नस्य राज्ञोऽनवलोकनमकामायास्तस्याः पुरूरवसा रत्यकरणम्, समयेष्वेषु कस्यापि भंगे उर्वश्याः शिलाभावः, सर्वप्रतिज्ञाहानिश्चेति, प्रतिष्ठानपुरसमृद्धिवर्णनम् 132 किञ्चिदवशिष्टदिवसभागं यापयितुं रम्भोर्वशीं पुरूरवस आक्रीडशोभावर्णनमिषेण विनोदयामास
text_mt: 131 When Urvaśī, accompanied by Rambhā, set out through the sky toward the city of Pratiṣṭhāna, her meeting with Nārada, who laid down the conditions: that the two rams she treated as sons must always remain in her bedchamber while dwelling in Purūravas's palace; that she would live on a diet of ghee alone; that she should never see the king naked; that Purūravas must not make love to her when she was unwilling; that upon the breach of any of these conditions Urvaśī would turn into stone and all agreements would be ruined; and a description of the opulence of the city of Pratiṣṭhāna. 132 To pass the little that remained of the day, Rambhā entertained Urvaśī on the pretext of describing the beauty of Purūravas's pleasure-garden.

sanskrit_iast: 133 candrodaye candrakāntagṛhe sakhisahāye purūravasyāgate rambhayā nṛpasākṣātkārānantaraṃ nāradapratijñāśrāvaṇaṃ putrīkṛtameṣayorarpaṇañca, rambhāśrāvitanāradasamayasya rājñāṃgīkaraṇe prasannarambhāyai rājño ratnārpaṇaṃ tasyāśca laṃkāyāṃ dhanadātmajasya nalakūbarasya svabhartuḥ savidhaṃ gamanaṃ purūravasaścorvaśyā saha ramaṇam
meaning: 133 चन्द्रोदये चन्द्रकान्तगृहे सखिसहाये पुरूरवस्यागते रम्भया नृपसाक्षात्कारानन्तरं नारदप्रतिज्ञाश्रावणं पुत्रीकृतमेषयोरर्पणञ्च, रम्भाश्रावितनारदसमयस्य राज्ञांगीकरणे प्रसन्नरम्भायै राज्ञो रत्नार्पणं तस्याश्च लंकायां धनदात्मजस्य नलकूबरस्य स्वभर्तुः सविधं गमनं पुरूरवसश्चोर्वश्या सह रमणम्
text_mt: 133 At moonrise, when Purūravas arrived at the moonstone palace accompanied by his friends, Rambhā, after meeting the king, communicated Nārada's stipulations and handed over the two rams treated as sons; when the king accepted the conditions of Nārada announced by Rambhā, he presented jewels to the pleased Rambhā, who then departed to Laṅkā to her husband Nalakūbara, son of Dhanada, while Purūravas made love with Urvaśī.

sanskrit_iast: 134 urvaśīpurūravasorvicitraprāsādaratnaveśamanadīpulinādiramyapradeśeṣu krīḍāvarṇanamāyvādipañcaputrotpattirgandharvvāṇāmurvaśyānayanārthaṃ mantraṇā ca
meaning: 134 उर्वशीपुरूरवसोर्विचित्रप्रासादरत्नवेशमनदीपुलिनादिरम्यप्रदेशेषु क्रीडावर्णनमाय्वादिपञ्चपुत्रोत्पत्तिर्गन्धर्व्वाणामुर्वश्यानयनार्थं मन्त्रणा च
text_mt: 134 Description of the sports of Urvaśī and Purūravas in delightful places such as wondrous palaces, jeweled mansions, and riverbanks; the birth of their five sons headed by Āyu; and the consultation among the Gandharvas to fetch Urvaśī back.

sanskrit_iast: 135 ugrasenagandharveṇa rātrāvurvaśīmeṣayorharaṇe tadanveṣaṇāya nagne purūravasi ca nirgate rājñaḥ pratijñābhaṅgādurvaśītirodhāne rājñaḥ pralāpaḥ
meaning: 135 उग्रसेनगन्धर्वेण रात्रावुर्वशीमेषयोर्हरणे तदन्वेषणाय नग्ने पुरूरवसि च निर्गते राज्ञः प्रतिज्ञाभङ्गादुर्वशीतिरोधाने राज्ञः प्रलापः
text_mt: 135 When the Gandharva Ugrasena abducted Urvaśī's two rams by night and Purūravas rushed out naked to search for them, Urvaśī vanished because the king had broken the condition, whereupon the king lamented.

sanskrit_iast: 136 purūravovirahasantaptāyā urvaśyā nāradopadeśādekarātraṃ sahavāsaḥ, gamanasamaye ca gandharvopāsanayā matsaṅgamo bhaviṣyatītyurvaśyupadeśādrājña ekavatsaraparyantaṃ ghoratapaścaraṇaṃ nāradaṃ puraskṛtya gandharvāṇāṃ tatra gatvā varadānānte gandharvatvakārakayāvanmanvantaraṃ tayā saha krīḍākaraṇasya tadanu ca candramaḥpraveśapitṛlokaprāpteśca vare prāpya sabālasya purūravasa urvaśīdattasasthālīkaviśvāyunāmakabālakasya svapure nayanam, mārge gandharvaiḥ sthālyāharaṇaṃ paścācchamīgarbhādagnyutpādanādyupadeśaṃ kṛtvā rājño gandharvatvakārakopadeśaḥ 137 aśvamedhavājapeyāgniṣṭomātirātrādiyajñakaraṇapūrvakaṃ rājño dharitryāmekarāṣṭratvaṃ prajānāmatīva saukhyaṃ rājye dharmaprādhānyatādyupabhujya rājño dehasahitaṃ tridivagamanam
meaning: 136 पुरूरवोविरहसन्तप्ताया उर्वश्या नारदोपदेशादेकरात्रं सहवासः, गमनसमये च गन्धर्वोपासनया मत्सङ्गमो भविष्यतीत्युर्वश्युपदेशाद्राज्ञ एकवत्सरपर्यन्तं घोरतपश्चरणं नारदं पुरस्कृत्य गन्धर्वाणां तत्र गत्वा वरदानान्ते गन्धर्वत्वकारकयावन्मन्वन्तरं तया सह क्रीडाकरणस्य तदनु च चन्द्रमःप्रवेशपितृलोकप्राप्तेश्च वरे प्राप्य सबालस्य पुरूरवस उर्वशीदत्तसस्थालीकविश्वायुनामकबालकस्य स्वपुरे नयनम्, मार्गे गन्धर्वैः स्थाल्याहरणं पश्चाच्छमीगर्भादग्न्युत्पादनाद्युपदेशं कृत्वा राज्ञो गन्धर्वत्वकारकोपदेशः 137 अश्वमेधवाजपेयाग्निष्टोमातिरात्रादियज्ञकरणपूर्वकं राज्ञो धरित्र्यामेकराष्ट्रत्वं प्रजानामतीव सौख्यं राज्ये धर्मप्राधान्यताद्युपभुज्य राज्ञो देहसहितं त्रिदिवगमनम्
text_mt: 136 By the counsel of Nārada, Urvaśī, who was distressed by separation from Purūravas, dwelled with him for one night, and at the time of her departure she instructed the king, 'You shall be reunited with me through worship of the Gandharvas'; after the king performed severe austerities for an entire year, he approached the Gandharvas led by Nārada, and after granting him boons—conferring the status of a Gandharva, sporting with her for the duration of a manvantara, and thereafter entering the moon and attaining the world of the ancestors—Purūravas took his young son named Viśvāyu, born of Urvaśī, along with a vessel given by her, and led him to his own city; on the way, the Gandharvas took back the vessel, but afterward instructed him on producing fire from the hollow of a śamī tree and gave the king the teachings that confer the status of a Gandharva. 137 Having performed sacrifices such as the horse sacrifice, the Vājapeya, the Agniṣṭoma, and the Atirātra, the king established sole dominion over the earth, the subjects enjoyed utmost happiness, dharma was preeminent in the kingdom, and, having experienced all this, the king ascended to heaven in his physical body.

sanskrit_iast: 138 sadehādehapitṛgaṇānāmasaṃkhyā śrāddhadātupitṛtṛptyabhyudayādi
meaning: 138 सदेहादेहपितृगणानामसंख्या श्राद्धदातुपितृतृप्त्यभ्युदयादि
text_mt: 138 The innumerable hosts of ancestors, both embodied and bodiless; the satisfaction of the ancestors for one who offers a śrāddha, his prosperity, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 139 hiraṇyākṣavadhānantaraṃ saukaravapuṣā rasātalādvasudhāmānīya daṃṣṭrāgralagnaṃ mṛtpiṇḍaṃ dakṣiṇe kare kṛtvā svaprasvedaromabhyāṃ tiladarbhau nirmāya viṣṇoḥ piṇḍadāna (śrāddha ) maryādāprakaṭanam
meaning: 139 हिरण्याक्षवधानन्तरं सौकरवपुषा रसातलाद्वसुधामानीय दंष्ट्राग्रलग्नं मृत्पिण्डं दक्षिणे करे कृत्वा स्वप्रस्वेदरोमभ्यां तिलदर्भौ निर्माय विष्णोः पिण्डदान (श्राद्ध ) मर्यादाप्रकटनम्
text_mt: 139 After slaying Hiraṇyākṣa and bringing the earth up from the nether world in the form of a boar, [Viṣṇu] placed the lump of earth clinging to the tip of his tusk upon his right hand, produced sesame seeds and darbha grass from his own sweat and body-hair, and established the proper rule of the offering of funeral cakes (śrāddha).

sanskrit_iast: 140 śrāddhadinenuvarāhaṃ viṣṇuṃ sampūjyāhitāgnyanāhitāgnyoryathādhikāraṃ yogyadvijapitrāvāhanapūjanapiṇḍanirvapaṇapūjanakṣīrānnādinivedanākṣayyadānaprārthanādipurassaraṃ śrāddhakartradhikārasaptarṣimantrakathanam
meaning: 140 श्राद्धदिनेनुवराहं विष्णुं सम्पूज्याहिताग्न्यनाहिताग्न्योर्यथाधिकारं योग्यद्विजपित्रावाहनपूजनपिण्डनिर्वपणपूजनक्षीरान्नादिनिवेदनाक्षय्यदानप्रार्थनादिपुरस्सरं श्राद्धकर्त्रधिकारसप्तर्षिमन्त्रकथनम्
text_mt: 140 Having worshipped Viṣṇu as the Boar on the day of the śrāddha, one who maintains the sacred fires or one who does not, according to his qualification, carries out the invocation of suitable twice-born ancestors, their worship, the scattering of funeral cakes, their adoration, the offering of milk-rice and other foods, the prayer for imperishable giving, and so forth; and the declaration of the Seven Sages' mantra as well as the qualification of the performer of the śrāddha.

sanskrit_iast: 141 śrāddhadeśastatra deyādeyādivicāraśca
meaning: 141 श्राद्धदेशस्तत्र देयादेयादिविचारश्च
text_mt: 141 The proper places for a śrāddha, and the deliberation on what should and should not be offered there.

sanskrit_iast: 142 śrāddhabhedāḥ sādhāraṇaviśeṣakāleṣu teṣāṃ phalāni ca
meaning: 142 श्राद्धभेदाः साधारणविशेषकालेषु तेषां फलानि च
text_mt: 142 The varieties of śrāddha, and their results at ordinary and special times.

sanskrit_iast: 143 śrāddhe pātrāpātravicāraḥ
meaning: 143 श्राद्धे पात्रापात्रविचारः
text_mt: 143 Deliberation on worthy and unworthy recipients at a śrāddha.

sanskrit_iast: 144 gaṅgāyamunāsannihatyāpuṇyāraṇyādiśrāddhadeśānukīrtanam
meaning: 144 गङ्गायमुनासन्निहत्यापुण्यारण्यादिश्राद्धदेशानुकीर्तनम्
text_mt: 144 Recitation of the places for śrāddha, such as the Gaṅgā, the Yamunā, Sannihatyā, sacred forests, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 145 aśūnyaśayanadvitīyāyāṃ vrataśrāddhakaraṇaphalam
meaning: 145 अशून्यशयनद्वितीयायां व्रतश्राद्धकरणफलम्
text_mt: 145 The fruit of observing the vow and performing a śrāddha on the Aśūnyaśayanadvitīyā.

sanskrit_iast: 146 avidyāvihitakarmaṇā saṃsāraṃ vidyāvihitasya ca tasya mokṣasādhanatāmuktvā pāṇḍavānāṃ kṛṣṇasācivyādbhāgyavattaratādikathanapurassaraṃ dharmarūpavṛṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam
meaning: 146 अविद्याविहितकर्मणा संसारं विद्याविहितस्य च तस्य मोक्षसाधनतामुक्त्वा पाण्डवानां कृष्णसाचिव्याद्भाग्यवत्तरतादिकथनपुरस्सरं धर्मरूपवृषलक्षणवर्णनम्
text_mt: 146 Having explained that rites performed in ignorance lead to worldly existence, whereas those performed with spiritual knowledge serve as the means to liberation, and having proclaimed the superior fortune of the Pāṇḍavas on account of Kṛṣṇa's assistance, description of the marks of the bull that is the embodiment of dharma.

sanskrit_iast: 147 vṛṣotsargakālaphalakartavyatādi ....
meaning: 147 वृषोत्सर्गकालफलकर्तव्यतादि ....
text_mt: 147 The time, fruit, duties, and so forth concerning the release of a bull […].

sanskrit_iast: 148 purūravasaḥ pūrvajanmacaritravarṇanam ... .
meaning: 148 पुरूरवसः पूर्वजन्मचरित्रवर्णनम् ... .
text_mt: 148 Description of the deeds of Purūravas in his previous life […].

sanskrit_iast: 149 himavadgiristherāvatīśobhāvarṇanam
meaning: 149 हिमवद्गिरिस्थेरावतीशोभावर्णनम्
text_mt: 149 Description of the beauty of the Irāvatī river situated on the Himavat mountain.

sanskrit_iast: 150 himavadvarṇanam
meaning: 150 हिमवद्वर्णनम्
text_mt: 150 Description of the Himavat.

sanskrit_iast: 151 suramyaprasūnaphalasampattisanāthānekavṛkṣavīrudrājivirājitavividhapakṣigaṇakalakalakalamukharitatyaktasāhajikavairabahuvidhaśvāpadavirājite, atrerāśrame dadhikṣīrakṣaracchilāvalokanasañjātaharṣasya rājñaḥ praveśaḥ
meaning: 151 सुरम्यप्रसूनफलसम्पत्तिसनाथानेकवृक्षवीरुद्राजिविराजितविविधपक्षिगणकलकलकलमुखरितत्यक्तसाहजिकवैरबहुविधश्वापदविराजिते, अत्रेराश्रमे दधिक्षीरक्षरच्छिलावलोकनसञ्जातहर्षस्य राज्ञः प्रवेशः
text_mt: 151 The king's entrance into the hermitage of Atri, which was adorned with rows of many trees and creepers possessing an abundance of delightful blossoms and fruits, made resonant with the sweet murmurs of various flocks of birds, adorned with many kinds of wild beasts that had abandoned their innate hostility, and which brought joy to the king upon beholding rocks that flowed with curd and milk.

sanskrit_iast: 152 añyāśramasarasi tatsiddhisañjātasauvarṇarājatavaidrumādiviṭapiśobhitavedikāyāṃ padmarāgacchadavatpadmaśobhādiyutāyāṃ vividharatnasanāthabhūmyāṃ tādṛśe ca prāsāde bhagavato janārdanasya bhogibhogāvalyāṃ śayānasya rājñā vandanam, tasyaivāśramasyaikadeśe tapaścaraṇañca
meaning: 152 अञ्याश्रमसरसि तत्सिद्धिसञ्जातसौवर्णराजतवैद्रुमादिविटपिशोभितवेदिकायां पद्मरागच्छदवत्पद्मशोभादियुतायां विविधरत्नसनाथभूम्यां तादृशे च प्रासादे भगवतो जनार्दनस्य भोगिभोगावल्यां शयानस्य राज्ञा वन्दनम्, तस्यैवाश्रमस्यैकदेशे तपश्चरणञ्च
text_mt: 152 The king's homage to the Lord Janārdana lying upon the coils of the serpent in another hermitage, on a platform adorned with trees of gold, silver, coral, and other treasures produced by its spiritual power, at a lake adorned with lotuses resembling rubies, upon ground rich in various gems, and inside such a palace; and [the king's] performance of austerities in a corner of that very hermitage.

sanskrit_iast: 153 tatrāśrame gandharvāṇāmapsarobhirvividhavihārānpaśyannapyalolo rājā mahattapaścakāra tatkarmatuṣṭagandharvebhyo madhusūdanaprasādaṃ yayāce
meaning: 153 तत्राश्रमे गन्धर्वाणामप्सरोभिर्विविधविहारान्पश्यन्नप्यलोलो राजा महत्तपश्चकार तत्कर्मतुष्टगन्धर्वेभ्यो मधुसूदनप्रसादं ययाचे
text_mt: 153 In that hermitage, the king, though witnessing the varied sports of the Gandharvas with the Apsarases, remained steadfast and performed severe austerities; and from the Gandharvas who were pleased by that deed he requested the grace of Madhusūdana.

sanskrit_iast: 154 madrarājasya ( bhāvipurūravasaḥ ) svapne'trisamāgamaḥ kṛtakṛtyatā ca bhaviṣyatīti darśanaṃ prabhāte jāgradavasthāyāmatridarśanaṃ, pūrvajanmani dvādaśīvratakaraṇādbhagavati viṣṇau prasanne tava madāśramaprāptiratra ca kṣaudrayuktaśilāprāye mākṣikādiphalayuktapradeśe niraśanapūrvakatapasā prasannena viṣṇunā bhavadicchā'moghīkriyata ityuttamarūpaprāptaye rūpasatropadeśaḥ
meaning: 154 मद्रराजस्य ( भाविपुरूरवसः ) स्वप्नेऽत्रिसमागमः कृतकृत्यता च भविष्यतीति दर्शनं प्रभाते जाग्रदवस्थायामत्रिदर्शनं, पूर्वजन्मनि द्वादशीव्रतकरणाद्भगवति विष्णौ प्रसन्ने तव मदाश्रमप्राप्तिरत्र च क्षौद्रयुक्तशिलाप्राये माक्षिकादिफलयुक्तप्रदेशे निरशनपूर्वकतपसा प्रसन्नेन विष्णुना भवदिच्छाऽमोघीक्रियत इत्युत्तमरूपप्राप्तये रूपसत्रोपदेशः
text_mt: 154 The king of Madra (the future Purūravas) experienced in a dream his meeting with Atri and had the vision that he would attain his goal; in the morning, while awake, he saw Atri, who gave him the instruction on the sacrifice of beauty (rūpasatra) for the attainment of supreme beauty, saying: 'Because you observed the dvādaśī vow in your previous birth, the blessed Lord Viṣṇu was pleased and you have reached my hermitage; and here, in this region largely consisting of rocks filled with honey and possessed of honey-like fruits, Viṣṇu, pleased by your austerities accompanied by fasting, will make your desire unfailing.'

sanskrit_iast: 155 jyotiḥśāstretihāsādivijñabrahmaṇaḥ gurūpadeśādrūpasatrakaraṇaṃ tatphalāni ca . . .
meaning: 155 ज्योतिःशास्त्रेतिहासादिविज्ञब्रह्मणः गुरूपदेशाद्रूपसत्रकरणं तत्फलानि च . . .
text_mt: 155 The performance of the sacrifice of beauty by a brahmin learned in astronomy, traditional histories, and other lores, according to the instruction of his guru, and its fruits […].

sanskrit_iast: 156 bhagavatātriṇā madrarājasya rūpasatre gurutvamurarīkṛtya yathāvidhi tatsatrasampādanaṃ tadavasāne ca rājño'pūrvarūpasampatyā paurajānapadeṣvadhikapūjyatā, bhūyaśca dehāvasāne budhaputratā, sadehasya tasya svarloke gamanañca
meaning: 156 भगवतात्रिणा मद्रराजस्य रूपसत्रे गुरुत्वमुररीकृत्य यथाविधि तत्सत्रसम्पादनं तदवसाने च राज्ञोऽपूर्वरूपसम्पत्या पौरजानपदेष्वधिकपूज्यता, भूयश्च देहावसाने बुधपुत्रता, सदेहस्य तस्य स्वर्लोके गमनञ्च
text_mt: 156 The revered Atri's accepting the role of guru in the sacrifice of beauty for the king of Madra and duly performing that sacrifice; at its conclusion, the king's receiving unprecedented beauty and thus greater reverence among the citizens and countryfolk; and further, at the end of his life, his being born as the son of Budha, and his ascending to heaven in his physical body.

sanskrit_iast: 157 mārgaśīrṣaśukladvādaśyāṃ rājyakāmasya vratavidhiḥ
meaning: 157 मार्गशीर्षशुक्लद्वादश्यां राज्यकामस्य व्रतविधिः
text_mt: 157 The procedure of the vow on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa for one who desires sovereignty.

sanskrit_iast: 158 kāmadvādaśīvarṇanam
meaning: 158 कामद्वादशीवर्णनम्
text_mt: 158 Description of the Kāmadvādaśī.

sanskrit_iast: 159 mārgaśīrṣādiśuklapakṣadvādaśīṣu keśavārcanādagniṣṭomādiyajñaphalāni ....
meaning: 159 मार्गशीर्षादिशुक्लपक्षद्वादशीषु केशवार्चनादग्निष्टोमादियज्ञफलानि ....
text_mt: 159 The fruits equal to sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma obtained by worshipping Keśava on the twelfth lunar days of the bright fortnights beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa […].

sanskrit_iast: 160 pratikṛṣṇapakṣadvādaśīvidhistatkaraṇaphalañca ....
meaning: 160 प्रतिकृष्णपक्षद्वादशीविधिस्तत्करणफलञ्च ....
text_mt: 160 The procedure for the twelfth lunar days of every dark fortnight, and the fruit of performing it […].

sanskrit_iast: 161 sarvadvādaśyupavāsāsamarthānāṃ bhādrapadamāsīyaśuklapakṣasthaśravaṇanakṣatropetadvādaśyupavāsaphalaṃ, tasyā eva budhaśravaṇayuktatve'tyantamahattvam
meaning: 161 सर्वद्वादश्युपवासासमर्थानां भाद्रपदमासीयशुक्लपक्षस्थश्रवणनक्षत्रोपेतद्वादश्युपवासफलं, तस्या एव बुधश्रवणयुक्तत्वेऽत्यन्तमहत्त्वम्
text_mt: 161 The fruit of fasting on the dvādaśī conjoined with the Śravaṇa asterism in the bright fortnight of the month of Bhādrapada for those unable to fast on all dvādaśīs, and the extreme greatness of that very [day] when conjoined with Wednesday and Śravaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: 162 śravaṇadvādaśīprasaṃgena puṇyanadīsaṃgamasnānatajjalapūrṇavāridhānyā dadhyodanasahitāyā dānasya prāśastyam . pūrvajanmani maruprāntasthaśākalanagaravāstavyasya kasyacidvaiśyasya śravaṇadvādaśyāṃ tauṣīcandrabhāgayornadyoḥ saṃgame sadadhyodanavāridhānīdānājjanmāntare pretādhipatāyāmapi nityaṃ bhojanasamaye dadhyodanayuktavāridhānyupasthitivarṇanam
meaning: 162 श्रवणद्वादशीप्रसंगेन पुण्यनदीसंगमस्नानतज्जलपूर्णवारिधान्या दध्योदनसहिताया दानस्य प्राशस्त्यम् . पूर्वजन्मनि मरुप्रान्तस्थशाकलनगरवास्तव्यस्य कस्यचिद्वैश्यस्य श्रवणद्वादश्यां तौषीचन्द्रभागयोर्नद्योः संगमे सदध्योदनवारिधानीदानाज्जन्मान्तरे प्रेताधिपतायामपि नित्यं भोजनसमये दध्योदनयुक्तवारिधान्युपस्थितिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 162 In connection with Śravaṇadvādaśī, the praise of bathing at the confluence of sacred rivers and donating a water vessel filled with that water accompanied by curd-rice; the account of a certain vaiśya residing in the city of Śākala on the edge of the desert, who, having donated a water vessel along with curd-rice on Śravaṇadvādaśī at the confluence of the Tauṣī and Candrabhāgā rivers in a previous birth, had a water vessel accompanied by curd-rice appear every day at mealtime in his next birth, even though he had become a lord of the deceased.

sanskrit_iast: 163 tiladvādaśyāṃ snānahomanaivedyadīpodakadāneṣu tilaprāśastyam
meaning: 163 तिलद्वादश्यां स्नानहोमनैवेद्यदीपोदकदानेषु तिलप्राशस्त्यम्
text_mt: 163 The praise of sesame on Tiladvādaśī for bathing, oblation, food offerings, lamps, and gifts of water.

sanskrit_iast: 164 māgadheṣu caṇḍavegarājamahiṣī nayanasundarī pūrvajanmani śravaṇadvādaśyāṃ tilahemadānādikāraṇādrājñītvamāpa, tatsakhīmatallikayā vāsantikayā tatkāraṇe pṛṣṭe pūrvajanmani brāhmaṇyai tasyaitaddeśasthadadhivāhanasya rājño bhāryayā kamalākhyayā sakhyavaśādumārūpavitastānadyāṃ snātvopavāsapūrvakaviṣṇupūjāhavanakarmaṇi vahnimukhabhraṣṭatilapuṇyaphaladānātsvasyā rājamahiṣītvādi nijagāda...
meaning: 164 मागधेषु चण्डवेगराजमहिषी नयनसुन्दरी पूर्वजन्मनि श्रवणद्वादश्यां तिलहेमदानादिकारणाद्राज्ञीत्वमाप, तत्सखीमतल्लिकया वासन्तिकया तत्कारणे पृष्टे पूर्वजन्मनि ब्राह्मण्यै तस्यैतद्देशस्थदधिवाहनस्य राज्ञो भार्यया कमलाख्यया सख्यवशादुमारूपवितस्तानद्यां स्नात्वोपवासपूर्वकविष्णुपूजाहवनकर्मणि वह्निमुखभ्रष्टतिलपुण्यफलदानात्स्वस्या राजमहिषीत्वादि निजगाद...
text_mt: 164 Among the Magadhas, Queen Nayanasundarī, wife of King Caṇḍavega, attained queenship because of gifts of sesame, gold, and other things on Śravaṇadvādaśī in a previous birth; when asked about that cause by her excellent friend Vāsantikā, she recounted her status as queen and so forth, [which came about] because in a previous birth, when she was a brahmin woman, Queen Kamalā, wife of King Dadhivāhana of that country, had out of friendship bathed in the Vitastā river which has the form of Umā, fasted, worshipped Viṣṇu and offered oblations, and given [her] the meritorious fruit of the sesame seeds that had fallen from the fire's mouth...

sanskrit_iast: 165 gāyatrīdevatāśaktipravacanaṃ tasyā gāyatrīsāvitryādyanvarthanāmanirvacana ñcābhidhāya tajjāpasya sarvārthasādhakatoṅkārasahitāyāstayāḥ paramapuruṣasahitacaturviṃśatitattvātmakatādivarṇanam ...
meaning: 165 गायत्रीदेवताशक्तिप्रवचनं तस्या गायत्रीसावित्र्याद्यन्वर्थनामनिर्वचन ञ्चाभिधाय तज्जापस्य सर्वार्थसाधकतोङ्कारसहितायास्तयाः परमपुरुषसहितचतुर्विंशतितत्त्वात्मकतादिवर्णनम् ...
text_mt: 165 The discourse on the power of the goddess Gāyatrī; having explained the etymological definitions of her meaningful names such as Gāyatrī and Sāvitrī, the description of how reciting her [mantra] accomplishes all goals, and how along with the syllable Oṃ she consists of the twenty-four principles along with the Supreme Person, and so forth...

sanskrit_iast: 166 dvādaśyamāvāsyādiṣu keśavādisthāneṣu dīpadānasya tathā kārtikamāsa ākāśadīpadānasya phalam
meaning: 166 द्वादश्यमावास्यादिषु केशवादिस्थानेषु दीपदानस्य तथा कार्तिकमास आकाशदीपदानस्य फलम्
text_mt: 166 The fruit of offering lamps at shrines of Keśava and others on the twelfth day, the new moon day, and so forth, as well as offering an aerial lamp in the month of Kārtika.

sanskrit_iast: 167 vidarbhādhipacitrarathatanayā lalitā triśatabhāryasyāpi kāśirājasya priyarājñītvaṃ viṣṇvāyatanādiṣu dīpadānādavāpa, sauvīrarājapurohitamaitreyeṇomārūpadevikāsarittīrthe nirmitaviṣṇvālaye kārtikamāsi dyūtasya dīpasya vartipreraṇena mṛtāyā mūṣikāyā janmāntare vidarbharājakanyātvaṃ kāśirājapriyamahiṣītvañca
meaning: 167 विदर्भाधिपचित्ररथतनया ललिता त्रिशतभार्यस्यापि काशिराजस्य प्रियराज्ञीत्वं विष्ण्वायतनादिषु दीपदानादवाप, सौवीरराजपुरोहितमैत्रेयेणोमारूपदेविकासरित्तीर्थे निर्मितविष्ण्वालये कार्तिकमासि द्यूतस्य दीपस्य वर्तिप्रेरणेन मृताया मूषिकाया जन्मान्तरे विदर्भराजकन्यात्वं काशिराजप्रियमहिषीत्वञ्च
text_mt: 167 Lalitā, the daughter of Citraratha, king of Vidarbha, became the beloved queen of the king of Kāśi—even though he had three hundred wives—because of offering lamps in temples of Viṣṇu and elsewhere; a female mouse, having died in a temple of Viṣṇu constructed at the tīrtha of the Devikā river in the form of Umā by Maitreya, the family priest of the Sauvīra king, by stirring the wick of a flickering lamp in the month of Kārtika, attained the status of a Vidarbha princess and the beloved queen of the king of Kāśi in her next birth.

sanskrit_iast: 168 upavāsāśaktadhanahīnānāmapi sarvasulabheṣu puṇyāraṇyeṣvayatnasādhyāsu ca puṣpaphalatoyādisāmagrīṣu keśavārciyā sarvakāmasamṛddhiḥ svāyattā
meaning: 168 उपवासाशक्तधनहीनानामपि सर्वसुलभेषु पुण्यारण्येष्वयत्नसाध्यासु च पुष्पफलतोयादिसामग्रीषु केशवार्चिया सर्वकामसमृद्धिः स्वायत्ता
text_mt: 168 Even for those incapable of fasting and destitute of wealth, the abundance of all desires is brought under one's control through the worship of Keśava with materials easily obtained by everyone in sacred forests without effort, such as flowers, fruits, and water.

sanskrit_iast: 169 viṣṇvālayādau mārjanādikartuḥ phalāni
meaning: 169 विष्ण्वालयादौ मार्जनादिकर्तुः फलानि
text_mt: 169 The rewards of one who performs sweeping and other cleaning in a temple of Viṣṇu and other places.

sanskrit_iast: 170 kasmiśriddhatadaive śūdre vāṇijyakṛṣinaṣṭadhane gaṃgātaṭasthavarāhamaṃdiralepanādyaśakte kākatālīyavaddharāhārcādidṛkṣārthaṃ sauvīrarāja āgataḥ tatsampattilubdhacittaḥ śūdraḥ pañcatāñjagāma, tadbhāryā tena sahaikacityā bhasmasādabhavat, tatpuṇyavaśātsa svargalokaṅgataḥ tadaiva yuvanāśvo putrīyavratena viṣṇumānārca, svapne bhārgavaṃ cyavanaṃ gaccheti viṣṇavādiṣṭaḥ sa nṛpastaṃ svavṛttamavadat cyavano'pi tadajñātaṃ putrīyaṃ jalaṃ kṛtvā kalaśe sthāpayāmāsa, niśīthe rājñā tṛṣārtena tajjale pīte munyanugrahādrājñaḥ kukṣau garbhaḥ sañjātaḥ māndhāteti tannāma śūdrātmā taṃ viveśa, śūdrabhāryā kāśirājaduhitṛtāṃ yātā māndhātror̤hā udvāhānantaraṃ yuvanāśvastamayodhyāyāmabhiṣicya vanastho nākamagamat
meaning: 170 कस्मिश्रिद्धतदैवे शूद्रे वाणिज्यकृषिनष्टधने गंगातटस्थवराहमंदिरलेपनाद्यशक्ते काकतालीयवद्धराहार्चादिदृक्षार्थं सौवीरराज आगतः तत्सम्पत्तिलुब्धचित्तः शूद्रः पञ्चताञ्जगाम, तद्भार्या तेन सहैकचित्या भस्मसादभवत्, तत्पुण्यवशात्स स्वर्गलोकङ्गतः तदैव युवनाश्वो पुत्रीयव्रतेन विष्णुमानार्च, स्वप्ने भार्गवं च्यवनं गच्छेति विष्णवादिष्टः स नृपस्तं स्ववृत्तमवदत् च्यवनोऽपि तदज्ञातं पुत्रीयं जलं कृत्वा कलशे स्थापयामास, निशीथे राज्ञा तृषार्तेन तज्जले पीते मुन्यनुग्रहाद्राज्ञः कुक्षौ गर्भः सञ्जातः मान्धातेति तन्नाम शूद्रात्मा तं विवेश, शूद्रभार्या काशिराजदुहितृतां याता मान्धात्रोर्̤हा उद्वाहानन्तरं युवनाश्वस्तमयोध्यायामभिषिच्य वनस्थो नाकमगमत्
text_mt: 170 When a certain ill-fated śūdra, having lost his wealth in trade and agriculture, was unable even to plaster the Varāha temple on the bank of the Gaṅgā, the Sauvīra king arrived as if by the coincidence of the crow and the palm fruit to view the image of Varāha; his mind covetous of that wealth, the śūdra met his death, and his wife was reduced to ashes on the same funeral pyre with him; by the power of that merit, he went to heaven; at that very time, Yuvanāśva worshipped Viṣṇu with a rite for obtaining a son; instructed by Viṣṇu in a dream to go to Bhārgava Cyavana, that king recounted his story to him; Cyavana, having consecrated water for obtaining a son without his knowledge, placed it in a pot; at midnight, when that water was drunk by the king who was afflicted with thirst, a child was conceived in the king's belly by the sage's grace; named Māndhātṛ, the soul of the śūdra entered him, while the śūdra's wife became the daughter of the king of Kāśi and was wedded to Māndhātṛ; after the marriage, Yuvanāśva consecrated him in Ayodhyā, went to the forest, and departed for heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
171 māndhātari viṣṇvaṃśasya vidyamāne'pi lavaṇena māheśvaraśūlena sa kathaṃ hata iti saṃśayodbhāvanapurassaraṃ śivaviṣṇvabhedasya puruṣasvarūpasya
varṇanam
meaning:
171 मान्धातरि विष्ण्वंशस्य विद्यमानेऽपि लवणेन माहेश्वरशूलेन स कथं हत इति संशयोद्भावनपुरस्सरं शिवविष्ण्वभेदस्य पुरुषस्वरूपस्य
वर्णनम्
text_mt: 171 Following the raising of a doubt as to how Māndhātṛ was killed by Lavaṇa with a spear of Maheśvara even though a portion of Viṣṇu was present [in him], the description of the non-difference between Śiva and Viṣṇu and of the nature of the Cosmic Person.

sanskrit_iast: 172 hareḥ prādurbhāveṣu suranaratiyaktvamanāsthāyaiva jagatpālanam .. māyāleśamantareṇa yathāruci dharmarakṣāpurassaramamānavīyakarmācaraṇam .
meaning: 172 हरेः प्रादुर्भावेषु सुरनरतियक्त्वमनास्थायैव जगत्पालनम् .. मायालेशमन्तरेण यथारुचि धर्मरक्षापुरस्सरममानवीयकर्माचरणम् .
text_mt: 172 In the manifestations of Hari, his protection of the world without relying on being a god, man, or animal; the performance of superhuman deeds, preserving dharma according to his wish, without the slightest trickery.

sanskrit_iast: 173 mārgaśīrṣamāsamārabhya māsanakṣatreṣūpavāsapūrvakaṃ harervāmajānvādyekaikamaṅgaṃ pūjayitvā gomūtreṇa snānaṃ raktapuṣpaiḥ pūjanaṃ tāmrasya dānamityādi krameṇa putrīyānantavratakathanam
meaning: 173 मार्गशीर्षमासमारभ्य मासनक्षत्रेषूपवासपूर्वकं हरेर्वामजान्वाद्येकैकमङ्गं पूजयित्वा गोमूत्रेण स्नानं रक्तपुष्पैः पूजनं ताम्रस्य दानमित्यादि क्रमेण पुत्रीयानन्तव्रतकथनम्
text_mt: 173 The explanation of the Putrīyānantavrata in order: beginning from the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, fasting on the asterisms of each month, worshipping each limb of Hari beginning with the left knee, bathing with cow urine, worshipping with red flowers, donating copper, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 174 kārtikamāsādārabhya māsanakṣatrapūjanavidhānam
meaning: 174 कार्तिकमासादारभ्य मासनक्षत्रपूजनविधानम्
text_mt: 174 The procedure for worshipping on the asterisms of each month beginning from the month of Kārtika.

sanskrit_iast: 175 śāmbarāyaṇyuktānekaśakracāritaṃ viṣṇukṛtatadvidveṣihananaśca , ....
meaning: 175 शाम्बरायण्युक्तानेकशक्रचारितं विष्णुकृततद्विद्वेषिहननश्च , ....
text_mt: 175 The deeds of many Śakras recounted by Śāmbarāyaṇi, and the slaying of their enemies by Viṣṇu...

sanskrit_iast: 176 brahmamānasaputraprathamamanutatputramarīcyādisaptarṣijayādisomapīthiviśvabhugindratadvidveṣidaityapravara bāṣkalādernāmakīrtanam
meaning: 176 ब्रह्ममानसपुत्रप्रथममनुतत्पुत्रमरीच्यादिसप्तर्षिजयादिसोमपीथिविश्वभुगिन्द्रतद्विद्वेषिदैत्यप्रवर बाष्कलादेर्नामकीर्तनम्
text_mt: 176 The mention of the names of the first Manu, the mind-born son of Brahmā, his sons, the seven seers beginning with Marīci, the Viśvabhuk Indra who drinks soma with Jaya and others, and the foremost Daityas who are his enemies, such as Bāṣkala.

sanskrit_iast: 177 śakraṃ prati śāmbarāyaṇyupākhyāne dvitīyamanusvārociṣāntare tadvaṃśyādināmakīrtanam
meaning: 177 शक्रं प्रति शाम्बरायण्युपाख्याने द्वितीयमनुस्वारोचिषान्तरे तद्वंश्यादिनामकीर्तनम्
text_mt: 177 In the narrative of Śāmbarāyaṇi addressed to Śakra, the mention of the names of the descendants and others in the interval of the second Manu, Svārociṣa.

sanskrit_iast: 178 tṛtīyasyauttamasya manorajādisaptaputtrāṇāṃ rajobāhvādisaptarcyādīnāśca kīrtanam 179 caturthasya tāmasākhyamanorjānujaṃghādiputtrāṇāṃ vanādināmakasaptarṣīṇāṃ satyādidevagaṇānāñca varṇanam
meaning: 178 तृतीयस्यौत्तमस्य मनोरजादिसप्तपुत्त्राणां रजोबाह्वादिसप्तर्च्यादीनाश्च कीर्तनम् 179 चतुर्थस्य तामसाख्यमनोर्जानुजंघादिपुत्त्राणां वनादिनामकसप्तर्षीणां सत्यादिदेवगणानाञ्च वर्णनम्
text_mt: 178 The mention of the seven sons beginning with Aja, the seven seers beginning with Rajobāhu, and others, of the third Manu, Auttama. 179 The description of the sons beginning with Jānujaṅgha, the seven seers named Vana and others, and the groups of gods beginning with the Satyas, of the fourth Manu named Tāmasa.

sanskrit_iast: 180 paṃcamasya raivatasya manormahāpurāṇādiputrāṇāṃ vedaśrutyādisaptarṣīṇāmābhūtarājasādidevagaṇānāṃ vibhorindrasya śambvākhyadaityapatyādīnāñca varṇanam
meaning: 180 पंचमस्य रैवतस्य मनोर्महापुराणादिपुत्राणां वेदश्रुत्यादिसप्तर्षीणामाभूतराजसादिदेवगणानां विभोरिन्द्रस्य शम्ब्वाख्यदैत्यपत्यादीनाञ्च वर्णनम्
text_mt: 180 The description of the sons beginning with Mahāpurāṇa, the seven seers beginning with Vedaśruti, the groups of gods beginning with the Ābhūtarajasas, the Indra named Vibhu, the Daitya lord named Śambhu, and others, of the fifth Manu, Raivata.

sanskrit_iast: 181 ṣaṣṭhasya manoścākṣuṣasyorvādiputrāṇāmāḍhyādisaptarṣīṇāṃ divaukasāmaṣṭakādipaṃcagaṇānāṃ manojavākhyasyendrasya ca kīrtanam, daityarājasya mahāmālasya varṇanam
meaning: 181 षष्ठस्य मनोश्चाक्षुषस्योर्वादिपुत्राणामाढ्यादिसप्तर्षीणां दिवौकसामष्टकादिपंचगणानां मनोजवाख्यस्येन्द्रस्य च कीर्तनम्, दैत्यराजस्य महामालस्य वर्णनम्
text_mt: 181 The mention of the sons beginning with Uru, the seven seers beginning with Āḍhya, the five groups of heaven-dwellers beginning with the Aṣṭakas, and the Indra named Manojava, of the sixth Manu, Cākṣuṣa; and the description of the Daitya king Mahāmāla.

sanskrit_iast: 182 saptamasya vaivasvatasya manorikṣvākvādiputtrāṇām atryādisaptarṣīṇām ekonapaṃcāśadasuradevānāmāśvinādidaśānāmaparadevānāmojambināmakasya śakrasya kīrtanaṃ hiraṇyākṣasya devārāternavarāharūpeṇa viṣṇunā yā vadhādikathanañca
meaning: 182 सप्तमस्य वैवस्वतस्य मनोरिक्ष्वाक्वादिपुत्त्राणाम् अत्र्यादिसप्तर्षीणाम् एकोनपंचाशदसुरदेवानामाश्विनादिदशानामपरदेवानामोजम्बिनामकस्य शक्रस्य कीर्तनं हिरण्याक्षस्य देवारातेर्नवराहरूपेण विष्णुना या वधादिकथनञ्च
text_mt: 182 The mention of the sons beginning with Ikṣvāku, the seven seers beginning with Atri, the forty-nine Asura gods, the ten other gods beginning with the Aśvins, and the Śakra named Ojambin, of the seventh Manu, Vaivasvata; and the account of the slaying of the gods' enemy Hiraṇyākṣa by Viṣṇu in the form of a new boar, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 183 aṣṭamasya bhaviṣyasya sāvarṇasya manorvijayādiputrāṇāmaśvatthāmādisaptarṣīṇāṃ sutapasādidevagaṇānāṃ balerindrasya niḥsapatnasya kīrtanamra, tasminmanvantare himācalasthaṃ nānolaṃ viṣṇurhaniṣyatīti kathanañca
meaning: 183 अष्टमस्य भविष्यस्य सावर्णस्य मनोर्विजयादिपुत्राणामश्वत्थामादिसप्तर्षीणां सुतपसादिदेवगणानां बलेरिन्द्रस्य निःसपत्नस्य कीर्तनम्र, तस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे हिमाचलस्थं नानोलं विष्णुर्हनिष्यतीति कथनञ्च
text_mt: 183 The mention of the sons beginning with Vijaya, the seven seers beginning with Aśvatthāman, the groups of gods beginning with the Sutapases, and Indra Bali without rivals, of the eighth, future Manu, Sāvarṇa; and the statement that in that manvantara Viṣṇu will slay Nānola residing on the Himālaya.

sanskrit_iast: 184 brahmaputrasya navamasya manorghṛtiketvādiputrāṇāṃ medhātithyādisaptaṣīṇāṃ parādidevagaṇānāṃ vibhunāmno bhaviṣyadindrasya kālakakṣādidevadāyādarājño vasunābhasya dhārmikatvādbhaviṣyadviṣṇuputratayā bhāvikālakālakākṣavadhaḥ
meaning: 184 ब्रह्मपुत्रस्य नवमस्य मनोर्घृतिकेत्वादिपुत्राणां मेधातिथ्यादिसप्तषीणां परादिदेवगणानां विभुनाम्नो भविष्यदिन्द्रस्य कालकक्षादिदेवदायादराज्ञो वसुनाभस्य धार्मिकत्वाद्भविष्यद्विष्णुपुत्रतया भाविकालकालकाक्षवधः
text_mt: 184 Of the ninth Manu, the son of Brahmā, the sons beginning with Dhṛtiketu, the seven seers beginning with Medhātithi, the groups of gods beginning with the Paras, the future Indra named Vibhu; because of the righteousness of King Vasunābha, an heir of the gods [opposed by] Kālakākṣa and others, he will be a future son of Viṣṇu, [leading to] the future slaying of Kālaka and Kālākṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
185 dharmaputrasya daśamasya manoḥ sukṣetrādiputrāṇāmāpomūrtyādisaptarṣīṇāṃ prāṇākhyādidevagaṇānāmindrasya śāntyākhyasya tadvidviṣā prabalasya
vālino viṣṇukartṛkaṃ hananam
meaning:
185 धर्मपुत्रस्य दशमस्य मनोः सुक्षेत्रादिपुत्राणामापोमूर्त्यादिसप्तर्षीणां प्राणाख्यादिदेवगणानामिन्द्रस्य शान्त्याख्यस्य तद्विद्विषा प्रबलस्य
वालिनो विष्णुकर्तृकं हननम्
text_mt: 185. An account of the sons of the tenth Manu, the son of Dharma, such as Sukṣetra; the seven sages, such as Āpomūrti; the classes of gods, such as the Prāṇas; the Indra named Śānti; and the killing of his mighty enemy Vālin by Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: 186 rudraputrasryakādaśasya manoḥ sarvartugādiputrāṇāṃ haviṣmadādisaptarṣīṇāṃ nirmathyādidevagaṇānāmindrasya vṛṣābhidheyasya dviṣantaṃ daśagrīvaṃ viṣṇuḥ straiṇaṃ rūpamāśrito vadhiṣyati ..
meaning: 186 रुद्रपुत्रस्र्यकादशस्य मनोः सर्वर्तुगादिपुत्राणां हविष्मदादिसप्तर्षीणां निर्मथ्यादिदेवगणानामिन्द्रस्य वृषाभिधेयस्य द्विषन्तं दशग्रीवं विष्णुः स्त्रैणं रूपमाश्रितो वधिष्यति ..
text_mt: 186. An account of the sons of the eleventh Manu, the son of Rudra, such as Sarvartuga; the seven sages, such as Haviṣmat; the classes of gods, such as the Nirmathyas; the Indra named Vṛṣa; and how Viṣṇu, having assumed a female form, will slay his enemy Daśagrīva.

sanskrit_iast: 187 dvādaśasya manordakṣaputrasya devavadādiputrāṇāṃ sattamādisaptarṣīṇāṃ suśarmādidevagaṇānāmindrasyārātiṃ naraka napuṃsakarūpeṇa viṣṇurhantā
meaning: 187 द्वादशस्य मनोर्दक्षपुत्रस्य देववदादिपुत्राणां सत्तमादिसप्तर्षीणां सुशर्मादिदेवगणानामिन्द्रस्यारातिं नरक नपुंसकरूपेण विष्णुर्हन्ता
text_mt: 187. An account of the sons of the twelfth Manu, the son of Dakṣa, such as Devavat; the seven sages, such as Sattama; the classes of gods, such as Suśarman; and how Viṣṇu, in the form of a eunuch, will slay Naraka, the enemy of Indra.

sanskrit_iast: 188 trayodaśasya raucyasya manościtrasenādiputrāṇāṃ dhṛtimadādisaptarṣīṇāṃ sutrāmādidevagaṇānāmindrasya bṛhaspaterasuradāyādasya ṭiṭṭibhasya māyūrarūpiviṣṇunā vināśaḥ
meaning: 188 त्रयोदशस्य रौच्यस्य मनोश्चित्रसेनादिपुत्राणां धृतिमदादिसप्तर्षीणां सुत्रामादिदेवगणानामिन्द्रस्य बृहस्पतेरसुरदायादस्य टिट्टिभस्य मायूररूपिविष्णुना विनाशः
text_mt: 188. An account of the sons of the thirteenth Manu, Raupya, such as Citrasena; the seven sages, such as Dhṛtimat; the classes of gods, such as Sutrāman; the Indra Bṛhaspati; and the destruction of the Asura heir Ṭiṭṭibha by Viṣṇu in the form of a peacock.

sanskrit_iast: 189 caturdaśasya bhautyasya manostaraṃgabhedābhidādiputrāṇāmagnīdhrādisaptarṣīṇāṃ cākṣuṣādidevagaṇānāṃ śucerindrasya śatrūṇāṃ rājño mahāsukhasya samaye divyavarṣasahasraparyantaṃ devāsurayuddhe jāte tāmasīmāyayā madhusūdano rīnvadhiṣyati .|
meaning: 189 चतुर्दशस्य भौत्यस्य मनोस्तरंगभेदाभिदादिपुत्राणामग्नीध्रादिसप्तर्षीणां चाक्षुषादिदेवगणानां शुचेरिन्द्रस्य शत्रूणां राज्ञो महासुखस्य समये दिव्यवर्षसहस्रपर्यन्तं देवासुरयुद्धे जाते तामसीमायया मधुसूदनो रीन्वधिष्यति .|
text_mt: 189. An account of the sons of the fourteenth Manu, Bhautya, such as Taraṅgabheda and Abhidā; the seven sages, such as Agnīdhra; the classes of gods, such as the Cākṣuṣas; the Indra Śuci; and how, when a war between the gods and Asuras occurs for a thousand divine years during the time of King Mahāsukha, Madhusūdana will slay the enemies of Indra by means of tāmasika delusion.

sanskrit_iast: 190 pratiyugaṃ yathākāryaṃ viṣṇoranekāvatāradhāraṇam
meaning: 190 प्रतियुगं यथाकार्यं विष्णोरनेकावतारधारणम्
text_mt: 190. Viṣṇu's assumption of many incarnations in each age according to the task at hand.

sanskrit_iast: 191 śakrapraśnānurodhena śāmbarāyaṇyā yāvajjīvaṃ māsanakṣatrapūjanena svasyā atītānāgatamanvantareṣu tadvṛttajñānam
meaning: 191 शक्रप्रश्नानुरोधेन शाम्बरायण्या यावज्जीवं मासनक्षत्रपूजनेन स्वस्या अतीतानागतमन्वन्तरेषु तद्वृत्तज्ञानम्
text_mt: 191. Śāmbarāyaṇī's knowledge of the events in past and future manvantaras through lifelong worship of the months and lunar mansions, in response to Śakra's question.

sanskrit_iast: 192 śrīviṣṇoḥ stutimāhātmyavarṇanam
meaning: 192 श्रीविष्णोः स्तुतिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
text_mt: 192. Description of the hymn of praise and the greatness of Śrī Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: 193 devalamunyavajñayā hāhāhūhvorgajanakrībhavanam
meaning: 193 देवलमुन्यवज्ञया हाहाहूह्वोर्गजनक्रीभवनम्
text_mt: 193. The transformation of Hāhā and Hūhū into an elephant and a crocodile through disrespect toward the sage Devala.

sanskrit_iast:
194 jambūdvīpe śrṛṅgavati kulācale hāhāgandharvasya hastitvena huhvo nakratvena ca nivasatormadhyāhne jalaṃ pātumantaḥsarasi praviṣṭe gajarāje raudreṇa
grāheṇa tasya grahaṇaṃ mitho yuddhe gajarājena puṣkarāgradhūtakamalapuṣpeṇa viṣṇormānasikasaparyā vyadhāyi tadbhāvākṛṣṭo viṣṇuḥ sarasi tatsānnidhyaṃ kalpayitvobhāvapi gandharvatāmanayata etadadhyāyapaṭhanaphalam
meaning:
194 जम्बूद्वीपे श्रृङ्गवति कुलाचले हाहागन्धर्वस्य हस्तित्वेन हुह्वो नक्रत्वेन च निवसतोर्मध्याह्ने जलं पातुमन्तःसरसि प्रविष्टे गजराजे रौद्रेण
ग्राहेण तस्य ग्रहणं मिथो युद्धे गजराजेन पुष्कराग्रधूतकमलपुष्पेण विष्णोर्मानसिकसपर्या व्यधायि तद्भावाकृष्टो विष्णुः सरसि तत्सान्निध्यं कल्पयित्वोभावपि गन्धर्वतामनयत एतदध्यायपठनफलम्
text_mt: 194. On the Śṛṅgavat mountain range in Jambūdvīpa, the Gandharva Hāhā living as an elephant and Hūhū living as a crocodile: when the lordly elephant entered the lake at midday to drink water, his capture by the fierce water-monster; in their mutual combat, the mental worship of Viṣṇu performed by the lordly elephant with a lotus flower shaken by the tip of his trunk; drawn by that devotion, Viṣṇu, having manifested his presence at the lake, brought them both back to the state of Gandharvas; and the fruit of reciting this chapter.

sanskrit_iast: 195 sarvaduṣṭopaśamanaṃ viṣṇupañjarastotram
meaning: 195 सर्वदुष्टोपशमनं विष्णुपञ्जरस्तोत्रम्
text_mt: 195. The Viṣṇupañjara hymn, which pacifies all wicked beings.

sanskrit_iast: 196 brahmaṇā tripuraṃ jighāṃsoḥ śaṅkarasya rakṣāyai, , vāgīśena ca balaṃ jighāṃsoḥ śakrasya rakṣāyai nirūpitasya viṣṇupañjarastotrasya kathanam...
meaning: 196 ब्रह्मणा त्रिपुरं जिघांसोः शङ्करस्य रक्षायै, , वागीशेन च बलं जिघांसोः शक्रस्य रक्षायै निरूपितस्य विष्णुपञ्जरस्तोत्रस्य कथनम्...
text_mt: 196. The recitation of the Viṣṇupañjara hymn, prescribed by Brahmā for the protection of Śaṅkara when he wished to destroy Tripura, and by the Lord of Speech for the protection of Śakra when he wished to destroy Bala.

sanskrit_iast: 197 kaśyapasya khaśākhyāyāṃ patnyāṃ yakṣotpatiḥ
meaning: 197 कश्यपस्य खशाख्यायां पत्न्यां यक्षोत्पतिः
text_mt: 197. The origin of the Yakṣas from Kaśyapa through his wife named Khaśā.

sanskrit_iast: 198 kapiṣāsutayorajaṣaṇḍhayorbrahmadhānayātudhānākhye tanaye babhūvatuḥ, tau te kanyake kṣudhitākāraṃ rākṣasaṃ dadatuḥ, tasya brahmadhānānvaye brahmadhānā niśācarāḥ, yātudhānānvaye yātudhānāḥ prasiddhāḥ . śleṣmātakavanasthāneṣu daśabrahmarākṣaseṣu sūryānucareṣu hetiprahetivaṃśyeṣu mālisumāli mālyavatsu sumālidauhitrastrilokavijayī rāvaṇaḥ, mālino dhareṇa vasunā nidhanaṃ mālyavāṃśca varṣatmā sukhaṃ jīvati
meaning: 198 कपिषासुतयोरजषण्ढयोर्ब्रह्मधानयातुधानाख्ये तनये बभूवतुः, तौ ते कन्यके क्षुधिताकारं राक्षसं ददतुः, तस्य ब्रह्मधानान्वये ब्रह्मधाना निशाचराः, यातुधानान्वये यातुधानाः प्रसिद्धाः . श्लेष्मातकवनस्थानेषु दशब्रह्मराक्षसेषु सूर्यानुचरेषु हेतिप्रहेतिवंश्येषु मालिसुमालि माल्यवत्सु सुमालिदौहित्रस्त्रिलोकविजयी रावणः, मालिनो धरेण वसुना निधनं माल्यवांश्च वर्षत्मा सुखं जीवति
text_mt: 198. The two daughters of Kapiṣā, Aja and Ṣaṇḍhā, bore two sons named Brahmadhāna and Yātudhāna; they gave those two maidens to a hungry-looking Rākṣasa; in his Brahmadhāna lineage, the Brahmadhāna night-wanderers became famous, and in his Yātudhāna lineage, the Yātudhānas; among the ten Brahmarākṣasas dwelling in the Śleṣmātaka forest, companions of the sun, descendants of Heti and Praheti, namely Māli, Sumāli, and Mālyavat, Rāvaṇa, the conqueror of the three worlds, was the maternal grandson of Sumāli; Māli met his death at the hands of the Vasu Dhara, while Mālyavat, possessing an aged body, lives happily.

sanskrit_iast: 199 pulomadānavendreṇa svajyeṣṭhatanayā pulomajā bhṛgave dattā, ekadā'ntarvatnīmagnihotragatāṃ tāṃ pulomā rākṣaso'bhyetya he'gne matpūrveyaṃ navetyuktavān, neyaṃ tvatpūrveti śrutvā'pi sa tāṃ jahāra, pathi garbhacyuteścyavana iti garbhajātasya saṃjñā, tena dṛṣṭamātrasya rakṣaso nāśaḥ pulomāśrunipātena vadhūvarānadīprārdubhāvo bhṛgoḥ sakāśādagneḥ sarvabhakṣakatvaśāpaḥ, brahmaṇāgneranugrahaśca .
meaning: 199 पुलोमदानवेन्द्रेण स्वज्येष्ठतनया पुलोमजा भृगवे दत्ता, एकदाऽन्तर्वत्नीमग्निहोत्रगतां तां पुलोमा राक्षसोऽभ्येत्य हेऽग्ने मत्पूर्वेयं नवेत्युक्तवान्, नेयं त्वत्पूर्वेति श्रुत्वाऽपि स तां जहार, पथि गर्भच्युतेश्च्यवन इति गर्भजातस्य संज्ञा, तेन दृष्टमात्रस्य रक्षसो नाशः पुलोमाश्रुनिपातेन वधूवरानदीप्रार्दुभावो भृगोः सकाशादग्नेः सर्वभक्षकत्वशापः, ब्रह्मणाग्नेरनुग्रहश्च .
text_mt: 199. Pulomajā, the eldest daughter of Puloman, the lord of the Dānavas, was given to Bhṛgu; once, when she was pregnant and had gone to the fire-sanctuary, the Rākṣasa Puloman approached and said, 'O Fire, was she not mine first?'; even after hearing 'She was not yours first,' he abducted her; because of the fall of the fetus on the path, the one born from the womb was named Cyavana; by his mere glance, the Rākṣasa was destroyed; from the falling of Pulomā's tears, the river Vadhūsaras appeared; the curse of consuming everything [laid] upon Fire by Bhṛgu, and the grace bestowed upon Fire by Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast: 200 svatapasā haraṃ prasādya labdhaśūlo madhudaityo rāvaṇasvāsāraṃ kumbhīlasīṃ hṛtvā tasyāṃ lavaṇaṃ sutamutpādayāmāsa, māndhātārañca yuddhe jaghāna
meaning: 200 स्वतपसा हरं प्रसाद्य लब्धशूलो मधुदैत्यो रावणस्वासारं कुम्भीलसीं हृत्वा तस्यां लवणं सुतमुत्पादयामास, मान्धातारञ्च युद्धे जघान
text_mt: 200. The Daitya Madhu, having pleased Hara through his own austerities and obtained a trident, abducted Rāvaṇa's sister Kumbhīnasī, begot on her a son named Lavaṇa, and killed Māndhātṛ in battle.

sanskrit_iast: 201 śailūṣavaṃśavarṇanam
meaning: 201 शैलूषवंशवर्णनम्
text_mt: 201. Description of the lineage of Śailūṣa.

sanskrit_iast: 202 duṣṭaśailūṣa ( gandharva ) jayāya bharataprasthānavarṇanam
meaning: 202 दुष्टशैलूष ( गन्धर्व ) जयाय भरतप्रस्थानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 202. Description of Bharata's departure to conquer the wicked Śailūṣa Gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast: 203 bharatayuddhayātrāyāṃ trilakṣasaṃkhyākānāmaśvānāṃ daśasahasrāṇāṃ dantināṃ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇāṃ rathānāṃ pañcakoṭipadātṝnāṃ vastrasuvarṇamaṇyādīnāṃ nicayaiḥ saha bahupaṇyayuktavaṇigādiviṣavaidyakāmavaidyakarmantikasthapatimārgikādīnāṃ preṣaṇam
meaning: 203 भरतयुद्धयात्रायां त्रिलक्षसंख्याकानामश्वानां दशसहस्राणां दन्तिनां षष्टिसहस्राणां रथानां पञ्चकोटिपदातॄनां वस्त्रसुवर्णमण्यादीनां निचयैः सह बहुपण्ययुक्तवणिगादिविषवैद्यकामवैद्यकर्मन्तिकस्थपतिमार्गिकादीनां प्रेषणम्
text_mt: 203. On Bharata's military expedition, the dispatching of three hundred thousand horses, ten thousand elephants, sixty thousand chariots, and fifty million foot-soldiers, along with heaps of garments, gold, jewels, and other treasures, as well as merchants provided with abundant merchandise, physicians for poison, specialists in aphrodisiacs, superintendents of works, architects, road-builders, and others.

sanskrit_iast: 204 bharatamāśīrvādairabhivarddhya gandharvānhatvā. sindhorubhayapārśvayornagare nirmāpyobhau putrau tatrābhiṣicya yudhājitaṃ sammānya ca śīghamāgacchetyādi śrīrāmeṇa samantraṇam, sa krośamātre sthāne nirmitaṃ śiviraṃ praviśya paurajānapadaṃ ca visarjyotaradainikakarmasūcanārthaṃ ḍiṇḍimadhvanikaraṇādikaṃ lakṣmaṇamupadideśa
meaning: 204 भरतमाशीर्वादैरभिवर्द्ध्य गन्धर्वान्हत्वा. सिन्धोरुभयपार्श्वयोर्नगरे निर्माप्योभौ पुत्रौ तत्राभिषिच्य युधाजितं सम्मान्य च शीघमागच्छेत्यादि श्रीरामेण समन्त्रणम्, स क्रोशमात्रे स्थाने निर्मितं शिविरं प्रविश्य पौरजानपदं च विसर्ज्योतरदैनिककर्मसूचनार्थं डिण्डिमध्वनिकरणादिकं लक्ष्मणमुपदिदेश
text_mt: 204. Having encouraged Bharata with blessings, [saying,] 'Kill the Gandharvas, build two cities on both banks of the Indus, consecrate both your sons there, honor Yudhājit, and return quickly,' and other counsel from Śrī Rāma; Bharata entered the camp constructed at a distance of merely a krośa, dismissed the citizens and countryfolk, and instructed Lakṣmaṇa regarding the sounding of drums and the like to signal the next day's duties.

sanskrit_iast: 205 prāyāṇikavādyaghoṣabṛṃhitaheṣitāditumule prayāntīnāṃ bharatāvarodharāmāṇāṃ dīnāndhakṛpaṇādibhyo dānadayādivarṇanapurassaraṃ prāyāṇikakṛtyanirdeśaḥ
meaning: 205 प्रायाणिकवाद्यघोषबृंहितहेषितादितुमुले प्रयान्तीनां भरतावरोधरामाणां दीनान्धकृपणादिभ्यो दानदयादिवर्णनपुरस्सरं प्रायाणिककृत्यनिर्देशः
text_mt: 205. In the tumult of the marching musical instruments, trumpeting, neighing, and the like, as the women of Bharata's inner apartments set forth, the direction of duties on the march, preceded by a description of charity, compassion, and so forth toward the poor, the blind, and the destitute.

sanskrit_iast: 206 gaṃgāyāṃ snānaśrāddhadānādidhārmikakriyānantaramaparapāragamanāya kūṭāgāradīpavṛkṣādinirmāṇāya ca bharatasya nideśānantaraṃ niśāyāmeva naukādibhistaraṇam
meaning: 206 गंगायां स्नानश्राद्धदानादिधार्मिकक्रियानन्तरमपरपारगमनाय कूटागारदीपवृक्षादिनिर्माणाय च भरतस्य निदेशानन्तरं निशायामेव नौकादिभिस्तरणम्
text_mt: 206. After performing pious rites such as bathing, ancestral offerings, and gifts at the Gaṅgā, and after Bharata's command to construct temporary pavilions, lamp-trees, and the like in order to cross to the other shore, the crossing by boats and the like even in the night.

sanskrit_iast: 207 mārge bharatasya damanakirātena saṃgamaḥ, yamunāyāṃ snānadānaśrāddhāderanantaraṃ matsyasālvādinṛpaiḥ saṃgatya bharatena kurukṣetrasya tīrthasannītināmadheyakāraṇe pṛṣṭe ghaṭodarabrāhmaṇena cyāvanadadhīcyasthinirmitavajreṇa daityanāśasya tathā māsaparyaṃtaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ kurukṣetre sannidhānasya kāraṇamavoci, tato'marakaṇṭakāditīrtheṣu snānādikaṃ kṛtvā devikānadyāṃ bharate gate kumārādipañcaparvatīyarājñāṃ tadabhyāśe āgamanaṃ tatra trirātramuṣitvā bharataścandrabhāgāṃ yayau. punaśca vitastāmuttīrya kaikayānāpya sa yudhājitā tanmātulena satkṛtaḥ
meaning: 207 मार्गे भरतस्य दमनकिरातेन संगमः, यमुनायां स्नानदानश्राद्धादेरनन्तरं मत्स्यसाल्वादिनृपैः संगत्य भरतेन कुरुक्षेत्रस्य तीर्थसन्नीतिनामधेयकारणे पृष्टे घटोदरब्राह्मणेन च्यावनदधीच्यस्थिनिर्मितवज्रेण दैत्यनाशस्य तथा मासपर्यंतं सर्वतीर्थानां कुरुक्षेत्रे सन्निधानस्य कारणमवोचि, ततोऽमरकण्टकादितीर्थेषु स्नानादिकं कृत्वा देविकानद्यां भरते गते कुमारादिपञ्चपर्वतीयराज्ञां तदभ्याशे आगमनं तत्र त्रिरात्रमुषित्वा भरतश्चन्द्रभागां ययौ. पुनश्च वितस्तामुत्तीर्य कैकयानाप्य स युधाजिता तन्मातुलेन सत्कृतः
text_mt: 207. On the road, Bharata's encounter with the Damanakirāta; after bathing, giving gifts, ancestral offerings, and the like at the Yamunā, meeting with kings such as the Matsyas and Sālvas; when Bharata inquired about the reason for the name of the sacred bathing-place Kurukṣetra as Sannīti, the reason was explained by the brahmin Ghaṭodara as the destruction of the Daityas by the thunderbolt made from the bones of Dadhīca, the descendant of Cyavana, and the presence of all sacred bathing-places at Kurukṣetra for the period of a month; then, having bathed and performed other rites at sacred bathing-places such as Amarakaṇṭaka, when Bharata went to the Devikā river, the arrival into his presence of five mountain kings headed by Kumāra; after residing there for three nights, Bharata went to the Candrabhāgā; and further, having crossed the Vitastā and reached the Kekayas, he was honored by Yudhājit, his maternal uncle.

sanskrit_iast: 208 pradyumnāṃśasamutpannetidarśanīye bharate yudhājitpuraṃ praviṣṭe paurastriyo vismṛtasakalavyāpārā niśceṣṭāstaṃ dadṛśuḥ, bharataśca mātulagṛhaṃ prāpya parārdhyabhojanapānādisatkāraṃ lebhe
meaning: 208 प्रद्युम्नांशसमुत्पन्नेतिदर्शनीये भरते युधाजित्पुरं प्रविष्टे पौरस्त्रियो विस्मृतसकलव्यापारा निश्चेष्टास्तं ददृशुः, भरतश्च मातुलगृहं प्राप्य परार्ध्यभोजनपानादिसत्कारं लेभे
text_mt: 208. When Bharata, born from a portion of Pradyumna and exceedingly handsome to behold, entered the city of Yudhājit, the women of the city, forgetting all their tasks, watched him motionless; and Bharata, having reached his maternal uncle's house, received hospitality consisting of the finest food, drink, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
209 bharato bandināṃ vicitrā navyā bhavyāśca racanāḥ śṛṇvannutthāya kṛtasandhyāhavanatarpaṇādinityakriyo brāhmaṇāndhanadānena tutoṣa, punaśva sabhāṃ gato tapodhanairdvijavaraiḥ kṛtāśīrvādo balamukhyānmahīpatīṃśca dadarśa, svadattatāmbūlena sapraśrayaṃ tānvisasarja ca tato yuddhāya maṃtraṇe jāte gārgyaṃ dautyakarmaṇi niyujya śve yoddhavyamiti ājñāpayāmāsa, sandhyāmupāsya gūḍhabhāṣitamākarṇya ca prāsādātsainikānāṃ pavanānaya
nākṣveḍāśabdādivṛtāntadarśanaśravaṇābhyāṃ mudamāpa
meaning:
209 भरतो बन्दिनां विचित्रा नव्या भव्याश्च रचनाः शृण्वन्नुत्थाय कृतसन्ध्याहवनतर्पणादिनित्यक्रियो ब्राह्मणान्धनदानेन तुतोष, पुनश्व सभां गतो तपोधनैर्द्विजवरैः कृताशीर्वादो बलमुख्यान्महीपतींश्च ददर्श, स्वदत्तताम्बूलेन सप्रश्रयं तान्विससर्ज च ततो युद्धाय मंत्रणे जाते गार्ग्यं दौत्यकर्मणि नियुज्य श्वे योद्धव्यमिति आज्ञापयामास, सन्ध्यामुपास्य गूढभाषितमाकर्ण्य च प्रासादात्सैनिकानां पवनानय
नाक्ष्वेडाशब्दादिवृतान्तदर्शनश्रवणाभ्यां मुदमाप
text_mt: 209 Bharata, rising while listening to the diverse, novel, and splendid compositions of the bards, performed his daily rites such as the twilight worship, fire-offering, and water-libations, and satisfied the brahmins with gifts of wealth; having gone again to the assembly, he was blessed by the foremost of the twice-born rich in asceticism, and received the chiefs of the army and the kings, and dismissed them with modesty after offering betel with his own hand; then, after consultations were held for battle, he appointed Gārgya to the task of an envoy and ordered, "Tomorrow battle is to be joined"; having performed the evening twilight worship and heard secret counsel, he derived joy from the palace by seeing and hearing the tidings of the soldiers, including the catching of the wind, the twanging of bows, and the roaring sounds.

sanskrit_iast: 210 bharatāhvānadundubhi śrutvā śalūṣatanayāḥ śailūṣaṃ rājānamupatasthuḥ bharatasaṃdiṣṭaṃ gārgyavākyaṃ saroṣaṃ mantrayāmāsuśca
meaning: 210 भरताह्वानदुन्दुभि श्रुत्वा शलूषतनयाः शैलूषं राजानमुपतस्थुः भरतसंदिष्टं गार्ग्यवाक्यं सरोषं मन्त्रयामासुश्च
text_mt: 210 Having heard the kettledrum sounding Bharata's challenge, the sons of Śailūṣa approached King Śailūṣa and, filled with anger, deliberated upon Gārgya's message sent by Bharata.

sanskrit_iast: 211 aparājitādisabhyānāṃ gandharvarājamuddiśya yuddhaviṣaye sammatidānam
meaning: 211 अपराजितादिसभ्यानां गन्धर्वराजमुद्दिश्य युद्धविषये सम्मतिदानम्
text_mt: 211 The granting of consent regarding battle by the assembly members, such as Aparājita, addressed to the king of the gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast: 212 kṛṣivāṇijyādikarmopayoginī bhūrmānuṣāṇāmevopayujyate kintayā devajātīyānāṃ gandharvāṇām, bharataśca pradyumnāṃśaḥ sumālinamapyavadhīttena sārdhaṃ vigraho na vidvatsammata iti nāḍāyano'mantrayata
meaning: 212 कृषिवाणिज्यादिकर्मोपयोगिनी भूर्मानुषाणामेवोपयुज्यते किन्तया देवजातीयानां गन्धर्वाणाम्, भरतश्च प्रद्युम्नांशः सुमालिनमप्यवधीत्तेन सार्धं विग्रहो न विद्वत्सम्मत इति नाडायनोऽमन्त्रयत
text_mt: 212 "Land suitable for works such as agriculture and commerce is useful only for human beings; what need of it have the gandharvas, who belong to the divine race? Moreover, Bharata is a portion of Pradyumna and he even slew Sumālin; war with him is not approved by the wise," thus Nāḍāyana advised.

sanskrit_iast: 213 vṛtre śakreṇa nihate daityāḥ samudramabdurgaṃ vidhāya rātrau prajā nijaghnuḥ, suraprārthito'gastyaḥ samudraṃ papau tena duṣṭadaityanāśaḥ samajani . raviniśākaramārgaṃ roddhuṃ pravṛtte vindhyagirāvagastyena svapraṇāmakaraṇāya namre tasminmama pratyāgamanaparyantamevameva nīcaistiṣṭhetyadyāpi tasya kharvatākaraṇam, ilvalavātāpinorbhakṣaṇena śaradi tvayyudite'pāmamalatvaṃ tava ca loke pūjā bhaviṣyatītyādyagastyāya devairvaradānam
meaning: 213 वृत्रे शक्रेण निहते दैत्याः समुद्रमब्दुर्गं विधाय रात्रौ प्रजा निजघ्नुः, सुरप्रार्थितोऽगस्त्यः समुद्रं पपौ तेन दुष्टदैत्यनाशः समजनि . रविनिशाकरमार्गं रोद्धुं प्रवृत्ते विन्ध्यगिरावगस्त्येन स्वप्रणामकरणाय नम्रे तस्मिन्मम प्रत्यागमनपर्यन्तमेवमेव नीचैस्तिष्ठेत्यद्यापि तस्य खर्वताकरणम्, इल्वलवातापिनोर्भक्षणेन शरदि त्वय्युदितेऽपाममलत्वं तव च लोके पूजा भविष्यतीत्याद्यगस्त्याय देवैर्वरदानम्
text_mt: 213 When Vṛtra was slain by Śakra, the daityas made the ocean an inaccessible fortress and slaughtered the creatures at night; Agastya, petitioned by the gods, drank up the ocean, whereby the destruction of the wicked daityas came about. When the Vindhya mountain set about blocking the path of the sun and moon, he bowed down to pay his respects to Agastya, who told him, "Remain low just like this until my return," which is the cause of its dwarf stature even today. Through his consumption of Ilvala and Vātāpi, the gods granted boons to Agastya, saying, "Upon your rising in the autumn, waters will become pure and there will be worship of you in the world," and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 214 mālyavatā vāryyamāṇāvapi mālisumālinau laṃkādurgamāśritya devānpīḍayāñcakratuḥ tataśca brahmeśasahitā devāḥ kṣīrapayodhau suptaṃ viṣṇumupatasthire
meaning: 214 माल्यवता वार्य्यमाणावपि मालिसुमालिनौ लंकादुर्गमाश्रित्य देवान्पीडयाञ्चक्रतुः ततश्च ब्रह्मेशसहिता देवाः क्षीरपयोधौ सुप्तं विष्णुमुपतस्थिरे
text_mt: 214 Though restrained by Mālyavat, Māli and Sumālin resorted to the fortress of Laṅkā and tormented the gods; thereupon the gods, accompanied by Brahmā and Śiva, approached Viṣṇu sleeping upon the milk-ocean.

sanskrit_iast: 215 sarve devā munayo nadīnadādayaśca śrīviṣṇumanujagmuḥ .... ....
meaning: 215 सर्वे देवा मुनयो नदीनदादयश्च श्रीविष्णुमनुजग्मुः .... ....
text_mt: 215 All the gods, sages, rivers, and streams followed Śrī Viṣṇu […].

sanskrit_iast: 216 devānāṃ raṇasamudyogamākarṇya mālisumālinau yuddhārthaṃ niryayatuḥ
meaning: 216 देवानां रणसमुद्योगमाकर्ण्य मालिसुमालिनौ युद्धार्थं निर्ययतुः
text_mt: 216 Having heard of the gods' preparation for battle, Māli and Sumālin set out for war.

sanskrit_iast: 217 devāsurasaṃgrāme viṣṇunā mālirākṣasaśiracchedaḥ ... ....
meaning: 217 देवासुरसंग्रामे विष्णुना मालिराक्षसशिरच्छेदः ... ....
text_mt: 217 In the battle between the gods and asuras, Viṣṇu severed the head of the rākṣasa Māli […].

sanskrit_iast: 218 mālinidhanānantaraṃ tārkṣyapakṣavātatāḍitarakṣasāṃ pātālagamanaṃ laṅkāyā vaiśravaṇe dānam
meaning: 218 मालिनिधनानन्तरं तार्क्ष्यपक्षवातताडितरक्षसां पातालगमनं लङ्काया वैश्रवणे दानम्
text_mt: 218 After the death of Māli, the rākṣasas, struck by the wind of Tārkṣya's wings, went to Pātāla, and Laṅkā was given to Vaiśravaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: 219 brahmamānasaputrapulastyasya viśravaso bṛhaspatipautrī bharadvājasutā devavarṇinī bhāryā''sīt tatputrāya vaiśravaṇāya tattapastuṣṭo brahmā yakṣeśadhaneśalokapālatvaṃ vitīrya puṣpakaṃ vimānaṃ viśvakarmanirmitāṃ laṃkāṃ ca dadau ..
meaning: 219 ब्रह्ममानसपुत्रपुलस्त्यस्य विश्रवसो बृहस्पतिपौत्री भरद्वाजसुता देववर्णिनी भार्या'ऽसीत् तत्पुत्राय वैश्रवणाय तत्तपस्तुष्टो ब्रह्मा यक्षेशधनेशलोकपालत्वं वितीर्य पुष्पकं विमानं विश्वकर्मनिर्मितां लंकां च ददौ ..
text_mt: 219 The wife of Viśravas, son of Pulastya who was the mind-born son of Brahmā, was Devavarṇinī, the daughter of Bharadvāja and granddaughter of Bṛhaspati; Brahmā, pleased by his austerities, bestowed upon her son Vaiśravaṇa the status of lord of the yakṣas, lord of wealth, and guardian of the worlds, and gave him the Puṣpaka aerial car and Laṅkā fashioned by Viśvakarman.

sanskrit_iast: 220 sumālinaḥ piturādeśātkaikasyā viśravasaḥ rāvaṇakumbhakarṇayoḥ sutayoḥ śūrpaṇakhāyāḥ kanyāyāścotpattiḥ, kadāciddhanādhyakṣavaibhavaṃ darśayantī kaikasī rāvaṇamūce tvamapyevaṃ śrīmānbhaveti, tataśca brahmaṇaḥ sakāśānmānuṣaṃ vihāya devādibhyo'vadhaṃ trailokyaviṣayañca yayāce, evaṃ vibhīṣaṇaṃ nityaṃ dharmamatimamaratvañca dattvā brahmaṇi yāte pātālādrakṣāṃsyāgatya daśavaktraṃ laṃkārājye'bhyaṣecayan . rāvaṇavacanātkubero laṃkāṃ tyaktvā'lakāyāmavasat punaśca trailokyavijayaṃ kṛtvā mayatanayāṃ mandodarīṃ rāvaṇa upayeme, tasyāśca meghanādaṃ sūnuṃ janayāmāsa sa rāmeṇāvadhi
meaning: 220 सुमालिनः पितुरादेशात्कैकस्या विश्रवसः रावणकुम्भकर्णयोः सुतयोः शूर्पणखायाः कन्यायाश्चोत्पत्तिः, कदाचिद्धनाध्यक्षवैभवं दर्शयन्ती कैकसी रावणमूचे त्वमप्येवं श्रीमान्भवेति, ततश्च ब्रह्मणः सकाशान्मानुषं विहाय देवादिभ्योऽवधं त्रैलोक्यविषयञ्च ययाचे, एवं विभीषणं नित्यं धर्ममतिममरत्वञ्च दत्त्वा ब्रह्मणि याते पातालाद्रक्षांस्यागत्य दशवक्त्रं लंकाराज्येऽभ्यषेचयन् . रावणवचनात्कुबेरो लंकां त्यक्त्वाऽलकायामवसत् पुनश्च त्रैलोक्यविजयं कृत्वा मयतनयां मन्दोदरीं रावण उपयेमे, तस्याश्च मेघनादं सूनुं जनयामास स रामेणावधि
text_mt: 220 By the instruction of her father Sumālin, the birth of two sons, Rāvaṇa and Kumbhakarṇa, and a daughter, Śūrpaṇakhā, took place from Kaikasī by Viśravas; once, showing the majesty of the lord of wealth, Kaikasī said to Rāvaṇa, "You too become glorious like this"; thereupon, he requested from Brahmā invulnerability from gods and others, excluding human beings, and lordship over the three worlds; when Brahmā departed after thus bestowing upon Vibhīṣaṇa constant devotion to dharma and immortality, the rākṣasas came from Pātāla and consecrated the ten-faced one to the kingdom of Laṅkā. At Rāvaṇa's word, Kubera left Laṅkā and dwelt in Alakā; then, having conquered the three worlds, Rāvaṇa married Mandodarī, the daughter of Maya, and fathered upon her a son, Meghanāda, who was [later] slain by Rāma.
