sanskrit_iast: 221 brahmadattavaradṛpto rāvaṇastridaśarāmāḥ kanyāśca jahāra, ayodhyāvāsyanaraṇyaṃ nṛpaṃ jaghāna sa ca matkulyāttava nidhanaṃ bhaviṣyatīti tamaśapat . maruttayajñe devāparādhaṃ ca kṛtavān, bṛhaspatisutakuśadhvajakanyā vedavatīti khyātā viṣṇupatyarthaṃ tapasyantī rāvaṇena pralobhitāpi na taṃ cakame, keśapāśe tena spṛṣṭā sā jvalanaṃ praviṣṭā'nyajanmani sītā babhūva, saṃkṣipya rāmasītācaritamuktvā tādṛśaviṣṇubhrātṛbharatena yuddhaṃ na śreya iti nāḍāyanasammatiḥ .
meaning: 221 ब्रह्मदत्तवरदृप्तो रावणस्त्रिदशरामाः कन्याश्च जहार, अयोध्यावास्यनरण्यं नृपं जघान स च मत्कुल्यात्तव निधनं भविष्यतीति तमशपत् . मरुत्तयज्ञे देवापराधं च कृतवान्, बृहस्पतिसुतकुशध्वजकन्या वेदवतीति ख्याता विष्णुपत्यर्थं तपस्यन्ती रावणेन प्रलोभितापि न तं चकमे, केशपाशे तेन स्पृष्टा सा ज्वलनं प्रविष्टाऽन्यजन्मनि सीता बभूव, संक्षिप्य रामसीताचरितमुक्त्वा तादृशविष्णुभ्रातृभरतेन युद्धं न श्रेय इति नाडायनसम्मतिः .
text_mt: 221 Proud with the boons granted by Brahmā, Rāvaṇa abducted the women and maidens of the thirty [gods]; he slew the king Anaraṇya, a dweller of Ayodhyā, who cursed him, saying, "Your destruction will come from one of my lineage"; and he committed an offense against the gods at the sacrifice of Marutta; the daughter of Kuśadhvaja, the son of Bṛhaspati, celebrated as Vedavatī, practicing austerities to obtain Viṣṇu as her husband, did not desire Rāvaṇa though enticed by him; touched by him on her mass of hair, she entered the fire and in another birth became Sītā. Having related the deeds of Rāma and Sītā in brief, Nāḍāyana's opinion is: "War with Bharata, who is the brother of such a Viṣṇu, is not beneficial."

sanskrit_iast: 222 mauddhatyaṃ kṛthāḥ suraistvadvadhaścintyata iti vaktāraṃ dhanadadūtaṃ hatvā tasya puṣpakavimānaṃ ca hṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ kailāśaṃ yayau, vānarākṛtiṃ nandinaṃ dṛṣṭvā prahasati rāvaṇe pulahaprajāpatikulasambhūtavānarebhyastava vināśaḥ syāditi nandikeśvaraśāpe jāte sakailāsaṃ haraṃ laṅkāṃ ninīṣau rāvaṇe, acalacalanasambhramajātasvayaṃgrahomā''śleṣatuṣṭo harastaṃ rāvaṇanāmānamakarot, tataśca rāvaṇaḥ saṃyaminyāṃ dharmarājaṃ kālapāśayāgapitṛgaṇāṃśca vijitya sūryeṇa yoddhumupatasthau, brahmā sūryaṃ nyavārayadrāvaṇaśca sendrāndevānvijigye .
meaning: 222 मौद्धत्यं कृथाः सुरैस्त्वद्वधश्चिन्त्यत इति वक्तारं धनददूतं हत्वा तस्य पुष्पकविमानं च हृत्वा रावणः कैलाशं ययौ, वानराकृतिं नन्दिनं दृष्ट्वा प्रहसति रावणे पुलहप्रजापतिकुलसम्भूतवानरेभ्यस्तव विनाशः स्यादिति नन्दिकेश्वरशापे जाते सकैलासं हरं लङ्कां निनीषौ रावणे, अचलचलनसम्भ्रमजातस्वयंग्रहोमा'ऽश्लेषतुष्टो हरस्तं रावणनामानमकरोत्, ततश्च रावणः संयमिन्यां धर्मराजं कालपाशयागपितृगणांश्च विजित्य सूर्येण योद्धुमुपतस्थौ, ब्रह्मा सूर्यं न्यवारयद्रावणश्च सेन्द्रान्देवान्विजिग्ये .
text_mt: 222 Having killed the messenger of the Lord of Wealth who said, "Do not commit insolence; your destruction is being contemplated by the gods," and having seized his Puṣpaka aerial car, Rāvaṇa went to Kailāsa; when Rāvaṇa laughed aloud seeing Nandin in the form of a monkey, Nandikeśvara uttered a curse, saying, "Your destruction shall be caused by monkeys born in the family of the patriarch Pulaha"; when Rāvaṇa wished to carry Hara together with Kailāsa to Laṅkā, Hara, pleased by the spontaneous embrace of Umā caused by the agitation of the mountain's shaking, gave him the name Rāvaṇa; and then Rāvaṇa, having conquered the King of Dharma together with the noose of Time, Yama, and the hosts of the ancestors in Saṃyaminī, approached to fight with Sūrya; Brahmā held back Sūrya, and Rāvaṇa conquered the gods led by Indra.

sanskrit_iast: 223 rāvaṇaḥ pātāle kālakhañjādidaityānvijitya brahmānurodhena nivātakavacaiḥ saha sakhyañcakāra, nāgānsasutaṃ varuṇañca jitvā kiṣkindhāyāṃ yuddhārthaṃ vālinaṃ papraccha, tāreṇa dundubhighātanaṃ sugrīvasya niṣkāsanaṃ hanūmatpauruṣañca varṇitam ..
meaning: 223 रावणः पाताले कालखञ्जादिदैत्यान्विजित्य ब्रह्मानुरोधेन निवातकवचैः सह सख्यञ्चकार, नागान्ससुतं वरुणञ्च जित्वा किष्किन्धायां युद्धार्थं वालिनं पप्रच्छ, तारेण दुन्दुभिघातनं सुग्रीवस्य निष्कासनं हनूमत्पौरुषञ्च वर्णितम् ..
text_mt: 223 In Pātāla, having conquered the daityas such as the Kālakhañjas, Rāvaṇa made an alliance with the Nivātakavacas at the request of Brahmā; having defeated the nāgas and Varuṇa along with his son, he asked Vālin in Kiṣkindhā for battle; the slaying of Dundubhi, the banishment of Sugrīva, and the heroism of Hanūmat are described by Tāra.

sanskrit_iast: ( itaḥparaṃ pāṭhaḥ khaṇḍitaḥ, etada'dhyāyaśeṣaśturviṃśatyuttaradviśatatamādhyāyaśdha nopalabdha:)
meaning: ( इतःपरं पाठः खण्डितः, एतदऽध्यायशेषश्तुर्विंशत्युत्तरद्विशततमाध्यायश्ध नोपलब्ध:)
text_mt: Thereafter the text is fragmentary; the remainder of this chapter and the two hundred and twenty-fourth chapter are not available.

sanskrit_iast: 225 tripuradāhānte śaṃkarānuṣṭhitagaṇeśastutiḥ ..
meaning: 225 त्रिपुरदाहान्ते शंकरानुष्ठितगणेशस्तुतिः ..
text_mt: 225 The hymn of praise to Gaṇeśa performed by Śaṅkara at the conclusion of the burning of Tripura.

sanskrit_iast: 226 andhakāsurasamare tadastrasañjātānekāndhakakhinnena śambhunā māheśvaryādimātṝḥ sṛṣṭvāpi yadā nāndhakāsṛkkṣayastadā tattuṣṭavāsudevasṛṣṭaśuṣkarevatīpītarudhirā andhakāḥ kṣayaṃ prāpuḥ mūlāndhakaṃ tatprārthanayā śivo gaṇeśatvaṃ svasāmīpyañca dadau tato mātṝṇāmupadrave vṛddhe rudrasmṛtanṛharirvāgīśvaryādīḥ sasarja, tattejobhītāḥ pūrvamātaraḥ nṛsiṃhaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ sa ca tatpūjakānāmabhīṣṭasiddhiṃ svīkṛtya tāḥ pūjyā vyadhatta
meaning: 226 अन्धकासुरसमरे तदस्त्रसञ्जातानेकान्धकखिन्नेन शम्भुना माहेश्वर्यादिमातॄः सृष्ट्वापि यदा नान्धकासृक्क्षयस्तदा तत्तुष्टवासुदेवसृष्टशुष्करेवतीपीतरुधिरा अन्धकाः क्षयं प्रापुः मूलान्धकं तत्प्रार्थनया शिवो गणेशत्वं स्वसामीप्यञ्च ददौ ततो मातॄणामुपद्रवे वृद्धे रुद्रस्मृतनृहरिर्वागीश्वर्यादीः ससर्ज, तत्तेजोभीताः पूर्वमातरः नृसिंहं शरणं जग्मुः स च तत्पूजकानामभीष्टसिद्धिं स्वीकृत्य ताः पूज्या व्यधत्त
text_mt: 226 In the battle with the asura Andhaka, when Śambhu, afflicted by the numerous Andhakas born from his weapon, created the Mothers such as Māheśvarī, yet the blood of Andhaka was not depleted, then the Andhakas met destruction when their blood was drunk by Śuṣkarevatī, who was created by Vāsudeva who was pleased with him; upon his request, Śiva granted the original Andhaka the status of a Gaṇeśa and proximity to himself; then, when the affliction caused by the Mothers grew, Rudra remembered Nṛhari, who created Vāgīśvarī and the others; frightened by their brilliance, the former Mothers took refuge in Nṛsiṃha, who, granting the attainment of desired ends for their worshippers, rendered them worthy of worship.

sanskrit_iast: 227 mātṛdoṣavināśanasnānānulepanadhūpabalipañcagavyādikathanam
meaning: 227 मातृदोषविनाशनस्नानानुलेपनधूपबलिपञ्चगव्यादिकथनम्
text_mt: 227 The description of the bath, ointment, incense, offerings, the five products of the cow, and so forth, which destroy the afflictions caused by the Mothers.

sanskrit_iast: 228 parasparaspardhamānaharagauryo rahasyakrīḍāyāmanyatarasyāviratatayā vahnestatra kapotarūpeṇa praveśe śaṅkararetaścyutaṃ vahnerāsyamaviśacchaśāpa ca girijādevānsvasvabhāryāsu naiva putrāṃllabhadhvamiti, atyugraṃ hi śivareto bahirujjagāra gaṅgā ca taddadhāra, gaṅgāpyasahyaṃ tattejaḥ śvete girau tatyāja, ṣaṭkṛttikāśca taddadhuḥ śaṅkarasūnuḥ ṣaḍānano bhūtvā tāsāṃ stanānpapau tatpayovṛddhaśca kṛttikācandrayoge vahniguhakṛttikāvaruṇapūjākarttarabhimateṣṭasiddhiṃ varaṃ dadau
meaning: 228 परस्परस्पर्धमानहरगौर्यो रहस्यक्रीडायामन्यतरस्याविरततया वह्नेस्तत्र कपोतरूपेण प्रवेशे शङ्कररेतश्च्युतं वह्नेरास्यमविशच्छशाप च गिरिजादेवान्स्वस्वभार्यासु नैव पुत्रांल्लभध्वमिति, अत्युग्रं हि शिवरेतो बहिरुज्जगार गङ्गा च तद्दधार, गङ्गाप्यसह्यं तत्तेजः श्वेते गिरौ तत्याज, षट्कृत्तिकाश्च तद्दधुः शङ्करसूनुः षडाननो भूत्वा तासां स्तनान्पपौ तत्पयोवृद्धश्च कृत्तिकाचन्द्रयोगे वह्निगुहकृत्तिकावरुणपूजाकर्त्तरभिमतेष्टसिद्धिं वरं ददौ
text_mt: 228 While Hara and Gaurī were engaged in secret sport competing with each other, because neither of them ceased, Agni entered there in the form of a dove; Śaṅkara’s semen dropped and entered the mouth of Agni; and Girijā cursed the gods, saying, “You shall never obtain sons in your own wives.” Indeed, Agni spewed out the extremely fierce semen of Śiva, and Gaṅgā held it; Gaṅgā too, unable to bear that splendour, cast it upon the Śveta mountain; and the six Kṛttikās took it up; the son of Śaṅkara, becoming six-faced, drank their breasts, and grown on their milk, he granted the boon of the attainment of desired wishes to anyone who worships Agni, Guha, the Kṛttikās, and Varuṇa during the conjunction of the Kṛttikās and the moon.

sanskrit_iast: 229 tvattejo'sahantyā mayā śvetagirau tvaṃ tyakta iti kathayantīṃ gaṅgāṃ kārtikeyo'kṣayatṛtīyāyāṃ kutrāpi snānakarturgaṅgāsnānaphalaprāptiṃ dānādeścākṣayaphalatāñcakāra
meaning: 229 त्वत्तेजोऽसहन्त्या मया श्वेतगिरौ त्वं त्यक्त इति कथयन्तीं गङ्गां कार्तिकेयोऽक्षयतृतीयायां कुत्रापि स्नानकर्तुर्गङ्गास्नानफलप्राप्तिं दानादेश्चाक्षयफलताञ्चकार
text_mt: 229 When Gaṅgā said, “Unable to bear your splendour, I abandoned you on the Śveta mountain,” Kārttikeya granted that anyone who bathes anywhere on Akṣayatṛtīyā obtains the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā, and that gifts and the like yield imperishable fruit.

sanskrit_iast: 230 śvetagirāvapūrvasattvaṃ śrutvā devadaityādibhirāmantrya śakrastannāśāya matiṃ cakre, skandastvaparāngrahānnirmāya sarvāstānnirvīryām̐ñcakre, nāstikādibhyastadvṛttimapi svīcakre
meaning: 230 श्वेतगिरावपूर्वसत्त्वं श्रुत्वा देवदैत्यादिभिरामन्त्र्य शक्रस्तन्नाशाय मतिं चक्रे, स्कन्दस्त्वपरान्ग्रहान्निर्माय सर्वास्तान्निर्वीर्याम्̐ञ्चक्रे, नास्तिकादिभ्यस्तद्वृत्तिमपि स्वीचक्रे
text_mt: 230 Hearing of the unprecedented being on the Śveta mountain, Śakra, having conferred with the gods, daityas, and others, resolved to destroy it; but Skanda, having created other grahas, rendered all of them powerless, and he accepted their livelihood from atheists and the like.

sanskrit_iast: 231 grahagṛhītalakṣaṇāni
meaning: 231 ग्रहगृहीतलक्षणानि
text_mt: 231 The marks of one seized by a graha.

sanskrit_iast: 232 abhyaṅgādinavagrahadoṣaharāḥ kriyā godvijadevārcakasya sadānukūlā grahāḥ
meaning: 232 अभ्यङ्गादिनवग्रहदोषहराः क्रिया गोद्विजदेवार्चकस्य सदानुकूला ग्रहाः
text_mt: 232 Rites beginning with anointing that remove the afflictions of the nine grahas; the grahas are always favourable to one who worships cows, twice-born people, and the gods.

sanskrit_iast: 233 śakrakṛtakārttikeyastutiḥ kārttikeyakṛtamahiṣāsuravadhaśca ...
meaning: 233 शक्रकृतकार्त्तिकेयस्तुतिः कार्त्तिकेयकृतमहिषासुरवधश्च ...
text_mt: 233 The praise of Kārttikeya spoken by Śakra, and the slaying of Mahiṣāsura performed by Kārttikeya.

text_mt: 234 When the gods did not assign a share to Śaṅkara in the sacrifice, Śiva terrified them: eating the sacrificial cake, he destroyed the teeth of Pūṣan and the left eye of Bhaga; the sacrifice fled to the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa and sought refuge with Viṣṇu, and Hara showed it favour.

sanskrit_iast: 235 gaṅgādvāre dakṣayajñe śaṅkarānāhvānādvīrabhadrabhadrakālībhyāṃ dakṣayajñavidhvaṃsaḥ, vīrabhadropadeśātstutabhadrakarṇeśvaro dakṣo'śvamedhasahasraphalaṃ lebhe . haradvāre kuśāvartāditīrthapañcakaprāśastyam

text_mt: 235 At Gaṅgādvāra, because Śaṅkara was not invited to Dakṣa’s sacrifice, the destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice by Vīrabhadra and Bhadrakālī; through the instruction of Vīrabhadra, Dakṣa praised Bhadrakarṇeśvara and obtained the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices. The excellence of the five holy bathing-places beginning with Kuśāvarta at Haradvāra.

sanskrit_iast: 236 śambhuṃ pūjayati śvetarṣau mūrtimān kālastasyāyuṣaḥ pūrṇatvāttamānetuṃ taddeśamāgataḥ, kṛtavaiṣṇavakavacarakṣaḥ śambhuḥ kālaṃ bhasmasādakarot ....

text_mt: 236 While the sage Śveta was worshipping Śambhu, embodied Kāla, because his lifespan was complete, arrived at that place to take him; having formed the protection of the Vaiṣṇava armour, Śambhu reduced Kāla to ashes.

text_mt: 238 When Rāvaṇa went to the abode of Bali out of curiosity about an opponent for himself, saying out of friendship, “I shall conquer Viṣṇu who bound you,” he was told by Bali, “Bring here my bracelet lying over there and sit down”; even with all his effort he could not bring [even] an earring; and [Bali said], “With these two earrings my great-grandfather Hiraṇyakaśipu shone, whom this [Viṣṇu] crushed like a bedbug; your hope to conquer him is in vain.”

sanskrit_iast: 239 rāvaṇasya viṣṇuvirāḍrūpadarśanam

sanskrit_iast: 240 ayodhyāyāṃ vasantavarṇanam ..

sanskrit_iast: 242 sādhukaṇṭakaṃ madhudaityaṃ jahati cyavanapuraḥsarayamunātīrthasthamunivṛnda āgate sasainyasya śatrughnasya rāmājñayā tadvadhāya gamanam
meaning: 242 साधुकण्टकं मधुदैत्यं जहति च्यवनपुरःसरयमुनातीर्थस्थमुनिवृन्द आगते ससैन्यस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य रामाज्ञया तद्वधाय गमनम्
text_mt: 242 When a host of sages dwelling on the bank of the Yamunā, led by Cyavana, arrived [complaining] that the Madhu daitya was afflicting the virtuous, the departure of Śatrughna with his army, by order of Rāma, to slay him.

sanskrit_iast: 243 prāvṛḍvarṇanam

sanskrit_iast: 246 śatrughnāya rāmopadeśe śiśiravarṇanam

sanskrit_iast: 247 śrīvaśiṣṭharāmādipādāvabhivādya śatrughno madhurājigamiṣayā prathamaṃ vālmīkyāśramaṃ prāpa, śatrughnakṛtalavaṇavadhānantaraṃ suprītadevecchayā śatrughnena mathurānirmāṇam
meaning: 247 श्रीवशिष्ठरामादिपादावभिवाद्य शत्रुघ्नो मधुराजिगमिषया प्रथमं वाल्मीक्याश्रमं प्राप, शत्रुघ्नकृतलवणवधानन्तरं सुप्रीतदेवेच्छया शत्रुघ्नेन मथुरानिर्माणम्
text_mt: 247 Having bowed to the feet of the venerable Vasiṣṭha, Rāma, and the others, Śatrughna, wishing to go to Madhurā, first reached the hermitage of Vālmīki; after the slaying of Lavaṇa by Śatrughna, the construction of Mathurā by Śatrughna in accordance with the wish of the well-pleased gods.

sanskrit_iast: 248 pulahavaṃśavarṇanaprasaṅge mṛgāmṛgamandādikanyānāṃ pulahadvārā mṛgādisṛṣṭivarṇanam.

text_mt: 248 In the context of describing the lineage of Pulaha, the description of the creation of deer and the like through Pulaha by the daughters beginning with Mṛgā and Mṛgamandā.

sanskrit_iast: 249 oṣadhidvijātinakṣatrayajñatapasāṃ candraṃ, sarvaprajāpatīnāṃ dakṣaṃ, sarvendriyāṇāṃ manasaṃ, surastrīṇāṃ manmathamityādi pratisamūhe rājakīrtanam

text_mt: 249 The proclamation of kings over each group: the Moon over medicinal herbs, the twice-born, constellations, sacrifices, and austerities; Dakṣa over all progenitors; the mind over all sense-faculties; Manmatha over celestial women; and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 250 brahmā devarājye kāśyapaṃ śakramabhiṣiṣeca

sanskrit_iast: 251 mataṃgajānāṃ kulāṣṭakāni vanāṣṭakañca

text_mt: 251 The eight families and the eight forests of elephants.

sanskrit_iast: 254 śvo bharatena saha yoddhavyamadya sarverviśrāmasukhamanubhūyāvaśyakaṃ kṛtvā śva āgantavyamiti śailūṣanirdeśaḥ

text_mt: 254 Śailūṣa’s command: “Tomorrow we must fight with Bharata; today, all should enjoy the comfort of rest, attend to necessities, and arrive tomorrow.”

sanskrit_iast: 255 ayodhyāyāṃ virahiṇīvarṇanam

sanskrit_iast: 264 pañcamadivasayuddhodantaḥ

text_mt: 265 When Śailūṣa had his chariot destroyed, and Bharata was in the same condition, after a terrifying battle, the cessation of fighting on the sixth day.

sanskrit_iast: 266 nānāmāyāyuddhe bharatavihitaśailūṣavadhe sañjāte śailūṣaputrādhiṣṭhitatrikoṭigandharvasainyānāmapi nāśe śakrasya bharatasamīpaṃ varadānārthaṃ gamanam, sindhukūlayoḥ puraddhaye tvatputrayo rājye sta ityabhidhāya svargagamanañca, bharataṃ sabhājāyitvā citrarathasyāpi nākaprayāṇam
meaning: 266 नानामायायुद्धे भरतविहितशैलूषवधे सञ्जाते शैलूषपुत्राधिष्ठितत्रिकोटिगन्धर्वसैन्यानामपि नाशे शक्रस्य भरतसमीपं वरदानार्थं गमनम्, सिन्धुकूलयोः पुरद्धये त्वत्पुत्रयो राज्ये स्त इत्यभिधाय स्वर्गगमनञ्च, भरतं सभाजायित्वा चित्ररथस्यापि नाकप्रयाणम्
text_mt: 266 When, in a battle of diverse sorceries, the slaying of Śailūṣa was accomplished by Bharata, and the army of thirty million Gandharvas commanded by Śailūṣa’s sons was also destroyed, Śakra’s arrival before Bharata to grant a boon; his departure to heaven after saying, “Let the two cities on the banks of the Sindhu be the kingdoms of your two sons”; and, having honoured Bharata, Citraratha’s departure to heaven as well.

sanskrit_iast: 267 bharatayudhājitoḥ svaśibiraṃ gacchatoryudhājitkṛtasamarabhūmivarṇanam

text_mt: 267 As Bharata and Yudhājit were returning to their camp, the description of the battlefield given by Yudhājit.

sanskrit_iast: 268 raṇabhūmau gatāsūngandharvānvilokya hṛdayadrāvakaṃ gandharvīvilapanam

text_mt: 268 The heart-rending lamentation of the Gandharva women on seeing the lifeless Gandharvas on the battlefield.

sanskrit_iast: 269 raṇātpratinivṛttasya bharatasya rāmasākṣātkāravijitagandharvaratnānāṃ rāmāya nivedanam

text_mt: 269 Bharata, returned from the battle, having won an audience with Rāma, offering the jewels of the conquered Gandharvas to Rāma.

At first, the victory of Bharata was told to me by your lordship;
hearing which, O brahmin, I know myself to be freed from taint.

Questioned by Rāma, the son of Varuṇa spoke of the duties of the best of kings, / full of substance and of great import, for the protection of all the world on earth, O moon among kings.
2.2 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Seated comfortably in Puṣkara's dwelling, the best among men, / Rāma, constant in dharma and with senses conquered, questioned Puṣkara.
Rāma said: / "What is the most urgent duty of a kingdom? Tell that to me as I ask, / at the very beginning, O fortunate one, O son of the king of aquatic creatures."
Puṣkara said: / "The duty of a kingdom, O knower of dharma, is indeed the consecration of a king. / A kingless, powerless kingdom the robbers overcome.
In kingless kingdoms, no order of dharma exists, / nor the proper maintenance of the classes and life-stages, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
In kingless kingdoms, a maiden is not given in marriage at all; / no sense of 'this is mine' exists in property for anyone.
The law of self-interest would prevail, as well as universal plunder; / no one in the world would be found carrying out the words of a guru.

text_mt:
The three twice-born classes would not study the threefold science; / there would be no sacrificing to the gods, and drought would result therefrom.
Both the world of mortals and the world of the gods would be placed in jeopardy; / a dreadful plague would arise if the king did not protect.
For the protection of the subjects, augmented by the splendour of Viṣṇu, / the king is born in human form, bearing a body of divine essence,
in whose pleasure the grace of the god arises, / and in whose anger the wrath of this people arises.
By vast accumulations of merit a king is born, O Rāma, / at whose sole command the entire world abides, O Rāma.
The four classes stand firm in their own dharma in those lands / in which, O best of kings, the king is righteous.
(Neither pestilence, nor famine, nor danger from fire and thieves, / nor danger from wild beasts exists for those who have a king devoted to dharma.)

Having taken the vow, desiring the kingdom, for the happiness of this entire world, / the king should choose an excellent brahmin astrologer,
characterised by all auspicious marks, disciplined, pleasant to look upon, / handsome, suitably attired, and always energetic in appearance,

knowing the truth of the sixty-four branches, skilled in reasoning and deduction, / knowing the past, present, and future, and especially skilled in mathematics.
Just as a night is without a moon, or a crown has lost its jewels, / even so is astrology devoid of mathematics, O best of kings.
An orthodox believer, faithful, and well-disposed to the king— / going to such an astrologer, the king, restrained and pure, should select him.
An astrologer consecrated by whom a king has perished, O ruler of men, / a wise man should not select, O best of kings.
Nor one of defective limbs, nor a chatterer, nor one devoid of wit, / nor one poorly clad, filthy, shaven-headed, an atheist, or resolved on evil;
nor should he select one of corrupted conduct; he should always select one with virtuous qualities. / Having selected him, he must be spoken to by the king himself:
‘Just as the gods have fire for their mouth, so subjects have the king for their mouth; / just as mantras have fire for their mouth, so kings have astrologers.’
‘You are indeed my mother, my father, my spiritual guide, and my teacher; / fate and human effort must always be examined by you.’

2.5 / Rāma said: / What kind of royal priest should be appointed by the king, and what kind of minister, / and likewise what kind of chief queen? Tell that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said: / Unmaimed, endowed with auspicious marks, agreeable, pleasant of speech, / learned in the Atharvaveda, and skilled in the Yajurveda;
the king should select a handsome brahmin priest learned in two Vedas, / adhering to the Atharvaveda, knowing the procedures of the five rituals.
The Nakṣatrakalpa, the Vaitāna, the third is the Saṃhitāvidhi, / the fourth is the ritual of the Aṅgirases, and the Śāntikalpa is the fifth.
Having obtained a teacher knowing the rules of the five rituals, / the king, with all portents pacified within him, enjoys the earth for a long time.
And he should always perform the king’s daily rites, / as well as occasional and optional rites, intent upon the astrologer’s word.

The king should not be abandoned by the astrologer and the royal priest; / but if fallen, he should be abandoned; there is no hesitation in this matter.
Likewise, O Rāma, unless fallen, those two must not be abandoned by the king; / by abandoning them, O best of kings, loss of the kingdom is indicated,
and an evil destination in the other world for a long time, beyond doubt. / But a royal priest who opposes the astrologer must be abandoned by the king. / Otherwise, the royal priest is to the king like a mother, like a father; / he averts his undesired misfortune arising from divine afflictions.
Where could expiation be possible for the king [if he harms] that brahmin, / so long as the wise astrologer and royal priest are not maintained by the king?
If their livelihood is cut off, the king’s family goes to hell / for three generations; therefore, he should always avoid cutting off their livelihood.
An allotment of immovable property, in particular, should be made to both of them / in suitable proportion, O knower of dharma, to the astrologer and royal priest.

Endowed with such hosts of virtues, faultless, / she should be consecrated in the kingdom alongside the king, or by the king established in royal power.
When a noble-minded wife is like this for the moon among rulers of men, / the realm of that king, together with its populace, will prosper; on this there is no doubt.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'Characteristics of the Chief Queen', in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the Second Book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara.

Rāma said:
Of men and women, of elephants together with horses, / of chowries, umbrellas, and likewise of the royal throne,
and of jewels, bows, and swords, O son of a deity, / I desire to hear the characteristics; tell that to me who am asking.
Puṣkara said:
At the very beginning I shall explain the characteristics of men; / listen to that as I speak, O enhancer of the Bhṛgu lineage.

He who is superior in one, white in two, and who pervades by three, / having three folds, bowing threefold, and knowing the three times, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
that man would be endowed with auspicious marks, and broad in three, / and he who has four lines, and likewise he who is even in four,
measuring four cubits, having four prominent incisors, and having four dark features, / having four fragrances, having four short features, and likewise having five fine features,
having five long features, O best of the Bhṛgus, and likewise having six elevated features, / having seven glosses, eight backbones, and pure in nine places,
having ten lotus-like parts, ten large parts, symmetrical like a banyan tree, / having fourteen equal pairs, and termed sixteen-fold, is praised.
Rāma said:
These qualities of a man beginning with 'superior in one' which were spoken of by you, / those I desire to hear as they truly are, O son of Varuṇa.
Puṣkara said:
All people are attached to dharma, artha, and kāma; / but he who is especially attached to dharma is to be known as 'superior in one'.

hrasvaṃ liṅgaṃ tathā grīvā jaṃghe hrasve tu dehinaḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
कथितः स भृगुश्रेष्ठ चतुर्गन्ध इति द्विजैः ..
ह्रस्वं लिङ्गं तथा ग्रीवा जंघे ह्रस्वे तु देहिनः .. 27 ..
text_mt: he is declared by the twice-born, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, to be one of four fragrances. / A person whose penis, neck, and shanks are short,

sanskrit_iast:
yasya bhārgavaśārdūla caturhrasvaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ ..
aṅgulīnāṃ tu parvāṇi nakhakeśadvijatvacam ..
sūkṣmaṇi yasya taṃ rāma pañca sūkṣmaṃ pracakṣate .. 28 ..

यस्य भार्गवशार्दूल चतुर्ह्रस्वः स कीर्तितः ..
अङ्गुलीनां तु पर्वाणि नखकेशद्विजत्वचम् ..
सूक्ष्मणि यस्य तं राम पञ्च सूक्ष्मं प्रचक्षते .. 28 ..

sanskrit_iast:
hanū netre lalāṭaṃ ca nāsā caiva stanāntaram ..

sanskrit_iast:

ṣaḍunnatāni yasyeha taṃ vadaṃti ṣaḍunnatama .. 30 ..
meaning:
वक्षः कक्षौ नखा नासा मुखं चैव कृकाटिका ..
षडुन्नतानि यस्येह तं वदंति षडुन्नतम .. 30 ..
text_mt: Chest, armpits, nails, nose, mouth, and nape of the neck: / one who has six elevated [parts] among these here, they call one of six elevated [parts].

sanskrit_iast:

त्वक्केशलोमदंताश्च दृष्टिर्वाणी नखास्तथा ..

sanskrit_iast:

जानुवंशावुभौ राम भुजवंशौ तथाप्युभौ ..
ऊरुवंशद्वयं चैव पृष्ठवंशं च भार्गव .. 32 ..
text_mt: Both knee-bones, O Rāma, likewise both arm-bones, / both thigh-bones, and the backbone, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

sanskrit_iast:

शिश्नाग्रवक्षो यस्यैते पद्माभा दश देहिनाम् ..

उच्छ्रायेण समो यः स न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलः ..

तेषां तु श्रोतुमिच्छामि लक्षणं वरुणात्मज .. 9 ..
.. पुष्कर उवाच ..
आयामेन न संपूर्णो योतिह्रस्वो भवेद्गजः ..
वामनस्तु समाख्यातो मत्कुणो दन्तवर्जितः .. 10 ..
दशां चतुर्थीं संप्राप्य वर्धते यस्य न द्विजौ ..
स्थूलावनायतौ स्यातां स मूढाख्यो गजाधमः .. 11 ..
अपाकलो विशालेन दन्तेनैकेन वारणः ..
संक्षिप्तवक्षोजघनः पृष्ठमध्यसमुन्नतः .. 12 ..
प्रमाणहीनतन्नाभिः स कुब्जो वारणाधमः ..
अत्युन्नतांसः सद्दन्तः कुदन्तः स्यान्नतो बहिः .. 13 ..
text_mt:
nor female elephants that are pregnant, nor elephants that are bewildered, / nor those that are diseased, hunchbacked, or possessing single tusks, O descendant of Bhṛgu;
those with bad tusks should likewise be avoided, and with care those with a defective left side, / those that touch blood, those that are deceitful, treacherous, and monstrous.
Rāma said:
Those elephants, beginning with the dwarf, which have been called of blameworthy marks—
I wish to hear their characteristics, O son of Varuṇa.
Puṣkara said:
An elephant that is deficient in length, and is excessively short,
is declared a dwarf; one devoid of tusks is a matkuṇa.
One whose two tusks do not grow even after reaching the fourth stage [of life],
and remain thick and unstretched, is a base elephant named mūḍha.
An apākala is an elephant with one large tusk,
with a contracted chest and rump, and raised in the middle of the back.
One whose navel is deficient in proportion is a kubja, a base elephant;
one whose shoulder is excessively high is a saddanta; a kudanta is one whose [tusks] are bent outwards.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmadantonnato nāgo vāmakūṭaśca kathyate ..
dantau vaktraspṛśau yasya so'sruspṛkkathito gajaḥ .. 14 ..
ekadantastathā nāgaḥ kūṭa ityabhidhīyate ..
pādayoḥ sannikarṣaḥ syādyasya nāgasya gacchataḥ .. 15 ..
sa śaṭhodhvani yuddhe ca lakṣaṇajñairnna pūjitaḥ ..
aratnyabhyadhikaṃ yasya vistareṇa stanāntaram .. 16 ..
vikaṭaḥ sa vinirdiṣṭo durgatirnindito gajaḥ ..
rāma uvāca ..
śrotumicchāmi dharmajña kuñjaraṃ saptasusthitam .. 17 ..
yaṃ prāpya kila rājāno jayanti vasudhāṃ nṛpāḥ ..
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
varṇaṃ sattvaṃ balaṃ rūpaṃ kāntissaṃhananaṃ javam ..
saptaitāni sadā yasya sa gajaḥ saptasusthitaḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
वामदन्तोन्नतो नागो वामकूटश्च कथ्यते ..
दन्तौ वक्त्रस्पृशौ यस्य सोऽस्रुस्पृक्कथितो गजः .. 14 ..
एकदन्तस्तथा नागः कूट इत्यभिधीयते ..
पादयोः सन्निकर्षः स्याद्यस्य नागस्य गच्छतः .. 15 ..
स शठोध्वनि युद्धे च लक्षणज्ञैर्न्न पूजितः ..
अरत्न्यभ्यधिकं यस्य विस्तरेण स्तनान्तरम् .. 16 ..
विकटः स विनिर्दिष्टो दुर्गतिर्निन्दितो गजः ..
राम उवाच ..
श्रोतुमिच्छामि धर्मज्ञ कुञ्जरं सप्तसुस्थितम् .. 17 ..
यं प्राप्य किल राजानो जयन्ति वसुधां नृपाः ..
.. पुष्कर उवाच ..
वर्णं सत्त्वं बलं रूपं कान्तिस्संहननं जवम् ..
सप्तैतानि सदा यस्य स गजः सप्तसुस्थितः .. 18 ..
text_mt:
An elephant whose left tusk is raised is called a vāmakūṭa;
an elephant whose tusks touch its mouth is declared an asruspṛś.
Likewise, an elephant with a single tusk is called a kūṭa;
an elephant whose feet touch each other as it walks—
that is a śaṭha, not praised on the march or in battle by those who know the marks.
One whose chest width exceeds a cubit [in excessive breadth]—
that elephant is designated a vikaṭa, of bad gait and censured.
Rāma said:
O knower of dharma, I wish to hear about the elephant well-established in seven [qualities],
by obtaining which kings indeed conquer the earth.
Puṣkara said:
Color, vitality, strength, beauty, splendor, bodily structure, and speed—
one who always possesses these seven is an elephant well-established in the seven.

sanskrit_iast:
yeṣāṃ bhaveddakṣiṇapārśvabhāge romṇāṃ ca puṃjaḥ piṭako'thavāpi ..
te nāgamukhyā vijayāya yuddhe bhavanti rājñāṃ na hi saṃśayo'tra .. 59 ..
meaning:
येषां भवेद्दक्षिणपार्श्वभागे रोम्णां च पुंजः पिटकोऽथवापि ..
ते नागमुख्या विजयाय युद्धे भवन्ति राज्ञां न हि संशयोऽत्र .. 59 ..
text_mt:
Those on whose right flank there is a tuft of hair or a boil,
those foremost of elephants lead to victory for kings in battle; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
2.11
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
aśvānāmṛṣibhiḥ proktā mahādoṣā bhṛgūttama ..

2.11

text_mt:
2.11
Puṣkara said:
Great flaws in horses have been taught by the sages, O foremost of the Bhṛgus;
listen to me declaring those endowed with which they are to be rejected:
title: Chatralakṣaṇam

sanskrit_iast:
hīnadanto dvidantaśca karālī kṛṣṇatālukaḥ ..
kṛṣṇajihvaśca yamajo jātamuṣkaśca yastathā .. 2..
meaning:
हीनदन्तो द्विदन्तश्च कराली कृष्णतालुकः ..
कृष्णजिह्वश्च यमजो जातमुष्कश्च यस्तथा .. 2..
text_mt:
One deficient in teeth, one with two teeth, one with projecting teeth, one with a black palate,
one with a black tongue, a twin-born one, and one born with testicles;

sanskrit_iast:
dviśaphaśca tathā śṛṅgī nṛvarṇo vyāghravarṇakaḥ ..
kharavarṇo bhasmavarṇo jātavarṇaśca kākudī .. 3 ..
meaning:
द्विशफश्च तथा शृङ्गी नृवर्णो व्याघ्रवर्णकः ..
खरवर्णो भस्मवर्णो जातवर्णश्च काकुदी .. 3 ..
text_mt:
one with cloven hooves, one with a horn, one colored like a human, one colored like a tiger,
one colored like a donkey, ash-colored, born-colored, and one having a kākuda curl;

sanskrit_iast:
śvitrī ca kākasādī ca kharaśārastathaiva ca ..
vānarākhyaḥ kṛṣṇasaṭaḥ kṛṣṇamuṣkastathaiva ca .. 4 ..
meaning:
श्वित्री च काकसादी च खरशारस्तथैव च ..
वानराख्यः कृष्णसटः कृष्णमुष्कस्तथैव च .. 4 ..
text_mt:
one having white leprosy, one upon whom a crow perches, one of the color of a donkey,
one called monkey[-faced], one with a black mane, and one with black testicles;

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇaprothaśca mūkaśca yaśca tittirasannibhaḥ ..
viṣamaśvetapādaśca dhruvāvartavivarjitaḥ .. 5 ..
meaning:
कृष्णप्रोथश्च मूकश्च यश्च तित्तिरसन्निभः ..
विषमश्वेतपादश्च ध्रुवावर्तविवर्जितः .. 5 ..
text_mt:
one with a black muzzle, one who is mute, and one resembling a partridge,
one with uneven white feet, and one lacking the fixed whorls;

sanskrit_iast:
aśubhāvartasaṃyukto varjanīyasturaṅgamaḥ ..
.. rāma uvāca ..
vājinaḥ ke dhruvāvartāḥ keṣu sthāneṣu śobhanāḥ ..
vājinaḥ ke tadā śastāstanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ .. 6 ..
meaning:
अशुभावर्तसंयुक्तो वर्जनीयस्तुरङ्गमः ..
.. राम उवाच ..
वाजिनः के ध्रुवावर्ताः केषु स्थानेषु शोभनाः ..
वाजिनः के तदा शस्तास्तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः .. 6 ..
text_mt:
a horse endowed with inauspicious whorls is to be avoided.
Rāma said:
What are the fixed whorls of a horse? In what places are they auspicious?
Which horses are then commendable? Tell this to me as I ask.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca ..
randhroparandhrayordvaudvau dvaudvau mastakavakṣasoḥ ..
pramāṇe ca lalāṭe ca dhruvāvartā daśa smṛtaḥ .. 7 ..
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच ..
रन्ध्रोपरन्ध्रयोर्द्वौद्वौ द्वौद्वौ मस्तकवक्षसोः ..
प्रमाणे च ललाटे च ध्रुवावर्ता दश स्मृतः .. 7 ..
text_mt:
Puṣkara said:
Two each on the nostrils and upper nostrils, two each on the crown of the head and the chest,
[one each] on the measurement [spot between the eyes] and the forehead—ten fixed whorls are taught.

sanskrit_iast:
ekopi na bhavedyasya dhuvāvartastu vājinaḥ ..
na taṃ śaṃsanti dharmajña tasmāttaṃ parivarjayeta ..8..
meaning:
एकोपि न भवेद्यस्य धुवावर्तस्तु वाजिनः ..
न तं शंसन्ति धर्मज्ञ तस्मात्तं परिवर्जयेत ..8..
text_mt:
A horse that does not have even one of these fixed whorls
is not praised, O knower of dharma; therefore one should avoid it.

sanskrit_iast:
uttaroṣṭhe bhṛguśreṣṭha pramāṇasya tathopari ..
nāsāpuṭe tathā prothe gaṇḍaprothākṣimadhyagaḥ ..9 ..
meaning:
उत्तरोष्ठे भृगुश्रेष्ठ प्रमाणस्य तथोपरि ..
नासापुटे तथा प्रोथे गण्डप्रोथाक्षिमध्यगः ..9 ..
text_mt:
On the upper lip, O best of the Bhṛgus, and above the measurement [spot],
on the nostril, on the muzzle, between the cheek, muzzle, and eye,

sanskrit_iast:
kathayoraśrupātena bhruvoḥ kaṇṭhāgrayostathā ..
nābhyāṃ hanubalā kakṣāskandhopaskandhasandhiṣu .. 10 ..
meaning:
कथयोरश्रुपातेन भ्रुवोः कण्ठाग्रयोस्तथा ..
नाभ्यां हनुबला कक्षास्कन्धोपस्कन्धसन्धिषु .. 10 ..
text_mt:
at the tear-channels of both [eyes], on the brows, at the tips of the neck,
on the navel, jaw, armpits, and joints of the shoulder and upper shoulder,

sanskrit_iast:
vido bāhupradeśe ca galamadhye tathaiva ca ..
āsane kakude prothe jānujaṃghāsu bhārgava .. 11 ..
meaning:
विदो बाहुप्रदेशे च गलमध्ये तथैव च ..
आसने ककुदे प्रोथे जानुजंघासु भार्गव .. 11 ..
text_mt:
in the region of the arms, and in the middle of the throat,
on the seat, the hump, the muzzle, on the knees and shanks, O Bhārgava,

sanskrit_iast:
kuṣṭikānābhikakṣāsu muṣkayormūtradeśajaḥ ..
trike ca mūlapucche ca upari sthūṇayostathā .. 12 ..
meaning:
कुष्टिकानाभिकक्षासु मुष्कयोर्मूत्रदेशजः ..
त्रिके च मूलपुच्छे च उपरि स्थूणयोस्तथा .. 12 ..
text_mt:
on the pasterns, navel, and flanks, born on the testicles and urinary tract,
on the sacrum and the root of the tail, and above the two buttocks,

sanskrit_iast:
piṇḍayorjaṭhare caiva sīvanīyopakukṣiṣu ..
āvarttairvarjanīyāḥ syuḥ prayatnena turaṅgamāḥ .. 13 ..
meaning:
पिण्डयोर्जठरे चैव सीवनीयोपकुक्षिषु ..
आवर्त्तैर्वर्जनीयाः स्युः प्रयत्नेन तुरङ्गमाः .. 13 ..
text_mt:
on the calves and belly, and on the perineum and lower sides of the belly—
horses with curls [in these places] are to be avoided with care.

sanskrit_iast:
kakude karṇayoścaiva yasyāvartaḥ kuvājinaḥ ..
atyantamapraśastaṃ taṃ rājā rāṣṭrādvivāsayet .. 14 ..
meaning:
ककुदे कर्णयोश्चैव यस्यावर्तः कुवाजिनः ..
अत्यन्तमप्रशस्तं तं राजा राष्ट्राद्विवासयेत् .. 14 ..
text_mt:
A bad horse that has a curl on the hump and ears,
being exceedingly inauspicious, the king should banish from the realm.

sanskrit_iast:
hastidevamaṇiḥ sarvaṃ pūrvakāyeṣu lakṣaṇaḥ ..
suvyakto rocamāno vā na tu kākudinaṃ kvacita..15..
meaning:
हस्तिदेवमणिः सर्वं पूर्वकायेषु लक्षणः ..
सुव्यक्तो रोचमानो वा न तु काकुदिनं क्वचित..15..
text_mt:
A hastidevamaṇi curl is a good mark anywhere on the forebody,
whether very distinct or shining, but never one having a kākuda curl.

sanskrit_iast:
mekhalā vāpyadhaḥkāyāddhanyādāvartasambhavam ..
doṣānsarvāṃsturaṅgasya na hanyātkākasādinam .. 16 ..
meaning:
मेखला वाप्यधःकायाद्धन्यादावर्तसम्भवम् ..
दोषान्सर्वांस्तुरङ्गस्य न हन्यात्काकसादिनम् .. 16 ..
text_mt:
Or a girdle [curl] destroys what arises from the lower body;
all faults of a horse it destroys, but it does not destroy [the fault of] one on whom a crow perches.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi śubhamāvartalakṣaṇam ..
sṛkkiṇyośca lalāṭe ca tathā śravaṇamūlayoḥ .. 17 ..
meaning:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि शुभमावर्तलक्षणम् ..
सृक्किण्योश्च ललाटे च तथा श्रवणमूलयोः .. 17 ..
text_mt:
Hereafter I shall speak of the auspicious marks of whorls:
at the corners of the mouth and on the forehead, and at the bases of the ears,

sanskrit_iast:
nigāle ca tathā kaṇṭhe stutakeśāntayostathā ..
bāhumūle tathā śastā romajātāsturaṅgamāḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
निगाले च तथा कण्ठे स्तुतकेशान्तयोस्तथा ..
बाहुमूले तथा शस्ता रोमजातास्तुरङ्गमाः .. 18 ..
text_mt:
on the throat and on the neck, at the edges of the hair on the head,
and at the base of the arms, the hair-whorls born on horses are commendable.

sanskrit_iast:
āvartastu nigālastho jñeyo devamaṇiḥ śubhaḥ ..
kaṇṭhajo rocamānaśca sarvāvartto janādhipaḥ .. 19 ..
meaning:
आवर्तस्तु निगालस्थो ज्ञेयो देवमणिः शुभः ..
कण्ठजो रोचमानश्च सर्वावर्त्तो जनाधिपः .. 19 ..
text_mt:
A whorl situated on the gullet is to be known as an auspicious devamaṇi;
that born on the neck is a rocamāna; one having all whorls is a lord of men.

sanskrit_iast:
arkendragopacandrābhā ye ca vāyasa sannibhāḥ ..
suvarṇavarṇāḥ snigdhāśca praśasyante sadaiva te .. 20 ..
meaning:
अर्केन्द्रगोपचन्द्राभा ये च वायस सन्निभाः ..
सुवर्णवर्णाः स्निग्धाश्च प्रशस्यन्ते सदैव ते .. 20 ..
text_mt:
Those having the lustre of the sun, the indragopa beetle, or the moon, or resembling a crow,
golden-colored and glossy, are always commended.

sanskrit_iast:
dīrghagrīvākṣakūṭāśca hrasvavarṇāśca ye tathā ..
hrasvaprothāśca śasyante meghaughasadṛśa svanāḥ ..
pṛthūrupādajavanā mukhapuṇḍrāśca vai hayāḥ ..21 ..
meaning:
दीर्घग्रीवाक्षकूटाश्च ह्रस्ववर्णाश्च ये तथा ..
ह्रस्वप्रोथाश्च शस्यन्ते मेघौघसदृश स्वनाः ..
पृथूरुपादजवना मुखपुण्ड्राश्च वै हयाः ..21 ..
text_mt:
Those with long necks and eye-sockets, short-haired,
and short-muzzled are commended, possessing voices like the rumble of clouds,
having broad thighs, feet, and loins, and white marks on the face.

sanskrit_iast:
candrāṃśuśuklāsturagāḥ praśastāḥ karṇāntakeśairgavalālivarṇaiḥ ..
ye raktavarṇāśca samagrapādaiḥ śuklāśca varṇaiśca mahānubhāvāḥ .. 22 ..

puṣkara uvāca ..
camarībālasambhūtāḥ śaśāṅkāṃśusamaprabhāḥ ..
saṃhatāḥ snigdhadīrghāśca tathā sthālinibandhanāḥ .. 1 ..
daṇḍaśca cāmare kāryo rukmarūpyamayastathā ..
pravālavaiḍūryamayastathaiva kanakānvitaḥ ..2..

ardhahastānna cāpyūno madhyardhānna tathādhikaḥ .. 4 ..
kartavyaṃ cāmaraṃ rājñā na ca bhārgava rañjitama ..5..
āpītavarṇaṃ tu bhavetpraśastaṃ sāṃvatsarāmātyapurohitānām ..
narendrapatnīyuvarājasainyasyālasya śeṣasya janasya kṛṣṇaḥ .. 6..
meaning:
चन्द्रांशुशुक्लास्तुरगाः प्रशस्ताः कर्णान्तकेशैर्गवलालिवर्णैः ..
ये रक्तवर्णाश्च समग्रपादैः शुक्लाश्च वर्णैश्च महानुभावाः .. 22 ..
2.12
पुष्कर उवाच ..
चमरीबालसम्भूताः शशाङ्कांशुसमप्रभाः ..
संहताः स्निग्धदीर्घाश्च तथा स्थालिनिबन्धनाः .. 1 ..
दण्डश्च चामरे कार्यो रुक्मरूप्यमयस्तथा ..
प्रवालवैडूर्यमयस्तथैव कनकान्वितः ..2..
क्षीरवृक्षस्य वा कार्यो रुक्मरूप्यनिबन्धनः ..
रत्नैः प्रशस्तैश्चित्रो वा काञ्चनस्य प्रशस्यते .. 3 ..
चन्दनस्याथ दन्तस्य शार्ङ्गः कार्यो यथा भवेत ..
अर्धहस्तान्न चाप्यूनो मध्यर्धान्न तथाधिकः .. 4 ..
कर्तव्यं चामरं राज्ञा न च भार्गव रञ्जितम ..5..

नरेन्द्रपत्नीयुवराजसैन्यस्यालस्य शेषस्य जनस्य कृष्णः .. 6..
text_mt:
Horses white as rays of the moon, with hair at the ear-tips the color of buffaloes or bees,
those red-colored with all their feet white, and of noble appearance, are commendable.
2.12
Puṣkara said:
Produced from the hair of a yak tail, with splendor like the rays of the moon,
dense, glossy, and long, and fastened in a socket,
the handle on a fly-whisk should be made of gold or silver,
or of coral and lapis lazuli, endowed with gold.
Or it should be made of a milky tree, bound with gold and silver,
or adorned with commendable jewels; one of gold is praised.
Or of sandalwood, ivory, or horn it should be made as suitable;
not less than half a cubit, and not more than one and a half cubits.
A fly-whisk should be made for a king, and it should not be dyed, O Bhārgava.
One of a yellowish color is commendable for astrologers, ministers, and domestic priests;
for the king's wife, crown prince, and general, [a white one]; for the rest of the people, a black one is [used].

mitrapakṣaṃ na kartavyaṃ hīnaṃ parimitaṃ tathā ..
caturasraṃ tu kartavyaṃ brāhmaṇasya bhṛgūttama.. 2 ..

sitaṃ dūkūlasaṃchannaṃ patākābhirvibhūṣitam .. 3 ..
etasmindigvibhāge tu kāryāścandrāṃśunirmalāḥ ..
catasrastasya dharmajña patākā rukmabhūṣitāḥ ..4..
daṇḍaṃ cāmaravatkāryaṃ vaiṇavaṃ ca praśasyate..
tricatuḥpañcaṣaḍsaptacāṣṭaparvaḥ praśasyate .. 5 ..
daśadvādaśabhirvāpi śeṣaistu parivarjayet ..
chatraṃ daṇḍograparvāṇaṃ daṇḍaḥ sarvatra śasyate .. 6 ..
dhārayanti ca daṇḍaṃ vai vaiṇavaṃ gṛhamedhinaḥ ..
rājñāṃ praśastaṃ ṣaḍḍhastaṃ chatradaṇḍaṃ bhṛgūttama .. 7..
meaning:
2.13
पुष्कर उवाच ..
हंसपक्षैर्विरचितं मयूरस्य शुकस्य च ..
पक्षैरथ बलच्छाया च्छत्रं राज्ञः प्रशस्यते .. 1 ..
मित्रपक्षं न कर्तव्यं हीनं परिमितं तथा ..
चतुरस्रं तु कर्तव्यं ब्राह्मणस्य भृगूत्तम.. 2 ..
वृत्तं राज्ञां प्रशस्तं स्याच्छुक्लवस्त्रविभूषितम् ..
सितं दूकूलसंछन्नं पताकाभिर्विभूषितम् .. 3 ..
एतस्मिन्दिग्विभागे तु कार्याश्चन्द्रांशुनिर्मलाः ..
चतस्रस्तस्य धर्मज्ञ पताका रुक्मभूषिताः ..4..
दण्डं चामरवत्कार्यं वैणवं च प्रशस्यते..
त्रिचतुःपञ्चषड्सप्तचाष्टपर्वः प्रशस्यते .. 5 ..
दशद्वादशभिर्वापि शेषैस्तु परिवर्जयेत् ..
छत्रं दण्डोग्रपर्वाणं दण्डः सर्वत्र शस्यते .. 6 ..
धारयन्ति च दण्डं वै वैणवं गृहमेधिनः ..
राज्ञां प्रशस्तं षड्ढस्तं छत्रदण्डं भृगूत्तम .. 7..
text_mt:
2.13
Puṣkara said:
An umbrella for a king is praised when fashioned from the feathers of a swan, of a peacock, / and of a parrot, affording strong shade.
It should not be made of [mere] friendly feathers, nor deficient, nor undersized; / but for a brahmin, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, it should be made square.
For kings it is praised as circular, adorned with white cloth, / white, covered with fine silk, and adorned with banners.
In its divisions of the directions, spotless as moonbeams, / four banners adorned with gold should be placed upon it, O knower of dharma.
The staff should be made like that of a fly-whisk, and one made of bamboo is praised; / one with three, four, five, six, seven, or eight joints is praised,
or with ten or twelve; but one should avoid the rest. / An umbrella whose staff has sharp joints [should be avoided]; a staff [properly jointed] is everywhere praised.
Householders indeed carry a bamboo staff. / For kings, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, an umbrella staff of six cubits is praised.

विभूषितं रश्मियुतं प्रशस्तं सदातपत्रं तु महीपतीनाम् .. 11 ..
2.14

भद्रासनं नरेन्द्रस्य क्षीरवृक्षेण कारयेत् ..
उच्छ्रायश्च तथा तस्य अध्यर्धं तु समं भवेत् .. 1 ..

text_mt:
Moreover, one of five cubits less a span is for the queen and the heir-apparent. / By generals, overseers of deities, astrologers, and family priests,
an umbrella staff of five cubits should be made, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / while for those who have not been mentioned here by me, it should be made four cubits.
The diameter of the umbrella is always praised as measuring half the staff. / One should adorn the umbrella of kings with crescents and suns.
Adorned with diamonds, sapphires, crystals, O Rāma, cat's-eyes, pearls, and fine corals, / furnished with rays, an umbrella is ever praised for lords of the earth.
2.14
Puṣkara said:
A throne for a lord of men should be made from a milk-yielding tree; / and its height should be equal to one and a half [cubits].
One should make it three cubits across in breadth, / and its length should be made equal to half the breadth.
The auspicious throne of a king should be made square; / it should not be octagonal, nor round, nor oblong, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.

text_mt:
palu, coral, mountain-diamond, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / the gem of the serpent king, and auspicious thunderbolt-gem;
ṭīṭibha, tāpiccha, bhrāmara, and utpala— / all these gems are to be worn by a ruler of the earth,
set in gold, for victory, health, and prosperity. / Their heaviness, color, clarity, possession of a garland of rays,
good pedigree, smoothness, and fine shape— / [gems] endowed with qualities are prescribed; those possessing these qualities are to be worn.
Those that are fractured, gritty, lusterless, and stained / are not to be worn by lords of men desiring victory, royal fortune, and life.
Even among the entire category of gems, the wearing of diamond is preferred: / that diamond which floats on water, is unbreakable and spotless,
and pure, hexagonal, and light, O joy of the Bhṛgus, / whose radiance resembles Indra's rainbow when facing the sun—

text_mt:
wearing that diamond, a king conquers all his enemies. / Resembling the bright fortnight, smooth, lustrous, and spotless,
endowed with minute specks resembling gold powder, / deep and elevated, an emerald is praised, O Rāma,
and is to be worn by lords of the earth, destroying all afflictions. / Origin may be from kuruvinda, and likewise from saugandhika, O twice-born,
[or] from crystal: of rubies, these are superior in ascending order. / Those that are born of kuruvinda have a bright red color here;
those born of saugandhika are designated as having an astringent [brownish-red] color; / and those born of crystal are to be known as clear and richly colored.
Many pearls arise from oysters, and many are produced from fish; / but those produced from conch-shells, O twice-born, are not as excellent as they.
Those produced from the frontal lobes of elephants are to be known as superior to them; / they are stated to be lusterless. Those produced from boars, O twice-born, are superior.

सुष्ठुता च सुशुक्लत्वं महत्त्वं च भृगूत्तम ..
इन्द्रनीलस्तु यः क्षीरं राजते भाजने स्थितम्.. 21 ..
रञ्जयेत्स्वप्रभावेन तममूल्यं विनिर्दिशेत् ..
नीलरक्तं तु वैडूर्यं सर्वतः श्रेष्ठमुच्यते .. 22 ..
text_mt:
Superior to them are those from bamboo stalks; superior to them, those produced from serpents; / and even beyond them, hard to obtain on earth, is the pearl produced from clouds.
By wearing it, all success is proclaimed for a king. / Roundness is said to be a virtue of all pearls,
as well as excellence, bright whiteness, and largeness, O foremost of the Bhṛgus. / As for a sapphire, which, placed in a vessel of milk,
colors it with its own radiance—one should designate that as priceless. / A cat's-eye that is blue and red is said to be the best of all.

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣāmeva ratnānāṃ dhāryaṃ karketanaṃ smṛtam ..
puṣparāgāstathā rāma ye cānye kīrtitā mayā .. 23 ..
meaning:
सर्वेषामेव रत्नानां धार्यं कर्केतनं स्मृतम् ..
पुष्परागास्तथा राम ये चान्ये कीर्तिता मया .. 23 ..
text_mt: Among all gems, the karketana is taught to be worn, / as well as topazes, O Rāma, and whatever others have been mentioned by me.

sanskrit_iast:
praśastaratnairbhūpānāṃ mukuṭānyaṅgadāni ca ..
hārāṇi rāma kāryāṇi keyūrābharaṇāni ca .. 24 ..
meaning:
प्रशस्तरत्नैर्भूपानां मुकुटान्यङ्गदानि च ..
हाराणि राम कार्याणि केयूराभरणानि च .. 24 ..
text_mt: With auspicious jewels, kings' crowns and armlets, / necklaces, O Rāma, and upper armbands should be made.

sanskrit_iast:
apraśastāni ratnāni varjanīyāni dūrataḥ ..
sarvaratnottamaṃ rājā vivarṇaṃ malinaṃ tathā .. 25 ..
meaning:
अप्रशस्तानि रत्नानि वर्जनीयानि दूरतः ..
सर्वरत्नोत्तमं राजा विवर्णं मलिनं तथा .. 25 ..
text_mt: Inauspicious gems are to be avoided from afar. / Even the best of all jewels, if discolored or dirty,

sanskrit_iast:
na dhārayeta dharmajñaḥ suśuddhaṃ dhārayetsadā ..
dhṛtiḥ praśastā bhṛguvaṃśacandra ratnottamānāṃ satataṃ nṛpāṇām ..
ratnāṃśudagdhaṃ tu narasya dehādanarthamāśu praśamaṃ prayāti .. 26 ..
meaning:
न धारयेत धर्मज्ञः सुशुद्धं धारयेत्सदा ..
धृतिः प्रशस्ता भृगुवंशचन्द्र रत्नोत्तमानां सततं नृपाणाम् ..
रत्नांशुदग्धं तु नरस्य देहादनर्थमाशु प्रशमं प्रयाति .. 26 ..
text_mt: the knower of dharma must not wear; he should always wear what is purely clean. / Constant wearing of excellent gems by kings is praised, O moon of the Bhṛgu lineage; / consumed by the rays of jewels, misfortune swiftly subsides from a man's body.

sanskrit_iast:
2.16
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
dhanurdravyatrayaṃ lohaṃ śṛṅgaṃ cāru ca bhārgava ..
jyādravyatritayaṃ carma vaṃśabhaṃgaṃ tvacastathā .. 1 ..
meaning:
2.16
.. पुष्कर उवाच .. ..
धनुर्द्रव्यत्रयं लोहं शृङ्गं चारु च भार्गव ..
ज्याद्रव्यत्रितयं चर्म वंशभंगं त्वचस्तथा .. 1 ..
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / The threefold material for a bow is metal, horn, and wood, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / The threefold material for a bowstring is hide, split bamboo, and bark.
title: Cāpaśaralakṣaṇam

sanskrit_iast:
vaṃśatvagvaṃśacāpaṃ tu kartavyaṃ bhṛgunandana ..
anyeṣu rāma cāpeṣu śeṣadravyamidaṃ bhaveta .. 2 ..
meaning:
वंशत्वग्वंशचापं तु कर्तव्यं भृगुनन्दन ..
अन्येषु राम चापेषु शेषद्रव्यमिदं भवेत .. 2 ..
text_mt: A bow of bamboo should be made from bamboo bark, O son of Bhṛgu; / for other bows, O Rāma, these remaining materials are used.

sanskrit_iast:
pramāṇaṃ nātra nirdiṣṭaṃ cāpayoḥ śārṅgalohayoḥ ..
dārucāpapramāṇaṃ tu śreṣṭhaṃ hastacatuṣṭayam .. 3 ..
meaning:
प्रमाणं नात्र निर्दिष्टं चापयोः शार्ङ्गलोहयोः ..
दारुचापप्रमाणं तु श्रेष्ठं हस्तचतुष्टयम् .. 3 ..
text_mt: No fixed measure is prescribed here for bows of horn and metal; / but for a wooden bow, the best measure is four cubits.

sanskrit_iast:
tadardhasamahīne tu prokte madhyakanīyasī ..
muṣṭigrāhyāṇi vṛttāni madhye sarvāṇi kārayet .. 4 ..
meaning:
तदर्धसमहीने तु प्रोक्ते मध्यकनीयसी ..
मुष्टिग्राह्याणि वृत्तानि मध्ये सर्वाणि कारयेत् .. 4 ..
text_mt: Shorter by half that and by a quarter are declared the middling and shortest [bows]. / All should be made round at the center where grasped by the hand.

sanskrit_iast:
svalpā koṭistu vārkṣāṇāṃ śārṅgalauhamayī dvija ..
kāminībhrūlatākārā koṭiḥ kāryā susaṃskṛtā ..5..
meaning:
स्वल्पा कोटिस्तु वार्क्षाणां शार्ङ्गलौहमयी द्विज ..
कामिनीभ्रूलताकारा कोटिः कार्या सुसंस्कृता ..5..
text_mt: The bow-tip of wooden bows is small, or it may be of horn or metal, O twice-born; / shaped like the creeper-like eyebrow of a lovely woman, the tip should be well finished.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthagvā dārumiśro vā lohaśārṅge tu kārayet ..
śārṅgaṃ snāyucitaṃ kāryaṃ rukmabinduvibhūṣitam .. 6 ..
meaning:
पृथग्वा दारुमिश्रो वा लोहशार्ङ्गे तु कारयेत् ..
शार्ङ्गं स्नायुचितं कार्यं रुक्मबिन्दुविभूषितम् .. 6 ..
text_mt: One may make [the bow] of metal and horn separately or mixed with wood. / A horn bow should be wrapped with sinew and adorned with gold dots.

sanskrit_iast:
kuṭilasphuṭitaṃ cāpaṃ sacchidraṃ ca na śasyate ..
hastibhagnā drumā ye ca vidyuddagdhāstathā ca ye .. 7 ..
meaning:
कुटिलस्फुटितं चापं सच्छिद्रं च न शस्यते ..
हस्तिभग्ना द्रुमा ये च विद्युद्दग्धास्तथा च ये .. 7 ..
text_mt: A bow that is crooked, cracked, or full of holes is not praised. / Trees broken by elephants, or scorched by lightning,

sanskrit_iast:
ārāmadevatāveśmatāpasāśramasaṃbhavāḥ ..
śmaśānasaṃbhavā ye ca na te kāryāḥ kathaṃcana .. 8 ..
meaning:
आरामदेवतावेश्मतापसाश्रमसंभवाः ..
श्मशानसंभवा ये च न ते कार्याः कथंचन .. 8 ..
text_mt: growing in pleasure gardens, shrines of gods, or hermitages of ascetics, / or those growing in cremation grounds, must never be used.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇināṃ yaḥ sajātyena śṛṅgī yudhi nipātitaḥ ..
tacchṛṅgaṃ varjayeccāpaṃ nityaṃ śārṅge vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 9 ..
meaning:
प्राणिनां यः सजात्येन शृङ्गी युधि निपातितः ..
तच्छृङ्गं वर्जयेच्चापं नित्यं शार्ङ्गे विचक्षणः .. 9 ..
text_mt: If a horned animal was struck down in combat by one of its own kind, / an expert should always avoid that horn for a horn bow.

sanskrit_iast:
lohāni rāma catvāri śasyante cāpakarmaṇi ..
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ tathā kṛṣṇāyasaṃ dvija .. 10 ..
meaning:
लोहानि राम चत्वारि शस्यन्ते चापकर्मणि ..
सुवर्णं रजतं ताम्रं तथा कृष्णायसं द्विज .. 10 ..
text_mt: Four metals, O Rāma, are praised in the making of bows: / gold, silver, copper, and black iron, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
kāñcanaṃ cāparatnaṃ tu saratnamapi kārayet ..
māhiṣaṃ śārabhaṃ śārṅgaṃ rauhījaṃ cāpi kārayet .. 11 ..
meaning:
काञ्चनं चापरत्नं तु सरत्नमपि कारयेत् ..
माहिषं शारभं शार्ङ्गं रौहीजं चापि कारयेत् .. 11 ..
text_mt: One may also make an excellent golden bow set with jewels. / A horn bow may be made from the horn of a buffalo, a śarabha, or a rohi deer.

sanskrit_iast:
vārkṣaṃ candanajaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vaitasaṃ dhānvataṃ tathā ..
sālaśālmalikāśānāṃ kakubhasyāñjanasya ca .. 12 ..
meaning:
वार्क्षं चन्दनजं श्रेष्ठं वैतसं धान्वतं तथा ..
सालशाल्मलिकाशानां ककुभस्याञ्जनस्य च .. 12 ..
text_mt: Among wooden bows, that made of sandalwood, cane, or dhānvana is best; / or of sāl, śālmali, kāśa, kakubha, and añjana,

sanskrit_iast:
vaṃśasya ca mahābhāga sarvaśreṣṭhatamaṃ viduḥ ..
śaradgṛhītaiḥ kāṣṭhaistu cāpaṃ kāryaṃ prayatnataḥ .. 13 ..
meaning:
वंशस्य च महाभाग सर्वश्रेष्ठतमं विदुः ..
शरद्गृहीतैः काष्ठैस्तु चापं कार्यं प्रयत्नतः .. 13 ..
text_mt: and of bamboo, O fortunate one, which is known as the best of all. / Bows should be carefully made from wood harvested in autumn.

sanskrit_iast:
vaṃśānāmapi tacchreṣṭhaṃ yatra gaṅgā mahānadī ..
sālānāmapi tacchreṣṭhaṃ gomatī yatra bhārgava .. 14 ..
meaning:
वंशानामपि तच्छ्रेष्ठं यत्र गङ्गा महानदी ..
सालानामपि तच्छ्रेष्ठं गोमती यत्र भार्गव .. 14 ..
text_mt: Even among bamboos, that is best which grows where the great river Gaṅgā is; / among sāl trees, that is best where the Gomatī is, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast:
vitastākūlajaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vetasīnāṃ tathaiva va ..
evaṃ dravyamayaṃ kāryaṃ cāpaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyutam ..15..
meaning:
वितस्ताकूलजं श्रेष्ठं वेतसीनां तथैव व ..
एवं द्रव्यमयं कार्यं चापं लक्षणसंयुतम् ..15..
text_mt: Cane growing on the banks of the Vitastā is likewise best. / Thus made of [proper] material, a bow should possess the auspicious marks.

sanskrit_iast:
grahaṇa lakṣaṇaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati ca khaḍgavat ..
sukhagrāhaṃ dṛṣṭikāntaṃ śaramokṣamukhaṃ tathā .. 16 ..
meaning:
ग्रहण लक्षणं चास्य भविष्यति च खड्गवत् ..
सुखग्राहं दृष्टिकान्तं शरमोक्षमुखं तथा .. 16 ..
text_mt: Its characteristic for holding will be like that of a sword: / easy to hold, pleasing to the eye, and suited for discharging arrows,

sanskrit_iast:
ślakṣṇaṃ śliṣṭaṃ susaṃsthānaṃ sāravantaṃ susaṃhatam ..
avanāmasukhaṃ nityaṃ puṃnāmanavalotkaṭam ..17..
meaning:
श्लक्ष्णं श्लिष्टं सुसंस्थानं सारवन्तं सुसंहतम् ..
अवनामसुखं नित्यं पुंनामनवलोत्कटम् ..17..
text_mt: smooth, well-joined, well-proportioned, solid, firm, / always easy to bend, bearing a masculine name, and not excessively heavy.

sanskrit_iast:
etadīdṛśakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ cāparatnaṃ vidurbudhāḥ ..
rājñā cāpasya kartavyā pūjā bāṇavarasya ca .. 18 ..
meaning:
एतदीदृशकं श्रेष्ठं चापरत्नं विदुर्बुधाः ..
राज्ञा चापस्य कर्तव्या पूजा बाणवरस्य च .. 18 ..
text_mt: Such a bow the wise know as a jewel among bows. / A king should perform worship of the bow and the excellent arrow,

sanskrit_iast:
nityaṃ devakule rāma khaḍgasya ca viśeṣataḥ ..
ayasaścātha vaṃśasya śarasyātha śaro bhavet .. 19 ..
meaning:
नित्यं देवकुले राम खड्गस्य च विशेषतः ..
अयसश्चाथ वंशस्य शरस्याथ शरो भवेत् .. 19 ..
text_mt: always in a shrine, O Rāma, and especially of the sword. / An arrow may be of iron, of reed, or of bamboo.

sanskrit_iast:
śaravaṃśau grahītavyau śaratkāle bhṛgūttama ..
śarāḥ kirātajāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ kāñcīpurasamīpataḥ .. 20 ..
meaning:
शरवंशौ ग्रहीतव्यौ शरत्काले भृगूत्तम ..
शराः किरातजाः श्रेष्ठाः काञ्चीपुरसमीपतः .. 20 ..
text_mt: Reeds and bamboos should be gathered in the autumn, O foremost of the Bhṛgus. / Arrows originating among the Kirātas near Kāñcīpura are excellent;

sanskrit_iast:
tebhyo'pi te śreṣṭhatamāḥ skandajanmamahībhavāḥ ..
snigdhā nimagnaparvāṇaḥ sāravantaḥ samāhitāḥ .. 21 ..
meaning:
तेभ्योऽपि ते श्रेष्ठतमाः स्कन्दजन्ममहीभवाः ..
स्निग्धा निमग्नपर्वाणः सारवन्तः समाहिताः .. 21 ..
text_mt: even better than those are arrows born in the land of Skanda's birth: / smooth, with flush joints, strong, straight,

sanskrit_iast:
ṛjavo madhuvarṇābhāḥ sujātāḥ śāradā dṛḍhāḥ ..
snāyuśliṣṭāḥ sunetrāśca supuṅkhāḥ kalavāsasaḥ .. 22 ..
meaning:
ऋजवो मधुवर्णाभाः सुजाताः शारदा दृढाः ..
स्नायुश्लिष्टाः सुनेत्राश्च सुपुङ्खाः कलवाससः .. 22 ..
text_mt: well-aligned, honey-colored, well-formed, autumnal, sturdy, / bound with sinew, with good notches, good feathers, and pleasing fletching.

sanskrit_iast:
tailadhautāśca kartavyā rukmapuṅkhavibhūṣaṇāḥ ..
tathā viṣamaparvāṇaḥ phalaiśca vraṇavarjitaiḥ .. 23 ..
meaning:
तैलधौताश्च कर्तव्या रुक्मपुङ्खविभूषणाः ..
तथा विषमपर्वाणः फलैश्च व्रणवर्जितैः .. 23 ..
text_mt: They should be washed with oil, adorned with gold fletchings, / with uneven knots, and with arrowheads free of flaws.

sanskrit_iast:
eka tripuṅkhaṃ kartavyaṃ rājahaṃsacchadottaram ..
rukmapuṅkhasuvarṇāgramayaḥphalamanuttamam ..24..
meaning:
एक त्रिपुङ्खं कर्तव्यं राजहंसच्छदोत्तरम् ..
रुक्मपुङ्खसुवर्णाग्रमयःफलमनुत्तमम् ..24..
text_mt: One should make [an arrow] with one or three fletchings, covered with feathers of wild geese, / with a gold nock, a gold tip, and an unsurpassed iron arrowhead.

sanskrit_iast:
snāyubaddhaṃ balaṃ tasya rukmabandhaṃ tu kārayet ..
vajraiśca lakṣaṇopetaiścitritaṃ taṃ tu kārayet..25..
meaning:
स्नायुबद्धं बलं तस्य रुक्मबन्धं तु कारयेत् ..
वज्रैश्च लक्षणोपेतैश्चित्रितं तं तु कारयेत्..25..
text_mt: Its strength should be secured with sinew, and bound with gold; / one should also decorate it with diamonds bearing auspicious marks.

sanskrit_iast:
grahaṇaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ sāṃvatsarakarānnṛpaiḥ ..
tasya pūjā sadā kāryā sābhiṣekasamā bhavet .. 26 ..
meaning:
ग्रहणं तस्य कर्तव्यं सांवत्सरकरान्नृपैः ..
तस्य पूजा सदा कार्या साभिषेकसमा भवेत् .. 26 ..
text_mt: It should be received by kings from the hand of an astrologer; / it should always be worshipped, equal to an royal consecration.

sanskrit_iast:
yātrāyāmabhiṣeke ca maṅgaleṣu ca karmasu ..
sapatāke tu taṃ cāpaṃ sapatākaṃ tu kārayet ..
maṅgalyaṃ tannarendrāṇāṃ kathitaṃ bhṛgunandana .. 27 ..
meaning:
यात्रायामभिषेके च मङ्गलेषु च कर्मसु ..
सपताके तु तं चापं सपताकं तु कारयेत् ..
मङ्गल्यं तन्नरेन्द्राणां कथितं भृगुनन्दन .. 27 ..
text_mt: On military expeditions, at consecrations, and during auspicious rites, / one should provide that bow with a banner; / it is declared to bring auspiciousness to kings, O son of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast:
ye cāparatnaṃ vinataṃ tu bhūpāḥ suvarṇaratnopacitaṃ sadaiva ..
bāṇena sākaṃ paripūjayanti bhavanti te rāma vipannaduḥkhāḥ .. 28 ..
2.17
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
purā sumeruśikhare kāñcane ratnaparvate ..
svargaṅgāyāstaṭe brahmā yajñaṃ yajati bhārgava .. 1 ..
tasminyajñe sa dadṛśe vighnaṃ khe lohadānavam ..
vighnasya śamanaṃ tasya cintayāmāsa tattvavit .. 2 ..
tadā cintayatastasya puruṣaḥ pāvakādbabhau ..
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaḥ svarucā vañcitekṣaṇaḥ .. 3..
prāṃśuḥ suvadanaḥ śrīmānbalenāpratimo bhuvi ..
sa vavande tadā gatvā devaṃ kamalasambhavam .. 4 ..
abhyanandanta jātena tena devāssavāsavāḥ ..
tasmātsa nandako nāma khaṅgaratnamabhūttadā .. 5 ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavānbrahmā keśavaṃ vākyamabravīt ..
khaḍgaṃ gṛhṇīṣva goptāraṃ dharmasya jagatāṃ pate .. 6 ..
meaning:
ये चापरत्नं विनतं तु भूपाः सुवर्णरत्नोपचितं सदैव ..
बाणेन साकं परिपूजयन्ति भवन्ति ते राम विपन्नदुःखाः .. 28 ..
2.17
.. पुष्कर उवाच ..
पुरा सुमेरुशिखरे काञ्चने रत्नपर्वते ..
स्वर्गङ्गायास्तटे ब्रह्मा यज्ञं यजति भार्गव .. 1 ..
तस्मिन्यज्ञे स ददृशे विघ्नं खे लोहदानवम् ..
विघ्नस्य शमनं तस्य चिन्तयामास तत्त्ववित् .. 2 ..

Those kings who always worship a bent jewel of a bow, / adorned with gold and jewels, together with an arrow, have their misfortunes destroyed, O Rāma.
Puṣkara said: / Formerly, on the golden peak of Sumeru, the mountain of jewels, / on the bank of the heavenly Gaṅgā, Brahmā was performing a sacrifice, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
At that sacrifice, he saw an obstacle in the sky: the iron demon Lohadānava. / The knower of truth meditated on the pacification of that obstacle.
As he was meditating then, a person appeared from the fire, / dark as a blue lotus petal, blinding the eye with his radiance,
tall, handsome-faced, splendid, peerless in strength on earth. / Going forward then, he bowed to the lotus-born god.
The gods together with Indra rejoiced at his birth; / therefore, named Nandaka, he then became the jewel among swords.
Seeing him, the blessed Brahmā spoke these words to Keśava: / 'Take this sword, the protector of dharma, O Lord of the worlds!

Slaying the causer of obstacles to the sacrifice with this sword, O Keśava, / strike down the mighty Lohadānava, O mighty-armed one!'
Addressed in this manner, Janārdana seized him by the neck; / as soon as he was taken by the god, he became unsheathed.
The sword, O Rāma, had eyes like lotus petals, a brilliance equal to a blue water-lily, / a jewel-studded hilt, was large, and resembled the cloudless sky.
At that moment, there appeared then a huge, / terrifying [demon] with a black face, a hundred arms, and a vast belly,
tall, with well-rounded tips of his fangs, the mighty iron-demon. / Seeing that iron-demon arrived, intent on obstructing the sacrifice,
Keśava took the sword and rushed swiftly toward him. / Disregarding Keśava, he [attacked] the gods headed by Śakra,
and then routed them with a club of terrible speed. / Then, when the gods were broken, Hari fought for a long time,
and in battle the slayer of Madhu severed his limbs with the sword. / The limbs severed by the sword [fell] upon the earth in various regions;

2.18
Puṣkara said:
Thus, when the provisions have been gathered, the king’s astrologer / should perform the consecration at the proper time; I shall declare that time to you.
When a king dies, no restriction of time is prescribed in this matter. / In that situation, his bathing should be performed according to rule with sesame seeds and mustard seeds.
Having proclaimed his victory, the astrologer and the royal chaplain / should gently present him, seated on another seat, to the people.
Having consoled his own people, fed those who were in prison, / and proclaimed freedom from fear, he should await the [proper] time.
A king should not be consecrated in the month of Caitra, nor in an intercalary month, O Bhārgava, / nor while Viṣṇu is asleep, especially in the rainy season, O twice-born;
nor on Tuesday, O Rāma, and likewise not on the fourth [tithi]; / he should not be consecrated on the ninth, nor on the fourteenth, O Bhārgava.

text_mt:
The fixed constellations, the constellation of Viṣṇu, that of Śakra, and Hasta and Puṣya / are commended for the consecration of a ruler of the earth.
Nāga, Catuṣpada, Viṣṭi, Kiṃstughna, and Śakuni— / these karaṇas are not commended, nor is a day of Vyatīpāta;
nor a constellation struck by a meteor or struck by an unnatural portent, / or one occupied by Saturn, the Sun, or Mars, or surrounded by a halo, O Bhārgava.
The muhūrtas belonging to the spoken constellations grant respect and welfare to the virtuous; / the horā of Mars is not desired, nor is Kulika everywhere.
Taurus, Scorpio, Leo, and Aquarius are commended in the ascendant; / of these, whichever is situated in an upacaya house from the ascendant at birth [is favored].
The second, sixth, fourth, eighth, / and ninth asterisms are praised, and a favorable Moon.
Benefics in angles, in the ascendant, and benefics in the two trines, / and malefics in upacaya houses [are favorable]; the Sun in the ascendant is commended.

A navāṃśa of Mars in the ascendant is to be avoided, as is his division, O noble one; / the entire division of the Sun is commended, along with the planet, for the consecration of kings.
Puṣkara said:
The Purandarī pacification rite must first be performed by his domestic priest. / When the day of the royal consecration has arrived, the domestic priest, observing a fast,
wearing a turban, clad in white garments, adorned with white sandalwood paste, / with a white garland and sacred thread, and adorned with all ornaments,
having carefully marked out the altar and duly prepared it, / the wise [priest] should then offer [oblations with] Vaiṣṇava mantras and Śākra mantras,
with Sāvitra mantras, Vaiśvadeva mantras, and Saumya mantras according to rule, / and likewise with the Śarmavarman group and the Svastyayana group,
with the Āyuṣya, the Abhaya, and likewise the Aparājita hymns. / He should also make a golden water-jar that holds the drops of oblation.
Standing on the right side of the fire, adorned with white sandalwood paste, / with white unguents, garlanded, and adorned with all ornaments,

Others too should closely observe the true nature [of the signs] at the astrologer's word, O Narasiṃha: / the leading assembly members of the astrologer, and the leading assembly members of the domestic priest.
Puṣkara said:
A sacrificial fire whose flames curl clockwise, gleaming like refined gold, / roaring like a multitude of chariots, and free of smoke,
fragrant along the wind, resembling the svastika shape, / of the form of a vardhamāna, and likewise resembling a nandyāvarta,
with bright radiance, large flames, and free of sparks, is auspicious. / When the fire itself, the mouth of the gods, consumes the oblation
at the end of [the call of] 'svāhā', O highly fortunate one, then it will be auspicious for the king. / And when from the sacrificial fire there is no sizzling of the oblation,
and cats, deer, birds, and ants do not cross through the middle [of the area], / O knower of dharma, then the king will be victorious.
When the fire resembles a pearl necklace or a lotus stalk, victory belongs to kings; / likewise, one should declare victory when it gives a steady base [of flame].

2.22
Rāma said:
With which mantra, O knower of dharma, should one perform the king's consecration? / I wish to hear that from you, O son of Varuṇa.
Puṣkara said:
Listen attentively, O Rāma, to the sin-destroying mantra / by which a king, when consecrated, endures long in renown.
At the end of the word for the king's consecration, the astrologer should perform sprinkling / from the water-jar with kuśa grass and water; at the end of the mantra he should place everything.
"May the gods consecrate you: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara; / Vāsudeva, Lord of the Universe, and the all-pervading Saṃkarṣaṇa;
may Pradyumna and Aniruddha be for your victory; / may Ākhaṇḍala, the blessed Agni, Yama, and Nairṛta,
Varuṇa, Pavana, Dhanādhyakṣa, and Śiva, / and Śeṣa together with Brahmā, the guardians of the directions, protect you always.
