text_mt:
Krītin, Prasadṛkṣa, the far-famed Śarabha,
Dhātṛ, Ugra, Dhvani, Bhīma, Atiyukta, Kṣipa, Saha,

sanskrit_iast:
dyutirvapuranādhṛṣyo vāsaḥ kāmo jayo virāṭ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu marutaste samā gatāḥ .. 56 ..
meaning:
द्युतिर्वपुरनाधृष्यो वासः कामो जयो विराट् ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु मरुतस्ते समा गताः .. 56 ..
text_mt:
Dyuti, Vapus, Anādhṛṣya, Vāsa, Kāma, Jaya, and Virāṭ;
may those Maruts, having gathered together, consecrate you,

sanskrit_iast:
devā ekonapañcāśanmahābalaparākramāḥ ..
citrāṅgadaścitrarathaścitrasenaśca vīryavān .. 57 ..
meaning:
देवा एकोनपञ्चाशन्महाबलपराक्रमाः ..
चित्राङ्गदश्चित्ररथश्चित्रसेनश्च वीर्यवान् .. 57 ..
text_mt:
the forty-nine gods of great strength and valour;
Citrāṅgada, Citraratha, and the mighty Citrasena,

sanskrit_iast:
ūrṇāyuranaghaścaiva ugrasenaśca vīryavān ..
dhṛtarāṣṭraśca gopaśca sūryāvartastathaiva ca .. 58 ..
meaning:
ऊर्णायुरनघश्चैव उग्रसेनश्च वीर्यवान् ..
धृतराष्ट्रश्च गोपश्च सूर्यावर्तस्तथैव च .. 58 ..
text_mt:
Ūrṇāyu, Anagha, and the mighty Ugrasena,
Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gopa, and Sūryāvarta,

sanskrit_iast:
yugapastraṇayaḥ kārṣṇirnaṃdaścitrastathaiva ca ..
kaliḥ śāliḥ śirā rājanparjanyo nāradastathā .. 59 ..
meaning:
युगपस्त्रणयः कार्ष्णिर्नंदश्चित्रस्तथैव च ..
कलिः शालिः शिरा राजन्पर्जन्यो नारदस्तथा .. 59 ..
text_mt:
Yugapa, Straṇaya, Kārṣṇi, Nanda, Citra,
Kali, Śāli, Śiras, O king, Parjanya, and Nārada,

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣaparvā ca haṃsaśca tathā caiva hahā hūhūḥ ..
viśvāvasustumburuśca tathā ca suruciśca yaḥ .. 60 ..
meaning:
वृषपर्वा च हंसश्च तथा चैव हहा हूहूः ..
विश्वावसुस्तुम्बुरुश्च तथा च सुरुचिश्च यः .. 60 ..
text_mt:
Vṛṣaparvan, Haṃsa, Hahā, Hūhū,
Viśvāvasu, Tumburu, and Suruci;

sanskrit_iast:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu gandharvāḥ pṛthivīpate ..
āhutyastā bhavatyaśca vargavatyastathaiva ca .. 61 ..
meaning:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु गन्धर्वाः पृथिवीपते ..
आहुत्यस्ता भवत्यश्च वर्गवत्यस्तथैव च .. 61 ..
text_mt:
may these gandharvas consecrate you, O lord of the earth;
Āhutis, Bhavatīs, and Vargavatīs,

sanskrit_iast:
āyurvatyastathorjāśca tathā vai kuravāḥ stavāḥ ..
bahvāyuścāmṛtāyuśca bhuvaścaiva rucastathā .. 62 ..
meaning:
आयुर्वत्यस्तथोर्जाश्च तथा वै कुरवाः स्तवाः ..
बह्वायुश्चामृतायुश्च भुवश्चैव रुचस्तथा .. 62 ..
text_mt:
Āyurvatīs, Ūrjās, Kurus, Stavas,
Bahvāyu, Amṛtāyu, Bhuvas, and Rucas,

sanskrit_iast:
bhīravaḥ śobhayaṃtyaśca divyā yāścāpsarogaṇāḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu samāgatya mahīpate .. 63 ..
meaning:
भीरवः शोभयंत्यश्च दिव्या याश्चाप्सरोगणाः ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समागत्य महीपते .. 63 ..
text_mt:
Bhīrus, Śobhayantīs, and whichever are the celestial troops of apsarases;
may these consecrate you, having gathered together, O lord of the earth;

sanskrit_iast:
anavadyā satyakāmā cānūnā varuṇā priyā ..
anūpā subhagā caiva sukeśā ca manovatī .. 64 ..
meaning:
अनवद्या सत्यकामा चानूना वरुणा प्रिया ..
अनूपा सुभगा चैव सुकेशा च मनोवती .. 64 ..
text_mt:
Anavadyā, Satyakāmā, Anūnā, Varuṇā, Priyā,
Anūpā, Subhagā, Sukeśā, and Manovatī,

sanskrit_iast:
menakā sahajanyā ca parṇāśā puñjikasthalā ..
kṛtasthalā ghṛtācī ca viśvācī pūrvacityapi .. 65 ..
meaning:
मेनका सहजन्या च पर्णाशा पुञ्जिकस्थला ..
कृतस्थला घृताची च विश्वाची पूर्वचित्यपि .. 65 ..
text_mt:
Menakā, Sahajanyā, Parṇāśā, Puñjikasthalā,
Kṛtasthalā, Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī, and Pūrvacitti,

sanskrit_iast:
pramlocā cāpyanumlocā raṃbhā caivorvaśī tathā ..
pañcacūḍā sānumatī citralekhā ca pārthiva .. 66 ..
meaning:
प्रम्लोचा चाप्यनुम्लोचा रंभा चैवोर्वशी तथा ..
पञ्चचूडा सानुमती चित्रलेखा च पार्थिव .. 66 ..
text_mt:
Pramlocā, Anumlocā, Rambhā, and Urvaśī,
Pañcacūḍā, Sānumatī, and Citralekhā, O king,

sanskrit_iast:
miśrakeśī marīciśca vidyutparṇā tilottamā ..
adrikā lakṣmaṇā kṣepā asitā rucikā tathā ..67..
meaning:
मिश्रकेशी मरीचिश्च विद्युत्पर्णा तिलोत्तमा ..
अद्रिका लक्ष्मणा क्षेपा असिता रुचिका तथा ..67..
text_mt:
Miśrakeśī, Marīci, Vidyutparṇā, Tilottamā,
Adrikā, Lakṣmaṇā, Kṣepā, Asitā, and Rucikā,

sanskrit_iast:
suhemā cātha hemā ca śāḍvalī ca vapustathā ..
suvratā ca subāhuśca sugandhā suvapustathā..68..
meaning:
सुहेमा चाथ हेमा च शाड्वली च वपुस्तथा ..
सुव्रता च सुबाहुश्च सुगन्धा सुवपुस्तथा..68..
text_mt:
Suhemā, Hemā, Śāḍvalī, Vapus,
Suvratā, Subāhu, Sugandhā, and Suvapus,

sanskrit_iast:
puṇḍarīkā sudānā cāsudānā surasā tathā ..
hemā śāradvatī caiva sūnṛtā kamalālayā..69..
meaning:
पुण्डरीका सुदाना चासुदाना सुरसा तथा ..
हेमा शारद्वती चैव सूनृता कमलालया..69..
text_mt:
Puṇḍarīkā, Sudānā, Asudānā, Surasā,
Hemā, Śāradvatī, Sūnṛtā, Kamalālayā,

sanskrit_iast:
sumukhī haṃsapādī ca vāruṇī ratilālasā ..
etāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājannapsarasaḥ śubhāḥ .. 70..
meaning:
सुमुखी हंसपादी च वारुणी रतिलालसा ..
एतास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजन्नप्सरसः शुभाः .. 70..
text_mt:
Sumukhī, Haṃsapādī, Vāruṇī, and Ratilālasā;
may these auspicious apsarases consecrate you, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
prahlādaśca mahātejāstathā rājanvirocanaḥ ..
balirbāṇastathānye ca ditiputrāḥ samāgatāḥ.....
abhiṣiñcantu daityāstvāṃ divyenāpyambhasā svayam ..
vipracittimukhāḥ sarve dānavāstvāṃ samāgatāḥ .. 72 ..
meaning:
प्रह्लादश्च महातेजास्तथा राजन्विरोचनः ..
बलिर्बाणस्तथान्ये च दितिपुत्राः समागताः.....
अभिषिञ्चन्तु दैत्यास्त्वां दिव्येनाप्यम्भसा स्वयम् ..
विप्रचित्तिमुखाः सर्वे दानवास्त्वां समागताः .. 72 ..
text_mt: And Prahlāda of great splendor, and likewise Virocana, O king, / Bali, Bāṇa, and the other sons of Diti who have assembled, / may the Daityas consecrate you themselves with divine water; / all the Dānavas headed by Vipracitti who have assembled,

sanskrit_iast:
abhiṣiñcantu rājendra rājarājyena satvarāḥ ..
hetiścaiva prahetiśca mālī śaṅkustathaiva ca .. 73 ..
meaning:
अभिषिञ्चन्तु राजेन्द्र राजराज्येन सत्वराः ..
हेतिश्चैव प्रहेतिश्च माली शङ्कुस्तथैव च .. 73 ..
text_mt: may they swiftly consecrate you, O king of kings, for imperial sovereignty; / and Heti, Praheti, Mālī, and likewise Śaṅku,

sanskrit_iast:
sukeśī pauruṣeyaśca yajñahā puruṣādhamaḥ ..
vidyutsphūrjastathā vyāghro vadhaśca rasanastathā .. 74 ..
meaning:
सुकेशी पौरुषेयश्च यज्ञहा पुरुषाधमः ..
विद्युत्स्फूर्जस्तथा व्याघ्रो वधश्च रसनस्तथा .. 74 ..
text_mt: Sukeśin, Pauruṣeya, Yajñahan, Puruṣādhama, / Vidyutsphūrja, likewise Vyāghra, Vadha, and Rasana,

sanskrit_iast:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu samāgamyādya rākṣasāḥ ..
siddhārtho maṇibhadraśca sumano nandanastathā .. 75..
meaning:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समागम्याद्य राक्षसाः ..
सिद्धार्थो मणिभद्रश्च सुमनो नन्दनस्तथा .. 75..
text_mt: having assembled today, may these Rākṣasas consecrate you; / Siddhārtha, Maṇibhadra, Sumana, and Nandana,

sanskrit_iast:
kāṇḍabhiḥ pañcamaścaiva maṇimānuyamām̐stathā ..
sarvānubhūtaḥ śaṃkhaśca piṅgākṣaścastarastathā .. 76 ..
meaning:
काण्डभिः पञ्चमश्चैव मणिमानुयमाम्̐स्तथा ..
सर्वानुभूतः शंखश्च पिङ्गाक्षश्चस्तरस्तथा .. 76 ..
text_mt: Kāṇḍabhi, and as the fifth Maṇimat, as well as Uyamānt, / Sarvānubhūta, Śaṅkha, Piṅgākṣa, and likewise Astar,

sanskrit_iast:
yaśo mandaraśobhī ca padmacandraprabhaṅkarāḥ ..
meghavarṇaḥ subhadraśca pradyotaśca mahāghasaḥ ..77..
meaning:
यशो मन्दरशोभी च पद्मचन्द्रप्रभङ्कराः ..
मेघवर्णः सुभद्रश्च प्रद्योतश्च महाघसः ..77..
text_mt: Yaśas, Mandaraśobhin, Padmacandraprabhaṅkara, / Meghavarṇa, Subhadra, Pradyota, and Mahāghasa,

sanskrit_iast:
dyutimānketumāṃścaiva maulimāṃśca sudarśanaḥ ..
śvetaśca vipulaścaiva puṣpadanto jayāvahaḥ .. 78 ..
meaning:
द्युतिमान्केतुमांश्चैव मौलिमांश्च सुदर्शनः ..
श्वेतश्च विपुलश्चैव पुष्पदन्तो जयावहः .. 78 ..
text_mt: Dyutimat, Ketumat, Maulimat, Sudarśana, / Śveta, Vipula, Puṣpadanta, Jayāvaha,

sanskrit_iast:
padmavarṇo balākaśca kumudaśca balāhakaḥ ..
padmanābhaḥ sugandhaśca pravīro vijayaḥ kṛtiḥ .. 79 ..
meaning:
पद्मवर्णो बलाकश्च कुमुदश्च बलाहकः ..
पद्मनाभः सुगन्धश्च प्रवीरो विजयः कृतिः .. 79 ..
text_mt: Padmavarṇa, Balāka, Kumuda, Balāhaka, / Padmanābha, Sugandha, Pravīra, Vijaya, Kṛti,

sanskrit_iast:
pūrṇamāso hiraṇyākṣaḥ śatajihvaśca vīryavān ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājanyakṣendra sattamāḥ .. 80 ..
meaning:
पूर्णमासो हिरण्याक्षः शतजिह्वश्च वीर्यवान् ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजन्यक्षेन्द्र सत्तमाः .. 80 ..
text_mt: Pūrṇamāsa, Hiraṇyākṣa, and the powerful Śatajihva— / may these best of Yakṣa chiefs consecrate you, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṃkhapadmastu rājendra makaraḥ kacchapastathā ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu nidhayastu samāgatāḥ .. 81 ..
meaning:
शंखपद्मस्तु राजेन्द्र मकरः कच्छपस्तथा ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु निधयस्तु समागताः .. 81 ..
text_mt: Śaṅkha and Padma, O king of kings, Makara and Kacchapa— / having assembled, may these treasures consecrate you.

sanskrit_iast:
palagāścaiva vakrāśca ye ca sūcīmukhā nṛpa ..
duḥpūraṇā viṣādāśca jvalanāṅgārakāstathā .. 82 ..
meaning:
पलगाश्चैव वक्राश्च ये च सूचीमुखा नृप ..
दुःपूरणा विषादाश्च ज्वलनाङ्गारकास्तथा .. 82 ..
text_mt: The Palagas, the Vakras, and those that have needles for mouths, O king, / the Duḥpūraṇas, the Viṣādas, and likewise the Jvalanāṅgārakas,

sanskrit_iast:
kumbhapātāḥ pratuṇḍāśca tapavīrā ulūkhalāḥ ..
akarṇāśca kuṣaṇḍāśca tathā ye pātra pāṇayaḥ .. 83 ..
meaning:
कुम्भपाताः प्रतुण्डाश्च तपवीरा उलूखलाः ..
अकर्णाश्च कुषण्डाश्च तथा ये पात्र पाणयः .. 83 ..
text_mt: the Kumbhapātas, the Pratuṇḍas, the Tapavīras, the Ulūkhalas, / the Akarṇas, the Kuṣaṇḍas, and likewise those who hold vessels in their hands,

sanskrit_iast:
pāṃsavaśca vituṇḍāśca nipuṇāḥ skandanāstathā ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu piśācānāñca jātayaḥ .. 84 ..
meaning:
पांसवश्च वितुण्डाश्च निपुणाः स्कन्दनास्तथा ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पिशाचानाञ्च जातयः .. 84 ..
text_mt: the Pāṃsus, the Vituṇḍas, the Nipuṇas, and likewise the Skandanas— / may these classes of Piśācas consecrate you.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmacarye sthitā dāntāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvadarśinaḥ ..
nānāprakāravadanā nānābāhuśirodharāḥ ..85..
meaning:
ब्रह्मचर्ये स्थिता दान्ताः सर्वज्ञाः सर्वदर्शिनः ..
नानाप्रकारवदना नानाबाहुशिरोधराः ..85..
text_mt: Steadfast in celibacy, restrained, all-knowing, all-seeing, / having various forms of faces, having manifold arms and necks,

sanskrit_iast:
catuṣpathapurāṭṭālaśūnyālayaniketanāḥ ..
madhuratve bhavedevaṃ ye gatā manujeśvarāḥ .. 86..
meaning:
चतुष्पथपुराट्टालशून्यालयनिकेतनाः ..
मधुरत्वे भवेदेवं ये गता मनुजेश्वराः .. 86..
text_mt: dwelling in crossroads, city watchtowers, and abandoned houses— / those lords of men who have departed may it be so in gentleness—

sanskrit_iast:
te tvāmadyābhiṣiñcantu bhūtā bhūtapateḥ svayam ..
mahākālaṃ puraskṛtya narasiṃhaṃ ca mātaraḥ .. 87 ..
meaning:
ते त्वामद्याभिषिञ्चन्तु भूता भूतपतेः स्वयम् ..
महाकालं पुरस्कृत्य नरसिंहं च मातरः .. 87 ..
text_mt: may those spirits of the Lord of Spirits themselves consecrate you today; / placing Mahākāla and Narasiṃha at the head, the Mothers,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājarājye narādhipa ..
guhaḥ skando viśākhaśca naigameyastathaiva ca .. 88 ..
meaning:
सर्वास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजराज्ये नराधिप ..
गुहः स्कन्दो विशाखश्च नैगमेयस्तथैव च .. 88 ..
text_mt: may they all consecrate you for imperial sovereignty, O ruler of men; / Guha, Skanda, Viśākha, and likewise Naigameya,

sanskrit_iast:
abhiṣiñcantu rājam̐stvāṃ sarve skandagrahāḥ śubhāḥ ..
ḍākinyo yāśca yoginyaḥ khecarībhūcarīśca yāḥ .. 89 ..
meaning:
अभिषिञ्चन्तु राजम्̐स्त्वां सर्वे स्कन्दग्रहाः शुभाः ..
डाकिन्यो याश्च योगिन्यः खेचरीभूचरीश्च याः .. 89 ..
text_mt: may all the auspicious Skanda-grahas consecrate you, O king; / and whatever ḍākinīs and yoginīs there are, both the sky-goers and earth-goers,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu sametya manujeśvara ..
garuḍaścāruṇaścaiva āruṇiśca mahākhagaḥ .. 90 ..
meaning:
सर्वास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समेत्य मनुजेश्वर ..
गरुडश्चारुणश्चैव आरुणिश्च महाखगः .. 90 ..
text_mt: having assembled, may all of them consecrate you, O lord of men; / Garuḍa, Aruṇa, and Āruṇi, the great bird,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃpātī vinataścaiva viṣṇugandhaḥ kumārakaḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu suparṇāḥ pṛthivīpate .. 91 ..
meaning:
संपाती विनतश्चैव विष्णुगन्धः कुमारकः ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सुपर्णाः पृथिवीपते .. 91 ..
text_mt: Saṃpāti, Vinata, Viṣṇugandha, and Kumāraka— / may these birds consecrate you, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
anantaśca mahānāgaḥ śeṣo vāsukitakṣakau ..
saparṇīraśca kumbhaśca vāmanaścāñjanastathā .. 92 ..
meaning:
अनन्तश्च महानागः शेषो वासुकितक्षकौ ..
सपर्णीरश्च कुम्भश्च वामनश्चाञ्जनस्तथा .. 92 ..
text_mt: And Ananta the great serpent, Śeṣa, Vāsuki, and Takṣaka, / Saparṇīra, Kumbha, Vāmana, and likewise Añjana,

sanskrit_iast:
airāvato mahānāgaḥ kambalāśvatarāvubhau ..
ailamantraśca śaṃkhaśca karkoṭakadhanañjayau .. 93 ..
meaning:
ऐरावतो महानागः कम्बलाश्वतरावुभौ ..
ऐलमन्त्रश्च शंखश्च कर्कोटकधनञ्जयौ .. 93 ..
text_mt: Airāvata the great serpent, both Kambala and Aśvatara, / Ailamantra, Śaṅkha, Karkoṭaka, and Dhanañjaya,

sanskrit_iast:
mahākarṇamahānīlau dhṛtarāṣṭrabalāhakau ..
kumāraḥ puṣpadantaśca sumukho durmukhastathā .. 94 ..
meaning:
महाकर्णमहानीलौ धृतराष्ट्रबलाहकौ ..
कुमारः पुष्पदन्तश्च सुमुखो दुर्मुखस्तथा .. 94 ..
text_mt: Mahākarṇa, Mahānīla, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Balāhaka, / Kumāra, Puṣpadanta, Sumukha, and likewise Durmukha,

sanskrit_iast:
sūcīmukho dadhimukhaḥ kāliyaḥ śālipiṇḍakaḥ ..
bilvapādaḥ pāṇḍurako nāgaścāpūraṇastathā .. 95..
meaning:
सूचीमुखो दधिमुखः कालियः शालिपिण्डकः ..
बिल्वपादः पाण्डुरको नागश्चापूरणस्तथा .. 95..
text_mt: Sūcīmukha, Dadhimukha, Kāliya, Śālipiṇḍaka, / Bilvapāda, Pāṇḍuraka, and the serpent Āpūraṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
kapilaścāmbarīṣaśca kumāraścātha kaśyapaḥ ..
prahrādaḥ puṣpadantaśca gandharvaśca manasvikaḥ.. 96 ..
meaning:
कपिलश्चाम्बरीषश्च कुमारश्चाथ कश्यपः ..
प्रह्रादः पुष्पदन्तश्च गन्धर्वश्च मनस्विकः.. 96 ..
text_mt: Kapila, Ambarīṣa, Kumāra, and then Kaśyapa, / Prahrāda, Puṣpadanta, Gandharva, and Manasvika,

sanskrit_iast:
nahuṣaḥ khararomā ca śaṃkhapālastathaiva ca ..
padmaśca kulikaścaiva pāṇirityevamādayaḥ .. 97 ..
meaning:
नहुषः खररोमा च शंखपालस्तथैव च ..
पद्मश्च कुलिकश्चैव पाणिरित्येवमादयः .. 97 ..
text_mt: Nahuṣa, Khararoman, and likewise Śaṅkhapāla, / Padma, Kulika, Pāṇi, and others of this kind—

sanskrit_iast:
nāgāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājarājyena pārthiva ..
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpa danto'tha vāmanaḥ .. 98 ..
meaning:
नागास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजराज्येन पार्थिव ..
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्प दन्तोऽथ वामनः .. 98 ..
text_mt: may the serpents consecrate you for imperial sovereignty, O king; / Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana,

sanskrit_iast:
supratīkoñjano nīlaḥ pāntu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā ..
cakraṃ triśūlaṃ vajraśca nandakostrāṇi cāpyatha .. 99 ..
meaning:
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नीलः पान्तु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ..
चक्रं त्रिशूलं वज्रश्च नन्दकोस्त्राणि चाप्यथ .. 99 ..
text_mt: Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—may they protect you always on all sides; / the discus, the trident, the vajra, Nandaka, and the weapons,

sanskrit_iast:
paitāmahāstathā haṃsā vṛṣabhaḥ śaṅkarasya ca ..
durgāsiṃhaśca pāntu tvāṃ yamasya mahiṣastathā ..100..
meaning:
पैतामहास्तथा हंसा वृषभः शङ्करस्य च ..
दुर्गासिंहश्च पान्तु त्वां यमस्य महिषस्तथा ..100..
text_mt: and the swans of the Grandfather, the bull of Śaṅkara, / Durgā’s lion, and Yama’s buffalo—may they protect you;

sanskrit_iast:
uccaiḥśravāścāśvapatistathā dhanvantarirnṛpa ..
kaustubhaḥ śaṃkharājaśca pāntu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā ..101..
meaning:
उच्चैःश्रवाश्चाश्वपतिस्तथा धन्वन्तरिर्नृप ..
कौस्तुभः शंखराजश्च पान्तु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ..101..
text_mt: Uccaiḥśravas, lord of horses, and likewise Dhanvantari, O king, / the Kaustubha jewel, and the king of conches—may they protect you always on all sides.

sanskrit_iast:
sarve'bhiṣekaṃ dattvā te diśantu vijayaṃ dhuvam ..
dharmaśca vyavasāyaśca satyo dānaṃ tapastathā .. 102 ..
meaning:
सर्वेऽभिषेकं दत्त्वा ते दिशन्तु विजयं धुवम् ..
धर्मश्च व्यवसायश्च सत्यो दानं तपस्तथा .. 102 ..
text_mt: Having all performed the consecration, may they grant you firm victory; / Dharma, Resolution, Truth, Generosity, and Asceticism,

sanskrit_iast:
yamo yajñastathā vāyurbrahmacarya damaḥ śamaḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu citraguptaśca pārthiva .. 103 ..
meaning:
यमो यज्ञस्तथा वायुर्ब्रह्मचर्य दमः शमः ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु चित्रगुप्तश्च पार्थिव .. 103 ..
text_mt: Yama, Sacrifice, Vāyu, Celibacy, Self-restraint, Tranquility— / may these consecrate you, and Citragupta, O king;

sanskrit_iast:
daṇḍaśca piṅgalaścaiva mṛtyukālāvubhau tathā ..
vālakhilyāstathā sarve bhavantu vijayāya te ..104..
meaning:
दण्डश्च पिङ्गलश्चैव मृत्युकालावुभौ तथा ..
वालखिल्यास्तथा सर्वे भवन्तु विजयाय ते ..104..
text_mt: Daṇḍa, Piṅgala, both Death and Time, / and likewise all the Vālakhilyas—may they be for your victory.

sanskrit_iast:
digdhenavaścatasrastvāṃ surābhiśca tathā nṛpa ..
abhiṣiñcantu sarvābhirgobhiḥ sārdhaṃ nareśvara ..105 ..
meaning:
दिग्धेनवश्चतस्रस्त्वां सुराभिश्च तथा नृप ..
अभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वाभिर्गोभिः सार्धं नरेश्वर ..105 ..
text_mt: May the four cows of the directions and Surabhi, O king, / consecrate you along with all cows, O ruler of men.

sanskrit_iast:
vedavyāsaśca vālmīkiḥ kamaṭho'tha parāśaraḥ ..
devalaḥ parvataścaiva durvāsāśca tathā muniḥ .. 106 ..
meaning:
वेदव्यासश्च वाल्मीकिः कमठोऽथ पराशरः ..
देवलः पर्वतश्चैव दुर्वासाश्च तथा मुनिः .. 106 ..
text_mt: Vedavyāsa, Vālmīki, Kamaṭha, then Parāśara, / Devala, Parvata, and likewise the sage Durvāsas,

sanskrit_iast:
yājñavalkyaśca jābāliḥ jamadagniḥ śuciśravāḥ ..
viśvāmitraḥ sthūlaśirāścyavano'trirvidūrathaḥ .. 107 ..
meaning:
याज्ञवल्क्यश्च जाबालिः जमदग्निः शुचिश्रवाः ..
विश्वामित्रः स्थूलशिराश्च्यवनोऽत्रिर्विदूरथः .. 107 ..
text_mt: Yājñavalkya, Jābāli, Jamadagni, Śuciśravas, / Viśvāmitra, Sthūlaśiras, Cyavana, Atri, Vidūratha,

sanskrit_iast:
ekataśca dvitaścaiva trito gautamagālavau ..
śāṇḍilyaśca bharadvājo maudgalyo vedavāhanaḥ .. 108..
meaning:
एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितो गौतमगालवौ ..
शाण्डिल्यश्च भरद्वाजो मौद्गल्यो वेदवाहनः .. 108..
text_mt: Ekata, Dvita, Trita, Gautama, Gālava, / Śāṇḍilya, Bharadvāja, Maudgalya, Vedavāhana,

sanskrit_iast:
bṛhadaśvaḥ kuṭiśaṭho jaṭājānurghaṭodaraḥ ..
yavakrīto'rtharaityaśca ātmavānatha jaiminiḥ ..109..
meaning:
बृहदश्वः कुटिशठो जटाजानुर्घटोदरः ..
यवक्रीतोऽर्थरैत्यश्च आत्मवानथ जैमिनिः ..109..
text_mt: Bṛhadaśva, Kuṭiśaṭha, Jaṭājānu, Ghaṭodara, / Yavakrīta, Artharaitya, Ātmavat, and then Jaimini,

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣiḥ śārṅgaravaścaiva tathāgastyo mahātapāḥ ..
unmuvurmumuvuścaiva idhmabāhurmahodayaḥ .. 110 ..
meaning:
ऋषिः शार्ङ्गरवश्चैव तथागस्त्यो महातपाः ..
उन्मुवुर्मुमुवुश्चैव इध्मबाहुर्महोदयः .. 110 ..
text_mt: the sage Śārṅgarava, and likewise Agastya of great austerities, / Unmuvu, Mumuvu, Idhmabāhu, Mahodaya,

sanskrit_iast:
kātyāyanaśca kaṇvaśca valvakāmborunandanaḥ ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu ṛṣayaḥ pārthivottama .. 111 ..
meaning:
कात्यायनश्च कण्वश्च वल्वकाम्बोरुनन्दनः ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु ऋषयः पार्थिवोत्तम .. 111 ..
text_mt: Kātyāyana, Kaṇva, and Valvakāmborunandana— / may these sages consecrate you, O best of kings.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthurdilīpo bharato duṣyantaḥ śatrujidbalī ..
manuḥ kakutsthaścānenā yuvanāśvo jayadrathaḥ .. 112 ..
meaning:
पृथुर्दिलीपो भरतो दुष्यन्तः शत्रुजिद्बली ..
मनुः ककुत्स्थश्चानेना युवनाश्वो जयद्रथः .. 112 ..
text_mt: Pṛthu, Dilīpa, Bharata, Duṣyanta, the mighty Śatrujit, / Manu, Kakutstha, Anenas, Yuvanāśva, Jayadratha,

sanskrit_iast:
māndhātā mucukundaśca tathā rājā purūravāḥ ..
āyuśca nahuṣaścaiva yayātiraparājitaḥ .. 113 ..
meaning:
मान्धाता मुचुकुन्दश्च तथा राजा पुरूरवाः ..
आयुश्च नहुषश्चैव ययातिरपराजितः .. 113 ..
text_mt: Māndhātṛ, Mucukunda, and likewise King Purūravas, / Āyu, Nahuṣa, and the undefeated Yayāti,

sanskrit_iast:
ikṣvākuśca yaduścaiva punarbhūriśravāstathā ..
ambarīṣaśca nābhāgo bṛhadaśvo mahāhanuḥ .. 114 ..
meaning:
इक्ष्वाकुश्च यदुश्चैव पुनर्भूरिश्रवास्तथा ..
अम्बरीषश्च नाभागो बृहदश्वो महाहनुः .. 114 ..
text_mt: Ikṣvāku, Yadu, and again Bhūriśravas, / Ambarīṣa, Nābhāga, Bṛhadaśva, Mahāhanu,

sanskrit_iast:
pradyumnaścātha sudyumno bhūridyumnaśca sṛñjayaḥ ..
ete cānye ca rājānastava rājandivaṅgatāḥ ..115 ..
meaning:
प्रद्युम्नश्चाथ सुद्युम्नो भूरिद्युम्नश्च सृञ्जयः ..
एते चान्ये च राजानस्तव राजन्दिवङ्गताः ..115 ..
text_mt: Pradyumna, Sudyumna, Bhūridyumna, and Sṛñjaya— / these and other kings of yours who have gone to heaven, O king,

sanskrit_iast:
samāyāntvabhiṣekāya vijayāya tathā śriye ..
parjanyādyāstathā sarve vāstudevāssamāsataḥ .. 116 ..
meaning:
समायान्त्वभिषेकाय विजयाय तथा श्रिये ..
पर्जन्याद्यास्तथा सर्वे वास्तुदेवास्समासतः .. 116 ..
text_mt: May they assemble for your consecration, for victory and prosperity, / and all the site-deities, beginning with Parjanya, in their entirety.

sanskrit_iast:
drumāścauṣadhayo ratnabījāni vividhāni ca ..
sarve tvāmabhiṣiñcantu rājanrājyena satvarāḥ .. 117 ..
meaning:
द्रुमाश्चौषधयो रत्नबीजानि विविधानि च ..
सर्वे त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राजन्राज्येन सत्वराः .. 117 ..
text_mt: May trees, medicinal herbs, jewels, and diverse seeds— / may all of them swiftly consecrate you to kingship, O king!

sanskrit_iast:
puruṣaścāprameyātmā mahābhūtāni yāni ca ..
pṛthivīvāyurākāśamāpo jyotistathaiva ca .. 118 ..
meaning:
पुरुषश्चाप्रमेयात्मा महाभूतानि यानि च ..
पृथिवीवायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिस्तथैव च .. 118 ..
text_mt: The Cosmic Person of immeasurable nature, and whichever gross elements there are: / earth, wind, ether, water, and fire;

sanskrit_iast:
manobuddhistathaivātmā avyaktaśca mahīpate ..
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu sametā vasudhādhipa .. 119 ..
meaning:
मनोबुद्धिस्तथैवात्मा अव्यक्तश्च महीपते ..
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समेता वसुधाधिप .. 119 ..
text_mt: mind, intellect, the self, and the unmanifest, O lord of the earth— / may these, assembled together, consecrate you, O ruler of the earth!

sanskrit_iast:
rukmabhaumaḥ śilābhaumaḥ pātālo nīlamṛttikaḥ ..
pīto raktakṣitiścaiva śvetabhaumastathaiva ca .. 120 ..
meaning:
रुक्मभौमः शिलाभौमः पातालो नीलमृत्तिकः ..
पीतो रक्तक्षितिश्चैव श्वेतभौमस्तथैव च .. 120 ..
text_mt: The golden-soiled [underworld], the stone-soiled, the netherworld with black soil, / the yellow-soiled, the red-earthed, and the white-soiled underworld;

sanskrit_iast:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu vijayāya mahīpate ..
bhūloko'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarloko'tha mahajjanaḥ .. 121 ..
meaning:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु विजयाय महीपते ..
भूलोकोऽथ भुवर्लोकः स्वर्लोकोऽथ महज्जनः .. 121 ..
text_mt: may these consecrate you for victory, O lord of the earth! / The earth-world, then the atmosphere, the heaven-world, and the Maharloka, Janaloka,

sanskrit_iast:
tapaḥ satyaśca rājendra vijayāya bhavantu te ..
jambūśākakuśakrauñcāḥ śālmalidvīpa eva ca .. 122 ..
meaning:
तपः सत्यश्च राजेन्द्र विजयाय भवन्तु ते ..
जम्बूशाककुशक्रौञ्चाः शाल्मलिद्वीप एव च .. 122 ..
text_mt: Tapoloka, and Satyaloka, O king of kings, may they be for your victory! / Jambu, Śāka, Kuśa, Krauñca, and Śālmalidvīpa,

sanskrit_iast:
gomedhaḥ puṣkaraścaiva svasāmyaṃ pradiśantu te ..
uttarāḥ kuravaḥ puṇyā ramyā hairaṇvatastathā .. 123 ..
meaning:
गोमेधः पुष्करश्चैव स्वसाम्यं प्रदिशन्तु ते ..
उत्तराः कुरवः पुण्या रम्या हैरण्वतस्तथा .. 123 ..
text_mt: Gomedha, and Puṣkara—may they bestow their mastery upon you! / The holy Northern Kurus, Ramyaka, and Hiraṇmaya,

sanskrit_iast:
bhadrāśvaḥ ketumālaśca varṣaścaiva ilāvṛtaḥ ..
harivarṣaḥ kiṃpuruṣo varṣo bhāratasaṃjñikaḥ .. 124..
meaning:
भद्राश्वः केतुमालश्च वर्षश्चैव इलावृतः ..
हरिवर्षः किंपुरुषो वर्षो भारतसंज्ञिकः .. 124..
text_mt: Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla, and the continent of Ilāvṛta, / Harivarṣa, Kiṃpuruṣa, and the continent named Bhārata—

sanskrit_iast:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu sametya vasudhādhipa ..
indradvīpaḥ kaśeruśca tāmravarṇo gabhastimān .. 125 ..
meaning:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु समेत्य वसुधाधिप ..
इन्द्रद्वीपः कशेरुश्च ताम्रवर्णो गभस्तिमान् .. 125 ..
text_mt: may these, coming together, consecrate you, O lord of the earth! / Indradvīpa, Kaśeru, Tāmravarṇa, Gabhastimat,

sanskrit_iast:
nāgadvīpastathā saumyo gāndharvo vāruṇastathā ..
ayaṃ caruvasasteṣāṃ svasāmyaṃ pradiśantu te .. 126 ..
meaning:
नागद्वीपस्तथा सौम्यो गान्धर्वो वारुणस्तथा ..
अयं चरुवसस्तेषां स्वसाम्यं प्रदिशन्तु ते .. 126 ..
text_mt: Nāgadvīpa, Saumya, Gāndharva, and Vāruṇa, / and this Caruva of theirs—may they bestow their mastery upon you!

sanskrit_iast:
himavānhemakūṭaśca niṣadho nīlaparvataḥ ..
śvetaśca śṛṅgavānmerurmālyavāngandhamādanaḥ ..127 ..
meaning:
हिमवान्हेमकूटश्च निषधो नीलपर्वतः ..
श्वेतश्च शृङ्गवान्मेरुर्माल्यवान्गन्धमादनः ..127 ..
text_mt: Himavat, Hemakūṭa, Niṣadha, the blue mountain Nīla, / Śveta, Śṛṅgavat, Meru, Mālyavat, and Gandhamādana;

sanskrit_iast:
mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimānṛkṣavāṃstathā ..
vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca sarva eva mahīdharāḥ .. 128 ..
meaning:
महेन्द्रो मलयः सह्यः शुक्तिमानृक्षवांस्तथा ..
विन्ध्यश्च पारियात्रश्च सर्व एव महीधराः .. 128 ..
text_mt: Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimat, and Ṛkṣavat, / Vindhya, and Pāriyātra, indeed all the mountains—

sanskrit_iast:
samāgamyābhiṣiñcantu tvāmadya vasudhādhipa! ..
ṛgvedo'tha yajurvedaḥ sāmavedastathaiva ca .. 129 ..
meaning:
समागम्याभिषिञ्चन्तु त्वामद्य वसुधाधिप! ..
ऋग्वेदोऽथ यजुर्वेदः सामवेदस्तथैव च .. 129 ..
text_mt: may they assemble and consecrate you today, O lord of the earth! / The Ṛgveda, then the Yajurveda, and likewise the Sāmaveda,

sanskrit_iast:
atharvavedo vedāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu pārthiva ..
itihāso dhanurvedo gandharvaścāyussaṃjñitaḥ .. 130 ..
meaning:
अथर्ववेदो वेदास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ..
इतिहासो धनुर्वेदो गन्धर्वश्चायुस्संज्ञितः .. 130 ..
text_mt: and the Atharvaveda: may the Vedas consecrate you, O king! / The Itihāsa, the Dhanurveda, the Gandharvaveda, and that named Āyus [Āyurveda],

sanskrit_iast:
vedopavedāśca tathā vijayāya bhavantu te ..
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ jyotiṣāṅgatiḥ .. 131 ..
meaning:
वेदोपवेदाश्च तथा विजयाय भवन्तु ते ..
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं ज्योतिषाङ्गतिः .. 131 ..
text_mt: the Vedas and secondary Vedas: may they be for your victory! / Phonetics, ritual procedure, grammar, etymology, the course of astronomy,

sanskrit_iast:
chandovicitiṣaṣṭhāni vijayaṃ pradiśantu te ..
aṅgāni vedāścatvāro mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ .. 132 ..
meaning:
छन्दोविचितिषष्ठानि विजयं प्रदिशन्तु ते ..
अङ्गानि वेदाश्चत्वारो मीमांसा न्यायविस्तरः .. 132 ..
text_mt: and metrics as the sixth [ancillary science]: may they grant you victory! / The limbs [of the Veda], the four Vedas, Mīmāṃsā, the extent of Nyāya,

sanskrit_iast:
dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇañca vidyā etāścaturdaśa ..
sāṃkhyayogaḥ pañcarātraṃ vedāḥ pāśupataṃ tathā .. 133 ..
meaning:
धर्मशास्त्रं पुराणञ्च विद्या एताश्चतुर्दश ..
सांख्ययोगः पञ्चरात्रं वेदाः पाशुपतं तथा .. 133 ..
text_mt: Dharmaśāstra, and the Purāṇa—these fourteen branches of learning, / Sāṃkhya-Yoga, Pāñcarātra, the Vedas, and Pāśupata;

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtānnapañcakaṃ hyetacchāstrāṇi vividhāni ca ..
gāyatrī pāpaśamanī durgā devī mahāśivā .. 134 ..
meaning:
कृतान्नपञ्चकं ह्येतच्छास्त्राणि विविधानि च ..
गायत्री पापशमनी दुर्गा देवी महाशिवा .. 134 ..
text_mt: these indeed are the established quintet, and the diverse treatises; / Gāyatrī, remover of sin, goddess Durgā, Mahāśivā,

sanskrit_iast:
gandhārī ca tathā vidyā vijayaṃ pradiśantu te ..
devadānavagandharvayakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ .. 135 ..
meaning:
गन्धारी च तथा विद्या विजयं प्रदिशन्तु ते ..
देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः .. 135 ..
text_mt: and the lore Gandhārī—may they grant you victory! / Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents;

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣayo manavo gāvo devamātara eva ca ..
devapatnyo drumā nāgāḥ daityāścāpsarasāṅgaṇāḥ .. 136 ..
meaning:
ऋषयो मनवो गावो देवमातर एव च ..
देवपत्न्यो द्रुमा नागाः दैत्याश्चाप्सरसाङ्गणाः .. 136 ..
text_mt: sages, Manus, cows, the mothers of the gods, / the wives of the gods, trees, serpents, Daityas, and hosts of Apsarases;

sanskrit_iast:
śastrāṇi sarvaśāstrāṇi rājāno vāhanāni ca ..
auṣadhāni ca ratnāni kālasyāvayavāstathā ..137..
meaning:
शस्त्राणि सर्वशास्त्राणि राजानो वाहनानि च ..
औषधानि च रत्नानि कालस्यावयवास्तथा ..137..
text_mt: weapons, all treatises of learning, kings, vehicles, / medicinal herbs, jewels, and the divisions of time;

sanskrit_iast:
sthānāni ca samastāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca ..
jīmūtāni ca sarvāṇi tadvikārāśca ye tathā .. 138 ..
meaning:
स्थानानि च समस्तानि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च ..
जीमूतानि च सर्वाणि तद्विकाराश्च ये तथा .. 138 ..
text_mt: all holy places, shrines, / all clouds, and their various transformations;

sanskrit_iast:
uktāni cāpya'nuktāni vijayāya bhavantu te ..
lavaṇaḥ kṣāratoyaśca ghṛtamaṇḍodakastathā .. 139 ..
meaning:
उक्तानि चाप्यऽनुक्तानि विजयाय भवन्तु ते ..
लवणः क्षारतोयश्च घृतमण्डोदकस्तथा .. 139 ..
text_mt: those mentioned and those unmentioned: may they be for your victory! / The salt ocean, the alkaline-watered ocean, and the clarified-butter-watered ocean,

sanskrit_iast:
dadhimaṇḍodakaścaiva surodaśca narādhipa ..
tathaivekṣurasodaśca tathā svādūdakaśca yaḥ .. 140 ..
meaning:
दधिमण्डोदकश्चैव सुरोदश्च नराधिप ..
तथैवेक्षुरसोदश्च तथा स्वादूदकश्च यः .. 140 ..
text_mt: the ocean of whey-waters, and the ocean of wine, O ruler of men, / and the ocean of sugarcane juice, and that which is of sweet water,

sanskrit_iast:
garbhodaśca svatoyaistvāmabhiṣiñcantu pārthiva ..
catvārassāgarāścaiva svena toyena pārthiva .. 141 ..
meaning:
गर्भोदश्च स्वतोयैस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु पार्थिव ..
चत्वारस्सागराश्चैव स्वेन तोयेन पार्थिव .. 141 ..
text_mt: and the ocean of the cosmic womb—may they consecrate you with their waters, O king! / And the four oceans with their waters, O king,

sanskrit_iast:
samāgamyābhiṣiñcantu vijayaṃ pradiśantu te ..
puṣkaraśca prayāgaśca prabhāso naimiṣastathā .. 142 ..
meaning:
समागम्याभिषिञ्चन्तु विजयं प्रदिशन्तु ते ..
पुष्करश्च प्रयागश्च प्रभासो नैमिषस्तथा .. 142 ..
text_mt: may they assemble, consecrate you, and bestow victory upon you! / Puṣkara, Prayāga, Prabhāsa, and Naimiṣa,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā brahmasaraḥ puṇyaṃ gayāśīrṣaṃ ca pārthiva ..
kālodako nandikuṇḍaḥ tathaivottaramānasaḥ .. 143 ..
meaning:
तथा ब्रह्मसरः पुण्यं गयाशीर्षं च पार्थिव ..
कालोदको नन्दिकुण्डः तथैवोत्तरमानसः .. 143 ..
text_mt: and the holy Brahmasaras, and Gayāśīrṣa, O king; / Kālodaka, Nandikuṇḍa, and Uttaramānasa;

sanskrit_iast:
svargamārgapradaścaiva tathā pañcanadaśca yaḥ ..
bhṛgutīrthaṃ caujasaśca tathaivāmarakaṇṭakaḥ..144..
meaning:
स्वर्गमार्गप्रदश्चैव तथा पञ्चनदश्च यः ..
भृगुतीर्थं चौजसश्च तथैवामरकण्टकः..144..
text_mt: the one that bestows the path to heaven, and the holy site Pañcanada; / Bhṛgutīrtha, Ojas, and Amarakaṇṭaka;

sanskrit_iast:
āśramaḥ kālikāyāśca tṛṇabindostathāśramaḥ..
gopatīrthaṃ cāpatīrthaṃ vimalaḥ svarga eva ca..145..
meaning:
आश्रमः कालिकायाश्च तृणबिन्दोस्तथाश्रमः..
गोपतीर्थं चापतीर्थं विमलः स्वर्ग एव च..145..
text_mt: the hermitage of Kālikā, and the hermitage of Tṛṇabindu; / Gopatīrtha, Āpatīrtha, Vimala, and Svarga;

sanskrit_iast:
jambūmārgaśca rājendra puṇyastaṇḍulikāśramaḥ ..
kapilasya tathā tīrthaṃ tīrthe vāṭikaṣaṇḍike .. 146 ..
meaning:
जम्बूमार्गश्च राजेन्द्र पुण्यस्तण्डुलिकाश्रमः ..
कपिलस्य तथा तीर्थं तीर्थे वाटिकषण्डिके .. 146 ..
text_mt: Jambūmārga, O king of kings, the sacred Taṇḍulikāśrama; / the holy bathing place of Kapila, the two holy places at Vāṭikaṣaṇḍika;

sanskrit_iast:
mahāsarastathāgastyaḥ kumārī tīrtha eva ca ..
gaṅgātīraḥ kuśāvarto bilvako nīlaparvataḥ .. 147 ..
meaning:
महासरस्तथागस्त्यः कुमारी तीर्थ एव च ..
गङ्गातीरः कुशावर्तो बिल्वको नीलपर्वतः .. 147 ..
text_mt: Mahāsaras, Agastya, and the holy bathing place Kumārī; / the bank of the Gaṅgā, Kuśāvarta, Bilvaka, and Nīlaparvata;

sanskrit_iast:
varāhaparvataścaiva tīrthaḥ kanakhalastathā ..
svargandhā vaśakumbhā ca tathā śākambharī ca yā .. 148 ..
meaning:
वराहपर्वतश्चैव तीर्थः कनखलस्तथा ..
स्वर्गन्धा वशकुम्भा च तथा शाकम्भरी च या .. 148 ..
text_mt: Varāhaparvata, and the holy bathing place Kanakhala; / Svargandhā, Vaśakumbhā, and Śākambharī;

sanskrit_iast: bhṛgutuṅgaḥ sakubjāmraḥ kapilasya tathāśramam .. 149 ..
meaning: भृगुतुङ्गः सकुब्जाम्रः कपिलस्य तथाश्रमम् .. 149 ..
text_mt: Bhṛgutuṅga, along with Kubjāmra, and the hermitage of Kapila;

sanskrit_iast:
camasodbhedanaḥ puṇyastathā vinaśanaḥ śubhaḥ ..
ajatuṅgaśca somaśca ajogandhaśca pārthiva ..
kāliñjaraśca kedāro rudrakoṭistathaiva ca .. 150 ..
meaning:
चमसोद्भेदनः पुण्यस्तथा विनशनः शुभः ..
अजतुङ्गश्च सोमश्च अजोगन्धश्च पार्थिव ..
कालिञ्जरश्च केदारो रुद्रकोटिस्तथैव च .. 150 ..
text_mt: holy Camasodbhedana, and auspicious Vinaśana; / Ajatuṅga, Soma, and Ajogandha, O king; / Kāliñjara, Kedāra, and Rudrakoṭi;

sanskrit_iast:
mahālagnaśca rājendra vadanāśrama eva ca ..
nandā ca sūryatīrthaṃ ca somatīrthaṃ śatakratoḥ .. 151 ..
meaning:
महालग्नश्च राजेन्द्र वदनाश्रम एव च ..
नन्दा च सूर्यतीर्थं च सोमतीर्थं शतक्रतोः .. 151 ..
text_mt: Mahālagna, O king of kings, and Vadanāśrama; / Nandā, Sūryatīrtha, and the Somatīrtha of Śatakratu [Indra];

sanskrit_iast:
aśvinorvaruṇasyāpi vāyovairśravaṇasya ca ..
brahmaṇaścaiva śarvasya yamasya cyavanasya ca ..152 ..
meaning:
अश्विनोर्वरुणस्यापि वायोवैर्श्रवणस्य च ..
ब्रह्मणश्चैव शर्वस्य यमस्य च्यवनस्य च ..152 ..
text_mt: [the holy bathing places] of the Aśvins, of Varuṇa, of Vāyu, of Vaiśravaṇa, / of Brahmā, of Śarva, of Yama, and of Cyavana;

sanskrit_iast:
virūpākṣasya dharmasya tathā cāpsarasāṃ nṛpa ..
ṛṣīṇāṃ ca vasūnāṃ ca sādhyānāṃ marutāṃ tathā .. 153 ..
meaning:
विरूपाक्षस्य धर्मस्य तथा चाप्सरसां नृप ..
ऋषीणां च वसूनां च साध्यानां मरुतां तथा .. 153 ..
text_mt: of Virūpākṣa, of Dharma, and of the Apsarases, O king; / of the ṛṣis, of the Vasus, of the Sādhyas, and of the Maruts;

sanskrit_iast:
ādityānāṃ ca rudrāṇāṃ tathā cāṅgirasāṃ nṛpa ..
viśvedevabhṛgūṇāṃ ca gandharvāṇāṃ ca mānada .. 154 ..
meaning:
आदित्यानां च रुद्राणां तथा चाङ्गिरसां नृप ..
विश्वेदेवभृगूणां च गन्धर्वाणां च मानद .. 154 ..
text_mt: of the Ādityas, of the Rudras, and of the Āṅgirases, O king; / of the Viśvedevas, of the Bhṛgus, and of the Gandharvas, O bestower of honor;

sanskrit_iast:
plakṣaprasravaṇaścaiva suṣeṇaśca narādhipa ..
śāligrāmasaraścaiva vārāho vāmanastathā .. 155 ..
meaning:
प्लक्षप्रस्रवणश्चैव सुषेणश्च नराधिप ..
शालिग्रामसरश्चैव वाराहो वामनस्तथा .. 155 ..
text_mt: Plakṣaprasravaṇa, and Suṣeṇa, O ruler of men; / the lake Śāligrāmasaras, Vārāha, and Vāmana;

sanskrit_iast:
kāmaśramastrikūṭaśca citrakūṭastathaiva ca ..
saptarcaḥ kratusāraśca tathā viṣṇupadaṃ saraḥ .. 156 ..
meaning:
कामश्रमस्त्रिकूटश्च चित्रकूटस्तथैव च ..
सप्तर्चः क्रतुसारश्च तथा विष्णुपदं सरः .. 156 ..
text_mt: Kāmāśrama, Trikūṭa, and Citrakūṭa; / Saptarca, Kratusāra, and the lake Viṣṇupada;

sanskrit_iast:
kapilasya tathā tīrthaṃ vāsukestīrthameva ca ..
sindhūttamaṃ tapo dānaṃ tathā śūrpākaraḥ śubhaḥ .. 157 ..
meaning:
कपिलस्य तथा तीर्थं वासुकेस्तीर्थमेव च ..
सिन्धूत्तमं तपो दानं तथा शूर्पाकरः शुभः .. 157 ..
text_mt: the holy bathing place of Kapila, and the holy bathing place of Vāsuki; / Sindhūttama, Tapodāna, and auspicious Śūrpākara;

sanskrit_iast:
pauṇḍīrakaśca rājendra gaṅgāsāgarasaṅgamaḥ ..
sindhusāgarayoścaiva saṅgamaḥ sumanoharaḥ .. 158 ..
meaning:
पौण्डीरकश्च राजेन्द्र गङ्गासागरसङ्गमः ..
सिन्धुसागरयोश्चैव सङ्गमः सुमनोहरः .. 158 ..
text_mt: Pauṇḍīraka, O king of kings, the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, / and the captivating confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean;

sanskrit_iast:
tathā kundāvasundhaśca mānasaṃ ca mahatsaraḥ ..
tathā bindusaraḥ puṇyaṃ saraścācchodakaṃ tathā .. 159 ..
meaning:
तथा कुन्दावसुन्धश्च मानसं च महत्सरः ..
तथा बिन्दुसरः पुण्यं सरश्चाच्छोदकं तथा .. 159 ..
text_mt: Kundāvasundha, the great lake Mānasa, / the holy lake Bindusaras, and Lake Acchodaka;

sanskrit_iast:
dharmāraṇyaṃ phalgutīrthaṃ savimuktaṃ tathaiva ca ..
lauhityaśca tathā puṇyo badarīpāvanaḥ śivaḥ .. 160 ..
meaning:
धर्मारण्यं फल्गुतीर्थं सविमुक्तं तथैव च ..
लौहित्यश्च तथा पुण्यो बदरीपावनः शिवः .. 160 ..
text_mt: Dharmāraṇya, Phalgutīrtha, along with Vimukta, / the holy Lauhitya, and auspicious Badarīpāvana.

sanskrit_iast:
tīrthaṃ saptaṛṣīṇāṃ ca vahnitīrthaṃ ca pārthiva ..
vastrāpathastato meṣaśchāgaleśaśca pārthiva .. ..161..
meaning:
तीर्थं सप्तऋषीणां च वह्नितीर्थं च पार्थिव ..
वस्त्रापथस्ततो मेषश्छागलेशश्च पार्थिव .. ..161..
text_mt: And the holy site of the Seven Sages, and the holy site of Agni, O king, / then Vastrāpatha, Meṣa, and Chāgaleśa, O king,

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpanyāsassakāmeśastīrtho haṃsapadastathā ..
aśvaśīrṣaḥ sa kṛṣṇākhyo maṇibhadrastathaiva ca .. 162 ..
meaning:
पुष्पन्यासस्सकामेशस्तीर्थो हंसपदस्तथा ..
अश्वशीर्षः स कृष्णाख्यो मणिभद्रस्तथैव च .. 162 ..
text_mt: Puṣpanyāsa with Kāmeśa, and the holy site Haṃsapada, / Aśvaśīrṣa named Kṛṣṇa, and Maṇibhadra as well,

sanskrit_iast:
devikā sindhumārgaśca svarṇabindustathaiva ca ..
āhalyakastathā tīrthastīrthaścairāvatastathā..163..
meaning:
देविका सिन्धुमार्गश्च स्वर्णबिन्दुस्तथैव च ..
आहल्यकस्तथा तीर्थस्तीर्थश्चैरावतस्तथा..163..
text_mt: Devikā, Sindhumārga, and Svarṇabindu as well, / and the holy site Āhalyaka, and the holy site Airāvata,

sanskrit_iast:
airāvatisamudbhede tīrthaṃ bhogayaśastathā ..
karavīrāśramaścaiva nāgamodānikastathā..164..
meaning:
ऐरावतिसमुद्भेदे तीर्थं भोगयशस्तथा ..
करवीराश्रमश्चैव नागमोदानिकस्तथा..164..
text_mt: and at the confluence of the Airāvatī, the holy site Bhogayaśas, / and the hermitage of Karavīra, and Nāgamodānika,

sanskrit_iast:
pāpamocanikaścaiva ṛṇamocanikastathā ..
udvejanastathā puṇyaḥ puṇyaśca hariśeśvaraḥ .. 165 ..
meaning:
पापमोचनिकश्चैव ऋणमोचनिकस्तथा ..
उद्वेजनस्तथा पुण्यः पुण्यश्च हरिशेश्वरः .. 165 ..
text_mt: and Pāpamocanika, and Ṛṇamocanika, / and holy Udvejana, and holy Hariśeśvara,

sanskrit_iast:
devabrahmasaraḥ puṇyaṃ sarpirdarvī ca pārthiva ..
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ puṇyasaṅkīrtanāḥ śubhāḥ .. 166 ..
meaning:
देवब्रह्मसरः पुण्यं सर्पिर्दर्वी च पार्थिव ..
एते चान्ये च बहवः पुण्यसङ्कीर्तनाः शुभाः .. 166 ..
text_mt: the holy Devabrahmasaras, and Sarpirdarvī, O king: / may these and many other auspicious [sites], holy to recite,

sanskrit_iast:
toyaistvāmabhiṣiñcantu sarvapātakanāśanaiḥ ..
gaṅgā mahānadī puṇyā hrādinī hlādinī tathā .. .. 167 ..
meaning:
तोयैस्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वपातकनाशनैः ..
गङ्गा महानदी पुण्या ह्रादिनी ह्लादिनी तथा .. .. 167 ..
text_mt: consecrate you with waters that destroy all sins. / The holy Gaṅgā, the great river, and Hrādinī and Hlādinī,

sanskrit_iast:
pāvanī ca tathā sītā cakṣuḥ sindhuśca narmadā ..
suprabhā kātarākṣī ca śithilā mānasī hradā .. 168 ..
meaning:

Having received royal consecration into sovereignty over kings by these [sites and waters] as proclaimed, O king, / enjoy the whole earth together with its oceans, live long, and may your mind be exceedingly devoted to dharma.
2.23
Puṣkara said: / The mantras which have been recited by me in this [chapter] for you, O Rāma, Bhārgava— / their recitation is auspicious and destroys all sins.
A man who, rising at dawn, recites these, / freed from all sins, attains the heavenly world.
He does not go to animal wombs, nor to hell, nor to mixed castes; / nor does he suffer grief, fear, or delusion at death.
And the restrained man who makes obeisance to these, / sin does not cling to him, like a drop of water on a lotus.
Having bathed, with a restrained mind, and having offered water to them, / even one burdened by a grave sin is released, like a snake from its slough.
By offering flowers to them, he attains great fortune; / by offering guest-water to them, a person becomes worthy of honor.

text_mt:
By offering lamps to them, they shine like the moon in heaven; / having given an oblation to them, he obtains abundant desires.
Having offered food-offerings and oblations, he attains peerless enjoyments. / Dedicating [it] to them, having given food to brahmins, O Bhārgava,
and having satisfied them with sacrificial fees, he attains heaven for a long time. / On the day of royal consecration of kings, and at the flower-bath as well,
and on the knot of the year, all should be worshiped by one seeking well-being. / And whichever holy sites and rivers have been stated in brief,
by visiting them, even sinful people are purified. / Bathing in them brings great fruit, as do austerity, ancestor rites, and rituals.
Giving [gifts there] is said to bear great fruit; seeing them destroys sin; / [and so does] reciting [their names], O best of the Bhṛgus—there is no doubt in my mind.
Then, having bathed in these holy sites, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, men immediately attain [the status of] a king of men. / Therefore, with diligence, holy sites are to be visited, and all the holy rivers, O Rāma.

2.24
Rāma said: / What should be the very first duty of a king just consecrated? / Explain all this to me, since you know everything.
Puṣkara said: / With his head still wet from royal consecration, O lotus-eyed one, / the king must appoint assistants; [for] kingdom is established thereon.
Even an action that is rather small is difficult for one man / without assistance to perform; how then kingship, a great station?
Therefore, the king himself should choose assistants of noble birth, / heroic, of the highest caste, endowed with strength, and possessed of sacred learning,
endowed with beauty, character, excellence, and nobility, joined with patience, / capable of enduring hardship, filled with great enterprise, knowing dharma, and speaking kindly,
giving beneficial counsel, wise, devoted to their master, and desiring renown. / Such assistants he should employ in auspicious tasks.
Likewise, having recognized those who are devoid of virtues, the king himself / should assign them only to suitable duties, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

text_mt:
Of noble birth, accomplished in virtue, skilled in the science of archery, / proficient in training elephants and horses, gentle in their speech,
skilled in portents and the knowledge of omens, in finance, medicine, and healing, / in discerning the differences among men, and resolved in the sixfold policy,
grateful, heroic in action, patient of hardship, upright, / knowing the rules of troop-array tactics, distinguishing the valueless from the substantial—
a commander-in-chief should be appointed by kings, either a brahmin or a kṣatriya. / Tall, handsome, capable, sweet-spoken, and not arrogant,
and winning the hearts of all—such is ordained as the doorkeeper. / Speaking as instructed, astute, skilled in the languages of the regions,
learned in grammar, capable of enduring hardship, eloquent, speaking according to place and time, / understanding the place or time and whatever is advantageous for the ruler of the earth,
and speaking it out at the proper time—he should be the king's envoy. / Tall, well-built, heroic, firmly devoted, calm,
patient of hardship, beneficial, incorruptible, not cruel, / and firmly devoted to the king—such should be appointed by the king as guards.

all people employed in the kitchen should have cut hair and nails. / Impartial toward enemy and friend, skilled in the legal codes,

One who writes letters with proper headings, fully formed, aligned straight, and even— / such a scribe is held to be the best.
Skilled in diplomatic speech, proficient in all treatises, / stating much meaning with few words—such should be the scribe, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Knowing the essential nature of different men, tall, and free from greed— / such men should be employed in the judicial court as summoners of people.
People of such kind should likewise be appointed as the king's doorkeepers. / Knowing the classification of metals, cloth, and gems,
a discerner of the worthless and the valuable, ever incorruptible and pure, / skillful and vigilant—such is declared as the treasurer.

text_mt:
At all avenues of revenue and at all avenues of expenditure, / men equal to the treasurer should be appointed by the ruler of the earth.
One who has reached the further shore in the eight-limbed science of medicine, / incorruptible, righteous, and born of good family—such should be the physician.
He should be known as the teacher of life; his word should always be obeyed / out of affection by the earth-protector, O Rāma, just as it is by ordinary men.
Knowing the rules of elephant-training, expert in forest species, / and capable of enduring hardship—such a one is commended as the king's superintendent of elephants.
Endowed with these very qualities and especially self-controlled, / the king's elephant-rider is commended in all operations.
Knowing the rules of horse-training, having mastered their medical treatment, / and having a firm seat—such is commended as the earth-lord's superintendent of horses.
Incorruptible, heroic, wise, born of good family, / and zealous in all tasks—such is remembered, O Rāma, as the superintendent of the fort.

Knowing the rules of architecture, sure-handed, having overcome weariness, / far-sighted, and courageous—such is proclaimed as the master architect.
In weapons discharged by machines, hurled by hand, retained, and hurled-and-retained, / and in hand-to-hand combat, a master of weapons is desired to be skilled.
Women over fifty years of age, and men over seventy, / should be employed by the king in all tasks inside the inner apartments.
Elderly, knowing the true nature of their classes, and continually vigilant— / in the king's armory there should be one who is capable and zealous in duties.
The duties of kings are immeasurable, O descendant of the Bhṛgu race. / Having understood duties as high, low, and middling, O ruler of the earth,
he should assign men who are high, low, and middling [accordingly]. / The king would not meet with ruin through confusion of tasks.
Having recognized in an appointed man his devotion, learning, valor, strength, and family, / a livelihood should be established for his men by the ruler of the earth.
When discerning the differences between men, whose reliance is upon true reality alone, / men possessing the royal marks and knowing dharma—on them the king should depend.

text_mt:
Well-nourished servants, continually honored, / should be made assistants by the king who wishes to conquer the earth.
And the king should employ the well-supported men in duties according to their merit: / the most righteous in matters of dharma, and heroes in the work of battle.
[He should assign] the skilled to financial duties, and likewise the pure everywhere. / He should assign eunuchs to women, and the fierce to cruel tasks.
In matters of dharma, wealth, pleasure, and fear, O son of Bhṛgu, / the king should suitably employ those who have been tested by secret tests.
Having passed [the tests], he should employ agents in the elephant-forest according to their suitability; / he should appoint superintendents there to carefully seek out whatever occurs.
Such tasks and others must be carried out with effort, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / By no means is the loss of harsh instruments desirable for a king.
Those deeds of kings that must be accomplished through sin, O foremost of the Bhṛgus— / good men do not do them; therefore the king must maintain these [fierce men].

nor should he ever divide the quarters of his servants. / Weapon, fire, poison, serpents, and a sword on one side,
and bad servants on the other, O tiger among men! / Ever ascertaining their conduct by means of spies,
the king should honor the virtuous and punish the unprincipled. / Kings are perpetually declared to have spies as their eyes, O Rāma.
In one's own country and in foreign territory, he should always appoint as spies / men of good birth and character, discerning, incorruptible, and capable of enduring hardship,
not conspicuous to people, gentle, and unknown to one another: / merchants, those skilled in statecraft, astrologers, physicians,
and likewise in the guise of wandering ascetics the king should employ spies. / A king should not believe the report of a single spy.
Ascertaining the agreement of two, the king should then rely upon it, / provided that the two were not known to each other.

text_mt:
Therefore the king should diligently employ secret spies. / The root of the kingdom is just this: that the king has spies for his sight.
The king must also examine his spies with care. / The loyalty and disaffection of his servants, the merits and faults of the people,
and the discernment of good and bad deeds, O Rāma, / are all dependent upon spies for kings; he should always rely upon them.
"By what deed of mine are all people in the world pleased with me? / And by what do they become estranged?" This must be known by the ruler of the earth. / Everything that causes disaffection must be avoided with care.
For royal fortune arises from the affection of the people, O moon of the Bhārgava lineage; / therefore, foremost rulers of men must diligently cultivate affection among people on earth.
2.25 / Puṣkara said: / How royal dependents should conduct themselves, O Rāma, / that I shall tell you; listen as I speak.

text_mt:
A command must be carried out with all one's heart, to the best of one's ability, O son of Bhṛgu. / One must not speak words contradicting his words.
What is agreeable and pleasing to him should be spoken in public; / when he is in private, that which is beneficial, even if unpleasant, should be spoken.
On another's behalf, one should speak when his mind is at ease, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / One's own comfort should be spoken of by friends, but never by oneself.
Neglect of duty must be guarded against with effort through one's deeds, / and when appointed to a duty, one must not destroy any property.
His honor should not be disregarded; thus one becomes dear to the king. / One should not imitate the king's dress, speech, or gestures.
Royal sports must not be engaged in, and what is appointed for him must be avoided. / One who knows should not adopt dress that is equal or superior to the king's.
In gambling and the like, he should display his skill to him; / yet having displayed his skill, he should not surpass the king.

text_mt:
With superintendents of the inner quarters and of the treasury, with envoys of enemies, and with those who have been dismissed, / one must not associate, O Rāma, without the ruler's command.
He should conceal low desire and any disrespect directed at him; / and whatever is secret to the king, he should not disclose to the world.
What has been disclosed by the king as the secret of secrets, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / he should not make known to the world; thus he will become dear to the king.
When another is being commanded, one who knows should rise with haste / and say to the king: "What may I do?"
Having recognized the state of the task, this duty should be performed thus. / If this is done constantly, the wise man would incur contempt.
One should not repeat words pleasing to the king excessively again and again. / One should not be given to laughter, nor should one have a frowning face.
He should not speak too much, nor be completely silent, nor be envious; / and by no means should he be self-conceited.

text_mt:
One should never proclaim the misdeeds of the ruler of men. / One should wear the garment, badge of honor, and ornament given by the king;
it should not be given to another out of generosity by one who desires prosperity. / Nor should he interrupt the king while he is eating or sleeping.
One should never enter through an unauthorized door, / nor should one look upon the king in inappropriate places.
He should sit on the king's right side or on his left side; / but a seat in front or behind is condemned.
Yawning, spitting, desire, anger, leaning against a couch, / a crown, breaking wind, and belching should be avoided near him. / The wise man should likewise not proclaim his own virtues himself; / when proclaiming his own virtues, he should employ only others.
Having made their hearts pure and having resorted to supreme devotion, / the hosts of dependents of kings should always be unwearied.

text_mt:
Deceit, greed, malice, atheism, meanness, / and fickleness should always be abandoned by the king's dependent.
Having joined himself by himself with sacred learning, sciences, and crafts, / increasing [others'] awe, he should then serve the king for prosperity.
His sons, favorites, and ministers should always be saluted by him, / but he should never place trust in his ministers.
Unasked, he should not speak to him, though he may speak at will in misfortune; / along with well-wishers, he should speak well-ascertained words that are beneficial and salutary.
And his mind must always be known by the dependent; / a man who knows [his lord's] mind pleases his master with ease.
One who desires prosperity should also know his affection and disaffection; / he should abandon an alienated king, but seek his livelihood from an affectionate one.
He causes the ruin of work and benefit, and likewise the rise of adversaries; / having raised expectations, he causes the ruin of the fruit;

meaning:
अजाश्च धार्या यत्नेन तुरगाणां हितैषिणा ..
गोगजाश्वविशालासु तत्पुरीषस्य निष्क्रमम् .. 22 ..
text_mt: and goats should be kept with care by one wishing the welfare of horses. / In the spacious stalls of cows, elephants, and horses, the removal of their dung

sanskrit_iast:
astaṅgate na kartavyaṃ devadeve divākare ..
tatastatra yathānyāyaṃ rājā vijñāya sāravit .. 23 ..
meaning:
अस्तङ्गते न कर्तव्यं देवदेवे दिवाकरे ..
ततस्तत्र यथान्यायं राजा विज्ञाय सारवित् .. 23 ..
text_mt: should not be carried out after the sun, god of gods, has set. / Then there, in accordance with rule, having understood [matters], the king who knows the essential...

sanskrit_iast:
dadyādāvasathasthānaṃ sarveṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ ..
yodhānāṃ śilpināṃ caiva sarveṣāmaviśeṣataḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
दद्यादावसथस्थानं सर्वेषामनुपूर्वशः ..
योधानां शिल्पिनां चैव सर्वेषामविशेषतः .. 24 ..
text_mt: He should provide living quarters to all in succession, / to warriors and craftsmen alike, all without distinction.

sanskrit_iast:
dadyādāvasathāndurge mantrakālavidāṃ satāma ..
govaidyānaśvavaidyāṃśca gajavaidyāṃstathaiva ca .. 25 ..
meaning:
दद्यादावसथान्दुर्गे मन्त्रकालविदां सताम ..
गोवैद्यानश्ववैद्यांश्च गजवैद्यांस्तथैव च .. 25 ..
text_mt: In the fort he should assign quarters to virtuous men who know mantras and proper times, / and likewise to bovine doctors, horse doctors, and elephant doctors.

sanskrit_iast:
āhareta bhṛśaṃ rājā durge parabalārujaḥ ..
kuśīlavānāṃ viprāṇāṃ durge sthānaṃ vidhīyate .. .. 205 ..
meaning:
आहरेत भृशं राजा दुर्गे परबलारुजः ..
कुशीलवानां विप्राणां दुर्गे स्थानं विधीयते .. .. 205 ..
text_mt: The king who destroys enemy forces should gather them abundantly in the fortress. / A place in the fort is also prescribed for actors and brahmins,

sanskrit_iast:
na bahūnāṃ na tairdurgaṃ vinā kāryaṃ tathā bhavet ..
durge ca yantrāḥ kartavyā nānāpraharaṇānvitāḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
न बहूनां न तैर्दुर्गं विना कार्यं तथा भवेत् ..
दुर्गे च यन्त्राः कर्तव्या नानाप्रहरणान्विताः .. 27 ..
text_mt: yet not for many, nor can the business of the fort proceed without them. / And in the fort mechanical contrivances fitted with diverse weapons should be installed,

sanskrit_iast:
sahasraghātino rāma taistu rakṣā vidhīyate ..
durge dvārāṇi guptāni kāryāṇyapi ca bhūbhujā .. 28 ..
meaning:
सहस्रघातिनो राम तैस्तु रक्षा विधीयते ..
दुर्गे द्वाराणि गुप्तानि कार्याण्यपि च भूभुजा .. 28 ..
text_mt: capable of slaying a thousand [foes], O Rāma, for defense is maintained by them. / The king should also construct secret gates in the fortress.

sanskrit_iast:
sañcayaścātra sarveṣāṃ cāyudhānāṃ praśasyate ..
dhanuṣāṃ kṣepaṇīyānāṃ tomarāṇāṃ ca bhārgava .. 29 ..
meaning:
सञ्चयश्चात्र सर्वेषां चायुधानां प्रशस्यते ..
धनुषां क्षेपणीयानां तोमराणां च भार्गव .. 29 ..
text_mt: And here the stockpiling of all weapons is commended: / of bows, missiles, and spears, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

sanskrit_iast:
śarāṇāmatha khaḍgānāṃ khanakānāṃ tathaiva ca ..
laguḍānāṃ guḍānāṃ ca huḍānāṃ parighaiḥ saha .. 30 ..
meaning:
शराणामथ खड्गानां खनकानां तथैव च ..
लगुडानां गुडानां च हुडानां परिघैः सह .. 30 ..
text_mt: of arrows, swords, and digging tools, / of clubs, balls of stone, huḍas, along with iron bars,

sanskrit_iast:
aśmanāṃ ca prabhūtānāṃ mudgarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ..
kaṇiyānāṃ triśūlānāṃ paṭṭiśānāṃ ca bhārgava .. 31 ..
meaning:
अश्मनां च प्रभूतानां मुद्गराणां तथैव च ..
कणियानां त्रिशूलानां पट्टिशानां च भार्गव .. 31 ..
text_mt: of abundant stones and mallets, / of javelins, tridents, and two-edged axes, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

sanskrit_iast:
prāsānāṃ ca tsarūṇāṃ ca śaktīnāṃ ca narottama ..
paraśvadhānāṃ cakrāṇāṃ carmaṇāṃ carmabhiḥ saha .. 32 ..
meaning:
प्रासानां च त्सरूणां च शक्तीनां च नरोत्तम ..
परश्वधानां चक्राणां चर्मणां चर्मभिः सह .. 32 ..
text_mt: of barbed darts, sword-hilts, and spears, O best of men, / of battle-axes, discs, and shields along with pelts,

sanskrit_iast:
kuddālarajjuvetrāṇāṃ piṭikānāṃ tathaiva ca ..
hrasvakānāṃ ca pātrāṇāmagarasya ca saṃśrayama .. 33 ..
meaning:
कुद्दालरज्जुवेत्राणां पिटिकानां तथैव च ..
ह्रस्वकानां च पात्राणामगरस्य च संश्रयम .. 33 ..
text_mt: of spades, ropes, reeds, and baskets, / of small vessels, and store of agaru,

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣāṃ citrabhāṇḍānāṃ sañcayaścātra iṣyate ..
vāditrāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāmauṣadhānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 384 ..
meaning:
सर्वेषां चित्रभाण्डानां सञ्चयश्चात्र इष्यते ..
वादित्राणां च सर्वेषामौषधानां तथैव च .. 384 ..
text_mt: and the accumulation of all painted vessels is desired here, / as well as of all musical instruments and medicines,

sanskrit_iast:
yavasānāṃ prabhūtānāṃ cendhanasya ca sañcayam ..
guḍasya sarvaśailānāṃ gorasānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 39 ..
meaning:
यवसानां प्रभूतानां चेन्धनस्य च सञ्चयम् ..
गुडस्य सर्वशैलानां गोरसानां तथैव च .. 39 ..
text_mt: and a stockpile of abundant fodder and fuel, / of treacle, all varieties of stones, and dairy products,

sanskrit_iast:
carmaṇāṃ ca sasajjānāṃ snāyūnāmasthibhiḥ saha ..
gorasasya paṭānāṃ ca dhānyānāṃ sarvatastathā .. 36 ..
meaning:
चर्मणां च ससज्जानां स्नायूनामस्थिभिः सह ..
गोरसस्य पटानां च धान्यानां सर्वतस्तथा .. 36 ..
text_mt: and of well-prepared skins, sinews along with bones, / dairy products, cloth, and all kinds of grain on every side,

sanskrit_iast:
tathaiva prapaṭānāṃ ca yavagodhūmayorapi ..
ratnānāṃ sarvavastrāṇāṃ lohānāṃ cāpyaśeṣataḥ ..37 ..
meaning:
तथैव प्रपटानां च यवगोधूमयोरपि ..
रत्नानां सर्ववस्त्राणां लोहानां चाप्यशेषतः ..37 ..
text_mt: and likewise fine woven fabrics, barley, and wheat, / precious gems, all textiles, and every kind of metal,

sanskrit_iast:
kalāyamudgamāṣāṇāṃ caṇakānāṃ tilaiḥ saha ..
tathā ca sarvasasyānāṃ pāṃśugomayayorapi ..388...
meaning:
कलायमुद्गमाषाणां चणकानां तिलैः सह ..
तथा च सर्वसस्यानां पांशुगोमययोरपि ..388...
text_mt: peas, mudga beans, and māṣa beans, chickpeas along with sesame seeds, / as well as all crops, dust, and cow dung.

sanskrit_iast:
saṇasarjarasaṃ bhūrjajatulākṣākaṭaṃkaṭām ..
rājā sañcinuyāddurge yaccānyadapi kiñcana .. 39 ..
meaning:
सणसर्जरसं भूर्जजतुलाक्षाकटंकटाम् ..
राजा सञ्चिनुयाद्दुर्गे यच्चान्यदपि किञ्चन .. 39 ..
text_mt: Hemp, resin of the sal tree, birch bark, and lac: / whatever else there may be, the king should store it in the fort.

sanskrit_iast:
kumbhāḥ sāṣīviṣā dhāryā vyāghrasiṃhādayastathā ..
mṛgāśca pakṣiṇaścaiva paśavaśca pṛthagvidhāḥ ..4 0 ..
meaning:
कुम्भाः साषीविषा धार्या व्याघ्रसिंहादयस्तथा ..
मृगाश्च पक्षिणश्चैव पशवश्च पृथग्विधाः ..4 0 ..
text_mt: Pots filled with venomous snakes should be kept, as well as tigers, lions, and the like, / and wild beasts, birds, and animals of various kinds.

sanskrit_iast:
sañceyāni viruddhānāṃ suguptāni pṛthakpṛthaka ..
kartavyāni mahābhāga yatnena pṛthivīkṣitā .. 41 ..
meaning:
सञ्चेयानि विरुद्धानां सुगुप्तानि पृथक्पृथक ..
कर्तव्यानि महाभाग यत्नेन पृथिवीक्षिता .. 41 ..
text_mt: Separate, well-guarded stocks of hostile creatures / must be maintained with effort by the ruler of the earth, O illustrious one.

sanskrit_iast:
uktāni cāpyanuktāni rājadravyāṇyaśeṣataḥ ..
suguptāni pure kuryājjanānāṃ hita kāmyayā .. 42 ..
meaning:
उक्तानि चाप्यनुक्तानि राजद्रव्याण्यशेषतः ..
सुगुप्तानि पुरे कुर्याज्जनानां हित काम्यया .. 42 ..
text_mt: All royal goods, both spoken of and unspoken, / he should keep well-secured in the citadel out of a desire for the welfare of the people.

sanskrit_iast:
jīvakarṣabhakākolīrāmalakyaḥ parūṣakam ..
śāliparṇī pṛśniparṇī mudgaparṇī tathaiva ca .. 43 ..
meaning:
जीवकर्षभकाकोलीरामलक्यः परूषकम् ..
शालिपर्णी पृश्निपर्णी मुद्गपर्णी तथैव च .. 43 ..
text_mt: Jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, kākolī, raw āmalakī, parūṣaka, / śāliparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, and mudgaparṇī,

sanskrit_iast:
māṣaparṇī tathā caiva sārive dve balābhayama ..
vīrāśvagandhā vṛthvīkā bṛhatī kaṇṭakārikā ..44..
meaning:
माषपर्णी तथा चैव सारिवे द्वे बलाभयम ..
वीराश्वगन्धा वृथ्वीका बृहती कण्टकारिका ..44..
text_mt: māṣaparṇī, the two kinds of sārivā, balā, and abhayā, / vīrā, aśvagandhā, vṛthvīkā, bṛhatī, and kaṇṭakārikā,

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṅgāṭikā rodragodhī varṣābhūdarbhagundrakā ..
madhuparṇīvidāryau dve mahādurgā mahā tathā .. 45 ..
meaning:
शृङ्गाटिका रोद्रगोधी वर्षाभूदर्भगुन्द्रका ..
मधुपर्णीविदार्यौ द्वे महादुर्गा महा तथा .. 45 ..
text_mt: śṛṅgāṭikā, rodra, godhī, varṣābhū, darbha-grass, gundrā, / madhuparṇī, the two kinds of vidārī, mahādurgā, and mahā,

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvanā mahaṛgvyāhyā trikoṭī raṇḍakaṃ viṣam ..
parṇāsanāhvī mṛdvīkā phalguḥ kharjūrayaṣṭikā .. 46 ..
meaning:
धन्वना महऋग्व्याह्या त्रिकोटी रण्डकं विषम् ..
पर्णासनाह्वी मृद्वीका फल्गुः खर्जूरयष्टिका .. 46 ..
text_mt: dhanvanā, mahaṛgvyāhyā, trikoṭī, raṇḍaka, poison, / parṇāsanā, grapes, fig, and dates and liquorice,

sanskrit_iast:
śukrātiśukrakāśmaryaśchatrāticchatravīraṇā ..
ikṣurikṣuvikāraśca phāṇitādyāśca bhārgava .. 47 ..
meaning:
शुक्रातिशुक्रकाश्मर्यश्छत्रातिच्छत्रवीरणा ..
इक्षुरिक्षुविकारश्च फाणिताद्याश्च भार्गव .. 47 ..
text_mt: śukrā, atiśukrā, kāśmarya, chatrā, aticchatrā, vīraṇa-grass, / sugarcane, sugarcane products, molasses and the like, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

sanskrit_iast:
sahāśca sahadevāśca viśvedevāḍharūpakam ..
madhūkapuṣpaṃ haṃsākhyā śatapuṣpamadhūlikā .. 48 ..
meaning:
सहाश्च सहदेवाश्च विश्वेदेवाढरूपकम् ..
मधूकपुष्पं हंसाख्या शतपुष्पमधूलिका .. 48 ..
text_mt: sahā, sahadevā, viśvedevā, and aḍharūpaka, / madhūka blossoms, haṃsākhyā, dill, and madhūlikā,

sanskrit_iast:
śatāvarī madhūkaṃ ca priyālaṃ tālameva ca ..
ātmaguptā kaṭphalākhyā daradā rājaserukā ..49..
meaning:
शतावरी मधूकं च प्रियालं तालमेव च ..
आत्मगुप्ता कट्फलाख्या दरदा राजसेरुका ..49..
text_mt: śatāvarī, madhūka, priyāla, and the palmyra palm, / ātmaguptā, that known as kaṭphala, daradā, and rājaserukā,

sanskrit_iast:
rājarṣabhakadhānakyā ṛṣyaproktā tathotkaṭā ..
kaṭaṃkaṭā padmabījaṃ govallī madhuvallikā ..50 ..
meaning:
राजर्षभकधानक्या ऋष्यप्रोक्ता तथोत्कटा ..
कटंकटा पद्मबीजं गोवल्ली मधुवल्लिका ..50 ..
text_mt: rājarṣabhaka, dhānakyā, ṛṣyaproktā, and utkaṭā, / kaṭaṅkaṭā, lotus seeds, govallī, and madhuvallikā,

sanskrit_iast:
śītapākī kuliṅgākṣī kākajihvorupatrikā ..
ervārumrapasau cobhau muñjātakapunarnavā ..51 ..
meaning:
शीतपाकी कुलिङ्गाक्षी काकजिह्वोरुपत्रिका ..
एर्वारुम्रपसौ चोभौ मुञ्जातकपुनर्नवा ..51 ..
text_mt: śītapākī, kuliṅgākṣī, kākajihvā, urupatrikā, / cucumber and melon, muñjātaka, and punarnavā,

sanskrit_iast:
kāśerukā tugākṣīrā bilveśālūkakesaram ..
śūkadhānyāni sarvāṇi śambīdhānyāni yāni ca .. 52 ..
meaning:
काशेरुका तुगाक्षीरा बिल्वेशालूककेसरम् ..
शूकधान्यानि सर्वाणि शम्बीधान्यानि यानि च .. 52 ..
text_mt: kāśerukā, bamboo manna, bilva, lotus root and filaments, / all awned grains and pod-bearing legumes,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīraṃ kṣaudraṃ tathā śuklaṃ majjā tailaṃ vasā ghṛtama ..
nikocābhiṣukākṣoṭaṃ vātāpaṃ sorukhāṇakam .. 53 ..
meaning:
क्षीरं क्षौद्रं तथा शुक्लं मज्जा तैलं वसा घृतम ..
निकोचाभिषुकाक्षोटं वातापं सोरुखाणकम् .. 53 ..
text_mt: milk, honey, white sugar, marrow, oil, fat, and clarified butter, / pistachios, walnuts, almonds, and dried fruits:

sanskrit_iast:
evamādīni cānyāni vijñeyo madhuro gaṇaḥ ..
rājā sañcinuyātsarvaṃ pure niravaśeṣataḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
एवमादीनि चान्यानि विज्ञेयो मधुरो गणः ..
राजा सञ्चिनुयात्सर्वं पुरे निरवशेषतः .. 54 ..
text_mt: these and others are to be known as the group of sweet substances. / The king should collect all of them in the fortress without remainder.

sanskrit_iast:
dāḍimāṃmrātakāṃ līnaṃ titantiḍīkāmlavetasam ..
bhavyakaḥ kaṇḍalīkaśca makarandakarūpakam ..55..
meaning:
दाडिमांम्रातकां लीनं तितन्तिडीकाम्लवेतसम् ..
भव्यकः कण्डलीकश्च मकरन्दकरूपकम् ..55..
text_mt: Pomegranates, hog-plums, sour tamarind, cane sorrel, / bhavya, kaṇḍalīka, makaranda, and karūpaka,

sanskrit_iast:
bījapūrakakāṇḍīramālatī rājadhanvanā ..
kolakadvayaparṇāni dvayorallīkayorapi..56..
meaning:
बीजपूरककाण्डीरमालती राजधन्वना ..
कोलकद्वयपर्णानि द्वयोरल्लीकयोरपि..56..
text_mt: citron, kāṇḍīra, mālatī, rājadhanvanā, / leaves of the two jujubes, and of the two allīkas,

sanskrit_iast:
pālevataṃ bhāgarikaṃ prācīnārūkameva ca ..
kapitthāmalakaṃ cukraṃ kalindaṃ ca śaṭhasya ca..57..
meaning:
पालेवतं भागरिकं प्राचीनारूकमेव च ..
कपित्थामलकं चुक्रं कलिन्दं च शठस्य च..57..
text_mt: pālevata, bhāgarika, prācīnā, peach, / wood-apple, āmalaka, sour gruel, kalinda, and śaṭha,

sanskrit_iast:
jāmbavaṃ navanītaṃ ca sauvīrakatupocake ..
surāsavaṃ ca madyāni maṇḍaṃ takradadhīni ca .. 58 ..
meaning:
जाम्बवं नवनीतं च सौवीरकतुपोचके ..
सुरासवं च मद्यानि मण्डं तक्रदधीनि च .. 58 ..
text_mt: rose apple, fresh butter, sauvīraka, and tupocaka, / liquor, distilled spirits, wine, scum of boiled rice, buttermilk, and curds,

sanskrit_iast:
śuklāni caiva sarvāṇi jñeyānyamlagaṇāni vai ..
saindhavodbhedanādeyapākyasāmudrarocasam ..
kūpyasauvarcalaviḍaṃ vālakailopabāhukam .. 59 ..
meaning:
शुक्लानि चैव सर्वाणि ज्ञेयान्यम्लगणानि वै ..
सैन्धवोद्भेदनादेयपाक्यसामुद्ररोचसम् ..
कूप्यसौवर्चलविडं वालकैलोपबाहुकम् .. 59 ..
text_mt: and all white sours are to be known as the sour group. / Rock salt, efflorescent salt, river salt, cooked salt, sea salt, rocasa, / well-salt, sochal salt, black salt, and the salts called vālaka and ailopabāhuka,

sanskrit_iast:
ūṣakṣāraṃ kālabhasma vijñeyau lāvaṇo gaṇaḥ ..
evamādīni cānyāni rājā sañcinuyātpure .. 60 ..
meaning:
ऊषक्षारं कालभस्म विज्ञेयौ लावणो गणः ..
एवमादीनि चान्यानि राजा सञ्चिनुयात्पुरे .. 60 ..

Long pepper, long pepper root, chavya, plumbago, and dry ginger, / kuṭheraka, along with black pepper, horseradish tree, marking-nut—the king [should maintain] the fort well-secured at all times.
Rāma said: / Tell me, O best of the upholders of dharma, / of those antidotes that destroy demons and counteract poisons, which the king must employ.
Puṣkara said: / Bilva, āḍhakī, barley alkali, pāṭalī, bāhlika, and black pepper, / combined with śrīparṇī and frankincense: this decoction is the supreme sprinkling.
Whatever is poisoned, when sprinkled with it, immediately becomes free of poison: / barley, rock salt, drinking water, wealth, bed, seat, cooked rice,
armor, ornaments, umbrellas, and hair fly-whisks. / Śailū, pāṭalī, ativiṣā, śigru, gopī, punarnavā,
tree-root bark with saṅgā, wood-apple, resinous sap, / along with danta and śaṭha: a similar sprinkling is destructive of poison.
Lac, priyaṅgu, Indian madder, samaṅgā, along with reṇukā, / combined with liquorice and incense, ground into a paste with brown mongoose bile:

One should bury [the paste] placed inside a cow's horn in the earth for seven nights. / Then, having made an amulet mounted in gold, one should wear it on the arm.
One afflicted with poison becomes free from poison at once when touched by it. / Realgar, orpiment, śamī flowers, cinnamon bark, turmeric, and white mustard;
Wood-apple, kuṣṭha, and madder, finely ground into a paste with bile / from a brown-speckled cow—this antidote, called Saumya, was spoken of of old.
It is declared to be the supreme conqueror of poison, and here too an amulet [is prepared] as before. / Also mūṣakājīrakā, bound on the arm, removes poison.
Hareṇu, māṣī, madder, turmeric, liquorice, honey, / bibhītaka bark, holy basil, [...] dog bile in an amulet as before.
Musical instruments and banners smeared with these substances / make one instantly free from poison upon hearing, seeing, or touching them.

No insects, no poisonous creatures, no frogs, and no reptiles, / no sorceries, nor any other hostile rites [persist] where this incense is burnt.
With pastes of sandalwood, kṣīrī, and the barks of the palāśa tree, / and the aforesaid elavālu, holy basil, nākulī, and taṇḍulīyaka,

2.28
Rāma said: / The secrets of kingly protection that should be deposited in a fortress, / or caused to be performed by the lord of the earth—tell me those quickly.
Puṣkara said: / Śirīṣa, udumbara, śamī, and citron, flooded with ghee— / this hunger-suppressing formula lasting half a month was declared by the ancients, O Rāma.
Roots of kaśeru, roots of utpala, and sugarcane root, likewise bimbī; / a paste prepared with dūrvā, milk, and ghee is supreme, lasting a month.
Having obtained a man impaled on a stake, a fire-drill should be made of his bone; / one should generate fire there with a bamboo of variegated hue.
Where that is carried counter-clockwise three times around a house, O Bhārgava, / no other fire burns there; no doubt should be entertained on this point.

Cotton-seeds and the supreme slough of a snake— / this is praised as a constant incense in the house for expelling snakes.
Clay dense in substance and aged, struck by lightning— / a house smeared with that is not burnt by fire, O twice-born.
Fire should be guarded against by day in the fortress, especially when the wind blows; / and the king must be protected from poison—hear from me the technique in that regard.
Beasts and birds should be kept for the entertainment of the king. / And food should first be tested in fire, and then upon men.
Garments, leaves, ornaments, as well as food and bed coverings— / the lord of the earth should not even touch anything before it has been tested.
With a dark, livid face and distressed, he looks around anxiously; / where poison has been administered, the poisoner keeps casting his gaze around.

पवनश्च महाभागाः पूर्वेणैते प्रकीर्तिताः ..
पुष्योऽथ त्रितुदश्चैव तथैव च ग्रहर्क्षतः .. 26 ..
यमो भृशश्च गन्धर्वो मृगोऽथ पितरस्तथा ..

दौवारिकश्च सुग्रीवः पुष्पदंतस्तथा सुरः ..

text_mt:
Eight deities are assigned to each of the cardinal and intermediate directions. / The first and the last of them, moreover, are proclaimed lords of the planets. / Parjanya is the first deity, and the second is Karagraha, / and then Mahendra, Ravi, Satya, Bhṛśa, and Gamana;
and Pavana, O fortunate ones, are declared on the east. / Then Puṣya and Trituda, and likewise Graharkṣata,
Yama, Bhṛśa, Gandharva, Mṛga, and the Pitṛs / are the deities assigned on the south, O scion of the Bhṛgu lineage.
Dauvārika, Sugrīva, Puṣpadanta, the god [Asura], / Varuṇa, Yakṣa, Roga, and Śoṣa:
[these] are the deities assigned on the west, destroyers of the Dānavas. / Then Nāgarāja, Mukhya, Bhallāṭa, Śaśin,
Aditi, Kubera, Nāga, and Hutāśana: / these are the deities assigned on the north, O twice-born.
One should construct doors precisely in the divisions of these deities; / I will tell you the auspicious ones among them, and one should avoid the rest.

चत्वारिंशद्विनिर्दिष्टास्तथा पञ्च च भार्गव ..
विन्यस्याजिरमेवादौ चतुष्षष्टिपदं द्विज .. 35 ..
तत्र देवविभागेन गृहकर्म विधीयते ..
चन्द्रसुग्रीवपर्जन्यसत्येन्द्रार्यमवारुणे .. 36 ..

सूर्यान्तरिक्षसत्याग्निभागेषु च महानसम् .. 37 ..
वाय्वन्तरिक्षसुग्रीवभल्लाटपितृदैवते ..
गंधर्वपुष्पदन्ताख्ये भागे कूपं तु कारयेत् .. 38 ..
text_mt:
Those sacred to Mahendra and Soma on the east are traditionally taught as bestowing good fortune. / On the south, [those sacred to] Gṛharkṣata and Puṣpa are auspicious.
On the west, O twice-born, [those of] Sugrīva and Puṣpadanta are auspicious; / and on the north, Bhallāṭa and the god Soma are best for a door.
Thirty-two are recorded as the outer deities, and twelve as the inner. / In the centre, Brahmā is proclaimed: thus are the deities of the site.
Forty-five [deities] in all are specified, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / First laying out the courtyard [as a grid of] sixty-four squares, O twice-born,
house construction is undertaken there according to the allocation of deities. / In [the divisions of] Candra, Sugrīva, Parjanya, Satya, Indra, Aryaman, and Vāruṇa,
one should make the sanctuary of the Lord according to his placement, O twice-born. / And in the divisions of Sūrya, Antarikṣa, Satya, and Agni [one should make] the kitchen.
In the divisions sacred to Vāyu, Antarikṣa, Sugrīva, Bhallāṭa, and the Pitṛs, / and in that named after Gandharva and Puṣpadanta, one should make a well.

text_mt:
one should not obstruct them with pegs and the like, O twice-born. / Trees that are entwined with banyan trees, and those that have hollows,
those struck by elephants or lightning, and those that grow in temples, / those touched by fire, and those grown in cremation grounds or at crossroads,
and any diseased trees—none of these is ever praised. / Having performed great worship of the tree and of its inhabitant,
the twice-born should cut it with an axe smeared with honey and clarified butter. / Falling toward the northeast is proclaimed most commendable;
falling in the remaining directions is censured, O best of the twice-born. / Banyan, aśvattha, nirguṇḍī, kovidāra, vibhītaka,
puṣyaka, śālmali, and palāśa should be avoided. / In a house, the door should be made twice as high as its width.
[A door] decorated with the foremost of treasures, serpents, haṃsas, and sārasas / [is auspicious]. A doorway [encroached upon] by a sewer, clouds, a crossroad, a temple,
pierced by a well, a solitary tree, or a street, one should avoid. / Leaving ground equal to twice the height of the house, it incurs no fault.

text_mt:
[A door] that is swollen, leaning, O Rāma, or flooded with water— / such a door they do not praise; therefore one should avoid it.
Larger than the town gate, it bestows prosperity, as does a water drain in its [proper] divisions. / The treasury is prescribed in the divisions of Kubera.
One should make a door elsewhere in [the divisions of] Indra, Satyendra, or Sugrīva. / Dividing a pillar into nine parts, one should assign one part to the base.
In one part a pot should be made; in one part one should place a lotus. / The shaft of the pillar should be made in three parts, octagonal or circular;
above it, in one part, is the āmalasāraka. / At the bracket part a beam is to be made, and in one part an upper beam.
A single-winged and a four-winged [house] should always be made at will. / A two-winged [house] should be made lacking the eastern and northern wings;
otherwise, O Rāma, it is censured and considered to cause the loss of sons and wealth. / One should not make a storey exceeding eight cubits in height.

sanskrit_iast:

तथारोहणनिष्पत्ती तथा वास्तुप्रवेशनम् ..
सर्वाण्येतानि कार्याणि दिवसे राम पूजिते ..62..
शेषेष्वेतेषु कर्तव्यं देवब्राह्मणपूजनम् ..

कृष्णपक्षत्रिभागान्ते शुक्लाद्ये च भृगूत्तम .. 64 ..
तिथिं चतुर्थी नवमीं वर्जयेच्च चतुर्दशीम् ..
अङ्गारकदिनं राम करणं विष्टिसंज्ञितम् .. 65 ..
दिव्यान्तरिक्षक्षितिजैरुत्पातैर्भं च पीडितम् ..

text_mt:
The height of the building should not exceed one hundred cubits. / The commencement, the laying of the stone, the erection of both the door and the pillars,
the roofing, the completion, and likewise the entrance into the house— / all these, O Rāma, should be performed on an auspicious day.
In the remainder of these, one must perform the worship of the gods and brahmins, / and the worship of the astrologer and the master builders, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Building work must not be undertaken by a wise person during the rainy season, / at the end of the third part of the dark fortnight, or at the beginning of the bright, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
One should avoid the fourth, ninth, and fourteenth lunar days, / Tuesday, Rāma, and the division of the day called Viṣṭi;
And a constellation afflicted by portents originating in the heavens, the atmosphere, or on earth, / touched by malefics, or struck by Vyatīpāta.
When the constellation is favorable to one's Moon and birth star, the wise should undertake building work. / The fixed [constellations] are auspicious, as well as the asterisms of Indra and Nirṛti;

सौम्यं च वैष्णवं पुष्यं पौष्णं सावित्रमेव च ..

अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि शिलान्यासविधिं तव ..

गन्धार्धपुष्प नैवेद्यधूपदीपैर्भृगूत्तम .. 73 ..

text_mt:
And Saumya, Vaiṣṇava, Puṣya, Pauṣṇa, and Sāvitra; / in a fixed ascendant, in a fixed navāṃśa, and one that is an upacaya house for the builder.
When benefic planets are in a center and a trine for him, O Bhārgava, / and malefics are in an upacaya position, entry into [the house] should be performed at that [time].
One should avoid a malefic in a center with every effort in all rites; / a center should have a benefic, O king, and never be empty.
After this, I shall explain to you the ritual of laying the foundation stones. / Having made a diagram of sixty-four squares on an even ground,
and having performed the ritual placement of the deities on that small diagram, O twice-born, / and having worshiped Śrī and then also Vāsudeva,
worship of the host of house deities should be performed on the sacred diagram / with perfumes, unbroken grains, flowers, food-offerings, incense, and lamps, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Having performed their worship and taken up the fire, / one should offer clarified butter preceded by the syllable Om to the bearer of Śrī;

text_mt:
then having made an oblation to Śrī, one should then make [an oblation] to Brahmā; / and placing Brahmā at the head, to the host of house deities
clarified butter must be offered, O knower of dharma. For whichever deity the oblation is being made, / if an inauspicious mark appears in the fire at that time, O best of the twice-born,
at the place belonging to that deity one should designate an extraneous bone. / The removal of that bone should be performed with effort by the wise [builder], O Rāma.
In the middle, the wise one should set up a stone jar and a gnomon, / and then first consecrate the stone in the north-eastern corner.
Then, O Rāma, the ritual placement of the stones is prescribed in a clockwise direction. / Then the bathing of the jar and of the stones is prescribed,
with a decoction of banyan and sacred fig, and then with water containing all medicinal herbs; / then anointing should be done with fragrant sandalwood.
Then covering must be done with garments and auspicious flowers; / one should present incense, lamps, and food-offerings to them, O Rāma.

text_mt:
Then the worship of the foremost brahmins with sacrificial fees is prescribed; / then the astrologer and the architect must be worshiped by the wise one, O Rāma.
Then the patron himself, the astrologer, and the architect should chant the mantra / that brings prosperity to the house, O Rāma, which issued from the mouth of the sage:
"O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, bring joy along with treasures and offspring! / O Jayā, bringer of victory, O goddess, bring victory to my progeny!
O Pūrṇā, heiress of Aṅgiras, make my desire fulfilled! / O Bhadrā, heiress of Kaśyapa, make my mind auspicious!
Furnished with all kinds of seeds, surrounded by all gems and medicinal herbs, / delightful, pleasing, O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, take delight here!
O goddess, daughter of Prajāpati, four-cornered, made of earth, / fortunate, of good vows, auspicious, O daughter of Kaśyapa, take delight in this house!
Worshiped by the supreme teachers, adorned with perfumes and garlands, / causing growth and prosperity, O goddess, O daughter of Bhṛgu, take delight in this house!

2.30 Puṣkara said: / To the north, a plakṣa tree is auspicious; a banyan tree to the east, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / an udumbara tree to the south, and a sacred fig tree to the north.
These arising to the south and other [wrong directions] are not desired in their order; / and similarly, thorny trees that have grown nearby should be avoided.
Likewise, one should make an auspicious garden on the left side of the dwelling house. / One should first sow sesame seeds there and crush them when they have flowered;
then, purified and concentrated in mind, having bathed, / having worshiped the tree, the brahmins, and Śiva, one should plant trees.
The five fixed asterisms, Vāyavya, Hasta, Puṣya, along with Vaiṣṇava, / and Mūla are recommended for the planting of trees.
When a garden with water is not charming, O Rāma, / then one should not introduce […], and one should construct water reservoirs.
