Spring water should be purified, and wells should be made with effort / under Hasta, Maghā, Maitra, Saumya, Puṣya, and Vāsava.
The three Uttarās, O Rāma, and Pūrvaphalgunī,
and Vāruṇa [Śatabhiṣaj] are commended at the commencement of a reservoir.
Having worshipped the god Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, and Parjanya,
and having gratified the twice-born with desirable gifts, one should undertake its commencement.
Now I shall tell of the trees commended in a park, O twice-born:
ariṣṭa, aśoka, punnāga, śirīṣa, mango, and priyaṅgu,
panasa, aśoka, kadalī, jambū, lakuca, and pomegranate—
auspicious, these should first be planted in a garden or in houses.
Having made these abundant, all others may indeed be planted thereafter,
avoiding śālmali, kovidāra, and vibhītaka,
asana, devadāru, palāśa, and puṣkara.
However, one who knows should not avoid any tree in divine groves.
Even there, a multitude of auspicious ones should be made, O best of the twice-born.

and in the rainy season when the ground dries up, the planted trees should be watered.
Twenty cubits apart is best, sixteen cubits interval is middling;
twelve [cubits] between one spot and another is the minimum distance to be made for trees.
Trees that have grown close together, touching one another,
become fruitless because their roots are indistinguishably intermingled, O twice-born.
When disease arises among them, hear the treatment, O Rāma.
First, one should perform a cleansing on them a little with an instrument;
smeared with viḍaṅga, ghee, and mud, one should sprinkle them with cool water.
In case of failure of fruit, watering with boiled and cooled milk with kulattha, māṣa,
mudga, sesame, and barley is always [effective] for fruit and flowers.
Powder of sheep and goat dung, barley meal, and sesame seeds,
beef, and water—one should let these sit for seven nights.
This watering promotes fruit, flowers, and growth for all trees.

And sprinkled with fish-water, branches grow.
Then I shall describe in principal detail the pregnancy cravings of trees.
Watering mango trees with cool fish-water is desired.
Likewise, it should be done in that manner for grapevines, O destroyer of foes;
and cooked blood is commended for pomegranates.
Chaff should be given to bhavyas, and wine to the bakula tree,
especially that which has virtue from contact with the mouth of a lovely woman.
And the kick of a lovely woman's foot is commended for aśoka trees;
jackal-meat broth is beneficial for orange and walnut trees.
Licorice water is commended for jujube trees,
and scented water and beef are commended for katakas.
By watering with milk, the saptaparṇa becomes beautiful;
watering with flesh-cleansed fat and marrow is beneficial for the kurabaka.
Putrid fish, ghee, and rotting cotton fruits—
this watering is commended for arimeda and for trumpet flowers.

sanskrit_iast:
asminnapi tathā loke prāpnoti ca parābhavam ..
pālayanti mahīṃ devāḥ pūjitāḥ pṛthivīkṣitā .. 4 ..
meaning:
अस्मिन्नपि तथा लोके प्राप्नोति च पराभवम् ..
पालयन्ति महीं देवाः पूजिताः पृथिवीक्षिता .. 4 ..
text_mt:
In this world too, he meets with defeat.
The gods, worshipped by the ruler of the earth, protect the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
daivāyattamidaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtalaṃ dvijapuṅgava ..
dhūpadīpanamaskārapuṣpamālyānulepanaiḥ .. 5 ..
meaning:
दैवायत्तमिदं सर्वं भूतलं द्विजपुङ्गव ..
धूपदीपनमस्कारपुष्पमाल्यानुलेपनैः .. 5 ..
text_mt:
This entire surface of the earth depends on fate, O bull among the twice-born.
With incense, lamps, salutations, flowers, garlands, ointments,

sanskrit_iast:
ratnānusampradānaiśca pūjanīyāḥ surottamāḥ ..
pūjitāḥ pūjayantyete cāyuṣā yaśasā śriyā .. 6 ..
meaning:
रत्नानुसम्प्रदानैश्च पूजनीयाः सुरोत्तमाः ..
पूजिताः पूजयन्त्येते चायुषा यशसा श्रिया .. 6 ..
text_mt:
and gifts of jewels, the foremost gods are to be worshipped.
When worshipped, they honor [him] with long life, renown, and fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
prāpyate devatābhaktyā cānuṣṭhāne mahatpadam ..
pūjitāḥ saṃprayacchanti kāmānnṛṇāmabhīpsitān .. 7 ..
meaning:
प्राप्यते देवताभक्त्या चानुष्ठाने महत्पदम् ..
पूजिताः संप्रयच्छन्ति कामान्नृणामभीप्सितान् .. 7 ..
text_mt:
Through devotion to the deities in ritual practice, a high station is attained;
when worshipped, they grant mortals their wished-for desires.

sanskrit_iast:
ekamapyāśrito devaṃ rājā bhārgavanandana ..
sarvāsāṃ pūjanaṃ kuryāddevatānāmasaṃśayam ..8 ..
meaning:
एकमप्याश्रितो देवं राजा भार्गवनन्दन ..
सर्वासां पूजनं कुर्याद्देवतानामसंशयम् ..8 ..
text_mt:
Even if devoted to one deity, O son of Bhṛgu,
the king should undoubtedly worship all deities.

sanskrit_iast:
devatānāṃ na cocchindyātpūrvadāyaṃ kathañcana ..
prāksthitaṃ tanna cocchiṃdyānna ca cchiṃdyāttathā navam .. 9 ..
meaning:
देवतानां न चोच्छिन्द्यात्पूर्वदायं कथञ्चन ..
प्राक्स्थितं तन्न चोच्छिंद्यान्न च च्छिंद्यात्तथा नवम् .. 9 ..
text_mt:
And he must never cut off an earlier endowment of the deities;
he should not revoke what was established previously, nor should he cut off a new one.

sanskrit_iast:
tacchettā narakaṃ yāti saha pūrvaiḥ pitāmahaiḥ ..
api svalpaṃ na hartavyaṃ devadravyaṃ vijānatā .. 10 ..
meaning:
तच्छेत्ता नरकं याति सह पूर्वैः पितामहैः ..
अपि स्वल्पं न हर्तव्यं देवद्रव्यं विजानता .. 10 ..
text_mt:
One who cuts it off goes to hell together with his former ancestors;
one who knows should not seize property of the gods, even if very little,

sanskrit_iast:
svalpasyāpi phalaṃ ghoraṃ yasmājjanmāntare bhavet ..
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca .. 11 ..
meaning:
स्वल्पस्यापि फलं घोरं यस्माज्जन्मान्तरे भवेत् ..
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि षष्टिवर्षशतानि च .. 11 ..
text_mt:
since even for a little there will be a terrible fruition in another birth.
For sixty thousand years and six hundred years

sanskrit_iast:
devadravyāpaharaṇānnarakaṃ pratipadyate ..
santīha devatāḥ saumyāḥ santyugrāścāpi bhārgava .. 12 ..
meaning:
देवद्रव्यापहरणान्नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ..
सन्तीह देवताः सौम्याः सन्त्युग्राश्चापि भार्गव .. 12 ..
text_mt:
one falls into hell because of stealing the property of the gods.
There are gentle deities here, and there are also fierce ones, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast:
darśayanti ruṣaṃ saumya rājyabhraṃśādibhirnṛṇām ..
asmim̐lloke ruṣaṃ krūrāṃ naiva kurvanti devatāḥ .. 13 ..
meaning:
दर्शयन्ति रुषं सौम्य राज्यभ्रंशादिभिर्नृणाम् ..
अस्मिम्̐ल्लोके रुषं क्रूरां नैव कुर्वन्ति देवताः .. 13 ..
text_mt:
Gentle deities show anger toward men through loss of kingdom and the like;
the deities do not display cruel anger in this world.

sanskrit_iast:
tāsāṃ vittāpaharaṇādrājā narakamṛcchati ..
pūrvaiḥ pitāmahaissārdhaṃ prāguktaṃ phalameva tu .. 14 ..
meaning:
तासां वित्तापहरणाद्राजा नरकमृच्छति ..
पूर्वैः पितामहैस्सार्धं प्रागुक्तं फलमेव तु .. 14 ..
text_mt:
Because of stealing their wealth, a king goes to hell
together with his former ancestors, reaping the very fruit spoken of earlier.

sanskrit_iast:
devadravyāpaharaṇaṃ naiva jātu bhavedvṛthā ..
sarvasvarahitānkṛtvā devadravyāpahāriṇaḥ .. 15 ..
meaning:
देवद्रव्यापहरणं नैव जातु भवेद्वृथा ..
सर्वस्वरहितान्कृत्वा देवद्रव्यापहारिणः .. 15 ..
text_mt:
Stealing the property of the gods never goes without effect.
Having deprived those who steal the property of the gods of all their possessions,

sanskrit_iast:
aṅkayitvā dvijaśreṣṭha svarāṣṭrādvipravāsayet ..
traividyā vaṇijo vaiśyā liṅgino devapālakāḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
अङ्कयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठ स्वराष्ट्राद्विप्रवासयेत् ..
त्रैविद्या वणिजो वैश्या लिङ्गिनो देवपालकाः .. 16 ..
text_mt:
and having branded them, O best of the twice-born, he should banish them from his kingdom.
Scholars of the three Vedas, traders, vaiśyas, ascetics, guardians of temples,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā tatpratibaddhāśca na kuryuḥ kalahaṃ mithaḥ ..
teṣāṃ sahāyakaḥ svāmī nigrahānugrahī bhavet .. 17 ..
meaning:
तथा तत्प्रतिबद्धाश्च न कुर्युः कलहं मिथः ..
तेषां सहायकः स्वामी निग्रहानुग्रही भवेत् .. 17 ..
text_mt:
and those connected with them should not quarrel among themselves;
the ruler should be their helper, meting out punishment and favor.

sanskrit_iast:
rāgadveṣaviyuktastu vivāsyaścānyathā bhavet ..
daṇḍaṃ ca devatāgāmi devadravyasya sūcakam .. 18 ..
meaning:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तस्तु विवास्यश्चान्यथा भवेत् ..
दण्डं च देवतागामि देवद्रव्यस्य सूचकम् .. 18 ..
text_mt: Free from passion and hatred, however, one should exile [them], or otherwise [punish them]; / and a fine for an informer regarding the property of a deity goes to that deity.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvānvivāsayedrājā dhārmiko dharmakāraṇāt ..
rājñā sarvaprayatnena pālanīyāḥ surālayāḥ .. 19 ..
meaning:
सर्वान्विवासयेद्राजा धार्मिको धर्मकारणात् ..
राज्ञा सर्वप्रयत्नेन पालनीयाः सुरालयाः .. 19 ..
text_mt: A righteous king should exile all [such wrongdoers] for the sake of dharma. / By the king, with every effort, the temples of the gods must be protected.

sanskrit_iast:
kartavyāśca mahābhāga suralokamabhīpsatā ..
devatāstu pratiṣṭhāpya tallokaṃ dhruvamāpnuyāta .. 20 ..
meaning:
कर्तव्याश्च महाभाग सुरलोकमभीप्सता ..
देवतास्तु प्रतिष्ठाप्य तल्लोकं ध्रुवमाप्नुयात .. 20 ..
text_mt: And they should be built, O fortunate one, by one desiring the world of the gods. / Having consecrated deities, he surely attains their world.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā devagṛhaṃ śubhraṃ svargamāpnotyanuttamam ..
tadā bhogapramāṇena lakṣmīstatrāpi bhārgava .. 21 ..
meaning:
कृत्वा देवगृहं शुभ्रं स्वर्गमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ..
तदा भोगप्रमाणेन लक्ष्मीस्तत्रापि भार्गव .. 21 ..
text_mt: Having made a bright temple for a god, he attains unsurpassed heaven. / Then, in proportion to his enjoyment, royal fortune [comes] there also, O Bhārgava.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛtprāsādāddaśaguṇaṃ sthūladārukṛte bhavet ..
phalaṃ daśaguṇaṃ tasmāttathā pakveṣṭakākṛte .. 22 ..
meaning:
मृत्प्रासादाद्दशगुणं स्थूलदारुकृते भवेत् ..
फलं दशगुणं तस्मात्तथा पक्वेष्टकाकृते .. 22 ..
text_mt: Tenfold the fruit of an earthen temple is obtained from one made of thick wood; / tenfold the fruit from that, likewise, from one made of baked bricks;

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāddaśaguṇaṃ śaile nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
yāvatsaṃkhyaṃ naraḥ kuryāddevaveśma sudhāsitam .. 23 ..
meaning:
तस्माद्दशगुणं शैले नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
यावत्संख्यं नरः कुर्याद्देववेश्म सुधासितम् .. 23 ..
text_mt: tenfold from that for a stone one; no doubt should be entertained on this point. / For as many years as a man whitewashes the temple of a god with lime,

sanskrit_iast:
tāvajjanmāntarāṇīha yaśasā sa virājate ..
kṛtvā ca citravinyāsaṃ gandharvaiḥ saha modate .. 24 ..
meaning:
तावज्जन्मान्तराणीह यशसा स विराजते ..
कृत्वा च चित्रविन्यासं गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते .. 24 ..
text_mt: for so many future births in this world he shines with renown. / And having painted pictures [there], he rejoices with the Gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā saṃśodhanaṃ tatra virogaḥ samapadyate ..
prokṣayitvā manastāpānmānavaḥ pratimucyate .. 25 ..
meaning:
कृत्वा संशोधनं तत्र विरोगः समपद्यते ..
प्रोक्षयित्वा मनस्तापान्मानवः प्रतिमुच्यते .. 25 ..
text_mt: Having performed a cleansing there, he becomes free of disease. / Having sprinkled it [with water], a human being is freed from mental anguish.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvopalepanaṃ rāma nākamāpnotyanuttamam ..
gāndharvalokamāpnoti kṛtvā varṇakarañjitam .. 26 ..
meaning:
कृत्वोपलेपनं राम नाकमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ..
गान्धर्वलोकमाप्नोति कृत्वा वर्णकरञ्जितम् .. 26 ..
text_mt: Having performed plastering, O Rāma, he attains unsurpassed heaven. / Having coloured it with paints, he reaches the world of the Gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast:
gandhaiḥ samukṣitaṃ kṛtvā gandharvaissaha modate ..
upakārapradānena śriyamāpnotyanuttamām .. 27 ..
meaning:
गन्धैः समुक्षितं कृत्वा गन्धर्वैस्सह मोदते ..
उपकारप्रदानेन श्रियमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् .. 27 ..
text_mt: Having sprinkled it with perfumes, he rejoices with the Gandharvas. / By offering assistance, he attains unsurpassed splendor.

sanskrit_iast:
gītavādyapradānena sukhamāpnotyanuttamam ..
prekṣaṇīyapradānena rūpavānabhijāyate .. 28 ..
meaning:
गीतवाद्यप्रदानेन सुखमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ..
प्रेक्षणीयप्रदानेन रूपवानभिजायते .. 28 ..
text_mt: By offering singing and instrumental music, he attains unsurpassed happiness. / By presenting a theatrical spectacle, he is reborn handsome,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā aujjvalyamāpnoti yatrayatrābhijāyate ..
snāpayitvā ghṛtenārcāṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 29 ..
meaning:
तथा औज्ज्वल्यमाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते ..
स्नापयित्वा घृतेनार्चां सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 29 ..
text_mt: and he attains radiance wherever he is reborn. / Having bathed the idol with ghee, he is freed from all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
snāpayitvā ca tailena virogaḥ samapadyata ..
ambunā snāpayitvā tu saubhāgyamadhigacchati .. 30 ..
meaning:
स्नापयित्वा च तैलेन विरोगः समपद्यत ..
अम्बुना स्नापयित्वा तु सौभाग्यमधिगच्छति .. 30 ..
text_mt: And having bathed it with oil, he becomes free of disease. / But having bathed it with water, he attains good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
virūkṣayitvā tāṃ rāma pāpaṃ jahati mānavāḥ ..
anulepanadānena rūpamāpnotyanuttamam .. 31 ..
meaning:
विरूक्षयित्वा तां राम पापं जहति मानवाः ..
अनुलेपनदानेन रूपमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् .. 31 ..
text_mt: Having dried it, O Rāma, humans cast off sin. / By giving anointment, one attains unsurpassed beauty.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā puṣpapradānena śriyamāpnotyanuttamām ..
dhūpadānena dharmajña ratimāpnoti śobhanām .. 32 ..
meaning:
तथा पुष्पप्रदानेन श्रियमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ..
धूपदानेन धर्मज्ञ रतिमाप्नोति शोभनाम् .. 32 ..
text_mt: Likewise, by giving flowers, he attains unsurpassed prosperity. / By giving incense, O knower of dharma, he attains delightful pleasure.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā dīpapradānena cakṣuṣmānabhijāyate ..
annadaḥ sarvamāpnoti yatkiṃcinmanasecchati ..33 ..
meaning:
तथा दीपप्रदानेन चक्षुष्मानभिजायते ..
अन्नदः सर्वमाप्नोति यत्किंचिन्मनसेच्छति ..33 ..
text_mt: Likewise, by giving a lamp, he is born endowed with good vision. / A giver of food attains everything, whatever he desires in his mind.

sanskrit_iast:
pānakānāṃ pradānena tṛptimāpnotyanuttamāma ..
vasudo rūpamāpnoti rūpamāpnoti rūpyadaḥ .. 34 ..
meaning:
पानकानां प्रदानेन तृप्तिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम ..
वसुदो रूपमाप्नोति रूपमाप्नोति रूप्यदः .. 34 ..
text_mt: By giving sweet beverages, he attains unsurpassed contentment. / A giver of wealth obtains beauty; a giver of silver obtains beauty.

sanskrit_iast:
rukmadassarvamāpnoti śriyamāpnoti sarvadaḥ ..
chatradaḥ svargamāpnoti tālavṛntaprado divam .. 35 ..
meaning:
रुक्मदस्सर्वमाप्नोति श्रियमाप्नोति सर्वदः ..
छत्रदः स्वर्गमाप्नोति तालवृन्तप्रदो दिवम् .. 35 ..
text_mt: A giver of gold attains everything; a giver of all attains prosperity. / A giver of an umbrella attains heaven; a giver of a palm-leaf fan attains the celestial realm.

sanskrit_iast:
cāmarāṇāṃ pradānena rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ ..
patākāyāḥ pradānena sarvapāpānvyapohati .. 36 ..
meaning:
चामराणां प्रदानेन राजा भवति धार्मिकः ..
पताकायाः प्रदानेन सर्वपापान्व्यपोहति .. 36 ..
text_mt: By the giving of chowries, one becomes a righteous king. / By the giving of a pennant, he removes all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
dhvajadānena loke'smindhvajabhūto bhavennaraḥ ..
nānāvidhānāṃ bhogānāṃ tathā rāma pradāyakaḥ .. 37 ..
meaning:
ध्वजदानेन लोकेऽस्मिन्ध्वजभूतो भवेन्नरः ..
नानाविधानां भोगानां तथा राम प्रदायकः .. 37 ..
text_mt: By giving a banner, a man becomes an eminent standard in this world. / So too, O Rāma, a giver of various kinds of pleasures

sanskrit_iast:
tāneva bhogānāpnoti sarvamāpnoti bhūmidaḥ ..
devamālyāpanayanādgodānaphalamāpnuyāt .. 38 ..
meaning:
तानेव भोगानाप्नोति सर्वमाप्नोति भूमिदः ..
देवमाल्यापनयनाद्गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् .. 38 ..
text_mt: attains those very pleasures; a giver of land attains everything. / From removing the old garlands of a god, one obtains the fruit of giving a cow.

sanskrit_iast:
tadāhutipradānena tallokamabhipadyate ..
namaskārapraṇāmābhyāmenobhiḥ pratimucyate .. 39 ..
meaning:
तदाहुतिप्रदानेन तल्लोकमभिपद्यते ..
नमस्कारप्रणामाभ्यामेनोभिः प्रतिमुच्यते .. 39 ..
text_mt: By offering oblations to him, he enters his world. / Through obeisance and prostrations, he is freed from sins.

sanskrit_iast:
pradakṣiṇaṃ tathā kṛtvā bhavatyācāravārannaraḥ ..
stutvā ca devatāṃ rāma manoduḥkhātpramucyate ..40..
meaning:
प्रदक्षिणं तथा कृत्वा भवत्याचारवारन्नरः ..
स्तुत्वा च देवतां राम मनोदुःखात्प्रमुच्यते ..40..
text_mt: And having circumambulated [the temple], a man becomes endowed with good conduct. / And having praised a deity, O Rāma, he is freed from grief of the mind.

sanskrit_iast:
santarpayitvā toyena tṛptiṃ samadhigacchati ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena viśuddhenāntarāpmanā .. 41 ..
meaning:
सन्तर्पयित्वा तोयेन तृप्तिं समधिगच्छति ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन विशुद्धेनान्तराप्मना .. 41 ..
text_mt: Having satisfied [the deity] with water, he arrives at contentment. / Therefore, with all effort, with a purified inner self,

sanskrit_iast:
arcāsthāḥ pūjayetsarvā devatā bhūridarśana ..
tadāśritāṃśca yuñjīta tadā tadvidhipāragān .. 42 ..
meaning:
अर्चास्थाः पूजयेत्सर्वा देवता भूरिदर्शन ..
तदाश्रितांश्च युञ्जीत तदा तद्विधिपारगान् .. 42 ..
text_mt: one should worship all the deities residing in images, O man of vast insight, / and one should employ their attendants, who are masters of the rituals for them.

sanskrit_iast:
tatpūjane tathā rāma tāṃśca sampūjayetsadā ..
brāhmaṇāśca niyoktavyā vedoktasurapūjane ..43 ..
meaning:
तत्पूजने तथा राम तांश्च सम्पूजयेत्सदा ..
ब्राह्मणाश्च नियोक्तव्या वेदोक्तसुरपूजने ..43 ..
text_mt: In their worship, O Rāma, one should always honour them as well. / And brahmins should be appointed to worship the gods as prescribed by the Veda.

sanskrit_iast:
yasya rājñastu viṣaye devaveśma viśīryate ..
tasya sīdati tadrāṣṭraṃ devaveśma yathā tathā .. 44 ..
meaning:

text_mt:
Therefore, worship of the gods should always be performed with effort by kings in their realm; / purified of all sins by the worship of the gods, rulers of the earth attain heaven for a long time.
2.32 / Puṣkara said: / A king should honour brahmins; he should always protect brahmins. / For brahmins, O fortunate one, are the deities even of the gods.
An earthly ruler should give land to brahmins and other enjoyments. / For what is given to brahmins is a treasure in the other world.
When the seed of a gift is sown in the fields of the twice-born / that are ploughed by the plough of the Vedas, O descendant of Bharata, there is no end to the fruit.
One must not seize the property of a brahmin, and one must protect the property of a brahmin. / From taking the property of a brahmin, O Rāma, a man beholds hell.
They say that poison is not poison; the property of a brahmin is called poison. / Poison slays a single individual; the property of a brahmin slays seven generations.
The property of a brahmin enjoyed out of fondness destroys the family up to the seventh [generation]; / that very property enjoyed out of hostility in this world brings down a hundred families.

text_mt:
Stealing a single piece of gold, a single cow, or even a single finger-breadth of land, / one goes to hell until the dissolution of all beings.
Having seen a deceitful or misbehaved brahmin, one must never hate him. / From slandering brahmins, a person meets destruction.
One should never kill a brahmin, even one persisting in all sins. / There is nowhere any sin greater than the killing of a brahmin.
A killer of a brahmin goes to hell until the dissolution of all beings. / For ten thousand years, O Rāma, he is cooked in a place filled with sinews.
For as many dust particles as the blood of the twice-born touches here, / for that many years the perpetrator of the deed must dwell in hell.
A twice-born person who, harassed by someone, should abandon his own life— / the sin of killing a brahmin accrues to that person; no doubt should be entertained on this point.
And from abandoning his body, even a brahmin goes to hell; / because of that, O Rāma, that vilest of men incurs even greater sin.
They can make a non-deity into a deity, and a deity into a non-deity; / the highly fortunate brahmins must indeed always be bowed to.

text_mt:
Likewise, a king should zealously attend to the affairs of brahmins; / and he should not cause any delay in the work of a brahmin.
The person through whose oppression a learned man fasts during the night, / he goes to hell, O Rāma, for a hundred thousand years.
A weeping brahmin woman surely destroys a family and makes it weep; / the fire of her tears surely burns a family for three generations.
Whether learned or unlearned, a brahmin is worthy of honor, / just as fire is, O best of the twice-born, whether consecrated or unconsecrated.
Here, gods installed by brahmins attain their proper standing.
The gods eat in their mouths together with the ancestors; / an offering poured into the fires of a brahmin's mouth is superior to an offering poured into [sacrificial] fire.
It does not spill, it is not hindered, and it is free from [need of] expiations; / as many mouthfuls as a learned, properly consecrated brahmin consumes,
just so many sacrifices are declared for the giver of food. / One should bear on one's head the water released from the hands of brahmins,

by their mere word—what could be greater than that? / Enjoyment, sovereignty, and heaven are obtained by their word.
Even their anger, which always abides in them, produces purification, O Rāma; / they should be worshipped, they should be honored, and one should provide them with wives.
Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas uphold the entire world; / here, brahmins cause the gods to prosper, O son of Bhṛgu.

Dharma, wealth, and pleasure are established in their speech; / both punishment and favor [rest] upon the word of brahmins.
In this world, both must always be carried out by the king who desires prosperity. / A king who, according to the word of a brahmin, carries out decrees and the like,
whether done properly or improperly, is honored in heaven by that [action]. / A king who transgresses the treatises and acts according to his own pleasure,

there the brahmin is not at fault; the king is stained with guilt. / A ten-year-old brahmin and a hundred-year-old king,
one should know them as father and son; and between the two, the brahmin is the father. / In whose realm a brahmin languishes with hunger, / that king's realm declines through famine, disease, and thieves.

text_mt:
Therefore, the twice-born must be worshipped, bowed down to, and given shares / with all effort by a king desiring both worlds.
What the fully contented brahmins say, that the deities applaud; / when the visible gods are pleased, the invisible gods are always pleased.
2.33
Puṣkara said:
A king should protect and honor virtuous women; / devoted wives, one and all, uphold the three worlds.
Devoted to her husband's vow, dedicated to her husband, intent on honoring her husband: / such a woman goes to heaven together with her husband, O best of the twice-born.
Whatever hardship devoted wives endure along with their followers, O twice-born, / through that, reaching heaven, they attain manifold happiness.
Great indeed is their power, and their splendor is exceedingly hard to endure; / they should not be angered, they should not be neglected, and one should never disrespect them.
A king should not summon [her] for offenses; her husband would be the one to be punished, / or her son; according to statecraft, the king is not the master [over her] anywhere.

text_mt:
A woman is not declared virtuous merely by guarding her sexual organ; / she who does not act disagreeably toward her husband, she is remembered as a virtuous woman.
She who seeks the pleasure and welfare of her husband in deed, mind, and speech, / intent on worshipping her husband—that woman is remembered as a virtuous woman.
They must be bowed to, worshipped, and saluted, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / by the king with every effort, and by people everywhere.
And the best of kings should support an unprotected virtuous woman; / whatever gift is given to her is proclaimed to be endless.
By dishonouring virtuous women, a man burns his family; / by revering them, O Rāma, he elevates his own family.
Not by wealth, not by grain, not by good conduct, not by kinsmen, / not by sacrifices accompanied by sacrificial fees, and likewise not by sacred study,
do they call families ignoble, but by the misconduct of women. / Families in which the women are virtuous, O Rāma, bearing the yoke of the lineage,

are great families in this world, even if impoverished in wealth. / Even among sons, that son is [superior] for whom a virtuous woman is the fire-drill.
One should employ the son of a virtuous woman in offerings to the gods and offerings to the ancestors; / the giving of even a little to him is declared to yield great religious merit.
Just as the Gāyatrī, O Rāma, just as the Gaṅgā, best of rivers, / is purifying merely by being recited, so is an excellent, virtuous woman.
Women, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, are never corrupted; / month after month their menses removes their misdeeds.
Soma gave them purity, a Gandharva cultured speech, / and Agni all-purifying quality; therefore women are free from blemish.
Brahmins are pure from the feet; cows are pure from the back; / goats and horses are pure from the mouth; but women are pure everywhere.
The households that the female relatives curse when not properly honoured / perish completely, as if destroyed by a Kṛtyā.

text_mt:
Between women and the fortunes of households there is no distinction at all; / therefore, with every effort, women should always be honoured.
Not falsely does a woman become virtuous in this world, and in the next world as well, O Rāma; / virtuous women are declared most worthy of honour in all the worlds, among both moving and unmoving beings.
Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, entitled “The Greatness of the Virtuous Woman,” in the second book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
2.34 / Rāma said: / I desire to hear completely, O lord, the dharmas of virtuous women; / for virtuous women are declared to be the foundation of the worlds in this world.
Puṣkara said: / This alone is the supreme cause of dharma for women, O Rāma: / namely, their perpetual dependence in all matters.
In childhood she should remain under the control of her father, in youth under that of her husband, / and under that of her sons when her husband is deceased; a woman does not deserve independence.
She should not wish for separation from her father, her husband, or her son in this world; / by separation from them, a woman would bring blame upon both families.

text_mt:
She should always be cheerful, skilled in household duties, / with household utensils well maintained, and unsparing in restraint regarding expenditure.
To whomsoever her father gives her, or, in his absence, the one authorized to give, / she should attend upon him while he lives, and should not transgress against him when he has passed away.
The benediction recited for auspiciousness constitutes their sacrifice; / the giving of the bride, arranged by the master, is performed at marriages.
The husband, who performs the sacrament with sacred formulas at the prescribed fertile time as well as outside it, / constantly bestows happiness upon a woman in this world and in the next world.
Though ill-behaved, given to sensual pleasure, or devoid of virtues, / a husband must always be served like a deity by a virtuous woman.
There is no separate sacrifice for women, no vow, and no fasting; / in that she attends upon her husband, by that she is exalted in heaven.
Toward the husband who took her hand, whether he is alive or dead, / a virtuous woman desiring the world of her husband should not do anything displeasing.
She may indeed emaciate her body with auspicious flowers, roots, and fruits, / but she should never even utter the name of another man when her husband is deceased.

text_mt:
Until death she should remain patient, self-controlled, and celibate, / aspiring to that unsurpassed dharma of women devoted to a single husband.
Many thousands of brahmins who were pure lifelong celibates / went to heaven without having produced lineage succession.
When her husband has died, a virtuous woman established in celibacy / goes to heaven even if sonless, just like those celibates.
However, the woman who transgresses against her husband out of desire for offspring / incurs blame in this world and falls from the next world.
Offspring begotten by another are not recognized here, nor is one who has accepted another [husband]; / no second husband is ever prescribed for virtuous women.
She who abandons her own inferior husband and serves a superior one / is blameworthy in the world and is called “previously belonging to another.”
Through unfaithfulness to her husband, a woman attains condemned worlds; / she obtains rebirth as a jackal and is tormented by loathsome diseases.
She who does not betray her husband, restraining her mind, speech, and body, / obtains foremost fame in this world and is praised in the next world.

text_mt:
A woman should not undertake a fast or a vow exceeding [that of] her husband; / that is declared, O best of the twice-born, to diminish the lifespan of her husband.
Or she may perform the worship of deities at will, O best of brahmins, / if, being a devoted wife, O Rāma, she has obtained permission from her husband.
Indeed, for a woman unauthorized by her father, husband, or son, / whatever funeral or ancestral rite she performs becomes fruitless for her.
The most venerable deities in the world for women are those dwelling in the house; / those which are to be worshipped must be properly revered by them.
And their worship must be done with the knowledge of the master; / if she acts otherwise, she is declared subject to restraint.
A woman who goes to another man reaches the hell / named Kūṭaśālmali until the dissolution of all beings.
Likewise, she who is contemptuous of her husband, O descendant of Bhṛgu, goes to hell / for ten thousand years, as does one who speaks harshly.
Under no circumstances is there killing of women, O twice-born; / if suspected [of infidelity] with another, one should keep her confined in the house.

text_mt:
Stripped of authority, unkempt, subsisting only on a ball of food, / humiliated, and sleeping on the ground—one should keep an unfaithful woman thus.
Sorcery with roots should never be performed by a woman under any circumstances; / a woman engaged in sorcery with roots will inhabit hell for an aeon.
She incurs great misfortune wherever she is reborn, / that woman who causes misfortune to her co-wives.
Through deceitful arts, she too, O twice-born, looks upon hell for aeons; / thus she destroys the masculine power and good fortune of her husband.
Always devoted to root-magic, she belongs to yakṣas, rakṣasas, and piśācas, / and so her husband becomes completely subject to her in the worlds.
Having made her husband subject [to her] continuously by root-magic, / a woman in the end attains misfortune, or is certainly devoured by spirits.
Therefore, with every effort she should avoid root-magic; / she would destroy both herself and her husband through root-magic.

text_mt:
A brahmin woman should not drink liquor, nor should the women of vaiśyas or kṣatriyas / drink liquor, O knower of dharma; through drinking it, they would meet destruction.
From that [sin], O knower of dharma, she becomes a blood-drinking leech / for all the remainder of an aeon, because of that terrible deed.
She should not desire another's house, nor should she be quarrelsome; / nor should she stand at the door, O Rāma, nor at a latticed window.
A woman whose husband has gone abroad should avoid adornment; / she should be devoted to the worship of the gods, intent on her husband's welfare.
She should wear some ornament for the sake of auspiciousness; / she should never, at any time, assume the appearance of a widow.
A devoted wife who has gone to heaven along with her husband / is honoured, full of joy, in the abode of the thirty [gods] for the remainder of an aeon.
A twice-born man who knows dharma should burn a devoted wife of the same class / who dies before him with the agnihotra fire and with sacrificial vessels.
Having offered the fires at the funeral rites for a wife who has died before him, / he should perform the ceremony of taking another wife and re-establish the fires.

text_mt:
When her husband has died, a virtuous woman who, taking refuge in her son, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / emaciates her body through asceticism, is glorified in heaven on account of that.
In the absence of a son, she should take refuge with some man of her husband's side; / and he should indeed maintain her always with food and clothing.
If the husband's side is extinct, the father's side is the guardian of the woman; / even when in distress, she is to be supported by her own relatives on the father's side.
Or if, taking her deceased husband, a devoted wife / should enter the blazing fire, O tiger among the twice-born,
as many as three and a half crores of hairs are on a human body, / for just that many hundreds of years she is honoured in the heavenly world.
Just as a snake-catcher forcefully pulls a serpent out of a hole, / in the same way, taking her husband, she goes together with him alone.
For those women who have gone to learn virtuous conduct, who are distressed by the wound of separation / when the beloved of their life is dead, there is indeed no other dharma than entering the fire.

Rāma said:
Declare the deities most worthy of worship by women in the world, / and their proper time, ritual rule, and the fruit arising from worship.
Puṣkara said:
Worship of Śrī should always be performed by women in the home / with flowers, arghya, garlands, food-offerings, incense, lamps, and ointments.
Sweeping the house, O Rāma, and smearing it [with cowdung], / presenting flower-offerings, and whitening it with lime,
one should know all this to be the worship of Śrī, O twice-born. / The bathing, anointing, and application of fragrance and colour,
and the golden complexion of women comes from the worship of Śrī. / On all eighth [tithis], Aśokikā should also be worshipped
with fragrances, garlands, reverent salutations, incense, lamps, and the like. / She who eats on that day at night without oil
becomes free from sorrow wherever she is born. / And if she is not able on all eighth [tithis], O descendant of Bhṛgu,

then on the dark eighth [tithi] after the full moon of Prauṣṭhapadā has passed, O twice-born, / the worship of the Goddess must certainly be performed according to rule.
Like water in the three worlds, Prakṛti is spoken of among women, / who impels deeds in the worlds, O best of the twice-born.
On the bright fifteenth [tithi], worship of her should be performed / with white garlands and ointments, and with fragrant incense,
and by the giving of red garments, and by the offering of lamps, / and with pulses, and likewise with pastries, cooked foods, and suckable foods.
And having worshipped that goddess, she should eat at night, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / If she is never able [to do this] on every fifteenth [tithi],
the worship of the Goddess must certainly be performed in Kārtika. / A woman who worships Upārti is indeed a devoted wife;
she becomes a virtuous woman always devoted to dharma in the world, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / and her mind never turns toward evil.

Having worshipped the two, she should place a fish, accompanied by sand / and with pearl-oysters for eyes, into milk, and give that to a twice-born.
Then she should eat at night, avoiding sesame and oil. / From the worship of these two, O Rāma, she suffers no ruin of the household;
the devoted wife, O highly fortunate one, attains a long life. / And likewise in the month of Kārttika, always along with the moon,

sanskrit_iast:
rohiṇyāṃ rohiṇīpūjā kartavyā vidhinā dvija ..
sarvairavidhavācihnairlavaṇena ca bhūriṇā .. 44 ..
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpānnasampadā ..
tathā kuṃkumaraktena śaktyā bhārgava vāsasā .. 45 ..
saubhāgyaṃ paramāpnoti kṛtvaitatparamāṅganā ..
śuklapakṣatrayodaśyāṃ yā ca nārī pativratā .. 46 ..

paṭṭavarṇakavinyāsaṃ tasya bhāryā tathā patim .. 47 ..
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpānnasampadā ..

gandhatoyāmbupūrṇena drumapallavaśālinā ..

text_mt:
worship of Rohiṇī must be performed according to rule upon the asterism of Rohiṇī, O twice-born, / with all the tokens of a non-widow and with abundant salt,
with an abundance of perfume, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food, / and according to capacity, O Bhārgava, with a garment dyed red with saffron.
Having performed this, the excellent woman obtains the highest good fortune. / And that devoted wife who, on the thirteenth of the bright fortnight,
fasting and unwearied, worships Kāmadeva, / as well as the painted figures of his wife and her husband,
with an abundance of perfume, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food, / with molasses, honey, white sugar, and ginger,
with salt and other liquids, distinct perfumes and grains, / with diverse kinds of sweetmeats and a garment moistened with saffron,
with an auspicious, full water-pot filled with fragrant water, / adorned with tree shoots, and with a garland around its neck, O Bhārgava—

sanskrit_iast:
kāmadevāya no dadyādyadamlaṃ kiñcideva tu ..
tataśca paścāddhoktavyaṃ sarvamamlavivarjitam .. 51 ..
meaning:
कामदेवाय नो दद्याद्यदम्लं किञ्चिदेव तु ..
ततश्च पश्चाद्धोक्तव्यं सर्वमम्लविवर्जितम् .. 51 ..
text_mt: she must not offer anything sour to Kāmadeva; / and afterwards, everything [she] eats must be free of sourness.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti kāmapūjāvidhāyinī ..
atha cennaiva śaknoti sarvāṃ rāma trayodaśīm .. 52 ..
meaning:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति कामपूजाविधायिनी ..
अथ चेन्नैव शक्नोति सर्वां राम त्रयोदशीम् .. 52 ..
text_mt: The woman who performs the worship of Kāma obtains all her desires. / If, however, she is not able [to perform this] on every thirteenth day, O Rāma,

sanskrit_iast:
caitraśuklena sarvāsāṃ phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena caitraśuklatrayodaśīm .. 53 ..
meaning:
चैत्रशुक्लेन सर्वासां फलमाप्नोत्यसंशयम्..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन चैत्रशुक्लत्रयोदशीम् .. 53 ..
text_mt: she undoubtedly obtains the fruit of all of them on the bright thirteenth of Caitra; / therefore, with every effort, on the thirteenth of the bright half of Caitra,

sanskrit_iast:
kāmasya pūjā kartavyā sarvakāmapradāyinī ..
kāmadevaṃ samabhyarcya kāryamātmābhipūjanam .. 54 ..
meaning:
कामस्य पूजा कर्तव्या सर्वकामप्रदायिनी ..
कामदेवं समभ्यर्च्य कार्यमात्माभिपूजनम् .. 54 ..
text_mt: worship of Kāma, bestower of all desires, is to be performed. / Having worshipped Kāmadeva, worship of oneself should be carried out.

sanskrit_iast:
kuṃkumāṅkaistathā vastrairgandhamālyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ ..
bhartāraṃ pūjayetpaścānnārī tu kṛtamaṇḍanā .. 55 ..
meaning:
कुंकुमाङ्कैस्तथा वस्त्रैर्गन्धमाल्यविभूषणैः ..
भर्तारं पूजयेत्पश्चान्नारी तु कृतमण्डना .. 55 ..
text_mt: With garments marked with saffron, and with perfumes, garlands, and ornaments, / the woman, having adorned herself, should then worship her husband

sanskrit_iast:
kukumāṃkena vastreṇa gandhamālyairmanoharaiḥ ..
puruṣo'pi samabhyarcya kāmadevamasaṃśayam .. 56 ..
meaning:
कुकुमांकेन वस्त्रेण गन्धमाल्यैर्मनोहरैः ..
पुरुषोऽपि समभ्यर्च्य कामदेवमसंशयम् .. 56 ..
text_mt: with a cloth marked with saffron, and with captivating perfumes and garlands. / A man also, having worshipped Kāmadeva, undoubtedly

sanskrit_iast:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
tathā śuklacaturthīṣu gaurīpūjā sadā bhavet .. 57 ..
meaning:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
तथा शुक्लचतुर्थीषु गौरीपूजा सदा भवेत् .. 57 ..
text_mt: attains all desires; of this there is no doubt. / Likewise, on the fourth days of the bright fortnight, worship of Gaurī should always be held

sanskrit_iast:
snātābhiḥ sopavāsābhiḥ sūryasyodayanaṃ prati ..
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpānnasampadā .. 58 ..
meaning:
स्नाताभिः सोपवासाभिः सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ..
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपान्नसम्पदा .. 58 ..
text_mt: by women who have bathed and fasted, at the rising of the sun, / with an abundance of perfume, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food,

sanskrit_iast:
guḍena sitayā cāpi madhunā cārdrakeṇa ca ..
sarvaiścāvidhavācihnairlavaṇena ca bhūriṇā .. 59 ..
meaning:
गुडेन सितया चापि मधुना चार्द्रकेण च ..
सर्वैश्चाविधवाचिह्नैर्लवणेन च भूरिणा .. 59 ..
text_mt: with molasses, white sugar, honey, and ginger, / with all tokens of a non-widow, and with abundant salt.

sanskrit_iast:
caturthīdvitaye pūjyā sarvaśaktyā viśeṣataḥ ..
āṣāḍhe'pyathavā māsi māghe cāpyathavā dvija .. 60 ..
meaning:
चतुर्थीद्वितये पूज्या सर्वशक्त्या विशेषतः ..
आषाढेऽप्यथवा मासि माघे चाप्यथवा द्विज .. 60 ..
text_mt: She should be worshipped especially, with all one's power, on the pair of fourth days / in the month of Āṣāḍha or in the month of Māgha, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
caturṇāmapi kuṇḍānāṃ madhye sūryāṃśusevinī ..
āṣāḍhe sopavāsā tu tṛtīyāyāṃ tathā vaset .. 61 ..
meaning:
चतुर्णामपि कुण्डानां मध्ये सूर्यांशुसेविनी ..
आषाढे सोपवासा तु तृतीयायां तथा वसेत् .. 61 ..
text_mt: Remaining in the midst of four fire pits, receiving the rays of the sun, / fasting in Āṣāḍha, she should stay thus on the third day.

sanskrit_iast:
na tasyā durlabhaṃ loke kiñcidbhavati bhārgava ..
māghe'pyupoṣitā māsi rātryante tuhinotkaraiḥ ..62..
meaning:
न तस्या दुर्लभं लोके किञ्चिद्भवति भार्गव ..
माघेऽप्युपोषिता मासि रात्र्यन्ते तुहिनोत्करैः ..62..
text_mt: Nothing in the world is difficult for her to attain, O Bhārgava. / Fasting also in the month of Māgha, at the end of the night, when by mounds of frost

sanskrit_iast:
śuklīkṛtyākhilānyaṅgānyadhyāste śayanaṃ yayā ..
tataśca śītatoyena paścātsnānaṃ samācaret .. .. 63 ..
meaning:
शुक्लीकृत्याखिलान्यङ्गान्यध्यास्ते शयनं यया ..
ततश्च शीततोयेन पश्चात्स्नानं समाचरेत् .. .. 63 ..
text_mt: all her limbs have been whitened, she who lies upon the ground / should afterwards perform a bath with cold water.

sanskrit_iast:
sāpi kāmānavāpnoti yānrāma manasecchati..
pativratā sadā lolā subhagā rūpasaṃyutā .. 64 ..
meaning:
सापि कामानवाप्नोति यान्राम मनसेच्छति..
पतिव्रता सदा लोला सुभगा रूपसंयुता .. 64 ..
text_mt: She too obtains the desires that she wishes for in her heart, O Rāma. / Devoted to her husband, ever playful, fortunate, endowed with beauty,

sanskrit_iast:
dharmapriyā ca bhavati gaurīpūjanatatparā ..
āṣāḍhe dāḍimaṃ puṣpaṃ madhau karpāsasambhavam .. 65 ..
meaning:
धर्मप्रिया च भवति गौरीपूजनतत्परा ..
आषाढे दाडिमं पुष्पं मधौ कर्पाससम्भवम् .. 65 ..
text_mt: and fond of dharma does she become, devoted to the worship of Gaurī. / Having offered a pomegranate flower in Āṣāḍha, and cotton blossoms in springtime,

sanskrit_iast:
nivedya sarvamāryāyai saubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute ..
śakrāṇī ca tathā pūjyā māsi bhādrapade bhavet .. .. 66 ..
meaning:
निवेद्य सर्वमार्यायै सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ..
शक्राणी च तथा पूज्या मासि भाद्रपदे भवेत् .. .. 66 ..
text_mt: all to the Noble Lady, she attains great good fortune. / Likewise, Śakrāṇī should be worshipped in the month of Bhādrapada

sanskrit_iast:
strīṇāṃ gaurīvidhānena sarvakāmapradā hi sā ..
proṣṭhapadasya māsasya caturthyāṃ dvijasattama .. 67 ..
meaning:
स्त्रीणां गौरीविधानेन सर्वकामप्रदा हि सा ..
प्रोष्ठपदस्य मासस्य चतुर्थ्यां द्विजसत्तम .. 67 ..
text_mt: by women according to the rite for Gaurī, for she bestows all desires. / On the fourth day of the month of Proṣṭhapada, O best of the twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
śakrāṇīpūjanaṃ kṛtvā nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate ..
pūjātithiṣu sarvāsu rāma brāhmaṇapūjanam ..68..
meaning:
शक्राणीपूजनं कृत्वा नाकपृष्ठे महीयते ..
पूजातिथिषु सर्वासु राम ब्राह्मणपूजनम् ..68..
text_mt: having worshipped Śakrāṇī, she is glorified on the surface of heaven. / On all days of worship, O Rāma, the worship of brahmins

sanskrit_iast:
kartavyaṃ yacca naivedyaṃ deyaṃ tatsubhagāsu ca ..
anabhyarcya tathā gaurīṃ gaurīdīpaṃ prapaśyati .. .. 69 ..
meaning:
कर्तव्यं यच्च नैवेद्यं देयं तत्सुभगासु च ..
अनभ्यर्च्य तथा गौरीं गौरीदीपं प्रपश्यति .. .. 69 ..
text_mt: must be performed, and whatever is offered as naivedya should be given to fortunate women. / And without having worshipped Gaurī, she who gazes upon the lamp of Gaurī

sanskrit_iast:
daurbhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti varjitaṃ tasya darśanam ..
gaurīpūjanakāmā strī tasminnahani yā dvija .. 70 ..
meaning:
दौर्भाग्यं महदाप्नोति वर्जितं तस्य दर्शनम् ..
गौरीपूजनकामा स्त्री तस्मिन्नहनि या द्विज .. 70 ..
text_mt:
She incurs great misfortune; gazing upon it is forbidden.
O twice-born, a woman desiring to worship Gaurī on that day

sanskrit_iast:
snānamuṣṇāmbunā kuryātsāpi saubhāgyamaśnute ..
sampūjya vidhinā gaurīṃ yatrayatrābhijāyate .. 71 ..
meaning:
स्नानमुष्णाम्बुना कुर्यात्सापि सौभाग्यमश्नुते ..
सम्पूज्य विधिना गौरीं यत्रयत्राभिजायते .. 71 ..
text_mt:
Should also bathe with hot water; she too attains good fortune.
Having worshipped Gaurī according to rule, wherever she is born,

sanskrit_iast:
rūpalāvaṇyasaubhāgyayuktā bhavati cāpyatha ..
nityaṃ cāvidhavā rāma tathaiva ca pativratā .. 72 ..
meaning:
रूपलावण्यसौभाग्ययुक्ता भवति चाप्यथ ..
नित्यं चाविधवा राम तथैव च पतिव्रता .. 72 ..
text_mt: She is endowed with beauty, charm, and good fortune, / and is never widowed, O Rāma, and likewise devoted to her husband.

sanskrit_iast:
etāḥ pūjyatamā strīṣu daivatāstāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
ataḥ paraṃ tu yā kuryātsatīmārgavivarjanam .. 73 ..
meaning:
एताः पूज्यतमा स्त्रीषु दैवतास्ताः प्रकीर्तिताः ..
अतः परं तु या कुर्यात्सतीमार्गविवर्जनम् .. 73 ..
text_mt:
These goddesses are proclaimed as the most worthy of worship among women.
Beyond this, however, whatever woman abandons the path of the chaste wife,

sanskrit_iast:
hiṃsātmakamanirdiṣṭamaśuddhaṃ vā dvijottama ..
devatārādhanaṃ sā tu ciraṃ narakamṛcchati .. 74 ..
meaning:
हिंसात्मकमनिर्दिष्टमशुद्धं वा द्विजोत्तम ..
देवताराधनं सा तु चिरं नरकमृच्छति .. 74 ..
text_mt: And performs worship of deities that is violent, unauthorised, or impure, O best of the twice-born, / goes to hell for a long time.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu cāpyanāyuṣyaṃ grahabhūtavivardhanam ..
hiṃsātmakā tu yā nārī devatārādhane ratā .. 75 ..
meaning:
ततस्तु चाप्यनायुष्यं ग्रहभूतविवर्धनम् ..
हिंसात्मका तु या नारी देवताराधने रता .. 75 ..
text_mt:
From that comes shortening of life and an increase of seizing spirits and ghosts.
A woman who is intent on violence in worshipping deities,

sanskrit_iast:
mūlakarmaratā bhartrā sā vivāhyā bhṛgūttama ..
pauṃścalyādapi nārīṇāṃ rāma hiṃsā vivarjitā .. 76 ..
meaning:
मूलकर्मरता भर्त्रा सा विवाह्या भृगूत्तम ..
पौंश्चल्यादपि नारीणां राम हिंसा विवर्जिता .. 76 ..
text_mt:
And engaged in sorcery against her husband, must be abandoned, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Even more than unchastity, O Rāma, violence is forbidden for women.

sanskrit_iast:
strīsvabhāvaṃ śubhaṃ rāma saumyatvaṃ mārdavaṃ dayā ..
nirdayā rākṣasī rāma piśācī vā dvijottama .. 77 ..
meaning:
स्त्रीस्वभावं शुभं राम सौम्यत्वं मार्दवं दया ..
निर्दया राक्षसी राम पिशाची वा द्विजोत्तम .. 77 ..
text_mt:
The auspicious natural disposition of women, O Rāma, is gentleness, softness, and compassion.
A merciless woman, O Rāma, is a rākṣasī or a piśācī, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
athavā sarvamutsṛjya patipūjanatatparā ..
keśavārādhanaṃ kuryācchriyaśca puruṣarṣabha .. 78 ..
meaning:
अथवा सर्वमुत्सृज्य पतिपूजनतत्परा ..
केशवाराधनं कुर्याच्छ्रियश्च पुरुषर्षभ .. 78 ..
text_mt: Or else, relinquishing everything and devoted to serving her husband, / she should perform the worship of Keśava and Śrī, O bull among men.

sanskrit_iast:
tenaiva sarvamāpnoti yatkiñcitparamṛcchati ..
aphalaṃ sarvameva syādbhartranujñāṃ vinā kṛtam ..79..
meaning:
तेनैव सर्वमाप्नोति यत्किञ्चित्परमृच्छति ..
अफलं सर्वमेव स्याद्भर्त्रनुज्ञां विना कृतम् ..79..
text_mt:
Through that alone she attains everything, whatever supreme [goal] she seeks.
All [other rites] performed without the husband's permission are fruitless.

sanskrit_iast:
keśavārādhanaṃ rāma tathāpi saphalaṃ striyaḥ ..
sarvabhūtāni govindo bhartā nānyastu yoṣitaḥ ..
bhartranujñāṃ vinā tasmāttataḥ pūjā vidhīyate .. 80 ..
meaning:
केशवाराधनं राम तथापि सफलं स्त्रियः ..
सर्वभूतानि गोविन्दो भर्ता नान्यस्तु योषितः ..
भर्त्रनुज्ञां विना तस्मात्ततः पूजा विधीयते .. 80 ..

sanskrit_iast:
nārāyaṇaḥ pūjyatamo hi loke nārāyaṇaḥ sarvagataḥ pradhānaḥ ..
nārāyaṇārādhanatatparā strī kāmānavāpnoti na saṃśayo'tra .. 81 ..
meaning:
नारायणः पूज्यतमो हि लोके नारायणः सर्वगतः प्रधानः ..
नारायणाराधनतत्परा स्त्री कामानवाप्नोति न संशयोऽत्र .. 81 ..
text_mt:
Nārāyaṇa is indeed the most worthy of worship in the world; Nārāyaṇa is omnipresent and supreme.
A woman intent on the worship of Nārāyaṇa attains her desires; there is no doubt in this.

2.36
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
vailomyaṃ dharmarājo'pi nācaratyatha yoṣitām ..
pativratānāṃ dharmajña pūjyāstasyāpi tāssadā .. 1 ..
meaning:
2.36
.. पुष्कर उवाच ..
वैलोम्यं धर्मराजोऽपि नाचरत्यथ योषिताम् ..
पतिव्रतानां धर्मज्ञ पूज्यास्तस्यापि तास्सदा .. 1 ..
text_mt:
2.36
Puṣkara said:
Even Dharmarāja does not act contrary to women [who are]
Devoted to their husbands, O knower of dharma; to him too they are ever worthy of reverence.
title: Vanapraveśaḥ

sanskrit_iast:

yathā vimokṣito bhartā mṛtyupāśāvṛtaḥ striyā ..2 ..
meaning:
अत्र ते वर्णयिष्यामि कथां पापप्रणाशिनीम् ..
यथा विमोक्षितो भर्ता मृत्युपाशावृतः स्त्रिया ..2 ..

सिद्धार्थकैर्हूयमाना सावित्री प्रत्यहं द्विज .. 4 ..

Invoked daily with oblations of mustard seeds, O twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:

text_mt:
Sāvitrī said:
O king, you are ever devoted to me; you shall obtain an auspicious daughter / given by me, and through her grace you will obtain splendid sons.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca .. etāvaduktvā sā rājñaḥ praṇatasyaiva bhārgava ..
jagāmādarśanaṃ devī khe yathā rāma cañcalā .. 7 ..

पुष्कर उवाच .. एतावदुक्त्वा सा राज्ञः प्रणतस्यैव भार्गव ..
जगामादर्शनं देवी खे यथा राम चञ्चला .. 7 ..
text_mt:
Puṣkara said:
Having spoken thus to the king while he was bowing down, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / the goddess vanished from sight into the sky, O Rāma, like lightning.

sanskrit_iast:

in due time she gave birth to a daughter who was the very image of Sāvitrī in form.

When in time she attained youth, her father gave her to Satyavat.
Then Nārada said to the king of blazing splendour:

sanskrit_iast:

क्षीणायुरेष वर्षेण भविष्यति नृपात्मजः ..

'In a year this prince will have his life exhausted.'
Reflecting that 'a maiden is given away once,' the lord of men

tathāpi pradadau kanyāṃ dyumatsenātmaje śubhāma ..
sāvitryapi ca bhartāramāsādya nṛpanandanam .. 12 ..
meaning:
तथापि प्रददौ कन्यां द्युमत्सेनात्मजे शुभाम ..
सावित्र्यपि च भर्तारमासाद्य नृपनन्दनम् .. 12 ..
text_mt:
Nevertheless bestowed the auspicious maiden upon the son of Dyumatsena.
Sāvitrī too, having obtained the prince as her husband,

sanskrit_iast:
nāradasya tu vākyena dūyamānena cetasā ..
śuśrūṣāṃ paramāṃ cakre bhartṛśvaśurayorvane .. 13 ..
meaning:
नारदस्य तु वाक्येन दूयमानेन चेतसा ..
शुश्रूषां परमां चक्रे भर्तृश्वशुरयोर्वने .. 13 ..

sanskrit_iast:

text_mt: Deprived of his kingdom, with his wife, and having lost his eyesight, the king / was delighted upon receiving that princess as a daughter-in-law.

sanskrit_iast:

text_mt: When on the fourth day Satyavat was destined to die, O twice-born, / then that daughter-in-law, permitted by her father-in-law, the king,

text_mt:
The heroic man consoled the exhausted princess, whose eyes were like lotus petals, in the forest, / by showing her the deer and birds and also the trees in the wilderness.
2.37
Satyavat said:
Behold in this forest the lovely mango tree, swarming with six-legged bees, / delightful to the ears, nose, and mouth, increasing passionate delight in springtime.
Having seen it in bloom in the forest, this red [creeper], charming as a verse, / seems to mock with envy the mind, like you, O wide-eyed lady.
Behold to the south this delightful woodland tract to the right, / covered with blossoming kiṃśuka trees, blazing, as it were, with brilliance.
Carrying the fragrance of sweetly scented flowers, issued from the line of the forest, / the southern wind courteously dispels the fatigue of us both.
O lady with eyes broad as blue lotuses, with well-blossomed karṇikāra trees, / this enchanting woodland line shines as if made of gold.
Behold on high the forest tracts whose paths are blocked by masses of atimukta creepers, / O lady of lovely limbs, adorned with heaps of flowers.

विभाति चारुतिलका त्वमिवैषा वनस्थली .. 8 ..

पुष्परेण्वनुलिप्ताङ्गः प्रियामनुसरन्वने ..
कुसुमात्कुसुमं याति कूजन्कामी शिलीमुखः .. 10 ..
मञ्जरीं सहकारस्य कान्ताचञ्च्वग्रखण्डिताम् ..
स्वादयत्यतिपुष्पेऽपि पुंस्कोकिलयुवा द्रुमे .. 11 ..
काकः प्रसूतां वृक्षाग्रे सामिषाग्रेण चञ्चुना ..
काकीं सम्पाययत्येष पक्षाच्छादित पुत्रकाम् .. 12 ..
भूभागं निम्नमासाद्य दयितासहितो युवा ..
नाहारमपि चादत्ते कामी कामं कपिञ्जलः .. 13 ..
कलविङ्कस्तु विरुतैः सप्रियो विटपे स्थितः ..
मुहुर्मुहुर्विशालाक्षि उत्कण्ठयति कामिनः ..14 ..
text_mt:
O woman of excellent complexion, under the guise of the humming of bees intoxicated with spring, / Love seems to string his bow-shaft with the desire to slay travellers.
With its fair face of open campaka blossoms, resounding with male cuckoos, / this woodland shines with lovely tilaka trees, just like you.
The cuckoo atop the mango branch, yellowed with pollen from flower sprays, / reveals its nature by its calls, just as a noble person does by deeds.
Its body smeared with flower pollen, following its beloved in the forest, / buzzing, the lustful bee goes from flower to flower.
The young male cuckoo savours a mango blossom, / broken by the tip of his beloved's beak, even on a tree heavy with flowers.
At the top of the tree, the crow feeds with a beak tipped with meat / the female crow who has laid eggs and covers her nestlings with her wings.
Having reached a low spot of ground together with his mate, / the impassioned young francolin, filled with longing, takes no food at all.
Perched on a branch with his beloved, the sparrow, / with his chirping, O wide-eyed one, repeatedly fills lovers with yearning.

meaning:
क्षुद्रशाखां समारूढः शुकोऽयं कान्तया सह ..

शेते सिंहयुवा कान्ताचरणावरणाननः .. 16 ..
व्याघ्रयोर्मिधुनं पश्य शैलकन्दर संस्थितम् ..
ययोर्नेत्रप्रभालोकैर्गुहा भिन्नेव लक्ष्यते .. 17 ..
अय द्वीपी प्रियां लेढि जिह्वाग्रेण पुनःपुनः ..

text_mt:
Mounted on a small bough together with his mate, / this parrot, bending the branch with his weight, makes it seem laden with fruit.
Satiated from savouring the flesh of a wild elephant and overtaken by sleep, / the young lion lies, his face shaded by his beloved's paws.
Behold the pair of tigers dwelling in the mountain cave, / by the blazing light of whose eyes the cave appears split open.
This leopard repeatedly licks his beloved with the tip of his tongue, / and being licked by his lovely mate, he feels great pleasure.
Resting his head in her lap, his consciousness stolen by sleep, / the female monkey delights her lover just by picking out vermin.

text_mt: Fallen on the ground, exposing her belly to her beloved, / this female cat pricks him with claws and teeth, yet does not hurt him.

meaning:

सम्̐ल्लीनगात्रचरणे कर्णैर्व्यक्तिमुपागते .. 21 ..
text_mt: The male hare and female hare, pressed together, are both fast asleep, / their limbs and paws tucked in, made visible only by their ears.

text_mt: Having bathed in a lotus-rich lake, the elephant, sluggish with rut, / is honoured by the female elephant, O slender-limbed one, with pieces of lotus stalks.

sanskrit_iast:
kāntapotrasamutkhātaiḥ kāntā mārgānusāriṇī ..
karoti kavalaṃ mustairvarāhī potakānane .. 23 ..
meaning:
कान्तपोत्रसमुत्खातैः कान्ता मार्गानुसारिणी ..
करोति कवलं मुस्तैर्वराही पोतकानने .. 23 ..
text_mt: Following the tracks of her beloved, the sow in the forest of saplings / makes a mouthful of nut-grass uprooted by the snout of her mate.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛḍhāṅgasandhirmahiṣaḥ kardamārdratanurvane ..
anuvrajati dhāvantīṃ priyāṃ baddhacatuṣkakaḥ ..24..
meaning:
दृढाङ्गसन्धिर्महिषः कर्दमार्द्रतनुर्वने ..
अनुव्रजति धावन्तीं प्रियां बद्धचतुष्ककः ..24..
text_mt: Firm-jointed of limb, his body damp with mud in the forest, / the buffalo gallops in rhythm behind his running mate.

sanskrit_iast:
paśya cārvaṅgi sāraṅgaḥ tvatkaṭākṣanibhaṃ vane ..
sabhāryāṃ māṃ tu paśyantaṃ kautūhalasamanvitam .. 25 ..
meaning:
पश्य चार्वङ्गि सारङ्गः त्वत्कटाक्षनिभं वने ..
सभार्यां मां तु पश्यन्तं कौतूहलसमन्वितम् .. 25 ..
text_mt: Behold, O fair-limbed one, the deer in the forest, like a sidelong glance from you, / gazing filled with curiosity at me accompanied by my wife.

sanskrit_iast:
paśya paścimapādena rohī kaṇḍūyate mukham ..
snehārdrabhāvaḥ kaṣati bhartā śṛṅgāgrakoṭinā .. 26 ..
meaning:
पश्य पश्चिमपादेन रोही कण्डूयते मुखम् ..
स्नेहार्द्रभावः कषति भर्ता शृङ्गाग्रकोटिना .. 26 ..
text_mt: Look, with her hind leg the doe scratches her face, / and her mate, feeling moist with tenderness, rubs it with the very tip of his horn.

sanskrit_iast:
dāḍime camarīṃ paśya sitavālāmagacchatīm ..
anvāste camaraḥ kāmī vīkṣate māṃ ca garvitaḥ .. .. 27 ..
meaning:
दाडिमे चमरीं पश्य सितवालामगच्छतीम् ..
अन्वास्ते चमरः कामी वीक्षते मां च गर्वितः .. .. 27 ..
text_mt: Look at the yak cow with white hair moving toward the pomegranate tree; / the lustful yak bull follows her and gazes haughtily at me.

sanskrit_iast:
ātape gavayaḥ paśya niviṣṭo bhāryayā saha ..
romanthamāsye kurvāṇaḥ kākaṃ kakudi dhārayan .. 28 ..
meaning:
आतपे गवयः पश्य निविष्टो भार्यया सह ..
रोमन्थमास्ये कुर्वाणः काकं ककुदि धारयन् .. 28 ..
text_mt: Behold the gayal seated in the sunlight with his mate, / chewing the cud in his mouth, bearing a crow upon his hump.

sanskrit_iast:
paśyājaṃ bhāryayā sārdhaṃ nyastāgracaraṇadvayam ..
vipule badarīskandhe tacchadagrāsakāmyayā .. 29 ..
meaning:
पश्याजं भार्यया सार्धं न्यस्ताग्रचरणद्वयम् ..
विपुले बदरीस्कन्धे तच्छदग्रासकाम्यया .. 29 ..
text_mt: Look at the wild goat along with his mate, having placed both forelegs / on the broad trunk of the jujube tree in a desire to chew its leaves.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsaṃ sabhāryaṃ sarasi vicarantaṃ sunirmale ..
suśuklasyendubimbasya paśyainaṃ sadṛśa śriyam .. 30 ..
meaning:
हंसं सभार्यं सरसि विचरन्तं सुनिर्मले ..
सुशुक्लस्येन्दुबिम्बस्य पश्यैनं सदृश श्रियम् .. 30 ..
text_mt: Behold this swan roaming with his mate in the crystal-clear lake, / resembling the splendour of the purely white orb of the moon.

sanskrit_iast:
sabhāryaścakravāko'yaṃ kamalākaramadhyagaḥ ..
karoti padminīṃ kāntāṃ sapuṣpāmiva sundari .. 31 ..
meaning:
सभार्यश्चक्रवाकोऽयं कमलाकरमध्यगः ..
करोति पद्मिनीं कान्तां सपुष्पामिव सुन्दरि .. 31 ..
text_mt: This cakravāka bird with his mate, dwelling amid the lotus pool, / makes his beloved lotus-bed appear full of blossoms, O beautiful one.

sanskrit_iast:
mayā phaloccayaḥ subhru tvayā puṣpoccayaḥ kṛtaḥ ..
indhanaṃ na kṛtaṃ kiñcittatkariṣyāmi sāṃpratam .. 32 ..
meaning:
मया फलोच्चयः सुभ्रु त्वया पुष्पोच्चयः कृतः ..
इन्धनं न कृतं किञ्चित्तत्करिष्यामि सांप्रतम् .. 32 ..
text_mt: A heap of fruits has been gathered by me, O fair-browed one, and a heap of flowers by you; / no firewood has been collected, so I will do that now.

sanskrit_iast:
tvamasya sarasastīre drumacchāyāmupāśritā ..
kṣaṇamātraṃ pratīkṣasva viśramasva ca bhāmini .. 33 ..
meaning:
त्वमस्य सरसस्तीरे द्रुमच्छायामुपाश्रिता ..
क्षणमात्रं प्रतीक्षस्व विश्रमस्व च भामिनि .. 33 ..
text_mt: Taking shelter under the shade of a tree on the bank of this lake, / wait for just a moment, and rest, O lovely lady.

sanskrit_iast:
.. sāvitryuvāca .. ..
evametatkariṣyāmi mama dṛṣṭipathāttvayā ..
dūre kānta na gantavyaṃ bibhemi gahane vane .. 34 ..
meaning:
.. सावित्र्युवाच .. ..
एवमेतत्करिष्यामि मम दृष्टिपथात्त्वया ..
दूरे कान्त न गन्तव्यं बिभेमि गहने वने .. 34 ..
text_mt:
Sāvitrī said:
I will do so, but you must not go far / out of my sight, my beloved; I am afraid in the dense forest.

sanskrit_iast:
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
tasya pātayataḥ kāṣṭhaṃ jajñe śirasi vedanā ..
sa vedanārttaḥ saṅgamya bhāryāṃ vacanamabravīt .. 35 ..
meaning:
.. पुष्कर उवाच .. ..
तस्य पातयतः काष्ठं जज्ञे शिरसि वेदना ..
स वेदनार्त्तः सङ्गम्य भार्यां वचनमब्रवीत् .. 35 ..
text_mt:
Puṣkara said:
As he was felling wood, a pain arose in his head; / afflicted by the pain, he approached his wife and spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast:
.. satyavānuvāca .. ..
āyāsena mamānena jātā śirasi vedanā ..
tamaśca praviśāmīva na ca jānāmi kiñcana .. 36 ..
meaning:
.. सत्यवानुवाच .. ..
आयासेन ममानेन जाता शिरसि वेदना ..
तमश्च प्रविशामीव न च जानामि किञ्चन .. 36 ..
text_mt:
Satyavān said:
From this exertion, a pain has arisen in my head; / I seem to be entering darkness, and I know nothing at all.

sanskrit_iast:
tvadutsaṅge śiraḥ kṛtvā nidropahatalocanaḥ ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
tadutsaṅge śiraḥ kṛtvā suṣvāpa gatacetanaḥ .. 37 ..
meaning:
त्वदुत्सङ्गे शिरः कृत्वा निद्रोपहतलोचनः ..
पुष्कर उवाच ..
तदुत्सङ्गे शिरः कृत्वा सुष्वाप गतचेतनः .. 37 ..
text_mt:
Having placed my head in your lap, my eyes overwhelmed by sleep—
Puṣkara said:
Placing his head in her lap, he fell asleep, bereft of consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
pativratā mahābhāgā tatassā rājakanyakā ..
dadarśa dharmarājaṃ tu svayaṃ taṃ deśamāgatam . 38..
meaning:
पतिव्रता महाभागा ततस्सा राजकन्यका ..
ददर्श धर्मराजं तु स्वयं तं देशमागतम् . 38..
text_mt: Then that princess, the fortunate woman devoted to her husband, / saw the King of Dharma himself arrived at that place.

sanskrit_iast:
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaṃ pītāmbaradharaṃ prabhum ..
vidyullatānibaddhāṅgaṃ satoyamiva toyadam .. 39 ..
meaning:
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामं पीताम्बरधरं प्रभुम् ..
विद्युल्लतानिबद्धाङ्गं सतोयमिव तोयदम् .. 39 ..
text_mt: The lord was dark as the petal of a blue lotus, wearing yellow garments, / his body bound with lightning flashes, like a cloud bearing water,

sanskrit_iast:
kirīṭenārkavarṇena kuṇḍalābhyāṃ virājitam ..
hārabhārārpitoraskaṃ tathāṅgadavibhūṣitam .. 40 ..
meaning:
किरीटेनार्कवर्णेन कुण्डलाभ्यां विराजितम् ..
हारभारार्पितोरस्कं तथाङ्गदविभूषितम् .. 40 ..
text_mt: resplendent with a crown coloured like the sun and with two earrings, / his chest adorned with the weight of necklaces, and similarly decorated with armlets,

sanskrit_iast:
tathānugamyamānaṃ ca kālena saha mṛtyunā ..
sa tu saṃprāpya taṃ deśaṃ dehātsatyavatastadā .. 41 ..
meaning:
तथानुगम्यमानं च कालेन सह मृत्युना ..
स तु संप्राप्य तं देशं देहात्सत्यवतस्तदा .. 41 ..
text_mt:
and likewise followed by Time together with Death.
Arriving at that place then, from the body of Satyavān,

sanskrit_iast:
aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ pāśabaddhaṃ vaśaṅgatam ..
ākṛṣya dakṣiṇāmāśāṃ prayayau satvaraṃ tadā .. 42 ..
meaning:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रं पुरुषं पाशबद्धं वशङ्गतम् ..
आकृष्य दक्षिणामाशां प्रययौ सत्वरं तदा .. 42 ..
text_mt: having pulled out the Person the size of a thumb, bound with a noose and brought under control, / he then quickly departed toward the southern quarter.

sanskrit_iast:
sāvitryapi varārohā tyaktvā taṃ gatajīvitam ..
anuvavrāja gacchantaṃ dharmarājamatandritā .. 43 ..
meaning:
सावित्र्यपि वरारोहा त्यक्त्वा तं गतजीवितम् ..
अनुवव्राज गच्छन्तं धर्मराजमतन्द्रिता .. 43 ..
text_mt: Sāvitrī too, of beautiful hips, leaving behind him who had departed this life, / unweariedly followed behind the departing King of Dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
tāmuvāca yamo gaccha yathāgatamanindite ..
aurdhvadaihikakāryeṣu yuktā bhartuḥ samācara ..44 ..
meaning:
तामुवाच यमो गच्छ यथागतमनिन्दिते ..
और्ध्वदैहिककार्येषु युक्ता भर्तुः समाचर ..44 ..
text_mt: Yama said to her: Go back the way you came, blameless lady; / intent on the funeral rites of your husband, perform them.

sanskrit_iast:
nānugantumasau śakyastvayā lokāntaraṃ gataḥ ..
pativratāsi tena tvaṃ muhūrtamanupaśyasi .. ..45 ..
meaning:
नानुगन्तुमसौ शक्यस्त्वया लोकान्तरं गतः ..
पतिव्रतासि तेन त्वं मुहूर्तमनुपश्यसि .. ..45 ..
text_mt: He cannot be followed by you, having gone to the other world; / you are devoted to your husband, and therefore you see [him] for a moment.

sanskrit_iast:
guruśuśrūṣaṇādbhadre tathā satyavato mahat ..
puṇyaṃ samarjitaṃ yena nayāmyenamahaṃ svayam .. 46 ..
meaning:
गुरुशुश्रूषणाद्भद्रे तथा सत्यवतो महत् ..
पुण्यं समर्जितं येन नयाम्येनमहं स्वयम् .. 46 ..
text_mt: From serving his elders, gentle lady, great religious merit / was gathered by Satyavān, because of which I myself lead him away.

sanskrit_iast:
etāvadeva kartavyaṃ puruṣasya vijānataḥ ..
mātuḥ pituśca śuśrūṣā gurośca varavarṇini .. 47 ..
meaning:
एतावदेव कर्तव्यं पुरुषस्य विजानतः ..
मातुः पितुश्च शुश्रूषा गुरोश्च वरवर्णिनि .. 47 ..
text_mt:
This much alone is to be done by a wise man:
service to mother and father, and to the teacher, O fair-complexioned one.

sanskrit_iast: gurutritayametacca sadā satyavatā vane .. 48 ..
meaning: गुरुत्रितयमेतच्च सदा सत्यवता वने .. 48 ..
text_mt: And this triad of elders was always in the forest by Satyavān

sanskrit_iast:
pūjitaṃ pūjitassvargastadānena ciraṃ śubhe ..
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa tvagniśuśrūṣayā tathā ..49..
meaning:
पूजितं पूजितस्स्वर्गस्तदानेन चिरं शुभे ..
तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण त्वग्निशुश्रूषया तथा ..49..
text_mt:
honoured; therefore heaven was honoured by him for a long time, O auspicious lady.
By austerity, by student-chastity, and likewise by tending the sacred fire,

sanskrit_iast:
puruṣāḥ svargamāyānti guruśuśrūṣaṇena ca ..
ācāryaśca pitā caiva mātā bhrātā ca pūrvajaḥ .. 50 ..
meaning:
पुरुषाः स्वर्गमायान्ति गुरुशुश्रूषणेन च ..
आचार्यश्च पिता चैव माता भ्राता च पूर्वजः .. 50 ..
text_mt:
and by serving the elders, men attain heaven.
The preceptor, the father, the mother, and the elder brother

sanskrit_iast:
nārtenāpyavamantavyā brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ ..
ācāryo brahmaṇo mūrtiḥ pitā mūrtiḥ prajāpateḥ ..51..
meaning:
नार्तेनाप्यवमन्तव्या ब्राह्मणेन विशेषतः ..
आचार्यो ब्रह्मणो मूर्तिः पिता मूर्तिः प्रजापतेः ..51..
text_mt:
must not be disrespected, even in distress, especially by a brahmin.
The preceptor is the embodiment of Brahmā, the father the embodiment of Prajāpati,

sanskrit_iast:
mātā pṛthivyā mūrtiśca bhrātā vai mūrtirātmanaḥ ..
yanmātāpitarau kleśaṃ sahete sambhave nṛṇām .. 52 ..
meaning:
माता पृथिव्या मूर्तिश्च भ्राता वै मूर्तिरात्मनः ..
यन्मातापितरौ क्लेशं सहेते सम्भवे नृणाम् .. 52 ..
text_mt:
the mother the embodiment of the earth, and the brother indeed the embodiment of oneself.
The distress that mother and father endure in the birth of human beings—

sanskrit_iast:
na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ śakyā kartuṃ varṣaśatairapi ..
tayornityaṃ priyaṃ kuryādācāryasya ca sarvadā .. 53 ..
meaning:
न तस्य निष्कृतिः शक्या कर्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ..
तयोर्नित्यं प्रियं कुर्यादाचार्यस्य च सर्वदा .. 53 ..
text_mt:
no recompense can be made for it even in a hundred years;
one should always do what is pleasing to them both, and to the preceptor at all times.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣveva triṣu tuṣṭeṣu tapaḥ satyaṃ samāpyate ..
teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate .. 54 ..
meaning:
तेष्वेव त्रिषु तुष्टेषु तपः सत्यं समाप्यते ..
तेषां त्रयाणां शुश्रूषा परमं तप उच्यते .. 54 ..
text_mt:
Only when those three are pleased is true austerity fulfilled;
service to those three is declared to be the highest austerity.

sanskrit_iast:
na tairanabhyanujñāto dharmamanyaṃ samācareta ..
ta eva hi trayo lokāsta eva traya āśramāḥ .. 55 ..
meaning:
न तैरनभ्यनुज्ञातो धर्ममन्यं समाचरेत ..
त एव हि त्रयो लोकास्त एव त्रय आश्रमाः .. 55 ..
text_mt: Without being permitted by them, he should not practice any other dharma. / For they are the three worlds, they are the three stages of life;

sanskrit_iast:
ta eva ca trayo vedāsta evoktāstrayo'gnayaḥ ..
pitā vai gārhapatyo'gnirmātāgnirdakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 56 ..
meaning:
त एव च त्रयो वेदास्त एवोक्तास्त्रयोऽग्नयः ..
पिता वै गार्हपत्योऽग्निर्माताग्निर्दक्षिणः स्मृतः .. 56 ..
text_mt: They are the three Vedas, and they are declared to be the three fires. / The father is indeed the Gārhapatya fire, the mother is regarded as the Dakṣiṇa fire,

sanskrit_iast:
gururāhavanīyastu agnitretā garīyasī ..
triṣvapramādyanneteṣu trīṃllokāñjayate gṛhī .. 57 ..
meaning:
गुरुराहवनीयस्तु अग्नित्रेता गरीयसी ..
त्रिष्वप्रमाद्यन्नेतेषु त्रींल्लोकाञ्जयते गृही .. 57 ..
text_mt: And the guru is the Āhavanīya: this triad of fires is supreme. / Not negligent toward these three, the householder conquers the three worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
sa hi divyena vapuṣā devavaddivi modate ..
imaṃ lokaṃ mātṛbhaktaḥ pitṛbhaktastu madhyamam .. 58 ..
meaning:
स हि दिव्येन वपुषा देववद्दिवि मोदते ..
इमं लोकं मातृभक्तः पितृभक्तस्तु मध्यमम् .. 58 ..
text_mt: With a divine body he rejoices in heaven like a god. / Devoted to his mother [he conquers] this world; devoted to his father, the middle [world];

sanskrit_iast:
guruśuśrūṣayā tvevaṃ brahmalokaṃ samaśnute ..
sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ .. 59 ..
meaning:
गुरुशुश्रूषया त्वेवं ब्रह्मलोकं समश्नुते ..
सर्वे तस्यादृता धर्मा यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः .. 59 ..
text_mt: And through service to his guru he attains the world of Brahmā. / All dharmas are honored by him by whom these three are honored;

sanskrit_iast:
anādṛtāstu yasyaite sarvāstasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ ..
yāvattrayaste jīveyustāvannānyatsamācaret .. 60 ..
meaning:
अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफलाः क्रियाः ..
यावत्त्रयस्ते जीवेयुस्तावन्नान्यत्समाचरेत् .. 60 ..
text_mt: But for him by whom these are disregarded, all ritual acts are fruitless. / As long as these three live, so long he should not practice another;

sanskrit_iast:
tanuṃ nivedayettebhyo mano vacanakarmabhiḥ ..
triṣveteṣvitikṛtyaṃ hi puruṣasya samāpyate .. 61 ..
meaning:
तनुं निवेदयेत्तेभ्यो मनो वचनकर्मभिः ..
त्रिष्वेतेष्वितिकृत्यं हि पुरुषस्य समाप्यते .. 61 ..
text_mt: He should dedicate his body to them in mind, speech, and action. / For in these three a man's whole duty is fulfilled.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa dharmaḥ paraḥ sākṣādupadharmo'nya ucyate ..
gurupūjāratirbhartā tvaṃ ca sādhvī pativratā .. 62 ..
meaning:
एष धर्मः परः साक्षादुपधर्मोऽन्य उच्यते ..
गुरुपूजारतिर्भर्ता त्वं च साध्वी पतिव्रता .. 62 ..
text_mt: This is the supreme dharma directly; any other is called a secondary dharma. / Your husband is devoted to honoring his gurus, and you are a virtuous wife devoted to her husband.

Who has lost his sight and fallen from his kingdom, O knower of dharma. / Yama said: / With your desire granted, turn back, O blessed one; all this that you have spoken will come to pass. / There would be obstruction for me and fatigue for you from the road; therefore I speak to you.
2.38 / Sāvitrī said: / Whence fatigue, whence sorrow in the company of the virtuous? / Therefore, being near you, O foremost of gods, I feel no weariness of the virtuous.
For the good or even for the wicked, the virtuous alone are the supreme refuge; / Never are the wicked [a refuge] for the wicked, never for the good, nor even for themselves.
Fear does not arise from poison, fire, serpents, or weapons / As it arises from wicked people who are gratuitous enemies of the world.
Just as the virtuous, even abandoning their lives, act for the sake of others, / So wicked men are likewise intent on tormenting others.
That for the sake of which this world abandons life like a blade of grass— / Those [wicked ones] are attached to defrauding others, but for the virtuous it is the other world.
In every community in ancient times, Brahmā, the teacher of the world, / Himself made kings for the suppression of the wicked.

A king should investigate through spies; he should always purge the rogues / And should punish the wicked; he is the supreme conqueror of worlds.
Just as one, clearing the weeds, cleanses [the field] to protect the grain, / And thus causes the grain to thrive, so should the subjects be made to thrive.
By punishing the wicked and protecting the virtuous— / This alone is to be done by a king desiring heaven.
For there is no other duty of kings in the worlds, O lord of the earth, / Than the suppression of the wicked and the protection of the virtuous.
A king is their chastiser, and you are the punisher of the wicked; / Therefore, O god, you appear to me as greater than the gods.
The world is upheld by the virtuous, and you are the foremost of the virtuous; / Therefore, O god, as I follow you, no fatigue is felt by me.
Yama said: / I am pleased with you, O large-eyed woman, by your words conjoined with dharma. / Choose a boon without [asking for] the life of Satyavat; do not delay.

Sāvitrī said: / I desire a hundred brothers born of the same womb, O lord; / May my childless father attain joy through the acquisition of sons.
Yama said: / With your desire granted, turn back, O blessed one; all this that you have spoken will come to pass. / There would be obstruction for me and fatigue for you now; therefore I speak to you.
2.39 / Sāvitrī said: / Dharma is indeed the deity of women; the husband alone is their ultimate refuge. / A husband, the lord of life and wealth, must be followed by a virtuous woman.
In acquiring dharma, O best of gods, whence weariness, whence fatigue? / This very base of your feet is the supreme foundation of dharma.
The acquisition of dharma should always be practiced by a discerning man; / For its gain, O god, is superior to all gains.
Dharma, wealth, and pleasure are the three ends, the fruit of living; / For one devoid of dharma, pleasure and wealth are both like the son of a barren woman.
From dharma comes wealth, and likewise pleasure; from dharma likewise come the two worlds. / Dharma alone follows him wherever he goes.

text_mt:
For everything else goes to destruction along with the body. / Alone a living creature is born, and alone it perishes;
Dharma alone follows it, not a friend and not relatives. / Form, good fortune, grace, and prosperity are obtained through dharma.
Those worlds that grant all desires, belonging to Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, Śarva, Indra, Yama, the Sun, Fire, Wind, the Waters, / The Vasus, the Aśvins, Kubera, and the rest,
A man attains through dharma, O ender of men, / As well as charming continents and pleasant realms.
Likewise, through dharma men attain immortality, having gone from here. / And whatever gardens of the gods there are, chief among them Nandana,
those are gained by men through merit, as is the vault of heaven, / and wondrous celestial chariots, and auspicious Apsarases.
Luminous bodies are ever the fruit of the meritorious, / as are kingship, honour from monarchs, and the attainment of desired wishes.
Eminent regalia are seen as the fruit of merit: / fly-whisks with shafts of gold and cat's-eye gems, resembling moonbeams,

celibacy, truthfulness, visiting holy bathing places, O auspicious one, / regular study of scripture, service of the virtuous, living together [with them], worship of the gods,
attendance upon teachers, honouring of brahmins, / mastery of the senses, gentleness, modesty, and freedom from malice.
Therefore, dharma should always be performed constantly by one who knows; / for Death does not wait [to see] whether one's duty has been done or not done.
Even while a child, one should practice dharma; life is transient, O god. / For who knows for whom death will occur today, and by what means?
Though this world sees death standing before it, / it acts as if it were immortal: this is a great wonder, O best of the gods.
In expectation of youth, one is a child; in expectation of old age, one is a youth; / mounted upon the lap of Death, what does an old man expect?
One may climb from the earth to a mountain, and then take refuge in the top of a tree; / finding no protection even there, what recourse is there for one terrified of Death?

There is nowhere any fear greater than death for living beings; / yet even in that, good people who always do good deeds remain fearless.
Yama said: / I am pleased with you, O large-eyed woman, because of your words conjoined with dharma. / Except for the life of Satyavat, choose a boon without delay.
Sāvitrī said: / I choose a hundred sons of my own body, granted by you; / for one without offspring has indeed no path in the worlds.
Yama said: / Your wish granted, turn back, O blessed lady; all this spoken by you shall come to pass. / It would be a hindrance to me and a weariness to you, and therefore I speak thus to you now.
2.40 / Sāvitrī said: / Knowing the ordinances of all dharmas, promoting all dharmas, / you alone are the lord of the worlds, Yama who restrains all creatures.
Because you restrain creatures according to their deeds, / therefore, O god, you are called by the very name Yama.
Because, O lord, you delight all these creatures through dharma, / therefore your name Dharmarāja is truly proclaimed.

Because people come into your presence / having placed both good deeds and evil deeds before them, therefore you are called Mṛtyu.
And because you make an end of all beings, / therefore you are called Antaka by all the gods, O you of great splendour.
You are celebrated as the first son of Vivasvat; / therefore you are named Vaivasvata among all the gods.
Indeed, you stand measuring the divisions of time beginning with kalās for all [beings]; / therefore the name Kāla is declared for you by those of true discernment.
When life and deed are exhausted, you seize a person by force; / therefore you are indeed called in the world the Stealer of All Life.
By your favour, O lord of the gods, creatures abide in dharma; / by your favour, O lord of the gods, confusion of classes does not arise.
You alone are celebrated, O god, as the constant refuge of the virtuous; / O lord of the world, protector of the bounds of this universe,

text_mt:
Their word never becomes false here in the worlds of moving and unmoving beings; / therefore, they must always be revered completely by those who desire all their wishes.
2.42 / Puṣkara said: / The protection of cows must indeed be performed by a king, O scion of Bhṛgu. / Cows are purifying by association; the worlds are established in cows.
Cows extend the sacrifice; cows are the mothers of the universe. / Their dung and urine are traditionally held to be the supreme destroyers of misfortune.
They should indeed be used with effort; Fortune is established there. / And one who knows should feel no aversion toward their dung and urine.
One should not emit spit or the like upon the urine and dung of cows. / The dust of cows is supremely holy, destroying misfortune and obstacles.
And scratching cows destroys all impurities. / And the water from their horns is equal to the water of the Jāhnavī.
Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and yellow pigment: / this sixfold collection is auspicious, and each part is purifying on its own.

text_mt:
Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and kuśa water: / this should be known as supremely purifying for bathing and drinking, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
This is auspicious, slaying demons, and destroying the distress of Kali. / Yellow pigment is likewise blessed, warding off demons, serpents, and diseases. / Whoever rises at dawn and gazes at his face in clarified butter, / his misfortune perishes and his sin does not increase.
By giving a mouthful of food to cows, one attains very great religious merit. / As many cows as one is able to keep comfortably in one's home,
so many he should keep constantly; but he should not keep hungry ones. / In whose house, O twice-born, cows dwell in misery,
he goes to hell; there should be no doubt about this. / Having given a mouthful of food to another's cow, one attains very great merit.
Having given a mouthful of food to another's cow throughout the winter season, / one attains heaven for six hundred years.

अग्रभक्तं नरो दत्त्वा नित्यमेव तथा गवाम् ..

परां तृप्तिमवाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते .. 17 ..

नरकं महदाप्नोति यावदिन्द्राश्चतुर्दश .. 16 ..
