ब्रह्महत्या कृता तेन घोरा भवति भार्गव ..
सिंहव्याघ्रभयत्रस्तां पङ्कमग्नां जले गताम् .. 19 ..
गामुद्धृत्य नरः स्वर्गे कल्पभोगानुपाश्नुते ..
गवां यवसदानेन रूपवानभिजायते .. 2.42.20 ..
text_mt:
A man who gives the first portion of his food to cows every day / attains the realm of heaven for ten thousand years within six months.
The evening and morning meals of men were ordained by the gods. / Giving such food to cows constantly and untiringly,
the man who eats the second portion himself, after one year, / attains the world of cows for as long as a manvantara lasts, O twice-born.
The best of men, having provided drinking water in the pasture of cows, / reaches the world of Varuṇa and sports there for ten thousand years; / and he attains supreme satisfaction wherever he is born.
Having plowed the pasture land of cows with a plow or the like, / one falls into a terrible hell for as long as fourteen Indras rule.
Whoever causes an obstacle to cows engaged in drinking, / by him the dreadful murder of a brahmin has been committed, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / [A cow] terrified by fear of a lion or tiger, sunk in mud, or fallen into water,
rescuing [such] a cow, a man enjoys pleasures in heaven for an aeon. / By the gift of grass to cows, one is born handsome,

text_mt: If, while they are grazing peacefully together in the forest, / a wolf should leap up and kill one of them, the herdsman is not guilty of sin.

यामुत्पत्य वृको हन्यात्पाले तत्किल्बिषं भवेत .. 25 ..

गोवधेन नरो याति नरकानेकविंशतिम् ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन कार्यं तासां तु पालनम् .. 26 ..
text_mt: By killing a cow, a man goes to twenty-one hells; / therefore, by all efforts, their protection must be performed.

तासां च कीर्तनादेव नरः पापाद्विमुच्यते .. 27 ..
text_mt: And from the sale of cows, O Rāma, one does not attain good fortune; / but simply by glorifying them, a man is freed from sin.

text_mt: Touching them brings blessing and destroys all defilements; / and likewise through the gift of them, one may uplift even [entire] lineages.

meaning:
गवां निश्वासवातेन परा शान्तिर्गृहे भवेत ..
नीराजनं तत्परमं सर्वस्थानेषु कीर्तितम् .. 2.42.30 ..
text_mt: Through the wind of the breath of cows, supreme peace arises in the house; / that is proclaimed the highest lustration in all places.

sanskrit_iast:
gavāṃ saṃsparśanādrāma kṣīyate kilbiṣaṃ nṛṇām ..
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam .. 31 ..
meaning:
गवां संस्पर्शनाद्राम क्षीयते किल्बिषं नृणाम् ..
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् .. 31 ..
text_mt: From touching cows, O Rāma, the sin of men diminishes. / Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curds, ghee, water with kuśa grass,

sanskrit_iast:
ekarātropavāsaṃ ca śvapākamapi śodhayet ..
pṛthaktvapratyayābhyastamatisantapanaṃ smṛtam .. 32 ..
meaning:
एकरात्रोपवासं च श्वपाकमपि शोधयेत् ..
पृथक्त्वप्रत्ययाभ्यस्तमतिसन्तपनं स्मृतम् .. 32 ..
text_mt: and fasting for a single night will purify even an outcaste. / Practised with each substance separately, it is known as the atisantāpana [penance];

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāśubhavimokṣāya purā caritamīśvareḥ ..
pratyekaṃ ca tryahābhyastaṃ cātisāṃtapanaṃ smṛtam .. 33 ..
meaning:
सर्वाशुभविमोक्षाय पुरा चरितमीश्वरेः ..
प्रत्येकं च त्र्यहाभ्यस्तं चातिसांतपनं स्मृतम् .. 33 ..
text_mt: it was undertaken of old by the lords for liberation from all misfortune. / Practised with each [substance] for three days, it is traditionally known as the atisāntāpana,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmapradaṃ rāma sarvāśubhavināśanam ..
kṛcchrātikṛcchraṃ payasā divasānekaviṃśatim .. 34 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामप्रदं राम सर्वाशुभविनाशनम् ..
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रं पयसा दिवसानेकविंशतिम् .. 34 ..
text_mt: which grants all desires, O Rāma, and destroys all misfortune. / The kṛcchrātikṛcchra [penance] is observed with milk for twenty-one days;

sanskrit_iast:
nirmalāstena cīrṇena bhavanti puruṣottamāḥ ..
tryahamuṣṇaṃ pibenmūtraṃ tryahamuṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pibet .. .. 35 ..
meaning:
निर्मलास्तेन चीर्णेन भवन्ति पुरुषोत्तमाः ..
त्र्यहमुष्णं पिबेन्मूत्रं त्र्यहमुष्णं घृतं पिबेत् .. .. 35 ..
text_mt: having observed it, men become spotless and supreme among men. / For three days one should drink warm urine; for three days one should drink warm ghee;

sanskrit_iast:
tryahamuṣṇaṃ payaḥ pītvā vāyubhakṣaḥ paraṃ tryaham ..
taptakṛcchramidaṃ proktaṃ sarvāśubhavināśanam .. 36 ..
meaning:
त्र्यहमुष्णं पयः पीत्वा वायुभक्षः परं त्र्यहम् ..
तप्तकृच्छ्रमिदं प्रोक्तं सर्वाशुभविनाशनम् .. 36 ..
text_mt: having drunk warm milk for three days, one subsists on air for the next three days. / This is declared the taptakṛcchra, destroying all misfortune.

sanskrit_iast:
śītakṛcchrastathaivaiṣa kramācchītaiḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
sarvāśubhavināśāya nirmito brahmaṇā svayam .. 37 ..
meaning:
शीतकृच्छ्रस्तथैवैष क्रमाच्छीतैः प्रकीर्तितः ..
सर्वाशुभविनाशाय निर्मितो ब्रह्मणा स्वयम् .. 37 ..
text_mt: Likewise, this cold penance (śītakṛcchra) is proclaimed in the same order with cold [substances]; / it was instituted by Brahmā himself for the destruction of all misfortune.

sanskrit_iast:
gomūtreṇa caretsnānaṃ vṛttiṃ kuryāttu gorasaiḥ ..
utthitāmutthitastiṣṭhedupaviṣṭāsu nā sthitaḥ .. 38 ..
meaning:
गोमूत्रेण चरेत्स्नानं वृत्तिं कुर्यात्तु गोरसैः ..
उत्थितामुत्थितस्तिष्ठेदुपविष्टासु ना स्थितः .. 38 ..
text_mt: One should bathe with cow urine and make one's livelihood through the products of cows. / When [the cow] stands up, one should stand; when they are seated, a man should remain [seated].

sanskrit_iast:
abhuktavatsu nāśnīyādapītāsu ca no pibet ..
trāṇaṃ tu rāmākṛtvaiva tathā deve pravarṣati .. 39 ..
meaning:
अभुक्तवत्सु नाश्नीयादपीतासु च नो पिबेत् ..
त्राणं तु रामाकृत्वैव तथा देवे प्रवर्षति .. 39 ..
text_mt: While they have not eaten, one should not eat; while they have not drunk, one should not drink. / And without providing shelter for them, O Rāma, when the god [Indra] rains,

sanskrit_iast:
trāṇaṃ naivātmanaḥ kāryaṃ bhayā rttāśca samuddharet ..
ātmānamapi santyajya govrataṃ tatprakīrtitam .. 2.42.40 ..
meaning:
त्राणं नैवात्मनः कार्यं भया र्त्ताश्च समुद्धरेत् ..
आत्मानमपि सन्त्यज्य गोव्रतं तत्प्रकीर्तितम् .. 2.42.40 ..
text_mt: one must not seek shelter for oneself, and one should rescue those afflicted by fear, / even giving up one's own life: that is declared the vow of cows (govrata).

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ māsenaikena bhārgava ..
vratenānena cīrṇena golokaṃ puruṣo vrajet .. 41 ..
meaning:
सर्वपापप्रशमनं मासेनैकेन भार्गव ..
व्रतेनानेन चीर्णेन गोलोकं पुरुषो व्रजेत् .. 41 ..
text_mt: In one month, O Bhārgava, it brings pacification of all sins; / by observing this vow, a man goes to the world of cows (Goloka),

sanskrit_iast:
abhīṣṭamatha vā rāma yāvadindrāścaturdaśa ..
gavāṃ nirhāranirmuktānaśnanpratidinaṃ yavān .. 42 ..
meaning:
अभीष्टमथ वा राम यावदिन्द्राश्चतुर्दश ..
गवां निर्हारनिर्मुक्तानश्नन्प्रतिदिनं यवान् .. 42 ..
text_mt: or to whatever is desired, O Rāma, for as long as fourteen Indras [endure]. / Eating daily barley grains that have passed out in cow dung,

sanskrit_iast:
māsena tadavāpnoti yatki ñcinmanasecchati ..
gomatīṃ ca tathā vidyāṃ sāyaṃ prātastathā japan .. 43 ..
meaning:
मासेन तदवाप्नोति यत्कि ञ्चिन्मनसेच्छति ..
गोमतीं च तथा विद्यां सायं प्रातस्तथा जपन् .. 43 ..
text_mt: in a month he attains whatever he desires in his mind. / And likewise, reciting the Gomatī hymn morning and evening,

sanskrit_iast:
golokamāpnoti naro nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
uparyupari sarveṣāṃ gavāṃ lokaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 44 ..
meaning:
गोलोकमाप्नोति नरो नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
उपर्युपरि सर्वेषां गवां लोकः प्रकीर्तितः .. 44 ..
text_mt: a man attains the world of cows; no doubt should be entertained on this point. / Above all [other worlds], the world of cows is proclaimed,

sanskrit_iast:
nivasanti sadā yatra gāvastvākāśagā divi ..
vimāneṣu vicitreṣu vṛteṣvapsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ .. 45 ..
meaning:
निवसन्ति सदा यत्र गावस्त्वाकाशगा दिवि ..
विमानेषु विचित्रेषु वृतेष्वप्सरसां गणैः .. 45 ..
text_mt: where cows, moving through the sky, dwell eternally in heaven, / on wonderful aerial chariots surrounded by celestial nymphs,

sanskrit_iast:
kiṅkiṇī jālacitreṣu vīṇāmurajanādiṣu ..
sadā kāmajalā nadyaḥ kṣīrapāyasakardamāḥ .. 46 ..
meaning:
किङ्किणी जालचित्रेषु वीणामुरजनादिषु ..
सदा कामजला नद्यः क्षीरपायसकर्दमाः .. 46 ..
text_mt: adorned with nets of small bells, resounding with lutes and drums, / [where there are] rivers whose water is always according to desire, having milk and rice-pudding for their mud,

sanskrit_iast:
śītalāmalapānīyāḥ suvarṇasikatāstathā ..
puṣkariṇyaḥ śubhāstatra vaiḍūryakamalotpalāḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
शीतलामलपानीयाः सुवर्णसिकतास्तथा ..
पुष्करिण्यः शुभास्तत्र वैडूर्यकमलोत्पलाः .. 47 ..
text_mt: with cool, pure water and sands of gold; / auspicious lotus-ponds are there, with blue and white lotuses of lapis lazuli;

sanskrit_iast:
mānasī ca tathā siddhiḥ tatra loke bhṛgūttama ..
tañca lokaṃ narā yānti gavāṃ bhaktyā na saṃśayaḥ .. 48 ..
meaning:
मानसी च तथा सिद्धिः तत्र लोके भृगूत्तम ..
तञ्च लोकं नरा यान्ति गवां भक्त्या न संशयः .. 48 ..
text_mt: and mental perfection exists in that world, O foremost of the Bhṛgus. / And to that world men go through devotion to cows, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
gomatīṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm ..

गोमतीं कीर्तयिष्यामि सर्वपापप्रणाशिनीम् ..
तां तु मे वदतो विप्र शृणुष्व सुसमाहितः .. 49 ..
text_mt: I shall proclaim the Gomatī [vidyā], which destroys all sins; / listen with an attentive mind, O brahmin, as I speak it to you:

sanskrit_iast:
gāvaḥ surabhayo nityaṃ gāvo guggu lugandhikāḥ...

meaning:
गावः सुरभयो नित्यं गावो गुग्गु लुगन्धिकाः...
गावः प्रतिष्ठा भूतानां गावः स्वस्त्ययनं परम् .. 2.42.50 ..
text_mt: 'Cows are fragrant always; cows smell of bdellium; / cows are the foundation of all creatures; cows are the supreme blessing;

sanskrit_iast:
annameva paraṃ gāvo devānāṃ haviruttamam ..
pāvanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ rakṣanti ca vahanti ca ..51..
meaning:
अन्नमेव परं गावो देवानां हविरुत्तमम् ..
पावनं सर्वभूतानां रक्षन्ति च वहन्ति च ..51..
text_mt: cows are the supreme food, the highest oblation of the gods; / they are the purifier of all beings; they protect and they carry;

sanskrit_iast:
haviṣā mantrapūtena tarpayantyamarāndivi ..
ṛṣīṇāmagnihotreṣu gāvo home prayojitāḥ .. 52 ..
meaning:
हविषा मन्त्रपूतेन तर्पयन्त्यमरान्दिवि ..
ऋषीणामग्निहोत्रेषु गावो होमे प्रयोजिताः .. 52 ..
text_mt: with oblation purified by mantras they satisfy the immortals in heaven; / in the agnihotras of the sages, cows are employed in the oblation;

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ śaraṇamuttamam ..
gāvaḥ pavitraṃ paramaṃ gāvo maṅgalamuttamam .. 53 ..
meaning:
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां गावः शरणमुत्तमम् ..
गावः पवित्रं परमं गावो मङ्गलमुत्तमम् .. 53 ..
text_mt: of all beings indeed, cows are the supreme refuge; / cows are the highest purifier; cows are the supreme auspiciousness;

sanskrit_iast:
gāvaḥ svargasya sopānaṃ gāvo dhanyāssanātanāḥ ..
oṃ namo gobhyaḥ śrīmatībhyaḥ saurabheyībhya eva ca .. 54 ..
meaning:
गावः स्वर्गस्य सोपानं गावो धन्यास्सनातनाः ..
ओं नमो गोभ्यः श्रीमतीभ्यः सौरभेयीभ्य एव च .. 54 ..
text_mt: cows are the stairway to heaven; cows are blessed and eternal. / Oṃ, reverence to the cows, the radiant daughters of Surabhi;

sanskrit_iast:
namo brahmasutābhyaśca pavitrābhyo namonamaḥ ..
brāhmaṇāścaiva gāvaśca kulamekaṃ dvidhā sthitam .. 55 ..
meaning:
नमो ब्रह्मसुताभ्यश्च पवित्राभ्यो नमोनमः ..
ब्राह्मणाश्चैव गावश्च कुलमेकं द्विधा स्थितम् .. 55 ..
text_mt: and reverence to the daughters of Brahmā, to the pure ones, reverence, reverence! / Brahmins and cows are a single family, standing divided in two:

sanskrit_iast:
ekatra mantrāstiṣṭhanti havirekatra tiṣṭhati ..
devabrāhmaṇagosādhusādhvībhiḥ sakalaṃ jagat .. 56 ..
meaning:
एकत्र मन्त्रास्तिष्ठन्ति हविरेकत्र तिष्ठति ..
देवब्राह्मणगोसाधुसाध्वीभिः सकलं जगत् .. 56 ..
text_mt: in the one place reside the mantras; in the other place resides the oblation. / By the gods, brahmins, cows, holy men, and virtuous women, the entire world

यत्र तीर्थे सदा गावः पिबन्ति तृषि ता जलम् ..
उत्तरन्ति पथा येन स्थिता तत्र सरस्वती ..57..
text_mt: is indeed always sustained; therefore, all are always most worthy of worship. / At whatever sacred ford thirsty cows always drink water, / and along whichever path they cross over, there Sarasvatī is present.

For Gaṅgā resides at the sacred water of cows, and nourishment grows in their dust; / Lakṣmī resides in their dung, and dharma in bowing to them; one should always bow down to them.'
Puṣkara said:
Hereafter I shall declare to you the treatment of cattle, O Rāma, / in brief, the meritorious essence; listen to that.
At the base of the horns of milch cows one should apply oil with rock salt, / prepared with a paste of śṛṅgī, vīrā, balā, and māṃsī, along with honey;
or likewise ghee mixed with powder of simi should be given. / At the base of all ears, [oil] prepared with Indian madder, asafoetida, and rock salt
should be applied, or alternatively cow's milk products. / Honey, rock salt, conch shell, tagarī, pippalī, and sihā,
having ground [these] with goat's milk, the physician should make a pill. / This is an excellent eye-salve when combined with ghee and honey.
Roots of bilva, apāmārga, dhātakī, along with pāṭalā, / and kuṭaja applied as an ointment to the roots of the teeth destroys toothache.

Ghee cooked with substances that alleviate toothache, O Rāma, / is known to remove diseases of the mouth; rock salt [should be used] in diseases of the tongue.
Ginger, both kinds of turmeric, and triphalā [should be used] in throat obstruction; / ginger, both kinds of turmeric, and the bark of kuṭaja,
Apāmārga and viḍaṅga, combined with salt, / is a medicine that destroys oral diseases and removes fever and burning sensation.
In chest pain, bladder pain, diseases of wind, and likewise in wounds, / a draught of milk mixed with triphalā and ghee is praised for cattle.
Oil boiled with dill, kuṭaja, and citraka / should be given to cattle, O Rāma; it destroys all heart disease.
In diarrhoea, one should administer the two types of turmeric and pāṭhā; / in constipation, one should administer padmacāriṇī mixed with ghee.
In all skin diseases and likewise in ailments of the extremities, / and in cough and asthma, one should administer ginger and dārvī.
Priyaṅgu combined with salt should be given for setting fractures. / In all diseases of wind, [oil] boiled with dill—

combined with palaṅkaśā, auspicious for the destruction of all harmful spirits. / A bell for cows should also be fumigated with this incense.
Aśvagandhā, sesame, and vinegar are praised in an enema mixture; / buttermilk combined with aśvagandhā and an enema of sesame are praised; / through that, O descendant of Bhṛgu's race, the cow becomes rich in milk.
Oil-cake alone is taught as a tonic for cattle, O Rāma; / one should avoid cold water for drinking and wet fodder.
[An animal] afflicted with old age and a cold shelter, O best of the twice-born, [should be avoided]; / and among cattle one should maintain vigour; they should always be vigorous.
Lamps should be kept at night in the dwelling of cattle, O Rāma.
Salt is indeed always beneficial for the alleviation of diseases in cattle when half a month has elapsed; / it destroys constipation, colic, and loss of appetite; it is likewise praised for goats and sheep.

Puṣkara said:
After this I shall declare to you the rite of pacification for cattle, / regular, occasional, and for specific desires, and likewise increasing nourishment. / On the fifth lunar days of the bright fortnight, worship of Śrī is prescribed / upon the dung of cows, O knower of dharma, with abundance of incense, lamps, and food,
with wild, lovely flowers offered in devotion, and worship of brahmins; / on that very day the worship of Vāsudeva must be performed.
For he is the all-pervading god whose abode is the ocean of milk, / especially [the refuge] of cows, who are the support of the three worlds.
On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / a sacrifice to the slayer of Vṛtra should be performed by the owner of cattle, / with abundance of perfume, incense, obeisance, flowers, lamps, and food. / [With the mantras] 'iha prajāyāḥ', 'sāmrādhaḥ', and likewise 'pṛṣadaśvā',

and with 'ghṛtapratīka', and with the Raudrī verses, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / and with the daily verses, the wise man should offer ghee into the fire.
And he should consecrate salt with the mantra 'ambhasthe'; / the eating [of salt] should then be done with curds, with the mantra 'dadhikrāvṇā'.
A cow should be given by the sacrificer who possesses a hundred cows; / one of lesser wealth should give a sacrificial fee to the hotṛ according to his capacity.
Afterwards, the cows, well-adorned with perfumes, garlands, fruits, and the like, / well-fed, and with calves released, should circumambulate the fire.
With shouts, joyous cries, and the sounds of conches and musical instruments, / he should arrange a contest of bulls and likewise of cowherds.
On the second day, that salt consecrated by a brahmin / should be given to the cows and bulls together with their calves.
And he should feed brahmins here with food consisting mostly of dairy products; / afterwards, benedictions should be pronounced, and having given their gifts, he should dismiss them.

text_mt:
This regular, auspicious pacification rite for cattle has been shown to you; / after this I shall declare to you the occasional rite.
When a murrain among cows has arrived, or an affliction such as disease, / or a loss of milk, or in any other disruption of their natural state,
the learned man, having fasted for three nights or having fasted for one night, / should prepare an altar in an auspicious place amidst the cattle.
He should draw an eight-petalled lotus endowed with a pericarp and filaments; / in the middle of the pericarp he should worship Vāsudeva together with Śrī.
Worship of the deities should be performed in proper order with rice boiled with pulses; / I shall declare their names to you, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
One should worship the quarter-cow named Subhadrā in the eastern part; / then Brahmā is to be worshipped, and immediately after him Surabhi.
Then the Sun, then the cow Bahurūpā, O best of the twice-born; / then one should worship the goddess Earth, and then Ananta.

A king must be diligent, especially in their protection. / Only so many horses should be kept as can be fed comfortably;
they must not be kept distressed and hungry; / distressed, they destroy fortune in the world, and likewise victory.
Properly maintained, nourished with grass and fodder according to rule, / maintained [thus], they bring victory in both worlds.
They are auspicious, they are pure, and so too is their dust; / they are devoted to the isolated, supreme god Parameṣṭhin alone.
Indeed, in the midst [of the gods] they were permitted by him alone among the gods; / therefore, the horse of the horse-sacrifice is offered to him alone.
Superior to all jewels, the horse was born from the churning for nectar; / hence the horse Uccaiḥśravas is considered the foremost of all jewels.
They were winged, the mounts of the gods; for men they became wingless, / created of old by Śālihotra, born from the lotus, for the purpose of riding.
Mighty, they consecrate the lands with their neighing; / they are declared to be Gandharvas, sons of Śrī, conquerors of fatigue.

Horses are the principal limb of the army and its supreme splendor; / for traveling far and in battle, horses are the best of vehicles.
Mounted on a galloping horse, standing tall, wearing a crest of chowries, / the satisfaction that one feels, O Rāma, does not exist [even] in heaven.
By horses well equipped, mounted by armored men, / at their mere sight the hearts of the enemy army sink completely.
The sky whose column of dust raised by the hooves of horses imitates a parasol— / the entire earth adorned with mountains becomes subject to him in this world.

title: Aśvacikitsā

sanskrit_iast:
śiṅghāṇakaharāpiṇḍī svedasya śirasastathā ..
yāvaśūkaṃ samadanaṃ pippalī viśvabheṣajam .. 2 ..
meaning:
शिङ्घाणकहरापिण्डी स्वेदस्य शिरसस्तथा ..
यावशूकं समदनं पिप्पली विश्वभेषजम् .. 2 ..
text_mt: a paste of these destroys nasal discharge, as does sweating of the head. / Barley-alkali together with madana, long pepper, dried ginger,

sanskrit_iast:
sarṣapā gṛhadhūmaśca nirguṇḍī surasā vacā ..
nimbapatrayutā pāyau vartiḥ śūlavināśinī .. 3 ..
meaning:
सर्षपा गृहधूमश्च निर्गुण्डी सुरसा वचा ..
निम्बपत्रयुता पायौ वर्तिः शूलविनाशिनी .. 3 ..
text_mt: mustard seeds, chimney soot, nirguṇḍī, basil, and calamus, / combined with leaves of nimba, [made into] a suppository in the anus, destroys colic.

sanskrit_iast:
hiṅgu puṣkaramūlaṃ ca nāgaraṃ sāmlavetasam ..
pippalī saindhavayutaṃ śūlaghnaṃ tūṣṇavāriṇā .. 4 ..
meaning:
हिङ्गु पुष्करमूलं च नागरं साम्लवेतसम् ..
पिप्पली सैन्धवयुतं शूलघ्नं तूष्णवारिणा .. 4 ..
text_mt: Asafoetida, puṣkaramūla, ginger, together with amlavetasa, / long pepper, and rock salt, taken with warm water, destroys colic.

sanskrit_iast:
nāgarātiviṣau mustā sānantā bilvamālakā ..
kvātho māsaṃ pibedvājī sarvātīsāranāśanam .. 5 ..
meaning:
नागरातिविषौ मुस्ता सानन्ता बिल्वमालका ..
क्वाथो मासं पिबेद्वाजी सर्वातीसारनाशनम् .. 5 ..
text_mt: Ginger, ativiṣā, nut grass, together with anantā, wood-apple, and āmalaka— / a horse should drink this decoction for a month; it cures all dysenteries.

sanskrit_iast:
priyaṃguśārivābhyāṃ ca yuktamājaṃ śṛtaṃ payaḥ ..
paryāptaśarkaraṃ pītvā śramādvājyavamucyate .. 6 ..
meaning:
प्रियंगुशारिवाभ्यां च युक्तमाजं शृतं पयः ..
पर्याप्तशर्करं पीत्वा श्रमाद्वाज्यवमुच्यते .. 6 ..
text_mt: Boiled goat’s milk mixed with priyaṅgu and sarsaparilla, / having ample sugar—by drinking this, a horse is freed from exhaustion.

sanskrit_iast:
droṇikāyāṃ tu dātavyā tailavastisturaṅgame ..
koṣṭhajāśca śirā vedhyāstena tasya sukhaṃ bhavet .. 7 ..
meaning:
द्रोणिकायां तु दातव्या तैलवस्तिस्तुरङ्गमे ..
कोष्ठजाश्च शिरा वेध्यास्तेन तस्य सुखं भवेत् .. 7 ..
text_mt: An oil enema should be administered to a horse in a tub, / and veins arising in the abdomen should be punctured; thereby ease will come to him.

sanskrit_iast:
dāḍimaṃ triphalāṃ vyoṣaṃ guḍaṃ ca samabhāgikam ..
piṇḍametatpradātavyamaśvānāṃ kāsanāśanam .. 8 ..
meaning:
दाडिमं त्रिफलां व्योषं गुडं च समभागिकम् ..
पिण्डमेतत्प्रदातव्यमश्वानां कासनाशनम् .. 8 ..
text_mt: Pomegranate, the three fruits, the three spices, and jaggery in equal portions— / this bolus should be given; it cures cough in horses.

sanskrit_iast:
priyaṅgurodhramadhubhiḥ pibanti sma rasaṃ hayāḥ ..
kṣīraṃ vāmaṃ ca kāloḍyaṃ kaśmalādvipramucyate .. 9 ..
meaning:
प्रियङ्गुरोध्रमधुभिः पिबन्ति स्म रसं हयाः ..
क्षीरं वामं च कालोड्यं कश्मलाद्विप्रमुच्यते .. 9 ..
text_mt: Horses drank the juice with priyaṅgu, lodhra, and honey; / or [having drunk] raw milk properly stirred, [a horse] is freed from stupor.

sanskrit_iast:
praskanneṣu ca sarveṣu śreya ādau viśoṣaṇam ..
abhyaṅgodvartanasnehanasyavartikramastataḥ .. 2.46.10 ..
meaning:
प्रस्कन्नेषु च सर्वेषु श्रेय आदौ विशोषणम् ..
अभ्यङ्गोद्वर्तनस्नेहनस्यवर्तिक्रमस्ततः .. 2.46.10 ..
text_mt: In all prolapses, desiccation is first recommended; / then the sequence of anointing, rubbing, unction, errhine, and medicated wick.

sanskrit_iast:
praskannaṃ praśamaṃ yāti yadi nānena karmaṇā ..
urasyupāntapārśve ca tato visrāvayecchirām .. 11 ..
meaning:
प्रस्कन्नं प्रशमं याति यदि नानेन कर्मणा ..
उरस्युपान्तपार्श्वे च ततो विस्रावयेच्छिराम् .. 11 ..
text_mt: If prolapse is not pacified by this treatment, / one should then bleed a vein in the chest and near the flank.

sanskrit_iast:
jvalitānāṃ turaṅgāṇāmayameva kriyākramaḥ ..
nasyamekaṃ vinā rāma sarvametatpraśasyate .. 12 ..
meaning:
ज्वलितानां तुरङ्गाणामयमेव क्रियाक्रमः ..
नस्यमेकं विना राम सर्वमेतत्प्रशस्यते .. 12 ..
text_mt: This is the very course of treatment for feverish horses; / except for the errhine alone, O Rāma, all of this is commended.

sanskrit_iast:
rodhrakarañjayormūlaṃ mātuluṅgāgnināgarāḥ ..
kuṣṭhahiṅguvacārāsnālepo'yaṃ śophanāśanaḥ .. 13 ..
meaning:
रोध्रकरञ्जयोर्मूलं मातुलुङ्गाग्निनागराः ..
कुष्ठहिङ्गुवचारास्नालेपोऽयं शोफनाशनः .. 13 ..
text_mt: Roots of lodhra and karañja, citron, plumbago, and ginger; / this plaster of kuṣṭha, asafoetida, vacā, and rāsnā cures swelling.

sanskrit_iast:
samāsena śirāṃ vidhyāddeyā vāpi jalaukasaḥ ..
tryahetryahe vā dharmajña nasyakarma samācaret .. 14 ..
meaning:
समासेन शिरां विध्याद्देया वापि जलौकसः ..
त्र्यहेत्र्यहे वा धर्मज्ञ नस्यकर्म समाचरेत् .. 14 ..
text_mt: Briefly, one should pierce a vein, or leeches may also be applied; / or every three days, O knower of dharma, one should perform nasal administration.

sanskrit_iast:
mañjiṣṭhā madhukaṃ drākṣā bṛhatyau raktacandanam ..
trapusībījamūlāni śṛṅgāṭakakaśerukam .. 15 ..
meaning:
मञ्जिष्ठा मधुकं द्राक्षा बृहत्यौ रक्तचन्दनम् ..
त्रपुसीबीजमूलानि शृङ्गाटककशेरुकम् .. 15 ..
text_mt: Madder, liquorice, grape, the two bṛhatīs, red sandalwood, / seeds and roots of cucumber, water chestnut, and kaśeruka—

sanskrit_iast:
ajāpayaḥ śṛtamidaṃ suśītaṃ śarkarānvitam..
pītvā niraśano vājī raktamehātpramucyate .. 16 ..
meaning:
अजापयः शृतमिदं सुशीतं शर्करान्वितम्..
पीत्वा निरशनो वाजी रक्तमेहात्प्रमुच्यते .. 16 ..
text_mt: this, boiled with goat's milk, well cooled, and mixed with sugar, / being drunk by a fasting horse, frees him from hematuria.

sanskrit_iast:
manyāhanunigālasthaḥ śiraḥśopho galagraha ..
abhyaṅgaḥ kaṭutailena tatra teṣveva śasyate .. 17 ..
meaning:
मन्याहनुनिगालस्थः शिरःशोफो गलग्रह ..
अभ्यङ्गः कटुतैलेन तत्र तेष्वेव शस्यते .. 17 ..
text_mt: For swelling of the head and throat spasms located in the nape, jaw, or throat, / massage with pungent oil is praised right there on those [spots].

sanskrit_iast:
yavaiḥ snigdhakulatthaiśca tataḥ svedaṃ prayojayet ..
mṛdūkṛte tataḥ śophe nasyakarma samācaret ..18..
meaning:
यवैः स्निग्धकुलत्थैश्च ततः स्वेदं प्रयोजयेत् ..
मृदूकृते ततः शोफे नस्यकर्म समाचरेत् ..18..
text_mt: Then one should apply fomentation with barley and unctuous horsegram; / after the swelling has been softened, one should then perform nasal administration.

sanskrit_iast:
vacā- - - - saindhavaṃ svaraso rasaḥ ..
kṛṣṇāhiṅuyutairebhiḥ kṛtvā nasyaṃ na sīdati ..19..
meaning:
वचा- - - - सैन्धवं स्वरसो रसः ..
कृष्णाहिङुयुतैरेभिः कृत्वा नस्यं न सीदति ..19..
text_mt: Vacā, [...], rock salt, fresh juice, and essence— / having prepared an errhine with these combined with long pepper and asafoetida, he does not sink down.

sanskrit_iast:
niśā jyotiṣmatī pāṭhā kṛṣṇā kuṣṭhā vacā madhu ..
jihvāstambhe ca lepo'yaṃ guḍamūtrayuto hitaḥ .. 2.46.20 ..
meaning:
निशा ज्योतिष्मती पाठा कृष्णा कुष्ठा वचा मधु ..
जिह्वास्तम्भे च लेपोऽयं गुडमूत्रयुतो हितः .. 2.46.20 ..
text_mt: Turmeric, jyotiṣmatī, pāṭhā, long pepper, kuṣṭha, vacā, and honey; / for stiffness of the tongue, this plaster mixed with jaggery and urine is beneficial.

sanskrit_iast:
tilairyuktā rajanyā ca nimbapatraiśca yojitā ..
kṣaudreṇa śodhanī piṇḍī sarpiṣā vraṇaropiṇī .. 21 ..
meaning:
तिलैर्युक्ता रजन्या च निम्बपत्रैश्च योजिता ..
क्षौद्रेण शोधनी पिण्डी सर्पिषा व्रणरोपिणी .. 21 ..
text_mt: Mixed with sesame and turmeric, and combined with neem leaves: / with honey, it is a cleansing bolus; with ghee, it heals wounds.

sanskrit_iast:
abhighātena khañjanti yenāśvāstīvravedanāḥ ..
pariṣekakriyā teṣāṃ tailenāśu rujāpahā ..22..
meaning:
अभिघातेन खञ्जन्ति येनाश्वास्तीव्रवेदनाः ..
परिषेकक्रिया तेषां तैलेनाशु रुजापहा ..22..
text_mt: When horses limp due to an injury and suffer intense pain, / an affusion with oil quickly takes away their pain.

sanskrit_iast:
doṣakopābhighātābhyāṃ tilaje jṛmbhate sadā ..
śāntirmadhvājyabandhābhyāṃ pakvambhinne vraṇe kramaḥ .. 23 ..
meaning:
दोषकोपाभिघाताभ्यां तिलजे जृम्भते सदा ..
शान्तिर्मध्वाज्यबन्धाभ्यां पक्वम्भिन्ने व्रणे क्रमः .. 23 ..
text_mt: If it constantly gapes open from sesame-oil [application] due to vitiation of the humors or an injury, / relief comes through honey and ghee with bandaging; such is the method when the wound is ripe and burst.

sanskrit_iast:
aśvatthodumbaraplakṣamadhūkavaṭakalkakaiḥ..
prabhūtasalilaḥ kvāthaḥ sukhoṣṇo vraṇaśodhanaḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
अश्वत्थोदुम्बरप्लक्षमधूकवटकल्ककैः..
प्रभूतसलिलः क्वाथः सुखोष्णो व्रणशोधनः .. 24 ..
text_mt: With pastes of aśvattha, udumbara, plakṣa, madhūka, and vaṭa, / a lukewarm decoction with plenty of water cleanses wounds.

sanskrit_iast:
śatāhvā nāgaraṃ rāsnā mañjiṣṭhākuṣṭhasaindhavaiḥ ..
devadāruvacāyugmarajanīraktacandanaiḥ .. 25 ..
meaning:
शताह्वा नागरं रास्ना मञ्जिष्ठाकुष्ठसैन्धवैः ..
देवदारुवचायुग्मरजनीरक्तचन्दनैः .. 25 ..
text_mt: With dill, ginger, rāsnā, madder, kuṣṭha, and rock salt, / deodar, vacā, the two turmerics, and red sandalwood,

sanskrit_iast:
tailaṃ siddhaṃ kaṣāyeṇa guḍūcyā payasā saha ..
prakṣīṇe vastinasye ca yojyaṃ sarvatra laṃghane .. 26 ..
meaning:
तैलं सिद्धं कषायेण गुडूच्या पयसा सह ..
प्रक्षीणे वस्तिनस्ये च योज्यं सर्वत्र लंघने .. 26 ..
text_mt: oil prepared with a decoction of guḍūcī together with milk / is to be used in wasting, as an enema, as an errhine, and universally in fasting therapy.

sanskrit_iast:
raktasrāvo jalaukābhirnetrānte netrarogiṇaḥ ..
khadirodumbarāśvatthakaṣāyeṇa ca dhāvanam .. 27 ..
meaning:
रक्तस्रावो जलौकाभिर्नेत्रान्ते नेत्ररोगिणः ..
खदिरोदुम्बराश्वत्थकषायेण च धावनम् .. 27 ..
text_mt: For a horse with eye disease, blood-letting by leeches is done at the outer corner of the eye, / and washing with a decoction of khadira, udumbara, and aśvattha.

sanskrit_iast:
dhātrīdurālabhātiktā priyaṅgukuṅkumaiḥ samaiḥ ..
guḍūcyā kṛtakaḥ kalko hitamuṣṇāvalambite .. .. 28 ..
meaning:
धात्रीदुरालभातिक्ता प्रियङ्गुकुङ्कुमैः समैः ..
गुडूच्या कृतकः कल्को हितमुष्णावलम्बिते .. .. 28 ..
text_mt: With equal parts of āmalakī, durālabhā, tiktā, priyaṅgu, and saffron, / a paste prepared with guḍūcī is beneficial when affected by heat.

sanskrit_iast:
upānte ca śirāsrāve muṣkaśophe tathaiva ca ..
kṣiprakāriṇi doṣe ca sadyo vedhanamiṣyate .. 29 ..
meaning:
उपान्ते च शिरास्रावे मुष्कशोफे तथैव च ..
क्षिप्रकारिणि दोषे च सद्यो वेधनमिष्यते .. 29 ..
text_mt: Near the border, vein-bleeding [is done], as well as in swelling of the scrotum; / and when the morbid humor acts swiftly, immediate vein-puncturing is desired.

sanskrit_iast:
gośakṛtsarjikākuṣṭharajanītilasarṣapaiḥ ..
gavāṃ mūtreṇa piṣṭaiśca mardanaṃ kaṇḍunāśanam .. 2.46.30 ..
meaning:
गोशकृत्सर्जिकाकुष्ठरजनीतिलसर्षपैः ..
गवां मूत्रेण पिष्टैश्च मर्दनं कण्डुनाशनम् .. 2.46.30 ..
text_mt: With cow dung, carbonate of soda, kuṣṭha, turmeric, sesame, and mustard, / ground with cow's urine, massage destroys itching.

sanskrit_iast:
sitāmadhuyutaḥ kvātho vāśikāyāḥ saśarkaraḥ ..
raktapittaharaḥ pānādaśvakarṇāttathaiva ca .. 31 ..
meaning:
सितामधुयुतः क्वाथो वाशिकायाः सशर्करः ..
रक्तपित्तहरः पानादश्वकर्णात्तथैव च .. 31 ..
text_mt: A decoction of vāsā with sugar candy and honey, sweetened with sugar, / cures bleeding disease through drinking, as does [a decoction] of aśvakarṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
āme pariṇate pakvaṃ pakvamāṃse jarāṃ gate ..
pakvamāṃsayutaṃ neṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ jīrṇaṃ praśasyate .. 32 ..
meaning:
आमे परिणते पक्वं पक्वमांसे जरां गते ..
पक्वमांसयुतं नेष्टं सर्वं जीर्णं प्रशस्यते .. 32 ..
text_mt: When raw, it is digested into cooked; when cooked meat has gone to digestion, / [food] combined with cooked meat is not desired; everything [fully] digested is praised.

sanskrit_iast:
saptamesaptame deyamaśvānāṃ lavaṇaṃ dine ..
tathā bhuktavatāṃ deyā paripāne tu vāruṇī .. 33 ..
meaning:
सप्तमेसप्तमे देयमश्वानां लवणं दिने ..
तथा भुक्तवतां देया परिपाने तु वारुणी .. 33 ..
text_mt: Salt is to be given to horses every seventh day; / likewise, to those who have eaten, vāruṇī liquor should be given as an after-drink.

sanskrit_iast:
jīvanīyaiḥ sumadhurairmṛdvīkāśarkarāyutaiḥ ..
sapippalīkaiḥ śaradi pratimānaṃ sapadmakam .. 34 ..
meaning:
जीवनीयैः सुमधुरैर्मृद्वीकाशर्करायुतैः ..
सपिप्पलीकैः शरदि प्रतिमानं सपद्मकम् .. 34 ..
text_mt: In autumn, an after-drink with life-giving drugs, very sweet, with raisins and sugar, / together with long pepper and padmaka [should be given].

sanskrit_iast:
viḍaṅgapippalīdhānyāśatāhvā rodhrasaindhavaiḥ ..
sāvitrakaisturaṅgāṇāṃ pratipānaṃ himāgame .. 35 ...
meaning:
विडङ्गपिप्पलीधान्याशताह्वा रोध्रसैन्धवैः ..
सावित्रकैस्तुरङ्गाणां प्रतिपानं हिमागमे .. 35 ...
text_mt: With viḍaṅga, long pepper, coriander, dill, lodhra, and rock salt, / along with sun-plant seeds, [is] the after-drink for horses at the onset of cold.

sanskrit_iast:
rodhraṃ priyaṅgukā rāsnā pippalīviśvabheṣajaiḥ ..
sakṣaudraiḥ pratipānaṃ syādvasante kaphanāśanam .. 36 ..
meaning:
रोध्रं प्रियङ्गुका रास्ना पिप्पलीविश्वभेषजैः ..
सक्षौद्रैः प्रतिपानं स्याद्वसन्ते कफनाशनम् .. 36 ..
text_mt: With lodhra, priyaṅgu, rāsnā, long pepper, and dry ginger, / mixed with honey, there should be an after-drink in spring to destroy kapha.

sanskrit_iast:
priyaṅgupippalīraudrayaṣṭyāhvaiḥ samahauṣadhaiḥ ..
nidāghe saguḍā deyā madirāpratipānake .. 37 ..
meaning:
प्रियङ्गुपिप्पलीरौद्रयष्ट्याह्वैः समहौषधैः ..
निदाघे सगुडा देया मदिराप्रतिपानके .. 37 ..
text_mt: With priyaṅgu, long pepper, lodhra, liquorice, and ginger, / liquor mixed with jaggery should be given as an after-drink in summer.

sanskrit_iast:
bhadrakāṣṭhā salavaṇaṃ pippalyā viśvabheṣajam ..
bhavettailayutairebhiḥ pratipānaṃ ghanāgame .. 38 ..
meaning:
भद्रकाष्ठा सलवणं पिप्पल्या विश्वभेषजम् ..
भवेत्तैलयुतैरेभिः प्रतिपानं घनागमे .. 38 ..
text_mt: Deodar, together with salt, long pepper, and ginger— / combined with oil, these make an after-drink at the onset of the rains.

sanskrit_iast:
nidāghāvṛtapittānāṃ kṣaranmadoṣṇaśoṇitāḥ ..
prāvṛḍbhinnapurīṣāśca pibeyurvājino ghṛtam .. 39 ..
meaning:
निदाघावृतपित्तानां क्षरन्मदोष्णशोणिताः ..
प्रावृड्भिन्नपुरीषाश्च पिबेयुर्वाजिनो घृतम् .. 39 ..
text_mt: Horses whose pitta is aggravated in summer, exuding ichor and hot blood, / and whose stool is loose during the rainy season, should drink clarified butter.

sanskrit_iast:
pibeyurvājinastailaṃ kaphavāyvadhikāstu ye ..
snehavyāpadbhavedyeṣāṃ teṣāṃ kāryaṃ virūkṣaṇam .. 2.46.40 ..
meaning:

text_mt:
Monkeys, goats, and roosters should be kept in the stables, and likewise a milk-cow; / armed men should keep guard over the horses at midnight, O Rāma.
Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter, named 'Treatment of Horses', in the narrative of Puṣkara to Rāma in the conversation of Mārkaṇḍeya, in the second book of the auspicious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Puṣkara said: / Learn from me the regular, occasional, and optional rite of pacification. / On every fifth lunar day one should fervently worship the bearer of Śrī;
and worship should be paid to Śrī and likewise to the king of horses, / O Rāma, to Uccaiḥśravas, constantly with perfumes, garlands, and unguents,
with incenses, lamps, salutations, and an abundance of food. / In autumn and spring, worship of Ekadanta should be performed.
The first, fifth, sixth, seventh, and twelfth lunar days / are praised, O Rāma, especially Sunday.

text_mt:
Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Bhāgya, Āryamṇa, and Aśvinī, / Tvāṣṭra, Sāvitra, Āditya, and Vāyavya, O foremost of the Bhṛgus—
these asterisms are praised, as is the bright fortnight. / In picturesque gardens and on sandy riverbanks,
or in a shrine of the gods, O Rāma, one should perform his worship / with water of hospitality, incense, salutations, lamps, flowers, and an abundance of food;
with boiled half-ripe grains, stuffed sweetmeats, food-preparations, liquor, meat, spirituous drinks, and wines; / with boiled rice, payasa, and auspicious fruits produced in season;
with dance, song, instrumental music, and the sounds of conches. / And one should offer ghee into the fire with the verses addressed to Savitṛ,
preceded by the syllable Om, again and again to Revanta. / Worship of the twice-born should be performed with garlands, sweetmeats, and sandalwood,
and with sacrificial fees in proper order, O knower of dharma. / One should withhold from women everything offered to Revanta.
Worshipped thus, he grants hundreds of horses, / and strength, fiery energy, and health to horses, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

text_mt:
On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month Aśvayuj, O best of men, / the pacification rite for horses should be performed; learn it from me.
Having gone out from the village toward the north-east to a pleasant place, / sloping to the east or north, O Rāma, one should prepare an altar-mound.
To the two Nāsatyas, to the god Varuṇa, and to Aśvayuj, O twice-born, / the wise man, composed, should offer worship with perfumes, garlands, and unguents,
with incenses, lamps, salutations, and abundant food. / Then, having outlined the altar, he should enclose it with branches,
and on all sides with fresh, unwashed garments. / In the cardinal directions he should place pots filled with all fluids according to rule;
and in the intermediate directions the wise man should set up banners and parasols. / Then, having established the fire, again with the Jaya mantras and others,
and having made oblations with the mantras that indicate the specified deities, he should offer clarified butter. / Then the horses are to be worshipped with perfumes and garlands.

Mounted by fully-armored men, the well-armored horses, / accompanied by armed men, should circumambulate the fire.
Having circumambulated the fire three times amidst roarings and cries of triumph, / mingled with the sounds of conches and instruments, they should then be led to their stall.
Those fluids, garments, a cow, bell-metal, and gold / should be given as a sacrificial fee to the officiating priest, O best of twice-born.
Through this rite, one's mounts become plentiful, O Rāma, / vigorous, sturdy, and free from sickness and disease, O knower of dharma.
This regular rite has been described to you; now hear the occasional one: / when a pestilence strikes horses, or when a very terrible disease occurs,
or when an unnatural alteration happens, O descendant of Bhṛgu's lineage, / one should prepare an altar-mound in a pure place in the horse enclosure.
One should draw a lotus there; in its center one should worship Hari / and the goddess Śrī right there, and in the filaments the deities:

Brahmā, Śaṅkara, Soma, Āditya, and the two Aśvins, / Revanta, Uccaiḥśravas, and the guardians of the directions upon the petals.
Worship of all of them should be performed with perfume, incense, an abundance of food, / lamps, garlands, salutations, flowers, roots, and milk-products;
for each [deity] with full jars adorned with perfumes, garlands, and the like, / with dishes of meat, vessels filled with rice grains,
and with protective amulets and banners, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Having prepared an altar to the north of it according to rule,
and having then established the fire, [offering] to each of the deities mentioned, / then, following the oblation into the fire, bell-metal, a cow, and gold,
and a pair of garments must be given to the officiant and likewise to the patron. / This rite destroys all diseases and dispels all afflictions.
It should be performed according to rule by a fasting brahmin; / the patron too should remain fasting at that time, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

Hereafter I shall declare to you the optional rite, O sinless one. / The patron and the priest should always fast on [the asterism] Pauṣṇa;
they should always perform a bath under the asterism Aśvinī, which learn from me: / two water-jars containing untimely roots, filled with Madhūka blossoms,
and combined with aśvagandhā, being prepared, he should then be bathed with them. / The wise man should worship the highest [Lord], the two Nāsatyas, and the Moon.
Wearing white garments, [he should worship] the Aśvins, Varuṇa, and Hari, / with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food.
Then a pair of horses should be made of clay mixed with all medicinal herbs; / then, bowing down, the wise man should offer it to the two Nāsatyas.
He should offer horse-hoof as incense, and in the same way to the deities / as described, O best of the twice-born, he should offer oblations separately,
with their names in the dative case, preceded by the praṇava, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / and ending with 'svāhā', hundreds of times, with ghee purified by mantras, O twice-born.

Horse hair should be worn, as well as fruits and roots; / having braided them together into three strands, an amulet should be worn as before.
Never omitting reverence to the Aśvins, a restrained man should always bathe; / he obtains horses by the thousands, born of noble breed, endowed with vigor and strength.
Puṣkara said: / Elephants are the supreme splendor of an encampment and of an army; / victory for earthly kings resides in elephants alone.
The king should duly take care in cleaning them and guarding them, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / elephants are regarded as gandharvas.
Only so many victorious [elephants] should be kept as can be comfortably nourished; / they should not be kept hungry and distressed.
When distressed, they would destroy the dynasties of men, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / therefore comfort should be given to them, which bestows fame, prosperity, and victory.
Even if an army capable of driving off the enemy's force is equipped / with numerous well-accoutred horses mounted by armoured warriors,

even then, O twice-born, it is impossible to stand in battle in front / of even a single armoured elephant rushing with momentum.
A single enraged elephant, properly driven in battle, / can break unbroken arrays and consolidated troops.
Who is able to describe the splendor of one whose temples are wet with rut, / whose eyes are slightly curved, and whose trunk has a vast expanse?
Who is capable of standing before a tusker charging with speed, / with outstretched trunk and stiffened ears?
At whose mere snorting even hundreds of horses, / even well-mounted, swiftly scatter in the ten directions!
That is an army where elephants are; he is a king who possesses elephants; / elephants proud with rut, O Rāma, are victory incarnate.
Endowed with wings, they were the mounts of the gods; but for mortals, they were made wingless / for the purpose of riding, O Rāma, by the Creator himself.

text_mt:
Seeing an army of noble elephants, mighty like a mountain and adorned with banners, / the hearts of enemies sink swiftly; therefore lordly elephants are always foremost.
Puṣkara said: / Hereafter I shall explain the medical treatment of elephants. / In all feverish conditions, [this] must be performed every day:
Sprinkling with ghee and oil, and a location free from wind; / and on the shoulders, O twice-born, treatment should be applied just as in fever.
In jaundice, cow's urine mixed with turmeric is beneficial; / in flatulence, staying in a place sheltered from wind is praised for one sprinkled with oil.
Vāruṇī wine mixed with the five salts should be given as a drink; / boluses should be prepared with viḍaṅga, triphalā, vyoṣa, and rock salt.
During fainting spells, one should not feed the elephant, but make him drink honey-water; / anointment of the head should be done, and errhine therapy is praised.
One should treat foot diseases of elephants with oily and pungent substances; / and cleansing is prescribed with a decoction of the five pastes.

[…] rubbing should be done, and one should feed soft and unctuous food; / with the meat juices of peacocks, partridges, and quails, mixed with long pepper and black pepper,
one should feed the elephant when tremors arise in him. / Tender bilva fruit, lodhra, and dhātakī along with husked grain,
the elephant should eat as a bolus for the destruction of diarrhea. / In stiffness of the trunk, ghee mixed with salt should be given as an errhine.
Gruel prepared with buttermilk, rich in long pepper and black pepper [should be given], / and wild-boar broth should be placed in his ear.
Oil cooked with daśamūla, horsegram, sour gruel, and kākamācī, / mixed with black pepper, cures the disease of throat spasm.
He should make him drink clear liquor combined with the eight ground salts; / or in retention of urine, a boiled decoction of cucumber seeds.
In skin diseases, the elephant should drink neem or vāsā decoction; / cow's urine and viḍaṅga are recommended in worm infections.
Milk boiled with ginger, long pepper, grapes, and sugar / removes wounds and wasting when drunk, and wholesome meat-broth likewise.

Rice cooked with mung beans and mixed with vyoṣa is commended in loss of appetite; / for soothing swelling of the throat, a soup of paṭolī, neem, and durgrāhyā [is recommended].
Trivṛt, vyoṣa, citraka, dantī, arka, śyāmā, spurge, and gajapippalī: / this medicated oil, and likewise an asava made of them, cures abdominal swellings.
Auspicious barks of milky trees, stream-jambū, and boswellia / should be given to alleviate heart disease, along with vidārī and boiled rice with broth.
By incision, blood-letting, unction, drinking of fats, and oily enemas, / he should treat all abscesses that have arisen.
He should drink sixty-day rice with mung-bean soup in autumn ailments; / and a plaster of tender bilva fruits is recommended in waist diseases.
Viḍaṅga, indrayava, asafoetida, pine resin, and the two turmerics: / he should give this bolus in the morning for the relief of all colic.
A tusker's tooth loosened by heavy load should be extracted. / Sixty-day rice, wild rice, and śāli rice are primary for their diet;
barley and wheat are middling, and the rest are remembered as inferior. / In preparing their food, one should carefully avoid burnt grain.

Hereafter, I shall declare recipes that promote mada, / which a king should employ when the time of battle has arrived.
Vāyasa, both kinds of kurava, kākolī, nākulī, and hari, / combined with honey, become a bolus that immediately induces rut.

And one should surround the lotus together with its intermediate petals with a circular line. / Then one should place the Nāsatyas along with the Ādityas in the east.
One should place the Vasus in the fire-quarter (southeast) and the Sādhyas in the southern quarter; / and in the southwest quarter one should place the divine Āṅgirasas.
In the western quarter, the Bhṛgus; and in the northwest, the Maruts; / likewise the Viśvedevas in the north, and one should place the Rudras in Śiva's quarter (northeast).
Having made this ritual placement of deities, one should divide [the space] with a circular line; / outside of it, twice-born one, one should place the sages who are authors of the sūtras.
In the east, O Rāma; in the south, the goddess Sarasvatī; / rivers in the west, and mountains in the north, O joy of the Bhṛgus.
The great elements on the altars located at the corner cubits; / one should place the lotus, discuss, club, and conch beginning with the northeast.
And a square sacred diagram should be made, having four doors; / the measure of the sacred diagram here should depend on the ground; / in the intermediate quarters one should place full jars accompanied by full bowls.

And on seven-cubit poles one should place banners / white, red, white, [and] yellow in due order; / in the cardinal directions, the setting up of archways and the wrapping of the archways
should be done with leaves of milk-trees, flowers, and fruits; / and the measure of an archway is declared to be six cubits.

one should place in the middle, above the archways, [as well as] the Dānavas; / one should place the hosts of deities endowed with characteristics upon the ear-tips,
with weapons, with banners, and Śatakratu with an umbrella; / and one should prepare the arrangement of the elephants of the quarters with medicinal herbs.
On the petal of Śakra, the wise man should place Airāvaṇa with parched grain; / on the southeast petal he should place the elephant Padma made of flowers.
Puṣpadanta, the southern elephant, should be made with priyaṅgu grains; / and in the southwest quarter the elephant Vāmana with flowers.

aśvamaśvaṃ tathānyā ca dakṣiṇā śaktito bhavet .. 53 ..
meaning:
कुल्माषपरमान्नाभ्यां पूज्यास्ते कृसरेण च ..
भूदकोल्लोपिकाभक्ष्यैः सितया गुडफाणितैः .. 46 ..
मासौदनपयःक्षौद्रदधिपायससक्तुभिः ..
अपूपफलमूलान्नरागखण्डवकैर्दलैः .. 47 ..
एवं सम्पूजनं कृत्त्वा शङ्खवाद्यरवैर्द्विज ..
गीतेन च महाभाग सुभगानर्तितेन च .. 48 ..
ततस्तु पूजनं कृत्वा पूजास्थानात्तथाप्युदक्..
आहिताग्निकुलादग्निं वेदिमुल्लिख्य बोधयेत् .. 49 ..
देवतानां तु सर्वासामेकैकं तु पृथक्पृथक् ..
चतुर्थ्यन्तेन नाम्ना तु प्रणवाद्येन भार्गव .. 2.50.50 ..
शतमाज्येन जुहयान्महाव्याहृतयस्तथा ..
ततस्तु पूजिता नागा वह्निं देवगणान्द्विजान्..51..
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं सर्वे व्रजेयुः स्वगृहाणि ते ..
उपद्रष्ट्रे तथा कर्त्रे सर्वं तत्र निवेदयेत् ..52..
भवेन्निष्कं च निष्कं च धेनुधेनुं भुवंभुवम् ..
अश्वमश्वं तथान्या च दक्षिणा शक्तितो भवेत् .. 53 ..
text_mt:
They should be worshipped with kulmāṣa grain and boiled rice with milk, and with kṛsara, / with pastries and ollopikā sweets, with sugar, jaggery, and treacle,
with meat, boiled rice, milk, honey, curds, rice pudding, and roasted barley meal, / with cakes, fruits, roots, foods, spiced drinks, sweetmeats, and leaves.
Having thus performed the worship accompanied by the sounds of conches and instruments, twice-born one, / and by song, O fortunate one, and by auspicious dances,
having performed the worship, then north of the place of worship / one should kindle fire taken from the household of a consecrated fire-keeper, having inscribed an altar.
For all the deities, one by one separately, / using the name ending in the dative case and preceded by the Praṇava, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
one should offer a hundred oblations of clarified butter, and likewise the Great Utterances; / then, having worshipped the elephants, the fire, the hosts of deities, and the twice-born,
and having circumambulated them clockwise, they should all go to their own homes; / one should present everything there to the overseer and to the priest.
A niṣka and a niṣka, a cow and a cow, a plot of land and a plot of land, / a horse and a horse should be given, and other sacrificial fees according to one's capacity;

sanskrit_iast:
na bhavetsā mahādroṇā kathañcidapi kasyacit ..
tathā ca hastibhiṣajā pravṛttena ca bhūriṇā .. 54 ..
meaning:
न भवेत्सा महाद्रोणा कथञ्चिदपि कस्यचित् ..
तथा च हस्तिभिषजा प्रवृत्तेन च भूरिणा .. 54 ..
text_mt: it should not cause great injury in any way to anyone; / and by the physician of elephants, engaged [for the rite] with abundant [means],

sanskrit_iast:
pūjanīyau tathaivātra sāṃvatsara purohitau ..
hastinyāṃ madamattāyāṃ śāntike'smindvijottama .. 55 ..
meaning:
पूजनीयौ तथैवात्र सांवत्सर पुरोहितौ ..
हस्तिन्यां मदमत्तायां शान्तिकेऽस्मिन्द्विजोत्तम .. 55 ..
text_mt: the astrologer and the royal priest must likewise be worshipped here; / when a female elephant is intoxicated with rut, in this pacification rite, O best of the twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
rāṣṭrānnirvāsya tāṃ kuryācchāntimetāṃ dvijottama ..
nāgarājñi mṛte kṛtvā tatraivānyaṃ mataṅgajam .. 56 ..
meaning:
राष्ट्रान्निर्वास्य तां कुर्याच्छान्तिमेतां द्विजोत्तम ..
नागराज्ञि मृते कृत्वा तत्रैवान्यं मतङ्गजम् .. 56 ..
text_mt: having expelled her from the kingdom, one should perform this pacification rite, O best of the twice-born; / when the royal elephant has died, having placed another elephant right there,

sanskrit_iast:
snātaṃ sarvauṣadhairnāgaṃ sarvagandhaistathaiva ca ..
sarvabījaiśca ratnaiśca sarvatīrthajalaistathā .. 57 ..
meaning:
स्नातं सर्वौषधैर्नागं सर्वगन्धैस्तथैव च ..
सर्वबीजैश्च रत्नैश्च सर्वतीर्थजलैस्तथा .. 57 ..
text_mt: an elephant bathed with all medicinal herbs, and with all fragrant substances, / and with all seeds, with jewels, and with waters of all holy fords,

sanskrit_iast:
āhatāmbarasaṃvītadarśanaṃ śvetalakṣaṇam ..
kāñcanāpīḍite vādyagītapuṇyāhanisvanaiḥ .. 58 ..
meaning:
आहताम्बरसंवीतदर्शनं श्वेतलक्षणम् ..
काञ्चनापीडिते वाद्यगीतपुण्याहनिस्वनैः .. 58 ..
text_mt: wrapped in fresh cloth, endowed with white auspicious marks, / crowned with a gold diadem, amid the sounds of instruments, song, and benedictory chants,

sanskrit_iast:
arcitaṃ daivato vahniṃ kṛtaviprapradakṣiṇam ..
kariṇīṃ tu samāruhya vadetkarṇe tu kālavit .. 59 ..
meaning:
अर्चितं दैवतो वह्निं कृतविप्रप्रदक्षिणम् ..
करिणीं तु समारुह्य वदेत्कर्णे तु कालवित् .. 59 ..
text_mt: worshipped with deity offerings, having circumambulated the fire and the brahmins clockwise, / mounting a female elephant, the knower of time should speak into its ear:

sanskrit_iast:
śrīgajastvatkṛte rājā bhavasvāsya gajāgraṇīḥ ..
gandhamālyāgrabhaktaistvāṃ pūjayiṣyati pārthivaḥ .. 2.50.60 ..
meaning:
श्रीगजस्त्वत्कृते राजा भवस्वास्य गजाग्रणीः ..
गन्धमाल्याग्रभक्तैस्त्वां पूजयिष्यति पार्थिवः .. 2.50.60 ..
text_mt: ‘You have become the royal elephant on the king's behalf; become the leader of his elephants; / the lord of the earth will honour you with scents, garlands, and the first portions of food;

sanskrit_iast:
lokastadājñayā pūjāṃ kariṣyati tathānagha ..
pālanīyastvayā rājā ghorayuddhe tathāhave .. 61 ..
meaning:
लोकस्तदाज्ञया पूजां करिष्यति तथानघ ..
पालनीयस्त्वया राजा घोरयुद्धे तथाहवे .. 61 ..
text_mt: the people, by his command, will likewise offer worship [to you], O sinless one; / the king must be protected by you in fierce battle and in war.

sanskrit_iast:
tiryagbhāvaṃ samutsṛjya divyaṃ bhāvamanusmara ..
devāsurāṇāṃ yuddhe ca śrīgajastridaśaiḥ kṛtaḥ .. 62 ..
meaning:
तिर्यग्भावं समुत्सृज्य दिव्यं भावमनुस्मर ..
देवासुराणां युद्धे च श्रीगजस्त्रिदशैः कृतः .. 62 ..
text_mt: Casting aside your animal nature, remember your divine nature; / in the war between gods and asuras, the royal elephant was created by the thirty [gods].

sanskrit_iast:
airāvaṇasutaḥ śrīmānariṣṭo nāma rāvaṇaḥ ..
śrīgajānāṃ tu tattejaḥ sarvamevātra tiṣṭhati .. 63 ..
meaning:
ऐरावणसुतः श्रीमानरिष्टो नाम रावणः ..
श्रीगजानां तु तत्तेजः सर्वमेवात्र तिष्ठति .. 63 ..
text_mt: The glorious son of Airāvaṇa, named Ariṣṭarāvaṇa, [arose]; / and all the splendor of royal elephants resides in you here.

sanskrit_iast:
tattejastava nāgendra divyabhāgasamanvitam ..
upatiṣṭhatu bhadraṃ te rakṣa rājānamāhave .. 64 ..
meaning:
तत्तेजस्तव नागेन्द्र दिव्यभागसमन्वितम् ..
उपतिष्ठतु भद्रं ते रक्ष राजानमाहवे .. 64 ..
text_mt: May that splendor, endowed with a divine share, attend upon you, O king of elephants; / may all be well with you; protect the king in battle!’

sanskrit_iast:
ityevamabhiṣiktvena śubhe'hani narādhipaḥ ..
nityaṃ caivāsya kartavyaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ svastivācanam .. 65 ..
meaning:
इत्येवमभिषिक्त्वेन शुभेऽहनि नराधिपः ..
नित्यं चैवास्य कर्तव्यं ब्राह्मणैः स्वस्तिवाचनम् .. 65 ..
text_mt: Thus consecrated on an auspicious day, the lord of men / must always have the blessing recited for him by brahmins.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyānugamanaṃ kuryuḥ śastrahastāśca mānavāḥ ..
sitavarṇaśca kartavyo rājñaḥ puṇyāhakarmasu .. 66 ..
meaning:
तस्यानुगमनं कुर्युः शस्त्रहस्ताश्च मानवाः ..
सितवर्णश्च कर्तव्यो राज्ञः पुण्याहकर्मसु .. 66 ..
text_mt: Men with weapons in hand should form his escort; / and he should be painted white in the king's auspicious rites.

sanskrit_iast:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ gajānāṃ śāntikarmasu ..
nakṣatrāṇi praśastāni tithayaśca tathā śṛṇu .. 67 ..
meaning:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं गजानां शान्तिकर्मसु ..
नक्षत्राणि प्रशस्तानि तिथयश्च तथा शृणु .. 67 ..
text_mt: All this has been told to you regarding pacification rites for elephants; / now listen to the praised lunar mansions and lunar days:

sanskrit_iast:
caturdaśīṃ caturthīṃ ca navamīṃ ca vivarjayet ..
aṅgārakadine rāma dinaṃ bhāskarajasya ca .. 68 ..
meaning:
चतुर्दशीं चतुर्थीं च नवमीं च विवर्जयेत् ..
अङ्गारकदिने राम दिनं भास्करजस्य च .. 68 ..
text_mt: one should avoid the fourteenth, the fourth, and the ninth [tithis], / the day of Mars, O Rāma, and the day of the son of the Sun (Saturday).

sanskrit_iast:
ṛkṣāṇi vaiṣṇavaṃ tvāṣṭraṃ śasyate śakradaivatam ..
nakṣatrāṇi muhūrtāśca eta eva mahābala .. 69 ..
meaning:
ऋक्षाणि वैष्णवं त्वाष्ट्रं शस्यते शक्रदैवतम् ..
नक्षत्राणि मुहूर्ताश्च एत एव महाबल .. 69 ..
text_mt: The constellations sacred to Viṣṇu, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Śakra are commended. / These are the asterisms and the auspicious moments, O mighty one.

sanskrit_iast:
deśakālopasampannaṃ vidhinā ca tathā kṛtam ..
śāntikarma gajendrāṇāṃ sarvabādhāvināśanam .. 2.50.70 ..
meaning:
देशकालोपसम्पन्नं विधिना च तथा कृतम् ..
शान्तिकर्म गजेन्द्राणां सर्वबाधाविनाशनम् .. 2.50.70 ..
text_mt: Performed in accordance with place, time, and rules, / this rite of pacification for lordly elephants destroys all afflictions;

sanskrit_iast:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ rājñāṃ ca vijayāvaham ..
bhārgavaścyavanaḥ kruddho yathā śakrasya bhārgava .. 71 ..
meaning:
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं राज्ञां च विजयावहम् ..
भार्गवश्च्यवनः क्रुद्धो यथा शक्रस्य भार्गव .. 71 ..
text_mt: it brings fortune, renown, longevity, and victory to kings. / Just as the descendant of Bhṛgu, Cyavana, when enraged against Śakra, O Bhārgava,

sanskrit_iast:
mado nāma samutpannastathā daityaḥ sudāruṇaḥ ..
indranāśāya śakrārthī tataḥ paścātprasāditaḥ .. 72 ..
meaning:
मदो नाम समुत्पन्नस्तथा दैत्यः सुदारुणः ..
इन्द्रनाशाय शक्रार्थी ततः पश्चात्प्रसादितः .. 72 ..
text_mt: produced a most dreadful demon named Mada / to slay Indra, desiring [to subdue] Śakra, and was thereafter propitiated;

sanskrit_iast:
madaṃ sa bahudhā cakre prajāpatisamo dvija ..
strīṣvakṣeṣu tathā pāne mṛgayāyāṃ dhane tathā .. 73 ..
meaning:
मदं स बहुधा चक्रे प्रजापतिसमो द्विज ..
स्त्रीष्वक्षेषु तथा पाने मृगयायां धने तथा .. 73 ..
text_mt: that twice-born sage, equal to Prajāpati, divided Mada into many parts: / in women, in dice, in drinking, in hunting, in wealth,

sanskrit_iast:
vidyāsu caiva sarvāsu sarvaśilpeṣu cāpyatha ..
jīveṣu rāma sarveṣu tathā rūpe bale kule .. 74 ..
meaning:
विद्यासु चैव सर्वासु सर्वशिल्पेषु चाप्यथ ..
जीवेषु राम सर्वेषु तथा रूपे बले कुले .. 74 ..
text_mt: and in all branches of learning, and in all crafts, / in all living beings, O Rāma, as well as in beauty, strength, and noble birth;

sanskrit_iast:
eko'sya dhāraṇe śakto na kaściditicintayan ..
yathokteṣvadhikaṃ bhāgaṃ kiñcitpāne niveśayet .. 75 ..
meaning:
एकोऽस्य धारणे शक्तो न कश्चिदितिचिन्तयन् ..
यथोक्तेष्वधिकं भागं किञ्चित्पाने निवेशयेत् .. 75 ..
text_mt: reflecting that no single being would be capable of bearing it, / he placed a larger portion in liquor among those mentioned,

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇināmatha sarveṣāṃ nāgeṣvabhyadhikaṃ tathā ..
mado yadā samabhyeti nāgaṃ brāhmaṇasattama .. 76 ..
meaning:
प्राणिनामथ सर्वेषां नागेष्वभ्यधिकं तथा ..
मदो यदा समभ्येति नागं ब्राह्मणसत्तम .. 76 ..
text_mt: and similarly an even greater portion among elephants of all living creatures. / When rut comes upon an elephant, O best of brahmins,

sanskrit_iast:
rāma śāntistadā kāryā yādṛśī tāṃ nibodha me ..
śālāprāguttare bhāge sthaṇḍilaṃ kalpayedbudhaḥ .. 77 ..
meaning:
राम शान्तिस्तदा कार्या यादृशी तां निबोध मे ..
शालाप्रागुत्तरे भागे स्थण्डिलं कल्पयेद्बुधः .. 77 ..
text_mt: the pacification that should then be performed, O Rāma, learn that from me: / In the north-eastern part of the stall, the wise man should prepare an altar.

sanskrit_iast:
sthaṇḍile kamalaṃ kṛtvā dikpatreṣu tatheśvarān ..
kesaraṃ cyavanaṃ nāgānbhuvaṃ kaṃ ca sarasvatīm .. 78 ..
meaning:
स्थण्डिले कमलं कृत्वा दिक्पत्रेषु तथेश्वरान् ..
केसरं च्यवनं नागान्भुवं कं च सरस्वतीम् .. 78 ..
text_mt: Having made a lotus upon the altar, [he should worship] the lords of the directions on the petals, / Cyavana on the filaments, the elephants, the earth, Brahmā, and Sarasvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
pūjayeḍḍiṇḍimaṃ madhye gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ ..
dhūpadīpanamaskārairvāsobhiśca pṛthakpṛthak .. 79 ..
meaning:
पूजयेड्डिण्डिमं मध्ये गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः ..
धूपदीपनमस्कारैर्वासोभिश्च पृथक्पृथक् .. 79 ..
text_mt: In the center, he should worship the ḍiṇḍima drum with perfumes, garlands, and unguents, / with incense, lamps, obeisance, and garments, each separately.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāsāṃ pūjanaṃ kṛtvā pādyādyanurato dvija ..
devatānāṃ ghṛtaṃ hutvā yathāśraddhamaninditam.. 2.50.80
meaning:
सर्वासां पूजनं कृत्वा पाद्याद्यनुरतो द्विज ..
देवतानां घृतं हुत्वा यथाश्रद्धमनिन्दितम्.. 2.50.80
text_mt: Having offered worship to all [the deities] with water for feet and the rest, devoted [to the rite], the twice-born / should offer oblations of ghee to the deities according to his faith, blamelessly.

sanskrit_iast:
rasapūrṇo ghaṭo deyo dakṣiṇārthe ca kāñcanam ..
dattvā vāsāṃsi nāgasya gajādhyakṣaṃ ca pūjayet .. 81 ..
meaning:
रसपूर्णो घटो देयो दक्षिणार्थे च काञ्चनम् ..
दत्त्वा वासांसि नागस्य गजाध्यक्षं च पूजयेत् .. 81 ..
text_mt: A jar filled with sweet liquids should be given, and gold for the sacrificial fee. / Having given garments to the elephant, he should also honour the superintendent of elephants,

sanskrit_iast:
hastipaṃ karmiṇaścānyāndakṣiṇābhirdvijottamān ..
sāṃvatsare ca vittena yataḥ sāṃvatsaraḥ svayam..82..
meaning:
हस्तिपं कर्मिणश्चान्यान्दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजोत्तमान् ..
सांवत्सरे च वित्तेन यतः सांवत्सरः स्वयम्..82..
text_mt: the mahout, other workers, and the best of twice-borns with sacrificial fees, / and [he should honour] the astrologer with wealth, since the astrologer is himself [an embodiment of time].

sanskrit_iast:
gajādhyakṣāya taṃ dadyāddiṇḍimaṃ prayataḥ svayam..
prāṅmukhaśca gajādhyakṣo vādayettaṃ yathāvidhi .. 83 ..
meaning:
गजाध्यक्षाय तं दद्याद्दिण्डिमं प्रयतः स्वयम्..
प्राङ्मुखश्च गजाध्यक्षो वादयेत्तं यथाविधि .. 83 ..
text_mt: Controlled in mind, he should personally hand over that ḍiṇḍima drum to the superintendent of elephants; / and facing east, the superintendent of elephants should beat it according to rule.

sanskrit_iast:
uccairgambhīranirghoṣe ḍiṇḍime tu śubhaṃ vadet ..
antarā pātite tasmim̐stathaivāpyaśubhaṃ vadet .. 84 ..
meaning:
उच्चैर्गम्भीरनिर्घोषे डिण्डिमे तु शुभं वदेत् ..
अन्तरा पातिते तस्मिम्̐स्तथैवाप्यशुभं वदेत् .. 84 ..
text_mt: If the ḍiṇḍima drum gives a loud and deep resonance, one should declare it auspicious; / but if it is dropped in the middle, one should declare it inauspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
ḍiṇḍime samyagādatte śubhameva vinirdiśet ..
tadā prabhṛti mattasya tadā nāgasya vai nṛpa .. 85 ..
meaning:
डिण्डिमे सम्यगादत्ते शुभमेव विनिर्दिशेत् ..
तदा प्रभृति मत्तस्य तदा नागस्य वै नृप .. 85 ..
text_mt: If the ḍiṇḍima drum is taken up properly, one should point out that it is entirely auspicious. / From that time on, of that elephant in rut, O king,

sanskrit_iast:
aśubhe lakṣaṇe jāte bhūyastatkarma cācaret ..
śubhe tu lakṣaṇe jāte gajādhyakṣasya ḍiṇḍimam .. 86..
meaning:
अशुभे लक्षणे जाते भूयस्तत्कर्म चाचरेत् ..

Endowed with good character, a king, though employing few allies and arrows, / effects the slaughter of enemies arrogant with their vast force of elephants and horses in battles.
Puṣkara said:
Henceforth I shall describe to you the medical treatment of men;
and even of those, first that of women, since reproduction is rooted in them.
One should drink both large jambu varieties, rodhra, madhuka, honey, and sugar,
mixed with rice-water, for menorrhagia.
After a year, one should purge a woman suffering from a blood tumor (raktagulma),
when her body has been lubricated and sweated, O Rāma, with sharp purgatives.
And in fever she should drink barley-gruel prepared with palāśa;
and for others, kindling of the digestive fire must likewise be performed with effort.
One should cook a prastha of oil with a prastha of vṛṣaka root;
it removes pain in disorders of the vaginal tract.
Saurāṣṭrī, rocanā, rodhra, madhūka, triphalā, honey,
and powders of bhadramustā are an excellent aphrodisiac.

text_mt:
Anointment with boar's fat boiled with aśvagandhā
is declared to bring about tightening of bodily tissues for women.
One should drink one āmalaka at the proper time with a handful of water,
after it has remained in an iron vessel; by that, she becomes slender-waisted.
One should always lick triphalā, citraka, and dry ginger with honey;
this is an excellent slimming regimen for corpulent, noble women.
Having mixed aśvagandhā and payasyā, one should drink them with milk;
using this for a month, an emaciated woman becomes fleshy.
Massaging the breasts should be done with boar's fat
boiled with aśvagandhā; by this, a woman becomes full-breasted.
Fallen radish seed and likewise [seed] of tagara,
[kept] in cow's urine for seven nights, is an excellent destroyer of sidhma-leprosy.
With the ash of elephant dung and the juice of avalguja—
sprinkled with this, white leprosy (śvitra) is destroyed in three nights.
The root of guñjā along with its fruit, citraka, tagara,
the fruit of bhallātaka, and the root of aśvamāraka—

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭukaṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ tu gomūtraparibhāvitam ..
bhuktvā tailena gaṇḍūṣaṃ vaktragandhaharaṃ param .. ..18..
meaning:
कटुकं दन्तकाष्ठं तु गोमूत्रपरिभावितम् ..
भुक्त्वा तैलेन गण्डूषं वक्त्रगन्धहरं परम् .. ..18..
text_mt:
A bitter tooth-stick impregnated with cow's urine;
and after eating, an oil gargle is supreme in removing mouth odor.

sanskrit_iast:
indīvarāṇi śuṣkāṇi prāśyāni taṇḍulaissaha ..
sarvarātraṃ mukhe vāti sugandhiviśadaṃ śuci ..19..
meaning:
इन्दीवराणि शुष्काणि प्राश्यानि तण्डुलैस्सह ..
सर्वरात्रं मुखे वाति सुगन्धिविशदं शुचि ..19..
text_mt:
Dried blue lotuses are to be eaten together with rice;
all night long, [her breath] blows sweet-smelling, clean, and pure in the mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
sarṣaponmathitaṃ kṛtvā śālmalīnāṃ tu kaṇṭakaiḥ ..
payaḥpiṣṭairmukhe lepānmukhaṃ syātkamalopamam .. 2.52.20 ..
meaning:
सर्षपोन्मथितं कृत्वा शाल्मलीनां तु कण्टकैः ..
पयःपिष्टैर्मुखे लेपान्मुखं स्यात्कमलोपमम् .. 2.52.20 ..
text_mt:
Having prepared a paste of mustard and the thorns of the silk-cotton tree
ground with milk, through application on the face, the face becomes like a lotus.

sanskrit_iast:
vyaṅgānāṃ tilakānāṃ ca śamanaṃ tatprakīrtitam ..
yauvane piṭakānāṃ ca ye ca doṣā mukhe smṛtāḥ .. 21 ..
meaning:
व्यङ्गानां तिलकानां च शमनं तत्प्रकीर्तितम् ..
यौवने पिटकानां च ये च दोषा मुखे स्मृताः .. 21 ..
text_mt:
It is declared to pacify dark facial spots, freckles,
youthful pimples, and whatever blemishes are known on the face.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṣāyakalkasiddhena śatāvaryā ghṛtena ca ..
abhyaṅgapānairbhavati nārī varṇayutā param .. 22 ..
meaning:
कषायकल्कसिद्धेन शतावर्या घृतेन च ..
अभ्यङ्गपानैर्भवति नारी वर्णयुता परम् .. 22 ..
text_mt:
By anointment and drinking of ghee prepared with the decoction and paste
of śatāvarī, a woman becomes possessed of supreme complexion.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣoḍaśartuniśāḥ strīṇāmādyāstisrastu ninditāḥ ..
aspṛśyā tāsu nārī syātspṛṣṭvā tāṃ snānamācaret .. 23 ..
meaning:
षोडशर्तुनिशाः स्त्रीणामाद्यास्तिस्रस्तु निन्दिताः ..
अस्पृश्या तासु नारी स्यात्स्पृष्ट्वा तां स्नानमाचरेत् .. 23 ..
text_mt:
Sixteen nights are the fertile period (ṛtu) of women; but the first three are censured.
During those [three nights], a woman is untouchable; having touched her, one should perform a bath.

sanskrit_iast:
dinatrayaṃ tu tannārī snānābhyaṅgau vivarjayet ..
āhāraṃ gorasānāṃ ca puṣpālaṅkāradhāraṇam .. 24 ..
meaning:
दिनत्रयं तु तन्नारी स्नानाभ्यङ्गौ विवर्जयेत् ..
आहारं गोरसानां च पुष्पालङ्कारधारणम् .. 24 ..
text_mt:
For three days that woman should avoid bathing and oil anointment,
food made from cow's milk, and wearing flowers and ornaments,

sanskrit_iast:
añjanaṃ kaṅkaṇaṃ gandhāḥ pītaṃ śayyādhirohaṇam ..
mṛllohabhāṇḍavarjyeṣu tathā bhāṇḍeṣu bhojanam .. 25 ..
meaning:
अञ्जनं कङ्कणं गन्धाः पीतं शय्याधिरोहणम् ..
मृल्लोहभाण्डवर्ज्येषु तथा भाण्डेषु भोजनम् .. 25 ..
text_mt:
collyrium, bracelets, perfumes, yellow garments, mounting a bed,
and eating in vessels other than earthenware and iron vessels.

sanskrit_iast:
agnisaṃsparśanaṃ caiva varjayettu dinatrayam ..
caturthe'hani kurvīta snānaṃ sā tu yathāvidhi .. 26 ..
meaning:
अग्निसंस्पर्शनं चैव वर्जयेत्तु दिनत्रयम् ..
चतुर्थेऽहनि कुर्वीत स्नानं सा तु यथाविधि .. 26 ..
text_mt:
And she should avoid touching fire for three days;
on the fourth day, however, she should bathe according to rule.

sanskrit_iast:
abhiṣekoditābhiśca mṛddhiradbhiśca mānasaiḥ ..
oṣadhyaśca tathā kumbhe nikṣipya snāpayettu tām ..27..
meaning:
अभिषेकोदिताभिश्च मृद्धिरद्भिश्च मानसैः ..
ओषध्यश्च तथा कुम्भे निक्षिप्य स्नापयेत्तु ताम् ..27..
text_mt:
And with earths prescribed for consecration, and waters from Lake Mānasa,
and throwing herbs into a jar, one should bathe her:

sanskrit_iast:
jyotiṣmatīṃ trāyamāṇāmabhayāmaparājitām ..
jīvāṃ viśveśvarīṃ pāṭhāṃ samaṅgāṃ vijayāṃ tathā .. 28 ..
meaning:
ज्योतिष्मतीं त्रायमाणामभयामपराजिताम् ..
जीवां विश्वेश्वरीं पाठां समङ्गां विजयां तथा .. 28 ..
text_mt:
jyotiṣmatī, trāyamāṇā, abhayā, aparājitā,
jīvā, viśveśvarī, pāṭhā, samaṅgā, vijayā,

sanskrit_iast:
sahāṃ ca sahadevīṃ ca pūrṇakośāṃ śatāvarīm ..
ariṣṭāṃ śivāṃ bhadrāṃ golomīṃ vijayapradām .. 29 ..
meaning:
सहां च सहदेवीं च पूर्णकोशां शतावरीम् ..
अरिष्टां शिवां भद्रां गोलोमीं विजयप्रदाम् .. 29 ..
text_mt:
sahā, sahadevī, pūrṇakośā, śatāvarī,
ariṣṭā, śivā, bhadrā, golomī, vijayapradā,

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmīṃ kṣetrāmajāṃ caiva sarvabījāni cāñjanam ..
bilvaṃ gandhāni ratnāni pañcagavyaṃ tathaiva ca .. 2.52.30 ..
meaning:
ब्राह्मीं क्षेत्रामजां चैव सर्वबीजानि चाञ्जनम् ..
बिल्वं गन्धानि रत्नानि पञ्चगव्यं तथैव च .. 2.52.30 ..
text_mt:
brāhmī, kṣetrā, ajā, all kinds of seeds, collyrium,
bilva, perfumes, jewels, and likewise the five products of the cow (pañcagavya)—

sanskrit_iast:
kumbhe nikṣipya kumbhaṃ ca gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ ..
pūjayitvā tato devaṃ tasyātra śubhavardhanam .. 31 ..
meaning:
कुम्भे निक्षिप्य कुम्भं च गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः ..
पूजयित्वा ततो देवं तस्यात्र शुभवर्धनम् .. 31 ..
text_mt:
having thrown [these] into a jar and having worshiped the jar
with perfumes, garlands, and unguents, and then the deity who increases auspiciousness for her here,

sanskrit_iast:
mantraṃ rājābhiṣekoktaṃ paṭhedatra ca kālavit ..
vastracchannamukhī snātā snāpake ca vinirgate .. .. 32 ..
meaning:
मन्त्रं राजाभिषेकोक्तं पठेदत्र च कालवित् ..
वस्त्रच्छन्नमुखी स्नाता स्नापके च विनिर्गते .. .. 32 ..
text_mt:
the knower of proper time should recite the mantra prescribed for the royal consecration.
When she has bathed with her face covered by a cloth, and the bath-attendant has departed,

sanskrit_iast:
paśyettadeva pratimāṃ vāsudevasya rūpiṇaḥ ..
athavā rāma bhartāraṃ nānyaṃ kaṃcana satvaram .. 33 ..
meaning:
पश्येत्तदेव प्रतिमां वासुदेवस्य रूपिणः ..
अथवा राम भर्तारं नान्यं कंचन सत्वरम् .. 33 ..
text_mt:
she should promptly behold that very image of Vāsudeva in bodily form,
or else her husband, O Rāma, and no one else.

sanskrit_iast:
tatkāle vadanaṃ tasya paśyatyatha yathā vidhi ..
sā prasūte sutaṃ rāma śubhaṃ vā'pyathavā śucim .. 34 ..
meaning:
तत्काले वदनं तस्य पश्यत्यथ यथा विधि ..
सा प्रसूते सुतं राम शुभं वाऽप्यथवा शुचिम् .. 34 ..
text_mt:
Whose face she beholds at that time according to rule,
she gives birth to a son [like that person], O Rāma, either handsome or pure.

sanskrit_iast:
pūjanaṃ vāsudevasya sā kṛtvātmana eva ca ..
maṇḍanaṃ ca yathānyāyaṃ śuklavastrottaracchadā. ..35 ..
meaning:
पूजनं वासुदेवस्य सा कृत्वात्मन एव च ..
मण्डनं च यथान्यायं शुक्लवस्त्रोत्तरच्छदा. ..35 ..
text_mt:
Having performed the worship of Vāsudeva and also of herself,
and ornamentation according to rule, covered with white garments and an upper garment,

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṣṭikānnaṃ tu payasā samaśnīyād ghṛtena sā ..
ghṛtasya pītvā prasṛtiṃ nāgapuṣpāvacūrṇitam .. 36 ..
meaning:
षष्टिकान्नं तु पयसा समश्नीयाद् घृतेन सा ..
घृतस्य पीत्वा प्रसृतिं नागपुष्पावचूर्णितम् .. 36 ..
text_mt:
she should eat sixty-day rice with milk and ghee;
having drunk a handful of ghee powdered with nāgapuṣpa,

sanskrit_iast:
ṛtukāle samāpnoti nārī garbhaṃ dvijottama ..
upoṣitena śucinā śuklapakṣe samuddhṛtam .. 37 ..
meaning:
ऋतुकाले समाप्नोति नारी गर्भं द्विजोत्तम ..
उपोषितेन शुचिना शुक्लपक्षे समुद्धृतम् .. 37 ..
text_mt:
at the time of the fertile period, a woman attains pregnancy, O best of the twice-born.
Extracted in the bright fortnight by one who is fasting and pure,

sanskrit_iast:
puṣyeṇa bṛhatīmūlamuttarāṃ vā mukhe nayeta ..
śvetapuṣpā tu bṛhatī drumūlasyaiṣa niścayaḥ ..38..
meaning:
पुष्येण बृहतीमूलमुत्तरां वा मुखे नयेत ..
श्वेतपुष्पा तु बृहती द्रुमूलस्यैष निश्चयः ..38..
text_mt:
under Puṣya or the Uttara constellations, she should put the root of bṛhatī into her mouth;
the white-flowered bṛhatī is the determination for this tree-root.

sanskrit_iast:
nasyā deyāśca catvāra unmūlā drumabindavaḥ ..
tasminnahani sā tena garbhaṃ dhatte varāṃganā .. 39 ..
meaning:
नस्या देयाश्च चत्वार उन्मूला द्रुमबिन्दवः ..
तस्मिन्नहनि सा तेन गर्भं धत्ते वरांगना .. 39 ..
text_mt:
Four drops of the tree root are to be given as nasal drops;
on that day, by that, the noble woman conceives an embryo.

sanskrit_iast:
evamapyabhavantī tu putrīyāṃ rāma saptamīm ..
putrīyamathavā snānaṃ keśavārādhanaṃ vratam .. 2.52.40 ..
meaning:
एवमप्यभवन्ती तु पुत्रीयां राम सप्तमीम् ..
पुत्रीयमथवा स्नानं केशवाराधनं व्रतम् .. 2.52.40 ..
text_mt:
Even if this does not happen, O Rāma, [she should observe] the Seventh Day for obtaining a son,
or the son-bestowing bath, or the observance of worshiping Keśava.

sanskrit_iast:
putrīyameva vā kuryātkeśavārādhanaṃ priyā ..
snātānuliptā bhartāraṃ hṛṣṭairbṛṃhitameva ca .. 41 ..
meaning:
पुत्रीयमेव वा कुर्यात्केशवाराधनं प्रिया ..
स्नातानुलिप्ता भर्तारं हृष्टैर्बृंहितमेव च .. 41 ..
text_mt:
Or the beloved wife should perform the worship of Keśava for obtaining a son.
Bathed and anointed, she should go at night to her husband,

sanskrit_iast:
yāyādrātrau tathā nārī gandhadhūpādivāsitā ..
āttagarbhāṃ cikitseta tatastāmaparājita .. 42 ..
meaning:
यायाद्रात्रौ तथा नारी गन्धधूपादिवासिता ..
आत्तगर्भां चिकित्सेत ततस्तामपराजित .. 42 ..
text_mt:
who is invigorated by joyful attendants, while she is perfumed with fragrances and incense.
Then, once she has conceived an embryo, O unconquered one, one should treat her

sanskrit_iast:
madhurauṣadhisiddhena payasā sarpiṣā tathā ..
icchāvimānagāḥ kāścinnāsyāḥ kāryā kathañcana .. 43 ..
meaning:
मधुरौषधिसिद्धेन पयसा सर्पिषा तथा ..
इच्छाविमानगाः काश्चिन्नास्याः कार्या कथञ्चन .. 43 ..
text_mt:
with milk and ghee prepared with sweet herbs.
No desires of hers that contravene her longing should ever be caused.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭutiktakaṣāyāṇi cātyuṣṇalavaṇāni ca ..
āyāsaṃ ca vyavāyaṃ ca garbhiṇī varjayetsadā .. 44 ..
meaning:
कटुतिक्तकषायाणि चात्युष्णलवणानि च ..
आयासं च व्यवायं च गर्भिणी वर्जयेत्सदा .. 44 ..
text_mt:
Pungent, bitter, and astringent, extremely hot and salty foods,
exertion, and sexual intercourse: a pregnant woman should always avoid these.

sanskrit_iast:
vinā karma na tiṣṭheta tathā sā rāhudarśane ..
prādurbhāvāṇi vedesya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ .. 45 ..
meaning:
विना कर्म न तिष्ठेत तथा सा राहुदर्शने ..
प्रादुर्भावाणि वेदेस्य विष्णोरमिततेजसः .. 45 ..
text_mt: Likewise, upon seeing [an eclipse of] Rāhu, she should not remain without performing a religious rite. / She should hear the manifestations of Viṣṇu of immeasurable radiance

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṇuyāttanmanā bhūtvā caritaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ ..
punnāmni nāmanakṣatre hyāsannaprasavā gṛham .. 46 ..
meaning:
शृणुयात्तन्मना भूत्वा चरितं च महात्मनः ..
पुन्नाम्नि नामनक्षत्रे ह्यासन्नप्रसवा गृहम् .. 46 ..
text_mt: and the deeds of that Great-souled One, with her mind fixed on Him. / When childbirth is near, in a male asterism or an auspicious asterism,

sanskrit_iast:
praviśetsūtikāsaṃjñaṃ kṛtarakṣaṃ samantataḥ ..
subhūmau nirmitaṃ ramyaṃ vāstuvidyāviśāradaiḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
प्रविशेत्सूतिकासंज्ञं कृतरक्षं समन्ततः ..
सुभूमौ निर्मितं रम्यं वास्तुविद्याविशारदैः .. 47 ..
text_mt: she should enter the house called the lying-in chamber, which has been protected on all sides, / built on good ground, delightful, by experts in the science of architecture,

sanskrit_iast:
prāgdvāramuttaradvāramathavā sudṛḍhaṃ śubham ..
devānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca gavāṃ kṛtvā ca pūjanam .. 48 ..
meaning:
प्राग्द्वारमुत्तरद्वारमथवा सुदृढं शुभम् ..
देवानां ब्राह्मणानां च गवां कृत्वा च पूजनम् .. 48 ..
text_mt: with an eastern or northern door, very firm and auspicious. / Having worshipped the gods, the brahmins, and the cows,

sanskrit_iast:
vipra puṇyāhaghoṣeṇa śaṃkhavādyaraveṇa ca ..
prasūtā bahuśastatra tathā kleśakṣamāśca yāḥ .. 49 ..
meaning:
विप्र पुण्याहघोषेण शंखवाद्यरवेण च ..
प्रसूता बहुशस्तत्र तथा क्लेशक्षमाश्च याः .. 49 ..
text_mt: O brahmin, to the chanting of 'Auspicious day!' and the sound of conches and musical instruments, / women who have given birth many times and are capable of enduring hardships,

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdyā viśvasanīyāśca paricareyuḥ striyaśca tām ..
vātānulomanairhṛdyaistatraināmupacārayet .. 2.52.50 ..
meaning:
हृद्या विश्वसनीयाश्च परिचरेयुः स्त्रियश्च ताम् ..
वातानुलोमनैर्हृद्यैस्तत्रैनामुपचारयेत् .. 2.52.50 ..
text_mt: charming and trustworthy, should attend upon her. / There one should care for her with delightful things that soothe the bodily wind,

sanskrit_iast:
āhāraiśca vihāraiśca prasavāya sukhaṃ dvija ..
eraṇḍamūlamiśreṇa saghṛtena tathaiva tām .. 51 ..
meaning:
आहारैश्च विहारैश्च प्रसवाय सुखं द्विज ..
एरण्डमूलमिश्रेण सघृतेन तथैव ताम् .. 51 ..
text_mt: both food and activities that ensure an easy delivery, O twice-born. / Likewise, with [a paste of] castor root mixed with clarified butter,

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaprasavanārthāya paścātkāye tu mrakṣayet ..
balākalkakaṣāyeṇa siddhaṃ kṣīraṃ caturguṇam .. 52 ..
meaning:
सुखप्रसवनार्थाय पश्चात्काये तु म्रक्षयेत् ..
बलाकल्ककषायेण सिद्धं क्षीरं चतुर्गुणम् .. 52 ..
text_mt: she should smear her lower body for the sake of an easy delivery. / Milk boiled with four times its quantity of a decoction and paste of balā

sanskrit_iast:
tailamabhyañjanārthāya sūtāyāmupakalpayet ..
atha jātānna pānecchāṃ pañcakolaprasāditām .. 53 ..
meaning:
तैलमभ्यञ्जनार्थाय सूतायामुपकल्पयेत् ..
अथ जातान्न पानेच्छां पञ्चकोलप्रसादिताम् .. 53 ..
text_mt: mixed with oil should be prepared for massage for the woman who has given birth. / Then, when she feels a desire for food and drink, flavored with pañcakola,

sanskrit_iast:
pibedyavāgūṃ sasnehāṃ tathā vai nīlakuñcikām ..
daśāhaṃ sūtikāgāraṃ cāyudhaiśca viśeṣataḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
पिबेद्यवागूं सस्नेहां तथा वै नीलकुञ्चिकाम् ..
दशाहं सूतिकागारं चायुधैश्च विशेषतः .. 54 ..
text_mt: she should drink gruel containing fat and also black cumin. / For ten days the lying-in room [must be guarded], especially with weapons,

sanskrit_iast:
vahni kātindukālātaiḥ pūrṇakumbhaiḥ pradīpakaiḥ ..
musalena tathā dvāri varṇakaiścitritena ca .. 55 ..
meaning:
वह्नि कातिन्दुकालातैः पूर्णकुम्भैः प्रदीपकैः ..
मुसलेन तथा द्वारि वर्णकैश्चित्रितेन च .. 55 ..
text_mt: with fire, glowing cinders of tinduka wood, full jars, lamps, / and with a pestle decorated with pigments at the doorway.

sanskrit_iast:
rakṣaṇīyā tathā ṣaṣṭhī niśā tatra viśeṣataḥ ..
