sanskrit_iast:
taddine tu nadī yatra yoge gacchatu tāṃ mudā ..
suvarṇarūpyagandhaśca dhāraṇīyastathā maṇiḥ .. 15 ..
meaning:
तद्दिने तु नदी यत्र योगे गच्छतु तां मुदा ..
सुवर्णरूप्यगन्धश्च धारणीयस्तथा मणिः .. 15 ..
text_mt: On that day, wherever there is a river, he should gladly go to it at the confluence [or astrological conjunction]; / an amulet of gold, silver, and fragrant substances should be worn.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā rāma dhenuḥ payasvinī ..
snātaḥ punarvasāveva jātiśraiṣṭhyamavāpnuyāt .. 16 ..
meaning:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या राम धेनुः पयस्विनी ..
स्नातः पुनर्वसावेव जातिश्रैष्ठ्यमवाप्नुयात् .. 16 ..
text_mt: And here a milch cow should be given as the sacrificial fee, O Rāma. / Having bathed under Punarvasu alone, one attains superiority of caste,

sanskrit_iast:
putrānvā sumahābhāga yadīcchati tadāpnuyāt ..
gaurasarṣapakalkena rāmotsāditavigrahaḥ ..17..
meaning:
पुत्रान्वा सुमहाभाग यदीच्छति तदाप्नुयात् ..
गौरसर्षपकल्केन रामोत्सादितविग्रहः ..17..
text_mt: or sons, O highly fortunate one, if he desires; he obtains whatever he wishes. / With his body smeared with paste of white mustard, O Rāma,

sanskrit_iast:
gavyājyapūrṇakumbhena snātaḥ snātastathauṣadhaiḥ ..
ahatāmbarasaṃvītaḥ pāyasaṃ vinivedayet .. 18 ..
meaning:
गव्याज्यपूर्णकुम्भेन स्नातः स्नातस्तथौषधैः ..
अहताम्बरसंवीतः पायसं विनिवेदयेत् .. 18 ..
text_mt: bathed with a jar filled with cow's ghee, and likewise bathed with medicinal herbs, / dressed in unwashed garments, he should offer rice boiled in milk,

sanskrit_iast:
śuklāni caiva mālyāni vāsāṃsyapahatāni ca ..
homaśca pāyasenātra dhūpaṃ gandhaiśca dāpayet .. 19 ..
meaning:
शुक्लानि चैव माल्यानि वासांस्यपहतानि च ..
होमश्च पायसेनात्र धूपं गन्धैश्च दापयेत् .. 19 ..
text_mt: and white garlands and unwashed garments. / Here the fire offering is with rice boiled in milk, and he should offer incense of perfumes.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇiḥ śirasi dhāryaśca daṇḍāgre brahmacāriṇaḥ ..
suvarṇagarbhaṃ puṣpeṇa snānaṃ puṣṭikaraṃ bhavet ..2.99.20...
meaning:
मणिः शिरसि धार्यश्च दण्डाग्रे ब्रह्मचारिणः ..
सुवर्णगर्भं पुष्पेण स्नानं पुष्टिकरं भवेत् ..2.99.20...
text_mt: The amulet should be worn on the head, or on the tip of the staff for a brahmacārin. / The bath containing gold and flowers brings nourishment.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā ghṛtaṃ kanakasaṃyutam ..
ṣaḍdhvajāṃ nīlasūtreṇa nīlapuṣpaiśca veṣṭitām .. 21 ..
meaning:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या घृतं कनकसंयुतम् ..
षड्ध्वजां नीलसूत्रेण नीलपुष्पैश्च वेष्टिताम् .. 21 ..
text_mt: And here ghee accompanied by gold should be given as the sacrificial fee. / Having six banners, wrapped with blue thread and blue flowers,

sanskrit_iast:
sarṣapānveṣṭayedrāma nāgapuṣpeṇa bhūriṇā ..
valmīkānāṃ sahastasya tathaivāgramṛdā dvija..22..
meaning:
सर्षपान्वेष्टयेद्राम नागपुष्पेण भूरिणा ..
वल्मीकानां सहस्तस्य तथैवाग्रमृदा द्विज..22..
text_mt: he should wrap mustard seeds with abundant nāgapuṣpa, O Rāma, / with the earth from ant-hills and likewise earth from the tip of an elephant's trunk, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
tai snātaḥ sarvanāgebhyo madhulājāṃ nivedayet..
gandhodakaṃ tathā dhānāḥ ṣaṭkṛtvātha punaḥpunaḥ..23...
meaning:
तै स्नातः सर्वनागेभ्यो मधुलाजां निवेदयेत्..
गन्धोदकं तथा धानाः षट्कृत्वाथ पुनःपुनः..23...
text_mt: Bathed with these, he should offer parched grain with honey to all the nāgas, / and perfumed water and parched grain six times, repeatedly.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīreṇa homaḥ kartavyo dhūpaḥ sarvatvacā tathā ..
sarpatvaṅ nāgapuṣpaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca maṇirbhavet .. 24 ..
meaning:
क्षीरेण होमः कर्तव्यो धूपः सर्वत्वचा तथा ..
सर्पत्वङ् नागपुष्पं च सुवर्णं च मणिर्भवेत् .. 24 ..
text_mt: The fire offering should be made with milk, and the incense with all [aromatic] barks; / snake-skin, nāgapuṣpa, and gold should form the amulet.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā śayanīyaṃ manoharam ..
snānaṃ sārpeṇa te proktaṃ bhogyaṃ siddhikaraṃ bhavet ..25..
meaning:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या शयनीयं मनोहरम् ..
स्नानं सार्पेण ते प्रोक्तं भोग्यं सिद्धिकरं भवेत् ..25..
text_mt: And here a delightful bed should be given as the sacrificial fee. / The bath under the serpent asterism [Āśleṣā] has been declared to you; it brings enjoyment and success,

sanskrit_iast:
śrīpradaṃ vā mahābhāga kathitaṃ kāmatastava ..
plakṣapatraistilaiḥ kṛṣṇairghaṭaṣaṭkaṃ tu pūrayet ..26..
meaning:
श्रीप्रदं वा महाभाग कथितं कामतस्तव ..
प्लक्षपत्रैस्तिलैः कृष्णैर्घटषट्कं तु पूरयेत् ..26..
text_mt: or it bestows prosperity, O highly fortunate one, declared according to your desire. / One should fill six jars with plakṣa leaves and black sesame seeds,

sanskrit_iast:
veṣṭayetkṛṣṇamālyaiśca tena snāto'hatāmbaraḥ ..
dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu saptapiṇḍānupāharet .. 27 ..
meaning:
वेष्टयेत्कृष्णमाल्यैश्च तेन स्नातोऽहताम्बरः ..
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु सप्तपिण्डानुपाहरेत् .. 27 ..
text_mt: and wrap them with black garlands. Bathed with that [water] and wearing unwashed garments, / he should offer seven piṇḍas on darbha grass with their points directed south.

sanskrit_iast:
subhāsvaro barhiṣado hyagniṣvāttāstathaiva ca ..
kravyādaścopahūtāśca ājyapāśca sukālinaḥ .. 28 ..
meaning:
सुभास्वरो बर्हिषदो ह्यग्निष्वात्तास्तथैव च ..
क्रव्यादश्चोपहूताश्च आज्यपाश्च सुकालिनः .. 28 ..
text_mt: The Subhāsvaras, the Barhiṣads, the Agniṣvāttas, / the Kravyāds, the Upahūtas, the Ājyapas, and the Sukālins:

sanskrit_iast:
pitaraḥ kathitāsteṣāṃ piṇḍaṃ dadyātkrameṇa ca ..
dhūpaṃ vrīhiyavairdadyāttilairhomaṃ tu kārayet .. 29 ...
meaning:
पितरः कथितास्तेषां पिण्डं दद्यात्क्रमेण च ..
धूपं व्रीहियवैर्दद्यात्तिलैर्होमं तु कारयेत् .. 29 ...
text_mt: these are declared to be the ancestors; he should offer a piṇḍa to them in order. / He should offer incense with rice and barley, and make the fire offering with sesame.

sanskrit_iast:
dātavyā dakṣiṇā cātra tilānrajatameva ca ..
vacā ca korakaṃ caiva trivṛtaṃ dhārayenmaṇim .. 2.99.30 ..
meaning:
दातव्या दक्षिणा चात्र तिलान्रजतमेव च ..
वचा च कोरकं चैव त्रिवृतं धारयेन्मणिम् .. 2.99.30 ..
text_mt: And here sesame and silver should be given as the sacrificial fee. / He should wear an amulet of three strands containing vacā and buds.

sanskrit_iast:
pitṛprasādaṃ prāpnoti karmasiddhimathāpi ca ..
maghāsnānamidaṃ kṛtvā nityameva samāhitaḥ .. 31 ..
meaning:
पितृप्रसादं प्राप्नोति कर्मसिद्धिमथापि च ..
मघास्नानमिदं कृत्वा नित्यमेव समाहितः .. 31 ..
text_mt: He attains the favor of the ancestors and the success of his work, / having performed this bath under Maghā, always composed in mind.

sanskrit_iast:
mākṣikaṃ ca madhūkaṃ ca tathaiva madhuyaṣṭikām ..
kṛtvā kumbhadvayaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhagnāṅgaḥ snāpayennaram .. 32 ..
meaning:
माक्षिकं च मधूकं च तथैव मधुयष्टिकाम् ..
कृत्वा कुम्भद्वयं पूर्णं भग्नाङ्गः स्नापयेन्नरम् .. 32 ..
text_mt: Having filled two jars with honey, madhūka, and liquorice, / a man with fractured limbs should bathe.

sanskrit_iast:
śālipiṣṭaṃ tataḥ snāto ghṛtena madhunā yutam ..
gandhamālyaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bahukṛtvā bhagāya tu .. 33 ..
meaning:
शालिपिष्टं ततः स्नातो घृतेन मधुना युतम् ..
गन्धमाल्यं बहुविधं बहुकृत्वा भगाय तु .. 33 ..
text_mt: Then, having bathed, [he should offer] rice flour mixed with ghee and honey, / and manifold perfumes and garlands, abundantly prepared, to Bhaga.

sanskrit_iast:
nivedayitvā deyāni citramāṃsāni cāpyatha ..
ghṛtena dhūpo dātavyo homaḥ kāryaḥ priyaṅgunā .. 34 ..
meaning:
निवेदयित्वा देयानि चित्रमांसानि चाप्यथ ..
घृतेन धूपो दातव्यो होमः कार्यः प्रियङ्गुना .. 34 ..
text_mt: Having offered [these], various kinds of meat should then be given. / Incense should be given with ghee, and the fire offering should be made with priyaṅgu.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā citravāsāṃsi cāpyatha ..
pārāvatasya pakṣāṇi cakravākasya mānada .. 35 ..
meaning:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या चित्रवासांसि चाप्यथ ..
पारावतस्य पक्षाणि चक्रवाकस्य मानद .. 35 ..
text_mt: And here various garments should be given as the sacrificial fee. / The wings of a pigeon and of a cakravāka bird, O honor-giver,

sanskrit_iast:
trivṛtāni tathā kṛtvā maṇiṃ śirasi dhārayet ..
saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti snātvaiva bhagadaivate .. 36 ..
meaning:
त्रिवृतानि तथा कृत्वा मणिं शिरसि धारयेत् ..
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति स्नात्वैव भगदैवते .. 36 ..
text_mt: having made into a three-stranded amulet, he should wear it on his head. / Having bathed under the deity Bhaga [Pūrvaphalgunī], he attains great good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
tilamākṣikapūrṇena snātaḥ kumbhadvayena tu ..
āryakṣe pāyasaṃ dadyātpītarakte ca vāsasī .. 37 ..
meaning:
तिलमाक्षिकपूर्णेन स्नातः कुम्भद्वयेन तु ..
आर्यक्षे पायसं दद्यात्पीतरक्ते च वाससी .. 37 ..
text_mt: Bathed with two jars filled with sesame and honey, / under the asterism of Aryaman [Uttarāphalgunī] he should offer rice boiled in milk and yellow and red garments.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpe śatāvarī deyā homaḥ kāryastathākṣataiḥ ..
tejovantī priyaṅguśca trivṛtaṃ dhārayenmaṇim .. 38 ..
meaning:
धूपे शतावरी देया होमः कार्यस्तथाक्षतैः ..
तेजोवन्ती प्रियङ्गुश्च त्रिवृतं धारयेन्मणिम् .. 38 ..
text_mt: Śatāvarī should be given for incense, and the fire offering should be made with unbroken grains. / He should wear a three-stranded amulet of tejovantī and priyaṅgu.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā tathā rakte ca vāsasī ..
uttarāphalgunīsnānaṃ sarvārambhaprasiddhidam .. 39 ..
meaning:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या तथा रक्ते च वाससी ..
उत्तराफल्गुनीस्नानं सर्वारम्भप्रसिद्धिदम् .. 39 ..
text_mt: And here two red garments should be given as the sacrificial fee. / The bath under Uttarāphalgunī grants success in all undertakings,

sanskrit_iast:
vīryasya vardhanaṃ cāpi kartavyamanusūnunā ..
gajakāmasya te snānaṃ haste pūrvaṃ mayoditam .. 2.99.40 ..
meaning:
वीर्यस्य वर्धनं चापि कर्तव्यमनुसूनुना ..
गजकामस्य ते स्नानं हस्ते पूर्वं मयोदितम् .. 2.99.40 ..
text_mt: and it increases strength; it should be performed by one who has sons. / The bath under Hasta for one desiring elephants was declared by me previously;

sanskrit_iast:
parasainyajayārthāya snānaṃ tadapi śasyate ..
maṃjiṣṭhāṃ ca samaṅgāṃ ca misikāntāṃ ca bhārgava .. 41 ..
meaning:
परसैन्यजयार्थाय स्नानं तदपि शस्यते ..
मंजिष्ठां च समङ्गां च मिसिकान्तां च भार्गव .. 41 ..
text_mt: that bath is also commended for victory over an enemy's army. / Mañjiṣṭhā, samaṅgā, and misikāntā, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

sanskrit_iast:
kanakaṃ rajataṃ caiva pūrṇakumbhe vinikṣipet ..
tenābhiṣiktaścitrāṇi mālyavāsāṃsyanantaram .. 42 ..
meaning:
कनकं रजतं चैव पूर्णकुम्भे विनिक्षिपेत् ..
तेनाभिषिक्तश्चित्राणि माल्यवासांस्यनन्तरम् .. 42 ..
text_mt: and gold and silver he should cast into a full jar. / Bathed with that [water], he should immediately with devotion offer variegated

sanskrit_iast:
tvāṣṭre nivedayedbhaktyā homaṃ kṣīreṇa kārayet ..
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā citravastrāṇi mānada .. 43 ..
meaning:
त्वाष्ट्रे निवेदयेद्भक्त्या होमं क्षीरेण कारयेत् ..
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या चित्रवस्त्राणि मानद .. 43 ..
text_mt: garlands and garments to Tvaṣṭṛ, and perform the fire offering with milk. / And here variegated garments should be given as the sacrificial fee, O honor-giver,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvagandhaistathā dhūpaṃ baliṃ citraṃ tathaiva ca ..
pṛthaksrutiprasūtānāṃ puṣpānāṃ kanakairvṛtam .. 44 ..
meaning:
सर्वगन्धैस्तथा धूपं बलिं चित्रं तथैव च ..
पृथक्स्रुतिप्रसूतानां पुष्पानां कनकैर्वृतम् .. 44 ..
text_mt: and incense with all perfumes, and a variegated offering of food. / An amulet covered in gold, made of eighteen flowers

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭādaśānāṃ ca tathā maṇiṃ śirasi dhārayet ..
evaṃ snātastu citrāsu saubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute .. 45 ..
meaning:
अष्टादशानां च तथा मणिं शिरसि धारयेत् ..
एवं स्नातस्तु चित्रासु सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते .. 45 ..
text_mt: sprung from separate streams, he should wear on his head. / Bathed thus under Citrā, he attains great good fortune,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvabhūteṣu cādhikyaṃ yadicchati tadāpnuyāt ..
rukmamaśvavatthapatraṃ ca khaḍgaśṛṅgaṃ tathaiva ca .. 46 ..
meaning:
सर्वभूतेषु चाधिक्यं यदिच्छति तदाप्नुयात् ..
रुक्ममश्ववत्थपत्रं च खड्गशृङ्गं तथैव च .. 46 ..
text_mt: and preeminence among all beings; whatever he wishes, that he obtains. / Gold, an aśvattha leaf, and the horn of a rhinoceros

sanskrit_iast:
pūrṇakumbhe vinikṣipya snātaḥ śīdhusurāsavam ..
vāyavye prayato dadyātkṣīraṃ sapalalaṃ dadhi .. 47 ..
meaning:
पूर्णकुम्भे विनिक्षिप्य स्नातः शीधुसुरासवम् ..
वायव्ये प्रयतो दद्यात्क्षीरं सपललं दधि .. 47 ..
text_mt: having placed in a full jar, bathed, restrained in mind, he should offer rum, wine, and liquor, / milk, sesamum paste, and curds to Vāyu [the deity of Svātī].

sanskrit_iast:
gandhaṃ dhūpaṃ tathā dadyāddhome kāryaṃ tathā ghṛtam .. .
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca .. 48 ..
meaning:
गन्धं धूपं तथा दद्याद्धोमे कार्यं तथा घृतम् .. .
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या वासांसि विविधानि च .. 48 ..
text_mt: He should give perfume and incense, and ghee should be used in the fire offering. / And here various garments should be given as the sacrificial fee.

sanskrit_iast:
dvaṣṭāśvaśyāmahārītahaṃsapakṣaiḥ payo'nvitam ..
dhārayecca maṇiṃ vidvānsvātāvevaṃ samācaret .. .. 49 ..
meaning:
द्वष्टाश्वश्यामहारीतहंसपक्षैः पयोऽन्वितम् ..
धारयेच्च मणिं विद्वान्स्वातावेवं समाचरेत् .. .. 49 ..
text_mt: With the wings of sixteen dark hārīta birds and geese, accompanied by milk, / the wise man should wear an amulet; he should perform thus under Svātī.

sanskrit_iast:
vāṇijye samyagāpnoti siddhiṃ ca mahatīṃ naraḥ ..
viśākhāsu tathā snānaṃ kāryaṃ kumbhadvayena tu .. 2.99.50 ..
meaning:
वाणिज्ये सम्यगाप्नोति सिद्धिं च महतीं नरः ..
विशाखासु तथा स्नानं कार्यं कुम्भद्वयेन तु .. 2.99.50 ..
text_mt: A man fully attains great success in commerce. / Under Viśākhā, a bath should likewise be performed with two jars.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛttikāsu mahābhāga tataḥ śākaṃ nivedayet ..
indrāgnibhyāṃ ca vāsāṃsi pītaraktāni cāpyatha .. 51 ..
meaning:
कृत्तिकासु महाभाग ततः शाकं निवेदयेत् ..
इन्द्राग्निभ्यां च वासांसि पीतरक्तानि चाप्यथ .. 51 ..
text_mt: Under Kṛttikā, O highly fortunate one, he should then offer vegetables, / and yellow and red garments to Indra and Agni,

sanskrit_iast:
mālyāni ca mahābhāga dhūpaṃ ca ghṛtaguggulam ..
homārthe ca ghṛtaṃ kuryāddakṣiṇā kanakaṃ tathā .. 52 ..
meaning:
माल्यानि च महाभाग धूपं च घृतगुग्गुलम् ..
होमार्थे च घृतं कुर्याद्दक्षिणा कनकं तथा .. 52 ..
text_mt: and garlands, O highly fortunate one, and incense of ghee and guggulu. / And for the fire offering he should use ghee, and gold as the sacrificial fee.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇādhipatyamāpnoti kṛtvaivaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
sahasravīryaṃ cānantāṃ madhūkaṃ ca tathā misim .. 53 ..
meaning:
गणाधिपत्यमाप्नोति कृत्वैवं नात्र संशयः ..
सहस्रवीर्यं चानन्तां मधूकं च तथा मिसिम् .. 53 ..
text_mt: By doing this, one attains leadership over hosts, there is no doubt of this. / [Placing] sahasravīryā, anantā, madhūka, and also misi

sanskrit_iast:
pūrṇakumbhatraye kṛtvā kṛtasvastikalakṣaṇe ..
ahatāmbarasaṃvītaḥ sarvagandhaphalākṣataiḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
पूर्णकुम्भत्रये कृत्वा कृतस्वस्तिकलक्षणे ..
अहताम्बरसंवीतः सर्वगन्धफलाक्षतैः .. 54 ..
text_mt: in three full jars marked with a svastika, / clad in unwashed garments, with all kinds of perfumes, fruits, and unbroken grains,

sanskrit_iast:
madhunā ca baliṃ dadyānmitrāya ca mahātmane ..
vṛścikena tathā dhūpaṃ yavairhomaṃ ca mānada .. 55 ..
meaning:
मधुना च बलिं दद्यान्मित्राय च महात्मने ..
वृश्चिकेन तथा धूपं यवैर्होमं च मानद .. 55 ..
text_mt: and with honey, he should offer an oblation to the great-souled Mitra. / [He should offer] incense with scorpion[-grass], and an oblation into fire with barley, O respectful one.

sanskrit_iast:
puradvāraṃ kaṭāhāśca cūḍākāṣṭhaṃ sakāñcanam ..
dhārayeddakṣiṇāṃ dadyāttathā ca kanakaṃ dvija .. 56 ..
meaning:
पुरद्वारं कटाहाश्च चूडाकाष्ठं सकाञ्चनम् ..
धारयेद्दक्षिणां दद्यात्तथा च कनकं द्विज .. 56 ..
text_mt: Wood from a city gate, frying pans, and crest-wood, together with gold, / he should wear; and he should give sacrificial fee, likewise gold, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ maitre sadā snātaḥ sarvabhūtaiḥ samāpnuyāt ..
maitrīṃ manujaśārdūla puraṃ vā kurute vaśe .. 57 ..
meaning:
एवं मैत्रे सदा स्नातः सर्वभूतैः समाप्नुयात् ..
मैत्रीं मनुजशार्दूल पुरं वा कुरुते वशे .. 57 ..
text_mt: Having bathed thus always under the star of Mitra, / he attains friendship with all beings, O tiger among men, or brings a city under his control.

sanskrit_iast:
taḍāgapadminīkūlanadīnadasamudbhavaiḥ ..
toyaiḥ pūrṇa ghaṭānkṛtvā sarvabījasamanvitān .. 58 ..
meaning:
तडागपद्मिनीकूलनदीनदसमुद्भवैः ..
तोयैः पूर्ण घटान्कृत्वा सर्वबीजसमन्वितान् .. 58 ..
text_mt: Having filled jars with water originating from ponds, lotus-pools, banks, / and flowing rivers, accompanied by all seeds,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvaratnauṣadhīpūrṇānstrīsnānaṃ taiḥ samācaret ..
kṣaumavāsāstu ratnāni mālyāni ca phalāni ca .. .. 59 ..
meaning:
सर्वरत्नौषधीपूर्णान्स्त्रीस्नानं तैः समाचरेत् ..
क्षौमवासास्तु रत्नानि माल्यानि च फलानि च .. .. 59 ..
text_mt: filled with all gems and medicinal herbs, one should perform a woman's bath with them. / Clad in linen garments, [offering] gems, garlands, and fruits,

sanskrit_iast:
ratnāni dadyācchakrāya prāṅmukhaḥ susamāhitaḥ ..
dhūpaṃ dadyācca śīrṣeṇa viśākhāvanmaṇirbhavet .. 2.99.60 ..
meaning:
रत्नानि दद्याच्छक्राय प्राङ्मुखः सुसमाहितः ..
धूपं दद्याच्च शीर्षेण विशाखावन्मणिर्भवेत् .. 2.99.60 ..
text_mt: facing east, deeply concentrated, he should offer gems to Śakra. / He should offer incense with his head; [and] there should be an amulet like Viśākhā.

sanskrit_iast:
chatraṃ ca dakṣiṇā deyā jyeṣṭhāyāṃ bhṛgunandana ..
snānameva sadā kṛtvā rājyamāpnotyakaṇṭakam .. 61 ..
meaning:
छत्रं च दक्षिणा देया ज्येष्ठायां भृगुनन्दन ..
स्नानमेव सदा कृत्वा राज्यमाप्नोत्यकण्टकम् .. 61 ..
text_mt: An umbrella should be given as the sacrificial fee under Jyeṣṭhā, O son of Bhṛgu. / By performing this bath constantly, he attains a kingdom free of thorns.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣikāmasya mūlena snānamuktaṃ mayā purā ..
tathā vāṇijyakāmasya prāgaṣāḍhāsu bhārgava .. 62 ..
meaning:
कृषिकामस्य मूलेन स्नानमुक्तं मया पुरा ..
तथा वाणिज्यकामस्य प्रागषाढासु भार्गव .. 62 ..
text_mt: The bath for one desiring agriculture under Mūla was spoken by me previously, / as well as for one desiring commerce under Pūrvāṣāḍhā, O Bhārgava.

sanskrit_iast:
athottarāsu ṣāḍhāsu kuryādghaṭacatuṣṭayam ..
puṣpabījaphalopetaṃ tena snātastu mānavaḥ .. 63 ..
meaning:
अथोत्तरासु षाढासु कुर्याद्घटचतुष्टयम् ..
पुष्पबीजफलोपेतं तेन स्नातस्तु मानवः .. 63 ..
text_mt: Now under Uttarāṣāḍhā he should prepare four jars / provided with flowers, seeds, and fruits; and having bathed therewith, a man,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣaumavāsāḥ surāṃ caiva pāyasaṃ ca nivedayet ..
mudgamiśraṃ ca dharmajña mālyavāsāṃsi cecchayā .. 64 ..
meaning:
क्षौमवासाः सुरां चैव पायसं च निवेदयेत् ..
मुद्गमिश्रं च धर्मज्ञ माल्यवासांसि चेच्छया .. 64 ..
text_mt: wearing linen garments, should offer liquor and milk-rice / mixed with mung beans, O knower of dharma, and garlands and garments at will.

sanskrit_iast:
home ca pāyasaṃ kuryāddhūpe gośṛṅgameva ca ..
dhātrīpuṣpaśamībilvairmaṇirdhāryaḥ sakāñcanaiḥ .. 65 ..
meaning:
होमे च पायसं कुर्याद्धूपे गोशृङ्गमेव च ..
धात्रीपुष्पशमीबिल्वैर्मणिर्धार्यः सकाञ्चनैः .. 65 ..
text_mt: For the oblation into fire he should use milk-rice, and cow-horn for incense. / An amulet of emblic myrobalan flower, śamī, and bilva, together with gold, should be worn.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā suvarṇaṃ raupyameva ca ..
rājaśreṣṭhatvamāpnoti vivādeṣu jayaṃ tathā .. 66 ..
meaning:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या सुवर्णं रौप्यमेव च ..
राजश्रेष्ठत्वमाप्नोति विवादेषु जयं तथा .. 66 ..
text_mt: And the sacrificial fee to be given here is gold and silver. / He attains supremacy among kings and victory in disputes.

sanskrit_iast:
bilvaṃ ca tagaraṃ caiva candanaṃ madhuyaṣṭikām ..
priyaṅguṃ ca madhūkaṃ ca triṣu kumbheṣu nikṣipet .. 67 ..
meaning:
बिल्वं च तगरं चैव चन्दनं मधुयष्टिकाम् ..
प्रियङ्गुं च मधूकं च त्रिषु कुम्भेषु निक्षिपेत् .. 67 ..
text_mt: Bilva, tagara, sandalwood, liquorice, / priyaṅgu, and madhūka he should cast into three jars,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃgamādāhṛtaṃ toyaṃ tanmṛdaṃ ca bhṛgūttama ..
tena snātastataḥ snānaṃ kuryātsarvauṣadhairdvija .. 68 ..
meaning:
संगमादाहृतं तोयं तन्मृदं च भृगूत्तम ..
तेन स्नातस्ततः स्नानं कुर्यात्सर्वौषधैर्द्विज .. 68 ..
text_mt: and water brought from a confluence and clay from it, O foremost of the Bhṛgus. / Having bathed with that, the twice-born should then perform a bath with all medicinal herbs.

sanskrit_iast:
kulatthā'nnaṃ saśālyannaṃ mukhyāni ca phalāni ca ..
baliṃ ca viṣṇave dadyānmudgairdhūpaṃ tathaiva ca .. 69 ..
meaning:
कुलत्थाऽन्नं सशाल्यन्नं मुख्यानि च फलानि च ..
बलिं च विष्णवे दद्यान्मुद्गैर्धूपं तथैव च .. 69 ..
text_mt: Food made of horse-gram together with śāli-rice food and choice fruits / and an offering he should present to Viṣṇu, and likewise incense with mung beans.

sanskrit_iast:
rājacchatrasya daṇḍāgrātkāṣṭhaṃ śakradhvajāttathā ..
siṃhadaṃṣṭrāmaṇiścātra sarukmaḥ śirasi smṛtaḥ .. 2.99.70 ..
meaning:
राजच्छत्रस्य दण्डाग्रात्काष्ठं शक्रध्वजात्तथा ..
सिंहदंष्ट्रामणिश्चात्र सरुक्मः शिरसि स्मृतः .. 2.99.70 ..
text_mt: Wood from the tip of the staff of a royal umbrella and from Śakra's banner, / and an amulet of a lion's tooth together with gold, is prescribed here for the head.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā dhenuḥ kāṃsyopadohinī..
evaṃ tu śravaṇasnāyī rājyamāpnotyakaṇṭakam .. 71 ..
meaning:
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या धेनुः कांस्योपदोहिनी..
एवं तु श्रवणस्नायी राज्यमाप्नोत्यकण्टकम् .. 71 ..
text_mt: And the sacrificial fee to be given here is a milk-cow with a bronze milking vessel. / Bathing thus under Śravaṇa, he attains a kingdom free of thorns,

sanskrit_iast:
anyadeśādhipatyaṃ vā rājyamāpnoti bhārgava ..
atimuktakapatrāṇi bilvasya ca tathā kṣipet .. 72 ..
meaning:
अन्यदेशाधिपत्यं वा राज्यमाप्नोति भार्गव ..
अतिमुक्तकपत्राणि बिल्वस्य च तथा क्षिपेत् .. 72 ..
text_mt: or he attains sovereignty over another realm or kingship, O Bhārgava. / He should then cast leaves of atimuktaka and bilva

sanskrit_iast:
kumbheṣu pañcasu tataḥ snānaṃ taistu samācaret ..
vāstubhyastu baliṃ dadyātsuvarṇaṃ mākṣike tataḥ .. 73 ..
meaning:
कुम्भेषु पञ्चसु ततः स्नानं तैस्तु समाचरेत् ..
वास्तुभ्यस्तु बलिं दद्यात्सुवर्णं माक्षिके ततः .. 73 ..
text_mt: into five jars, and then perform a bath with them. / Then he should present an offering to the Vāstus, [and] gold in honey;

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpaṃ vāyasapakṣaistu homaḥ kāryo ghṛtena tu ..
brahmacāriśilālopakākapakṣaṃ tathaiva ca .. 74 ..
meaning:
धूपं वायसपक्षैस्तु होमः कार्यो घृतेन तु ..
ब्रह्मचारिशिलालोपकाकपक्षं तथैव च .. 74 ..
text_mt: incense with crow-feathers, and an oblation into fire should be made with ghee. / [With] a stone-flake of a celibate student and a crow's feather likewise,

sanskrit_iast:
kākamācīṃ rukmayutāṃ maṇiṃ śirasi dhārayet ..
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā dhenu kāṃsyopadohinī .. 75 ..
meaning:
काकमाचीं रुक्मयुतां मणिं शिरसि धारयेत् ..
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या धेनु कांस्योपदोहिनी .. 75 ..
text_mt: and black nightshade joined with gold, he should wear an amulet on his head. / And the sacrificial fee to be given here is a milk-cow with a bronze milking vessel.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanaṃ prāpnoti sumahadvivāhe vāpi kanyakām ..
evaṃ snāto dhaniṣṭhāsu nityameva bhṛgūttama .. 76 ..
meaning:
धनं प्राप्नोति सुमहद्विवाहे वापि कन्यकाम् ..
एवं स्नातो धनिष्ठासु नित्यमेव भृगूत्तम .. 76 ..
text_mt: He attains immense wealth, or indeed a maiden in marriage, / having bathed thus constantly under Dhaniṣṭhā, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.

sanskrit_iast:
ārogyakārakaṃ snānaṃ pūrvamuktaṃ tu vāruṇam ..
ratnodakena snātastu naraḥ kumbhadvayena tu .. 77 ..
meaning:
आरोग्यकारकं स्नानं पूर्वमुक्तं तु वारुणम् ..
रत्नोदकेन स्नातस्तु नरः कुम्भद्वयेन तु .. 77 ..
text_mt: The bath under the star of Varuṇa that produces health was described previously. / But a man bathed with gem-water from two jars

sanskrit_iast:
ajaikapādāya baliṃ chāgaṃ dadyāttu pāyasam ..
śuklāni caiva mālyāni phalāni vividhāni ca .. 78 ..
meaning:
अजैकपादाय बलिं छागं दद्यात्तु पायसम् ..
शुक्लानि चैव माल्यानि फलानि विविधानि च .. 78 ..
text_mt: should give an offering to Aja Ekapād: a goat and milk-rice, / and white garlands and diverse fruits,

sanskrit_iast:
khaṭvāṅgañca tathā dhūpaṃ homaṃ ca payasā tathā ..
vyāghradaṃṣṭrā tathā lomanakhaṃ kanakameva ca .. 79 ..
meaning:
खट्वाङ्गञ्च तथा धूपं होमं च पयसा तथा ..
व्याघ्रदंष्ट्रा तथा लोमनखं कनकमेव च .. 79 ..
text_mt: and khaṭvāṅga for incense, and an oblation into fire with milk. / A tiger's tooth, hair, a claw, and gold—

sanskrit_iast:
maṇirdhāryo bhavedrāma chāgo deyā ca dakṣiṇā ..
ajaikapāde snātastu nityameva samāhitaḥ .. 2.99.80 ..
meaning:
मणिर्धार्यो भवेद्राम छागो देया च दक्षिणा ..
अजैकपादे स्नातस्तु नित्यमेव समाहितः .. 2.99.80 ..
text_mt: an amulet [of these] should be worn, O Rāma, and a goat should be given as sacrificial fee. / Bathing under Aja Ekapād, always concentrated,

sanskrit_iast:
uddharettu nidhiṃ rāma śatrūnvā vijayeddhruvam ..
āhirbudhnyaṃ tathā snānaṃ godamuktaṃ purā tava .. 81..
meaning:
उद्धरेत्तु निधिं राम शत्रून्वा विजयेद्ध्रुवम् ..
आहिर्बुध्न्यं तथा स्नानं गोदमुक्तं पुरा तव .. 81..
text_mt: he would recover a treasure, O Rāma, or surely conquer his enemies. / The bath under Ahirbudhnya, granting cattle, was previously spoken to you.

sanskrit_iast:
candanaṃ ca haridrā ca darbhamūlaṃ tathaiva ca..
kṛtvā kumbhe naraḥ snāyātkṛtvā piṣṭena kanyakām.. .. 82 ..
meaning:
चन्दनं च हरिद्रा च दर्भमूलं तथैव च..
कृत्वा कुम्भे नरः स्नायात्कृत्वा पिष्टेन कन्यकाम्.. .. 82 ..
text_mt: Having placed sandalwood, turmeric, and root of darbha-grass / in a jar, a man should bathe, having made a maiden of flour.

sanskrit_iast:
snānālaṅkāravastrādyānpūṣṇe dadyādbaliṃ tataḥ ..
madhulājāstathaivātra dhūpaṃ dadyādghṛtena ca .. 83..
meaning:
स्नानालङ्कारवस्त्राद्यान्पूष्णे दद्याद्बलिं ततः ..
मधुलाजास्तथैवात्र धूपं दद्याद्घृतेन च .. 83..
text_mt: After [presenting] bath, ornaments, garments, and so forth, he should give an offering to Pūṣan; / likewise honey and parched grains here, and he should offer incense with ghee.

sanskrit_iast:
homaṃ ghṛtena kartavyaṃ dakṣiṇā kanakaṃ bhavet ..
brāhmīṃ suvarcalāṃ homaṃ homagarbho maṇirbhavet .. 84 ..
meaning:
होमं घृतेन कर्तव्यं दक्षिणा कनकं भवेत् ..
ब्राह्मीं सुवर्चलां होमं होमगर्भो मणिर्भवेत् .. 84 ..
text_mt: An oblation into fire should be made with ghee, [and] the sacrificial fee should be gold. / An oblation with brāhmī and suvarcalā; the amulet should contain [ashes of] the oblation.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ pauṣṇe sadā snāto yaḥ sadā yujyate naraḥ ..
āśvine supradaṃ snānaṃ pūrvamuktaṃ mayā tava .. .. 85 ..
meaning:
एवं पौष्णे सदा स्नातो यः सदा युज्यते नरः ..
आश्विने सुप्रदं स्नानं पूर्वमुक्तं मया तव .. .. 85 ..
text_mt: Thus bathed constantly under the star of Pūṣan, a man is always joined [with prosperity]. / The bath under the star of the Aśvins, bestowing beauty, was previously spoken by me to you.

sanskrit_iast:
vaijayantīṃ balāṃ caiva samaṅgāṃ ca bhṛgūttama ..
indrahastāṃ madhūkaṃ ca kuryādrāma ghaṭatraye .. 86 ..
meaning:
वैजयन्तीं बलां चैव समङ्गां च भृगूत्तम ..
इन्द्रहस्तां मधूकं च कुर्याद्राम घटत्रये .. 86 ..
text_mt: Vaijayantī, balā, and samaṅgā, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / indrahastā, and madhūka, he should place in three jars, O Rāma.

sanskrit_iast:
tena snāto yamāyātha prapadyāttilataṇḍulam ..
mālyāni caiva citrāṇi pītāni vasanāni ca .. 87 ..
meaning:
तेन स्नातो यमायाथ प्रपद्यात्तिलतण्डुलम् ..
माल्यानि चैव चित्राणि पीतानि वसनानि च .. 87 ..
text_mt: Bathed with that, he should then offer sesame and rice to Yama, / and variegated garlands and yellow garments,

sanskrit_iast:
urabhraśṛṅgaṃ dhūpārthe homārthe ca tathā tilam ..
dakṣiṇā cātra dātavyā tilaṃ kanakameva ca .. 88 ..
meaning:
उरभ्रशृङ्गं धूपार्थे होमार्थे च तथा तिलम् ..
दक्षिणा चात्र दातव्या तिलं कनकमेव च .. 88 ..
text_mt: a ram's horn for the purpose of incense, and likewise sesame for the purpose of the fire-oblation. / And the sacrificial fee to be given here is sesame and gold.

sanskrit_iast:
darbhamūlairmaṇiḥ kāryaḥ kanakena ca veṣṭitaḥ ..
evaṃ snāto naro yāmye dīrghaṃ jīvitamāpnuyāt .. 89 ..
meaning:
दर्भमूलैर्मणिः कार्यः कनकेन च वेष्टितः ..
एवं स्नातो नरो याम्ये दीर्घं जीवितमाप्नुयात् .. 89 ..
text_mt: An amulet should be made with roots of darbha-grass and wrapped with gold. / Bathed thus under the star of Yama, a man attains a long life.

sanskrit_iast:
snānāni mukhyāni tavoditāni kāmyāni pāpapraśamāya rāma ..
etāni kāryāṇi sadā dvijendra dharānvitenātha vicakṣaṇena ..2.99.90..

puṣkara uvāca ..
upoṣya cottarāṣāḍhāṃ brahmasnānaṃ vidhīyate ..
sūrye madhyamanuprāpte narendro - - - ..
sarvairbījaistathā ratnaiḥ phalaiḥ puṣpaistathauṣadhaiḥ ..
snātaśca sodakaiḥ kuryāttataḥ pūjāṃ svayaṃbhuvaḥ .. 2 ..

The principal optional baths for the pacification of sins have been spoken to you, O Rāma. / These should always be performed, O chief of the twice-born, by a discerning man accompanied by dharma.
2.100 / Puṣkara said: / Having fasted under Uttarāṣāḍhā, the bath to Brahmā is prescribed. / When the sun has reached the middle, the king […] / and bathed with water containing all seeds, gems, fruits, flowers, and medicinal herbs, / he should then perform the worship of the Self-born.
He should also offer incense, O knower of dharma, with kuśa roots, ghee, and unbroken grains. / He should make an oblation into fire with ghee and unbroken grains, and give gold.
While the ladle is being made, powder […], and likewise […], O twice-born; / with soma powder and trivṛt, he should wear an amulet on his head.
This bath has been described by me to you for one who desires kingship, / and according to what was taught, at one's own pleasure, for one who desires brahmic splendor.
This bath of Brahmā has been ordained for you for the destruction of all mental distress, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / it should always be performed when the sun has reached midday, fulfilling desires and praiseworthy.

text_mt:
A person who has bathed at the conjunction with the asterism of Śravaṇa always attains desired wishes; / he abandons all sin, O Rāma, and attains dharma and preeminent fame.
Puṣkara said: / When the moon is in one's birth asterism, one should prepare a well-worshiped pitcher / filled with all medicinal herbs, and have the bath performed with it.
Having bathed, one should worship the god Vāsudeva, the lord of the universe, / the deity of the asterism, the moon, and likewise the asterism sacred to Varuṇa,
and one should worship Vāyu, the pedestal of weapons and so forth, as well as the parasol; / and one should offer clarified butter with mantras containing the marks of the deities as prescribed.
And a sacrificial fee should be given according to one's capacity to the brahmins, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / then anointed, fragrant, wearing garlands and adorned with various ornaments,
standing, O tiger among men, eating sacrificial food, with senses subdued— / even without fasting, this is purifying and destroys sin.
The birth star is prescribed in the position of the mother of the worlds, / and the blessed Viṣṇu, possessing the form of the moon, is proclaimed as the father.

text_mt:
Having always performed worship of the moon when situated in the birth asterism, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / a man attains all desires, and would always be happy on earth, with sins destroyed.
Puṣkara said: / During the waxing of the lunar orb, and also during the northern course of the sun, / on an auspicious lunar day and asterism, and at an auspicious muhūrta,
when the moon is in Tiṣya or Aśvinī, and also when it is in Hasta or Śravaṇa, / having gone out of the city toward either the east or the north direction,
on a delightful plot of ground specified by the lore of architecture, / one should make an auspicious, square sacred diagram measuring eight cubits.
One should make another for the bali offering, and one specifically for the fire-altar, / smeared with cow dung and furnished with lines of lime,
One should honor it with banners, parasols, fans, garlands, strings, kuśa grass, and unbroken grains, / with fried grain, scents, and other principal auspicious articles.
One should likewise adorn it with fried grain and utensils for parched grain; / then, indeed, the learned man should arrange new jars from four springs,

text_mt:
she who does not receive seed, or gives birth to non-humans; / or the maiden who does not obtain a husband, or love from him;
and who attains no good fortune among friends, kin, and relatives— / for these mentioned and others not mentioned, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
the expert who knows the ritual, having considered [their case], should perform this bath. / The wise man should bathe those possessed by planets on a riverbank.
For those afflicted by consumption and those with malarial fever, / he should perform the bath in a temple of God or in a place frequented by the perfected.
For those tormented by shadow-madness and those wasting from epilepsy, / bathing is prescribed at a hermitage of sages or at a sacred bathing place.
For those afflicted by the seizure of Vināyaka and those who are deluded and out of their minds, / bathing is prescribed in a place frequented by virtuous people.
For those who do not master the triple knowledge, whose virtues are revered, / bathing is prescribed here in a temple of a perfected god.
For those who have no victory in battle, and those whose kin are dying out, / bathing is commended in a wilderness, in a forest, or at a sacred bathing place.

text_mt:
For those between whom constant quarrel arises everywhere, / one should arrange the bath at a crossroads of three paths or at a pool.
One should bathe a woman whose fetus miscarries in a lotus pond; / she whose child dies as soon as born should be bathed near an aśoka tree.
She who does not conceive semen should be bathed near a fruit-bearing tree; / she whose offspring perishes should be bathed on the shore of the ocean.
She who gives birth to non-humans should be bathed at a four-way crossroads; / and the excellent woman who cannot obtain a husband suited to her
should be bathed at a solitary liṅga or in a place dense with trees. / For a woman endowed with beauty and charm who finds no good fortune,
one should arrange a bath that increases it in a courtesan's house. / Then for others, an attractive bath should always be performed
in an even, clean, thornless place crowded with virtuous people. / Along with restrained assistants, a twice-born, having fasted for a day and night,
should employ the rite of bathing for one who is fasting, O giver of honor; / or for one unable to fast for a day and night, eating sacrificial food is to be observed.

text_mt:
A cane seat, an auspicious stool, a wicker seat, and a wooden seat / are proclaimed as the seat for the castes in regular order.
A black antelope skin, a tiger skin, a ruru deer skin, and a goat skin / should be arranged as the footstool for the castes in regular order.
Upon the back of a bull, a horse, a chariot, and likewise on the back of an elephant, / or on a man's shoulder or in a woman's lap, one should generally bathe children.
For him who desires to bathe, anointing is prescribed beforehand; / I shall declare next, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, the substances with which it is to be done:
Punarnavā, rocanā, śatāhvā, aguru, and cinnamon bark, / madhūka, the two turmerics, tagara, nāgakesara,
āsurī, sarjikā, māṃsī, asafoetida, and sandalwood, / priyaṅgu, mustard seeds, kuṣṭha, saffron, and bahuputrikā,
balā, indrahastī, and brāhmī, and likewise the five products of the cow; / mixing these with barley-meal, an unguent should be made.

text_mt:
Then he should have peace rites recited by virtuous brahmins, / having worshipped them with sacrificial fees, flowers, unbroken rice, and fruits.
Then he should place jars in the sacred diagram above the oceans, / marked with the names of the directional deities in the directions and intermediate directions,
made of gold, silver, copper, or earthen; / I shall now declare their names; listen to them as I speak:
Bhadra, Subhadra, Siddhārtha, and the fourth Puṣṭivardhana, / Amogha, Citrabhānu, Parjanya, and Sudarśana.
Having filled them with water from tanks, wells, and rivers, / furnished with herbs and worshipped with respectful offerings, garlands, and so on,
consecrated with mantras—hear from me the mantra for that: / 'May the hosts of the Rudras and Maruts, together with the Aśvins, establish these jars;
likewise, may the Viśvedevas, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the sages, / well-pleased, abide [here], and so also the other deities.'
Having thus established those jars, they should then be placed in the circles; / they should be set sequentially beginning with Indra's [direction] on the seats prescribed earlier.

text_mt:
Conferring wealth, bringing renown, destroying foes, slaying demons, removing sin, pure, / warding off disease, and destroying obstacles—the bath has been truly prescribed by me for you.
Thus ends the hundred and fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Bath of the Guardians of the Directions', in the second book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the narrative of Puṣkara to Rāma.
Rāma said: / Declare another bath, O venerable one, which removes misfortune, / for those afflicted by Vināyaka, accomplishing all undertakings.
Puṣkara said: / Vināyaka was appointed for the accomplishment of obstacles to actions / and to the lordship of the Gaṇas by Keśava and the grandfathers.
Learn from me the signs of one who is seized by him: / In a dream he plunges deeply into water and sees a shaven-headed person.
He mounts those wearing ochre robes and carnivorous animals. / He stays in one place with outcasts, donkeys, and camels.
Likewise, as he walks, he thinks himself followed by others. / Despondent, his undertakings fruitless, he sinks down without cause.

text_mt:
Seized by him, a king's son does not obtain a kingdom, / nor does a maiden obtain a husband, nor a woman offspring [or] pregnancy.
Nor does a learned brahmin attain the status of a teacher, nor a pupil his study; / a merchant does not gain profit, nor does a farmer [attain] agriculture.
A bath should be performed for him on an auspicious day according to the rule, / under any auspicious [constellation] such as Hasta, Puṣya, Aśvinī, Mṛgaśiras, or Śravaṇā,
and under an auspicious lunar mansion and in a favorable moment sacred to Mitra or Brahmā. / An auspicious seat should be placed upon the red hide of an ox.
One should have the foremost twice-born recite blessings for him when he is seated on the auspicious seat / and has been rubbed with pure paste of white mustard,
and whose head has been anointed with all herbs and all perfumes. / The bath should be performed with four jars accompanied by mantras.
Likewise, the jars should be made of one color, with water from a lake, / and with earth from a horse-stable, an elephant-stable, an anthill, a confluence, and a pool.

One should throw into them yellow orpiment, perfumes, bdellium, / all herbs, and seeds. Hear now the mantras for the bath:
'[The water] has a thousand eyes and a hundred streams, made purifying by the sages. / With it we consecrate you; may the purifying verses cleanse you.
May King Varuṇa grant you good fortune; may Śukra and Bṛhaspati grant you good fortune; / may Indra and Vāyu grant you good fortune; may the Seven Sages grant you good fortune.
Whatever misfortune is in your hair, in your parting, and on your crown, / on your forehead, in your ears, or in your eyes—may the waters destroy that always for you.'
Then, taking a bundle of darbha-grass in his left hand, the guru, / using a ladle made of udumbara wood, should offer into the mustard oil
upon the crown of the one who has bathed, O knower of dharma, with names ending in the dative, / purified by the syllable Om, O knower of dharma, and joined with the exclamation Svāhā:
'To Mita, to Saṃmita, then to Sālaṅkaṭakaṭa, / to Kūṣmāṇḍarājaputra, and likewise to the great-souled one.'

With the names and offering-mantras accompanied by the exclamation Vaṣaṭ, / having strewn kuśa grass all around, he should offer it at a crossroads, upon the head:
rice grains colored red, boiled rice with sesamum paste, / cooked fish as well as raw, and meat of just this sort,
variegated fragrant flowers, and the three kinds of liquor, / radish, fried cakes, and pies, and likewise sweets of flour.
Having brought all these and placed his head on the ground, / he should then wait upon Ambikā, the mother of Vināyaka:
'Grant me beauty, grant me renown, grant me good fortune, O auspicious lady; / grant me sons, grant me wealth, and grant me all desires.'
Then, wearing white garments, adorned with white garlands and unguents, / he should feed the brahmins and also give a pair of garments to the guru.
This bath of Vināyaka brings renown, slays demons, destroys obstacles, / removes all diseases, and destroys foes; it should be performed by strict rule, O Rāma.

For having performed this bath sacred to Maheśvara, which destroys demons and eradicates enemies, / a man attains all desires whatever his mind wishes for, O Rāma.
2.107 / Puṣkara said: / I shall tell you of other baths; listen as I speak, / which are particularly destructive of demons, bring renown, and are auspicious.
A bath with ghee is declared to be the highest prolonger of life; / a bath with cow dung, O Rāma, is supreme for increasing prosperity.
And a bath with curd is declared to be supreme for increasing prosperity; / likewise, a bath with water infused with darbha grass destroys all sins.
A bath with palāśa, bilva, lotus, and kuśa is beneficial, [performed] facing eastward; / sweet flag, turmeric, madder, tagara, and cāraka—
this bath is prescribed as slaying demons and eliminating sins. / A bath combined with sweet flag and turmeric is supreme for slaying demons.
It grants longevity, brings renown, brings fortune, and increases intellect; / such is the pure, auspicious bath with water [infused with] gold.

Having placed a cat's-eye gem in the centre, one should surround it with corals; / the bath [taken] with that vessel fulfills all desires and is beneficial.
A bath with all medicinal herbs is foremost, granting victory in a dispute; / a bath with water [infused with] all perfumes brings good fortune and health.
Likewise, a bath with water [infused with] seeds accomplishes all undertakings; / and in the same way, a bath with myrobalan is supreme for destroying misfortune.
A bath with sesame and white mustard seeds destroys inauspiciousness, / or a bath with sesame alone, or with white mustard seeds.
A bath with priyaṅgu is declared to increase good fortune; / likewise, an auspicious bath [is taken] with nāgakāntā and priyaṅgu.

With spikenard, murā, coraka, and nāgapuṣpa, together with nāgadāna, it destroys distress; / with turuṣka, kakkola, nutmeg, and betel nut, with all these fruits, he should thoroughly administer [the bath].
2.108 / Rāma said: / Among all baths here, that bath which surpasses [all others]— / tell me all about that, which destroys all impurities.
Puṣkara said: / Hear of the bath with the water from [the Lord's] feet, which destroys all sins; / for without the asterism Śravaṇa, this yields only half its fruit.
Therefore, it should be undertaken with effort, especially under the asterism Śravaṇa, / or under Uttarāṣāḍhā, fasting and with senses conquered.
With all medicinal herbs and all perfumes, the wise man should smear the feet / of the God of gods who holds the discus, the Fourfold-formed, in succession.
Then he should prepare four firm, new water-jars / made of gold, silver, copper, or indeed of clay.
Then he should wash the two feet of Aniruddha with well water; / the jar filled with that [water] is to be placed before him.

Then the two feet of Pradyumna are to be washed with water from a cascade; / and that jar, filled, should be placed before him.
The two feet of Saṃkarṣaṇa are to be washed with lake waters; / and the jar filled with them should be placed before him.
The wise man should wash the two feet of Vāsudeva with river waters; / and the jar filled with them is to be placed before him.
Then worship of the Fourfold-formed [Lord] is to be performed as prescribed; / and he should worship those water-jars with perfumes, garlands, fruits, and unbroken rice.
Then, when the second day arrives, having bathed, having fasted previously, / facing Aniruddha, he should be bathed [with water from the jar] …
and of the god Pradyumna, then of Saṃkarṣaṇa, / and then of Vāsudeva, as of Rāma, the discus-bearer.
(Consecration of all the bells is to be performed / with purifying mantras by the pure Sāttvata, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.

2.109 / Rāma said: / Now I wish to hear the procedure for optional amulets, / which fulfills all desires, is supreme, and likewise removes misfortune.
Puṣkara said: / Learn from me the operation of the amulet according to the Atharvanic rule. / One should address the tree visibly with the verse: “Stand firm.”
With the second [verse] minus a quarter-verse, one should sprinkle the site of the amulet; / then with the subsequent quarter of this [verse], one should fashion the amulet.
With the verse “With a kinsman,” one should cut it from that [tree], so says the revelation; / from that hymn, with the third [verse], one should take the amulet.
Everywhere the fashioning of the amulets should be pure; / and the substances suitable for use are declared to be only [proper] seeds.
They should be made the size of a thumb-joint all around; / one should properly produce four knots on them.

kṛtaśāntyudake pātre ramye lohamaye dṛḍhe .. 2.109.10 ..
svaliṅgoddhṛmantreṇa darvidaṇḍādataḥ param ..
vimucya sarvaṃ tenaiva mantreṇa bhrāmayenmaṇim .. 11 ..
pātre tasmiṃstatastasmāduddhṛtyā bandhanaṃ bhavet ..
sakalenaiva mantreṇa mantrayecca tathodgatam .. 12 ..
sāmānyamidamuktaṃ te śṛṇu vaiśeṣikaṃ dvija ..
abhīvartamaṇau karma tava vakṣyāmyataḥ param .. 13 ..
meaning:
अग्रतो मूलतो वापि कल्पमानेऽतिरिच्यते ..
अरातीयोरित्यनया छिन्द्याच्छस्त्रेण तत्त्ववित् .. 7 ..
अर्थं च सुशिरः कृत्वा ततः प्रक्षाल्य वारिणा ..
पात्रं तमग्नौ कृत्वा तु सम्यगेव यथाविधि .. 8 ..
यत्राचक्रुरित्यनया ससूत्रमत उत्तरम् ..
कुर्यात्तदग्निकुण्डं च प्रबोध्य जुहुयाद् घृतम् .. 9 ..
प्रत्यृचा स्वेन मन्त्रेण सम्पातानयनं भवेत् ..
कृतशान्त्युदके पात्रे रम्ये लोहमये दृढे .. 2.109.10 ..
स्वलिङ्गोद्धृमन्त्रेण दर्विदण्डादतः परम् ..
विमुच्य सर्वं तेनैव मन्त्रेण भ्रामयेन्मणिम् .. 11 ..
पात्रे तस्मिंस्ततस्तस्मादुद्धृत्या बन्धनं भवेत् ..
सकलेनैव मन्त्रेण मन्त्रयेच्च तथोद्गतम् .. 12 ..
सामान्यमिदमुक्तं ते शृणु वैशेषिकं द्विज ..
अभीवर्तमणौ कर्म तव वक्ष्याम्यतः परम् .. 13 ..
text_mt:
If while shaping it anything is left over at the tip or at the base, / the knower of truth should cut it off with an instrument using the [verse]: “Those who are hostile.”
And making it properly hollow, then washing it with water, / having placed that vessel in the fire duly according to rule,
with the [verse] “Where they made,” along with a thread thereafter, / one should kindle that fire-pit and offer ghee.
With each verse and with its own mantra, the collecting of consecrated drops should take place / in a lovely, firm vessel made of iron, in which propitiatory water has been prepared.
With the mantra containing its own characteristic mark, taken out from the handle of the ladle after that, / freeing everything, one should rotate the amulet with that very mantra.
Then, having taken it out from that vessel, the fastening takes place; / and one should consecrate it when it has emerged with the complete mantra.
This has been spoken to you as the general [rule]; listen to the specific one, O twice-born. / Hereafter I shall tell you the rite for the Abhīvarta amulet.

sanskrit_iast:
abhīvarttena maṇinetyādyābhistisṛbhirmaṇau ..
atrāyaṃ vāsavaṃ pātraṃ dvebhyaśca pratyṛcaṃ punaḥ 14 ..
dattvā sarveṇa sūktena maṇerādhanvanaṃ bhavet ..
abhīvartamaṇiḥ prokto no vā kāṣṭhānbhṛgūttama .. 15 ..
ayaṃ yonirata iti tasya homo vidhīyate ..
śaśakeṣviha ye śrāntavatsabhaiṣajyabhājanama .. 16 ..
kṣudreṣu yadapāmārgaṃ maṇiḥ śāntavisaṃjñakaḥ ..
ityete yāvaduktāḥ syurvivāhamadhurāśca ye .. 17 ..
pūrvoktena bhaveddharma eteṣāmiti me matiḥ ..
dravyauṣadhimaṇīnāṃ ca sabhāryāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 18 ..
dākṣāyaṇamaṇīnāṃ ca bhaveddhomādhiko vidhiḥ ..
oṣadhīnāmihedānīṃ vidhānaṃ śṛṇu bhārgava .. 19 ..
vrīhīṇāṃ vā yavānāṃ vā mūle tu paritaḥ kiret ..
yadi saumya sumantreṇa phalakānyekaviṃśatiḥ .. 2.109.20 ..
meaning:
अभीवर्त्तेन मणिनेत्याद्याभिस्तिसृभिर्मणौ ..
अत्रायं वासवं पात्रं द्वेभ्यश्च प्रत्यृचं पुनः 14 ..
दत्त्वा सर्वेण सूक्तेन मणेराधन्वनं भवेत् ..
अभीवर्तमणिः प्रोक्तो नो वा काष्ठान्भृगूत्तम .. 15 ..
अयं योनिरत इति तस्य होमो विधीयते ..
शशकेष्विह ये श्रान्तवत्सभैषज्यभाजनम .. 16 ..
क्षुद्रेषु यदपामार्गं मणिः शान्तविसंज्ञकः ..
इत्येते यावदुक्ताः स्युर्विवाहमधुराश्च ये .. 17 ..
पूर्वोक्तेन भवेद्धर्म एतेषामिति मे मतिः ..
द्रव्यौषधिमणीनां च सभार्याणां तथैव च .. 18 ..
दाक्षायणमणीनां च भवेद्धोमाधिको विधिः ..
ओषधीनामिहेदानीं विधानं शृणु भार्गव .. 19 ..
व्रीहीणां वा यवानां वा मूले तु परितः किरेत् ..
यदि सौम्य सुमन्त्रेण फलकान्येकविंशतिः .. 2.109.20 ..
text_mt:
With the three beginning with “With the victorious amulet,” [one should act] upon the amulet; / here [there is] a vessel for Indra, and again with each verse for the two,
having offered, the fastening of the amulet should be done with the entire hymn. / The Abhīvarta amulet has been declared, or from wood, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
The fire oblation for it is prescribed with “This is the womb from which…” / Among rabbits, here, those which are a vessel of medicine for weary calves,
what is Apāmārga among small [creatures], the amulet called Śāntavi— / as many as these are spoken of, and those which are sweet for marriage,
their procedure should be according to what was said previously; such is my opinion, / for amulets made of substances and herbs, and likewise for married couples.
And for Dākṣāyaṇa amulets there should be an additional rule regarding the fire oblation. / Now hear the procedure for herbs here, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
At the root of rice plants or of barley plants, one should scatter around / twenty-one boards with the auspicious mantra, if it is gentle.

sanskrit_iast:
amuṣminsthānarūḍhāsu yathābhilaṣitāṃ budhaḥ ..
yojayennāma sambhūtāmamukasya vibhūtaye .. 21 ..
ghṛtāhuteti ca dvābhyāṃ ghṛtena prokṣayettataḥ ..
mā te riṣasītyanayā hyā tvā tamabhimantrayet .. 22 ..
gandhaṃ saṃchādayeccaiva tato bhūmetyanantaram ..
ityauṣadhīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ sāmānyo'yaṃ vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ .. 23 ..
ekakādyāstu maṇayaḥ saliṅgaṃ nikhanedbudhaḥ ..
mantreṇa tānpravakṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ .. 24 ..
ekāṅka ekakāmāyetyekāṃke vidhivatkhanet ..
ākrandayati sūktena pradadhnāṃ yadyathāvidhi .. 25 ..
iyaṃ vīrudityanayā vidhivanmadhughaḥ khanet ..
sūktena sukalenāsya maṇerābandhanaṃ bhavet .. 26 ..
imāṃ khanāmītyanayā nitanīliṅgayā khanim ..
pratīcī saumamasitāṃ badhnīyāttu yathāvidhi .. 27 ..
meaning:
अमुष्मिन्स्थानरूढासु यथाभिलषितां बुधः ..
योजयेन्नाम सम्भूताममुकस्य विभूतये .. 21 ..
घृताहुतेति च द्वाभ्यां घृतेन प्रोक्षयेत्ततः ..
मा ते रिषसीत्यनया ह्या त्वा तमभिमन्त्रयेत् .. 22 ..
गन्धं संछादयेच्चैव ततो भूमेत्यनन्तरम् ..
इत्यौषधीनां सर्वासां सामान्योऽयं विधिः स्मृतः .. 23 ..
एककाद्यास्तु मणयः सलिङ्गं निखनेद्बुधः ..
मन्त्रेण तान्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावदनुपूर्वशः .. 24 ..
एकाङ्क एककामायेत्येकांके विधिवत्खनेत् ..
आक्रन्दयति सूक्तेन प्रदध्नां यद्यथाविधि .. 25 ..
इयं वीरुदित्यनया विधिवन्मधुघः खनेत् ..
सूक्तेन सुकलेनास्य मणेराबन्धनं भवेत् .. 26 ..
इमां खनामीत्यनया नितनीलिङ्गया खनिम् ..
प्रतीची सौममसितां बध्नीयात्तु यथाविधि .. 27 ..
text_mt:
Among those grown in that place, the wise one should take the desired one, / naming the one that has arisen for the prosperity of so-and-so.
And with the two [verses beginning with] “Offered with ghee,” one should then sprinkle it with ghee; / and one should consecrate it with the [verse] “May you not come to harm,” [saying] “Hither to you…”
And one should conceal its fragrance, and then immediately thereafter with [the hymn] “Earth…” / This is remembered as the general procedure for all herbs.
A wise man should dig up the amulets such as Ekakā with the [verse] bearing the characteristic mark; / I shall declare them properly in due order along with the mantra.
With “O Ekāṅka, for one desire,” one should dig duly for the Ekāṅka [amulet]; / with the hymn “He causes to cry out,” one should offer curds duly.
With the [verse] “This plant,” one should dig duly for the Madhugha [plant]; / with the complete hymn, the fastening of this amulet should be performed.
One should make the excavation with the [verse] “I dig this up,” containing the characteristic mark of the Nitanī; / and one should duly bind the dark [plant] that faces west and belongs to Soma.

sanskrit_iast:
yātvā gandharva indrābhyāṃ kapikacchuṃ khanedvadhaḥ ..
sūktenānena tanmeḍhre prabadhnīyāditi sthitaḥ .. 28 ..
imāṃ khanāmītyanayā daśadhāsrutayā khanet ..
pāṭhāsūktena badhnīyādekā rājñīmiti śrutiḥ .. 29 ..
daśaśīrṣa iti dvābhyāṃ mahākhyaṃ vidhivatkhanet ..
āpaḥ punantvityanena badhnīyāttāṃ yathāvidhi .. 2.109.30 ..
meaning:
यात्वा गन्धर्व इन्द्राभ्यां कपिकच्छुं खनेद्वधः ..
सूक्तेनानेन तन्मेढ्रे प्रबध्नीयादिति स्थितः .. 28 ..
इमां खनामीत्यनया दशधास्रुतया खनेत् ..
पाठासूक्तेन बध्नीयादेका राज्ञीमिति श्रुतिः .. 29 ..
दशशीर्ष इति द्वाभ्यां महाख्यं विधिवत्खनेत् ..
आपः पुनन्त्वित्यनेन बध्नीयात्तां यथाविधि .. 2.109.30 ..
text_mt:
With [the mantra] "Yātvā gandharva indrābhyām", one should dig up cowhage downwards. / With this hymn, standing, he should tie it on his penis.
With [the mantra] "Imāṃ khanāmi", he should dig [it] flowing tenfold. / With the Pāṭhā hymn he should tie it; "one is queen", so says the scripture.
With the two [verses beginning] "Daśaśīrṣaḥ", he should duly dig up the [herb] called Mahā. / With "Āpaḥ punantu", he should duly tie it.

sanskrit_iast:
imāṃ khanāmyauṣadhīṃ tvāṃ ḍhabīṃ nāma tathotkhanet ..
kāṇḍīyāṛktayā tvete badhnīyāttu yathāvidhi .. 31 ..
meaning:
इमां खनाम्यौषधीं त्वां ढबीं नाम तथोत्खनेत् ..
काण्डीयाऋक्तया त्वेते बध्नीयात्तु यथाविधि .. 31 ..
text_mt: With "Imāṃ khanāmy oṣadhīm", he should likewise dig up the [herb] named Ḍhabī. / With the verse relating to Kāṇḍa, he should duly tie these.

sanskrit_iast:
ya ātmajā ityanayā khanyāditi tathaiva tām ..
anenaiva prabadhnīyādvidvānsūktena taṃ maṇim .. 32 ..
meaning:
य आत्मजा इत्यनया खन्यादिति तथैव ताम् ..
अनेनैव प्रबध्नीयाद्विद्वान्सूक्तेन तं मणिम् .. 32 ..
text_mt: With "Ya ātmajāḥ", he should likewise dig that up. / With this very hymn, the wise man should bind that amulet.

sanskrit_iast:
ariṣṭastvā khanatu vai pippalaṃ tu khanettathā ..
yāvaddyauriti sūktena tasya cābandhanaṃ bhavet .. 33 ..
meaning:
अरिष्टस्त्वा खनतु वै पिप्पलं तु खनेत्तथा ..
यावद्द्यौरिति सूक्तेन तस्य चाबन्धनं भवेत् .. 33 ..
text_mt: With "Ariṣṭas tvā khanatu vai", he should dig up Pippala. / With the hymn "Yāvad dyauḥ", its binding should take place.

sanskrit_iast:
sāhasīnāvacetyevaṃ saidhakaṃ ca tathā khanet ..
anevaiva prabadhnīyātsūtreṇa tu yathāvidhi .. 34 ..
meaning:
साहसीनावचेत्येवं सैधकं च तथा खनेत् ..
अनेवैव प्रबध्नीयात्सूत्रेण तु यथाविधि .. 34 ..
text_mt: With "Sāhasīnāvaca", he should likewise dig up Saidhaka. / With this very [hymn], he should duly tie it with a cord.

sanskrit_iast:
payo'sītyathavā hanyātsvargapatrīṃ yathāvidhi ..
sūktena tāṃ prabadhnīyādanenaiva yathākramam .. 35 ..
meaning:
पयोऽसीत्यथवा हन्यात्स्वर्गपत्रीं यथाविधि ..
सूक्तेन तां प्रबध्नीयादनेनैव यथाक्रमम् .. 35 ..
text_mt: Or with "Payo 'si", he should duly strike Svargapatrī. / With this very hymn, he should bind it in due order.

sanskrit_iast:
imāṃ khanāmītyanayā māṣaparṇīṃ tathā khanet ..
dvābhyāṃ cānarthasaktatvaprabadhnīyāditi śrutiḥ ..36..
meaning:
इमां खनामीत्यनया माषपर्णीं तथा खनेत् ..
द्वाभ्यां चानर्थसक्तत्वप्रबध्नीयादिति श्रुतिः ..36..
text_mt: With "Imāṃ khanāmi", he should likewise dig up Māṣaparṇī. / And with two [verses], because it clings without purpose, he should tie it, so says the scripture.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ khaṇḍārikāṃ khanyādrājā tvāṃ varuṇaḥ khanet..
ṛcānayā samastena sūktenābandhanaṃ bhavet ..37..
meaning:
ततः खण्डारिकां खन्याद्राजा त्वां वरुणः खनेत्..
ऋचानया समस्तेन सूक्तेनाबन्धनं भवेत् ..37..
text_mt: Then he should dig up Khaṇḍārikā with the verse "Rājā tvāṃ varuṇaḥ khanat". / With the entire hymn, its binding should take place.

sanskrit_iast:
ekārkaprabhṛtīnāṃ tu liṅgaḥ kalpyaṃ phalaṃ budhaiḥ ..
sāmīyātvāha varuṇetyevamādiṣu saṃśritāḥ .. 38 ..
meaning:
एकार्कप्रभृतीनां तु लिङ्गः कल्प्यं फलं बुधैः ..
सामीयात्वाह वरुणेत्येवमादिषु संश्रिताः .. 38 ..
text_mt: For [amulets] beginning with Ekārka, however, the fruit is to be conceived by the wise from the characteristic marks, / based on [mantras] such as "Sāmīyā tvāha varuṇa" and others.

sanskrit_iast:
sāmīdayaḥ padārthāste upaklṛptāstathā smṛtāḥ ..
dravyaistaistu maṇiṃ kuryādāmnāyoktairyathāvidhi .. 39 ..
meaning:
सामीदयः पदार्थास्ते उपक्लृप्तास्तथा स्मृताः ..
द्रव्यैस्तैस्तु मणिं कुर्यादाम्नायोक्तैर्यथाविधि .. 39 ..
text_mt: The substances beginning with Sāmī are handed down as prepared in that manner. / With these substances, one should make an amulet according to the injunctions in the traditional texts,

sanskrit_iast:
talliṅgena tu mantreṇa yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ ..
kuṣṭhasya maṇayaḥ pañca udapātre vidurbudhāḥ .. 2.109.40 ..
meaning:
तल्लिङ्गेन तु मन्त्रेण यथावदनुपूर्वशः ..
कुष्ठस्य मणयः पञ्च उदपात्रे विदुर्बुधाः .. 2.109.40 ..
text_mt: duly in regular order, with the mantra indicating that characteristic. / The wise know five amulets of Kuṣṭha in a water vessel.

sanskrit_iast:
pratyaikapāṭhasaṃskāra śuddhaye veti naḥ śrutam ..
caturasraṃ prabadhnīyānmaṇimañjanavattathā .. 41 ..
meaning:
प्रत्यैकपाठसंस्कार शुद्धये वेति नः श्रुतम् ..
चतुरस्रं प्रबध्नीयान्मणिमञ्जनवत्तथा .. 41 ..
text_mt: Or, as we have heard, for purification through individual recitation and consecration, / he should bind a four-cornered amulet just like collyrium.

sanskrit_iast:
saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ siddhamubhayatra parigrahāt ..
kuryādvākṣyaṃ ca saṃskāraṃ vyāghratyapamaṇau tathā..42 ..
meaning:
सैन्धवं लवणं सिद्धमुभयत्र परिग्रहात् ..
कुर्याद्वाक्ष्यं च संस्कारं व्याघ्रत्यपमणौ तथा..42 ..
text_mt: Rock salt is perfected from grasping it in both places. / He should also perform the tree consecration on the amulet against tigers.

sanskrit_iast:
caturasrau tu kartavyau maṇī kāraṇakālajau ..
naimittikāśca maṇayo maṇayaḥ saṃviduśca ye .. 43 ..
meaning:
चतुरस्रौ तु कर्तव्यौ मणी कारणकालजौ ..
नैमित्तिकाश्च मणयो मणयः संविदुश्च ये .. 43 ..
text_mt: Two four-cornered amulets should be made, produced by the occasion and the time. / And those amulets that are occasional, and those amulets that are known [as regular]—

sanskrit_iast:
svaṃsvaṃ mantraṃ bhavetteṣāmiti me niścitā matiḥ ..
naimittikānāṃ ghorāste teṣāṃ naimittikaṃ bhavet .. 44 ..
meaning:
स्वंस्वं मन्त्रं भवेत्तेषामिति मे निश्चिता मतिः ..
नैमित्तिकानां घोरास्ते तेषां नैमित्तिकं भवेत् .. 44 ..
text_mt: each has its own mantra; such is my settled opinion. / The terrible ones among the occasional amulets have an occasional [rite].

sanskrit_iast:
sampadānāṃ tathā madhye sāmpadaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
sīmātryātvāhetyanena sīmasaṃ janavadbhavet .. 45 ..
meaning:
सम्पदानां तथा मध्ये साम्पदं नात्र संशयः ..
सीमात्र्यात्वाहेत्यनेन सीमसं जनवद्भवेत् .. 45 ..
text_mt: Likewise among the [amulets] of prosperity, it belongs to prosperity, there is no doubt here. / With "Sīmātryā tvāha", the lead should become like the people.

sanskrit_iast:
piśācaśātanaḥ puṃsāṃ yātudhānavināśanaḥ ..
mantraliṅgādayaṃ jñeyo mantraścāsya pravakṣyate .. 46 ..
meaning:
पिशाचशातनः पुंसां यातुधानविनाशनः ..
मन्त्रलिङ्गादयं ज्ञेयो मन्त्रश्चास्य प्रवक्ष्यते .. 46 ..
text_mt: It dispels piśācas for men and destroys yātudhānas. / This is to be known from the mark of the mantra, and its mantra will be stated:

sanskrit_iast:
śarakāṣṭhe tu saṃyojya sīsaṃ kṛtveti buddhimān ..
bhārṅgīṃ jyāṃ dhanuṣaḥ kṛtvā bādhakenātha tena tata .. 47 ..
meaning:
शरकाष्ठे तु संयोज्य सीसं कृत्वेति बुद्धिमान् ..
भार्ङ्गीं ज्यां धनुषः कृत्वा बाधकेनाथ तेन तत .. 47 ..
text_mt: Fixing [an arrow-head] of lead onto an arrow-shaft of reed, the wise man, / having made a bowstring of bhārṅgī on the bow, then with that tormentor,

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmau piśācamālikhya bhagavena tu tāḍayet ..
uttareṇa śareṇaiva piśāco nāśamāpnuyāt .. 48 ..
meaning:
भूमौ पिशाचमालिख्य भगवेन तु ताडयेत् ..
उत्तरेण शरेणैव पिशाचो नाशमाप्नुयात् .. 48 ..
text_mt: having drawn a piśāca on the ground, he should strike it with the bow; / with the following arrow indeed the piśāca will meet destruction.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṃkudhāramaṇermantra anusūryamiti smṛtiḥ ..
prajñātavarṇaśābdāśca rohitasya parigrahaḥ .. 49 ..
meaning:
शंकुधारमणेर्मन्त्र अनुसूर्यमिति स्मृतिः ..
प्रज्ञातवर्णशाब्दाश्च रोहितस्य परिग्रहः .. 49 ..
text_mt: The traditional rule for the mantra of the Śaṅkudhāra amulet is "Anusūryam". / The taking up of a red [hide] has a well-known color and sound.

sanskrit_iast:
carmaṇaḥ syāttathā vargo rohitāsābhavecca gāḥ ..
śaṃkurnidhīyate yatra vistarārthaṃ tu carmaṇaḥ .. 2.109.50 ..
meaning:
चर्मणः स्यात्तथा वर्गो रोहितासाभवेच्च गाः ..
शंकुर्निधीयते यत्र विस्तरार्थं तु चर्मणः .. 2.109.50 ..
text_mt: There should be a set of skins, and they should be cattle that are red. / Where a peg is fixed for the sake of stretching out the hide,

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāddeśānmaṇiḥ kāryaḥ śaṃkurdhanaparigrahaḥ ..
maṇidhanaṃ ca dugdhaṃ syādupaviṣṭāya carmaṇi .. 51 ..
meaning:
तस्माद्देशान्मणिः कार्यः शंकुर्धनपरिग्रहः ..
मणिधनं च दुग्धं स्यादुपविष्टाय चर्मणि .. 51 ..
text_mt: from that place the amulet is to be made, the peg being the receipt of wealth. / And the wealth of the amulet should be milk for him seated on the hide,

sanskrit_iast:
yajamānāya dharmajña udapātraṃ tathāmayā ..
atikāmala rogaghnamāyuṣyaśca tathā maṇiḥ .. 52 ..
meaning:
यजमानाय धर्मज्ञ उदपात्रं तथामया ..
अतिकामल रोगघ्नमायुष्यश्च तथा मणिः .. 52 ..
text_mt: for the sacrificer, O knower of dharma, likewise a water vessel with disease-curing [herbs]. / The amulet destroys severe jaundice and grants longevity.

sanskrit_iast:
imaṃ me kuṣṭhetyanena pañcānāṃ syātparigrahaḥ ..
atyarthameva naiteṣāṃ jalaṃ kuṣṭhena saṃyutam .. 53 ..
meaning:
इमं मे कुष्ठेत्यनेन पञ्चानां स्यात्परिग्रहः ..
अत्यर्थमेव नैतेषां जलं कुष्ठेन संयुतम् .. 53 ..
text_mt: With "Imaṃ me kuṣṭha", the acquisition of the five takes place. / Not excessively indeed is water combined with Kuṣṭha for these.

sanskrit_iast:
satkṛtya pānayogatvādyajamānaḥ pibettataḥ .
maṇayaḥ pañcakuṣṭhe dvau maṇiśabdaparigraham .. 54 ..
meaning:
सत्कृत्य पानयोगत्वाद्यजमानः पिबेत्ततः .
मणयः पञ्चकुष्ठे द्वौ मणिशब्दपरिग्रहम् .. 54 ..
text_mt: Having honored it, because it is fit for drinking, the sacrificer should then drink it. / There are five amulets; in Kuṣṭha two receive the designation of amulet.

sanskrit_iast:
tulyena vidhinā kāryāḥ phalaṃ teṣāṃ pṛthakpṛthak ..
śirortināśanaḥ pūrvo dvitīyo viṣadūṣakaḥ .. 59 ..
meaning:
तुल्येन विधिना कार्याः फलं तेषां पृथक्पृथक् ..
शिरोर्तिनाशनः पूर्वो द्वितीयो विषदूषकः .. 59 ..
text_mt: They should be made by equal procedure, [yet] their fruits are distinct: / The first destroys headache; the second destroys poison;

sanskrit_iast:
tṛtīyaśca tathā prokto viṣamajvaranāśanaḥ ..
caturthaśca tathā proktaḥ satatajvaranāśanaḥ .. 56 ..
meaning:
तृतीयश्च तथा प्रोक्तो विषमज्वरनाशनः ..
चतुर्थश्च तथा प्रोक्तः सततज्वरनाशनः .. 56 ..
text_mt: the third is declared likewise to destroy intermittent fever; / the fourth is declared likewise to destroy continuous fever;

sanskrit_iast:
cakṣuṣyaḥ pañcamaḥ prokto maṇirbhārgavanandana ..
kṛtvodapātraṃ kuṣṭhāmbho navanītavimiśritam .. 57 ..
meaning:
चक्षुष्यः पञ्चमः प्रोक्तो मणिर्भार्गवनन्दन ..
कृत्वोदपात्रं कुष्ठाम्भो नवनीतविमिश्रितम् .. 57 ..
text_mt: the fifth amulet is declared beneficial to the eyes, O son of Bhṛgu. / Having made a water vessel containing kuṣṭha-water mixed with fresh butter,

sanskrit_iast:
bhūyaḥ kuṣṭhaṃ kṣipettatra maṇiṃ tatrāvatārayet ..
maṇibandhaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā toyaṃ tatpāyayennaram .. 58 ..
meaning:
भूयः कुष्ठं क्षिपेत्तत्र मणिं तत्रावतारयेत् ..
मणिबन्धं ततः कृत्वा तोयं तत्पाययेन्नरम् .. 58 ..
text_mt: he should again throw Kuṣṭha into it and immerse the amulet there. / Then, having tied the amulet, he should make the man drink that water,

sanskrit_iast:
lipyecca sarujaṃ deśamudapātrajalena tu ..
yāḥ purastādityanena maṇiḥ syāllavaṇasya tu .. 59 ..
meaning:
लिप्येच्च सरुजं देशमुदपात्रजलेन तु ..
याः पुरस्तादित्यनेन मणिः स्याल्लवणस्य तु .. 59 ..
text_mt: and he should smear the painful area with water from the water vessel. / With "Yāḥ purastāt", there is an amulet of salt.

sanskrit_iast:
piturvastrapuṭe baddhvā lavaṇasya tu tanmaṇim ..
ābandhe kuṣṭhavatsyācca yātudhānavināśanaḥ .. 2.109.60 ..
meaning:
पितुर्वस्त्रपुटे बद्ध्वा लवणस्य तु तन्मणिम् ..
आबन्धे कुष्ठवत्स्याच्च यातुधानविनाशनः .. 2.109.60 ..
text_mt: Having tied that amulet of salt in a fold of his father's garment, / its tying should be like Kuṣṭha, and it destroys yātudhānas.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāghrarūpa ityanena khaṃtavyaṃ vāṭarūṣakam ..
vyāghrarūpa iti dvābhyāmṛgbhyāmābandhanaṃ bhavet .. 61 ..
meaning:
व्याघ्ररूप इत्यनेन खंतव्यं वाटरूषकम् ..
व्याघ्ररूप इति द्वाभ्यामृग्भ्यामाबन्धनं भवेत् .. 61 ..
text_mt: With "Vyāghrarūpaḥ", Vāṭarūṣaka is to be dug up. / With the two verses "Vyāghrarūpaḥ", the tying should take place.

sanskrit_iast:
piśācanāśakastvevaṃ sa maṇiḥ syādasaṃśayam ..
evamevottarābhyāṃ ca bhavepratyabhicārakaḥ .. .. 62 ..
meaning:
पिशाचनाशकस्त्वेवं स मणिः स्यादसंशयम् ..
एवमेवोत्तराभ्यां च भवेप्रत्यभिचारकः .. .. 62 ..
text_mt: That amulet is truly a destroyer of piśācas, without doubt. / In this very way, with the following two [verses], it counteracts sorcery.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣkandasyetyanenāha triparṇī viśvabheṣajī ..
skandasyopari yaḥ skando bhavettasya vināśinī .. 63 ..
meaning:
विष्कन्दस्येत्यनेनाह त्रिपर्णी विश्वभेषजी ..
स्कन्दस्योपरि यः स्कन्दो भवेत्तस्य विनाशिनी .. 63 ..
text_mt: With "Viṣkandasya", he said, Triparṇī is a universal remedy; / it destroys that skanda which occurs on top of a skanda.

sanskrit_iast:
yasmādaṅgāditi bhavedgaṇāditvātparigrahaḥ ..
gaṇasya karma sāmānyaṃ pratisūktaṃ na kārayeta .. 64 ..
meaning:
यस्मादङ्गादिति भवेद्गणादित्वात्परिग्रहः ..
गणस्य कर्म सामान्यं प्रतिसूक्तं न कारयेत .. 64 ..
text_mt: With "Yasmād aṅgāt", the grasping is due to its belonging to a class. / The rite of the class is common; he should not perform it hymn by hymn.

sanskrit_iast:
gorācavāri karmāṇi hantavyānīvamādibhiḥ ..
pataṅgādyāśca catvāraḥ saṃskṛtya prāṇino budhaḥ .. 65 ..
meaning:
गोराचवारि कर्माणि हन्तव्यानीवमादिभिः ..
पतङ्गाद्याश्च चत्वारः संस्कृत्य प्राणिनो बुधः .. 65 ..
text_mt: Actions of the bile-water of a cow are to be performed with these [mantras] and others. / The wise man, having consecrated the four living beings beginning with insects,

sanskrit_iast:
tṛṣṇatvaptaiśca mantreṇa gātraṃ prakṣālayetkhilam ..
prathamena tu sūktena veṇupautre dravo maṇiḥ .. 66 ..
meaning:
तृष्णत्वप्तैश्च मन्त्रेण गात्रं प्रक्षालयेत्खिलम् ..
प्रथमेन तु सूक्तेन वेणुपौत्रे द्रवो मणिः .. 66 ..
text_mt: should wash the entire body with the mantra "Tṛṣṇatvaptaiḥ". / With the first hymn, a liquid amulet in a bamboo vessel—

sanskrit_iast:
veṇuḥ kuryādbhaveddharmo vākṣavaddevadāruṇaḥ ..
saṃskṛtya pūrvamantreṇa māṣakādīnpramardayet .. 67 ..
meaning:
वेणुः कुर्याद्भवेद्धर्मो वाक्षवद्देवदारुणः ..
संस्कृत्य पूर्वमन्त्रेण माषकादीन्प्रमर्दयेत् .. 67 ..
text_mt: a bamboo [vessel] he should make; its dharma is like wood, made of Devadāru. / Having consecrated with the previous mantra, he should rub down the beans and other grains.

sanskrit_iast:
gātrasaṃskārasahitaiḥ piṣṭairvā prakṛtirbhṛśam ..
kevalenaiva mantreṇa mardayettu vinaśyati .. 68 ..
meaning:
गात्रसंस्कारसहितैः पिष्टैर्वा प्रकृतिर्भृशम् ..
केवलेनैव मन्त्रेण मर्दयेत्तु विनश्यति .. 68 ..
text_mt: Or, along with body-consecration, the nature [of the disease] is violently crushed with paste; / if he rubs down with the mantra alone, it perishes.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā svalomaprabhṛtī vidhūlo dhūśiro yutiḥ ..
devapraveśaṃ jatunā sthagayitvā tu raktikā .. 69 ..
meaning:
तथा स्वलोमप्रभृती विधूलो धूशिरो युतिः ..
देवप्रवेशं जतुना स्थगयित्वा तु रक्तिका .. 69 ..
text_mt: Likewise, beginning with his own hair, [...] / having sealed the entrance of deities with lac, the raktikā [seed]

sanskrit_iast:
dūṣyā iti pratīkena kuryātpratisaraṃ maṇim..
kṛtvā dūṣaṇamāyuṣyaṃ tadā pratyabhivādakaḥ..2.109.70..
meaning:
दूष्या इति प्रतीकेन कुर्यात्प्रतिसरं मणिम्..
कृत्वा दूषणमायुष्यं तदा प्रत्यभिवादकः..2.109.70..
text_mt: with the initial words "Dūṣyāḥ", he should make the amulet into a protective thread. / Having counteracted [harm], granting long life, then it is a counter-salutation.

sanskrit_iast:
ayaṃ pratisaraḥ pāṇau yātrākāle sapatnahā ..
sūtreṇānena badhnīyālliṅgātpratisaro paraḥ..71..
meaning:
अयं प्रतिसरः पाणौ यात्राकाले सपत्नहा ..
सूत्रेणानेन बध्नीयाल्लिङ्गात्प्रतिसरो परः..71..
text_mt: This protective thread on the hand slays enemies at the time of departure. / He should bind it with this cord; by its mark it is another protective thread.

sanskrit_iast:
anena vidhinā vṛtraṃ nijaghāna śatakratuḥ ..
aśaṃsa iti mantreṇa prabadhnīyādyathāvidhi..72..
meaning:
अनेन विधिना वृत्रं निजघान शतक्रतुः ..
अशंस इति मन्त्रेण प्रबध्नीयाद्यथाविधि..72..
text_mt: By this procedure Śatakratu slew Vṛtra. / One should fasten [the amulet] according to rule with the mantra 'Aśaṃsa'.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtiśrīprabhṛtīnāṃ ca vighnamevaṃ karoti yaḥ ..
vināśanaṃ tasya bhavedābandhādyakṣanāśanam..73..
meaning:
भूतिश्रीप्रभृतीनां च विघ्नमेवं करोति यः ..
विनाशनं तस्य भवेदाबन्धाद्यक्षनाशनम्..73..
text_mt: And whoever causes an obstacle to prosperity, fortune, and the like, / his destruction occurs; from its binding, consumption is destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
jyāsūtraprothitāḥ sapta vaṃśaprāptāḥ samudbhavāḥ ..
rattayāntaravyavahitā garbhiṇyā uddhared budhaḥ .. 74..
meaning:
ज्यासूत्रप्रोथिताः सप्त वंशप्राप्ताः समुद्भवाः ..
रत्तयान्तरव्यवहिता गर्भिण्या उद्धरेद् बुधः .. 74..
text_mt: Strung on a bowstring, seven [amulet-gems] obtained from bamboo and sprung from it, / separated by intervals of red seeds, the wise man should take for a pregnant woman.

sanskrit_iast:
māse caturthe badhnīyānmantreṇānena buddhimān ..
ekaikasminnatīte tu māse sūtrāntare maṇiḥ .. 75..
meaning:
मासे चतुर्थे बध्नीयान्मन्त्रेणानेन बुद्धिमान् ..
एकैकस्मिन्नतीते तु मासे सूत्रान्तरे मणिः .. 75..
text_mt: In the fourth month, the wise man should bind it with this mantra; / and as each month passes, a gem [is placed] in the interval of the cord.

sanskrit_iast:
ekaikaṃ prakṣipeddhīmānsasūtraṃ paścimaṃ tathā ..
prācī digiti mantreṇa udīcī bhayanāśanī ..76 ..
meaning:
एकैकं प्रक्षिपेद्धीमान्ससूत्रं पश्चिमं तथा ..
प्राची दिगिति मन्त्रेण उदीची भयनाशनी ..76 ..
text_mt: The intelligent man should add one by one with its cord, and the last one likewise, / with the mantra 'The eastern quarter', and 'the northern' which destroys fear.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣīyābhyāmityanena dāpyaḥ syādyakṣmanāśanaḥ ..
sandhānārthaṃ śītamagne rātrīmāteta mohanaḥ ..
mayūragosuravṛddhau dvau vetīti prakīrtitam ..77..
meaning:
अक्षीयाभ्यामित्यनेन दाप्यः स्याद्यक्ष्मनाशनः ..
सन्धानार्थं शीतमग्ने रात्रीमातेत मोहनः ..
मयूरगोसुरवृद्धौ द्वौ वेतीति प्रकीर्तितम् ..77..
text_mt: With [the mantra] 'From both eyes', [an amulet] destroying consumption should be applied; / for healing, 'The cold of fire'; 'Night has spread out' is bewildering; / for the increase of peacocks and cattle, two [mantras beginning with] 'Ve' are proclaimed.

sanskrit_iast:
proktāstathaite maṇayo nṛvīra kāmyā mayā sarvahitāya puṇyāḥ ..
yeṣāṃ hi bandho duritāpahārī bhayāpahaḥ kevalavṛddhikārī ..78..
meaning:
प्रोक्तास्तथैते मणयो नृवीर काम्या मया सर्वहिताय पुण्याः ..
येषां हि बन्धो दुरितापहारी भयापहः केवलवृद्धिकारी ..78..
text_mt: And thus these desired, meritorious amulet-gems have been spoken of by me, O hero among men, for the benefit of all, / whose binding indeed takes away misfortune, removes fear, and brings about unmitigated increase.

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare dvitīyakhaṇḍe mā0saṃ0 rāmaṃ prati puṣkaropākhyāne maṇibandhavarṇanannāma navottaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 109..
2.110
rāma uvāca ..
bhagavañchrotumicchāmi karma kāmyamahaṃ nṛṇām ..
kṛtena yena kāmānāṃ naro bhavati bhājanam .. 1..
puṣkara uvāca ..
sarveṣāmeva kāmānāmīśvaro bhagavānhariḥ ..
tasya sampūjanādeva sarvānkāmānupāśnute .. 2 ..
snāpayitvā ghṛtakṣīraiścandanenānulepayet ..
śuklaiḥ sampūjya puṣpaiśca saptamasya baliṃ haret .. 3 ..
raktapittānnaro ghorānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
tailakṣaudraghṛtairdevaṃ snāpayitvā janārdanam .. 4 ..
bhasmatrayeṇānulipya sampūjya kusumaiḥ sitaiḥ ..
pañcamudgabaliṃ dadyādatīsārātpramucyate .. 5 ..
saṃsnāpya pañcagavyena dattvā pañcānulepanam ..
pañcasasyabaliṃ dattvā sukhaṃ kuṣṭhātpramucyate .. 6 ..
meaning:
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे द्वितीयखण्डे मा0सं0 रामं प्रति पुष्करोपाख्याने मणिबन्धवर्णनन्नाम नवोत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. .. 109..
2.110
राम उवाच ..
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि कर्म काम्यमहं नृणाम् ..
कृतेन येन कामानां नरो भवति भाजनम् .. 1..
पुष्कर उवाच ..
सर्वेषामेव कामानामीश्वरो भगवान्हरिः ..
तस्य सम्पूजनादेव सर्वान्कामानुपाश्नुते .. 2 ..
स्नापयित्वा घृतक्षीरैश्चन्दनेनानुलेपयेत् ..
शुक्लैः सम्पूज्य पुष्पैश्च सप्तमस्य बलिं हरेत् .. 3 ..
रक्तपित्तान्नरो घोरान्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ..
तैलक्षौद्रघृतैर्देवं स्नापयित्वा जनार्दनम् .. 4 ..
भस्मत्रयेणानुलिप्य सम्पूज्य कुसुमैः सितैः ..

Thus in the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the Second Book, in the discourse of Mārkaṇḍeya, in the narrative of Puṣkara to Rāma, the hundred and ninth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Binding of Amulet-Gems'.
2.110 / Rāma said: / O Blessed One, I wish to hear the optional rites for human beings, / by performing which a man becomes a vessel for [the attainment of] his desires.
Puṣkara said: / The Blessed Lord Hari is the lord of all desires; / solely through worshipping Him, one obtains all desires.
Having bathed [Him] with ghee and milk, one should anoint [Him] with sandalwood. / Having worshipped [Him] with white flowers, one should offer an oblation of seven [grains].
A man is freed from terrible internal haemorrhage; there is no doubt about this. / Having bathed the god Janārdana with oil, honey, and ghee,
anointed [Him] with the three ashes, and worshipped [Him] with white flowers, / one should offer an oblation of five varieties of mung bean; he is completely freed from diarrhoea.
Having bathed [Him] with pañcagavya and applied the five ointments, / and having given an oblation of five grains, he is easily freed from leprosy.

Having bathed [Him] with oil, one should anoint [Him] with the three pungent substances. / Having given an oblation of five black lentils, he leaves behind wind disease.
Having bathed the god with two fats and anointed [Him] with the cold and hot [substance], / and having bathed the god Janārdana with the five juices,
and anointed [Him], O knower of dharma, with the five fragrances, / having properly offered flowers of five colours,
and having offered an unsurpassed incense of five resins, / one should then properly present an oblation of the five sweet substances.
By this one is quickly freed from disease; there is no doubt about this. / Praising Viṣṇu, the thousand-headed Hari, the guru of the moving and unmoving,
with the thousand names, one dispels all fevers. / One should anoint the god, bathed with ghee, with sandalwood.

Then one should worship the all-pervading Lord with five water-born flowers. / One should offer incense thrice, and likewise pañcagavya as an oblation,
and the five molasses preparations, O Rāma; one who is bound is freed from bondage. / One should anoint the god, bathed with the three cooling substances, with the three cooling substances.

One should anoint the god, bathed with cold and hot substances, with the three cooling substances. / Having offered an incense of cold and hot substances, and likewise an oblation of cold and hot substances,

worshipped [Him] with twin flowers, one should burn twin incenses. / And having offered a twin oblation, a man attains good fortune.
A woman desiring good fortune attains great good fortune; / even a man desiring good fortune attains great good fortune.

text_mt:
The enumeration of hells for sins has been declared to you by me, O Rāma; / and this becomes terrible because of the binding consequences for human beings.
Rāma said: / How does a living being come into existence, and how does it perish? / How does it pass to another body? Explain that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said: / The enclosure of the universe, O Rāma, is indeed the [cosmic] egg, which is not made of gold; / likewise, O mighty-armed one, is the earthly nature of a creature's body.
Just as the egg is stationed in space, O tiger among men, / exactly so here is the cavity located in the body of a man.
Just as wind, fire, and soma, stationed within the egg, / constantly sustain the universe, so do they sustain the body of embodied beings.
The two elements that serve as the foundation, at the beginning and the end of all embodied beings, / immediately attain the state of an embryo, O fortunate one.
And then, impelled by karma, the individual soul, having become wind, / makes an entrance there, having abandoned the body that promotes enjoyment, / whether from heaven, from hell, or from an animal womb.

text_mt:
Thus that individual soul then enters the womb through the bondage caused by the power of karma; / then, having entered, deluded, it remains for six months, [though] eternal, as the Veda [declares].
2.113
Rāma said:
How does the soul, having abandoned the body of experience, enter the womb?
And what is meant by the body of experience? Explain that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said:
The subtle transit body is the body of the embryo, O Bhārgava.
It belongs only to human beings when the time of death arrives.
That body of human beings is led by the messengers of Yama, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / along Yama's path, and not that of other living beings, O twice-born.
Human beings attain heaven or hell;
no other living beings at all do so, for they all only experience the fruits [of past deeds].
The accumulation of auspicious or inauspicious deeds, O son of Bhṛgu,
is made in this world solely by human beings.
Therefore, a dead human goes to the realm of Yama;
no other living creature does, O fortunate one, as they remain in wombs destined for experiencing fruits.

text_mt:
As he proceeds to that realm, Yama then determines
for the person the wombs and the hells according to his deeds.
And they [human beings] should revere him; without seeing Vaivasvata,
it is taught that after death, animals enter the womb.
And transformed into wind, they enter the womb without doubt;
but a dead human being, O Rāma, is taken to the abode of Yama.
Then, in accordance with his deeds, he beholds Yama:
as terrible if he is a sinner, and as gentle-looking if he is devoted to dharma.
The righteous person is honored there with a seat and water;
while the sinner, his neck bound with nooses, is tormented before Yama.
Then the Citraguptas announce heaven and hell for him,
O knower of dharma, and he then eats the funeral balls of rice.
Then, having cast off that [transit] body, he assumes a deceased body;
and his residence in the realm of the deceased is declared to last for one year.

There, hunger and thirst arise for him every day, O son of Bhṛgu;
and even there, a day and night is declared to be that of humans.
Uncooked śrāddha offerings given by men are consumed there;
without the funeral balls for the deceased, a man from the subtle transit body
does not obtain release; he eats the rice-balls right there.
When the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite is performed after one year, a man
casts off the deceased body and assumes the body of experience.
At that beginning, whatever little [deed] exists is experienced first, O son of Bhṛgu.
Two bodies of experience are taught, named auspicious and inauspicious;
an auspicious body of experience is born for him having the form of a deity.
The inauspicious one is of various kinds, formless and terrible to behold.
Whatever human form he previously had,
he obtains some resemblance to it even there.
Having enjoyed heaven with that body of experience according to the proper time,
