It stands in the upper part facing the [mother's] back;
and in whatever womb it remains, it knows that without doubt.
It remembers all events from the moment of birth,
and in the deep darkness it experiences pain, O Bhārgava.
From the great smell of worms, it experiences intense misery;
when water brought in by the mother is drunk, it feels extreme cold.
When hot food is eaten, it then experiences intense burning, O Bhārgava;
and through illnesses it undergoes extreme, sharp, and unbearable suffering.
When the mother engages in exertion, it suffers great exhaustion;
and when she is sick, it likewise experiences sharp agony.
Frightful diseases afflict it there again and again,
and neither the mother, nor the father, nor any physician knows of it then.
Because of its tenderness, these diseases produce sharp pain for it,
as it is afflicted by dreadful mental and physical diseases.

Then, within that brief span, the time passes like a hundred years; / and thus he suffers in the womb because of his past deeds.
Again and again he forms wishes to perform good deeds: / 'If by the stroke of fate I attain human birth,
then I shall perform action through which my liberation may come about. / Without liberation there is no happiness whatsoever in dwelling within the womb.
And dwelling in the womb is the supreme, sole cause of suffering in the world.' / While he thus reflects, those three months
seem like a hundred years to him as he suffers within the womb. / Then, when the time is complete, by the powerful winds of birth,
the creature is turned upside down, experiencing extreme pain. / Facing downward, by the wind through the constricted vaginal passage,
he is driven out feverish, like an arrow through the opening of an engine. / From exiting the vaginal passage [he suffers] pain resembling the flaying of the skin,

2.115
Rāma said: / O lord, you ought to explain to me the entire body; / for this indeed is the highest knowledge, and you know it, O mighty-armed one.
Puṣkara said: / Earth is to be known as having five qualities, water is to be known as having four qualities, / fire, O Rāma, has three qualities, and wind is regarded as having two qualities.
Ether in that regard is always to be known by the wise as having one quality. / Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as the fifth—
one should know [all five] as the qualities of earth; [those of water] lack smell at the end; / while those lacking taste and smell are proclaimed to belong to fire.

Likewise, their objects are five; I shall declare them hereafter: / excretion, pleasure, grasping, and walking;
these are the ten organs, [and] the mind is indeed their leader; / here are five organs of action and five organs of perception,
and here are five sense-objects and five gross elements. / Four are declared higher than the organs, O delight of the Bhṛgus:
the mind, the intellect, the self, and the unmanifest, O mighty-armed one. / The organs depend on them, and they are higher than the organs.
Know these principles to be twenty-four in number; / their unity, O fortunate one, is the twenty-fifth principle, the Cosmic Person.
Joined with them and separated from them, like both a fish and water, / the mind is ever producing doubt, and likewise the intellect is discerning.
The self is remembered as the living being, O Rāma, which is the experiencer of pleasure and pain; / the unmanifest is here the intermingled rajas, sattva, and tamas.

The Cosmic Person is to be known as another, great and all-pervading; / he who stands eternally distinct from the group of twenty-four,
the principles of the Cosmic Person are unified on the one hand; / and the principles are not separate from the supreme Cosmic Person.
Prakṛti [and] the Cosmic Person, O Rāma, is the partless twenty-fifth; / its modification is to be known by the wise [as] the rest of the group of principles.
Hands and feet are his everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces are his everywhere; / that supreme Cosmic Person is to be known, having all powers everywhere;
of whose two—pervasion and origin—the sages know neither beginning, middle, nor end; / he who knows him knows the Veda.
He goes to the supreme state who knows the supreme Cosmic Person; / and hear this very discernment introduced [now], O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Seven receptacles are recorded in the body; hear them also, O descendant of Bhṛgu: / one is the receptacle of blood, and another is that of phlegm;

the other two are the receptacles of undigested food and bile, [and] another is to be known as the receptacle of digested food; / the other two are the receptacles of wind and urine; seven receptacles are proclaimed.
For women, O Rāma, the womb is between the receptacle of bile and digested food; / for them that is the eighth, wherein the fetus resides.
In season, the vagina is always open like a lotus; / then it bears the semen united with blood in the womb.
At other times, the vagina of women is closed like a bud; / therefore, O sage, semen deposited in the vagina does not reach the womb.
Even in season, if the vagina is covered with wind, bile, and phlegm, / because of her impurity no offspring is born of her.
The kidneys, the lungs, the spleen, the heart, the viscera, the liver, solid masses, / and the taṇḍula, O fortunate one—they are bound to the receptacle.
From the essence of the chyle being digested of embodied beings arise / the spleen and the liver, O knower of dharma, and the lung from the foam of blood.

गर्भाशये तथा ज्ञेयाश्चतस्रो गर्भचिन्तकैः ..
त्रिंशच्छतसहस्राणि तथान्यानि दशैव तु .. 89 ..
षट्पञ्चाशत्सहस्राणि शिराणां कथितानि तु ..
ता वहन्ति रसं देहे केदारमिव कुल्यकाः .. 2.115.90 ..
अभ्यंगादि तथा सर्वं स्वेदलेपादिकं च यत् ..
द्विसप्ततिस्तथा कोट्यो रोम्णां विद्धि महाभुज .. 91 ..

sanskrit_iast:
majjāyā medasaścaiva vasāyāśca tathā dvija ..
mūtrasya caiva pittasya śleṣmaṇaḥ śakṛtastathā .. 92 ..
raktasya ca rasasyātha kramaśoñjalayaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
ardhārdhābhyadhikāḥ sarvāḥ pūrvārdhāñjalitaḥ smṛtāḥ ..93..
ardhāṃjaliśca śukrasya tathārdhā ca tathaujasaḥ ..
rajasastu tathā strīṇāṃ catasraḥ kathitā budhaiḥ ..94..
samadhātoridaṃ proktaṃ pramāṇaṃ dehacintakaiḥ ..
vilakṣaṇāni dehāni nityameva śarīriṇām ..
teṣāṃ bhedena bhidyante maladoṣānurūpataḥ .. 95 ..
etaccharīraṃ maladoṣapiṇḍaṃ dhātvāśrayaṃ karmavaśānubaddham ..
mokṣāya yasyeha bhavetsa dhanyo mokṣe ca hetuḥ paramo hi viṣṇuḥ ..96..
meaning:
मज्जाया मेदसश्चैव वसायाश्च तथा द्विज ..
मूत्रस्य चैव पित्तस्य श्लेष्मणः शकृतस्तथा .. 92 ..
रक्तस्य च रसस्याथ क्रमशोञ्जलयः स्मृताः ..
अर्धार्धाभ्यधिकाः सर्वाः पूर्वार्धाञ्जलितः स्मृताः ..93..
अर्धांजलिश्च शुक्रस्य तथार्धा च तथौजसः ..
रजसस्तु तथा स्त्रीणां चतस्रः कथिता बुधैः ..94..
समधातोरिदं प्रोक्तं प्रमाणं देहचिन्तकैः ..
विलक्षणानि देहानि नित्यमेव शरीरिणाम् ..
तेषां भेदेन भिद्यन्ते मलदोषानुरूपतः .. 95 ..
एतच्छरीरं मलदोषपिण्डं धात्वाश्रयं कर्मवशानुबद्धम् ..
मोक्षाय यस्येह भवेत्स धन्यो मोक्षे च हेतुः परमो हि विष्णुः ..96..

sanskrit_iast:
2.116
puṣkara uvāca ..
āyuṣi karmaṇi kṣīṇe saṃprāpte maraṇe nṛṇām ..
ūṣmā prakupitaḥ kāye tīvravāyusamīritaḥ .. 1 ..
meaning:
2.116
पुष्कर उवाच ..
आयुषि कर्मणि क्षीणे संप्राप्ते मरणे नृणाम् ..
ऊष्मा प्रकुपितः काये तीव्रवायुसमीरितः .. 1 ..
text_mt:
Puṣkara said:
When life and karman are exhausted, and death arrives for men,
the bodily heat, provoked in the body and stirred by a violent wind,
title: adhyāyāḥ 116-120

sanskrit_iast:
śarīramuparudhyātha kṛtsnāndoṣānruṇaddhi vai ..
bhinatti prāṇasthānāni punarmarmāṇi caiva hi .. 2 ..
meaning:
शरीरमुपरुध्याथ कृत्स्नान्दोषान्रुणद्धि वै ..
भिनत्ति प्राणस्थानानि पुनर्मर्माणि चैव हि .. 2 ..
text_mt:
obstructs the body, and then checks all the humoral faults;
it splits open the seats of breath and then the vital points;

sanskrit_iast:
śaityātprakupito vāyuśchidramanviṣyate tataḥ ..
dve netre ca tathā karṇau dvau tu nāsāpuṭau tathā ..3..
meaning:
शैत्यात्प्रकुपितो वायुश्छिद्रमन्विष्यते ततः ..
द्वे नेत्रे च तथा कर्णौ द्वौ तु नासापुटौ तथा ..3..
text_mt:
the wind, provoked by coldness, then searches for an aperture:
the two eyes, and likewise the two ears, and the two nostrils,

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhva tu sapta cchidrāṇi saptakaṃ vadanaṃ tathā ..
etaiḥ prāṇo viniryāti prāyaśaḥ śubhakarmaṇām .. 4 ..
meaning:
ऊर्ध्व तु सप्त च्छिद्राणि सप्तकं वदनं तथा ..
एतैः प्राणो विनिर्याति प्रायशः शुभकर्मणाम् .. 4 ..
text_mt:
and the upper apertures are seven, with the mouth being the seventh;
through these the breath departs, mostly in those of virtuous deeds;

sanskrit_iast:
adhaḥ pāyurupasthaṃ ca chidradvayamudāhṛtam ..
chidradvayena tenātha mriyante'śubhakāriṇaḥ .. 5 ..
meaning:
अधः पायुरुपस्थं च छिद्रद्वयमुदाहृतम् ..
छिद्रद्वयेन तेनाथ म्रियन्तेऽशुभकारिणः .. 5 ..
text_mt:
below, the anus and the genitals are declared as the pair of apertures;
through that pair of apertures, those who do unwholesome deeds die;

sanskrit_iast:
mūrdhānaṃ yogināṃ bhittvā jīvo vrajati bhārgava ..
athavā svecchayā rāma yena cecchanti yoginaḥ .. 6 ..
meaning:
मूर्धानं योगिनां भित्त्वा जीवो व्रजति भार्गव ..
अथवा स्वेच्छया राम येन चेच्छन्ति योगिनः .. 6 ..
text_mt:
splitting open the crown of the head, the soul of yogins departs, O Bhārgava,
or according to their own wish, O Rāma, by whatever [aperture] yogins desire.

sanskrit_iast:
antakāle tu saṃprāpte prāṇāpāneṣvavasthitaḥ ..
tamasā saṃvṛte jñāne saṃvṛteṣu ca marmasu .. 7 ..
meaning:
अन्तकाले तु संप्राप्ते प्राणापानेष्ववस्थितः ..
तमसा संवृते ज्ञाने संवृतेषु च मर्मसु .. 7 ..
text_mt:
When the hour of death has arrived, [the soul] remains in the prāṇa and apāna breaths;
when consciousness is shrouded by darkness, and the vital points are sealed,

sanskrit_iast:
sa jīvo nābhyadhiṣṭhānaścālyate mātariśvanā ..
sa jīvaścālyamānastu karmabhistaiḥ purātanaiḥ .. 8 ..
meaning:
स जीवो नाभ्यधिष्ठानश्चाल्यते मातरिश्वना ..
स जीवश्चाल्यमानस्तु कर्मभिस्तैः पुरातनैः .. 8 ..
text_mt:
that soul, seated at the navel, is moved by the wind;
and that soul, being moved by those past deeds,

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭāṅgāṃ prāṇavṛttiṃ tāṃ śanaiścyāvayate dvija ..
śarīraṃ prajahātyasmānniśvāsastu bhavettataḥ .. 9 ..
meaning:
अष्टाङ्गां प्राणवृत्तिं तां शनैश्च्यावयते द्विज ..
शरीरं प्रजहात्यस्मान्निश्वासस्तु भवेत्ततः .. 9 ..
text_mt:
slowly casts off that eightfold activity of breath, O twice-born;
it abandons this body, and then the [last] out-breath occurs.

sanskrit_iast:
cyavantaṃ jāyamānaṃ vā praviśantaṃ ca yoniṣu ..
paśyantyevaṃvidhaṃ siddhā jīvaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā .. 10 ..
meaning:
च्यवन्तं जायमानं वा प्रविशन्तं च योनिषु ..
पश्यन्त्येवंविधं सिद्धा जीवं दिव्येन चक्षुषा .. 10 ..
text_mt:
Falling away or being born, or entering into wombs,
such a soul the perfected ones behold with divine vision.

sanskrit_iast:
sa tu dehaparityāgakāle prāpte tadānagha ..
tatkṣaṇādeva gṛhṇāti śarīramativāhikam .. 11 ..
meaning:
स तु देहपरित्यागकाले प्राप्ते तदानघ ..
तत्क्षणादेव गृह्णाति शरीरमतिवाहिकम् .. 11 ..
text_mt:
When the time for abandoning the body has arrived, O sinless one,
at that very moment it assumes a subtle body;

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvaṃ bhajanti bhūtāni trīṇyasmāttasya vigrahāt ..
ākāśavāyutejāṃsi dve cādho bhṛgunandana .. 12 ..
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वं भजन्ति भूतानि त्रीण्यस्मात्तस्य विग्रहात् ..
आकाशवायुतेजांसि द्वे चाधो भृगुनन्दन .. 12 ..
text_mt:
three elements depart upward from this form of his:
space, wind, and fire; and two go downward, O descendant of Bhṛgu:

sanskrit_iast:
salilaṃ ca mahābhāga tathaiva ca vasundharā ...
evaṃ pañcatvamāpannaḥ puruṣastvabhidhīyate .. 13 ..
meaning:
सलिलं च महाभाग तथैव च वसुन्धरा ...
एवं पञ्चत्वमापन्नः पुरुषस्त्वभिधीयते .. 13 ..
text_mt:
water, O highly fortunate one, and likewise earth;
thus a person having attained fivefold dissolution is spoken of.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ pañcatvamāpanne taddehamativāhikam ..
bhayānakairmahāghorairnānāveṣadharaistathā .. 14 ..
meaning:
एवं पञ्चत्वमापन्ने तद्देहमतिवाहिकम् ..
भयानकैर्महाघोरैर्नानावेषधरैस्तथा .. 14 ..
text_mt:
When fivefold dissolution has thus occurred, that subtle body of his,
by terrifying, most dreadful [beings] wearing diverse attire,

sanskrit_iast:
uccaistasya tadā baddhaṃ kālapāśena satvaram ..
nīyate kālapuruṣairyāmyaṃ mārgaṃ sudustaram .. 15 ..
meaning:
उच्चैस्तस्य तदा बद्धं कालपाशेन सत्वरम् ..
नीयते कालपुरुषैर्याम्यं मार्गं सुदुस्तरम् .. 15 ..
text_mt:
tightly bound then by the noose of time, is swiftly
led by the minions of Yama along the path of Yama, which is exceedingly difficult to traverse;

sanskrit_iast:
taptāmbarīṣasaṃkāśaṃ tvayoguṇanibhaṃ mahat ..
saṃtaptasikataṃ ghoraṃ tāmraparṇanibhaṃ tathā .. 16 ..
meaning:
तप्ताम्बरीषसंकाशं त्वयोगुणनिभं महत् ..
संतप्तसिकतं घोरं ताम्रपर्णनिभं तथा .. 16 ..
text_mt:
resembling a heated frying pan, vast like an iron ball,
horrible with heated sand, and resembling copper leaves;

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ mahītalam ..
yamasya tu purī rāma ghorā saṃyamanī smṛtā .. 17 ..
meaning:
षडशीतिसहस्राणि योजनानां महीतलम् ..
यमस्य तु पुरी राम घोरा संयमनी स्मृता .. 17 ..
text_mt:
eighty-six thousand leagues along the earth's surface,
the dreadful city of Yama, Saṃyamanī, is remembered, O Rāma;

sanskrit_iast:
nīyate tena mārgeṇa tādṛśena tu tāṃ purīm ..
ākṛṣyamāṇaṃ puruṣairyāmyairghorairmahītale .. 18 ..
meaning:
नीयते तेन मार्गेण तादृशेन तु तां पुरीम् ..
आकृष्यमाणं पुरुषैर्याम्यैर्घोरैर्महीतले .. 18 ..
text_mt:
along such a path he is led to that city,
being dragged over the surface of the earth by the dreadful minions of Yama;

sanskrit_iast:
pīḍāmanubhavam̐statra mriyate na ca mānada ..
atyarthaviṣamaḥ proktaḥ sa mārgo ghoradarśanaḥ....
viśvarūpadharo rāma bhuvi śītāvṛto mahān ..
himaprapātabahulaścātiśītaḥ sudustaraḥ ..20..
meaning:
पीडामनुभवम्̐स्तत्र म्रियते न च मानद ..
अत्यर्थविषमः प्रोक्तः स मार्गो घोरदर्शनः....
विश्वरूपधरो राम भुवि शीतावृतो महान् ..
हिमप्रपातबहुलश्चातिशीतः सुदुस्तरः ..20..

sanskrit_iast:
andhakāravṛte durge garbhavāsopamastathā..
agnisaṃsparśavadanaiḥ kākakākolajambukaiḥ .. 21 ..
meaning:
अन्धकारवृते दुर्गे गर्भवासोपमस्तथा..
अग्निसंस्पर्शवदनैः काककाकोलजम्बुकैः .. 21 ..
text_mt:
shrouded in darkness, impassable, and like dwelling in a womb;
with crows, ravens, and jackals whose mouths feel like fire,

sanskrit_iast:
makṣikādaṃśamaśakairāvṛtaḥ sarpavṛścikaiḥ ..
bhakṣyamāṇo'pi tairjanturbhakṣyate cāpi rākṣasaiḥ .. 22 ..
meaning:
मक्षिकादंशमशकैरावृतः सर्पवृश्चिकैः ..
भक्ष्यमाणोऽपि तैर्जन्तुर्भक्ष्यते चापि राक्षसैः .. 22 ..
text_mt:
covered with flies, gnats, mosquitoes, snakes, and scorpions;
even while being eaten by them, the creature is also devoured by rākṣasas.

sanskrit_iast:
utkṛtyotkṛtya sahasā na ca prāṇairviyujyate ..
mudgaraiścūrṇyate ghoraistudyate lohakaṇṭakaiḥ .. 23 ..
meaning:
उत्कृत्योत्कृत्य सहसा न च प्राणैर्वियुज्यते ..
मुद्गरैश्चूर्ण्यते घोरैस्तुद्यते लोहकण्टकैः .. 23 ..
text_mt: Torn to pieces again and again suddenly, he is not separated from his vital breaths; / he is crushed by dreadful clubs and pierced by iron thorns.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣudhayā tṛṣayā caiva ghorayā cāpi pīḍyate ..
dahyamāno'tighoreṇa saikatena ca nīyate .. 24 ..
meaning:
क्षुधया तृषया चैव घोरया चापि पीड्यते ..
दह्यमानोऽतिघोरेण सैकतेन च नीयते .. 24 ..
text_mt: He is afflicted by hunger and dreadful thirst; / burning from intensely hot sand, he is carried away.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ saṃyāpyamānastu prāpyate yamamandiram ..
daśabhiḥ sa muhūrtaistu panthānamatidustaram .. 25 ..
meaning:
एवं संयाप्यमानस्तु प्राप्यते यममन्दिरम् ..
दशभिः स मुहूर्तैस्तु पन्थानमतिदुस्तरम् .. 25 ..
text_mt: Being thus driven along, he is brought to the abode of Yama / after ten muhūrtas along an extremely impassable road.

sanskrit_iast:
prāpnoti bhīmanirghoṣaṃ durgandhibhayadarśanam ..
tatkālaṃ sumahadvetti puruṣo devamāyayā .. 26 ..
meaning:
प्राप्नोति भीमनिर्घोषं दुर्गन्धिभयदर्शनम् ..
तत्कालं सुमहद्वेत्ति पुरुषो देवमायया .. 26 ..
text_mt: He reaches [a place of] terrifying roars, foul-smelling and fearful to behold; / through divine delusion, the man perceives that duration as immense.

sanskrit_iast:
pāpānurūpaṃ tatkālaṃ tasya tatrābhijāyate ..
kasyacidviśataṃ kālaṃ kasyacicchatasambhavam .. 27 ..
meaning:
पापानुरूपं तत्कालं तस्य तत्राभिजायते ..
कस्यचिद्विशतं कालं कस्यचिच्छतसम्भवम् .. 27 ..
text_mt: In accordance with his sins, that period arises for him there: / for some, it is an entry of time, for others, [a state] arising for a hundred [years].

sanskrit_iast:
kṣuttṛṣṇāsambhavāścaiva bhavantyatha mahābhayāḥ ..
daṇḍapiṇḍasya dharmajña pretatvamupajāyate .. 28 ..
meaning:
क्षुत्तृष्णासम्भवाश्चैव भवन्त्यथ महाभयाः ..
दण्डपिण्डस्य धर्मज्ञ प्रेतत्वमुपजायते .. 28 ..
text_mt: Great terrors born of hunger and thirst arise; / O knower of dharma, the state of a deceased spirit befalls the bodily frame.

sanskrit_iast:
preta loke sa vasati tataḥ saṃvatsaraṃ naraḥ ..
sodakumbhamatonnādyaṃ bāndhavaistasya dīyate .. 29 ..
meaning:
प्रेत लोके स वसति ततः संवत्सरं नरः ..
सोदकुम्भमतोन्नाद्यं बान्धवैस्तस्य दीयते .. 29 ..
text_mt: The man dwells in the realm of the deceased for a year after that; / food along with a water-pot is given for him by his kinsmen.

sanskrit_iast:
dinedine yaddharmajña tadbhuṅkte nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
na dīyate tu yasyaitatsa tu tatra yathā svayam .. 30 ..
meaning:
दिनेदिने यद्धर्मज्ञ तद्भुङ्क्ते नात्र संशयः ..
न दीयते तु यस्यैतत्स तु तत्र यथा स्वयम् .. 30 ..
text_mt: O knower of dharma, he consumes daily whatever [is given], there is no doubt of this; / but for the one to whom this is not given, he [fares] there just as by himself:

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvadattamathānnādyaṃ prāpnoti svayameva tu ..
svayameva na dattaṃ tu tathā dātā na vidyate .. 31 ..
meaning:
पूर्वदत्तमथान्नाद्यं प्राप्नोति स्वयमेव तु ..
स्वयमेव न दत्तं तु तथा दाता न विद्यते .. 31 ..
text_mt: he obtains only the food and nourishment given by himself previously; / but if nothing was given by himself, then no giver is found.

sanskrit_iast:
na cāstyudakadātā ca sa tu tatparitapyate ..
bāndhavaistūdakaṃ datta tatra tatrāsya jāyate.. 32 ..
meaning:
न चास्त्युदकदाता च स तु तत्परितप्यते ..
बान्धवैस्तूदकं दत्त तत्र तत्रास्य जायते.. 32 ..
text_mt: And there is no giver of water, so he suffers intensely there; / but the water given by kinsmen arises for him there at every step

sanskrit_iast:
nadī śītajalā nāma bahupānīyasaṃyutā ..
māsimāsi ca yacchrāddhaṃ tasya tatra pradīyate .. 33 ..
meaning:
नदी शीतजला नाम बहुपानीयसंयुता ..
मासिमासि च यच्छ्राद्धं तस्य तत्र प्रदीयते .. 33 ..
text_mt: as a river named Cold Water, filled with abundant water; / and whatever ancestral rite is offered for him month after month,

sanskrit_iast:
tena tṛptimavāpnoti paramāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
mānuṣyeṇa tu māsena pitṛloke dinaṃ smṛtam .. 34 ...
meaning:
तेन तृप्तिमवाप्नोति परमां नात्र संशयः ..
मानुष्येण तु मासेन पितृलोके दिनं स्मृतम् .. 34 ...
text_mt: by that he attains supreme satisfaction, there is no doubt of this. / A month among humans is regarded as a day in the realm of the ancestors;

sanskrit_iast:
pretaloke tu divaso mānuṣyeṇa vidhīyate ..

आश्रमेषु यथोक्तेषु वर्तन्ते ये द्विजोत्तमाः ..

देहधातून्परित्यज्य सलिलारण्यवह्निषु ..
अनाशने वा धर्मज्ञ मृताः स्युः स्वर्गगामिनः .. 6 ..
text_mt:
Those who, relying upon a pure mental disposition, are devoted to Janārdana, the lord of the gods— / their destination, O Rāma, is where radiant men reside, freed from all sins.
2.117 / Rāma said: / O venerable one, I wish to hear which men go to heaven, / and by what means, O best of upholders of dharma, [they go], as well as those who go to hell.
Puṣkara said: / The best of twice-born men who abide in the prescribed stages of life, / constantly dedicated to their own dharma, those men go to heaven.
Those who act in accordance with the royal duties, O protector of the earth, / kings intent upon the counsel of their royal priest, go to heaven.
Those whose happiness lies in the happiness of their subjects and who grieve in their sorrow, / who inflict restraint upon the wicked—they are to be known as goers to heaven.
Those who are slain for the sake of their master, for the sake of a brahmin, or on behalf of a friend, / and those who are killed in recovering cattle, those men go to heaven.
Those who have relinquished the bodily constituents in water, in the forest, or in fire, / or who die through fasting, O knower of dharma, go to heaven.

वैवाहिकानां वस्त्राणां प्रपाणां ये प्रदायिनः ..
उद्यानारामकर्तारस्ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः .. 10 ..

उपासकाश्च वृद्धानां ते ज्ञेयाः स्वर्गगामिनः ..14..
text_mt:
Those devoted to pilgrimage, perpetually worn out on the road, / and those emaciated by ascetic penance—they are to be known as goers to heaven.
Those who abstain from liquor and meat, who abstain from drinking alcohol, / and who abstain from lustful sexual intercourse are to be recognized as goers to heaven.
Those devoted to mother and father, self-controlled, devoted to their elders, speaking kindly, / and intent on truth and uprightness, those men go to heaven.
Those who provide wedding garments and public water-sheds, / and who create parks and pleasure-groves, those men go to heaven.
Those who construct reservoirs and wells, and those who give away maidens [in marriage], / and givers of umbrellas and shoes, those men go to heaven.
Those who provide firewood, and those who bestow cattle and villages, / and those who attend to cows, those men go to heaven.
Those devoted to helping others, free from binding others, / and who revere those worthy of reverence—such men go to heaven.
Wise men devoted to self-study, dedicated to serving their elders, / and who attend upon the aged—they should be known as goers to heaven.

text_mt:
Those who provide shelter, and likewise those who provide free feeding-halls, / devoted to cows, gods, and brahmins—such men go to heaven.
Those who listen to the dharmas, and likewise those who perform sacrifices, / and those dedicated to fasting—they should be known as goers to heaven.
Those who endure hardships in this world intent upon the study of the śāstras, / and who are engaged in what is beneficial to the śāstras—they should be known as goers to heaven.
Those who grant life to the distressed, and those who refrain from injury, / and do not torment living beings—such men go to heaven.
Those who give to the poor, masters endowed with forbearance, / and those who, though in their youth, are peaceful—such men go to heaven.
Those endowed with grandsons and daughter's sons, who live long lives, / and who do what is pleasing to children—such men go to heaven; / and those who support orphans, who arrange marriages, / and who give for the bride's second arrival—such men go to heaven.
Those who worship the planets, and likewise those who perform ancestral rites, / and those who share their food—such men go to heaven.

text_mt:
Those who are always devoted to the worship of all deities, / and those devoted to all manner of gift-giving—such men go to heaven.
And having performed extremely difficult deeds there unslain, / dying only in the course of time, O Rāma, such men go to heaven.
Those who constantly possess devotion to Madhusūdana, the lord of gods, the matchless one, / free from sattva, separated from rajas—they go to heaven, worshipped by the host of gods.
Puṣkara said:
People who commit great sins, and those who commit lesser sins, / men who eat meat, and likewise those who approach forbidden women, / and those devoted to another's wife—they indeed go to hell.
Those who transgress against their wife and torment men, / and those who are despised in assemblies—they indeed go to hell.
Those who have many wives and do not behave equally toward their wives, / and those who neglect the fertile period—they indeed go to hell. / Women who do not behave properly toward their husbands out of arrogance, / and likewise are devoted to what is displeasing—they should be known as goers to hell.

text_mt:
Those who despise their husband, speak unpleasant things, / and act according to their own independence—they should be known as goers to hell.
Those rulers of the earth who, abandoning the instruction of the royal treatises, / act in all matters [as they please]—they indeed go to hell.
Men who live abandoning the dharma prescribed for the social classes and stages of life, / outside the śāstras, O fortunate one—they indeed go to hell.
Those who sacrifice for those unfit to sacrifice, and those who give false testimony, / and likewise those devoted to falsehood—they indeed go to hell.
Those engaged in legal disputes who utter biased statements, / and those who do not see things impartially—they indeed go to hell.
Men who eat sweet delicacies while their dependents look on, / without sharing, O knower of dharma—they indeed go to hell.
Hired servants, O fortunate one, who do not do their hired work, / and those who eat what is not allotted to them—they indeed go to hell.
Deceivers of hired servants, and likewise deceivers of dependents, / and deceivers of others—they should be known as goers to hell.

text_mt:
Those who are ungrateful, pitiless, and those who seize another's property, / and those who behave deceitfully toward friends—they indeed go to hell.
Those who cause an obstacle to cows engaged in drinking, / and likewise to other living beings—they indeed go to hell.
Those men who cause an obstacle to one engaged in an act of dharma, / and those who encourage sin—they indeed go to hell.
Those who abandon dependents, and those who abandon sacrificial priests, / their patrons, and their teachers—they indeed go to hell.
Those who abandon deities, and those who abandon the sacred fires, / and those who abandon the śāstras—they indeed go to hell.
Those who always eat before children, guests, brahmins, / and gods, O bestower of honor—they indeed go to hell.
Those who go to a menstruating woman, and those who go to a female servant, / and those who go to an unnatural orifice—they indeed go to hell.

text_mt:
Pitiless men who emit semen in an unnatural orifice, in open air, / or during the forbidden days of the lunar cycle, O knower of dharma—they indeed go to hell.
Those who engage in self-study on prohibited study days here, O Rāma, / and those who revile their teachers—they indeed go to hell.
Revilers of deities, of the Vedas, and of brahmins, / and of the stories of the Purāṇas—they indeed go to hell.
Those men who are materialists, O Rāma, and those devoid of faith, / and seized by egotism—they indeed go to hell.
Men attached to evil deeds, who abandon good deeds, / and who betray their masters and friends—they indeed go to hell.
Those who are intent on malice toward kings, brahmins, and cows, / and toward friends as well, O knower of dharma—they indeed go to hell.
Those mortals addicted to calumny, who touch upon another's vulnerable points, / and are impure—they indeed go to hell.
Those who sell soma, and likewise those who sell seed, / and those who sell themselves—they should be known as goers to hell.

text_mt:
Those in whose house maiden daughters see their menses, O knower of dharma, / and those by whom she is given away for a bride-price—they indeed go to hell.
Those men who assert difference among Brahmā, Īśa, and Keśava, / utterly overcome by darkness—they indeed go to hell.
Those who omit the funeral cake for the sapiṇḍas born in their family, / and who do not offer the ancestral rites to their ancestors—they indeed go to hell.
And men whose nature is desire, and likewise those devoted [only] to wealth, / and those in the world who hate dharma—they indeed go to hell.
Those who do not look after the wretched, the sick, and their dependents according to their ability, / and do not run to help one who is distressed—they indeed go to hell.
And those proud with arrogance who mock the wretched, / and insult the innocent—these go to hell.
By causing torment to a person, O Rāma, one goes to hell in one way or another; / therefore, with effort, causing torment to another must be avoided by a person, O Rāma.

2.119
Rāma said:
O blessed one, I wish to hear the names of the hells, / and likewise the various torments of men who go to hell.
Puṣkara said:
Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, Mahāraurava and Raurava, / the hell Kālasūtra, and Mahānaraka,
Saṃjīvana, Mahāvīci, Tapana, Saṃpratāpana, / Saṃghāta, Sakākola, Kaśmala, Pūtimṛttika,
Lohaśaṅku, Nṛbhīma, Manthāna, Śālmali, Nadī, / Asipatravana, and likewise Lohakāra.
In the netherworlds, O mighty-armed one, [arranged] in groups of three in order of increase, / and likewise eight for each one, in the cardinal and intermediate directions,
are situated the hells of dreadful appearance that should be known, / into which these men of evil deeds go, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Some men, O Rāma, go into one hell, others successively into many, / being tormented again and again.

text_mt:
They strike others with whips, and other men as well, / O illustrious one, they force to eat iron balls heated in fire.
Likewise [they force] others [to eat] dust, and elsewhere others [to eat] vomit, / and elsewhere feces, and phlegm, and elsewhere thorns;
and elsewhere, O Bhārgava, sands resembling fire; / and elsewhere they force them to drink liquor colored like fire.
Elsewhere they cut the limbs of the denizens of hell limb by limb; / and elsewhere they tear them apart again and again with saws.
And elsewhere, placing the hell-dwellers in machines, they press them; / and placing others in a mortar, they strike them with pestles.
And elsewhere, those who are in pots or who have emerged slightly from a pot, / having attained great agony, they strike with iron mallets.
And elsewhere, having stripped off their skin, they cast the hell-dwellers to dogs, / and they are eaten by [dogs] with sharp teeth again and again.

text_mt:
And elsewhere, into a dark, terribly foul-smelling, terrifying, / intensely hot place like the dwelling of a womb, people are thrown by them.
By crows, jackals, serpents, scorpions, and mice, / and by flies they are eaten elsewhere by their command.
Elsewhere the vilest of men are forced to climb a dreadful Śālmali tree, / scorching, with sharp thorns, filled with serpents, insects, and other vermin.
And elsewhere, by their very command, they embrace / a dreadful heated slab of iron, exceedingly painful to touch.
Elsewhere, afflicted with fear, they dwell in an unapproachable abode; / there, O giver of honor, into their nostrils, eyes, ears, and mouths
enter flesh-eating worms with large coils; / and likewise others are repeatedly cast into an alkaline river.
And others are cast into a hell of extreme cold and darkness; / others enter a great river carrying streams of blood.
And others of dreadful appearance are dragged through the forest of sword-leaves; / and other men are afflicted there with thirst and hunger.

sharp smoke, having tied them upside down to trees, O giver of honor; / elsewhere the flaying of skin is done bit by bit by the soldiers.

having needle-like mouths elsewhere, they are made to suffer greatly with hunger; / and elsewhere they are sprinkled with oil and with molasses,
heated, O illustrious one, which cause intense pain to them; / elsewhere, with boils formed, their tongues lolling out, exceedingly distraught,
cast down in terrible heat, they are eaten by ants; / elsewhere, beginning from the feet in order, with a thread are cut
into sesame-seed-sized bits, O tiger among the Bhṛgus, the mountain-like hell-dwellers, / all the way up to their heads, again and again.

And having ground them into flour, others are thoroughly cooked in a pot; / and elsewhere, in iron vessels, with sharp iron stakes,
they are bound by dreadful [demons] on heated [vessels], O mighty-armed one; / and elsewhere, seized, they are dashed against rocks.
Throwing earth over them into pits, they are violently pounded with pestles; / elsewhere men, bound to a post, are shot at with arrows.
They are bound with chains and rolled among thorns; / elsewhere they are roused again and again by a noxious stench.
And by infernal creatures of various terrifying guises / and by many torments they are severely afflicted in hell.
And others devour one another's flesh, / weeping again and again, 'Alas, father! Alas, mother!'
Cursing their own deeds and beaten by those soldiers, / they are made to endure many torments, O son of Bhṛgu.

text_mt:
Others, released from infernal fire, perceive another fire / as very cool, O highly fortunate one, and of most pleasant touch.
Released from infernal cold, one considers a mass of snow pleasantly warm, / and everything else as possessing the most pleasant touch.
And that basest of men who is released from the weapons of hell / finds other weapons that strike him to be like pleasant touches.
In human life there are both pleasure and pain, but in heaven only pleasure; / in hell there is only fierce suffering unceasingly, O son of Bhṛgu.
Thirst is there, hunger is there, and an intense, terrifying stench; / manifold torments are proclaimed, and fear there is exceedingly terrible.
Strewn with foul-smelling thorns, crowded with corpses, / filled with hair and bones—dreadful hell is nothing but suffering.
It is filled with cries of distress, loud shrieks, crows, and carnivorous beasts, / teeming with worms, insects, and moths, and full of pus and blood,

text_mt:
Exceedingly frightful are the hells, most terrible, teeming with hosts of frightening venomous serpents; / those who bear devotion to Puruṣottama do not go there, O head of the lineage of Bhṛgu.
2.120 / Rāma said: / By what action, O knower of dharma, do men residing in hell / enter this or that womb of animals? Tell me that.
Puṣkara said: / People who commit great sins become worms in the midst of filth, / in many forms upon the earth, and then within rocks.
Gradually they attain the state of grass, shrubs, creepers, bushes, and trees; / and afterwards they become deer, constantly afflicted by the fear of hunters.
Those who steal the property of a brahmin, being violent and ever cruel in conduct, / are born in a terrible forest as brahmarākṣasas.
Fools devoted to other men's wives are born on parched ground / as chameleons, and immediately thereafter as piśācas; / and after that, without doubt, / they are born as black snakes in the hollow of a withered tree in a terrible forest.

text_mt:
Sinners who give false testimony become worms in filth for a long time; / having done so, they become snakes, and immediately thereafter piśācas.
Sinful people who betray their gurus and friends, those who betray their master, / those who betray twice-born men and students, the ungrateful, and atheists,
those who abandon their relatives, those who abandon seekers of refuge, / those who embezzle deposits, and those who purchase maidens,
become worms in filth, snakes, deer, and beasts of prey; / then those wicked ones are born as jackals associated with a terrible pack.
Sinners who steal another's property are born as elephants, horses, donkeys, / oxen, and camels; there is no doubt in this.
And according to their own fault, they are born as [beasts of burden for] that wealthy man / whose wealth was stolen by them, in proportion to his fortune.
Men who eat during an eclipse of the moon or the sun are born as elephants; / eating an uncooked śrāddha offering, they are born in the wombs of vultures.
Having accepted improper gifts, O Rāma, [they are born] as monkeys; / and having broken hopes, those base men become jackals.

text_mt:
An informer of bad conduct is born as an ensnarer; / for a long time, O highly fortunate one, again and again—so says the scripture.
O Rāma, of as many embodied beings as a meat-eater eats the meat, / into that many wombs he enters again and again; of this there is no doubt.
And his flesh must without doubt be eaten by them, O Rāma; / as many living creatures as are slain by someone outside the sacrificial altar,
to that many wombs he must go, O best of the Bhṛgus, / and in womb after womb he must be killed by that [creature]; there is no doubt in this.
Eaters of vomit, eaters of corpses, eaters of pus, and eaters of blood— / classes that have fallen away from their own duties are born in the wombs of pretas.
Stealing grain, one becomes a mouse; brass, a goose; water, a water-fowl; / honey, a gadfly; milk, a crow; juice, a dog; and ghee, a mongoose.
Stealing meat, [one becomes] a vulture; marrow, a diver-bird; oil, a bird that drinks oil; / salt, a cricket; and curd, a crane or bird of prey.

text_mt:
Stealing silk, [one becomes] a partridge; stealing linen, a frog; / cotton fabric, a curlew; a cow, an iguana; and molasses, a bat.
Stealing fine perfumes, [one becomes] a musk-shrew; leafy vegetables, a peacock; / cooked food, a fly; and uncooked food, a porcupine.
Stealing fire, a thief becomes a frog; stealing a house, a gecko; / and stealing red garments, one is born as a jīvañjīvaka bird.
[Stealing] a deer, [one becomes] a wolf; an elephant, a tiger; a horse, a monkey; and fruits and flowers, a monkey; / stealing a woman, one becomes a yakṣa; a vehicle, a camel; and livestock, a goat.
Stealing by force whatever property of another, / or eating an oblation that has not been offered, a man inevitably goes to an animal state.
Knowing that supreme suffering exists among animals, a man must always avoid sins; / and devotion should be offered to Madhusūdana: through it, he abandons all suffering.

text_mt:
The principal animal wombs and their signs have indeed been spoken by me; / nor is it possible for me to declare in full the torments of the lowest of men.
2.122 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having heard this, O best of the Yadus, Rāma, who gave delight to his father, / fell lifeless to the ground like a tree cut down at the root.
Celestial maidens with full, raised breasts sprinkled him / who was unconscious, O illustrious one, with cool water mixed with sandalwood.
And by command of the son of Varuṇa, other [maidens] fanned / Rāma, the best of the upholders of dharma, with beautiful palm-leaf fans, O illustrious one.
When the descendant of Bhṛgu whose mind was distraught regained consciousness in a moment, / the son of Varuṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, comforted him then.
Then, being comforted, the heroic Rāma, the best of the upholders of dharma, / asked the son of Varuṇa about crossing over distresses.
Rāma said: / When living beings are afflicted everywhere by various states of mind, / tell me, O son of Varuṇa, that by which one may cross over distresses.

text_mt:
Puṣkara said: / Those twice-born who abide properly in the prescribed stages of life, / self-restrained, cross over distresses.
Those who do not abandon [dharma] here out of hypocrisy, whose livelihood is concealed, / and who do not grasp sense-objects, cross over distresses.
Those who always lodge guests, who are always free from malice, / and who are constantly devoted to personal study of the Vedas, cross over distresses.
Those who, skilled in dharma, follow the conduct of their mother and father, / and avoid sleeping by day, cross over distresses.
Being devoted to the agnihotra, those who engage with their own wives / in lawful intercourse in every fertile period cross over distresses.
Those who, brave in battles, having abandoned the fear born of death, / desire victory through righteousness, cross over distresses.
Those who do not commit sins in deed, thought, or word, / and have laid down their staff against living beings, cross over distresses.

2.123 / Rāma said: / Tell me further by what action men / quickly cross over difficulties, O best of all upholders of dharma.
Puṣkara said: / Men who perform penances quickly cross over difficulties, / and they obtain all desires cherished in the mind.
Rāma said: / I wish to hear the names and the procedures of the penances; / speak thus to me, O knower of dharma, for you know [them] as they truly are.
Puṣkara said: / These penances are to be performed, O Rāma, by the three castes; / for a śūdra, no eligibility is prescribed in these penances.
At the beginning, tonsure is to be performed in every penance, O Bhārgava, / bathing at the three junctures of the day constantly, and the worship of Keśava,

This is to be done in all penances without distinction; / and the hero's posture is to be observed, whether by desire or not.
A penance accompanied by the hero's posture becomes multiplied in virtue; / without the hero's posture, it is said to be deficient in procedure.
Rāma said: / I wish to hear about the hero's posture from you, O one of good vows, / since a penance accompanied by the hero's posture is multiplied in virtue.
Puṣkara said: / One should remain standing by day and seated at night; / this is declared to be the hero's posture, destroying great sins.
For two months on curd-mixture, a fortnight on milk, / eight nights on curds, and three nights on ghee,
and fasting without food for three nights, one should perform the vātālaka vow, / which pacifies all sins and grants all desires.

One should bathe the fire for one's own sake, O descendant of Bhṛgu; / one should then offer into the fire and give food to someone.
While it is being prepared with the mantra 'brahmā devāḥ,' a wise man / should tie darbha grasses for protection; so is our traditional learning.
Over that which is boiled, being boiled, and placed in the vessel, / a man should consecrate it three times with this mantra, O Rāma:
"You are barley, you are the king of grains, sacred to Varuṇa, mixed with honey; / the dispeller of all sins, remembered by the sages as a purifier.
Ghee is barley, honey is barley, water indeed is nectar, barley; / purify all my sin, whatever misdeed has been done by me:
done by speech, done by action, a bad dream, an evil thought; / and destroy misfortune; purify all, O grains of barley!
What has been licked by a dog or a boar, and what is brought as leftovers, / non-attendance upon mother and teacher—purify all, O grains of barley!

Food of a multitude, food of a courtesan, food of a śūdra, and of merchants, / food of a thief, a new funeral feast—purify all, O grains of barley!
Behavior [improper for] a child, adharma, and what is done [improperly] in the duties of a king, / theft of gold, non-vow observance, sacrificing for one unfit to sacrifice,
slander of brahmins—purify all, O grains of barley!" / This is the mantra over what has been placed in the vessel, and then he should proclaim:
("Those gods born of the mind, yoked by the mind, of great skill, whose fathers are skilled—may they protect us, may they help us; to them, svāhā!") / With this, O knower of dharma, one should always offer into oneself with restraint; / one should not overindulge; for this is the barley-gruel vow.
For three nights for one desiring intelligence; six nights for a great sinner; / seven nights is prescribed for one guilty of a secondary sin, O tamer of enemies;
and for one guilty of a great sin, twice six nights is handed down; / by twenty-one nights, he attains desired wishes;
by a month, he obtains liberation from all sins without doubt. / By performing this very [vow] with barley grains retrieved from cow dung,

He should eat balls [of food] mixed with sandalwood, increasing by one each day; / in the dark [fortnight], he should decrease [them] by one in succession, beginning from the first day.
On the disappearance of the moon, O fortunate one, he should eat nothing of sacrificial food; / this is declared by the great-souled ones as the barley-middle cāndrāyaṇa.
This very [vow] reversed is proclaimed as the thunderbolt-middle; / with eight morsels every day, it is handed down as the ascetic's cāndrāyaṇa.
With four in the morning and [four] in the evening, it is handed down as the child's cāndrāyaṇa; / in whatever manner, two hundred and forty balls [in all].
If one consumes this over a month, it is known as the suracāndrāyaṇa.

meaning:
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रं पयसा दिवसानेकविंशतीन् ..
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् .. 37 ..
text_mt:
The kṛcchrātikṛcchra is performed with milk for twenty-one days.
Cow's urine, cow dung, milk, curd, ghee, water with kuśa grass,

sanskrit_iast:
ekarātropavāsaśca kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ smṛtam ..
etacca pratyahābhyastaṃ mahāsāntapanaṃ smṛtam .. 38 ..
meaning:
एकरात्रोपवासश्च कृच्छ्रं सान्तपनं स्मृतम् ..
एतच्च प्रत्यहाभ्यस्तं महासान्तपनं स्मृतम् .. 38 ..
text_mt:
and fasting for a single night: this is known as the sāntapana kṛcchra.
And when this is practiced every day [in succession], it is known as the mahāsāntapana.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛcchraṃ parākasaṃjñaṃ syāddvādaśāhamabhojanam ..
ekabhuktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca .. 39 ..
meaning:
कृच्छ्रं पराकसंज्ञं स्याद्द्वादशाहमभोजनम् ..
एकभुक्तेन नक्तेन तथैवायाचितेन च .. 39 ..
text_mt:
Fasting for twelve days is the penance named parāka.
By eating once [a day], by [eating only] at night, and likewise by [eating only food] unasked-for,

sanskrit_iast:
upavāsena caikena kṛcchrapādaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
etadeva trirabhyastaṃ śiśukṛcchraṃ prakīrtitam .. 2.123.40 ..
meaning:
उपवासेन चैकेन कृच्छ्रपादः प्रकीर्तितः ..
एतदेव त्रिरभ्यस्तं शिशुकृच्छ्रं प्रकीर्तितम् .. 2.123.40 ..
text_mt:
and with a single fast, a kṛcchrapāda is proclaimed.
This very [practice] repeated three times is proclaimed as the śiśukṛcchra.

sanskrit_iast:
tryahaṃ sāyaṃ tryahaṃ prātastryahamadyādayācitam ..
tryahaṃ paraṃ ca nāśnīyātprājāpatyaṃ carandvijaḥ .. 41 ..
meaning:
त्र्यहं सायं त्र्यहं प्रातस्त्र्यहमद्यादयाचितम् ..
त्र्यहं परं च नाश्नीयात्प्राजापत्यं चरन्द्विजः .. 41 ..
text_mt:
For three days in the evening, for three days in the morning, for three days one may eat unasked-for [food],
and for three days beyond that one must not eat: [thus] a twice-born performs the prājāpatya.

sanskrit_iast:
piṇyākācāmatakrāmbusaktūnāṃ prativāsaram ..
ekaikamupavāsaṃ ca saumyakṛcchaṃ prakīrtitam .. 42 ..
meaning:
पिण्याकाचामतक्राम्बुसक्तूनां प्रतिवासरम् ..
एकैकमुपवासं च सौम्यकृच्छं प्रकीर्तितम् .. 42 ..
text_mt:
On each day, respectively: oil-cake, gruel, buttermilk-water, roasted barley meal,
and a single fast: this is proclaimed as the saumyakṛcchra.

sanskrit_iast:
ambusiddhaistathā māsaḥ kevalairvāruṇaṃ samaiḥ ..
phalairmāsena kathitaṃ phalakṛcchraṃ manīṣibhiḥ .. 43 ..
meaning:
अम्बुसिद्धैस्तथा मासः केवलैर्वारुणं समैः ..
फलैर्मासेन कथितं फलकृच्छ्रं मनीषिभिः .. 43 ..
text_mt:
Likewise, a month with [food] cooked in water, alone, in equal portions, is the vāruṇa [penance].
A month with fruits is declared by the wise as the phalakṛcchra.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīkṛcchraṃ śrīphalaiḥ proktaṃ padmākṣairaparaṃ tathā ..
māsamāmalakaireva śrīkṛcchramaparaṃ smṛtam 44 ..
meaning:
श्रीकृच्छ्रं श्रीफलैः प्रोक्तं पद्माक्षैरपरं तथा ..
मासमामलकैरेव श्रीकृच्छ्रमपरं स्मृतम् 44 ..
text_mt:
The śrīkṛcchra is proclaimed [to be performed] with bilva fruits; another [is performed] with lotus seeds;
and another śrīkṛcchra is remembered [to be performed] for a month with only myrobalan fruits.

sanskrit_iast:
patrairmataṃ patrakṛcchraṃ puṣpaistatkṛcchramucyate ..
mūlakṛcchraṃ tathā mūlaistoyakṛcchraṃ jalena tu .. 45 ..
meaning:
पत्रैर्मतं पत्रकृच्छ्रं पुष्पैस्तत्कृच्छ्रमुच्यते ..
मूलकृच्छ्रं तथा मूलैस्तोयकृच्छ्रं जलेन तु .. 45 ..
text_mt:
With leaves, it is considered the patrakṛcchra; with flowers, that penance is called [puṣpakṛcchra];
likewise, the mūlakṛcchra with roots, and the toyakṛcchra with water.

sanskrit_iast:
dadhnā kṣīreṇa takreṇa piṇyākena kaṇaistathā ..
śākairmāsaṃ tu kāryāṇi sunāmāni vicakṣaṇaiḥ .. 46 ..
meaning:
दध्ना क्षीरेण तक्रेण पिण्याकेन कणैस्तथा ..
शाकैर्मासं तु कार्याणि सुनामानि विचक्षणैः .. 46 ..
text_mt:
With curd, with milk, with buttermilk, with oil-cake, and with grain-tips,
and with vegetables, for a month: auspiciously named [penances] should be performed by the discerning.

sanskrit_iast:
sāyaṃ prātastu bhuñjāno naro yo nāntarā pibet ..
ṣaḍabhirvarṣairidaṃ proktaṃ kṛcchraṃ nityopavāsitā .. 47 ..
meaning:
सायं प्रातस्तु भुञ्जानो नरो यो नान्तरा पिबेत् ..
षडभिर्वर्षैरिदं प्रोक्तं कृच्छ्रं नित्योपवासिता .. 47 ..
text_mt:
A man who, eating in the evening and the morning, does not drink in between:
this is declared to be the penance of perpetual fasting for six years.

sanskrit_iast:
ekabhaktena māsena kathitaṃ caikabhaktakam ..
na tu kṛcchraṃ tu naktena mahatsaṃvatsarādbhavet .. 48 ..
meaning:
एकभक्तेन मासेन कथितं चैकभक्तकम् ..
न तु कृच्छ्रं तु नक्तेन महत्संवत्सराद्भवेत् .. 48 ..
text_mt:
With a single meal [daily] for a month, it is declared as the aikabhaktika.
A great penance does not result from [eating only] at night except after a year.

sanskrit_iast:
naktāśinastu dharmajña ekabhuktasya vā punaḥ ..
tryahaṃ vopavasedyuktaḥ snāyīta savanatrayam..49..
meaning:
नक्ताशिनस्तु धर्मज्ञ एकभुक्तस्य वा पुनः ..
त्र्यहं वोपवसेद्युक्तः स्नायीत सवनत्रयम्..49..
text_mt:
For one who eats at night, O knower of dharma, or again for one who eats once [a day],
or one who, disciplined, fasts for three days and bathes at the three ritual junctions,

sanskrit_iast:
nimnavatsu tathaivāpsu triḥ paṭhedaghamarṣaṇam .. .
devatābhāvavṛttastu cchandaścaivāpyanuṣṭubham .. 2.123.50 ..
meaning:
निम्नवत्सु तथैवाप्सु त्रिः पठेदघमर्षणम् .. .
देवताभाववृत्तस्तु च्छन्दश्चैवाप्यनुष्टुभम् .. 2.123.50 ..
text_mt:
one should recite the Aghamarṣaṇa [hymn] three times in flowing waters.
Adopting the state of the deity, with the anuṣṭubh meter,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃsmarettasya ca tathā ṛṣiṃ caivāghamarṣaṇam ..
caturthe'hani dātavyā brāhmaṇāya tapasvine .. 51 ..
meaning:
संस्मरेत्तस्य च तथा ऋषिं चैवाघमर्षणम् ..
चतुर्थेऽहनि दातव्या ब्राह्मणाय तपस्विने .. 51 ..
text_mt:
and one should also remember its seer, Aghamarṣaṇa.
On the fourth day, [a cow] should be given to an ascetic brahmin.

sanskrit_iast:
tryahaṃ japedyathāśakti śuciścaivāghamarṣaṇam ..
bhāvavṛttastathā devastathā ca puruṣaḥ paraḥ .. 52 ..
meaning:
त्र्यहं जपेद्यथाशक्ति शुचिश्चैवाघमर्षणम् ..
भाववृत्तस्तथा देवस्तथा च पुरुषः परः .. 52 ..
text_mt:
Purified, one should recite the Aghamarṣaṇa according to one's ability for three days.
Likewise, the deity is the Creator, and likewise the supreme Cosmic Person.

sanskrit_iast:
taddaivatyaṃ vijānīyātsūktaṃ tadaghamarṣaṇam ..
yathāśvamedhaḥ kraturāṭ sarvapāpāpanodanaḥ .. 53 ..
meaning:
तद्दैवत्यं विजानीयात्सूक्तं तदघमर्षणम् ..
यथाश्वमेधः क्रतुराट् सर्वपापापनोदनः .. 53 ..
text_mt:
One should know that Aghamarṣaṇa hymn to have that deity.
Just as the horse-sacrifice is the king of sacrifices, dispelling all sins,

sanskrit_iast:
tathāghamarṣaṇaṃ sūktaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
kṛṣṇājinaṃ vā kutapaṃ paridhāyātha valkalam..54..
meaning:
तथाघमर्षणं सूक्तं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ..
कृष्णाजिनं वा कुतपं परिधायाथ वल्कलम्..54..
text_mt:
so the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn destroys all impurities.
Wearing a black antelope skin, or a woolen blanket, or bark garments,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvatsaraṃ vrataṃ kuryātsammitaṃ nāma bhārgava ..
gṛhaṃ na praviśettatra bhavedākāśaśāyakaḥ .. 55 ..
meaning:
संवत्सरं व्रतं कुर्यात्सम्मितं नाम भार्गव ..
गृहं न प्रविशेत्तत्र भवेदाकाशशायकः .. 55 ..
text_mt:
one should observe for a year the vow named sammita, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
There he should not enter a house; he should sleep beneath the open sky.

sanskrit_iast:
aśaktau vā bhavedrāma tathā śailaguhāśayaḥ ..
nityaṃ triṣavaṇasnāyī tathā syāddvijasattama..56..
meaning:
अशक्तौ वा भवेद्राम तथा शैलगुहाशयः ..
नित्यं त्रिषवणस्नायी तथा स्याद्द्विजसत्तम..56..
text_mt:
Or, in case of inability, O Rāma, he may sleep in a mountain cave.
He should constantly bathe at the three ritual junctions, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
bhaikṣyaśākaphalāhāraḥ kāmaṃ syāddvijapuṅgava ..
vīrāsanaṃ tathā kuryātkāṣṭhamaunaṃ tathaiva ca..57..
meaning:
भैक्ष्यशाकफलाहारः कामं स्याद्द्विजपुङ्गव ..
वीरासनं तथा कुर्यात्काष्ठमौनं तथैव च..57..
text_mt:
His food may freely consist of alms, vegetables, and fruits, O bull among the twice-born;
and he should practice the hero's posture, and likewise absolute silence.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmapradaṃ hyetatsarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
vāyavyaṃ kṛcchramuktaṃ tu pāṇipūrānnabhojinaḥ .. 58 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामप्रदं ह्येतत्सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ..
वायव्यं कृच्छ्रमुक्तं तु पाणिपूरान्नभोजिनः .. 58 ..
text_mt:
For this grants all desires and destroys all impurities.
The vāyavya penance is declared for one who eats food filling [only] his palm,

sanskrit_iast:
māsenaikena dharmajña sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
tilairdvādaśarātreṇa kṛcchramāgneyamucyate .. 59 ..
meaning:
मासेनैकेन धर्मज्ञ सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ..
तिलैर्द्वादशरात्रेण कृच्छ्रमाग्नेयमुच्यते .. 59 ..
text_mt:
over one month, O knower of dharma, destroying all impurities.
A penance with sesame seeds for twelve nights is called the āgneya.

sanskrit_iast:
lājāprasṛtimapyekāṃ kanakena samanvitām ..
bhuñjānasya tathā māsaṃ kṛcchraṃ dhanadadaivatam .. 2.123.60 ..
meaning:
लाजाप्रसृतिमप्येकां कनकेन समन्विताम् ..
भुञ्जानस्य तथा मासं कृच्छ्रं धनददैवतम् .. 2.123.60 ..
text_mt:
For one eating just a handful of fried grain mixed with gold
for a month, that is the penance whose deity is the Giver of Wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
gavāṃ nirhāranirmuktairyavaiḥ saktūnsamantrataḥ ..
yāmyaṃ kṛcchraṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ māsena bhṛgunandana .. 61 ..
meaning:
गवां निर्हारनिर्मुक्तैर्यवैः सक्तून्समन्त्रतः ..
याम्यं कृच्छ्रं विनिर्दिष्टं मासेन भृगुनन्दन .. 61 ..
text_mt:
With roasted barley flour [made from] barley passed through the dung of cows, accompanied by mantras,
the yāmya penance is prescribed for a month, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast:
gomūtreṇa caretsnānaṃ vṛttiṃ gomayamācaret ..
gavāṃ madhye sadā tiṣṭhedgopurīṣe ca saṃvaset..62..
meaning:
गोमूत्रेण चरेत्स्नानं वृत्तिं गोमयमाचरेत् ..
गवां मध्ये सदा तिष्ठेद्गोपुरीषे च संवसेत्..62..
text_mt:
One should bathe with cow's urine; one should maintain one's livelihood with cow dung;
one should always stay in the midst of cows and reside among cow dung.

sanskrit_iast:
goṣvatṛptāsu na pibedudakaṃ bhṛgunandana ..
abhuktāsu tu nāśrīyādutthitāsūtthito bhavet..63..
meaning:
गोष्वतृप्तासु न पिबेदुदकं भृगुनन्दन ..
अभुक्तासु तु नाश्रीयादुत्थितासूत्थितो भवेत्..63..
text_mt:
When the cows are not satisfied, he must not drink water, O descendant of Bhṛgu;
when they have not eaten, he must not eat; when they stand up, he should stand up;

sanskrit_iast:
tathā caivopaviṣṭāsu sarvāsūpaviśennaraḥ ..
māsenaikena kathitaṃ gomūtraṃ kalmaṣāpaham .. 64 ..
meaning:
तथा चैवोपविष्टासु सर्वासूपविशेन्नरः ..
मासेनैकेन कथितं गोमूत्रं कल्मषापहम् .. 64 ..
text_mt:
and when all of them sit down, the man should sit down.
Performed for one month, this [penance of] cow's urine is declared to remove impurities.

sanskrit_iast:
ajākṛcchraṃ tathaivaitadajāmadhye tu vartataḥ ..
tṛṇānāṃ bhakṣaṇeneha samatulyaphale ubhe .. 65 ..
meaning:
अजाकृच्छ्रं तथैवैतदजामध्ये तु वर्ततः ..
तृणानां भक्षणेनेह समतुल्यफले उभे .. 65 ..
text_mt:
Likewise, the ajākṛcchra is for one living in the midst of goats;
by eating grass here, both yield an equal fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
dvādaśāhena kathitaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam ..
upoṣitaścaturdaśyāṃ pañcadaśyāmanantaram .. 66 ..
meaning:
द्वादशाहेन कथितं सर्वपातकनाशनम् ..
उपोषितश्चतुर्दश्यां पञ्चदश्यामनन्तरम् .. 66 ..
text_mt:
It is declared to destroy all cardinal sins in twelve days.
Having fasted on the fourteenth day, immediately on the fifteenth

sanskrit_iast:
pañcagavyaṃ samaśnīyāddhaviṣyāśī tvanantaram ..
brahmakūrcamidaṃ kuryāduktapraśamanāya vai .. 67 ..
meaning:
पञ्चगव्यं समश्नीयाद्धविष्याशी त्वनन्तरम् ..
ब्रह्मकूर्चमिदं कुर्यादुक्तप्रशमनाय वै .. 67 ..
text_mt:
one should consume pañcagavya, and thereafter eat sacrificial food.
One should perform this brahmakūrca indeed for the pacification of what has been spoken of.

sanskrit_iast:
pakṣānte tvatha vā kāryaṃ māsamadhye tu vā punaḥ ..
brahmakūrcaṃ naraḥ kuryātpaurṇamāseṣu yaḥ sadā ..68..
meaning:
पक्षान्ते त्वथ वा कार्यं मासमध्ये तु वा पुनः ..
ब्रह्मकूर्चं नरः कुर्यात्पौर्णमासेषु यः सदा ..68..
text_mt:
Or it should be done at the end of a fortnight, or again in the middle of the month.
A man who always performs the brahmakūrca on full moon days,

sanskrit_iast:
tasya pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti durbhuktādi na saṃśayaḥ ..
māsābhyāṃ ca naraḥ kṛtvā brahmakūrcaṃ samāhitaḥ .. 69 ..
meaning:
तस्य पापं क्षयं याति दुर्भुक्तादि न संशयः ..
मासाभ्यां च नरः कृत्वा ब्रह्मकूर्चं समाहितः .. 69 ..
text_mt:
his sin arising from eating forbidden food and the like is destroyed, without doubt.
And having performed the brahmakūrca for two months with a concentrated mind,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpavinirmukto yatheṣṭāṃ gatimāpnuyāt ..
brahmabhūtamamāvasyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tathaiva ca .. 2.123.70 ..
meaning:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो यथेष्टां गतिमाप्नुयात् ..
ब्रह्मभूतममावस्यां पौर्णमास्यां तथैव च .. 2.123.70 ..
text_mt:
a man, completely freed from all sins, attains whatever destination he desires.
On the new moon day and likewise on the full moon day, having become one with Brahman,

sanskrit_iast:
yogabhūtaṃ paricaretkeśavaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..
evametāni kṛcchrāṇi kathitāni mayā tava ..71 ..
meaning:
योगभूतं परिचरेत्केशवं महदाप्नुयात् ..
एवमेतानि कृच्छ्राणि कथितानि मया तव ..71 ..
text_mt:
he should serve Keśava, absorbed in yoga; he shall attain greatness.
In this way, these penances have been told by me to you

sanskrit_iast:
śāsanānīha pāpānāṃ duritānāṃ ca bhārgava ..
saṃvatsarasyaikamapi caretkṛcchraṃ dvijottamaḥ .. 72 ..
meaning:
शासनानीह पापानां दुरितानां च भार्गव ..
संवत्सरस्यैकमपि चरेत्कृच्छ्रं द्विजोत्तमः .. 72 ..
text_mt:
as the punishments for sins and misdeeds here, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
A best of the twice-born should perform even a single penance each year,

sanskrit_iast:
ajñātabhuktaśuddhyarthaṃ jñātasya tu viśeṣataḥ ..
ajñātaṃ yadi vā jñātaṃ kṛcchraṃ pāpaṃ viśodhayet .. 73 ..
meaning:
अज्ञातभुक्तशुद्ध्यर्थं ज्ञातस्य तु विशेषतः ..
अज्ञातं यदि वा ज्ञातं कृच्छ्रं पापं विशोधयेत् .. 73 ..
text_mt:
for the purification of what was eaten unknowingly, and especially of what was known.
Whether unknown or known, a penance purifies the sin.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛcchrasaṃśuddhapāpānāṃ narakaṃ na vidhīyate ..

2.124
Rāma said: / Declare, O best of the gods, the Vedic rites / for which one who performs the kṛcchra penance becomes qualified immediately thereafter.
Puṣkara said: / Hear from me, O sinless one, the abundant desire-prompted rites / according to each Veda, O fortunate descendant of Bhṛgu, as I speak.
While inside water, or during an oblation, one should murmur [it] for the desire of one's heart; / the Gāyatrī fulfills one's desire, especially through breath control.
A recitation of ten thousand repetitions of the Gāyatrī by one eating only at night, O twice-born, / who has bathed outdoors right there, destroys all sins.
And having recited one hundred thousand [repetitions], eating sacrificial food and well-restrained, / having become like the wind, he attains that supreme step of Viṣṇu.
The praṇava is regarded as the signifier of the supreme Brahman, O Rāma, / of the immeasurable, all-pervading, imperishable Cosmic Person.

text_mt:
By its recitation, even those who have committed evil deeds are purified in this world. / Standing in water reaching up to the navel, [having consecrated] water purified by the [praṇava] syllable,
he who drinks [it] over which [the praṇava] has been recited a hundred times is freed from sins. / The syllable 'a', the syllable 'u', and the syllable 'ma', O foremost of the Bhṛgus,
are stated by the wise to be the Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, and Ṛgveda, / and the praṇava is proclaimed to have three measures.
The three measures of the praṇava are the three eternal gods; / these very [measures] are the three worlds, and likewise the three fires.
From offering oblations with the Great Utterances, one is freed from all sins. / The Great Utterances are to be known by the wise as the seven worlds.
The Gāyatrī is supreme in recitation, and likewise the Utterances in oblations; / and inside water, O Rāma, the Aghamarṣaṇa is proclaimed.
'Agnim īḷe purohitam'—this hymn has Agni as its deity; / one who recites it for a year should bear fire upon his head.
He should perform oblations with it at the three junctures of the day; / he should keep a fire unignited [in himself] and subsist on begged food for years.

text_mt:
Beyond this, seven verses are proclaimed as dedicated to Agni; / reciting them constantly with self-control, he attains his desired wishes.
Desiring intelligence, one should constantly recite the verse 'sadasatpadam'; / the [verses] proclaimed as 'ambayo yānti' [and] 'na bandhoḥ' destroy death.
Likewise, one who is imprisoned should recite [the hymns of] the sage Śunaḥśepha; / a sick man, reciting it, is freed from disease and all sins.
If he should desire an enduring wish obtained from Indra, Purandara, / he should praise Indra day after day with sixteen verses.
Reciting this [hymn], 'hiraṇyastūpam', he repels enemies; / and a man reciting 'ye te paktā' becomes secure when suffering from flatulence.
He who praises Īśāna day after day with the six verses to Rudra, / or prepares a sacrificial mush for Rudra, achieves supreme peace.
Reciting 'ud', he should attend upon the rising sun day after day; / he should cast seven handfuls of water, which destroys mental distress.

text_mt:
Then, having worshiped, reciting 'dviṣantam', he should remember his enemy; / within seven nights, without [the enemy] approaching, he brings about hostility [for him].
A diseased person desiring health should recite the best [verse] of 'praskannasya'; / and for the destruction of enmity he should recite the highest [verse] of it.
At sunrise, [he recites it for] inexhaustible lifespan; at midday, he should recite it for splendor; / and as the sun sets, 'dviṣantam' is prescribed.
Reciting the hymns beginning with 'navapadā', he restrains his enemies; / he should point out the eleven [verses] of Suvarṇa for all desires.
Reciting this [verse], 'kaḥ', with spiritual [intent], he would attain liberation; / with this [verse], 'āsano rudram', he would attain a long life.
And looking at the new moon with the hymn 'tvaṃ soma', / he should attend upon it with kindling wood in hand; he attains garments, without doubt.
Desiring life, when he practices this Kautsa hymn, 'idam'; / having praised the sun at midday with 'apa naḥ śośucad',
just as the reed [stalk is drawn] from the muñja grass, so he casts off sin; / he should recite this [verse], 'jātavedase', as an auspicious rite on a journey.

text_mt:
He is freed from all fears and reaches home safely; / and at the dawn of the night, this destroys bad dreams.
He should recite the solar [hymn] 'pramanditā' for release from the womb; / having bathed, reciting 'indram', [or] the seven verses to the Viśvedevas,
and offering clarified butter [into the fire], a man is freed from all sin; / reciting 'imām' constantly, he attains his desired wishes.
Having fasted for three nights, pure, with the two [verses beginning with] 'mā nas toke', / he should offer [sticks of] udumbara wood prepared with curd, honey, and clarified butter.
Having severed all the nooses of death, he lives free from disease; / with uplifted arms, having praised the weapon with this very [hymn],
and when the tying of the topknot is done with the verse 'mā nas toke', a man / becomes invisible to all beings, without doubt.
With 'citram', a man with kindling wood in hand should regularly attend upon the sun / at the three junctures of the day; he would attain wealth and lifespan.

text_mt:
And reciting 'etad duḥsvapnasya' in the morning day after day, / he burns away all bad dreams and obtains wholesome food.
And the [hymn] 'ubhe suṣumnā' is proclaimed as a protection; / having completed the five great sacrifices, offered oblation into the fire, and performed daily rites,
reciting this [verse] to the goddess, 'devāsau', he obtains his desires; / seeing an assailant approaching, such as a tiger, a man,
reciting 'na mā giran', is freed from them; / and reciting 'kayā śubhā', he attains preeminence among his kin.
With "[May I enjoy] this Soma now" [RV 6.47.1], he obtains all desires. / He should constantly worship cooked food that is served with "May they protect [our] father" [RV 6.52.15].
No illness arising from food will befall him, and even poison will turn into [harmless] food. / With the hymn "O Agni, lead [us]" [RV 1.189.1], he should offer clarified butter with each verse.
Even after doing a censured, prohibited deed, he will obtain cooked food. / Whoever constantly recites [the hymn] together with its stanza obtains a heroic lineage.
With the hymn "Which? By what means?" he ward off all obstacles. / With the hymn "He who as soon as born" [RV 2.12.1], he attains unsurpassed happiness.

The verse "They who fled" is to be known as pacifying bad dreams; / and that [verse] "I myself [rule] alone" [RV 10.159.1] brings prosperity.
Having fasted on one fourteenth lunar day of the dark fortnight, he should offer clarified butter; / by means of the hymn to Rudra that has been taken, he is released from each disease.
Having bathed and fasting, unwearied, he should recite the three cool [verses] in water; / or having performed a censured deed out of delusion through these two [forms] of meat,
when set out on a road, whoever sees an omen that has arisen, / whether inauspicious or auspicious, he should recite this [verse]: "Crying out repeatedly" [RV 2.42.1].
This [verse], which confounds thieves, is to be recited without touching [anything]. / Whoever would cross a river should recite in the midst of the waters the verse beginning with "Oṃṣu".
One mounted on a chariot while crossing should recite this [verse], "With high waves..."; / and set out on a journey, he should remember [them] with these mantras.
For abundant nourishment, [he should recite] "A generous giver" [RV 1.8.3], a man established in all the Vedas; / one who has no acquisition of learning, even when well-applied, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

reciting "He [drinks] clarified butter" for a month, he acquires it. / Seeing the axle of a carriage breaking on a difficult road, O twice-born,
he should recite the verse "May you help us...", maintaining axle-strength. / Fasted for three nights, pure, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,
in a place sloping toward the south, stationed in a cremation ground, concentrated in mind, / wearing a red turban, with a sword in hand, subsisting on air for the Taulāki [rites],
for seven days he should offer mustard oil mixed with salt / and fuel sticks of the rājavṛkṣa tree, reciting the [verses] hateful to Vasiṣṭha.
Having made [an effigy] of the one whom he hates, brought with a peg at night, / and stepping on it, the twice-born should perform [the rite] with three verses.
This oblation is directed [against him], O Rāma; he does not live for seven nights. / Reciting the twenty-second spiritual hymn, which is unsurpassed,
on the auspicious days, constantly restrained, he attains desired wishes. / To Bṛhaspati, and the goat-steeded [Pūṣan], and to [Indra] with the stars, and to the Brown One,
praising them with the five-verse hymn, he attains five desires. / Reciting the hymn "Make [power]" [RV 4.4.1], offering clarified butter, concentrated in mind,

he takes away the lives of enemies and also destroys demons. / Whoever approaches the fire, having circumambulated it day after day,
him the fire itself protects on all sides, facing all directions. / And with the hymn "Who today..." [RV 1.84.1], he obtains excellent garments.

one undertaking agriculture should offer a domestic cooked oblation according to rule / in the middle of the field with the five [verses beginning with] "May the plows...".
To Indra, and to the Maruts, and to Parjanya, and to Bhaga, / according to the characteristic mark [in the mantras], the cultivator should guide the plow.
To Pūṣan, to Grain, to Sītā, and then next to Śunāsīra; / and he should worship these deities with perfumes, garlands, and offerings.
At sowing, at weeding, and at offerings to the threshing-floor and the furrow, / his work becomes unfailing, and agriculture ever flourishes.
To the Lord of the Field—the sun-seer gains that field and earth. / In molehills he should worship the mouse's two feet with this [mantra].
