With the hymn "Wide-stepping..." [RV 5.38.1], he undoubtedly obtains wealth. / Desiring offspring, he should constantly recite [the verses] together with "From Varuṇa, the god...".
In the morning he should recite the Svastyātreya [hymn]; he should always recite an auspicious benediction. / Having proclaimed "A safe path...", he travels safely on the road.
Desiring to abandon [evils] at the edge of the forest, there will be harassment of his enemies. / For a woman whose embryo is confused, it is the best deliverance of the fetus.
With the hymn "From the covering...", one desiring rain should employ [the rite]; / without food, with wet clothes, it rains before long.

sanskrit_iast:
śriyaḥ pañcadaśarcaṃ tu japañjuhuyād ghṛtena vā..
upaitu māṃ devasakha iti sarvauṣadhījalaiḥ ..75..
sadā snātaḥ śriyaṃ dīptāṃ kule prāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
manasaḥ kāma ityetāṃ paśukāmo naro japet ..76 ..
kardameneti ca snāyātprajākāmaḥ śuci vrataḥ..
aśvapūrvāmiti snāyādrājyakāmastu mānavaḥ..77..
rohite carmaṇi snāyādbrāhmaṇastu yathāvidhi ..
rājā carmaṇi vaiyāghre chāge vaiśyastathaiva ca ..78..
daśasāhasriko homaḥ pratyekaṃ parikīrtitaḥ ..
apsu vā juhuyādrāma padmānyayutaśo'gniṣu..79 ..
meaning:
श्रियः पञ्चदशर्चं तु जपञ्जुहुयाद् घृतेन वा..
उपैतु मां देवसख इति सर्वौषधीजलैः ..75..
सदा स्नातः श्रियं दीप्तां कुले प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् ..
मनसः काम इत्येतां पशुकामो नरो जपेत् ..76 ..
कर्दमेनेति च स्नायात्प्रजाकामः शुचि व्रतः..
अश्वपूर्वामिति स्नायाद्राज्यकामस्तु मानवः..77..
रोहिते चर्मणि स्नायाद्ब्राह्मणस्तु यथाविधि ..
राजा चर्मणि वैयाघ्रे छागे वैश्यस्तथैव च ..78..
दशसाहस्रिको होमः प्रत्येकं परिकीर्तितः ..
अप्सु वा जुहुयाद्राम पद्मान्ययुतशोऽग्निषु..79 ..
text_mt:
Reciting the fifteen-verse hymn of Śrī, he should also offer with clarified butter; / with "May the friend of the gods approach me..." [RV Khila 4.8.7] [and] with waters of all herbs,
constantly bathed, he undoubtedly obtains radiant prosperity in his family. / A man desiring cattle should recite this [verse], "The desire of the mind..." [RV Khila 4.8.10].
With "By Kardama..." [RV Khila 4.8.11], desiring offspring, pure, observing vows, he should bathe. / A man desiring kingship should bathe with "Preceded by horses..." [RV Khila 4.8.3].
A brahmin should bathe according to rule on a red hide; / a king on a tiger's skin, and likewise a vaiśya on a goat's [skin].
An oblation of ten thousand [offerings] is proclaimed for each. / Or he should offer lotuses into waters, O Rāma, by the tens of thousands into fires.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭāna ityṛcā vahniṃ stuvañśatrūnvināśayet..
ācāra iti sūktena goṣṭhe gāṃ lokamātaram..2.124.80 ..
meaning:
इष्टान इत्यृचा वह्निं स्तुवञ्शत्रून्विनाशयेत्..
आचार इति सूक्तेन गोष्ठे गां लोकमातरम्..2.124.80 ..
text_mt: Praising the fire with the verse "[O Agni, burn] the desired [places of the enemies]...", he destroys enemies. / With the hymn "Conduct...", in a cow-pen, to the cow, mother of the world,

sanskrit_iast:
upatiṣṭhedvrajeccaiva ya icchedgāḥ sadākṣayāḥ..
vāksiddhiṃ tu stuvañśakraṃ mahaddhanamavāpnuyāt .. 81 ..
meaning:
उपतिष्ठेद्व्रजेच्चैव य इच्छेद्गाः सदाक्षयाः..
वाक्सिद्धिं तु स्तुवञ्शक्रं महद्धनमवाप्नुयात् .. 81 ..
text_mt: he should approach and go, he who desires ever-inexhaustible cows. / Praising Śakra with [prayers for] accomplishment of speech, he obtains great wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
upaiteti mṛtī rājño dundubhīnabhimantrayet ..
tejo balaṃ ca prāpnoti śatrūṃścaiva niyacchati .. 82 ..
meaning:
उपैतेति मृती राज्ञो दुन्दुभीनभिमन्त्रयेत् ..
तेजो बलं च प्राप्नोति शत्रूंश्चैव नियच्छति .. 82 ..
text_mt: With "Approach...", he should consecrate the war drums of the king; / he obtains splendor and strength, and subdues his enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
tṛṇapāṇirjapetsūktaṃ rakṣoghnaṃ dasyubhirvṛtaḥ ..
ye ke ca metyṛcaṃ japtvā dīrghamāyuravāpnuyāt ..83..
meaning:
तृणपाणिर्जपेत्सूक्तं रक्षोघ्नं दस्युभिर्वृतः ..
ये के च मेत्यृचं जप्त्वा दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ..83..
text_mt: With grass in hand, surrounded by bandits, he should recite the demon-slaying hymn. / Having recited the verse "Whoever [has transgressed against] me...", he attains long life.

sanskrit_iast:
yasya naṣṭaṃ bhaveddravya sampūjya sa japenniśi ..
saumāraudraṃ japansūktaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..84..
meaning:
यस्य नष्टं भवेद्द्रव्य सम्पूज्य स जपेन्निशि ..
सौमारौद्रं जपन्सूक्तं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ..84..
text_mt: One whose property is lost should, after worshiping, recite at night. / Reciting the hymn to Soma and Rudra, he is released from all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
jīmūtasūktena tathā senāṅgānabhimantrayet ..
yathāliṅgaṃ tato rājā vinihanti raṇe ripūn .. 85 ..
meaning:
जीमूतसूक्तेन तथा सेनाङ्गानभिमन्त्रयेत् ..
यथालिङ्गं ततो राजा विनिहन्ति रणे रिपून् .. 85 ..
text_mt: Likewise, he should consecrate the divisions of the army with the Jīmūta hymn; / then, in accordance with the signs, the king slays his enemies in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
agniṃ nareti sūktena stuvannagniṃ sukhī bhavet ..
prāṇapeti tribhiḥ sūktairdhanamāpnoti cākṣayam .. 86 ..
meaning:
अग्निं नरेति सूक्तेन स्तुवन्नग्निं सुखी भवेत् ..
प्राणपेति त्रिभिः सूक्तैर्धनमाप्नोति चाक्षयम् .. 86 ..
text_mt: Praising Agni with the hymn beginning with 'agniṃ naraḥ', one becomes happy. / And with the three hymns beginning with 'prāṇāpa', one attains imperishable wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
abhītayaḥ pragāthena stutvā śakraṃ dhanī bhavet ..
śaṃvatīḥ śanna indrāgnī japedvyādhivināśanam .. 87 ..
meaning:
अभीतयः प्रगाथेन स्तुत्वा शक्रं धनी भवेत् ..
शंवतीः शन्न इन्द्राग्नी जपेद्व्याधिविनाशनम् .. 87 ..
text_mt: Having praised Śakra with the pragātha beginning with 'abhītayaḥ', one becomes wealthy. / One should mutter the śaṃvatī verses and 'śanna indrāgnī', which destroy disease.

sanskrit_iast:
samudrajyeṣṭheti japetsūktametajjayāvaham .
vāstoṣpate pratītyetatsūktaṃ vātoṣpaterjapet .. 88 ..
meaning:
समुद्रज्येष्ठेति जपेत्सूक्तमेतज्जयावहम् .
वास्तोष्पते प्रतीत्येतत्सूक्तं वातोष्पतेर्जपेत् .. 88 ..
text_mt: One should mutter this hymn beginning with 'samudrajyeṣṭhā', which brings victory. / One should mutter the hymn to Vāstoṣpati beginning with 'vāstoṣpate prati'.

sanskrit_iast:
anīvaheti sūktena bhūtānniḥsvāpayenniśi ..
sambādhe viṣame durge bandhe vā nigaḍaiḥ kvacit .. 89 ..
meaning:
अनीवहेति सूक्तेन भूतान्निःस्वापयेन्निशि ..
सम्बाधे विषमे दुर्गे बन्धे वा निगडैः क्वचित् .. 89 ..
text_mt: With the hymn beginning with 'anīvahan', one should put the spirits to sleep at night, / when trapped in a tight pass, in rough terrain, in a stronghold, or bound in chains somewhere.

sanskrit_iast:
palāyitvā gṛhīto vā sūktametattathā japet ..
trirātraṃ niyatopoṣya śrapayetpāyasaṃ carum .. 2.124.90 ..
meaning:
पलायित्वा गृहीतो वा सूक्तमेतत्तथा जपेत् ..
त्रिरात्रं नियतोपोष्य श्रपयेत्पायसं चरुम् .. 2.124.90 ..
text_mt: Or having fled and been captured, one should likewise mutter this hymn. / Having fasted with restraint for three nights, one should cook a caru of milk-rice.

sanskrit_iast:
tenāyutaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ juhuyāttryambaketyṛcā ..
samuddiśya mahādevaṃ jīvedabdaśataṃ sukhī .. 91..
meaning:
तेनायुतशतं पूर्णं जुहुयात्त्र्यम्बकेत्यृचा ..
समुद्दिश्य महादेवं जीवेदब्दशतं सुखी .. 91..
text_mt: With that, with the verse beginning with 'tryambakam', one should offer a full one hundred myriads [of oblations] / dedicated to Mahādeva, and live happily for a hundred years.

sanskrit_iast:
taccakṣurityṛcā snāta upatiṣṭheddivākaram ..
udyantaṃ madhyamaṃ caiva dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ .. 92 ..
meaning:
तच्चक्षुरित्यृचा स्नात उपतिष्ठेद्दिवाकरम् ..
उद्यन्तं मध्यमं चैव दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः .. 92 ..
text_mt: Having bathed, desiring to live a long life, one should worship the sun / with the verse beginning with 'taccakṣuḥ' as it rises and at midday.

sanskrit_iast:
vyuṣā ityupatiṣṭheta yaḥ prātaḥ prayataḥ śuciḥ ..
prāpnuyātsahiraṇyādi nānārūpadharaṃ bahu .. 93 ..
meaning:
व्युषा इत्युपतिष्ठेत यः प्रातः प्रयतः शुचिः ..
प्राप्नुयात्सहिरण्यादि नानारूपधरं बहु .. 93 ..
text_mt: Whoever, restrained and pure, worships [the sun] at dawn with [the verse beginning with] 'vyuṣāḥ', / will obtain abundant [wealth] taking various forms, such as gold.

sanskrit_iast:
dhruvaṃ sandhyāsu kṣitiṣu japanbaddhaḥ pramucyate ..
idamāpaḥ pravahata yatkiṃcidduritaṃ punaḥ .. 94 ..
meaning:
ध्रुवं सन्ध्यासु क्षितिषु जपन्बद्धः प्रमुच्यते ..
इदमापः प्रवहत यत्किंचिद्दुरितं पुनः .. 94 ..
text_mt: Muttening 'dhruvam' at the twilights while upon the earth, one who is bound is set free. / [With the verse beginning with] 'idamāpaḥ pravahata yat kiṃcid duritam', moreover,

sanskrit_iast:
apaḥ praviśya tu japansarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..
sūktābhyāṃ para etābhyāṃ hutābhyāṃ bhūtimāpnuyāt .. 95 ..
meaning:
अपः प्रविश्य तु जपन्सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ..
सूक्ताभ्यां पर एताभ्यां हुताभ्यां भूतिमाप्नुयात् .. 95 ..
text_mt: entering the waters and muttering, one is freed from all sins. / Beyond these, by offering oblations with these two hymns, one attains prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
sūktābhyāṃ tisra etābhyāmāsyadalpodakasthitaḥ ..
upatiṣṭhanraviṃ devaṃ pañcarātre gate naraḥ .. 96 ..
meaning:
सूक्ताभ्यां तिस्र एताभ्यामास्यदल्पोदकस्थितः ..
उपतिष्ठन्रविं देवं पञ्चरात्रे गते नरः .. 96 ..
text_mt: Standing in water up to the mouth or shallow water, a man worshipping the divine sun / with these two hymns or these three [verses], after five nights have elapsed,

sanskrit_iast:
anaśnanbhārgavaśreṣṭha mahaddharṣamavāpnuyāt ..
indrāsometi sūktaṃ tu kathitaṃ śatrunāśanam .. 97 ..
meaning:
अनश्नन्भार्गवश्रेष्ठ महद्धर्षमवाप्नुयात् ..
इन्द्रासोमेति सूक्तं तु कथितं शत्रुनाशनम् .. 97 ..
text_mt: eating no food, O best of the Bhṛgus, attains great joy. / The hymn beginning with 'indrāsomā' is declared to destroy enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
yasya lupyedvrataṃ mohādvātyairvā saṃsṛjetsaha ..
upoṣyājyasya juhuyāttvamagne vratapā iti.. 98 ..
meaning:
यस्य लुप्येद्व्रतं मोहाद्वात्यैर्वा संसृजेत्सह ..
उपोष्याज्यस्य जुहुयात्त्वमग्ने व्रतपा इति.. 98 ..
text_mt: One whose vow has failed through delusion or who has associated with outcastes / should fast and offer clarified butter with [the verse beginning with] 'tvamagne vratapāḥ'.

sanskrit_iast:
ādityadṛkpramādraujaṃ japtvā vādī jayī bhavet ..
samagniragnibhiśceti prapadyedvāyubhāskarau .. 99 ..
meaning:
आदित्यदृक्प्रमाद्रौजं जप्त्वा वादी जयी भवेत् ..
समग्निरग्निभिश्चेति प्रपद्येद्वायुभास्करौ .. 99 ..
text_mt: A litigant, having muttered the [hymn] seen by the Ādityas, 'pramādraujam', becomes victorious. / With 'samagniragnibhiḥ', one should take refuge in Vāyu and the Sun.

sanskrit_iast:
agniṃ prathamataḥ stutvā mahatkaṣṭātpramucyate ..
na hīti ca catuṣkeṇa mucyate mahato bhayāt .. 2.124.100 ..
meaning:
अग्निं प्रथमतः स्तुत्वा महत्कष्टात्प्रमुच्यते ..
न हीति च चतुष्केण मुच्यते महतो भयात् .. 2.124.100 ..
text_mt: Having first praised Agni, one is freed from great distress. / And with the four verses beginning with 'na hi', one is freed from great danger.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛcaṃ japtvā ya ityetatsarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..
prāgbhojanamidaṃ brahma mānavānāṃ maharṣiṇām .. 101 ..
meaning:
ऋचं जप्त्वा य इत्येतत्सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ..
प्राग्भोजनमिदं ब्रह्म मानवानां महर्षिणाम् .. 101 ..
text_mt: Having muttered the verse beginning with 'yaḥ', one attains all desires. / This is the prayer for the morning meal of men and great sages.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvāhṇe japato nityaṃ tvarthasiddhiḥ parā bhavet ..
agninetyāśvinaṃ sūktaṃ mṛjākaramudāhṛtam .. 102 ..
meaning:
पूर्वाह्णे जपतो नित्यं त्वर्थसिद्धिः परा भवेत् ..
अग्निनेत्याश्विनं सूक्तं मृजाकरमुदाहृतम् .. 102 ..
text_mt: For one who mutters it daily in the morning, the highest attainment of one's purpose takes place. / The hymn to the Aśvins beginning with 'agninā' is declared to effect purification.

sanskrit_iast:
samidheti juhotyagnau prāpnuyātkīrtimuttamām ..
dvicatvāriṃśakaṃ caindraṃ japtvā nāśayate ripūn .. 103 ..
meaning:
समिधेति जुहोत्यग्नौ प्राप्नुयात्कीर्तिमुत्तमाम् ..
द्विचत्वारिंशकं चैन्द्रं जप्त्वा नाशयते रिपून् .. 103 ..
text_mt: One who offers oblations into the fire with 'samidhā' attains supreme renown. / And having muttered the forty-second hymn to Indra, one destroys enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
nāśaṃ mahīti japtvā ca prāpnotyārogyameva ca ..
duḥsvapnaghnāḥ parā japyā naraḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 104 ..
meaning:
नाशं महीति जप्त्वा च प्राप्नोत्यारोग्यमेव च ..
दुःस्वप्नघ्नाः परा जप्या नरः पापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 104 ..
text_mt: And having muttered 'na aśaṃ mahī', one attains health. / The supreme verses that destroy bad dreams are to be muttered; a man is freed from sins.

sanskrit_iast:
śanno bhaveti dvābhyāṃ tu bhuktvānnaṃ prayataḥ śuciḥ ...
hṛdayaṃ pāṇinā spṛṣṭvā vyādhibhirnābhibhūyate .. 105 ..
meaning:
शन्नो भवेति द्वाभ्यां तु भुक्त्वान्नं प्रयतः शुचिः ...
हृदयं पाणिना स्पृष्ट्वा व्याधिभिर्नाभिभूयते .. 105 ..
text_mt: Restrained and pure, having eaten food, touching the heart with the hand / with the two verses beginning with 'śanno bhava', one is not overcome by diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
ahorātroṣitaḥ snātvā śakraṃ sampūjya mānavaḥ ..
ita ityājyamutpūya juhuyādindramacaryet .. 106 ..
meaning:
अहोरात्रोषितः स्नात्वा शक्रं सम्पूज्य मानवः ..
इत इत्याज्यमुत्पूय जुहुयादिन्द्रमचर्येत् .. 106 ..
text_mt: Having fasted for a day and night, bathed, and worshipped Śakra, a man, / having purified clarified butter with 'itaḥ', should offer oblations and worship Indra.

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtaṃ tilaṃ vā dharmajña bhayebhyo vipramucyate ..
tattvāmandamiti snāto hutvā śatrūnpramāpayet ..107..
meaning:
घृतं तिलं वा धर्मज्ञ भयेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते ..
तत्त्वामन्दमिति स्नातो हुत्वा शत्रून्प्रमापयेत् ..107..
text_mt: [Offering] ghee or sesame, O knower of dharma, he is fully freed from fears. / Having bathed and offered oblations with 'tat tvā mandam', one slays one's enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
tānvidyādityadaivatyaṃ japtvā mucyeta bandhanāt ..
yaddyāva iti japtvā ca sarvānkāmānsamaśnute .. 108 ..
meaning:
तान्विद्यादित्यदैवत्यं जप्त्वा मुच्येत बन्धनात् ..
यद्द्याव इति जप्त्वा च सर्वान्कामान्समश्नुते .. 108 ..
text_mt: Having muttered 'tān vidyāt' dedicated to the Ādityas, one is freed from bondage. / And having muttered 'yad dyāvaḥ', one obtains all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ tu pāvamānaṛcaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
vaikhānasaṛcastriṃśatpavitrāḥ paramāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 109 ..
meaning:
पवित्राणां पवित्रं तु पावमानऋचः स्मृताः ..
वैखानसऋचस्त्रिंशत्पवित्राः परमाः स्मृताः .. 109 ..
text_mt: The verses addressed to Pavamāna are regarded as the purifier of purifiers. / The thirty verses seen by Vaikhānasa are regarded as supreme purifiers.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛcāṃ dviṣaṣṭiḥ proktaṃ copavasedṛṣisattamaiḥ ..
sarvakalmaṣanāśāya pāvanāya śivāya ca .. 2.124.110 ..
meaning:
ऋचां द्विषष्टिः प्रोक्तं चोपवसेदृषिसत्तमैः ..
सर्वकल्मषनाशाय पावनाय शिवाय च .. 2.124.110 ..
text_mt: A fast is also prescribed by the best of sages for [muttering] sixty-two verses, / for the destruction of all impurities, for purification, and for auspiciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
svādiṣṭayeti sūktānāṃ saptaṣaṣṭirudāhatāḥ ..
daśottarā ṛcaścaitāḥ pāvamānyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ 111 ..
meaning:
स्वादिष्टयेति सूक्तानां सप्तषष्टिरुदाहताः ..
दशोत्तरा ऋचश्चैताः पावमान्यः शतानि षट् 111 ..
text_mt: Sixty-seven hymns beginning with 'svādiṣṭhayā' are cited. / These verses addressed to Pavamāna are six hundred and ten [in number].

sanskrit_iast:
etajjuhvañjapaṃścaiva ghoraṃ mṛtyubhayaṃ jayet ..
ādhyātmikaṃ pavitraṃ ca sūktaṃ japtvālpataḥ kvacit .. 112 ..
meaning:
एतज्जुह्वञ्जपंश्चैव घोरं मृत्युभयं जयेत् ..
आध्यात्मिकं पवित्रं च सूक्तं जप्त्वाल्पतः क्वचित् .. 112 ..
text_mt: Offering oblations and muttering this, one overcomes terrible fear of death. / Having muttered the spiritual and purifying hymn even briefly somewhere,

sanskrit_iast:
gatimiṣṭāmavāpnoti vindate mahatīṃ śriyam ..
āpohiṣṭheti mahataḥ prayuñjītodakasthitaḥ .. 113 ..
meaning:
गतिमिष्टामवाप्नोति विन्दते महतीं श्रियम् ..
आपोहिष्ठेति महतः प्रयुञ्जीतोदकस्थितः .. 113 ..
text_mt: one attains a desired state and acquires great fortune. / Standing in water, one should employ the great [hymn] beginning with 'āpo hi ṣṭha'.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpavinirmuktastvaśeṣaphalamaśnute ..
upatiṣṭheta rājānaṃ yamasūktena vai dvija .. .. 114 ..
meaning:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तस्त्वशेषफलमश्नुते ..
उपतिष्ठेत राजानं यमसूक्तेन वै द्विज .. .. 114 ..
text_mt: Freed from all sins, one enjoys the entire fruit. / O twice-born, one should worship the King with the hymn to Yama.

sanskrit_iast:
caturdaśyā tu kurvīta sthālīpākaṃ yathāvidhi ..
pareyivāṃsamityetatsūktamatra prayojayet .. 115 ..
meaning:
चतुर्दश्या तु कुर्वीत स्थालीपाकं यथाविधि ..
परेयिवांसमित्येतत्सूक्तमत्र प्रयोजयेत् .. 115 ..
text_mt: On the fourteenth day, one should prepare the vessel-cooked food according to rule. / Here one should employ this hymn beginning with 'pareyivāṃsam'.

sanskrit_iast:
purāyuṣaḥ pramīyeta na sa jātu kathañcana ..
mṛtyumeva prapadyeta paraṃ mṛtyoriva dvija .. 116 ..
meaning:
पुरायुषः प्रमीयेत न स जातु कथञ्चन ..
मृत्युमेव प्रपद्येत परं मृत्योरिव द्विज .. 116 ..
text_mt: He will never, by any means, die before his full lifespan. / O twice-born, he would meet death only at the other end of death, as it were.

sanskrit_iast:
vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu naktabhojī sadā naraḥ ..
purāyuṣaḥ pramīyeta na sa jātu kathañcana .. 117 ..
meaning:
वैशाख्यां पौर्णमास्यां तु नक्तभोजी सदा नरः ..
पुरायुषः प्रमीयेत न स जातु कथञ्चन .. 117 ..
text_mt: A man who continually eats only at night on the full moon day of Vaiśākha / will never, by any means, die before his full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast:
phalāhāro jayenmṛtyuṃ tribhirvarṣaiḥ sadā naraḥ ..
daśākṣaraṃ tu śāntyarthaṃ bhadraṃ na iti saṃsmaran .. 118 ..
meaning:
फलाहारो जयेन्मृत्युं त्रिभिर्वर्षैः सदा नरः ..
दशाक्षरं तु शान्त्यर्थं भद्रं न इति संस्मरन् .. 118 ..
text_mt: A man who continually lives on fruit for three years overcomes death. / Remembering the ten-syllable [mantra] 'bhadraṃ naḥ' for the sake of peace,

sanskrit_iast:
phalāhāro bhavenmāsaṃ māsānmāsaṃ payaḥ pibet ..
vāyubhakṣyo bhavenmāsaṃ japannetatsahasraśaḥ .. 119 ..
meaning:
फलाहारो भवेन्मासं मासान्मासं पयः पिबेत् ..
वायुभक्ष्यो भवेन्मासं जपन्नेतत्सहस्रशः .. 119 ..
text_mt: he should live on fruit for a month; from month to month he should drink milk; / he should feed on air for a month, muttering this [mantra] thousands of times.

sanskrit_iast:
antardhānamavāpnoti siddhānpaśyati cāraṇān ..
pradevateti niyato japeta marudhanvasu .. 2.124.120 ..
meaning:
अन्तर्धानमवाप्नोति सिद्धान्पश्यति चारणान् ..
प्रदेवतेति नियतो जपेत मरुधन्वसु .. 2.124.120 ..
text_mt: He attains invisibility and beholds the siddhas and cāraṇas. / Self-controlled, he should mutter [the hymn beginning with] 'pradevatā' in desert regions.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇāntike bhaye prāpte kṣipramāyustu vindati ..
vaibhītakāṃstu trīnakṣāngandhaiḥ samadhivāsayet .. 121 ..
meaning:
प्राणान्तिके भये प्राप्ते क्षिप्रमायुस्तु विन्दति ..
वैभीतकांस्तु त्रीनक्षान्गन्धैः समधिवासयेत् .. 121 ..
text_mt: When a life-threatening danger has arrived, he quickly finds [full] life. / One should perfume three dice of vibhītaka wood with fragrances,

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpairavakireccaiva sthāpayitvā vihāyasi ..
saṃhṛtya pādau tau tatra tiṣṭheddakṣastutiṃ japet .. 122 ..
meaning:
पुष्पैरवकिरेच्चैव स्थापयित्वा विहायसि ..
संहृत्य पादौ तौ तत्र तिष्ठेद्दक्षस्तुतिं जपेत् .. 122 ..
text_mt: and scatter flowers over them, placing them in the open air. / Drawing up both feet, he should stand there and mutter the praise of Dakṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
prāve māsetyṛcāmekāṃ japecca manasā niśi ..
vyuṣṭāyāmudite sūrye dyūte jayamavāpnuyāt .. 123 ..
meaning:
प्रावे मासेत्यृचामेकां जपेच्च मनसा निशि ..
व्युष्टायामुदिते सूर्ये द्यूते जयमवाप्नुयात् .. 123 ..
text_mt: And he should mentally mutter the single verse beginning with 'prāve māsa' at night. / When dawn has broken and the sun has risen, he will win victory in gambling.

sanskrit_iast:
abradhnamuṣasānaktetyetatsvastyayanaṃ japet ..
namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣuṣeti ca nityaśaḥ .. 124 ..
meaning:
अब्रध्नमुषसानक्तेत्येतत्स्वस्त्ययनं जपेत् ..
नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षुषेति च नित्यशः .. 124 ..
text_mt: One should mutter 'abradhnam' and 'uṣasānaktā' as an auspicious rite, / and constantly [the verse beginning with] 'namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣuṣe'.

sanskrit_iast:
tathājyaṃ juhuyānnityaṃ bhītibhyo vipramucyate ..
devasyarīti nityaṃ tu japeddevaṃ samaśnute .. 125 ..
meaning:
तथाज्यं जुहुयान्नित्यं भीतिभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते ..
देवस्यरीति नित्यं तु जपेद्देवं समश्नुते .. 125 ..
text_mt: One should likewise offer clarified butter daily; one is freed from fears. / One should constantly mutter [the verse beginning with] 'devasya rīti'; one attains the deity.

sanskrit_iast:
mā pragāmīti mūḍhastu panthānaṃ pathi vindati ..
kṣīṇāyuriti manyeta yaṃ kacitsuhṛdaṃ priyam ..126..
meaning:
मा प्रगामीति मूढस्तु पन्थानं पथि विन्दति ..
क्षीणायुरिति मन्येत यं कचित्सुहृदं प्रियम् ..126..
text_mt: A bewildered person finds the way on the path with [the verse beginning with] 'mā pragāma'. / When one considers some dear friend to have his lifespan depleted,

sanskrit_iast:
yatteyamiti tu snātastasya mūrdhānamālabhet ..
sahasrakṛtvā pañcāhaṃ tenāyurvindate punaḥ..127..
meaning:
यत्तेयमिति तु स्नातस्तस्य मूर्धानमालभेत् ..
सहस्रकृत्वा पञ्चाहं तेनायुर्विन्दते पुनः..127..
text_mt: having bathed, one should touch his head with [the verse beginning with] 'yat te iyam', / a thousand times for five days; by that, he regains his life.

sanskrit_iast:
sruksruve daśamenaiva idhmamaudumbaraṃ bhavet ..
idamidhmeti juhuyād ghṛtaṃ prājñaḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 128..
meaning:
स्रुक्स्रुवे दशमेनैव इध्ममौदुम्बरं भवेत् ..
इदमिध्मेति जुहुयाद् घृतं प्राज्ञः सहस्रशः .. 128..
text_mt: The wooden ladle and spoon should be made [as prescribed] by the tenth [rule]; the firewood should be of udumbara. / With 'idam idhmam', the wise man should offer clarified butter thousands of times.

sanskrit_iast:
paśukāmo gavāṃ goṣṭhe annakāmaścatuṣpathe ..
pārāvataḥ svastyayanaṃ snātakasya vidhīyate .. 129 ..
meaning:
पशुकामो गवां गोष्ठे अन्नकामश्चतुष्पथे ..
पारावतः स्वस्त्ययनं स्नातकस्य विधीयते .. 129 ..
text_mt: One desiring cattle [should offer] in a cowpen; one desiring food, at a crossroads. / Pārāvata is prescribed as an auspicious blessing for a snātaka.

sanskrit_iast:
bṛhaspate prathamamiti jñānakāmasya bhārgava ..
vayaḥ suparṇamityetāṃ japanvai vindate śriyam ..2.124.130..
meaning:
बृहस्पते प्रथममिति ज्ञानकामस्य भार्गव ..
वयः सुपर्णमित्येतां जपन्वै विन्दते श्रियम् ..2.124.130..
text_mt: "O Bṛhaspati, first..." is for one who desires knowledge, O Bhārgava. / Reciting "The well-winged bird...", one indeed attains fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
yaste manyo iti sadā mayatnaghnaṃ vidhīyate ..
haviṣmatīyamabhyasya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 131 ..
meaning:
यस्ते मन्यो इति सदा मयत्नघ्नं विधीयते ..
हविष्मतीयमभ्यस्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 131 ..
text_mt: "Your wrath..." is always prescribed for destroying enemies. / Having practiced the Haviṣmatī hymn, one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
yā oṣadhīḥ svastyayanaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam .. .
tasya māyā vinaśyeta kāyāgnirvardhate tathā .. 132 ..
meaning:
या ओषधीः स्वस्त्ययनं सर्वपापविनाशनम् .. .
तस्य माया विनश्येत कायाग्निर्वर्धते तथा .. 132 ..
text_mt: "The herbs..." is an auspicious blessing, destroying all sins. / His illusion would be destroyed, and bodily fire increases as well.

sanskrit_iast:
bṛhaspatiḥ pratītyetad vṛṣṭikāmaḥ prayojayet ..
sarvatra tu parā śaktirjñeyā pratirathā tathā .. .. 133 ..
meaning:
बृहस्पतिः प्रतीत्येतद् वृष्टिकामः प्रयोजयेत् ..
सर्वत्र तु परा शक्तिर्ज्ञेया प्रतिरथा तथा .. .. 133 ..
text_mt: One desiring rain should employ "Bṛhaspati..." / But everywhere the Pratiratha hymn is to be known as supreme power.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtāṃśaṃ kāśyapaṃ nityaṃ prajākāmasya kīrtitam ..
ahaṃ rudrebhirityetadvāggmī bhavati mānavaḥ .. 134 ..
meaning:
भूतांशं काश्यपं नित्यं प्रजाकामस्य कीर्तितम् ..
अहं रुद्रेभिरित्येतद्वाग्ग्मी भवति मानवः .. 134 ..
text_mt: The hymn to Bhūtāṃśa Kāśyapa is declared as constant for one desiring offspring. / Through "I with the Rudras...", a man becomes eloquent.

sanskrit_iast:
na yonau jāyate vidvāṃñjapannatrīti rātriṣu ..
rātrisūktaṃ japanrātrau rātrikṣemī bhavennaraḥ .. 135 ..
meaning:
न योनौ जायते विद्वांञ्जपन्नत्रीति रात्रिषु ..
रात्रिसूक्तं जपन्रात्रौ रात्रिक्षेमी भवेन्नरः .. 135 ..
text_mt: The wise man reciting "Atri..." at night is not reborn in a womb. / Reciting the Rātrisūkta at night, a man becomes secure at night.

sanskrit_iast:
yā kalpayatīti japennityaṃ kṛtvā vināśanam ..
āyuṣyaṃ caiva varcasyaṃ sūktaṃ dākṣāyaṇaṃ mahat .. 136 ..
meaning:
या कल्पयतीति जपेन्नित्यं कृत्वा विनाशनम् ..
आयुष्यं चैव वर्चस्यं सूक्तं दाक्षायणं महत् .. 136 ..
text_mt: Having made it a daily practice, one should recite "She who prepares..." for destruction [of evils]. / The great Dākṣāyaṇa hymn bestows longevity and luster.

sanskrit_iast:
uta devā iti japedāmayaghnaṃ dhṛtavrataḥ ..
agne agnāva ityeddhanakāmaḥ prayojayet .. 137 ..
meaning:
उत देवा इति जपेदामयघ्नं धृतव्रतः ..
अग्ने अग्नाव इत्येद्धनकामः प्रयोजयेत् .. 137 ..
text_mt: One observing vows should recite "Even the gods...", which destroys disease. / One desiring wealth should employ "Agni in Agni..."

sanskrit_iast:
vaibhītake'bdaṃ hutvāgniṃ dviṣaddveṣaṃ tato japet ..
dviṣantu dhanvinaṃ hutvā dviṣato vindate dhanam .. 138 ..
meaning:
वैभीतकेऽब्दं हुत्वाग्निं द्विषद्द्वेषं ततो जपेत् ..
द्विषन्तु धन्विनं हुत्वा द्विषतो विन्दते धनम् .. 138 ..
text_mt: Having offered into fire with bibhītaka wood for a year, one should then recite the Dviṣaddveṣa hymn. / Having offered against the hostile archer, he wins the enemy's wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
ayamagne janiteti japedagniṃ bhaye sati ..
dvimārjanniti pāṭhaṃ tu japannutthāpayeddvijaḥ .. 139 ..
meaning:
अयमग्ने जनितेति जपेदग्निं भये सति ..
द्विमार्जन्निति पाठं तु जपन्नुत्थापयेद्द्विजः .. 139 ..
text_mt: When there is fear, one should recite "This Agni is the producer..." over fire. / A twice-born, reciting the text "Wiping twofold...", should awaken [the fire].

sanskrit_iast:
prātaśca pāṭhayedenaṃ saṃsadi brahmacāriṇām ..
imāmiti ca sūktena śatakṛtvo'bhimantritam .. 2.124.140 ..
meaning:
प्रातश्च पाठयेदेनं संसदि ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ..
इमामिति च सूक्तेन शतकृत्वोऽभिमन्त्रितम् .. 2.124.140 ..
text_mt: And in the morning he should have him recite it in the assembly of students. / And consecrated a hundred times with the hymn "This..."

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtena pītvā taṃ prātaḥ sapatnībhirvimucyate ..
araṇyānītyaraṇyeṣu japettadbhayanāśanam .. 141 ..
meaning:
घृतेन पीत्वा तं प्रातः सपत्नीभिर्विमुच्यते ..
अरण्यानीत्यरण्येषु जपेत्तद्भयनाशनम् .. 141 ..
text_mt: Having drunk it with ghee in the morning, one is freed from co-wives. / One should recite "O Araṇyānī..." in forests; it destroys the fear of them.

sanskrit_iast:
śraddhāsūktaṃ japennityaṃ śraddhākāmavivardhanam ..
brāhmī yadyasya sūkte dve japeta niyataḥ sadā .. 142..
meaning:
श्रद्धासूक्तं जपेन्नित्यं श्रद्धाकामविवर्धनम् ..
ब्राह्मी यद्यस्य सूक्ते द्वे जपेत नियतः सदा .. 142..
text_mt: One should daily recite the Śraddhāsūkta, which increases faith and desire. / If restrained, he should always recite the two hymns to Brāhmī.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṃkhapuṣpīṃ tu payasā brāhmīpuṣpāṇi sarpiṣā ..
śatāvarī tu payasā vacāmadbhirghṛtena vā .. 143 ..
meaning:
शंखपुष्पीं तु पयसा ब्राह्मीपुष्पाणि सर्पिषा ..
शतावरी तु पयसा वचामद्भिर्घृतेन वा .. 143 ..
text_mt: śaṅkhapuṣpī with milk, brāhmī flowers with ghee, / śatāvarī with milk, or vacā with water or ghee:

sanskrit_iast:
sūktābhyāṃ hyanumantrābhyāṃ caikaikaṃ tu tryahaṃ pibet ..
śraddhāṃ medhāṃ smṛtiṃ puṣṭiṃ varṇaṃ lakṣmīṃ ca vindati .. 144 ..
meaning:
सूक्ताभ्यां ह्यनुमन्त्राभ्यां चैकैकं तु त्र्यहं पिबेत् ..
श्रद्धां मेधां स्मृतिं पुष्टिं वर्णं लक्ष्मीं च विन्दति .. 144 ..
text_mt: Consecrated by the two hymns, he should drink each one for three days. / He attains faith, intelligence, memory, strength, complexion, and fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
śāsannarthāñjapannityaṃ saṃgrāme vijigīṣataḥ ..
gṛhītadakṣiṇādarbhāngṛhītvā saṃspṛśejjapet .. 145 ..
meaning:
शासन्नर्थाञ्जपन्नित्यं संग्रामे विजिगीषतः ..
गृहीतदक्षिणादर्भान्गृहीत्वा संस्पृशेज्जपेत् .. 145 ..
text_mt: Reciting daily "Ordering the aims...", of those wishing to conquer in battle, / taking up darbha grass held in the right hand, touching it, one should recite.

sanskrit_iast:
muñcāmi tvā haviṣeti yakṣmāṇamapakarṣati ..
brahmaṇāgniḥ saṃvidānaṃ garbhamṛtyuvināśanam .. 146 ..
meaning:
मुञ्चामि त्वा हविषेति यक्ष्माणमपकर्षति ..
ब्रह्मणाग्निः संविदानं गर्भमृत्युविनाशनम् .. 146 ..
text_mt: "I release you with the oblation..." drives away consumption. / "Agni knowing along with prayer..." destroys the death of the embryo.

sanskrit_iast:
apehīti japetsūktaṃ śucirduḥsvapnanāśanam ..
devāḥ kapota iti tu kapotasyopaveśane .. 147 ..
meaning:
अपेहीति जपेत्सूक्तं शुचिर्दुःस्वप्ननाशनम् ..
देवाः कपोत इति तु कपोतस्योपवेशने .. 147 ..
text_mt: Pure, one should recite the hymn "Depart...", which destroys bad dreams. / And "The gods, the dove..." [is recited] upon the landing of a dove.

sanskrit_iast:
kauśikasya japetsūktaṃ ghṛtena juhuyāttathā ..
sapatnaghnaṃ prayuñjīta ṛṣabhaṃ japahomayoḥ .. 148 ..
meaning:
कौशिकस्य जपेत्सूक्तं घृतेन जुहुयात्तथा ..
सपत्नघ्नं प्रयुञ्जीत ऋषभं जपहोमयोः .. 148 ..
text_mt: One should recite the hymn of Kauśika and offer oblations with ghee. / One should employ the Ṛṣabha hymn, which destroys rivals, in recitation and homa.

sanskrit_iast:
yenedamiti japtvā vai samādhiṃ vindate parām ..
mayobhūrvāta iti tu gavāṃ svastyayanaṃ param .. 149 ..
meaning:
येनेदमिति जप्त्वा वै समाधिं विन्दते पराम् ..
मयोभूर्वात इति तु गवां स्वस्त्ययनं परम् .. 149 ..

2.125
Puṣkara said:
The great utterances, preceded by the syllable Om, are remembered / as destroying all impurities and granting [the fruit of] all rites.
With a thousand oblations of clarified butter, a twice-born should worship the god. / It grants the desire wished by the mind, O Rāma, fulfilling what is sought by the intellect.
Desiring pacification, one should perform it with barley; with sesame seeds for the dispelling of sins; / and with grains and white mustard seeds, it fulfills all desires.
With kindling sticks of udumbara wood it is praised for one desiring cattle; / and ten [oblations] for one desiring food; with milk for one wishing pacification;
and with kindling sticks of apāmārga for one desiring much gold; / one desiring a maiden [should offer] pairs tied together and smeared with ghee
of jasmine flowers; one seeking a beautiful woman should offer sesame and rice. / In a rite of subjugation, [he should offer] śākhoṭa, vāsā, and apāmārga.

text_mt:
Kindling sticks mixed with fat and blood are for the destruction of disease, O Bhārgava. / But when angered, one should offer properly with the desire to kill enemies.
Having made an effigy of a king out of all grains of rice, a twice-born / should offer into the fire by thousands; he would become one under whom the subjects fall.
Flowers are for one desiring garments; dūrvā grass destroys disease. / And for one desiring brahminical luster, the left tip is prescribed.
One desiring [to practice] counter-sorcery should sacrifice with chaff, thorns, and ashes; / and in causing hatred, likewise with the wings of a crow and an owl.
Having offered ghee from a brown cow, O twice-born, during a lunar eclipse, / and fetching those [roots of] vacā saturated with vacā powder,
and eating them consecrated a thousand times with mantras, a man becomes intelligent. / A man desiring a son should chant facing the sun at sunrise.
On the eleventh day, bdellium, iron, or [wood] of bilva or khadira, / [with the mantra,] 'I bind you who hate,' one should bury in the enemy's dwelling.

text_mt:
This rite of eradication of enemies has been told to you. / A king will become firm like Śakra by means of the Mahāvyāhṛtis.
With the mantra 'Sūryas tvā', the supreme Pratyaṅgirā is to be understood. / With this and with firewood of udumbara, one will surely make the god rain.
Having chanted 'Cakṣuṣmān' in water for a day and night, O twice-born, / one who has lost his sight, O knower of dharma, obtains the use of his eyes.
A brahmin having offered the anuvāka beginning with 'Upaprayantam' in the kitchen, / O illustrious one, is constantly provided with food.
And one afflicted with sickness, having offered dūrvā grass with 'Tanūpāgne ’si,' / attains freedom from disease; no doubt should be entertained here.
Taking cow-dung fallen from them right here, O twice-born, / and offering it mixed with clarified butter and honey, he obtains that very milch cow.
Having offered gavedhukā grass with 'Eṣa te rudra bhāgaḥ,' O Rāma, / he likewise obtains wealth through the half-verse; there is no doubt about this.

Having offered with black sesame seeds a thousand times using "yo 'smabhyam arātīyān", / a twice-born is freed from black magic and distortion.
Having offered food with "annenānnapate", he obtains food. / The rite of the Daitya using "suparṇo 'si" should be performed like the vyāhṛtis.
And having muttered "manaḥsvatī", he obtains liberation from bondage. / When the moon is eclipsed, a king should plant vacā in a body of water;
muttering "yā oṣadhayaḥ", he should uproot it again. / Having fasted for three nights, making a brush of it in a copper vessel,
and consecrated with that very [mantra], looking at the moon, he should recite it constantly for a month. / Having drunk it with clarified butter and milk of a tawny cow, he becomes a bearer of the Veda.
When drinking this herbal preparation, O twice-born, he should constantly mutter this very mantra. / The herbs consecrated with this mantra become perfected.
She who is named Drupadā is established in the Yajurveda; / repeating it three times under water, one is freed from all sins.

This mantra "iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvam" promotes nourishment / when offered with clarified butter, curds, milk, or pāyasa.
And having offered leaves and fruits with "śataṃ vaḥ", / he attains long-lasting health and achieves a long life.
One should constantly mutter "oṣadhīḥ pratimodadhvam" like a farmer; / especially at harvest or during sowing, one attains success.
Having brought all medicinal herbs together with all types of rice, / the twice-born, offering in the middle of the field, attains nourishing agriculture.
Offering apāmārga, barley, and grain with "oṣadhīr iti mātaraḥ", / one who desires cattle or horses quickly attains that desire.
And having offered clarified butter with "oṣadhīḥ samajanta", a man / never incurs any fear arising from Yātudhānas in this world.
And with "granthāvatī", a twice-born should offer pāyasa; / he attains pacification everywhere, there is no need to deliberate here.
Having offered with "sīrā yuñjanti", he obtains agriculture. / And with "ucchugmāḥ", one who is bound is set free.

With "yuvā suvāsāḥ", he obtains clothes without a doubt. / Taking the piece of wood upon which water stood, a wise man,
with the mantra "sāyaṃ yakṣmā", should bury it in the enemy's footprint; / [the enemy] becomes afflicted with leprosy. Or again, with a feather of a blue jay or vulture,
having consecrated it a thousand times, then binding an image of the enemy / with it, the enemy attains death without a doubt.
It quickly destroys an enemy and destroys all illness. / With the verse "prapatanti", O twice-born, he should offer herbs.
He partakes of sweet food and becomes a guardian of vessels. / And offered with clarified butter, "mā mā hiṃsīḥ" destroys enemies.
With "kāntāram adhvarasya", one desiring good fortune should offer [oblations] / mixed with honey and rock-salt, for the sake of a woman or a man.

text_mt:
The verse 'mā no mahāntam' brings peace to children; / the anuvāka 'namo hiraṇyabāhave' brings joy. / One should offer black mustard smeared with sesame oil to destroy enemies.
When a hundred thousand lotuses are offered with 'namo vaḥ kirikebhyaḥ', a man / attains royal fortune; there should be no doubt about this. / Likewise, having offered [fruits] of bilva, he obtains abundant gold. / Having performed an oblation of sesame seeds with 'imā rudrāya', a wise man / quickly attains desired wealth, O fortunate one.
By this very mantra, through an oblation of dūrvā grass, a man / is freed from all diseases and wards off all fears.
With kindling-sticks of varāroha, having offered ten thousand [oblations] / with 'yā te rudra śivā tanūḥ', one obtains the desired son, O knower of dharma.
The mantras 'asaṃkhyātāḥ sahasrāṇi' are for sorcery. / 'namo 'stu rudrebhyaḥ' is declared to be the supreme Pratyaṅgirā [mantra].
Wearing a red turban, red garments, red garlands, and red unguent, / with this very [mantra], in a cremation ground, O best of men,

text_mt:
one should offer an iron spike measuring a span a thousand times, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / One raises an arisen Kṛtyā, and should worship her with a red jar
and likewise with a full vessel; she becomes the doer of all deeds. / 'āśuḥ śiśānaḥ' is for the protection of weapons.
In battle, O Rāma, it is taught to destroy all enemies. / With 'imaṃ somam', having gone to a river flowing to the sea,
having bathed in the water and recited it ten thousand times, then having offered a thousand and eight [oblations], / one attains the desired village, O tiger among men.
With 'vājaś ca me', a twice-born should offer a thousand oblations of ghee / with five [verses], O knower of dharma; he is freed from eye disease.
Likewise, having offered [oblations] in the house with 'manobhavasva', the wise man / then quickly removes all architectural defects of the site.
And with this 'agne āyūṃṣi', having offered ghee without sloth / a thousand times, O knower of dharma, one never comes under anyone's subjugation.
With 'apām phenena', by offering parched grain, one attains victory. / One who is deprived of sense organs, reciting 'bhadrāḥ', becomes possessed of all sense organs.

text_mt:
'agniś ca pṛthivī ca' is supreme subjugation. / Reciting the mantra 'adhvani', one becomes victorious in legal affairs.
And one should recite 'brahmarājābhyām' at the commencement of deeds; / in all of them, O knower of all dharma, one attains their success.
With 'nū na pāt [asuro]', under a banyan tree, O best of twice-born, / one should offer a hundred thousand aśoka flowers mixed with ghee.
Then one sees a daughter of the Dānavas right there with one's own eyes. / With the remainder of the anuvāka, one should present food to her.
Then she gives gold; one should remain silent there at will. / Then, taking the man by the hand, she silently follows him;
she leads him into a cave, O Rāma; there should be no doubt about this. / Having approached an abandoned shrine, [offering] boiled rice mixed with māṣa beans,
a man reciting and offering with 'kayā naś citraḥ'— / when a hundred thousand [oblations] are offered, a Vidyādhara
quickly gives him his own heap of gold, O knower of dharma. / With 'saṃvatsaro 'si', a wise man having offered ghee,

text_mt:
a learned man becomes free from disease for as long as he lives by a hundred thousand oblations. / 'ketuṃ kṛṇvan' increases victory in battle.
'aindrāgnaṃ varma' is for binding armor in battle. / And the mantra 'dhanvanāgā' is supreme for taking up the bow.
The mantra 'vakṣyantī' is to be known for consecrating the bowstring. / And the mantra 'ahir iva' is declared to be the mantra for the archer's arm-guard.
Likewise, 'yuñjanti' is called the mantra for yoking the horses. / 'āśuḥ śiśānaḥ' is said to be for touching the limbs [of the chariot].
And the mantra 'viṣṇoḥ krameṇa' is supreme for mounting the chariot. / 'ājaṅghanti' is taught for striking the horses.
Facing the enemy's army, one should recite 'yāḥ senā abhītvarīḥ'. / Or this 'ḍuṇḍubhaḥ' is for striking the kettle-drum.
With these mantras offered beforehand, victory is achieved in this way. / From ten million oblations of this 'yamena dattam', a wise man

quickly produces a chariot that bestows victory in battle. / And the rite of 'ā kṛṣṇena' is like that of the Vyāhṛtis.
'yuvaṃ cyavānam' destroys danger in times of danger / through a thousand oblations of ghee; there should be no doubt about this.
'mitraṃ huve' is commended for one desiring intelligence. / And with 'sa rājā', a man performs the propitiation of deities,
O Bhārgava, everywhere according to desire through homas and recitations. / By recitation of the Śivasaṅkalpa [hymn], one attains concentration of the mind.
Having offered a hundred thousand lotuses steeped in ghee with 'pañca nadyaḥ', / one quickly obtains royal fortune wearing a lotus garland.
'ubhāv api te' is commended for one desiring beauty. / With 'yad ābadhnan dākṣāyaṇāḥ', consecrated by this mantra,
one should wear gold [consecrated] a thousand times; it destroys enemies / and is the supreme defense against all Guhyakas.
And with 'imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ', one should throw clods from a furrow in all four directions / of the house; then there is no fear of thieves at night.

text_mt:
'parīme gām aneṣata' is supreme subjugation. / A man, even if come to plunder, comes under his power.
One gives edible things, betel, flowers, and the like, consecrated [with it]; / whomever one seeks to subject to one's purpose, that person will quickly become subservient.
'śaṃ no mit [raḥ]' brings peace always and everywhere. / 'manasaḥ kāmam ākūtim' is commended for one desiring prosperity.
The Camaka six [sections], O knower of dharma, are taught to fulfill all desires. / And oblation with the six propitiates all gods.
Having touched water with generosity, one is freed from that fault. / And this [homa] performed with clarified butter, uncovered, removes colic.
Having performed a homa at a crossroads with the verse “Gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatim” / using all kinds of grain, one surely brings the whole world under one's control.
And when offering a homa with firewood of Vikāṅkata wood with the verse “Samās tvāgne,” / one attains immense glory; there is no doubt about this.

gāḥ samāpnoti dharmajña nāttra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
uduttamaṃ varuṇa iti juhuyādbhṛgunandana .. 153 ..
meaning:
अग्निर्मूर्धेतिमन्त्रेण हुत्वैवाज्यं हुताशने ..
तत्प्रसादमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा..147..
एवं हि देवतालिङ्गैस्तथा राम यथा स्वकैः ..
हुतैः प्रसादयेदिष्टां देवतां नात्र सशयः .. 148 ..
हिरण्यवर्णाः शुचयो मन्त्रोऽयमभिषेचने ..
शन्न आपश्च धन्वन्याः सर्वपापहराः स्मृताः .. 149 ..
शन्नो देवीरभिष्टये चेति शान्तिकरः परः ..
एकचक्रेति मन्त्रेण हुतेनाज्येन भार्गव .. 2.125.150 ..
ग्रहेभ्यः शीघ्रमाप्नोति प्रसादं नात्र संशयः ..
याज्यानुवाकौ वृक्षाणां समाग्ने वर्च इत्यपि..151..
तत्प्रसादमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
गावो भग इति द्वाभ्यां हुत्वैवाज्यं सहस्रशः .. 152 ..
गाः समाप्नोति धर्मज्ञ नात्त्र कार्या विचारणा ..
उदुत्तमं वरुण इति जुहुयाद्भृगुनन्दन .. 153 ..
text_mt:
Having offered clarified butter into the fire with the mantra “Agnir mūrdhā,” / one obtains his grace; no doubt should be entertained here.
Thus, indeed, through the marks of the deities, O Rāma, according to their respective [mantras], / one should propitiate the chosen deity by means of oblations; there is no doubt about this.
The mantra “Hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ” is traditionally used for consecration, / and “Śan na āpaś ca dhanvanyāḥ” is regarded as removing all sins.
The verse “Śan no devīr abhiṣṭaye” is supremely pacifying. / By offering clarified butter with the mantra “Ekacakra,” O Bhārgava,
one swiftly receives grace from the planets; there is no doubt about this. / With the two offering verses for trees, and likewise “Samāgne varcaḥ,”
one obtains their grace; no doubt should be entertained here. / Having offered clarified butter thousands of times with the two [mantras beginning] “Gāvo bhagaḥ,”
one obtains cows, O knower of dharma; no doubt should be entertained here. / One should offer with “Ud uttamaṃ varuṇa,” O delight of the Bhṛgus,

saṃvadattāṃ hiraṇyakośaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā tathaiva ca .. 154..
pravādasāṃ seti caiva gṛhe yajño vidhīyate ..
devebhyo vanaspata iti brahmayajño vidhīyate..155..
rātrīyakhya iti dvābhyāṃ rātriyajñāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..

udumbaraṃ ca nyagrodhamapāmārgaṃ ca gomayam..
yāṃ kuryāddarbhapiṃjūlāṃ dūrvāṃ prācīnagāminīm ..157..

सीतां लोष्टं सुवर्णं च तथा वल्मीकमृत्तिकाम् ..

text_mt:
at rivers, streams, and ponds, when they are well-constructed, O best of the twice-born. / Likewise, having formed a shape [with the mantra] “Saṃvadattāṃ hiraṇyakośam,”
a sacrifice is prescribed in the house with “Pravādasāṃ sā.” / The sacrifice to Brahman is prescribed with “Devebhyo vanaspate.”
The night-sacrifices are proclaimed with the two [mantras] called Rātrīya. / In a pacification [ritual]: śamī, śamyāka, aśvattha, and plakṣa,
udumbara, nyagrodha, apāmārga, and cow dung. / One should make a tuft of darbha grass and eastward-spreading dūrvā grass,
furrow-earth, a clod, gold, and also ant-hill clay. / With the two verses “Saṃ vaḥ sṛjāmi,” one should cast seeds into the waters.
Then one should recite the anuvāka “Yā oṣadhayaḥ.” / After that, sprinkling is prescribed with “Apām ivedu.”
A twice-born should offer the eight-verse hymn “Inno bhayam,” / and likewise the three verses “Yad devā devaheḍanam.”

gāyatrī vaiṣṇavī jñeyā tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ..
sarvapāpapraśamanī sarvakarmakarī tathā .. 162 ..
etāvaduktaṃ yajuṣāṃ vidhānaṃ mayā hi kiñcittava dharmaniṣṭha ..
ataḥ paraṃ vacmi nṛvīra sāmnāṃ tanme śṛṇuṣvāyatalohitākṣa ..163 ..
meaning:
हुत्वा सम्प्रोक्षणं कुर्याद्भूयः सर्वत्र मानवः ..
सर्वोत्पातप्रशमनं कर्मैतत्परिकीर्तितम् .. 161 ..
गायत्री वैष्णवी ज्ञेया तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ..
सर्वपापप्रशमनी सर्वकर्मकरी तथा .. 162 ..
एतावदुक्तं यजुषां विधानं मया हि किञ्चित्तव धर्मनिष्ठ ..
अतः परं वच्मि नृवीर साम्नां तन्मे शृणुष्वायतलोहिताक्ष ..163 ..
text_mt:
Having offered, a man should once again perform sprinkling everywhere. / This rite is proclaimed to pacify all portents.
The Vaiṣṇavī Gāyatrī is known to be “Tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam”; / it pacifies all sins and accomplishes all rites.
This much of the procedure of Yajur[-veda mantras] has been briefly declared by me to you, O you who are devoted to dharma. / Beyond this, I shall speak of the Sāmans, O hero among men; listen to that from me, O you with wide, reddish eyes.

2.126
puṣkara uvāca ..
saṃhitāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ japtvā viṣṇuṃ prīṇāti mānavaḥ ..

meaning:
2.126
पुष्कर उवाच ..
संहितां वैष्णवीं जप्त्वा विष्णुं प्रीणाति मानवः ..
सर्वकाममवाप्नोति तथा हुत्वा च भार्गव ..1..
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / Having recited the Vaiṣṇavī Saṃhitā, a man pleases Viṣṇu; / and having offered oblations [with it], O Bhārgava, he attains all desires.
title: adhyāyāḥ 126-130

sanskrit_iast:
skandasya saṃhitāṃ japtvā skandātkāmānupāśnute ..
āsyadaghne jale tiṣṭhannaghenākīrṇamānasaḥ ..2 ..

स्कन्दस्य संहितां जप्त्वा स्कन्दात्कामानुपाश्नुते ..
आस्यदघ्ने जले तिष्ठन्नघेनाकीर्णमानसः ..2 ..
text_mt: Having recited the Saṃhitā of Skanda, one attains desires from Skanda. / Standing in neck-deep water, with his mind overwhelmed by sin,

sanskrit_iast:
triḥsaptakṛtvo japtvā ca sarvānkāmānupāśnute .. ..
tathā ca saṃhitāṃ pitryāṃ tatprasādamupāśnute .. 3 ..

तथा च संहितां पित्र्यां तत्प्रसादमुपाश्नुते .. 3 ..
text_mt: and having recited it thrice-seven times, one attains all desires. / And likewise, [having recited] the ancestral Saṃhitā, he obtains their favor.

sanskrit_iast:
gurugobrāhmaṇādīnāmuktvā nāma priyaṃ naraḥ ..
sopavāso japettoye tvidaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame .. 4 ..

गुरुगोब्राह्मणादीनामुक्त्वा नाम प्रियं नरः ..
सोपवासो जपेत्तोये त्विदं विष्णुर्विचक्रमे .. 4 ..
text_mt: Having uttered the dear name of his guru, cows, brahmins, and others, / a man, fasting, should recite in the water: “Idaṃ viṣṇur vicakrame.”

sanskrit_iast:
sadā gāvaśca śucayaḥ prayājyayajane japet ..
amedhyadarśane jāpoḥ panthā ame divaḥ .. 5 ..

सदा गावश्च शुचयः प्रयाज्ययजने जपेत् ..
अमेध्यदर्शने जापोः पन्था अमे दिवः .. 5 ..
text_mt: At an animal sacrifice, one should always recite: “Gāvaś ca śucayaḥ.” / Upon seeing something impure, the recitation is: “Panthā ame divaḥ.”

sanskrit_iast:
etadindrastavāmīti sarvapāpaharaṃ japet ..
śukraṃ te'nyadyajataṃ japtvā steyādvimucyate .. 6 ..
meaning:
एतदिन्द्रस्तवामीति सर्वपापहरं जपेत् ..
शुक्रं तेऽन्यद्यजतं जप्त्वा स्तेयाद्विमुच्यते .. 6 ..
text_mt: One should recite this “Indrastavāmīti,” which removes all sins. / Having recited “Śukraṃ te 'nyad yajatam,” one is freed from [the guilt of] theft.

sanskrit_iast:
cakrāniti tathā japtvā pārayāyī vimucyate ..
sahantaḥ somamityetajjaptvā mucyetpratigrahāt .. 7 ..

सहन्तः सोममित्येतज्जप्त्वा मुच्येत्प्रतिग्रहात् .. 7 ..
text_mt: Having recited “Cakrān,” one is freed from transgressions of order. / Having recited “Sahantaḥ somam,” one is freed from [the fault of] accepting improper gifts.

sanskrit_iast:
yattatsoma indra iti hiṃsādoṣavināśanam ..
agnerbhayātpramucyeta agnistigmeti vai japan .. 8 ..
meaning:
यत्तत्सोम इन्द्र इति हिंसादोषविनाशनम् ..
अग्नेर्भयात्प्रमुच्येत अग्निस्तिग्मेति वै जपन् .. 8 ..

sanskrit_iast:

पर्वासुसोमेति जपेज्जीवितुं तु सुकर्मणा .. 9 ..
text_mt: The verse “Parito ṣiñcatām” should be known as removing all sins. / One should recite “Parvāsu soma” in order to live by good deeds.

sanskrit_iast:
avikreyaṃ ca vikreyaṃ japedghṛtavatītviti ..
apyānī devasavito jñeyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam .. 2.126.10 ..

अविक्रेयं च विक्रेयं जपेद्घृतवतीत्विति ..
अप्यानी देवसवितो ज्ञेयं दुःस्वप्ननाशनम् .. 2.126.10 ..

शुद्धाशुद्धीयमेतच्च तं वचोसूक्तमेव च .. 12 ..

nyagrodhaśṛṅgamādāya śaramūlaṃ tathaiva ca ..

sanskrit_iast:

स्वस्तिमांस्तेन भवति यत्र क्वचन गच्छति ..
पथि देवव्रतं जप्त्वा भयेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते .. 23 ..
text_mt: becomes prosperous wherever he goes. / Having recited the Devavrata on the road, one is freed from fears.

sanskrit_iast:
yadindro anayatveti hutaṃ saubhāgyavardhanam ..
bhadrānno agniriti ca dantakāṣṭhaṃ ca bhakṣayet .. 24 ..
meaning:
यदिन्द्रो अनयत्वेति हुतं सौभाग्यवर्धनम् ..
भद्रान्नो अग्निरिति च दन्तकाष्ठं च भक्षयेत् .. 24 ..
text_mt: An oblation made with "May Indra bring [it] here" increases good fortune. / And one should chew a tooth-stick with "Agni from the auspicious."

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvatsaramaniṣṭhīvanmadhvājyasahitaṃ sadā ..
saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti yatra kvacana gacchati .. 25 ..
meaning:
संवत्सरमनिष्ठीवन्मध्वाज्यसहितं सदा ..
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति यत्र क्वचन गच्छति .. 25 ..
text_mt: Always accompanied by honey and clarified butter, not spitting for a year, / one obtains great good fortune wherever one goes.

sanskrit_iast:
bhago na citra etena netrayorañjanaṃ smṛtam ..
saubhāgyavardhanaṃ rāma nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 26 ..
meaning:
भगो न चित्र एतेन नेत्रयोरञ्जनं स्मृतम् ..
सौभाग्यवर्धनं राम नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 26 ..
text_mt: With "Bhaga not wondrous," collyrium for the eyes is prescribed; / it increases good fortune, O Rāma, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
japannindreti vargaṃ ca tathā saubhāgyamāpnuyāt ..
karipriyo divaḥ kaviḥ kāmyāṃ saṃśrāvayetstriyam .. 27 ..
meaning:
जपन्निन्द्रेति वर्गं च तथा सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् ..
करिप्रियो दिवः कविः काम्यां संश्रावयेत्स्त्रियम् .. 27 ..
text_mt: And repeating the group of verses beginning with "Indra," one obtains good fortune in the same way. / An elephant-loving poet of heaven should cause a desired woman to hear it;

sanskrit_iast:
sā taṃ kāmayate rāma nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
rathantaraṃ vāmadevyaṃ brahmavarcasavardhanam .. 28 ..
meaning:
सा तं कामयते राम नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
रथन्तरं वामदेव्यं ब्रह्मवर्चसवर्धनम् .. 28 ..
text_mt: she will love him, O Rāma, of this there is no doubt. / The Rathantara and Vāmadevya [sāmans] increase spiritual lustre.

sanskrit_iast:
yaśasāmeti juhuyātpuṣpeṇa tu priyaṅgukam ..
yaśasā yogamāpnoti karmaṇānena mānavaḥ .. 29 ..
meaning:
यशसामेति जुहुयात्पुष्पेण तु प्रियङ्गुकम् ..
यशसा योगमाप्नोति कर्मणानेन मानवः .. 29 ..
text_mt: One should offer priyaṅgu with a flower [chanting] "Of fame"; / through this rite a man attains union with fame.

sanskrit_iast:
prāśayedbālakaṃ nityaṃ vacācūrṇaṃ ghṛtāplutam ..
indramidgāthinaṃ japtvā bhavecchrutidharastvasau .. 2.126.30 ..
meaning:
प्राशयेद्बालकं नित्यं वचाचूर्णं घृताप्लुतम् ..
इन्द्रमिद्गाथिनं जप्त्वा भवेच्छ्रुतिधरस्त्वसौ .. 2.126.30 ..
text_mt: One should daily feed a boy powdered calamus immersed in clarified butter / after chanting "Indra indeed, the singer"; he will become one who retains what he hears.

sanskrit_iast:
hutvā rathantaraṃ japtvā putramāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
gīrvāṇaḥ pāhi satataṃ japtaṃ syādaghatārakam .. 31 ..
meaning:
हुत्वा रथन्तरं जप्त्वा पुत्रमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ..
गीर्वाणः पाहि सततं जप्तं स्यादघतारकम् .. 31 ..
text_mt: Having offered oblations while chanting the Rathantara, one undoubtedly obtains a son. / "O deity, protect always" recited delivers from sin.

sanskrit_iast:
mayi śrīriti mantreṇa japtavyaṃ śrīvivardhanam ..
dānāviśati devo'pi mantreṇānena dharmavit .. 32 ..
meaning:
मयि श्रीरिति मन्त्रेण जप्तव्यं श्रीविवर्धनम् ..
दानाविशति देवोऽपि मन्त्रेणानेन धर्मवित् .. 32 ..
text_mt: "In me be glory" is the mantra to be recited for increasing prosperity. / Through this mantra even a god, knower of dharma, enters into gifts.

sanskrit_iast:
krītvā ghṛtaṃ tu puṣpeṇa suṣumāṇītyataḥ pibet ..
alakṣmīnāśanaṃ karma mayaitatte prakīrtitam .. 33 ..
meaning:
क्रीत्वा घृतं तु पुष्पेण सुषुमाणीत्यतः पिबेत् ..
अलक्ष्मीनाशनं कर्म मयैतत्ते प्रकीर्तितम् .. 33 ..
text_mt: Having bought clarified butter with a flower, one should then drink it [reciting] "Suṣumāṇi." / This rite destroying misfortune has been proclaimed by me to you.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpeṇa sarṣapāngaurāṃścūrṇayitvā vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
indrehimatsyaṃ dharmeti kuryādutsādanaṃ budhaḥ .. 34 ..
meaning:
पुष्पेण सर्षपान्गौरांश्चूर्णयित्वा विचक्षणः ..
इन्द्रेहिमत्स्यं धर्मेति कुर्यादुत्सादनं बुधः .. 34 ..
text_mt: A wise man, having crushed white mustard seeds with a flower, / should perform anointment, O wise one, with "Indra, come fish, dharma."

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtasnānaṃ budhaḥ kṛtvā sarṣapāñjuhuyāttataḥ ..
adyetvīḍāvindriyeti mantreṇānena mantritam .. 35 ..
meaning:
घृतस्नानं बुधः कृत्वा सर्षपाञ्जुहुयात्ततः ..
अद्येत्वीडाविन्द्रियेति मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रितम् .. 35 ..
text_mt: The wise man, having bathed in clarified butter, should then offer mustard seeds / consecrated with this mantra: "Today let Iḍā, through the sense-power."

sanskrit_iast:
puṣṭidaṃ karma kathitaṃ mayaitattava bhārgava ..
miśrānvrīhi yavānagnau hutvā bhṛgukulodbhava .. 36 ..
meaning:
पुष्टिदं कर्म कथितं मयैतत्तव भार्गव ..
मिश्रान्व्रीहि यवानग्नौ हुत्वा भृगुकुलोद्भव .. 36 ..
text_mt: This rite bestowing nourishment has been declared by me to you, O Bhārgava. / Having offered mixed rice and barley into the fire, O scion of the Bhṛgu race,

sanskrit_iast:
munīśo dhāma etena dhānyabhāgī bhavetsadā ..
madhvājyadadhimiśrāṇi viprāṇīti juhoti yaḥ .. 37 ..
meaning:
मुनीशो धाम एतेन धान्यभागी भवेत्सदा ..
मध्वाज्यदधिमिश्राणि विप्राणीति जुहोति यः .. 37 ..
text_mt: with "The lord of sages, the abode," he will always be a possessor of grain. / He who offers [substances] mixed with honey, clarified butter, and curd [reciting] "The sages,"

sanskrit_iast:
sāṣṭaṃ sahasraṃ dharmajña śrāvayantīha mānavāḥ ..
māsopavāsī labhate kanakaṃ bahu bhārgava .. 38 ..
meaning:
साष्टं सहस्रं धर्मज्ञ श्रावयन्तीह मानवाः ..
मासोपवासी लभते कनकं बहु भार्गव .. 38 ..
text_mt: a thousand and eight times, O knower of dharma—men proclaim this here— / fasting for a month, obtains much gold, O Bhārgava.

sanskrit_iast:
gavyeṣuṇeti ca dvābhyāṃ yastu saṃvatsaraṃ naraḥ ..
nyagrodhajapaniṣṭhīvaṃ bhakṣayeddantadhāvanam .. 39 ..
meaning:
गव्येषुणेति च द्वाभ्यां यस्तु संवत्सरं नरः ..
न्यग्रोधजपनिष्ठीवं भक्षयेद्दन्तधावनम् .. 39 ..
text_mt: The man who, for a year, with the two [mantras] beginning with "With the bovine wish," / chews a banyan tooth-stick, reciting it without spitting,

sanskrit_iast:
sahasrasaṅkhyaṃ sa dhanaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
bhadro na agna ityetattathā hutvā sahasraśaḥ .. 2.126.40 ..
meaning:
सहस्रसङ्ख्यं स धनं लभते नात्र संशयः ..
भद्रो न अग्न इत्येतत्तथा हुत्वा सहस्रशः .. 2.126.40 ..
text_mt: obtains wealth numbered in the thousands, there is no doubt here. / Likewise, having offered [oblations] by the thousands with "Auspicious to us, O Agni,"

sanskrit_iast:
audumbaredhmahomena mantreṇānena gāṃ labhet ..
hutvā vrīhiyavānagnau dhānyamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 41 ..
meaning:
औदुम्बरेध्महोमेन मन्त्रेणानेन गां लभेत् ..
हुत्वा व्रीहियवानग्नौ धान्यमाप्नोति मानवः .. 41 ..
text_mt: through an oblation with kindling of udumbara wood, with this mantra he obtains a cow. / Having offered rice and barley into the fire, a man obtains grain.

sanskrit_iast:
evāsi vīreyuriti dvādaśāhamupoṣitaḥ ..
sarpiṣā tvayutaṃ hutvā grāmamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 42 ..
meaning:
एवासि वीरेयुरिति द्वादशाहमुपोषितः ..
सर्पिषा त्वयुतं हुत्वा ग्राममाप्नोति मानवः .. 42 ..
text_mt: Having fasted for twelve days [chanting] "Thus you are heroically," / and having offered ten thousand [oblations] of clarified butter, a man obtains a village.

sanskrit_iast:
vairūpāṣṭakavannityaṃ prayuñjānaḥ śriyaṃ labhet ..
śrāntāṣṭakaṃ prayuñjānaḥ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 43 ..
meaning:
वैरूपाष्टकवन्नित्यं प्रयुञ्जानः श्रियं लभेत् ..
श्रान्ताष्टकं प्रयुञ्जानः सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् .. 43 ..
text_mt: Constantly employing [the mantra] like the Vairūpa octet, one obtains prosperity. / Employing the Śrānta octet, one attains all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
gavyeṣuṇeti yo nityaṃ sāyaṃ prātaratandritaḥ ..
upasthānaṃ gavāṃ kuryāttasya syustāḥ sadā gṛhe .. 44 ..
meaning:
गव्येषुणेति यो नित्यं सायं प्रातरतन्द्रितः ..
उपस्थानं गवां कुर्यात्तस्य स्युस्ताः सदा गृहे .. 44 ..
text_mt: He who constantly, evening and morning, unwearied, attends upon cows / with "With the bovine wish," they will always remain in his house.

sanskrit_iast:
agne vivasvaduṣasā mantreṇānena mantravit ..
bhājanasyopanītasya yastvagraṃ juhuyātsadā .. 45 ..
meaning:
अग्ने विवस्वदुषसा मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रवित् ..
भाजनस्योपनीतस्य यस्त्वग्रं जुहुयात्सदा .. 45 ..
text_mt: With this mantra, "O Agni, radiant with the dawn," the knower of mantras / who always offers the top portion of the vessel brought forward,

sanskrit_iast:
uttareṇa baliṃ dattvā sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..
kṣīraikavṛkṣamāsādya maṇibhadrāya mānavaḥ .. 46 ..
meaning:
उत्तरेण बलिं दत्त्वा सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ..
क्षीरैकवृक्षमासाद्य मणिभद्राय मानवः .. 46 ..
text_mt: and gives an offering with the subsequent [verse], attains all desires. / A man, having approached a solitary milk-tree, for Maṇibhadra,

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭarātroṣitaḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā dadyāttato balim ..
susaṃskṛtena māṃsena kṛṣṇapakṣaṃ kṣapedbudhaḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
अष्टरात्रोषितः पूजां कृत्वा दद्यात्ततो बलिम् ..
सुसंस्कृतेन मांसेन कृष्णपक्षं क्षपेद्बुधः .. 47 ..
text_mt: having fasted for eight nights, having performed worship, should then offer an oblation. / With well-prepared meat, the wise man should pass the dark fortnight.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣasyateti madhumannindra etena bhārgava ..
suvarṇamāpnoti naro yāvadicchati śatruhan .. 48 ..
meaning:
एषस्यतेति मधुमन्निन्द्र एतेन भार्गव ..
सुवर्णमाप्नोति नरो यावदिच्छति शत्रुहन् .. 48 ..
text_mt: With "He speeds," [and] "O sweet Indra," with this, O Bhārgava, / a man obtains gold as much as he desires, O slayer of foes.

sanskrit_iast:
śuklapakṣacaturdaśyāṃ trirātropoṣito naraḥ ..
maunaṃ māsaṃ pāyasaṃ ca rasatraya samanvitam .. 49 ..
meaning:
शुक्लपक्षचतुर्दश्यां त्रिरात्रोपोषितो नरः ..
मौनं मासं पायसं च रसत्रय समन्वितम् .. 49 ..
text_mt: On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, a man who has fasted for three nights, / in silence, for a month, [offers] milk-rice endowed with the three essences;

sanskrit_iast:
saptadhenavo duduhurmantreṇānena mantravit ..
kṛṣṇapakṣacaturdaśyāṃ trirātropoṣitastathā .. 2.126.50 ..
meaning:
सप्तधेनवो दुदुहुर्मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रवित् ..
कृष्णपक्षचतुर्दश्यां त्रिरात्रोपोषितस्तथा .. 2.126.50 ..
text_mt: the knower of mantras, with the mantra "Seven milk-cows milked," / and likewise having fasted for three nights on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,

sanskrit_iast:
matsyānupaharedrātrāvāsurīmāpnuyācchriyam ..
balayuktaśca bhavati dīptatejāstathaiva ca .. 21 ..
meaning:
मत्स्यानुपहरेद्रात्रावासुरीमाप्नुयाच्छ्रियम् ..
बलयुक्तश्च भवति दीप्ततेजास्तथैव च .. 21 ..
text_mt: should offer fishes at night; he obtains demonic prosperity, / and he becomes endowed with strength and likewise with radiant splendor.

sanskrit_iast:
dhānāvantaṃ karambhiṇaṃ mantreṇānena pāyasam ..
hutvā digaṣṭake dadyāddikpālānāṃ tato balim .. 52 ..
meaning:
धानावन्तं करम्भिणं मन्त्रेणानेन पायसम् ..
हुत्वा दिगष्टके दद्याद्दिक्पालानां ततो बलिम् .. 52 ..
text_mt: Having offered milk-rice with this mantra, "Possessing grain, possessing porridge," / he should then present an oblation to the guardians of the directions in the eight directions.

sanskrit_iast:
vāstudoṣaharaṃ karma mayaitatparikīrtitam ..
rājā samācaretsnānaṃ puṣyeṇa śravaṇena ca .. 53 ..
meaning:
वास्तुदोषहरं कर्म मयैतत्परिकीर्तितम् ..
राजा समाचरेत्स्नानं पुष्येण श्रवणेन च .. 53 ..
text_mt: This rite removing defects of the dwelling has been proclaimed by me. / A king should perform a bath under Puṣya and under Śravaṇa;

sanskrit_iast:
āprātṛvya iti sadā rahasyaṃ snānamācaret ..
svecchāpatitajīvantīgavāṃ śṛṅgasamudbhavaiḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
आप्रातृव्य इति सदा रहस्यं स्नानमाचरेत् ..
स्वेच्छापतितजीवन्तीगवां शृङ्गसमुद्भवैः .. 54 ..
text_mt: with "O rival," he should constantly perform a secret bath / with the horn-receptacles of living cows that have fallen naturally,

sanskrit_iast:
kāśairmadhvājyasampūrṇairdadhikṣīrayutaistathā ..
niḥsapatnamavāpnoti rājyaṃ nirgatakaṇṭakam .. 55 ..
meaning:
काशैर्मध्वाज्यसम्पूर्णैर्दधिक्षीरयुतैस्तथा ..
निःसपत्नमवाप्नोति राज्यं निर्गतकण्टकम् .. 55 ..
text_mt: which are filled with honey and clarified butter and endowed with curd and milk; / he attains a kingdom without rivals and free from thorns.

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtāktaṃ tu yavadroṇaṃ vāta āvatabheṣajam ..
anena hutvā vidhivatsarvāndoṣānvyapohati ..56..
meaning:
घृताक्तं तु यवद्रोणं वात आवतभेषजम् ..
अनेन हुत्वा विधिवत्सर्वान्दोषान्व्यपोहति ..56..
text_mt: A droṇa of barley anointed with clarified butter, with "O wind, blow medicine"— / having offered this according to rule, he dispels all defects.

sanskrit_iast:
prādevo dāsa etena kṛṣṇānhutvā tathā tilān ..
kṛtvā karmāṇi tīrthodaiḥ stainyātkṣipraṃ vimucyate ..57 ..
meaning:
प्रादेवो दास एतेन कृष्णान्हुत्वा तथा तिलान् ..
कृत्वा कर्माणि तीर्थोदैः स्तैन्यात्क्षिप्रं विमुच्यते ..57 ..
text_mt: With this [mantra], "The god is a servant," having offered black sesame seeds / and performed rites with waters of sacred fords, he is quickly released from theft.

sanskrit_iast:
abhi tvā pūrvapītaṃ ye vaṣaṭkārasamanvitam ..
bādhakedhmasahasraṃ tu hutaṃ yuddhe jayapradam .. 58 ..
meaning:
अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतं ये वषट्कारसमन्वितम् ..
बाधकेध्मसहस्रं तु हुतं युद्धे जयप्रदम् .. 58 ..
text_mt: With "Unto you, drunk of old," accompanied by the exclamation vaṣaṭ, / a thousand kindling sticks of bādhaka offered grant victory in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
hastyaśvapuruṣānkuryādbudhaḥ piṣṭamayāñchubhān ..
parakīyānathoddiśya pradhānapuruṣām̐stathā .. 59..
meaning:
हस्त्यश्वपुरुषान्कुर्याद्बुधः पिष्टमयाञ्छुभान् ..
परकीयानथोद्दिश्य प्रधानपुरुषाम्̐स्तथा .. 59..
text_mt: The wise man should make auspicious figures of elephants, horses, and men out of flour, / and then designating the enemy's leading men,

sanskrit_iast:
svastyannāpiṣṭapacane kṣureṇotkṛtya bhāgaśaḥ ..
abhitvā śūra no numo mantreṇānena mantravit .. 2.126.60 ..
meaning:
स्वस्त्यन्नापिष्टपचने क्षुरेणोत्कृत्य भागशः ..
अभित्वा शूर नो नुमो मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रवित् .. 2.126.60 ..
text_mt: cutting them up piece by piece with a blade on the flour-baking pan of the meal of blessing, / the knower of mantras, with this mantra, "Unto you, O hero, we praise,"

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā sarṣapatailāktānkrodhena juhuyāttataḥ ..
etatkṛtvā budhaḥ karma saṃgrāme jayamāpnuyāt .. 61 ..
meaning:
कृत्वा सर्षपतैलाक्तान्क्रोधेन जुहुयात्ततः ..
एतत्कृत्वा बुधः कर्म संग्रामे जयमाप्नुयात् .. 61 ..
text_mt: having smeared them with mustard oil, should then offer them with wrath. / Having performed this rite, the wise man attains victory in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
āṣāḍhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu sopavāso vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
sāyaṃ dhānyāni vastrāṇi sasyāni tolayeda budhaḥ ..62 ..
meaning:

text_mt:
The ritual rule of the sāmans, an effective worker of acts, has been told to you in brief by me, O hero among men; / learn that of the Atharvan which I speak, having concentrated your mind, O person of noble soul.
Puṣkara said: / Having offered the Śāntātīta hymn-group, a person obtains peace; / and having offered the Bhaiṣajya hymn-group, he dispels all diseases.
Having offered the Triṣaṣtīya hymn-group, he is released from all sins; / and having offered the Abhaya hymn-group, he encounters no fear anywhere.
No defeat occurs anywhere, O Rāma, after offering the [Aparājita] hymn-group; / and having offered the Āyuṣya hymn-group, he dispels untimely deaths.
These should be offered tenfold in regular order, / O knower of dharma, descendant of Bhṛgu, in the eighteen peace rites and the ten peace rites:
Vaiṣṇavī and Aindrī, Brāhmī and Raudrī, / Vāyavyā, Vāruṇī, Kauberī, and Bhārgavī,
Prājāpatyā, Tvāṣṭrī, Kaumārī, Vahnidevatā, / Mārudgaṇī, Gāndhārī, Rudatī peace rite,

text_mt:
the peace rite Āṅgirasī, Yāmyā, and Pārthivī, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / these peace rites are declared to be always beneficial for all actions.
This mantra 'yastvā mṛtyuḥ…', recited, destroys death; / and having offered with the names of the Mothers, one obtains desires in this manner.
Having offered with 'suparṇaḥ…', he is not troubled by serpents; / and one desiring land should always recite 'yasyedaṃ bhūmiḥ…'.
Offered with 'pṛthivyām uttamo 'si', it always bestows supremacy; / likewise, with 'audumbaraṃ yo naḥ', it increases vigor.
The mantra 'indreṇa dattam…' destroys all afflictions; / and bathing with 'hiraṇyavarṇāḥ…' removes sin.
All the verses beginning with 'asitasya…' destroy poison, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / a wise man should employ the mantras beginning with 'sārasvatī…' as poison-destroying.
All those beginning with 'śarabha…' destroy piśācas; / this mantra 'yamasya lokāt…' is supreme for pacifying bad dreams.
'agner vaḥ' is also taught as destroying anger; / one should know that performing [rites with] 'ūrdhvo bhavati' is supreme, securing high station.

text_mt:
The mantra 'indraṃ vayaṃ vaṇijam…' brings supreme gain of merchandise; / offering with 'kāmo me rājñī…' increases the good fortune of women.
One should recite this 'bhadrāya karṇam…' for an ear discharge; / also 'bhadrāsākṣivadhe jātā…' for an ear discharge.
Offered with 'tubhyamevājir…', it bestows long life; / this offered with 'āyātu pītam…' brings the gaining of friends.
One should offer 'āśāsānam idaṃ janāḥ' into the fire with mixed grains; / thereby one attains sovereignty everywhere, O best of men.
This mantra 'agnirīśebhiḥ…' is supreme for increasing cattle; / one should offer it for twelve days, especially with the parāka penance.
This mantra 'śāto haviḥ…' brings well-being to a village; / having made a likeness of the altar with earth from that village, one obtains it.
All those beginning with 'vidhāya sva…' are for winning a kingdom; / this mantra 'tribhyo bhadrebhyaḥ…' is proclaimed as relating to Vāstoṣpati.
Offered with 'dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa…', it brings the gain of a position; / likewise 'acyutāpaḥ…', O Rāma, is declared to grant the gain of a position.

Likewise 'imaṃ tapasvin…' increases good fortune; / this mantra 'yatpṛthivyāmanāvṛttam…', offered according to rule,
having performed, should be known as pacification; no doubt should be entertained here. / […]

text_mt:
This mantra 'śivaṃ śivābhiḥ…' brings supreme welfare; / this 'dūtyā dūṣaṇam…' is called the destroyer of black magic.
The mantra 'bṛhaspatiḥ paripātu…' provides an auspicious journey on the road; / 'mano vivat…' giving no fear provides an auspicious journey on the road.
The mantra 'ayaṃ no agniradhyakṣaḥ…' succeeds through the favour of Agni; / he who carries fire upon his head for a year,
should constantly recite this mantra, facing towards the south-eastern direction; / he can ignite fire without fuel, O Rāma, when a year has passed.
One should recite this unsurpassed mantra: 'dūtyā dūtirasī…'; / he should tie an amulet, which destroys all defects.
The Prāṇasūkta is taught as increasing life-force; / 'muñcāmi tvā' is taught as liberation from untimely death.
A student of the Atharvaśiras is freed from all sins; / for that is supremely purifying and the destroyer of all impurities.
Thus these auspicious mantras have been related to you by me for each Veda, / in summary, O Rāma, by extracting the principal ones.

And the applications of each single mantra in their thousands / have been proclaimed, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, by the ancient high-souled sages.
They cannot be spoken, O fortunate one, even in hundreds of years; / nevertheless, through the pre-eminent mantras, some rituals have been taught to you.
Where no material for fire-oblation was specified by me to you previously, / I shall tell you the oblation materials for that; listen to me speak them.
Sacrificial firewood of sacrificial trees is the primary oblation material, / along with clarified butter, rice grains, and white mustard seeds;
Unbroken rice grains, sesame seeds, curds, and milk, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / darbha grass, dūrvā grass, bilva fruits, and lotuses,
they declare these substances to produce peace and prosperity, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Oil, firewood, O knower of dharma, mustard seeds, blood, and poison
One should employ thorny firewood in malevolent rites. / O foremost of the Bhṛgus, without knowing the seer, deity, and meter,

treating the seer as unauthoritative, incurs demerit. / Therefore, with every effort, one should not transgress one's own manual.

Puṣkara said: / The Śrīsūkta is to be understood for each Veda as increasing fortune, / in this world or in the next, according to the wish of a twice-born.
Rāma said: / Declare the Śrīsūkta that increases prosperity for each Veda, / and also the ritual of the Śrīsūkta, O best of all upholders of dharma!
Puṣkara said: / The fifteen verses beginning with 'hiraṇyavarṇāṃ hariṇīm,' O twice-born, / are proclaimed as the meritorious Śrīsūkta that increases prosperity in the Ṛgveda.
The four verses beginning with 'rathe akṣeṣu vājiṣu' / are proclaimed as the Śrīsūkta that increases prosperity in the Yajurveda.
The hymn beginning with 'śrāyantīyam' is proclaimed in the Sāmaveda, / and that beginning with 'śriyaṃ dātarmayi dehi' is declared in the Atharvaveda.
Misfortune is destroyed for him who recites the Śrīsūkta with devotion, / and who offers oblations, O knower of dharma, especially with sacrificial food.
He who offers ten thousand lotuses smeared with clarified butter / in fire with the Śrīsūkta, a man full of devotion, O foremost of the Bhṛgus—

Lakṣmī, holding lotuses in both hands, waits upon that man. / And he who offers one hundred thousand lotuses in water,
Lakṣmī does not depart from his family, just as she does not leave the chest of Viṣṇu. / Having offered ten thousand bilva fruits smeared with clarified butter, O Rāma,
he obtains abundant wealth, as much as his mind desires. / By offering one hundred thousand bilva fruits, he enjoys Lakṣmī in his family.
One should perform an offering of ten million lotuses or bilva fruits; / full of faith, he certainly attains even the lordship of the gods.
Having duly worshipped the boon-granting goddess with lotuses, white flowers, or other blooms, / with milk, incense, and choice edible offerings, he attains fortune according to rule.
2.129
Rāma said: / Declare a single auspicious mantra that accomplishes all deeds, / both of this world and of the next, O knower of all dharmas!
Puṣkara said: / The hymn remembered as the Pauruṣa for each Veda, O fortunate one, / is to be known as the accomplisher of all deeds, pure, related to the slayer of Madhu.

text_mt:
Having bathed and offered handfuls of water with each verse of the Pauruṣa hymn, O Rāma, / one is freed from all sins. / Having recited the Pauruṣa hymn while submerged in water, / freed from all defilements, one attains whatever destination one desires.
Having bathed, one should offer flowers one by one with each verse / to the Cosmic Person in water, O Rāma; one is freed from all sins.
Having bathed, offering fruits one by one with each verse, O Rāma, / one attains all desires, whatever one wishes in the mind.
Breath control accompanied by the Pauruṣa hymn yields great fruit; / likewise, recitation and oblations, O Rāma, destroy all defilements.
A drinker of liquor, a killer of a brahmin, a thief, and likewise a violator of the guru's bed / are freed from their sins by reciting the Pauruṣa hymn.
Previously purified by penances, having entered the waters at midday, / and having bathed, one should recite the Pauruṣa hymn constantly without slackness.
Within a year, he sees Vāsudeva, the lord of the gods, / in person, O fortunate one, while subsisting on vegetables, roots, and fruits.

From him he obtains whatever desire he wishes in his mind, O Rāma: / foremost fortune, beauty, and long life,
the power of atomicity, lightness, reach, and greatness, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / lordship, subjugation, and irresistible will, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
He obtains from him the capacity to fulfill desires wherever they are, O giver of honor, / or whatever else is difficult to attain that he desires in his mind.
Having recited the Pauruṣa hymn constantly without slackness, free of desire, / he goes, O fortunate one, to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
This is taught to be supreme auspiciousness, pure, destroying the flood of worldly miseries, / bestowing happiness, granting dharma to men, and causing the attainment of all delightful things.

text_mt:
Puṣkara said: / Having dwelled happily in the householder stage of life, the twice-born who has duly concluded his studentship / should dwell in the forest, restrained and with his senses duly subdued.
When a householder sees wrinkles and grey hair on himself, / and sees the child of his child, he should then take refuge in the forest.
Abandoning food from the village and all household goods, / entrusting his wife to his sons, or together with her, he should go to the forest.
Taking the agnihotra fires and the domestic fire and utensils, / departing from the village to the forest, he should live with senses conquered.
With pure grains fit for sages of various kinds, or with greens, roots, and fruits, / he should offer all the great sacrifices according to the rule.
He should wear an animal skin or bark, and bathe in the evening and at dawn; / and he should always keep matted locks, a beard, body hair, and nails.
From whatever he has, he should offer bali and alms to the best of his ability; / he should honour those who come to the hermitage with gifts of alms of roots and fruits.

text_mt:
He should constantly engage in recitation of the Veda, be self-restrained, friendly, composed, / ever a giver, never a receiver, compassionate toward all beings.
And he should offer the agnihotra with the sacrificial fires according to rule, / properly observing the new moon, full moon, and conjunction rites.
He should perform the sacrifice to the lunar mansions, the first-fruits offering, and the four-month sacrifices, / and duly the northern course of the sun and the southern course of the sun.
With pure sage-grains gathered in the spring and autumn, / he should duly offer sacrificial cakes and boiled rice portions separately.
Having offered to the deities that wild, most pure sacrificial oblation, / he should partake of the remainder for himself, as well as salt prepared by himself.
He should eat land-grown and water-grown vegetables, flowers, roots, and fruits / produced from trees, as well as oils extracted from fruits.
He should avoid honey and meat, ground-growing mushrooms, / and bhūstṛṇa grass, horse-radish tree, and bhallātaka fruits.

text_mt:
In the month of Āśvayuja, he should discard previously gathered sage-grains, / worn-out garments, and flowers, roots, and fruits.
He should not eat what is grown by a ploughshare, even if cast away by someone; / nor food, flowers, and fruits produced in a village.
He may eat food cooked by fire, or he may consume only what is ripened by time; / he may grind with a stone, or use his teeth as a mortar.
He may wash his bowl immediately [having no store], or store for a month, / or store for six months, or store for a year.
He may eat food at night, having gathered it by day to the best of his ability; / or he may eat at every fourth mealtime, or at every eighth mealtime.
Or he may conduct himself according to the rules of the cāndrāyaṇa fast in the bright and dark fortnights; / or at the end of each fortnight he may eat boiled barley gruel once.
Or he may always subsist solely on flowers, roots, and fruits / ripened by time and fallen by themselves, steadfast on the path of the Vaikhānasa.
He may roll upon the ground or stand on the tips of his toes for the day; / he should move between standing and sitting, entering the water at the ritual ablutions.
