ग्रीष्मे पञ्चतपास्तु स्याद्वर्षासु भावकाशकः ..
आर्द्रवासास्तु हेमन्ते क्रमशो वर्धयंस्तपः .. 25 ..
उपस्पृशंस्त्रिषवणं पितॄन्देवांश्च तर्पयेत् ..
तपश्चरंश्चोग्रतरं शोषयेद्देहमात्मनः .. 26 ..
अग्नीनात्मनि वैतानान्समारोप्य यथाविधि ..
अनग्निरनिकेतश्च मुनिर्मूलफलाशनः .. 27 ..
अप्रपन्नः सुखार्थेषु ब्रह्मचारी धराश्रयः..
शरणेषु समश्चैव वृक्षमूलनिकेतनः .. 28 ...
तापसेष्वेव विप्रेषु यात्रिकं भैक्षमाहरेत् ..
गृहमेध्येषु चान्येषु द्विजेषु वनवासिषु .. 29 ..
ग्रामादाहृत्य नाश्नीयादष्टौ ग्रासान्वने वसन् ...
विविधाश्चोपनिषदो ह्यात्मसंशुद्धये श्रुतीः .. 2.130.30 ..
ऋषिभिर्ब्राह्मणैश्चैव गृहस्थैरेव सेविताः ..
विद्यातपोभिवृद्ध्यर्थं शरीरस्य च शुद्धये .. 31 ..
अपराजितां वास्थाय व्रजेद्दिशमजिह्मगः ..
आनिपाताच्छरीरस्य युक्तो वार्यनिलाशनम् .. 32 ..
text_mt:
In summer he should be five-fire penance-performing; in the rainy season, exposed to the open sky; / and in the cold season, wearing wet clothes, steadily increasing his austerity.
Performing ablutions at the three daily sandhyās, he should satisfy the ancestors and the gods; / undertaking more severe austerity, he should dry up his body.
Having duly deposited the sacred fires within himself, / without fire and without a dwelling, a silent sage eating roots and fruits,
unattached to objects of pleasure, celibate, taking refuge on the bare earth, / indifferent to shelters, having the root of a tree as his abode,
he should collect alms just for sustenance from ascetic brahmins alone, / or from other twice-born householders residing in the forest.
Living in the forest, he should not eat eight mouthfuls brought from a village; / and [he should study] various Upaniṣads and Vedic texts for the purification of the self,
which were practiced by seers, brahmins, and householders, / for the increase of knowledge and austerity and for the purification of the body.
Or, setting out in the unconquered direction, he should walk straight ahead without swerving, / concentrated, subsisting on water and air until the collapse of the body.

sanskrit_iast:
tyaktvā tanuṃ samyagathoditasya vidherathaikasya vane nivāsī ..
prāpnoti lokaṃ sa pitāmahasya tyaktvā bhayaṃ nātra vicāramasti .. 33 ..
meaning:
त्यक्त्वा तनुं सम्यगथोदितस्य विधेरथैकस्य वने निवासी ..
प्राप्नोति लोकं स पितामहस्य त्यक्त्वा भयं नात्र विचारमस्ति .. 33 ..
text_mt: Having cast off his body by properly following one of the prescribed rules mentioned, a forest-dweller, / casting aside fear, reaches the world of the Grandfather; in this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
2.131
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
vaneṣu ca vihṛtyaivaṃ tṛtīyaṃ bhāgamāyuṣaḥ ..
caturthamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ tyaktasaṅgaḥ parivrajet .. 1 ..
meaning:
2.131
.. पुष्कर उवाच ..
वनेषु च विहृत्यैवं तृतीयं भागमायुषः ..
चतुर्थमायुषो भागं त्यक्तसङ्गः परिव्रजेत् .. 1 ..
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / Having thus spent the third portion of one's lifespan in forests, / one should renounce the world and wander as a mendicant in the fourth portion of one's lifespan, free from attachment.
title: Nānāvidhotpātakathanaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
āśramādāśramaṃ gatvā hutahomo jitendriyaḥ ..
bhikṣābalapariśrāntaḥ pravrajedvratavarjitaḥ .. 2 ..
meaning:
आश्रमादाश्रमं गत्वा हुतहोमो जितेन्द्रियः ..
भिक्षाबलपरिश्रान्तः प्रव्रजेद्व्रतवर्जितः .. 2 ..
text_mt: Having passed from stage of life to stage of life, having offered oblations into the fires, with senses conquered, / worn out by alms and offerings, he should renounce the world, free from ritual observances.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṇāni trīṇyapākṛtya mano mokṣe niveśayet .. ..
anapākṛtya ca ṛṇaṃ mokṣamicchanvrajatyadhaḥ .. 3 ..
meaning:
ऋणानि त्रीण्यपाकृत्य मनो मोक्षे निवेशयेत् .. ..
अनपाकृत्य च ऋणं मोक्षमिच्छन्व्रजत्यधः .. 3 ..
text_mt: Having discharged the three debts, he should set his mind on liberation; / desiring liberation without having discharged the debts, he goes downward.

sanskrit_iast:
adhītya vidhivadvedānputrāṃścotpādya dharmataḥ ..
iṣṭvā ca śaktito yajñairmano mokṣe niveśayet .. 4 ..
meaning:
अधीत्य विधिवद्वेदान्पुत्रांश्चोत्पाद्य धर्मतः ..
इष्ट्वा च शक्तितो यज्ञैर्मनो मोक्षे निवेशयेत् .. 4 ..
text_mt: Having studied the Vedas according to rule, having begotten sons in accordance with dharma, / and having sacrificed with offerings according to his ability, he should set his mind on liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
anadhītya dvijo vedānanutpādya tathā sutān ..
aniṣṭvā caiva yajñaiśca mokṣamicchanvrajatyadhaḥ .. 5 ..
meaning:
अनधीत्य द्विजो वेदाननुत्पाद्य तथा सुतान् ..
अनिष्ट्वा चैव यज्ञैश्च मोक्षमिच्छन्व्रजत्यधः .. 5 ..
text_mt: A twice-born man who has not studied the Vedas, has not begotten sons, / and has not offered sacrifices, desiring liberation, goes downward.

sanskrit_iast:
prājāpatyāṃ nirūpyeṣṭiṃ sarvavedasa-dakṣiṇām ..
ātmanyagnīnsamāropya pravrajatyabhayaṃ gṛhī .. 6 ..
meaning:
प्राजापत्यां निरूप्येष्टिं सर्ववेदस-दक्षिणाम् ..
आत्मन्यग्नीन्समारोप्य प्रव्रजत्यभयं गृही .. 6 ..
text_mt: Having performed the Prājāpatya sacrifice with all his possessions given as sacrificial fees, / and having deposited the fires within himself, a householder renounces the world with fearlessness.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya tejomayā lokā bhavanti brahmavādinaḥ ..
yasmādaṇvapi bhūtānāṃ dvija notpadyate bhayam ..
tasya dehādvimuktasya bhayaṃ nāsti kathañcana .. 7 ..
meaning:
तस्य तेजोमया लोका भवन्ति ब्रह्मवादिनः ..
यस्मादण्वपि भूतानां द्विज नोत्पद्यते भयम् ..
तस्य देहाद्विमुक्तस्य भयं नास्ति कथञ्चन .. 7 ..
text_mt: Luminous worlds belong to that teacher of the Veda; / for from whom not even the slightest fear arises for living beings, O twice-born one, / for him, released from the body, there is no fear whatsoever.

sanskrit_iast:
agārādabhiniṣkrāntaḥ pavitropacito muniḥ ..
samupoḍheṣu kāmyeṣu nirapekṣaḥ parivrajet .. 8 ..
meaning:
अगारादभिनिष्क्रान्तः पवित्रोपचितो मुनिः ..
समुपोढेषु काम्येषु निरपेक्षः परिव्रजेत् .. 8 ..
text_mt: Having gone forth from home, pure, furnished with means of purification, a silent sage, / indifferent when desirable objects present themselves, he should wander as a mendicant.

sanskrit_iast:
eka eva carennityaṃ siddhyarthamasahāyavān ..
siddhimekasya tāṃ paśyanna jahāti na hīyate .. 9 ..
meaning:
एक एव चरेन्नित्यं सिद्ध्यर्थमसहायवान् ..
सिद्धिमेकस्य तां पश्यन्न जहाति न हीयते .. 9 ..
text_mt: He should always wander alone without companions for the attainment of perfection; / seeing that attainment belongs to one alone, he neither abandons nor is abandoned.

sanskrit_iast: anagniraniketaḥ syādgrāmamannārthamāśrayeta .. 2.131.10 ...
meaning: अनग्निरनिकेतः स्याद्ग्राममन्नार्थमाश्रयेत .. 2.131.10 ...
text_mt: Without fire and without a dwelling, he should approach a village only for food.

sanskrit_iast:
upekṣako'sañcayako munirbhāvasamāhitaḥ ..
kapālaṃ vṛkṣamūlāni kucailamasahāyatā ..
mamatā naiva sarvasminnetanmuktasya lakṣaṇam .. 11 ..
meaning:
उपेक्षकोऽसञ्चयको मुनिर्भावसमाहितः ..
कपालं वृक्षमूलानि कुचैलमसहायता ..
ममता नैव सर्वस्मिन्नेतन्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् .. 11 ..
text_mt: Indifferent, making no accumulation, a silent sage with thoughts composed; / a skull-bowl, the roots of trees, ragged garments, solitude, / and no sense of "mine" in anything: this is the characteristic of one who is liberated.

sanskrit_iast:
nābhinandeta maraṇaṃ nābhinandeta jīvitam ..
kālameva parīkṣeta nirdoṣabhṛtako yathā .. 12 ..
meaning:
नाभिनन्देत मरणं नाभिनन्देत जीवितम् ..
कालमेव परीक्षेत निर्दोषभृतको यथा .. 12 ..
text_mt: He should neither rejoice at death nor rejoice at life; / he should merely await the appointed time, as a blameless servant awaits [his wages].

sanskrit_iast:
(dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyasetpādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pibet ..
satyapūtāṃ vadedvācaṃ manaḥpūtaṃ samācaret ..13..
meaning:
(दृष्टिपूतं न्यसेत्पादं वस्त्रपूतं जलं पिबेत् ..
सत्यपूतां वदेद्वाचं मनःपूतं समाचरेत् ..13..
text_mt: One should set down one's foot purified by sight, drink water purified by cloth, / speak speech purified by truth, and act with a mind purified.

sanskrit_iast: atijaḍāṃstitikṣeta nāvamanyeta kañcana .. 14 ..)
meaning: अतिजडांस्तितिक्षेत नावमन्येत कञ्चन .. 14 ..)
text_mt: One should endure the very foolish and despise no one.

sanskrit_iast:
na cainaṃ gṛhamāśritya vairaṃ kurvīta kenacit ..
krudhyantaṃ na pratikrudhyedāpṛṣṭaḥ kuśalaṃ vadet .. 15 ..
meaning:
न चैनं गृहमाश्रित्य वैरं कुर्वीत केनचित् ..
क्रुध्यन्तं न प्रतिक्रुध्येदापृष्टः कुशलं वदेत् .. 15 ..
text_mt: And depending on this body, one should not form enmity with anyone. / One should not become angry in return at an angry person; addressed, one should speak pleasantly.

sanskrit_iast:
saptadvārāvakīrṇāñca na vācamanṛtāṃ vadet ..
adhyātmaratirāsīno nirapekṣo nirāmiṣaḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
सप्तद्वारावकीर्णाञ्च न वाचमनृतां वदेत् ..
अध्यात्मरतिरासीनो निरपेक्षो निरामिषः .. 16 ..
text_mt: And one should not speak false speech scattered through the seven gates. / Sitting delighted in the supreme self, indifferent, free from longing,

sanskrit_iast: ātmanaiva sahāyena tareddurgatimātmanaḥ .. 17 ..
meaning: आत्मनैव सहायेन तरेद्दुर्गतिमात्मनः .. 17 ..
text_mt: with the self alone as an ally, one should cross over the misfortune of oneself.

sanskrit_iast:
na cotpātanimittābhyāṃ na nakṣatrāṅgavidyayā ..
nānṛtasvanavādābhyāṃ bhikṣāṃ lipseta karhicit .. 18..
meaning:
न चोत्पातनिमित्ताभ्यां न नक्षत्राङ्गविद्यया ..
नानृतस्वनवादाभ्यां भिक्षां लिप्सेत कर्हिचित् .. 18..
text_mt: Not by portents or omens, nor by astrology and the knowledge of the limbs [of the Veda], / nor by deceit, sounds, and disputation, should one ever seek alms.

sanskrit_iast:
na tāpasairbrāhmaṇairvā na yogibhirathāśramaiḥ ..
ākīrṇairbhikṣukairvarṇairāgāramupasaṃvrajet ..19..
meaning:
न तापसैर्ब्राह्मणैर्वा न योगिभिरथाश्रमैः ..
आकीर्णैर्भिक्षुकैर्वर्णैरागारमुपसंव्रजेत् ..19..
text_mt: Not crowded with ascetics, brahmins, yogins, hermits, / or beggars of various classes, should one approach a house.

sanskrit_iast:
klṛptakeśanakhaśmaśruḥ pātrī daṇḍī kusumbhavān ..
viracenniyato nityaṃ sarvabhūtānyapīḍayan .. 2.131.20..
meaning:
क्लृप्तकेशनखश्मश्रुः पात्री दण्डी कुसुम्भवान् ..
विरचेन्नियतो नित्यं सर्वभूतान्यपीडयन् .. 2.131.20..
text_mt: With hair, nails, and beard trimmed, carrying a bowl, bearing a staff, wearing saffron garments, / restrained, one should wander constantly, not harming any living beings.

sanskrit_iast:
ataijasāni pātrāṇi tasya syurnirvraṇāni ca ..
teṣāmadbhiḥ smṛtaṃ śaucaṃ camasānāmivādhvare .. 21 ..
meaning:
अतैजसानि पात्राणि तस्य स्युर्निर्व्रणानि च ..
तेषामद्भिः स्मृतं शौचं चमसानामिवाध्वरे .. 21 ..
text_mt: His vessels should be non-metallic and without fissures; / their purification by water is prescribed, like that of the ladles in a sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
alābuṃ dārupātrañca mṛnmayaṃ vaidalaṃ tathā ..
etāni yatipātrāṇi vijñeyāni manīṣibhiḥ .. 22 ..
meaning:
अलाबुं दारुपात्रञ्च मृन्मयं वैदलं तथा ..
एतानि यतिपात्राणि विज्ञेयानि मनीषिभिः .. 22 ..
text_mt: A bottle-gourd, a wooden vessel, an earthen one, and split-bamboo: / these are to be understood by the wise as vessels for the ascetic.

sanskrit_iast:
sauvarṇamaṇipātreṣu kāṃsyaraupyāyaseṣu ca ..
bhikṣāṃ dadyānna dharmajña grahītā narakaṃ vrajet .. 23 ..
meaning:
सौवर्णमणिपात्रेषु कांस्यरौप्यायसेषु च ..
भिक्षां दद्यान्न धर्मज्ञ ग्रहीता नरकं व्रजेत् .. 23 ..
text_mt: In vessels of gold, jewels, bronze, silver, and iron, / one who knows dharma should not give alms; the receiver would go to hell.

sanskrit_iast:
ekakālaṃ caredbhaikṣyaṃ na prasajyeta vistare ..
bhaikṣye prasaktasya matirviṣayeṣvapi sajjate .. 24..
meaning:
एककालं चरेद्भैक्ष्यं न प्रसज्येत विस्तरे ..
भैक्ष्ये प्रसक्तस्य मतिर्विषयेष्वपि सज्जते .. 24..
text_mt: One should go for alms once a day; one should not be attached to excess. / For of one attached to alms, the mind clings to sense-objects too.

sanskrit_iast:
vidhūme nyastamusale vyaṅgāre bhuktavajjane ..
vṛtte śarāvasampāte bhikṣāṃ nityaṃ yatiścaret .. 25 ..
meaning:
विधूमे न्यस्तमुसले व्यङ्गारे भुक्तवज्जने ..
वृत्ते शरावसम्पाते भिक्षां नित्यं यतिश्चरेत् .. 25 ..
text_mt: When smoke is gone, the pestle is laid down, the coals are extinguished, and people have eaten, / when the clearing of the platters has ended, the ascetic should always go for alms.

sanskrit_iast:
alābhī na viṣādī syāllābhe cāpi na harṣayet ..
prāṇayātrikamātraḥ syānmātrāsaṃgādvinirgataḥ ..
abhipūjitalābhām̐stu yadi mukto'pi badhyate .. 26 ..
meaning:
अलाभी न विषादी स्याल्लाभे चापि न हर्षयेत् ..
प्राणयात्रिकमात्रः स्यान्मात्रासंगाद्विनिर्गतः ..
अभिपूजितलाभाम्̐स्तु यदि मुक्तोऽपि बध्यते .. 26 ..
text_mt: Not obtaining, he should not be despondent; obtaining, he should not rejoice. / He should take only what sustains life, free from clinging to possessions. / For if even a liberated man accepts honorific gains, he is bound.

sanskrit_iast:
alpānnābhyavahāreṇa rahaḥ sthānāsanena ca ..
hriyamāṇāni viṣayairindriyāṇi nivartayet .. 27 ..
meaning:
अल्पान्नाभ्यवहारेण रहः स्थानासनेन च ..
ह्रियमाणानि विषयैरिन्द्रियाणि निवर्तयेत् .. 27 ..
text_mt: By consuming little food and by standing and sitting in solitude, / one should turn back the senses that are being carried away by the sense-objects.

sanskrit_iast:
indriyāṇāṃ nirodhena rāgadveṣabhayena ca ..
ahiṃsayā ca bhūtānāmamṛtatvāya kalpate .. 28 ..
meaning:
इन्द्रियाणां निरोधेन रागद्वेषभयेन च ..
अहिंसया च भूतानाममृतत्वाय कल्पते .. 28 ..
text_mt: By restraining the senses, by shedding passion, hatred, and fear, / and by non-violence toward living beings, one becomes fit for immortality.

sanskrit_iast:
avekṣeta gatiṃ nṝṇāṃ karmadoṣasamudbhavām ..
niraye caiva patanaṃ vyādhibhiścopapīḍanam .. 29 ..
meaning:
अवेक्षेत गतिं नॄणां कर्मदोषसमुद्भवाम् ..
निरये चैव पतनं व्याधिभिश्चोपपीडनम् .. 29 ..
text_mt: One should contemplate the destiny of men arising from the fault of actions: / their falling into hell and their torment by diseases,

sanskrit_iast:
dehānukramaṇaṃ cāsmātpunargarbhe ca sambhavam ..
yonikoṭisahasreṣu mṛtau cāsyāntarātmanaḥ .. 2.131.30 ..
meaning:
देहानुक्रमणं चास्मात्पुनर्गर्भे च सम्भवम् ..
योनिकोटिसहस्रेषु मृतौ चास्यान्तरात्मनः .. 2.131.30 ..
text_mt: and the passage from this body, and rebirth in the womb / through thousands of millions of wombs, and death for this inner self,

sanskrit_iast:
adharmaprabhavaṃ caiva karmayogaṃ śarīriṇām ..
dharmārthaprabhavaṃ caiva sukhasaṃyogamakṣayam .. 31 ..
meaning:
अधर्मप्रभवं चैव कर्मयोगं शरीरिणाम् ..
धर्मार्थप्रभवं चैव सुखसंयोगमक्षयम् .. 31 ..
text_mt: and the connection of embodied beings with actions arising from non-dharma, / and the imperishable union with happiness arising from dharma and purpose,

sanskrit_iast:
sūkṣmatāṃ cānuvīkṣeta yogena paramātmanaḥ ..
deheṣu caiva patitamuttameṣvadhameṣu ca .. 32..
meaning:
सूक्ष्मतां चानुवीक्षेत योगेन परमात्मनः ..
देहेषु चैव पतितमुत्तमेष्वधमेषु च .. 32..
text_mt: and by yoga one should observe the subtlety of the Supreme Self, / even fallen into bodies, both the highest and the lowest.

sanskrit_iast:
dūṣito'pi careddharmaṃ yatrayatrāśrame rataḥ ..
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu na liṅgaṃ dharmakāraṇam .. 33 ..
meaning:
दूषितोऽपि चरेद्धर्मं यत्रयत्राश्रमे रतः ..
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु न लिङ्गं धर्मकारणम् .. 33 ..
text_mt: Even if reviled, one should practice dharma, in whatever stage of life one is engaged, / impartial toward all beings; the external mark is not the cause of dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
phalaṃ katakavṛkṣasya yadyapyambuprasādakam ..
na nāmagrahaṇādeva tasya vāri prasīdati .. 34 ..
meaning:
फलं कतकवृक्षस्य यद्यप्यम्बुप्रसादकम् ..
न नामग्रहणादेव तस्य वारि प्रसीदति .. 34 ..
text_mt: Although the fruit of the kataka tree clears water, / the water does not become clear simply by uttering its name.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ jantūnāṃ rātrāvahani vā sadā ..
śarīrasyātyaye vāpi samīkṣya vasudhāṃ careta .. 35..
meaning:
संरक्षणार्थं जन्तूनां रात्रावहनि वा सदा ..
शरीरस्यात्यये वापि समीक्ष्य वसुधां चरेत .. 35..
text_mt: For the protection of living beings, whether by night or day, / even in the peril of one's body, one should walk inspecting the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
ahorātracayājjantūnhinastyajñānato yadi ..
teṣāṃ snātvā viśuddhyarthaṃ prāṇāyāmānṣaḍācaret .. 36 ..
meaning:
अहोरात्रचयाज्जन्तून्हिनस्त्यज्ञानतो यदि ..
तेषां स्नात्वा विशुद्ध्यर्थं प्राणायामान्षडाचरेत् .. 36 ..
text_mt: If through ignorance over the course of day and night one harms living creatures, / having bathed, one should perform six breath-controls for their purification.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇāyāmā brāhmaṇasya trayo'pi vidhivatkṛtāḥ ..
vyāhṛtipraṇavairyuktā vijñeyaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ .. 37 ..
meaning:
प्राणायामा ब्राह्मणस्य त्रयोऽपि विधिवत्कृताः ..
व्याहृतिप्रणवैर्युक्ता विज्ञेयं परमं तपः .. 37 ..
text_mt: Even three breath-controls of a brahmin, performed according to rule / and joined with the sacred syllables and the Praṇava, are to be understood as supreme austerity.

sanskrit_iast:
dahyante dhmāyamānānāṃ dhātūnāṃ hi yathā malāḥ ..
tathendriyakṛtā doṣā dahyante prāṇanigrahāt .. .. 38 ..
meaning:
दह्यन्ते ध्मायमानानां धातूनां हि यथा मलाः ..
तथेन्द्रियकृता दोषा दह्यन्ते प्राणनिग्रहात् .. .. 38 ..
text_mt: For as the impurities of metallic ores are burned as they are smelted, / so the faults caused by the senses are burned by the restraint of breath.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇāyāmairdaheddoṣāndhāraṇābhistu kilbiṣam ..
pratyāhāreṇa saṃsargāndhyānenānīśvarānguṇān .. 39 ..
meaning:
प्राणायामैर्दहेद्दोषान्धारणाभिस्तु किल्बिषम् ..
प्रत्याहारेण संसर्गान्ध्यानेनानीश्वरान्गुणान् .. 39 ..
text_mt: By breath-controls one should burn away faults, by concentrations sin, / by sensory withdrawal attachments, and by meditation unspiritual qualities.

sanskrit_iast:
uccāvaceṣu bhūteṣu durjñeyamakṛtātmabhiḥ ..
jñānayogena sampaśyedgatimasyāntarātmanaḥ ..2.131.40..
meaning:
उच्चावचेषु भूतेषु दुर्ज्ञेयमकृतात्मभिः ..
ज्ञानयोगेन सम्पश्येद्गतिमस्यान्तरात्मनः ..2.131.40..
text_mt: Through the yoga of knowledge, one should observe the destiny of this inner self / in high and low creatures, difficult to know for those of unformed self.

sanskrit_iast:
samyagdarśanasaṃpannaḥ karmabhirna nibadhyate ..
darśanena vihīnastu saṃsāraṃ pratipadyate .. 41 ..
meaning:
सम्यग्दर्शनसंपन्नः कर्मभिर्न निबध्यते ..
दर्शनेन विहीनस्तु संसारं प्रतिपद्यते .. 41 ..
text_mt: Endowed with correct vision, one is not bound by actions; / but lacking vision, one enters saṃsāra.

sanskrit_iast:
ahiṃsayendriyāsaṅgairvaidyakaiścaiva karmabhiḥ ..
tapasaścaraṇaiścograiḥ sādhayantīha tatpadam .. 42 ..
meaning:
अहिंसयेन्द्रियासङ्गैर्वैद्यकैश्चैव कर्मभिः ..
तपसश्चरणैश्चोग्रैः साधयन्तीह तत्पदम् .. 42 ..
text_mt: Through non-violence, non-attachment of the senses, prescribed ritual actions, / and the performance of fierce austerities, they attain that supreme state here.

sanskrit_iast:
asthisthūṇaṃ snāyuyutaṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepitam ..
carmāvanaddhaṃ durgandhi pātraṃ mūtrapurīṣayoḥ .. 43 ..
meaning:
अस्थिस्थूणं स्नायुयुतं मांसशोणितलेपितम् ..
चर्मावनद्धं दुर्गन्धि पात्रं मूत्रपुरीषयोः .. 43 ..
text_mt: Having bones as its pillars, bound with sinews, plastered with flesh and blood, / covered with skin, foul-smelling, a vessel of urine and feces,

sanskrit_iast:
jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ rogāyatanamāturam ..
rajasvalamanityañca bhūtāvāsamidaṃ tyajet .. 44 ..
meaning:
जराशोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनमातुरम् ..
रजस्वलमनित्यञ्च भूतावासमिदं त्यजेत् .. 44 ..
text_mt: beset by old age and sorrow, the dwelling of diseases, afflicted, / impure and impermanent: one should abandon this abode of the elements.

sanskrit_iast:
nadīkūle yathā vṛkṣo vṛkṣe vā śakuniryathā ..
tathā tyajannimaṃ dehaṃ kṛcchragrāhādvimucyate .. 45 ..
meaning:
नदीकूले यथा वृक्षो वृक्षे वा शकुनिर्यथा ..
तथा त्यजन्निमं देहं कृच्छ्रग्राहाद्विमुच्यते .. 45 ..
text_mt: As a tree on a riverbank [falls], or as a bird [leaves] a tree, / so abandoning this body, one is released from the perilous crocodile [of saṃsāra].

sanskrit_iast:
priyeṣu sveṣu sukṛtaṃ cāpriyeṣu ca duṣkṛtam ..
visṛjya dhyānayogena brahmābhyeti sanātanam..46..
meaning:
प्रियेषु स्वेषु सुकृतं चाप्रियेषु च दुष्कृतम् ..
विसृज्य ध्यानयोगेन ब्रह्माभ्येति सनातनम्..46..
text_mt: Casting off good deeds upon his friends and bad deeds upon those he dislikes, / through the yoga of meditation he approaches eternal Brahman.

sanskrit_iast:
yadā bhāvena bhavati sarvabhāveṣu niḥsṛtiḥ ..
tadā sukhamavāpnoti pretya ceha ca śāśvatam..47..
meaning:
यदा भावेन भवति सर्वभावेषु निःसृतिः ..
तदा सुखमवाप्नोति प्रेत्य चेह च शाश्वतम्..47..
text_mt: When through disposition of mind there is detachment from all worldly states, / then he attains perpetual happiness both here and in the hereafter.

sanskrit_iast:
anena vidhinā sarvānkāmāṃstyaktvā śanaiḥśanaiḥ ..
sarvadvandvairvinirmukto brahmaṇyevāvatiṣṭhati .. 48 ..
meaning:
अनेन विधिना सर्वान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा शनैःशनैः ..
सर्वद्वन्द्वैर्विनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मण्येवावतिष्ठति .. 48 ..
text_mt: Abandoning all desires gradually by this rule, / released from all dualities, he abides in Brahman alone.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānikaṃ sarvamevaitadyadetadatiśābdikam ..
na hyādhyātma kaviḥ kaścitkriyāphalamupāśnute .. 49 ..
meaning:
ध्यानिकं सर्वमेवैतद्यदेतदतिशाब्दिकम् ..
न ह्याध्यात्म कविः कश्चित्क्रियाफलमुपाश्नुते .. 49 ..
text_mt: All this is based on meditation, which is superior to the words of Vedic study; / for no sage of the supreme self experiences the fruit of ritual actions.

sanskrit_iast:
adhiyajñaṃ brahma japetsādhidaivikameva ca ..
ādhyātmikaṃ ca satataṃ vedāntābhihitaṃ phalam .. 2.131.50 ..
meaning:
अधियज्ञं ब्रह्म जपेत्साधिदैविकमेव च ..
आध्यात्मिकं च सततं वेदान्ताभिहितं फलम् .. 2.131.50 ..
text_mt: One should continuously chant Brahman concerning sacrifice, that concerning the gods, / and that concerning the self, which is declared as the fruit by the Upaniṣads.

sanskrit_iast:
idaṃ śaraṇamajñānāmidaṃ daivaṃ vijānatām ..
idamanvicchatāṃ svargamidamānantyamicchatām .. 51 ..
meaning:
इदं शरणमज्ञानामिदं दैवं विजानताम् ..
इदमन्विच्छतां स्वर्गमिदमानन्त्यमिच्छताम् .. 51 ..
text_mt: This is the refuge for the ignorant, this is the deity for those who know, / this is for those seeking heaven, and this is for those desiring infinity.

sanskrit_iast:
anena kramayogeṇa parivrajati yo dvijaḥ ..
sa vidhūyeha pāpmānaṃ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati .. 52 ..
meaning:
अनेन क्रमयोगेण परिव्रजति यो द्विजः ..
स विधूयेह पाप्मानं परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति .. 52 ..
text_mt: The twice-born who renounces according to this sequential order, / shaking off evil here, attains the supreme Brahman.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa dharmo'nuśiṣṭaste yatīnāṃ niyatātmanām ..
eva saṃnyāsakānāntu karmayogaṃ nibodha me .. 53..
meaning:
एष धर्मोऽनुशिष्टस्ते यतीनां नियतात्मनाम् ..
एव संन्यासकानान्तु कर्मयोगं निबोध मे .. 53..
text_mt: This dharma of self-restrained ascetics has been taught to you. / Now learn from me the yoga of action for those who have embraced renunciation.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmacārī gṛhasthaśca vānaprastho yatistathā ..
ete gṛhasthaprabhavāścatvāraḥ pṛthagāśramāḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थश्च वानप्रस्थो यतिस्तथा ..
एते गृहस्थप्रभवाश्चत्वारः पृथगाश्रमाः .. 54 ..
text_mt: The student, the householder, the forest hermit, and the ascetic: / these are the four distinct stages of life, all originating from the householder.

sanskrit_iast:
sarve'pi kramaśastvete yathāśāstraṃ niṣevitāḥ ..
yathoktakāriṇaṃ vipraṃ nayanti paramāṃ gatim .. 55 ..
meaning:
सर्वेऽपि क्रमशस्त्वेते यथाशास्त्रं निषेविताः ..
यथोक्तकारिणं विप्रं नयन्ति परमां गतिम् .. 55 ..
text_mt: All these, practiced in proper order according to scripture, / lead the wise brahmin who acts as taught to the supreme path.

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣāmeva caiteṣāṃ vedaśrutividhānataḥ ..
gṛhastha ucyate śreṣṭhaḥ sa trīnetānbibharti hi .. 56 ..
meaning:
सर्वेषामेव चैतेषां वेदश्रुतिविधानतः ..
गृहस्थ उच्यते श्रेष्ठः स त्रीनेतान्बिभर्ति हि .. 56 ..
text_mt: And among all these, according to the injunction of the Vedic revelation, / the householder is said to be the foremost, for he supports these three.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā nadīnadāḥ sarve sāgare yānti saṃsthitim ..
tathaivāśramiṇaḥ sarve gṛhasthe yānti saṃsthitim..57..
meaning:
यथा नदीनदाः सर्वे सागरे यान्ति संस्थितिम् ..
तथैवाश्रमिणः सर्वे गृहस्थे यान्ति संस्थितिम्..57..
text_mt: Just as all rivers and streams find their rest in the ocean, / even so all dwellers in the stages of life find their rest in the householder.

sanskrit_iast:
caturbhirapi tattvajñairnityamāśramibhirdvijaiḥ ..
daśalākṣaṇiko dharmaḥ sevitavyaḥ prayatnataḥ ..58..
meaning:
चतुर्भिरपि तत्त्वज्ञैर्नित्यमाश्रमिभिर्द्विजैः ..
दशलाक्षणिको धर्मः सेवितव्यः प्रयत्नतः ..58..
text_mt: By twice-born people of all four stages of life, knowing the truth, / the tenfold dharma must always be cultivated with effort:

sanskrit_iast:
dhṛtiḥ kṣamā damo'steyaṃ śaucamindriyanigrahaḥ ..
dhīrvidyā satyamakrodho daśakaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam..59..
meaning:
धृतिः क्षमा दमोऽस्तेयं शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः ..
धीर्विद्या सत्यमक्रोधो दशकं धर्मलक्षणम्..59..
text_mt: Resolution, forgiveness, self-restraint, non-stealing, purity, subduing the senses, / wisdom, learning, truthfulness, and freedom from anger—this is the tenfold mark of dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
daśa cihnāni dharmasya ye viprāḥ samadhīyate ..
adhītya cānuvartante te yānti paramāṃ gatim .. 2.131.60 ..
meaning:
दश चिह्नानि धर्मस्य ये विप्राः समधीयते ..
अधीत्य चानुवर्तन्ते ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् .. 2.131.60 ..
text_mt: Those brahmins who thoroughly study these ten marks of dharma, / and, having studied, put them into practice, attain the supreme state.

sanskrit_iast:
daśalākṣaṇikaṃ dharmamanutiṣṭhansamāhitaḥ ..
vedāntaṃ vidhivacchrutvā manyehamanṛṇo dvijaḥ ..61..
meaning:
दशलाक्षणिकं धर्ममनुतिष्ठन्समाहितः ..
वेदान्तं विधिवच्छ्रुत्वा मन्येहमनृणो द्विजः ..61..
text_mt: Practicing the tenfold dharma with a concentrated mind, / having heard the Vedānta according to rule, a twice-born man becomes free of debt.

sanskrit_iast:
sannyasya sarvakarmāṇi sarvāndoṣānupānudet ..
niyato dharmamabhyasya putraiḥ saha sukhaṃ vaseta..62..
meaning:
सन्न्यस्य सर्वकर्माणि सर्वान्दोषानुपानुदेत् ..
नियतो धर्ममभ्यस्य पुत्रैः सह सुखं वसेत..62..
text_mt: Renouncing all ritual actions, he should remove all defects; / self-restrained, practicing dharma, he may live happily with his sons.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ sanyasya karmāṇi svakārye paramo'spṛhaḥ ..
saṃnyāsenāpahṛtyenaṃ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim ..
eṣa te'bhihito dharmo dvijātīnāṃ caturvidhaḥ .. 63 ..
meaning:
एवं सन्यस्य कर्माणि स्वकार्ये परमोऽस्पृहः ..
संन्यासेनापहृत्येनं प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ..
एष तेऽभिहितो धर्मो द्विजातीनां चतुर्विधः .. 63 ..
text_mt: Having thus renounced actions, entirely free from desire in his own concern, / having removed this [bondage] by renunciation, he attains the supreme state. / This fourfold dharma of the twice-born has been declared to you.

sanskrit_iast:
svalpo'pi dharmaścarito yathāyaṃ mahāphalaḥ syātsatataṃ dvijānām ..
tasmātprayatnādayameva kāryaḥ sarvaṃ samutsṛjya mahānubhāvaḥ .. 64 ..
2.132
rāma uvāca ..
aṣṭādaśabhyaḥ śāntibhyaḥ śāntayo yāḥ surottama ..
bhidyante vā na bhidyante tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
amṛtā cābhayā saumyāstisronyāḥ santi bhārgava ..
ekāpi tāsāṃ vijñeyā sarvakarmaphalapradā .. 2 ..
sarvotpātapraśamanī maṅgalyā siddhikārikā ...
pūrvoktāḥ kathiteṣveva kartavyā adbhuteṣu ca .. 3 ..
rāma uvāca ..
śāntīnāṃ me tvamācakṣva svarūpāṇi mahābhuja ..
pitāmahasamo loke sarvajño'pi mato mama..4..
puṣkara uvāca ..
amṛtā śarvadaivatyā abhayā brahmadaivatā ..
saumyā ca somadaivatyā kathitā bhṛgunandana .. 5 ..
anyāsāṃ devatā jñānaṃ nāmnaiva kathitaṃ tava ..
ātharvaṇānāṃ śāntīnāṃ nibodha gadato mama .. 6 ..
meaning:
स्वल्पोऽपि धर्मश्चरितो यथायं महाफलः स्यात्सततं द्विजानाम् ..
तस्मात्प्रयत्नादयमेव कार्यः सर्वं समुत्सृज्य महानुभावः .. 64 ..
2.132
राम उवाच ..
अष्टादशभ्यः शान्तिभ्यः शान्तयो याः सुरोत्तम ..
भिद्यन्ते वा न भिद्यन्ते तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः .. 1 ..
पुष्कर उवाच ..
अमृता चाभया सौम्यास्तिस्रोन्याः सन्ति भार्गव ..
एकापि तासां विज्ञेया सर्वकर्मफलप्रदा .. 2 ..
सर्वोत्पातप्रशमनी मङ्गल्या सिद्धिकारिका ...
पूर्वोक्ताः कथितेष्वेव कर्तव्या अद्भुतेषु च .. 3 ..
राम उवाच ..
शान्तीनां मे त्वमाचक्ष्व स्वरूपाणि महाभुज ..
पितामहसमो लोके सर्वज्ञोऽपि मतो मम..4..
पुष्कर उवाच ..
अमृता शर्वदैवत्या अभया ब्रह्मदैवता ..
सौम्या च सोमदैवत्या कथिता भृगुनन्दन .. 5 ..
अन्यासां देवता ज्ञानं नाम्नैव कथितं तव ..
आथर्वणानां शान्तीनां निबोध गदतो मम .. 6 ..
text_mt:
Even a little of this dharma, when performed, brings great fruit constantly to the twice-born. / Therefore, abandoning everything, this very glorious [dharma] must be practiced with effort.
2.132 / Rāma said: / O best of gods, concerning the rites of pacification [other] than the eighteen rites of pacification, / tell me as I ask: are they different or not different?
Puṣkara said: / There are three other [rites], O Bhārgava: Amṛtā, Abhayā, and Saumyā. / Even a single one of them should be understood to bestow the fruit of all rites.
They pacify all portents, bring auspiciousness, and effect success. / The previously mentioned ones are to be performed only with respect to the portents already described.
Rāma said: / Tell me the individual forms of the rites of pacification, O long-armed one; / in my view, you are omniscient in this world, equal to the Grandfather [Brahmā].
Puṣkara said: / Amṛtā has Śarva as its deity, Abhayā has Brahmā as its deity, / and Saumyā has Soma as its deity, O delight of the Bhṛgus.
The knowledge of the deities of the others has been told to you through their very names. / Learn from me as I speak of the rites of pacification belonging to the Atharvaveda.

sanskrit_iast:
amṛtā citravarṇā syādabhayā tu śaśiprabhā..
saumyā śuklaiva vijñeyā nīlā bhavati vaiṣṇavī .. 7 ..
bālārkasadṛśā raudrī brāhmī śaṃkhasamaprabhā ..
rukmavarṇā tathaivaindrī vāyavyā haritā bhavet.. 8 ..
śuklā ca vāruṇī jñeyā kauberī padmasuprabhā ..

text_mt:
Amṛtā is multicolored, while Abhayā has the luster of the moon. / Saumyā is known to be white, and Vaiṣṇavī is blue.
Raudrī resembles the morning sun; Brāhmī has a radiance like a conch. / Aindrī is of golden color, and Vāyavyā is green.
Vāruṇī is to be known as white, and Kauberī has the bright luster of a lotus. / Bhārgavī is white in color, and Prājāpatyā is yellowish.
Tvāṣṭrī is to be known as white, and Kaumārī has the bright luster of copper. / Āgneyī has the excellent color of fire, and Mātaṅginī is white.
Gāndharvī has the appearance of coral, and Nairṛtī is black. / Āṅgirasī has the appearance of yellow orpiment, and Yāmyā is black.
Pārthivī has the appearance of a peacock. Thus they have been described to you by color. / Hereafter I shall explain their spheres of application according to rule.
The three, Amṛtā, Abhayā, and Saumyā, O delight of the Bhṛgus— / their location everywhere has been declared by the ancients.

text_mt:
Prājāpatyā, Āgneyī, Yāmyā, Nairṛtī, / Kauberī, and Pārthivī are proclaimed to belong to the earth.
Vāyavyā, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, and Rudradaivatā / are stated to belong to the mid-space, O best of the twice-born.
Aindrī, Mātaṅginī, Tvāṣṭrī, and Brāhmī are spoken of as celestial, / as well as Vāruṇī, Gāndhārī, Bhārgavī, and Āṅgirasī.
The primary ones have been explained to you; they must be performed by one who knows, / according to rule, whenever portents arise in their respective domains.
The mantras addressed to their deities are called the interior deposit of them all; / and the interior deposits of the amulets are called the mantra of them all.
The mantras of the amulets are to be known from the characteristics of the mantras. / And for all the rites of pacification, the ten groups [of mantras] are to be offered into the fire:
Śāntyātīta, Bhaiṣajya, Trisaptīya, / Abhayā, O Rāma, and Aparājitā,

Assessing the gravity of the portent, the royal priest should perform a penance. / Even beforehand, at the very beginning of the portent, he should perform pacification.
Having performed the penance, fasting, he should then perform the rite of pacification. / He should kindle the fire with the fire-sticks in all these rites of pacification.
At the end of the day of fasting, having produced the fire with effort, / he should divide the prepared food into the flesh-eating portion and the benign portion.
Having placed the flesh-eating portion in a skull, [facing] the south-western direction with a firm [mind], / he should deposit it in the hall of pacification, or else the benign portion for the sake of pacification.
Wearing a black turban, black clothes, and black garlands and unguents, / the royal priest, having gone to the area, should worship Nirṛti.

On an earthen [vessel] or on a worn-out skull, having endowed [it] with fragrances and garlands, / and covered [it] with black garments, he should then present the offering.
With the great sound of musical instruments and with auspicious shouts, / then, O twice-born, he should properly offer fat and other [substances] into the fire.
With the four [verses beginning with] "Ye piśācāḥ," reed and pebbles then / he should offer into the bare fire with a ladle made of clay.
Having offered chaff into the fire and fed the fire, / he should go to his own house without looking back; then, having bathed, clad in white garments,
and having recited the Ahomuc and the appeasing [hymn], he should remain well-controlled. / When one third of the night remains, he should commence the appeasing rite.
Then, knowing the procedure of the appeasing ritual, accompanied by the assembly members, / one should be engaged in the action, and one in determining the mantra.
This procedure of appeasement has been declared in brief for all appeasing rites; / in detailed treatment, the detailed rite of appeasement is indeed Atharvanic.

When an unction is impending, and in fears of foreign armies, / in division within one's own realm, and in slaying enemies, the Aindrī appeasing rite is praised.
When a harsh wind blowing from all directions exceeds three days, / in unnatural occurrences, and in wind-born disease, the Vāyavī appeasing rite is prescribed.
When fear of drought has arisen, when abnormal rain has occurred, / and in abnormality of water reservoirs, the Vāruṇī appeasing rite is prescribed.
When fear of a curse has arrived, the Bhārgavī [is prescribed], O twice-born; / when unnatural delivery has occurred, the Prājāpatyā [is prescribed], O mighty-armed one.
In abnormality of household utensils, the Tvāṣṭrī [is prescribed], O delight of the Bhṛgus; / and for one desiring the appeasement of children, the Kaumārī is auspicious.

Rāma said: / Tell me, O god, the fruit of portents and likewise their pacification; / for you, O wide-eyed one, know all that is to be known without remainder.
Puṣkara said: / Here I shall describe to you what the one of great asceticism spoke, / who was the elder Garga here, the foremost among all upholders of dharma.
O descendant of Bhṛgu, to Garga, who was seated comfortably by the stream of the Sarasvatī, / the glorious Atri questioned Garga, who was dear to the company of sages:
Atri said: / Tell me the portents of men, / of cities, and of kings who are about to perish; for you are called all-knowing.
Garga said: / Because of the transgressions of men, the deities inevitably become alienated; / from that alienation of the gods, affliction arises.

text_mt:
It is proclaimed to be threefold: celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial. / An unnatural condition of planets and asterisms is celestial; understand from me the atmospheric:
The falling of meteors, the burning of the quarters, a halo [around the sun or moon], / a city of the Gandharvas, and unnatural rainfall—
one should declare such phenomena in this world to be atmospheric. / Fear affecting moving and unmoving things on earth, and also earthquakes, are born of the earth.
An unnatural alteration of reservoirs of water is also proclaimed to be on the earth. / A terrestrial [portent] is to be known as yielding its result slowly, seen on earth after a long time.
An atmospheric [portent] grants a moderate result, bestowing its result in a moderate time. / A celestial [portent] is to be known as yielding a severe result and as acting quickly.
When a portent has arisen, if auspicious rain should occur / within seven days, that portent is indeed known to be without result.
If the maturation of a portent is not seen [averted] without pacification, / it is known to cause very great danger within three years.

text_mt:
The wondrous sight of celestial women, spirits, Gandharvas, and flying chariots, / and the sighting of planets, asterisms, and stars when the sun is shining;
the sound of singing and musical instruments in forests and on mountain ridges, / and the increase and emergence of sap and juices—these are remembered as auspicious in autumn.
Cold, frost, the delight of domestic birds, / the sighting of beings such as Rākṣasas and Yakṣas, non-human speech,
smoky darkness in the quarters, mountains rich in reeds, / and the rising and setting of the sun high up are remembered as auspicious in the cold season.
Snowfall, portents of wind, the sighting of deformed wonders, / the sky resembling black collyrium and tawny with falling stars and meteors,
manifold births from the womb among women, cows, goats, horses, wild beasts, and birds, / and alterations in leaves, sprouts, and creepers—these are auspicious in the winter season.
When a portent has arisen and been seen without the natural character of the season, / after immediately effecting appeasement, a rite of pacification should then be performed as stated by the lord of the earth.

text_mt:
Garga said: / [When] images of the deities dance, tremble, and blaze, / cry out, weep, sweat, and laugh;
stand up, sit down, run forward, and take shelter; / eat, or toss about their limbs, weapons, and banners;
stand facing downward, wander from place to place, / and vomit fire, smoke, oil, blood, and fat—
when such unnatural alterations are seen arising suddenly / in liṅgas, temples, and painted images, one should not desire to reside there.
Misfortune will befall the king there, or the entire country will perish. / Having seen a festival procession of the deities accompanied by portents, one should declare danger to the country.
An omen regarding the Grandfather, the sages, or Dharma pertains to the twice-born; / those arising from Bṛhaspati, Śukra, or Agni pertain to the domestic priest.
That arising from Rudra is to be known as pertaining to cattle; that from the guardians of the world, to kings; / and whatever pertains to Skanda and Vināyaka is to be known as affecting commanders of the army.
Portents arising from Viṣṇu, Vāyu, Indra, and Viśvakarman pertain to the people; / that arising from Vināyaka is to be known as affecting those who are leaders of troops.

Portents among the messengers of the gods pertain to messengers of the king; among divine women, to women of the king; / among the household deities, it is to be known as affecting householders alone, not otherwise.
In the event of unnatural alterations in the images of the deities, the domestic priest, learned in the Vedic scriptures, / should then approach the divine image, bathe it, clothe it, and adorn it.
And, O fortunate one, he should worship it with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, and food; / thereafter he should approach it with the honey-mixture according to the prescribed rule.
And with the mantra characteristic of that [deity], the domestic priest, unflagging, / should sacrifice a cooked offering of grains into the fire according to rule for seven nights.
And brahmins should be honoured with sweet food and drink, along with sacrificial fees, for seven days, O foremost of the twice-born; / when the eighth day arrives, the evil reaches pacification through gifts of land, cows, and gold.

2.137 / Garga said: / In whichever cities trees are seen impelled by fate, / weeping, laughing, or exuding many fluids,
shedding branches effortlessly, without wind, / or three-year-old saplings displaying fruit and flowers,
displaying fruit and flowers out of season in every state, / and exuding milk, oil, wine, blood, honey, and water,
drying up suddenly without disease, or dry ones sprouting again, / or fallen ones standing up here and standing ones falling—
in that regard I shall tell you, O brahmin, the outcome and indeed the fruit. / By weeping, it indicates disease; by laughing, destruction of the land.
By the falling of branches, it causes downfall in battle; / the bearing of fruit and flowers by young saplings causes the death of children.

Perennial fruit and flowers cause internal division in one's own realm; / milk flowing everywhere causes destruction; oil is a sign of famine.
In liquor, one should predict a loss of mounts; in blood, battle. / With the exudation of honey there will be disease; with the exudation of water it rains.
From drying up without disease, O brahmin, a sign of famine is to be known; / when dry [trees] sprout again, virility and food are lost.
And at the rising of fallen ones, there will be a fear that causes schism; / from place to place, for horses, one should likewise predict ruin of the land.
When trees chatter and weep, there is loss of wealth. / All this ripens upon the king when it happens to sacred trees.

2.138 / Garga said: / Both excessive rain and drought are considered [causes] of famine; / rain falling falsely, on an inauspicious lunar day, empty, is known to bring fear.
And abnormal [rain] from a cloudless sky is to be understood as leading to the king's death; / when cold and heat are reversed, there is danger for living beings arising from enemies.
Where blood rains down, there danger from weapons will occur; / through a rain of burning coals and dust, that city is destroyed.
With [a rain of] marrow, bone, fat, and flesh, there will be fear of an epidemic; / but [a rain of] fruit, flowers, grain, gold, and so forth brings danger.
With a raining of dust, creatures, and stones, there is danger arising from disease; / and in a downpour of perforated things, an increase of blights on the crops.
When the sun is free of dust and the sky is cloudless, and a shadow is not seen, / or is seen distorted, there danger to the country will occur.

or a conflagration of the quarters, halos, or an illusion of a city in the sky, / one should declare danger from a foreign army or calamity in the land.
A sacrifice to the Sun, Moon, Parjanya, and the Wind should be performed according to rule, O foremost of twice-borns; / and sacrificial fees of grain, food, cows, and gold should be given to twice-borns for the sake of dispelling danger.
2.139 / Garga said: / If [waters] recede from a city or approach near it, / or dry up though they cannot dry, or flow nearby,
or if rivers, lakes, springs, and streams become / discoloured, turbid, hot, filled with hard foam,
or if the waters of springs carry milk, oil, wine, and blood, / within six months there will be danger from a foreign army.
Or if reservoirs of water roar, chatter, or boil, / or, O brahmin, emit smoke and dust from the water,

or if water appears where no pit is dug, or reservoirs contain monstrous beings, / or if sounds of music are perceived, one should predict fear of an epidemic.
Upon an anomaly of water reservoirs, self-controlled at the reservoir of water, / one should worship Varuṇa with cooked sacrificial offerings and an animal victim, O twice-born.
Celestial water, milk, clarified butter, and honey are the libation here; / mantras addressed to Varuṇa are to be recited, and with them the burnt offering should be made in the water.
Here, supreme food combined with honey and ghee should be given to twice-borns, O twice-born, for their meal. / And cows draped in garments, as well as water jars, should be given to twice-borns for the pacification of every limb.
2.140 / Garga said: / If women give birth untimely or past their time, / or give birth to abnormal [offspring] or twins,
or if non-human, headless, or afflicted [beings], / or those with deficient limbs or redundant limbs are born, or if women,
animals, birds, and likewise reptiles [do so], / one should predict the destruction of that country and of the family as well.

text_mt:
2.143 / Garga said: / When wild beasts and birds enter a village, / or village [animals] go to the wilderness, or water-born creatures go to dry land,
or land-born creatures go into water, or cry dreadfully without fear; / and jackals at the king's gate or at the city gate bring misfortune;
or night-prowlers by day, or day-prowlers by night; / or domestic animals abandon a village—one should predict its desolation.
Or if blazing [creatures] howl at the twilights and make circles, / or where they howl discordantly, then too one should predict this result.
If a rooster crows in the evening, or a cuckoo in winter, / or a dog faces the sun at sunrise, there will be danger for the king.
If a dove enters a house, or a flesh-eater settles on one's head, / or bees make honey, one should predict the death of the master of the house.
If a carnivorous bird alights on city walls, gates, houses, / arched gateways, shops, or streets, or upon banners, parasols, weapons, and the like,

Rāma said:
What indeed is the highest duty of a king? Tell that to me as I ask:
how should statecraft be maintained by a wise king?
Puṣkara said:
By a king endowed with correct intent, for a kingdom of seven constituents,
this alone is the statecraft to be executed, O foremost of the Bhṛgus:
Conciliation, gift, likewise the fort, treasury, and also the army,
the ally, and the countryside: the kingdom is said to have seven constituents.
The king should banish those who cause obstruction to the sevenfold kingdom;
without deliberation, he should quickly execute those who are hostile.
The development of the seven-constituent kingdom should be carried out in one's own realm,
and the king should draw resources from all [surrounding] realms.
Rāma said:
Explain properly the circles of rulers for an ambitious king,
relying on which kings must consider peace and war.

देवाज्ञाबृंहितो राजा सन्नद्धः समरं प्रति ..8..
text_mt:
Roars, shouts of joy: 'My enemy has been slain!'
[and] 'Empowered by divine command, the king is girded for battle!'

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ prakārā dvijavarya māyāḥ kāryā narendrairariṣu prahṛṣṭaiḥ ..
māyāhataḥ śatruratha prasahya śakyaḥ sukhaṃ hantumadīnasattvaḥ .. 9 ..
2.149
puṣkara uvāca ..
caturaṅgaṃ balaṃ rājā māyājālena darśayet ..
sahāyārthamanuprāptāndarśayettridivaukasaḥ .. 1 ..
raktavṛṣṭiśca saṃdarśyā pareṣāṃ śivaraṃ prati ..
chinnāni ripuśīrṣāṇi prasādāgreṣu darśayet .. 2 ..
ādhitsatā sandhimahīnasatva kāryaṃ bhavedrāma mahendrajālam ..
vakṣyāmi taccopaniṣatsu tubhyaṃ yogāni cānyāni jayāvahāni .. 3 ..
2.150
puṣkara uvāca ..
sandhiśca vigrahaścaiva vaiguṇyaṃ kathitaṃ budhaiḥ ..
yadāśritya tathaivānyaiḥ ṣāḍguṇyaṃ parikīrtitam ..1..
sandhiśca nigrahaścaiva yānamāsanameva ca ..
dvaidhībhāvaṃ saṃśrayaṃ ca ṣāḍguṇyaṃ parikīrtitam .. 2 ..
meaning:
एवं प्रकारा द्विजवर्य मायाः कार्या नरेन्द्रैररिषु प्रहृष्टैः ..
मायाहतः शत्रुरथ प्रसह्य शक्यः सुखं हन्तुमदीनसत्त्वः .. 9 ..
2.149
पुष्कर उवाच ..
चतुरङ्गं बलं राजा मायाजालेन दर्शयेत् ..
सहायार्थमनुप्राप्तान्दर्शयेत्त्रिदिवौकसः .. 1 ..
रक्तवृष्टिश्च संदर्श्या परेषां शिवरं प्रति ..
छिन्नानि रिपुशीर्षाणि प्रसादाग्रेषु दर्शयेत् .. 2 ..
आधित्सता सन्धिमहीनसत्व कार्यं भवेद्राम महेन्द्रजालम् ..
वक्ष्यामि तच्चोपनिषत्सु तुभ्यं योगानि चान्यानि जयावहानि .. 3 ..
2.150
पुष्कर उवाच ..
सन्धिश्च विग्रहश्चैव वैगुण्यं कथितं बुधैः ..
यदाश्रित्य तथैवान्यैः षाड्गुण्यं परिकीर्तितम् ..1..
सन्धिश्च निग्रहश्चैव यानमासनमेव च ..
द्वैधीभावं संश्रयं च षाड्गुण्यं परिकीर्तितम् .. 2 ..
text_mt:
Subtle deceptions of such kinds should be employed by kings against enemies with rejoicing, O best of the twice-born;
for an enemy stricken by deceptions, even if of undiminished spirit, can easily be slain by force.
Puṣkara said:
The king should display a fourfold army by magical illusion;
he should display the gods arrived to assist him.
A rain of blood should be displayed over the camp of the enemies;
he should display severed heads of the enemy upon palace roofs.
When wishing to force a treaty, O one of unyielding spirit, the great sorcery should be employed, O Rāma;
and I shall tell you in the secret doctrines about that and other practices bringing victory.
Puṣkara said:
Peace and war are spoken of by the wise as a duality,
upon which basis the sixfold foreign policy is also described by others.
Peace, war, marching, and encamping,
duplicity, and seeking refuge are described as the sixfold policy.

sanskrit_iast:
paṇabandhaḥ smṛtaḥ sandhirapakārastu vigrahaḥ ..
jigīṣoḥ śatruviṣaye yānaṃ yātrā vidhīyate .. 3 ..
vigrahe'pi svake deśe sthitirāsanamucyate ..
balārdhena pramāṇaṃ tu dvaidhībhāvaṃ taducyate .. 4..
udāsīne madhyame vā saṃśrayātsaṃśrayaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
samena sandhiranveṣyo hīnena ca balīyasaḥ .. .. 5 ..
hīnena vigrahaḥ kāryaḥ svayaṃ rājñā balīyasā ..
tatrāpi tasya pārṣṇistu balīyānna samāśrayet .. 6 ..
āsīnaḥ karmavicchedaṃ śaktaḥ kartuṃ ripuryadā ..
aśuddhapārṣṇirbalavāndvaidhībhāvaṃ samāśrayet .. 7 ..
balinā nigṛhītantu yo manyedyena pārthivaḥ ..
saṃśrayastena kartavyo guṇānāmadhamo guṇaḥ ..8..
bahukṣayavyayāyāsaṃ teṣāṃ yānaṃ prakīrtitam ..
bahulābhakarambhaḥ syāttadā rāma samāśrayet .. 9 ..
meaning:
पणबन्धः स्मृतः सन्धिरपकारस्तु विग्रहः ..
जिगीषोः शत्रुविषये यानं यात्रा विधीयते .. 3 ..
विग्रहेऽपि स्वके देशे स्थितिरासनमुच्यते ..
बलार्धेन प्रमाणं तु द्वैधीभावं तदुच्यते .. 4..
उदासीने मध्यमे वा संश्रयात्संश्रयः स्मृतः ..
समेन सन्धिरन्वेष्यो हीनेन च बलीयसः .. .. 5 ..
हीनेन विग्रहः कार्यः स्वयं राज्ञा बलीयसा ..
तत्रापि तस्य पार्ष्णिस्तु बलीयान्न समाश्रयेत् .. 6 ..
आसीनः कर्मविच्छेदं शक्तः कर्तुं रिपुर्यदा ..
अशुद्धपार्ष्णिर्बलवान्द्वैधीभावं समाश्रयेत् .. 7 ..
बलिना निगृहीतन्तु यो मन्येद्येन पार्थिवः ..
संश्रयस्तेन कर्तव्यो गुणानामधमो गुणः ..8..
बहुक्षयव्ययायासं तेषां यानं प्रकीर्तितम् ..
बहुलाभकरम्भः स्यात्तदा राम समाश्रयेत् .. 9 ..

sanskrit_iast: sarvaśaktivihīnastu tadā kuryāttu saṃśrayam ..2.150.10 ..
meaning: सर्वशक्तिविहीनस्तु तदा कुर्यात्तु संश्रयम् ..2.150.10 ..
text_mt: One who is bereft of all power should then seek refuge.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ ca buddhvā nṛpatirguṇānāṃ kāle ca deśe ca tathā vibhāge ..
samāśrayedbhārgavavaṃśamukhyaṃ caitāvaduktaṃ nṛpatestu kāryam .. 11 ...
meaning:
एवं च बुद्ध्वा नृपतिर्गुणानां काले च देशे च तथा विभागे ..
समाश्रयेद्भार्गववंशमुख्यं चैतावदुक्तं नृपतेस्तु कार्यम् .. 11 ...
text_mt:
Thus understanding the division of policies according to time and place,
he should employ them, O chief of Bhṛgu's lineage; and this much is declared as the duty of a king.

sanskrit_iast:
2.151
.. rāma uvāca .. ..
ajasraṃ karma me brūhi rājñāṃ rājīvalocana ..
yacca kāryaṃ narendrāṇāṃ tadhā ca prativatsaram .. 1 ..
meaning:
2.151
.. राम उवाच .. ..
अजस्रं कर्म मे ब्रूहि राज्ञां राजीवलोचन ..
यच्च कार्यं नरेन्द्राणां तधा च प्रतिवत्सरम् .. 1 ..
text_mt:
Rāma said:
Tell me the daily duty of kings, O lotus-eyed one,
and what must be done by rulers of men year by year.
title: Ājasrikaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ...
dvimuhūrtāvaśeṣāyāṃ rātrau nidrāṃ tyajennṛpaḥ ..
veṇuvīṇāmṛdaṅgānāṃ paṭahānāṃ ca niḥsvanaiḥ .. 2 ..
meaning:
.. पुष्कर उवाच .. ...
द्विमुहूर्तावशेषायां रात्रौ निद्रां त्यजेन्नृपः ..
वेणुवीणामृदङ्गानां पटहानां च निःस्वनैः .. 2 ..
text_mt:
Puṣkara said:
With two muhūrtas remaining in the night, the king should give up sleep
to the sounds of flutes, vīṇās, mṛdaṅgas, and drums.

sanskrit_iast:
bandināṃ niḥsvanaiścaiva tathā maṅgalavādinām ..
tataḥ paśyenmahīpālo gūḍhāṃśca puruṣānniśi .. 3 ..
meaning:
बन्दिनां निःस्वनैश्चैव तथा मङ्गलवादिनाम् ..
ततः पश्येन्महीपालो गूढांश्च पुरुषान्निशि .. 3 ..
text_mt:
and by the cries of bards and those who recite auspicious words.
Then in the night, the ruler of the earth should consult secret agents

sanskrit_iast:
vijñāyante na ye loke tadīyā iti kenacit ..
āyavyayasya śravaṇaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ yathāvidhi .. 4 ..
meaning:
विज्ञायन्ते न ये लोके तदीया इति केनचित् ..
आयव्ययस्य श्रवणं ततः कार्यं यथाविधि .. 4 ..
text_mt:
whom no one in the world knows to be his.
Then, in accordance with rule, he should hear the account of income and expenditure.

sanskrit_iast:
vegotsargaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā rājā snānagṛhaṃ vrajet..
dattābhyaṅgaḥ pradoṣe tu kalpamutsāditastataḥ ..5..
meaning:
वेगोत्सर्गं ततः कृत्वा राजा स्नानगृहं व्रजेत्..
दत्ताभ्यङ्गः प्रदोषे तु कल्पमुत्सादितस्ततः ..5..
text_mt:
Having then discharged the urges [of nature], the king should go to the bathhouse.
Anointed with oil, rubbed with fragrant powders according to rule,

sanskrit_iast:
snānaṃ kuryāttataḥ paścāddantadhāvanapūrvakam..
sauṣadhairmantrapūtaistu pānīyairvividhaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 6 ..
meaning:
स्नानं कुर्यात्ततः पश्चाद्दन्तधावनपूर्वकम्..
सौषधैर्मन्त्रपूतैस्तु पानीयैर्विविधैः शुभैः .. 6 ..
text_mt:
he should then take his bath, preceded by brushing his teeth,
with diverse auspicious waters mixed with medicinal herbs and consecrated by mantras.

sanskrit_iast:
sandhyāmupāsya prayataḥ kṛtajapyaḥ samāhitaḥ ..
agnyāgāraṃ praviśyātha vahnīn paśyetpurodhasā .. 7 ..
meaning:
सन्ध्यामुपास्य प्रयतः कृतजप्यः समाहितः ..
अग्न्यागारं प्रविश्याथ वह्नीन् पश्येत्पुरोधसा .. 7 ..
text_mt:
Having performed the dawn twilight worship, purified, having recited his prayers, composed,
he should then enter the fire chamber and see the fires

sanskrit_iast:
hutān samyaktataḥ kuryādvāsudevasya cārcanam ..
duḥsvapnaśamanaṃ karma tatra kuryātpurohitaḥ ..8..
meaning:
हुतान् सम्यक्ततः कुर्याद्वासुदेवस्य चार्चनम् ..
दुःस्वप्नशमनं कर्म तत्र कुर्यात्पुरोहितः ..8..
text_mt:
duly offered by the royal priest, and then perform the worship of Vāsudeva.
The royal priest should there perform the rite that calms bad dreams.

sanskrit_iast:
svayaṃ caupasade vahnau pavitrāṃ juhuyānnṛpaḥ ..
tarpayedudakairdevānpitṝnatha yathāvidhi..9..
meaning:
स्वयं चौपसदे वह्नौ पवित्रां जुहुयान्नृपः ..
तर्पयेदुदकैर्देवान्पितॄनथ यथाविधि..9..
text_mt:
And the king himself should offer the sacred blade of grass into the upasada fire.
He should then satisfy the gods and the ancestors with water according to rule.

sanskrit_iast:
dadyāddvijātaye dhenuṃ savatsāṃ ca sakāñcanām.
śaktyā dhanaiḥ pūjayitvā dattāśīḥ satataṃ dvijaiḥ..2.151.10.. .
meaning:
दद्याद्द्विजातये धेनुं सवत्सां च सकाञ्चनाम्.
शक्त्या धनैः पूजयित्वा दत्ताशीः सततं द्विजैः..2.151.10.. .
text_mt:
He should give to a twice-born a milch cow with its calf and with gold,
having honoured [him] with wealth according to his ability, continuously blessed by the twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
anuliptastataḥ sragvī suvāsāścāpyalaṃkṛtaḥ ..
darpaṇe ca mukhaṃ paśyetsasuvarṇe ca sarpiṣi .. 11 ..
meaning:
अनुलिप्तस्ततः स्रग्वी सुवासाश्चाप्यलंकृतः ..
दर्पणे च मुखं पश्येत्ससुवर्णे च सर्पिषि .. 11 ..
text_mt:
Then, anointed [with perfumes], wearing a garland, well dressed and adorned,
he should look at his face in a mirror and in clarified butter with gold.

sanskrit_iast:
ājyaṃ prasannaṃ surabhi yadi syādvijayo bhavet .. .
dīyamāne ca durgandhe patite ca bhayaṃ bhavet..12..
meaning:
आज्यं प्रसन्नं सुरभि यदि स्याद्विजयो भवेत् .. .
दीयमाने च दुर्गन्धे पतिते च भयं भवेत्..12..
text_mt:
If the ghee is clear and fragrant, there will be victory;
if it gives off a foul smell or is spilled, there will be danger.

sanskrit_iast:
vikṛtaṃ cenmukhaṃ paśyedrājā mṛtyumavāpnuyāt ..
suprabhaṃ ca yadā paśyettadā tasya śubhaṃ bhavet ..13 ..
meaning:
विकृतं चेन्मुखं पश्येद्राजा मृत्युमवाप्नुयात् ..
सुप्रभं च यदा पश्येत्तदा तस्य शुभं भवेत् ..13 ..
text_mt:
If the king sees a distorted face, he will meet with death;
and when he sees [his face] bright and radiant, then good fortune will be his.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu śṛṇuyādrājā sāṃvatsaramukhodgatam ..
divase tithinakṣatre sarvāśubhavināśanam ..14..
meaning:
ततस्तु शृणुयाद्राजा सांवत्सरमुखोद्गतम् ..
दिवसे तिथिनक्षत्रे सर्वाशुभविनाशनम् ..14..
text_mt:
Then the king should hear from the mouth of the astrologer
the day, lunar day, and lunar mansion that destroy all inauspiciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
bhiṣajāṃ ca vacaḥ kuryāttatastvārogyavardhanam ..
maṅgalālambhanaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ paśyedgurūnnṛpaḥ ..15..
meaning:
भिषजां च वचः कुर्यात्ततस्त्वारोग्यवर्धनम् ..
मङ्गलालम्भनं कृत्वा ततः पश्येद्गुरून्नृपः ..15..
text_mt:
And he should follow the advice of physicians that promotes health.
Having touched auspicious objects, the king should then look upon his elders.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvāśīrgurubhiḥ paścādrājā gacchetsamantataḥ ..
tatrasthānbrāhmaṇānpaśyedamātyānmantriṇastathā ..16..
meaning:
कृत्वाशीर्गुरुभिः पश्चाद्राजा गच्छेत्समन्ततः ..
तत्रस्थान्ब्राह्मणान्पश्येदमात्यान्मन्त्रिणस्तथा ..16..
text_mt:
After receiving blessings from the elders, the king should proceed all around.
He should see the brahmins situated there, as well as the executive officers and counsellors,

sanskrit_iast:
prakṛtīśca mahābhāga pratīhāranibodhataḥ ..
tatretihāsaśravaṇaṃ kuryātkiñcidatandritaḥ .. 17 ..
meaning:
प्रकृतीश्च महाभाग प्रतीहारनिबोधतः ..
तत्रेतिहासश्रवणं कुर्यात्किञ्चिदतन्द्रितः .. 17 ..
text_mt:
and the subjects, O fortunate one, as announced by the doorkeeper.
There he should listen a little to historical narratives, free from indolence.

sanskrit_iast: tataḥ kāryārthināṃ kuryādyathādhīḥ kāryanirṇayam ..18..
meaning: ततः कार्यार्थिनां कुर्याद्यथाधीः कार्यनिर्णयम् ..18..
text_mt: Then, according to his intellect, he should make decisions on matters for those who seek redress.

sanskrit_iast:
vyavahārāṃstataḥ paśyetsamo bhūtvārimitrayoḥ ..
tyaktvā sabhāṃ tataḥ kuryānmantraṃ tu saha mantribhiḥ .. 19 ..
meaning:
व्यवहारांस्ततः पश्येत्समो भूत्वारिमित्रयोः ..
त्यक्त्वा सभां ततः कुर्यान्मन्त्रं तु सह मन्त्रिभिः .. 19 ..
text_mt:
He should then examine legal disputes, being impartial towards enemy and friend.
Leaving the assembly, he should then deliberate on policy with his ministers,

sanskrit_iast:
yatrāsya kaścittaṃ mantraṃ śṛṇuyānna kathañcana..
ekena saha taṃ kuryānna kuryādbahubhiḥ saha .. 2.151.20 ..
meaning:
यत्रास्य कश्चित्तं मन्त्रं शृणुयान्न कथञ्चन..
एकेन सह तं कुर्यान्न कुर्याद्बहुभिः सह .. 2.151.20 ..
text_mt:
where no one at all may hear his deliberation.
He should deliberate with one; he should not deliberate with many,

sanskrit_iast:
na ca mūrkhairna cānāmaistathā nādhārmikairnṛpaḥ ..
mantraṃ svadhiṣṭhitaṃ kuryādyena rāṣṭraṃ na dhāvati ..21..
meaning:
न च मूर्खैर्न चानामैस्तथा नाधार्मिकैर्नृपः ..
मन्त्रं स्वधिष्ठितं कुर्याद्येन राष्ट्रं न धावति ..21..
text_mt:
nor with fools, nor with unproven men, nor with the unrighteous, O king.
He should make his deliberation firmly established, so that the realm does not waver.

sanskrit_iast:
rājñāṃ vināśamūlastu kathito mantravibhramaḥ ..
nāśaheturbhavenmantraḥ kuprayuktastvamantravat .. 22 ..
meaning:
राज्ञां विनाशमूलस्तु कथितो मन्त्रविभ्रमः ..
नाशहेतुर्भवेन्मन्त्रः कुप्रयुक्तस्त्वमन्त्रवत् .. 22 ..
text_mt:
The disclosure of counsel is declared to be the root of destruction for kings.
Counsel improperly applied, like an unchanted mantra, becomes a cause of ruin.

sanskrit_iast:
maṃtre suniścite siddhiḥ kathitā pṛthivīkṣitām ..
kriyamāṇāni karmāṇi yasya vetti na kaścana .. 23 ..
meaning:
मंत्रे सुनिश्चिते सिद्धिः कथिता पृथिवीक्षिताम् ..
क्रियमाणानि कर्माणि यस्य वेत्ति न कश्चन .. 23 ..
text_mt:
When counsel is well settled, success is declared for rulers of the earth.
He whose undertakings being done no one knows,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtānyeva vijānāti sa rājā pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
pṛthak ca mantribhirmantraṃ kṛtaṃ vai saṃhitaiḥ punaḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
कृतान्येव विजानाति स राजा पृथिवीपतिः ..
पृथक् च मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रं कृतं वै संहितैः पुनः .. 24 ..
text_mt:
and knows only when they are completed, he is a king, a lord of the earth.
Counsel taken separately with the ministers, and again [with them] assembled,

2.152
Puṣkara said:
On his birth-asterism every month, the king should perform
the rite of cleansing one’s birth, which was previously spoken of by me.
The ruler of men should then perform a flower bath each month.
At a solstice or equinox, he should worship the sun and likewise the crescent moon.
The king should worship a planet that has emerged from the orb of the sun.
Likewise, worship should be performed by rulers of men at the rising of Agastya.
He should worship Madhusūdana while he sleeps for four months.
In the bright half of Proṣṭhapada, he should observe protection and worship Śatakratu.
On the ninth day of the bright half of Āśvayuja, he should worship Bhadrakālī.
When the sun reaches Svātī, he should likewise perform the lustration of arms.

At the turn of a year, he should perform a ten-million oblation offering using ghee alone. / On the anniversary of his royal consecration, he should perform the worship of Rudra. / Now these perpetual duties of the ruler of men have been spoken to you by me, O Rāma; / having performed these according to rule, the king rules the entire earth for a long time.
Rāma said: / How indeed should the worship of Keśava be performed during the four months / by an earthly king, O best of gods? Tell that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said: / A king must always be prepared, O bearer of the Bhṛgu lineage. / At the end of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, the king should take up a station
that is unassailable by hostile kingdoms, abundant in grass and firewood, / supplied with water, free of mud, and likewise untouched by the [hazards of the] rainy season,
and staying where he is able to protect his entire domain. / Staying there, the king should nourish his subjects for four months
with various kinds of fatty drinks and after-potions, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / At the end of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, after the tenth day, the ruler of men

should hold a great festival, intent on worshipping the deity. / He should then worship the god fashioned in an image or on a cloth,
Viṣṇu, full of divine delights, accompanied by Śrī, the slayer of his foes, / with various offerings, flowers, and fragrant incenses.
The king should hold a great festival for five days thereafter; / from that time onward, there should be daily worship of Vāsudeva.
O best of the Bhṛgus, through the Sāttvatas, astrologers, and royal priests, / he should especially worship the god here with songs and dances.
At this very time he should likewise perform a ten-million oblation offering, / so that its conclusion occurs on the full-moon day of Kārtika, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Then, in the final third of the bright fortnight of Kārtika, the king / should hold a very great festival as well as the worship of the God of gods.
He should worship the god Vaikuṇṭha in an image or on a cloth; / then he should give a great gift and likewise present a theatrical performance,

Having done this, an expedition is to be undertaken by kings / in the autumn season, free from anxieties, with well-nourished horses, chariots, and elephants.
And thus for four months the supreme god, the remover [of sins], is to be worshipped by the king; / and having worshipped Madhusūdana whose insignia have been laid aside, the expedition shall bestow desired success.
Rāma said: / How should the worship of Śakra be performed by a king, O best of gods, / properly in the month of Bhādrapada? Tell that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said: / Formerly the gods, broken in battle by the asuras, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / went for refuge to Brahmā, who is intent on the welfare of all beings.
To those gods, all bewildered, conquered by the Dānavas and facing slaughter, / Brahmā then spoke, [directing them] to Madhusūdana in the Ocean of Milk:
'Go all together; he will bring about your welfare.' / Having spoken thus, all the gods went to Keśava in the Ocean of Milk,

text_mt:
and then they beheld the god Vāsudeva, the teacher of the world, / resembling a cloud swollen with nectar, bearing the conch, discus, and mace.
And the thirty [gods] praised that fortunate one again and again, / the god who is the lord of all, the sole cause of the world.
The gods said: / Homage to you, O lotus-eyed one, loving toward those who come for refuge, / destroyer of the pride of the hosts of the gods' enemies, giver of happiness to the king of the thirty [gods]!
O you whose garment resembles gold, whose excellent banner bears Tārkṣya, / who sleep upon the couch of Śeṣa, darling of Lakṣmī's heart!
O you whose lotus feet are rubbed by the crest-jewels of gods and asuras, / whose lotus hands are adorned with wide-open, beautiful lotuses!
And when we were once broken by the asuras, you / were our refuge; therefore, routed by the Daityas, we have come into your presence.
Be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods! Slay those vilest of asuras, / who continually afflict us, O Lord of the gods of gods!
The Lord said: / I will give you this banner, which destroys enemies, / by the mere sight of which the Dānavas will flee here.

Illustrious Puṣkara said: / Having spoken thus, Viṣṇu gave them the peerless banner, / golden, raised high, divine, renowned as Śakra's banner.
Taking it, all the gods set out for the abode of the Dānavas. / Hearing that the gods had arrived, the Dānavas then came forth,
all with their forces well equipped and with weapons raised. / And seeing the army of the gods radiant with Śakra's banner,
they were instantly stupefied by its splendor, O fortunate one; / and being stupefied, the Daityas were then struck down by the thirty [gods].
Some, broken, fled to the directions; others entered the ocean. / Thereupon Śakra, having attained victory, worshipped that banner.
Having worshipped it, he then presented it to King Vasu; / and Vasu worshipped it according to the rule declared by Garga.
Pleased with him on account of this, Maghavan spoke these words. / Indra said: / Whatever other excellent kings [celebrate] the great festival of Śakra's banner

Famine, pestilence, disease, and fear of an enemy army— / all these perish when the festival of Śakra's banner is performed.
Puṣkara said: / From that time onward, kings, O Rāma, perform the great festival of Śakra / as declared by Garga, which destroys all fear.
Auspicious, bringing renown, destroying enemies, granting fame, and bestowing the fruits of dharma, / the festival of Śakra must be performed diligently by kings for victory; I shall describe that to you.

with garments, clean beds, and various dyes as well. / Then, having set up the place for Śakra's banner in the middle with care,
one should make an image on cloth of Maghavat on its right side.

If none of these woods is available, one should make a bamboo pole / bound with gold, O knower of dharma, and bring it properly inside.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Proṣṭhapada, O slayer of foes, / Śakra's pole is to be known as being of standard measure, O king.
Reduced by four aṅgulas at the top, it brings welfare; / having cut eight [aṅgulas] off at the base, he should cast it into water.
Having raised it up, he should enter the city; it proceeds in proper order. / At its entry, the city should be decorated with strings of flags and banners,

With houses properly worshipped, O Rāma, and with sacred trees worshipped, / the king should be followed by citizens of good families bearing fruits in their hands.
On the eighth day, to the sound of musical instruments, he should bring that pole in; / then he should set it with its tip to the east, covered with auspicious garments.
He should worship it, already revered, until that reward of the twelfth day. / On the eleventh day, fasting, the king should keep vigil,
accompanied by the astrologer, the minister, and the royal chaplain; / and a night vigil should be kept by the city people.
In various places, O fortunate one, spectacles and wine should be given; / the king should worship Śakra at night with dance and song.
On the twelfth day, having bathed his head, the king, purified and collected in mind, / should raise Śakra's banner by means of a mechanical apparatus.

text_mt:
He should secure it well within a pavilion of four pillars; / he should worship it, O fortunate one, with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, and food.
He should daily perform the worship of the two cloth images and the worship of the pole, / with various oblations and with worship of brahmins.
The royal chaplain should daily offer oblations with mantras to Śakra and Viṣṇu; / and he should daily worship Śakra with dance and song.
On the twelfth day, the king should honor the brahmins with heaps of wealth, / and especially the astrologer and the royal chaplain, O knower of dharma.
At its raising and at its entry, the king should embody Śakra / through the mantra to be spoken, accompanied by the royal chaplain who knows the right time.
He should worship the raised banner with various ornaments, / with a parasol, with garments, and with garlands and wreaths.
In this way, O Rāma, he should worship it for four days; / when the fifth day arrives, he should dismiss Śakra's banner.

text_mt:
Having worshipped it, O fortunate one, [accompanied] by the fourfold army, / having it carried by lordly elephants, he should then set the triad afloat in a river.
With a great sound of musical instruments, music is celebrated there; / the urban and rural folk should make sport in the water then, / and a great festival should be held by those assembled on the riverbank.
Having performed this rite, the king attains an increase of wealth and vehicles, / the destruction of hosts of enemies, O Rāma, and the great grace of the lord of the gods.

And cows accompanied by gold, garments, and silver must be given to foremost twice-born men; / when this is done, evil is pacified, and the ruler of men prospers.
Rāma said:
Now, what mantras should a king recite, while fasting, during the raising of Śakra['s banner]?
I wish to hear those, O best of all upholders of dharma.
Puṣkara said:
Hear completely these mantras that destroy all sins,
which a restrained king should recite when the time for raising Śakra's banner arrives:
"O best one, conqueror of Indra['s foes], friend, slayer of Vṛtra, chastiser of Pāka,
O god of gods, fortunate one, you have indeed attained growth.
You are the lord, eternal, devoted to the welfare of all beings,
of infinite splendour, free of passion, increasing fame and victory.
Though sovereign, you are always the lord; arise, O you who are worshipped by the gods!
May the self-born god Brahmā, the grandfather of all the worlds,
[and] Rudra, wielder of the Pināka, proud, praised by the two pairs [of Vedas],

and Agni, made of splendour, and the portion who is Rudra's essence, the son of Pārvatī,
Kārtikeya, bearer of the spear, six-faced, and holder of the mace,
the hundredfold, the choice, the granter of boons, the omnipresent lord, increase [your] splendour!

the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Sādhyas, the gods, and the two Aśvins,

2.158
Rāma said:
By what procedure should a ruler of men worship Bhadrakālī
on the ninth lunar day of the light fortnight in the month of Āśvina, O best of men?
Puṣkara said:
In the north-eastern direction from the military camp, in a very pleasant spot,
he should construct a house for Bhadrakālī, adorned with multicoloured cloth.
Having depicted Bhadrakālī on a cloth, the twice-born should worship her there,
with self-restraint, on the eighth lunar day in the light fortnight of Āśvina.
Right there he should worship the weapons, armour, parasol, and banner;
he should worship all the royal insignia as well as the missile weapons,
with flowers, perfumes, fruits, snacks, and most delightful foods,
and with many diverse theatrical presentations and gifts.
The ruler of the earth should keep vigil there throughout the night;
thus he should worship the goddess who grants boons and is affectionate to her devotees,

text_mt:
Kātyāyanī, who moves at will, of excellent form, who grants boons;
when worshipped, she endows the ruler of the earth with all desires.
Having thus worshipped the foremost [power] of the universe, a military march should be undertaken by the ruler of the earth;
the great lord attains supreme success, and any other person also does so according to his financial capacity.
2.159
Rāma said:
O best of virtuous beings, I wish to hear from you the rule of the lustration rite. / How should the pacification rite in the lustration be performed for a king, O lord?
Puṣkara said:
In the north-eastern direction from the city, in a very pleasant place, / the king should have a spacious and delightful shelter erected.
Enclosed with mats, strewn with kuśa grass, adorned with pennants and banners, / he should have three auspicious archways erected there, facing eastward.
An archway should be made sixteen cubits high, / and its breadth should be made ten cubits, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
To the south of the archway, he should make an enclosure / where the worship of deities and the offering into the fire may take place.

To the left, an eight-cubit long and high / heap of dry brand-sticks is to be erected, O scion of Bhṛgu’s lineage.
With five-coloured thread he should make a charming [cord] with a hundred knots, / a hundred-loop snare positioned in the middle, at the middle archway.
Having covered it with kuśa grass, he should then cover it with clay. / It must be zealously avoided from being stepped over by any creature,
so long as it has not first been crossed over by the royal elephant. / When the sun departs from Citrā and enters Svātī,
from then on it must be performed, as long as the sun remains in Svātī; / each day in the enclosure the deities must be worshipped, O best of the twice-born:
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Śakra, Fire and Wind, / Vināyaka, Kumāra, Varuṇa, Dhanada, Yama,
the Viśvedevas, O fortunate one, and Uccaiḥśravas. / The eight great elephants are to be worshipped; hear their names from me:

and the horses, O fortunate one; and then, having adorned them, / next, for the consecrated elephant and that consecrated horse,
a ball of food should then be given by the royal priest after consecrating it with mantras. / In its acceptance [of the food], the king's discipline and success are proclaimed;
in its rejection, it is to be known that a great danger has approached. / Then he should cause the elephants to go out first through the archways.
There too, first, O Rāma, having sprinkled the best of elephants— / if before it a human, or a five-clawed animal,
or any other should step over that hundred-loop cord, one should predict the king's death. / If it is crossed by cows, donkeys, or camels, famine is to be understood there.
If the royal elephant should step over it with its left foot, / it brings welfare to the king, the royal priest, the ministers, and the prince.
One should declare death for the king if another [foot] should tread upon it; / if it crosses it with the right foot, it announces victory for the king.

Rāma said: / Tell me, O sinless one, the mantras for the umbrella, the flag, the elephants, / the banner, the sword, and the armour, as well as for the kettle-drums and bows.
Puṣkara said: / Hear, O fortunate one, the mantras that the venerable Parāśara, / the foremost of all upholders of dharma, formerly spoke to Gālava.
Parāśara said: / Just as a raincloud covers this earth for its welfare, / so cover the king for the increase of victory and health.
Thus ends the mantra for the umbrella.
Parāśara said: / You are a king of the Gandharva lineage; do not become a defiler of your race! / By the truthful word of Brahmā, and of Soma and Varuṇa,

Protect your master, O lord of elephants; let the pact be observed! / Attain victory in battle, and march on our journey with blessing!

तेनान्तरिक्षं दिव्यं वा धत्ते कल्मषनाशनम् .. 12 ..

sanskrit_iast:

सर्वे तदाज्यसंस्पर्शात्प्रणाशमुपगच्छतु ..
ततो विरूक्षितं स्नातं स्नानवेद्यां नराधिपम् .. 13 ..
text_mt: May all that perish by contact with clarified butter.” / Then, the ruler of men, unctuous and bathed, [standing] on the bathing platform,

sanskrit_iast:
gacchettaṃ tu puraskṛtya sāṃvatsarapurohitau ..
snānavedī tu kartavyā lājākusumamaṇḍitā ..14 ..

गच्छेत्तं तु पुरस्कृत्य सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ ..
स्नानवेदी तु कर्तव्या लाजाकुसुममण्डिता ..14 ..
text_mt: should proceed with the astrologer and the royal priest leading the way. / A bathing platform should be constructed, adorned with parched grain and flowers,

sanskrit_iast:
caturbhiḥ pūrṇakumbhaistu vidikṣu hyupaśobhitā ..
catvāri tasyāścarmāṇi prāggrīvāṇi samāstaret .. 15 ..
meaning:
चतुर्भिः पूर्णकुम्भैस्तु विदिक्षु ह्युपशोभिता ..
चत्वारि तस्याश्चर्माणि प्राग्ग्रीवाणि समास्तरेत् .. 15 ..
text_mt: embellished with four full jars placed in the intermediate directions. / Upon it he should spread four skins with their necks to the east:

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣasya dvīpinaścaiva siṃhaśārdūlayostathā ..
bhadrāsanaṃ nyasedrāma teṣāmupari carmaṇām .. 16 ..
meaning:
वृषस्य द्वीपिनश्चैव सिंहशार्दूलयोस्तथा ..
भद्रासनं न्यसेद्राम तेषामुपरि चर्मणाम् .. 16 ..
text_mt: of a bull, a leopard, and likewise of a lion and a tiger. / O Rāma, he should place an auspicious throne upon those skins.

sanskrit_iast:
svāsīnaṃ nṛpatiṃ tatra vastrairācchādayennṛpaiḥ ..
kārpāsikaistataḥ paścādāvikaiḥ kṛmijaistataḥ .. 17 ..
meaning:
स्वासीनं नृपतिं तत्र वस्त्रैराच्छादयेन्नृपैः ..
कार्पासिकैस्ततः पश्चादाविकैः कृमिजैस्ततः .. 17 ..
text_mt: The king, seated comfortably there, he should cover with regal garments: / with cotton cloths, then woolen ones, and then silk ones.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu sarpiṣaḥ kumbhaiḥ pūrṇaistamabhiṣecayet ..
kumbhāṣṭakaṃ tu kartavyamaṣṭāviṃśatireva vā ..18 ..
meaning:
ततस्तु सर्पिषः कुम्भैः पूर्णैस्तमभिषेचयेत् ..
कुम्भाष्टकं तु कर्तव्यमष्टाविंशतिरेव वा ..18 ..
text_mt: Then he should sprinkle him with full jars of clarified butter; / eight jars should be prepared, or twenty-eight,

sanskrit_iast:
athavāṣṭaśataṃ rāma vṛddhireṣā guṇottarā ..
tatopanīya vastrāṇi tasyāṃ vedyāṃ purohitaḥ .. 19 ..
meaning:
अथवाष्टशतं राम वृद्धिरेषा गुणोत्तरा ..
ततोपनीय वस्त्राणि तस्यां वेद्यां पुरोहितः .. 19 ..
text_mt: or one hundred and eight, O Rāma—this increase brings greater excellence. / Then, taking away the garments, the royal priest on that platform

sanskrit_iast:
śūlena mṛnmayaṃ bhiṃdyācchatruṃ krodhasamanvitaḥ ..
rājñastu kalaśaṃ dattvā svayaṃ sāṃvatsarastataḥ .. 2.161.20 ..
meaning:
शूलेन मृन्मयं भिंद्याच्छत्रुं क्रोधसमन्वितः ..
राज्ञस्तु कलशं दत्त्वा स्वयं सांवत्सरस्ततः .. 2.161.20 ..
text_mt: should pierce a clay enemy with a spear, filled with wrath. / Then the astrologer himself, having given the water-jar to the king,

sanskrit_iast:
abhiṣecanamantreṇa svarcitaṃ kalpitaṃ dṛḍham ...
jyotiṣmatīṃ trāyamāṇāmabhayāmaparājitām ..21..
meaning:
अभिषेचनमन्त्रेण स्वर्चितं कल्पितं दृढम् ...
ज्योतिष्मतीं त्रायमाणामभयामपराजिताम् ..21..
text_mt: consecrated with the sprinkling mantra, well honored and firmly set— / jyotiṣmatī, trāyamāṇā, abhayā, aparājitā,

sanskrit_iast:
jīvāṃ viśveśvarīṃ pāṭhāṃ samaṃgāmabhayāṃ tathā ..
sahāṃ ca sahadevāṃ ca pūrṇakośāṃ śatāvarīm ..22..
meaning:
जीवां विश्वेश्वरीं पाठां समंगामभयां तथा ..
सहां च सहदेवां च पूर्णकोशां शतावरीम् ..22..
text_mt: jīvā, viśveśvarī, pāṭhā, samaṅgā, and likewise abhayā, / sahā, sahadevā, pūrṇakośā, śatāvarī,

sanskrit_iast:

brāhmī kṣemāmajāṃ caiva sarvabījāni kāñcanam .. 23 ..
meaning:
अरिष्टिकां शिवां भद्रां कलशं तत्र विन्यसेत् ..
ब्राह्मी क्षेमामजां चैव सर्वबीजानि काञ्चनम् .. 23 ..
text_mt: ariṣṭikā, śivā, bhadrā—he should deposit into the jar: / brāhmī, kṣemā, ajā, and all seeds, gold,

sanskrit_iast:
maṅgalyāśca yathālābhaṃ sarvauṣadhyo rasastathā ..
ratnāni sarvagandhāśca bilvaṃ ca savikaṅkatam .. 24 ..

मङ्गल्याश्च यथालाभं सर्वौषध्यो रसस्तथा ..
रत्नानि सर्वगन्धाश्च बिल्वं च सविकङ्कतम् .. 24 ..

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ snāto ghṛte dṛṣṭvā vadanaṃ tarpaṇaṃ tathā ..
maṅgalālabhanaṃ kṛtvā dhautavāsāḥ samāhitaḥ .. 25 ..
meaning:
एवं स्नातो घृते दृष्ट्वा वदनं तर्पणं तथा ..
मङ्गलालभनं कृत्वा धौतवासाः समाहितः .. 25 ..
text_mt: Thus bathed, gazing into clarified butter, making a libation, / touching auspicious objects, wearing clean garments, and concentrated in mind,

sanskrit_iast:
abhyarcanaṃ tataḥ kuryāddevādīnāṃ pṛthakpṛthak ..
teṣāmeva tato vahnau caturthyantaistu nāmabhiḥ .. 26 ..
meaning:
अभ्यर्चनं ततः कुर्याद्देवादीनां पृथक्पृथक् ..
तेषामेव ततो वह्नौ चतुर्थ्यन्तैस्तु नामभिः .. 26 ..

sanskrit_iast:

ओङ्कारपूतं जुहुयाद् घृतं बहु पुरोहितः ..
आयुधाभ्यर्चनं कार्यं वाहनाभ्यर्चनं ततः ..27 ..

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
राजचिह्नार्चनं कृत्वा ह्यलङ्कृत्य स्वकां तनुम् ..

शुभं वसनमादद्याच्छ्रीसूक्तेनाभिमंत्रितम् ..
श्रियं धातर्मयि देहि मंत्रः सुमनसां भवेत .. 29 ..

ततोनुलिप्तः सुरभिः स्रग्वी रुचिरभूषणः .. 2.161.30 ..
