tatastu rāma carmāṇi prāggrīvāṇi tu vinyaset .. 32 ..
meaning:
सिंहासनं न्यसेत्पृष्ठे भव्यास्तरणसंयुतम् ..
ततस्तु राम चर्माणि प्राग्ग्रीवाणि तु विन्यसेत् .. 32 ..
text_mt: he should place a lion throne behind, fitted with a splendid spread. / Then, O Rāma, he should arrange skins with their necks to the east:

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣasya vṛṣadaṃśasya kareśca pṛṣatasya ca ..
teṣāmupari siṃhasya vyāghrasya ca tataḥ param .. 33 ..
meaning:
वृषस्य वृषदंशस्य करेश्च पृषतस्य च ..
तेषामुपरि सिंहस्य व्याघ्रस्य च ततः परम् .. 33 ..
text_mt: of a bull, a cat, an elephant, and a spotted deer; / on top of them, a lion's skin, and after that, a tiger's.

sanskrit_iast:
dhruvā dyauriti mantreṇa nṛpaṃ tatropaveśayeta ..
darbhapāṇistato rājā tathaiva ca purohitaḥ .. 34 ..

ध्रुवा द्यौरिति मन्त्रेण नृपं तत्रोपवेशयेत ..
दर्भपाणिस्ततो राजा तथैव च पुरोहितः .. 34 ..
text_mt: With the mantra “Dhruvā dyauḥ…” he should seat the king upon it. / Then the king holding darbha grass in hand, and likewise the royal priest,

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
तयोर्हस्तगतावग्रे दर्भौ संग्रथयेद्द्विजः ..
ततः पुरोधा जुहुयाद्ब्राह्मैर्मन्त्रैर्घृतं शुचिः .. 38 ..
text_mt: the twice-born priest should knot the two pieces of darbha grass held in their hands at the tips. / Then the pure royal priest should offer clarified butter with Vedic mantras,

sanskrit_iast:

bārhaspatyaistataḥ kuryāttaṃtramuttarasaṃjakam .. 36 ..
meaning:
रौद्रवैष्णव वायव्यशाक्रसौम्यैः सवारुणैः ..
बार्हस्पत्यैस्ततः कुर्यात्तंत्रमुत्तरसंजकम् .. 36 ..
text_mt: with mantras to Rudra, Viṣṇu, Vāyu, Śakra, Soma, together with Varuṇa, / and to Bṛhaspati; then he should perform the ritual known as the northern procedure.

sanskrit_iast:
daivajñaḥ prayataḥ kuryāddevatānāṃ visarjanam ..
yāntu devagaṇāḥ sarve sānugāḥ saparicchadāḥ .. 37 ..
meaning:
दैवज्ञः प्रयतः कुर्याद्देवतानां विसर्जनम् ..

ādāya pārthivātpūjāṃ nagarāgamanāya ca ..
tatastu pūjayedrājā sāṃvatsarapurohitau .. 38 ..

text_mt: having accepted the worship from the king, in order to return to the city.” / Then the king should honor the astrologer and the royal priest,

śāntighoṣeṇa mahatā rājā kuñjaragastataḥ .. 39 ..

धनेन ब्राह्मणानां च ततो दद्याच्च दक्षिणाम् ..
मङ्गलालभनं कृत्वा खड्गपाणिर्गृहाद्व्रजेत् ..
शान्तिघोषेण महता राजा कुञ्जरगस्ततः .. 39 ..
text_mt: and should then bestow a sacrificial fee of wealth upon the brahmins. / Touching auspicious objects, sword in hand, the king should depart from the building, / mounted upon an elephant, amidst a great proclamation of peace.

text_mt:
This propitiatory rite has been declared by me to you, O heroic ruler, auspicious, granting fame, destroying enemies, / bringing happiness, promoting the prosperity of the realm, and yielding growth of dharma, to be performed by kings.
2.162
Rāma said:
Tell me also about the annual consecration of the ruler of the earth.
I have a doubt regarding that, O god, for you perceive everything.
Puṣkara said:
Every year, on the asterism of the king's consecration,
a twice-born should perform the consecration according to the rite of the previous consecration.
The annual consecration of the king is proclaimed to bring fortune, renown, the destruction of enemies, / bestow good luck, enhance prosperity, bring happiness, and promote the growth of the kingdom.
2.163
Rāma said: / O Blessed One, knower of all dharma, foremost among those who know all treatises, / tell me the proper timing for the military expeditions of kings.
Puṣkara said:
When the king considers that the ally in the rear is overpowered
by a stronger rear-invader, then he should undertake a campaign.

text_mt:
[When he thinks,] "My dependents are well-nourished, fed, and supported, and my army is abundant;
I am capable of protecting the base," then he should undertake a campaign.
Or he may depart after stationing an army at his base superior to the rear-invader.
The king should undertake a campaign in either Caitra or Mārgaśīrṣa.
For in Caitra, it destroys the autumn harvest, beginning with the spring crop, and impairs prosperity.
The opposite is true in Mārgaśīrṣa, O ruler of men.
Or he should go during an enemy's calamity, for such a time is very difficult to find;
[or against an enemy] heavily afflicted by celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial portents,
consumed by the affliction of six lunar mansions, and likewise afflicted by the planets;
or towards whichever direction meteors blaze and fall.
Toward whichever direction an earthquake travels, and which a comet envelops in smoke,
and where a thunderclap is heard, the ruler of the earth should march.
Against an enemy who is beset by calamity among his own troops, afflicted by famine,
and whose internal dissension has broken out, the king should march swiftly.

Full of lice and flies, full of obstacles, like a hollow burrow,
atheistic, violating propriety, yet professing auspiciousness,
deserted by his subjects, and despairing—he should conquer such a one;
likewise an army led by pressed laborers and mutually divided.
A king should direct his force against a monarch devoted to vice.
He should set out from behind, O knower of dharma, but when bad omens appear ahead,
[such as] "Where are you going? Stop, do not go, what is the use of going there?"
and whatever other such words are heard, they bring about misfortune.
Likewise, the perching of carnivorous beasts on banners and such is reprehensible;
so also the stumbling of conveyances and the catching of garments,
and bumping one's head upon exiting through doors and gateways;
and the falling of umbrellas, banners, garments, and the like is inauspicious.
Seeing a first inauspicious omen that portends destruction,
the wise man should worship Keśava, the slayer of Madhu.

text_mt:
Faith in the sacred, trust, and the worship of those worthy of worship—
these are recommended, O knower of dharma, and whatever is pleasing to the mind.
Satisfaction of the mind alone is the supreme sign of victory here:
on one side are all the signs, and on the other is the mind's satisfaction.
Eagerness to depart, gladness of mind, the obtaining of good dreams, tranquility of the mind, / and the receiving and hearing of auspicious things, O Rāma, are always to be known as bringing victory.
Puṣkara said:
Omens indicate the good and bad fortune of a man who is staying,
departing, or asking a question, as well as of a region and a city.
[The sign affects] a traveler on the road, a king in an army, a solar ray indicating a deity,
a leader in a caravan, and, when equals are present, the one superior in lineage, learning, or age.
An inflamed [omen] is considered to bear the fruit of all evil, while a peaceful one bears good fruit.
Six kinds of inflammation are prescribed for omens:
Time, direction, place, action, and division of species;
each preceding one among these is to be known as more powerful.

text_mt:
A diurnal animal moving at night, and likewise a nocturnal animal moving by day, / belongs to the fierce, time-blazed class, in cases of restraint by malefic asterisms and the like.
That [direction] to which the sun will proceed is known as 'smoky'; / that in which it stands is 'blazing', and that which it has left is considered 'charcoal-like'.
These three are remembered as blazed; the other five are peaceful. / A bird in a blazed direction is declared direction-blazed.
A wild [creature] in an inhabited place, a domestic one in the forest, and likewise [one situated] upon a censured tree / and in an inauspicious region, is to be known as place-blazed, O best of the twice-born.
One performing an action inappropriate to its own kind is designated action-blazed. / Then, one that emits an unnatural and dreadful cry is declared blazed [by voice].
Likewise, one that eats only meat is to be known as counter-blazed. / The blazed and the peaceful are designated and proclaimed according to all these varieties.
One is designated mixed or unmixed; from that, its effect must be declared in terms of strength. / Cattle, horses, camels, donkeys, dogs, starlings, house lizards, / musk-shrews, and bats are declared village-dwellers.

कुलालकुक्कुटश्येनफांटवं जलवानराः .. 14 ..

तित्तिरिः शतपत्रश्च कपोताश्च तथा त्रयः .. 15 ..
खञ्जरीटकदात्यूह शुकाण्डीवहतिक्तकाः ..
भारद्वाजश्च सारङ्गः इति ज्ञेया दिवाचराः .. 16 ..
वल्गुल्युलूकः शशका शरभोत्क्रोशपिच्छलौ ..
माषिका पिङ्गली काकः कथिता रात्रिचारिणः .. 17 ..
हंसाजमृगमार्जारनकुलर्क्ष भुजङ्गमाः ..

श्वावित्पृथुतगोमायुघृतकोकिलसारसाः ..
तुरङ्गमो द्वीपिनराश्चोरा उभयचारिणः ..19..
text_mt:
Goats, sheep, parrots, elephants, donkeys, buffaloes, and crows / are designated both village and forest animals; all others range in the forest.
A cat [living with people] is domestic, whereas another ranges in the forest. / All [such creatures] are to be understood in this way, always according to differences in appearance.
The green woodpecker, peacock, ruddy goose, and those that are green pigeons and crows, / the crane, cock, falcon, francolin, water monkeys,
the goshawk, sparrow, black robin, roller, vulture, grey partridge, / the francolin partridge, woodpecker, and likewise three kinds of doves,
the wagtail, watercock, parrot, cuckoo, yellow tit, / the skylark, and the pied cuckoo: these are to be known as diurnal.
The bat, owl, hare, fabulously-horned beast, curlew, picchala bird, / the mouse, owlet, and raven are declared nocturnal wanderers.
Swans, goats, deer, cats, mongooses, bears, serpents, / the wolf, lion, tiger, camel, dog, boar, and horse,
the porcupine, large jackal, wild dog, butter-cuckoo, cranes, / the horse, leopard, men, and thieves wander at both times.

meaning:
रणप्रस्थानयोः सर्वे पुरस्तात्सङ्गचारिणः ..
जयावहा विनिर्दिष्टाः पश्चाद्विजयकारिणः ..2.164.20..
गृहे गम्यो यदा चायं व्याहरेत्पुरतः स्थितः ..
नृपावमानं वदति वामः कलहभोजने ..21..
याने तद्दर्शनं धन्यं सपतङ्गस्य चाप्यथ ..
चौरैर्दोषमथाख्याति मयूरो भिन्ननिःस्वनः .. ..22..
वमते कपिलः श्रेष्ठः तथा दक्षिणसंस्थितः ..
पृष्ठतो निन्दितफलः तित्तिरिस्तत्र शस्यते .. 23 ..

text_mt:
In battle and setting out, all those moving together in front / are declared to bring victory; [moving] behind, they produce victory.
When this [creature] is to be approached at a house and cries out standing in front, / it indicates insult from a king; on the left, [it indicates] a dispute over food.
Its sight during travel is auspicious, as well as [when accompanied] with a bird. / A peacock with a broken cry declares trouble caused by thieves.
If a brown [animal] vomits, it is most excellent, and likewise when situated on the right; / behind, its fruit is censured, [but] a partridge is praised there.
Blackbucks, boars, and spotted deer, having moved from the left to the right, / always produce wealth; reversed, they are censured.
Wolves, jackals, tigers, lions, cats, and donkeys, / going from the right side to the left side, are to be known as granting desired goals.
The female jackal, blackbird, civet, shrew, owlet, house lizards, / sow, cuckoo, and those with masculine names are auspicious on the left.
Those named with śrī, the blue jay, barking deer, monkey, śrīkarṇa, chikkara, / the monkey, śrīkarṇa, pippīkā, ruru deer, and falcons are auspicious on the right.

sanskrit_iast:
jāhakāhiśaśakroḍagodhānāṃ kīrtanaṃ śubham ..
tataḥ sandarśanaṃ neṣṭaṃ pratīpaṃ vānararkṣayoḥ .. 28 ..
phalakṛtpūrvaśakunaḥ prasthitasya ca yonvaham ..
bhavettasya phalaṃ vānyattadeva divasaṃ budhaiḥ .. 29 ..
mattā bhikṣārthino bālā viraktābhāstathaiva ca ..
sīmāntanadyantaritā vijñeyā niṣphalā dvija .. 2.164.30 ..
ekadvitricaturbhistu śivā dhanyā tato bhavet ..
pañcabhiśca tathā ṣaḍbhiradhanyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 31 ..
saptabhiśca tathā dhanyā niṣphalā parato bhavet ..
nṛṇāṃ romāñcajananī vāhanānāṃ bhayapradā.. 32 ..
jvālānanā sūryamukhī vijñeyā bhayavardhinī ..
prathamaṃ śārṅgake dṛṣṭe śubhe deśe śubhaṃ vadet .. 33 ..
saṃvatsaraṃ manuṣyasya hyaśubhe cāśubhaṃ tathā ..
yathāvidhi naraḥ paśyañchakunaṃ prathamehani .. 34 ..
meaning:
जाहकाहिशशक्रोडगोधानां कीर्तनं शुभम् ..
ततः सन्दर्शनं नेष्टं प्रतीपं वानरर्क्षयोः .. 28 ..
फलकृत्पूर्वशकुनः प्रस्थितस्य च योन्वहम् ..
भवेत्तस्य फलं वान्यत्तदेव दिवसं बुधैः .. 29 ..
मत्ता भिक्षार्थिनो बाला विरक्ताभास्तथैव च ..
सीमान्तनद्यन्तरिता विज्ञेया निष्फला द्विज .. 2.164.30 ..
एकद्वित्रिचतुर्भिस्तु शिवा धन्या ततो भवेत् ..
पञ्चभिश्च तथा षड्भिरधन्याः परिकीर्तिताः .. 31 ..
सप्तभिश्च तथा धन्या निष्फला परतो भवेत् ..
नृणां रोमाञ्चजननी वाहनानां भयप्रदा.. 32 ..
ज्वालानना सूर्यमुखी विज्ञेया भयवर्धिनी ..
प्रथमं शार्ङ्गके दृष्टे शुभे देशे शुभं वदेत् .. 33 ..
संवत्सरं मनुष्यस्य ह्यशुभे चाशुभं तथा ..
यथाविधि नरः पश्यञ्छकुनं प्रथमेहनि .. 34 ..
text_mt:
Mentioning the hedgehog, serpent, hare, boar, and monitor lizard is auspicious; / the sight of them is not desired; the opposite applies to the monkey and bear.
An initial omen brings result for one who has departed day after day; / its result, or another, should be known by the wise on that very day.
The intoxicated, beggars, children, and likewise those appearing disaffected, / or those separated by a boundary or river, O twice-born, are to be known as fruitless.
A female jackal howling once, twice, thrice, or four times is fortunate; / howling five or six times, they are declared unfortunate.
Howling seven times, she is fortunate; beyond that, she is fruitless. / She causes horripilation in men and inflicts fear upon horses and mounts.
Flashing flames from her mouth and facing the sun, she must be known as increasing dread. / When a śārṅgaka is first seen in an auspicious place, one should predict good
for a human being for a year; and in an inauspicious place, likewise evil. / A person observing an omen according to rule on the first day [of the year]

sanskrit_iast:
ātmanaśca tathā tena jñātavyaṃ vatsaraṃ phalam ..
śārṅgaka ca naro dṛṣṭvā bhujaṅgamaśirogataḥ .. 35 ..
avaśyaṃ tadavāpnoti yatkiñcinmanasecchati ..
viśanti yena mārgeṇa vāyasā bahavaḥ param .. 36 ..
tena mārgeṇa vai tasya purasya grahaṇaṃ bhavet ..
senāyāṃ yadi vāsārthe viniṣṭo vāyaso bhavet .. 37 ..
vāso bhayāya rātrastho bhayaṃ vadati dustaram ..
chāyāṅgavāhanopānacchatravastrādikuṇṭhanaiḥ .. 38 ..
mṛtyustatpūjane pūjā tadviṣṭhākaraṇe śubham ..
proṣitāgamakṛtkākaḥ kurvandvāri gatāgatam .. 39 ..
raktaṃ dagdhaṃ gṛhe dravyaṃ vikṣapanvahnivedakaḥ ..
nyasedrajaṃ purastāccennivedayati bandhanam .. 2.164.40 ..

आत्मनश्च तथा तेन ज्ञातव्यं वत्सरं फलम् ..
शार्ङ्गक च नरो दृष्ट्वा भुजङ्गमशिरोगतः .. 35 ..
अवश्यं तदवाप्नोति यत्किञ्चिन्मनसेच्छति ..
विशन्ति येन मार्गेण वायसा बहवः परम् .. 36 ..
तेन मार्गेण वै तस्य पुरस्य ग्रहणं भवेत् ..
सेनायां यदि वासार्थे विनिष्टो वायसो भवेत् .. 37 ..
वासो भयाय रात्रस्थो भयं वदति दुस्तरम् ..
छायाङ्गवाहनोपानच्छत्रवस्त्रादिकुण्ठनैः .. 38 ..
मृत्युस्तत्पूजने पूजा तद्विष्ठाकरणे शुभम् ..
प्रोषितागमकृत्काकः कुर्वन्द्वारि गतागतम् .. 39 ..
रक्तं दग्धं गृहे द्रव्यं विक्षपन्वह्निवेदकः ..
न्यसेद्रजं पुरस्ताच्चेन्निवेदयति बन्धनम् .. 2.164.40 ..
text_mt:
should thereby know the fruit for himself for that year. / If a man sees a śārṅgaka perched on the head of a serpent,
he surely obtains whatever he desires in his mind. / By whatever path many crows enter exceedingly,
by that path indeed the capture of that city will take place. / If a crow enters an army seeking an abode,
its stay leads to danger; resting at night, it indicates insurmountable fear. / By dulling one's shadow, limbs, vehicles, shoes, parasol, garments, and the like,
it causes death; if it performs worship, [it brings] honor; if it drops excrement on them, it is auspicious. / A crow moving to and fro at the door indicates the arrival of one who has journeyed abroad.
Scattering a red or burnt object in a house, it announces fire; / if it places dust before [someone], it indicates imprisonment.

sanskrit_iast:
pītadravyaṃ tathā rukmaṃ rūpyaṃ śvetaṃ tu bhārgava ..
yaścaivopalabheddravyaṃ tasya labdhiṃ vinirdiśet .. 41 ..
meaning:
पीतद्रव्यं तथा रुक्मं रूप्यं श्वेतं तु भार्गव ..
यश्चैवोपलभेद्द्रव्यं तस्य लब्धिं विनिर्दिशेत् .. 41 ..
text_mt: A yellow object indicates gold, whereas a white one indicates silver, O descendant of Bhṛgu; / and whatever object it obtains, one should predict the gain thereof.

sanskrit_iast:
dravyaṃ copanayedyattu tasya hāniṃ dvijottama ..
parato dhanalabdhiḥ syādrāma māṃsasya bhakṣaṇe .. 42 ..
meaning:
द्रव्यं चोपनयेद्यत्तु तस्य हानिं द्विजोत्तम ..
परतो धनलब्धिः स्याद्राम मांसस्य भक्षणे .. 42 ..
text_mt: And whatever object it carries off, O best of the twice-born, indicates loss of that thing. / If it eats meat, Rama, gain of wealth from another will ensue.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīlabdhiḥ syānmṛgakṣepe rājyaṃ ratnārpaṇe mahat ..
yātuḥ kākonukūlasthaḥ kṣepyaḥ karṇasamo bhavet .. 43 ..
meaning:
श्रीलब्धिः स्यान्मृगक्षेपे राज्यं रत्नार्पणे महत् ..
यातुः काकोनुकूलस्थः क्षेप्यः कर्णसमो भवेत् .. 43 ..
text_mt: If it drops a dead animal, there is gain of fortune; if it presents a jewel, a great kingdom. / A crow positioned favorably for a traveler, hovering level with his ears,

sanskrit_iast: nanvarthasādhako jñeyaḥ pratikūlo bhayāvahaḥ .. 44 ..
meaning: नन्वर्थसाधको ज्ञेयः प्रतिकूलो भयावहः .. 44 ..
text_mt: is truly to be known as accomplishing his goal; unfavorable, it brings danger.

sanskrit_iast:
samukho'bhyeti vitataḥ yātrāghātakaro bhavet ..
vāmaḥ kākaḥ smṛto dhanyo dakṣiṇastu vināśakṛt .. 45 ..
meaning:
समुखोऽभ्येति विततः यात्राघातकरो भवेत् ..
वामः काकः स्मृतो धन्यो दक्षिणस्तु विनाशकृत् .. 45 ..
text_mt: Coming directly toward one with wings outspread, it strikes down the expedition. / A crow on the left is remembered as fortunate, but on the right it causes ruin.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmo'nulomagaḥ preṣṭho madhyamo dakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
pratilomakṛtirvāmo gamanapratiṣedhakṛt .. .. 46 ..
meaning:
वामोऽनुलोमगः प्रेष्ठो मध्यमो दक्षिणः स्मृतः ..
प्रतिलोमकृतिर्वामो गमनप्रतिषेधकृत् .. .. 46 ..
text_mt: On the left and moving in the natural direction, it is most beloved; on the right, it is considered middling. / Moving against the natural direction on the left, it forbids departing.

sanskrit_iast:
nivedayati yātrārthamabhipretaṃ gṛhe rataḥ ..
ekākṣicaraṇastvarka vakṣyamāṇo bhayāvahaḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
निवेदयति यात्रार्थमभिप्रेतं गृहे रतः ..
एकाक्षिचरणस्त्वर्क वक्ष्यमाणो भयावहः .. 47 ..
text_mt: Sporting upon a house, it indicates the attainment of one's desire for the expedition. / A crow having one eye and one foot, to be described [hereafter], brings dread.

sanskrit_iast:
koṭare vāsamānastu mahānarthakaro bhavet ..
na śubhaḥ sūkare kākaḥ paṅkāntaḥ sa tu dṛśyate .. 48 ..
meaning:
कोटरे वासमानस्तु महानर्थकरो भवेत् ..
न शुभः सूकरे काकः पङ्कान्तः स तु दृश्यते .. 48 ..
text_mt: Cawing inside a tree hollow, it brings great disaster. / A crow upon a boar is not auspicious, but it is seen in mud.

sanskrit_iast:
amedhyapūrṇavadanaḥ kākaḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ ..
jñeyāḥ patatriṇo'nyemī kākavadbhṛgunandana .. .. 49..
meaning:
अमेध्यपूर्णवदनः काकः सर्वार्थसाधकः ..
ज्ञेयाः पतत्रिणोऽन्येमी काकवद्भृगुनन्दन .. .. 49..
text_mt: A crow whose mouth is full of impure matter accomplishes all purposes. / These other birds are to be known as behaving like the crow, O delight of the Bhṛgus.

sanskrit_iast:
skandādau rāma savyasthāḥ śvāno ripuvināśakāḥ ..
indrasthāne narendrasya pureśasya tu gopure .. 2.164.50 ..
meaning:
स्कन्दादौ राम सव्यस्थाः श्वानो रिपुविनाशकाः ..
इन्द्रस्थाने नरेन्द्रस्य पुरेशस्य तु गोपुरे .. 2.164.50 ..
text_mt: O Rāma, dogs situated on the left at the shoulder and the like destroy enemies; / in the abode of Indra, [they indicate death] of the king, but at the gatehouse, of the lord of the city.

sanskrit_iast:
antargṛhe gṛheśasya maraṇāya bhavedbhṛśam ..
yasya vrajati vāmāṅgaṃ tasya syāddīrghasiddhaye .. 51 ..
meaning:
अन्तर्गृहे गृहेशस्य मरणाय भवेद्भृशम् ..
यस्य व्रजति वामाङ्गं तस्य स्याद्दीर्घसिद्धये .. 51 ..
text_mt: Inside the house, it brings certain death to the master of the house. / If it approaches someone's left side, it leads to long-lasting success for him.

sanskrit_iast:
bhayāya dakṣiṇaṃ cāṃgaṃ tathā bhujamadakṣiṇam ..
yātrāghātakaro yastu harṣaṃ prati mukhāgataḥ .. 52 ..
meaning:
भयाय दक्षिणं चांगं तथा भुजमदक्षिणम् ..
यात्राघातकरो यस्तु हर्षं प्रति मुखागतः .. 52 ..
text_mt: To the right side, it brings danger, and likewise to the right arm. / But one that approaches from the front towards joy impedes an expedition.

sanskrit_iast:
mārgāvarodhako mārge caurastudati bhārgava ..
alātāsthimukhaḥ pāpo rajjumīramukhastathā .. 53 ..
meaning:
मार्गावरोधको मार्गे चौरस्तुदति भार्गव ..
अलातास्थिमुखः पापो रज्जुमीरमुखस्तथा .. 53 ..
text_mt: One that blocks the way on the road, O descendant of Bhṛgu, portends that a thief will harass [the traveller]. / A dog with an ember or a bone in its mouth is inauspicious, as is one with a rope in its mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
sopānatkamukho dhanyo māṃsapūrṇamukho'pi ca ..
amaṅgalyamatha dravyaṃ deśaṃ caivāśubhaṃ tathā .. 54 ..
meaning:
सोपानत्कमुखो धन्यो मांसपूर्णमुखोऽपि च ..
अमङ्गल्यमथ द्रव्यं देशं चैवाशुभं तथा .. 54 ..
text_mt: One with a shoe in its mouth brings fortune, as does one whose mouth is full of meat. / If [a dog] urinates on an inauspicious object or an unholy place,

sanskrit_iast:
avamūlyāgrato yāti yātasya na bhayaṃ bhavet ..
tathāvamūttyāṃ vrajati śubhaṃ deśaṃ tathā kramam .. 55 ..
meaning:
अवमूल्याग्रतो याति यातस्य न भयं भवेत् ..
तथावमूत्त्यां व्रजति शुभं देशं तथा क्रमम् .. 55 ..
text_mt: and then moves forward, there will be no danger for the traveller. / Likewise, if it urinates upon and proceeds to an auspicious place in due order,

sanskrit_iast:
maṅgalyaṃ ca tathā dravyaṃ tasya syādarthasiddhaye ..
evañca rāma vijñeyāstathā vai jambukādayaḥ .. 56 ..
meaning:
मङ्गल्यं च तथा द्रव्यं तस्य स्यादर्थसिद्धये ..
एवञ्च राम विज्ञेयास्तथा वै जम्बुकादयः .. 56 ..
text_mt: and likewise an auspicious object, it will lead to the accomplishment of his goal. / In this way, O Rāma, jackals and others are likewise to be understood.

sanskrit_iast:
bhayāya svāmino jñeyā animittabhayaṃ gavām ..
niśi caurabhayāya syādvikṛtaṃ mṛtyave tathā .. 97 ..
meaning:
भयाय स्वामिनो ज्ञेया अनिमित्तभयं गवाम् ..
निशि चौरभयाय स्याद्विकृतं मृत्यवे तथा .. 97 ..
text_mt: Cows' unprovoked fear is known to bring danger to their master. / At night, it indicates fear of thieves, and if unnatural, it portends death.

sanskrit_iast:
śivāya svāmino rātrau balīvardo nadanbhavet ..
utsṛṣṭavṛṣabho rājño vijayaṃ saṃprayacchati ..58..
meaning:
शिवाय स्वामिनो रात्रौ बलीवर्दो नदन्भवेत् ..
उत्सृष्टवृषभो राज्ञो विजयं संप्रयच्छति ..58..
text_mt: An ox bellowing at night is for the welfare of its master. / A bull set free bestows victory upon the king.

sanskrit_iast:
abhakṣyaṃ bhakṣyayantaśca gāvo nyāsastathāmbakān ..
tyaktasnehāśca vatseṣu gavāṃ kṣayakaro mataḥ .. 59 ..
meaning:
अभक्ष्यं भक्ष्ययन्तश्च गावो न्यासस्तथाम्बकान् ..
त्यक्तस्नेहाश्च वत्सेषु गवां क्षयकरो मतः .. 59 ..
text_mt: Cows eating what is not to be eaten, [...] their eyes, / and abandoning affection for their calves, are considered to bring destruction to the herd.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmiṃ pādairvinirhatya dīnā bhūtā vikāraṇāt ..
anyonyalagnapucchāśca gāvo bhayakarā matāḥ..2.164.60..
meaning:
भूमिं पादैर्विनिर्हत्य दीना भूता विकारणात् ..
अन्योन्यलग्नपुच्छाश्च गावो भयकरा मताः..2.164.60..
text_mt: Pounding the ground with their hooves, becoming wretched without cause, / and with their tails tangled together, cows are considered to cause danger.

sanskrit_iast:
ārdrāṅgā hṛṣṭaromāśca praviśantyastathā gṛham ..
śṛṅgalagnamṛdo vāpi vijñeyāḥ svāmivṛddhaye .. 61 ..
meaning:
आर्द्राङ्गा हृष्टरोमाश्च प्रविशन्त्यस्तथा गृहम् ..
शृङ्गलग्नमृदो वापि विज्ञेयाः स्वामिवृद्धये .. 61 ..
text_mt: Entering the house with wet limbs and bristling hair, / or with mud clinging to their horns, they are known to bring prosperity to their master.

sanskrit_iast:
mahiṣyādiṣu cāpyetatsarvaṃ vācyaṃ vijānatā ..
netranāsāpuṭaprothaskaṃdhasyāsanamūrdhasu .. 62 ..
meaning:
महिष्यादिषु चाप्येतत्सर्वं वाच्यं विजानता ..
नेत्रनासापुटप्रोथस्कंधस्यासनमूर्धसु .. 62 ..
text_mt: All this must also be pronounced for buffalo cows and others by one who knows. / In the eyes, nostrils, muzzle, shoulders, seat, and head,

sanskrit_iast:
hayānāṃ jvalanaṃ śastamatonyatra praśasyate ..
sarvāṅgajvalanaṃ neṣṭaṃ tathā dhūmasamuddhavaḥ .. 63 ..
meaning:
हयानां ज्वलनं शस्तमतोन्यत्र प्रशस्यते ..
सर्वाङ्गज्वलनं नेष्टं तथा धूमसमुद्धवः .. 63 ..
text_mt: a glowing of horses is commendable; otherwise it is not praised. / A burning of all the limbs is not desired, nor is the rising of smoke,

sanskrit_iast:
visphuliṅgodbhavaścaiva śakṛtyāṃ svaśanaṃ tathā ..
ārohaṇaṃ tathānyena saparyāṇasya vājinaḥ .. 64 ..
meaning:
विस्फुलिङ्गोद्भवश्चैव शकृत्यां स्वशनं तथा ..
आरोहणं तथान्येन सपर्याणस्य वाजिनः .. 64 ..
text_mt: nor the emission of sparks, nor [a horse] smelling its own dung, / nor the mounting of a saddled steed by another [horse].

sanskrit_iast:
jalopaveśanaṃ neṣṭaṃ bhūmau ca parivartanam ..
vipatkalpataraṅgasya svato vāpyanimittataḥ .. 65 ..
meaning:
जलोपवेशनं नेष्टं भूमौ च परिवर्तनम् ..
विपत्कल्पतरङ्गस्य स्वतो वाप्यनिमित्ततः .. 65 ..
text_mt: Sitting down in water is not desired, nor rolling on the ground, / nor disaster to a horse of noble pedigree, whether spontaneously or without apparent cause.

sanskrit_iast:
yavasodakayordveṣastvakasmāccaiva śasyate ..
krītaḥ kākaiḥ kapotairvā śārikābhisturaṅgamaḥ .. 66 ..
meaning:
यवसोदकयोर्द्वेषस्त्वकस्माच्चैव शस्यते ..
क्रीतः काकैः कपोतैर्वा शारिकाभिस्तुरङ्गमः .. 66 ..
text_mt: Aversion to grass and water, especially all of a sudden, is not commended. / A horse beset by crows, pigeons, or mynas,

sanskrit_iast:
ātmanaḥ svāmino vāpi tadā maraṇavedakaḥ ..
duḥkhārtadhyānaśīlaśca sāśrunetro bhayāvahaḥ .. 67 ..
meaning:
आत्मनः स्वामिनो वापि तदा मरणवेदकः ..
दुःखार्तध्यानशीलश्च साश्रुनेत्रो भयावहः .. 67 ..
text_mt: then portends the death of itself or of its master. / One addicted to gloomy brooding and with tearful eyes brings danger.

sanskrit_iast:
jihvayā leḍhi caraṇamasāvapi bhayaṅkaraḥ ..
nirnimittaṃ patati vā tadā syānnṛṣu vṛddhaye .. 68 ..
meaning:
जिह्वया लेढि चरणमसावपि भयङ्करः ..
निर्निमित्तं पतति वा तदा स्यान्नृषु वृद्धये .. 68 ..
text_mt: If it licks its foot with its tongue, it is also terrifying. / If it falls without cause, then it leads to [loss of] prosperity among men.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmapādena ca tathā vilikhaṃśca vasundharām ..
svenaiva vāmapārśvena divā vā na śubhapradaḥ .. 69 ..
meaning:
वामपादेन च तथा विलिखंश्च वसुन्धराम् ..
स्वेनैव वामपार्श्वेन दिवा वा न शुभप्रदः .. 69 ..
text_mt: Scratching the earth with its left foot, / or lying on its left side during the day, does not bestow good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
pravepamānā hreṣante rodante ca muhurmuhuḥ ..
śakṛnmūtre vimuñcanto vedayanti mahadbhayam .. 2.164.70 ..
meaning:
प्रवेपमाना ह्रेषन्ते रोदन्ते च मुहुर्मुहुः ..
शकृन्मूत्रे विमुञ्चन्तो वेदयन्ति महद्भयम् .. 2.164.70 ..
text_mt: Trembling, neighing, weeping repeatedly, / and voiding dung and urine, they announce great danger.

sanskrit_iast:
uttiṣṭhanto niṣīdantaḥ sandhyāyāṃ dīnamānasāḥ ..
srastāḥ sāsrāśca dīnāśca hreṣamāṇā bhayāvahāḥ .. 71 ..
meaning:
उत्तिष्ठन्तो निषीदन्तः सन्ध्यायां दीनमानसाः ..
स्रस्ताः सास्राश्च दीनाश्च ह्रेषमाणा भयावहाः .. 71 ..
text_mt: Rising up and sitting down at twilight with dejected minds, / drooping, tearful, miserable, and neighing, they bring danger.

sanskrit_iast:
hreṣatastu yadā jvālā jyotsnā vā mukhato bhavet ..
tadā vijayamākhyāti svāmino dhruvameva hi .. 72 ..
meaning:
ह्रेषतस्तु यदा ज्वाला ज्योत्स्ना वा मुखतो भवेत् ..
तदा विजयमाख्याति स्वामिनो ध्रुवमेव हि .. 72 ..
text_mt: When a flame or moonlight appears from the mouth of a neighing [horse], / then indeed it definitely announces victory for its master.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇena padā bhūmiṃ vikirañjayavardhanaḥ ..
rātrau dakṣiṇapārśvena prasvapaṃśca narottama .. 73 ..
meaning:
दक्षिणेन पदा भूमिं विकिरञ्जयवर्धनः ..
रात्रौ दक्षिणपार्श्वेन प्रस्वपंश्च नरोत्तम .. 73 ..
text_mt: Scattering the earth with its right foot, it increases victory, / as it does when sleeping on its right side at night, O best of men.

sanskrit_iast:
ārohaṇaṃ nave dadyātpratīpaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vrajet ..
yātrāvighātamācaṣṭe vāmaṃ pādaṃ tathā spṛśan .. 74 ..
meaning:
आरोहणं नवे दद्यात्प्रतीपं वा गृहं व्रजेत् ..
यात्राविघातमाचष्टे वामं पादं तथा स्पृशन् .. 74 ..
text_mt: If it should not allow mounting anew, or should turn back towards home, / or if it touches its left foot, it announces the obstruction of the expedition.

sanskrit_iast:
anulomaṃ yadā yāti purastātpratihreṣite ..
dakṣiṇaṃ vā tathā pārśvaṃ mukhenopari mārjati ..75..
meaning:
अनुलोमं यदा याति पुरस्तात्प्रतिह्रेषिते ..
दक्षिणं वा तथा पार्श्वं मुखेनोपरि मार्जति ..75..
text_mt: When it moves smoothly forward while neighing in front, / or wipes its right flank above with its mouth,

sanskrit_iast:
,preritastvanukūlena pavanena raṇe hayaḥ ..
hreṣamāṇaḥ parānyāti tadā syādvijayāvahaḥ .. 76 ..
meaning:
,प्रेरितस्त्वनुकूलेन पवनेन रणे हयः ..
ह्रेषमाणः परान्याति तदा स्याद्विजयावहः .. 76 ..
text_mt: and impelled by a favourable wind in battle, the horse / advances neighing against the enemies, then it brings victory.

sanskrit_iast:
grāme vrajati nāgaścenmaithunaṃ deśahā bhavet ..
prasūtā nāgavanitā mattā cāntāya bhūpateḥ .. 77 ..
meaning:
ग्रामे व्रजति नागश्चेन्मैथुनं देशहा भवेत् ..
प्रसूता नागवनिता मत्ता चान्ताय भूपतेः .. 77 ..
text_mt: If an elephant enters a village and mates, it will destroy the country. / A female elephant giving birth while in rut leads to the destruction of the king.

sanskrit_iast:
dantabhaṅge śubhe deśe drume vā bhayavardhanaḥ ..
krūreṣu velālagneṣu tathā rāma viśeṣataḥ .. 78 .. .
meaning:
दन्तभङ्गे शुभे देशे द्रुमे वा भयवर्धनः ..
क्रूरेषु वेलालग्नेषु तथा राम विशेषतः .. 78 .. .
text_mt: If its tusk breaks in an auspicious place or against a tree, it increases danger, / especially, O Rāma, during cruel astrological moments and ascendants.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇḍūṣadhāraṇaṃ kṛtvā vaktrabhāge tu dakṣiṇe ..
hastaṃ gṛhītvā hastena nāgasyānyasya vā punaḥ .. 79 ..
meaning:
गण्डूषधारणं कृत्वा वक्त्रभागे तु दक्षिणे ..
हस्तं गृहीत्वा हस्तेन नागस्यान्यस्य वा पुनः .. 79 ..
text_mt: Holding a mouthful of water on the right side of its mouth, / or grasping with its trunk the trunk of another elephant,

sanskrit_iast:
uccairvā karamunnamya viṣāṇe vātha dakṣiṇe ..
gambhīraṃ śrotramadhuraṃ rājñastadvijayāvaham .. 2.164.80 ..
meaning:
उच्चैर्वा करमुन्नम्य विषाणे वाथ दक्षिणे ..
गम्भीरं श्रोत्रमधुरं राज्ञस्तद्विजयावहम् .. 2.164.80 ..
text_mt: or raising its trunk high, or touching its right tusk, / [trumpeting] deep and sweet to the ear, brings victory to the king.

sanskrit_iast:
atonyathā viparyastaṃ tvaśubhaṃ parikīrtitam ..
arohaṇaṃ na ceddadyātpratīpaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vrajet ..81..
meaning:
अतोन्यथा विपर्यस्तं त्वशुभं परिकीर्तितम् ..
अरोहणं न चेद्दद्यात्प्रतीपं वा गृहं व्रजेत् ..81..
text_mt: The reverse of this is proclaimed to be inauspicious. / If it does not allow mounting, or should turn back towards home,

sanskrit_iast:
madaṃ vā vāraṇo jahyādyātrāghātakaro bhavet ..
grāhagṛhīto dviradaḥ sagrāhaḥ salilāśayāt .. 82 ..
meaning:
मदं वा वारणो जह्याद्यात्राघातकरो भवेत् ..
ग्राहगृहीतो द्विरदः सग्राहः सलिलाशयात् .. 82 ..
text_mt: or if the elephant should lose its rut, it becomes a spoiler of the expedition. / An elephant seized by a crocodile, or emerging with a crocodile from a body of water,

sanskrit_iast:
uttaranvijayāya syātsagrāho bhayavardhanaḥ ..
śastrāṅkuśapatākānāṃ bhūmau nipatanaṃ gajāt .. 83..
meaning:
उत्तरन्विजयाय स्यात्सग्राहो भयवर्धनः ..
शस्त्राङ्कुशपताकानां भूमौ निपतनं गजात् .. 83..
text_mt: leads to victory if it emerges victorious, but with the crocodile [still holding it] it increases danger. / The falling to the ground of weapons, goads, and banners from the elephant,

sanskrit_iast:
loṣṭakāṣṭhakarīṣāṇāṃ kṣepaṇe cāpi yadbhavet ..
anuyātraṃ jayāyaitatpratiyātraṃ na śasyate .. .. 84 ..
meaning:
लोष्टकाष्ठकरीषाणां क्षेपणे चापि यद्भवेत् ..
अनुयात्रं जयायैतत्प्रतियात्रं न शस्यते .. .. 84 ..
text_mt: or whatever occurs when it flings clods, wood, and dry dung: / this, if done following the march, is for victory; done against the march, it is not praised.

sanskrit_iast:
vāryamāṇo yadā nāgaḥ śatruṇābhimukho vrajet ..
tanprasuptatāraṃ ca tadā tejaḥ praśaṅkitaḥ .. 85 ..
meaning:
वार्यमाणो यदा नागः शत्रुणाभिमुखो व्रजेत् ..
तन्प्रसुप्ततारं च तदा तेजः प्रशङ्कितः .. 85 ..
text_mt: When an elephant, though held back, charges towards the enemy, / then, with wide-awake energy, it is praised for its splendour.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭāṃstu yastu bhakṣyāṃśca tathā spṛśati hastinīm ..
rāma bṛṃhitaghaṇṭānāṃ pratiśabdena kupyate .. 86 ..
meaning:
इष्टांस्तु यस्तु भक्ष्यांश्च तथा स्पृशति हस्तिनीम् ..
राम बृंहितघण्टानां प्रतिशब्देन कुप्यते .. 86 ..
text_mt: One that eats desired foods, touches a female elephant, / and is provoked, O Rāma, by the echo of trumpeting bells,

sanskrit_iast:
kakṣāyāṃ baddhyamānāyāṃ yadā voccairnadatyapi ..
yātrānugaśca bhavati prahṛṣṭaścaiva vāraṇaḥ .. 87 ..
meaning:
कक्षायां बद्ध्यमानायां यदा वोच्चैर्नदत्यपि ..
यात्रानुगश्च भवति प्रहृष्टश्चैव वारणः .. 87 ..
text_mt: or roars loudly when its girth is being fastened, / and eagerly follows the expedition, such an elephant brings joy.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmaṃ dakṣiṇapādena pādamākramate tathā ..
dakṣiṇaṃ ca tathā dante parimārṣṭi kareṇa cet .. 88 ..
meaning:
वामं दक्षिणपादेन पादमाक्रमते तथा ..
दक्षिणं च तथा दन्ते परिमार्ष्टि करेण चेत् .. 88 ..
text_mt: If it steps on its left foot with its right foot, / and likewise rubs its right tusk with its trunk,

sanskrit_iast:
veṣṭayatyatha vā karṇau tathā stabdhau karoti ca ..
jayāya rājño bhavati janayannapi śīkaram .. 89 ..
meaning:
वेष्टयत्यथ वा कर्णौ तथा स्तब्धौ करोति च ..
जयाय राज्ञो भवति जनयन्नपि शीकरम् .. 89 ..
text_mt: or if it flaps or stiffens its ears, / producing a fine spray, it brings victory to the king.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmaṃ tu veṣṭayeddanta pādaṃ vāmena dakṣiṇam ..
pādamākramamāṇaśca praskhalannipatannapi .. 2.164.90 ..
meaning:
वामं तु वेष्टयेद्दन्त पादं वामेन दक्षिणम् ..
पादमाक्रममाणश्च प्रस्खलन्निपतन्नपि .. 2.164.90 ..
text_mt: If it touches its left tusk, or steps on its right foot / with its left foot, stumbling or falling,

sanskrit_iast:
agrahastaṃ noddharati yadā ca vasudhātalāt ..
sāsuśca kavaladveṣī dīno bhayavivardhanaḥ .. 91 ..
meaning:
अग्रहस्तं नोद्धरति यदा च वसुधातलात् ..
सासुश्च कवलद्वेषी दीनो भयविवर्धनः .. 91 ..
text_mt: and does not lift the tip of its trunk from the surface of the earth, / and is breathless, averse to morsels of food, and miserable, it greatly increases danger.

sanskrit_iast:
niḥśvāsaṃ paramaṃ kurvañchāntaṃ vikṛtameva ca ..
bhayāvaho vinirdiṣṭaḥ pratilomagatistathā .. 92 ..
meaning:
निःश्वासं परमं कुर्वञ्छान्तं विकृतमेव च ..
भयावहो विनिर्दिष्टः प्रतिलोमगतिस्तथा .. 92 ..
text_mt: Breathing heavily, or breathing faint and unnaturally, / moving in reverse, it is declared to bring danger.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīrapādapagulmānāṃ nihantā vijayāvahaḥ ..
tathā vikāsitākṣaśca rāma labdhapado'pi ca ..93..
meaning:
क्षीरपादपगुल्मानां निहन्ता विजयावहः ..
तथा विकासिताक्षश्च राम लब्धपदोऽपि च ..93..
text_mt: An elephant that strikes milk-trees and bushes brings victory, / as does one whose eyes are wide open, O Rāma, and who gains firm footing.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣośvaḥ kuñjaro vāpi ripusainyaṃ yadā vrajet ..

Stationed on a wing of the army, O foremost of the twice-born, a carnivore or a fly causes fear; / wood-peckers, blue jays, peacocks, swans, and pheasant-cuckoos are auspicious.
Puṣkara said: / If the inquirer's place is auspicious, O descendant of Bhṛgu, good is to be known; / if inauspicious, evil, O Rāma. Hear that from me as I speak.
In cremation grounds, slaughterhouses, [prisons] and places of confinement, / in alleys, muddy spots, fortresses, and empty buildings,
in [places] filled with thorny trees, in houses with broken enclosure walls, / [places] with anthills, mice, snakes, and insects, one should declare misfortune.
In [places] touched and smeared with meat, especially with beautiful flowers, / endowed with praised trees, one should know the mark of victory.
On grassy banks of rivers and lakes, / [and] in multi-colored mansions, good is to be spoken by the knower.
[If] they approach an [astrologer who is] anointed [with oil], grieving, with disheveled hair, / or seated on the ground, one should know misfortune for them.

Delighted, wearing white garments, and of cheerful mind, / [if] they approach the astrologer, one should know good for them, O twice-born.
Many people holding staffs, dressed in red-brown garments, / anointed with oil, shaven-headed, fallen, and likewise eunuchs and women,
holding chains and ropes, carrying wet fruit in their hands— / these asking [questions] should be known as bringing total fear to men.
Clothed in white garments, with flowers, and carrying fruits in hand, / with jewels in hand, speaking blessings, they should be known as auspicious.
He should examine all the times of the one who asks in the morning; / at the two twilights, in the afternoon, and at night, they are condemned.
Taking a stand in a peaceful direction, he should declare success to the inquirer, / especially [in] the north, the north-east, and the east.
Thumb, nail, foot, thigh, ankle, testicle, chest, breasts, / cheek, horn, two corners of the eye, ears, tooth, lip, arm, head,
the gullet, large bladder, chest, armpits, joints of the thighs— / touching masculine-named [limbs] such as these, the inquirer has good fortune.

Earlobe, eyebrows, nose, tongue, neck, nape, / navel, hips, buttocks, two shanks, calves, and fingers,
lines dependent on the hand and foot, folds in all joints, / the heel—such as these should be indicated as feminine-named.
Head, forehead, chin, mouth, back, belly, sacrum, / abdomen, upper bladder, penis, and both knees,
the hollow of the ear, the socket of the eye, the sides, and the heart— / those skilled in the science of bodily signs should know these as neuter.
When he touches a masculine-named [part of the body that is] firm, smooth, unbroken, unpained, / even, well-formed, and free from pain,
success should be indicated for whatever object he inquires about. / When the enemy's ascendant rises, or when the inquirer's rising sign [is afflicted],
at the rising of the enemy's sign, or at the rising of their lord, / defeat should be declared; [so too] at the rising of the eighth [house] from one's own ascendant.

text_mt:
And from one's own sign, O fortunate one, likewise one should know misfortune. / At the rising of one's own ascendant, O Rāma, and likewise at the rising of the enemy's sign,
from the ascendant or from the sign, at the rising of the third, sixth, or tenth, / or at the rising of the eleventh, or at the rising of their lords,
attainment of all aims of the inquirer is to be known, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / In the ascendant, or in its fourth, seventh, or tenth,
or in the fifth or ninth, benefic planets are considered commendable; / malefic [planets] in the third, sixth, tenth, and likewise in the eleventh are auspicious.
They should be known as accomplishing all aims of the inquirer, O upholder of the Bhṛgu lineage; / benefics should be known as possessing great strength, and malefics as weak.
And a strong ascendant gives auspicious [results] at the time of inquiry. / Thus, having known good through the time of inquiry, a king's
march, O Rāma, should be known as auspicious, but never otherwise. / And knowing the horoscope, at an auspicious time of planetary period,

adhimāsaśeṣasya kalpādhimāsakairbhāge hate eṣyādhimāsakairbhāge hate gatādhimāsakasya dinādiḥ kālo labhyate . adhimāsaśeṣaṃ kalparavidivasebhyaḥ saṃśodhyāvaśeṣasya kalpādhimāsakairbhāge hate eṣyedhimāsekatāsya kālo labhyate . avamaśeṣasya kalpena rātrerbhāge hate eṣyonarātrakālaḥ avamaśeṣakalpacandradivasebhyaḥ saṃśodhyāvaśeṣasya kalponarātrenarātrerbhāge hate eṣyonarātrapātakālaḥ saṃvatsaragaṇātpaṃcahatāvaśeṣe saṃvatsarādyobdaḥ ādityaḥ, candraḥ , bhaumaḥ, budhaḥ, jīvaḥ, sitaḥ, sauraśceti krameṇa grahaṇaṃ saṃvatsarāḥ saptahatāvaśeṣe caturthakrameṇa saṃvatsarādhipaḥ sāvanāddinagaṇātsaptahṛtātkrameṇaiva divasādhipaḥ cāndrāḥ dinagaṇā daśātyadhikaśatahatāllabdhaṃ saptahataṃ tadavaśeṣaṃ parva brahmacandreṃdravaiśravaṇavaruṇāgniyamāśca parvapatayaḥ dinagaṇami ṣṭagrahabhagaṇaguṇabhūdinairvibhajet .
labdhaṃ bhagaṇādiḥ lekhārkodayo graho bhavati .
evaṃrūpeṇāhargaṇena grahabhuktiḥ .
iṣṭāṃ kālādyāvatākālenārkodayo bhaviṣyati tāvatā kālena grahasyekadivasabhuktiṃ saṃguṇya ṣaṣṭyā vibhajet .
avāptaṃ ravyudaye grahasya dhanamastamaye ṛṇam .
evamuttaragole dakṣiṇena viparīta diśāntarayojanāni ṣaṣṭhyāsaṅguṇya pañcabhiḥ sahasrairvibhajet .
labdhaṃ lekhāprāgbhāve saṃśodhyamaparasmindeyamevamiṣṭe deśe .
iṣṭe ca kāle graho madhyamo bhavati .
tatkālārkacandramandakarmaṇaiva sphuṭe kāryo bhaumaḥ karmacatuṣṭayena tasya manda śīghraṃ maṃdaṃ śīghramiti ca karmāṇi .
anyeṣāṃ mandaśīghre karmaṇī tatra bhaumamardaḥ saṃskāryaḥ tacchīghraparidhiśca śukrasya paridhidvayamapi tatra bhaumajīvasaurāṇāmarkaḥ śīghraḥ .
svayaṃ madhyamo budhaśukrayorarko madhyamaḥ .
svayaṃ śīghrośīghro grahonaṃ kendraḥ grahaśca mandonaḥ bhaumaśīghrakendrapadabhuktābhuktayoralpasya jīvaṃ caturbhiḥ śataiḥ grahaiśca mandonaḥ bhāṇitaṃ dvādaśyā jīvayā vibhajet .
labdhena kendre makarādige bhaumamandayutaṃ kāryaṃ karkaṭādige conamiti śukramadaṃ kendrajyāṃ nyāsārdhāvahūtāṃ
labdhena taṃ madaṃ paridhirūnaḥ spaṣṭo bhavati .
tasyaiva śīghrakendrajyāṃ vyāsārdhaṃ pañcamena vibhajet .
labdhe yutaḥ śukraśīghraparidhiḥ spaṣṭo bhavatīti mandakendrāt jīvā bhujajyā trirāśisahitārkoṭijyākoṭibhujajye svamardavāridhihate kharasāmibhirvibhajeta .
labdhaṃ bhujakoṭipāte makarādikendre koṭiphalaṃ vyāsārthe dadyāta .
kulīrādike śodhayetkoṭirbhavati .
bhujāphalaṃ bhujā koṭibhujāvargayogamūlaṃ karṇaḥ vyāsārdhahatāṃ bhujajyāṃ sphuṭakarṇena vibhajet .
labdhacāpaṃ phalakalāḥ meṣādikendre grahe śodhyāstulādau deyāḥ .
bhaumasya śyamamandakarmaṇyadhikṛtāḥ evaṃ spandasphuṭagrahaṃ śīghrādapāsya kendraṃ kṛtaitadeva śīghraparidhinā karma kuryāt . tatphalaṃ mandasphuṭe grahe meṣādikendre dhanaṃ tulādṛṇamiti .
bhaumasya prathame śīghrakarmaṇi tadūnīkṛtaṃ evaṃ grahaḥ sphuṭo bhavati.
budhasitapātau viparītena abdaphalena sphuṭo kāryo bhaumajīvasaurāṇāṃ śīghrāntyaphalenānulomenānītavartamānasphuṭaṃ grahāntaraṃ sphuṭabhuktiḥ arkaphalam .
sphuṭabhaktihataṃ bhavanakalābhirvibhajet labdhamarkakendravaśe tadvadeva grahasya dhanarṇe yojye .
antyaśīghrakarmāviśeṣaṃ kendrasya vakrādikendrasya vāntaraṃ sphuṭabhuktiśīghramutsaṃtareṇa vibhajet .
labdho vakrāderdinādiḥ kālaḥ dhuvakakendredhika eṣyaḥ śīghrakendredhiketītaḥ ..
meaning:
2.169
अथ यथाकालं.
गतमनवस्त्वेकसप्ततिहताश्चतुर्युगाब्दहताः कार्याः .
तेषु कृतप्रमाणं क्षेप्यम् .
तमेव तत्र भूयो गतसंख्याहतं च ततो वर्तमानमन्वन्तराद्गतचतुर्युगसंख्याहतानि चतुर्युगाब्दानि युगानि च वर्तमानयुगाच्चैत्रप्रभवगताब्दानि च एवमिष्टकालाब्दगणो भवति .
स द्वादशहतश्चैत्रसितादिमासयुक्तस्त्रिंश द्धतोवमानमितादितिथिसहितः कार्यः .
एवं सौरो दिनगणो भवति .
तं पृथक्कल्पाधिमासकहतं कल्पनविदिनैर्विभजेत् .
लब्धं गताधिमासाः .
तैस्त्रिंशदब्दैरर्काहर्गणोयुक्ते चन्द्राहर्गणो भवति .
तं पृथक्कल्पावमहतं कल्पचन्द्रदिनैर्विभजेत् .
लब्धं गतोनरात्रिः तैश्चन्द्राहर्गणाद्धनं साधनाहर्गणो भवति .
अधिमासशेषस्य कल्पाधिमासकैर्भागे हते एष्याधिमासकैर्भागे हते गताधिमासकस्य दिनादिः कालो लभ्यते . अधिमासशेषं कल्परविदिवसेभ्यः संशोध्यावशेषस्य कल्पाधिमासकैर्भागे हते एष्येधिमासेकतास्य कालो लभ्यते . अवमशेषस्य कल्पेन रात्रेर्भागे हते एष्योनरात्रकालः अवमशेषकल्पचन्द्रदिवसेभ्यः संशोध्यावशेषस्य कल्पोनरात्रेनरात्रेर्भागे हते एष्योनरात्रपातकालः संवत्सरगणात्पंचहतावशेषे संवत्सराद्योब्दः आदित्यः, चन्द्रः , भौमः, बुधः, जीवः, सितः, सौरश्चेति क्रमेण ग्रहणं संवत्सराः सप्तहतावशेषे चतुर्थक्रमेण संवत्सराधिपः सावनाद्दिनगणात्सप्तहृतात्क्रमेणैव दिवसाधिपः चान्द्राः दिनगणा दशात्यधिकशतहताल्लब्धं सप्तहतं तदवशेषं पर्व ब्रह्मचन्द्रेंद्रवैश्रवणवरुणाग्नियमाश्च पर्वपतयः दिनगणमि ष्टग्रहभगणगुणभूदिनैर्विभजेत् .
लब्धं भगणादिः लेखार्कोदयो ग्रहो भवति .
एवंरूपेणाहर्गणेन ग्रहभुक्तिः .
इष्टां कालाद्यावताकालेनार्कोदयो भविष्यति तावता कालेन ग्रहस्येकदिवसभुक्तिं संगुण्य षष्ट्या विभजेत् .
अवाप्तं रव्युदये ग्रहस्य धनमस्तमये ऋणम् .
एवमुत्तरगोले दक्षिणेन विपरीत दिशान्तरयोजनानि षष्ठ्यासङ्गुण्य पञ्चभिः सहस्रैर्विभजेत् .
लब्धं लेखाप्राग्भावे संशोध्यमपरस्मिन्देयमेवमिष्टे देशे .
इष्टे च काले ग्रहो मध्यमो भवति .
तत्कालार्कचन्द्रमन्दकर्मणैव स्फुटे कार्यो भौमः कर्मचतुष्टयेन तस्य मन्द शीघ्रं मंदं शीघ्रमिति च कर्माणि .
अन्येषां मन्दशीघ्रे कर्मणी तत्र भौममर्दः संस्कार्यः तच्छीघ्रपरिधिश्च शुक्रस्य परिधिद्वयमपि तत्र भौमजीवसौराणामर्कः शीघ्रः .
स्वयं मध्यमो बुधशुक्रयोरर्को मध्यमः .
स्वयं शीघ्रोशीघ्रो ग्रहोनं केन्द्रः ग्रहश्च मन्दोनः भौमशीघ्रकेन्द्रपदभुक्ताभुक्तयोरल्पस्य जीवं चतुर्भिः शतैः ग्रहैश्च मन्दोनः भाणितं द्वादश्या जीवया विभजेत् .
लब्धेन केन्द्रे मकरादिगे भौममन्दयुतं कार्यं कर्कटादिगे चोनमिति शुक्रमदं केन्द्रज्यां न्यासार्धावहूतां
लब्धेन तं मदं परिधिरूनः स्पष्टो भवति .
तस्यैव शीघ्रकेन्द्रज्यां व्यासार्धं पञ्चमेन विभजेत् .
लब्धे युतः शुक्रशीघ्रपरिधिः स्पष्टो भवतीति मन्दकेन्द्रात् जीवा भुजज्या त्रिराशिसहितार्कोटिज्याकोटिभुजज्ये स्वमर्दवारिधिहते खरसामिभिर्विभजेत .
लब्धं भुजकोटिपाते मकरादिकेन्द्रे कोटिफलं व्यासार्थे दद्यात .
कुलीरादिके शोधयेत्कोटिर्भवति .
भुजाफलं भुजा कोटिभुजावर्गयोगमूलं कर्णः व्यासार्धहतां भुजज्यां स्फुटकर्णेन विभजेत् .
लब्धचापं फलकलाः मेषादिकेन्द्रे ग्रहे शोध्यास्तुलादौ देयाः .
भौमस्य श्यममन्दकर्मण्यधिकृताः एवं स्पन्दस्फुटग्रहं शीघ्रादपास्य केन्द्रं कृतैतदेव शीघ्रपरिधिना कर्म कुर्यात् . तत्फलं मन्दस्फुटे ग्रहे मेषादिकेन्द्रे धनं तुलादृणमिति .
भौमस्य प्रथमे शीघ्रकर्मणि तदूनीकृतं एवं ग्रहः स्फुटो भवति.
बुधसितपातौ विपरीतेन अब्दफलेन स्फुटो कार्यो भौमजीवसौराणां शीघ्रान्त्यफलेनानुलोमेनानीतवर्तमानस्फुटं ग्रहान्तरं स्फुटभुक्तिः अर्कफलम् .
स्फुटभक्तिहतं भवनकलाभिर्विभजेत् लब्धमर्ककेन्द्रवशे तद्वदेव ग्रहस्य धनर्णे योज्ये .
अन्त्यशीघ्रकर्माविशेषं केन्द्रस्य वक्रादिकेन्द्रस्य वान्तरं स्फुटभुक्तिशीघ्रमुत्संतरेण विभजेत् .
लब्धो वक्रादेर्दिनादिः कालः धुवककेन्द्रेधिक एष्यः शीघ्रकेन्द्रेधिकेतीतः ..
text_mt: Now, according to the desired time: / The elapsed Manus multiplied by seventy-one are to be multiplied by the years of a four-age cycle. / To them the measure of the Kṛta age is to be added. / That itself being multiplied there again by the number elapsed, and then the years of the four-age cycles multiplied by the number of four-age cycles elapsed from the current Manvantara, and the yugas, and from the current yuga the elapsed years beginning from Caitra—in this way the collection of years for the desired time is obtained. / Multiplied by twelve, increased by the months beginning with the bright fortnight of Caitra, multiplied by thirty, and combined with the tithis beginning from the calculated omit-day, it should be made. / In this way the solar day-collection is obtained. / Having separately multiplied it by the intercalary months of the kalpa, one should divide it by the civil days of the kalpa. / The quotient is the elapsed intercalary months. / When the solar ahargaṇa is combined with those [converted into days] thirtyfold, it becomes the lunar ahargaṇa. / Having multiplied that separately by the omit-days of the kalpa, one should divide by the lunar days of the kalpa. / The quotient is the elapsed omit-days; subtracted from the lunar ahargaṇa, the result is the civil ahargaṇa. / When the remainder of the intercalary month is divided by the intercalary months of the kalpa, the time beginning with days of the past intercalary month is obtained; having subtracted the intercalary-month remainder from the solar days of the kalpa, when the remainder is divided by the intercalary months of the kalpa, the time of the future intercalary month is obtained; when the omit-day remainder is divided by the nights of the kalpa, the future omit-day time [is obtained]; having subtracted the omit-day remainder from the lunar days of the kalpa, when the remainder is divided by the omit-days of the kalpa, the time of the occurrence of the future omit-day [is obtained]; from the collection of years multiplied by five, with the remainder, the lord of the beginning of the year is: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn in regular order; when the years are divided by seven, by the remainder, counting every fourth in succession, the lord of the year [is found]; from the civil day-collection divided by seven, in direct order, the lord of the day [is found]; from the lunar day-collection multiplied by one hundred and ten, the quotient divided by seven, the remainder is the parvan; Brahmā, Moon, Indra, Kubera, Varuṇa, Agni, and Yama are the lords of the parvans; one should divide the day-collection multiplied by the revolutions of the desired planet by the civil days; the quotient is revolutions and the rest; the planet is [thus] at sunrise on the prime meridian. / In this manner, through the ahargaṇa, [is calculated] the daily motion of the planet. / By whatever time sunrise will occur from the desired time, by that much time having multiplied the one-day motion of the planet, one should divide by sixty; the obtained [result] is additive to the planet at sunrise, and subtractive at sunset; thus in the northern hemisphere, and the reverse in the southern; having multiplied the yojanas of terrestrial longitude by sixty, one should divide by five thousand; the result is to be subtracted when east of the prime meridian, and added when west; thus at the desired locality and at the desired time, the mean planet is determined. / The Sun and the Moon at that time are to be made true by the slow operation alone; Mars by four operations—its operations are the slow, the fast, the slow, and the fast; for the others, the slow and the fast operations [are used]; therein the slow [periphery] of Mars is to be corrected, as well as its fast periphery, and both peripheries of Venus; therein, of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, the Sun is the fast [centre], and the planet itself is the mean; of Mercury and Venus, the Sun is the mean, and the planet itself is the fast; the anomaly is the planet subtracted from the fast, and the planet subtracted from the slow; of the traversed and untraversed [parts] of the quadrant of Mars's fast anomaly, the sine of the smaller, multiplied by four hundred and reduced by the slow of the planets, one should divide by the twelve-fold sine; with the quotient, when the anomaly is in [the half] beginning with Capricorn, it should be added to Mars's slow, and when beginning with Cancer, subtracted; having divided the sine of the slow anomaly of Venus by the radius, with the quotient that slow periphery reduced becomes true; having divided the sine of its fast anomaly by one-fifth of the radius, when added to the quotient, the fast periphery of Venus becomes true; the sine from the slow anomaly is the base-sine; increased by three signs, it is the perpendicular-sine; one should divide the perpendicular-sine and base-sine multiplied by their own slow periphery by three hundred and sixty; in the arrival of the base and perpendicular obtained, in an anomaly beginning with Capricorn one should add the perpendicular-fruit to the radius; in [an anomaly] beginning with Cancer one should subtract it; it becomes the perpendicular; the base-fruit is the base; the square root of the sum of the squares of the perpendicular and the base is the hypotenuse; one should divide the base-sine multiplied by the radius by the true hypotenuse; the arc of the quotient is the minutes of the fruit; in an anomaly beginning with Aries, they are to be subtracted from the planet, and in [one] beginning with Libra, they are to be added; thus applied in the slow operation of Mars; having then subtracted the slow-true planet from the fast [planet], making it the anomaly, one should perform this very operation with the fast periphery; that fruit is additive to the slow-true planet in an anomaly beginning with Aries, and subtractive in [one] beginning with Libra; in the first fast operation of Mars, it is reduced by that; thus the planet becomes true; the nodes of Mercury and Venus are to be made true by the reverse year-fruit; for Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, by the final fast-fruit in direct order, the difference between the determined present true planets is the true daily motion; the solar fruit multiplied by the true daily motion one should divide by the minutes of a sign; the quotient, according to the Sun's anomaly, is to be applied just so as additive or subtractive to the planet; the difference between the anomaly of the final fast operation and the anomaly of retrograde motion or the like, one should divide by the difference between the true motion and the fast motion; the quotient is the time beginning with days of the retrograde motion or the like; when the fixed anomaly is greater, it is future; when the fast anomaly is greater, it is past.

2.170
sphuṭagrahaṃ liptīkṛtam aṣṭabhiḥ śatairvibhajet .
labdhaṃ graheṇa bhuktānyaśvinyādyāni nakṣatrāṇi śeṣaṃ sphuṭabhuktyā vibhajet .
labdhaṃ dinādiḥ kālā nakṣatrapraviṣṭasya avaśeṣamaṣṭabhyaḥ śatebhyaḥ saṃśodhyāvameṣāta prāgghatakālo nakṣatrasthiteḥ rāśau bhuktā abhuktā vā sphuṭabhuktā vibhajeta .
labdhaṃ dinādiḥ saṃkrāntergataiṣyaḥ kālaḥ atha yojanakarṇāntaṃ sarvāṃtyāviśeṣakarṇādyantaṃ vyastaṃ vyāsārdhena vibhajet .
labdhaṃ sphuṭayojanakarṇārthā grahā pramāṇaviṣkabhayojanāni vyāsādhehatāni sphuṭayojanakarṇārdhena vibhajet .
labdhaṃ sphuṭagrahāpramāṇavyāsakalāḥ sphuṭānyarkakarṇārdhayojanati pāṃcasāhasrikasyaparidheḥ karṇonāni tenaiva guṇitāni ravinyāse na tadgaṇena vibhajet .
labdhaṃ bhūcchāyā sphuṭarāśikarṇārdhonapāñcasāhasrikasya .
paridheḥ karṇahatāṃ bhūcchāyayā vibhajet .
labdhaṃ vyāsārdhaguṇaṃ candrasphuṭayojanakarṇārdhena vibhajet labdhaṃ rāhumānakalāḥ .
grahamānārdhakalāḥ ṣaṣṭiguṇā bhuktyā vibhajet .
labdhaṃ saṃkrāṃtikālātprāgapareṇa ca puṇyakālaḥ .
arkonāccandrālliptīkṛtāt vayamāgatabhaktācchuklapratipadādyā tithiḥ .
śeṣātṣaṣṭiguṇyādbhuktāntarahṛtādghaṭikādiḥ kālaḥ kṛṣṇacaturdaśāṃtaḥ sadaiva śakuniḥ amāyā ādyardhe catuṣpāt dvitīye nāgaḥ pratipadādyardhe kiṃstughnama arkonacandraliptāḥ kharadāgnibhirvibhajet.
avaśeṣāttithivatkālaḥ labdhādekonātsaptamahṛtādavaśeṣaṃ bavādyaṃ karaṇaṃ candrārkayoge candrārdhayorāsaneghātavai
dhṛte tena candrārkayoḥ krāntisāmye .

स्फुटग्रहं लिप्तीकृतम् अष्टभिः शतैर्विभजेत् .
लब्धं ग्रहेण भुक्तान्यश्विन्याद्यानि नक्षत्राणि शेषं स्फुटभुक्त्या विभजेत् .
लब्धं दिनादिः काला नक्षत्रप्रविष्टस्य अवशेषमष्टभ्यः शतेभ्यः संशोध्यावमेषात प्राग्घतकालो नक्षत्रस्थितेः राशौ भुक्ता अभुक्ता वा स्फुटभुक्ता विभजेत .
लब्धं दिनादिः संक्रान्तेर्गतैष्यः कालः अथ योजनकर्णान्तं सर्वांत्याविशेषकर्णाद्यन्तं व्यस्तं व्यासार्धेन विभजेत् .
लब्धं स्फुटयोजनकर्णार्था ग्रहा प्रमाणविष्कभयोजनानि व्यासाधेहतानि स्फुटयोजनकर्णार्धेन विभजेत् .
लब्धं स्फुटग्रहाप्रमाणव्यासकलाः स्फुटान्यर्ककर्णार्धयोजनति पांचसाहस्रिकस्यपरिधेः कर्णोनानि तेनैव गुणितानि रविन्यासे न तद्गणेन विभजेत् .
लब्धं भूच्छाया स्फुटराशिकर्णार्धोनपाञ्चसाहस्रिकस्य .
परिधेः कर्णहतां भूच्छायया विभजेत् .
लब्धं व्यासार्धगुणं चन्द्रस्फुटयोजनकर्णार्धेन विभजेत् लब्धं राहुमानकलाः .
ग्रहमानार्धकलाः षष्टिगुणा भुक्त्या विभजेत् .
लब्धं संक्रांतिकालात्प्रागपरेण च पुण्यकालः .
अर्कोनाच्चन्द्राल्लिप्तीकृतात् वयमागतभक्ताच्छुक्लप्रतिपदाद्या तिथिः .
शेषात्षष्टिगुण्याद्भुक्तान्तरहृताद्घटिकादिः कालः कृष्णचतुर्दशांतः सदैव शकुनिः अमाया आद्यर्धे चतुष्पात् द्वितीये नागः प्रतिपदाद्यर्धे किंस्तुघ्नम अर्कोनचन्द्रलिप्ताः खरदाग्निभिर्विभजेत्.
अवशेषात्तिथिवत्कालः लब्धादेकोनात्सप्तमहृतादवशेषं बवाद्यं करणं चन्द्रार्कयोगे चन्द्रार्धयोरासनेघातवै
धृते तेन चन्द्रार्कयोः क्रान्तिसाम्ये .
तत्र व्यतीपातौर्भिन्ननयने गोलैकत्वे च वैधृतः समायने गोलभेदे च ध्रुवकार्कचन्द्रयोगान्तरं चन्द्रार्कभुक्तियोगेन विभजेत् .

ततोर्कात्क्रान्तिस्तात्कालिकपातेन चन्द्रात्स्वकान्तिः प्रथमतृतीयपादान्तस्थे चन्द्रस्य क्रान्तेः चन्द्रक्रान्तिर्यदोना भवति तदा क्रांतिसाम्यारावाः प्रथमतृतीयपदस्थे चन्द्रमसि तदपक्रममर्कापक्रमादूने एष्यः क्रान्तिसाम्यकालोन्यथातीतः. द्वितीयचतुर्थपदस्थान्यथाविक्षेपेण स्वक्रान्तिदिगुत्पत्तौ चन्द्रापक्रममधिकृतं कल्पयेत्.

text_mt: 2.170 / One should divide the true planet, converted into minutes, by eight hundred. / The quotient is the asterisms, beginning with Aśvinī, traversed by the planet; one should divide the remainder by the true daily motion. / The quotient is the elapsed time in days and so forth since entry into the asterism; having subtracted the remainder from eight hundred, [the quotient is] the remaining time until passing from it; or dividing the traversed or untraversed [minutes] of the zodiacal sign by the true daily motion, / the quotient is the elapsed or remaining time in days and so forth of the transit (saṃkrānti). Now, dividing the distance of the hypotenuse in yojanas, reversed between the extremities of all the differential hypotenuses, by the semi-diameter, / the quotient is the semi-hypotenuse in true yojanas. Multiplying the yojanas of the measured diameter of the planet by the semi-diameter, one should divide by the true semi-hypotenuse in yojanas. / The quotient is the minutes of the measured diameter of the true planet. Subtracting from the hypotenuse of the circumference of five thousand [yojanas] the true yojanas of the sun's semi-hypotenuse, multiplying by that [remainder], one should divide by that aggregate at the sun's position. / The quotient is the Earth's shadow. Of the circumference of five thousand [yojanas] diminished by the semi-hypotenuse of the true sign, / multiplied by the hypotenuse, one should divide by the Earth's shadow; / the quotient, multiplied by the semi-diameter, one should divide by the true semi-hypotenuse of the moon in yojanas: the quotient is the minutes of the measure of Rāhu. / The minutes of the half-measure of the planet, multiplied by sixty, one should divide by its daily motion; / the quotient is the auspicious period before and after the moment of transit. / From the moon diminished by the sun and converted into minutes, divided by [seven hundred and twenty], [arises] the lunar day (tithi) beginning with the bright fortnight's pratipad. / From the remainder multiplied by sixty and divided by the difference in their daily motions, the time in ghaṭikās and so forth is obtained. At the end of the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight is always Śakuni; in the first half of the new moon day is Catuṣpāt, in the second Nāga; in the first half of pratipad is Kiṃstughna. One should divide the minutes of the moon diminished by the sun by three hundred and sixty (kharadāgni); / from the remainder, the time is calculated as for a lunar day; from the quotient diminished by one and divided by seven, the remainder is the karaṇa beginning with Bava. When there is a conjunction of the sun and moon, [or] in the Vaidhṛta [aspect] when the declinations of the sun and moon are equal: / there, in Vyatīpāta there are different solstices (ayana) and the same celestial hemisphere (gola); in Vaidhṛta, the same solstice and different hemispheres. One should divide the difference of the longitude-sum of the sun and moon from the constant by the sum of the daily motions of the sun and moon; / by the quotient, the sun and moon's sum is increased or decreased relative to the constant. / Then, from the sun, the declination [is calculated], and from the moon with its node at that time, its own declination. When the moon is at the end of the first or third quadrant, if the moon's declination is less than the [requisite] declination, then the moments of equal declination [are determined]: when the moon is in the first or third quadrant, if its declination is less than the sun's declination, the time of equal declination is yet to come; otherwise, it is past. In the second or fourth quadrant, it is opposite; when its own declination arises in its direction by latitude, one should determine the moon's declination accordingly. / The sum of declinations in opposite directions, or the difference in the same direction, is the first Vyatīpāta; otherwise, it is called the first Vaidhṛti. / Thus, by the sun, moon, and node at the desired time, the second and further [moments are found]. Then, if at both the first and second times the node is yet to come or has passed, [one takes] their difference; / otherwise, their sum is the divisor. For the desired time multiplied by the first, by that time repeatedly performing the second, the true time should be determined by the method of successive approximation: that is the middle time of the Vyatīpāta conjunction. / The sum of the measures of the sun and moon, multiplied by sixty and divided by the difference of their daily motions, yields the duration [of the eclipse or aspect].

text_mt: 2.171 / For the lesser time elapsed or remaining of the day, subtracted from midnight in the northern hemisphere and added in the southern: its sine, multiplied by the day-and-night radius and divided by the radius (trijyā), then reversed by hemisphere and added to the radius, is the other divisor. / The divisor, multiplied by the cosine of latitude (avalambaka) and divided by the radius, is the gnomon (śaṅku). / The square root of the square of the radius diminished by the square of the gnomon is the visible [base]; multiplied by twelve and divided by the gnomon, it is the shadow. The sum or difference of the latitude with the noon declination of the sun in the southern or northern hemisphere respectively: subtracting that from three signs, the sine thereof is the divisor; [the radius] multiplied by twelve, divided by that intact sine, yields the noon shadow. The radius multiplied by twelve, divided by the divisor of the noon shadow, is its hypotenuse. One should divide the radius multiplied by the equinoctial hypotenuse by the hypotenuse of one's desired shadow; the result, increased or decreased in the northern and southern hemispheres by the earth-sine (kṣitijyā), multiplied by the semi-diameter, one should divide by the half of its own day-and-night circle. / And this result, subtracted or added by half the ascensional difference (caradala) according to the reverse of the hemisphere, becomes the elapsed or remaining [part] of the day.

text_mt: 2.172 / The traversed minutes of the true sign of the sun at the desired time, multiplied by the respiration-periods (prāṇa) of the rising of that sign of the ecliptic, one should divide by the minutes of the sign. The quotient is the daytime portion of the sun's sign of the ecliptic. That is [subtracted] from the respiration-periods of the desired time, and the untraversed minutes of the sun are to be added; and at that time, referring to the subsequent rising of the sun […] ascensional difference and rising is to be given; from the remainder, by means of the unexhausted risings of the signs, the houses (bhāva) and so forth [are found]. / Thus the rising of the ascendant (lagna) for the elapsed time of the sign [is determined]. From the sun with six signs added are the times of the sun's traversed time and so forth; and the ascendants are from the traversed minutes; in their conjunction, the rising of the ascendant is the time when the difference is added to the rising.

text_mt:
Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn [have] the anomaly [as] the quick [apogee/epicycle]; when retrograde, Mercury and Venus are slow, and otherwise quick. When the slow planet is situated between [itself] and the sun by degrees of visible and invisible time, then in the eastern half of rising and setting, the planet pertains to sunrise; by the western half, it pertains to sunset. One should divide the true celestial latitude of the planet for that time, multiplied by the sine of the slow [anomaly], by the radius.
From the result, [it is] subtractive for the rising planet, [and] additive for the setting one; one should divide by the maximum declination of northern latitude.
The obtained [value] should be subtracted from the other solstice-latitude, otherwise added.
Thus are the rising and setting ascendants of the planet.
Then, from the difference of the planets, as with the ascendant, is the time; one should divide the degree by the difference of the arms of the minutes and degrees of planetary difference.
When the planet is retrograde, by the sum of the motions the time in days and so forth of the setting is obtained; thus for the lunar mansions, their visible and invisible degrees are twelve. Having performed the two directional operations of the fixed star Canopus, one should increase [it] by its two ghaṭikās in the rising of the signs in one's own locality.
In that degree is the rising of Canopus; when retrograde, the setting. The daily rising up to the planet is by virtue of the ascendant.

text_mt:
The rising and setting ascendants of the sun and the moon are their own; from that, the times of rising and setting of the moon are to be determined. One should divide [the sine of] the sun's and moon's own declination at the desired time, multiplied by the radius, by its own sine [of the diurnal circle].
The results being the amplitude in the direction of the declination, then the gnomons of the sun and the moon are to be made; one should divide separately the sine of latitude multiplied by the gnomon by the equinoctial gnomon/colatitude.
The results being the base of the gnomons, those two are in the north in their own night, [and] in the south by day. If the directions of the bases of the twelve[-finger] gnomons are the same, there is addition; if the directions differ, subtraction: [this is] the separate base. If their directions are the same, subtraction; otherwise, addition: [this is] the corrected base. The square root of the difference between the squares of the base and its own visibility is added when the hemispheres differ; when identical, there is subtraction. The direction arising from the first part is difference; when directions differ, it is sum; the second, the square root of the sum of the squares of the first and second is the upright; the square root of the sum of the squares of the upright and base is the hypotenuse. Subtracting the sun from the moon's and sun's [distance] is half; from that, the sine of the minutes of anomaly are the minutes of the lunar month. From that, the sine of the minutes of anomaly multiplied by the moon's measure, divided by ninety: when situated in the first and fourth quadrant of this anomaly, [it is bright]; when situated in the second, dark. The cords of the base, hypotenuse, and upright made into a fourth part of the moon's measure reach the state of inches. With the anomaly of the sun and moon facing the eastern and western quarters, when situated in the first quadrant, one should delineate the measured cusp.
Thus, when situated in the second and third, conceiving the black dot as the sun, then the base is to be placed as the moon is from the sun; from its tip, facing oneself, the upright. Then, by the ascendant at its end, the eastern limit repeatedly, well-calculated,
until it becomes identical without difference. Thus, parallax in longitude having been corrected at the end of the lunar day, the middle of the eclipse [occurs]. The moon's own declination is from two or three signs conceived like the moon; north in the latitude is to be subtracted, south to be added; that sine multiplied by the difference between the mean motions of the moon and sun, multiplied by the arrow and the sun, one should divide by the radius.
The result is parallax in latitude. If latitude is greater than its own declination, it is north; otherwise south. If the contemporaneous lunar latitude has the same direction as the other, there is addition; if different directions, subtraction: [this is] the corrected latitude. By that, with the planets increased or decreased by half the duration of the eclipse, the parallax values at the times of first contact, total obscuration, beginning of emergence, and completion of release are to be calculated. The difference between the addition and subtraction of the middle parallax and the desired parallax is the result.
By that, the two [times] of half the middle duration, combined with the sun and slow [planet], become corrected for their own time. When fifteen ghaṭikās are decreased by the result in parallax at that time, they are to be made into half the duration; the remainder, filled with the eclipse-diagram, is like a lunar eclipse.
This calculation of the planets brings fortune, brings renown, grants long life, and bestows the world of heaven; it grants all desires and is auspicious.
Having understood the motion of a single planet, deeply concentrated,
one attains that planet's realm; no doubt should be entertained here.
Having understood the motion of all the planets, one reaches the world of Brahmā.
One who seeks dharma will obtain dharma; one who seeks wealth will obtain wealth;
one who has desires will obtain desires; one who seeks liberation will obtain the supreme abode.
Having fully understood the motion of the planets, a twice-born person truly becomes worthy of gifts;
if he does not make a living by it, he should thus abandon [such] livelihood;
he who knows the motion of the planets is the most worthy among worthy recipients.
The Vedas are indeed undertaken for the sake of sacrifice, and sacrifices are prescribed in accordance with the divisions of time;
therefore, this scripture of the ordinances of time—he who knows astronomy knows everything.
Thus ends the one hundred and seventy-fourth chapter, entitled 'The Paitāmaha Siddhānta', in the Second Book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the conversation between Mārkaṇḍeya [and Vajra].

text_mt: 2.166 / Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then Rāma, descendant of Bhṛgu, asked Puṣkara, the son of Varuṇa: / "O venerable one, I wish to hear the science of astronomy and astrology." / Varuṇa's son said to him: / "Formerly, Bhṛgu made a request to the lord, the foremost creator, protector, and destroyer of the whole universe, the illustrious Brahmā, who was seated amidst a host of gods and celestial seers: / 'O venerable one, I wish to hear the course of the celestial luminaries.' / The venerable Grandfather said to him: / 'When you were born from my heart at the beginning of the aeon, I taught you the course of the celestial luminaries in twenty-four hundred thousand verses; that very same [teaching] I will declare to you in extreme brevity, since you were born in another birth after issuing forth through the flame by the curse of Mahādeva in this sacrifice of Varuṇa. / Hearing that, all the knowledge of the celestial luminaries declared to you in your previous birth will manifest.' / Now, the thousand-rayed lord [the Sun], pure with clear rays, brings welfare; [when] shaped like a peacock's feather, [it is suited] for grasping praise; the Moon, visible like the moon, [leads] to the acquisition of a kingdom; and in a planetary conjunction, if the Moon is seen situated to the north and in the middle. / And in a conjunction of asterisms, asterisms and the like are also praised according to circumstances. / Now, from the asterism in which Mars rises, in the seventh, eighth, and ninth asterisms, he makes an opening called 'Pūṣan's Face', by which fire-worshipping brahmins and those who live by fire are afflicted. / In the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth, he makes [one] called 'Horse's Face', causing pestilence. / In the thirteenth and fourteenth, [he makes one] called 'Beast's Face', causing an increase in beasts of prey. / In the fifteenth and sixteenth, [he makes] 'Blood Face', portending battle. / In the seventeenth and eighteenth, [he makes] 'Sword Face', causing the predominance of thieves. / Now, Mercury, moving in Bharaṇī, Kṛttikā, and Rohiṇī, moves with the natural course that produces abundance of food.

text_mt: In Āśleṣā, Ārdrā, and Maghā, [he moves with] the mixed [course], granting mixed fruit; in Punarvasu, Puṣya, Pūrvaphālgunī, and Uttaraphālgunī, [he moves with] the shortened [course], likewise granting mixed fruit; in [the asterisms] named Uttarabhādrapadā, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Revatī, Jyeṣṭhā, and Kṛttikā, [he moves with] the sharp [course], causing conflict; through connection with the triad beginning with Mūla, [he moves with the course] granting radiance, fame, and the like; in Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣaj, and Citrā, [he moves with] the terrible [course], bearing terrible fruit. / Jupiter, moving through a zodiacal sign in thirteen months, is auspicious; otherwise, his fruit is difficult. / Now, by the movements of rising and setting of Venus: the first circle of four asterisms beginning with Bharaṇī produces abundance of food; the four beginning with Ārdrā also brings fear to the twice-born; the five asterisms beginning with Jyeṣṭhā produces disease; the six asterisms beginning with Dhaniṣṭhā causes excessive rain. / In whichever asterisms of a country, commodity, or person Saturn moves, many afflictions befall them. / In whichever direction the tail of a comet is blazing, in that direction the king should attack. / An eclipse of Rāhu that is white, red, yellow, or black causes affliction to brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras [respectively]. / Agastya, [if] trembling and summoned by dryness, resembling the crest of a peacock, [is] for fear. / Such also are the Seven Seers; when they are such, even the threefold world is afflicted. In the north-eastern direction, Kumāra rises together with the Pleiades; when he is such, there is affliction to children. / Jupiter, Mercury, and Saturn are city planets. / Mars and Venus are marching planets. / The Moon and the Sun are intermediate. / There, planetary setting occurs in conjunction with the Sun. / Conjunction with the Moon is a mutual battle. / The planet that is gone to the northern path and is very bright becomes victorious. / When a marching planet is victorious and direct, the king should attack his enemies; otherwise, when the city planets are strong, destruction of the marching [attackers] would occur. / When an asterism is afflicted like Agastya, affliction occurs to the country, commodity, and person born of it. / Or, in whichever direction the earthquake goes, to that direction the king should march. / If it is accompanied by a thunderous crash and is prolonged, there would be the death of the king. / In whichever direction a meteor goes, to that direction the king should march.

text_mt: A daytime meteor emerging from the Moon or the Sun, striking upwards, extremely thick, accompanied by sparks, and moving upwards from there, would be for the death of the king. / When a halo is multicolored, there would be affliction of the subjects; whichever direction the halo is broken, to that direction the king should march. / An exceedingly terrifying thunderous crash is for the death of the king. / And in whichever direction it goes, in that direction the king should march. / A city of the gandharvas that appears is for great fear. / A white rainbow at night and in a cloudless sky is for great fear. / A mock sun to the north and south of the Sun causes wind; / standing on both sides, it causes heavy rain; above, it is for the death of the king; / likewise, below, it causes the destruction of the people; / on both sides, it brings great fear everywhere and brings affliction to the three worlds. / Whichever direction is illuminated by the burning of the horizon, in that direction the king should march. / When it is exceedingly bright, showing shadows, one should know it portends the death of the king. / Or rather, in [asterisms classified as] fixed, cruel, fierce, swift, movable, and common, work of a fixed nature and the like, performed appropriately according to each kind, attains success; in [asterisms connected with] Vyatīpāta, Viṣṭi, Vaidhṛta, or in set asterisms, none at all. / And so in asterisms that are smoked, blazed, burnt, or struck by the Sun, fire, or Rāhu, and similarly afflicted by various portents: the asterism in which a person is born is his birth asterism, and from that asterism the tenth, and from that the nineteenth, is to be known as a birth asterism. / From every birth asterism: the second brings prosperity; / the third brings misfortune; / the fourth brings welfare; / the fifth is inimical; / the sixth brings accomplishment; / the seventh brings death; / the eighth brings friendship; / and the ninth brings supreme friendship. / There, in [asterisms that are] prosperity-bringing, welfare-bringing, accomplishing, friendly, and exceedingly friendly, one should perform all undertakings, / and in the tenth asterism. / Performed in an asterism suitable to the actions, avoiding an empty lunar day, / on a day made auspicious and ruled by a gentle [planet], my child, it undoubtedly attains success.

Puṣkara said:
Then Bhṛgu requested the blessed Brahmā: "O Blessed One, I wish to know the wheel of the lunar asterisms."
The Blessed One said to him:
"Child, the wheel of asterisms consists of twelve signs.
And thirty degrees [make up] a sign.
And sixty minutes [make up] a degree.
And sixty seconds [make up] a minute; sixty thirds [make up] a second.
And sixty nāḍikās [make up] a day and night.
Sixty vināḍikās [make up a nāḍikā].
There, that which is a breath in time corresponds to a minute in space.
Therefore, in the amount of time in which a breath occurs—
defined as ten long syllables—in that much time, one minute of the wheel of asterisms rises.
The entire wheel of asterisms [rises] in sixty nāḍikās. There, at the very beginning, the sign is the Ram: red-colored, the head of Time, wild by day and domestic by night, facing east, four-footed, strong at night in the southern direction, movable, rising by the back, cruel, odd, male, the debilitation of Saturn—at twenty [degrees] thus reached is his deep debilitation—the exaltation of the Sun, and at his tenth degree is his deep exaltation, the domicile of Mars, and his trine.
The Bull: white-colored, the face of Time, wild by day and domestic by night, facing south, four-footed, strong at night in the southern direction, fixed, rising by the back, even, gentle, a female sign, the domicile of Venus, the trine of the Moon, and at its third degree is its deep exaltation.
The Twins: a man holding a club and a woman holding a lute, green-colored, the arms of Time, domestic, facing west, two-footed, strong in the eastern direction by day, dual-natured, rising by the head, cruel, odd, a male sign, the domicile of Mercury.
[The Crab] strong, movable, rising by the back, a creature, gentle, even, a female sign, the domicile of the Moon, the debilitation of Mars—at its twenty-eighth degree is his deep debilitation—the exaltation of Jupiter, and at his fifth degree is his deep exaltation.
The Lion: of leonine form, pale-colored, the belly of Time, wild, facing east, four-footed, strong in the southern direction at night, fixed, rising by the head,
