text_mt:
One should fight with this [division] or with two divisions; / but one should station three divisions solely for their protection.
The king should never be placed in the battle array. / When leaves are cut, when fruit is cut, when the branches of a tree are pruned,
it shoots forth again, but when the root is cut, it perishes. / The king should not fight personally, even if possessed of all weapons.
For in the world there are always seen those who are mightier than the mighty. / The ruler of the earth should remain behind the army, just a krośa away.
Rallying broken warriors there is declared [his duty]. / If the leader is broken, no rallying of the army is prescribed.
He should not harass broken enemies, for they have recourse to desperate measures; / resolved on death, they might all kill the enemies and the army as well.
Even by the pretence of a rogue retreat, [a commander] leads [the enemy] to his own advantageous ground. / Then, when they are stationed on his own ground, their slaughter will be easy.

text_mt:
He should not arrange the warriors in the array too closely packed or too scattered, / in such a way that there is no clash of weapons among one another.
Such an arrangement of warriors should be made, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Desiring to break through the enemy's force, he should break it only with dense [units].
Likewise, dense [units] should be formed by one intent on guarding against being broken. / He should form an array according to his own will or after knowing what the enemy has formed.
The king should devise in the array that which brings division to the enemy's array. / Four chariots should be assigned for the protection of an elephant, O twice-born;
and four horses for a chariot, and for a horse, an armoured man; / and bowmen equal [in number] to the armoured men are prescribed there.
Shield-bearers should be placed in front; after them bowmen should be placed; / after the bowmen, cavalry; and after them he should employ chariots.
Elephants should be assigned after chariots by the ruler of the earth. / Armour should be diligently provided for infantry, elephants, and horses.

text_mt:
The man who, without armouring his mount, arms himself, / goes to hell by his own deed, O Rāma.
Warriors of valour should be placed at the forefront; cowards should never be placed there. / Or, having placed warriors at the head, merely a display of an army's bulk
should be made with a multitude of cowards, causing the enemy to flee. / But in the front, fleeing cowards tear through [their own ranks] ahead.
Firmly stationed, they repel the cowards [and encourage] the brave once more. / Men who are tall, have parrot-like noses, and have squinting eyes,
and whose eyebrows meet, who are prone to anger and fond of strife, / always cheerful, short in stature, and lustful, should be known as brave.
Southerners should be known as skilled sword-and-shield fighters; / the Vaṅkalas should be known as archers, and likewise the mountaineers;
the mountain-dwellers are also skilled in stone-fighting. / The men of Pañcāla and Śūrasena are skilled in chariots;

those of Kamboja and Gāndhāra are skilled on horses; / and generally the mlecchas are to be known as snare-fighters;
the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, and Kaliṅgas are to be known as elephant-fighters. / The task of carrying the wounded and the slain from the battlefield,
the giving of water and the like to foot-soldiers and elephants, / and the fetching of weapons is prescribed as the work of the infantry.
The protection of one's own army against enemies wishing to divide it, / and the piercing of dense [ranks] is proclaimed as the work of the shield-bearer.
Turning the bowmen around in battle is also thus spoken of. / The rallying even of broken [troops] is accomplished by heroic shield-bearers.
As far as the retreat of the brave is concerned, that is spoken of as belonging to the cavalry; / the terrifying of enemy armies is spoken of as the work of the chariot.
The demolition of ramparts, gates, towers, and trees, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / which is unbearable to enemies, is designated as the work of elephants.
Uneven ground is to be known as that of infantry, and even ground as that of chariots and horses; / ground with soft soil and trees is declared the battleground for elephants.

text_mt:
Having thus arranged the battle array, with the sun behind his back, / or likewise with Venus in his favour, as well as the guardians of the directions, Mercury, and the wind,
he should encourage all the warriors, O Rāma, by their lineage and past deeds: / 'There is the attainment of enjoyment in victory, and attainment of heaven for the slain!
Auspicious omens declare victory, O twice-born: / the throbbing of auspicious limbs, the seeing of auspicious dreams,
and auspicious signs of elephants and horses are seen on every side; / indeed, omens and auspicious birds are seen agreeable to the mind!
Death touches only the contrary crawlers [on the ground], not otherwise! / You also are born of good family, masters of all weapons and missiles,
always devoted to noble conduct, always adhering to the right path, / never corruptible by enemies; how could victory not be mine?
The majesty of royalty is yours alone, and mine is solely through you. / Only two chowries and a parasol, resembling a shield, are superior [as royal marks], O warriors!

शूराणां यद्विनिर्याति रक्तमाबाधतः क्वचित् ..
तेनैव सह पाप्मानं सर्व त्यजति धार्मिक .. 58 ..
तथा बाधचिकित्सायां वेदनासहिते तथा ..
ततो नास्त्यधिकं लोके किञ्चित्परमदारुणम् .. 59 ..
मृतस्य नाग्निसंस्कारो नाशौचन्नोदकक्रिया ..
कर्तुमिच्छति यस्येह संग्रामादधिकं नु किम् .. 2.177.60 ..
text_mt:
To the victors belongs the attainment of enjoyment, and to the slain the highest destination. / Discharging the master's bread [has no equal]; there is no state equal to battle!
Whatever blood issues forth from the wound of warriors anywhere, / with that alone he casts off all sin, O righteous one!
Likewise, in the treatment of wounds, when accompanied by intense pain, / there is nothing greater or more terrible in the world than that.
For the slain there is no cremation rite, no ritual impurity, and no water-offering; / for one who wishes to make [an offering], what indeed is greater in this world than battle?

sanskrit_iast:
tapasvino dānaparā yajvāno bahudakṣiṇāḥ ..
śūrāṇāṃ gatimicchanti dṛṣṭvā bhogānanuttamān ..61 ..
meaning:
तपस्विनो दानपरा यज्वानो बहुदक्षिणाः ..
शूराणां गतिमिच्छन्ति दृष्ट्वा भोगाननुत्तमान् ..61 ..
text_mt: Ascetics, the generous, and sacrificers who give lavish sacrificial fees / desire the destiny of heroes upon seeing their unsurpassed enjoyments.

sanskrit_iast:
varāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi śūramāyodhane hatam ..
abhidravanti kāmārtā mama bhartā bhaviṣyati .. 62 ..
meaning:
वराप्सरःसहस्राणि शूरमायोधने हतम् ..
अभिद्रवन्ति कामार्ता मम भर्ता भविष्यति .. 62 ..
text_mt: Thousands of foremost apsarases rush toward a hero slain in battle, / afflicted with longing: "He shall be my husband!"

sanskrit_iast:
svāmī sukṛtamādatte bhagnānāṃ vinivartatām ..
brahmahatyāphalaṃ teṣāṃ tathā proktaṃ padepade .. 63 ..
meaning:
स्वामी सुकृतमादत्ते भग्नानां विनिवर्तताम् ..
ब्रह्महत्याफलं तेषां तथा प्रोक्तं पदेपदे .. 63 ..
text_mt: The master takes the good karma of those who are routed and turn back; / the fruit of killing a brahmin is proclaimed for them at every step.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ sahāyānparityajya svastimāngantumicchati ..
asvasti tasya kurvanti devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ .. 64 ..
meaning:
यः सहायान्परित्यज्य स्वस्तिमान्गन्तुमिच्छति ..
अस्वस्ति तस्य कुर्वन्ति देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः .. 64 ..
text_mt: He who, abandoning his companions, wishes to escape safely, / the gods headed by Śakra bring misfortune upon him.

sanskrit_iast:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ proktaṃ bhagnānāmanivartatām ..
padepade mahābhāgā saṃmukhānāṃ mahātmanām .. 65 ..
meaning:
अश्वमेधफलं प्रोक्तं भग्नानामनिवर्तताम् ..
पदेपदे महाभागा संमुखानां महात्मनाम् .. 65 ..
text_mt: The fruit of the horse sacrifice is declared at every step, O fortunate one, / for those who are broken but do not turn back, confronting [the enemy], noble in spirit.

sanskrit_iast:
devastriyastathā lakṣmīḥ pāpmānamayaśastathā ..
pratīkṣante mahābhāga saṃgrāme samupasthite .. 66 ..
meaning:
देवस्त्रियस्तथा लक्ष्मीः पाप्मानमयशस्तथा ..
प्रतीक्षन्ते महाभाग संग्रामे समुपस्थिते .. 66 ..
text_mt: Celestial women and fortune, as well as sin and dishonour, / await, O fortunate one, when battle is at hand.'

sanskrit_iast:
parāṅmukhā mayā grāhyā jīvantopyabhavā mṛtāḥ ..
ityevamayaśastasya pāpmanā saha tiṣṭhati .. 67 ..
meaning:
पराङ्मुखा मया ग्राह्या जीवन्तोप्यभवा मृताः ..
इत्येवमयशस्तस्य पाप्मना सह तिष्ठति .. 67 ..
text_mt: "Those who turn their backs are to be seized by me; whether living or dead, they have no future." / In this way disgrace stands along with sin for him.

sanskrit_iast: lakṣmīḥ santiṣṭhate tasya jīvataḥ kṛtakarmaṇaḥ .. 68 ..
meaning: लक्ष्मीः सन्तिष्ठते तस्य जीवतः कृतकर्मणः .. 68 ..
text_mt: Fortune abides with him who is alive and has done his duty;

sanskrit_iast:
mṛtasya cāpi tiṣṭhanti vimānasthā surastriyaḥ ..
evamudghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā dharmeṇecchejjayaṃ raṇe .. 69 ..
meaning:
मृतस्य चापि तिष्ठन्ति विमानस्था सुरस्त्रियः ..
एवमुद्घोषणं कृत्वा धर्मेणेच्छेज्जयं रणे .. 69 ..
text_mt: and for him who is dead, celestial women seated in aerial chariots await. / Having made such a proclamation, he should desire victory in battle according to dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
adharmavijayo rājño nṛpaloke bhayāvahaḥ ..
adharmavijayādarthairyacchidramupadhīyate .. 2.177.70 ..
meaning:
अधर्मविजयो राज्ञो नृपलोके भयावहः ..
अधर्मविजयादर्थैर्यच्छिद्रमुपधीयते .. 2.177.70 ..
text_mt: A king's victory through adharma brings terror to the world of kings. / Whatever gap is covered by wealth gained from victory through adharma,

sanskrit_iast:
chidrādeva paraṃ chidraṃ tasya syānnātra saṃśayaḥ ..
na karṇī na tathā digdhaḥ śaraḥ syāddharmayodhinām .. 71 ..
meaning:
छिद्रादेव परं छिद्रं तस्य स्यान्नात्र संशयः ..
न कर्णी न तथा दिग्धः शरः स्याद्धर्मयोधिनाम् .. 71 ..
text_mt: a greater gap indeed arises from that very gap; of this there is no doubt. / An arrow should not be barbed, nor poisoned, for those who fight according to dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsthiśalyaḥ śaraḥ kāryo dāruśalyaśca bhārgava ..
samaḥ samena yoddhavyo nāpacāro raṇe dvija .. 72 ..
meaning:
नास्थिशल्यः शरः कार्यो दारुशल्यश्च भार्गव ..
समः समेन योद्धव्यो नापचारो रणे द्विज .. 72 ..
text_mt: An arrow should not have a bone tip, nor a wooden tip, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / An equal should fight with an equal; there must be no transgression in battle, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
sannaddhena ca sannaddhaḥ sāśvaścāśvagatena tu ..
rathī ca rathinā rāma padātiśca padātinā .. 73 ..
meaning:
सन्नद्धेन च सन्नद्धः साश्वश्चाश्वगतेन तु ..
रथी च रथिना राम पदातिश्च पदातिना .. 73 ..
text_mt: An armored man [should fight] with an armored man, and a horseman with one mounted on a horse; / a charioteer with a charioteer, O Rāma, and a foot-soldier with a foot-soldier.

sanskrit_iast:
kuñjarastho gajasthena yoddhavyo bhṛgunandana ..
vimukho bhagnaśastraśca strībālaparirakṣitā .. 74 ..
meaning:
कुञ्जरस्थो गजस्थेन योद्धव्यो भृगुनन्दन ..
विमुखो भग्नशस्त्रश्च स्त्रीबालपरिरक्षिता .. 74 ..
text_mt: One mounted on an elephant should fight with one on an elephant, O scion of Bhṛgu. / One whose back is turned, one whose weapon is broken, one protecting women and children,

sanskrit_iast:
vyāyudho bhagnagātraśca tathaiva śaraṇāgataḥ ..
pareṇa yuddhyamānaśca yuddhaprekṣaka eva ca .. 75 ..
meaning:
व्यायुधो भग्नगात्रश्च तथैव शरणागतः ..
परेण युद्ध्यमानश्च युद्धप्रेक्षक एव च .. 75 ..
text_mt: one who has laid down weapons, one whose limbs are broken, and likewise one who has sought refuge, / one fighting with another, and a spectator of the battle,

sanskrit_iast:
ārtastoyapradātā ca daṇḍapāṇistathaiva ca ..
ete raṇe na hantavyā kṣatradharmamabhīpsatā .. 76 ..
meaning:
आर्तस्तोयप्रदाता च दण्डपाणिस्तथैव च ..
एते रणे न हन्तव्या क्षत्रधर्ममभीप्सता .. 76 ..
text_mt: a distressed person, a water-giver, and likewise one who holds only a staff— / these must not be slain in battle by one who desires the kṣatriya dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
pāpiṣṭho kūṭayuddhe ca kartavyamapi cāhave ..
śrāntena vābhibhūtena ardhottīrṇabalena ca .. 77 ..
meaning:
पापिष्ठो कूटयुद्धे च कर्तव्यमपि चाहवे ..
श्रान्तेन वाभिभूतेन अर्धोत्तीर्णबलेन च .. 77 ..
text_mt: The most wicked [deed] must be done in deceptive warfare and in combat / against one who is exhausted, overcome, or whose army has only half-crossed [a river].

sanskrit_iast: durdine na ca yuddhāni kartavyāni mahābala .. 78 ..
meaning: दुर्दिने न च युद्धानि कर्तव्यानि महाबल .. 78 ..
text_mt: And battles should not be fought on a bad day, O mighty one.

sanskrit_iast:
pravṛtte samare rāma pareṣāṃ nāmakāraṇāt ..
bāhū pragṛhya vikrośedbhagnā bhagnāḥ pare tviti ..
prāptaṃ mitrabalaṃ bhūri nāyako'tra nipātitaḥ .. 79 ..
meaning:
प्रवृत्ते समरे राम परेषां नामकारणात् ..
बाहू प्रगृह्य विक्रोशेद्भग्ना भग्नाः परे त्विति ..
प्राप्तं मित्रबलं भूरि नायकोऽत्र निपातितः .. 79 ..
text_mt: When the battle has begun, O Rāma, for the purpose of [demoralizing] the enemies, / holding up both arms he should shout: "Broken, the enemies are broken! / An abundant allied force has arrived! The leader here is struck down!

sanskrit_iast:
senānīrnihataścāyaṃ sarvā senāpi vidrutā ..
evaṃ citrāsanaṃ kuryātpareṣāṃ bhṛgunandana .. 2.177.80 ..
meaning:
सेनानीर्निहतश्चायं सर्वा सेनापि विद्रुता ..
एवं चित्रासनं कुर्यात्परेषां भृगुनन्दन .. 2.177.80 ..
text_mt: This army commander is slain! The entire army has fled!" / In this way, O scion of Bhṛgu, one should cause dismay among the enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
vidrutānāṃ tu yodhānāṃ suvighāto vidhīyate ..
dhanurvedavidhānena kalpanā ca tathā bhavet .. 81 ..
meaning:
विद्रुतानां तु योधानां सुविघातो विधीयते ..
धनुर्वेदविधानेन कल्पना च तथा भवेत् .. 81 ..
text_mt: A successful pursuit of fleeing warriors is prescribed; / and an arrangement should be made according to the rules of the Dhanurveda.

sanskrit_iast:
pāpāśca deyā dharmajña tathaiva paramohanāḥ ..
patākābhyucchrayaḥ kāryaḥ svabale ca tathā śubhaḥ .. 82 ..
meaning:
पापाश्च देया धर्मज्ञ तथैव परमोहनाः ..
पताकाभ्युच्छ्रयः कार्यः स्वबले च तथा शुभः .. 82 ..
text_mt: And wicked [tricks] should be used, O knower of dharma, which cause extreme confusion. / An auspicious raising of banners should be done among one's own troops,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃskāraścaiva kartavyo vāditrāṇāṃ bhayāvahaḥ ..
etasya varṣaṃ vakṣyāmi tavopaniṣadi dvija .. 83 ..
meaning:
संस्कारश्चैव कर्तव्यो वादित्राणां भयावहः ..
एतस्य वर्षं वक्ष्यामि तवोपनिषदि द्विज .. 83 ..
text_mt: and terrifying preparation of musical instruments should be made. / I shall declare its verse to you in the secret teaching, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃprāpya vijayaṃ yuddhe kāryaṃ daivatapūjanam ..
pūjayedbrāhmaṇāṃścātra gurūnapi ca pūjayet .. 84 ..
meaning:
संप्राप्य विजयं युद्धे कार्यं दैवतपूजनम् ..
पूजयेद्ब्राह्मणांश्चात्र गुरूनपि च पूजयेत् .. 84 ..
text_mt: Having obtained victory in battle, worship of the deities must be performed; / one should worship the brahmins there, and also worship the elders.

sanskrit_iast:
ratnāni rājagāmīni carma vāhanamāyudham ..
sarvamanyadbhavettasya yadyenaiva raṇe hṛtam .. 85 ..
meaning:
रत्नानि राजगामीनि चर्म वाहनमायुधम् ..
सर्वमन्यद्भवेत्तस्य यद्येनैव रणे हृतम् .. 85 ..
text_mt: Gems go to the king, as do shields, mounts, and weapons; / everything else belongs to him by whom it was seized in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
kulastriyastu vijñeyāstathā rāma na kasyacit ..
svadeśe paradeśe vā sādhvīṃ yatnānna dūṣayet .. 86 ..
meaning:
कुलस्त्रियस्तु विज्ञेयास्तथा राम न कस्यचित् ..
स्वदेशे परदेशे वा साध्वीं यत्नान्न दूषयेत् .. 86 ..
text_mt: Women of noble family, however, O Rāma, should be known as belonging to no one; / in one's own country or in a foreign country, one should not dishonor a virtuous woman with effort.

sanskrit_iast:
anyathā saṃkaro ghoro bhavatīha kṣayāvahaḥ ..
śakraḥ prāpya raṇe muktaḥ putrastasya prakīrtitaḥ .. 87 ..
meaning:
अन्यथा संकरो घोरो भवतीह क्षयावहः ..
शक्रः प्राप्य रणे मुक्तः पुत्रस्तस्य प्रकीर्तितः .. 87 ..
text_mt: Otherwise, a terrible mixture [of castes] arises here, which brings ruin. / Śakra, captured in battle, was released; his son is proclaimed [as an example].

sanskrit_iast:
purastenāsya yoddhavyaṃ tasya dharmaṃ vijānatā ..
deśedeśe ya ācāraḥ pāramparyakramāgataḥ .. 88 ..
meaning:
पुरस्तेनास्य योद्धव्यं तस्य धर्मं विजानता ..
देशेदेशे य आचारः पारम्पर्यक्रमागतः .. 88 ..
text_mt: One who knows dharma should fight in front of him. / Whatever custom exists in each country, handed down through tradition,

sanskrit_iast:
sa eva paripālyaḥ syātprāpya deśaṃ mahīkṣitā ..
nṛṇāṃ pradarśayedrājā samare'pi hate ripau .. 89 ..
meaning:
स एव परिपाल्यः स्यात्प्राप्य देशं महीक्षिता ..
नृणां प्रदर्शयेद्राजा समरेऽपि हते रिपौ .. 89 ..
text_mt: that very [custom] should be protected by the ruler of the earth upon acquiring the land. / Even when the enemy is slain in battle, the king should show to the people:

sanskrit_iast:
na me priyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena yenāyaṃ samare hataḥ ..
kintu pūjā karomyasya svacchandamavijānataḥ .. 2.177.90 ..
meaning:
न मे प्रियं कृतं तेन येनायं समरे हतः ..
किन्तु पूजा करोम्यस्य स्वच्छन्दमविजानतः .. 2.177.90 ..
text_mt: "Nothing pleasing was done for me by him by whom this [foe] was killed in battle. / Yet I show honor to him who did not know my wish;

sanskrit_iast:
hato'yaṃ maddhitārthāya priyaṃ yadyapi no mama ..
aputrāśca striyaścaiva nṛpatiḥ paripālayet .. 91 ..
meaning:
हतोऽयं मद्धितार्थाय प्रियं यद्यपि नो मम ..
अपुत्राश्च स्त्रियश्चैव नृपतिः परिपालयेत् .. 91 ..
text_mt: he was slain for my benefit, even though it is not pleasing to me." / And the king should protect the childless women [of the enemy].

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu svapuraṃ prāpya nṛpatiḥ praviśedgṛham ..
yātrāvidhānavihitaṃ bhūyo daivatapūjanam .. 92 ..
meaning:
ततस्तु स्वपुरं प्राप्य नृपतिः प्रविशेद्गृहम् ..
यात्राविधानविहितं भूयो दैवतपूजनम् .. 92 ..
text_mt: Then, having reached his own city, the king should enter his palace. / Worship of the deities as prescribed for the return from an expedition [should be done] again,

sanskrit_iast:
pitṝṇāṃ pūjanaṃ caiva tathā kuryādviśeṣavat ..
saṃvibhāgaṃ parāvāpteḥ kuryādbhṛtyajanasya tu .. 93 ..
meaning:
पितॄणां पूजनं चैव तथा कुर्याद्विशेषवत् ..
संविभागं परावाप्तेः कुर्याद्भृत्यजनस्य तु .. 93 ..
text_mt: and he should particularly perform worship of the ancestors. / He should make a distribution of the spoils to his attendants.

sanskrit_iast:
avāpya dharmeṇa nṛpastu pṛthvīmārāmayūpādisurālayāṅkām ..
kṛtvā tathānyāṃ dvijasācca śaktyā lokaṃ jayaṃtyasya narādhipasya .. 94 ..
2.178
rāma uvāca ..
dhanurvedaṃ samācakṣva saṃkṣepātsuranandana ..
sarvaṃ tvameva jānāsi yathā devaḥ pitāmahaḥ .. .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
catuṣpādo dhanurvedastathā pañcavidho dvija ..
rathanāgāśvapattīnāṃ pādānāśritya kīrtitaḥ .. 2 ..
yantramuktaṃ prāṇimuktaṃ muktasandhāritaṃ tathā ..
amuktaṃ bāhuyuddhaṃ ca pañcadhā tatprakīrtitam .. 3 ..
tacca śastrāstrasaṃpattyā dvividhaṃ parikīrtitam ..
daṇḍamāyāvibhedena bhūyo dvividhamucyate ..
ṛjumāyāvibhedena bhūyo dvividhamucyate .. 4 ..
kṣepaṇīcāpayantrādyaṃ yantramuktaṃ prakīrtitam .. 5 ..
śilātomaracakrādyaṃ pāṇimuktaṃ tathaiva ca ..
muktasandhāritaṃ jñeyaṃ pāśādyamapi yadbhavet .. 6 ..
meaning:
अवाप्य धर्मेण नृपस्तु पृथ्वीमारामयूपादिसुरालयाङ्काम् ..
कृत्वा तथान्यां द्विजसाच्च शक्त्या लोकं जयंत्यस्य नराधिपस्य .. 94 ..
2.178
राम उवाच ..
धनुर्वेदं समाचक्ष्व संक्षेपात्सुरनन्दन ..
सर्वं त्वमेव जानासि यथा देवः पितामहः .. .. 1 ..
पुष्कर उवाच ..
चतुष्पादो धनुर्वेदस्तथा पञ्चविधो द्विज ..
रथनागाश्वपत्तीनां पादानाश्रित्य कीर्तितः .. 2 ..
यन्त्रमुक्तं प्राणिमुक्तं मुक्तसन्धारितं तथा ..
अमुक्तं बाहुयुद्धं च पञ्चधा तत्प्रकीर्तितम् .. 3 ..
तच्च शस्त्रास्त्रसंपत्त्या द्विविधं परिकीर्तितम् ..
दण्डमायाविभेदेन भूयो द्विविधमुच्यते ..
ऋजुमायाविभेदेन भूयो द्विविधमुच्यते .. 4 ..

Having acquired the earth through dharma, marked with gardens, sacrificial posts, and temples of the gods, / and having given other [lands] according to his ability to twice-born men, [the subjects] conquer the world for this lord of men.
Rāma said: / Explain the Dhanurveda in brief, O delight of the gods; / you know everything, just like the divine Grandfather.
Puṣkara said: / The Dhanurveda has four quarters and five divisions, O twice-born, / proclaimed as resting on the quarters of chariots, elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers.
Discharged from machines, discharged by hand, discharged and retained, / unreleased, and hand-to-hand combat—thus it is declared to be fivefold.
And that is declared to be twofold through the attainment of weapons and missiles; / it is further said to be twofold by the distinction of force and deceit; / it is further said to be twofold by the distinction of straightforward and deceptive [methods].
Sling, bow, machine, and the like are declared to be discharged from machines.
A stone, a javelin, a discus, and the like are discharged by hand; / that which is a noose and the like should be known as discharged and retained.

In that regard, fitness of the limbs is prescribed at the very beginning, / as well as practice of exercise and pulling loads.
For he who has conquered fatigue will attain fitness for action in battles. / And he should practice those weapons on the backs of chariots, horses, and elephants; / they have swords as the chief and hands as the lowest. / In the Dhanurveda, an inspired teacher is declared to be the teacher for the two [upper] classes.
A twice-born may or may not act as teacher to a vaiśya; / a śūdra should never act as a teacher in the Dhanurveda.
Fitness for action should be acquired by a śūdra by himself; / therefore, even a śūdra has the qualification for fighting, O lord of the people.
He should also be beneficial in battles for his master by himself. / A king should be protected with effort by means of all precious things, O great king.

Puṣkara said:
If both the palms, soles of the feet, and the back are aligned,
this stance is seen as sāmapada, according to its characteristics.
With the toes turned outwards, the buttocks [tucked], both feet with knees stiff and firm, / and an interval of three spans—thus the vaiśākha stance is described.
Where both knees are raised with feet forming a circle, / divided into four kinds and separated by three [spans], that is known as the maṇḍala stance.
That which resembles an arrowhead, with the right knee and thigh held rigid, / and five spans in breadth, is celebrated as the ālīḍha stance.
The forward shank bent is always prescribed for the ālīḍha;
the left [foot] should be placed transversely, and the right should be straight.
The two ankles firmly resting on the heels, separated by five fingers' width—
this posture is twelve fingers in length.

text_mt:
Those skilled in the science of archery know the eldest as the supreme.
The eldest should be known as Pāvaka, and consists of twelve fist-lengths.
The Sādhya has eleven, and the smallest has ten fist-lengths.
A bow of four cubits is best, and its application is middling.
A bow of three [cubits] is declared as the smallest, always for a foot-soldier;
on a horse, chariot, or elephant, that same [four-cubit bow] is proclaimed as the best.
Lesser than that indeed would be middling, and lesser still the smallest.
This rule for one equipped with weapons has been told to you in brief, O foremost of the Bhrgu lineage.
2.180
Puṣkara said:
Equipped with weapons, having made an offering with the flesh of dead / boars, deer, and sheep, and likewise of buffaloes and the like, O twice-born,
the king, knowing the rituals, should then have the chariot washed by sages;
provided with a soft spread, he should harness soft and charming [steeds].
Then, having mounted the steed, armored and well-concentrated, / having mounted swiftly, he should fasten the right girth securely.

text_mt:
He should wear that bow across the chest, placed in a harness.
Then he should draw an arrow with his right hand,
swiftly grasping and holding everything together in the middle.
With the left hand, he should indeed draw the bow from that side.
Having the wrist firmly settled, he should place the nock on the bowstring;
pressing firmly with the lion's ear grip, level with the nock,
with the arrowhead resting above the left ear from holding it an arm-span wide,
he should hold the string with the middle and the left finger.
Having directed his mind and his gaze onto the target, knowing the ritual well,
he should quickly release the string on the right side of the body.
Positioned at the hollow of the forehead, he should direct the arrow at the target.
Having drawn back, he should strike the sixteen-finger rod there;
having released the arrow, he should then practice with the bowstring from time to time.
He should grasp [the string] with the middle finger again and again;
aiming at the target, he should shoot arrows, [whether standing] square or on the right.

Striking the eyes, striking the arms, and striking the flanks, O Bhārgava, / straight, crooked, and thrusting: [these] are proclaimed [the actions] of the lance.
Joined, extended, leftward, zigzag like cow-urine, moving like a lotus, / then bent half-way, left and right,
turned around, turned back, kicked up by the feet, unobstructed, / and the swan's path and wrong path: [these] are proclaimed the actions of the mace.
The terrifying, monastery-felling, the ten calamities, / thrown, held in hand, and empty: one should designate [these] of the battle-axe.
Beating, cutting, O Rāma, and crushing: / these are the actions of the mallet, and also of the club.
Edge, middle, turned back, and half-command: / these indeed are the actions of the thunderbolt, and likewise of the paṭṭiśa.

text_mt:
The principal actions have been told to you regarding the chief weapons, O hero among men; / these are the names and forms to be known, each according to its nature.
Puṣkara said: / [The warriors] must be armored, bearing shields, and with girded daggers. / The shields there should be of tiger, buffalo, and bull hides,
or shields made of bucklers and so forth, O Rāma; / likewise, the foremost shields and various types of swords,
with bound [weapons] and the like, with quivers, and, O Rāma, with lances; / with fastened arm-guards and finger-guards, with fastened breastplates, formidable,
and equipped with battle-axes, O Rāma, fighters proficient with the bow.
Likewise, mace-bearers here, accompanied by attendants with daggers, / well-armored, resolute-minded, should possess vast energy.
Wherever and in whatever skill one is especially proficient with weapons or missiles, / precisely that is prescribed for him, properly, O best of men.

With bits, with saddles, and with saddlecloths, the horses / should be equipped with armor in battle, wearing chowries and crests.
The cavalryman should be well-armored, skilled in holding the reins, / and with a shield, O Rāma, having a dagger and equipment,
with fastened sword, fastened bowstring, firm in riding a horse, / with a good spear, O Rāma, and bearing various weapons.
The chariot should likewise be prepared, fitted with lovely yoke-poles and shafts, / equipped with good wheels and accessories, of all forms, splendid with banners,
covered with three woven bands, shielded with tiger skin, / having the sound of nets of jingling bells, and indeed very stable;
with quivers, arrow-cases, quivers, excellent bows, / equipped with all weapons, and furnished with missile-throwers,
furnished with water, cumin, flour balls, and likewise with horns; / armored there, O Rāma, the charioteer should have a goad,
knowing how to take the reins, and skilled in circular movements, / and knowing the horse's nature, far-sighted, well-controlled,

sitting well, knowing time, with fastened sword, provided with a noose; / the rear-guard should know weapons, likewise being skilled in arms,
whose long-established place is at the base, mighty-armed, / who shields the banner and supplies weapons,
and protects the charioteer when an illustrious [foe] approaches. / There should be two archers there, and both should be car-warriors,
two warriors, O best of bowmen, skilled in all weapons. / The horses on the chariot should be well-armored and trained,
of equal speed and strength, and lightly equipped. / Hereafter I shall declare to you the preparation of royal elephants.
The elephant should be well-armored, with a saddle, covered with a carpet, / carrying all weapons, and the warriors [upon it] bearing excellent weapons.
[They should be] holding battle-axes in hand, provided with water and cumin, / properly stationed, and likewise equipped with chains.

text_mt:
And a very splendid banner should be fixed upon the elephant. / Two bull-like men should be there, wielding excellent goads:
one of them stationed on the back, and the second should be on the neck. / Two warriors should be excellent bowmen, and two holding swords [...],
and devoted to protecting them both. / Stationed at the rear should be one bearing an excellent spear and banner,
so that he protects the hindquarters of the elephant, O wise one. / In this way their mutual protection should be arranged,
of the elephant-driver, O knower of dharma, and of the elephant-warrior. / In this very same way, a chariot-warrior must be protected by another chariot-warrior.
For the protection of an elephant, there should be four chariots. / For every chariot or elephant, there should be three horses.
Three bowmen are prescribed for the protection of a horse; / for the protection of an archer, one should also deploy armored soldiers.

text_mt:
Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-third chapter, entitled 'Equipping the Mounts' in the Dhanurveda, within the discourse of Puṣkara to Rāma, in the conversation between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the second book of the venerable Viṣṇudharmottara, [part of] the second section in the venerable Viṣṇu Mahāpurāṇa.
Here ends the second book of the Viṣṇudharmottara.

sanskrit_iast: 30 grahocitradikṣu vṛkṣaropaṇamudyānakūpavāpyādinirmāṇaṃ phalapuṣpasampattaye bheṣajyadohanaṃ vṛkṣāyurvedādi ca
meaning: 30 ग्रहोचित्रदिक्षु वृक्षरोपणमुद्यानकूपवाप्यादिनिर्माणं फलपुष्पसम्पत्तये भेषज्यदोहनं वृक्षायुर्वेदादि च
text_mt: 30. Planting trees in appropriate directions around houses, constructing gardens, wells, and cisterns; medicinal fumigations and milking to ensure abundance of fruits and flowers; and Vṛkṣāyurveda.

sanskrit_iast: 31 devatāgṛhalepanamārjanagandhānulepanapatākādānapūjanādimāhātmyakathanapurassaraṃ devadravyāpahārādidoṣakathanam
meaning: 31 देवतागृहलेपनमार्जनगन्धानुलेपनपताकादानपूजनादिमाहात्म्यकथनपुरस्सरं देवद्रव्यापहारादिदोषकथनम्
text_mt: 31. Smearing, cleaning, fragrant anointing, offering flags, and worshiping at shrines; statement of faults such as stealing divine property, preceded by a discourse on their greatness.

sanskrit_iast: 32 brāhmaṇamāhātmyavarṇanam -
meaning: 32 ब्राह्मणमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् -
text_mt: 32. Description of the greatness of brahmins.

sanskrit_iast: 33 sādhvīpraśaṃsābhidhānam
meaning: 33 साध्वीप्रशंसाभिधानम्
text_mt: 33. Declaration of praise for a virtuous wife.

sanskrit_iast: 34 pativratākartavyavarṇane mūlakarma-( mantratantravaśīkaraṇādi ) nindā
meaning: 34 पतिव्रताकर्तव्यवर्णने मूलकर्म-( मन्त्रतन्त्रवशीकरणादि ) निन्दा
text_mt: 34. In describing the duties of a faithful wife, condemnation of root-sorcery (subjugation by mantras and tantric rites).

sanskrit_iast: 35 strīdevatāpūjananirūpaṇam
meaning: 35 स्त्रीदेवतापूजननिरूपणम्
text_mt: 35. Exposition on the worship of female deities.

sanskrit_iast: 36 sāvitryupākhyāne sāvitrīsatyavratayorindhanānayanārthaṃ vanagamanam |
meaning: 36 सावित्र्युपाख्याने सावित्रीसत्यव्रतयोरिन्धनानयनार्थं वनगमनम् |
text_mt: 36. In the narrative of Sāvitrī: the journey to the forest by Sāvitrī and Satyavat to gather firewood.

sanskrit_iast: 37 kāṣṭhāni pātayataḥ satyavataḥ śirovedanayā paṃcatve yamena tasya liṃgaśarīrasya nayanaṃ sāvitryāśca tadanugamanadārḍhyaṃ vilokya yamena varadānam
meaning: 37 काष्ठानि पातयतः सत्यवतः शिरोवेदनया पंचत्वे यमेन तस्य लिंगशरीरस्य नयनं सावित्र्याश्च तदनुगमनदार्ढ्यं विलोक्य यमेन वरदानम्
text_mt: 37. Satyavat while chopping wood succumbs to death from a headache; Yama leads away his subtle body; seeing Sāvitrī's steadfastness in following him, Yama grants a boon.

sanskrit_iast: 38 sāvitrīyamopākhyāne sāvitryai sahodarabhrātṛśataprāptivaradānam
meaning: 38 सावित्रीयमोपाख्याने सावित्र्यै सहोदरभ्रातृशतप्राप्तिवरदानम्
text_mt: 38. In the narrative of Sāvitrī and Yama: granting the boon of obtaining a hundred uterine brothers to Sāvitrī.

sanskrit_iast: 39 sāvitryai yamenaurasraśataputraprāptivaradānam ...
meaning: 39 सावित्र्यै यमेनौरस्रशतपुत्रप्राप्तिवरदानम् ...
text_mt: 39. Yama granting to Sāvitrī the boon of obtaining a hundred sons born of her own body.

sanskrit_iast: 40 sāvitrīstutituṣṭayamena satyavataḥ parityāgastasmā āyuṣonte svargabhogaprāptivaradānam
meaning: 40 सावित्रीस्तुतितुष्टयमेन सत्यवतः परित्यागस्तस्मा आयुषोन्ते स्वर्गभोगप्राप्तिवरदानम्
text_mt: 40. Yama, pleased by Sāvitrī's praise, releases Satyavat and grants the boon of heavenly enjoyment at the end of his lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: 41 prāptajīvanaḥ satyavān sāvitryā saha gṛhaṃ gataḥ, tatpitā labdhacakṣurbhūtvā rājyamapi lebhe .
meaning: 41 प्राप्तजीवनः सत्यवान् सावित्र्या सह गृहं गतः, तत्पिता लब्धचक्षुर्भूत्वा राज्यमपि लेभे .
text_mt: 41. Restored to life, Satyavat returned home with Sāvitrī; his father regained his eyesight and also recovered his kingdom.

sanskrit_iast: 42 rājñā sadā gopālanaṃ kartavyaṃ, gogrāsapradāna gosevana tadanugamana tadārtiharaṇādimāhātmyavarṇanam
meaning: 42 राज्ञा सदा गोपालनं कर्तव्यं, गोग्रासप्रदान गोसेवन तदनुगमन तदार्तिहरणादिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
text_mt: 42. A king should always protect cattle; description of the greatness of feeding mouthfuls to cows, serving cows, following them, relieving their distress, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 43 gocikitsāvarṇanam
meaning: 43 गोचिकित्सावर्णनम्
text_mt: 43. Description of veterinary medicine for cows.

sanskrit_iast: 44 gośāntikarmaprasaṃgenāśvayukśuklapaṃcadaśyāmindrayāgavarṇanam
meaning: 44 गोशान्तिकर्मप्रसंगेनाश्वयुक्शुक्लपंचदश्यामिन्द्रयागवर्णनम्
text_mt: 44. In the context of cow-pacification rites, description of the Indra sacrifice on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina.

sanskrit_iast: 45 sainye aśvapraśaṃsā, kṣudhiteṣu teṣvaśvapateramaṃgalam
meaning: 45 सैन्ये अश्वप्रशंसा, क्षुधितेषु तेष्वश्वपतेरमंगलम्
text_mt: 45. Praise of horses in the army; misfortune for the owner of horses if they are hungry.

sanskrit_iast: 46 aśvacikitsā
meaning: 46 अश्वचिकित्सा
text_mt: 46. Veterinary treatment of horses.

sanskrit_iast: 47 aśvaśāṃtiḥ
meaning: 47 अश्वशांतिः
text_mt: 47. Pacification ritual for horses.

sanskrit_iast: 48 gajapraśaṃsā, kṣudhiteṣu teṣu rājanāśaḥ –
meaning: 48 गजप्रशंसा, क्षुधितेषु तेषु राजनाशः –
text_mt: 48. Praise of elephants; the ruin of the king when they are starved.

sanskrit_iast: 49 hasticikitsā
meaning: 49 हस्तिचिकित्सा
text_mt: 49. Medical treatment of elephants.

sanskrit_iast: 42 rājñā sadā gopālanaṃ kartavyaṃ, gogrāsapradānagosevanatadanugamanatadārti
meaning: 42 राज्ञा सदा गोपालनं कर्तव्यं, गोग्रासप्रदानगोसेवनतदनुगमनतदार्ति
text_mt: 42. Protection of cattle must always be performed by the king: offering mouthfuls of grass to cows, tending cows, following them, [relieving] their distress...

sanskrit_iast: 50 gajaśāntikavidhānam
meaning: 50 गजशान्तिकविधानम्
text_mt: 50. Procedure for the pacification ritual for elephants.

sanskrit_iast: 51 rājapuruṣapraśaṃsā
meaning: 51 राजपुरुषप्रशंसा
text_mt: 51. Praise of royal officials.

sanskrit_iast: 52 śoṇitapradararaktagulmauṣadhaśatodarīkaraṇamāṃsalīkaraṇapīnastanīkaraṇādipūrvakaṃ śubhasantatyarthaṃ keśavārādhanecchāvimānagauṣadhaniṣevaṇādikathanam, viṣṇuprādurbhāvādiśravaṇagodevabrāhmaṇapūjanapurassaraṃ yogyaparicārikābhiḥ sūtikāgṛhaṃ praviśya susaṃtānārthinī nārī vātānulomanādi kṛtvā prasūtyanupadaṃ balikarmādyācaret . tataśca jātanāma karmaniṣkramaṇānnaprāśanadurdantajanane śāṃtyādi
meaning: 52 शोणितप्रदररक्तगुल्मौषधशतोदरीकरणमांसलीकरणपीनस्तनीकरणादिपूर्वकं शुभसन्तत्यर्थं केशवाराधनेच्छाविमानगौषधनिषेवणादिकथनम्, विष्णुप्रादुर्भावादिश्रवणगोदेवब्राह्मणपूजनपुरस्सरं योग्यपरिचारिकाभिः सूतिकागृहं प्रविश्य सुसंतानार्थिनी नारी वातानुलोमनादि कृत्वा प्रसूत्यनुपदं बलिकर्माद्याचरेत् . ततश्च जातनाम कर्मनिष्क्रमणान्नप्राशनदुर्दन्तजनने शांत्यादि
text_mt: 52. Account of worship of Keśava, medicines from desire-granting aerial cars, and so forth, preceded by medicines for menorrhagia, blood-tumours, creating a slender abdomen, creating firm flesh, and enlarging breasts, for the sake of auspicious progeny; entering the lying-in chamber with suitable attendants after hearing of the manifestations of Viṣṇu and worshipping cows, deities, and brahmins, a woman desiring good offspring, having brought about the downward movement of the bodily wind and other measures, should perform the offering of oblations immediately upon giving birth; and thereafter, the birth-rite, naming ceremony, first outing, first feeding of solid food, and rites of pacification upon the untimely eruption of teeth.

sanskrit_iast: 53 putrīyarohiṇīsnānavarṇanam
meaning: 53 पुत्रीयरोहिणीस्नानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 53. Description of the Rohiṇī bath for obtaining a son.

sanskrit_iast: 54 putrīyasaptamīvratakathanam
meaning: 54 पुत्रीयसप्तमीव्रतकथनम्
text_mt: 54. Account of the Seventh-day observance for obtaining a son.

sanskrit_iast: 55 putrīyāṣṭamīvratam –
meaning: 55 पुत्रीयाष्टमीव्रतम् –
text_mt: 55. The Eighth-day observance for obtaining a son.

sanskrit_iast: 56 nānauṣadhaiḥ puruṣacikitsākathane viṣṇubhakteḥ sarvāmayaikauṣadhitvakathanam
meaning: 56 नानौषधैः पुरुषचिकित्साकथने विष्णुभक्तेः सर्वामयैकौषधित्वकथनम्
text_mt: 56. Account of devotion to Viṣṇu as the single remedy for all illnesses in the context of treating humans with various medicines.

sanskrit_iast: 57 sarvaroganāśakaśatabhiṣāsnānāvidhiḥ
meaning: 57 सर्वरोगनाशकशतभिषास्नानाविधिः
text_mt: 57. Rule for the Śatabhiṣaj bath that destroys all diseases.

sanskrit_iast: 58 pauṣaśukladvitīyā-( ārogyadvitīyā)-yāṃ bālendorbrāhmaṇānāṃ ca pūjanādārogyapuṣṭyādilābhaḥ
meaning: 58 पौषशुक्लद्वितीया-( आरोग्यद्वितीया)-यां बालेन्दोर्ब्राह्मणानां च पूजनादारोग्यपुष्ट्यादिलाभः
text_mt: 58. Attainment of health, strength, and other benefits by worshipping the crescent moon and brahmins on the bright second lunar day of Pauṣa (the Second of Health).

sanskrit_iast: 59 ārogyapratipadvidhānaṃ phalañca
meaning: 59 आरोग्यप्रतिपद्विधानं फलञ्च
text_mt: 59. Injunction and fruit of the First-day observance of Health.

sanskrit_iast: 60 ārogyavratavidhānam .
meaning: 60 आरोग्यव्रतविधानम् .
text_mt: 60. Injunction for the observance of Health.

sanskrit_iast: 61 grāmadaśagrāmaśatagrāmeśaviṣayeśāvekṣaṇādiprabandhena dhanavṛddhipurassaraṃ prajārakṣaṇam
meaning: 61 ग्रामदशग्रामशतग्रामेशविषयेशावेक्षणादिप्रबन्धेन धनवृद्धिपुरस्सरं प्रजारक्षणम्
text_mt: 61. Protection of the subjects along with the increase of wealth through the system of inspecting the lords of single villages, lords of ten villages, lords of a hundred villages, and lords of districts.

sanskrit_iast: 62 dharmāvirodhikāmasevāvicārapurassaramanta:puracintanam
meaning: 62 धर्माविरोधिकामसेवाविचारपुरस्सरमन्त:पुरचिन्तनम्
text_mt: 62. Reflection upon the inner apartments preceded by consideration of the pursuit of pleasure that does not conflict with dharma.

sanskrit_iast: 63 bhojyabhakṣyalehyacoṣyapeyeti bhojyakalpanākathanam . .
meaning: 63 भोज्यभक्ष्यलेह्यचोष्यपेयेति भोज्यकल्पनाकथनम् . .
text_mt: 63. Account of the preparation of food, namely chewable, crunchable, lickable, suckable, and drinkable items.

sanskrit_iast: 64 śodhanavamanavirecanabhāvanāpākabodhanadhūpanavāsanādigandhayuktikathanam
meaning: 64 शोधनवमनविरेचनभावनापाकबोधनधूपनवासनादिगन्धयुक्तिकथनम्
text_mt: 64. Account of the preparation of perfumes through purification, vomiting, purging, infusion, cooking, awakening, fumigation, perfuming, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 69 rājadharmavarṇanam
meaning: 69 राजधर्मवर्णनम्
text_mt: 69. Description of the duties of kings.

sanskrit_iast: 66 daivapauruṣayo rathacakrayoriva kriyāsiddhau samabalatve'pi puruṣakārasya śreṣṭhatvam ....
meaning: 66 दैवपौरुषयो रथचक्रयोरिव क्रियासिद्धौ समबलत्वेऽपि पुरुषकारस्य श्रेष्ठत्वम् ....
text_mt: 66. Superiority of human effort even though fate and human effort possess equal strength in the accomplishment of an action, like two chariot wheels...

sanskrit_iast: 67 sāmasādhyapuruṣanirdeśaḥ
meaning: 67 सामसाध्यपुरुषनिर्देशः
text_mt: 67. Specification of persons who are to be won over by conciliation.

sanskrit_iast: 68 jayasiddherāsannaṃ bhedavidhānam
meaning: 68 जयसिद्धेरासन्नं भेदविधानम्
text_mt: 68. Injunction on sowing dissension as an immediate [means] to achieve victory.

sanskrit_iast: 69 dānamāhātmyam
meaning: 69 दानमाहात्म्यम्
text_mt: 69. The majesty of gift-giving.

sanskrit_iast: 70 daṇḍapraśaṃsā
meaning: 70 दण्डप्रशंसा
text_mt: 70. Praise of punishment.

sanskrit_iast: 71 daṇḍapraśaṃsanapurassaraṃ rājñaḥ sūryacandravāyuyamapāvakakuberavaruṇātmakatvam
meaning: 71 दण्डप्रशंसनपुरस्सरं राज्ञः सूर्यचन्द्रवायुयमपावककुबेरवरुणात्मकत्वम्
text_mt: 71. The king's embodiment of the Sun, Moon, Wind, Yama, Fire, Kubera, and Varuṇa, preceded by praise of punishment.

sanskrit_iast: 72 vividhāparādhānusāraṃ daṇḍapraṇayanam
meaning: 72 विविधापराधानुसारं दण्डप्रणयनम्
text_mt: 72. Meting out punishment according to various offences.

sanskrit_iast: 73 vividhaniṣiddhakarmasevananikṛntakaprāyaścittāni
meaning: 73 विविधनिषिद्धकर्मसेवननिकृन्तकप्रायश्चित्तानि
text_mt: 73. Expiations that eradicate the performance of various forbidden acts.

sanskrit_iast: ৩4 rahasyaprāyaścittākhyānam
meaning: ৩4 रहस्यप्रायश्चित्ताख्यानम्
text_mt: 74. Account of secret expiations.

sanskrit_iast: 75 maraṇāśaucaśuddhikālakathanam '
meaning: 75 मरणाशौचशुद्धिकालकथनम् '
text_mt: 75. Account of the period for purification from ritual impurity due to death.

sanskrit_iast: 76 pretanirharaṇāsthisañcayanādipretakriyāgaṅgāsthinikṣepanārāyaṇabalyādi pretahitakṛtyam –
meaning: 76 प्रेतनिर्हरणास्थिसञ्चयनादिप्रेतक्रियागङ्गास्थिनिक्षेपनारायणबल्यादि प्रेतहितकृत्यम् –
text_mt: 76. Rites beneficial to the deceased, such as carrying out the deceased, gathering the bones, funeral rites, casting the bones into the Gaṅgā, and the offering to Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: 77 sapiṇḍīkaraṇaśrāddham
meaning: 77 सपिण्डीकरणश्राद्धम्
text_mt: 77. The ancestral rite of sapindisation.

sanskrit_iast: 78 saṃsārāsāratākhyānapurassaraṃ dharmanityatādyāśvāsanam....
meaning: 78 संसारासारताख्यानपुरस्सरं धर्मनित्यताद्याश्वासनम्....
text_mt: 78. Consolation regarding the eternity of dharma and so forth, preceded by an account of the worthlessness of worldly existence...

sanskrit_iast: 79 dravyaśuddhyupākhyānam...
meaning: 79 द्रव्यशुद्ध्युपाख्यानम्...
text_mt: 79. Account of the purification of substances...

sanskrit_iast: 80 varṇānāṃ sāmānyaviśeṣadharmadigdarśanam
meaning: 80 वर्णानां सामान्यविशेषधर्मदिग्दर्शनम्
text_mt: 80. General survey of the general and specific duties of the social classes.

sanskrit_iast: 81 varṇaśaṅkaradharmopadeśaḥ
meaning: 81 वर्णशङ्करधर्मोपदेशः
text_mt: 81. Instruction on the duties of mixed social classes.

sanskrit_iast: 82 āpaddharmanirdeśaḥ
meaning: 82 आपद्धर्मनिर्देशः
text_mt: 82. Direction concerning the duties in times of distress.

sanskrit_iast: 83 vyāpāralābhakārakaṃ pūrvāṣāḍhāsnānavarṇanam
meaning: 83 व्यापारलाभकारकं पूर्वाषाढास्नानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 83. Description of the Pūrvāṣāḍhā bath that brings gain in trade.

sanskrit_iast: 84 mūlasnānavarṇanam
meaning: 84 मूलस्नानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 84. Description of the Mūla bath.

sanskrit_iast: 85 garbhādhānādisaṃskārābhidhānam
meaning: 85 गर्भाधानादिसंस्काराभिधानम्
text_mt: 85. Mention of the sacraments beginning with conception.

sanskrit_iast: 86 brahmacaryavarṇanam
meaning: 86 ब्रह्मचर्यवर्णनम्
text_mt: 86. Description of student celibacy.

sanskrit_iast: 87 varṇānupūrveṇa bhāryākaraṇaṃ, brāhmādivivāhabhedāḥ śacīyāgavivāhārthatithivārādi
meaning: 87 वर्णानुपूर्वेण भार्याकरणं, ब्राह्मादिविवाहभेदाः शचीयागविवाहार्थतिथिवारादि
text_mt: 87. Taking a wife in the order of the social classes; the varieties of marriage beginning with the Brāhma rite; the sacrifice to Śacī, and the lunar days, weekdays, and so on for marriage.

sanskrit_iast: 88 brāhmāditīrthasnānavarṇanam
meaning: 88 ब्राह्मादितीर्थस्नानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 88. Description of bathing at holy water-sites beginning with the Brāhma.

sanskrit_iast: 89 mālyavastracandanopānadbrahmasūtradhāraṇaṃ, hīnādhikāṅgādibhiḥ sahāgamanaṃ, mārge dakṣiṇataḥ kartavyapadārthāḥ deyamārgāśca, paśuripugṛhayoranadvārapraveśādikartavyakarmasaṃgrahaḥ
meaning: 89 माल्यवस्त्रचन्दनोपानद्ब्रह्मसूत्रधारणं, हीनाधिकाङ्गादिभिः सहागमनं, मार्गे दक्षिणतः कर्तव्यपदार्थाः देयमार्गाश्च, पशुरिपुगृहयोरनद्वारप्रवेशादिकर्तव्यकर्मसंग्रहः
text_mt: 89. Wearing garlands, garments, sandalwood, shoes, and the sacred thread; travelling with those who have missing or surplus limbs and the like; objects to be kept on the right while on the road, and those to whom right of way must be given; a compendium of duties such as not entering through non-doors into the houses of animals or enemies.

sanskrit_iast: 90 devārcāmantrapratīkakathanam
meaning: 90 देवार्चामन्त्रप्रतीककथनम्
text_mt: 90. Account of the initial words of mantras for the worship of deities.

sanskrit_iast: 91 udakānulepanavastrābharaṇapuṣpabilvapatradūrvādidevanivedanīyavastuyogyatākathanam
meaning: 91 उदकानुलेपनवस्त्राभरणपुष्पबिल्वपत्रदूर्वादिदेवनिवेदनीयवस्तुयोग्यताकथनम्
text_mt: 91. Account of the suitability of articles to be offered to deities, such as water, unguents, garments, ornaments, flowers, bilva leaves, and dūrvā grass.

sanskrit_iast: 92 vaiśvadevātithipūjanavarṇanam
meaning: 92 वैश्वदेवातिथिपूजनवर्णनम्
text_mt: 92. Description of the universal offering to all deities and the honouring of guests.

sanskrit_iast: 93 candrasūryoparāge bhojanavarjanaṃ bālakānāṃ pūrvaṃ dattvaiva gṛhasthasya bhojanamityādibhojananiyamakathanam
meaning: 93 चन्द्रसूर्योपरागे भोजनवर्जनं बालकानां पूर्वं दत्त्वैव गृहस्थस्य भोजनमित्यादिभोजननियमकथनम्
text_mt: 93. Account of the rules of dining, such as abstention from eating during an eclipse of the moon or sun, and the householder eating only after first feeding children.

sanskrit_iast: 94. śayanānarhadeśakathanapurassaraṃ rajasvalādibhiḥ saṅganiṣedhavarṇanam
meaning: 94. शयनानर्हदेशकथनपुरस्सरं रजस्वलादिभिः सङ्गनिषेधवर्णनम्
text_mt: 94. Description of the prohibition of intercourse with menstruating women and others, preceded by an account of places unsuitable for sleeping.

sanskrit_iast: 95 gṛhasthadharmavarṇanam.
meaning: 95 गृहस्थधर्मवर्णनम्.
text_mt: 95. Description of the duties of a householder.

sanskrit_iast: 96 sarvaśatrunāśakakṛttikāsnānavarṇanam
meaning: 96 सर्वशत्रुनाशककृत्तिकास्नानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 96. Description of the Kṛttikā bath that destroys all enemies.

sanskrit_iast: 97 bharaṇīkṛttikayorupavāsapūrvakavāsudevapūjanena śatrunāśaḥ
meaning: 97 भरणीकृत्तिकयोरुपवासपूर्वकवासुदेवपूजनेन शत्रुनाशः
text_mt: 97. Destruction of enemies through the worship of Vāsudeva preceded by fasting on Bharaṇī and Kṛttikā.

sanskrit_iast: 98 kāmyasnāneṣu sādhāraṇasnānavarṇanam
meaning: 98 काम्यस्नानेषु साधारणस्नानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 98. Description of common baths among baths performed for specific desires.

sanskrit_iast: 99 rohiṇyādinakṣatrasnānakathanam
meaning: 99 रोहिण्यादिनक्षत्रस्नानकथनम्
text_mt: 99. Account of lunar-mansion baths beginning with Rohiṇī.

sanskrit_iast: 100 sarvādhivināśanamabhijitsnānam
meaning: 100 सर्वाधिविनाशनमभिजित्स्नानम्
text_mt: 100. The Abhijit bath that destroys all mental anguish.

sanskrit_iast: 101 puṣṭipradamabhijitsnānam
meaning: 101 पुष्टिप्रदमभिजित्स्नानम्
text_mt: 101. The Abhijit bath that grants nourishment.

sanskrit_iast: 102 janmarkṣasnānavarṇanam
meaning: 102 जन्मर्क्षस्नानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 102. Description of the birth-constellation bath.

sanskrit_iast: 103 puṣyasnānavarṇanam
meaning: 103 पुष्यस्नानवर्णनम्
text_mt: 103. Description of the Puṣya bath.

sanskrit_iast: 104 dikpālasnānavarṇanam |
meaning: 104 दिक्पालस्नानवर्णनम् |
text_mt: 104. Description of the bath of the guardians of the directions.

sanskrit_iast: 105 vināyakasnānavarṇanam .
meaning: 105 विनायकस्नानवर्णनम् .
text_mt: 105. Description of the Vināyaka bath.

sanskrit_iast: 106 rakṣoghnaṃ sarvaśatrukṣayakāri māheśvarasnānam
meaning: 106 रक्षोघ्नं सर्वशत्रुक्षयकारि माहेश्वरस्नानम्
text_mt: 106. The bath sacred to Maheśvara, which destroys demons and causes the ruin of all enemies.

sanskrit_iast: 107 ghṛtagośakṛddadhidarbhodakapalāśabilvakamalavacāmañjiṣṭhādisnānam
meaning: 107 घृतगोशकृद्दधिदर्भोदकपलाशबिल्वकमलवचामञ्जिष्ठादिस्नानम्
text_mt: 107. The bath with ghee, cow dung, curd, darbha-grass water, palāśa, bilva, lotus, vacā, mañjiṣṭhā, and other [herbs].

sanskrit_iast: 108 puruṣottamapādodakasnānam
meaning: 108 पुरुषोत्तमपादोदकस्नानम्
text_mt: 108. The bath with water from the feet of Puruṣottama.

sanskrit_iast: 109 maṇibandhavarṇanam
meaning: 109 मणिबन्धवर्णनम्
text_mt: 109. Description of the protective amulet (maṇibandha).

sanskrit_iast: 110 nānārogamocakavividhavāñchitārthapradabhagavadanulepanavarṇanam
meaning: 110 नानारोगमोचकविविधवाञ्छितार्थप्रदभगवदनुलेपनवर्णनम्
text_mt: 110. Description of the anointing of the Lord, which delivers from diverse diseases and grants various desired objects.

sanskrit_iast: 111 prāyaścittānusāreṇa narakagamanādidaṇḍavidhānam
meaning: 111 प्रायश्चित्तानुसारेण नरकगमनादिदण्डविधानम्
text_mt: 111. Prescribing punishments such as going to hell in accordance with [the lack of] penance.

sanskrit_iast: 112 jīvasya garbhasaṃkrāntivarṇanam
meaning: 112 जीवस्य गर्भसंक्रान्तिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 112. Description of the soul’s transmigration into the womb.

sanskrit_iast: 113 pretaloke jīvasya karmānusāramādaratāḍanādyanantaraṃ bhogadehe phalabhogaḥ .
meaning: 113 प्रेतलोके जीवस्य कर्मानुसारमादरताडनाद्यनन्तरं भोगदेहे फलभोगः .
text_mt: 113. In the realm of the deceased, the soul experiences its fruits in an experiential body, following honour, beating, and the like according to its deeds.

sanskrit_iast: 114 garbhe kalalaghanībhūtāṃganirmāṇatvakcarmādyutpattipurassaraṃ garbhavyathādikathanam
meaning: 114 गर्भे कललघनीभूतांगनिर्माणत्वक्चर्माद्युत्पत्तिपुरस्सरं गर्भव्यथादिकथनम्
text_mt: 114. Account of the pains of the womb and so forth, preceded by the formation of solid limbs from the embryo, and the emergence of outer and inner skin in the womb.

sanskrit_iast: 115 śarīraviṣayavarṇanam
meaning: 115 शरीरविषयवर्णनम्
text_mt: 115. Description concerning the physical body.

sanskrit_iast: 116 vividhadānakartṝṇāṃ dharmamācaratāṃ ca jīvotkramaṇānantaraṃ sasukhaṃ yamapure gamanaṃ tadviruddhānāṃ tatra vividhayātanāsahanam
meaning: 116 विविधदानकर्तॄणां धर्ममाचरतां च जीवोत्क्रमणानन्तरं ससुखं यमपुरे गमनं तद्विरुद्धानां तत्र विविधयातनासहनम्
text_mt: 116. The comfortable journey to the city of Yama after the departure of the soul for performers of diverse gifts and practitioners of dharma; and the enduring of various torments there for those who act contrary to it.

sanskrit_iast: 117 svavarṇāśramadharmamanurundhatāṃ svargavāsaḥ
meaning: 117 स्ववर्णाश्रमधर्ममनुरुन्धतां स्वर्गवासः
text_mt: 117. Residence in heaven for those who adhere to the dharma of their own caste and stage of life.

sanskrit_iast: 118 śāstroktaviruddhavarṇāśramadharmakāriṇāṃ nirayagamanam
meaning: 118 शास्त्रोक्तविरुद्धवर्णाश्रमधर्मकारिणां निरयगमनम्
text_mt: 118. Going to hell for those who perform acts contrary to the dharma of caste and stage of life taught in scripture.

sanskrit_iast: 119 vividhanarakanāmapradarśanapūrvakaṃ pāpināṃ teṣuteṣu narakeṣu yātanāvarṇanam
meaning: 119 विविधनरकनामप्रदर्शनपूर्वकं पापिनां तेषुतेषु नरकेषु यातनावर्णनम्
text_mt: 119. Description of the torments of sinners in various hells, preceded by displaying their various names.

sanskrit_iast: 120 pāpakarmānusāraṃ nārakayātanā anubhūya nārakāṇāṃ saṃsāre brahmarākṣasatiryagādiyoniṣu janma
meaning: 120 पापकर्मानुसारं नारकयातना अनुभूय नारकाणां संसारे ब्रह्मराक्षसतिर्यगादियोनिषु जन्म
text_mt: 120. Having experienced the torments of hell according to their sinful deeds, the denizens of hell are reborn in worldly existence in the wombs of brahmarākṣasas, animals, and the like.

sanskrit_iast: 121 narakavedanābhogānantaraṃ maṇimuktādihartuḥ svarṇakārajātau, svarṇacorasya kunakhitvaṃ, surāpasya kṛṣṇadantatā, gurupratikūlasyāpasmāritvādipūrvajanma karmaprakāśakacihnayuktavapustvam
meaning: 121 नरकवेदनाभोगानन्तरं मणिमुक्तादिहर्तुः स्वर्णकारजातौ, स्वर्णचोरस्य कुनखित्वं, सुरापस्य कृष्णदन्तता, गुरुप्रतिकूलस्यापस्मारित्वादिपूर्वजन्म कर्मप्रकाशकचिह्नयुक्तवपुस्त्वम्
text_mt: 121. After experiencing the agonies of hell, the stealer of gems, pearls, and the like is born in the goldsmith caste; a thief of gold has deformed nails; a drinker of liquor has black teeth; one hostile to his guru suffers from epilepsy, possessing a body marked with signs disclosing the deeds of previous births.

sanskrit_iast: 122 varṇāśramadharmakāriṇāṃ bhītyabhāvaḥ ( durgātitaraṇam)
meaning: 122 वर्णाश्रमधर्मकारिणां भीत्यभावः ( दुर्गातितरणम्)
text_mt: 122. Absence of fear (crossing over difficulties) for performers of the dharma of caste and stage of life.

sanskrit_iast: 123 sarvapāpavināśaka cāndrāyaṇakṛcchrādivarṇanam
meaning: 123 सर्वपापविनाशक चान्द्रायणकृच्छ्रादिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 123. Description of the cāndrāyaṇa, kṛcchra, and other [penances] that destroy all sins.

sanskrit_iast: 124 vividhapāpanāśakanānādravyadāyakavaidikasūktajapādi
meaning: 124 विविधपापनाशकनानाद्रव्यदायकवैदिकसूक्तजपादि
text_mt: 124. Recitation of Vedic hymns and other rites that destroy diverse sins and bestow various goods.

sanskrit_iast: 125 vaidikavividhamantraistattatkāryasādhakatantravidhānam
meaning: 125 वैदिकविविधमन्त्रैस्तत्तत्कार्यसाधकतन्त्रविधानम्
text_mt: 125. The ritual procedure for accomplishing various objectives through diverse Vedic mantras.

sanskrit_iast: 126 anekakāmanāsiddhikarasāmaprayogakathanam
meaning: 126 अनेककामनासिद्धिकरसामप्रयोगकथनम्
text_mt: 126. Account of the application of Sāma [chants] which accomplishes numerous desires.

sanskrit_iast: 127 atharvavidhinānekaprayogasādhakavidhikathanam
meaning: 127 अथर्वविधिनानेकप्रयोगसाधकविधिकथनम्
text_mt: 127. Account of the procedure that accomplishes many rites according to the Atharvan rule.

sanskrit_iast: 128 śrīsūktamāhātmyakathanam
meaning: 128 श्रीसूक्तमाहात्म्यकथनम्
text_mt: 128. Account of the greatness of the Śrīsūkta.

sanskrit_iast: 129 puruṣasūktamāhātmyavarṇanam
meaning: 129 पुरुषसूक्तमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
text_mt: 129. Description of the greatness of the Puruṣasūkta.

sanskrit_iast: 130 vānaprasthāśramadharmakathanam
meaning: 130 वानप्रस्थाश्रमधर्मकथनम्
text_mt: 130. Account of the dharma of the forest-dweller stage of life.

sanskrit_iast: 131 yatidharmanirūpaṇam
meaning: 131 यतिधर्मनिरूपणम्
text_mt: 131. Exposition of the dharma of the ascetic.

sanskrit_iast: 132 sarvaśāntiṣvātharvaṇaśāntividhiḥ
meaning: 132 सर्वशान्तिष्वाथर्वणशान्तिविधिः
text_mt: 132. The procedure for pacifying rites according to the Atharvaveda among all pacifications.

sanskrit_iast: 133 bhaumāntarikṣādiśāntiṣu, amṛtābhayādiśāntikathanam.
meaning: 133 भौमान्तरिक्षादिशान्तिषु, अमृताभयादिशान्तिकथनम्.
text_mt: 133. Account of the Amṛtā, Abhayā, and other pacifying rites among earthly, atmospheric, and other pacifications.

sanskrit_iast: 134 vividhotpātakathanam
meaning: 134 विविधोत्पातकथनम्
text_mt: 134. Account of various portents.

sanskrit_iast: 135 arthāvikāropaśamanavarṇanam
meaning: 135 अर्थाविकारोपशमनवर्णनम्
text_mt: 135. Description of the appeasement of disturbances concerning wealth.

sanskrit_iast: 136 autpātāgniśāntivarṇanam
meaning: 136 औत्पाताग्निशान्तिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 136. Description of the pacification of portents relating to fire.

sanskrit_iast: 137 autpātike vṛkṣavaikṛtyavarṇanam
meaning: 137 औत्पातिके वृक्षवैकृत्यवर्णनम्
text_mt: 137. Description of portents involving unnatural changes in trees.

sanskrit_iast: 138 autpātike vṛṣṭivaikṛtyavarṇanam
meaning: 138 औत्पातिके वृष्टिवैकृत्यवर्णनम्
text_mt: 138. Description of portents involving unnatural changes in rain.

sanskrit_iast: 139 autpātike jalavaikṛtyavarṇanam
meaning: 139 औत्पातिके जलवैकृत्यवर्णनम्
text_mt: 139. Description of portents involving unnatural changes in water.

sanskrit_iast: 140 strīprasavavarṇanam
meaning: 140 स्त्रीप्रसववर्णनम्
text_mt: 140. Description of childbirth in women.

sanskrit_iast: 141 vaḍavāhastinyādiyugmaprasavavaikṛtādiśāntiḥ
meaning: 141 वडवाहस्तिन्यादियुग्मप्रसववैकृतादिशान्तिः
text_mt: 141. Pacification of portents such as twin births in mares, female elephants, and the like.

sanskrit_iast: 142 upaskaravaikṛtavarṇanam
meaning: 142 उपस्करवैकृतवर्णनम्
text_mt: 142. Description of unnatural changes in household implements.

sanskrit_iast: 143 āraṇyagrāmyapaśvādīnāṃ grāmāraṇyagamanādivaikṛtaśāntiḥ
meaning: 143 आरण्यग्राम्यपश्वादीनां ग्रामारण्यगमनादिवैकृतशान्तिः
text_mt: 143. Pacification of unnatural behaviour such as wild and domestic animals entering villages or forests.

sanskrit_iast: 144 prasādatoraṇādīnāmanimittapatane grahādīnāṃ vicchāyatve gurumitradrohādīnāmudaye ca śāntiḥ
meaning: 144 प्रसादतोरणादीनामनिमित्तपतने ग्रहादीनां विच्छायत्वे गुरुमित्रद्रोहादीनामुदये च शान्तिः
text_mt: 144. Pacification when palaces, archways, and the like fall without cause, when planets and stars lose their lustre, and when treachery against gurus and friends arises.

sanskrit_iast: 145 rājyamaṇḍalavarṇane kulyādibhedena śatruvarṇanam
meaning: 145 राज्यमण्डलवर्णने कुल्यादिभेदेन शत्रुवर्णनम्
text_mt: 145. Description of enemies according to their division into kin and the like in the description of the circle of states.

sanskrit_iast: 146 śatruṣu daṇḍapraṇayanam .
meaning: 146 शत्रुषु दण्डप्रणयनम् .
text_mt: 146. The infliction of punishment on enemies.

sanskrit_iast: 147 yuddhakaraṇe hāniṃ vicāryopekṣākaraṇam
meaning: 147 युद्धकरणे हानिं विचार्योपेक्षाकरणम्
text_mt: 147. Resorting to indifference after considering the loss involved in waging war.

sanskrit_iast: 148 śatruvyākulīkaraṇāya tadrājye guptotpādādiprakaṭanam
meaning: 148 शत्रुव्याकुलीकरणाय तद्राज्ये गुप्तोत्पादादिप्रकटनम्
text_mt: 148. Manifesting secret portents and the like in the enemy’s kingdom to throw him into confusion.

sanskrit_iast: 149 indrajālena śatrurājye caturaṅgabalaraktavṛṣṭicchinnaśirāṃsi darśanīyāni
meaning: 149 इन्द्रजालेन शत्रुराज्ये चतुरङ्गबलरक्तवृष्टिच्छिन्नशिरांसि दर्शनीयानि
text_mt: 149. Showing through illusionism a fourfold army, showers of blood, and severed heads in the enemy’s kingdom.

sanskrit_iast: 150 ṣāḍguṇyavarṇanam
meaning: 150 षाड्गुण्यवर्णनम्
text_mt: 150. Description of the six measures of foreign policy.

sanskrit_iast: 151 rājāhnikavarṇanam
meaning: 151 राजाह्निकवर्णनम्
text_mt: 151. Description of the daily duties of a king.

sanskrit_iast: 152 janmanakṣatrakṣālanapuṣpasnānasūryasaṃkramaṇanimittakasūryapūjanabālendupūjanādīni rājakarmāṇi
meaning: 152 जन्मनक्षत्रक्षालनपुष्पस्नानसूर्यसंक्रमणनिमित्तकसूर्यपूजनबालेन्दुपूजनादीनि राजकर्माणि
text_mt: 152. Royal ceremonies such as the washing away [of evil on] the natal asterism, the flower bath, sun worship on the occasion of the sun’s transit, and worship of the crescent moon.

sanskrit_iast: 153 rājñaścāturmāsyavidhivarṇanam
meaning: 153 राज्ञश्चातुर्मास्यविधिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 153. Description of the king’s cāturmāsya observance.

sanskrit_iast: 154 śakradhvajotpattikathanapurassaraṃ tanmahotsavakartuḥ saṃgrāme jayaḥ
meaning: 154 शक्रध्वजोत्पत्तिकथनपुरस्सरं तन्महोत्सवकर्तुः संग्रामे जयः
text_mt: 154. Victory in battle for the performer of the great festival of Śakra's banner, preceded by the account of its origin.

sanskrit_iast: 155 śakradhvajamahotsavakālavidhiphalādikathanam
meaning: 155 शक्रध्वजमहोत्सवकालविधिफलादिकथनम्
text_mt: 155. Account of the time, procedure, fruits, and other aspects of the great festival of Śakra's banner.

sanskrit_iast: 156 indradhvajapatanabhaṅgādiśāntivarṇanam
meaning: 156 इन्द्रध्वजपतनभङ्गादिशान्तिवर्णनम्
text_mt: 156. Description of the pacification for the falling, breaking, and other mishaps of Indra’s banner.

sanskrit_iast: 157 śakradhvajāropaṇaprasaṅgena stāvakamantrāḥ
meaning: 157 शक्रध्वजारोपणप्रसङ्गेन स्तावकमन्त्राः
text_mt: 157. Hymnic mantras on the occasion of raising Śakra's banner.

sanskrit_iast: 158 āśvinaśuklanavamyāṃ śivirottare bhadrakālīgṛhaṃ nirmāya paṭe bhadrakālīṃ sampūjyāṣṭamyāṃ chatravarmādyāyudhāni pūjayet
meaning: 158 आश्विनशुक्लनवम्यां शिविरोत्तरे भद्रकालीगृहं निर्माय पटे भद्रकालीं सम्पूज्याष्टम्यां छत्रवर्माद्यायुधानि पूजयेत्
text_mt: 158. On the ninth day of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, one should erect a shrine for Bhadrakālī to the north of the camp, worship Bhadrakālī on a painted cloth, and on the eighth day worship the parasol, armour, and other weapons.

sanskrit_iast: 159 hastyaśvādinīrājanaśāntividhiḥ
meaning: 159 हस्त्यश्वादिनीराजनशान्तिविधिः
text_mt: 159. The pacification rite of lustration for elephants, horses, and the like.

sanskrit_iast: 160 chatrāśvadhvajagajapatākākhaḍgavarmadundubhyādimantrāḥ
meaning: 160 छत्राश्वध्वजगजपताकाखड्गवर्मदुन्दुभ्यादिमन्त्राः
text_mt: 160. Mantras for the parasol, horse, banner, elephant, flag, sword, armour, war drum, and other regalia.

sanskrit_iast: 161 rājyavivṛddhikaraṇaṃ ghṛtakambalaśāntikarma
meaning: 161 राज्यविवृद्धिकरणं घृतकम्बलशान्तिकर्म
text_mt: 161. The pacification rite of the ghee blanket, which brings about the expansion of the kingdom.

sanskrit_iast: 162 saṃvatsarābhiṣekaḥ
meaning: 162 संवत्सराभिषेकः
text_mt: 162. The annual royal consecration.

sanskrit_iast: 163 yātrāyāṃ śakunavidhānam
meaning: 163 यात्रायां शकुनविधानम्
text_mt: 163. The rule of omens on a journey.

sanskrit_iast: 164 yātrāyāṃ śakunavidhānam
meaning: 164 यात्रायां शकुनविधानम्
text_mt: 164. The rule of omens on a journey.

sanskrit_iast: 165 śubhāśubhapraśnaphalam
meaning: 165 शुभाशुभप्रश्नफलम्
text_mt: 165. The outcome of inquiries regarding auspicious and inauspicious signs.

sanskrit_iast: 166 jyotiḥśāstravarṇane śāstraśākhāvarṇanam
meaning: 166 ज्योतिःशास्त्रवर्णने शास्त्रशाखावर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 166. Description of the branches of the science in the exposition of astronomy.

sanskrit_iast: 167 kālamānarāśigrahaṃ svarūpasaptavargagrahamaitryādipratimāsagarbhagatajīvāvayavakathanam, māsādhipabalādivaśādgarbhapuṣṭẏādergrahāyuvicāramaraṇakāra ṇāṣṭavargarājayogādeśca kathanam
meaning: 167 कालमानराशिग्रहं स्वरूपसप्तवर्गग्रहमैत्र्यादिप्रतिमासगर्भगतजीवावयवकथनम्, मासाधिपबलादिवशाद्गर्भपुष्ट्ẏआदेर्ग्रहायुविचारमरणकार णाष्टवर्गराजयोगादेश्च कथनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 167. Exposition of the measures of time, zodiacal signs, planetary natures, the seven divisions, planetary friendships, and the limbs of the embryo month by month; and exposition of the nourishment of the embryo and so forth through the strength of the lord of the month, the determination of planetary life-spans, the causes of death, the aṣṭavarga, royal yogas, and so on.

sanskrit_iast: 168 saurādidivasasatyayugādimānakalpagrahabhagaṇagrahakakṣāmānajyādisādhanakrāntiśarasādhanalagnamānānayananakṣatradhruvakabhaumādivakrādikendrādivarṇanam
meaning: 168 सौरादिदिवससत्ययुगादिमानकल्पग्रहभगणग्रहकक्षामानज्यादिसाधनक्रान्तिशरसाधनलग्नमानानयननक्षत्रध्रुवकभौमादिवक्रादिकेन्द्रादिवर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 168. Description of solar and other days, the measures of the Kṛta and other ages, the aeon, planetary revolutions, planetary orbits, the calculation of sines and so on, the calculation of declination and celestial latitude, the derivation of the measure of the ascendant, the polar longitudes of the lunar mansions, the retrogradation and other motions of Mars and other [planets], the cardinal points, and so on.

sanskrit_iast: 169 iṣṭakālābdasauradinacandrāhassādhanāhargaṇagataiṣyādhimāsadinādheṣyo narātrakālapātakālasaṃvatsarābdānayanatadadhipadivasādhipārkodayagrahaṃbhuktyādivarṇanam
meaning: 169 इष्टकालाब्दसौरदिनचन्द्राहस्साधनाहर्गणगतैष्याधिमासदिनाधेष्यो नरात्रकालपातकालसंवत्सराब्दानयनतदधिपदिवसाधिपार्कोदयग्रहंभुक्त्यादिवर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 169. Description of the calculation of the desired time, years, solar days, and lunar days; the collection of days; elapsed and future intercalary months; omitted lunar days; the time of the [astronomical] nodes; the calculation of cyclic and solar years, their lords, the lords of the days, sunrise, planetary motions, and so on.

sanskrit_iast: 170 nakṣatratithikaraṇādyānayanaprakāraḥ
meaning: 170 नक्षत्रतिथिकरणाद्यानयनप्रकारः
text_mt: [Chapter] 170. Method of calculating lunar mansions, lunar days, karaṇas, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 171 chedaśaṅkucchāyādivaśāddivasasya gataśeṣajñānam
meaning: 171 छेदशङ्कुच्छायादिवशाद्दिवसस्य गतशेषज्ञानम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 171. Knowledge of the elapsed and remaining parts of the day by means of the divisor, the gnomon's shadow, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 172 lagnodayakālajñānavarṇanam
meaning: 172 लग्नोदयकालज्ञानवर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 172. Description of the knowledge of the rising time of the ascendant.

sanskrit_iast: 173 grahodayāstalagnāgastyodayapratidaivasikodayādijñānam
meaning: 173 ग्रहोदयास्तलग्नागस्त्योदयप्रतिदैवसिकोदयादिज्ञानम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 173. Knowledge of the rising and setting of planets, the rising of the ascendant, the rising of Agastya, daily risings, and so on.

sanskrit_iast: 174 grahaṇakālikārkacandrayoḥśaṅkuśaṅkutalabhujalambanāvanatiṃ sphuṭaśarasammīlonmīlanādisādhanaṃ grahagatijñānāmutkṛṣṭatvavarṇanañca
meaning: 174 ग्रहणकालिकार्कचन्द्रयोःशङ्कुशङ्कुतलभुजलम्बनावनतिं स्फुटशरसम्मीलोन्मीलनादिसाधनं ग्रहगतिज्ञानामुत्कृष्टत्ववर्णनञ्च
text_mt: [Chapter] 174. Calculation of the gnomon, the base of the gnomon, the base-sine, parallax in longitude, parallax in latitude, the true celestial latitude, immersion, emersion, and so forth of the sun and moon at the time of an eclipse, and description of the excellence of knowing planetary motion.

sanskrit_iast: 175 paurayāyigrahau, yāyigrahabale rājayātrāyāḥ śreṣṭhatā, śukrāstādau tanniṣedhaḥ, yātropayogimāsadivasanakṣatradigdvāranakṣatralagnatithisiddhiyogakathanapurassaraṃ janmarāśyupacayarkṣādau yātrāyāḥ siddhipradatvam
meaning: 175 पौरयायिग्रहौ, यायिग्रहबले राजयात्रायाः श्रेष्ठता, शुक्रास्तादौ तन्निषेधः, यात्रोपयोगिमासदिवसनक्षत्रदिग्द्वारनक्षत्रलग्नतिथिसिद्धियोगकथनपुरस्सरं जन्मराश्युपचयर्क्षादौ यात्रायाः सिद्धिप्रदत्वम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 175. Fixed and mobile planets; the excellence of a king's march when the mobile planets are strong; its prohibition at the setting of Venus and so forth; followed by an exposition of the months, days, lunar mansions, directional gate-mansions, ascendants, lunar days, and yogas of success suitable for a march; and the granting of success in a march in the upacaya mansions of one's birth-sign and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 176 rājñāṃ vijayayātrāyai śubhanakṣatraṃ vicārya taddinātsaptarātrapūrvavidheyavidhivarṇanapurassaraṃ yātrādivase trivikramaṃ sampūjya homānantaraṃ yātrika sūktādipaṭhanapūrvakaṃ diṅnakṣatrayornaivedyaṃ dattvā kiñcitprāśya yāyāt
meaning: 176 राज्ञां विजययात्रायै शुभनक्षत्रं विचार्य तद्दिनात्सप्तरात्रपूर्वविधेयविधिवर्णनपुरस्सरं यात्रादिवसे त्रिविक्रमं सम्पूज्य होमानन्तरं यात्रिक सूक्तादिपठनपूर्वकं दिङ्नक्षत्रयोर्नैवेद्यं दत्त्वा किञ्चित्प्राश्य यायात्
text_mt: [Chapter] 176. Having determined an auspicious lunar mansion for the victorious march of kings, preceded by a description of the rites to be performed for seven nights prior to that day, one should worship Trivikrama on the day of the march, and after the fire sacrifice, preceded by the recitation of the hymn for marching and so on, having offered food to the direction and the lunar mansion and eaten a little, one should set out.

sanskrit_iast: 177 vastraśastrādidhāraṇapattyaśvarathagajādivinyāsapurassaraṃ yuddhavarṇanam
meaning: 177 वस्त्रशस्त्रादिधारणपत्त्यश्वरथगजादिविन्यासपुरस्सरं युद्धवर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 177. Description of battle, preceded by the donning of armour, weapons, and so on, and the deployment of infantry, cavalry, chariots, elephants, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 178 rathanāgāśvapattīnāṃ pādānāśritya dhanurvedasya catuṣpādatā, yantramuktaprāṇimuktamuktasandhāritāmuktetiśastrāstrasampattyā yuddham
meaning: 178 रथनागाश्वपत्तीनां पादानाश्रित्य धनुर्वेदस्य चतुष्पादता, यन्त्रमुक्तप्राणिमुक्तमुक्तसन्धारितामुक्तेतिशस्त्रास्त्रसम्पत्त्या युद्धम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 178. The four divisions of archery based on the feet of chariots, elephants, horses, and infantry; battle conducted through the possession of arms and missiles that are machine-released, hand-released, released-and-held, and unreleased.

sanskrit_iast: 179 samapadavaiśākhamaṇḍalālīḍhapratyākhyātasampuṭādidhanurvedavarṇanam
meaning: 179 समपदवैशाखमण्डलालीढप्रत्याख्यातसम्पुटादिधनुर्वेदवर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 179. Description of archery postures: samapada, vaiśākha, maṇḍala, ālīḍha, pratyālīḍha, sampuṭa, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast: 180 bāṇavyāpāre kṛtahastādiśikṣaṇādyabhyāsavarṇanam
meaning: 180 बाणव्यापारे कृतहस्तादिशिक्षणाद्यभ्यासवर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 180. Description of training and practice in manual dexterity and so on in the operation of arrows.

sanskrit_iast: 181 dhanurvede tryaiṣukavidhivarṇanam
meaning: 181 धनुर्वेदे त्र्यैषुकविधिवर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 181. Description of the threefold arrow method in archery.

sanskrit_iast: 182 khaḍgaprāsadhāraṇaśūlatomaragadāparaśumudgaralaguḍavajrapaṭṭiśakṛpāṇīkṣepaṇīgadāniyuddhakarmāṇi
meaning: 182 खड्गप्रासधारणशूलतोमरगदापरशुमुद्गरलगुडवज्रपट्टिशकृपाणीक्षेपणीगदानियुद्धकर्माणि
text_mt: [Chapter] 182. Combat actions with the sword, javelin, trident, iron club, mace, battle-axe, mallet, club, thunderbolt, broad-bladed spear, knife, sling, and mace.

sanskrit_iast: 183 skhalīnaparyāṇāstaraṇādiyuktāśvānāñca raśmipragrahakovidakṛpāntavaraṇādiyuktasārathe rathahastyādīnāṃ varṇanam
meaning: 183 स्खलीनपर्याणास्तरणादियुक्ताश्वानाञ्च रश्मिप्रग्रहकोविदकृपान्तवरणादियुक्तसारथे रथहस्त्यादीनां वर्णनम्
text_mt: [Chapter] 183. Description of horses equipped with bits, saddles, blankets, and so on, of charioteers skilled in controlling the reins and equipped with armour, and of chariots, elephants, and the like.

sanskrit_iast: iti viṣṇudharmottaradvitīyakhaṇḍaḥ .
meaning: इति विष्णुधर्मोत्तरद्वितीयखण्डः .
text_mt: Thus ends the Second Book of the Viṣṇudharmottara.

sanskrit_iast:
oṃ śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ..
.. oṃnamo nārāyaṇāya ..
.. atha śrīviṣṇumahāpurāṇe viṣṇudharmottaratṛtīyakhaṇḍaprārambhaḥ ..
meaning:
ओं श्रीगणेशाय नमः ..
.. ओंनमो नारायणाय ..
.. अथ श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे विष्णुधर्मोत्तरतृतीयखण्डप्रारम्भः ..
text_mt:
Oṃ, homage to the blessed Gaṇeśa.
Oṃ, homage to Nārāyaṇa.
Now begins the Third Book of the Viṣṇudharmottara in the illustrious Viṣṇu Mahāpurāṇa.
title: Śabdādhyāyaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
.. vajra uvāca ..
kiṃ kartavyaṃ manuṣyeṇa kiṃ kurvansukhamedhate ..
asmim̐lloke pare caiva kenāpnoti mahatsukham .. 1 ..
meaning:
.. वज्र उवाच ..
किं कर्तव्यं मनुष्येण किं कुर्वन्सुखमेधते ..
अस्मिम्̐ल्लोके परे चैव केनाप्नोति महत्सुखम् .. 1 ..
text_mt:
Vajra said:
What should be done by a human being? Doing what does one prosper in happiness? / How does one attain great happiness in this world and in the next? (1)

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
antarvedi bahirvedi puruṣeṇa vijānatā ..
devatāpūjanaṃ kāryaṃ lokadvayamabhīpsatā .. 2 ..
meaning:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच .. ..
अन्तर्वेदि बहिर्वेदि पुरुषेण विजानता ..
देवतापूजनं कार्यं लोकद्वयमभीप्सता .. 2 ..
text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Desiring both worlds, a discerning man should worship the gods / both inside the sacrificial enclosure and outside the sacrificial enclosure. (2)

sanskrit_iast:
yajñeṣu devayajanamantarvedi prakīrtitam ..
bahirvedi tathaivoktamupavāsavratādikam ..
iṣṭāpūrtena labhyante ye lokāstānbubhūṣatā .. 3 ..
meaning:
यज्ञेषु देवयजनमन्तर्वेदि प्रकीर्तितम् ..
बहिर्वेदि तथैवोक्तमुपवासव्रतादिकम् ..
इष्टापूर्तेन लभ्यन्ते ये लोकास्तान्बुभूषता .. 3 ..
text_mt: Sacrificing to the gods in Vedic rites is declared to be inside the enclosure; / fasts, vows, and the like are likewise stated to be outside the enclosure. / One wishing to attain those worlds which are gained through sacrificial and charitable works (3)

sanskrit_iast:
devānāmālayaḥ kāryo dvayamapyatra dṛśyate ..
viśeṣeṇa kalau kāle kartavyaṃ devatāgṛham .. 4 ..
meaning:
देवानामालयः कार्यो द्वयमप्यत्र दृश्यते ..
विशेषेण कलौ काले कर्तव्यं देवतागृहम् .. 4 ..
text_mt: should make an abode for the gods; both [forms of merit] are seen in this. / Especially in the Kali age, a temple for the gods should be made. (4)

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtatretādvāpareṣu narāḥ paśyanti devatām ..
tiṣyaṃ prāpya na paśyanti pūjāstvarcāgatā yataḥ .. 5 ..
meaning:
कृतत्रेताद्वापरेषु नराः पश्यन्ति देवताम् ..
तिष्यं प्राप्य न पश्यन्ति पूजास्त्वर्चागता यतः .. 5 ..
text_mt: In the Kṛta, Tretā, and Dvāpara ages, men behold the deity; / having reached the Kali age, they do not behold [the deity], because worship is directed to images. (5)

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtādiṣvapi dṛṣṭvā ca devānmanujasattama ..
arcāgataviśeṣeṇa pūjayanti vidhānataḥ .. 6 ..
meaning:
कृतादिष्वपि दृष्ट्वा च देवान्मनुजसत्तम ..
अर्चागतविशेषेण पूजयन्ति विधानतः .. 6 ..
text_mt: Even in the Kṛta and other ages, O best of men, having beheld the gods, / they worship them according to rule, particularly when present in images. (6)

sanskrit_iast:
citrasūtravidhānena devatārcāṃ vinirmitām ..
surūpāṃ pūjayedvidvāṃstatra saṃnihitā bhavet .. 7..
meaning:
चित्रसूत्रविधानेन देवतार्चां विनिर्मिताम् ..
सुरूपां पूजयेद्विद्वांस्तत्र संनिहिता भवेत् .. 7..
text_mt: A wise man should worship an image of a deity fashioned / according to the rules of the Citrasūtra and well-proportioned; [the deity] will be present there. (7)

sanskrit_iast:
svākārāṃ lakṣaṇopetāṃ yastāṃ saṃpūjayennaraḥ ..
sa sarvakāmānāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
asmim̐lloke pare caiva sukhavānsa bhavetsadā .. 8 ..
meaning:
स्वाकारां लक्षणोपेतां यस्तां संपूजयेन्नरः ..
स सर्वकामानाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
अस्मिम्̐ल्लोके परे चैव सुखवान्स भवेत्सदा .. 8 ..
text_mt: A man who worships it properly shaped and endowed with the required characteristics / attains all desires; there is no doubt in this; / he will always be happy in this world and in the next. (8)

sanskrit_iast:
athārcāṃ lakṣaṇairhīnāṃ yastu pūjayate naraḥ ..
tasyānarthā vivardhante tasmāttāṃ ca vivarjayet .. 9 ..
meaning:
अथार्चां लक्षणैर्हीनां यस्तु पूजयते नरः ..
तस्यानर्था विवर्धन्ते तस्मात्तां च विवर्जयेत् .. 9 ..
text_mt: Now, as for the man who worships an image devoid of the required characteristics, / his misfortunes multiply; therefore, one should avoid it. (9)

sanskrit_iast:
prāsādakaraṇaṃ puṇyaṃ devārcākaraṇaṃ tathā ..
surārcāpūjanaṃ puṇyaṃ tatra puṇyā namaskriyā .. 3.1.10 ..
meaning:
प्रासादकरणं पुण्यं देवार्चाकरणं तथा ..
सुरार्चापूजनं पुण्यं तत्र पुण्या नमस्क्रिया .. 3.1.10 ..
text_mt: Building a temple is meritorious, as is making an image of a deity; / worship of a divine image is meritorious, and bowing down to it is meritorious. (10)

sanskrit_iast:
tasmātsarvapratnena surārcāṃ lakṣaṇānvitām ..
kārayetpūjanaṃ vidvānna tvalakṣaṇasaṃyutām ..11 ..
meaning:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रत्नेन सुरार्चां लक्षणान्विताम् ..
कारयेत्पूजनं विद्वान्न त्वलक्षणसंयुताम् ..11 ..
text_mt: Therefore, with every effort a wise man should have an image of a deity made / endowed with the required characteristics, and worship it, never one devoid of characteristics. (11)

sanskrit_iast:
dharmamarthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yadunandana ..
prayacchanti mahārāja narāṇāmiha devatāḥ .. 12 ..
meaning:
धर्ममर्थं तथा कामं मोक्षं च यदुनन्दन ..
प्रयच्छन्ति महाराज नराणामिह देवताः .. 12 ..
text_mt: Dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, O delight of the Yadus, / the gods bestow upon men here, O great king. (12)

sanskrit_iast:
kāmāniṣṭānprayacchanti svargamatyantameva ca ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena nṛṇāṃ pūjyā divaukasaḥ .. 13 ..
meaning:
कामानिष्टान्प्रयच्छन्ति स्वर्गमत्यन्तमेव च ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन नृणां पूज्या दिवौकसः .. 13 ..
text_mt: They bestow cherished desires, and heaven that is supreme. / Therefore, with all effort the denizens of heaven must be worshipped by men. (13)

sanskrit_iast:
nityaṃ narāṇāṃ surapūjakānāṃ lokā manojñāḥ sulabhā bhavanti ..

यस्मात्सन्निहिता नित्यं शास्त्रवत्साकृतिर्भवेत्..1..
मार्कण्डेय उवाच..
चित्रसूत्रं न जानाति यस्तु सम्यङ् नराधिप ..
प्रतिमालक्षणं वेत्तुं न शक्यन्तेन कर्हिचित् .. 2 ..
वज्र उवाच ..

text_mt:
For men who continually worship the gods, delightful worlds are easily obtained; / likewise in this world, men become endowed with wealth and grain, and enjoy prosperity. (14)
3.2
Vajra said:
Tell me, O sinless one, about the fashioning of the forms of the deities, / by which [an image] made according to the treatise may always possess their presence. (1)
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
He who does not thoroughly know the Citrasūtra, O lord of men, / can never know the characteristics of an image. (2)
Vajra said:
Explain the Citrasūtra, O promoter of the race of Bhṛgu, / since only he who knows the Citrasūtra knows the characteristics of sacred words.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Without the treatise on dance, the Citrasūtra is very hard to know; (3)
for no depiction of the world can be made by either of the two [without the other], O king.
Vajra said:
Explain the treatise on dance; you will [then] speak of the Citrasūtra, / since one who knows the rules of the treatise on dance knows painting, O twice-born one. (4)

वज्र उवाच ..
गीतशास्त्रं समाचक्ष्व सर्वधर्मभृतां वर ..

मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..

देशभाषाविशेषेण तस्यान्तो नेह विद्यते ..

text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
He who does not know instrumental music finds dance hard to know; / without instrumental music, dance cannot exist in any way. (5)
Vajra said:
You, O knower of dharma, will speak of instrumental music and the treatise on dance; / when that is well known, one understands dance, O best of the Bhṛgus. (6)
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Even instrumental music cannot be understood without vocal music;
he who knows the rules of the science of vocal music knows everything according to rule.
Vajra said:
Explain the science of vocal music, O best of all maintainers of dharma;
indeed, one who knows the science of vocal music is all-knowing, the highest of men.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Vocal music is said to be of two kinds: Sanskrit and Prakrit;
and the third is Apabhraṃśa, which is endless, O lord of men.
Through the distinctions of regional languages, there is no end to it here;
vocal music is to be known through recitation, and that recitation is considered twofold:
prose and verse, O knower of dharma. Prose is held [to be used] in narrative;
verse is [defined] by specific metres, and metre can be of many kinds.

एकविंशतिसंख्याः स्युः सुपः सुप्तिङ्परं स्मृतम् ..

sanskrit_iast:

text_mt:

sanskrit_iast:

परिमाणे च कथिता विभक्तिः प्रथमा बुधैः .. 17 ..

In the sense of the nominal stem, in the singular, dual and plural, in address,

sanskrit_iast:
dvitīyā karmaṇi matā tṛtīyā karaṇe smṛtā ..

sanskrit_iast:

3.3
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ṣaḍakṣareṇa pādena gāyatraṃ chanda ucyate ..
uṣṇik saptākṣaraṃ caiva aṣṭākṣaramanuṣṭubham .. 1..
