caturdaśākṣarā caiva śakvarī yadunandana..3..
atiśakvarī ca kathitā tathā pañcadaśākṣarā ..
ṣoḍaśākṣaramicchanti cchando'ṣṭiriti yatsmṛtam..4..
atyaṣṭisaṃjñaṃ chandaśca tathā saptadaśākṣaram..
aṣṭādaśākṣaraṃ caiva vṛttisaṃjñaṃ prakīrtitam .. 5 ..
tathātivṛttisaṃjñaṃ ca viṃśati stvekavarjitā..
viṃśatiścākṣarāṇi syuḥ kṛtisaṃjñaṃ yadūttama..6..
meaning:
प्रातिपदिकमिह स्वं प्रकृतिः स्यात्तत्प्रकृतिमपि धातुमिच्छन्ति ..
वाङ्मयमखिलमनेन निबद्धं गद्यमपि यदथ पद्यसमेतम् ..21 ..
3.3
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
षडक्षरेण पादेन गायत्रं छन्द उच्यते ..
उष्णिक् सप्ताक्षरं चैव अष्टाक्षरमनुष्टुभम् .. 1..
नवाक्षरा च बृहती पंक्तिसंज्ञं दशाक्षरम् ..
एकादशाक्षरं त्रिष्टुब्जगती द्वादशाक्षरम्..2..
त्रयोदशाक्षरं ज्ञेयमतिपूर्वं तथैव हि ..
चतुर्दशाक्षरा चैव शक्वरी यदुनन्दन..3..
अतिशक्वरी च कथिता तथा पञ्चदशाक्षरा ..
षोडशाक्षरमिच्छन्ति च्छन्दोऽष्टिरिति यत्स्मृतम्..4..
अत्यष्टिसंज्ञं छन्दश्च तथा सप्तदशाक्षरम्..
अष्टादशाक्षरं चैव वृत्तिसंज्ञं प्रकीर्तितम् .. 5 ..
तथातिवृत्तिसंज्ञं च विंशति स्त्वेकवर्जिता..
विंशतिश्चाक्षराणि स्युः कृतिसंज्ञं यदूत्तम..6..

sanskrit_iast:
viṃśatistvekasaṃyuktā prakṛtiḥ parikīrtitā..
dvāviṃśatiśca kathitaṃ tathaivākṛtisaṃjñakama ..7..
trayoviṃśatiśca vikṛtiḥ sā caikātsaṃkṛtirmatā ..
saṃkṛtiścaikasaṃyuktā kathitā vikṛtirnṛpa ..8..
ṣaḍviṃśatiścātikṛtiśchandaścoktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ ..
yathāyathaṃ caturbhiḥ svaiḥ pādairetāni nirdiśet .. 9 ..

meaning:
विंशतिस्त्वेकसंयुक्ता प्रकृतिः परिकीर्तिता..
द्वाविंशतिश्च कथितं तथैवाकृतिसंज्ञकम ..7..
त्रयोविंशतिश्च विकृतिः सा चैकात्संकृतिर्मता ..
संकृतिश्चैकसंयुक्ता कथिता विकृतिर्नृप ..8..
षड्विंशतिश्चातिकृतिश्छन्दश्चोक्तं मनीषिभिः ..
यथायथं चतुर्भिः स्वैः पादैरेतानि निर्दिशेत् .. 9 ..
मात्रकस्तु लघुर्वर्णः स्पष्टलेखाभिचिह्नितः ..
संस्थाप्यः स्याद्द्विमात्रस्तु गुरुर्वक्रस्तथा भवेत् .. 3.3.10 ..
लघुश्चान्त्यश्च यो वर्णः स गुरुश्च भवेन्नृप ..
दीर्घप्लुतौ च कथितौ तथैव गुरुसंज्ञकौ ..11 ..
संयोगाद्याः परे यस्मात्स लघुश्च गुरुः स्मृतः ..
लघुगुरुविभागेन प्रस्तारोनेन यादव .. 12 ..
सर्वे छन्दोविकल्पाश्च भवन्ति बहुशो नृप ..

sanskrit_iast:
yāvatsaṃkhyākṣaraṃ cchaṃdastāvanto guruvo nṛpa ..
sthāpyā adhaśca pūrvāṇāṃ laghu pūrvasya vinyaset .. 14 ..
ato'nyeṣu tvavasthāpyaṃ nṛpamukhya yathāsthitam ..
evameva vidhiṃ kuryādādiśca gurubhiḥ punaḥ .. 15 ..
pūrayedakṣaraistāvatkuryādetaṃ nṛpottama ..
yāvadakṣarasaṃkhyā syuḥ sarve hi laghavo nṛpa .. 16 ..
etatsyādakṣaraicchando mātrāśchandāstathaiva hi ..
uktavarṇākṣaraṃ chando bhavedekavivarjitaḥ .. 17 ..
yadā tadā nivṛtsaṃjño hyadhikena tamattathā ..
varṇadvayena rahitaṃ virāḍiti hi śabditam .. 18 ..
adhikaṃ ca surāsaṃjñaṃ kathitaṃ yadusattama ..
tebhyo bhavanti sarvāṇi mātrācchandāṃsi yādava .. 19 ..
diṅmātrametatkathitaṃ narendra vistārajijñāsurato manuṣyaḥ ..
saṃsādhayettatsvadhiyā yathāvatsudustaraṃ vistaraśo hi vaktum .. 3.3.20 ..
meaning:
यावत्संख्याक्षरं च्छंदस्तावन्तो गुरुवो नृप ..
स्थाप्या अधश्च पूर्वाणां लघु पूर्वस्य विन्यसेत् .. 14 ..
अतोऽन्येषु त्ववस्थाप्यं नृपमुख्य यथास्थितम् ..
एवमेव विधिं कुर्यादादिश्च गुरुभिः पुनः .. 15 ..
पूरयेदक्षरैस्तावत्कुर्यादेतं नृपोत्तम ..
यावदक्षरसंख्या स्युः सर्वे हि लघवो नृप .. 16 ..
एतत्स्यादक्षरैच्छन्दो मात्राश्छन्दास्तथैव हि ..
उक्तवर्णाक्षरं छन्दो भवेदेकविवर्जितः .. 17 ..
यदा तदा निवृत्संज्ञो ह्यधिकेन तमत्तथा ..

text_mt:
As many syllables as the metre has, so many heavy ones, O king,
are to be set down; and below the previous ones, one should place a light syllable of the former.
Then in the others, O foremost of kings, it should be placed as it stands;
one should perform this same procedure, and beginning again with heavy syllables,
one should fill it with syllables, doing this until, O best of kings,
all the syllables become light in number, O king.
This is metre by syllables, and likewise metre by morae.
A metre lacking one syllable from the stated syllables
is then called Nicṛt; and with an additional one, it is [called] Bhūrij.
That which is deprived of two syllables is named Virāj;
and that which has [two] additional is called Svarāj, O best of the Yadus.
From them arise all the moraic metres, O Yādava.
This has been told merely as an indication, O ruler of men; from this a man desiring to know the full extent
should accomplish it with his own intellect properly, for it is very difficult to explain in detail.

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
There, speech which is authoritative, unambiguous, brilliant, with deep sound,
and sometimes accompanied by etymology, is the speech of the Self-born [Brahmā].
Speech which is somewhat mixed, furnished with nominal case-endings,
and refers to what is directly perceived, is held to be the speech of women like that.
Speech which abounds in various Vedic words and particles,
and is not very long, is remembered as the speech of the Ṛcīkas.
The speech of sons of sages is to be known as having indistinct words, O king.
Knowledge of past, future, and present, and reviling of the misery of birth:
that is the speech of friends, as well as directing [the mind] to the origins [of things].
Speech that is commanding and devoid of reasoning
is to be known as that of royal seers, with much meaning and extensive elaboration.
Speech with many names for many meanings is proclaimed as that of the gods.
That which has many words and little meaning is proclaimed to belong to the dānavas. / That which has few words and little meaning belongs likewise to the gandharvas.

That which is difficult to comprehend and irregular is proclaimed to belong to the rākṣasas. / That which has hidden syllables belongs to the yakṣas, and similarly [speech] as spoken by the kinnaras.
That which is exceedingly clear and accompanied by repetitions belongs to the nāgas. / Human [speech] is accompanied by attachment and aversion, and is endowed with reasoning.
Mantras characterized by the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma [Vedas] are said to be of nine kinds: / praise, blame, commendation, abuse, and command,
question, permission, narration, and benediction are considered their topics. / Thus the full definition of all sciences has been laid down for you […] / And that is found in human [speech] and not elsewhere; this is the conclusion. / Those who are not human never depart from their own nature.
For a certain man is seen [to be ordinary], while a certain man is supreme in intellect; / therefore, O king, his intellect is said to be supreme precisely therein.
This excellent examination of speech has been spoken by me to you, O best of those who know speech; / and here it should be understood by the wise through attachment and through the presence of aversion.

Whether it equals divine speech or speech of the ṛṣis, or whether it equals other speech, / the speech of men, O king, is to be understood as arising from attachment and from the presence of aversion.
3.5 / Having few syllables, free from ambiguity, containing the essence, facing in all directions, / free from superfluous words, and blameless: such is an aphorism known to those who know aphorisms.
It is proclaimed to be of two kinds: general rule and exception. / The aphorism, the counter-exclusion, the example, O king,
and the counter-example are proclaimed to be the four limbs. / And the sentence, the meaning of the sentence, the meaning of the word, and the word itself—
this too is proclaimed elsewhere as four limbs. / Thesis, reason, example, application,
and conclusion are accepted as the five members [of a syllogism]. / The initial statement, the connection, the meaning of the aphorism, its qualification,
the objection, and the resolution: this is the sixfold exposition of an aphorism. / For all that is cited [and] exemplified is indeed contained in aphorisms.

What is spoken at great length destroys the intellect; what is spoken too concisely is not grasped. / Leaving aside conciseness and verbosity, one should state what one intends to say.
One should avoid that which is devoid of meaning, contradictory, tautological, / similarly of disjointed arrangement, and devoid of logic.
Breach of order, division [of an indivisible rule], an overly heavy aphorism, / and alteration of an expression: these should not occur without a reason.
Having made all the word-analysis, and immediately thereafter the compound analysis, / when the compound analysis has been made, the wise man should explain the meaning.
The meaning of the aphorism, the meaning of the words, the reason, the sequence, / the etymology, and the arrangement: this is the sixfold exposition of a rule.
Perception, inference, and authoritative testimony: / endowed with these three means of valid knowledge, a treatise is entitled to authoritativeness.
Pseudo-perception is also mentioned, such as a mirage; / an apparent inference is like a mass of vapor or dust,

which generates the doubt of smoke, but does not lead to the apprehension of fire. / But that which is uttered by an untrustworthy person who makes a show of trustworthiness,
that, O best of kings, they call pseudo-authoritative testimony. / One who is completely free from attachment and aversion is called authoritative.
Know etymological interpretation to be twofold: established and natural. / What is to be derived is established, but the establishment of the meaning is eternal.
Therein, all [terms] like 'cow', 'horse', and 'man' are natural. / It is declared to be of ten kinds by the tradition; I shall state that as it has been received:
the categorical, the causal, the manifested, the conventional, the artificial, / the metaphorical, the relational, the secondary, and the derivative.
We see the secondary from a quality, such as 'great' and the like; / and from a cause, the causal, as 'broken', 'shaven', and the like.
Metaphorically [one says] 'devoted' because of devotion, 'man-lion' because of the mouth, or 'mother-like' toward one who is not a mother. / And where they speak alike, that is convention, such as 'a courtesan'.
The artificial is that which is made, such as Devadatta and the like. / Metaphor arises from figurative transference, as 'oil-noose' or 'balance'.

text_mt:
3.6
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now, these are the hermeneutic devices (tantrayukti): the topic (adhikaraṇa), connection (yoga), word-meaning (padārtha), purpose of reason (hetvartha), brief statement (uddeśa), detailed statement (nirdeśa), local application (pradeśa), extended application (atideśa), exception (apavarga), sentence-completion (vākyaśeṣa), presumption (arthāpatti), context (prasaṅga), certainty (ekānta), uncertainty (naikānta), prima facie view (pūrvapakṣa), conclusive determination (nirṇaya), prescription (vidhāna), synonym (paryāya), reference to the past (atītakrāntāvekṣaṇa), doubt (saṃśaya), explanation (vyākhyāna), assent (anumati), special nomenclature (svasaṃjñā), etymology (nirvacana), illustrative example (dṛṣṭānta), disjunction (viyoga), option (vikalpa), and conjunction (samuccaya).
There, topic is that by which the sentence's meaning is joined together; connection is that meaning which is the modified word of a sūtra; word-meaning is that; purpose of reason is the establishment of an object by logical reasoning from another [source].
Brief statement is an abbreviated expression; detailed statement is an expanded expression; "precisely thus" is instruction; "for this reason" is assigned reason; local application is the establishment of a present matter through a future one; […] exception is that by which a meaning is concluded;
sentence-completion is [accomplished] by supplying an ellipsis; presumption is what follows necessarily from what has not been explicitly stated; context is what is mentioned as part of a topic and then stated again through some parenthetical relevance; certainty is that which holds true everywhere; uncertainty is that which holds true in some cases but otherwise elsewhere; conclusive determination is a statement of refutation; prescription is the ordered arrangement of a topic, and its inversion is called contrary.
Reference to the past is [such]; reference to the future is saying "I shall explain later"; doubt is seeing arguments on both sides; explanation is the detailed description thereof; assent is another's doctrine that is unrefuted; special nomenclature is a word not agreed upon by others; etymology is an example well known in common parlance; illustrative example is the display of that logic; option is saying "either this or that"; conjunction is saying "this and that"; and that which is unstated here but comprehensible through reasoning is to be inferred.
The purpose, doubt and conclusive determination, specific explanation and brevity of qualities, / the rejection of what has been done, the prescription of what has not been done, and the eightfold quality of dharma conducive to dissolution.

Now next I will declare to you the characteristics of Prākṛt: / here there are no ṛ, ṝ, lṛ, or lṝ, nor any sibilants [ṣ and ś], nor both ma and ṣa.

text_mt:
The treatises, O king, were composed by the ancients; Smṛti is called tradition, and Śruti is the Veda; / that conduct which belongs to the knowers of the treatises, O king, is indeed designated as proper practice.
3.9 / A year is saṃvatsara, abda, varṣa, samā, and hāyana; / a day is divasa, vāsara, dina, and ahan.
Night is doṣā, vibhāvarī, rātri, śarvarī, yāminī, and kṣapā; / twilight is proclaimed as saṃdhi and sandhyā; darkness is known as andhakāra and tamas.
Moonlight is candrikā and jyotsnā; Caitra is known as Madhu; / Vaiśākha is called Mādhava; Jyeṣṭha is spoken of as Śuci.
Āṣāḍha is proclaimed as Śukla; Śrāvaṇa is acknowledged as Nabhas; / Bhādrapada is Nabhasya; and Āśvina is known as Iṣa.
Kārtika is called Ūrja; Mārgaśīrṣa is Sahas; / Pauṣa is spoken of as Sahasya; and Māgha is Tapas.
And Phālguna is the month named Tapasya, O scion of the Yadu race; / when the sun enters Libra and Aries, it is called the equinox day.

text_mt:
From Sagittarius to the end of Gemini is his southern course; / the end of Aries and the end of Libra are known as the days marking the beginning of an era.
Likewise, the step of Viṣṇu is proclaimed at the ends of Cancer and Capricorn; / at the entry of the sun into Virgo, Gemini, Pisces, and Sagittarius,
the four days are to be known by the name of ṣaḍaśītimukha; / a ray [of light] is raśmi, gabhasti, bhadrā, kara, and dīdhiti.
At sunrise and sunset, that long [halo] becomes a paridhi; / that very streak of clouds lying crosswise becomes a parigha.
A cloud resembling a staff is called daṇḍa; / Indra's rainbow is Śakracāpa and Śakradhanus; when elongated, it is a rohita.
A cloud resembling a staff is called daṇḍa; / Indra's bow is Śakracāpa and Śakradhanus; when elongated, it is considered a rohita.
When yellow and small, it is [...] a mock sun; / the streak of clouds encircling the disc of the moon and sun is a pariveṣa.

text_mt:
Falling from heaven when auspicious merit is exhausted, it is called a meteor; / seen transiently with a crest, a star is recognized as a comet.
A horizon wiped with the colour of fire is renowned as a fire-glow of the quarters; / a city seen in empty space is known as a city of the gandharvas.
Thunder without the sight of clouds is proclaimed as a thunderclap; / the illusory sight of water appearing here and there is called a mirage.
A cloud is megha, ghana, vārida, jīmūta, and balāhaka; / one should know thunder as stanita and garjita; rain is spoken of as pravarṣaṇa.
A torrential rain is āsāra; a gentle drizzle is called pṛṣata; / while the sun is visible, rain is proclaimed as divine.
While the moon is visible, it is declared to be endowed with nectar; / a cyclone is born of wind; mist is called darkness.
Dew is called śīkara and avaśyāya; frost is tuṣāra, tuhina, and hima; / lightning is vidyut, taḍit, lolā, cañcalā, and śatahradā.
Oceans are samudras, ambunidhis, sāgaras, and salt waters; / rivers are winding streams, nimnagās, and sarits.

text_mt:
The Gaṅgā is called Viṣṇupadī, Jāhnavī, and Tripathā; / the Yamunā is called Kālindī; the Narmadā is called Revā; / the Vipāśā is named Sanandā; and the Śatadru is known as Śauri.
Intellect is proclaimed as the sun, and the elements are spoken of as the senses; / speech is proclaimed as Sarasvatī, and the mind, O king, is called the moon.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / A man is manuṣya, manuja, puruṣa, and pūruṣa; / a woman is known as rāmā, yoṣit, strī, and lalanā.
An excellent woman is varārohā, purandhrī, and mattakāśinī; / a brāhmaṇa is vipra; a kṣatriya is regarded as rājanya.
A vaiśya is known as kīnāśa; a śūdra is called antyaja; / an outcaste is caṇḍāla, pukkasa, and is likewise called mātaṅga.
An elephant is hastin, dvipa, ibha, dantin, mātaṅga, kuñjara, and gaja; / a horse is aśva, turaga, sapti, haya, vājin, and hari.
A bull is go and ukṣan; a goat is chāgala and aja; / a ram is called urabhra and avi.

text_mt:
A sword is asi, viśasana, khaḍga, tīkṣṇadhāra, durāsada, / śrīgarbha, vijaya, and eighth, dharmādhāra.
Gold is suvarṇa, kanaka, rukma, hema, and kārtasvara; / that of the gods is jāmbūnada; silver is designated as rūpya and rajata.
Copper is known as udumbara; iron is proclaimed as ayas and loha; / brass is ārakūṭa and rīti; a jewel is called māṇikya.
The parasol is called *ātapatra* or *chatra*; the conch is referred to as *kambu* or *śaṅkha*. / The lotus is known as *paṅkaja*, *kamala*, *padma*, [and] *puṇḍarīka*,
as well as *tāmarasa*, and *śatapatra*, which belongs to the gods; / the blue water-lily is *indīvara* and *utpala*, and *kahlāra* is indeed the white [water-lily].
Battle is *saṃgrāma*, *āji*, *yuddha*, *janya*, and *āhava*; / a gift is declared to be *dāna* and *saṃvanana*; marriage is *vivāha* and *viniveśana*.
Wife is *patnī*, *bhāryā*, and *jāyā*; son is *suta*, *putra*, and *tanūdbhava*; / mother is *mātā*, *janitrī*, and *jananī*; father is *janitā*, *janaka*, and *pitā*.

text_mt:
A dwelling is called *kṣaya*, *bhavana*, *mandira*, and *gṛha*; / a storehouse is called *bhāṇḍāgāra* and *kośa*; a hiding place is considered *dhanvana* and *gupti*.
A conveyance has the name *vāhana* and *patra*; a vessel is called *amatra* and *pātra*; / a shallow dish is called *vardhamāna* and *śarāva*; a bow is called *cāpa* and *dhanus*.
An arrow is called *sāyaka*, *śara*, *iṣu*, *bāṇa*, and *śilīmukha*; / that which is released by the hand is also spoken of as *bṛhanta* and *tovara*.
A shower of flowers is called *puṣpaprakara* and *upakāra*, O king; / a fly-whisk of hair is also named *bālavyajana* as well as *cāmara*.
Beauty is designated as *mṛjā* and *śobhā*; ornament is *alaṅkāra* and *vibhūṣaṇa*; / decoration is *prasādhana* and *maṇḍana*; strength is declared to be *bala* and *sāra*.
A child is called *arbhaka* and *bāla*; a young horse is a *kiśoraka*; / an elephant [calf] is called *kalabha*; and a [young] bull is called *vatsa* and *ukṣan*.
In every case, a lion is *keśarin* and *siṃha*; a tiger is called *śārdūla* and *vyāghra*; / an uninhabited [forest] is called *vipina* and *nirjana*; a courtyard of a house is *ajira* and *gṛhāṅgaṇa*.
He who initiates and imparts the Veda is declared to be an *ācārya*; / he who teaches a portion [of the Veda] is an *upādhyāya*; the priest who performs the sacrifice is called an *ṛtvij*.

these words that belong to the feminine have been declared to you by me in summary, O king; / the wise consider all these to be infinite among words designating the feminine.

3.14 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The repeated placement of each single syllable, / for the sake of conveying meaning, was designated as alliteration (anuprāsa) by the ancients.
Done excessively, O king, it descends into vulgarity. / Words [repeated] in identical sequence, on the other hand, are declared as rhyme (yamaka).
That is desired at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end of a quarter-verse; / likewise, the [two varieties of] rhyme known as saṃdaṣṭaka and samudra are recognised.
A rhyme involving an entire quarter-verse is declared to be difficult to compose. / The equality of the object of comparison (upameya) with the standard of comparison (upamāna) is metaphor (rūpaka).
The heightened metaphor (rūpakābhyadhika) is that very same figure with one superior quality. / Contrast (vyatireka) is exemplified by a distinction in qualities,
and it is held to be another [variety] through qualities opposed to the standard of comparison. / Through words expressing two or three meanings, it is designated as pun (śleṣa).

text_mt:
And when a thing of one form is imagined as something otherwise, / that is declared by the ancients as the poetic figure called poetic fancy (utprekṣā).
Likewise, another statement may occur, distinct from what is under discussion; / that is to be known as corroboration (arthāntaranyāsa) if it conforms to the preceding sense.
Or when another matter is proclaimed by means of the statement of something else, / that, O lord of men, they call the poetic figure of statement (upanyāsa).
When an effect achieves expansion without an [apparent] cause, that is special indication (vibhāvanā). / And hyperbole (atiśayokti) is declared through incomparable qualities of comparison.
The description of a thing as it actually is, is proclaimed as natural description (svabhāvokti). / And the sequential presentation of several things that have been taught,
is named relative order (yathāsaṃkhya) as a poetic figure by the ancients. / Special mention (viśeṣokti), O king, is spoken of from the attainment of a specific excellence.
An action that yields a different fruit is held to be incongruity (virodha). / Reproach in the form of praise is called reproachful praise (nindāstuti) here;
praise in the form of reproach is likewise declared to be nindāstuti. / Illustration (nidarśana) is the showing [of a concept] through an object that depicts it.

Where, O hero among men, a comparison occurs without [another object], such that it belongs to that very [subject] alone, / it is called self-comparison (ananvaya) by the ancients. Thus much has been declared to you, merely in brief.
3.15 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / A treatise (śāstra) must be an instruction in dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation. / What was practiced by the virtuous of old, achieving dharma, pleasure, and wealth,
wherein an exposition of liberation is given, is called epic history (itihāsa). / That very same thing is declared to be poetry (kāvya) when composed without [direct] instruction.
Poetry is likewise proclaimed from the life of a single [hero] alone, / in which, O best of kings, a protagonist and an antagonist are composed.
That which is furnished with marches, readiness, envoys, and battles, / and endowed with the triumph of the protagonist, is held to be a court epic (mahākāvya).
And in a court epic one should describe countries, cities, and kings, / seasons, mountains, rivers, and likewise women, O king.
The protagonist and the antagonist should likewise be described here; / the protagonist must be victorious through dharma, adhering to the path of the good.

text_mt:
And the antagonist is to be understood as one who conquers the world; / but the slaying of the antagonist is to be narrated, not of the other.
O great king, one should never depict the death of the hero; / one should depict it [only] for one who attains [heaven] in his own body.
Prose devoid of meter, contrary to grammar, / having an arrangement of words with harsh syllables, and accompanied by vulgar speech,
or in which the meaning of the sentences is hard to grasp, containing obscure expressions, / and what is repetitive—such poetic composition should not be made.
In wonder, or in indignation, in fear, sorrow, and haste, / and in joy, repetition should be employed; they do not consider that to be tautology.
In an envoy's speech, likewise in a dream, when an event has thus transpired through the course of affairs, / [or] in mentioning something again for further amplification—they consider that [too] not to be tautology.
[Speech] attended by doubt must not be uttered, nor [speech] lacking a proposition, / nor what is internally contradictory, nor that which is censured by the world.

paryāyavacanādyasyāṃ vanditā sā prakīrtitā .. 3 ..
meaning:
तस्यां मात्रावशादर्थो गोप्यते सा समागता ..
पर्यायवचनाद्यस्यां वन्दिता सा प्रकीर्तिता .. 3 ..
text_mt: That [riddle] in which the meaning is concealed by virtue of morae is [called] Samāgatā; / that in which [the meaning is concealed] through synonyms is proclaimed as Vanditā.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛttāntagopikāntāyā padairvyavahitairbhavet ..
aprasiddhaistu paryāyairduḥkhitā nāma sā smṛtā .. 4 ..
meaning:
वृत्तान्तगोपिकान्ताया पदैर्व्यवहितैर्भवेत् ..
अप्रसिद्धैस्तु पर्यायैर्दुःखिता नाम सा स्मृता .. 4 ..
text_mt: That which conceals the story by words that are separated [is known as Vṛttāntagopikā]; / while that which [does so] through unfamiliar synonyms is remembered as Duḥkhitā.

sanskrit_iast:
kalpanāgopitārthāttu kathitā parihāsikā ..
samānarūpatulyārtho śabdairanyaiḥ prakīrtitā .. 5 ..
meaning:
कल्पनागोपितार्थात्तु कथिता परिहासिका ..
समानरूपतुल्यार्थो शब्दैरन्यैः प्रकीर्तिता .. 5 ..
text_mt: That whose meaning is concealed by imagination is declared to be Parihāsikā; / that which has a similar form and identical meaning expressed by other words is proclaimed [as Samānarūpā].

sanskrit_iast:
durbodhākṣarabandhā ca paruṣā nāmataḥ smṛtā..
saṃkhyāmātrasamānatvātsaṃkhyātākhyā tathocyate .. 6 ..
meaning:
दुर्बोधाक्षरबन्धा च परुषा नामतः स्मृता..
संख्यामात्रसमानत्वात्संख्याताख्या तथोच्यते .. 6 ..
text_mt: That which has a composition of obscure syllables is remembered by the name Paruṣā; / that which is called Saṃkhyātā is spoken of thus on account of identity in mere number.

sanskrit_iast:
arthāntarānkalpanayā kalpitā ca tathocyate ..
anyasya saṃjñāyāmohānnamāntaritasaṃjñitā ..7..
meaning:
अर्थान्तरान्कल्पनया कल्पिता च तथोच्यते ..
अन्यस्य संज्ञायामोहान्नमान्तरितसंज्ञिता ..7..
text_mt: That formed through the imagining of another meaning is spoken of as [Kalpitā]; / because of confusion regarding the name of another, [a riddle] is designated Nāmāntaritā.

sanskrit_iast:
arthavyāmohataḥ proktā nibhṛtā ca mahānṛpa ..
samānaśabdā kathitā tulyaśabdanibandhanā ..8..
meaning:
अर्थव्यामोहतः प्रोक्ता निभृता च महानृप ..
समानशब्दा कथिता तुल्यशब्दनिबन्धना ..8..
text_mt: From confusion of meaning, O great king, [a riddle] is said to be Nibhṛtā; / that which is constructed with identical words is declared to be Samānaśabdā.

sanskrit_iast:
arthānulomadurbodhā vyāmūḍheti tathocyate ..
gucchākhyā kathitā vṛtte nānābandhani bandhanā .. 9 ..
meaning:
अर्थानुलोमदुर्बोधा व्यामूढेति तथोच्यते ..
गुच्छाख्या कथिता वृत्ते नानाबन्धनि बन्धना .. 9 ..
text_mt: That which is hard to understand even though the meaning runs naturally is spoken of as Vyāmūḍhā; / that constructed with various meters in a stanza is declared to be named Gucchā.

sanskrit_iast:
ekobhayabahucchanne yathārthaparigopite ..
saṃkīrṇā sambhavopetā yā tadarthakarī bhavet .. 3.16.10 ..
meaning:
एकोभयबहुच्छन्ने यथार्थपरिगोपिते ..
संकीर्णा सम्भवोपेता या तदर्थकरी भवेत् .. 3.16.10 ..
text_mt: When one, both, or many [meanings] are concealed, properly hidden in their real sense, / [a riddle] that possesses plausibility and conveys that meaning is Saṃkīrṇā.

sanskrit_iast:
tadarthakārī yatrārtho jñāyate'nyārthakāmukaḥ ..
rājañśabdavaśātsā ca kathitā vyabhicāriṇī .. 11 ..
meaning:
तदर्थकारी यत्रार्थो ज्ञायतेऽन्यार्थकामुकः ..
राजञ्शब्दवशात्सा च कथिता व्यभिचारिणी .. 11 ..
text_mt: Where an expression conveying its own sense is understood as desiring another meaning / through the power of words, O king, that is declared to be Vyabhicāriṇī.

sanskrit_iast:
ukterthe vṛttabandhena mātrābhiḥ sthāpitā tathā ..
naṣṭārthā vā ca sā proktā vṛttabandhanidarśitā .. 12 ..
meaning:
उक्तेर्थे वृत्तबन्धेन मात्राभिः स्थापिता तथा ..
नष्टार्था वा च सा प्रोक्ता वृत्तबन्धनिदर्शिता .. 12 ..
text_mt: When the stated meaning is fixed by metrical form and by morae, / that is declared to be Naṣṭārthā, illustrated through metrical composition.

sanskrit_iast:
naṣṭākṣarā tu kathitā vinaikena tadārthadā ..
anyārthatā tathaivoktā varṇabhraṣṭā nareśvara .. 13 ..
meaning:
नष्टाक्षरा तु कथिता विनैकेन तदार्थदा ..
अन्यार्थता तथैवोक्ता वर्णभ्रष्टा नरेश्वर .. 13 ..
text_mt: That which yields its meaning when deprived of one syllable is called Naṣṭākṣarā; / that which likewise yields another meaning is said to be Varṇabhraṣṭā, O lord of men.

sanskrit_iast:
kālasya rūparūpāṇāṃ vyākhyānena tadārthadā ..
bījamātreṇa leśākhyā bhūmipāla prakīrtitā .. 14 ..
meaning:
कालस्य रूपरूपाणां व्याख्यानेन तदार्थदा ..
बीजमात्रेण लेशाख्या भूमिपाल प्रकीर्तिता .. 14 ..
text_mt: That which yields its meaning through explanation of time and various forms, / [or] by a mere hint, O protector of the earth, is proclaimed as named Leśā.

sanskrit_iast:
aślīlametāsvapi naiva kāryaṃ tadvarjyamāhuḥ kavayo narendra ..
udvejanīyaṃ tu satāṃ taduktamaślīlabandhaṃ sukhadaṃ na kāvyam .. 15 ..
3.17
.. vajra uvāca .. ..
mantrāḥ sabrāhmaṇāḥ proktāstadarthaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ smṛtam ..
kalpanā ca tathā kalpaḥ kalpaśca brāhmaṇastathā .. 1 ..
kathitāni tathārthāni purāṇaṃ ca tathā dvija ..
prakriyā prathamaḥ pādaḥ kathāvastuparigrahaḥ .. 2 ..
upodghātānuṣaṅgau ca tathā saṃhāra eva ca ..
catuṣpādaṃ hi kathitaṃ purāṇaṃ bhṛgunandana .. 3 ..
sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca ..
vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam .. 4 ..
tatra vā viditaṃ sarvaṃ tatroktaṃ gītalakṣaṇam ..
vṛttasya lakṣaṇaṃ caiva nāṭakākhyānalakṣaṇam .. 5 ..
tasmādahaṃ tvāṃ pṛcchāmi dvija nāṭyasya lakṣaṇam ..
sabhedaṃ tanmamācakṣva sarvajño'si yataḥ prabho..6..
meaning:
अश्लीलमेतास्वपि नैव कार्यं तद्वर्ज्यमाहुः कवयो नरेन्द्र ..
उद्वेजनीयं तु सतां तदुक्तमश्लीलबन्धं सुखदं न काव्यम् .. 15 ..
3.17
.. वज्र उवाच .. ..
मन्त्राः सब्राह्मणाः प्रोक्तास्तदर्थं ब्राह्मणं स्मृतम् ..
कल्पना च तथा कल्पः कल्पश्च ब्राह्मणस्तथा .. 1 ..
कथितानि तथार्थानि पुराणं च तथा द्विज ..
प्रक्रिया प्रथमः पादः कथावस्तुपरिग्रहः .. 2 ..
उपोद्घातानुषङ्गौ च तथा संहार एव च ..
चतुष्पादं हि कथितं पुराणं भृगुनन्दन .. 3 ..
सर्गश्च प्रतिसर्गश्च वंशो मन्वन्तराणि च ..
वंशानुचरितं चैव पुराणं पञ्चलक्षणम् .. 4 ..
तत्र वा विदितं सर्वं तत्रोक्तं गीतलक्षणम् ..
वृत्तस्य लक्षणं चैव नाटकाख्यानलक्षणम् .. 5 ..
तस्मादहं त्वां पृच्छामि द्विज नाट्यस्य लक्षणम् ..
सभेदं तन्ममाचक्ष्व सर्वज्ञोऽसि यतः प्रभो..6..
text_mt:
Even in these, vulgarity must never be introduced; poets say that is to be avoided, O ruler of men. / For that which is distressing to the virtuous is said to be [vulgar]; a poem with vulgar composition brings no pleasure.
Vajra said: / Mantras along with Brāhmaṇas have been spoken of, and the Brāhmaṇa is considered to explain their meaning; / so also ritual arrangement and the Kalpa, and the Kalpa is like the Brāhmaṇa.
Likewise, their meanings and the Purāṇa have been told, O twice-born one. / The first quarter is Prakriyā, the adoption of the narrative subject matter;
and Upodghāta, Anuṣaṅga, and likewise Saṃhāra— / indeed, the Purāṇa is declared to have four quarters, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Creation, secondary creation, genealogy, the Manvantaras, / and the history of dynasties—the Purāṇa has these five characteristics.
All that is known therein; therein the definition of song was stated, / as well as the definition of meter, and the definition of dramatic narratives.
Therefore I ask you, O twice-born one, about the characteristics of drama; / explain that to me along with its divisions, since you are omniscient, O lord.

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
itihāsānusāreṇa purāṇānāṃ samīkṣitam ..
caritaṃ tridaśānāṃ vā nāṭakaṃ tatra kīrtitam..7..
ekanāyakasaṃyuktaṃ nāyakapratināyakaiḥ.
saṃyuktamathavā kāryaḥ kāvye vai tatra nāyakaḥ ..8..
sarvāstu vṛttayastatra tatra sarve tathā rasāḥ ..
kālaprayogaṃ ca tathā yuktyā saṃdarśayennṛpa ..9..
pañcāvarāṅkaṃ tatproktaṃ tathādaśaparaṃ śubham ..
ekadaivatikaṃ vṛttamaṅke rājanpradarśayeta .. 3.17.10 ..
tadante sarvapātrāṇāṃ niṣkramaśca vidhīyate ..
yuktyupanyāsasaṃyuktaṃ tathā niṣkamaṇaṃ matam ..11..
maraṇaṃ rājyavibhraṃśo nagarasyoparodhanam ..
etāni darśayennāṃke tathā yuddhaṃ ca pārthiva .. 12 ..
praveśakena kartavyaṃ teṣāmākhyānakaṃ budhaiḥ ..
pātradvayena kartavyaṃ tathā nityaṃ praveśakam .. 13 ..
meaning:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
इतिहासानुसारेण पुराणानां समीक्षितम् ..
चरितं त्रिदशानां वा नाटकं तत्र कीर्तितम्..7..
एकनायकसंयुक्तं नायकप्रतिनायकैः.
संयुक्तमथवा कार्यः काव्ये वै तत्र नायकः ..8..
सर्वास्तु वृत्तयस्तत्र तत्र सर्वे तथा रसाः ..
कालप्रयोगं च तथा युक्त्या संदर्शयेन्नृप ..9..
पञ्चावराङ्कं तत्प्रोक्तं तथादशपरं शुभम् ..
एकदैवतिकं वृत्तमङ्के राजन्प्रदर्शयेत .. 3.17.10 ..
तदन्ते सर्वपात्राणां निष्क्रमश्च विधीयते ..
युक्त्युपन्याससंयुक्तं तथा निष्कमणं मतम् ..11..
मरणं राज्यविभ्रंशो नगरस्योपरोधनम् ..
एतानि दर्शयेन्नांके तथा युद्धं च पार्थिव .. 12 ..
प्रवेशकेन कर्तव्यं तेषामाख्यानकं बुधैः ..
पात्रद्वयेन कर्तव्यं तथा नित्यं प्रवेशकम् .. 13 ..
text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Drama is proclaimed therein as that which examines the deeds of the gods / or [human heroes] in accordance with Itihāsa and the Purāṇas.
It may be provided with a single hero, or provided with a hero and a rival hero; / the hero should be made [prominent] in that poetic work.
All dramatic styles are to be employed therein, likewise all rasas therein; / and one should appropriately demonstrate the passage of time, O king.
It is stated to have a minimum of five acts, and auspiciously a maximum of ten; / in an act, O king, one should show an incident concerning a single principal deity.
At the end of it, the exit of all characters is prescribed; / their exit is considered proper when connected with an appropriate dramatic pretext.
Death, loss of a kingdom, the siege of a city, / and likewise battle—these one should not show in an act, O king.
The wise should present the narrative of these through an introductory scene; / an introductory scene should always be performed by two characters.

sanskrit_iast:
pātre parijane tatra kartavyaṃ nāyakena tu ..
bhinnaṃ pātradvayaṃ yatra tatra viṣkambhakaṃ smṛtam ..14..
tayorante tu kartavyā tathā raṅgasya śūnyatā ..
aṅgānte ca tathā kāryā na kāryā sānyathā bhavet .. 15 ..
meaning:
पात्रे परिजने तत्र कर्तव्यं नायकेन तु ..
भिन्नं पात्रद्वयं यत्र तत्र विष्कम्भकं स्मृतम् ..14..
तयोरन्ते तु कर्तव्या तथा रङ्गस्य शून्यता ..
अङ्गान्ते च तथा कार्या न कार्या सान्यथा भवेत् .. 15 ..
text_mt:
There it should be performed by [minor] characters or attendants of the hero; / where two different characters [of intermediate rank] are used, that is remembered as a Viṣkambhaka.
At the conclusion of both, the stage should be left empty; / likewise it should be made [empty] at the end of an act; it should not be otherwise.

sanskrit_iast:
bahudaivatikaṃ vṛttaṃ kartavyaṃ tu praveśakam ..
saṃkṣapoktiśca kartavyā kartavyo nahi vistaraḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
बहुदैवतिकं वृत्तं कर्तव्यं तु प्रवेशकम् ..
संक्षपोक्तिश्च कर्तव्या कर्तव्यो नहि विस्तरः .. 16 ..
text_mt: An introductory scene, however, should treat an action involving many deities; / it should be composed with concise speech; extensive detail must not be made.

sanskrit_iast:
prakhyātanāyakavadhaṃ na ca tatra praveśayet..
tasya prakāśanaṃ kāryamaṅkepyeva narādhipa .. 17 ..
meaning:
प्रख्यातनायकवधं न च तत्र प्रवेशयेत्..
तस्य प्रकाशनं कार्यमङ्केप्येव नराधिप .. 17 ..
text_mt: And one should not introduce therein the slaying of a celebrated hero; / its revelation should be made only in an act, O ruler of men.

sanskrit_iast:
nāyakābhyudayaḥ kāryo nāṭakānte tathaiva ca ..
bahvyo'pi nāyikā yatra tāsāmapi tathā bhavet .. 18 ..
meaning:
नायकाभ्युदयः कार्यो नाटकान्ते तथैव च ..
बह्व्योऽपि नायिका यत्र तासामपि तथा भवेत् .. 18 ..
text_mt: Likewise, the prosperity of the hero should be brought about at the end of the drama; / where there are many heroines, the same should also happen for them.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃvidhā saśṛṅgārā caturaṅkāḥ tu nāṭikā ..
kṛtaṃ prakaraṇaṃ tadvatsvayamutpādya vastunā .. 19 ..
meaning:
एवंविधा सशृङ्गारा चतुरङ्काः तु नाटिका ..
कृतं प्रकरणं तद्वत्स्वयमुत्पाद्य वस्तुना .. 19 ..
text_mt: A nāṭikā of this kind has four acts and is accompanied by the erotic sentiment. / Likewise, a prakaraṇa is composed with its plot invented by the poet himself.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇo nāyakastatra vaṇikca nṛpasattama ..
evaṃ prakaraṇī kāryā caturaṅkāpi sā bhavet .. 3.17.20 ..
meaning:
ब्राह्मणो नायकस्तत्र वणिक्च नृपसत्तम ..
एवं प्रकरणी कार्या चतुरङ्कापि सा भवेत् .. 3.17.20 ..
text_mt: A brahmin or a merchant is the hero in that, O best of kings. / In this way a prakaraṇī should be made, and it too should have four acts.

sanskrit_iast:
itihāsānubandho vā svayamutpādya vā kṛtaḥ ..
bhāratīkaruṇaprāyo nivṛttaṃ samanantaram .. 21 ..
meaning:
इतिहासानुबन्धो वा स्वयमुत्पाद्य वा कृतः ..
भारतीकरुणप्रायो निवृत्तं समनन्तरम् .. 21 ..
text_mt: Whether connected to traditional history or invented by the author himself, / consisting predominantly of the verbal style and pathos, whose action ceases immediately thereafter,

sanskrit_iast:
catuṣṭayāṅkaḥ kartavyo divyanāyakavartitaḥ ..
itihāsānusāreṇa prāṇaścaikāhikaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 22 ..
meaning:
चतुष्टयाङ्कः कर्तव्यो दिव्यनायकवर्तितः ..
इतिहासानुसारेण प्राणश्चैकाहिकः स्मृतः .. 22 ..
text_mt: it should be made in four acts, enacted by a divine hero. / Based on traditional history, its duration is taught to be limited to a single day.

sanskrit_iast:
ekāṃko yuddhabahulasvātmaśaṃsāparastathā ..
ākāśakathanairyuktastvekapātrakṛtakriyaḥ .. 23 ..
meaning:
एकांको युद्धबहुलस्वात्मशंसापरस्तथा ..
आकाशकथनैर्युक्तस्त्वेकपात्रकृतक्रियः .. 23 ..
text_mt: Consisting of a single act, full of fighting, devoted to self-praise, / joined with aerial discourses, its action performed by a single character—

sanskrit_iast:
proktaḥ samavatārākhyastridaśāsuranāyakaḥ ..
triśṛṅgārastrikapaṭastathā dvādaśanāyakaḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
प्रोक्तः समवताराख्यस्त्रिदशासुरनायकः ..
त्रिशृङ्गारस्त्रिकपटस्तथा द्वादशनायकः .. 24 ..
text_mt: [this] is called the samavakāra, having gods and demons as its heroes, / having three varieties of the erotic sentiment, three deceptions, and twelve heroes.

sanskrit_iast:
īhāmṛgo'tha bahvaṅkastathā gandharvanāyakaḥ ..
śṛṅgārabahulaḥ kāryo'tṛpta yonirasāśrayaḥ .. 25 ..
meaning:
ईहामृगोऽथ बह्वङ्कस्तथा गन्धर्वनायकः ..
शृङ्गारबहुलः कार्योऽतृप्त योनिरसाश्रयः .. 25 ..
text_mt: Then the īhāmṛga has many acts and has a gandharva as its hero; / it should be filled with the erotic sentiment, resting on an unsatisfied, divine source of aesthetic experience.

sanskrit_iast:
aikāhiko dṛptaraso vyāyogaścaikanāyakaḥ ..
vīthī trayodaśāṅkā syāttathā nāyakavarjitā ..26 ..
meaning:
ऐकाहिको दृप्तरसो व्यायोगश्चैकनायकः ..
वीथी त्रयोदशाङ्का स्यात्तथा नायकवर्जिता ..26 ..
text_mt: The vyāyoga lasts a single day, has an arrogant aesthetic tone, and has a single hero; / the vīthī should have thirteen divisions and is destitute of a [major] hero.

sanskrit_iast:
ḍimākhyaśca tathā prokto rasastu suranāyakaḥ ..
tathā raudrarasaprāyaḥ prakhyastaviṣayānvitaḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
डिमाख्यश्च तथा प्रोक्तो रसस्तु सुरनायकः ..
तथा रौद्ररसप्रायः प्रख्यस्तविषयान्वितः .. 27 ..
text_mt: And that which is called a ḍima is declared to have gods as its heroes; / likewise, it is predominantly filled with the furious sentiment and is endowed with an illustrious subject matter.

sanskrit_iast:
ekāṅko hāsyabahulastathaivodāttanāyakaḥ ..
kāryaḥ prahasanākhyastu veśyāviṭasamanvitaḥ .. 28 ..
meaning:
एकाङ्को हास्यबहुलस्तथैवोदात्तनायकः ..
कार्यः प्रहसनाख्यस्तु वेश्याविटसमन्वितः .. 28 ..
text_mt: Consisting of a single act, abundant in comedy, and with an exalted hero— / that drama called prahasana should be made, joined with courtesans and rogues.

sanskrit_iast:
sūtradhārasya vākyena kāvyavastunibandhanam ..
sarvaṃ prakāśayedādau sarveṣveteṣu vastu yat .. 29 ..
meaning:
सूत्रधारस्य वाक्येन काव्यवस्तुनिबन्धनम् ..
सर्वं प्रकाशयेदादौ सर्वेष्वेतेषु वस्तु यत् .. 29 ..
text_mt: Through the words of the stage-manager, the composition of the poetic plot— / he should illuminate at the beginning whatever entire plot exists in all of these.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃskataṃ nāyakavaco liṅgiśrotriyabhūbhujām ..
dvijanmanāṃ surāṇāṃ ca daityagandharvabhoginām .. 3.17.30 ..
meaning:
संस्कतं नायकवचो लिङ्गिश्रोत्रियभूभुजाम् ..
द्विजन्मनां सुराणां च दैत्यगन्धर्वभोगिनाम् .. 3.17.30 ..
text_mt: Sanskrit is the speech of heroes, ascetics, Vedic scholars, and kings, / of twice-born men, of gods, and of serpent-demons and gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast:
nāyikādevarāmāṇāṃ vyājaliṅgavatāṃ tathā ..
vidūṣakāṇāṃ ca bhavetprākṛtaṃ vacanaṃ nṛpa .. 31 ..
meaning:
नायिकादेवरामाणां व्याजलिङ्गवतां तथा ..
विदूषकाणां च भवेत्प्राकृतं वचनं नृप .. 31 ..
text_mt: The speech of heroines, of younger brothers-in-law, and of women, / as well as of hypocritical ascetics and jesters, should be Prakrit, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
bālastrīnīcaṣaṇḍānāṃ ye cānye nānukīrtitāḥ ..
teṣāṃ vākyamapabhraṣṭaṃ tacca jñātvā prayojayet .. 32 ..
meaning:
बालस्त्रीनीचषण्डानां ये चान्ये नानुकीर्तिताः ..
तेषां वाक्यमपभ्रष्टं तच्च ज्ञात्वा प्रयोजयेत् .. 32 ..
text_mt: Of children, women, the low-born, eunuchs, and whoever else have not been mentioned— / their speech is corrupt [vernacular]; knowing that, one should employ it.

sanskrit_iast:
svayamutpāditānāṃ me nānātvaṃ śṛṇu lakṣaṇam ..
śarma varmadhanānyante varṇānāṃ dāsavattathā .. 33 ..
meaning:
स्वयमुत्पादितानां मे नानात्वं शृणु लक्षणम् ..
शर्म वर्मधनान्यन्ते वर्णानां दासवत्तथा .. 33 ..
text_mt: Listen from me to the distinctive characteristics of names invented by oneself: / [the names] of the castes should end in -śarman, -varman, -dhana, and like -dāsa.

sanskrit_iast:
rājñāṃ vikramasaṃyuktamamātyānāṃ tathā bhavet ..
strīṇāṃ sukhodyamakrūraṃ nāyikānāṃ manoharam .. 34 ..
meaning:
राज्ञां विक्रमसंयुक्तममात्यानां तथा भवेत् ..
स्त्रीणां सुखोद्यमक्रूरं नायिकानां मनोहरम् .. 34 ..
text_mt: [The names] of kings should be connected with valor; those of ministers should be likewise. / For women, they should be easy to pronounce and unharsh; for heroines, delightful.

sanskrit_iast:
rājñīparijanastrīṇāṃ kalākauśalasaṃyutam ..
rājñaḥ parijanastrīṇāṃ vijayottaramiṣyate .. 35 ..
meaning:
राज्ञीपरिजनस्त्रीणां कलाकौशलसंयुतम् ..
राज्ञः परिजनस्त्रीणां विजयोत्तरमिष्यते .. 35 ..
text_mt: For the female attendants of the queen, they should be connected with skill in arts; / for the female attendants of the king, [a name] ending in victory is desired.

sanskrit_iast:
sāṃvatsarāṇāṃ māṅgalyaṃ śāntiprāyaṃ purodhasām ..
śūraprāyamamātyānāmāyupyaṃ bhiṣajāmapi .. 36 ..
meaning:
सांवत्सराणां माङ्गल्यं शान्तिप्रायं पुरोधसाम् ..
शूरप्रायममात्यानामायुप्यं भिषजामपि .. 36 ..
text_mt: For astrologers, [a name] denoting auspiciousness; for royal priests, mostly denoting peace; / for ministers, mostly denoting heroism; and for physicians, denoting longevity.

sanskrit_iast:
viṭānāṃ bhūṣaṇaprāyaṃ dāsīnāṃ kusumādikam ..
ṛṣigotradharau kāryau kañcukīyavidūṣakau .. 37 ..
meaning:
विटानां भूषणप्रायं दासीनां कुसुमादिकम् ..
ऋषिगोत्रधरौ कार्यौ कञ्चुकीयविदूषकौ .. 37 ..
text_mt: For gallants, mostly denoting ornaments; for female servants, flowers and the like. / The chamberlain and the jester should be made to bear the gotra of a sage.

sanskrit_iast:
dattā mitrā tathā senā vaiśyā nāma tato bhavet ..
adhikārānurūpāṇi tathā caivādhikāriṇām .. 38 ..
meaning:
दत्ता मित्रा तथा सेना वैश्या नाम ततो भवेत् ..
अधिकारानुरूपाणि तथा चैवाधिकारिणाम् .. 38 ..
text_mt: -dattā, -mitrā, and likewise -senā may then be the name of a vaiśya woman. / And [the names] of officials should be in accordance with their office.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yena vācyastu yo yathā ..
deveti rājā vaktavyo bhṛtyaiḥ prakṛtibhistathā .. 39 ..
meaning:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन वाच्यस्तु यो यथा ..
देवेति राजा वक्तव्यो भृत्यैः प्रकृतिभिस्तथा .. 39 ..
text_mt: Hereafter I shall declare by whom who should be addressed and in what manner: / A king should be addressed as 'Lord' by servants and by subjects;

sanskrit_iast:
rājeti viprairvaktavyo ṛṣibhirnāmagotrataḥ ..
apatyapratyayāddevairvayasyeti samo janaḥ .. 3.17.40 ..
meaning:
राजेति विप्रैर्वक्तव्यो ऋषिभिर्नामगोत्रतः ..
अपत्यप्रत्ययाद्देवैर्वयस्येति समो जनः .. 3.17.40 ..
text_mt: as 'King' by brahmins; by sages by name and gotra; / by gods with reference to his lineage; and an equal person with 'Friend'.

sanskrit_iast:
vidūṣako'pi vaktavyo vayasya iti nāyakaiḥ ..
āyuṣmāniti sūtena rathī vācyastathā bhavet ..41 ..
meaning:
विदूषकोऽपि वक्तव्यो वयस्य इति नायकैः ..
आयुष्मानिति सूतेन रथी वाच्यस्तथा भवेत् ..41 ..
text_mt: The jester also should be addressed as 'Friend' by heroes. / The warrior in the chariot should be addressed as 'Long-lived one' by the charioteer.

sanskrit_iast:
bhagavanniti vaktavyā ṛṣayo guravaḥ surāḥ ..
putra vatseti śiṣyasya tathā vā nāmagotrataḥ .. 42 ..
meaning:
भगवन्निति वक्तव्या ऋषयो गुरवः सुराः ..
पुत्र वत्सेति शिष्यस्य तथा वा नामगोत्रतः .. 42 ..
text_mt: Sages, teachers, and gods should be addressed as 'Reverend Sir'. / A student should be addressed as 'Son', 'Child', or by name and gotra.

sanskrit_iast:
āryaputreti vaktavyaḥ striyā bhartā narādhipa ..
nāmnā bhāryā tu vaktavyā rājñī devīti nāyikā .. 43 ..
meaning:
आर्यपुत्रेति वक्तव्यः स्त्रिया भर्ता नराधिप ..
नाम्ना भार्या तु वक्तव्या राज्ञी देवीति नायिका .. 43 ..
text_mt: A husband should be addressed by his wife as 'Son of an Aryan', O ruler of men. / A wife, however, should be addressed by name; a queen and a heroine as 'My Lady'.

sanskrit_iast:
pitā tātastathā vācyo mātuścaivāryakaḥ pitā ..
yuvarājaḥ kumāraḥ syānmānyo bhāvaḥ samīritaḥ .. 44 ..
meaning:
पिता तातस्तथा वाच्यो मातुश्चैवार्यकः पिता ..
युवराजः कुमारः स्यान्मान्यो भावः समीरितः .. 44 ..
text_mt: A father should be addressed as 'Dear Father', and a mother's father as 'Respected Elder'. / A crown prince should be 'Prince'; an honorable man is addressed as 'Noble Sir'.

sanskrit_iast:
mānyamānastathā bhāmo bhartṛdāraḥ kumārakaḥ ..
haleti tu samānā strī vaktavyā samayā tathā .. 45 ..
meaning:
मान्यमानस्तथा भामो भर्तृदारः कुमारकः ..
हलेति तु समाना स्त्री वक्तव्या समया तथा .. 45 ..
text_mt: An esteemed person is likewise 'Noble Sir', and a master's son is 'Prince'. / An equal woman should be addressed by an equal as 'Friend' (halā).

sanskrit_iast:
hañjetyāmantrayennārī haṇḍe parijane svake ..
svaseti bhaginī vācyā liṅgasthā vratinī tathā .. 46 ..
meaning:
हञ्जेत्यामन्त्रयेन्नारी हण्डे परिजने स्वके ..
स्वसेति भगिनी वाच्या लिङ्गस्था व्रतिनी तथा .. 46 ..
text_mt: One should address a [maid]servant as 'hañje', and one's own servant girl as 'haṇḍe'. / A sister should be addressed as 'Sister', and an ascetic woman as 'Lady of Vows'.

sanskrit_iast:
āryeti brāhmaṇī vācyā śeṣā liṅgārthatastathā ..
antaḥpuracaro yastu strībhogaparivarjitaḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
आर्येति ब्राह्मणी वाच्या शेषा लिङ्गार्थतस्तथा ..
अन्तःपुरचरो यस्तु स्त्रीभोगपरिवर्जितः .. 47 ..
text_mt: A brahmin woman should be addressed as 'Noble Lady', and others according to the sense of their sectarian attire. / But he who walks within the inner apartments, devoid of the enjoyment of women,

sanskrit_iast:
sa tu varṣadharo jñeyastadadhyakṣastu kañcukiḥ ..
brāhmaṇaḥ sa bhaved vṛddho mānyaśca vasudhādhipaiḥ .. 48 ..
meaning:
स तु वर्षधरो ज्ञेयस्तदध्यक्षस्तु कञ्चुकिः ..
ब्राह्मणः स भवेद् वृद्धो मान्यश्च वसुधाधिपैः .. 48 ..
text_mt: he should be known as an eunuch, and their supervisor is the chamberlain; / he should be an elderly brahmin and honored by rulers of the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
vidūṣako brāhmaṇaḥ syānnāyakasya rahasyavit ..
naṭaḥ pradhānaḥ sa bhavetsūtradhāro narādhipa .. 49 ..
meaning:
विदूषको ब्राह्मणः स्यान्नायकस्य रहस्यवित् ..
नटः प्रधानः स भवेत्सूत्रधारो नराधिप .. 49 ..
text_mt: The jester should be a brahmin who knows the secrets of the hero. / The foremost actor is the stage-manager, O ruler of men.

sanskrit_iast:
jñeyā bījasamutpattirmukhaṃ nānā rasodbhavaḥ ..
mukhotthabījodghaṭanaṃ tathā pratimukhaṃ smṛtam .. 3.17.50 ..
meaning:
ज्ञेया बीजसमुत्पत्तिर्मुखं नाना रसोद्भवः ..
मुखोत्थबीजोद्घटनं तथा प्रतिमुखं स्मृतम् .. 3.17.50 ..
text_mt: The origin of the seed is to be known as the opening (mukha), from which various sentiments arise. / The unfolding of the seed that arose in the opening is taught as the progression (pratimukha).

sanskrit_iast:
prāpyāprātiyuto garbhastasyaivodbhedasaṃjñitaḥ ..
tadevodbhinnabījārtho visargo vyasanānvitaḥ .. 51 ..
meaning:
प्राप्याप्रातियुतो गर्भस्तस्यैवोद्भेदसंज्ञितः ..
तदेवोद्भिन्नबीजार्थो विसर्गो व्यसनान्वितः .. 51 ..
text_mt: Joined with attainment and non-attainment, the development (garbha) is designated as its burgeoning. / The pause (avamarśa/visarga) is connected with calamity, when the purpose of the sprouted seed [is endangered].

sanskrit_iast:
mukhādīnāṃ nirvahaṇaṃ tathā nirvahataṃ bhavet ..
nāṭake saprakaraṇe kartavyāḥ pātrasandhayaḥ .. 52 ..
meaning:
मुखादीनां निर्वहणं तथा निर्वहतं भवेत् ..
नाटके सप्रकरणे कर्तव्याः पात्रसन्धयः .. 52 ..
text_mt: The conclusion (nirvahaṇa) of the opening and the other [junctures] is the denouement. / In a nāṭaka along with a prakaraṇa, the dramatic junctures must be constructed with suitable characters.

sanskrit_iast:
ḍime samavakāre ca visargaṃ naiva kārayet ..
vyāyogehāmṛgau kāryo tathā garbhavivarjitau .. 53 ..
meaning:
डिमे समवकारे च विसर्गं नैव कारयेत् ..
व्यायोगेहामृगौ कार्यो तथा गर्भविवर्जितौ .. 53 ..
text_mt: In a ḍima and a samavakāra, one should never employ the pause. / The vyāyoga and īhāmṛga should be constructed without the development.

sanskrit_iast:
utsṛṣṭāṅka prahasanaṃ vīthī bhāṇakameva ca ..
eteṣāṃ nāvakartavyaṃ tathā pratimukhaṃ nṛpa .. 54 ..
meaning:
उत्सृष्टाङ्क प्रहसनं वीथी भाणकमेव च ..
एतेषां नावकर्तव्यं तथा प्रतिमुखं नृप .. 54 ..
text_mt: In the utsṛṣṭikāṅka, the prahasana, the vīthī, and the bhāṇa, / the progression (pratimukha) should not be made for these, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
audāryasatpathaṃ śauryaṃ nāyakastu na saṃtyajet ..
nāyikāpi tathā rājanyajedvā pratināyakaḥ .. 55 ..
meaning:
औदार्यसत्पथं शौर्यं नायकस्तु न संत्यजेत् ..
नायिकापि तथा राजन्यजेद्वा प्रतिनायकः .. 55 ..
text_mt: The hero must not abandon nobility, the virtuous path, or heroism; / nor should the heroine, O king, or the antagonist may abandon them.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi nāyikāṣṭakalakṣaṇam ..
nijāparādhātsvagṛhe vāsasajjā tu nāyikā .. 56 ..
meaning:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि नायिकाष्टकलक्षणम् ..
निजापराधात्स्वगृहे वाससज्जा तु नायिका .. 56 ..
text_mt: Hereafter I shall state the definitions of the eight types of heroine: / She who is dressed and waiting in her own house owing to her own fault is the vāsakasajjā heroine;

sanskrit_iast:
virahotkaṇṭhitā saiva yā tvanāgatanāyikā ..
svādhīna bhartṛkā proktā yā syātsvādhīnabhartṛkā .. 57 ..
meaning:
विरहोत्कण्ठिता सैव या त्वनागतनायिका ..
स्वाधीन भर्तृका प्रोक्ता या स्यात्स्वाधीनभर्तृका .. 57 ..
text_mt: she whose hero has not arrived is the virahotkaṇṭhitā; / she who has her husband under her control is proclaimed the svādhīnabhartṛkā;

sanskrit_iast:
kalahāntaritā proktā kalahāhatanāyakā ..
khaṇḍitā yā ca nakharairyutameti pragopatim .. 58 ..
meaning:
कलहान्तरिता प्रोक्ता कलहाहतनायका ..
खण्डिता या च नखरैर्युतमेति प्रगोपतिम् .. 58 ..
text_mt: she whose hero is repulsed in a quarrel is called the kalahāntaritā; / she who meets her lord while he is marked with nail-scratches is the khaṇḍitā;

sanskrit_iast:
vipralabdhā tu sā jñeyā saṃkete kāntavarjitā ..
pravāsagatakāntā tu tathā proṣitabhartṛkā .. 59 ..
meaning:
विप्रलब्धा तु सा ज्ञेया संकेते कान्तवर्जिता ..
प्रवासगतकान्ता तु तथा प्रोषितभर्तृका .. 59 ..
text_mt: she who is without her beloved at the rendezvous is to be known as the vipralabdhā; / and she whose beloved has gone on a journey is the proṣitabhartṛkā.

sanskrit_iast:
etāsāmucitākāralīlābhirbandhanaṃ ghanam ..
nāṭakādiṣu rūpeṣu kartavyaṃ dvādaśasvapi .. 3.17.60 ..
meaning:
एतासामुचिताकारलीलाभिर्बन्धनं घनम् ..
नाटकादिषु रूपेषु कर्तव्यं द्वादशस्वपि .. 3.17.60 ..
text_mt: A dense composition with suitable expressions and graceful movements of these [heroines] / should be made in all twelve types of dramatic forms, beginning with the nāṭaka.

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṅgārahāsyakaruṇavīraraudrabhayānakāḥ ..
bībhatsādbhutaśāntākhyā nava nāṭyarasāḥ smṛtāḥ ..61..
meaning:
शृङ्गारहास्यकरुणवीररौद्रभयानकाः ..
बीभत्साद्भुतशान्ताख्या नव नाट्यरसाः स्मृताः ..61..
text_mt: The erotic, the comic, the pathetic, the heroic, the furious, the terrifying, / the loathsome, the marvelous, and that called the peaceful are taught as the nine dramatic sentiments.

sanskrit_iast:
bandho rasānugaḥ kāryaḥ sarveṣveteṣu yatnataḥ ..
rasapradhānamevaitatsarvanāṭyaṃ narādhipaḥ .. 62 ..
meaning:
बन्धो रसानुगः कार्यः सर्वेष्वेतेषु यत्नतः ..
रसप्रधानमेवैतत्सर्वनाट्यं नराधिपः .. 62 ..
text_mt: The composition in all of these should be carefully made to follow the sentiments. / All dramatic performance is primarily based on sentiment, O ruler of men.

sanskrit_iast:
ete kalākauśalaśīlayuktāḥ kāryāstathā loka vidhānayuktāḥ ..
dharmārvakāmādyupadeśagāśca hitāya lokasya narendracandra .. 63 ..
meaning:
एते कलाकौशलशीलयुक्ताः कार्यास्तथा लोक विधानयुक्ताः ..
धर्मार्वकामाद्युपदेशगाश्च हिताय लोकस्य नरेन्द्रचन्द्र .. 63 ..
text_mt: Endowed with skill in arts and good character, and endowed with the ways of worldly conduct, / these should convey instructions on dharma, wealth, pleasure, and the rest, for the welfare of the world, O moon among kings.

sanskrit_iast:
3.18
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
atha gītalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati tasya trīṇi sthānāni uraḥ kaṇṭhaḥ śiraśca, tebhyo mandramadhyatārotpattiḥ .
trayo grāmāḥ . ṣaḍjamadhyamagāndhārāḥ .
saptasvarā . ṣaḍjarṣabha gāndhāramadhyamapañcamaniṣādadhaivatāḥ
ekaviṃśatimūrcchanāḥ sapta sapta pratigrāmāśritāḥ .
tadyathāsāṃ nāmāni sauvīrī hāriṇāśvā kalopanatā śuddhamadhyamā mārgī pauravī ṛṣyakā ceti ..

3.18
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now comes the definition of vocal music: it has three registers: the chest, the throat, and the head; from these arises the low, middle, and high.
There are three scales: the ṣaḍja, madhyama, and gāndhāra.
There are seven notes: ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, madhyama, pañcama, niṣāda, and dhaivata.
There are twenty-one modal shifts, seven belonging to each scale.
Their names are as follows: Sauvīrī, Hāriṇāśvā, Kalopanatā, Śuddhamadhyamā, Mārgī, Pauravī, and Ṛṣyakā;
these seven belong to the madhyama scale and are called Uttarā.
Prāñcinī, Uttarāyatā, Śuddhaṣaḍjā, Matsarīkṛtā, Aśvakrāntā, and Udgatā—these seven belong to the ṣaḍja scale.
Ālāpī, Kuntimā, Śraddhā, Uttarā, Ṣaḍjā, Pañcāyatā [...] these seven belong to the gāndhāra scale.
Now, the forty-nine melodic patterns: Āgniṣṭomika, Atyagniṣṭomika, Pauṇḍarīka, Āśvamedhika, Rājasūyika, Bahusuvarṇika, Gosavika, Mahāvratika, Brahmatāna, Prājāpatya, Nagāśraya, Yajñāśraya, Godānika, Hayakrānta, Ajakrānta, Viṣṇukrānta, Araṇya, Mattakokila, and Ujjīvika—these twenty belong to the madhyama scale.
Prasvāpana, Paiśāca, Jīvana, Sāvitra, Ardhasāvitra, Sarvatobhadra, Suvarṇa, Viṣṇu, Jiṣṇu, Viṣṇuvara, Śārada, Vijaya, Haṃsa, and Jyeṣṭha—these fourteen belong to the ṣaḍja scale.
Tumburupriya, Mahālakṣmaṇa, Gandharvānumata, Alambusapriya, Nāradapriya, Bhīmasenapriya, Vitāna, Mātaṅga, Bhārgavapriya, Abhirāma, Saṃśrāvya, Kinnarapriya, Puṇya, Manohara, and Kalyāṇakara—these fifteen belong to the gāndhāra scale.
This is fourfold through the application of notes, words, tempo, and attentiveness.
In the modal shifts, at the beginning, middle, and end, there are three modes designated as sonant, consonant, and final consonant.
And the previously mentioned nine aesthetic sentiments: there, in the comic and the erotic, are the madhyama and pañcama notes;
in the heroic, furious, and marvellous, the ṣaḍja and pañcama;
in the pathetic, the niṣāda and gāndhāra;
in the odious and terrible, the dhaivata;
in the peaceful, the madhyama.
Likewise, the tempos: in the comic and the erotic, the moderate tempo;
in the odious and terrible, the slow tempo;
in the heroic, furious, and marvellous, the fast tempo.
The clean performance of notes in worship in the dramas conforms to the context; they occur under the designation of passionate expression.
And here are verses:
The initial note, the predominant note, the high and the low registers, the final note, and the penultimate note,
the paucity and the abundance, as well as the hexatonic and pentatonic forms—
thus indeed the melodic types should be known by the wise to have ten characteristics.
And there are four melodic ornaments, O lord of the earth:
that which begins clearly, that which ends clearly, that which begins and ends clearly,
and that which is clear in the middle; thus should one specify in order.
The Aparāntaka, the Ullopya, the Mandraka, and the Makarī,
the Uveṇaka, the Sarobindu, and the Uttama are the song forms.
The Ṛg-song, the Gāthā, the Pāṇikā, the Brahmagītikā arranged by Dakṣa—
this is vocal music, and its practice, on account of its purpose, is called pure.
It has been declared by me in brief for the sake of worshipping the gods.
If one who knows vocal music does not attain the supreme state through song,
he becomes an attendant of the god and rejoices with him.

3.19
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now the rule for musical instruments:
Musical instruments are fourfold: stringed, wind, solid, and covered with hide.
The stringed is the vīṇā and the like; the wind is the flute and the like; the solid is the cymbals and the like; the covered with hide is the drum and the like. There, the notes of the human throat and of the vīṇā are equal.
Likewise the flute; however, as the ascent and descent are for the human voice, so they are the opposite for flutes of reed. Rhythm is determined by time.
A measure is the time of uttering five short syllables; there are three modes of execution:
the varied, the intermediate, and the southern, which are twofold.
In the varied, a measure is one time-unit; in the intermediate, four time-units; in the southern, eight time-units.
In the southern, of eight time-units, the limbs are the silent beat, the throwing out, the entry, the clapping beat, and the striking down.
The collection of time-units is connected.
In the even time-measure, the uneven time-measure ending with a protracted note, the five-beat measure is the empty beat, situated according to the syllables.
There, the tempos are fast, moderate, and slow.
Rhythm is possessed of tempo.
The section is twofold: the collective and the divided.
Now, the covered instrument: there, like the puṣkara drum, it is endowed with resonance and pathos.
There, the sixteen syllables are: ka, kha, ga, gha, ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ṇa, ta, tha, da, dha, ya, ra, la, va. There, the syllables beginning with ka, ṭa, ra, tha, and ga are on the right face; gha, dha, and ma on the left; ga and da on the top; ṭa, ṇa, la, and ha on the encompassing face; a, ā, i, u, e, o, ai, and au, appropriately; the combination of kha, ga, and dha is with the letter r;
of ka, ha, bha, and da, with ṇa, la, tha, and va.
By the stroke of the flat hand, by the movement of the fingers on the upper and left sides, by the stroke of the flat hand with the index finger, likewise is the combination of the ḍa-la syllables: with the level hand, the half-hand, the non-elongated hand, the single hand, struck with the two hands and the index finger; struck with the flat hand for the auxiliary syllables gha, tha, ga, ḍa, and ra; on the hand-and-a-half, the syllables ka and tha;
on the hand-and-a-half, ṭha, ṇa, la, and ha; struck with the flat hand and index finger of both hands. The tuning paths are Addhita, Vitasta, Ālipta, and Gomukhī: Addhita is in the erotic and comic sentiments;
in the heroic, furious, and marvellous, Vitasta; in the pathetic and peaceful, Ālipta;
in the odious and terrible, Gomukha; the dardura and paṇava drums follow the mṛdaṅga drum.
And here are verses:
Facing the stage in alignment with the door of the tiring-room,
the drums should be behind them, and likewise the plastering.
To the south of that, the dardura and paṇava are to be known.
Facing north should be the singer, and thus to his south,
to his left the clay-drummer, and to his right two flute players;
the positioning of the singers is directly facing the main singer.

Dramatic performance is stated by those learned in theatre to be the imitation of another, O king. / Dance serves as its embellishment, enhancing its beauty.
Dance is declared to be of two kinds, always based on dramatic performance and lyrical dance. / Each of these two kinds is again twofold, O ruler of men:
the internal and the external; the external is devoid of rules, / while the internal possesses rules and is auspicious through its proper execution.
Lyrical dance may be performed freely, either in a playhouse or outside. / Dramatic performance should be held only in a playhouse; the playhouse is of two kinds:
rectangular and square, measured at thirty-two cubits. / The square should not be made [longer], while the rectangular is twice as long.
It should not be made deficient or excessive, as it bestows visible and invisible auspicious results. / In a deficient [theatre] there is crowding, and in one too spacious, the drama and song
fail to achieve distinct clarity; therefore, one should avoid both of those. / At the very beginning, worship of the gods must be performed,

as well as worship of the Jarjara staff and worship of the site-deity. / Having done this, the dramatic performance is then undertaken, preceded by the preliminary benediction.
Then follows the entrance of each character with the tossing aside of the curtain. / Entrances and exits should be executed having indicated the dramatic business.
An offering of folded hands with flowers must be made, and at the end of the drama, worship of the site. / Devoted to the recitation and song, the movement across the stage corresponds to the character.
It consists of four kalās for heroes, three kalās for middling characters, / and two kalās for low characters in the intermediate action of a king.
One [kalā] more or less should be applied for all according to the demands of the dramatic action. / Gods are to be known as heroic and fierce; Dānavas and others are fierce;
kings are firm and playful; their attendants are firm; / sages are tranquil and firm; their disciples are tranquil;
brahmins are firm and noble; merchants are regarded as noble. / Such varieties are explained through the combination of these very traits.
Costume and makeup, internal psychological states, vocal expression, and bodily movement— / fourfold is the representation to be employed in dramatic action.

Costume and makeup is said to be the altered dress consisting of headdresses, masks, and the like. / For the firm and fierce, the dress should not be exceedingly ostentatious;
it should be fierce for the fierce, and for kings it is desired to be charming. / The dress of the antagonist should likewise be made fierce.
For others, the dress should be appropriate, conforming to their region and profession. / Horses and the like should be constructed to resemble [real ones] using hide, wood, and other materials.
Next, I shall explain to you the representation through internal psychological states: / shedding of tears, horripilation, sweating, trembling,
and likewise changes of complexion constitute the representation through internal states. / Vocal representation is declared to be through speech; bodily representation I shall describe in what follows.
Dramatic dance should always be performed extensively in scenes of joy; / in scenes of sorrow it should not be performed, or only a little should be executed thereafter.
The recaka movement is stated to be fourfold, based on the waist, feet, shanks, and [hands]. / The cārī movement is regarded as twofold: the cārī and the other, the mahācārī.
The cārī consists of delicate limbs, speech, and gestures, O descendant of Yadu; / enhanced by these [energetic movements], it is to be recognized as the mahācārī, O lord of men.

asarpitatala, and siṃhavikrīḍita, / vṛṣabhakrīḍita, and gaṅgāvataraṇa.
One hundred and eight karaṇas have thus been proclaimed. / Dramatic practice is said to be of two kinds: delicate and forceful.
The elevated consists mostly of men, whereas the delicate consists mostly of women. / The piṇḍī-formation assumes the shape of the emblem of a deity, O king.
Four styles of dramatic performance are proclaimed: bhāratī, sāttvatī, / kauśikī, and ārabhaṭī. The bhāratī style has speech as its principal element;
likewise, O king, sāttvatī should be understood as abounding in the heroic sentiment, / and ārabhaṭī is always characterised by furious conduct;
kauśikī abounds in the erotic and comic sentiments. / Then there are the regional modes here: āvantī, dākṣiṇātyā, māgadhī,
pañcālī, and madhyamā; thus regional mode is fourfold. / The imitation of dress and speech, as well as the adoption of conduct,
is known as local usage, and these [usages] depend upon the dramatic styles. / Practice is considered two-fold, based on theatrical convention and worldly convention.

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Svastha, mandālasa, ākrānta, prasthālasa, and also / viṣkambhita, tatkaṭuka, muktajānu, and sama,
jānugata, and vimukta are the postures in sitting. / The two feet crossed and bent, the chest slightly raised,
the two hands placed comfortably on the waist and thighs—this is comfortable sitting. / One foot is stretched out, and the other rests upon the seat,
and the side of the body should be bent: that is the mandālasa posture. / In anxiety, longing, dejection, and separation,
as well as in despair, this posture should always be assigned by performers. / The two hands resting upon the chin, the head inclined towards the upper arm,
and all dramatic acting are to be known as showing an exhausted hero. / For one restrained by a powerful enemy, or broken by a foe,

3.23 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Vaiṣṇava, samapāda, vaiśākha, and maṇḍala, / as well as pratyālīḍha and ālīḍha: these are the six standing postures for men.
One foot in its natural [position], the other placed obliquely at three aṅgulas, / and with the shank slightly curved: this is called the vaiṣṇava posture.
In this posture, natural conversation is to be represented. / The samapāda is to be known by the feet being even, at a distance of one tāla apart,
endowed with the elegance of their respective nature, [appropriate for] deities such as Rudra and Brahmā. / In this posture, the gathering of brahmins is to be represented,
as well as [the movements] of troops and birds, and the eagerness of the bridegroom; / it is the proper posture for those standing on chariots and on celestial vehicles;
one should employ this posture for those who stand before a liṅga or observe vows. / When the distance between the two feet is two and a half tālas,

With this posture the wise should represent the riding of horses, / exercise, departure, and the stringing of a bow.
Next is the maṇḍala [posture], with a distance of three tālas [between the feet], / where the waist is on a level with the knees, and the feet are placed obliquely.
Striking with a bow or a thunderbolt should be performed in the maṇḍala [posture], / as well as the riding of elephants and the lifting movement in dance.
First, one should stretch out the right foot by five tālas; / that is the posture named ālīḍha, and Rudrakālī is its presiding deity.

संज्ञोपदेशपृच्छासु स्वभावाभाषणे भवेत् ..

विषादे विस्मये चैव प्रतिषेधे तदिष्यते ..
विधुतं नामतः प्रोक्तं तथा पार्श्वविकम्पनैः .. 4 ..
शीतग्रस्ते ज्वरार्ते च मत्ते च त्वरिते भवेत् ..
मण्डलारम्भणे चैव भवेत्तु परिगर्हितम् .. 5..
साधने विस्मये हर्षे लीलायां च तदिष्यते ..
सकृदुद्वाहितं चोर्ध्वं तदुद्वाहितमिष्यते ..6..

sanskrit_iast:
ucchrāye darśane garve tattathordhvanirīkṣaṇe ...
ākṣiptaṃ sakṛdeva syādavavratamadhogatam .. 7 ..
sandehālāpasaṃjñāsu tattathā vāhanādiṣu ..
kiñcitpārśvanatagrīvaṃ śiro vijñeyamañcitam .. 8 ..
mūrcchite vyathite caiva sañcite duḥkhite bhavet ..
( utkṣiptabāhuśikharaṃ tathācitaśirodharam .. 9 ..
nikuñcitaṃ ca tadgarve vilāse ca prayojayet ..
parāvṛttaparāvṛttaṃ kāryaṃ pṛṣṭhanirīkṣaṇe .. 3.24.10 ..)
utkṣiptaṃ cāpi vijñeyamunmukhāvasthitaṃ śiraḥ ..
āśu divyārthayoge ca kāryaṃ tacca prayoktṛbhiḥ .. 11 ..
adhomukhasthitaṃ cāpi budhāḥ prāhuradhogatam ..
lajjāyāṃ ca pramāṇe ca duḥkhe tacca prayojayet .. 12 ..
sarvato lolanāccaiva parilolitamucyate ..
vyādhite mūrcchite matte bhavettu parilolitam .. 13 ..
meaning:
उच्छ्राये दर्शने गर्वे तत्तथोर्ध्वनिरीक्षणे ...
आक्षिप्तं सकृदेव स्यादवव्रतमधोगतम् .. 7 ..
सन्देहालापसंज्ञासु तत्तथा वाहनादिषु ..
किञ्चित्पार्श्वनतग्रीवं शिरो विज्ञेयमञ्चितम् .. 8 ..
मूर्च्छिते व्यथिते चैव सञ्चिते दुःखिते भवेत् ..
( उत्क्षिप्तबाहुशिखरं तथाचितशिरोधरम् .. 9 ..
निकुञ्चितं च तद्गर्वे विलासे च प्रयोजयेत् ..
परावृत्तपरावृत्तं कार्यं पृष्ठनिरीक्षणे .. 3.24.10 ..)
उत्क्षिप्तं चापि विज्ञेयमुन्मुखावस्थितं शिरः ..
आशु दिव्यार्थयोगे च कार्यं तच्च प्रयोक्तृभिः .. 11 ..
अधोमुखस्थितं चापि बुधाः प्राहुरधोगतम् ..
लज्जायां च प्रमाणे च दुःखे तच्च प्रयोजयेत् .. 12 ..
सर्वतो लोलनाच्चैव परिलोलितमुच्यते ..
व्याधिते मूर्च्छिते मत्ते भवेत्तु परिलोलितम् .. 13 ..
text_mt:
it occurs in looking up at height, seeing, pride, and gazing upward. / When it is thrown down just once, bent downwards,
in doubt, conversation, signaling, and likewise on vehicles and the like; / with the neck slightly bent to one side, the head is to be known as añcita;
it occurs in one who is faint, distressed, collected, or sorrowful. / When the top of the arm is raised and the neck is curved,
And one should employ [the head called] nikuñcita in arrogance and playful grace; / parāvṛtta should be performed when looking behind.
And the head held facing upward should be known as utkṣipta; / that should be executed swiftly by performers in connection with celestial matters.
And the wise call [the head] held facing downward adhogata; / and one should employ that in shame, in measurement, and in grief.
And because of rolling in every direction, it is called parilolita; / parilolita should occur when sick, swooning, and intoxicated.

sanskrit_iast:
etattu śirasaḥ karma kathitaṃ te narādhipa ..
añcitaṃ recitaṃ muktaṃ vivṛtaṃ caturaṃ tathā .. 14 ..
prasāritaṃ tathā stabdhaṃ grīvākarmaṇi nirdiśet ..
añcitaṃ kiñcidekāṃśaṃ lolanādrecitaṃ tu tat .. 15 ..
recitaṃ bhramaṇānmuktaṃ vivṛtaṃ calitaṃ ca tat ..
madhuraṃ caturaṃ proktamāyataṃ syātprasāritam .. 16 ..
stabdhaṃ stabdhaṃ tathā proktaṃ śiraḥkarmānugāmi ca ..
añcitaṃ syādvilāsādau recitaṃ maṇḍalekṣaṇe .. 17 ..
muktaṃ mūrcchādiyogeṣu vivṛttaṃ lalitādiṣu ..
saumyabhāve tu caturaṃ dṛṣṭau kāryaṃ prasāritam .. 18 ..
stabdhaṃ śīte'tha vā vyādhāvavikāri svabhāvataḥ ..
vibuddhaṃ vinivṛttaṃ ca nirbhugnaṃ bhugnameva ca .. 19 ..
vivṛttaṃ ca tathaivarjukarmaṇyasya vinirdiśet ..
vyāvṛttaṃ syādvibuddhākhyaṃ nivṛttaṃ pihitaṃ bhavet ..3.24.20..
meaning:
एतत्तु शिरसः कर्म कथितं ते नराधिप ..
अञ्चितं रेचितं मुक्तं विवृतं चतुरं तथा .. 14 ..
प्रसारितं तथा स्तब्धं ग्रीवाकर्मणि निर्दिशेत् ..
अञ्चितं किञ्चिदेकांशं लोलनाद्रेचितं तु तत् .. 15 ..
रेचितं भ्रमणान्मुक्तं विवृतं चलितं च तत् ..
मधुरं चतुरं प्रोक्तमायतं स्यात्प्रसारितम् .. 16 ..
स्तब्धं स्तब्धं तथा प्रोक्तं शिरःकर्मानुगामि च ..
अञ्चितं स्याद्विलासादौ रेचितं मण्डलेक्षणे .. 17 ..
मुक्तं मूर्च्छादियोगेषु विवृत्तं ललितादिषु ..
सौम्यभावे तु चतुरं दृष्टौ कार्यं प्रसारितम् .. 18 ..
स्तब्धं शीतेऽथ वा व्याधावविकारि स्वभावतः ..
विबुद्धं विनिवृत्तं च निर्भुग्नं भुग्नमेव च .. 19 ..
विवृत्तं च तथैवर्जुकर्मण्यस्य विनिर्दिशेत् ..
व्यावृत्तं स्याद्विबुद्धाख्यं निवृत्तं पिहितं भवेत् ..3.24.20..

sanskrit_iast:
avāṅmukhamavābhugnaṃ nibhugnaṃ cordhvagaṃ tu tat ..
bhugnaṃ syādānataṃ kiñcinnivṛttaṃ vivṛtaṃ bhavet.. ..21..
ṛjusvabhāvasaṃsthaṃ ca tayoḥ karmāṇi cakṣate ..
viruddhavāraṇe kāryaṃ maivamityevamādiṣu..22..
vinivṛttamasūyāyāmīrṣyākopakṛteṣu ca ..
vibhugnaṃ cāpi vijñeyaṃ gambhīrālokanādiṣu .. 23 ..
bhugnaṃ tu lajjite yojyaṃ yatīnāṃ tu svabhāvataḥ ..
nivṛttaṃ vāpi kartavyaṃ hāsyaśokabhayādiṣu .. 24 ..
ṛjusvabhāvasaṃsthāne kartavyaṃ yadunandana ..
ābhugnamatha nirbhugnaṃ tathā caiva prakaṃpitam .. 25 ..
meaning:
अवाङ्मुखमवाभुग्नं निभुग्नं चोर्ध्वगं तु तत् ..
भुग्नं स्यादानतं किञ्चिन्निवृत्तं विवृतं भवेत्.. ..21..
ऋजुस्वभावसंस्थं च तयोः कर्माणि चक्षते ..
विरुद्धवारणे कार्यं मैवमित्येवमादिषु..22..
विनिवृत्तमसूयायामीर्ष्याकोपकृतेषु च ..
विभुग्नं चापि विज्ञेयं गम्भीरालोकनादिषु .. 23 ..
भुग्नं तु लज्जिते योज्यं यतीनां तु स्वभावतः ..
निवृत्तं वापि कर्तव्यं हास्यशोकभयादिषु .. 24 ..
ऋजुस्वभावसंस्थाने कर्तव्यं यदुनन्दन ..
आभुग्नमथ निर्भुग्नं तथा चैव प्रकंपितम् .. 25 ..

sanskrit_iast:
udvāhitaṃ samaṃ caiva pañcarodhaḥ prakīrtitam ..
dhāryate yacca nirbhugnaṃ tadā bhugnaṃ prakīrtitam .. 26 ..
meaning:
उद्वाहितं समं चैव पञ्चरोधः प्रकीर्तितम् ..
धार्यते यच्च निर्भुग्नं तदा भुग्नं प्रकीर्तितम् .. 26 ..
text_mt: udvāhita, and sama: five [movements of the chest] are proclaimed. / When [the chest] is held depressed, it is then proclaimed as bhugna;

sanskrit_iast:
śastrakṣate vighāte ca hṛdroge ca tadiṣyate ..
stabdhaṃ ca nimnapṛṣṭhaṃ ca nirbhugnaṃ nāma tatsmṛtam .. 27 ..
meaning:
शस्त्रक्षते विघाते च हृद्रोगे च तदिष्यते ..
स्तब्धं च निम्नपृष्ठं च निर्भुग्नं नाम तत्स्मृतम् .. 27 ..
text_mt: that is prescribed in sword wounds, obstacles, and heart disease. / Motionless and with the back depressed, that is known as nirbhugna;

sanskrit_iast:
stambhe savismaye māne viṣāde ca tatheṣyate ..
urasastūrdhvavikṣepaḥ prakampitamihocyate .. 28 ..
meaning:
स्तम्भे सविस्मये माने विषादे च तथेष्यते ..
उरसस्तूर्ध्वविक्षेपः प्रकम्पितमिहोच्यते .. 28 ..
text_mt: that is prescribed in paralysis, with wonder, in pride, and in despondency. / But the upward tossing of the chest is here called prakampita;

sanskrit_iast:
hasite rucite kāryaṃ śrame vyādhibhaye tathā ..
udvāhitaṃ yadūrdhvaṃ tu tadudvāhitamucyate .. 29 ..
meaning:
हसिते रुचिते कार्यं श्रमे व्याधिभये तथा ..
उद्वाहितं यदूर्ध्वं तु तदुद्वाहितमुच्यते .. 29 ..
text_mt: it should be done in laughing, weeping, fatigue, disease, and fear. / That which is lifted upward is called udvāhita;

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvaṃ nigamite kāryaṃ jṛmbhiteṣu prayogataḥ ..
caturasraṃ samaṃ nāma vijñeyaṃ sauṣṭhaveṣu tat .. 3.24.30 ..
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वं निगमिते कार्यं जृम्भितेषु प्रयोगतः ..
चतुरस्रं समं नाम विज्ञेयं सौष्ठवेषु तत् .. 3.24.30 ..
text_mt: it should be performed in practice when raised upward, and in yawnings; / caturasra is known as sama, [employed] in graceful posture.

sanskrit_iast:
samunnataṃ nataṃ caiva prasāritavivartite ..
tathāpasṛtamevaṃ hi pārśvayoḥ karma pañcadhā .. 31 ..
meaning:
समुन्नतं नतं चैव प्रसारितविवर्तिते ..
तथापसृतमेवं हि पार्श्वयोः कर्म पञ्चधा .. 31 ..
text_mt: Samunnata and nata, prasārita and vivartita, / and likewise apasṛta: thus indeed is the action of the sides fivefold.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭipārśvabhujāṃsāntairunnataiḥ syātsasunnatam ..
kaṭī yatra sunirbhugnā pārśvaṃ taddvinataṃ bhavet .. 32 ..
meaning:
कटिपार्श्वभुजांसान्तैरुन्नतैः स्यात्ससुन्नतम् ..
कटी यत्र सुनिर्भुग्ना पार्श्वं तद्द्विनतं भवेत् .. 32 ..
text_mt: With the waist, flanks, arms, and tips of the shoulders raised, it is samunnata; / where the waist is well bent, that side should be double-bent;

sanskrit_iast:
prasāraṇādubhayataḥ pārśvayoḥ syātprasāritam ..
parivartanāttrikasyāpi vivartitamiheṣyate .. 33 ..
meaning:
प्रसारणादुभयतः पार्श्वयोः स्यात्प्रसारितम् ..
परिवर्तनात्त्रिकस्यापि विवर्तितमिहेष्यते .. 33 ..
text_mt: from extending on both sides, it becomes prasārita in the sides; / and from turning of the sacrum, it is here deemed vivartita;

sanskrit_iast:
asya caivopagamanādbhavedapasṛtaṃ punaḥ ..
nataṃ tvapasṛte kāryaṃ connataṃ tūpasarpite .. 34 ..
meaning:
अस्य चैवोपगमनाद्भवेदपसृतं पुनः ..
नतं त्वपसृते कार्यं चोन्नतं तूपसर्पिते .. 34 ..
text_mt: and from its moving forward, it becomes apasṛta again; / nata should be performed when stepping back, and unnata when advancing;

sanskrit_iast:
prasārite praharṣādau trāse cāpasṛte punaḥ ..
vivartitaṃ vivarte ca kāraṇaṃ pārśvamucyate .. 35 ..
meaning:
प्रसारिते प्रहर्षादौ त्रासे चापसृते पुनः ..
विवर्तितं विवर्ते च कारणं पार्श्वमुच्यते .. 35 ..
text_mt: in prasārita during intense joy and the like, and in apasṛta during terror; / and vivartita is used in turning: this is declared the purpose of the side.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣāmaṃ nimnaṃ ca pūrṇaṃ ca saṃproktamudaraṃ tridhā ..
kṣāmaṃ tu hasite kāryaṃ tathā caiva vijṛmbhite .. 36 ..
meaning:
क्षामं निम्नं च पूर्णं च संप्रोक्तमुदरं त्रिधा ..
क्षामं तु हसिते कार्यं तथा चैव विजृम्भिते .. 36 ..
text_mt: Kṣāma, nimna, and pūrṇa: the belly is declared threefold. / Kṣāma should be performed in laughter, and likewise in yawning;

sanskrit_iast:
vyādhite tapasi śrānte kṣudhārte nimnameva ca ..
pūrṇaṃ niḥśvasite caiva hyārogye lalitaṃ tathā .. 37 ..
meaning:
व्याधिते तपसि श्रान्ते क्षुधार्ते निम्नमेव च ..
पूर्णं निःश्वसिते चैव ह्यारोग्ये ललितं तथा .. 37 ..
text_mt: in disease, austerity, fatigue, and hunger, it should be nimna; / and pūrṇa in sighing, and likewise gracefully in good health;

sanskrit_iast:
prakampitā ca cchinnā ca nivṛttā recitā tathā ..
udvāhitā caiva kaṭirnṛtte pañcavidhā smṛtā .. 38 ..
meaning:
प्रकम्पिता च च्छिन्ना च निवृत्ता रेचिता तथा ..
उद्वाहिता चैव कटिर्नृत्ते पञ्चविधा स्मृता .. 38 ..
text_mt: Tremulous, severed, turned away, emptied, / and raised up—the waist in dance is traditionally declared to be of five kinds.

sanskrit_iast:
tiryaggatā gatā kṣipraṃ vijñeyā vaprakampitā ..
madhyasthabalanāccaiva cchinnā saṃparikīrtitā .. 39 ..
meaning:
तिर्यग्गता गता क्षिप्रं विज्ञेया वप्रकम्पिता ..
मध्यस्थबलनाच्चैव च्छिन्ना संपरिकीर्तिता .. 39 ..
text_mt: Moving sideways and moving quickly, it should be known as tremulous; / and from turning while staying in the middle, it is proclaimed to be severed.

sanskrit_iast:
parāṅmukhasyābhimukhī nivṛttā parikīrtitā ..
sarvatobhramaṇāccaiva recitetyabhidhīyate .. 3.24.40...
meaning:
पराङ्मुखस्याभिमुखी निवृत्ता परिकीर्तिता ..
सर्वतोभ्रमणाच्चैव रेचितेत्यभिधीयते .. 3.24.40...
text_mt: Facing toward what is turned away, it is proclaimed to be turned away; / and from rotating in all directions, it is designated as emptied.

sanskrit_iast:
niścitodvāhanāccaiva tathaivodvāhitā matā ..
nīca vāmanakubjānāṃ gatau kāryā prakampitā .. 41 ..
meaning:
निश्चितोद्वाहनाच्चैव तथैवोद्वाहिता मता ..
नीच वामनकुब्जानां गतौ कार्या प्रकम्पिता .. 41 ..
text_mt: And from a distinct raising, it is likewise considered raised up. / The tremulous [waist] should be performed in the gait of base people, dwarfs, and hunchbacks.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāyāme tvatha saṃprāpte vyāvṛttaprekṣiteṣu ca ..
chinnā kāryā kaṭistajjñairnivṛttā vartiteṣu ca .. 42 ..
meaning:
व्यायामे त्वथ संप्राप्ते व्यावृत्तप्रेक्षितेषु च ..
छिन्ना कार्या कटिस्तज्ज्ञैर्निवृत्ता वर्तितेषु च .. 42 ..
text_mt: When physical exercise occurs, and in glances cast looking backward, / the severed waist should be performed by experts, and the turned away in turned [movements].

sanskrit_iast:
recitā recite kāryā anyā līlāgate tridhā ..
kampanaṃ valanaṃ caiva stambhanodvartane tathā ..43 ..
meaning:
रेचिता रेचिते कार्या अन्या लीलागते त्रिधा ..
कम्पनं वलनं चैव स्तम्भनोद्वर्तने तथा ..43 ..
text_mt: The emptied [waist] should be performed in the emptied [movement]; the other, in graceful gait, is threefold. / Shaking, turning, rigidifying, uplifting,

sanskrit_iast:
vivartanaṃ ca pañcaiva ūrvoḥ karmāṇi nirdiśet ..
namanonnamane pārantyormahīpṛṣṭhedbhute yadā .. 44 ..
meaning:
विवर्तनं च पञ्चैव ऊर्वोः कर्माणि निर्दिशेत् ..
नमनोन्नमने पारन्त्योर्महीपृष्ठेद्भुते यदा .. 44 ..
text_mt: and rolling over—one should indicate these as the five actions of the thighs. / When bending and raising [...] on the surface of the earth,

sanskrit_iast:
sthitā pādatalāgreṇa kampitaṃ tattadiṣyate ..
gacchedabhyantaraṃ jānu śanairyadvalitaṃ tu tat .. 45 ..
meaning:
स्थिता पादतलाग्रेण कम्पितं तत्तदिष्यते ..
गच्छेदभ्यन्तरं जानु शनैर्यद्वलितं तु तत् .. 45 ..
text_mt: standing on the tip of the sole of the foot, that is regarded as shaken. / When the knee slowly goes inward, that is turned.

sanskrit_iast:
stambhanaṃ cāpi vijñeyamapavṛttakriyākulam ..
valitāviddhabhāvaṃ syādudvartanamathāpi ca .. 46 ..
meaning:
स्तम्भनं चापि विज्ञेयमपवृत्तक्रियाकुलम् ..
वलिताविद्धभावं स्यादुद्वर्तनमथापि च .. 46 ..
