3.25
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Kāntā, bhayānakā, hāsyā, karuṇā, and adbhutā, / raudrā, vīrā, and bībhatsā are to be known as the glances of the sentiments.
Snigdhā, hṛṣṭā, jihmā, kruddhā, bhītā, lajjitā, / tṛptā, then vismitā, and saumyā are the glances in the permanent emotional states.
Malinā, kekarā, śrāntā, abhitaptā, and viplutā, […]
viṣaṇṇā, śaṅkitā, trastā, śokā, nimīlitā, / vibhrāntā, kuñcitā, śūnyā, muktalā, and vitarkitā, / madirā, lalitā, and mlānā: such is the summary of glances.
These thirty-six glances have indeed been declared by me by name. / With a play of brows and sidelong glance, kāntā is to be known as charming;
bhayānakā has inverted eyelids and eyelash-tips, with trembling pupil; / hāsyā has slightly contracted lids and a wandering pupil.

text_mt:
the sorrowless is in knowledge, and the closed should be used in touch. / The bewildered should be used in confusion, and the contracted in viewing subtle things;
the vacant is of one overcome by worry, and the released in the act of smelling. / In deliberation it is the reflective, and in intoxication it should be the intoxicated [gaze];
the graceful is prescribed in the playful dalliance of women, and the languid in exhaustion. / Elevation, closing, opening, rolling,
contracting, level, throbbing, striking, / and beating: the movement of the eyelids is proclaimed to be ninefold.
The coming together of the eyelids is known as closing, / and the separation between them is proclaimed as opening.
Where the two eyelids are widened, that is rolling; / when they are contracted, it should be known by the wise as contracting.
The natural position of the eyelids is proclaimed as level; / where the two eyelids quiver, it is here called throbbing.

yo niṣkramo'dharasyātha sa visarga iti smṛtaḥ .. 71 ..
meaning:
वेपनं चापि विज्ञेयमधरस्य तु कम्पने ..
यो निष्क्रमोऽधरस्याथ स विसर्ग इति स्मृतः .. 71 ..
text_mt: and shaking is to be known in kampana (trembling) of the lower lip; / and that which is the protruding of the lower lip is remembered as visarga (thrusting out);

sanskrit_iast:
antaḥpraveśanaṃ caiva vinigūhitamucyate ..
dantoṣṭhapīḍanāccaiva saṃdaṣṭakamiti smṛtam .. 72 ..
meaning:
अन्तःप्रवेशनं चैव विनिगूहितमुच्यते ..
दन्तोष्ठपीडनाच्चैव संदष्टकमिति स्मृतम् .. 72 ..
text_mt: and drawing inside is called vinigūhita (concealed); / and from the pressure of the teeth and lip it is remembered as saṃdaṣṭaka (bitten);

sanskrit_iast:
piṇḍitābhyudgataścaiva samudgaka iti smṛtaḥ ..
vivartitamasūyāyāṃ roṣe kampitamiṣyate ..
bhayānake visargaśca karṣaṇe'tha nigūhanam .. 73 ..
meaning:
पिण्डिताभ्युद्गतश्चैव समुद्गक इति स्मृतः ..
विवर्तितमसूयायां रोषे कम्पितमिष्यते ..
भयानके विसर्गश्च कर्षणेऽथ निगूहनम् .. 73 ..
text_mt: and gathered and elevated is remembered as samudgaka (pursed). / Turned around is desired in envy, trembling in anger,

sanskrit_iast:
tatonmādavikāreṣu sandaṣṭaṃ vīraraudrayoḥ ..
samudgamanakampāyāṃ śeṣe kāryaṃ svabhāvajam .. 74 ..
meaning:
ततोन्मादविकारेषु सन्दष्टं वीररौद्रयोः ..
समुद्गमनकम्पायां शेषे कार्यं स्वभावजम् .. 74 ..
text_mt: thrusting out in the terrible [sentiment], and concealing in dragging; / then in the modifications of madness, bitten in the heroic and furious [sentiments], / samudgama (pursed) in trembling; in the rest the natural one should be used.

sanskrit_iast:
upāṅgakarmābhihitaṃ tathaitaṃ mayā samāsena narendracandra ..
kāryaḥ prayatno'tra sadā budhena yasmādupāṅgāśrayameva nṛtyam .. 75 ..
meaning:
उपाङ्गकर्माभिहितं तथैतं मया समासेन नरेन्द्रचन्द्र ..
कार्यः प्रयत्नोऽत्र सदा बुधेन यस्मादुपाङ्गाश्रयमेव नृत्यम् .. 75 ..
text_mt: Thus has this action of the minor limbs been declared by me in brief, O moon among kings; / an effort should always be made herein by the wise person, because dance rests entirely on the minor limbs.

sanskrit_iast:
3.26
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
patākastripatākaśca tathā vaikartaremukhaḥ ..
ardhacandro hyaṭālaśca gurutuṇḍastathāparaḥ .. 1 ..
meaning:
3.26
.. मार्कण्डेय उवाच .. ..
पताकस्त्रिपताकश्च तथा वैकर्तरेमुखः ..
अर्धचन्द्रो ह्यटालश्च गुरुतुण्डस्तथापरः .. 1 ..
text_mt: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Patāka (flag), tripatāka (three-fingered flag), and vaikartaremukha (kartarīmukha), / ardhacandra (crescent moon), arāla, and another, gurutuṇḍa (śukatuṇḍa);
title: Nṛttahastavyavasthāvarṇanaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
muṣṭiśca śikhirākhyaśca kapitthaḥ khaṭakāmukhaḥ ..
sūcyardhaḥ padmakośaśca mṛgaśīrṣo mṛgasya ca .. 2 ..
meaning:
मुष्टिश्च शिखिराख्यश्च कपित्थः खटकामुखः ..
सूच्यर्धः पद्मकोशश्च मृगशीर्षो मृगस्य च .. 2 ..
text_mt: muṣṭi (fist), the one called śikhira (peak), kapittha (wood-apple), and khaṭakāmukha; / sūcyardha (half-needle), padmakośa (lotus-bud), mṛgaśīrṣa (deer-head) of the deer;

sanskrit_iast:
lāṅgūlaḥ kālapadmaśca caturo bhramarastathā ..
haṃsāsyo haṃsapakṣaśca saṃdaṃśo mukulastathā .. 3 ..
meaning:
लाङ्गूलः कालपद्मश्च चतुरो भ्रमरस्तथा ..
हंसास्यो हंसपक्षश्च संदंशो मुकुलस्तथा .. 3 ..
text_mt: lāṅgūla (tail), kālapadma (lotus), catura, and bhramara (bee); / haṃsāsya (swan-face), haṃsapakṣa (swan-wing), saṃdaṃśa (pincers), and mukula (bud)—

sanskrit_iast:
asaṃyutāḥ karā hyete dvāviṃśatirudāhṛtāḥ ..
atha saṃyuktato hastāngadatastānnibodha me .. 4 ..
meaning:
असंयुताः करा ह्येते द्वाविंशतिरुदाहृताः ..
अथ संयुक्ततो हस्तान्गदतस्तान्निबोध मे .. 4 ..
text_mt: these single-hand gestures are stated to be twenty-two. / Now learn from me the combined hand gestures as I declare them:

sanskrit_iast:
aṃjaliśca kapotaśca karkaṭaḥ svastikastathā ..
khaṭako vardhamānaśca utsaṅgo niṣidhastathā .. 5 ..
meaning:
अंजलिश्च कपोतश्च कर्कटः स्वस्तिकस्तथा ..
खटको वर्धमानश्च उत्सङ्गो निषिधस्तथा .. 5 ..
text_mt: añjali, kapota (dove), karkaṭa (crab), and svastika; / khaṭaka, vardhamāna, utsaṅga, and niṣiddha;

sanskrit_iast:
dolaḥ puṣpapuṭaścaiva tathā makara eva ca ..
gajadanto'vahitthaśca vardhamānastathaiva ca .. 6 ..
meaning:
दोलः पुष्पपुटश्चैव तथा मकर एव च ..
गजदन्तोऽवहित्थश्च वर्धमानस्तथैव च .. 6 ..
text_mt: dola (swing), puṣpapuṭa (flower-casket), and likewise makara (sea-monster); / gajadanta (elephant-tusk), avahittha, and likewise vardhamāna—

sanskrit_iast:
ete vai saṃyutā hastā mayā proktāstrayodaśa ..
nṛttahastāryupaścaiva bhūyo nāmni nibodhata .. 7 ..
meaning:
एते वै संयुता हस्ता मया प्रोक्तास्त्रयोदश ..
नृत्तहस्तार्युपश्चैव भूयो नाम्नि निबोधत .. 7 ..
text_mt: these combined hands declared by me are thirteen. / Learn also further the names of the dance-hands:

sanskrit_iast:
caturasrastathā vṛttastathā laghumukhau smṛtau ..
tathā caiva tu vijñeyau hyarālakhaṭakāmukhau .. 8 ..
meaning:
चतुरस्रस्तथा वृत्तस्तथा लघुमुखौ स्मृतौ ..
तथा चैव तु विज्ञेयौ ह्यरालखटकामुखौ .. 8 ..
text_mt: caturasra (square), vṛtta (circular), and both are known as laghumukha; / and likewise to be known are arāla and khaṭakāmukha;

sanskrit_iast:
āviddhavakrasaṃvyāsvau recitāvarddharecitau ..
avahitthaḥ pallavito nitambaḥ keśavardhanau .. 9 ..
meaning:
आविद्धवक्रसंव्यास्वौ रेचितावर्द्धरेचितौ ..
अवहित्थः पल्लवितो नितम्बः केशवर्धनौ .. 9 ..
text_mt: āviddhavakra and saṃvyāsu, recita and ardharecita; / avahittha, pallavita, nitamba, and both keśavardhana;

sanskrit_iast:
latākhyau karihastau ca pakṣodyotā'rthavardhitau ..
jñeyau garuḍapakṣau ca daṇḍapakṣau tathaiva ca ...3.26.10...
meaning:
लताख्यौ करिहस्तौ च पक्षोद्योताऽर्थवर्धितौ ..
ज्ञेयौ गरुडपक्षौ च दण्डपक्षौ तथैव च ...3.26.10...
text_mt: both called latā (creeper) and karihasta (elephant-trunk), pakṣodyota and arthavardhita; / and garuḍapakṣa and daṇḍapakṣa are to be known;

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvamaṇḍalajau caiva pārśvamaṃḍalājāvapi ..
pārśvārdhamaṇḍalau caiva uromaṇḍalakau tathā..11..
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वमण्डलजौ चैव पार्श्वमंडलाजावपि ..
पार्श्वार्धमण्डलौ चैव उरोमण्डलकौ तथा..11..
text_mt: and both ūrdhvamaṇḍala, and both pārśvamaṇḍala; / both pārśvārdhamaṇḍala, and both uromaṇḍalaka;

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭasvastikakāvanyau tathā vai padmakauśikau ..
allipallavasaṃjñau ca tathā colvanasaṃjñitau .. 12 ..
meaning:
इष्टस्वस्तिककावन्यौ तथा वै पद्मकौशिकौ ..
अल्लिपल्लवसंज्ञौ च तथा चोल्वनसंज्ञितौ .. 12 ..
text_mt: two others, iṣṭasvastika, and padmakośa; / both named allipallava, and both designated ulbaṇa;

sanskrit_iast:
lalitau valitau caiva jñeyā nṛtyakarāḥ sadā ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi karāṇāṃ karmalakṣaṇam .. 13 ..
meaning:
ललितौ वलितौ चैव ज्ञेया नृत्यकराः सदा ..
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि कराणां कर्मलक्षणम् .. 13 ..
text_mt: lalita and valita are always to be known as dance-hands. / Hereafter I shall declare the characteristics and functions of the hands.

sanskrit_iast:
prasāritāgrā sahitā yasyāṅgulyo bhavanti hi ..
kuñcitaśca tathāṅguṣṭhaḥ sa patāka iti smṛtaḥ .. 14 ..
meaning:
प्रसारिताग्रा सहिता यस्याङ्गुल्यो भवन्ति हि ..
कुञ्चितश्च तथाङ्गुष्ठः स पताक इति स्मृतः .. 14 ..
text_mt: That [hand] whose fingers are extended at the tips and joined together, / and the thumb is contracted, is remembered as patāka (flag).

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa prahāragrahaṇe rodhane syātpratāpane ..
calitāṅgulirapyeṣa vāyuvṛṣṭinirūpaṇe .. 15 ..
meaning:
एष प्रहारग्रहणे रोधने स्यात्प्रतापने ..
चलिताङ्गुलिरप्येष वायुवृष्टिनिरूपणे .. 15 ..
text_mt: This may be used in taking a blow, checking, and scorching; / with fingers moving, it [serves] in depicting wind and rain;

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvagaśca tathotsāhe chatrādiṣvapyadhomukhaḥ ..
puṣkaraprahitastāle samaḥ pracalitāṅguliḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वगश्च तथोत्साहे छत्रादिष्वप्यधोमुखः ..
पुष्करप्रहितस्ताले समः प्रचलिताङ्गुलिः .. 16 ..
text_mt: turned upward in enthusiasm, turned downward in parasols and the like; / placed on a drum in rhythm, level with trembling fingers,

sanskrit_iast:
pakṣmotkṣepe recitaka utkṣiptaścaiva dhāraṇe ..
asyaikānāmikā vakrā tripatākā tathā bhavet .. 17 ..
meaning:
पक्ष्मोत्क्षेपे रेचितक उत्क्षिप्तश्चैव धारणे ..
अस्यैकानामिका वक्रा त्रिपताका तथा भवेत् .. 17 ..
text_mt: in recitaka of eyebrow-raising, and raised up in supporting. / When the ring finger of this is bent, it becomes tripatāka (three-fingered flag).

sanskrit_iast:
āvāhane prayuñjīta mukuṭābhinaye'pyuta ...
acalāṅgulirapyeṣa laghupakṣinirūpaṇe 118 ..
meaning:
आवाहने प्रयुञ्जीत मुकुटाभिनयेऽप्युत ...
अचलाङ्गुलिरप्येष लघुपक्षिनिरूपणे 118 ..
text_mt: One should employ it in invocation and in acting out a crown, / and with motionless fingers in indicating a small bird.

sanskrit_iast:
tayānāsikayā kāryaṃ tathaivāśrupramārjanam ..
maṅgalasparśanaṃ kāryaṃ śirasaśca niveśanam .. 19 ..
meaning:
तयानासिकया कार्यं तथैवाश्रुप्रमार्जनम् ..
मङ्गलस्पर्शनं कार्यं शिरसश्च निवेशनम् .. 19 ..
text_mt: With that [hand] at the nose, touching auspicious objects / and wiping away tears are to be performed, as well as placing [the hand] on the head.

sanskrit_iast:
śrotrasaṃvaraṇaṃ caiva kāryaṃ bhūmimukhena tu ..
bhujaṅgānāmābhinayaṃ bhramarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 3.26.20 ..
meaning:
श्रोत्रसंवरणं चैव कार्यं भूमिमुखेन तु ..
भुजङ्गानामाभिनयं भ्रमराणां तथैव च .. 3.26.20 ..
text_mt: Covering the ears should be performed with [the hand] facing the earth, / and likewise the depiction of serpents and bees.

sanskrit_iast:
tripatākā yadā haste bhavetpṛṣṭhāvalokinī ..
tarjanī tu tadā jñeyaḥ kartarīmukhasaṃjñakaḥ..21..
meaning:
त्रिपताका यदा हस्ते भवेत्पृष्ठावलोकिनी ..
तर्जनी तु तदा ज्ञेयः कर्तरीमुखसंज्ञकः..21..
text_mt: When the tripatākā hand has the forefinger looking backward, / it is then known by the name kartarīmukha.

sanskrit_iast:
kāryo'yaṃ parivāreṣu bhinnaśca pataneṣu ca..
anāmikā tu sāṅguṣṭhā ardhacandre kare bhavet..22..
meaning:
कार्योऽयं परिवारेषु भिन्नश्च पतनेषु च..
अनामिका तु साङ्गुष्ठा अर्धचन्द्रे करे भवेत्..22..
text_mt: This is to be used for retinues, separations, and fallings. / When the ring finger is joined with the thumb, it is the ardhacandra hand.

sanskrit_iast:
bālacandrābhinayane bālasyāttaravastathā..
mekhalāṃ jaghanaṃ caiva kuryāccānena kuṇḍalam..23..
meaning:
बालचन्द्राभिनयने बालस्यात्तरवस्तथा..
मेखलां जघनं चैव कुर्याच्चानेन कुण्डलम्..23..
text_mt: In representing the crescent moon, and similarly the limbs of a child, / one should portray a girdle, the hips, and an earring with this.

sanskrit_iast:
khaṇḍapradeśinī kāryā aṅgulyaḥ kuṃcitāstathā..
śeṣā bhinnordhvavalitā mrarāleṅgulayaḥ kare .. 24 ..
meaning:
खण्डप्रदेशिनी कार्या अङ्गुल्यः कुंचितास्तथा..
शेषा भिन्नोर्ध्ववलिता म्ररालेङ्गुलयः करे .. 24 ..
text_mt: The forefinger should be bent and the [other] fingers curled; / when the remaining fingers are separated and bent upward, the fingers are in the arāla hand.

sanskrit_iast:
gāmbhīryasattvaśauṃḍīryakeśasaṃgrahaṇādiṣu ..
svedasya cāpanayane śeṣe caiṣa karo bhavet .. . .. 25 ..
meaning:
गाम्भीर्यसत्त्वशौंडीर्यकेशसंग्रहणादिषु ..
स्वेदस्य चापनयने शेषे चैष करो भवेत् .. . .. 25 ..
text_mt: In [representing] depth, courage, valor, grasping hair, and the like, / and in wiping away sweat, this hand is used for the rest.

sanskrit_iast:
mrarālaḥ śukatuṇḍaśca vakritānāmikāṅguliḥ ..
nāhantvamityathaitena nityaṃ cābhinayedbudhaḥ .. 26 ..
meaning:
म्ररालः शुकतुण्डश्च वक्रितानामिकाङ्गुलिः ..
नाहन्त्वमित्यथैतेन नित्यं चाभिनयेद्बुधः .. 26 ..
text_mt: The arāla with the ring finger bent becomes śukatuṇḍa. / With this, the wise actor should always represent 'not I' or 'not you'.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgulyo yasya hastasya talamadhye'grasaṃsthitāḥ ..
tāsāmuparitāṅguṣṭhaḥ sa muṣṭiriti saṃjñitaḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
अङ्गुल्यो यस्य हस्तस्य तलमध्येऽग्रसंस्थिताः ..
तासामुपरिताङ्गुष्ठः स मुष्टिरिति संज्ञितः .. 27 ..
text_mt: The hand whose fingertips are positioned in the middle of the palm, / with the thumb over them, is designated muṣṭi.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa prahāre vyāyāme nirdayastanapīḍane .. .
sandhāraṇe'siyaṣṭyośca grahaṇe kuntadaṇḍayoḥ .. 28 ..
meaning:
एष प्रहारे व्यायामे निर्दयस्तनपीडने .. .
सन्धारणेऽसियष्ट्योश्च ग्रहणे कुन्तदण्डयोः .. 28 ..
text_mt: This is used in striking, wrestling, merciless squeezing of the breasts, / holding a sword or a staff, and grasping a spear or a rod.

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvāṅguṣṭho'yameva syātkaraḥ śikharasaṃjñitaḥ ..
eṣa raśmigrahe kāryaścāpāṅkuśadhanurgrahe ..29.. .
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वाङ्गुष्ठोऽयमेव स्यात्करः शिखरसंज्ञितः ..
एष रश्मिग्रहे कार्यश्चापाङ्कुशधनुर्ग्रहे ..29.. .
text_mt: This very [hand] with the thumb raised is the hand named śikhara; / this is to be used in holding the reins, a bow, a goad, or a weapon.

sanskrit_iast:
muṣṭimadhyagatoṅguṣṭhaḥ kapittha iti kīrtitaḥ ..
anenābhinayaḥ kāryo madhye cakre śare tathā .. 3.26.30 ..
meaning:
मुष्टिमध्यगतोङ्गुष्ठः कपित्थ इति कीर्तितः ..
अनेनाभिनयः कार्यो मध्ये चक्रे शरे तथा .. 3.26.30 ..
text_mt: When the thumb enters the middle of the muṣṭi, it is called kapittha; / with this, dramatic depiction should be made of the middle, a discus, and an arrow.

sanskrit_iast:
utkṣiptavakrā tu yadānāmikā sakanīyasī ...
asyaiva tu kapitthasya tataḥ syātkhaṭakāmukhaḥ ..31..
meaning:
उत्क्षिप्तवक्रा तु यदानामिका सकनीयसी ...
अस्यैव तु कपित्थस्य ततः स्यात्खटकामुखः ..31..
text_mt: When the ring finger and the little finger of this very kapittha / are raised and bent, it becomes khaṭakāmukha.

sanskrit_iast:
hotre chatragraha caiva karṣaṇe vyajane tathā ..
sragdāmadhāraṇe kāryo hyasaṅkocosya saṃgrahaḥ ..32...
meaning:
होत्रे छत्रग्रह चैव कर्षणे व्यजने तथा ..
स्रग्दामधारणे कार्यो ह्यसङ्कोचोस्य संग्रहः ..32...
text_mt: It should be used in offering oblations, holding an umbrella, pulling, fanning, / and holding a garland; its grasp should be uncompressed.

sanskrit_iast:
prasṛtā tarjanī cātra yadā sūcīmukhastadā ..
niṣpādane cābhinayennetraśakramaheśayoḥ .. 33 ..
meaning:
प्रसृता तर्जनी चात्र यदा सूचीमुखस्तदा ..
निष्पादने चाभिनयेन्नेत्रशक्रमहेशयोः .. 33 ..
text_mt: And when the forefinger here is extended, it is then sūcīmukha; / it should represent manifestation, the eye, Śakra, and Maheśvara.

sanskrit_iast:
asyāṅgulyastu vipulāḥ sahāṃṅguṣṭhena kuñcitāḥ ...
ūrdhvāhaṃsanakhasyaiva sa bhavetpadmakośakaḥ .. 34 ..
meaning:
अस्याङ्गुल्यस्तु विपुलाः सहांङ्गुष्ठेन कुञ्चिताः ...
ऊर्ध्वाहंसनखस्यैव स भवेत्पद्मकोशकः .. 34 ..
text_mt: When the fingers of this [hand] are spread and bent along with the thumb, / with the nails pointing upward like a goose, it is padmakośa.

sanskrit_iast:
śliṣṭoṅguṣṭho nimnamadhyaḥ patākohiśiro bhavet ..
salilasya pradāne tu kāryā tena ca sūcanam .. .. 35 ..
meaning:
श्लिष्टोङ्गुष्ठो निम्नमध्यः पताकोहिशिरो भवेत् ..
सलिलस्य प्रदाने तु कार्या तेन च सूचनम् .. .. 35 ..
text_mt: When the thumb is joined and the center is hollowed, the patāka becomes ahiśiras; / it is to be used in offering water and in making a gesture of indication.

sanskrit_iast:
adhomukhīnāṃ sarvāsāmaṅgulīnāṃ yadā bhavet ..
kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhakā cordhvā tadā syānmṛgaśīrṣakaḥ .. 36 ..
meaning:
अधोमुखीनां सर्वासामङ्गुलीनां यदा भवेत् ..
कनिष्ठाङ्गुष्ठका चोर्ध्वा तदा स्यान्मृगशीर्षकः .. 36 ..
text_mt: When all the fingers are turned face down, / and the little finger and the thumb are raised, it is mṛgaśīrṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
sūcite cchedite kāryaṃ śakyā svoccālane tathā ..
tretāgnisaṃsthitā madhyā tarjanyaṅguṣṭhayoryadā .. 37 ..
meaning:
सूचिते च्छेदिते कार्यं शक्या स्वोच्चालने तथा ..
त्रेताग्निसंस्थिता मध्या तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठयोर्यदा .. 37 ..
text_mt: It should be used in pointing, cutting, capacity, and raising oneself. / When the middle finger, forefinger, and thumb are arranged like the three sacrificial fires,

sanskrit_iast:
kāṅgule nāmikā vakrā tathā cordhvā kanīyasī ..
anena khalu kartavyaṃ phalānāṃ tu nirūpaṇam .. 38 ..
meaning:
काङ्गुले नामिका वक्रा तथा चोर्ध्वा कनीयसी ..
अनेन खलु कर्तव्यं फलानां तु निरूपणम् .. 38 ..
text_mt: the ring finger bent, and the little finger likewise raised, / it is kāṅgula; with this, indeed, the depiction of fruits should be made.

sanskrit_iast:
āvartyante karatale yasyāṅgulyaḥ karasya vai ..
pārśvāgatavikīrṇāśca kolapadma iti smṛtaḥ .. 39 ..
meaning:
आवर्त्यन्ते करतले यस्याङ्गुल्यः करस्य वै ..
पार्श्वागतविकीर्णाश्च कोलपद्म इति स्मृतः .. 39 ..
text_mt: The hand whose fingers are curled inward in the palm / and spread out from the side is known as alapadma.

sanskrit_iast:
pratiṣedha kṛte yojyo nāsti śūnyeṣu cāpyatha ..
tisraḥ prasāritāṅgulyastathā cordhvā kanīyasī .. 3.26.40 ..
meaning:
प्रतिषेध कृते योज्यो नास्ति शून्येषु चाप्यथ ..
तिस्रः प्रसारिताङ्गुल्यस्तथा चोर्ध्वा कनीयसी .. 3.26.40 ..
text_mt: It is to be employed in making a denial, and in [representing] 'it is not' or emptiness. / When three fingers are extended and the little finger is raised,

sanskrit_iast:
tasyā madhyāśritoṅguṣṭhaḥ karaḥ sa caturaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
vacasāṃ viniyoge ca mādhye caiva prayojayet..41..
meaning:
तस्या मध्याश्रितोङ्गुष्ठः करः स चतुरः स्मृतः ..
वचसां विनियोगे च माध्ये चैव प्रयोजयेत्..41..
text_mt: and the thumb rests on the middle finger, that hand is called catura; / one should employ it in the application of words and in sweetness.

sanskrit_iast:
anenaiva tathā kāryaṃ varṇānāṃ tu nirūpaṇam ..
ūrdhvasthe ca nave cśvetaṃ rakte syādardhamaṇḍalam ..42..
meaning:
अनेनैव तथा कार्यं वर्णानां तु निरूपणम् ..
ऊर्ध्वस्थे च नवे च्श्वेतं रक्ते स्यादर्धमण्डलम् ..42..
text_mt: With this very [hand], the depiction of colors is to be made: / held upward and fresh, it indicates white; in red, it forms a semicircle;

sanskrit_iast:
maṇḍalaṃ na bhavetpītaṃ nīlaṃ ca mṛditaṃ bhavet ..
svabhāvasthena kṛtsnaṃ ca śeṣā varṇāstathaiva ca .. 43 ..
meaning:
मण्डलं न भवेत्पीतं नीलं च मृदितं भवेत् ..
स्वभावस्थेन कृत्स्नं च शेषा वर्णास्तथैव च .. 43 ..
text_mt: a circle is yellow; rubbed, it is dark blue; / in its natural state, it indicates everything, and likewise the remaining colors.

sanskrit_iast:
madhyamāṅguṣṭhasandeśo vakrā caiva pradeśinī ..
ūrdhvamanyāḥ prakīrṇāśca bhramaraśca tadā bhavet .. 44 ..
meaning:
मध्यमाङ्गुष्ठसन्देशो वक्रा चैव प्रदेशिनी ..
ऊर्ध्वमन्याः प्रकीर्णाश्च भ्रमरश्च तदा भवेत् .. 44 ..
text_mt: When the middle finger and thumb form a pincer, the forefinger is bent, / and the other fingers are raised and separated, it is then bhramara.

sanskrit_iast:
padmādigrahaṇe kāryaṃ karṇapūre tathāpyayam ..
tarjanīmadhyamāṅguṣṭhā tretāgnisthā nirantaram .. .. 45 ..
meaning:
पद्मादिग्रहणे कार्यं कर्णपूरे तथाप्ययम् ..
तर्जनीमध्यमाङ्गुष्ठा त्रेताग्निस्था निरन्तरम् .. .. 45 ..
text_mt: It should be used in holding a lotus or the like, and also for an ear ornament. / When the forefinger, middle finger, and thumb continuously stand like the three fires,

sanskrit_iast:
bhaveyurhaṃsavaktrasya śeṣā hyanyāḥ prasāritāḥ ..
ślakṣṇalāghavaniḥsāramārdaveṣu prayojayet .. 46 ..
meaning:
भवेयुर्हंसवक्त्रस्य शेषा ह्यन्याः प्रसारिताः ..
श्लक्ष्णलाघवनिःसारमार्दवेषु प्रयोजयेत् .. 46 ..
text_mt: they form the haṃsavaktra hand, while the other fingers are extended; / one should employ it in smoothness, lightness, insubstantiality, and softness.

sanskrit_iast:
tiryak piṇḍīkṛtā yasminunnatā ca kaniṣṭhikā ..
aṅguṣṭhaḥ kuñcitastvevaṃ haṃsapakṣa iti smṛtaḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
तिर्यक् पिण्डीकृता यस्मिनुन्नता च कनिष्ठिका ..
अङ्गुष्ठः कुञ्चितस्त्वेवं हंसपक्ष इति स्मृतः .. 47 ..
text_mt: The hand in which [the fingers] are pressed together obliquely, the little finger is raised, / and the thumb is bent, is known as haṃsapakṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇḍasaṃśrayametena bhojanaḥ saparigrahaḥ ..
sparśe caivānulāpārthe kārye saṃvāhane tathā .. 48 ..
meaning:
गण्डसंश्रयमेतेन भोजनः सपरिग्रहः ..
स्पर्शे चैवानुलापार्थे कार्ये संवाहने तथा .. 48 ..
text_mt: Resting on the cheek is done with this, as well as eating with acceptance, / touching, conversation, and massage.

sanskrit_iast:
tarjanyaṅguṣṭhasaṃdaṃśastvarālasya yadā bhavet ..
nirbhugnatalamadhyaśca sasandaṃśa iti smṛtaḥ .. 49 ..
meaning:
तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठसंदंशस्त्वरालस्य यदा भवेत् ..
निर्भुग्नतलमध्यश्च ससन्दंश इति स्मृतः .. 49 ..
text_mt: When there is a pinching together of the forefinger and thumb of the arāla, / and the center of the palm is bent, it is known as sandaṃśa.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃdaṃśastrividho jñeyastvagraho mukhajastathā ..
tathā pārśvakṛtaścaiva tasya karmāṇi me śṛṇu .. 3.26.50 ..
meaning:
संदंशस्त्रिविधो ज्ञेयस्त्वग्रहो मुखजस्तथा ..
तथा पार्श्वकृतश्चैव तस्य कर्माणि मे शृणु .. 3.26.50 ..
text_mt: Sandaṃśa should be known as threefold: situated at the tip, at the mouth, / and held at the side; hear from me its functions:

sanskrit_iast:
sandaṃśagrahaṇe kāryaḥ śalyoddhāre tathāgrajaḥ ..
ālekhārañjane caiva tarjanīpīḍane tathā .. 51 ..
meaning:
सन्दंशग्रहणे कार्यः शल्योद्धारे तथाग्रजः ..
आलेखारञ्जने चैव तर्जनीपीडने तथा .. 51 ..
text_mt: The one at the tip is to be used in grasping with pincers, extracting splinters, / painting and coloring, and pressing with the forefinger.

sanskrit_iast:
yajñopavītī pārśvasthaḥ śiraḥsaṃdarśane tathā ..
samāgatāgrāṅguliko muktalaḥ padmakośakaḥ .. 52 ..
meaning:
यज्ञोपवीती पार्श्वस्थः शिरःसंदर्शने तथा ..
समागताग्राङ्गुलिको मुक्तलः पद्मकोशकः .. 52 ..
text_mt: Held at the side, it represents the sacred thread and touching the head. / When the fingertips are brought together, it is mukula or padmakośa.

sanskrit_iast:
devārcākaraṇe kāryo balo padmanirūpaṇe ..
asaṃyutāḥ karā hyete yathāvatkīrtitā mayā .. 53 ..
meaning:
देवार्चाकरणे कार्यो बलो पद्मनिरूपणे ..
असंयुताः करा ह्येते यथावत्कीर्तिता मया .. 53 ..
text_mt: It should be used in worshipping deities, offering oblations, and representing a lotus. / These single hands have thus been properly described by me.

sanskrit_iast:
patākābhyāṃ tu hastābhyāṃ sasphuṭoñjalirucyate ..
devatānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ceṣyate punaḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
पताकाभ्यां तु हस्ताभ्यां सस्फुटोञ्जलिरुच्यते ..
देवतानां गुरूणां च पितॄणां चेष्यते पुनः .. 54 ..
text_mt: Two patāka hands joined closely together are called añjali; / it is desired in honoring deities, elders, and the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
anyonyapārśvasaktābhyāṃ karābhyāṃ syātkapotakaḥ ..
śīte bhaye ca kāryo'yaṃ viniyogagame tathā .. 55 ..
meaning:
अन्योन्यपार्श्वसक्ताभ्यां कराभ्यां स्यात्कपोतकः ..
शीते भये च कार्योऽयं विनियोगगमे तथा .. 55 ..
text_mt: When two hands are joined side by side, it is kapota; / this is to be used in cold, fear, and in expressing agreement.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgulyo yasya hastasya aḍulyantaraniḥsṛtāḥ ..
sa karkaṭa iti jñeyaḥ kartavyastu vijṛmbhite .. 56 ..
meaning:
अङ्गुल्यो यस्य हस्तस्य अडुल्यन्तरनिःसृताः ..
स कर्कट इति ज्ञेयः कर्तव्यस्तु विजृम्भिते .. 56 ..
text_mt: The hand whose fingers are interlocked between the fingers [of the other] / is to be known as karkaṭa, and it should be used in yawning.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇibandhana vinyastāvarālau vardhamānakaḥ ..
uttānau natapārśvasthau svastikaḥ parikīrtitaḥ .. 57 ..
meaning:
मणिबन्धन विन्यस्तावरालौ वर्धमानकः ..
उत्तानौ नतपार्श्वस्थौ स्वस्तिकः परिकीर्तितः .. 57 ..
text_mt: Two arāla hands placed at the wrists form vardhamānaka; / turned palms upward and held on bent sides, it is called svastika.

sanskrit_iast:
vistīrṇaṃ sarvametena ṛtavo gaganaṃ ghanam ..
samudraścābhineyaḥ syādbhūmiśca manujeśvara .. 58 ..
meaning:
विस्तीर्णं सर्वमेतेन ऋतवो गगनं घनम् ..
समुद्रश्चाभिनेयः स्याद्भूमिश्च मनुजेश्वर .. 58 ..
text_mt: With this, everything vast—the seasons, the sky, clouds, / the ocean, and the earth—is to be depicted, O lord of men.

sanskrit_iast:
khaṭakaḥ khaṭake nyasya khaṭakā vardhamānakaḥ ..
śṛṅgārārthe prayoktavyaḥ praṇāmakaraṇeṣu ca .. 59 ..
meaning:
खटकः खटके न्यस्य खटका वर्धमानकः ..
शृङ्गारार्थे प्रयोक्तव्यः प्रणामकरणेषु च .. 59 ..
text_mt: Placing one khaṭaka upon another khaṭaka forms khaṭakāvardhamānaka; / it should be employed for erotic love and in making salutations.

sanskrit_iast:
arālau tu viparyastāvuttānau vardhamānakau ..
utsaṅga iti vijñeyaḥ sparśasya grahaṇe paraḥ .. 3.26.60 ..
meaning:
अरालौ तु विपर्यस्तावुत्तानौ वर्धमानकौ ..
उत्सङ्ग इति विज्ञेयः स्पर्शस्य ग्रहणे परः .. 3.26.60 ..
text_mt: Two reversed arāla hands turned upwards and forming vardhamāna / are to be known as utsaṅga; it is supreme in perceiving touch.

sanskrit_iast:
muktalaṃ tu yadā hastaṃ kapitthaṃ pariveṣṭayet ..
sa vijñeyastadā hasto niṣadho nāma nāmataḥ .. 61..
meaning:
मुक्तलं तु यदा हस्तं कपित्थं परिवेष्टयेत् ..
स विज्ञेयस्तदा हस्तो निषधो नाम नामतः .. 61..
text_mt: When a kapittha hand encloses a mukula hand, / that hand is then known by the name niṣadha.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃkṣipte caiva nikṣipte tathā kāryaḥ prapīḍite ..
patākau lambitau hastau doleti parikīrtitāḥ .. .. 62 ..
meaning:
संक्षिप्ते चैव निक्षिप्ते तथा कार्यः प्रपीडिते ..
पताकौ लम्बितौ हस्तौ दोलेति परिकीर्तिताः .. .. 62 ..
text_mt: It should be used in contracting, tossing down, and squeezing; / two patāka hands hanging down are celebrated as dolā.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānādidāne kartavyo bhakṣyādikaraṇeṣu ca ..
dvitīyapārśvasaṃśliṣṭaḥ pūrvaḥ puṣpapuṭaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 63 ..
meaning:
ध्यानादिदाने कर्तव्यो भक्ष्यादिकरणेषु च ..
द्वितीयपार्श्वसंश्लिष्टः पूर्वः पुष्पपुटः स्मृतः .. 63 ..
text_mt: It should be performed in offering gifts in meditation and the like, and in preparing eatables and so on. / Joined at the second side, the former [patāka] is remembered as puṣpapuṭa.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvāṇi cābhineyāni karaṇāneva pārthiva ..
patākau tu yadā hastau mūrtahastāvadhomukhau .. 64 ..
meaning:
पूर्वाणि चाभिनेयानि करणानेव पार्थिव ..
पताकौ तु यदा हस्तौ मूर्तहस्तावधोमुखौ .. 64 ..
text_mt: The previously described movements are indeed to be performed, O king. / When the two hands are patāka, turned downwards and held as bodies,

sanskrit_iast:
uparyupari vinyastau tadā samakaraḥ karaḥ ..
siṃhavyāghramṛgādyānāṃ kartavyo'bhinayo bhavet ..65..
meaning:
उपर्युपरि विन्यस्तौ तदा समकरः करः ..
सिंहव्याघ्रमृगाद्यानां कर्तव्योऽभिनयो भवेत् ..65..
text_mt: placed one above the other, then the hand is samakara. / It should be used in enacting lions, tigers, deer, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
añcitau kūrparāsā tu yadā syātsarpaśīrṣake ..
gajadantastathā nāmnā kāryaḥ śailanibarhaṇe ..66..
meaning:
अञ्चितौ कूर्परासा तु यदा स्यात्सर्पशीर्षके ..
गजदन्तस्तथा नाम्ना कार्यः शैलनिबर्हणे ..66..
text_mt: When [the hands] are bent at the elbows and become sarpaśīrṣa, / it is called gajadanta by name, and should be used in breaking a mountain.

sanskrit_iast:
śukatuṇḍau karau kṛtvā vakṣasyabhimukhāñcitau ..
śanairadhomukhau viddhāvavahittha iti smṛtaḥ..67..
meaning:
शुकतुण्डौ करौ कृत्वा वक्षस्यभिमुखाञ्चितौ ..
शनैरधोमुखौ विद्धाववहित्थ इति स्मृतः..67..
text_mt: Having made the hands śukatuṇḍa, bent facing the chest, / and slowly turned downwards and pierced, it is remembered as avahittha.

sanskrit_iast:
daurbalyaśca site kāryo gātrāṇāṃ ca nidarśane..
jñeyo vai vardhamānastu haṃsapakṣau parāṅmukhau .. 68 ..
meaning:
दौर्बल्यश्च सिते कार्यो गात्राणां च निदर्शने..
ज्ञेयो वै वर्धमानस्तु हंसपक्षौ पराङ्मुखौ .. 68 ..
text_mt: It is to be used in indicating weakness, cold, and the limbs. / When haṃsapakṣa hands are turned away, it is known as vardhamāna.

sanskrit_iast:
jālavātāyanādīnāṃ prayogastena ceṣyate ..
saṃyutānāṃ karāṇāṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ kathitaṃ mayā .. 69 ..
meaning:
जालवातायनादीनां प्रयोगस्तेन चेष्यते ..
संयुतानां कराणां तु लक्षणं कथितं मया .. 69 ..
text_mt: Its application is desired in [depicting] latticed windows and the like. / Thus the characteristics of combined hands have been spoken by me.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ jñeyāḥ karāḥ sarve nānārasasamudbhavāḥ ..
ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi nustuhastamapāśrayam .. 3.26.70 ..
meaning:
एवं ज्ञेयाः कराः सर्वे नानारससमुद्भवाः ..
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि नुस्तुहस्तमपाश्रयम् .. 3.26.70 ..
text_mt: All these hands are to be known as originating from various aesthetic sentiments. / Hereafter I shall explain the dance hands according to tradition.

sanskrit_iast:
vakṣaso'ṣṭāṃgulasthau tu prāṅmukhau khaṭakāmukhau ..
samānakūrparāsau tu caturasro prakīrtitau..71..
meaning:
वक्षसोऽष्टांगुलस्थौ तु प्राङ्मुखौ खटकामुखौ ..
समानकूर्परासौ तु चतुरस्रो प्रकीर्तितौ..71..
text_mt: Held eight aṅgulas from the chest, facing forward as khaṭakāmukha, / with elbows and shoulders level, they are declared to be caturasra.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsapakṣau smṛtau hastau vyāvṛttau tālavṛntavat ..
udvṛttāviti vijñeyāvatha va. tālavṛntakau .. 72 ..
meaning:
हंसपक्षौ स्मृतौ हस्तौ व्यावृत्तौ तालवृन्तवत् ..
उद्वृत्ताविति विज्ञेयावथ व. तालवृन्तकौ .. 72 ..
text_mt: When the hands are remembered as haṃsapakṣa, rotated like palm-leaf fans, / they are known as udvṛtta, or as tālavṛntaka.

sanskrit_iast:
caturasrīkṛtau hastau haṃsapakṣīkṛtau tathā ..
tiryaṅamukhāvūrdhvatalau jñeyau laghumukhāviti .. 73 ..
meaning:
चतुरस्रीकृतौ हस्तौ हंसपक्षीकृतौ तथा ..
तिर्यङमुखावूर्ध्वतलौ ज्ञेयौ लघुमुखाविति .. 73 ..
text_mt: Hands made caturasra and likewise made haṃsapakṣa, / facing obliquely with upturned palms, are to be known as laghumukha.

sanskrit_iast:
tāveva maṇidhanvāṃtāvarālakacitau karau ..
jñeyāvabhinaye tvetau hyarālakhaṭakāmukhau .. 74 ..
meaning:
तावेव मणिधन्वांतावरालकचितौ करौ ..
ज्ञेयावभिनये त्वेतौ ह्यरालखटकामुखौ .. 74 ..
text_mt: Those same hands, with tips extending to the wrists and curved in arāla, / should be known in dramatic performance as arālakhaṭakāmukha.

sanskrit_iast:
bhujau sakūrparāgrau tu kuṭilāvartitau karau ..
adhomukhatalāviddhāvāviddhāviti kīrtitau .. 75 ..
meaning:
भुजौ सकूर्पराग्रौ तु कुटिलावर्तितौ करौ ..
अधोमुखतलाविद्धावाविद्धाविति कीर्तितौ .. 75 ..
text_mt: The arms with elbows forward, the hands curved and rotated, / their palms turned downwards and pierced, are declared to be āviddha.

sanskrit_iast:
sarpaśīrṣau yadā hastau bhavatāṃ svastika sthitau ..
tiryakprasāritāsyau ca jñeyau sūcīmukhāviti .. 76 ..
meaning:
सर्पशीर्षौ यदा हस्तौ भवतां स्वस्तिक स्थितौ ..
तिर्यक्प्रसारितास्यौ च ज्ञेयौ सूचीमुखाविति .. 76 ..
text_mt: When the hands are sarpaśīrṣa and placed in a svastika, / with their faces extended obliquely, they are known as sūcīmukha.

sanskrit_iast:
recitau cāpi vijñeyau haṃsapakṣādbhutabhramau ..
prasāritottānatalau racitāveva saṃ jñitau .. 77 ..
meaning:
रेचितौ चापि विज्ञेयौ हंसपक्षाद्भुतभ्रमौ ..
प्रसारितोत्तानतलौ रचितावेव सं ज्ञितौ .. 77 ..
text_mt: They are to be known as recita when moving with wonderful rotation from haṃsapakṣa; / extended with palms turned upwards, they are designated as recita.

sanskrit_iast:
caturasro bhavedvāmaḥ savyahastaśca recitaḥ ..
vijñeyo nāṭyatattvajñairevaṃ recitasaṃjñitaḥ .. 78 ..
meaning:
चतुरस्रो भवेद्वामः सव्यहस्तश्च रेचितः ..
विज्ञेयो नाट्यतत्त्वज्ञैरेवं रेचितसंज्ञितः .. 78 ..
text_mt: The left hand is caturasra, and the right hand is recita; / this is known by knowers of the truth of drama as designated recita.

sanskrit_iast:
añcitau kūrparābhyāṃ tu tri patākau yadā karau ..
kiṃcittiryaggatāvetāvāvahittha prakīrtitaḥ .. 79 ..
meaning:
अञ्चितौ कूर्पराभ्यां तु त्रि पताकौ यदा करौ ..
किंचित्तिर्यग्गतावेतावावहित्थ प्रकीर्तितः .. 79 ..
text_mt: When the hands are tripatāka, bent from the elbows, / and move slightly obliquely, this is declared as avahittha.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇibandhananirmuktau śithilau pallavau smṛtau ..
bāhu śīviniṣkrāntau nitambau parikīrtitau .. 3.26.80 ..
meaning:
मणिबन्धननिर्मुक्तौ शिथिलौ पल्लवौ स्मृतौ ..
बाहु शीविनिष्क्रान्तौ नितम्बौ परिकीर्तितौ .. 3.26.80 ..
text_mt: Released from the wrists and loose, they are remembered as pallava. / Brought out from the head and shoulders, they are declared as nitamba.

sanskrit_iast:
aṃsadeśe pravṛttau tu paripārśvotthitau tathā ..
vijñeyau keśabaṃdhākhyau karāvācāryasammatau .. 81 ..
meaning:
अंसदेशे प्रवृत्तौ तु परिपार्श्वोत्थितौ तथा ..
विज्ञेयौ केशबंधाख्यौ करावाचार्यसम्मतौ .. 81 ..
text_mt: Proceeding from the region of the shoulders and raised at the sides, / the hands are known as keśabandha, accepted by the teachers.

sanskrit_iast:
tiryakprasāritāveva pārśvasaṃsthau tathaiva ca ..
latākhyau tu karau jñeyau nṛttābhinayanaṃ prati .. 82 ..
meaning:
तिर्यक्प्रसारितावेव पार्श्वसंस्थौ तथैव च ..
लताख्यौ तु करौ ज्ञेयौ नृत्ताभिनयनं प्रति .. 82 ..
text_mt: Extended obliquely and positioned at the sides, / the hands are known as latā in the dramatic enactment of dance.

sanskrit_iast:
samunnatā latāhastaḥ pārśvātpārśvaviloḍitaḥ ..
dvitīyaḥ khaṭakākhyaśca karihastaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 83 ..
meaning:
समुन्नता लताहस्तः पार्श्वात्पार्श्वविलोडितः ..
द्वितीयः खटकाख्यश्च करिहस्तः प्रकीर्तितः .. 83 ..
text_mt: One hand is latā, raised high and swaying from side to side, / and the second is khaṭakā; it is declared as karihasta.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭiśīrṣaniviṣṭāgrau tripatākau yadā karau ..
pakṣāvañcitakau vāme tadā jñeyau prayoktṛbhiḥ .. 84 ..
meaning:
कटिशीर्षनिविष्टाग्रौ त्रिपताकौ यदा करौ ..
पक्षावञ्चितकौ वामे तदा ज्ञेयौ प्रयोक्तृभिः .. 84 ..
text_mt: When the hands are tripatāka with tips placed at the waist and head, / they are known by practitioners as pakṣāvañcita on the left.

sanskrit_iast:
tāveva tu parāvṛttau pakṣāghātau karāviti ..
adhomukhatalāviddhau jñeyau garuḍapakṣakau .. 85 ..
meaning:
तावेव तु परावृत्तौ पक्षाघातौ कराविति ..
अधोमुखतलाविद्धौ ज्ञेयौ गरुडपक्षकौ .. 85 ..
text_mt: Those same hands reversed are the pakṣāghāta hands; / with palms turned downwards and pierced, they are to be known as garuḍapakṣaka.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā prasāritabhujau daṇḍapakṣāviti smṛtau ..
tau cordhvamaṇḍalau jñeyau gurudeśavivartanāt .. 86 ..
meaning:
तथा प्रसारितभुजौ दण्डपक्षाविति स्मृतौ ..
तौ चोर्ध्वमण्डलौ ज्ञेयौ गुरुदेशविवर्तनात् .. 86 ..
text_mt: Likewise, with arms extended, they are remembered as daṇḍapakṣa; / and those two are known as ūrdhvamaṇḍala from rotating in the upper region.

sanskrit_iast:
tāveva pārśvavinyastau vijñeyau pārśvamaṇḍalau ..
veṣṭitāveṣṭitau hastau tayormaṇḍalakau smṛtau .. 87 ..
meaning:
तावेव पार्श्वविन्यस्तौ विज्ञेयौ पार्श्वमण्डलौ ..
वेष्टितावेष्टितौ हस्तौ तयोर्मण्डलकौ स्मृतौ .. 87 ..
text_mt: Those same hands placed at the sides are to be known as pārśvamaṇḍala. / The two hands, winding and unwinding, are remembered as their maṇḍalaka.

sanskrit_iast:
tāveva maṇibandhāntau svastikākṛtisaṃjñitau ..
svastikāviti vikhyātau vikhyātau ca prakī rṇakau .. 88 ..
meaning:
तावेव मणिबन्धान्तौ स्वस्तिकाकृतिसंज्ञितौ ..
स्वस्तिकाविति विख्यातौ विख्यातौ च प्रकी र्णकौ .. 88 ..
text_mt: Those same hands at the ends of the wrists, designated as having the form of a svastika, / are celebrated as svastika, and also celebrated as prakīrṇaka.

sanskrit_iast:
dvāveva padmakośābhau padmakośāviti smṛtau ..
karāvuddhe jitāgrau tu vijñeyāvalipallavau .. 89 ..
meaning:
द्वावेव पद्मकोशाभौ पद्मकोशाविति स्मृतौ ..
करावुद्धे जिताग्रौ तु विज्ञेयावलिपल्लवौ .. 89 ..
text_mt: Both resembling padmakośa are remembered as padmakośa; / the hands with agitated and turned tips are to be known as alipallava.

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvaprasāritau viddhau vijñeyāvulvaṇāviti ..
pallavau tu śirodeśe samprāptau lalitāviti .. 3.26.90 ..
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वप्रसारितौ विद्धौ विज्ञेयावुल्वणाविति ..
पल्लवौ तु शिरोदेशे सम्प्राप्तौ ललिताविति .. 3.26.90 ..
text_mt: Extended upwards and pierced, they are known as ulvaṇa; / but when the two pallava hands reach the region of the head, they are lalita.

sanskrit_iast:
kūrparasvastikanyastau lalitāvalitau smṛtau ..
saṃyutā viyutāścaiva nṛttahastāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 91 ..
meaning:
कूर्परस्वस्तिकन्यस्तौ ललितावलितौ स्मृतौ ..
संयुता वियुताश्चैव नृत्तहस्ताः प्रकीर्तिताः .. 91 ..
text_mt: Placed in a svastika at the elbows, they are remembered as lalitāvalita. / Thus the dance hands, both combined and single, are declared.

sanskrit_iast:
nānārtharasasaṃyuktaṃ prayogakālasaṃśrayam ..
vijñeyaṃ nṛttahastānāṃ tena nābhihitaṃ mayā .. 92..
meaning:
नानार्थरससंयुक्तं प्रयोगकालसंश्रयम् ..
विज्ञेयं नृत्तहस्तानां तेन नाभिहितं मया .. 92..
text_mt: Endowed with various meanings and sentiments, and dependent on the time of performance, / is what is to be understood of the dance hands; therefore it has not been fully stated by me.

sanskrit_iast:
ādhigraste jagante ca niyamasthe jagardite ..
matte pramatte cintāyāṃ nābhineyaḥ karo bhavet .. 93 ..
meaning:
आधिग्रस्ते जगन्ते च नियमस्थे जगर्दिते ..
मत्ते प्रमत्ते चिन्तायां नाभिनेयः करो भवेत् .. 93 ..
text_mt: In one seized by anguish, in one dead, in one practicing self-restraint, in one afflicted by illness, / in an intoxicated person, in a negligent one, or in sorrow, no hand gesture is to be performed.

sanskrit_iast:
udveṣṭaṃ samaveṣṭaṃ ca viceṣṭitavivartite ..
karmedaṃ nṛttahastānāṃ vijñeyaṃ ca caturvidham .. 94 ..
meaning:
उद्वेष्टं समवेष्टं च विचेष्टितविवर्तिते ..
कर्मेदं नृत्तहस्तानां विज्ञेयं च चतुर्विधम् .. 94 ..
text_mt: Outward winding, inward winding, gesturing, and rotating— / this fourfold movement of the dance hands is to be known.

sanskrit_iast:
kāryā lalitasaṃcārā nṛttahastāparā budhaiḥ..
lālityameva vijñeyaṃ vṛttasya pratibodhanam ..95..
meaning:
कार्या ललितसंचारा नृत्तहस्तापरा बुधैः..
लालित्यमेव विज्ञेयं वृत्तस्य प्रतिबोधनम् ..95..
text_mt: Other dance hands should be executed by the wise with graceful movement; / grace alone is to be known as the awakening of the dance.

sanskrit_iast:
deśaṃ kālaṃ prayogaṃ ca hyarthayuktimavekṣya ca ..
hastā ete prayoktavyā strīṇāṃ nṝṇāṃ ca nartake .. 96 ..
meaning:
देशं कालं प्रयोगं च ह्यर्थयुक्तिमवेक्ष्य च ..
हस्ता एते प्रयोक्तव्या स्त्रीणां नॄणां च नर्तके .. 96 ..
text_mt: Considering the place, time, dramatic application, and fitness of meaning, / these hand gestures should be employed for women and men in dance.

text_mt:
These hand gestures have been spoken by me, O hero among men; for this entire dance depends on the hands. / Therefore, effort should be made regarding the hands, endowed with skill, graceful dance, and dramatic expression.
3.27 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Verbal, and likewise costume and make-up, physical, and emotional: / fourfold is dramatic representation declared by experts in drama.
The verbal is said to be by speech; hear of costume and make-up, O lord of men. / It is to be known as fourfold: model-work, ornament,
and painting of the body, as well as living beings. / Whether with clay, with wood, with cloth, or with leather,
or an imitation made with metals, it is designated as model-work. / For gods, dānavas, and yakṣas, and for elephants, horses, beasts, and birds,
masks should be made by experts in drama through model-work. / Ornament, moreover, is to be known as consisting of garlands, jewellery, and garments,
diverse in combination, applied to the limbs and secondary limbs. / An intelligent person should execute that after comprehending the role and class,

text_mt:
as well as the sovereignty and status in the region, O best of kings. / Next I shall declare to you the painting of the body produced from colours, O king.
White, red, yellow, black, and green: / these are celebrated as the five primary colours, O best of kings.
By the combination of one, two, or three, and through the imagination of states, / it is impossible to count the intermediate colours in the world.
Because of their extreme relevance in the world, O bull among kings, / I shall explain the division of the two colours: dark and fair.
Since complexion is proclaimed to be of two kinds for everyone here: / among them, the fair is fivefold, and the dark should be of twelve kinds.
Gold-fair, ivory-fair, and also blooming-sandalwood-fair, / fair like an autumn cloud, and like the moon—the fair is remembered as fivefold.
First is reddish-dark; contiguous to it is mung-bean-dark; / then dūrvā-sprout-dark, and pale-dark, O king;

Vāsuki should be made dark, but the serpents are fair in the Dvāpara age; / daityas and dānavas, rākṣasas, followers of the guhyakas,

the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, and Kaliṅgas are mostly dark in colour. / Twice-borns should be made moon-coloured, and kṣatriyas lotus-like;
vaiśyas slightly pale, and śūdras dark in colour. / Bhūtas, gandharvas, and apsarases are remembered as of various colours.
Kings have the colour and lustre of a lotus, as do people who are happy. / Evil-doers, those possessed by planetary spirits, the diseased, those devoted to asceticism,
and those fatigued by labour are dark, [even if] born of noble family. / The colour of what is seen with one's own eyes should be made similar [to reality].
For gods, gandharvas, and siddhas, and for youths, O king, / no beard should be made, nor for those who have undertaken initiation.
Heavenly men and also vidyādharas, / amorous men and kings are wearers of trimmed beards.

For those whose vows are unfulfilled, the sorrowful, ascetics, / and sages bound for a long time, a long beard is proclaimed.
The dress of a śūdra follows the pursuit of dharma, O lord of men; / of merchants, chamberlains, and likewise of brahmins,
the dress of kings should be variegated, and of courtesans, O Yādava. / The dress of others should conform to their status according to ordinary life.

broad crowns of a single band, auspicious, should be made. / For vidyādharas, siddhas, and likewise for monkeys,

text_mt:
That which is called sajjīva, I will state its characteristic: / the entrance of animals is designated as sajjīva.
Their nature should be made by means of models containing men within; / likewise, for those with weapons in hand, beautiful weapons should be made.
Thus, according to worldly convention, by one's own intellect and resources, / one should properly arrange the theatrical accessories here.
The discharge of weapons should not be done on the stage, O foremost of royal scions. / This extrinsic representation has been explained in brief; henceforth I will declare to you the bodily representation.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, named Extrinsic Representation, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara.
3.28 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall explain to you general representation; / in that, effort should be made, established within the theatrical art.
Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell— / the wise actor should represent the sense organs and sense objects through emotional expression.

These five sense objects are declared to be threefold: / agreeable, disagreeable, and neutral, O best of kings.
By the delight of the limbs, by horripilation, / and by actions of abundant tears, one should depict everything agreeable.
With an averted head, with averted eyes, / and with the contraction of the eyes and nose, one should indicate what is disagreeable.

Then, by looking downward, one should represent things situated on the ground. / The wise one should enact the moon, moonlight, the face, and the wind through touch.
The sun, dust, smoke, and fires [should be enacted] by veiling oneself with cloth; / and one should represent the heat of the ground and warmth by sighs and longing speech.
With an upward squinting glance [one should show] the midday sun, / and when rising and setting, one should display it in the sense of wonder.

Accompanied by self-control, with a serene face, / one should depict autumn filled with the sight of diverse blossoms.

By the trembling of the limbs and as desiring another, by those who know it, / winter should be expressed by middling and low characters.
By the trembling of the head, teeth, and lips, by the contraction of the limbs, / by low groans, and with hissing sounds, the representation of cold takes place.
With undertakings generating delight and with eager enjoyments, / spring should be enacted through the display of various flowers.
By wiping off sweat, by seeking the shade on the ground, / and through the touch of hot wind, the depiction of summer occurs.
From hearing a deep roar, the rainy season should be enacted. / The enactment of the seasons, in pleasure and in pain, should be made with speech.
In natural acting, the vaiṣṇava stance should be assumed by men; / the āyuta and the avahittha [stances] should be assumed naturally by women.
The movement of men is endowed with fortitude, good conduct, and proper limbs; / the movement of women should be performed with gentle movements and gestures.

Jealous anger should be enacted devoid of garlands and ornaments, / with a shaking of the head, and likewise with breakdowns of composure.
With face cast down and sighing, a man should display sorrow; / for women, that is [shown] by striking the ground with the hands and by weeping.
Weeping is remembered as twofold: arising from joy [or from grief]. / One should depict it with a joyous or unjoyous face.
Fear of men occurs through gestures of agitation and alarm, / through seeking a protector, and by crying out loudly;
and by embracing a man, fear of women should be performed. / With two trembling tripatāka fingers one should represent
the parrot, the myna, and whatever small birds there are; / peafowl, cranes, swans, and the like, and whatever birds dwell naturally on the ground,

He should display a gathering, a very large army, and something widely spread out / with both hands [in] patāka raised up. / He should display heroism, the arrogance of fortitude, pride, generosity, and high station / with the arāla [hand] placed at the forehead.

Making the hand slightly stretched out with the palm turned downward and upward, / the representation of two [things is made]: catching a creature in a hole, and house by house.
For those afflicted by desire, those with fever, and those whose minds are struck by a curse, / their representation should be done with sighs and with trembling.
A direct representation should be made for swinging on a swing. / Now I shall explain speech addressed to the air and [speeches] kept to oneself.
Aside to one person, speaking into the wing, and also / conversation with another—that is considered speech to the air.
What is inaudible to others is called janāntika here; / apavāritaka is spoken of as repeated in the ear.

Covering [the mouth] with the hand [held in] tripatāka, actors / should perform janāntika, and likewise apavāritaka.
In the representation of dreaming, it should be with a faltering voice. / For the old, one should employ cunning with faltering, stumbling syllables.
For children, [the voice] has unfinished syllables and sweet tones; / for the sick, one should employ [a voice] accompanied by long sighs and languid.
With a long sigh one should act out the moment of death; / the representation of one who is dead should be by the condition of motionless limbs. / O king, I shall [now] explain sattva-based representation in the sentiments and emotional states.
Only this much in representation can be spoken by me to you, foremost of kings; / for drama is an imitation of the whole universe, so it cannot be spoken in its entirety, O lord.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall explain to you the characteristics of gaits. / In an elevated gait by nature, [the lifting of the foot] should be equal [in height] to the knee and waist.

in transformation, in concealment, and likewise when filled with longing, / in the erotic, in sorrow, and in moving at will—
in all these alone, a steady gait should be executed by the wise. / In uneasiness, in trembling, in fear, in terror,
in agitation, and in joy, and whatever action is hurried, / on hearing what is disagreeable, in tossing about, and on seeing a marvel,
also in urgent business, and likewise in pursuing an enemy, / in following an offense, and in pursuing wild beasts—
in actions of this kind, one should employ a swift gait. / An erotic gait should be used when a composed lover is present.

the two hands should also be made by actors to follow the feet. / When going [as] a secret lover, not overly adorned,

The furious is considered threefold: by bodily form, by nature, and by costume. / With his body wet with blood, holding intestines like lotuses as ornaments,
bearing many weapons, he is proclaimed [furious] by the furious costume. / Harsh, speaking with threats, and pitiless by nature—
the gait of the various [types of] furious [character] has an interval of four spans. / Where the ground is unpleasant, crowded with cremation grounds and battle,
near and drawn back, there is the odious gait. / And in the heroic [sentiment], a gait should be performed accompanied by sweeping strides of the feet.
In wonder and in joy, the stride of the feet is cast out; / the gait is declared to have steady steps in the pathetic sentiment.
There no bodily grace is to be shown, nor such measure; / the gait has a swaying body, rigid, and slack.

For one heavily struck, a gait should be performed with a huddled body. / A swift [gait] should be used in the terrible [sentiment], and a rigid one according to circumstances.
When a deformed creature is seen, the gait has wide-open eyes. / For ascetics, the gait should be slow, with the gaze cast a yoke's length ahead.
In darkness, the gait should also be slow from touching with the hands. / For one standing in a chariot, the gait should be performed with slow steps.
Assuming the samapāda posture of the wise, he should adopt the movement of a chariot, / holding a bow with one hand, and likewise the chariot pole with the other.
And his charioteer should have the appearance of holding a whip. / For one seated in an aerial chariot, the gait should be joyous.
Ascents and descents [are indicated] by movements with upward and downward glances; / moving in the sky should be performed with circular turns.
Falling from the sky should be done with feet coming straight and raised; / climbing high should be performed with step-by-step strides,

and descent should be performed with [feet] close together as if apprehensive. / Movement in water should have raised footsteps.
In climbing a tree, there should be movement with raised hands, / with feet crossed, stepped aside, and turned sideways.
By holding a goad, [he indicates] an elephant; by holding a bridle, a horse; / by holding reins, he should represent the gait of others.
In riding a horse, the gait should be executed in the vaiśākha posture; / the gait of serpents should be performed with crossed feet.
For a gallant, the gait should be executed with graceful strides; / for a chamberlain, a trembling and stumbling gait should be performed.
The gait of an emaciated person should be characterized by staggering and halting breaths, / and likewise for one afflicted by disease, and indeed one fatigued from ascetic penance.
And for one who has traversed a long road, [the gait should consist] of walking slowly and sluggishly. / But for an intoxicated person, the gait is to be made staggering to both sides.

text_mt:
For an insane person as well, the gait is to be made according to theatrical representation; / he should be raving incoherently, dirty, and hairy.
The gait of disabled people should be made according to the requirements of the action; / for a corpulent body, a gait that drags the body is to be performed.
For the vidūṣaka, a gait giving rise to laughter is likewise to be performed, / having placed a natural crook in his left hand.
In walking, servants should take pleasure, and their gaze should be wandering about the noble ones; / [the gaits] of men born in various regions arise from their natural character.
The gait of wild beasts and cattle should be performed [accordingly], O king; / for the rest, one should employ the postures in accordance with the thematic context.
The gait of superior characters is endowed with firmness; the gait of middling characters is moderate; / the gait of common inferior characters is rapid; the three tempos are to be applied according to character.
The movement of footsteps, varying on stage with comings and goings, O foremost of kings, / is always to be done under the control of the stage-space, having properly examined the stage appropriately.

The gait of women should have a graceful movement; that of men should be steady and bold; / the movement of gait should be applied according to the context—this much has been told to you, O lion among kings.
First, the costume corresponds to age; and the movement of gait corresponds to the costume; / drama follows the movement of gait; and dramatic representation must be made corresponding to drama.
3.30 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The comic, erotic, pathetic, furious, terrifying, / odious, marvelous, and peaceful: nine rasas are remembered in dramatic art.
The peaceful rasa is autonomous here, established quite distinct; / for from the erotic arises the comic, and from the furious arises the pathetic.
And from the heroic arises the marvelous, and from the odious the terrifying; / their body colors and their dramatic representation are remembered as internal.
The color of the peaceful rasa is declared to be natural, O king; / the erotic is dark blue, and the furious is proclaimed to be red.
The comic is to be known as white, and the terrifying as black; / the heroic is to be known as fair, and the marvelous is recorded as yellow.

text_mt:
The pathetic is dove-colored, and the odious is blue; / the comic has the pramathas as deity, while the erotic has Viṣṇu as presiding deity.
The furious has Rudra as its presiding deity, and the pathetic has Yama as presiding deity; / Mahākāla is the deity of the odious, and the god of death is the deity of the terrifying.
The heroic has Mahendra as deity, and the marvelous has Brahmā as presiding deity; / the deity of the peaceful is to be known as the Supreme Cosmic Person alone.
The arising of the peaceful, O king, is remembered to be from dispassion; / and it is to be represented through the assumption of ascetic garb,
and through compassion for all beings, meditation, and embarking on the path of liberation; / where there is neither pleasure nor pain, neither hatred nor envy,
and equanimity toward all beings, that celebrated rasa is the peaceful. / The arising of the comic, however, is from incoherent talk,
and it is determined that it arises from improper dress; / and it is proclaimed as twofold: situated in oneself and situated in another.
Situated in oneself is from one's own laughing; situated in another is from making another laugh; / it is then threefold for superior, inferior, and middling characters.

text_mt:
With slightly trembling cheeks, with glances endowed with grace, / and with teeth unseen, is the smile of superior persons.
Showing the teeth is described for middling persons; / for inferior persons, it is with tears and with sound, O king.
The erotic is declared to be twofold: from union and from separation; / in the case of that caused by separation in love, world-weariness is the mode of representation.
In separation in love, ten stages of passion are designated; / pleasure of the eyes is designated as the first, O king,
and attachment of the mind is declared in the second; / and continuous recollecting is declared in the third.
Disruption of sleep is in the fourth, and emaciation in the fifth; / turning away from sense objects is stated in the sixth, O king;
loss of shame is in the seventh; madness immediately after that; / fainting in the ninth; and death would be in the tenth.

आश्चर्येण समुत्पत्तिरद्भुतं तत्प्रकीर्तितम् .. 26 ..
प्रस्फुरिताक्षिरोमाञ्चैरङ्गुलीभ्रमणादिभिः ..
स्वेदेन चाभिनेयः स्यादद्भुतस्तु तथा रसः .. 27 ..
text_mt:
There, the representation of union is between two radiant lovers, / where there are garlands and unguents, abounding in pleasure and endowed with desired objects.
The union of a man and a woman is called the erotic; / from grief, O king of kings, the pathetic rasa likewise arises.
Its dramatic representation here is by trembling limbs, sighs, lamentations, weeping, / loss of facial color, and drying up [of the mouth].
The arising of the furious rasa takes place from anger; / by red eyes, knit brows, rage, intolerance, along with reckless deeds,
by oppression, and by clashing of weapons, its representation is done here; / the arising of the odious takes place from disgust.
Its [representation is] by turning away the nose and likewise by agitation; / the marvelous is proclaimed as having its origin from astonishment.
With wide-open eyes, horripilation, rotating of the fingers and so forth, / and with perspiration, the marvelous rasa is likewise to be represented.

sanskrit_iast:
nāṭyasya mūlaṃ tu rasaḥ pradiṣṭo rasena hīnaṃ na hi vṛttamasti ..
tasmātprayatnena rasāśrayasya vṛttasya yatnaṃ puruṣeṇa kāryam .. 28 ..
meaning:
नाट्यस्य मूलं तु रसः प्रदिष्टो रसेन हीनं न हि वृत्तमस्ति ..
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन रसाश्रयस्य वृत्तस्य यत्नं पुरुषेण कार्यम् .. 28 ..
text_mt: Rasa is declared to be the root of dramatic art, for no dramatic plot exists devoid of rasa; / therefore, an effort must be made by a person with great care concerning a plot that has rasa as its foundation.

sanskrit_iast:
3.31
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bhāvādhyāyamato vacmi tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu ..
hāsādyāḥ kathitā bhāvāḥ pañcāśattvekavarjitāḥ .. 1 ..
meaning:
3.31
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
भावाध्यायमतो वच्मि तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ..
हासाद्याः कथिता भावाः पञ्चाशत्त्वेकवर्जिताः .. 1 ..
text_mt: 3.31 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Next, I will tell the chapter on emotional states; hear that from me as I speak: / forty-nine emotional states, beginning with laughter, have been declared.
title: Āyāmocchrāyamānavarṇanaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
paraceṣṭānukaraṇādyaddhāsyamupajāyate ..
smitahāsābhihasitairabhineyasya paṇḍitaiḥ .. 2 ..
meaning:
परचेष्टानुकरणाद्यद्धास्यमुपजायते ..
स्मितहासाभिहसितैरभिनेयस्य पण्डितैः .. 2 ..
text_mt: The laughter that arises from imitating another’s actions / should be represented by the wise through smiles, laughter, and loud laughter.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭārthaviṣayaprāptau ratirityupajāyate ..
saumyatvādabhineyā sā vāṅmādhuryādibhistathā .. 3 ..
meaning:
इष्टार्थविषयप्राप्तौ रतिरित्युपजायते ..
सौम्यत्वादभिनेया सा वाङ्माधुर्यादिभिस्तथा .. 3 ..
text_mt: Upon attaining a desired object or sensory pleasure, love arises. / It should be represented through gentleness, sweetness of speech, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭabandhuviyogena dhananāśena pārthiva ..
śoko bhavati tasya syādruditābhinayakriyā .. 4 ..
meaning:
इष्टबन्धुवियोगेन धननाशेन पार्थिव ..
शोको भवति तस्य स्याद्रुदिताभिनयक्रिया .. 4 ..
text_mt: From separation from a dear relative or loss of wealth, O king, / sorrow arises; its dramatic action should be weeping.

sanskrit_iast:
krodhaścatuḥprakāraśca kartavyo nāṭyayoktṛbhiḥ ..
ripujo gurujaścaiva bhṛtyajaḥ praṇayodbhavaḥ .. 5 ..
meaning:
क्रोधश्चतुःप्रकारश्च कर्तव्यो नाट्ययोक्तृभिः ..
रिपुजो गुरुजश्चैव भृत्यजः प्रणयोद्भवः .. 5 ..
text_mt: Anger is of four kinds to be presented by directors of dramatic performance: / born of an enemy, born of a guru, born of a servant, and born of affection.

sanskrit_iast:
niryantritaḥ sa śatrūṇāṃ gurūṇāṃ svedasaṃyutaḥ ..
bhṛtyānāṃ ca dayāluḥ syātstrīṇāṃ ca praṇayodbhavaḥ .. 6 ..
meaning:
निर्यन्त्रितः स शत्रूणां गुरूणां स्वेदसंयुतः ..
भृत्यानां च दयालुः स्यात्स्त्रीणां च प्रणयोद्भवः .. 6 ..
text_mt: That [directed toward] enemies is unrestrained; toward gurus, it is accompanied by perspiration; / toward servants, it should be compassionate; and toward women, it arises from affection.

sanskrit_iast:
karmātiśayanirvṛttau vismayo harṣasaṃbhavaḥ ..
siddhisthāne tvasau sādhyo romāñcahasanādibhiḥ ..7..
meaning:
कर्मातिशयनिर्वृत्तौ विस्मयो हर्षसंभवः ..
सिद्धिस्थाने त्वसौ साध्यो रोमाञ्चहसनादिभिः ..7..
text_mt: Upon the achievement of an extraordinary deed, astonishment arises, born of joy; / in the realm of success, it is to be effected through horripilation, laughter, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
asau mohābhinirvṛttau vyavasāyanayātmakaḥ..
utsāhastvabhineyaḥ syādapramādakriyādibhiḥ..8..
meaning:
असौ मोहाभिनिर्वृत्तौ व्यवसायनयात्मकः..
उत्साहस्त्वभिनेयः स्यादप्रमादक्रियादिभिः..8..
text_mt: In the absence of delusion, [arising] from resolve and prudent conduct, / enthusiasm should be represented through vigilant actions and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
svāparādhasamudbhūtaṃ bhayaṃ nāmeha jāyate ..
vepathutrāsapatanairabhineyasya sambhramaiḥ..9..
meaning:
स्वापराधसमुद्भूतं भयं नामेह जायते ..
वेपथुत्रासपतनैरभिनेयस्य सम्भ्रमैः..9..
text_mt: Arising from one’s own offense, fear is produced here; / it is to be represented through trembling, terror, falling, and agitated movements.

sanskrit_iast: bībhatsadarśanādyaistu jugupsā nāma jāyate..3.31.10..
meaning: बीभत्सदर्शनाद्यैस्तु जुगुप्सा नाम जायते..3.31.10..
text_mt: Disgust arises from the sight of repulsive things.

sanskrit_iast:
udvejanaissahṛllekhairabhineyo vikūṇanaiḥ..
dāridryeṣṭavināśe ca nirvedo nāma jāyate..11..
meaning:
उद्वेजनैस्सहृल्लेखैरभिनेयो विकूणनैः..
दारिद्र्येष्टविनाशे च निर्वेदो नाम जायते..11..
text_mt: It should be represented through shuddering, retching, and contracting the limbs. / Upon poverty or the destruction of what is dear, despondency arises.

sanskrit_iast:
parasparaviniḥśvāsaistasyābhinayanakriyā..
vānte virakte śrānte ca glāniḥ syāttapasā tathā..12..
meaning:
परस्परविनिःश्वासैस्तस्याभिनयनक्रिया..
वान्ते विरक्ते श्रान्ते च ग्लानिः स्यात्तपसा तथा..12..
text_mt: Its dramatic representation is through mutual deep sighs. / In one who has vomited, one who is purged, one who is exhausted, or through asceticism, exhaustion occurs.

sanskrit_iast: mandākramaṇakampādyaiḥ kṣāmatvenaṃ ca darśayet ..13..
meaning: मन्दाक्रमणकम्पाद्यैः क्षामत्वेनं च दर्शयेत् ..13..
text_mt: One should show it through slow movement, trembling, and emaciation.

sanskrit_iast:
cauryādibhirgṛhītasya śaṅkā nāmeha jāyate ..
ākārāvaraṇaṃ tasyāḥ kāryaṃ digavalokanam ..
parāparādhasambhūtā asūyā nāma jāyate .. 14 ..
meaning:
चौर्यादिभिर्गृहीतस्य शङ्का नामेह जायते ..
आकारावरणं तस्याः कार्यं दिगवलोकनम् ..
परापराधसम्भूता असूया नाम जायते .. 14 ..
text_mt: In one apprehended for theft and the like, apprehension arises here; / its representation should be concealment of the body and looking in all directions. / Arising from another's offense, envy arises.

sanskrit_iast:
guṇanāśanavidveṣaiḥ sābhineyā tathā budhaiḥ ..
madyopayogena mado jāyate ca tribhistathā .. 15 ..
meaning:
गुणनाशनविद्वेषैः साभिनेया तथा बुधैः ..
मद्योपयोगेन मदो जायते च त्रिभिस्तथा .. 15 ..
text_mt: It should be represented by the wise through decrying virtues and through malice. / Through the use of intoxicating liquor, intoxication arises, and it is threefold:

sanskrit_iast:
uttamādhamamadhyatvātpuruṣāṇāṃ svabhāvataḥ ..
dṛgbhrameṇottamānāṃ syānmadhyānāṃ vākpralāpataḥ .. 16 ...
meaning:
उत्तमाधममध्यत्वात्पुरुषाणां स्वभावतः ..
दृग्भ्रमेणोत्तमानां स्यान्मध्यानां वाक्प्रलापतः .. 16 ...
text_mt: due to the nature of persons being superior, inferior, or middling. / For superior ones, it is by rolling of the eyes; for middling ones, through incoherent speech;

sanskrit_iast:
adhamānāṃ ca patanairasambaddhaparikramaiḥ ..
āyāsenādhamanāñca śramo nāmeha jāyate..17..
meaning:
अधमानां च पतनैरसम्बद्धपरिक्रमैः ..
आयासेनाधमनाञ्च श्रमो नामेह जायते..17..
text_mt: and for inferior ones, through fallings and unsteady walking. / Through exertion and walking, weariness arises here.

sanskrit_iast:
gātramardanaviśvāsajṛmbhaṇaistatprayojayet ..
garveṇa khedādrāgeṇa hyālasya syātsvabhāvataḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
गात्रमर्दनविश्वासजृम्भणैस्तत्प्रयोजयेत् ..
गर्वेण खेदाद्रागेण ह्यालस्य स्यात्स्वभावतः .. 18 ..
text_mt: One should employ it through rubbing the limbs, deep sighs, and yawning. / From pride, distress, or passion, indolence arises naturally.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ śayanāsanasevanāt ..
daurgatyena manastāpāddainyaṃ nāmeha jāyate .. 19 ...
meaning:
तस्य प्रयोगः कर्तव्यः शयनासनसेवनात् ..
दौर्गत्येन मनस्तापाद्दैन्यं नामेह जायते .. 19 ...
text_mt: Its performance should be executed by resorting to lying down and sitting. / From destitution or mental distress, wretchedness arises here.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdayasya vitarkeṇa tasya tvabhinayo bhavet ..
asthāne taskarāndṛṣṭvā trāsanairvividhaistathā .. 3.31.20 ..
meaning:
हृदयस्य वितर्केण तस्य त्वभिनयो भवेत् ..
अस्थाने तस्करान्दृष्ट्वा त्रासनैर्विविधैस्तथा .. 3.31.20 ..
text_mt: Its dramatic representation should be through deliberation of the heart. / Having seen thieves in an inappropriate place, and through various frights,

sanskrit_iast:
tatpratīkāraśūnyasya mohaḥ samupajāyate ...
vyasanenābhighātena vairānusmaraṇena ca ..21 ..
meaning:
तत्प्रतीकारशून्यस्य मोहः समुपजायते ...
व्यसनेनाभिघातेन वैरानुस्मरणेन च ..21 ..
text_mt: stupefaction arises in one who is devoid of remedy. / Through calamity, physical blow, or remembering enmity,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvendriyāṇāṃ mohena sa tu kāryaḥ prayoktṛbhiḥ ..
smaraṇātpūrvavṛttānāṃ smṛtirnāmeha jāyate .. 22 ..
meaning:
सर्वेन्द्रियाणां मोहेन स तु कार्यः प्रयोक्तृभिः ..
स्मरणात्पूर्ववृत्तानां स्मृतिर्नामेह जायते .. 22 ..
text_mt: it must be enacted by performers through the stupefaction of all the senses. / From recollection of past events, memory arises here;

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛśamutkṣepaṇāttasyāḥ prayogaḥ kāryalolanāt ..
lokaṃ vṛttāntavijñānād vṛttirnāmeha jāyate ..23..
meaning:
भृशमुत्क्षेपणात्तस्याः प्रयोगः कार्यलोलनात् ..
लोकं वृत्तान्तविज्ञानाद् वृत्तिर्नामेह जायते ..23..
text_mt: its performance is through raising [the brows] repeatedly and rolling the eyes toward the object. / From knowledge of the world’s events, fortitude arises here;

sanskrit_iast:
prayojyo labdhabhogena alabdhasya vivarjitam ..
krīḍā nāmeha bhavati cāpalyāddharṣasaṃbhavā .. 24 ..
meaning:
प्रयोज्यो लब्धभोगेन अलब्धस्य विवर्जितम् ..
क्रीडा नामेह भवति चापल्याद्धर्षसंभवा .. 24 ..
text_mt: it is to be presented through enjoying what has been obtained, avoiding [desire for] what is not obtained. / Sportiveness arises here from inconstancy, born of joy;

sanskrit_iast:
krīḍanena prayojyā sā guruvākyapratikramaiḥ ..
kṛtākāryasya rājendra vrīḍā nāmeha jāyate ..25..
meaning:
क्रीडनेन प्रयोज्या सा गुरुवाक्यप्रतिक्रमैः ..
कृताकार्यस्य राजेन्द्र व्रीडा नामेह जायते ..25..
text_mt: it should be enacted through playing and transgressing the words of elders. / In one who has done what should not be done, O foremost of kings, shame arises here.

sanskrit_iast:
adhomukhena sā kāryā mūle svīkaraṇena ca ..
jñeyā capalatā rājanna vicāryā kriyāvatā .. 26 ..
meaning:
अधोमुखेन सा कार्या मूले स्वीकरणेन च ..
ज्ञेया चपलता राजन्न विचार्या क्रियावता .. 26 ..
text_mt: It should be enacted with a downcast face and drawing [lines] on the ground. / Inconstancy, O king, is to be understood as unconsidered action by an active person.

sanskrit_iast:
ayameva prayogasya tathaiva samudāhṛtaḥ .. .
manorathānāṃ lābhe tu harṣo nāmeha jāyate ..27..
meaning:
अयमेव प्रयोगस्य तथैव समुदाहृतः .. .
मनोरथानां लाभे तु हर्षो नामेह जायते ..27..
text_mt: This very manner of its performance has been explained accordingly. / Upon the attainment of one’s desires, joy arises here;

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaprasādaromāñcaprasvedairdarśayed budhaḥ ..
sambhramājjāyate rājannāvega iti sarvadā ..28..
meaning:
सुखप्रसादरोमाञ्चप्रस्वेदैर्दर्शयेद् बुधः ..
सम्भ्रमाज्जायते राजन्नावेग इति सर्वदा ..28..
text_mt: the wise should show it through ease, serenity, horripilation, and perspiration. / Agitation, O king, always arises from sudden alarm;

sanskrit_iast:
āḥ śabdaiḥ sahasānarthā darśanīyā budhaistu te ..
viṣādasya samutpattiḥ kāryanāśena jāyate .. 09 ..
meaning:
आः शब्दैः सहसानर्था दर्शनीया बुधैस्तु ते ..
विषादस्य समुत्पत्तिः कार्यनाशेन जायते .. 09 ..
text_mt: its sudden misfortunes should be shown by the wise with cries of 'Ah!' / The arising of despair occurs through the ruin of an undertaking;

sanskrit_iast:
nidrāniḥśvasitavyājaiḥ sābhineyā tathā bhavet ..
utkaṇṭhākaraṇaiḥ sarvairautsukyaṃ nāma jāyate .. 3.31.30 ..
meaning:
निद्रानिःश्वसितव्याजैः साभिनेया तथा भवेत् ..
उत्कण्ठाकरणैः सर्वैरौत्सुक्यं नाम जायते .. 3.31.30 ..
text_mt: it should be represented through sleepiness, sighs, and pretenses. / From all the causes of longing, impatience arises;

sanskrit_iast:
ālasyagurugātratve dhyānenābhinavaiśca tat ..
rātrijāgaraṇālasyamadairnidreha jāyate .. 31 ..
meaning:
आलस्यगुरुगात्रत्वे ध्यानेनाभिनवैश्च तत् ..
रात्रिजागरणालस्यमदैर्निद्रेह जायते .. 31 ..
text_mt: that is [to be represented] through indolence, heaviness of limbs, and deep reflection. / Sleep arises here from keeping awake at night, indolence, and intoxication;

sanskrit_iast:
netrābhimardanātkāryā jṛmbhaṇā gātragauravāt ..
apasmārastu bhavati devādīnāṃ prakopataḥ .. 32 ..
meaning:
नेत्राभिमर्दनात्कार्या जृम्भणा गात्रगौरवात् ..
अपस्मारस्तु भवति देवादीनां प्रकोपतः .. 32 ..
text_mt: it should be enacted through rubbing the eyes, yawning, and heaviness of limbs. / Epilepsy occurs from the wrath of gods and the like;

sanskrit_iast:
niḥsaṃjñatvaṃ samūrddhānaṃ tasyehābhinayo bhavet ..
nidrāsamarthaṃ suptatvaṃ svapanaṃ tatra yojayet .. 33 ..
meaning:
निःसंज्ञत्वं समूर्द्धानं तस्येहाभिनयो भवेत् ..
निद्रासमर्थं सुप्तत्वं स्वपनं तत्र योजयेत् .. 33 ..
text_mt: its representation here should be unconsciousness accompanied by fallen head. / Lying down fit for sleep—there one should employ slumber;

sanskrit_iast:
nidrocchedāddhi bodhantu jṛmbhaṇaṃ tatra yojayet ..
vidyāśauryadhanādiryairamarṣo nāma jāyate .. 34 ..
meaning:
निद्रोच्छेदाद्धि बोधन्तु जृम्भणं तत्र योजयेत् ..
विद्याशौर्यधनादिर्यैरमर्षो नाम जायते .. 34 ..
text_mt: and from the cessation of sleep, one should employ awakening and yawning. / From learning, valor, wealth, and the like, indignation arises;

sanskrit_iast:
śirasaḥ kampanaistasya kāryastvabhinayo budhaiḥ ..
dhārṣṭyajaihmayādisambhūto hyavahitthobhayātmakaḥ .. 32..
meaning:
शिरसः कम्पनैस्तस्य कार्यस्त्वभिनयो बुधैः ..
धार्ष्ट्यजैह्मयादिसम्भूतो ह्यवहित्थोभयात्मकः .. 32..
text_mt: its representation should be enacted by the wise through shaking the head. / Arising from insolence, deceit, and the like, dissimulation has a twofold nature;

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāṃgagopanātkāryo'bhinayo nartanasya ca ..
cauryādijātamarthasya glāniḥ kāryā prayoktṛbhiḥ .. 36..
meaning:
सर्वांगगोपनात्कार्योऽभिनयो नर्तनस्य च ..
चौर्यादिजातमर्थस्य ग्लानिः कार्या प्रयोक्तृभिः .. 36..
text_mt: its representation is to be enacted through concealing all the limbs and dancing. / Exhaustion born of the theft and the like of property is to be enacted by performers.

sanskrit_iast:
vātaprāyastathonmādo yathā jñeyo viyogajaḥ ..
asacceṣṭāpralāpena tasyābhinayakāraṇam.. .. 37 ..
meaning:
वातप्रायस्तथोन्मादो यथा ज्ञेयो वियोगजः ..
असच्चेष्टाप्रलापेन तस्याभिनयकारणम्.. .. 37 ..
text_mt: Madness is mostly caused by wind, and likewise is to be understood as born of separation; / its dramatic representation is through improper actions and incoherent talk.

sanskrit_iast:
vyādhibhirvā prahārairvā maraṇaṃ nāma jāyate ..
kartavyobhinayastasya mūḍhendriyaviceṣṭanaiḥ .. 38 ..
meaning:
व्याधिभिर्वा प्रहारैर्वा मरणं नाम जायते ..
कर्तव्योभिनयस्तस्य मूढेन्द्रियविचेष्टनैः .. 38 ..
text_mt: From diseases or from blows, death arises; / its dramatic representation is to be enacted through senseless movements of the faculties.

sanskrit_iast:
mahābhairavanādādyaistrāsaḥ samupajāyate ..
saṃkṣiptāṅgaprakampādyaistasya tvabhinayo bhavet .. 39 ..
meaning:
महाभैरवनादाद्यैस्त्रासः समुपजायते ..
संक्षिप्ताङ्गप्रकम्पाद्यैस्तस्य त्वभिनयो भवेत् .. 39 ..
text_mt: Terror arises from loud, dreadful sounds and the like; / its dramatic representation should be through contracting the limbs, trembling, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
vicāraṇārthe saṃdehaḥ kāryo bhūkṣepakampanaiḥ ..
krodho'parādhādbhavati krodhābhinayadarśanaḥ .. 3.31.40..
meaning:
विचारणार्थे संदेहः कार्यो भूक्षेपकम्पनैः ..
क्रोधोऽपराधाद्भवति क्रोधाभिनयदर्शनः .. 3.31.40..
text_mt: In the case of deliberation, doubt should be enacted through moving the brows and trembling. / Anger arises from an offense; it shows the representation of anger.

sanskrit_iast:
bhayoparādhajo jñeyo dṛgbhayābhinayātmakaḥ ..
manorathāptijo harṣo romāñcena pradarśayet .. 41 ..
meaning:
भयोपराधजो ज्ञेयो दृग्भयाभिनयात्मकः ..
मनोरथाप्तिजो हर्षो रोमाञ्चेन प्रदर्शयेत् .. 41 ..
text_mt: Arising from fear or offense, it is to be known as having the representation of fearful eyes. / Joy born of the attainment of one’s desires should be shown through horripilation.

sanskrit_iast:
bhītakrodhaśca ubhaye romāñcasya samudbhavaḥ ..
svarabhedo bhayādraukṣyātsvarabhedena darśayet .. 42 ..
meaning:
भीतक्रोधश्च उभये रोमाञ्चस्य समुद्भवः ..
स्वरभेदो भयाद्रौक्ष्यात्स्वरभेदेन दर्शयेत् .. 42 ..
text_mt: In both fear and anger, the arising of horripilation occurs. / Change of voice arises from fear or harshness; one should show it through a broken voice.

sanskrit_iast:
śokānandasamudbhūtamaśru syādrodanena tu ..
varṇāvaratvādvijñeyaṃ vaivarṇyaṃ nāṭyayoktṛbhiḥ ..43..
meaning:
शोकानन्दसमुद्भूतमश्रु स्याद्रोदनेन तु ..
वर्णावरत्वाद्विज्ञेयं वैवर्ण्यं नाट्ययोक्तृभिः ..43..
text_mt: Tears, born of sorrow or joy, occur through weeping. / Pallor is to be known by directors of dramatic performance from a diminution of complexion.

sanskrit_iast:
vaivarṇyaṃ nābhinetavyaṃ prayatnāttaddhi duṣkaram ..
glāniḥ śaṅkābhyasūyā ca śramaścapalatā tathā .. 44 ..
meaning:
वैवर्ण्यं नाभिनेतव्यं प्रयत्नात्तद्धि दुष्करम् ..
ग्लानिः शङ्काभ्यसूया च श्रमश्चपलता तथा .. 44 ..
text_mt: Pallor should not be represented by effort, for it is difficult to accomplish. / Exhaustion, apprehension, envy, weariness, and inconstancy,

sanskrit_iast:
romāñcaharṣe nidrā ca unmādo mada eva ca..
svedaścaiva vahitthaśca bhāvā hāsyarase smṛtāḥ .. 45 ..
meaning:
रोमाञ्चहर्षे निद्रा च उन्मादो मद एव च..
स्वेदश्चैव वहित्थश्च भावा हास्यरसे स्मृताः .. 45 ..
text_mt: horripilation, joy, sleep, madness, intoxication, / perspiration, and dissimulation are remembered as states in the comic sentiment.

sanskrit_iast:
ālasyogryajugupsābhirbhāvā hi parivarjitāḥ ..
udbhāvayanti śṛṅgāraṃ rasamāsvādyasaṃjñakam .. 46 ..
meaning:
आलस्योग्र्यजुगुप्साभिर्भावा हि परिवर्जिताः ..
उद्भावयन्ति शृङ्गारं रसमास्वाद्यसंज्ञकम् .. 46 ..
text_mt: The states, when free from indolence, ferocity, and disgust, / manifest the erotic sentiment, whose designation is enjoyable.

sanskrit_iast:
vedasyaiva ca cintā ca dainyaglānyaśrupātanam ..
jaḍatā maraṇaṃ caiva vyādhiśca karuṇārase .. 47 ..
meaning:
वेदस्यैव च चिन्ता च दैन्यग्लान्यश्रुपातनम् ..
जडता मरणं चैव व्याधिश्च करुणारसे .. 47 ..
text_mt: Anxiety, wretchedness, exhaustion, shedding of tears, / stupor, death, and disease belong to the pathetic sentiment.

sanskrit_iast:
asammohastathonmādo viṣādo mada eva ca ..
mṛtyurvyādhirbhayaṃ caiva bhāvā bībhatsasaṃśrayāḥ .. 48 ..
meaning:
असम्मोहस्तथोन्मादो विषादो मद एव च ..
मृत्युर्व्याधिर्भयं चैव भावा बीभत्ससंश्रयाः .. 48 ..
text_mt: Absence of bewilderment, as well as madness, despondency, and intoxication, / death, disease, and fear are the states residing in the odious [sentiment].

sanskrit_iast:
stambhaḥ svedaśca romāñco jugupsā vismayastathā ..
pravego jaḍatā harṣo'sūyā daivādbhute rase .. .. 49 ..
meaning:
स्तम्भः स्वेदश्च रोमाञ्चो जुगुप्सा विस्मयस्तथा ..
प्रवेगो जडता हर्षोऽसूया दैवाद्भुते रसे .. .. 49 ..
text_mt: Paralysis, perspiration, horripilation, disgust, and wonder, / agitation, stupor, joy, and envy belong to the wonderful sentiment pertaining to the divine.

sanskrit_iast:
svedaśca vepathuścaiva romāñco gadgadastathā ..
matiścaiva tathogratvamamarṣo mada eva ca .. 3.31.50 ..
meaning:
स्वेदश्च वेपथुश्चैव रोमाञ्चो गद्गदस्तथा ..
मतिश्चैव तथोग्रत्वममर्षो मद एव च .. 3.31.50 ..
text_mt: Perspiration, trembling, horripilation, faltering of voice, / intelligence, fieriness, indignation, and intoxication,

sanskrit_iast:
romāñcaḥ svarabhedaśca krodho'sūyā dhṛtistathā ..
garvaścaiva vitarkaśca vīre bhāvā bhavanti vai..51..
meaning:
रोमाञ्चः स्वरभेदश्च क्रोधोऽसूया धृतिस्तथा ..
गर्वश्चैव वितर्कश्च वीरे भावा भवन्ति वै..51..
text_mt: horripilation, change of voice, anger, envy, firmness, / pride, and deliberation are the states that arise in the heroic.

sanskrit_iast:
ye cānye sāttvikā bhāvā nānābhinayayonijāḥ ..
raseṣveteṣu te sarve vijñeyā nāṭyakovidaiḥ ..52..
meaning:
ये चान्ये सात्त्विका भावा नानाभिनययोनिजाः ..
रसेष्वेतेषु ते सर्वे विज्ञेया नाट्यकोविदैः ..52..
text_mt: And whatever other involuntary states arise from the manifold modes of acting, / all those are to be understood in these sentiments by experts in dramatic art.

sanskrit_iast:
bahūnāṃ samavetānāṃ rūpaṃ yasya bhavedbahu ..
sa mantavyo rasaḥ sthāyī śeṣāḥ sañcāriṇaḥ smṛtāḥ .. 53 ..
meaning:
बहूनां समवेतानां रूपं यस्य भवेद्बहु ..
स मन्तव्यो रसः स्थायी शेषाः सञ्चारिणः स्मृताः .. 53 ..
text_mt: Of many assembled together, that whose form is predominant / should be considered the permanent sentiment; the rest are remembered as transitory.

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṅgāraṃ trividhaṃ vindyādvā nepathyakriyātmakam ..
aṅganepathyabhāvaśca hāsyaraudrau prakīrtitau ..54..
meaning:
शृङ्गारं त्रिविधं विन्द्याद्वा नेपथ्यक्रियात्मकम् ..
अङ्गनेपथ्यभावश्च हास्यरौद्रौ प्रकीर्तितौ ..54..
text_mt: One should know the erotic as threefold, consisting of speech, dress, and action; / and the states of limbs and costume are declared for the comic and furious.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmārthabandhughātena karuṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
yuddhavīraṃ dayāvīraṃ dānavīraṃ tathaiva ca .. 55 ..
meaning:
धर्मार्थबन्धुघातेन करुणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ..
युद्धवीरं दयावीरं दानवीरं तथैव च .. 55 ..
text_mt: The pathetic is traditionally threefold, arising from the destruction of dharma, wealth, and kin. / Likewise, heroic in battle, heroic in compassion, and heroic in generosity:

sanskrit_iast:
rasaṃ vīramiti prāhustajjñāstrividhameva ca ..
vyājatrāsāparādhaiśca tridhā vidyādbhayānakam .. 56 ..
meaning:
रसं वीरमिति प्राहुस्तज्ज्ञास्त्रिविधमेव च ..
व्याजत्रासापराधैश्च त्रिधा विद्याद्भयानकम् .. 56 ..
text_mt: the connoisseurs declare the heroic sentiment to be threefold in this way. / And one should know the terrible as threefold: through pretexts, fright, and transgression.

sanskrit_iast:
na hyekarasajaṃ kāvyaṃ kiñcidasti prayogajam ..
bhāvo vāpi raso vāpi pravṛttirvṛttireva ca ..57..
meaning:
न ह्येकरसजं काव्यं किञ्चिदस्ति प्रयोगजम् ..
भावो वापि रसो वापि प्रवृत्तिर्वृत्तिरेव च ..57..
text_mt: Indeed, no dramatic work produced through performance arises from a single sentiment alone, / nor does a state, a sentiment, a regional style, or a dramatic style.

sanskrit_iast:
ekonapañcāśadime samagrā bhāvavyavasthā gaditā mayā te ..
yuktyā ca ye yatra rase niyuktāḥ proktaṃ tadapyatra narendracandra .. 58..
meaning:
एकोनपञ्चाशदिमे समग्रा भावव्यवस्था गदिता मया ते ..
युक्त्या च ये यत्र रसे नियुक्ताः प्रोक्तं तदप्यत्र नरेन्द्रचन्द्र .. 58..
text_mt: These forty-nine states in their entirety have been described by me to you as an orderly system; / and which ones are employed by rule in which sentiment has also been stated here, O moon among kings.
