The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now, therefore, we shall explain the hand-gestures.
When the bent forefinger is over the extended thumb of the left [hand], that is oṃkāra.
When all the fingers have entered the palm of the hand and are curled in succession, beginning with the thumb, [they form] a, i, u, e, o; when extended, a, i, u, ū, ai, o, aṃ; [it is] mukula; aḥ is a special mukula. With the forefinger of the other hand placed at the base of the thumb, [it forms] the ka-varga in succession.
Placed on the line furthest below all, [it forms] the ta-varga.
Above that, with groups of b, v, and ś, the pa-varga.
The forefinger and others, when placed on the first knuckle, [form] the pa-varga.
On the tips, the śa-varga.
Upon touching the nail of the middle finger, ra and kṣa.
a is Vāsudeva.
ā is Saṅkarṣaṇa; aṃ is Pradyumna;
aḥ is Aniruddha.
Añjalipuruṣa is with the backs of the two hands joined to each other.
Little finger with little finger, forefinger with forefinger, and thumb with thumb: this is the Tārkṣya-mudrā.
Patāka with its tip bent is tāla; with the thumb extended sideways, it is makara.
With the fingers bent, it is ardhacandra.
Two visible śikharas joined at the tips of the little fingers [form …].
With the thumbs pressed together, it is a conch.
Two aḥ-kāras joined with clearly separated fingers form a lotus.
With the thumb bent, it is Lakṣmī.
With the fingers extended, it is a makara.
Śeṣa is on the śikhara above that, destroying worldly enjoyment.
The aḥ-kāra itself with the middle finger extended is Garuḍa.
The middle finger right there, held by a śikhara, is the mount of Garuḍa.
When the tips of the middle and ring fingers join with the thumbs, it is a discus.
With two kapitthas one above the other held at the chin, it is a mace.
Kapittha with the middle finger bent is a plough.
In karkaṭaka, it is sumūla.
Kapittha with the middle finger dropped [is …].
Kapittha is a shield; with fingers on the back of the palm, a sword; śikhara with the middle finger dropped is a bow.
From the separation of the forefinger, middle finger, and thumb when joined together, an arrow.
With the little finger drawn into a mukula, it is the Kaustubha.
Two separate śikharas are a garland of forest flowers.
aḥ-kāra joined separately is Nṛsiṃha.
A śikhara with the little finger extended downwards is Varāha.
i is the Horse-headed One.
oṃ is Vāmana.
Vitolita is Trivikrama.
Ardhacandra is the Fish.
With face turned down, a bent patāka is the Tortoise.
A śikhara with the little finger extended and the thumb turned upward is the Swan.
Patāka with the middle of the palm hollowed is Dattātreya.
Kapittha is Paraśurāma.
Two śikharas joined together are the two sons of Daśaratha.
Patāka is Kṛṣṇa; tripatāka is Baladeva.
Śikhara is Viṣṇu.
An upturned patāka is the earth.
A bent patāka with the thumb extended is water.
Fingers with the thumb-tip wiped over the nails is fire.
A trembling patāka is wind.
A fist held sideways with the forefinger extended is the intermediate space.
The union of two spans formed into a circle is the sun; curved with half the ring finger, it is the moon.
When all are formed into a mukula and the middle and forefinger are extended, they are Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
In that very [gesture], with the nose-tip extended, [they are] the qualities: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara.
With fingers of the left hand extended, and the right hand likewise placed above it, it is Kapila.
All four fingers extended, with the thumb bent at their base, is the inner self, water.
With the little finger extended, it is the Ṛgveda.
That same [gesture] with the ring finger extended is the Yajurveda.
Caturātmā with the thumb extended is the Sāmaveda.
With the fingers being enveloped as they enter the middle of the palm, it is Gāyatrī.
The Sāmaveda [hand] with fingers turned downward is Śikṣā.
That very [hand] led to the right direction is Kalpa.
In the union of the forefinger and thumb is Vyākaraṇa.
In śikhara, with the thumb placed between the forefinger and middle finger, it is Nirukta.
With two khaṭakāmukhas, Jyotiṣa.
Turned downward, it is Chandoviciti.
These secret mudrās have been spoken to you by me, O best of kings.
Hereafter, I shall declare the common ones; listen to them from me.

3.33
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having made the palm upturned, with four fingers bent, / the thumb should be joined at the side; this is proclaimed as the bhasma-mudrā.
That [hand] with fingers raised obliquely is proclaimed as the liṅga-mudrā. / Three fingers with their tips gathered together with the thumb,
and having the forefinger extended, is proclaimed as the jaṭā-mudrā. / It is the vetra-mudrā when the forefinger in it is at the corner of the eye.
One should hold [the hand] firm and extend the thumb; / joined face upward on the head, one should indicate the moon.
All fingers extended, curved in the shape of horns; / having made that mudrā on the head, one should indicate the bull.
Holding that hand obliquely with all fingers contracted, / wrapping the middle finger around the thumb, one should indicate 'thrown down' (paryasta).
One should place the contracted little finger over the thumb; / the right thumb is placed between the little finger and the ring finger.

Three fingers turned downward and positioned sideways,

sanskrit_iast:
kanīyasyupari tvāsāṃ tāśca sarvā adhomukhāḥ ..
tāsāmupari cāṅguṣṭhe dakṣiṇaṃ samprayojayeta .. 68 ..
meaning:
कनीयस्युपरि त्वासां ताश्च सर्वा अधोमुखाः ..
तासामुपरि चाङ्गुष्ठे दक्षिणं सम्प्रयोजयेत .. 68 ..
text_mt:
all of them turned downward above the little finger;
and above them, on the thumbs, one should apply the right [finger].

sanskrit_iast:
vāme dharmajñamudraiṣā kathitā lāṅgalasya tu ..
bandhe tvanāmikā tvasminmudrā hyastrasya kīrtitā .. 69 ..
meaning:
वामे धर्मज्ञमुद्रैषा कथिता लाङ्गलस्य तु ..
बन्धे त्वनामिका त्वस्मिन्मुद्रा ह्यस्त्रस्य कीर्तिता .. 69 ..
text_mt:
On the left, O knower of dharma, this mudrā is declared to be that of the plow;
but when the ring finger is bound in this [gesture], it is proclaimed as the mudrā of the weapon.

sanskrit_iast:
uttānau tu karau kṛtvā ubhāvekatra yojayeta ..
karajāstu smṛtāḥ sarvā mudrā gāyatrasaṃjñitāḥ .. 3.33.70 ..
meaning:
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा उभावेकत्र योजयेत ..
करजास्तु स्मृताः सर्वा मुद्रा गायत्रसंज्ञिताः .. 3.33.70 ..
text_mt:
Having turned both hands upward, one should join them both together;
all fingernails are remembered [thus] in the mudrā named Gāyatra.

sanskrit_iast:
muṣṭau prasārayedekāmaṃgulīṃ tu kramānnṛpa ..
tarjanyantāṃ kaniṣṭhādyāṃ śaktimudrā prakīrtitā .. 71 ..
meaning:
मुष्टौ प्रसारयेदेकामंगुलीं तु क्रमान्नृप ..
तर्जन्यन्तां कनिष्ठाद्यां शक्तिमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता .. 71 ..
text_mt:
From a fist, one should extend one finger in succession, O king,
beginning with the little finger and ending with the index finger—this is proclaimed as the Śaktimudrā.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdi nyasto'ñjalirjñeyo namaskāro narādhipa ..
kapitthayajanīṃ gṛhya śikhareṇa dhvajo bhaveta .. 72 ..
meaning:
हृदि न्यस्तोऽञ्जलिर्ज्ञेयो नमस्कारो नराधिप ..
कपित्थयजनीं गृह्य शिखरेण ध्वजो भवेत .. 72 ..
text_mt:
The hollowed palms placed at the heart is to be known as Namaskāra, O lord of men.
Taking the Kapittha-holding [gesture], with the Śikhara it becomes the banner.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅguṣṭhe yojya tarjanyau hastottānau smṛtāṅgulī ..
maṇibandhau nipīḍyaiva śaśikarṇī bhavennṛpa .. 73 ..
meaning:
अङ्गुष्ठे योज्य तर्जन्यौ हस्तोत्तानौ स्मृताङ्गुली ..
मणिबन्धौ निपीड्यैव शशिकर्णी भवेन्नृप .. 73 ..
text_mt:
Joining the index fingers to the thumb, with the hands turned upward and fingers remembered [as such],
and pressing the wrists, it becomes the Śaśikarṇī, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
sampuṭīkṛtya hastau dvau kiñcitsaṅkucitāṅguliḥ ..
mukulā tu samākhyātā paṅkajaṃ prasṛtaiva sā ..74 ..
meaning:
सम्पुटीकृत्य हस्तौ द्वौ किञ्चित्सङ्कुचिताङ्गुलिः ..
मुकुला तु समाख्याता पङ्कजं प्रसृतैव सा ..74 ..
text_mt:
Cupping both hands with the fingers slightly contracted,
it is proclaimed as Mukulā; that very same [gesture] expanded is the lotus.

sanskrit_iast:
uttāno tu sṛtau hastau kṛtvāṅguṣṭhau tu kuñcitau ..
madhyasaṃsthau karau kṛtvā āvāhanyāstu lakṣaṇam .. 75 ..
meaning:
उत्तानो तु सृतौ हस्तौ कृत्वाङ्गुष्ठौ तु कुञ्चितौ ..
मध्यसंस्थौ करौ कृत्वा आवाहन्यास्तु लक्षणम् .. 75 ..
text_mt:
Turning the hands upward and spreading them, with the thumbs bent,
and placing both hands in the middle, this is the characteristic of the Āvāhanī.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅguṣṭhau kuñcitau dvau tu svakīyāṅguliveṣṭitau ..
ubhau cābhimukhau hastau yojayitvā tu riṣṭrarā .. 76 ..
meaning:
अङ्गुष्ठौ कुञ्चितौ द्वौ तु स्वकीयाङ्गुलिवेष्टितौ ..
उभौ चाभिमुखौ हस्तौ योजयित्वा तु रिष्ट्ररा .. 76 ..
text_mt:
Both thumbs bent, wrapped by their own fingers,
and having joined both hands facing each other, O protector of the realm,

sanskrit_iast:
uttānaṃ dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhaṃ vāmāṅguṣṭhena veṣṭayet ..
bhrāmayedvartulāṅguṣṭhā mudrā proktā visarjane .. 77 ..
meaning:
उत्तानं दक्षिणाङ्गुष्ठं वामाङ्गुष्ठेन वेष्टयेत् ..
भ्रामयेद्वर्तुलाङ्गुष्ठा मुद्रा प्रोक्ता विसर्जने .. 77 ..
text_mt:
one should wrap the upturned right thumb with the left thumb;
rotating the thumbs in a circle, this mudrā is declared for dismissal.

sanskrit_iast:
vitastidvayasaṃyogādbhadramudrā prakīrtitā ..
muṣṭiḥ pramārjitā jñeyā liṅgamudrā tathaiva ca .. 78..
meaning:
वितस्तिद्वयसंयोगाद्भद्रमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ..
मुष्टिः प्रमार्जिता ज्ञेया लिङ्गमुद्रा तथैव च .. 78..
text_mt:
By the union of two spans, it is proclaimed as the Bhadramudrā;
a smoothed fist is likewise to be known as the Liṅgamudrā.

sanskrit_iast:
sandaṣṭe mārjitāvoṣṭhau tīrṇamudrā prakīrtitā ..
prasāritau bhujau kṛtvā bhujāgrau kuñcitau tathā .. 79 ..
meaning:
सन्दष्टे मार्जितावोष्ठौ तीर्णमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ..
प्रसारितौ भुजौ कृत्वा भुजाग्रौ कुञ्चितौ तथा .. 79 ..
text_mt:
When wiped over closed lips, it is proclaimed as the Tīrṇamudrā.
Extending both arms and bending the forearms,

sanskrit_iast:
agrāgrau kuñcitāṃśena karapallavasannibhau ..
tarjanīṃ kuñcitāṃ kṛtvā aṅguṣṭhopari vinyaset .. 3.33.80 ..
meaning:
अग्राग्रौ कुञ्चितांशेन करपल्लवसन्निभौ ..
तर्जनीं कुञ्चितां कृत्वा अङ्गुष्ठोपरि विन्यसेत् .. 3.33.80 ..
text_mt:
with the fingertips curved like sprouting leaves of the hand,
and bending the index finger, one should place it upon the thumb.

sanskrit_iast:
nikubjau bāhudaṇḍau tu badhnīyācca pṛthakpṛthaka ..
kairiṇī nāma mudraiṣā kathitā sūryadevatā .. 81 ..
meaning:
निकुब्जौ बाहुदण्डौ तु बध्नीयाच्च पृथक्पृथक ..
कैरिणी नाम मुद्रैषा कथिता सूर्यदेवता .. 81 ..
text_mt:
One should hold the rod-like arms bent downward separately;
this mudrā, named Kairiṇī, is declared to have the Sun as its deity.

sanskrit_iast:
padmākārau karau kṛtvā saṃśliṣṭau grathitāṅgulīḥ ..
aṅgulyā kārayettasminviśvamudreti kīrtitā .. 82 ..
meaning:
पद्माकारौ करौ कृत्वा संश्लिष्टौ ग्रथिताङ्गुलीः ..
अङ्गुल्या कारयेत्तस्मिन्विश्वमुद्रेति कीर्तिता .. 82 ..
text_mt:
Having made both hands lotus-shaped, joined together with fingers interlaced,
one should form it with the finger; it is proclaimed as the Viśvamudrā.

sanskrit_iast:
sammukhau tu karau kṛtvā saṃśliṣṭau grathitāṅgulīḥ ..
kaniṣṭhāmadhyame yojyau tarjanyau madhyame tathā .. 83 ..
meaning:
सम्मुखौ तु करौ कृत्वा संश्लिष्टौ ग्रथिताङ्गुलीः ..
कनिष्ठामध्यमे योज्यौ तर्जन्यौ मध्यमे तथा .. 83 ..
text_mt:
Having brought both hands facing each other, joined together with fingers interlaced,
the little and middle fingers should be joined, and likewise the index and middle fingers.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdi mūrdhni śikhābandhe mudreyaṃ vyomasaṃjñitā ..
muṣṭibandhocchritāṃ kṛtvā madhyahastasya tarjanīm .. 84 ..
meaning:
हृदि मूर्ध्नि शिखाबन्धे मुद्रेयं व्योमसंज्ञिता ..
मुष्टिबन्धोच्छ्रितां कृत्वा मध्यहस्तस्य तर्जनीम् .. 84 ..
text_mt:
At the heart, on the crown of the head, or at the tying of the topknot, this mudrā is named Vyoma.
Having made a fist and raised the index finger of the middle hand,

sanskrit_iast:
tālaśabdakṛtāsau tu mudrā cāsrasya kīrtitā ..
madhyamā tarjanī caiva savyahastasya cocchrite .. 85 ..
meaning:
तालशब्दकृतासौ तु मुद्रा चास्रस्य कीर्तिता ..
मध्यमा तर्जनी चैव सव्यहस्तस्य चोच्छ्रिते .. 85 ..
text_mt:
and making a clapping sound, this is proclaimed as the mudrā of the weapon.
When the middle and index fingers of the right hand are raised,

sanskrit_iast:
kaniṣṭhānāmike kubje sāṅguṣṭhenaiva saṃjñitā ..
netrapradarśitā jñeyā govṛṣāgamane tathā .. 86 ..
meaning:
कनिष्ठानामिके कुब्जे साङ्गुष्ठेनैव संज्ञिता ..
नेत्रप्रदर्शिता ज्ञेया गोवृषागमने तथा .. 86 ..
text_mt:
and the little and ring fingers are bent along with the thumb, it is designated [as such];
it is to be known as indicated for the eye and on the approach of a bull.

sanskrit_iast:
uttānau tu karau kṛtvā sarvāṅgulyo vikuñjitāḥ ..
kṛtvā copari cāṅguṣṭhaṃ cālayeta punaḥ punaḥ .. 87 ..
meaning:
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा सर्वाङ्गुल्यो विकुञ्जिताः ..
कृत्वा चोपरि चाङ्गुष्ठं चालयेत पुनः पुनः .. 87 ..
text_mt:
Having turned both hands upward, with all fingers curled,
and placing the thumb above, one should move it again and again.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāsāmeva śaktīnāṃ mudraiṣā samprakīrtitā ..
dīptā sūkṣmā jayā bhadrā vibhūtirvimalā tathā ..88 ..
meaning:
सर्वासामेव शक्तीनां मुद्रैषा सम्प्रकीर्तिता ..
दीप्ता सूक्ष्मा जया भद्रा विभूतिर्विमला तथा ..88 ..
text_mt:
This is proclaimed as the mudrā of all the powers:
Dīptā, Sūkṣmā, Jayā, Bhadrā, Vibhūti, Vimalā,

sanskrit_iast:
amoghā vidyutā caiva navamā sarvatomukhī ..
iti nāmāni śaktīnāṃ sarahasyāni nirdiśet .. 89 ..
meaning:
अमोघा विद्युता चैव नवमा सर्वतोमुखी ..
इति नामानि शक्तीनां सरहस्यानि निर्दिशेत् .. 89 ..
text_mt:
Amoghā, Vidyutā, and the ninth, Sarvatomukhī—
thus one should indicate the secret names of the powers.

sanskrit_iast:
sammukhau tu karau kṛtvā śliṣṭau caiva prasāritau ..
iyaṃ mudrā namaskāre ravi sānnidhyakāriṇī .. 3.33.90 ..
meaning:
सम्मुखौ तु करौ कृत्वा श्लिष्टौ चैव प्रसारितौ ..
इयं मुद्रा नमस्कारे रवि सान्निध्यकारिणी .. 3.33.90 ..
text_mt: Having placed the hands facing each other, joined and extended, / this is the mudrā for salutation, bringing about the presence of the Sun.

sanskrit_iast:
anāmikāyāḥ sandeśo ravimudrā prakīrtitā ..
somamudrā madhyamayā bhīmamudrā hyanāmayā .. 91 ..
meaning:
अनामिकायाः सन्देशो रविमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ..
सोममुद्रा मध्यमया भीममुद्रा ह्यनामया .. 91 ..
text_mt: The contact of the ring finger is declared to be the Sun mudrā; / with the middle finger, the Moon mudrā; with the ring finger, the Bhīma mudrā.

sanskrit_iast:
kanīyasyā budhe mudrā unmūle jīvasaṃjñitā ..
anāmikāmūlagā tu śukramudrā prakīrtitā..92 ..
meaning:
कनीयस्या बुधे मुद्रा उन्मूले जीवसंज्ञिता ..
अनामिकामूलगा तु शुक्रमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता..92 ..
text_mt: With the little finger, the mudrā for Mercury; at its root, it is named for Jupiter; / but at the base of the ring finger is declared to be the mudrā for Venus.

sanskrit_iast:
madhyamāmūlagāṃguṣṭhā śanimudrā prakīrtitā ..
tarjanīmūlagāṃguṣṭhe rāhu mudrā prakīrtitā .. 93 ..
meaning:
मध्यमामूलगांगुष्ठा शनिमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ..
तर्जनीमूलगांगुष्ठे राहु मुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता .. 93 ..
text_mt: The thumb at the base of the middle finger is declared to be the Saturn mudrā; / with the thumb at the base of the forefinger, it is declared to be the Rāhu mudrā.

sanskrit_iast:
tarjanī calanājjñeyā ketumudrā narādhipa ..
vāmahastena śikharāḥ krodhamudrā prakīrtitā .. 94 ..
meaning:
तर्जनी चलनाज्ज्ञेया केतुमुद्रा नराधिप ..
वामहस्तेन शिखराः क्रोधमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता .. 94 ..
text_mt: By moving the forefinger, O lord of men, the Ketu mudrā is to be known; / the śikhara hand with the left hand is declared to be the Anger mudrā.

sanskrit_iast:
sampuṭau tu karau kṛtvā vāmocchrāyāṃ narādhipa ..
eṣā varāhamudrā tu sarvakarmakarī śubhā .. 95 ..
meaning:
सम्पुटौ तु करौ कृत्वा वामोच्छ्रायां नराधिप ..
एषा वराहमुद्रा तु सर्वकर्मकरी शुभा .. 95 ..
text_mt: Having cupped the hands, raised towards the left, O king, / this is the Boar mudrā, auspicious and fulfilling all actions.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmena veṣṭitau hastau dakṣiṇā bhairavī bhavet ..
hastāvadho mukhau yatra dṛṣṭiścādhastathā bhavet .. 96 ..
meaning:
वामेन वेष्टितौ हस्तौ दक्षिणा भैरवी भवेत् ..
हस्तावधो मुखौ यत्र दृष्टिश्चाधस्तथा भवेत् .. 96 ..
text_mt: When the hands are wrapped around with the left, it becomes the Bhairavī; / where both hands face downwards and the gaze is likewise directed downwards,

sanskrit_iast:
pātālabhañjinī nāma mudraiṣā kathitā nṛpa ..
kapitthānāmikā dīrghāstambhanī tu nigadyate .. 97 ..
meaning:
पातालभञ्जिनी नाम मुद्रैषा कथिता नृप ..
कपित्थानामिका दीर्घास्तम्भनी तु निगद्यते .. 97 ..
text_mt: this mudrā is called Pātālabhañjinī, O king. / The kapittha with the ring finger outstretched is said to be the Stambhanī.

sanskrit_iast:
karamadhyāttu saṃgrāhyamiva madhyena cāhatam ..
evaṃ madhyena saṃyuktā krodhinī parikīrtitā .. 98 ..
meaning:
करमध्यात्तु संग्राह्यमिव मध्येन चाहतम् ..
एवं मध्येन संयुक्ता क्रोधिनी परिकीर्तिता .. 98 ..
text_mt: Seized from the middle of the hand, struck with the middle [finger], / thus joined with the middle [finger], it is proclaimed as Krodhinī.

sanskrit_iast:
sahamadhyā tu saṃgrāhyā khātamadhye dvidhāhatam ..
evamadhyena saṃyuktā vīryamudrā prakīrtitā .. 99 ..
meaning:
सहमध्या तु संग्राह्या खातमध्ये द्विधाहतम् ..
एवमध्येन संयुक्ता वीर्यमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता .. 99 ..
text_mt: Held together in the middle, struck doubly in the hollow of the middle, / thus joined with the middle, it is declared to be the Vīryamudrā.

sanskrit_iast:
evamadhyena saṃyuktaṃ bhairavī cāparā bhavet ..
kṣetramadhyā tu saṃgrāhyā iramadhyena saṃyutam .. 3.33.100 ..
meaning:
एवमध्येन संयुक्तं भैरवी चापरा भवेत् ..
क्षेत्रमध्या तु संग्राह्या इरमध्येन संयुतम् .. 3.33.100 ..
text_mt: Thus joined in the middle, another Bhairavī arises. / Held in the center of the hand, joined in the middle,

sanskrit_iast:
evamadhyena ca krāntaṃ stambhanī cāparā bhavet ..
lasanmadhyā tu saṃgrāhyamekamadhyena cāhatam .. 101 ..
meaning:
एवमध्येन च क्रान्तं स्तम्भनी चापरा भवेत् ..
लसन्मध्या तु संग्राह्यमेकमध्येन चाहतम् .. 101 ..
text_mt: and crossed in this manner in the middle, it becomes another Stambhanī. / Shining in the middle, grasped, struck by the one in the middle,

sanskrit_iast:
pātālabhañjanī nāma mudreyamaparā bhavet ..
tarjanī madhyamā caiva tathā caiva tvanāmikām .. 102 ..
meaning:
पातालभञ्जनी नाम मुद्रेयमपरा भवेत् ..
तर्जनी मध्यमा चैव तथा चैव त्वनामिकाम् .. 102 ..
text_mt: this becomes another mudrā named Pātālabhañjanī. / The forefinger, the middle finger, and likewise the ring finger,

sanskrit_iast:
madhyaparvasu saṃyuktāṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kārayetkare ..
śaṅkhamudreyamuddiṣṭā pūrvamuktā tathāparā ..] 03 ..
meaning:
मध्यपर्वसु संयुक्तां पृष्ठतः कारयेत्करे ..
शङ्खमुद्रेयमुद्दिष्टा पूर्वमुक्ता तथापरा ..] 03 ..
text_mt: joined at the middle joints, one should place at the back of the hand; / this is designated as the Conch mudrā, and another was mentioned previously.

sanskrit_iast:
prasārya sarvāścāṅgulyaḥ karapṛṣṭhe ca yojayet ..
cakramudrā bhavetteṣāṃ pūrvamuktā tathāparā .. 104 ..
meaning:
प्रसार्य सर्वाश्चाङ्गुल्यः करपृष्ठे च योजयेत् ..
चक्रमुद्रा भवेत्तेषां पूर्वमुक्ता तथापरा .. 104 ..
text_mt: Having extended all fingers and joined them at the back of the hand, / it becomes the Discus mudrā among them; another was also stated earlier.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭibhāgapradeśe tu muṣṭistu triśirā bhavet ..
gadā mudrā bhavatyeṣā sarvavighnapraṇāśinī .. 105 ..
meaning:
कटिभागप्रदेशे तु मुष्टिस्तु त्रिशिरा भवेत् ..
गदा मुद्रा भवत्येषा सर्वविघ्नप्रणाशिनी .. 105 ..

text_mt:
This much has been told in brief concerning the treatise on dance, O king, foremost of the royal lineage; / all of this profound meaning has been proclaimed at length, foremost in all the world.
Vajra said: / By whom was dance originated—by a sage or by a deity? / Sever this doubt of mine, for you are said to know everything.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Formerly, when the world was a single ocean, motionless and moving beings destroyed, / while the Slayer of Madhu slept upon the couch of Śeṣa,
his feet being massaged by Lakṣmī, O scion of the Yadu lineage, / from his navel arose a lotus, O lotus-eyed one.
There was born self-existent Brahmā, the auspicious four-faced god, / together with the deities, O fortunate one, endowed with bodies, O king.
Born from two drops of water on that lotus, right there, were Madhu and Kaiṭabha, / full of rajas and tamas, thieves, two terrifying Dānavas.
Then, O king, the two seized the Vedas from Brahmā; / bereft of the Vedas, Brahmā then praised Madhusūdana:

text_mt:
“The Vedas are my supreme eye, the Vedas are my supreme strength; / the Vedas have been stolen by the Dānavas; I have become blind, O slayer of foes!”
Thus addressed then by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Puruṣottama, / rising up from that water, wandered upon the body of water.
With graceful major body-movements and step-sequences,
as the god was roaming in this way, the wide-eyed [goddess] saw him.
Lakṣmī became exceedingly charmed, especially filled with love.
And the god, having assumed a horse's head, went in an instant to the underworld.
He saw the demons and the Vedas, abandoned the horse-headed form,
and slew the two giant-bodied Dānavas, Madhu and Kaiṭabha.
Having slain [them], accompanied by the Vedas he approached Brahmā;
then the god of gods gave the Vedas to the self-born [creator].
Having given the Vedas, he then said, "Carry out creation, grandfather!"
Then the lord Brahmā, endowed with the assembly of the Vedas, performed creation.

text_mt:
Lakṣmī questioned the god seated on the lap of Śeṣa, O king:
Lakṣmī said:
"O god of gods, lord of the world, wielder of the conch, discus, and mace!
A graceful stepping was seen by me in the water, O lord,
with exceedingly beautiful limbs. Tell me, O lord, what was that?"
The Holy One said:
"Indeed, this dance was created by me, O lotus-eyed one,
joined with major body-movements, minor body-movements, and step-sequences.
The devoted will worship me through dance, O auspicious one;
the representation of the three worlds is established in dance, O goddess."
Having said this much to her, the god spoke these words to Brahmā:
"Receive the dance, O knower of dharma, along with its practice and theory!"
Having spoken this much to Brahmā, Keśava instructed him.
Having received it, Brahmā then transmitted it to the creator Rudra;
and Rudra, having received it, also pleased Keśava
constantly with that dance—the lord of gods who is loving to devotees.

text_mt:
In this way dance was created by Vāsudeva, O king,
long ago when the world was a single ocean and the mobile and immobile had perished.
From then on, the lord of gods Śaṅkara, who brings peace to men,
remains worshipping the god who bears the discus and mace with dance.
And he attained lordship over dance and praised the slayer of Madhu;
Hara too is pleased when properly worshipped through dance.
And other gods are pleased when properly gratified with dance;
for this is declared to be the supreme gratification of the celestials.
This alone indeed is divinity for those constantly sporting in heaven;
the gift of dance is superior to the gifts of flowers and food-offerings.
Whoever performs the worship of the god of gods himself through dance—
Keśava is especially pleased with him, O fortunate one.
Having offered dance, song, and instrumental music to the god Viṣṇu,
one enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice rich in all desires.
He who makes a livelihood by dance is to be diligently avoided,
who practices with actors and musicians, a seller of dance.

However, the knower of dharma who performs the worship of deities with dance
obtains all desires and finds the means to liberation.
[It is] auspicious, bringer of fame and longevity, granter of the heavenly realm,
the sport of lords, and the destroyer of suffering for the afflicted;
it is instruction for the ignorant, the enhancer of fortune for women,
pacifying, nourishing, fulfilling desires, fashioned by Vāsudeva.
"This dance treatise has been told to you in brief for the welfare of the world, O king;
indeed, an effort with dance should be made by a man desiring to conquer both worlds."
3.35

Formerly, while creating Urvaśī, the Citrasūtra [was produced], O prince,
by the sage Nārāyaṇa, desiring the welfare of the worlds,
for the sake of deceiving the celestial women who had arrived, the great sage.
Having taken mango juice, he drew an excellent woman upon the earth;
through painting she was then born, an excellent apsaras endowed with beauty.

Having seen her, all those celestial women departed in shame.
Having thus made a painting endowed with [canonical] characteristics, the great sage
then transmitted it to the unswerving Viśvakarman.
Just as in dance, so in painting, the representation of the three worlds is recognized.
The glances, the emotional states, and all the major and minor limbs,
and the hands which were earlier declared in [the chapter on] great dance, O best of kings—
those very ones are to be known in painting; dance and painting are considered supreme.
Listen now as I will explain the proportion that has been stated in dance.
Haṃsa, Bhadra, and then Mālavya, Rucaka, and Śaśaka:
five [types of] men are to be recognized; I will declare their characteristics.
Their height and span should all be known as equal in proportion;
by his own finger-measure it should be one hundred and eight [aṅgulas]:
the measure of the Haṃsa, O king; but of the Bhadra it is six more [than a hundred];
of the Mālavya it is to be known as four more [than a hundred], O king;

3.36
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now begins the division of individual limbs. In that regard, the crown of the head is twelve digits in circumference.
The forehead is eight digits wide and four digits high.
The temples are four digits across and two digits high; the cheeks are five digits; the chin is four digits.
The ears are two digits across and four digits high.
The ear-aperture inside is one digit, and water [should be clear within it].
The ear-lobe is without fixed measure. (The pendant lobe of the ear.)
The nose is four digits long, two digits high at the tip, and three [digits wide] across the bridge; the nostrils are one digit broad and twice that in length.
The space between the nose and the upper lip is half a digit.
The upper lip is one digit.
The mouth is four digits in length.
The lower lip is one digit; the chin is two digits.
There are forty teeth.
Among them are eight tusks.
The teeth are half a digit high.
The tusks are one-twelfth of a digit.
The eyes are one digit broad and three digits in length.
The dark circle of the eye is one-third of the eye.
The pupil is one-fifth [of that].
The eyebrows are half a digit broad and three digits in length.
The space between them is two digits.
The space between the corner of the eye and the ear is four digits.
The neck is ten digits broad,
twenty-one digits in circumference; the space between the breasts is sixteen digits.
The space between the breast and the collarbone is six digits.
The circumference of the base of the arm is sixteen digits.
At the tip [the wrist] it is twelve [digits in circumference]; the palm of the hand is seven digits long
and five digits broad; the middle finger is five digits in length.
The index finger is less by the first phalange of that [middle finger].
The ring finger is equal to that [index finger].
The little finger is smaller than that; all [fingers] have phalanges equal to one-third [of their length].
The nails are half a phalange.
The thumb is three digits long and has two phalanges.
The circumference of the belly is forty-two digits.
The navel is one digit in depth and width.
The waist is eighteen digits across;
its circumference is forty-four digits.
The testicles are four digits broad.
The penis is six digits long and of the same circumference.
Between them, the thighs are four digits [in separation].
The two knees are two digits broad and twice that in circumference.
The top of the calf is three times that in circumference.
The foot is five digits [high], fourteen in circumference, twelve digits long, and six digits broad; the big toes are three [digits] in length.
The second toe is equal to the big toe.
The remaining toes are each less by an eighth of that.
The nail of the big toe is less than a fourth of a digit.
That of the second toe is half that measure.
That of the remaining toes is an eighth part of that.
The whole foot has [toes each of] one digit, and its elevation is eight digits.
The heels are three digits wide
and four digits high. Such is the measure of the Haṃsa type.
And on this subject there are [these verses]:
One should logically calculate the measure of the remaining kings
according to this very model, in accordance with their own measure.

3.37
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Just as five types of men are known through the measures of their major and minor limbs, / so too should five types of women be known, O best among men.
A woman standing beside a man should be depicted, O lord: / she should be made to reach up to the man's shoulder, according to proper proportion.
A woman's waist is prescribed to be two digits narrower than a man's; / and her hips should be made larger by four digits in the same manner.
Her breasts should be made charming according to the proportion of her chest, O king. / And all kings should be depicted with the marks of a cosmic man.
Universal emperors should be depicted with webbed hands and feet; / and an auspicious tuft of hair between their eyebrows should also be made.
Three charming lines should be depicted on the hands of kings; / their weapons, resembling the blood of a hare, should have slender tips.

gives [prosperity] when belonging to deities, O king, and brings welfare to subjects. / Symmetrical, with the colour and luster of cow's milk, glossy, with curved tips on the eyelashes,
serene, lotus-cornered, charming, pleasant to behold, / having black pupils, and broad—eyes such as these bestow fortune and happiness.

Elongated, circular, discus-like, and triangular [shapes] / should be avoided for the gods by one wishing welfare among the subjects.

On the rest of their limbs, the gods should be free of hair. / The dwellers of heaven should be made looking sixteen years of age,
ever with serene faces and smiling glances. / Adorned with diadems, earrings, necklaces, keyūras, and armlets,
they must be made wearing auspicious garlands and wreaths, / with a broad girdle and ankle-ornaments,
having sacred threads and ear-ornaments as well, / and wearing a handsome waist-garment hanging down below the knees.
On the left side, O tiger among men, one should show the right knee; / and the charming garment of the deities should be depicted in this manner.
A halo should be made on their head, proportionate to the head, / circular in appearance, O great king, matching the deity.
An upward gaze, a downward gaze, or an oblique gaze must be avoided for them, / or one that is deficient, excessive, wretched, angry, or dry.
For an upward gaze is said to bring death, a downward one is declared to bring grief, / an oblique one destroys wealth, and a deficient one causes demise.

text_mt:
A painting endowed with auspicious marks is proclaimed blessed for the country, for the patron, and for the sovereign of the earth; / therefore, men devoted to careful exertion should diligently make it possessed of auspicious marks according to rule.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / With auspicious forms and movements, and bearing various colours, / there are nine stances of figures; hear them in proper order.
The frontal stance comes first, and next to that the non-frontal; / then the stance with turned body, and then the half-eyed.
Then the profile stance, next the averted; / the back-view is to be depicted downwards, [then] the averted, and the bowed.
These are the nine stances, having various divisions, O adorned one; / hear from me, O king, the characteristic of each one here.
Among them, first is the frontal stance, endowed with clear virtues of measurement, / fully complete, with very lovely limbs, very smooth, with subtle modelling,
very pure, sweet, adorned with refined and distinct line-work; / that stance in which the body is not diminished is indeed [to be known as] the [true frontal stance].

From the front of the face, the chest and belly are undiminished; / but at the waist, shoulder-region, and thighs, they are foreshortened.
A fourth part of the nostrils and the lower lip, O wise one, / and a third part from the limbs is brought to foreshortening;
a supreme stance of lovely form, executed through vertical plummets— / this very stance is called straight, endowed with multiple bodily gestures.
That which, by oblique vertical plummet, is eye-captivating, with excellent shading, / delicate, reduced by a fourth part, and charming in all its limbs,
with one and a half eyebrows and forehead, with a prominent one and a half nose, / having a remaining half after the reduction of parts, and an eye diminished by a kalā,
with the line of the eyebrow reduced by a kalā, drawn with a glossy line, / not fallen into dark shadow, and not trembling with crooked anger—
this is here called sācīkṛta, O king, because of its slanted stance. / In which half an eye is vanished on the face, and likewise on the lower brow,

and the curve is merely of the forehead, which is the very essence of what is seen, / and the cheek is seen on one side reduced by half a measure, foreshortened by half—
Half a measure of the throat line is revealed, and one barley-corn of the chin; / half of the chest and face is obscured, and one finger-breadth remains from the navel and mouth.

text_mt:
When the plastered wall has dried and been prepared,
[then] with that clay mixed with pine-resin and a proportion of oil,
he should diligently make it smooth with coats [of plaster] and smooth polishes,
sprinkled again and again with milk, through careful wiping.
That wall which has instantly attained dryness, O ruler of men,
even at the end of a hundred years would never be destroyed.
In this very manner, endowed with two kinds of pigments,
various jewel-floors should be made with painted forms.
When the wall is dry, on an auspicious lunar day, [when it is] free of moisture and endowed with [good] qualities,
especially in the conjunction with the constellation Citrā, clad in white, self-controlled,
having worshipped the brahmins, caused them to utter blessings, bowed down,
and [honoured] those skilled in the art according to rule, and his teachers, fond of his preceptors,
facing east, meditating on the deity, he should undertake the work of painting.
With white, yellow, and black brushes, in due order,

text_mt:
and mudga-dark complexions should be made, O king.
Blue mixed with pale yellow becomes an altered colour, and that too is manifold,
through the determination of parts where one exceeds the other, is less, or is equal;
by this, [a complexion] resembling a blue lotus and having the fair lustre of black gram,
charming complexions are made through accurate application.
Joined with white lac, bound with a mordant of lac,
red, and dark like a red lotus, the complexion becomes beautiful;
it also generates many other various colours.
The colour substances are gold, silver, copper,
mica, ivory, red lead, and tin,
yellow orpiment, lime, lac, and cinnabar, O king,
and indigo, O best of men; and likewise there are others in large numbers.
In various regions, O great king, they are to be prepared with a binding medium.
There should be the application of leaf or liquid preparation of metals.
When applied with metals, thick mica should be liquefied;
thus occurs the fitness of metals for work in painting.

The liquefaction of mica is declared in [liquids] produced from earth, tulsi, and indraja;
there may be camphor, nut-grass, or the resin from the bakula for binding.
For all colours, the milk of the sindūra [tree] is preferred.
A painting bound with juices of elephant-grass and dūrvā on a cloth base, fixed with noble [hair] brushes,
even when washed with water would not perish, and endures for many years.

mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..

text_mt:
3.41
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
'Satya', 'vaiṇika', 'nāgara', and 'miśra'—
painting is declared to be of four kinds; I shall state their characteristics.
title: Vartanaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
yatkiñcillokasādṛśyaṃ citraṃ tatsatyamucyate ..
dīrghāṅge sapramāṇaṃ ca sukumāraṃ subhūmikama..2..

यत्किञ्चिल्लोकसादृश्यं चित्रं तत्सत्यमुच्यते ..
दीर्घाङ्गे सप्रमाणं च सुकुमारं सुभूमिकम..2..
text_mt:
That painting which has some resemblance to the world is called 'satya';
[it is] with elongated limbs, proportionate, delicate, and on an excellent ground.

sanskrit_iast:
caturasraṃ susampūrṇaṃ na dīrghaṃ nolbaṇākṛtim..

चतुरस्रं सुसम्पूर्णं न दीर्घं नोल्बणाकृतिम्..
प्रमाणं स्थानलम्भाढ्यं वैणिकं तन्निगद्यते..3..
text_mt:
Square, well-proportioned, not long, not of exaggerated form,
rich in proportion, posture, and line—that is called 'vaiṇika'.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛḍhopacitasarvāṅgaṃ vartulaṃ nadyanolbaṇama ..
citraṃ taṃ nāgaraṃ jñeyaṃ svalpamālyavibhūṣaṇam .. 4 ..

दृढोपचितसर्वाङ्गं वर्तुलं नद्यनोल्बणम ..
चित्रं तं नागरं ज्ञेयं स्वल्पमाल्यविभूषणम् .. 4 ..
text_mt:
Having firm, well-developed limbs all over, rounded, not slack, not exaggerated,
with few garlands and ornaments—that painting is to be known as 'nāgara'.

sanskrit_iast:
citramiśraṃ samākhyātaṃ samāsānmanujottama ..

The mixed [style] of painting is declared concisely, O best of men.
And three methods of shading are spoken of: produced by lines, by hairs, and by dots.

sanskrit_iast:

पत्राकृतिभी रेखाभिः कथितात्र च वर्तना ..

Shading by lines of leaf-like shape is declared here;
likewise, shading by hairs is spoken of as exceedingly fine;

sanskrit_iast:

and shading by dots is declared as combined with binding.
Weakness, line of dots, lack of differentiation,

sanskrit_iast:

ऋषयस्तत्र कर्तव्या जटाजूटोपशोभिताः .. 3 ..
कृष्णाजिनोत्तरासङ्गा दुर्बलास्तेजसा युताः ..
देवताश्चापि गन्धर्वा मुकुटेन विवर्जिताः .. 4 ..
कर्तव्यास्ते महाराज शिखरैरुपशोभिताः ..
ब्रह्मवर्चस्विनो विप्राः शुक्लाम्बरधरास्तथा .. 5 ..
मन्त्रिणश्च महाराज सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ ..
सर्वालङ्कारसंयुक्तानेवोल्बणविभूषणान् .. 6 ..
text_mt:
A painting made by the wise [artist] with very glossy, distinct, and beautifully coloured lines, with dress appropriate to the specific region,
not lacking in proportion and beauty, becomes exceedingly wondrous.
3.42
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Just as a god is, so should he be made in painting, O ruler of the earth;
each single hair should be made in the depiction of kings of the earth.
Sages, along with gandharvas, daityas together with dānavas,
and ministers, O great king, the astrologer and the family priest,
And brahmins, O lord of men, should be made according to the Bhadra proportion. / There, sages should be represented adorned with matted locks,
having upper garments of black antelope skin, emaciated, [yet] full of spiritual brilliance. / The gods and also Gandharvas, devoid of crowns,
should be made, O great king, adorned with crests. / Brahmins should be endowed with the splendour of sacred learning and dressed in white garments.
Ministers as well, O great king, and the astrologer and the royal priest, / should be provided with all ornaments, yet without excessive embellishment.

sanskrit_iast:
mukuṭena vihīnāṃstu soṣṇīṣānkārayecca tān ..
daityāśca dānavāścaiva kartavyā bhrukuṭīmukhāḥ .. '7 ..
vartulākṣāstathā kāryā bhīmavaktrāstathaiva ca ..
teṣāmabhyuddhato veṣaḥ kartavyaḥ pṛthivīpate .. 8 ..
rudrapramāṇāḥ kartavyāstathā vidyādharā nṛpa ..
sapatnīkāśca te kāryā mālyālaṅkāradhāriṇaḥ .. 9 ..
khaḍgahastāśca te kāryā gagane vātha vā bhuvi ..
mālavyaparimāṇena kinnaroragarākṣasāḥ .. 3.42.10 ..
rucakasya pramāṇena yakṣāḥ kāryā narādhipa ..
śaśakasya pramāṇena pradhānaṃ mānavaṃ likhet .. 11 ..
piśācā vāmanāḥ kubjāḥ pramathāśca mahībhujaḥ ..
mānanniyamataḥ kāryaṃ rūpanniyamatastathā .. 12..
svānurūpapramāṇāśca sarveṣāṃ yoṣitaḥ smṛtāḥ..
kinnarā dvividhāḥ proktā nṛvaktrā hayavigrahāḥ .. 13 ..
meaning:
मुकुटेन विहीनांस्तु सोष्णीषान्कारयेच्च तान् ..
दैत्याश्च दानवाश्चैव कर्तव्या भ्रुकुटीमुखाः .. '7 ..
वर्तुलाक्षास्तथा कार्या भीमवक्त्रास्तथैव च ..
तेषामभ्युद्धतो वेषः कर्तव्यः पृथिवीपते .. 8 ..
रुद्रप्रमाणाः कर्तव्यास्तथा विद्याधरा नृप ..
सपत्नीकाश्च ते कार्या माल्यालङ्कारधारिणः .. 9 ..
खड्गहस्ताश्च ते कार्या गगने वाथ वा भुवि ..
मालव्यपरिमाणेन किन्नरोरगराक्षसाः .. 3.42.10 ..
रुचकस्य प्रमाणेन यक्षाः कार्या नराधिप ..
शशकस्य प्रमाणेन प्रधानं मानवं लिखेत् .. 11 ..
पिशाचा वामनाः कुब्जाः प्रमथाश्च महीभुजः ..
मानन्नियमतः कार्यं रूपन्नियमतस्तथा .. 12..
स्वानुरूपप्रमाणाश्च सर्वेषां योषितः स्मृताः..
किन्नरा द्विविधाः प्रोक्ता नृवक्त्रा हयविग्रहाः .. 13 ..
text_mt:
One should have them made devoid of crowns, but wearing turbans. / Daityas and Dānavas should be made with frowning faces; / they should also be made round-eyed and with terrible mouths. / Their attire, O lord of the earth, should be haughty.
Vidyādharas, O king, should be made according to the Rudra proportion; / and they should be represented accompanied by their wives, wearing garlands and ornaments.
They should be made with swords in hand, whether in the sky or on the earth. / Kinnaras, serpents, and Rākṣasas are to be made according to the Mālavya proportion.
Yakṣas, O lord of men, should be made according to the Rucaka proportion; / one should paint the principal mortal according to the Śaśaka proportion.
Piśācas, dwarfs, hunchbacks, and the Pramathas of the lord of the earth / should be made in measurement according to rule, and likewise in form according to rule.
And the women of all [these classes] are taught to have the proportion appropriate to their [males]. / Kinnaras are declared to be of two kinds: having human faces and horse bodies,

sanskrit_iast:
nṛdehāścāśvavaktrāśca tathānye parikīrtitāḥ ..
aśvavaktrāstu kartavyāḥ sarvālaṅkāradhāriṇaḥ .. 14 ..
gītavādyasamāyuktā dyutimantastathaiva ca ..
utkacā rākṣasāḥ kāryā vikalākṣā vibhīṣaṇāḥ .. 15 ..
meaning:
नृदेहाश्चाश्ववक्त्राश्च तथान्ये परिकीर्तिताः ..
अश्ववक्त्रास्तु कर्तव्याः सर्वालङ्कारधारिणः .. 14 ..
गीतवाद्यसमायुक्ता द्युतिमन्तस्तथैव च ..
उत्कचा राक्षसाः कार्या विकलाक्षा विभीषणाः .. 15 ..
text_mt:
and the others are renowned as having human bodies and horse faces. / Those with horse faces should be made wearing all ornaments,
accompanied by song and musical instruments, and endowed with radiant beauty. / Rākṣasas should be made with dishevelled hair, irregular eyes, and terrifying.

sanskrit_iast:
devakārāśca kartavyā nāgāḥ phaṇavirājitāḥ ..
sālaṃkārā smṛtāḥ sarve yakṣāste'bhihitā mayā .. 16 ..
meaning:
देवकाराश्च कर्तव्या नागाः फणविराजिताः ..
सालंकारा स्मृताः सर्वे यक्षास्तेऽभिहिता मया .. 16 ..
text_mt: Nāgas should be made in the form of gods, adorned with hoods. / All Yakṣas have been declared by me as endowed with ornaments.

sanskrit_iast:
surāṇāṃ pramathāḥ kāryāḥ pramāṇena vivarjitāḥ ..
piśācāśca tathā kāryā pramāṇena vivarjitāḥ .. 17 ..
meaning:
सुराणां प्रमथाः कार्याः प्रमाणेन विवर्जिताः ..
पिशाचाश्च तथा कार्या प्रमाणेन विवर्जिताः .. 17 ..
text_mt: The Pramathas of the gods should be made devoid of [standard] proportions; / Piśācas, likewise, should be made devoid of [standard] proportions.

sanskrit_iast:
nānāsattvamukhāḥ kāryā devatānāṃ tathā gaṇāḥ ..
nānāveśā mahārāja nānāyudhadharāstathā .. 18 ..
meaning:
नानासत्त्वमुखाः कार्या देवतानां तथा गणाः ..
नानावेशा महाराज नानायुधधरास्तथा .. 18 ..
text_mt: The troops of the gods should be made with faces of various creatures, / in various dress, O great king, and bearing various weapons,

sanskrit_iast:
nānākrīḍāprasaktāśca nānākarmakarāstathā ..
ekarūpāstu kartavyā vaiṣṇavānāṃ tathā gaṇāḥ .. 19 ..
meaning:
नानाक्रीडाप्रसक्ताश्च नानाकर्मकरास्तथा ..
एकरूपास्तु कर्तव्या वैष्णवानां तथा गणाः .. 19 ..
text_mt: intent upon various sports and performing various tasks. / But the troops of the Vaiṣṇavas should be made of uniform appearance.

sanskrit_iast:
tatrāpi teṣāṃ kartavyā bhedāścatvāra eva ca ..
vāsudevasamāḥ kāryā vāsudevagaṇāḥ śubhāḥ .. 3.42.20 ..
meaning:
तत्रापि तेषां कर्तव्या भेदाश्चत्वार एव च ..
वासुदेवसमाः कार्या वासुदेवगणाः शुभाः .. 3.42.20 ..
text_mt: Even there, four divisions of them should be made: / the auspicious attendants of Vāsudeva should be made resembling Vāsudeva;

sanskrit_iast:
saṃkarṣaṇena sadṛśāstadgaṇāśca tathā smṛtāḥ ..
pradyumnenāniruddhena tadgaṇāḥ sadṛśāstathā .. 21 ..
meaning:
संकर्षणेन सदृशास्तद्गणाश्च तथा स्मृताः ..
प्रद्युम्नेनानिरुद्धेन तद्गणाः सदृशास्तथा .. 21 ..
text_mt: his attendants are also taught to be similar to Saṃkarṣaṇa; / likewise, his attendants are similar to Pradyumna and Aniruddha.

sanskrit_iast:
tatprabhāvāḥ smṛtāḥ sarve tadāyudhadharāstathā ..
nīlotpaladalaśyāmāścandraśubhrāstathaiva ca .. 22 ..
meaning:
तत्प्रभावाः स्मृताः सर्वे तदायुधधरास्तथा ..
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामाश्चन्द्रशुभ्रास्तथैव च .. 22 ..
text_mt: They are all taught to have their splendour and to bear their weapons: / dark like the petal of a blue lotus, and bright as the moon,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā marakatākārā sindūrasadṛśaprabhāḥ ..
rucakasya tu mānena veśyāḥ kāryāstathā striyaḥ .. 23 ..
meaning:
तथा मरकताकारा सिन्दूरसदृशप्रभाः ..
रुचकस्य तु मानेन वेश्याः कार्यास्तथा स्त्रियः .. 23 ..
text_mt: and also having the appearance of emerald, or radiant like red lead. / Courtesans and [similar] women should be made according to the Rucaka proportion.

sanskrit_iast:
veśyānāmuddhataṃ veśaṃ kāryaṃ śṛṅgārasammatam ..
mālavyāmānataḥ kāryā lajjāvatyaḥ kulastriyaḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
वेश्यानामुद्धतं वेशं कार्यं शृङ्गारसम्मतम् ..
मालव्यामानतः कार्या लज्जावत्यः कुलस्त्रियः .. 24 ..
text_mt: The dress of courtesans should be made alluring, appropriate to erotic passion. / Women of good family, possessing modesty, should be made according to the Mālavya proportion,

sanskrit_iast:
nātyunnatena veśena sālaṃkārāstathaiva ca ..
daityadānavayakṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 25 ..
meaning:
नात्युन्नतेन वेशेन सालंकारास्तथैव च ..
दैत्यदानवयक्षाणां राक्षसानां तथैव च .. 25 ..
text_mt: with attire not excessively prominent, and likewise adorned with ornaments. / For Daityas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas alike,

sanskrit_iast:
rūpavatyastathā kāryāḥ patayo manujasattama ..
mātaraḥ svena rūpeṇa tathā kāryā narādhipa .. 26 ..
meaning:
रूपवत्यस्तथा कार्याः पतयो मनुजसत्तम ..
मातरः स्वेन रूपेण तथा कार्या नराधिप .. 26 ..
text_mt: their wives, O best of men, should be made beautiful. / The mothers should be represented in their own form, O lord of men;

sanskrit_iast:
piśācānāṃ ca patnyo'pi kāryāstadrūpasaṃyutā ..
vibhartṛkāstu kartavyā striyaḥ palitasaṃyutāḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
पिशाचानां च पत्न्योऽपि कार्यास्तद्रूपसंयुता ..
विभर्तृकास्तु कर्तव्या स्त्रियः पलितसंयुताः .. 27 ..
text_mt: and the wives of Piśācas should also be made endowed with their form. / Women without husbands, however, should be made with grey hair,

sanskrit_iast:
śuklavastraparīdhānāḥ sarvālaṅkāravarjitāḥ ..
kubjā vāmanikā vṛddhā tathā rūpavatī bhavet .. 28 ..
meaning:
शुक्लवस्त्रपरीधानाः सर्वालङ्कारवर्जिताः ..
कुब्जा वामनिका वृद्धा तथा रूपवती भवेत् .. 28 ..
text_mt: clad in white garments, and stripped of all ornaments. / A hunchbacked, dwarfish, or elderly woman may likewise be beautiful.

sanskrit_iast:
rājastrīṇāṃ parīvāre vṛddhaḥ syātkañcukī punaḥ ..
rucakasya tu mānena vaiśyamānaṃ vidhīyate .. 29 ..
meaning:
राजस्त्रीणां परीवारे वृद्धः स्यात्कञ्चुकी पुनः ..
रुचकस्य तु मानेन वैश्यमानं विधीयते .. 29 ..
text_mt: In the retinue of royal women there should also be an aged chamberlain. / The proportion of a vaiśya is prescribed according to the Rucaka [measurement],

sanskrit_iast:
śaśakasya tu mānena śūdramānaṃ tathaiva ca ..
yathā jātyanurūpeṇa veṣeṇa manujeśvara .. 3.42.30 ..
meaning:
शशकस्य तु मानेन शूद्रमानं तथैव च ..
यथा जात्यनुरूपेण वेषेण मनुजेश्वर .. 3.42.30 ..
text_mt: and the proportion of a śūdra according to the Śaśaka [measurement]. / In attire according to caste, O lord of men,

sanskrit_iast:
daityādiyoṣitāṃ kāryāḥ paricārastriyaḥ sadā ..
mahāśirā mahorasko mahānāso mahāhanuḥ .. 31 ..
meaning:
दैत्यादियोषितां कार्याः परिचारस्त्रियः सदा ..
महाशिरा महोरस्को महानासो महाहनुः .. 31 ..
text_mt: the maidservants of the women of Daityas and the rest should always be made. / With a large head, broad chest, large nose, and large jaw,

sanskrit_iast:
pīta skandhabhujagrīvaḥ parimāṇena cocchritaḥ ..
tritaraṅgalalāṭaśca vyomadṛṣṭirmahākaṭiḥ .. 32 ..
meaning:
पीत स्कन्धभुजग्रीवः परिमाणेन चोच्छ्रितः ..
त्रितरङ्गललाटश्च व्योमदृष्टिर्महाकटिः .. 32 ..
text_mt: with stout shoulders, arms, and neck, tall in stature, / with a forehead [creased] with three waves, gazing towards the sky, with a broad waist,

sanskrit_iast:
dṛptaścitravidā kāryaḥ senāyāḥ patirūrjitaḥ .. .
yodhāḥ kāryā mahārāja prāyaśo bhrukuṭīmukhāḥ .. 33 ..
meaning:
दृप्तश्चित्रविदा कार्यः सेनायाः पतिरूर्जितः .. .
योधाः कार्या महाराज प्रायशो भ्रुकुटीमुखाः .. 33 ..
text_mt: haughty and mighty, the commander of an army should be made by one skilled in painting. / Warriors, O great king, should mostly be made with frowning faces,

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃciduddhatavegāśca kāryāścoddhatadarśanāḥ ..
abhyudgatāśca kartavyā āyudhīyāḥ padātayaḥ .. 34 ..
meaning:
किंचिदुद्धतवेगाश्च कार्याश्चोद्धतदर्शनाः ..
अभ्युद्गताश्च कर्तव्या आयुधीयाः पदातयः .. 34 ..
text_mt: with somewhat impetuous speed, and having a haughty appearance. / Infantrymen bearing weapons should be made rushing forward;

sanskrit_iast:
khaḍgacarmadharāḥ kāryāḥ karṇāṭakavapurdharāḥ ..
varabāṇadharāḥ kāryā nagnajaṅghāśca dhanvinaḥ .. 35 ..
meaning:
खड्गचर्मधराः कार्याः कर्णाटकवपुर्धराः ..
वरबाणधराः कार्या नग्नजङ्घाश्च धन्विनः .. 35 ..
text_mt: they should be made holding sword and shield, with the build of Karṇāṭaka [soldiers]. / Archers should be made bearing excellent arrows, with bare shanks,

sanskrit_iast:
nātyuddhatena veṣeṇa sopānatkāstathaiva te ..
yathoktalakṣaṇāḥ kāryāḥ kuñjarāsturagādayaḥ .. 36 ..
meaning:
नात्युद्धतेन वेषेण सोपानत्कास्तथैव ते ..
यथोक्तलक्षणाः कार्याः कुञ्जरास्तुरगादयः .. 36 ..
text_mt: with attire not excessively showy, and wearing shoes. / Elephants, horses, and the like should be made with their prescribed characteristics.

sanskrit_iast:
hastyārohāstu kartavyā muhuḥ śyāmāstu varṇataḥ ..
keśaiśca jūṭaṭamaraiḥ sālaṃkārāstathaiva ca. .. 37 ..
meaning:
हस्त्यारोहास्तु कर्तव्या मुहुः श्यामास्तु वर्णतः ..
केशैश्च जूटटमरैः सालंकारास्तथैव च. .. 37 ..
text_mt: Elephant riders, however, should be made dark in complexion, / with hair tied in high topknots, and likewise adorned with ornaments.

sanskrit_iast:
udīcyaveśāḥ kartavyāsturagāṇāṃ tu sādinaḥ ..
uddhatena tu veṣeṇa kartavyā bandinastathā ..38 ..
meaning:
उदीच्यवेशाः कर्तव्यास्तुरगाणां तु सादिनः ..
उद्धतेन तु वेषेण कर्तव्या बन्दिनस्तथा ..38 ..
text_mt: Horse riders should be made in northern dress. / Bards should be made in haughty attire,

sanskrit_iast:
sirādarśitakaṇṭhāśca tathaivonmukhadṛṣṭayaḥ ..
āhvānakāstu kartavyāḥ kapilāḥ kekarekṣaṇāḥ .. 39 ..
meaning:
सिरादर्शितकण्ठाश्च तथैवोन्मुखदृष्टयः ..
आह्वानकास्तु कर्तव्याः कपिलाः केकरेक्षणाः .. 39 ..
text_mt: with veins visible in their necks, and with their gaze directed upward. / Summoners should be made tawny, with squinting eyes,

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃciddānavasaṅkāśāḥ prāyaśo daṇḍapāṇayaḥ ..
na kekarānna kapilānyuddhe dvaṃdvānsamālikhet .. 3.42.40 ..
meaning:
किंचिद्दानवसङ्काशाः प्रायशो दण्डपाणयः ..
न केकरान्न कपिलान्युद्धे द्वंद्वान्समालिखेत् .. 3.42.40 ..
text_mt: somewhat resembling Dānavas, mostly holding a staff in hand. / One should not paint combatants in a duel as squint-eyed or tawny.

sanskrit_iast:
nātyunnatena veṣeṇa na ca śāntena śasyate ..
pārśvabaddhena khaḍgena pratīhārastu daṇḍavān .. 41 ..
meaning:
नात्युन्नतेन वेषेण न च शान्तेन शस्यते ..
पार्श्वबद्धेन खड्गेन प्रतीहारस्तु दण्डवान् .. 41 ..
text_mt: A doorkeeper is commended with attire neither excessively prominent nor subdued, / bearing a staff, with a sword fastened at his side.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃveṣṭitaśiraskāśca kartavyā vaṇijastathā ..
gāyanā nartakā ye vā vādyavādaviśuddhaye .. 42 ..
meaning:
संवेष्टितशिरस्काश्च कर्तव्या वणिजस्तथा ..
गायना नर्तका ये वा वाद्यवादविशुद्धये .. 42 ..
text_mt: Merchants should be made with their heads wrapped [in turbans]. / Singers and dancers who [perform] for the excellence of instrumental music

sanskrit_iast:
uddhatena tu veṣeṇa kāryāste manujottama ..
āsannapalitā kāryāḥ svabhūṣaṇavibhūṣitāḥ .. 43 ..
meaning:
उद्धतेन तु वेषेण कार्यास्ते मनुजोत्तम ..
आसन्नपलिता कार्याः स्वभूषणविभूषिताः .. 43 ..
text_mt: should be made in haughty attire, O best of men. / Elders with grey hair should be made adorned with their proper ornaments.

sanskrit_iast:
paurajānapadāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ śubhavastravibhūṣaṇāḥ ..
prasṛtapravaṇāḥ prahvāḥ svabhāvapriyadarśinaḥ .. 44 ...
meaning:
पौरजानपदाः श्रेष्ठाः शुभवस्त्रविभूषणाः ..
प्रसृतप्रवणाः प्रह्वाः स्वभावप्रियदर्शिनः .. 44 ...
text_mt: Eminent citizens and villagers should have auspicious garments and ornaments; / they should be gracious, humble, bowed, and pleasing in their natural appearance.

sanskrit_iast:
svakarmopaskaravyagraḥ kāryaḥ karmakaro janaḥ..
prāṃśavaḥ pīnagātrāśca pīnagrīvaśirodharāḥ .. 45 ..
meaning:
स्वकर्मोपस्करव्यग्रः कार्यः कर्मकरो जनः..
प्रांशवः पीनगात्राश्च पीनग्रीवशिरोधराः .. 45 ..
text_mt: A working person should be made occupied with the implements of his work. / Tall, stout of body, with thick necks and heads,

sanskrit_iast:
ugrāśca nīcakeśāśca mallāḥ kāryāstathoddhatāḥ ..
vṛṣāḥ kesariṇaścaiva yāścānyāḥ sattvajātayaḥ .. 46 ..
meaning:
उग्राश्च नीचकेशाश्च मल्लाः कार्यास्तथोद्धताः ..
वृषाः केसरिणश्चैव याश्चान्याः सत्त्वजातयः .. 46 ..
text_mt: fierce, with cropped hair, and arrogant should wrestlers be made. / Bulls, lions, and other species of animals

sanskrit_iast:
yathābhūminiveśāste lokaṃ dṛṣṭvā narādhipa ..
etadrūpasamuddeśamadṛṣṭānāṃ taveritam .. 47 .
meaning:
यथाभूमिनिवेशास्ते लोकं दृष्ट्वा नराधिप ..
एतद्रूपसमुद्देशमदृष्टानां तवेरितम् .. 47 .
text_mt: should be placed according to their habitat, having observed the world, O lord of men. / This brief statement of forms has been declared to you for [things] unseen.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭaṃ susadṛśaṃ kāryaṃ sarveṣāmaviśeṣataḥ ..
citre sādṛśyakaraṇaṃ pradhānaṃ parikīrtitam .. 48 ..
meaning:
दृष्टं सुसदृशं कार्यं सर्वेषामविशेषतः ..
चित्रे सादृश्यकरणं प्रधानं परिकीर्तितम् .. 48 ..
text_mt: What is visible should be rendered in faithful likeness for all without distinction; / in painting, the production of likeness is proclaimed as foremost.

sanskrit_iast:
buddhyā rūpaṃ yathāveśaṃ varṇaṃ ca manujottama ..
deśedeśe narāḥ kāryā yathāvattatsamudbhavāḥ ..49..
meaning:
बुद्ध्या रूपं यथावेशं वर्णं च मनुजोत्तम ..
देशेदेशे नराः कार्या यथावत्तत्समुद्भवाः ..49..
text_mt: Having understood their form, dress, and colour, O best of men, / people native to each respective region should be rendered correctly.

sanskrit_iast:
deśaṃ niyogaṃ sthānaṃ ca karma buddhvā ca yatnataḥ ..
āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ veśaṃ kāryaṃ narādhipa .. 3.42.50 ..
meaning:
देशं नियोगं स्थानं च कर्म बुद्ध्वा च यत्नतः ..
आसनं शयनं यानं वेशं कार्यं नराधिप .. 3.42.50 ..
text_mt: Having carefully ascertained the region, the occupation, the rank, and the activity, / the seat, bed, vehicle, and dress should be executed, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
saritāṃ saśarīrāṇāṃ vāhanāni pradarśayet ..
pūrṇakumbhakarāḥ kāryāstathā nāmitajānavaḥ .. 51 ..
meaning:
सरितां सशरीराणां वाहनानि प्रदर्शयेत् ..
पूर्णकुम्भकराः कार्यास्तथा नामितजानवः .. 51 ..
text_mt: One should show the mounts of the personified rivers; / they should be made holding full jars in their hands, with knees slightly bent.

sanskrit_iast:
śailānāṃ śikharaṃ mūrdhni darśayenmanujottama ..
dvīpānāṃ ca karaiḥ kāryaṃ tathā bhūmaṇḍalaṃ śubham .. 92 ..
meaning:
शैलानां शिखरं मूर्ध्नि दर्शयेन्मनुजोत्तम ..
द्वीपानां च करैः कार्यं तथा भूमण्डलं शुभम् .. 92 ..
text_mt: One should show the crest of mountains on their heads, O best of men; / and of continents, the auspicious orb of the earth should be depicted in their hands.

sanskrit_iast:
. .. ... ..........rājaṃstathā śikharapāṇayaḥ ..
ratnapātrakarāḥ kāryāḥ sāgarā manujottama .. 53 ..
meaning:
. .. ... ..........राजंस्तथा शिखरपाणयः ..
रत्नपात्रकराः कार्याः सागरा मनुजोत्तम .. 53 ..
text_mt: [...] O king, holding mountain crests in their hands; / the oceans should be made holding vessels filled with jewels, O best of men.

sanskrit_iast:
samudrāṇāṃ prabhāsthāne salilaṃ tu pradarśayet ..
āyudhānāṃ ca taccihnaṃ kiñcinmūrdhani darśayet .. 54 ..
meaning:
समुद्राणां प्रभास्थाने सलिलं तु प्रदर्शयेत् ..
आयुधानां च तच्चिह्नं किञ्चिन्मूर्धनि दर्शयेत् .. 54 ..
text_mt: In place of the halo of oceans, one should display water; / and as for weapons, one should show a small sign of each upon their heads.

sanskrit_iast:
nidhīnāṃ darśayetkumbhaṃ śaṃkhaṃ śaṃkhasya darśayet ..
padmaṃ padmasya rājendra śeṣāṇāmanurūpataḥ .. 55 ..
meaning:
निधीनां दर्शयेत्कुम्भं शंखं शंखस्य दर्शयेत् ..
पद्मं पद्मस्य राजेन्द्र शेषाणामनुरूपतः .. 55 ..
text_mt: Of the treasures, one should show a jar; one should show a conch for Śaṅkha, / a lotus for Padma, O king of kings, and in accordance with the form of the rest.

sanskrit_iast:
kāryasyāvayavāḥ kāryāḥ svaddehasadṛśāḥ pṛthak ..
divyānāṃ darśayeccihnamakṣamālāṃ ca pustakam .. 56 ..
meaning:
कार्यस्यावयवाः कार्याः स्वद्देहसदृशाः पृथक् ..
दिव्यानां दर्शयेच्चिह्नमक्षमालां च पुस्तकम् .. 56 ..
text_mt: The limbs of an activity should be executed appropriately to their respective bodies; / one should show the emblems of divine beings, such as the rosary and the book.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi rūpaṃ yadyasya dṛśyate ..
ākāśaṃ daśaryedvidvānvivarṇaṃ khagamākulam .. 57 ..
meaning:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि रूपं यद्यस्य दृश्यते ..
आकाशं दशर्येद्विद्वान्विवर्णं खगमाकुलम् .. 57 ..
text_mt: Henceforth I will declare the form of each thing as it is seen: / the wise painter should show the sky devoid of colour and crowded with birds.

sanskrit_iast:
tathaiva darśayedrājaṃstārakāmaṇḍitaṃ divam .
bhūmiṃ ca jāṅgalānūpamiśrāṃ svaiḥsvaistathā guṇaiḥ .. 58 ..
meaning:
तथैव दर्शयेद्राजंस्तारकामण्डितं दिवम् .
भूमिं च जाङ्गलानूपमिश्रां स्वैःस्वैस्तथा गुणैः .. 58 ..
text_mt: Likewise, O king, one should show the heavens adorned with stars; / and the earth, whether arid, marshy, or mixed, along with their respective attributes.

sanskrit_iast:
parvataṃ tu śilājālaiḥ śikharairdhātubhirdrumaiḥ ..
nirjharairbhujagaiścaiva darśayennṛpasattama .. 59 ..
meaning:
पर्वतं तु शिलाजालैः शिखरैर्धातुभिर्द्रुमैः ..
निर्झरैर्भुजगैश्चैव दर्शयेन्नृपसत्तम .. 59 ..
text_mt: A mountain, however, one should show with heaps of stones, peaks, minerals, trees, / waterfalls, and serpents, O best of kings.

sanskrit_iast:
vanaṃ nānāvidhairvṛkṣairvihaṅgaiḥ śvāpadaistathā ..
toyaṃ ca darśayedvidvānanantairmatsyakacchapaiḥ .. 3.42.60 ..
meaning:
वनं नानाविधैर्वृक्षैर्विहङ्गैः श्वापदैस्तथा ..
तोयं च दर्शयेद्विद्वाननन्तैर्मत्स्यकच्छपैः .. 3.42.60 ..
text_mt: A forest with diverse kinds of trees, birds, and wild beasts; / and the wise painter should show water with innumerable fish and tortoises,

sanskrit_iast:
padmākṣaiśca mahārāja tathānyairjalajairguṇaiḥ ..
devatāveśmabhiścitraiḥ prāsādāpaṇaveśmabhiḥ .. 61 ..
meaning:
पद्माक्षैश्च महाराज तथान्यैर्जलजैर्गुणैः ..
देवतावेश्मभिश्चित्रैः प्रासादापणवेश्मभिः .. 61 ..
text_mt: and with lotuses, O great king, as well as other aquatic qualities; / a city the wise painter should show with diverse shrines of deities, with palaces, shops, and houses,

sanskrit_iast:
nagaraṃ darśayedvidvān rājamārgaiśca śobhanaiḥ ..
vamatyā darśayedgrāmaṃ kiñcidudyānabhūṣitam .. 62 ..
meaning:
नगरं दर्शयेद्विद्वान् राजमार्गैश्च शोभनैः ..
वमत्या दर्शयेद्ग्रामं किञ्चिदुद्यानभूषितम् .. 62 ..
text_mt: and with splendid royal highways; / one should show a village with residences, slightly adorned with gardens.

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣāmatha durgāṇāṃ kartavyaṃ darśanaṃ tathā ..
svabhūmiviniveśena vaprāṭṭālakaparvataiḥ .. 63 ..
meaning:
सर्वेषामथ दुर्गाणां कर्तव्यं दर्शनं तथा ..
स्वभूमिविनिवेशेन वप्राट्टालकपर्वतैः .. 63 ..
text_mt: Likewise, the presentation of all kinds of fortresses is to be executed / according to their proper placement on the terrain, with ramparts, turrets, and mountains.

sanskrit_iast:
paṇyayuktāstu kartavyāstathaivāpaṇabhūmayaḥ ..
ādhānabhūmiḥ kartavyā pānayuktā narākulā .. 64 ..
meaning:
पण्ययुक्तास्तु कर्तव्यास्तथैवापणभूमयः ..
आधानभूमिः कर्तव्या पानयुक्ता नराकुला .. 64 ..
text_mt: Marketplaces should indeed be made provided with merchandise; / a tavern should be made provided with liquor and crowded with people.

sanskrit_iast:
uttarīyavihīnāṃśca dyūtasaktānpradarśayet..
jitāñśokasamāyuktānhṛṣṭāṃllabdhajayāṃstathā .. 65 ..
meaning:
उत्तरीयविहीनांश्च द्यूतसक्तान्प्रदर्शयेत्..
जिताञ्शोकसमायुक्तान्हृष्टांल्लब्धजयांस्तथा .. 65 ..
text_mt: One should show those engaged in gambling stripped of their upper garments, / those defeated filled with grief, and the victorious rejoicing.

sanskrit_iast:
caturaṅgabalopetāṃ praharadbhirnarairyutām ..
mṛtāvayavaraktāḍhyāṃ raṇabhūmiṃ pradarśayet .. 66 ..
meaning:
चतुरङ्गबलोपेतां प्रहरद्भिर्नरैर्युताम् ..
मृतावयवरक्ताढ्यां रणभूमिं प्रदर्शयेत् .. 66 ..
text_mt: One should show a battlefield furnished with the fourfold army, full of men striking, / and rich in dead limbs and blood.

sanskrit_iast:
citākuṇapasaṃyuktaṃ śmaśānaṃ ca tathā nṛpa ..
yuktaṃ sabhārairuṣṭrādyairmārgaṃ sārthaṃ pradarśayet .. 67 ..
meaning:
चिताकुणपसंयुक्तं श्मशानं च तथा नृप ..
युक्तं सभारैरुष्ट्राद्यैर्मार्गं सार्थं प्रदर्शयेत् .. 67 ..
text_mt: Likewise, O king, a cremation ground filled with pyres and corpses; / one should show a road with a caravan accompanied by loaded camels and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
sacandragrahanakṣatrāṃ tathā darśitalaukikām ..
āsannataskarāṃ rātriṃ darśayetsuptamānavām .. 68
meaning:
सचन्द्रग्रहनक्षत्रां तथा दर्शितलौकिकाम् ..
आसन्नतस्करां रात्रिं दर्शयेत्सुप्तमानवाम् .. 68
text_mt: One should show the night with the moon, planets, and constellations, showing people asleep, / with thieves lurking near.

sanskrit_iast:
prāgrātre darśayettatra tathā caivābhisārikām ..
sāruṇo mlānadīpaśca pratyūṣo rutakukkuṭaḥ ..69..
meaning:
प्राग्रात्रे दर्शयेत्तत्र तथा चैवाभिसारिकाम् ..
सारुणो म्लानदीपश्च प्रत्यूषो रुतकुक्कुटः ..69..
text_mt: There, in the early night, one should likewise show a woman going to meet her lover; / the dawn is reddish, with dimming lamps and the crowing of roosters,

sanskrit_iast:
karmavyagrajanaprāyaḥ kartavyo vānarastathā ..
dvijairniyamabhiryuktāṃ gāṃ sandhyāṃ pradarśayet .. 3.42.70 ..
meaning:
कर्मव्यग्रजनप्रायः कर्तव्यो वानरस्तथा ..
द्विजैर्नियमभिर्युक्तां गां सन्ध्यां प्रदर्शयेत् .. 3.42.70 ..
text_mt: mostly filled with people occupied in their tasks, or a monkey; / one should show the twilight, along with cattle, accompanied by brahmins observing vows.

sanskrit_iast:
tamaso darśanaṃ kāryaṃ vāse saṃsarpakairnaraiḥ ..
kumudānāṃ vikāśe ca jyotsnāṃ candre pradarśayet ..71..
meaning:
तमसो दर्शनं कार्यं वासे संसर्पकैर्नरैः ..
कुमुदानां विकाशे च ज्योत्स्नां चन्द्रे प्रदर्शयेत् ..71..
text_mt: Darkness should be shown by men groping about inside a house; / and in the blooming of the night-lotuses, one should show moonlight, along with the moon.

sanskrit_iast:
darśayetsarajasyaṃ ca śayyāṃ karṇotkarāvṛtām ..
sadvṛttamānavaprāyāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ vṛṣṭyāmpradarśayet..72..
meaning:
दर्शयेत्सरजस्यं च शय्यां कर्णोत्करावृताम् ..
सद्वृत्तमानवप्रायां वृष्टिं वृष्ट्याम्प्रदर्शयेत्..72..
text_mt: One should show [...] a bed covered with heaps of ears [of grain]; / in a rain scene, one should show rain with mostly well-behaved people.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇināṃ kleśataptānāmādityena nidarśanam ..
vṛkṣairvasantajaiḥ phullaiḥ kokilāmadhupotkaṭaiḥ .. 73 ..
meaning:
प्राणिनां क्लेशतप्तानामादित्येन निदर्शनम् ..
वृक्षैर्वसन्तजैः फुल्लैः कोकिलामधुपोत्कटैः .. 73 ..
text_mt: [Summer is] the depiction of living beings scorched by the affliction of the sun; / with trees native to spring in full bloom, swarming with cuckoos and bees,

sanskrit_iast:
prahṛṣṭanaranārīkaṃ vasantaṃ ca pradarśayet ..
klāntaiḥ kāryaṃ narairgrīṣmaṃ mṛgaiśchāyāgataistathā .. 74 ..
meaning:
प्रहृष्टनरनारीकं वसन्तं च प्रदर्शयेत् ..
क्लान्तैः कार्यं नरैर्ग्रीष्मं मृगैश्छायागतैस्तथा .. 74 ..
text_mt: and with delighted men and women, one should show the spring; / the summer should be made with exhausted men, and beasts gone into the shade,

sanskrit_iast:
mahiṣaiḥ paṅkamalinaistathā śuṣkajalāśayam ..
vihaṅgairdrumasaṃlīnaiḥ siṃhavyāghrairguhāgataiḥ .. 75..
meaning:
महिषैः पङ्कमलिनैस्तथा शुष्कजलाशयम् ..
विहङ्गैर्द्रुमसंलीनैः सिंहव्याघ्रैर्गुहागतैः .. 75..
text_mt: with buffaloes soiled with mud, dry reservoirs of water, / birds hiding in trees, and lions and tigers retreated into caves.

sanskrit_iast:
toyanamraghanairyuktaṃ sendracāpavibhūṣaṇaiḥ ..
vidyudvidyotanairyuktāṃ prāvṛṣaṃ darśayettathā .. 76 ..
meaning:
तोयनम्रघनैर्युक्तं सेन्द्रचापविभूषणैः ..
विद्युद्विद्योतनैर्युक्तां प्रावृषं दर्शयेत्तथा .. 76 ..
text_mt: One should likewise show the rainy season furnished with clouds heavy with water and adorned with rainbows, / accompanied by flashing lightning.

sanskrit_iast:
saphaladrumasaṃyuktāṃ pakvasasyāṃ vasundharām ..
sahasapadmasalilāṃ śaradaṃ tu tathā likhet .. 77 ..
meaning:
सफलद्रुमसंयुक्तां पक्वसस्यां वसुन्धराम् ..
सहसपद्मसलिलां शरदं तु तथा लिखेत् .. 77 ..
text_mt: One should paint autumn with the earth filled with fruit-laden trees and ripe grain, / and with water filled with swans and lotuses.

sanskrit_iast:
savāṣpasalilasthānaṃ tathā lūnavasundharam ..
sanīhāradigantaṃ ca hemantaṃ darśayedbudhaḥ .. 78 ..
meaning:
सवाष्पसलिलस्थानं तथा लूनवसुन्धरम् ..
सनीहारदिगन्तं च हेमन्तं दर्शयेद्बुधः .. 78 ..
text_mt: The wise painter should show early winter with steamy waters, the earth reaped, / and the horizon misty.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛṣṭavāyasamātaṅgaṃ śītārtajanasaṅkulam ..
śiśiraṃ tu likhedvidvānhimacchannadigantarama .. 79 ..
meaning:
हृष्टवायसमातङ्गं शीतार्तजनसङ्कुलम् ..
शिशिरं तु लिखेद्विद्वान्हिमच्छन्नदिगन्तरम .. 79 ..
text_mt: The wise painter should paint late winter with joyous crows and elephants, crowded with people suffering from the cold, / and the horizons veiled in frost.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛkṣāṇāṃ puṣpaphalataḥ prāṇināṃ madatastathā.. ..
ṛtūnāṃ darśanaṃ kāryaṃ lokāndṛṣṭvā narādhipa .. 3.42.80 ..
meaning:
वृक्षाणां पुष्पफलतः प्राणिनां मदतस्तथा.. ..
ऋतूनां दर्शनं कार्यं लोकान्दृष्ट्वा नराधिप .. 3.42.80 ..
text_mt: The depiction of the seasons should be made by means of the flowers and fruits of trees and the rutting of creatures, / having observed the worlds, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
rasabhāvāśca kartavyā yathāpūrvamudāhṛtāḥ ..
yathāyogaṃ tu yuñjīta nṛttābhihitamatra ca ..83 ..
meaning:

Thus painted by the wise through conceptualisation, with postures, grace, playfulness, aesthetic flavours, and the like, / a painting delights the gaze of the eyes and respectfully grants desired wishes.
3.43 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The erotic, comic, pathetic, heroic, furious, terrifying, / odious, wondrous, and peaceful are traditionally known as the nine aesthetic flavours of painting.
Among these, whatever is beautiful with splendour, charm, sweetness of line, / and the clever ornaments of women, belongs to the erotic aesthetic flavour.
Whatever is largely composed of hunchbacks and dwarfs, looking slightly grotesque, / and needlessly contracting the hand, produces laughter in the comic aesthetic flavour.
Whatever evokes pity in circumstances of begging, separation, abandonment, sale, misfortune, and the like, / one should paint in the pathetic aesthetic flavour.
Harshness, deformity, and anger do not impair [the work] if intended for an expressive purpose; / executed with blazing weapons and ornaments, it belongs to the furious aesthetic flavour.
In matters of heroic resolution, displaying nobility, / having a proud smile, knitted brows, valorous, wondrous—this belongs to the heroic sentiment (vīrarasa).

Whatever involves the wicked, repulsive sights, madmen, beasts of prey, murderers, and the like, / that belongs to the fearful sentiment (bhayānakarasa) in the application of the art of painting.
Despised cremation grounds, acts of slaughter, fearful places— / whatever painting is excellent in being varied, that belongs to the odious sentiment (bībhatsarasa).
When it shows modest horripilation, thought, the face bent like Tārkṣya's, / and looking at one another, that is based on the wondrous sentiment (adbhutarasa).
Whatever has gentle forms, postures of meditation and absorption, / consisting mostly of ascetics, that belongs to the peaceful sentiment (śāntarasa).
Those known as the erotic, the comic, and the peaceful should be painted in residential homes.
The remaining ones should never be made anywhere for anyone. / In the house of the gods, all sentiments are to be made, O king, and in a king's palace.
They must not be made in the royal residence, in the bedchambers of kings; / in the assembly halls in the king's palace all sentiments are to be made.

must always be painted, O great king, in the homes of men. / A man must not execute painting in his own house by himself, O king.
Weakness, heaviness of line, lack of division, / and confusion of colors are declared here to be the defects of painting.
Stance, proportion, weightiness, sweetness, clarity of division, / resemblance, and foreshortening and elongation: this is remembered as the group of eight virtues.
Lacking stance, bereft of sentiment, blank-eyed, dirty, / or devoid of life: that is declared inauspicious.
Where weightiness seems to shine forth, [where it] seems to fear, O king, / where sweetness seems to smile, [there] it appears as if alive.

and with disheveled hair: a man of good fortune should avoid [these]. / And the wise man should paint what is known, never what is unknown.
A painting made well by skilled men knowledgeable in the treatises, O king, / quickly brings prosperity and removes misfortune;
it washes away longing, obstructs incoming misfortune, / spreads pure joy, and produces peerless [delight];
it destroys bad dreams, and pleases the deity of the house. / And where a painting is established, [the place] does not seem empty.
[…] ear, unadorned, / pierced by an arrow, and aged: he who executes [these] is a knower of painting.
Waves, tongues of flame, smoke, fluttering banners, and the like: / he who paints these according to the motion of the wind is considered an accomplished knower of painting.

The sleeping imbued with consciousness, and the dead devoid of consciousness, / and the differentiation of depressions and elevations: he who executes [these] is a knower of painting.
For all these, natural perspective is indeed praised; / frontal positioning should be avoided with effort in painting.
As painting is, so is relief-work declared, O king; / and that should be displayed in metals: gold, silver, copper, and the like.
The making of images in stone, wood, and metals / should be done by this very rule, just as set forth for painting.
Likewise, modeling in clay or plaster (pustakarma) is prescribed by this rule; / and that is spoken of as twofold: solid and hollow.
The solid should always be made with metals, stones, wood, and clay; / the hollow should be made with leather, and likewise with wood and metals.
A firm coating of clay is to be applied to a model made of leather. / According to this rule in the treatise, one should likewise paint on cloth.
When this has been told to you in mere summary, O king, / it is impossible to state it in detail even in many hundreds of years.

Painting is the foremost of the arts, conferring dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation; / and it is the first auspicious thing in a house where it is established.
Just as Sumeru is foremost of mountains, just as Garuḍa is chief of birds, / just as a king is foremost of men, so in this world the art of painting is foremost of arts.
The Citrasūtra is completed.
3.44
Vajra said:
Tell me, O sinless one, about the fashioning of divine forms,
so that, made according to the treatise, [the deity] may always be present.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Listen, O king, as I speak of the fashioning of divine forms;
at the very beginning I will describe the Triple Form to you, O king.
The auspicious characteristics of the image of Viṣṇu of boundless valor: / his form associated with Brahmā is passionate (rājasī), setting everything into motion;
his Vaiṣṇava form is known as pure (sāttvikī), protecting the world; / and his form associated with Rudra is known as dark (tāmasī), bringing about dissolution.

This form of the threefold image of the noble Janārdana has been spoken to you. / I shall tell you the nature of the lotus, O king, upon which the worship of the lords is to be performed. 21
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Made of gold, silver, copper, or brass, / measuring two cubits, a lotus should be made with lovely filaments. 1
Its circular pericarp should be made of eight parts, O king, / and elevated by an eighth part; it should be made resting upon the petals. 2
One should make forty-nine divisions upon the pericarp; / circular segments of the pericarp measuring the size of a barley corn. 3
It should be made with a sixteenth part according to its width; / and one should fill the rest with eight very glossy petals. 4
Its consecration should be performed, and there one should worship the gods: / there one should worship Brahmā; there one should worship Hari; 5

Thus this incomparable form of his, who consists of the entire universe, has been declared to you; / in this way, the foremost of the universe indeed sustains the entire universe through his body. 19
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
This modification in the cycle of transmigration is considered to belong to the supreme Puruṣa; / and all modification is dark, so through it the cycle of transmigration is preserved.
The Lord, the creator of beings, assumes a dark form; / Hari’s wearing of all ornaments is declared to be through Brahmā.
Hari bears upon his chest knowledge, the spotless Kaustubha jewel; / the forest garland is proclaimed to be dark, long, and variegated,
by which, O king, this entire world of moving and unmoving beings is bound. / Ignorance is his garment, which protects the cycle of transmigration.
Knowledge is taught to be white; ignorance is said to be dark; / positioned between ignorance and knowledge, nescience is declared.
It is neither dark nor likewise white, and therefore it is this superior knowledge. / He indeed bears an intermediate realm resembling pure gold.

The mind is to be known as Garuḍa, moving within the bodies of all beings; / there is nothing swifter than it, and likewise nothing stronger.
The four cardinal directions, O knower of dharma, and as many intermediate directions— / eight arms are designated for that god who wields the Śārṅga bow. / Strength, knowledge, sovereignty, and energy, O scion of Yadu— / these are to be known as the four faces of that god of gods.
Lord Vāsudeva, the powerful Saṃkarṣaṇa, / Pradyumna, and Aniruddha are proclaimed as beginning with strength.
Two arms are to be known for each face of the great soul; / in the hands of Vāsudeva are to be understood the sun and the lord of the night.
In Saṃkarṣaṇa’s hands are the pestle and plough; / in Pradyumna’s, O mighty-armed one, bow and arrow are to be known.
The shield and sword of Aniruddha are to be known by the wise; / the sun and moon are both to be understood as Puruṣa and Prakṛti.

text_mt:
And these are considered the discus and mace in the hand of Vāsudeva. / Know Time to be the plough, and Death likewise the pestle.
With these two, Rudra-Saṃkarṣaṇa drags this world of moving and unmoving beings. / The Śārṅga bow in the hand of Pradyumna is remembered as fire,
and the supreme object of meditation is the target: with these two, yogins cut through. / The shield in the hand of Brahmā-Aniruddha, O mighty-armed one,
is to be known as the veil of ignorance, whose purpose is the creation of the world. / The sword Nandaka is detachment; having cut through bondage with it, / yogins rejoice, and therefore it is called Nandaka.
This peerless form of him, consisting of the whole universe, has thus been proclaimed to you; / thus does that god, the foremost of the universe, uphold the entire world with his body.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, and Aghora, O mighty-armed one; / likewise Puruṣa is to be known, and Īśāna as the fifth face.

Sadyojāta is taught to be earth, and Vāmadeva water; / one should know Aghora to be fire, and Tatpuruṣa is considered wind.
And Īśāna is space, the fifth face situated above. / Now I will describe in detail the five faces of Śambhu.
The eastern face of the great-souled Śambhu is to be known as Mahādeva; / its three eyes, O dear one, are the moon, the sun, and fire.
The southern face is fierce, proclaimed as Bhairava; / that which is his western face is called the face of Nandin.
The northern face of that god is to be known as the face of Umā; / the fifth, named Sadāśiva, is to be known as his purifying [face].
All are three-eyed; Vāmadeva is two-eyed. / The face of Mahādeva is earth; then there is the face of Bhairava.
The face of Nandin is wind; the Raudra face is said to be water; / the face of Sadāśiva, O scion of Yadu, is to be known as space.

His ten arms are the directions, to be understood as corresponding to the faces; / in the hand of Mahādeva are to be known the rosary and water-pot.
In the face of Sadāśiva, bow and arrow are to be known, O mighty-armed one; / the bow of Maheśvara is thence called Pināka.
The explanation of these has already been stated, O slayer of foes. / In the hands of Bhairava are the staff and the citron.
Death is designated as the staff, and the citron likewise in the hand: / whatever atoms exist of all the seeds of the universe, O king,
filled with them, the jewel-like seed vessel is held in Bhairava's hand. / In the hands of Nandin, O scion of Yadu, the shield and trident are to be known.
And the exposition of dharma has already been explained to you by me. / The staff of the trident is the unmanifest, which reaches manifest status in the prongs.
Sattva, rajas, and tamas are thus to be understood, O best of kings. / In the two hands of the Goddess, a mirror and a blue lotus are to be known.

Sovereignty is proclaimed to be the digit of the moon upon the head of Śambhu; / wrath, which calms the three worlds, is remembered by the name of Vāsuki.
Broad and variegated craving is proclaimed to be the tiger skin; / the bull, indeed, is Lord Dharma, proclaimed to have four feet.
The entity that brings forth the universe is proclaimed to be Prakṛti; / and all Prakṛti is white, and therefore Maheśvara is white.

Vajra said:
Tell me of the fashioning of the forms of the two Nāsatyas, O infallible one, / and of the appearances of the two Nāsatyas, for you are called omniscient.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
With the hue and radiance of lotus leaves, wearing garments like lotus leaves, / two-armed, accompanied by gods, the two divine physicians are to be made.
Endowed with all ornaments, especially charming-eyed; / divine medicinal herbs should be placed in their right hands.
In their left hands, books should be made, pleasing to see, O twice-born; / on the right side of one and on the left of the other, O Yādava,
a pair of women should be made, shapely and lovely to behold; / and their two names are proclaimed as Rūpasaṃpad and Ākṛti.
Rūpasaṃpad is described as resembling a madhūka blossom; / Ākṛti is spoken of in the world as resembling a reed-stalk; / they should not hold vessels in hand, and they should be clad in moon-white garments.
