Vajra said:
Of Śakra, Kīnāśa, Varuṇa, and Dhanada, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / relate the making of their forms along with the reasons, O infallible one.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Śakra, the lord of the gods, should be depicted white, upon a four-tusked elephant; / and Śacī should be placed on his left lap, being protected.
Clad in blue garments, possessing the radiance of gold, endowed with all ornaments, / and adorned with an eye situated obliquely on his forehead, he should be made.
Śakra should be made four-armed, and likewise Śacī two-armed; / a lotus and an elephant-goad should be made in Śakra's right hands.
One left [arm] rests behind Śacī's back, and the second is joined with a thunderbolt; / in the left hand of Śacī, a charming sprig of the santāna-tree should be placed.
Her right [hand] should be placed behind the back of the lord of gods; / the wearing of ornaments by him was specified by Brahmā himself.

text_mt:
By him likewise his four arms were declared; / and his state of having three eyes was spoken of by Śambhu, the god of gods.
His gold-like hue is due to his being a source of splendors; / that which is his blue garment is proclaimed to be space.
The elephant-goad in his hand is his command, which subdues all beings; / holding royal majesty, situated on a lotus together with a lotus, O lord of the earth,
with his hand, the glorious Maghavan is the foremost among the gods; / wrath, which calms the wicked, is remembered as the thunderbolt in Śakra's hand.
Śakra is remembered as Vāsudeva, and therefore Śacī is considered Lakṣmī; / and the sprig of the santāna-tree in her hand is to be known as progeny.
Airāvaṇa is to be understood as material wealth, and his tusks are proclaimed / to be the might of divine favor, counsel, and personal energy, endowed with great power.
This form of Vāsudeva as Śakra, the king of the gods, has been declared to you, O king; / now I shall tell you the form of Yama, under whose power are the pleasure and pain of mortals.

yo moho maraṇaṃ nṝṇāṃ vijñeyo mahiṣastu saḥ ..3.51.10..

ब्रह्मणा तस्य निर्दिष्टं सर्वाभरणधारणम् ..

sanskrit_iast:
amoghaṃ tu kare daṇḍaṃ mṛtyuṃ dhārayate yamaḥ ..
aniruddhena tasyoktaṃ dhāraṇaṃ khaḍgacarmaṇoḥ .. 11 ..
meaning:
अमोघं तु करे दण्डं मृत्युं धारयते यमः ..
अनिरुद्धेन तस्योक्तं धारणं खड्गचर्मणोः .. 11 ..
text_mt: Yama holds death in his hand as an unfailing staff; / his holding of the sword and shield was spoken of through Aniruddha.

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
कालरात्री तु विज्ञेया धूमोर्णा यदुनन्दन ..
तस्यास्तु शूलिना प्रोक्तं बीजपूरकधारणम् .. 12 ..
text_mt: Dhūmorṇā is to be understood as Kālarātrī, O delight of the Yadus; / her holding of the citron was declared by the Trident-bearer.

sanskrit_iast:

चित्रगुप्तो विनिर्दिष्टस्तथात्मा सर्वदेहगः ..
पत्रं धर्ममधर्मं च करस्था तस्य लेखिनी .. 13 ..
text_mt: Citragupta is designated likewise as the Self abiding in all bodies; / the leaf is dharma and adharma, and the pen is held in his hand.

sanskrit_iast:
kāla eva svarūpeṇa kālo yamasamīpagaḥ ..
tasya pāśaḥ kare ghoro yamamārgaḥ suduṣkaraḥ .. 14 ..
meaning:
काल एव स्वरूपेण कालो यमसमीपगः ..
तस्य पाशः करे घोरो यममार्गः सुदुष्करः .. 14 ..
text_mt: Kāla near Yama is Time itself in its essential nature; / his terrible noose in hand is the path of Yama, exceedingly difficult to traverse.

sanskrit_iast:
vajra uvāca ..
saṃhārahetukī mūrtirviṣṇoḥ saṅkarṣaṇo mataḥ ..
sa tu devastvayā proktaścandraśuklavapurmahān .. 12 ..
meaning:
वज्र उवाच ..
संहारहेतुकी मूर्तिर्विष्णोः सङ्कर्षणो मतः ..
स तु देवस्त्वया प्रोक्तश्चन्द्रशुक्लवपुर्महान् .. 12 ..
text_mt:
Vajra said:
Saṃkarṣaṇa is considered the form of Viṣṇu that causes destruction; / yet that god was described by you as having a vast body white as the moon.

sanskrit_iast:
talpe saṃhārakartṛtve kṛṣṇamūrtiḥ kathaṃ yamaḥ ..
etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ chindhi bhṛguvaṃśavivardhana ..16..
meaning:
तल्पे संहारकर्तृत्वे कृष्णमूर्तिः कथं यमः ..
एतं मे संशयं छिन्धि भृगुवंशविवर्धन ..16..
text_mt: How is Yama, who performs destruction on the bed [of time], a dark form? / Sever this doubt of mine, O enlarger of the Bhṛgu lineage.

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṃḍeya uvāca ..
mūrtiḥ sāṅkarṣiṇī viṣṇo rudraḥ saṃhārakārakaḥ ..
kalpakṣaye tu saṃhāre karoti jagatāṃ hi sā .. 17 ..
meaning:
मार्कंडेय उवाच ..
मूर्तिः साङ्कर्षिणी विष्णो रुद्रः संहारकारकः ..
कल्पक्षये तु संहारे करोति जगतां हि सा .. 17 ..
text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Rudra, who causes destruction, is the Saṃkarṣaṇa form of Viṣṇu; / indeed, at the end of an aeon, she brings about the destruction of the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
prakṛto yāti dharmajña saṃhṛtaṃ tu tadā jagata ..
tena prakṛtivarṇasthaḥ karoti jagatāṃ kṣayam .. 18 ..
meaning:
प्रकृतो याति धर्मज्ञ संहृतं तु तदा जगत ..
तेन प्रकृतिवर्णस्थः करोति जगतां क्षयम् .. 18 ..
text_mt: Then, O knower of dharma, the world dissolved goes to Prakṛti; / therefore, abiding in the color of Prakṛti, he brings about the destruction of the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvāpi prāṇisaṃhāraṃ yamarūpī punaḥpunaḥ ..
prāṇināṃ prakṛtau yogaṃ na vidhatte kadācana .. 19 ..
meaning:
कृत्वापि प्राणिसंहारं यमरूपी पुनःपुनः ..
प्राणिनां प्रकृतौ योगं न विधत्ते कदाचन .. 19 ..
text_mt: Even having repeatedly caused the destruction of living beings in the form of Yama, / he never brings about the union of beings with Prakṛti.

sanskrit_iast:
vikāre yojayatyeva sukhaduḥkhātmake tadā ..
vikārarūpavarṇaṃ tu tena saṃharate jagat .. 3.51.20 ..
meaning:
विकारे योजयत्येव सुखदुःखात्मके तदा ..
विकाररूपवर्णं तु तेन संहरते जगत् .. 3.51.20 ..
text_mt: He connects [them] then only to transformation, which consists of pleasure and pain; / therefore, with the color and form of transformation, he destroys the world.

sanskrit_iast:

rūpamataḥ kathayāmi mahātmaṃstoyapatervaruṇasya tavāham .. 21 ..
3.52
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
saptahaṃse rathe kāryo varuṇo yādasāmpatiḥ ..

kiñcitpralambajaṭharo muktāhāravibhūṣaṇaḥ ..

meaning:
रूपमिदं कथितं तव याम्यं पापविनाशकरं विबुधानाम् ..
रूपमतः कथयामि महात्मंस्तोयपतेर्वरुणस्य तवाहम् .. 21 ..
3.52
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
सप्तहंसे रथे कार्यो वरुणो यादसाम्पतिः ..
स्निग्धवैडूर्यसङ्काशः श्वेताम्बरधरस्तथा ..1..
किञ्चित्प्रलम्बजठरो मुक्ताहारविभूषणः ..
सर्वाभरणवान्राजा तया देवश्चतुर्भुजः .. 2 ..
वामभागगतं केतुं मकरस्य तु कारयेत् ..
छत्रं च सुसितं मूर्ध्नि भार्या सर्वाङ्गसुन्दरी .. 3 ..
वामोत्संगगताकार्या गौरी तद्द्विभुजा नृप ..
उत्पलं तु करे वामे दक्षिणं देवपृष्ठगम् .. 4 ..
पद्मपाशौ करे कार्यौ देवदक्षिणहस्तयोः ..
शङ्खं च रत्नपात्रं च वामयोस्तस्य कारयेत् .. 5 ..
text_mt:
This form of Yama has been declared to you, which destroys the sins of the wise; / next I shall declare to you, O great-souled one, the form of Varuṇa, the lord of waters.
3.52
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
On a chariot drawn by seven swans, Varuṇa, the lord of aquatic creatures, should be made, / resembling glossy cat's-eye gem and wearing white garments.
Having a slightly pendulous belly, adorned with a pearl necklace, / having all ornaments, a king, and that god should have four arms.
On his left side, one should make a banner marked with a makara, / and a pure white umbrella above his head; his wife, beautiful in all her limbs,
fair-complexioned, should be made seated on his left lap, having two arms, O king; / [holding] a blue lotus in her left hand, while her right hand goes behind the god.
A lotus and a noose should be placed in the two right hands of the god; / a conch and a vessel of jewels should be made in his two left hands.

sanskrit_iast:
bhāge tu dakṣiṇe gaṅgā makarasthā sacāmarā ..
devī padmakarā kāryā candragaurī varānanā .. 80 ..
vāme tu yamunā kāryā kūrmasaṃsthā sacāmarā ..
nīlotpalakarā saumyā nalinīrajasannibhā .. 7 ..
snigdhavaiḍūrya saṅkāśastvāpovarṇo yato nṛpa ..
tayoranugrahārthāya tadvarṇo varuṇastataḥ .. 8 ..
svarūpavarṇāḥ susitāstā eva dvijapuṃgava ..
vasanaṃ tasya kathitaṃ tā eva susitaṃ nṛpa ..9..
vajra uvāca ..
ambhasastu kathaṃ varṇaḥ satyāsatye tvayerite ..
etattu śrotumicchāmi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me ..3.52.10..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
vaiḍūryābhamapāṃ varṇamatathyaṃ yadunandana ..
chāyāgatasya nabhasastadrūpaṃ tāsu dṛśyate .. 11..
prapātapātairyadrūpamaṃbhasāṃ nṛpa dṛśyate ..
śaśāṅkāṃśupratīkāśaṃ tatsvarūpe pratiṣṭhitam .. 12 ..
meaning:
भागे तु दक्षिणे गङ्गा मकरस्था सचामरा ..
देवी पद्मकरा कार्या चन्द्रगौरी वरानना .. 80 ..
वामे तु यमुना कार्या कूर्मसंस्था सचामरा ..
नीलोत्पलकरा सौम्या नलिनीरजसन्निभा .. 7 ..
स्निग्धवैडूर्य सङ्काशस्त्वापोवर्णो यतो नृप ..
तयोरनुग्रहार्थाय तद्वर्णो वरुणस्ततः .. 8 ..
स्वरूपवर्णाः सुसितास्ता एव द्विजपुंगव ..
वसनं तस्य कथितं ता एव सुसितं नृप ..9..
वज्र उवाच ..
अम्भसस्तु कथं वर्णः सत्यासत्ये त्वयेरिते ..
एतत्तु श्रोतुमिच्छामि परं कौतूहलं हि मे ..3.52.10..
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
वैडूर्याभमपां वर्णमतथ्यं यदुनन्दन ..
छायागतस्य नभसस्तद्रूपं तासु दृश्यते .. 11..
प्रपातपातैर्यद्रूपमंभसां नृप दृश्यते ..
शशाङ्कांशुप्रतीकाशं तत्स्वरूपे प्रतिष्ठितम् .. 12 ..
text_mt:
On his right side, Gaṅgā should be made, standing on a makara, holding a fly-whisk, / a goddess holding a lotus in her hand, fair as the moon, with an auspicious face.
On his left side, Yamunā should be made, standing on a tortoise, holding a fly-whisk, / holding a blue lotus in her hand, gentle, resembling the pollen of a lotus.
Because water is of the hue of glossy cat's-eye gem, O king, / therefore, to favor them, Varuṇa has that same color.
The waters themselves in their intrinsic form are pure white, O best of the twice-born; / his garment is declared to be those very [waters], pure white, O king.
Vajra said:
How is water spoken of by you as having both true and untrue color? / I wish to hear this, for great is my curiosity.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
The hue of water resembling cat's-eye gem is not real, O delighter of the Yadus; / that appearance is seen in them because of the shadow of the sky.
The appearance of the waters that is seen in the falling of waterfalls, O king, / resembling the rays of the moon, is established in its true nature.

sanskrit_iast:
pradyumno vāsudevastu varuṇo yādasāṃ patiḥ ..
tasya bhāryā ratirjñeyā gaurī yādavanandana ..13..
saubhāgyamutpalaṃ tasyāḥ kare suratagaṃ vibho ..
varuṇasya kare padmaṃ vidhidharme mahābhuja .. 14 ..
śaṅkhamarthaṃ vijānīhi pāśaṃ saṃsārabandhanam ..
ratnapātraṃ kare jñeyaṃ sarvaratnadharā dharā .. 15 ..
yaśaśca susitaṃ chatraṃ saukhyaṃ makara eva ca ..
brahmaṇā kathitaṃ tasya bhujābharaṇadhāraṇam .. 16 ..
lavaṇakṣīraājyādi dadhimaṇḍasurodakāḥ ..
tathaivekṣurasodaśca surodaśca tathāparaḥ . 17 ..
samudrāste tu vikhyātā loke naravarottama ..
saptahaṃsā rathe tasya varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ .. 18 ..
jāyā tu yamunā jñeyā siddhirbhāgīrathī dvija ..
vīryakālau vinirdiṣṭau tathā makarakacchapau .. 19 ..
svargagaṅgākare padmaṃ vṛddhayāmunamutpalam .. 3.52.20 ..
meaning:
प्रद्युम्नो वासुदेवस्तु वरुणो यादसां पतिः ..
तस्य भार्या रतिर्ज्ञेया गौरी यादवनन्दन ..13..
सौभाग्यमुत्पलं तस्याः करे सुरतगं विभो ..
वरुणस्य करे पद्मं विधिधर्मे महाभुज .. 14 ..
शङ्खमर्थं विजानीहि पाशं संसारबन्धनम् ..
रत्नपात्रं करे ज्ञेयं सर्वरत्नधरा धरा .. 15 ..
यशश्च सुसितं छत्रं सौख्यं मकर एव च ..
ब्रह्मणा कथितं तस्य भुजाभरणधारणम् .. 16 ..
लवणक्षीरआज्यादि दधिमण्डसुरोदकाः ..
तथैवेक्षुरसोदश्च सुरोदश्च तथापरः . 17 ..
समुद्रास्ते तु विख्याता लोके नरवरोत्तम ..
सप्तहंसा रथे तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः .. 18 ..
जाया तु यमुना ज्ञेया सिद्धिर्भागीरथी द्विज ..
वीर्यकालौ विनिर्दिष्टौ तथा मकरकच्छपौ .. 19 ..
स्वर्गगङ्गाकरे पद्मं वृद्धयामुनमुत्पलम् .. 3.52.20 ..
text_mt:
Varuṇa, the lord of aquatic creatures, is Pradyumna, [an emanation of] Vāsudeva; / his wife, fair-complexioned, is to be known as Rati, O joy of the Yadus.
The blue lotus in her hand, who is set in amorous delight, represents good fortune, O lord; / the lotus in the hand of Varuṇa represents cosmic law and dharma, O mighty-armed one.
Know the conch to be wealth, and the noose to be the bond of worldly existence; / the vessel of jewels in his hand should be known as the earth, bearer of all jewels.
The pure white umbrella is fame, and the makara is pleasure; / the wearing of armlets has been spoken of by Brahmā.
Salt, milk, ghee, whey, liquor, / and likewise sugarcane juice, and another, wine,
those oceans are renowned in the world, O best among men; / [they are] the seven swans on the chariot of that great-souled Varuṇa.
Yamunā should be known as his wife, and Bhāgīrathī as spiritual perfection, O twice-born; / the makara and the tortoise are designated as virility and time.
The lotus is in the hand of the celestial Gaṅgā, [and] the blue lotus in Yamunā's hand indicates prosperity.

कर्तव्यः पद्मपत्राभो धनदो नरवाहनः ..

लम्बोदरश्चतुर्बाहुर्वामपिङ्गललोचनः ..
अपीच्यवेशः कवची हारभारार्पितोदरः .. 2 ..
द्वे च दंष्ट्रे मुखे तस्य कर्तव्ये श्मश्रुधारिणः ..
वामेन विनता कार्या मौलिस्तस्यारिमर्दिनी .. 3 ..
वामोत्संगगता कार्या ऋद्धिर्देवी वरप्रदा ..
देवपृष्ठगतं पाणिं द्विभुजायास्तु दक्षिणम् .. 4 ..

शङ्खपद्मौ निधी कार्यौ स्वरूपौ निधिसंस्थितौ .. 6 ..
text_mt:
This form of the lord of waters, bearer of the noose at the head, has been described to you by me; / beyond this, I shall describe to you the form of the lord of wealth, O moon of the Yadu race.
3.53
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Dhanada, who has man as his mount, should be made with the radiance of lotus petals; / Dhanada is lustrous like gold, adorned with all ornaments.
Pot-bellied, four-armed, with his left eye tawny, / in northern attire, clad in armor, his belly weighed down by heavy necklaces.
Two fangs should be made in his mouth, [and he should be] bearing a beard; / his crown, destroyer of foes, should be made bent towards the left.
Goddess Ṛddhi, grantor of boons, should be made seated on his left lap; / the right hand of the two-armed [goddess] goes behind the god,
and her left hand should be made holding a vessel of jewels, O slayer of foes; / a mace and a spear should be placed in his two right hands.
A round [litter] marked with the emblem of a lion, or a palanquin at his feet; / the treasures Śaṅkha and Padma should be made in their personified forms, resting on treasures.

text_mt:
Their faces emerging from within a conch and a lotus at his sides; / the god, lord of wealth, should be known by you as Aniruddha.
The equipping of all ornaments for him was spoken of by Brahmā; / gold is renowned as the foremost wealth among wealths, / through its favor, he wears a garment resembling gold; / the spear is remembered as power, and the mace as statecraft.
Ṛddhi is declared to be the course of worldly affairs, and is known by her own nature.
The vessel of jewels in her hand is called the receptacle of virtues.
Know the man to be sovereignty, upon which the all-pervading lord always stands; / and the treasures Śaṅkha and Padma are to be understood according to their intrinsic nature.
A portion of wealth triumphs in him, [and] from those two ten-thousandfold is produced; / wealth should be known as accompanied by forbearance, and the banner has the mark of a lion; / the two fangs of that great-souled one, O dear one, are punishment and favor.

Such is [the form] of the lord of yakṣas with endless fangs, in the forest of the river of yakṣas, O king; / what further should I tell you beyond this? Tell me that, O one with wide red eyes.
3.54
Vajra said:
I wish to hear the creation of the images of Suparṇa, the palm tree, / the makara, the deer, and the Maruts, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Tārkṣya, resembling an emerald, with a nose shaped like an owl's, / should be made four-armed, with round eyes and face.
Having the thighs, knees, and feet of a vulture, adorned with two wings.
Golden in lustre and form, devoid of a tail-feathers ornament; / an umbrella and a full water-pot should be placed in his two hands.
In his other two hands, anjali should be formed; / likewise, behind him, the Lord's hands hold an umbrella and a pot.
They should not be made [empty], but should touch the divine feet; / he should be made slightly pot-bellied, adorned with all ornaments.

text_mt:
A palm tree should be made in the shape of a palm tree, and a makara in the shape of a makara; / above it, Acyuta should be made as praised in the Ṛgveda.
Mind, the world, desire, and action are traditionally taught in this order:
Vāsudeva, Acyuta, mighty-armed Pradyumna, / and Aniruddha are proclaimed in this sequence.
Tārkṣya, with the palm-tree and the crocodile, is likewise to be worshipped, O lord of gods, as the lord of death, waters, and wealth. / They alone have been indicated by the wise among the worlds as the lords of fire, the sun, the waters, and the birds.
3.55 / Vajra said: / Tell me, O knower of dharma, the fashioning of the form of Śiva, of Agni, of Nirṛti, / and of Vāyu; herein my doubt is great.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Pārvatī is to be made on the left half, and Śiva is to be made four-armed. / In his right hands are a rosary and a trident.
A mirror and a blue lotus are to be made in the left hands, O joy of the Yadus. / Śambhu should have a single face, and the left is his beloved body.

He has two eyes, O highly fortunate one, and is adorned with all ornaments. / Prakṛti, undivided, is differentiated by the Cosmic Person, O mighty-armed one.
Renowned as Gaurī-Śarva, [this form] is bowed down to by all worlds. / The reason for the trident and the other [attributes] was previously told to you by me.
This form of Īśāna has been related to you; now hear the form of Agni, who is ever devoted to dharma, / for whose sake the Vedas have arisen in the world, and who is the mouth of all gods and asuras.

3.57 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Virūpākṣa has twisted eyes, a tall staff, a radiant face, / upward-standing hair, a tawny beard, two arms, and a terrifying countenance.
In complexion his limbs are reddish-black, and he wears black garments. / He wears all ornaments and holds a staff and reins in his hands.
And his wife should be made, the goddess Nirṛti, / with black limbs, a black face, and a noose in hand, on his left.
Virūpākṣa is declared to be Time, and Nirṛti is Death. / Therefore, O king, he bears a dark form and dark garments.
The staff in his hand is killing, and the camel's reins are binding; / and the camel on his left is spoken of as great delusion.
This form of Virūpākṣa, that peerless lord of rākṣasas, has been indicated. / Henceforth, O king, I tell you today the form of Vāyu, the supreme abode.

3.58 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Vāyu has the colour of the sky, and his garment should have the form of that [sky]. / His garment is filled with wind, and he is two-armed and endowed with beauty.
His wife, the auspicious Gamanecchā, should be made on his left. / The wind[-god] should be made holding the ends of his garment with both hands, O twice-born.
Likewise, the goddess Śivā should be made supremely beautiful. / The god should be made with an open mouth and dishevelled hair.
Because the wind takes on scent, colour, and the like from its support, / it therefore has the colour of collyrium, through its connection with motion.
That very sky is proclaimed to be his garment. / That motion is the goddess Śivā; and he who is Aniruddha is the wind.
Indeed, this form of Pavana, who consists of the universe, / and of the goddess Śivā has been spoken to you, O king of great majesty, known as supremely holy to the twice-born.
3.59 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Now I shall tell you the fashioning of the form of Bhairava. / One should make him pot-bellied and with round, reddish-brown eyes,

This form of Bhairava is proclaimed as turned sideways. / This same [form] is declared to be facing forward for Mahākāla.
The goddess is to be made on the left, and a snake in his hand; / but the goddess, the mountain-daughter, is not to be made in front of him.
She should not be made white, nor red, when near him at the head of the group of mothers. / Further, his attendants should be made, and the gaṇas should be made of manifold forms.
3.60 / Vajra said: / O lord, enhancer of the lineage of Bhṛgu, describe the fashioning / of the forms of Viṣṇu, the Earth, the Sky, and Brahmā.

text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The lord has one face, two arms, and holds a mace and a discus; / the other arrangement of Hari's body has been proclaimed before.
Gāndhārī, the Vaiṣṇava Māyā, is known [as created] for binding the universe; / the mace is always in the god's hand, bringing all beings into subjection.
She indeed is Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Kīrti, Puṣṭi, Śraddhā, Sarasvatī, / Gāyatrī, mother of the Vedas, and likewise Kālarātri.
The wheel turning through saṃsāra is the discus resting in Viṣṇu’s hand; / it is the wheel of dharma, the wheel of time, and the wheel of constellations, O mighty-armed one.
For the fixed [pole] is declared to be the blessed lord Viṣṇu; that hero constantly sets the wheel spinning. / By this function, the foremost of the universe, the blessed lord, is described as holding the discus in hand.

The remaining reason is known to the wise, and therefore has not been told to you today, O king. / But now I shall speak of the form of the formless, the Sky, which has been delineated by the Siddhas.
3.62 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The Sky should have the lustre of a blue lotus, wearing garments of that same colour, / holding the moon and sun in its hands, two-armed, and of gentle appearance.
This form of the Sky has indeed been told to you by me, O king, as conceived [by the Siddhas]; / now learn, for I shall declare to you the form of that matchless Grandfather.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Brahmā should be made seated upon a lotus-petal seat, four-faced; / and Sāvitrī should be placed upon his left lap.
She is of sun-like splendour, O knower of dharma, holding a rosary in her hand; / all else of his form should be made as previously stated, O lord of the world.
This form of the matchless Grandfather, the giver of boons, should be made, O gentle one, / or as previously described for that giver of boons, under whose sway rests the entire world.

3.64 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Goddess Sarasvatī should be made adorned with all ornaments; / she should be made four-armed and standing upright.
A book and a rosary should be in her right hands; / and in her left [hands] should be placed a lute and a water-pot.
She should be made standing firmly with feet even, facing straight forward; / her arms are to be understood as the Vedas, and the book as all the scriptures.
The goddess’s water-pot is to be understood as the nectar-essence of all scriptures; / the rosary in her hand is time, O king.
The lute is to be understood as accomplishment embodied—of this there is no doubt; / her face is declared to be Sāvitrī, the foremost of all.

This form of Sarasvatī, pure, supreme, and charming, has been told to you by me; / it should be meditated upon and fashioned, O foremost of kings, by those desiring the attainment of all goals.
3.65 / Vajra said: / Describe to me, O god-born one, the fashioning of the form of Ananta, / Viṣṇu of boundless valour, Śeṣa who supports the earth.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / One should make him resembling the moon, endowed with hoods shining with jewels, / dressed in blue garments, four-armed, and wearing all ornaments.
Many hoods should be made; upon that hood which is his central one, / the shapely Earth should be made, O delight of the Yadus.
A lotus and a pestle should be placed in the god’s right hands; / in his left [hands], a plough and a conch, and in his hand the ocean of liquor.
The entire universe is proclaimed to be the palmyra tree, O mighty-armed one; / the plough and the pestle have already been explained to you by me.
And the forest garland is likewise celebrated, O enhancer of the Yadu race; / by him the earth is supported along with its mountains, forests, and groves.

For the pleasure of the goddesses, that lord, the sovereign protector of the world, resides in their midst; / granting desires to his devotees, he who slays the enemies of the gods is worthy of worship.
3.67 / Vajra said: / Previously the fashioning of the forms of the moon and the lord of the waters was described by you; / tell of that other form of the two, the sun and the moon.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Ravi should be made with an auspicious beard, shining like an ornament of vermilion, / wearing blazing attire, well-proportioned, and endowed with all ornaments,
four-armed, of great splendour, covered with armour; / and his belt should be made, which is called yaviyāṅga.
Rays should be placed in his left and right hands, / standing upwards like garlands, adorned with all flowers and auspicious.
Handsome in form and well-shaped, Daṇḍin should be placed on his left; / on the right side, Piṅgala should be placed, extremely tawny.
Both of them should be made wearing radiant attire, O descendant of Yadu; / resting on their heads, the two hands of the sun should be placed.

A lion-banner is to be made likewise on Sūrya's left; / and his four sons should be made at his sides:
Revanta and Yama, and the two Manus; / or Ravi, the king of planets, should be made surrounded by the planets.
Rājñī and Rikṣubhā, Chāyā, and the goddess Suvarcasā: / these four wives should also be made on either side.
In an excellent chariot with one wheel, seven horses, and marked with six lines, / the seated god should be made, having the son of Varuṇa as his charioteer.
Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, / Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī: the seven metres are the horses of Arka's chariot.

on the left, Śobhā should likewise be placed, matchless in form on earth; / and his emblem marked with a lion should be visible on the left side alone.
Or a ten-horse chariot should be made, two-wheeled, with the sky as charioteer: / Sraj, Trimanas, Vṛṣa, Vādin, Nara, Haya,

many bodies resembling their lord deity were assumed by the asterisms, / O delight of the Yadus, and then those dānavas were slain.
Whichever deity's form was assumed by a Nakṣatra, / that very deity is proclaimed as the deity of that Nakṣatra.
When the battle between the gods and asuras took place, O descendant of Yadu, / the gods then assumed female forms by willful power, in that same number.
The moon is indeed considered the father of all the world, O knower of dharma; / when he was created, the entire world attained supreme joy.
His gentle form is supreme, and should be known as belonging to the great-souled Viṣṇu; / the two white night-lotuses in Candra's hands are to be understood as joy and serenity.
Śobhā and Kānti are indicated as his own form, O descendant of Bhṛgu; / because he consists of the essence of waters, the moon is indeed white in colour.

Vajra said: / Relate the fashioning of the forms of the planets, O long-armed one; / on this very occasion, I deem you to be omniscient.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Mars should be made resembling the couch of Agni, on a golden chariot with eight horses. / Mercury should be made resembling the couch of Viṣṇu, on a chariot like the couch of Mars.
Bṛhaspati should be made [colored like] refined gold and two-armed; / one should place a manuscript and a rosary in his two hands.
Guru is endowed with all ornaments and similarly clad in yellow garments, / on an eight-horse, golden, divine chariot delightful to the eye.
Venus should be made white-bodied and wearing white garments; / his two hands are described as holding a treasure and a manuscript.

Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The present Manu should be made endowed with the marks of kingship; / but the future [Manu] should be made devoid of all ornaments,
wearing matted locks, bearing a rosary and holding a water pot; / emaciated, yet endowed with spiritual luster, and absorbed in ascetic practice.

text_mt:
Because he makes the universe, he is therefore remembered as Viśvakarman; / the creator of the universe is the blessed Viṣṇu: he is called Viśvakarman.
3.72 / Vajra said: / Tell me the auspicious form of the Vasus, O god, and likewise of the Āṅgirases, / and the deities of the Viśvedevas and also of the Rudras,
and of the Bhṛgus, the Sādhyas, and the Ādityas, / as well as the form of the Maruts, O one worshipped by the gods.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The Vasu named Dhara should have the form of Prajāpati; / the one named Dhruva is proclaimed to have the form of Viṣṇu;
Soma with the form of the Moon, and Anila with that of Vāyu; / Anala should be made with the form of Agni, and Prabhāsa with that of Varuṇa.
The Viśvedevas, the gods, should be made bearing the form of Śakra; / the king of nāgas is devoid of a transverse eye on the forehead.
And the Āṅgiras gods should be made with the form of Jīva (Bṛhaspati); / the Rudras with the form of Maheśvara; and the Sādhyas with that of Viṣṇu.

3.73

मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
प्राजापत्येन रूपेण कर्तव्यः कश्यपः प्रभुः ..
अदितिर्दितिर्दनुः काष्ठा दनायुः सिंहिका मुनिः..2..

text_mt:
The twelve Ādityas, O Yādava, [should be made] in the form of Sūrya. / When they are made separately, however, they are traditionally held to resemble the rising sun.
Viṣṇu, Indra, and Varuṇa should be made as described by me previously. / The deities called Maruts should be made in the form of Śukra.
3.73 / Vajra spoke: / Describe, O highly fortunate one, the fashioning of the forms of the other gods as well; / for you are said to be all-knowing.
Mārkaṇḍeya spoke: / Lord Kaśyapa should be made in the form of Prajāpati. / Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kāṣṭhā, Danāyu, Siṃhikā, Muni,
Kadrū, Krodhā, Darā, Prādhā, Vinatā, Surabhi, and Khaśā— / all these primeval mothers should be made beautiful and two-armed.
Aditi, Diti, Vinatā, and Surabhi— / their gaze should be made gentle, O delighter of the Yādavas.
Indeed, all the mothers of the gods should be made / with this very form in the act of fashioning images, O best of the Yādavas.

सुरूपरूपः कर्तव्यो रत्नपात्रकरो विभुः ..
द्विदंष्ट्रायुक्तवदनो धनादिर्नलकूबरः ..12..
text_mt:
The other wives of Kaśyapa should be made with agitated eyes. / Dhruva, the lord of the planetary host, should be made bearing the form of Viṣṇu,
holding rays [of light] like a discus, glorious, two-armed, and of gentle appearance. / The great sage Agastya should be made in the form of the future Manu.
The form of the noble [sages] beginning with Bhṛgu has thus been described. / The two sons of Śukra and Jayanta should be made endowed with beauty,
holding a bow and arrow, glorious, two-armed, and of gentle appearance. / Bala, the son of Yama, the lord, should be made holding a shield and spear.
Puṣkara should be made with a radiance like a lotus petal; / one should cause both a sword and a book to be placed in his hands.
And Jyotsnā, daughter of the Moon, incomparable in beauty on earth, / should be made on his left side, adorned with all ornaments.
Nalakūbara, [son of] Dhanada and others, the lord, should be made handsome in form, / holding a jewel-vessel, his face having two tusks.

text_mt:
The wise know Maṇibhadra to have the form of Dhanada; / he should not have a litter, [but] have a human mount, accompanied by his wife.
The son of Vāyu, Purojava, should be made with the form of Vāyu. / The lord Varcas, son of Soma, should be made exceedingly handsome,
with a play-lotus in his hand, so that he appears radiant. / Nandī should be made three-eyed, four-armed, and mighty-armed,
resembling red vermilion, wearing a tiger-skin as a garment; / and one should place a trident and a bhindipāla javelin in his hands,
the third [hand] placed upon his head, and the other gesturing threateningly; / he should be made looking from afar at people who are approaching.
By this very form the wise know Vīrabhadra. / Later on I will declare to you the form of Dharma.

sanskrit_iast:

text_mt:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:

sanskrit_iast:

text_mt:

sanskrit_iast:

फलवेदं मही देवी नृत्यशास्त्रं महेश्वरः .. 47 ..
text_mt:
Medicine is the lord god Dhanvantari in visible form;
the Veda of agriculture is the goddess Earth; the treatise on dance is Maheśvara.

sanskrit_iast:

text_mt:

लिङ्गस्य रूपनिर्माणं कथयस्व ममानघ .. 1 ..
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
लिङ्गे हि पूजितं पूजा कृता तु जगतो भवेत् ..
भोगोस्य वृत्तः कर्तव्यो भागमष्टास्रमेव तु .. 2 ..

लिङ्गोपरिष्टात्तु गता पुरस्ताल्लेखा सुवृत्ता तु तथैव कार्या ..
ऊर्ध्वायता बुद्धिगुणा तथास्या या ब्रह्मसूत्रे विबुधैः प्रदिष्टा..5..
text_mt:
The form of a division of time should be made equal to the form of its presiding deity, O slayer of foes!
This form of the foremost gods has been described by me to you, O moon of the Yadu lineage!
3.74
Vajra said:
Tell me the making of the form of the liṅga, O sinless one!
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
For when worship is offered to the liṅga, worship is rendered to the universe.
Its shaft should be made round, and one part octagonal,
and one part should be made square, O you of bountiful sacrificial fees!
The round part should be made visible; the octagonal part enters the pedestal;
and the square part should be made to enter the base of Brahmā.
The wise know the base of Brahmā to be beneath the auspicious pedestal.
Going above the liṅga, in front, a well-rounded line should likewise be made;
it extends upwards, three times in length, which is prescribed by the wise on the cord of Brahmā.

vajra uvāca ..

3.75
वज्र उवाच ..
व्योमरूपं समाचक्ष्व सर्वधर्मभृतां वर..
व्योम्नि तु पूजिते पूजा कृता स्याज्जगतो भवेत्.. 1 ..
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..

ततोल्पचतुरस्रं च चतुरस्रं ततो भवेत् .. 2 ..
ततोल्पचतुरस्रं च मेरुवत्संस्थितं ततः ..
भद्रपीठमिदं प्रोक्तं व्योमभागं तृतीयकम् .. 3 ..
सर्वेषां भद्रपीठानामेतल्लक्षणमुच्यते ..

text_mt:
Thus ends the seventy-fourth chapter, entitled 'The Making of the Form of the Liṅga', in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
3.75
Vajra said:
Describe the form of the sky, O best of all upholders of dharma!
For when the sky is worshipped, worship would be rendered to the universe.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
At the base it should be square; then round, O strong-armed one;
then a smaller square, and then it should be square.
And then a smaller square, situated like Mount Meru;
this is declared to be the auspicious pedestal, the third part representing the sky.
This is stated as the characteristic mark of all auspicious pedestals;
the central portion is declared to be of square form.

Vajra said:
Tell me the making of the form of Dharma and of Knowledge, O scorcher of foes,
and of Dispassion, O knower of dharma, as well as of Sovereignty.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
With four faces, four feet, four arms, and white garments,
adorned with all ornaments and white, Dharma should be made by one who knows.
In his right [hand] a rosary, and in his left a book;
and Endeavour should be made embodied, standing on his right side.
Standing on his left side, Happiness should be made extremely handsome;
the two hands of Dharma should be made placed on the heads of those two.
The rosary is recorded as Time, and the book is recorded as Scripture;
sacrifice, truth, asceticism, and generosity are his four faces.

tearing the chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu with his sharp claws, / having the lustre of a blue lotus, he should be made thus, with the demon fallen on his knees.
Hiraṇyakaśipu is the Daitya; the wise know him to be ignorance. / The Lord, whose self is Saṃkarṣaṇa, is the destroyer of ignorance.
The three-fold impurity of the worlds arising from speech, mind, and body— / this, O twice-born, the divine Saṃkarṣaṇa ever tears asunder.

text_mt:
Or his hand may be raised with the discus to sever the head of Hiraṇyākṣa; / the Lord should face Hiraṇyākṣa, who has raised his trident.
The wise know Hiraṇyākṣa to be personified lack of sovereignty. / By sovereign power, the Boar, the crusher of enemies, struck him down.
Or the man-boar should be made situated in meditation like Kapila; / or he should be made two-armed, intent upon carrying the lump [of earth],
or in the form of an entire boar, standing in the midst of many demons. / Either the man-boar or the boar should be made supporting the earth.
By the yoga of sovereignty, the divine Boar Aniruddha, who lifted up all the worlds, should be made, / whose power is nowhere obstructed, who removes all sins, O king.
3.80 / Vajra said: / Now I wish to hear about the form of the horse-headed Viṣṇu of boundless splendour / in this very connection, O mighty-armed one.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / O ruler of the earth, with the bodily lustre of his hands and feet smiling, / clad in blue garments, the horse-headed god should be made.

Know the horse-headed god to indeed be a limb of Saṃkarṣaṇa. / The god should be made eight-armed, and in four of his hands,
the wise one should have conch, discus, mace, and lotus made in personified form; / and four hands should be made placed on the heads
of the personified Vedas by the god wearing all ornaments. / In ancient times, the Vedas were retrieved by the horse-necked god.
The Vedas, stolen by two foremost demons, from the netherworld by that best of gods, / by the horse-headed Puruṣottama, were retrieved, O chief of Yadu’s lineage.

3.82
Vajra said:
Describe to me the form of Lakṣmī, O enhancer of the lineage of Bhṛgu, / she who is the mother of all the worlds and the wife of the great-souled Viṣṇu.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Beside Hari, Lakṣmī should be made with two arms, O king, / of divine form, with a lotus in her hand, adorned with all ornaments;
fair-complexioned, clothed in white garments, the goddess of matchless beauty on earth. / Separately, the goddess should be made with four arms on an auspicious lion-throne.
On her lion-throne a lotus with a lovely pericarp should be made, / eight-petalled, O fortunate one; and she is seated upon the pericarp.
Seated like Vināyaka, the goddess should be made, O mighty-armed one. / In her hand should be made an auspicious lotus with a large stalk,
situated on the right, O best of the Yādavas, resting near the edge of her armlet. / On the left should be made a jar of nectar, similarly charming, O king.

Mārkaṇḍeya said: / He has one face, four arms, a gentle form, handsome to look upon, / resembling a cloud swollen with water, and adorned with all ornaments,
shining with a neck having auspicious lines and resembling a conch, / endowed with excellent ornaments, adorned with superior earrings,
wearing armlets, bound with bracelets, adorned with a forest-garland, / bearing the Kaustubha gem upon his chest, and likewise a diadem on his head.
Likewise, the lotus on his head should be made with a beautiful pericarp; / his long arms joined with fists, his fingers slender with coppery nails,
his waist adorned with the fold of three lines, exceedingly charming. / The Earth, bearing the form of a woman, should be made standing between his feet.
The god Janārdana should be made with both his feet resting in her hands, / the placement of his feet separated by a tāla, with his right [foot] slightly advanced.
