text_mt: Then, having taken a firm water-pot made of gold, silver, copper, or clay, or of unseasoned root, filled with water from sacred fords, together with all medicinal herbs, all fragrant substances, all seeds, all gems, gold, sandalwood, and fruits, with a purifying ring placed at its mouth prepared with anointing unguents and guest-offering, its neck tied with thread and garlands, the ritualist should set it in place in front. The water-pot is to the east. / In the middle of the mound, one should draw an eight-petalled lotus. / Then one should commence the rite. / One should recite the Gāyatrī preceded by the Praṇava and Vyāhṛtis, along with its head: / Oṃkāra, salutation, the commencement of the rite, and the purifier. / Then one should have some praise recited. / Then, with protective mantras against demons, one should place white mustard seeds in the cardinal and intermediate directions. / Then, in a ditch twelve finger-breadths deep, with the mantra ‘Lord of the forest, firm of limb,’ one should perform the placement of the archways in order, beginning with the east. / The four archways represent the four ages: / in the east is the Kṛta age, in the south the Tretā, in the west the Dvāpara, and in the north the Kali. / Having thus performed the placement of the archways, with the mantra ‘Youthful, well-robed,’ one should wrap the four archways with darbha grass, fresh leaves, and flower garlands. / Then banners are to be set upon the archways: / in the east, Garuḍa with a yellow flag; in the south, a palm tree with a blue flag; in the west, a makara with a white flag; in the north, an antelope with a red flag. / On the flanks of Garuḍa are the mace and discus; of the palm, the plough and pestle; of the makara, the bow and arrows; of the antelope, the sword and shield. / In the space between the archways, in the south-eastern quarter, is an umbrella; / in the south-west, a victory banner; / in the north-west, a flag; / in the north-east, a staff. / Above the mound is a canopy. / On each archway, a bell and a mirror. / On the sacrificial mound, a canopy. / And there, door-keepers drawn on pots: Subhadra and Bhadra in the east; / Āṣāḍha and Yajñatānta in the south; / Jaya and Vijaya in the west; / Moda and Pramoda in the north. / Having done this, one should recite the verse beginning ‘Dhruvā dyauḥ’.

text_mt: And recite the Māthura mantra, saying ‘Explain.’ / Then, sprinkling the patron of the sacrifice, the officiating priests, and the ritual paraphernalia with the water of the water-pot using the Pavītra mantra, one should recite the Gāyatrī. / With the mantra ‘Whatever herbs,’ one should drive into the ground four strong arrows, fitted with feathers and points, beginning in the north-east direction. Their names are: / Kandarpa, Somana, Durdhara, and Śikhara. / Their four world-protectors are Indra, Yama, Varuṇa, and the Bestower of Wealth. / And at their setting, one should utter the mantra beginning ‘From joint to joint.’ / Then one should tie a five-coloured thread with the mantra ‘From joint to joint.’ / With that very thread one should enclose the directions. / Because of having five colours, the five-strand thread represents the five great elements; it is the thread of worldly existence: / blue is earth, white is water, red is fire, yellow is wind, and black is the intermediate space. / At its tying, the mantra is ‘Dūṣyādūṣyā…’ / and ‘The thread proclaimed by Indrāṇī.’ Then, at the roots of the posts within the mound, in the four directions, one should set four full jars. / Those four are known to be accompanied by the gods; there too, one should set the first jar in the north-eastern direction; / then the others in sequence. / Their names are Sahasravīrya, Vimala, Śatadhāra, and Pramandana. / One should supply them with gold, sandalwood, flowers, and bunches of wild plants. / There, one should consecrate the first with ‘May the waters be auspicious to us’; / the second with ‘May the divine waters be auspicious to us’; / the third with ‘Waters indeed are healing’; / the fourth with ‘Carry this off, O waters.’ / Then, in the east, one should place a vessel filled with parched grain; / in the south, a vessel of sesame; / in the west, a vessel of white mustard; / in the north, a vessel of unbroken grain. / According to the particular vessel, one should utter ‘You have chosen the brahmin.’ / Then, in the four intermediate directions, within the jars, four lamps should be provided. / And they are the Vedas, beginning from the north-east: Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman, and Atharvan. / And at their installation, one should utter ‘You are splendour, the brilliant.’ / Then one should once again perform the scattering of white mustard seeds with the protective mantras against demons.

3.99
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now the five cow-products: / among them, the cow's milk of a tawny cow; / the curds of a black one; / the clarified butter of a blue one; / the cow-dung of a white one; / the cow-urine of a copper-coloured one. / One should take the cow-urine with the Gāyatrī; / the cow-dung with the mantra ‘Having the scent of the door’; / the milk with ‘Swell up’; / the curds with ‘Dadhikrāvan’; / the clarified butter with ‘Rich in ghee, of the worlds’; / the kuśa-water with ‘At the impulse of the god.’ / Combining them with the Aghamarṣaṇa mantra, one should utter the Gāyatrī. / Then, with that fivefold cow-product, one should sprinkle the building, / and one should set it aside for the archways and the purification of the icon. / In a great bathing-rite, that very one should be used, or one may prepare another. / Now the preparation of the guest-offering: / it is prepared in a silver vessel; one should place within it a conch shell, bilva, lotus, uśīra root, darbha root, dūrvā grass, milk, unbroken grain, and white mustard seeds. / One should flood it with water from sacred fords. / One should utter the mantra beginning ‘Ratha-akṣa.’ / With the mantras ‘Draviṇam,’ ‘Pāpamanyaḥ,’ ‘Drupada,’ ‘Pavitra,’ ‘Śaṅkhamaṇi,’ ‘Śrīsūkta,’ and ‘From joint to joint,’ as purifying agents, one should then prepare the foot-washing water in an auspicious, strong, well-worshipped vessel, / beginning with the three verses ‘Golden-hued,’ O king, / with the three beginning ‘Waters indeed are healing,’ and also ‘May the divine waters be auspicious to us.’

3.100
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now occurs the purification of the image.
There, one should purify an earthen [image] and one made as a painting.
One should perform the purification and the preliminary consecration of both upon a ring of darbha grass, and whatever the material [of the image], one should first perform the purification prescribed for that material.
Then one should perform [the washing] with water using the Gāyatrī mantra.
The second [purification is] with earth, using [the verse beginning] 'Having stepped upon' (ākrāmya). And here is another mantra for this:
'Stepped upon by horses, stepped upon by chariots, stepped upon by Viṣṇu, O earth-bearing one, / O earth, remove my sin, whatever misdeed has been done by me.'

3.101
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now, after the purification of the image, one should prepare the purification ring for the image.
There, upon the pericarp of a lotus, with the mantra 'Firm is the sky' (dhruvā dyauḥ), one should place [the image] upon a couch, with its head to the south or with its head to the east.
Then one should spread five coverings of five colors.
And one should recite the Śuddhāvatī verses.
Then one should provide a covering cloth with [the verse] 'A youth, well-attired' (yuvā suvāsāḥ),
and a pillow for the cheek.
Then one should make an Ananta serpent having seven heads, made of inner core [grasses],
and place it upon the couch.
Then one should invoke the living soul and recite the Śivasaṃkalpa [hymn].
Then one should perform the invocation of Ananta.
Then one should worship Ananta with guest-water, foot-washing water, sipping-water, ointment, garlands, lamps, incense, honey-mixture, and the offering of garments, each in turn with the Sāvitra mantra.
Then [one chants] the Sarpasāman,
and recites the mantra 'Homage be to the serpents' (namo 'stu sarpebhyaḥ) and 'At every yoke' (yoge-yoge),
or speaks the greatness of Ananta.
Then, with the mantra 'Firm is the sky' (dhruvā dyauḥ), one should place the image of the blessed Lord upon Ananta on the purification ring.
Then one should invoke the living soul.
One should recite the Śivasaṅkalpa.
Then one should invoke the Lord.
Then all, with knees placed upon the ground, should make prostration and say, 'The Lord has arrived!'
Then they should worship [Him] with sounds of conches, kettle-drums, wardrums, and cries of victory.
Then one should worship the blessed Lord with gifts of guest-water, foot-washing water, sipping-water, bathing-water, ointment, garlands, incense, lamps, honey-mixture, and the offering of garments, each in turn with the Sāvitra mantra.
Then one should recite [the verse] 'May Indra grant us welfare' (svasti na indraḥ).
Then one should cover the blessed Lord with a pair of large garments with [the verse] 'A youth, well-attired' (yuvā suvāsāḥ); scatter [flowers] over Him with [the verse] 'They yoke their minds' (yuñjate manaḥ);
scatter white mustard seeds over Him with [the verse] 'Awakening and heedfulness' (bodhaś ca mā pratibodhaś ca);
and have [the accounts of] the manifestations read aloud.
Thus the preliminary consecration is to be performed.
And when the Lord has received the preliminary consecration, having established an altar upon the bare ground for the image, as well as seats and footstools, one should purify the altar and the seats according to the rite for the purification of an image.
Then a Sāttvata should perform worship according to the rite taught in the Śaṅkaragītā.
At the very time of the worship, the Hotṛ priest once performs the fire sacrifice on the sacrificial ground, the purification of the altar, and that of the seats.
Both the worship and the fire sacrifice must be performed daily once the preliminary consecration has taken place, / along with adoration by songs and dances, until the consecration has arrived. / This preliminary consecration has been properly declared to you by me.

Vajra said:
Tell me the invocations of the deities, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / since the gods, invoked by mantras, become present.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I shall tell you the invocations of the gods, O delight of the Yadus, / omitting what has already been said for some, and [giving them] again for others.
At the end of every invocation, this half-verse is prescribed: / “May this water for respectful offering, this water for washing feet, and this incense be accepted.”
I invoke the two gods, the Nāsatyas, the sons of the Sun; / may the highly fortunate, boon-granting, and auspicious Aśvins come.
I will invoke the Vasus, the eight boon-granting gods; / may the boon-granting gods, the Vasus who destroy sin, arrive.
I will invoke the Viśvedevas, gods of wondrous splendor; / may all the boon-granting Viśvedevas, endowed with great strength, arrive.

I invoke the gods who are the Aṅgirases, of wondrous splendor; / may the god-like Aṅgirases of great strength and valor arrive.
I will invoke the Rudras, three-eyed and riding on bulls; / may the boon-granting Rudras, who grant boons to the three worlds, auspicious ones, arrive.
I will invoke the Ādityas, boon-granting and of radiant splendor; / may all those suns arrive, boon-granting and fierce in splendor.
I will invoke the Bhṛgus, divine beings whose wealth is radiant austerity; / may the divine Bhṛgus arrive, boon-granting and of radiant splendor.
I will invoke the gods, the Maruts, supreme in splendor; / may the divine Maruts arrive, boon-granting lords of the universe.
I will invoke the gods, indeed all the dwellers of heaven; / may all the gods arrive, desiring worship with mantras.
I will invoke the Daityas of great strength and valor; / may the righteous Daityas arrive, following the God of gods for me.
I will invoke the Gandharvas endowed with beauty and wealth; / may all the Gandharvas arrive, boon-granting and taking form at will.

text_mt:
I will invoke the ancestors who possess subtle forms; / may all the ancestors arrive, each group standing distinctly.
I will likewise invoke the exceedingly strong Suparṇas; / may the Suparṇas arrive, augmented by the splendor of Viṣṇu.
I invoke all the boon-granting Prajāpatis; / may the lords of creatures arrive, protectors of the three worlds.
I invoke the lords of the gods, the deities who are masters of the world; / may my lords of the gods arrive, boon-granting and taking form at will.
I will invoke the Manus established in sovereign authority over the world; / may all the Manus arrive, their sins destroyed by austerity.
I will invoke the medicinal plants, auspicious and sustaining all living beings; / and may all the medicinal plants arrive, auspicious and granting all desires.
I will invoke the sages whose radiance shines through austerity; / may all the accomplished sages of radiant splendor arrive for me. / I will invoke the mountains endowed with all herbs;

may all the constellations arrive, all lords of the universe. / And I will invoke the directions, starting with the east, exceedingly delightful.
May all the directions arrive, bringing happiness to all living beings. / And I will invoke the heavenly orbits, the dwelling of the nine planets.
May all the orbits arrive, adorned with planets and lunar mansions. / I will invoke the muhūrtas, subtle in form.
May the muhūrtas quickly arrive, auspicious parts of Time. / I will invoke the six seasons, the lords of the worlds.
May all the seasons arrive, set in motion the wheel of the universe. / I will likewise invoke the five years.
May all the years arrive, setting in motion the wheel of Time. / I will invoke the four yugas of blazing splendour.
May all the yugas arrive, established in their four forms. / And I will invoke the fourteen Manus.
May the manvantaras arrive, established with the gods as their span. / I will invoke the god Time, having parts and auspicious.

text_mt:
Come, blessed Time, God of gods, Janārdana! / I will invoke the gods, bearing the form of sacrifice.
May all the gods arrive, boon-givers of many forms. / I will invoke completely the subjects of knowledge […].
May all [these] arrive here, desiring the welfare of the worlds. / I will invoke the scriptures, peaceful and established in vision.
May weapons quickly arrive, the supreme ornament of armies. / I will invoke the divine missiles, truly beneficial to the three worlds.
And may all arrive here, who establish the dam of dharma. / I will invoke the many scriptures of the Veda.
May the Vedic scriptures arrive, intent on the protection of the world. / I will invoke all the mounts of the gods.
May all the mounts of the gods arrive here. / I will invoke the elephants of the quarters, sons of gods, of great strength.
May the lordly elephants, steeds of the gods, quickly arrive in haste. / I will invoke the treasures, preceded by Śaṅkha and Padma. / May all the treasures arrive, bringing welfare to all the worlds.

text_mt:
Come, inconceivable best of gods, who ever sets crafts in motion: / on you, lord of all, depends the course of all actions!
I shall invoke Ketu, banner of all the celestial beings, / devoted to brahmins, knower of all dharma, granter of fearlessness to devotees:
Dhūmaketu, come hither, equal in radiance to fire, / with fierce, bristling crest, destroyer of the afflictions of your worshippers!
I shall invoke the auspicious Kṛttikā, worshipped by the gods: / come, neutral goddess, eldest daughter of Dakṣa, auspicious one!
I invoke Rohiṇī, granter of boons, beloved of the Moon: / come, Rohiṇī, knower of dharma, brilliant in fixed actions!
I invoke Ilvilā, granter of boons, beloved of the Moon: / come to me, goddess Ilvilā, brilliant in gentle actions!
I shall invoke Rudra, three-eyed, holding the trident in his hand: / come, Śaṅkara, self of all, sovereign of the great hosts of gaṇas!
I shall invoke Ārdrā, the asterism known as the Arm: / come, Ārdrā, lovely in all limbs, fierce, equal to Rudra!

text_mt:
I shall invoke Diti, whose sins are burned away by ascetic heat: / kindler of the Ādityas, knower of dharma, come, goddess of great vows!
I shall invoke the asterism Punarvasu, knower of dharma: / come hither, Punarvasu, accomplisher of movable actions!
I shall invoke Tiṣya, the asterism known as swift: / come, Puṣya, highly fortunate one, increase nourishment everywhere!
I shall invoke the serpents whose range extends over the three worlds without end: / let the serpents come from every side; let them assume gentle forms!
I invoke Āśleṣā, who increases the prosperity of devotees: / come hither, Āśleṣā, fierce, granter of victory!
I shall invoke the ancestors, assuming mortal forms: / let the ancestors come swiftly, consuming nectar and ancestral food, imperishable!
I shall invoke Maghā, the fierce asterism, forthwith: / come to me, fortunate goddess, destroyer of all sins!
I shall invoke Bhaga, who increases the good fortune of devotees: / come, inconceivable best of gods, destroyer of distress for devotees!

text_mt:
I shall invoke the asterism named Pūrvaphalgunī: / come, Bhāgī, highly fortunate one, accomplisher of fierce actions!
I shall invoke Aryaman, the Āditya, treasure of splendours: / come forward, Aryaman, destroyer of distress for devotees!
I shall invoke the auspicious asterism Uttarāphalgunī: / come, fortunate goddess, fixed one, beautiful in all limbs!
I shall invoke Hasta, sacred to Savitṛ, swift, directly: / come, sacred to Savitṛ, knower of dharma, destroyer of sins of devotees!
I invoke the god Tvaṣṭṛ of dark lustre: / come to me, Lord Tvaṣṭṛ, intent upon protecting creatures!
I shall invoke Citrā of variegated form, enchanting: / come to me, boon-granting goddess, accomplisher of gentle actions!
I will invoke Vāyu, all-pervading and of blazing splendor. / O divine Vāyu, beloved of all beings and the world, come near.
I will invoke Svāti, always moving everywhere in the north. / O goddess Svāti, auspicious in mobile actions, come near.

text_mt:
I will invoke Indra and Agni together, endowed with blazing splendor. / Come here, O Indra, lord of the world! Come, O Agni, grantor of victory!
I will invoke the asterism Viśākhā, endowed with foremost splendor. / Come here, O Viśākhā, auspicious goddess of intermediate nature.
I will invoke the god Mitra, endowed with the radiance of blazing rays. / Come, O fortunate Mitra; grant fearlessness to your devotees.
I will invoke the asterism Anurādhā, grantor of boons. / O Anurādhā, auspicious in gentle actions, come near.
The invocation of Śakra has been spoken; hear that of Jyeṣṭhā, O king. / I will invoke Jyeṣṭhā, the lunar mansion whose deity is Śakra.
O goddess Jyeṣṭhā, terrible yet fair-eyed, come near. / I will invoke the god Nirṛti, praised by heroes.
Come, O god Virūpākṣa, of great strength, constant refuge. / I will invoke Mūla, the great and terrible lunar mansion.
Come, O fortunate Mūla, granter of fearlessness to devotees. / I will invoke the Waters, all-pervading, boongiving, and auspicious.

text_mt:
I will invoke the Waters, named Pūrvāṣāḍhā. / Come, O fierce one, giver of boons, designated as Pūrvāṣāḍhā.
I will invoke the asterism that is called Abhijit. / Come to the highest station, O accomplisher of swift deeds.
I will invoke the asterism Śravaṇa, which fulfills all desires. / Gracious, come near, O accomplisher of mobile actions.
Come here, O Dhaniṣṭhā, accomplisher of mobile actions.
I will invoke the auspicious asterism named Śatabhiṣaj. / Approach, O Śatabhiṣaj, auspicious in mobile actions.
I invoke Ajaikapād, the boon-giving Rudra. / Approach, O boon-giving Rudra, whose supreme weapon is the trident.
I will invoke the asterism Pūrvabhadrapadā. / Come, O Pūrvabhadrapadā, accomplisher of fierce actions.
I invoke Ahirbudhnya, the illustrious Rudra. / O Ahirbudhnya, adorned with matted hair, come near.

I invoke the god Pūṣan, destroyer of sins. / O Pūṣan, destroyer of all blemishes, come duly here.
I will invoke the asterism Revatī, of timid appearance. / Come, O Revatī, knower of dharma, accomplisher of gentle actions.
I will invoke the swift asterism named Aśvinī. / Come, O fortunate Aśvinī, grantor of boons, fulfiller of desires.
I will invoke Yama, the king of dharma, who never falls away. / Come, O best among upholders of dharma, son of Vivasvat, mighty-armed one.
I will invoke the fierce asterism named Bharaṇī. / Come, O goddess Bharaṇī, fortunate and lovely in appearance.
I will invoke the eastern direction, adorned by the rising of the sun. / Come, O boongiving east, accomplisher of auspicious actions.
I will invoke the boon-bestowing south-eastern direction. / Beloved of Agni, boongiver, come near, O south-east.

3.105
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I shall invoke the charming worlds in the form of swans; / may those who stand as vehicles of Parameṣṭhin arrive.
I shall invoke the four-footed, humped bull: / Come, O bull, highly fortunate one, embodiment of dharma, granter of boons!
I shall invoke the trident, the abode of virtues, endowed with great splendour: / Come, O trident, highly fortunate one, destroyer of the hosts of Daitya chiefs!
I shall invoke the divine lord Nandīśvara: / Come, O blessed Nandin, reverenced by all the worlds!
I invoke the boon-giving, mighty Vīrabhadra: / Come, O Vīrabhadra, lord over the great host of gaṇas!
I shall invoke Fever, the three-footed, three-armed lord: / Come, O Fever, highly fortunate one, constantly radiant on your feet!

text_mt:
I shall invoke the goddess Bhadrakālī, the bestower of happiness: / Come, O boon-giving Durgā, reverenced by all the worlds!
I invoke Paulomī, the boon-giver who continuously delights: / Come, O wife of Śakra, boon-giver who assume any form at will!
I shall likewise invoke the elephant known as Airāvaṇa: / Come here, O highly fortunate one, elephant of Śakra, bringer of victory!
I shall invoke the swift thunderbolt that pierces all: / Come quickly, O thunderbolt, destroyer of all wicked ones!
I shall invoke the charming horses who embody the Vedic meters: / May the coursers moving through the sky come here to me today!
I shall invoke the one named Daṇḍa, towering with strength: / O Daṇḍa, come here quickly, of mighty strength and valour!
I shall invoke Piṅgala, who is of very great power: / Come, O witness of the worlds, O mighty Piṅgala!
I shall invoke the splendid banner, bright as the sun: / Come quickly, O Dharma, steadfast one placed upon the sun's banner!

text_mt:
I shall invoke the goddess endowed with solar radiance, who takes forms at will: / O goddess, reverenced by all the worlds, come swiftly!
I shall invoke Rājñī, the lovely wife of the sun: / Come, O boon-giving Rājñī, supporter of the universe, worthy of worship!
I shall invoke the radiant wife of the sun: / Come, O goddess Dhyāyī, who discerns what is done and left undone!
I shall invoke the ten horses of the Moon; / may all the horses of the Moon, taking forms at will, come here quickly! / I shall invoke Kānti, beloved of the gods: / Come quickly, O auspicious Kānti, beloved of the Moon!
I shall invoke Śobhā, the cherished ruler of the world: / Come quickly, O Śobhā, the sole beauty of all the worlds!
I shall invoke Day, the destroyer of all darkness: / Come quickly, O Day, you who reveal the entire realm! / I shall invoke Night, the bringer of comfort to all beings: / Come, O goddess Night, granter of boons to all beings!

text_mt:
I shall invoke Twilight, the goddess worshipped by brahmins: / Come, O boon-giving Twilight, reverenced by all beings!
I shall invoke Svāhā, the shining portion of Fire: / Come, O highly fortunate Svāhā, boon-giver who assume any form at will!
I shall invoke the Vedas, who bear auspicious forms: / May they arrive as the mount, situated on the smoke-bannered [Fire]!
I shall invoke the buffalo of great strength and valour: / Come here, O highly fortunate one, destroyer of all wicked ones!
I shall invoke the Staff, worshipped among all mounts: / Come, O highly fortunate Staff, destroyer of all living beings!
I shall invoke the goddess Dhūmrorṇā of lovely eyes: / Come, O goddess Dhūmrorṇā, reverenced by all the worlds!
I shall invoke Time, worshipped as unthwarted everywhere: / Come, O highly fortunate Time, inspirer of dread in all beings!
I shall invoke the goddess Death, who takes away all: / Come, O goddess Death, all-pervading one who assume any form at will!

text_mt:
I invoke the boon-giving Citragupta, who brings happiness: / Come, O Citragupta, who view all things equally everywhere!
I shall invoke the mighty Virūpākṣa: / Come, O Virūpākṣa, lord over the hosts of night-wanderers!
I shall invoke the camel known as Great Delusion: / Come, O highly fortunate camel, of long neck and great stride!
I shall invoke Gaurī, the beautiful wife of the lord of the waters: / Come, O Gaurī, great goddess, boon-giver who assume any form at will!
I shall invoke the swans well worshipped by the ocean: / May the boon-giving swans, birds dwelling on the waters, arrive!
I shall invoke the noose, intent on drawing in all: / Come, O highly fortunate noose, who subjugate all beings!
I shall invoke the Gaṅgā, destroyer of all sins: / Come quickly, O Gaṅgā, whose water is like nectar!
I shall invoke Yamunā, the younger sister of Yama: / Come, O goddess Yamunā, destroyer of all sins!

I shall invoke Śivā, the radiant wife of the Wind: / Come, O highly fortunate Śivā, boon-giver who assume any form at will!
I shall invoke the very spacious palanquin: / Come here, O palanquin, who bring comfort to all beings!
I shall invoke the man, the mount of the lord of men: / Come quickly, O man, and likewise leader of sovereigns!
I shall invoke Śaṅkha, the supreme and best of treasures: / Come quickly, O Śaṅkha, beloved of the lord of wealth!
I shall invoke Padma, the supreme and best of treasures: / Come quickly, O Padma, source of great abundance!
I shall invoke the goddess Pārvatī, beloved of Hara: / Come quickly, O goddess, producer of great magnificence!
I shall invoke Jayanta, the son of Śakra: / Come quickly, O Jayanta, crusher of all Asuras!
I shall invoke the boon-granting Puṣkara, who moves at will and is auspicious:
O Puṣkara, come here, you who reveal all knowledge.

text_mt:
I shall invoke Moonlight, the sole beauty of the three worlds:
Come, boon-granting Moonlight, bringer of joy to all beings.
I shall invoke you yourself, Nalakūbara:
Come here, most fortunate one, son of the Giver of Wealth.
I shall likewise invoke the son of the Sun, elder brother of Yama:
Come here, son of the Sun, author of welfare for your devotees.
I shall invoke Dharma, bringer of joy to all the worlds:
Come here, O Dharma, most fortunate one, protector of the worlds.
I shall invoke Artha, bringer of joy to all the worlds:
Come here, O Artha, most fortunate one, destroyer of all afflictions.
I shall invoke Kāma, the fruit and cause of everything:
O Kāma, come quickly, you who dwell in the heart of every living being.
I shall invoke Night, the goddess dear to all the world:
Come here, boon-granting goddess, O Night, you who are unconquered.
I shall invoke Sleep, who bestows joy upon all the worlds:
Come, boon-granting Sleep, you who enchant the three worlds.

text_mt:
I shall invoke the boon-granting great goddess Sarasvatī:
Come quickly, O goddess, granter of the boons of all desires.
I shall likewise invoke the lord Dhanvantari:
O Dhanvantari, come here, you who arose from the Ocean of Milk.
I shall invoke Uccaiḥśravas, the guardian of horses:
Come here, king of horses, you who arose from the Ocean of Milk.
For those whose invocation has been stated, one should recite this mantra:
Bowing low with kuśa grass in hand, unflagging, I praise the two Aśvins.
Thus the group of invocations has been proclaimed, most auspicious, purifying, and removing sins;
when invoked, the gods born of noble lineage inevitably become present.

sanskrit_iast:
yājakaṃ yajamānaṃ ca śreyasābhyetya yojaya ..
idamarghyamidaṃ pādyaṃ dhūpoyaṃ pratigṛhyatām .. 2 ..
meaning:
याजकं यजमानं च श्रेयसाभ्येत्य योजय ..
इदमर्घ्यमिदं पाद्यं धूपोयं प्रतिगृह्यताम् .. 2 ..
text_mt:
"Come and unite both the officiating priest and the patron of the sacrifice with the highest good;
let this water for respectful offering, this water for the feet, and this incense be accepted."

sanskrit_iast:
āvāhayāmyahaṃ devaṃ vāsudevaṃ jagatpatim ..
amṛtādhmātameghābhaṃ vidyudṛśavasāsasam .. 3 ..
meaning:
आवाहयाम्यहं देवं वासुदेवं जगत्पतिम् ..
अमृताध्मातमेघाभं विद्युदृशवसाससम् .. 3 ..
text_mt:
I invoke the divine Vāsudeva, lord of the universe,
resembling a cloud filled with nectar, with garments like flashes of lightning,

sanskrit_iast:
caturvaktraṃ mahābāhuṃ caturvedadharaṃ prabhum ..
caturāśramagoptāraṃ cāturvarṇyadharaṃ tathā .. 4 ..
meaning:
चतुर्वक्त्रं महाबाहुं चतुर्वेदधरं प्रभुम् ..
चतुराश्रमगोप्तारं चातुर्वर्ण्यधरं तथा .. 4 ..
text_mt:
four-faced, mighty-armed, the lord who sustains the four Vedas,
protector of the four stages of life, and maintainer of the four social classes,

sanskrit_iast:
caturyugaṃ catuṣketuṃ caturmūrtidharaṃ param ..
caturaṃghritanuṃ nāthaṃ caturvidhavibhāvanama .. 5 ..
meaning:
चतुर्युगं चतुष्केतुं चतुर्मूर्तिधरं परम् ..
चतुरंघ्रितनुं नाथं चतुर्विधविभावनम .. 5 ..
text_mt:
manifest as the four ages, having four emblems, supreme bearer of the four forms,
the lord whose body consists of four quarters, who displays himself in fourfold manner,

sanskrit_iast:
jarāyujasya kartavyaṃ tathā cāṇḍodbhavasya ca ..
sarvagaṃ varadaṃ nityaṃ sūkṣmaṃ sthūlamajaṃ vibhum .. 6 ..
meaning:
जरायुजस्य कर्तव्यं तथा चाण्डोद्भवस्य च ..
सर्वगं वरदं नित्यं सूक्ष्मं स्थूलमजं विभुम् .. 6 ..
text_mt:
the maker of both the womb-born and the egg-born,
all-pervading, boon-granting, eternal, subtle and gross, unborn and all-powerful,

sanskrit_iast:
ātmasthaṃ ca bahisthaṃ ca dūrasthaṃ cāntikaṃ ca tam ..
guṇādhāraṃ guṇairhīnaṃ guṇātītaṃ guṇottaram .. 7 ..
meaning:
आत्मस्थं च बहिस्थं च दूरस्थं चान्तिकं च तम् ..
गुणाधारं गुणैर्हीनं गुणातीतं गुणोत्तरम् .. 7 ..
text_mt:
dwelling within the self and dwelling outside, far off and yet near,
the foundation of qualities, devoid of qualities, transcending qualities, beyond all qualities,

sanskrit_iast:
saguṇaṃ nirguṇātmānaṃ cājeyaṃ jagataḥ parama ..
ehi me puṇḍarīkākṣa śaraṇāgata vatsala ..8..
meaning:
सगुणं निर्गुणात्मानं चाजेयं जगतः परम ..
एहि मे पुण्डरीकाक्ष शरणागत वत्सल ..8..
text_mt:
possessed of qualities yet having the nature of the quality-less, invincible, supreme over the world:
Come to me, lotus-eyed one, affectionate to those who take refuge in you,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣaraparyantavaktrāntarnirastāsuramaṇḍala ..
gadāveganirastogradaityanāthagaṇeśvara ..9..
meaning:
क्षरपर्यन्तवक्त्रान्तर्निरस्तासुरमण्डल ..
गदावेगनिरस्तोग्रदैत्यनाथगणेश्वर ..9..
text_mt:
you who have cast out the host of asuras within your mouth that reaches the end of creation,
you who repelled the fierce lords of the daitya armies by the force of your mace,

sanskrit_iast:
utphullacārukamalavirājitakarāmbuja ..
śaṅkhanādodbhavaśvāsamūḍhīkṛtamahāsura .. 3.106.10 ..
meaning:
उत्फुल्लचारुकमलविराजितकराम्बुज ..
शङ्खनादोद्भवश्वासमूढीकृतमहासुर .. 3.106.10 ..
text_mt:
whose lotus hands are adorned with an open, lovely lotus,
who stupefied the great asuras with the breath born of your conch's blast,

sanskrit_iast:
mahīkarāmbujanyastacaraṇadvayarājita ..
kaustubhodbhūtagojālahatāsuravilocana .. 11 ..
meaning:
महीकराम्बुजन्यस्तचरणद्वयराजित ..
कौस्तुभोद्भूतगोजालहतासुरविलोचन .. 11 ..
text_mt:
splendid with both feet placed upon the lotus-like hands of the Earth,
who destroyed the eyes of the asuras with the web of rays issuing from the Kaustubha gem,

sanskrit_iast:
vanamālāṅkitoraska kirīṭodbhāsitānana ..
yajña yajñopayajñāṅgayajñayone jagadguro .. 12 ..
meaning:
वनमालाङ्कितोरस्क किरीटोद्भासितानन ..
यज्ञ यज्ञोपयज्ञाङ्गयज्ञयोने जगद्गुरो .. 12 ..
text_mt:
whose chest is marked with the forest garland, whose face is illuminated by a diadem,
O sacrifice, O you who are the subsidiary rites of sacrifice, origin of sacrifice, teacher of the world,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmapradācintya sarvaśaktibalānvita ..
āvāhayāmyahaṃ devaṃ saṅkarṣaṇamayonijam .. 13 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामप्रदाचिन्त्य सर्वशक्तिबलान्वित ..
आवाहयाम्यहं देवं सङ्कर्षणमयोनिजम् .. 13 ..
text_mt:
granter of all desires, inconceivable one, endowed with all powers and might:
I invoke the unborn god Saṃkarṣaṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
śaśāṅkaśatasaṅkāśaṃ sajalāmbudavāsasam ..
krodhāgniśamitāśeṣakalpāṃtabhuvanatrayam .. 14 ..
meaning:
शशाङ्कशतसङ्काशं सजलाम्बुदवाससम् ..
क्रोधाग्निशमिताशेषकल्पांतभुवनत्रयम् .. 14 ..
text_mt:
resembling a hundred moons, clothed in water-laden clouds,
who appeased the three worlds at the end of the aeon with the fire of his wrath,

sanskrit_iast:
vāṅmanaḥkāyasambhūtamalatritayanāśanam ..
ehi saṃkarṣaṇācintya deva bhaktajanapriya .. 15 ..
meaning:
वाङ्मनःकायसम्भूतमलत्रितयनाशनम् ..
एहि संकर्षणाचिन्त्य देव भक्तजनप्रिय .. 15 ..
text_mt:
the destroyer of the threefold impurity born of speech, mind, and body:
Come, inconceivable Saṃkarṣaṇa, O god dear to your devotees,

sanskrit_iast:
lāṅgūlākṛṣṭadaityendra dīnekṣaṇanirīkṣaṇa ..
musalāgravinirbhinna tamomūrtivināśana .. 16 ..
meaning:
लाङ्गूलाकृष्टदैत्येन्द्र दीनेक्षणनिरीक्षण ..
मुसलाग्रविनिर्भिन्न तमोमूर्तिविनाशन .. 16 ..
text_mt:
you who dragged the daitya kings with your plough, whose glance looks upon the miserable,
who shattered and destroyed the embodiments of darkness with the tip of your pestle,

sanskrit_iast:
hārdamūrte niśīthasya tamasaśca vināśaka ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi pradyumnamaparājitam .. 17 ..
meaning:
हार्दमूर्ते निशीथस्य तमसश्च विनाशक ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि प्रद्युम्नमपराजितम् .. 17 ..
text_mt:
whose form is within the heart, destroyer of the darkness of the dead of night:
I shall invoke the unconquered god Pradyumna,

sanskrit_iast:
dūrvāṅkuradalaśyāmaṃ śaśāṅkāṃśusamāmba ram ..
kāmaṃ kāmapradaṃ śāntaṃ kamanīyaṃ suśobhitam .. 18 ..
meaning:
दूर्वाङ्कुरदलश्यामं शशाङ्कांशुसमाम्ब रम् ..
कामं कामप्रदं शान्तं कमनीयं सुशोभितम् .. 18 ..
text_mt:
dark as the blade of a dūrvā sprout, with garments like the rays of the moon,
desire itself, granter of desires, tranquil, lovely, exceedingly radiant,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvamānabhṛtāṃ devaṃ manoviṣayagocaram ..
pradyumnābhyehi deveśa pradyotitacarācara .. 19 ..
meaning:
सर्वमानभृतां देवं मनोविषयगोचरम् ..
प्रद्युम्नाभ्येहि देवेश प्रद्योतितचराचर .. 19 ..
text_mt:
the god who is the object of the mind's domain for all who possess consciousness:
O Pradyumna, come, lord of gods, illuminator of all that moves and is still,

sanskrit_iast:
tejomūrte durādharṣaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabha ..
ajñātamadhyaparyanta devārigaṇanāśana .. 3.106.20 ..
meaning:
तेजोमूर्ते दुराधर्षं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभ ..
अज्ञातमध्यपर्यन्त देवारिगणनाशन .. 3.106.20 ..
text_mt:
whose form is brilliance, unassailable, with splendour like ten million suns,
whose middle and limits are unknown, destroyer of the hosts of the gods' enemies,

sanskrit_iast:
cāpakṛṣṭivinirmuktaśarāhatajagattraya ..
āvāhayāmyahaṃ devaṃ cāniruddhaṃ jagadgurum ..21..
meaning:
चापकृष्टिविनिर्मुक्तशराहतजगत्त्रय ..
आवाहयाम्यहं देवं चानिरुद्धं जगद्गुरुम् ..21..
text_mt:
who struck the three worlds with arrows released from his drawn bow:
I invoke the god Aniruddha, teacher of the world,

sanskrit_iast:
padmapatrāgrasaṅkāśaṃ raktāmbaravibhūṣaṇam ..
aruddhamārgaṃ sarvatra dīptānalasamaprabham..22..
meaning:
पद्मपत्राग्रसङ्काशं रक्ताम्बरविभूषणम् ..
अरुद्धमार्गं सर्वत्र दीप्तानलसमप्रभम्..22..
text_mt:
resembling the tip of a lotus petal, adorned with red garments,
whose path is unobstructed everywhere, with splendour equal to blazing fire,

sanskrit_iast:
kāryaṃ paramamīśānaṃ jagatkāraṇakāraṇam ..
aniruddha tvamabhyehi vyāptāśeṣacarācara .. 23..
meaning:
कार्यं परममीशानं जगत्कारणकारणम् ..
अनिरुद्ध त्वमभ्येहि व्याप्ताशेषचराचर .. 23..
text_mt:
the supreme effect, the sovereign, the cause of the causes of the world:
O Aniruddha, come, you who pervade all that moves and is still,

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśatulyasadvajravidāritasurāhita ..
carmasañchāditāśeṣabhuvanāditya vikrama..24..
(sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ karmma saṃsāraparipālaka ..24..)
meaning:
आकाशतुल्यसद्वज्रविदारितसुराहित ..
चर्मसञ्छादिताशेषभुवनादित्य विक्रम..24..
(सर्वेषां प्राणिनां कर्म्म संसारपरिपालक ..24..)
text_mt:
who tore apart the enemies of the gods with your true thunderbolt resembling the sky,
who covered all the worlds with your shield, possessing the valour of the sun,
[you who are the action of all living beings, protector of worldly existence.]

sanskrit_iast:
āvāhayiṣye varadaṃ cānanta dīptatejasam ..
phaṇāvaligatāśīrṣamahīmaṇḍaladhāriṇam ..25..
meaning:
आवाहयिष्ये वरदं चानन्त दीप्ततेजसम् ..
फणावलिगताशीर्षमहीमण्डलधारिणम् ..25..
text_mt:
I shall invoke the boon-granting Ananta of blazing splendour,
who supports the orb of the earth upon the heads of his array of hoods,

sanskrit_iast:
lāṃgalāliṅgatakaraṃ musalāsaktavigraham ..
mahocchritena tālena tathā cihnena rājitam..26..
meaning:
लांगलालिङ्गतकरं मुसलासक्तविग्रहम् ..
महोच्छ्रितेन तालेन तथा चिह्नेन राजितम्..26..
text_mt:
whose hand embraces a plough, whose body is joined to a pestle,
splendid with his emblem, a very tall palm tree:

sanskrit_iast:
ehyananta mahābhāga śeṣāhe dharaṇīdhara ..
śaśāṅka śatasaṅkāśa tathāmbarasuśobhita .. 27 ..
meaning:
एह्यनन्त महाभाग शेषाहे धरणीधर ..
शशाङ्क शतसङ्काश तथाम्बरसुशोभित .. 27 ..
text_mt:
Come, Ananta, most fortunate one, serpent Śeṣa, supporter of the earth,
resembling a hundred moons, brilliantly adorned with such garments;

sanskrit_iast:
ādhāraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tvameko bhūtabhāvanaḥ ..
tvayedaṃ dhāryate viśvaṃ trailokyaṃ ca jagatpate .. 28 ..
meaning:
आधारः सर्वभूतानां त्वमेको भूतभावनः ..
त्वयेदं धार्यते विश्वं त्रैलोक्यं च जगत्पते .. 28 ..
text_mt:
you alone are the foundation of all beings, the creator of beings;
by you this universe and the three worlds are sustained, O lord of the world.

sanskrit_iast:
lakṣmīmāvāhayiṣyāmi viṣṇorvakṣasi saṃsthitām ..
padmānanāṃ padmakarāṃ śaśāṃkasadṛśāmbarām .. 29 ..
meaning:
लक्ष्मीमावाहयिष्यामि विष्णोर्वक्षसि संस्थिताम् ..
पद्माननां पद्मकरां शशांकसदृशाम्बराम् .. 29 ..
text_mt:
I shall invoke Lakṣmī, who rests upon the chest of Viṣṇu,
with lotus-like face, holding a lotus in her hand, with garments resembling the moon,

sanskrit_iast:
hitasthāṃ sarvalokasya varadāṃ kāmarūpiṇīm ..
sarvagāṃ sarvajananīṃ devīṃ tribhuvaneśvarīm .. 3.106.30 ..
meaning:
हितस्थां सर्वलोकस्य वरदां कामरूपिणीम् ..
सर्वगां सर्वजननीं देवीं त्रिभुवनेश्वरीम् .. 3.106.30 ..
text_mt:
abiding for the welfare of all the world, boon-granting, assuming forms at will,
all-pervading, mother of all, goddess and sovereign of the three worlds:

sanskrit_iast:
āgaccha varade lakṣmi durdhare bhūtabhāvane ..
haripriye viśālākṣi sarvalokanamaskṛte .. 31 ..
meaning:
आगच्छ वरदे लक्ष्मि दुर्धरे भूतभावने ..
हरिप्रिये विशालाक्षि सर्वलोकनमस्कृते .. 31 ..
text_mt:
Come, boon-granting Lakṣmī, unassailable, creator of beings,
beloved of Hari, wide-eyed one, revered by all the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
yatra tvaṃ tatra sakalaṃ trailokyaṃ varavarṇini ..
yunakṣi bhogaiḥ sakalaṃ smṛtiprāptaṃ janaṃ śubham .. 32 ..
meaning:
यत्र त्वं तत्र सकलं त्रैलोक्यं वरवर्णिनि ..
युनक्षि भोगैः सकलं स्मृतिप्राप्तं जनं शुभम् .. 32 ..
text_mt: Where you are, there is the entire triple world, O fair-complexioned one; / you unite with all enjoyments the virtuous person who remembers you.

sanskrit_iast:
tārkṣyamāvāhayiṣyāmi manomārutaraṃhasam ..
pakṣavātasamuddhūtasamastabhuvanatrayam .. 33 ..
meaning:
तार्क्ष्यमावाहयिष्यामि मनोमारुतरंहसम् ..
पक्षवातसमुद्धूतसमस्तभुवनत्रयम् .. 33 ..
text_mt: I will invoke Tārkṣya, who has the speed of mind and wind, / by the wind of whose wings the entire triple world is shaken.

sanskrit_iast:
garuḍairhi samabhyehi dīptānalacayopama ..
mahāviṣatamograstanirviṣīkaraṇācyuta .. 34 ..
meaning:
गरुडैर्हि समभ्येहि दीप्तानलचयोपम ..
महाविषतमोग्रस्तनिर्विषीकरणाच्युत .. 34 ..
text_mt: Come, Garuḍa, come forward, like a mass of blazing fire, / you who are unfailing in removing poison swallowed in the darkness of great venom.

sanskrit_iast:
tālamāvāhayiṣyāmi ketuṃ saṃkarṣaṇasya tu ..
ehi me bhagavam̐stāla samastabhuvaneśvara .. 35 ..
meaning:
तालमावाहयिष्यामि केतुं संकर्षणस्य तु ..
एहि मे भगवम्̐स्ताल समस्तभुवनेश्वर .. 35 ..
text_mt: I will invoke the palmyra palm, the banner of Saṃkarṣaṇa. / Come to me, Lord Palmyra, ruler of all the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
jhaṣamāvāhayiṣyāmi kāmaketuṃ varapradam ..
ehi me makarāgryeha samastabhuvaneśvara .. 36 ..
meaning:
झषमावाहयिष्यामि कामकेतुं वरप्रदम् ..
एहि मे मकराग्र्येह समस्तभुवनेश्वर .. 36 ..
text_mt: I will invoke the fish, the boon-granting banner of Kāma. / Come to me, foremost of sea-monsters, here, ruler of all the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣyamāvāhayiṣyāmi ṛṣirājaṃ mahābalam ..
ehi ṛṣya mahābhāga karmamūrte durāsada ..37..
meaning:
ऋष्यमावाहयिष्यामि ऋषिराजं महाबलम् ..
एहि ऋष्य महाभाग कर्ममूर्ते दुरासद ..37..
text_mt: I will invoke the white-footed antelope, the mighty king of antelopes. / Come, highly fortunate antelope, form of ritual action, unassailable one.

sanskrit_iast:
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi nṛsiṃhaṃ jñānarūpiṇam ..
daṃṣṭrākarālavadanamalātamasitekṣaṇam .. 38 ..
meaning:
देवमावाहयिष्यामि नृसिंहं ज्ञानरूपिणम् ..
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनमलातमसितेक्षणम् .. 38 ..
text_mt: I will invoke the god Nṛsiṃha, whose form is knowledge, / whose mouth is terrifying with fangs, who has dark eyes like a firebrand,

sanskrit_iast:
sahasrayamasakrodhaṃ sahasrendraparākramam ..
sahasradhanadanaṃ sphītaṃ manasopyatiśīghragam .. .. 39 ..
meaning:
सहस्रयमसक्रोधं सहस्रेन्द्रपराक्रमम् ..
सहस्रधनदनं स्फीतं मनसोप्यतिशीघ्रगम् .. .. 39 ..
text_mt: having the wrath of a thousand Yamas, the valour of a thousand Indras, / rich as a thousand Kuberas, moving swifter even than thought,

sanskrit_iast:
vidyujjihvaṃ vyāditāsyaṃ bhrukuṭīkuṭilānanam ..
vahnijvālāvalīpuñjadurnirīkṣyamukhaśriyam ..3.106.40 ..
meaning:
विद्युज्जिह्वं व्यादितास्यं भ्रुकुटीकुटिलाननम् ..
वह्निज्वालावलीपुञ्जदुर्निरीक्ष्यमुखश्रियम् ..3.106.40 ..
text_mt: with a lightning-like tongue, a gaping mouth, and a face furrowed with a frown, / the splendour of whose face is difficult to look upon like a heap of blazing flames.

sanskrit_iast:
āgaccheha nṛsiṃhādya mahābalaparākrama ..
vajratīkṣṇanakhākrāntamahādaityendrajīvita .. 41 ..
meaning:
आगच्छेह नृसिंहाद्य महाबलपराक्रम ..
वज्रतीक्ष्णनखाक्रान्तमहादैत्येन्द्रजीवित .. 41 ..
text_mt: Come here today, Nṛsiṃha of great strength and prowess, / who crushed the life of the great lord of daityas with claws sharp as thunderbolts,

sanskrit_iast:
ajñānadhvāntamātaṅgabhaṅgavispaṣṭakesara ..
mahāmantrakapāṭogradāruṇācintyavikrama .. 42 ..
meaning:
अज्ञानध्वान्तमातङ्गभङ्गविस्पष्टकेसर ..
महामन्त्रकपाटोग्रदारुणाचिन्त्यविक्रम .. 42 ..
text_mt: whose mane is distinct in shattering the elephant that is the darkness of ignorance, / who has incomprehensible prowess, fierce and dreadful like a door of great mantras.

sanskrit_iast:
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi kāpilīṃ tanumāśritam ..
tejonidhānamajitaṃ sāgarātmajavāḍavam .. 43 ..
meaning:
देवमावाहयिष्यामि कापिलीं तनुमाश्रितम् ..
तेजोनिधानमजितं सागरात्मजवाडवम् .. 43 ..
text_mt: I will invoke the god who assumed the form of Kapila, / the unconquered store of splendour, the submarine fire to the sons of Sagara.

sanskrit_iast:
ehi me kapilādyeha paramātmansanātana ..
dhyānavīkṣitasadbhāva sāṃkhyamārgapravartaka .. 44 ..
meaning:
एहि मे कपिलाद्येह परमात्मन्सनातन ..
ध्यानवीक्षितसद्भाव सांख्यमार्गप्रवर्तक .. 44 ..
text_mt: Come to me here today, Kapila, eternal Supreme Self, / whose true nature is seen in meditation, promulgator of the path of Sāṃkhya.

sanskrit_iast:
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi nṛvarāhaṃ mahābalam ..
bhinnāñjanacayaśyāma līloddhṛtavasundhara .. 45 ..
meaning:
देवमावाहयिष्यामि नृवराहं महाबलम् ..
भिन्नाञ्जनचयश्याम लीलोद्धृतवसुन्धर .. 45 ..
text_mt: I will invoke the god, the mighty Man-Boar, / dark as a heap of split collyrium, who lifted up the earth in play.

sanskrit_iast:
āgaccha nṛvarāheha hiraṇyākṣavināśana ..
śeṣābhabhogavinyastamahācaraṇapaṅkaja .. 46 ..
meaning:
आगच्छ नृवराहेह हिरण्याक्षविनाशन ..
शेषाभभोगविन्यस्तमहाचरणपङ्कज .. 46 ..
text_mt: Come here, Man-Boar, destroyer of Hiraṇyākṣa, / whose great lotus feet are placed upon the coils of Śeṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṅkhanādodbhava trāhi niyantā suranāyakam ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi varāhaṃ varadarpitam .. 47 ..
meaning:
शङ्खनादोद्भव त्राहि नियन्ता सुरनायकम् ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि वराहं वरदर्पितम् .. 47 ..
text_mt: O you who arose from the blast of the conch, protect [us], ruler of the leader of the gods! / I will invoke the god, the Boar proud of his boons,

sanskrit_iast:
bālendulekhādaṃṣṭrāgravibhāsitajagattraya ..
vismayotphullanayana bhūmivīkṣitavigraha .. 48 ..
meaning:
बालेन्दुलेखादंष्ट्राग्रविभासितजगत्त्रय ..
विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयन भूमिवीक्षितविग्रह .. 48 ..
text_mt: who illuminated the triple world with the tip of his crescent-moon-like tusk, / whose eyes expanded with wonder, whose form was gazed upon by the Earth,

sanskrit_iast:
bālendutulyadaṃṣṭrāgra līloddhṛtavasundhara ..
ehi me bhagavandeva varāhāmitavikrama .. 49 ..
meaning:
बालेन्दुतुल्यदंष्ट्राग्र लीलोद्धृतवसुन्धर ..
एहि मे भगवन्देव वराहामितविक्रम .. 49 ..
text_mt: who lifted up the earth in play with the tip of his tusk resembling the crescent moon. / Come to me, Lord God, Boar of boundless prowess,

sanskrit_iast:
nirastāśeṣadaityeṃdra dīnabhaktajanoddhara ..
dharmamāvāhayiṣyāmi sarvabhūtasukhāvaham .. 3.106.50 ..
meaning:
निरस्ताशेषदैत्येंद्र दीनभक्तजनोद्धर ..
धर्ममावाहयिष्यामि सर्वभूतसुखावहम् .. 3.106.50 ..
text_mt: who drove away all the lordly daityas, uplifter of miserable devotees! / I will invoke Dharma, who brings happiness to all beings,

sanskrit_iast:
durvijñeyaṃ bahudvāraṃ khalamūrtidurāsadam ..
ehi dharma mamābhyehi bhuvanatrayapālaka .. 51 ..
meaning:
दुर्विज्ञेयं बहुद्वारं खलमूर्तिदुरासदम् ..
एहि धर्म ममाभ्येहि भुवनत्रयपालक .. 51 ..
text_mt: hard to know, possessing many doors, unapproachable by the wicked. / Come, Dharma, approach me, protector of the triple world,

sanskrit_iast:
samastapāpaśamana sarvabādhāvināśana ..
rudramāvāhayiṣyāmi tejomūrtiṃ durāsadam .. 52 ..
meaning:
समस्तपापशमन सर्वबाधाविनाशन ..
रुद्रमावाहयिष्यामि तेजोमूर्तिं दुरासदम् .. 52 ..
text_mt: calmer of all sins, destroyer of all afflictions! / I will invoke Rudra, whose form is splendour, who is difficult to approach,

sanskrit_iast:
aiśvaryamatigambhīraṃ sarvasaṃhārakārakam ..
ehi me bhagavannrudra jaṭāmaṇḍala durdṛśa .. 53 ..
meaning:
ऐश्वर्यमतिगम्भीरं सर्वसंहारकारकम् ..
एहि मे भगवन्न्रुद्र जटामण्डल दुर्दृश .. 53 ..
text_mt: whose sovereignty is exceedingly profound, the cause of the dissolution of all. / Come to me, Lord Rudra, difficult to look upon with your circle of matted hair,

sanskrit_iast:
nirdagdhāśeṣabhuvana tṛtīyekṣaṇatejasā ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi brāhmaṇaṃ dīptatejasam .. 54 ..
meaning:
निर्दग्धाशेषभुवन तृतीयेक्षणतेजसा ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि ब्राह्मणं दीप्ततेजसम् .. 54 ..
text_mt: who completely burned all the worlds with the splendour of your third eye! / I will invoke the god Brahmā, of blazing splendour,

sanskrit_iast:
caturmukhaṃ caturbāhuṃ guṇādhīnaṃ guṇottaram ..
devadeva tvamabhyehi pitāmaha sureśvara .. 55 ..
meaning:
चतुर्मुखं चतुर्बाहुं गुणाधीनं गुणोत्तरम् ..
देवदेव त्वमभ्येहि पितामह सुरेश्वर .. 55 ..
text_mt: four-faced, four-armed, dependent upon the guṇas yet superior to the guṇas. / Come, God of gods, Grandfather, Lord of gods,

sanskrit_iast:
samastabhuvanādhyakṣa jagatkāraṇakāraṇa ..
bhūmimāvāhayiṣyāmi dhāriṇīṃ sarvadehinām .. 56 ..
meaning:
समस्तभुवनाध्यक्ष जगत्कारणकारण ..
भूमिमावाहयिष्यामि धारिणीं सर्वदेहिनाम् .. 56 ..
text_mt: overseer of all the worlds, cause of the cause of the universe! / I will invoke the Earth, supporter of all embodied beings,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvabhūtapratiṣṭhāṃ ca kṣitiṃ kṣoṇīṃ sarasvatīm ..
ehi me varade devi vasudhe bhūtabhāvini .. 57 ..
meaning:
सर्वभूतप्रतिष्ठां च क्षितिं क्षोणीं सरस्वतीम् ..
एहि मे वरदे देवि वसुधे भूतभाविनि .. 57 ..
text_mt: the foundation of all beings, Kṣiti, Kṣoṇī, Sarasvatī. / Come to me, boon-granting goddess, Vasudhā, creator of beings,

sanskrit_iast: sarvāśraye mahābhāge devavadbhayahāriṇi .. 58 ..
meaning: सर्वाश्रये महाभागे देववद्भयहारिणि .. 58 ..
text_mt: refuge of all, highly fortunate, dispelling fear like a deity!

sanskrit_iast: śaṅkhamāvāhayiṣyāmi nabhomūrtimathāvyayam .. 59 ..
meaning: शङ्खमावाहयिष्यामि नभोमूर्तिमथाव्ययम् .. 59 ..
text_mt: I will invoke the conch, whose form is the sky, imperishable,

sanskrit_iast:
śabdayoniṃ nirālambaṃ samastabhuvanāśrayam ..
ehyehi śaṅkhapravara pāñcajanya mahāsvana .. 3.106.60 ..
meaning:
शब्दयोनिं निरालम्बं समस्तभुवनाश्रयम् ..
एह्येहि शङ्खप्रवर पाञ्चजन्य महास्वन .. 3.106.60 ..
text_mt: the origin of sound, without support, the refuge of all the worlds. / Come, come, foremost of conches, Pāñcajanya of mighty sound,

sanskrit_iast:
śabdamātrahatāśeṣamahādānavamaṇḍala ..
padmamāvāhayiṣyāmi samastabhuvanāśrayam .. 61 ..
meaning:
शब्दमात्रहताशेषमहादानवमण्डल ..
पद्ममावाहयिष्यामि समस्तभुवनाश्रयम् .. 61 ..
text_mt: who slew the entire circle of great dānavas by mere sound! / I will invoke the lotus, the refuge of all the worlds,

sanskrit_iast:
apāṃ mūrtimayaṃ saumyaṃ puṇḍarīkamiti smṛtam ..
ehi padma mahābhāga bhūtabhavyabhavaprabho .. 62 ..
meaning:
अपां मूर्तिमयं सौम्यं पुण्डरीकमिति स्मृतम् ..
एहि पद्म महाभाग भूतभव्यभवप्रभो .. 62 ..
text_mt: composed of the form of water, gentle, remembered as the white lotus. / Come, lotus, highly fortunate one, lord of past, present, and future,

sanskrit_iast:
lakṣmīnilaya vistīrṇa brahmayone jaganmaya ..
cakramāvāhayiṣyāmi kṣaratparyantamaṇḍalam .. 63 ..
meaning:
लक्ष्मीनिलय विस्तीर्ण ब्रह्मयोने जगन्मय ..
चक्रमावाहयिष्यामि क्षरत्पर्यन्तमण्डलम् .. 63 ..
text_mt: abode of Lakṣmī, vast, source of Brahmā, containing the universe! / I will invoke the discus, whose circular rim pours forth [splendour],

sanskrit_iast:
vajranābhaṃ viśālākṣaṃ vāyumūrjitamavyayam ..
kālacakraṃ jagaccakraṃ dharmacakraṃ sudarśanam .. 64 ..
meaning:
वज्रनाभं विशालाक्षं वायुमूर्जितमव्ययम् ..
कालचक्रं जगच्चक्रं धर्मचक्रं सुदर्शनम् .. 64 ..
text_mt: with a thunderbolt navel, wide-eyed, possessing the form of wind, mighty, imperishable, / the wheel of time, the wheel of the universe, the wheel of dharma, Sudarśana,

sanskrit_iast:
nityaṃ satatagaṃ devaṃ tṛptaṃ dānavaśoṇitaiḥ ..
ehi cakrāmitaśita jagatpālanatatpara .. 65 ..
meaning:
नित्यं सततगं देवं तृप्तं दानवशोणितैः ..
एहि चक्रामितशित जगत्पालनतत्पर .. 65 ..
text_mt: eternal, ever-moving, divine, satiated with the blood of dānavas. / Come, discus of boundless sharpness, intent on protecting the universe,

sanskrit_iast:
devendrahṛdayatrāsatamonāśanatatpara ..
gadāmāvāhayiṣyāmi tejomūrtiṃ durāsadām .. 66 ..
meaning:
देवेन्द्रहृदयत्रासतमोनाशनतत्पर ..
गदामावाहयिष्यामि तेजोमूर्तिं दुरासदाम् .. 66 ..
text_mt: intent on destroying the darkness of fear in the heart of the lord of gods! / I will invoke the mace, whose form is splendour, difficult to approach,

sanskrit_iast:
gāyatrīṃ devajananīṃ kālarātrīṃ bhayaṅkarīm ..
ehi kaumodaki gade samastāsuranāśini .. 67 ..
meaning:
गायत्रीं देवजननीं कालरात्रीं भयङ्करीम् ..
एहि कौमोदकि गदे समस्तासुरनाशिनि .. 67 ..
text_mt: Gāyatrī, mother of the gods, Kālarātrī, terrifying. / Come, mace Kaumodakī, destroyer of all asuras,

sanskrit_iast:
yāsāṃ tvaṃ gahvarā proktā vaiṣṇavī tu sudurdharā ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi sāvantaṃ nāma lāṅgalam ..68..
meaning:
यासां त्वं गह्वरा प्रोक्ता वैष्णवी तु सुदुर्धरा ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि सावन्तं नाम लाङ्गलम् ..68..
text_mt: of whom it is said you are the impenetrable Vaiṣṇavī, exceedingly difficult to withstand! / I will invoke the plough named Sāvanta.

sanskrit_iast:
āgaccha lāṅgalāsyeha vyāhṛtiṃ bhuvanatrayam ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi saudhanvaṃ musalaṃ prabhum .. .. 69 ..
meaning:
आगच्छ लाङ्गलास्येह व्याहृतिं भुवनत्रयम् ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि सौधन्वं मुसलं प्रभुम् .. .. 69 ..
text_mt: Come here, plough, the vyāhṛti of the triple world! / I will invoke the pestle Saudhanva, the lord.

sanskrit_iast:
āgaccha musalādyeha devārigaṇasūdana ..
cāpamāvāhayiṣyāmi śārṅgaṃ ripuniṣūdanam .. 3.106.70 ..
meaning:
आगच्छ मुसलाद्येह देवारिगणसूदन ..
चापमावाहयिष्यामि शार्ङ्गं रिपुनिषूदनम् .. 3.106.70 ..
text_mt: Come here today, pestle, slayer of the hosts of the enemies of the gods! / I will invoke the bow Śārṅga, destroyer of foes.

sanskrit_iast:
āgaccha cāpa varada devāsuragaṇapriya ..
śaramāvāhayiṣyāmi mohanaṃ ripumohanam .. 71 ..
meaning:
आगच्छ चाप वरद देवासुरगणप्रिय ..
शरमावाहयिष्यामि मोहनं रिपुमोहनम् .. 71 ..
text_mt: Come, boon-granting bow, dear to the hosts of gods and asuras! / I will invoke the arrow Mohana, which confounds enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
ehi viddhāribalaja gacchāristribhuvaneśvara ..
carma cāvāhayiṣyāmi khyātamāvaraṇeti yat..72...
meaning:
एहि विद्धारिबलज गच्छारिस्त्रिभुवनेश्वर ..
चर्म चावाहयिष्यामि ख्यातमावरणेति यत्..72...
text_mt: Come, born of the pierced host of enemies, go against enemies, lord of the triple world! / And I will invoke the shield known as the Cover.

sanskrit_iast:
carmābhyehi viśāla tvaṃ sarvasyāvaraṇaṃ smṛtam ..
khaḍgamāvāhayiṣyāmi nandakaṃ nāma nāmataḥ .. 73 ..
meaning:
चर्माभ्येहि विशाल त्वं सर्वस्यावरणं स्मृतम् ..
खड्गमावाहयिष्यामि नन्दकं नाम नामतः .. 73 ..
text_mt: Come, broad shield, remembered as the protection of all! / I will invoke the sword, Nandaka by name.

sanskrit_iast:
ehi khaḍga mamāśeṣadaityanāthakulāntaka ...
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi vanamālāṃ sukhāvahām .. 74 ..
meaning:
एहि खड्ग ममाशेषदैत्यनाथकुलान्तक ...
अहमावाहयिष्यामि वनमालां सुखावहाम् .. 74 ..
text_mt: Come to me, sword, destroyer of the race of all the lords of daityas! / I will invoke the forest garland that brings joy.

sanskrit_iast:
vanamāle tvamabhyehi buddhāśeṣajagattraye ..
maṇimāvāhayiṣyāmi kaustubhaṃ keśavāṅgagam ..75...
meaning:
वनमाले त्वमभ्येहि बुद्धाशेषजगत्त्रये ..
मणिमावाहयिष्यामि कौस्तुभं केशवाङ्गगम् ..75...
text_mt: Come, forest garland, who know the entire triple world! / I will invoke the Kaustubha gem, resting upon Keśava's body.

sanskrit_iast:
kaustubha tvamihābhyehi marīcivikacodbhava ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi hariṃ hayaśirodharam .. 76 ..
meaning:
कौस्तुभ त्वमिहाभ्येहि मरीचिविकचोद्भव ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि हरिं हयशिरोधरम् .. 76 ..
text_mt: Come here, Kaustubha, origin of blossoming rays! / I will invoke the god Hari, who bears a horse's head,

sanskrit_iast:
śaśāṅkaśatasaṅkāśa vedoddharaṇaniścita ...
hayagrīva tvamabhyehi śaṅkhacakragadādhara .. 77 ..
meaning:
शशाङ्कशतसङ्काश वेदोद्धरणनिश्चित ...
हयग्रीव त्वमभ्येहि शङ्खचक्रगदाधर .. 77 ..
text_mt: resembling a hundred moons, determined to rescue the Vedas. / Come, Hayagrīva, holder of the conch, discus, and mace,

sanskrit_iast:
vedāharaṇaduḥkhārtasamāśvāsitapadmaja ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi ṛgvedaṃ padabhūṣitam .. 78 ...
meaning:
वेदाहरणदुःखार्तसमाश्वासितपद्मज ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि ऋग्वेदं पदभूषितम् .. 78 ...
text_mt: who consoled the Lotus-Born one afflicted with sorrow over the theft of the Vedas! / I will invoke the Ṛgveda, adorned with words.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛgveda tvamihābhyehi brahmamūrte varaprada ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi yajurvedamatipriyam .. 79 ..
meaning:
ऋग्वेद त्वमिहाभ्येहि ब्रह्ममूर्ते वरप्रद ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि यजुर्वेदमतिप्रियम् .. 79 ..
text_mt: Come here, Ṛgveda, form of Brahmā, giver of boons! / I will invoke the Yajurveda, exceedingly beloved.

sanskrit_iast:
yajurveda tvamabhyehi deveśagaṇanāyaka ... .
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi devamātharvaṇaṃ śubham .. 3.106.80 ..
meaning:
यजुर्वेद त्वमभ्येहि देवेशगणनायक ... .
अहमावाहयिष्यामि देवमाथर्वणं शुभम् .. 3.106.80 ..
text_mt: Come, O Yajurveda, leader of the hosts of the lord of the gods! / I shall invoke the auspicious Atharvaṇa god.

sanskrit_iast:
āgacchātharvavedeha sarvakarmaphalaprada ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi bhogibhogāsanasthitam .. 81 ..
meaning:
आगच्छाथर्ववेदेह सर्वकर्मफलप्रद ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि भोगिभोगासनस्थितम् .. 81 ..
text_mt: Come here, O Atharvaveda, bestower of the fruit of all rites! / I shall invoke the god seated upon the coils of the serpent.

sanskrit_iast:
bhogibhogāsanāsīna samāgaccha jagadguro ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi bhogibhogaśayaṃ prabhum .. 82 ..
meaning:
भोगिभोगासनासीन समागच्छ जगद्गुरो ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि भोगिभोगशयं प्रभुम् .. 82 ..
text_mt: Come, O teacher of the world, seated upon the coils of the serpent! / I shall invoke the lord who lies upon the coils of the serpent,

sanskrit_iast:
lakṣmīsahāyaṃ varadaṃ lokasākṣiṇamavyayam ..
ehyehi puṇḍarīkākṣa bhogibhogāśayācyuta .. 83 ..
meaning:
लक्ष्मीसहायं वरदं लोकसाक्षिणमव्ययम् ..
एह्येहि पुण्डरीकाक्ष भोगिभोगाशयाच्युत .. 83 ..
text_mt: Accompanied by Lakṣmī, boon-giver, witness of the world, imperishable! / Come, come, O lotus-eyed Acyuta, resting upon the coils of the serpent,

sanskrit_iast:
trailokyanātha govinda madhukaiṭabhasūdana ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi viṣṇudevaṃ trivikramam .. 84 ....
meaning:
त्रैलोक्यनाथ गोविन्द मधुकैटभसूदन ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि विष्णुदेवं त्रिविक्रमम् .. 84 ....
text_mt: Lord of the three worlds, Govinda, slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha! / I shall invoke the god Viṣṇu as Trivikrama,

sanskrit_iast:
samastabhuvanātīta pādākrāntajagattraya ..
trivikrama tvamabhyehi daityadīnākṣivīkṣita .. 85 ..
meaning:
समस्तभुवनातीत पादाक्रान्तजगत्त्रय ..
त्रिविक्रम त्वमभ्येहि दैत्यदीनाक्षिवीक्षित .. 85 ..
text_mt: Who transcends all the worlds, who strode over the three worlds with his feet! / Come, O Trivikrama, beheld by the pitiable eyes of the Daityas,

sanskrit_iast:
vikacotphullanayana tridaśaiḥ śatamīkṣita ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi viśvarūpadharaṃ vibhum .. 86 ..
meaning:
विकचोत्फुल्लनयन त्रिदशैः शतमीक्षित ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि विश्वरूपधरं विभुम् .. 86 ..
text_mt: With wide open, blossoming eyes, gazed upon a hundred times by the gods! / I shall invoke the all-pervading lord who bears the universal form,

sanskrit_iast:
śvasantamaniśaṃ vaktrairbhūtagrāmamaśeṣataḥ ..
sṛjaṃti ca mahārāja sarvabhūtānyanekaśaḥ .. 87 ..
meaning:
श्वसन्तमनिशं वक्त्रैर्भूतग्राममशेषतः ..
सृजंति च महाराज सर्वभूतान्यनेकशः .. 87 ..
text_mt: Ceaselessly breathing forth the entire multitude of beings with his mouths, / And creating, O great king, all beings manifoldly,

sanskrit_iast:
dhārayantaṃ śarīreṇa sarvaṃ jagadidaṃ tathā ..
viśvarūpa tvamabhyehi sarvāyudhavibhūṣita .. 88 ..
meaning:
धारयन्तं शरीरेण सर्वं जगदिदं तथा ..
विश्वरूप त्वमभ्येहि सर्वायुधविभूषित .. 88 ..
text_mt: And likewise upholding this entire universe with his body! / Come, O Universal Form, adorned with all weapons,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvabhūtena tātena nānāvarṇadharāpaha ..
dehasthāśeṣabhuvana jagatkāraṇakāraṇa..89..
meaning:
सर्वभूतेन तातेन नानावर्णधरापह ..
देहस्थाशेषभुवन जगत्कारणकारण..89..
text_mt: Constituting all beings, O father, dispelling [afflictions], bearing various colours, / Within whose body all worlds abide, cause of the cause of the world,

sanskrit_iast:
durnirīkṣyātigambhīra māyādarśitavigraha ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi matsyaṃ salilagocaram..3.106.90..
meaning:
दुर्निरीक्ष्यातिगम्भीर मायादर्शितविग्रह ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि मत्स्यं सलिलगोचरम्..3.106.90..
text_mt: Difficult to behold, exceedingly profound, whose form is displayed through māyā! / I shall invoke the god who moves in the waters, the Fish.

sanskrit_iast:
matsyadeva tvamabhyehi lokajīvadharācyuta ..
haṃsamāvāhayiṣyāmi devaṃ jñānapradaṃ vibhum..91..
meaning:
मत्स्यदेव त्वमभ्येहि लोकजीवधराच्युत ..
हंसमावाहयिष्यामि देवं ज्ञानप्रदं विभुम्..91..
text_mt: Come, O divine Fish, Acyuta who preserves the life of the world! / I shall invoke the all-pervading divine Swan, bestower of knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsa śīghraṃ tvamabhyehi sarvajñānavināśana..
kūrmamāvāhayiṣyāmi dhṛtamandaraparvatam..92..
meaning:
हंस शीघ्रं त्वमभ्येहि सर्वज्ञानविनाशन..
कूर्ममावाहयिष्यामि धृतमन्दरपर्वतम्..92..
text_mt: Come quickly, O Swan, destroyer of all [ignorant] knowledge! / I shall invoke the Tortoise who bore Mount Mandara.

sanskrit_iast:
ehyehi bhagavankūrma śyāmotpattikarācyuta ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi strīrūpaṃ dharmamīśvaram .. 93 ..
meaning:
एह्येहि भगवन्कूर्म श्यामोत्पत्तिकराच्युत ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि स्त्रीरूपं धर्ममीश्वरम् .. 93 ..
text_mt: Come, come, O blessed Tortoise, dark one, originator [of beings], Acyuta! / I shall invoke the sovereign god, dharma in the form of a woman.

sanskrit_iast:
strīrūpadhārinnabhyehi surasomapradāyaka ..
naramāvāhayiṣyāmi devaṃ tapasi niṣṭhitam .. 94 ..
meaning:
स्त्रीरूपधारिन्नभ्येहि सुरसोमप्रदायक ..
नरमावाहयिष्यामि देवं तपसि निष्ठितम् .. 94 ..
text_mt: Come, O bearer of a female form, who gave soma to the gods! / I shall invoke the god Nara, steadfast in asceticism.

sanskrit_iast:
narābhyehi mahābhāga dharmamūrte jagatpate ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi tathā nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum .. 95 .
meaning:
नराभ्येहि महाभाग धर्ममूर्ते जगत्पते ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि तथा नारायणं प्रभुम् .. 95 .
text_mt: Come, O Nara, illustrious one, embodiment of dharma, lord of the world! / I shall likewise invoke the lord, the god Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
nārāyaṇa samabhyehi sarvapāpaharāvyaya ..
harimāvāhayiṣyāmi deveśaṃ kanakaprabham .. 96 ..
meaning:
नारायण समभ्येहि सर्वपापहराव्यय ..
हरिमावाहयिष्यामि देवेशं कनकप्रभम् .. 96 ..
text_mt: Come, O Nārāyaṇa, imperishable one, remover of all sins! / I shall invoke Hari, lord of the gods, radiant as gold.

sanskrit_iast:
hare deva tvamabhyehi paradarpavināśaka ..
kṛṣṇamāvāhayiṣyāmi sajalāmbudasannibham .. 97 ..
meaning:
हरे देव त्वमभ्येहि परदर्पविनाशक ..
कृष्णमावाहयिष्यामि सजलाम्बुदसन्निभम् .. 97 ..
text_mt: Come, O divine Hari, destroyer of the pride of foes! / I shall invoke Kṛṣṇa, resembling a water-laden cloud.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇābhyehi mahābhāga devadeva jagatpriya ..
devamāvāhayiṣyāmi dattātreyaṃ taponvitam .. 98
meaning:
कृष्णाभ्येहि महाभाग देवदेव जगत्प्रिय ..
देवमावाहयिष्यामि दत्तात्रेयं तपोन्वितम् .. 98
text_mt: Come, O Kṛṣṇa, illustrious one, god of gods, beloved of the world! / I shall invoke the divine Dattātreya, endowed with asceticism.

sanskrit_iast:
dattātreya tvamabhyehi vedoddharaṇatatpara ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi vālmīkiṃ tapasāṃ nidhim .. 99 ..
meaning:
दत्तात्रेय त्वमभ्येहि वेदोद्धरणतत्पर ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि वाल्मीकिं तपसां निधिम् .. 99 ..
text_mt: Come, O Dattātreya, intent upon rescuing the Vedas! / I shall invoke Vālmīki, storehouse of asceticism.

sanskrit_iast:
vālmīke tvamihābhyehi vedoddharaṇatatpara ..
rāmamāvāhayiṣyāmi hatakṣattriyamaṇḍalam .. 3.106.100 ..
meaning:
वाल्मीके त्वमिहाभ्येहि वेदोद्धरणतत्पर ..
राममावाहयिष्यामि हतक्षत्त्रियमण्डलम् .. 3.106.100 ..
text_mt: Come here, O Vālmīki, intent upon rescuing the Vedas! / I shall invoke Rāma, who destroyed the host of kṣatriyas.

sanskrit_iast:
bhāgarvābhyehi me nātha jaṭāmaṇḍaladurdṛśa ..
āvāhanaṃ kariṣyāmi paraśuṃ dīptatejasam .. 101 ..
meaning:
भागर्वाभ्येहि मे नाथ जटामण्डलदुर्दृश ..
आवाहनं करिष्यामि परशुं दीप्ततेजसम् .. 101 ..
text_mt: Come, O Bhārgava, my lord, formidable with your circle of matted hair! / I shall perform the invocation of the Axe of blazing splendour.

sanskrit_iast:
āgaccha paraśo śīghraṃ lakṣīkṛtavasundhara ..
pṛthumāvāhayiṣyāmi cakravartinamūrjitam .. 102 ..
meaning:
आगच्छ परशो शीघ्रं लक्षीकृतवसुन्धर ..
पृथुमावाहयिष्यामि चक्रवर्तिनमूर्जितम् .. 102 ..
text_mt: Come quickly, O Axe, that made the earth your target! / I shall invoke Pṛthu, the mighty universal emperor.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛtho śīghraṃ tvamabhyehi pṛthvīnātha mahābala ..
rāmamāvāhayiṣyāmi kṛtarākṣasanigraham .. 103 ..
meaning:
पृथो शीघ्रं त्वमभ्येहि पृथ्वीनाथ महाबल ..
राममावाहयिष्यामि कृतराक्षसनिग्रहम् .. 103 ..
text_mt: Come quickly, O Pṛthu, lord of the earth, of great might! / I shall invoke Rāma, who subdued the rākṣasas.

sanskrit_iast:
rāma śīghraṃ tvamabhyehi dharmaseto durāsada ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi pradyumnaṃ bharataṃ vibhum .. 104 ..
meaning:
राम शीघ्रं त्वमभ्येहि धर्मसेतो दुरासद ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि प्रद्युम्नं भरतं विभुम् .. 104 ..
text_mt: Come quickly, O Rāma, bridge of dharma, unassailable one! / I shall invoke the all-pervading Bharata, who is Pradyumna.

sanskrit_iast:
bharata tvamihābhyehi kṛtagandharvanigraha ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇaṃ ripunāśanam .. 105 ..
meaning:
भरत त्वमिहाभ्येहि कृतगन्धर्वनिग्रह ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि लक्ष्मणं रिपुनाशनम् .. 105 ..
text_mt: Come here, O Bharata, who subdued the gandharvas! / I shall invoke Lakṣmaṇa, destroyer of foes.

sanskrit_iast:
lakṣmaṇa tvamihābhyehi meghanādāstrabhāskara ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi śatrughnaṃ dīptatejasam .. 106 ..
meaning:
लक्ष्मण त्वमिहाभ्येहि मेघनादास्त्रभास्कर ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि शत्रुघ्नं दीप्ततेजसम् .. 106 ..
text_mt: Come here, O Lakṣmaṇa, sun [drying up] the missile of Meghanāda! / I shall invoke Śatrughna of blazing splendour.

sanskrit_iast:
śatrughna śīghramabhyehi lavaṇāsuramardana ..
vyāsamāvāhayiṣyāmi vedavyāsaṃ jagadgurum .. 107 ..
meaning:
शत्रुघ्न शीघ्रमभ्येहि लवणासुरमर्दन ..
व्यासमावाहयिष्यामि वेदव्यासं जगद्गुरुम् .. 107 ..
text_mt: Come quickly, O Śatrughna, crusher of the asura Lavaṇa! / I shall invoke Vyāsa, Vedavyāsa, teacher of the world.

sanskrit_iast:
vedavyāsa tvamabhyehi sarvadharmapradarśaka ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram .. 108 ..
meaning:
वेदव्यास त्वमभ्येहि सर्वधर्मप्रदर्शक ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम् .. 108 ..
text_mt: Come, O Vedavyāsa, revealer of all dharmas! / I shall invoke Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
yudhiṣṭhira tvamabhyehi sarvadharmabhṛtāṃvara ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi bhīmaṃ mārutaputrakam .. 109 ..
meaning:
युधिष्ठिर त्वमभ्येहि सर्वधर्मभृतांवर ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि भीमं मारुतपुत्रकम् .. 109 ..
text_mt: Come, O Yudhiṣṭhira, foremost of all upholders of dharma! / I shall invoke Bhīma, son of the Wind.

sanskrit_iast:
bhīmasena tvamabhyehi śatrunāśa tamohara ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi pārthaṃ ripuniṣūdanam .. 3.106.110 ..
meaning:
भीमसेन त्वमभ्येहि शत्रुनाश तमोहर ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि पार्थं रिपुनिषूदनम् .. 3.106.110 ..
text_mt: Come, O Bhīmasena, destroyer of foes, dispeller of darkness! / I shall invoke Pārtha, slayer of enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
arjunābhyehi me śīghraṃ laghvīkṛtavasundhara ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi nakulaṃ rūpaśobhitam .. 111 ..
meaning:
अर्जुनाभ्येहि मे शीघ्रं लघ्वीकृतवसुन्धर ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि नकुलं रूपशोभितम् .. 111 ..
text_mt: Come quickly to me, O Arjuna, who lightened the burden of the earth! / I shall invoke Nakula, adorned with beauty.

sanskrit_iast:
nakula tvamihābhyehi śaṅkhacarmmadharācyuta ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi sahadevaṃ raṇapriyam .. 112 ..
meaning:
नकुल त्वमिहाभ्येहि शङ्खचर्म्मधराच्युत ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि सहदेवं रणप्रियम् .. 112 ..
text_mt: Come here, O Nakula, Acyuta who bears the conch and shield! / I shall invoke Sahadeva, who loves battle.

sanskrit_iast:
sahadeva tvamabhyehi rūpadraviṇasaṃyuta ..
kṛṣṇāmāvāhayiṣyāmi svargalakṣmīṃ manoharām .. 113 ..
meaning:
सहदेव त्वमभ्येहि रूपद्रविणसंयुत ..
कृष्णामावाहयिष्यामि स्वर्गलक्ष्मीं मनोहराम् .. 113 ..
text_mt: Come, O Sahadeva, endowed with beauty and wealth! / I shall invoke Kṛṣṇā, the captivating fortune of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
yājñaseni tvamabhyehi lakṣīkṛtavasundhare ..
sītāmāvāhayiṣyāmi rāmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm .. 114 ..
meaning:
याज्ञसेनि त्वमभ्येहि लक्षीकृतवसुन्धरे ..
सीतामावाहयिष्यामि रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम् .. 114 ..
text_mt: Come, O Yājñasenī, who made the earth your aim! / I shall invoke Sītā, the renowned wife of Rāma.

sanskrit_iast:
sīte devi tvamabhyehi mahītalasamukṣite ..
ahamāvāhayipyāmi devakīṃ kṛṣṇamātaram ..115..
meaning:
सीते देवि त्वमभ्येहि महीतलसमुक्षिते ..
अहमावाहयिप्यामि देवकीं कृष्णमातरम् ..115..
text_mt: Come, O divine Sītā, sprung from the surface of the earth! / I shall invoke Devakī, mother of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
devaki tvaṃ samabhyehi devamātarjagatpriye ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi yaśodāṃ jagataḥ priyām ..116..
meaning:
देवकि त्वं समभ्येहि देवमातर्जगत्प्रिये ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि यशोदां जगतः प्रियाम् ..116..
text_mt: Come, O Devakī, mother of the god, beloved of the world! / I shall invoke Yaśodā, dear to the world.

sanskrit_iast:
yaśode tvamihābhyehi saṃvardhitajanārdane ..
devīmāvāhayiṣyāmi ekānāśīti viśrutām..117..
meaning:
यशोदे त्वमिहाभ्येहि संवर्धितजनार्दने ..
देवीमावाहयिष्यामि एकानाशीति विश्रुताम्..117..
text_mt: Come here, O Yaśodā, who nurtured Janārdana! / I shall invoke the goddess renowned as Ekānaṃśā.

sanskrit_iast:
ekānāśe tvamabhyehi kṛṣṇarakṣārthamudyate ..
devīmāvāhayiṣyāmi rukmiṇīṃ kṛṣṇavallabhām .. 118 ..
meaning:
एकानाशे त्वमभ्येहि कृष्णरक्षार्थमुद्यते ..
देवीमावाहयिष्यामि रुक्मिणीं कृष्णवल्लभाम् .. 118 ..
text_mt: Come, O Ekānaṃśā, intent on protecting Kṛṣṇa! / I shall invoke the goddess Rukmiṇī, beloved of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
rukmiṇi tvamihābhyehi jagatāmekasundari ..
devīmāvāhayiṣyāmi satyabhāmāṃ manoharām ..119 ..
meaning:
रुक्मिणि त्वमिहाभ्येहि जगतामेकसुन्दरि ..
देवीमावाहयिष्यामि सत्यभामां मनोहराम् ..119 ..
text_mt: Come here, O Rukmiṇī, peerless beauty of the worlds! / I shall invoke the captivating goddess Satyabhāmā.

sanskrit_iast:
satyabhāme tvamabhyehi devi keśavavallabhe ..
devīstvāvāhayiṣyāmi kṛṣṇapatnīrahaṃ śubhāḥ ..3.106.120..
meaning:
सत्यभामे त्वमभ्येहि देवि केशववल्लभे ..
देवीस्त्वावाहयिष्यामि कृष्णपत्नीरहं शुभाः ..3.106.120..
text_mt: Come, O Satyabhāmā, O goddess beloved of Keśava! / I shall invoke the auspicious goddesses, the wives of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
devyaḥ sarvāḥ samāyāntu gāndhārīpramukhāstviha ..
rāmamāvāhayiṣyāmi madavibhrāntalocanam .. 321 ..
meaning:
देव्यः सर्वाः समायान्तु गान्धारीप्रमुखास्त्विह ..
राममावाहयिष्यामि मदविभ्रान्तलोचनम् .. 321 ..
text_mt: Let all the goddesses headed by Gāndhārī come here! / I shall invoke Rāma, whose eyes roll with intoxication,

sanskrit_iast:
kuṇḍalaikadharaṃ śāntaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam ..
ehi rāma mahābhāga revatīdayitācyuta ..122..
meaning:
कुण्डलैकधरं शान्तं वनमालाविभूषितम् ..
एहि राम महाभाग रेवतीदयिताच्युत ..122..
text_mt: Wearing a single earring, tranquil, adorned with a woodland garland! / Come, O Rāma, illustrious one, beloved of Revatī, Acyuta,

sanskrit_iast:
hatapralambasīrāgravyākṛṣṭayamunodaka ..
kṛṣṇamāvāhayiṣyāmi toyapūrṇāmbudacchavim .. 123 ..
meaning:
हतप्रलम्बसीराग्रव्याकृष्टयमुनोदक ..
कृष्णमावाहयिष्यामि तोयपूर्णाम्बुदच्छविम् .. 123 ..
text_mt: Slayer of Pralamba, who dragged the water of the Yamunā with the tip of his plow! / I shall invoke Kṛṣṇa, of the complexion of a water-filled cloud,

sanskrit_iast:
cāṇūrabaladarpaghnaṃ kaṃsāsuravināśanam ..
ehi kṛṣṇa mahābhāga lakṣīkṛtavasundhara .. 124 ..
meaning:
चाणूरबलदर्पघ्नं कंसासुरविनाशनम् ..
एहि कृष्ण महाभाग लक्षीकृतवसुन्धर .. 124 ..
text_mt: Who broke the pride of Cāṇūra's strength, destroyer of the asura Kaṃsa! / Come, O Kṛṣṇa, illustrious one, who took the earth as your target,

sanskrit_iast:
nirastadānavaśreṣṭha dhṛtagovardhanācala ..

The mantras that have been stated for invocation are to be known as the very same in awakening; / for invocation and for awakening, they should be employed by the wise, O lord of Yadu's lineage.
3.107
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
O hero, a mantra for awakening was indeed not declared for the gods; / I shall proclaim to you, O king, the awakening of Vāsudeva.
I shall awaken the lord, the unborn, all-pervading Vāsudeva, / who has no beginning, middle, or end, endowed with great strength and valour,
endless, all-pervading, the protector, greater than the great, / subtler than the subtlest, far away yet close at hand,
Nārāyaṇa of gentle hand, the god who bears the bow Śārṅga, / dark as the atasī flower, clad in yellow garments, the infallible one.
[Awake!] The lotus-eyed one is awakened, he who is tender toward those who take refuge in him! / O you who showed mercy to the broken elephant plunged in the lake of worldly existence!
O you who severed the snout of the crocodile of bad dreams with the rim of your discus, unassailable one! / O you whose eyes were closed in deep meditation through the great yogic sleep you resorted to!

text_mt:
O unfailing one, whose spacious couch extends along the coils of the serpent Śeṣa! / O you who have an upper canopy formed by the rays of the gems in his rows of hoods!
O you who shine with both lotus feet being massaged by Lakṣmī! / O you who destroyed the great Daityas and secured the safety of the three worlds!
O unfailing one, who sleep upon the ocean of milk gleaming like a web of cool moonbeams! / O destroyer of the fear of falling into the pits of hell for your devotees!
O you who offer a supporting hand to them for journeying to your own world! / O great ship for crossing the ocean of worldly existence, O Janārdana!
O you who bring about the destruction of dense [sins] merely by the utterance of your name! / O you whose praise alone yields the great fruit of all desires!
O you whose strides as Trivikrama overstepped the upper pavilion of the cosmic egg! / O you who lifted up the earth in sport with the tip of your tusk that resembled the crescent moon!
These gods, led by Indra, are awakening you, / as well as the highly fortunate sages whose vision of the three worlds is stainless.
The god Brahmā of auspicious four faces is awakening you, / and the Yajurveda with its verses of praise, O best of gods, O unfailing one!

Cast off sleep today, O slayer of the enemies of the hosts of gods; be the remover of the accumulation of my sins, O lord of the world! / For he who has intense devotion to you, O lord, attains a state that surpasses even that of the gods.
3.108
Vajra said:
O blessed one, the bodily forms of all the gods have been proclaimed; / because they consist of the five gross elements, therefore for them, O foremost of the Bhṛgus,
the rule of invocation has been declared, which is considered most proper; / where, when invoked, they attain the fulfilment of desires.
[The gods come,] resorting to magnitude, attainment, and lightness, O gods. / Viṣṇu is the all-pervading god, greater than even the great,
subtler than the subtle, all-pervading, and composed of the universe. / There is nothing in this universe where Janārdana is not.
The real and the unreal, O fortunate one, are pervaded by that Great Soul. / What is the use of invocation for him who is all-pervading?
[He who is beyond] the great senses, O fortunate one, is experienced everywhere. / Dispel this doubt of mine, for you are called omniscient.

text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Just as all the hosts of gods, O Vajra, possess condensed forms, / even so is the god, the slayer of Madhu, when he has assumed a manifestation.
Every form endowed with the five elements becomes adorned, / joined with beginning, end, and middle for everything, O best of Yadus.
Just as the hosts of gods, so too Viṣṇu, having assumed a manifestation, / being invoked, becomes present: this is the certain conclusion.
Twofold is the form of the god: higher and lower. / The form of the higher is of the Cosmic Person, shining with the five elements;
by it, the all-pervading Supreme Lord possesses a form. / Without the Cosmic Person, nothing whatsoever exists here in the world.
He is without beginning, middle, or end, and of immeasurable body; / he is power, mind, and all senses in every direction, O king.
That omnipotence of his, even when he has assumed a manifestation, / is declared to be [present] when he wills it, but not when he does not will it, O king.
Indeed, in the state of the Cosmic Person, that omnipotence of the Infinite One, O king, / should be known as naturally accomplished, always and everywhere, O Yādava.

text_mt:
Moreover, as to the invocation of the Lord of the world that is performed here, / even of Parameṣṭhin who is eternally present everywhere,
the sole reason there is to cause satisfaction to the mind: / 'The god has been invoked by me in this place, even though he was already present.'
Just as invocation exists for the self-satisfaction of the person, / even so, O fortunate one, the worship has self-satisfaction as its purpose.
For him who is eternally satisfied, what purpose does he have with worship?
Only to satisfy devotion does he accept [it] from his devotees. / That god who is worshipped, where the god is worshipped by the wise,
and with whatever dispositions one worships—know that all that is identical with him. / Know that the performance of his worship has as its purpose the pleasure of the performer.
Likewise, the self of that all-pervading one should be known. / By that causeless, eternally satisfied one, O Yādava,
[this] was set in motion for the grace of devotees and of himself, / so that, though bodiless, he abides in a body, O lord of the earth.

text_mt:
Indeed, he is invoked precisely for the comprehension of the mark of devotion. / For the formless, O great king, fixing the target is difficult.
Fixing the target can indeed be easily done with forms; / and the form of one who has assumed a manifestation, according to rule,
has been described by me earlier, O tiger among kings, according to the treatise. / Whatever disposition a man may have in contemplation,
with that very [disposition] contemplation and worship should be performed by him, O Yādava. / Having first fixed the target on a form, O fortunate one,
he then becomes capable of meditation on the void, O best of men. / Thus his invocation and likewise his worship, O Yādava,
is performed with effort by the awakened for the sake of grace upon themselves. / The eternally satisfied one does not offer a presentation for the sake of his own satisfaction;
he accepts [it], O great king, as one who bestows grace upon his devotees. / Both of these should be known by you as leading to the attainment of liberation, O mighty-armed one:

3.109
Vajra said:
O blessed one, tell [me] the rule for the fire-offering.
The blessed Mārkaṇḍeya said to him:
The Blessed One having been ritually inhabited, [the priest], having kindled the fire, swept around it, and offered melted clarified butter with festivity between the portions of ghee [accompanied by] the demon-destroying mantras as stated before, should offer eight, twenty-eight, or one hundred and eight oblations of ghee, or barley, sesame, and white mustard seeds, with the names about to be spoken, ending in 'svāhā' and employed in the dative case, one by one with each name:
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vāsudeva!'
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Saṃkarṣaṇa!'
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Pradyumna!'
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Aniruddha!'
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Cosmic Person!'
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Satya!'
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Acyuta!'
'Oṃ, homage to Śrī!'
'Oṃ, homage to Kālarātri!'
'Oṃ, homage to Sṛṣṭi!'
'Oṃ, homage to Garuḍa!'
'Oṃ, homage to Tāla!'
'Oṃ, homage to Makara!'
'Oṃ, homage to Ṛṣya!'
'Oṃ, homage to Ananta!'
'Oṃ, homage to the Kaustubha!'
'Oṃ, homage to the forest-garland!'
'Oṃ, homage to the Earth!'
'Oṃ, homage to the conch!'
'Oṃ, homage to the lotus!'
'Oṃ, homage to the mace!'
'Oṃ, homage to the discus!'
'Oṃ, homage to the plough!'
'Oṃ, homage to the pestle!'
'Oṃ, homage to the bow!'
'Oṃ, homage to the shield!'
'Oṃ, homage to the sword!'
'Oṃ, homage to Subhadra!'
'Oṃ, homage to Vasubhadra!'
'Oṃ, homage to Āṣāḍha!'
'Oṃ, homage to Yajñatāta!'
'Oṃ, homage to Jaya!'
'Oṃ, homage to Vijaya!'
'Oṃ, homage to Āmoda!'
'Oṃ, homage to Pramoda!'
Then the offering with the sacred utterances should be performed.
Then he should perform the offering with the Gāyatrī.
Then with this [verse]: 'That highest step of Viṣṇu'; then with the Vaiṣṇava Gāyatrī.
Then with the section beginning 'They yoke the mind'.
Then with the Puruṣasūkta.
Then with the four verses beginning 'The chariot among the dice'.
Then with the six [verses] of the Camaka.
Then with clarified butter.
He should complete the subsequent rite with the actions preceded by the fire-offering to the Year, the gods, and so forth.
This fire-offering is proclaimed for the consecration of Viṣṇu;
and for other deities, he should offer the oblation with [mantras containing] their specific marks.
