3.110
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now, when the day of consecration and the rest has arrived, one should awaken the glorious Blessed One with conches, drums, and wind instruments.
One should recite the awakening mantra.
Then the master of rites, bearing the image of countless aeons with arms raised, and the architect holding a water-jar, should enter the temple of the deity with the mantra: 'The Blessed One who is here, and whoever is the Blessed One here'.
Then one should bury all-herbs mixed with the five products of the cow, all-perfumes, all-jewels, and gold in the cavity of the pedestal.
And there, the mantras are:
'Mahābhāga' [Greatly Fortunate One];

'Bhāsa' [Radiance];
'Trisuparṇa';
'Bhāruṇḍa';
'Mṛtyulāṅgala';
'May Indra grant us well-being'; the twelve-verse hymn on the inner self;
and the 'Ātmavyūha'. Then, at the time appointed by the astrologer, [he should set] the Blessed One well-balanced upon the pedestal, facing right forward.
With this very mantra, 'Firm is the sky', he should make Him motionless.
And he should utter His name,
and recite the Sāman of consecration.
And all the people should make an uproar with shouts of victory and showers of fried grain and flowers.
He should have musical instruments played.
He should utter: 'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vāsudeva!'
And he should recite the Brahmasūkta.
With 'You are the life-span of Agni', he should perform the infusion of life.
And the master of rites, water-jar in hand, should recite:
'Oṃ! You are established, O Blessed One; may this consecration be auspicious! / Enter into proximity for the prosperity of the patron of the sacrifice!
May there be peace always for our two-footed, and may there be peace for our four-footed! / May there be peace for all the world, and likewise may there be peace for the king!
The patron of the sacrifice, together with his servants, sons, cattle, and kin, / is ever to be protected by the Blessed One, and so too this land. Homage to You!'

तत्रादावेवोङ्कारनमस्कारपवित्राभिर्ज्ञात्वा दशाध्यात्ममृत्पिण्डमाधुरैः सात्त्वतो दद्यात् ..
ततः सामविन्महावामदेवलक्षरथन्तरशाक्वरभारुण्डबृहत्सामभिः ..
अथर्वविदथर्वशिराः प्रत्यङ्गिरः शङ्खमणिप्राणसूक्तमणिप्रतिसरमणिभिः ..
ऋग्वेदवित् गायत्रीसावित्रीगोसूक्ताश्च ..
सूर्यसूक्तपुरुषसूक्तश्रीसूक्तैर्यजुर्वेदवित् ..
कृष्णाजिनचमसषट्कषडृतुकूष्माण्डरुद्रद्रविणैः .
ततः स्वशक्त्या कलशसहस्रकलशाष्टशत पञ्च वा शतानि चत्वारि वा शतमष्टाधिकं वा अष्टाविंशतिर्वाष्टौ वा स्वर्चितान्वनस्पतिकालापगर्भशङ्खध्वनिस्वनेन वाद्यशब्देन जयजयकारवंदिशब्देन प्रसुभगानर्तितेन देयाः ..
ततः पवित्रेणोपकलशान्विश्राम्य वेद्यां क्षिपेत् ..
घृतवतीति घृतावेक्षं दर्शयेत् ..
सहस्रशीर्षेण शिखण्डोदग्रहणशाटकं दद्यात् ..
युवासुवास इति प्रतिनिर्वसनशाटकम् ..
इदमापः प्रवहत इत्याचमनीयं ततो जानुभ्यां पाणिभ्यां शिरसा च नमस्कारं कुर्यात् ..
बृहत्स्नपनमेतद्धि यः करोति नरो हरेः..
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोके महीयते..
न केवलं प्रतिष्ठायां सर्वदैवं समाचरेत् ..
शान्तिदं पौष्टिकं काम्यं बृहत्स्नपनमुत्तमम ..
दिव्यान्तरिक्षभौमानामुत्पातानां समुद्भवे ..
देवदेवस्य राजेन्द्र बृहत्स्नपनमाचरेत् ..
नास्ति लोके समुत्पातो यो ह्यनेन न शाम्यति ..
आरोग्यकामः श्रीकामो मोक्षकामश्च बन्धनात् ..
सौभाग्यशान्तिकामश्च बृहत्स्नपनमाचरेत् ..
विद्यार्थी प्राप्नुयाद्विद्यां पुत्रकामस्तथात्मजान् ..
प्रियाश्च मुख्याः प्राप्नोति याश्च कामयते यदि ..
अकामकामः प्राप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ..

3.111
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now, one should begin the Great Bathing of the installed Lord; then one should recite the Gāyatrī.
With 'Iṣe tvā', one should present the spittoon.
With the Vaiṣṇava Gāyatrī, the pair of sandals.
With 'Bhūmyā vṛtvā yano 'si', clay.
With 'Śanno āpaḥ', the offering of honorific water.
With 'Devebhyo vanaspate', the tooth-stick.
With 'Yāmālikha', the tongue-scraper.
With 'Āpo hi ṣṭhā', sipping water.
With a vessel, the respectful offering of water.
With 'Yuvā suvāsāḥ', the bathing cloth.
With 'Dhruvā dyauḥ', the seat.
With the Pratiṣṭhā-sāman, the footstool.
With 'Kanikradat', the seed-vessel.
With 'Tejo śukram asi', the lamp.
With 'Mukhād indra', the mirror.
Likewise, the face-paste.
Lodhra, cinnamon, jujube marrow, sweet flag, costus, blue water-lilies, and saffron: this is the face-paste.
With 'Sahasraśīrṣā', the oil.
With 'Bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ', the rubbing with unguents.
With Supratīka, bathing with the ladle.
With Ṛṣabha, bathing with the cleansing [water].
With 'Ghṛtavatī', the bath with clarified butter.
With 'Dadhikrāvṇaḥ', with curd.
With 'Payasvatī', with milk.
With 'Gandhadvārā', with cow dung.
With the Gāyatrī, with cow urine.
With Aghamarṣaṇa, with the five bovine products.
With 'Dhruvā dyauḥ', with the firm cleansing [water].
With 'Madhu vātā ṛtāyate', with honey.
With Supratīka, with sugarcane juice.
With the Bhauma [hymn], with molasses-water.
With the Atharvaśiras, with sugar-water.
With Vāmadeva, with clay from both banks of a river.
With 'Śāntā dyauḥ', with clay from a confluence.
With the Prāṇasūkta, with clay from a lake.
With the Vārāha [hymn], with clay uprooted by a boar.
With Vāmadeva, with clay from an elephant's tusk.
With Vṛṣabha, with clay from the horn of a bull.
With 'Aśvakrāntā', with all [clays combined].
With the Bhāruṇḍa [hymn], with myrobalan fruits.
With Vikarṇa, with lodhra.
With the Jyeṣṭhasāman, with kāleyaka sandal.
With the Bṛhatsāman, with citron.
With Kṛṣṇājina, with colored bathing powder.
With 'Agna āyur asi', with tagara.
With the Śrīsūkta, with priyaṅgu.
With 'Viṣṇo rarāṭam', with white mustard seeds.
With Kṛṣṇamaṇi, with cultivated [grain].
With Śiribhiṭa, with kuśa grass water.
With 'Yā oṣadhayaḥ', with all medicinal herbs.
With 'Ā brahman brāhmaṇaḥ', with seeds.
With 'Puṣpavatī', with flowers.
With 'Vanaspate vīḍvaṅgaḥ', with bundles of forest trees.
With 'Puṣpavatī', with fruits.
With 'Āśuḥ śiśānaḥ', with jewels.
With 'Gandhadvārā', with perfumes.
With medicinal herbs for the head-bath purified by the praṇava and obeisance, namely: costus, lodhra, mustā, sweet flag, mustard seeds, jayantī, viṣṇukrāntā, punarnavā, brāhmī, tagara, atibalā, navabalā, nāgabalā, cassia leaf, eaglewood, bālaka, hareṇuka, clove, agarwood, vetiver, nālikā, cūraka, and the two kinds of turmeric.
In this manner occurs the presentation of the pots for the bath.
There, right at the beginning, knowing [them] by means of the purifications with the praṇava and obeisance, the Sāttvata should present the ten spiritual sweet clay balls.
Then the knower of the Sāmaveda [should officiate] with the Mahāvāmadeva, Lakṣa, Rathantara, Śākvara, Bhāruṇḍa, and Bṛhat sāmans.
The knower of the Atharvaveda with the Atharvaśiras, Pratyaṅgiras, Śaṅkhamaṇi, Prāṇasūkta, and Maṇipratisara jewels.
The knower of the Ṛgveda with the Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, and Gosūkta.
The knower of the Yajurveda with the Sūryasūkta, Puruṣasūkta, and Śrīsūkta;
with the Kṛṣṇājina, Camasa, Ṣaṭka, Ṣaḍṛtu, Kūṣmāṇḍa, and Rudradraviṇa [hymns].
Then, according to one's capacity, a thousand pots, eight hundred pots, five hundred, four [hundred], a hundred and eight, twenty-eight, or eight, well-worshipped, containing bundles of forest trees, should be offered amidst the sounding of conches, musical instruments, cries of 'Victory! Victory!', words of bards, and auspicious dancing.
Then, having rested the subsidiary pots with a strainer, he should place them on the altar.
With 'Ghṛtavatī', he should present the gazing into clarified butter.
With 'Sahasraśīrṣā', he should present the cloth for wiping the head-hair.
With 'Yuvā suvāsāḥ', the cloth for changing garments.
With 'Idam āpaḥ pravahata', the water for sipping; then he should make prostration with his knees, hands, and head.
Indeed, the man who performs this Great Bathing for Hari,
freed from all sins, is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
One should perform it not only at an installation, but at all times;
the Great Bathing is supreme, bestowing peace, nourishing, and fulfilling desires.
Upon the occurrence of portents—celestial, atmospheric, or terrestrial—
O king of kings, one should perform the Great Bathing of the God of gods.
There is no portent in the world that is not pacified by this.
One who desires health, one who desires fortune, one who desires liberation from bondage,
and one who desires good luck and peace should perform the Great Bathing.
A seeker of knowledge will attain knowledge; likewise, one desiring a son [will attain] offspring;
and he attains beloved and foremost [women], if he so desires.
One who has no desire desires and attains that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

3.112
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
He should worship the holy Lord once bathed.
He should make an ointment of all [together] or individually: sandalwood, abundant resin, nutmeg, musk, and camphor.
With "Gandhadvārā...", he should anoint the holy Lord.
With "Vāyur agregāḥ...", he should present a palm-leaf fan.
With "Vāta ā vātu bheṣajam...", he should fan [him].
With "Sāvitrāṇi sāvitrasya...", he should present a chowrie.
With the holy Viṣṇu-gāyatrī, he should present seeds.
With "Yuvā suvāsāḥ...", he should cover the holy Lord with costly garments.
He should worship [him] with ornaments that are golden-coloured, not previously used and not dark.
With "Kaṅkato na kaṅkataḥ..." [he should groom him] with a comb; with "Indrāviśva..." with a comb; with turban-cloth on the head, counting, collyrium, an ornament, […] with an arrangement of himself, with combing the beard; with "Puṣpavatī..." with flowers strung together and unstrung.
With "Prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ...", with fragrant powder.
With "Agni-mūrdhā...", with a lamp.
With "Dhūr asi dhūrva...", with incense.
With "Abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ...", with a parasol.
With the Viṣṇu-gāyatrī, with two sandals.
With "Idaṃ viṣṇur vicakrame...", with a carriage; with the same [mantra], with a covered litter.
With "Ketuṃ kṛṇvan...", with banners; with the same [mantra], with flags and the like.
Then he should praise the holy Lord with hymns.
Then with "Agnir mūrdhā...", with an offering for completing all enjoyments.
Then with stringed instruments, then with the sounds of conches, kettle-drums, and large drums, with "Subhagaṃ teneva...".
Having worshipped Janārdana with enjoyments according to this rule,
he obtains all desires and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

3.113
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Next, he should worship the holy Lord with the honey-mixture.
With "Hiraṇyavarṇā...", he should give the reverential offering.
With "Dadhikrāvṇā...", curds.
With "Ghṛtavatī...", clarified butter.
With "Madhu vātā ṛtāyate...", honey.
Having combined them with the three-gold [mantra], he should offer it with the Sāvitra [mantra].
With "Āpo hi ṣṭhā...", he should give water for satisfaction.
With "Vāta ā vātu bheṣajam...", wiping [the lips].
With "Śan no āpaḥ...", water for sipping.
According to the rule of the aṣṭakā, an animal, or a measure with "Hiraṇyavarṇā...".
With that, he should present auspicious items such as the disc, conch, and lotus.
This rule of the honey-mixture has thus been told to you by me, sinless one.
Having performed this, O great king, he is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu.

text_mt:
3.114
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
With "Hiraṇyavarṇā...", he should give the reverential offering.
Then, with the Sāvitra [mantra], he should offer food together with solid edibles, side dishes, sauces, savouries, and fruits.
According to his ability, he should worship the holy Lord with fragrant and very savoury water-drinks, with satisfaction by "Āpo hi ṣṭhā...", with wiping [the lips] by "Vāta ā vātu bheṣajam...", with sipping water by "Śan no āpaḥ...", again with this same procedure by "Agnir mūrdhā...", and with a subordinate sacrifice for the purpose of distribution.
With "Mukhād indraś ca...", he should offer betel.
With the same [mantra], fragrant mouth-perfumes; with the same, a mirror.
Once more, he should worship the holy Lord with songs, instruments, and dances.
Having worshipped the eternal God of gods with the food-sacrifice,
he obtains all desires and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

text_mt:
3.115
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then, according to the procedure declared in the song of Śaṅkara, he should perform worship in the Sāttvata manner.
And the patron should honour the Pure One with enjoyments.
In front of the deity itself, he should give to each of the officiating priests a large quantity of gold, a garment, and a bell-metal vessel made with a cow and calf.
And he should honour them according to his capacity.
Then he should feed the brahmins.
And as they eat, he should cause the greatness of the holy Lord to be recited.
Then the sacrificer should eat sacrificial food.
Then he should remain in the temple listening to songs, dances, musical instruments, and sacred texts.
Having performed the installation of the Bow-bearing Lord by this rule, a man
obtains all desires and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Sāttvata Worship', in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.

text_mt:
3.116
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
According to the Vedic rule of sacrifice and with the homa prescribed in the Sāttvata view, he should perform worship every day for seven days.
Then on the seventh day, having performed the great ablution, the ritual expert, pot in hand, should sprinkle the archways with the hymn, "The herbs that...".
He should worship with ointment reciting, "By the door of fragrance...";
with flowers reciting, "Possessing flowers...";
with a lamp reciting, "Agni is the head...";
with incense reciting, "You are the yoke-pin...";
[and] with food-offerings reciting the Sāvitra hymns beginning with "Of Savitṛ...".
Then he should lift up the archways with the Śrī-Viṣṇu-Gāyatrī: first in the northeast, then in the east, then in the south, [and then] in the west.
All these priests, taking the archways, should go to a river mounted on elephants, mounted on horse-drawn chariots, mounted on ox-carts, or carried in palanquins.
And there they should cast them in with the mantra, "May Indra grant us well-being...".
With the mantra, "May we hear with our ears what is auspicious...", they should proceed to the temple of the deity, and with the mantra, "And the Lord who is here...", they should enter.
Then they should wait upon the holy Lord by every rite prescribed for installation, preceded by the rule of offerings.
Then, when the brahmins have eaten, he should untie the tied initiation-cord of the sacrificer with the mantra, "I release you...".
And he should make protection with the armour mantra.
Excluding the removal of the archways, he should perform month by month the rite taught for the seven days.
For up to a year [this] rite should be performed regularly; in this manner, it grants all desires.
This procedure for installation has thus been spoken to you by me, O best of earthly kings;
it is to be known as taking away all evil, granting long life, and unconquered.
Having performed the installation of the Bow-Wielder according to this rule, a man
obtains all desires and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
Herbs, wind, trees, whatever is employed
in the installation, all that indeed is magnified in the world of Viṣṇu.
Those who even behold an installation being performed, O king of men,
and the devotees who rejoice in it, those men also attain heaven.
According to the rule spoken by the Sāttvatas, one should always worship
the Lord of the gods of gods, once installed, if he desires the eternal abode.

text_mt:
3.117
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now begins the rule for the festival procession of the god.
Whatever lunar day is stated as belonging to whichever god, on that lunar day one should perform his procession.
If one does not know his lunar day, one should perform it on the full moon.
To the holy Blessed Lord Vāsudeva belong all lunar days; there is no single lunar day for him. There, at the very beginning, having made the temple white with lime and well painted, on an auspicious day one should perform worship of Vināyaka.
On the second day, worship of the planets and lunar mansions; on the third day, worship of the serpents;
on the fourth day, worship of the Pramathas;
on the fifth day, worship of brahmins and gifts to the poor and helpless; and on the sixth day, the ablution.
There, having performed the great ablution, all the city folk, wearing very white clothes and with hands purified by darbha-grass, should go, amidst the great sound of musical instruments and graceful dancing, to the nearest reservoir, river, spring, or pavilion adjacent to the city. Taking water jars from there, carried on the back of an elephant and covered with a beautiful cloth, one should bring them in.
Having brought them in, one should bathe the holy Blessed Lord, worship him according to the rule of ritual offerings and the injunctions for consecration, and venerate the holy Blessed Lord with dance, instrumental music, and song. Then, when the day of the procession arrives, having secured the small ritual image called the pratimā on a chariot with an attractive pavilion, covered with various fabrics, equipped with small bells, and adorned with gems, garlands, and banners, one should have it paraded around the city by trained horses or strong men.
The citizens, well dressed and holding only bows in hand, should process before the pavilion.
Others should scatter flower garlands.
And they should sing praises.
Bards and panegyrists chanting blessings should walk in front.
Playing musical instruments and accompanied by an army of four divisions, the king should follow behind.
Or the city prefect, or the official in charge, seated on the back of an elephant, should follow with the royal astrologer and observe the portents.
If the banner breaks without wind, one should foretell the death of kings.
If the parasol breaks, destruction of the countryside [is portended].
If the axle breaks, death of the king’s wife.
If the rope snaps, afflictions to children.
If a horse, a steer, or a man perishes, distress to the countryside; if the support frame breaks, distress to the king's mother.
If the image breaks or falls, destruction of the people; if the entire pavilion collapses, destruction of the kingdom along with its king; if musical instruments go out of tune, the arrival of a hostile army; if a beast of prey settles on the flag, fear of battle.
If the populace is indifferent, fear of famine.
Whatever auspicious deed children perform under an auspicious asterism, it turns out just so.
And whatever happiness or sorrow a man experiences on that day,
such is to be known for him throughout the year.
Therefore, on that day, a citizen should be well fed, well clothed, and distinguished.
Having thus paraded through the city and recognized the omens, when the ritual image has re-entered [the temple], one should hold a great festival.
Beginning on the second day, according to one's means, one should daily give wealth to actors, male and female dancers, wrestlers, magicians, and others after witnessing spectacles.
At the time of the spectacle, one should honor the spectators by giving garlands, betel, unguents, and the like.
For the invisible spirits among the spectators, one should scatter food and water, fruits, flowers, and cakes of crushed sesamum and sweetmeats in all directions and intermediate directions around the stage and surroundings.
And one should say to the departing spectators, “May there be welfare!”
And one should say, “May the spectators who have arrived see the coming procession!”
If inauspicious portents arise, one should duly perform the procession again by this rule to appease them.
He who performs the procession in the temple of a deity according to this rule
attains all desires and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
Conferring fortune, fame, and longevity, granting victory to kings,
and beneficial to the citizens is the ritual of the procession declared to be.
For the satisfaction of the rulers of the gods, and for the welfare of the city
and its people, O king, the ritual of the procession that brings victory must be performed.
It is declared to cause copious rain and to destroy drought.
This ritual of procession must always be performed in the deity’s abode
every year, O king, by a king desiring victory.

Vajra said: / When what undertaking has arrived, which form should one worship, / seeking the success of his undertaking? Tell me that, O great sage.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / On a journey by boat upon the ocean, one should worship the all-pervading Matsya, / or Varāha, O highly fortunate one; likewise when crossing a river.
At the beginning of study, a man should worship Hayagrīva; / and at the time of a journey, he should worship the god Trivikrama.
When the time for marriage has arrived, O king, one should worship Pradyumna; / and in all sacraments, one should worship Dattātreya.
At the beginning of a poem, one should [worship] Vālmīki and Vyāsa; / and at a royal consecration, the king should worship Mṛtyu and Vainya.

Necessarily, in litigation, in battle, or indeed in gambling, / or at the beginning of agricultural work, one should worship the god Varāha;
or else, O great king, the all-pervading god Saṃkarṣaṇa. / One should worship Nṛsiṃha when undertaking the destruction of enemies,
Rāma, either the descendant of Bhṛgu or the descendant of Raghu, in fulfilling a vow; / and at the beginning of [administering] medicine, Kūrma or [the god in] female form.
At the commencement of a pilgrimage to sacred fords, one should worship the all-pervading Haṃsa; / likewise, at the commencement of trade, the one who has Garuḍa on his banner.
At the commencement of artistic craft, one should worship the Universal Form; / and at the commencement of austerity, both Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
Likewise, upon entering a new house, [one should worship] the all-pervading god reclining on the serpent; / and one should worship the god Dharma when initiating righteous deeds.
One should worship Varāha at a funeral offering, in a sacrifice, [or in rites against] Dānavas; / amid [threats of] wild beasts, elephants, and impassable places, and amid fears of enemies and thieves,
one should worship Narasiṃha, who destroys all afflictions. / O knower of dharma, one may also worship the form chosen according to one's wish in all undertakings.

Worshipped by those who have desires, O Vajra, the best of gods grants the desired wish; / and abiding as desired in all images, he brings about liberation for those who are free from desires.
Vajra said: / At what time should one worship which manifestation of the god? / Dispel this doubt of mine, O increaser of the lineage of Bhṛgu.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hayagrīva, Nṛvarāha, Narasiṃha, Vāmana, / and Trivikrama, O knower of dharma, one should worship in the five years [of the lustrum].
One should worship Vāsudeva and the plough-holder in the two solstices; / and the lord Pradyumna, Aniruddha, and the one reclining on the serpent-coils,
Padmanābha, the son of Daśaratha, and Rāma, descendant of Bhṛgu,
one should worship, O knower of dharma, in order in the seasons beginning with spring. / Likewise, the deliverer of Gajendra, Pṛthu, and Vālmīki,
Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa, Nara, and Nara and Nārāyaṇa, / Rāma, Rāma, likewise Rāma, and Hari, in order in [the months] beginning with Caitra.

Vahni, Prajāpati, Soma, Rudra, and likewise the one in female form, / Vyāsa, Śeṣa, Varāha, Pradyumna, and Arjuna, O king,
Āditya, Viśvakarman, Cakra, the god Nṛkesarin, / Garuḍa, Puruhūta, Kapila, and Padma,
the Universal Form, Brahmā, and likewise the god Trivikrama, / [the protector] of cattle, Kūrma, Nara, and likewise Nārāyaṇa, Hari, / Rāma, and boon-granting Kṛṣṇa, one should worship in [the lunar mansions] beginning with Kṛttikā. / Hayagrīva, Nṛvarāha, and likewise the god Trivikrama,
Kapila, the one reclining on the serpent, Varāha, and Matsya, / Rāma and Rāma, O knower of dharma, Kūrma, and Haṃsa, O Yādava,
Pradyumna, Baladeva, and Varāha: in this order / one should worship in sequence on the lunar days beginning with the first.
Or one may worship at all times the god dwelling in any form one wishes, / since for that teacher of the universe of great power, every [day] is his day.

Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Through 'Vāsudeva', 'Acyuta', 'Ananta', 'Satya', 'Aja', 'Puruṣottama', / and through 'Paramātman', 'Īśvara', and so forth, he grants liberation thereafter. [2]
'Knower of dharma', 'Maker of dharma', 'Righteous', 'Self of the universe', 'Maker of the universe', 'Pure', / 'Possessing purity', 'Viṣṇu', named 'Lotus', named 'Puṣkara', and indeed 'Adhokṣaja', [3]

attains great dharma and the destruction of the bondage of sins. / 'Bestower of prosperity', 'Lord of prosperity', 'Abode of prosperity', 'Bearer of prosperity', 'Dwelling of prosperity', [5]
'Husband of Śrī', 'Supreme Śrī', 'Possessor of prosperity', 'Marked by the Śrīvatsa', / 'Nṛsiṃha', 'Subduer of the wicked', 'Victory', 'Viṣṇu', 'Trivikrama'— [6]

text_mt:
For all his names, O king, bestow all desires; / whichever one recites according to one's capacity, from that he indeed obtains the fulfillment of desire. [14]
Vajra said: / And at the beginning of an undertaking, which name should one recite, O twice-born? / Dispel this doubt of mine, for you know everything! [1]
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Desiring safety when traveling away from home, O king, one should remember / the wielder of the discus, the ploughman, the wielder of the bow Śārṅga, and the sword-bearer in the directions beginning with the east. [2]
The worshiped, the superior, the all, the sovereign lord, the master— / the Cosmic Person one should always remember with devotion in daily undertakings. [3]
One should remember the Tortoise, the Boar, and the Fish when crossing waters; / when lighting a fire, one should murmur, unwearied, 'the Radiant One', and 'Rāma'. [4]
Going toward battle, one should remember the Unconquered; / likewise, for [wealth equal to] a lotus-treasure, one should murmur 'Keśava', and 'Lotus-eyed'. [5]
In all eye afflictions, one should likewise [murmur] 'Hṛṣīkeśa'; / and in the application of medicine, one should murmur 'Acyuta' and 'Amṛta'. [6]

From the remembrance of the Garuḍa-bannered one, a man is freed from distress; / the potency of fever, vicious headache, and poison is pacified. [7]
During afflictions from planets and asterisms, in attacks from spirits and in wild forests, / in ambushes by robbers and enemies, in dangers from tigers, lions, and the like, [8]
and in thick darkness, one should recite 'Narasiṃha'. / At the time of depositing wealth and likewise of storing grain, [9]
becoming focused on him, one should recite 'Ananta' and 'Acyuta'. / 'Nārāyaṇa', 'Wielder of the bow Śārṅga', 'Bearer of prosperity', 'Liberator of the elephant', [10]
'Vāmana', and 'Sword-bearer' one should remember in bad dreams. / When a conflagration breaks out, one should remember the one lying on the waters. [11]
One should remember Balabhadra for prosperity; at the start of plowing, the Plough-weaponed one; / one desirous of trade, 'the Deliverer'; in times of prosperity, 'the Lord of prosperity', O king. [12]
In auspicious events, one should recite 'Auspicious Viṣṇu'; in inauspicious events, [Viṣṇu]; / when portents are averted, and at remaining times, one should murmur [him] as 'Free of sorrow'. [13]
Rising, a man should recite 'Viṣṇu'; falling asleep, 'Mādhava'; / at meals, 'Govinda'; everywhere, 'Madhusūdana'; [14]

text_mt:
For all his names, O king, accomplish all purposes for a person; / therefore, with devotion, one should murmur indeed any desired name of the god in all undertakings. [17]
Vajra said: / But at what time should one recite which particular name of the god? / Dispel this doubt of mine, for you know everything! [1]
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Cosmic Person, Vāmadeva, and the lord Saṃkarṣaṇa,
Pradyumna, and Aniruddha should be successively avoided in sounds.
Viṣṇu, the Slayer of Madhu, and likewise the god Trivikrama,
Vāmana, Śrīdhara, and likewise Hṛṣīkeśa,
Dāmodara, Padmanābha, and Keśava, O best of the Yadus,
Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, and Govinda, in successive order,
in the months beginning with Caitra one should recall the God of gods;
and Pradyumna and Aniruddha in the bright and dark fortnights.
Sarva, Śarva, Śiva, Sthāṇu, the imperishable storehouse of beings—
on the days of the week beginning with Sunday, one should recall the god in this order.

tasmātsadā sarvagatasya nāma grāhyaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ varadasya rājan .. 13 ..
meaning:
विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कारो भूतभव्यभवः प्रभुः..
भूतकृत् भूतभृद्भावो भूतात्मा भूतभावनः..7..
अव्यक्तः पुंडरीकाक्षो विश्वकर्मा शुचिश्रवाः ..
सम्भवो भावनो भर्ता प्रभवः प्रभुरीश्वरः .. 8 ..
अप्रमेयो हृषीकेशः पद्मनाभः परः प्रभुः ..
अग्राह्यः शाश्वतो धाता कृष्णश्चैतान्यनुस्मरेत्..9..
देवदेवस्य नामानि कृत्तिकादिषु यादव ..
ब्रह्माणं श्रीपतिं विष्णुं कपिलं श्रीधरं प्रभुम् .. 3.124.10 ..
दामोदरं हृषीकेशं गोविन्दं मधुसूदनम् ..
भूधरं गदिनं चैव शिखिनं पद्मिनं तथा .. 11 ..
चक्रिणं च महाराज प्रथमादिषु संस्मरेत् ..
सर्वं वा सर्वदा राम देवदेवस्य यादव .. 12 ..
नामानि सर्वाणि जनार्दनस्य कालश्च सर्वः पुरुषप्रवीर ..
तस्मात्सदा सर्वगतस्य नाम ग्राह्यं यथेष्टं वरदस्य राजन् .. 13 ..
text_mt:
Viśva, Viṣṇu, the Vaṣaṭ call, the sovereign of past, future, and present,
the maker of beings, the bearer of beings, existence, the self of beings, the source of beings,
the unmanifest, the lotus-eyed, the all-maker, of pure fame,
the origin, the producer, the sustainer, the source, the lord, the master,
the immeasurable, Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha, the supreme lord,
the ungraspable, the eternal, the creator, and Kṛṣṇa—one should recall these,
the names of the God of gods, in the asterisms beginning with Kṛttikā, O Yādava:
Brahmā, Śrīpati, Viṣṇu, Kapila, the lord Śrīdhara,
Dāmodara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Govinda, the Slayer of Madhu,
the Bearer of the Earth, the Wielder of the Mace, the Crested, and the Lotus-bearer,
and the Wielder of the Discus, O great king, one should recall on the lunar days beginning with the first;
or [recall] everything at all times, O Rama, of the God of gods, O Yādava.
All times are for Janārdana's names, O hero among men;
therefore, at all times the name of the all-pervading giver of boons may be taken as desired, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
3.125
vajra uvāca ..
kasminkṣetre tu devasya kiṃkiṃ nāma prakīrtayet ..
etanme saṃśayaṃ chindhi bhṛguvaṃśavivardhana .. 1 ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam..
vāsudevasya saṃvādamarjunasya ca yādava .. 2 ..
vṛtte bhāratasaṃgrāme rājyaṃ prāpte yudhiṣṭhire.
asminneva sabhoddeśe vijahrāte yathāsukham ..3..
vāsudevārjunau vīrau lakṣīkṛtavasundharau ..
tataḥ kathānte kasmiṃścitkṛṣṇaṃ papraccha phālgunaḥ .. 4 ..
arjuna uvāca ..
kṣetreṣu yeṣuyeṣu tvaṃ kīrtanīyo mayācyuta ..
cetasā praṇidhānārthaṃ tvaṃ mamākhyātumarhasi .. 5 ..
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
sarvagaḥ sarvabhūto'haṃ na hi kiñcinmayā vinā ..
carācare jagatyasminvidyate kurusattama .. 6 ..
tathāpi yeṣu sthāneṣu cintanīyohamarjuna ..
stotavyo nāmabhiryaiśca śṛṇu tvaṃ tadvadāmi te .. 7 ..
meaning:
3.125
वज्र उवाच ..
कस्मिन्क्षेत्रे तु देवस्य किंकिं नाम प्रकीर्तयेत् ..
एतन्मे संशयं छिन्धि भृगुवंशविवर्धन .. 1 ..
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्..
वासुदेवस्य संवादमर्जुनस्य च यादव .. 2 ..
वृत्ते भारतसंग्रामे राज्यं प्राप्ते युधिष्ठिरे.
अस्मिन्नेव सभोद्देशे विजह्राते यथासुखम् ..3..
वासुदेवार्जुनौ वीरौ लक्षीकृतवसुन्धरौ ..
ततः कथान्ते कस्मिंश्चित्कृष्णं पप्रच्छ फाल्गुनः .. 4 ..
अर्जुन उवाच ..
क्षेत्रेषु येषुयेषु त्वं कीर्तनीयो मयाच्युत ..
चेतसा प्रणिधानार्थं त्वं ममाख्यातुमर्हसि .. 5 ..
श्रीभगवानुवाच ..
सर्वगः सर्वभूतोऽहं न हि किञ्चिन्मया विना ..
चराचरे जगत्यस्मिन्विद्यते कुरुसत्तम .. 6 ..
तथापि येषु स्थानेषु चिन्तनीयोहमर्जुन ..
स्तोतव्यो नामभिर्यैश्च शृणु त्वं तद्वदामि ते .. 7 ..
text_mt:
Vajra said:
In which sacred place should what name of the god be proclaimed?
Dispel this doubt of mine, O enhancer of the Bhṛgu lineage.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In this regard too they cite this ancient history,
the dialogue between Vāsudeva and Arjuna, O Yādava.
When the Bhārata war was concluded and Yudhiṣṭhira had attained the kingdom,
in this very area of the assembly hall they strolled at their pleasure,
Vāsudeva and Arjuna, the two heroes, having made the earth their aim.
Then, at the end of a certain conversation, Arjuna asked Kṛṣṇa.
Arjuna said:
In which sacred places are you to be proclaimed by me, O Acyuta?
For the sake of mental concentration, you ought to tell me.
The Blessed One said:
I am all-pervading, the self of all beings; indeed, nothing exists
without me in this moving and unmoving world, O best of the Kurus.
Even so, in which places I am to be contemplated, O Arjuna,
and with which names I am to be praised, hear that; I shall tell it to you.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkare puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ gayāyāṃ ca gadādharam ..
lohadaṇḍe tathā viṣṇuṃ stuvaṃstarati duṣkṛtam .. 8 ..
rāghavaṃ citrakūṭe tu prabhāse daityasūdanam ..
vṛndāvane ca govindaṃ māṃ stuvanpuṇyabhāgbhavet .. 9 ..
jayaṃ jayantyāṃ stunvaṃśca jayantaṃ hastināpure ..
varāhaṃ kandamāle ca kaśmīreṣu ca cakriṇam .. 3.125.10 ..
janārdanastu kubjāmre mathurāyāṃ ca keśavam ..
śrīkubje śrīdharaṃ tadvadgaṅgādvāre surottamam .. 11 ..
śāligrāme mahāyogyaṃ hariṃ govardhanācale ..
piṇḍārake caturbāhuṃ śaṃkhadvāre ca śaṃkhinam .. 12 ..
vāmanaṃ tu kurukṣetre yamunāyāṃ trivikramam ..
viśveśvaraṃ tathā śoṇe kapilaṃ pūrvasāgare .. 13 ..
śvetadvīpapatiṃ cāpi gaṅgāsāgarasaṃgame ..
bhūdharaṃ devikātīre prayāge yogaśāyinam .. 14 ..
meaning:
पुष्करे पुण्डरीकाक्षं गयायां च गदाधरम् ..
लोहदण्डे तथा विष्णुं स्तुवंस्तरति दुष्कृतम् .. 8 ..
राघवं चित्रकूटे तु प्रभासे दैत्यसूदनम् ..
वृन्दावने च गोविन्दं मां स्तुवन्पुण्यभाग्भवेत् .. 9 ..
जयं जयन्त्यां स्तुन्वंश्च जयन्तं हस्तिनापुरे ..
वराहं कन्दमाले च कश्मीरेषु च चक्रिणम् .. 3.125.10 ..
जनार्दनस्तु कुब्जाम्रे मथुरायां च केशवम् ..
श्रीकुब्जे श्रीधरं तद्वद्गङ्गाद्वारे सुरोत्तमम् .. 11 ..
शालिग्रामे महायोग्यं हरिं गोवर्धनाचले ..
पिण्डारके चतुर्बाहुं शंखद्वारे च शंखिनम् .. 12 ..
वामनं तु कुरुक्षेत्रे यमुनायां त्रिविक्रमम् ..
विश्वेश्वरं तथा शोणे कपिलं पूर्वसागरे .. 13 ..
श्वेतद्वीपपतिं चापि गङ्गासागरसंगमे ..
भूधरं देविकातीरे प्रयागे योगशायिनम् .. 14 ..

sanskrit_iast:
naranāraṇāyākhyau ca tathā badarikāśrame ..
samudre dakṣiṇe nāma padmanābheti phālguna .. 15 ..
dvārakāyāṃ tathā kṛṣṇaṃ stuvaṃstarati durgatim ..
evaṃ rāmaṃ mahendrādrau hṛṣīkeśaṃ tathā budha .. 16 ..
aśvatīrthe hayagrīvaṃ viśvarūpaṃ himācale ..
nṛsiṃhaṃ kṛtaśauce tu vipāśāyāṃ dvijapriyam .. 17 ..
meaning:
नरनारणायाख्यौ च तथा बदरिकाश्रमे ..
समुद्रे दक्षिणे नाम पद्मनाभेति फाल्गुन .. 15 ..
द्वारकायां तथा कृष्णं स्तुवंस्तरति दुर्गतिम् ..
एवं रामं महेन्द्राद्रौ हृषीकेशं तथा बुध .. 16 ..
अश्वतीर्थे हयग्रीवं विश्वरूपं हिमाचले ..
नृसिंहं कृतशौचे तु विपाशायां द्विजप्रियम् .. 17 ..

sanskrit_iast:
naimiṣe yajñapuruṣaṃ jambumāle tathācyutam ..
anantaṃ saindhavāraṇye daṇḍake śārṅgadhāriṇam .. 18 ..
meaning:
नैमिषे यज्ञपुरुषं जम्बुमाले तथाच्युतम् ..
अनन्तं सैन्धवारण्ये दण्डके शार्ङ्गधारिणम् .. 18 ..
text_mt:
the Sacrifice-Person at Naimiṣa, and likewise Acyuta at Jambumāla,
Ananta in the Saindhava forest, and the Bearer of the Śārṅga Bow in Daṇḍaka;

sanskrit_iast:
utpalāvartake śauriṃ narmadāyāṃ śriyaḥ patim ..
dāmodaraṃ raivatake nandāyāṃ jalaśāyinam .. 19 ..
meaning:
उत्पलावर्तके शौरिं नर्मदायां श्रियः पतिम् ..
दामोदरं रैवतके नन्दायां जलशायिनम् .. 19 ..
text_mt:
Śauri at Utpalāvartaka, the Lord of Śrī on the Narmadā,
Dāmodara on Raivataka, and the One Sleeping on the Waters at Nandā;

sanskrit_iast:
sarvayogeśvaraṃ caiva sindhusāgarasaṃgame ..
sahyādrau devadeveśaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ mādhave vane ..3.125.20 ..
meaning:
सर्वयोगेश्वरं चैव सिन्धुसागरसंगमे ..
सह्याद्रौ देवदेवेशं वैकुण्ठं माधवे वने ..3.125.20 ..
text_mt:
and the Master of all Yoga at the confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean,
the Sovereign of the God of gods on the Sahya mountain, Vaikuṇṭha in the grove of Mādhava;

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpaharaṃ viṃdhye coḍreṣu puruṣottamam ..
hradaye cāpi kaunteya paramātmā sanātanaḥ .. 21 ..
meaning:
सर्वपापहरं विंध्ये चोड्रेषु पुरुषोत्तमम् ..
ह्रदये चापि कौन्तेय परमात्मा सनातनः .. 21 ..
text_mt:
the Remover of all Sins in the Vindhya, and Puruṣottama in the Oḍra lands;
and in the heart, O son of Kuntī, the eternal Supreme Self.

sanskrit_iast:
vaṭevaṭe vaiśravaṇaṃ catvarecatvare śivam ..
parvateparvate rāmaṃ sarvatra madhusūdanam .. 22 ..
meaning:
वटेवटे वैश्रवणं चत्वरेचत्वरे शिवम् ..
पर्वतेपर्वते रामं सर्वत्र मधुसूदनम् .. 22 ..
text_mt:
At every banyan tree [recall] Vaiśravaṇa, at every crossroads Śiva,
on every mountain Rāma, and everywhere the Slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit_iast:
naraṃ bhūmau tathā vyomni kaunteya garuḍadhvajam ..
vāsudevaṃ ca sarvatra saṃsmarejjyotiṣāṃ patim .. 23 ..
meaning:
नरं भूमौ तथा व्योम्नि कौन्तेय गरुडध्वजम् ..
वासुदेवं च सर्वत्र संस्मरेज्ज्योतिषां पतिम् .. 23 ..
text_mt:
Recall Nara on the earth, and in the sky the Garuḍa-bannered one, O son of Kuntī;
and everywhere recall Vāsudeva, the Lord of the Luminaries.

sanskrit_iast:
arcayanpraṇamanstunvansaṃsmareśca dhanañjaya ..
eteṣvetāni nāmāni naraḥ pāpātpramucyate .. 24 ..
meaning:
अर्चयन्प्रणमन्स्तुन्वन्संस्मरेश्च धनञ्जय ..
एतेष्वेतानि नामानि नरः पापात्प्रमुच्यते .. 24 ..
text_mt:
Worshipping, bowing, praising, and recollecting these names in these [places],
O Dhanañjaya, a person is freed from sin.

sanskrit_iast:
sthāneṣveteṣu mannāmnāmeteṣāṃ prīṇayennaraḥ ..
dvijānāṃ prīṇanaṃ kṛtvā svargaloke mahīyate .. 25 ..
meaning:
स्थानेष्वेतेषु मन्नाम्नामेतेषां प्रीणयेन्नरः ..
द्विजानां प्रीणनं कृत्वा स्वर्गलोके महीयते .. 25 ..
text_mt:
If a man pleases [the god] in these places with these names of mine,
and brings pleasure to the twice-born, he is honoured in the world of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
nāmānyetāni kaunteya sthānānyetāni cātmavān ..
japanvai pañca pañcāśattrisandhyaṃ matparāyaṇāḥ .. 26 ..
meaning:
नामान्येतानि कौन्तेय स्थानान्येतानि चात्मवान् ..
जपन्वै पञ्च पञ्चाशत्त्रिसन्ध्यं मत्परायणाः .. 26 ..
text_mt:
A self-controlled person devoted to me who recites these names
and these fifty-five places at the three junctures of the day, O son of Kuntī,

sanskrit_iast:
trīṇi janmāni yatpāpaṃ cāvasthātritaye kṛtam ..
tatkṣālayatyasandigdhaṃ jāyate ca satāṃ kule .. 27 ..
meaning:
त्रीणि जन्मानि यत्पापं चावस्थात्रितये कृतम् ..
तत्क्षालयत्यसन्दिग्धं जायते च सतां कुले .. 27 ..
text_mt:
undoubtedly washes away the sin committed across three lifetimes
and in the three stages of life, and is born in a family of the virtuous.

sanskrit_iast:
dvikālaṃ vā japanvaitaddivārātrau ca yatkṛtam ..
tasmādvimucyate pāpātsaṃstuvanparamo naraḥ .. 28 ..
meaning:
द्विकालं वा जपन्वैतद्दिवारात्रौ च यत्कृतम् ..
तस्माद्विमुच्यते पापात्संस्तुवन्परमो नरः .. 28 ..
text_mt:
Or reciting this at the two twilight periods, the supreme person, offering praise,
is freed from the sin that was committed by day and by night.

sanskrit_iast:
japtānyetāni kaunteya sakṛcchraddhāsamanvitam ..
mocayanti naraṃ pāpādyattatraiva dine kṛtam .. 29 ..
meaning:
जप्तान्येतानि कौन्तेय सकृच्छ्रद्धासमन्वितम् ..
मोचयन्ति नरं पापाद्यत्तत्रैव दिने कृतम् .. 29 ..
text_mt:
Recited but once with faith, O son of Kuntī,
these [names] free a person from the sin committed on that very day.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanyo yaśasyaḥ śatrughno jayaḥ kurukulodvaha ..
grahānukūlatāṃ caiva karotyāśu na saṃśayaḥ .. 3.125.30..
meaning:
धन्यो यशस्यः शत्रुघ्नो जयः कुरुकुलोद्वह ..
ग्रहानुकूलतां चैव करोत्याशु न संशयः .. 3.125.30..
text_mt:
It brings fortune, brings fame, destroys enemies, and grants victory, O upholder of the Kuru line;
and it quickly brings the favour of the planets, without a doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
upoṣitāśca manasaḥ sthāneṣveteṣu mānavaḥ ..
kṛtāyatanavāsaśca prāpnotyabhimataṃ phalam .. 31 ..
meaning:
उपोषिताश्च मनसः स्थानेष्वेतेषु मानवः ..
कृतायतनवासश्च प्राप्नोत्यभिमतं फलम् .. 31 ..
text_mt: And having fasted in thought, a man dwelling in these sacred sites, / having made his residence in the sanctuary, obtains the desired fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
utkrāntirapyaśeṣeṣu sthāneṣveteṣu śasyate ..
anyasthānācchataguṇameteṣvanaśanādikam .. 32 .. ..
meaning:
उत्क्रान्तिरप्यशेषेषु स्थानेष्वेतेषु शस्यते ..
अन्यस्थानाच्छतगुणमेतेष्वनशनादिकम् .. 32 .. ..
text_mt: Departure from the body as well is praised in all these places; / fasting unto death and the like in these yields a hundred times more than in other places.

sanskrit_iast:
yastu matparamaḥ kālaṃ karotyeteṣu mānavaḥ..
devānāmapi pūjyo'sau mama loke mahīyate..33..
meaning:
यस्तु मत्परमः कालं करोत्येतेषु मानवः..
देवानामपि पूज्योऽसौ मम लोके महीयते..33..
text_mt: Moreover, a man who, devoted solely to Me, meets his end in these [places] / is worthy of worship even to the gods and is exalted in My world.

sanskrit_iast:
sthāneṣvathaiteṣu ca ye vasanti saṃpūjayante mama sarvakālam ..
tadeha cānte tridivaṃ prayānti nākaṃ ca lokaṃ samavāpnuvanti..34..
meaning:
स्थानेष्वथैतेषु च ये वसन्ति संपूजयन्ते मम सर्वकालम् ..
तदेह चान्ते त्रिदिवं प्रयान्ति नाकं च लोकं समवाप्नुवन्ति..34..
text_mt: And those who dwell in these sacred sites and worship Me at all times, / having left their bodies here, go to the third heaven and attain the heavenly realm.

sanskrit_iast:
3.126
.. vajra uvāca .. ..
nāmnāṃ saṃpūjanaṃ viṣṇostvayā kāryaṃ prakīrtitam..
prādurbhāveṣu kāmyaṃ ca pūjanaṃ ca tvayeritam .. 1 ..
meaning:
3.126
.. वज्र उवाच .. ..
नाम्नां संपूजनं विष्णोस्त्वया कार्यं प्रकीर्तितम्..
प्रादुर्भावेषु काम्यं च पूजनं च त्वयेरितम् .. 1 ..
text_mt: Vajra said: / The worship of Viṣṇu's names has been proclaimed by you as an obligatory duty; / and the worship regarding desires in His manifestations has also been stated by you.

A king who performs this observance becomes a knower of the Vedas on earth, constantly devoted to dharma; / having performed it for twelve years, a person goes to the world of the Ordainer [Brahmā].
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / I shall declare to you, O Yādava, the worship of that threefold deity, / the second of Viṣṇu of boundless valour, O crusher of foes.
Brahmā's form is made of rajas, setting the realms in motion; / the Vaiṣṇava form is known as sattva, sustaining the world;
and the form of Rudra is known as tamas, causing dissolution. / On the first lunar day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, a man should worship Brahmā
with an abundance of scents, garlands, prostrations, incense, lamps, and food; / then he should offer milk into the sacrificial fire with mantras dedicated to Brahmā.
He should give an iron vessel filled with milk, along with gold, to a twice-born; / and when the sun has reached midday, he should take a meal of curds.
He should also sleep in a place covered with kuśa grass, dressed in a single garment. / Then on the fourth day, he should perform a thorough bath

Then on the third day, O king, worship of Rudra should be performed / with scents, garlands, prostrations, incense, and lamps likewise; / an oblation of clarified butter is prescribed with the mantra 'Mā nastoke'.
An iron vessel filled with clarified butter, along with gold and a sacrificial fee [is to be given]; / and in the third part of the day, he should subsist on air alone.
Likewise, he should offer the three sweet substances and eat that as food. / Having performed this observance month after month for three days, / in the course of a year, O knower of dharma, a man attains his desired destination.
Having attained human birth, he becomes free from disease, self-controlled, devoted to truth, and well-disciplined; / endowed with good fortune, beauty, and wealth, he becomes Śiva incarnate, bearing the burdens of the world.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / All this universe is traditionally remembered as one, as prakṛti and puruṣa. / At the beginning of the bright fortnight of Caitra, fasting and with senses subdued,

one should worship Viṣṇu as the Cosmic Person, either on land or in water, / with an abundance of scents, garlands, prostrations, incense, lamps, and food.
A man should recite the Puruṣasūkta while immersed in water; / and likewise, the wise man should offer a double handful of water for each eight [verses].
Likewise, O knower of dharma, flowers and fruits, O mighty-armed one; / he should offer incense along with food offerings, and recite that [hymn] according to his ability.
And he should offer oblations with clarified butter, and give gold to a twice-born; / and at night he should take nourishment with milk, O Bhārgava.
Having performed this regular observance unwearied for a year, / in both fortnights, O hero, he is freed from all sins.
Having attained the grace of Vāsudeva, the Lord of all, inconceivable, the Lord of all hosts, / the Lord of the worlds, he goes to the state of liberation where the famed perfected beings and sages go.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Both the Cosmic Person and primordial nature are declared to be the entire universe; / everything is likewise declared to be of the nature of fire and soma.

text_mt:
Vāsudeva and Lakṣmī are declared to be those two very principles; / and on the first day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, fasting and with senses subdued,
A man should worship the fire with the Puruṣasūkta, / granting abundance of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food.
And he should worship the boon-giving goddess Lakṣmī with water / and with the Śrīsūkta, O knower of dharma, as prescribed, O lord of men.
He should give both gold and silver to brahmins as a sacrificial fee. / The wise man should sustain his life with milk and with ghee.
Having performed this observance for a year, having fasted properly, / he is released from all sins and finds the means to liberation.
Or he obtains his desires: manifold and foremost worlds, the entire earth, / supreme beauty instead of ugliness, foremost fame, and foremost sons.
3.130 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The two Nāsayas are declared to be the physicians of the gods, the Aśvins; / they alone are proclaimed in the world as the sun and the lord of the stars, O king.

text_mt:
Because they delight in traveling by horse, they are called the Aśvins. / On the second day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, fasting, with senses subdued,
intent and pure, one should worship the two Nāsatyas, the physicians of the gods, / with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food.
Having fashioned their likenesses, a man should worship the two Nāsatyas; / then he should especially offer a garland of lamps to the two at night.
He should give both gold and silver to brahmins as a sacrificial fee. / Closing his two eyes, a man should remember Viṣṇu;
he becomes radiant with splendor and is endowed with sight. / He should sustain his life with curd mixed with ghee.
Having performed the eye-observance for twelve years, he becomes an acknowledged lord of the earth, / endowed with a handsome form, crushing the hosts of his enemies, delighting in dharma, foremost among the best of kings.

text_mt:
This observance is declared to be purifying, destroying enemies, / bestowing good fortune, and dispelling disease, O king, O foremost of the Yādava race; it should be performed diligently by a woman as well.
3.132 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Listen to me, O king, regarding the second day of the unempty bed, / fasting on which a woman never undergoes widowhood,
nor does a man ever suffer separation from his wife. / That lunar day is to be observed on the second day of the dark fortnight under the constellation Śravaṇa.
Upon a well-spread bed, O Bhārgava, one should worship / Viṣṇu and the goddess Lakṣmī with fruits, flowers, perfumes, and respectful offerings.
Then one should offer food-offerings, a lamp, and incense according to one's capacity. / Then, having worshipped the lord of gods, pure, one should recite this mantra:
"O bearer of the Śrīvatsa, O beloved of Śrī, O abode of Śrī, O lord of Śrī, O Acyuta, / let not my householdership, which yields dharma, wealth, and desire, come to ruin!
Let not the fires perish, let not the deities perish, / let not the ancestors perish away from me through a breach in marital union!

Free from widowhood, fortunate, free from disease, devoted to her husband, intent on dharma, virtuous, / endowed with beauty, free from fear, a woman becomes possessed of all good qualities.
3.133 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / On the third day of the bright fortnight, fasting, with senses subdued, / one should make three sacred diagrams separately with pigment.
A man should make a white sacred diagram in the southern part; / in the middle below, a red one; and in the north, a white one for Dhruva.
The three steps of Viṣṇu are to be worshipped in these sacred diagrams: / the first step on the ground, the second in the orb of the sun,
and the third in the divine Dhruva, he should worship, intent and pure, / with perfumes, garlands, and the like, according to the color-mark of the sacred diagram, O twice-born.
"Tad viṣṇoḥ paramam..." is prescribed as the mantra for the fire oblation; / and "To Trivikrama" [is the mantra] for a woman or a śūdra, O best of the twice-born.
He should offer into the fire the three combined: unbroken grains, sesame seeds, and ghee. / And according to his ability, he should give copper, silver, and gold as a sacrificial fee.

And he should feed an excellent brahmin a meal of three sweet substances,
and he should sustain his life that day with three cow-products.
Having done this for three years, at the end of the vow, having indeed given
a three-year-old cow to a brahmin, he obtains all desires.
On earth, likewise in the intermediate space, and in heaven, O best of men,
O slayer of foes, his movement becomes unimpeded
for three thousand years, going everywhere without hindrance.
He is released from mental, vocal, and bodily
all evil, O fortunate one; through that he is born a man
in a family rich in wealth, endowed with beauty and prosperity.
Free from disease, his every purpose accomplished, achieving the three aims of life,
having observed [this vow] for twelve years, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.

text_mt:
There too, he constantly beholds the boon-giver, the foremost, accompanied by Lakṣmī, the ancient Cosmic Person,
the unfailing, the all-pervading, the unfathomable, the eternal cause of the destruction of sorrow.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I will tell you the second vow of Trivikrama; listen.
The earth is the first step, and the intermediate space is the second;
and heaven is to be known as the third of the God of gods, the Discus-bearer.
Agni is declared the lord of the earth, and likewise next the intermediate space;
and Sūrya is the lord of heaven: that is the triad of steps of Viṣṇu.
Fasting on the third day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha, with senses conquered,
having bathed in the morning in well-water, a man should worship Agni
with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, obeisances, incense, lamps, and food.
Then, having bathed in river water when the sun has reached midday,
having performed the worship of Vāyu, he should give barley-groats to a twice-born.
And having bathed in lake water in the evening, he should worship Sūrya;
and then, restrained in speech and pure, he should eat sacrificial food at night.

text_mt:
Performing the vow thus for a year, unwearied, O king,
having concluded it in Vaiśākha, he should give a sacrificial fee to brahmins:
copper, silver, and gold—the three metals, O Yādava;
and a pair of garments along with a turban—and three garments,
a pair of sandals, and an umbrella—these three, with devotion.
Having performed this vow of Trivikrama for a year, a man
attains the fruit of a sacrifice abundant in all desires.
In a celestial aerial chariot having the color of the sun, adorned with a network of tiny bells,
filled with hosts of king-like gods, resounding with vīṇās and muraja drums,
food, longevity, and sons [are granted] when Garuḍadhvaja is pleased.
Having worshipped the three steps of him who stepped over the three worlds, O best among upholders of dharma,
men attain their desires and movement wherever they wish, O hero among men.
3.135
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
The vow of Trivikrama has been explained to you, O fortunate one.
Hear from me as I speak of the third, O tiger among kings.

In a celestial aerial chariot having the color of the sun, adorned with a network of tiny bells,
yoked with swans, divine, resounding with vīṇās and muraja drums,
filled with groups of choice apsarases, moving as he pleases, beautiful,

And having obtained birth in human state, he attains threefold purity

And whoever worships the three steps of that peerless Trivikrama,
the lord of the moving and unmoving, all his desires become fulfilled; there is no doubt of this.

text_mt:
This worship of Viṣṇu of three bodies has been told to you by me, O illustrious one; / worshipped through it, the chief lord of the universe grants the desired wishes to the wise.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Further, I will explain to you the vow of Viṣṇu’s forms. / The form of the god of gods is twofold, O Yādava:
one is terrible, and the other is auspicious; the terrible one is the Purifier [Fire], / and the auspicious one is the Lord of Waters [Soma], since the universe consists of Agni and Soma.
The terrible is taught as twofold, and again the gentle is twofold: / the terrible are Fire and Sun, and the gentle are Soma and the Lord of Waters.
Worship of these is to be performed in order, beginning from the first day, / starting from the bright fortnight of Phālguna, O best of the twice-born.
On the first day, exceedingly pure, the king should worship the Sun; / on the second day, Fire; on the third day, the Lord of Waters;
and on the fourth day, the Moon, according to rule, O best of men. / Having made images of these, the wise man should worship them

on the second, O tiger among the Yadus, an auspicious bath with myrobalan fruits; / on the third, with priyaṅgu; and on the fourth, with white mustard.
With wheat, sesame, rice, and barley respectively by day, / an oblation is to be performed, O knower of dharma; and now hear the sacrificial fee:
saffron, red cloth, sandalwood, and a parasol. / In this [vow], subsistence should be maintained each day solely with milk.
Having observed this vow for a complete year, O best of men, / he obtains the fruit of a sacrifice endowed with all desires.
And he goes to the world of heaven in an aerial chariot having the colour of the sun. / Having dwelt there for a very long time, he is born into an exalted family.
Having attained human birth, he becomes free from disease, a lord of the earth who has conquered hostile factions, / abiding in dharma, devoted to truth, disciplined, with senses subdued, delightful to all people.

Mārkaṇḍeya said: / I will declare to you this other vow of the fourfold form: / Śakra, Kīnāśa [Yama], Varuṇa, and the Lord of Wealth [Kubera], O best of Yadus.
Vāsudeva, the Lord of the Universe, is taught as having four forms. / Having made images of them, the wise man should worship them
with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, obeisance, incense, lamps, and food. / On the first day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, he should worship the Lord of the Thirty [Indra];
on the second day, the god Yama; on the third, the Lord of Waters; / and on the fourth day, the Lord of Wealth. Each day he should bathe,
having reached a riverbank, beholding the deity each day in turn. / The oblation should be made with barley, sesame seeds, ghee, and sesame mixed with rice grains,
and [he should offer] red, yellow, black, and white cloth in the order of the days. / Having observed this auspicious vow for a full year, a man / attains the celestial world for as long as fourteen Indras endure.

3.139
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I will tell you of another four-form vow:
Viṣṇu, the Earth, the Sky, and Brahmā are his four forms.
Having fashioned their forms, one should then worship them / with an abundance of perfume, garlands, prostrations, incense, lamps, and food.
On the first day of the bright half of Caitra, one should worship the god Viṣṇu; / on the second and following days, O knower of dharma, the Earth, [the Sky], and the Grandfather.
All the other procedures should be as stated in the previous vow. / Having performed this vow, a man attains the heavenly world.
Attaining human birth, he becomes free from disease, delighted in dharma, endowed with wealth, / endowed with riches, beauty, and happiness, pleasing to the people, and triumphant over his enemies.

text_mt:
3.140
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I will tell you of another four-form vow:
Strength, knowledge, sovereignty, and power, O joy of the Yadus,
are known as the four forms of that god of gods. / The form of dharma has indeed been spoken of as that of strength;
the form of knowledge has been declared to you as Narasiṃha, O king; / and sovereignty has been described to you by me as the form of Rudra, O king.
Power has been declared to be the Boar, the god who is the slayer of Madhu. / Thus from each face of him who bears the four forms has it been declared to you.
His eastern face, representing strength, is the face of Vāsudeva. / They know the southern face, representing knowledge, to be the god Saṃkarṣaṇa.
The western face, representing sovereignty, belongs to Rudra and removes sins; / and the northern face is declared to be the Boar, Aniruddha.
Having fasted for three nights, one should worship the eastern face in Caitra; / likewise in the month of Vaiśākha one should worship the southern face; / in Jyeṣṭha the western face, and in Āṣāḍha likewise the northern.

text_mt:
In the month of Caitra, one should give what is useful for the household to a twice-born; / in Vaiśākha, one should give what is useful for battle, O best of the Yādavas;
likewise in Jyeṣṭha, one should give what is useful for sacrifice to a twice-born; / and in the month of Āṣāḍha, one should likewise give what is useful for the sacred rite.
When a man has observed this vow for four full months, / when the first conclusion is reached, he becomes [sanctified]—such is the certainty.
Having performed the first conclusion, he is honoured in the heavenly world; / having enjoyed heaven for ten thousand years as stated,
in the gentle and other watches of the day, the second conclusion takes place. / Having performed the second conclusion, pure, he should feed brahmins / with food consisting mostly of milk-products, along with raisins and sugar.
And when the third conclusion for the twice-born is reached, he attains residence in the same realm as the god; / and having enjoyed the worlds of heaven and the Moon for the stated time, happy, he has all his desires fulfilled.

3.142
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I will tell you of another four-form vow, / how the worship of the teacher of the world, who is the self of all, should be performed:
Fasting, with subdued senses, on the fourth day of the bright half of Caitra,
having performed the auspicious worship of Vāsudeva on the fourth day, / he should give gold as a sacrificial fee to a celibate student who is a twice-born.
Likewise, having worshipped the god Saṃkarṣaṇa, the teacher of the world, / in Vaiśākha, he should give a well-prepared bed to a householder.
Having duly worshipped the god Pradyumna in the month of Jyeṣṭha, / he should give fruits and roots along with milk-products to a forest-dweller.
Likewise, having worshipped Aniruddha, the teacher of the world, in Āṣāḍha, / he should give a gourd-vessel to a twice-born established in yoga.

And when the third conclusion is reached, he attains residence in the same realm as Keśava. / Thus have I told you this excellent vow named after the stages of life, which destroys all impurities.

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I will tell you of another four-form vow:
Hari is declared to be fourfold in nature, and the sacrificial fires are four.
A twice-born who has established the sacred fires, in whom the four fires are present, / fasting on the fourth day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna,
Worshipping Vāsudeva of fourfold self with unflagging zeal, / he should give sixteen prasthas of sesame to that lord among twice-borns,
a suvarṇa of gold, clothing, and a tulā of ghee. / Having performed this vow with unflagging zeal for one year in this manner,
he obtains the fruit of a sacrifice complete with all desires, / and travels to the heavenly world in a sun-colored aerial chariot.

As a mortal, he becomes blazing in splendor, possessed of blazing digestive fire, dear to women; / he conquers enemies in battle and likewise becomes wealthy.
Those four fires that have been declared are indeed Vāsudeva, spoken of fourfold; / one who worships a brahmin who maintains the sacred fires, by him that god is also worshipped.

3.147 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / I will declare to you another vow of the four forms: / Īśāna, Agni, Virūpākṣa, and the wind,
are to be understood as the four divine forms, O tiger among the Yadus. / Having fashioned their figures, the wise person should worship them
with an abundance of fragrant paste, garlands, obeisances, incense, lamps, and food, / in the bright fortnight of Caitra, O fortunate one, beginning from the first lunar day in due order.
He should bathe in waters from the earth, rivers, tanks, and natural lakes; / oblations of curd, sesame, barley, and ghee should be offered.
And camphor, saffron, and likewise agallochum and sandalwood / should be given to brahmins, O king, in the order of the days.
Likewise, for three days one should eat unbegged food in the evening and the morning. / For one day one should eat thus, living as a celibate student, O best of men.

text_mt:
Having observed this vow for a year, O best of men, / one enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice rich in all desires.
Attaining human birth, he becomes free from disease, a ruler of the earth whose enemies are conquered; / in another birth he will be foremost among the best of twice-born, devoted to the Vedas, offering many sacrifices.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / I will declare another vow of the Four Forms for you. / Conch, discus, mace, and lotus are proclaimed as the four-fold Self.
Vāsudeva is considered the conch, and the discus is Saṃkarṣaṇa; / Pradyumna is the mace, and the lotus is Aniruddha, the teacher of the world.
In the months beginning with Śrāvaṇa, bathing outdoors and eating once a day, / one should worship them month by month, in proper sequence,
with an abundance of perfume, garlands, obeisance, incense, lamps, and food. / Then, at the end of Kārtika, when the vow has concluded,
one should feed brahmins with devotion and give a sacrificial fee according to one's capacity, / along with a bronze vessel filled with clarified butter and containing gold.

Reaching human birth, he becomes free of disease, endowed with strength, a slayer of hosts of foes, / possessed of learning, beauty, and virtue, delightful to people, and dear to women.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / I shall declare to you another observance of the five forms: / Saṃvatsara is remembered as fire; Parivatsara is the sun;
preceded by Iḍā [i.e., Iḍāvatsara] is the moon; preceded by Anu [i.e., Anuvatsara] is Prajāpati; / and preceded by Tat [i.e., Idvatsara] is declared to be the god of gods, Maheśvara.
By arranging their sacred diagrams, [the rite] is enjoined just as before. / Sacrifice and worship are to be performed, and the oblation is to be performed in like manner,
with sesame, unhusked rice, barley, ghee, and white mustard, / either with the mantras characteristic of them or with their names, daily in succession.
He should remain eating only at night, as before, for a period of five days. / He should begin this observance in the year called Saṃvatsara.
At the conclusion of the observance, five [measures of] gold are to be given, O Yādava; / it should be given to knowers of the four Vedas according to the division of their branches, O Yādava.

One [measure] each [is given to the four], and the fifth should be given likewise to a knower of time. / This observance yielding the fruit of a horse sacrifice has thus been declared by me to you.
He reaches whichever realm he desires, moving at will like a bird, / honored by gods and demons—[all that] is accomplished by this, O knower of dharma.
Reaching human birth, he becomes free of disease, endowed with high status, beauty, and strength, / a king whose adversaries are bowed by his majesty, or an exalted god, an offerer of many sacrifices.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Now then, I shall declare to you the observance named the observance of Śrī. / On the third day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, having bathed preceded by unction,
dressed in white garments, O king, wearing white garlands and ointments, / he should subsist on food of rice with ghee and sleep on the ground for that night.
On the fourth day, going outside, he should likewise perform a bath, / especially in a lotus pool; then, dressed in white garments and pure,
he should worship Lakṣmī on a lotus, either artificial or natural, / with white perfumes and garlands, and also with a ghee lamp,

and with curd, milk-rice, ginger, molasses, / sugarcane, preparations of sugarcane, and plenty of salt,
and according to his ability, O great king, with abundant offerings. / Then, pure, he should offer lotuses into the fire with the Śrīsūkta.
If that is unavailable, [he should offer] bilva fruits; if that is unavailable, likewise ghee. / He should feed the brahmins [food] consisting mostly of milk and abundant in ghee.
He should give a māṣaka of gold as a sacrificial fee to the brahmins. / Then, without food, he should sleep in a pure place according to the rule.
Then, having reached the fifth day, having bathed in the morning in the water of a lotus pool, / he should perform worship just as before, as beloved [to her].
Once more he should give the aforementioned gold māṣaka to a twice-born. / Immediately thereafter he should eat a lotus seed or a bilva fruit.
Then, keeping silent, that best of men should eat sacrificial food. / For a year [he should eat a bilva fruit; immediately thereafter,] / having performed this observance for a year, O best of kings,

text_mt:
Thus ends the one hundred fifty-fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Observance of Lakṣmī in the Rule of the Five Forms,' in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra in the third book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Now I shall declare to you another observance of the five forms: / the conch, the discus, the mace, the lotus, and the earth, O mighty-armed one.
Having made diagrams with perfumes, he should worship the five on five [days], / beginning from the end of the bright fortnight of Caitra, starting with the fifth day, O king.
Fasting, bathed outside, likewise dressed in white garments, pure, / with perfumes, garlands, obeisance, incense, lamps, and an abundance of food,
having performed worship of all, he should offer into the fire / ghee with the names of all the deities.
And here he should feed brahmins sweet food at that time. / Having performed this for a year, at the end of the observance [he should give] five garments.
Giving [garments] of five colours to one who knows the Pañcarātra, O king of kings, / he attains [the fruit of] an Aśvamedha and obtains the fruit of a Rājasūya.

The Subhāsvaras, Barhiṣads, and likewise the Agniṣvāttas, / the Kravyāds, Upahūtas, Ājyapas, and Sukālins—
he should worship [them] daily, O king, with perfumes, garlands, and unguents; / he should offer kṛsara as an oblation, and offer sesame seeds into the fire.
He should feed the brahmins kṛsara and give sesame seeds as a sacrificial fee; / he should eat only at night, eating sacrificial food, O lord of men.
Having performed this observance for a year, O best of men, / at the conclusion of the observance he should give a pala of silver to a twice-born.
By the performance of this observance, he attains the world of the sun, / honoured by the gods, moving at will as a celestial bird.

A man, having performed [it] for a whole year, obtains liberation from worldly existence, O ruler of men; / having performed it for twelve years, on attaining human birth he would become a ruler of the earth.
3.158 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Beginning from the month of Caitra, day by day in the dark fortnight, / one should worship the netherworlds from the first day onwards in due order:
the golden-earthed, the [bare-]earthed netherworld, the blue-soiled, / the red-earthed, the yellow-earthed, as well as the white- and black-soiled,
with gold, perfumes, garlands, abundant offerings of food, / with the presentation of ghee-lamps, and with the propitiation of fire.
Having thus observed the vow for a year, eating only at night, / at the conclusion of the observance he should present lamps in the homes of the twice-born,
and also garments according to their colours, O king of kings. / Having performed this observance, a man becomes a lord of men.
By hundreds and thousands divine maidens obtain him as their husband / and delight him, O great king, just like [the son of] Iḍaviḍā.

He should always bathe outside [the house], / offer oblations of ghee into the fire, and give the seven grains.
He should take only one single meal at night, / and should constantly sleep on the ground for three days dedicated to that deity.
When the year is completed, he should give a representation made of silver, / weighing a hundred palas, shaped like a continent.
A man who performs this observance pure for a full year / attains the heavenly world until the dissolution of all beings.

one should worship [the oceans of] salt, milk, flood of clarified butter, curd-scum, wine, / and likewise sugarcane juice and sweet water.
He should always take his daily bath outside his house, / offer oblations of ghee into the fire, and give the seven grains.
He should eat sacrificial food at night and maintain the observance for a year; / and at the end of the year he should give a milch cow.
By the performance of this observance, he becomes a king who enjoys the earth / girdled by the seven oceans for seven successive births.
One desirous of health should observe this supreme observance, / as should one desirous of dharma, one desirous of fame, or another desirous of fortune.

text_mt:
And having enjoyed pleasures in heaven, O king, and attained human birth as described, / he obtains all that has been proclaimed by me, O ruler of men, for seven successive lives.
3.162 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Beyond this, I shall proclaim to you the auspicious world-observance: / those seven sacred utterances that are renowned in the three worlds—
one should perform an outdoor bath daily, constantly unwearied, / beginning from the bright [fortnight] of Caitra, in order for seven days.
Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, water with kuśa grass, / and fasting for one night—one should observe [these] in this very order.
Day after day, an oblation of sesame seeds should be made with the great sacred utterances; / and at the end of the year, one should likewise give a sacrificial fee to brahmins:
gold, an unbleached garment, bronze, and a milch cow. / Having performed this observance for a year, O best of men,
one becomes prosperous and moves through all worlds at will, O lord of men, / until the end of the aeon; and at the beginning of an aeon, he becomes an earthly king.

text_mt:
A universal emperor worshipped by the best of kings, having power superior to gods and demons, / pleasing to all, he protects the earth for ten million years.
3.163 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Beginning from the bright [fortnight] of Caitra, daily for seven days, / one should worship Hlādinī, Hrādinī, and Pāvanī,
Sītā, Rāma, Sindhu, and Bhāgīrathī in order. / Then one should bathe outdoors and constantly eat at night.
Day after day, one should offer milk into water in their names, / and water-vessels filled with milk should be given to the twice-born.
One should subsist on milk in that manner for seven days. / Having done this for a year, when the year is completed, a man
should then give pala by pala of silver to the twice-born, / in the bright fortnight of Phālguna, in order of the days up to the seventh.
A man attains that world where the mud is sweet rice-milk, / where divine rivers flow with milk, granting the fruits of all desires.

text_mt:
Having dwelt there for a very long time, that great-souled one attains human birth and becomes free from disease, / endowed with beauty, good character, and wealth, a king or an eminent brahmin.
3.164 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Beginning from the bright [fortnight] of Caitra, daily for seven days, / [one should worship] Suprabhā, Kāñcanākṣī, Viśālā, Lake Mānasa,
Trinādā, Suveṇu, and likewise Vimalodakā. / One should constantly worship them with devotion and bathe outdoors.
And day after day one should perform an oblation of curd in their names; / and here one should feed brahmins food mixed with curd.
Likewise, one should eat rice cooked with clarified butter only once, at night. / Having done this for a year, when the year is completed, a man
should give seven garments in the bright fortnight of Phālguna daily, in order of the days, / to an eminent twice-born who has bathed in a sacred bathing place.
Having observed the Sarasvatī observance thus for a year, one should recite [mantras]. / Having dwelt there for a very long time, a human is then born.

Then he becomes a king who has conquered enemy factions, or an eminent twice-born who has performed many sacrifices, / endowed with beauty, good character, and wealth, possessed of sacred learning, and pleasing to the people.
3.165 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Beginning from the bright [fortnight] of Caitra, daily for seven days, / [one should worship] Marīci, Atri and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,
and Vasiṣṭha, O highly fortunate one, in order of the days, / individually with seasonal fruits, flowers, and dairy products.
One should bathe outdoors daily and eat at night, / offering an oblation with the great sacred utterances using fruits, roots, and dairy products.
And water-vessels filled with milk should be given to the twice-born. / Having done this for a year, at the end of the observance, to one who maintains the sacred fire,
O king, one should give a black antelope skin as previously stated by me. / Having performed this observance, a man finds the means to liberation;
having attained the means to liberation, he undoubtedly attains liberation.

endowed with wealth, beauty, and strength, pleasing to people, dear to women, / with a disease-free body, with his faction of enemies destroyed, eloquent, and an upholder of the scriptures in the world.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having fasted properly on the sixth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, / one should worship the Sun, the god of gods, on the seventh day.
Having bathed outside, the man should smear an altar / that has been smeared with cow dung, well prepared with white clay, O king.
There he should draw an eight-petalled lotus with colours; / in its pericarp he should ritually place Vibhāvasu, the god of gods.
On the eastern petal he should place two gods, O king, and on the northern petal; / and on the south-eastern petal he should place the two gandharvas of the season.
And on the southern petal he should place likewise two apsarases; / he should place two rākṣasas, O great king, on the south-western petal.
On the western [petal], the two great nāgas born of Kadrū, protectors of the season; / likewise on the north-western [petal], two yātudhānas, O best of kings.

text_mt:
And on the northern petal he should ritually place two sages; / on the north-eastern petal he should ritually place one planet, O best of men.
Their worship should be performed with fragrant perfumes, garlands, and ointments, / with incenses, lamps, and food offerings, individually, O tamer of enemies.
Having thus worshipped all of them, immediately thereafter / one should perform an oblation with clarified butter with one hundred and eight [recitations] for Sūrya.
And for the others one should offer eight each, O lord of men; / and he should feed one twice-born for each of them by name.
And a sacrificial fee should be given to them according to one's capacity, O best of the Yadus. / Having observed this vow thus for one year, O best of men,
at the end of the vow he should then duly give a milch cow / and gold to a brahmin versed in the Purāṇas, O best of the Yadus.
This vow is proclaimed by the Self-born as granting all desires; / having observed this vow, one reaches the realm of Sūrya.
If the king performs this great vow for twelve years, / piercing the solar orb, he goes to union with Viṣṇu.

text_mt:
This vow destroys sins, brings wealth, brings fame, and destroys enemies; / and in this world and the next, O king, it confers heaven and brings about liberation.
Vajra said: / In each sacrifice, O brahmin, which gods and others / follow the lord Ravi, that you should tell me.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Dhātṛ and Aryaman, O king of kings, are the pair of deities in spring, / and Tumburu and Nārada, the two excellent singing gandharvas.
And the apsaras Kṛtasthalā, and likewise she who is Puñjikasthalā, / and Hotṛ and Prahotṛ, the two foremost Yakṣas who destroy demons,
and both the serpent Vāsuki and Vāṣṭakarṇī, / and Rathakṛtsnā and Rathaujas, the two excellent yātudhānas,
and Mitra and Pulaha, the two best of ṛṣis; / and Venus follows as the planet in spring.
Hear from me those who follow the sun god in summer: / Mitra and Varuṇa are the two deities dwelling [with him] in summer,

and the ṛṣis Atri and Vasiṣṭha, and the two nāgas Rambhaka and Takṣaka, / and Menakā and Sahajanyā, and the two gandharvas Hāhā and Hūhū,
and both Rathasvanapramāṇa and Rathakṛtsa; / and Pauruṣāda and Vadha are recalled as the two yātudhānas,
and Mars follows as the planet in summer. / Hear from me those who follow the sun god in the rainy season:
Indra and Vivasvat, and Aṅgiras and Bhṛgu, / and the serpent Elāpatra and the snake Śaṅkhapāla,
and Śucisena and Ugrasena, and Vrāta and Aruṇa; / and both the apsarases Pramlocā and Nimlocantī,
and the yātudhāna Sarpa and Vyāghra, O lord of men. / In the rainy season, the priest of the gods follows him as the planet.
Hear thereafter concerning the autumn season, O ruler of men: / Parjanya and Pūṣan, and Bharadvāja and Gautama,

3.169
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
On the seventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Caitra, O ruler of men, / on [ground] smeared with cow dung, one should make a maṇḍala with clay.
An eight-petalled lotus should be made there with auspicious pigments. / Having observed a fast, a man should worship the sun in its centre,
and Aruṇa, Dantāka, Māṭhara, and Dama, / and Yamunā, Yama, Kāla, and the second Manu,
and Saturn, the queen, Chāyā, and Revanta, / the seven metres, the year, the sky, and Piṅgala.
One should worship the declared deities either on the filaments or on the petals. / The worship of the directions and time should be performed outside the lotus, O king,
with an abundance of perfume, garlands, obeisances, incense, lamps, and food. / When the observance is completed, a horse should be given to a brahmin.

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, O ruler of men, / fasting on the seventh day, one should worship the sun on a lotus,
either in an icon or on the ground, with white flowers according to rule, / with red sandalwood, with fried cakes, and with rice-and-pulse gruel.
Desiring the destruction of enemies, he should give two red garments to an eminent twice-born at the end of the observance; / and desiring good fortune, he likewise attains a kingdom, and at the end, the worlds of the sun.

3.172
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Vara, Dhruva, Soma, Āpa, Anila, Anala, / Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa are celebrated as the eight Vasus.
This eight-formed Vāsudeva is through origination and dissolution. / Whoever worships on the eighth lunar day while fasting, O king,
beginning from the month of Caitra in the bright fortnight, O Yādava, / either in sacred diagrams or in images, duly, O lord of men,
with an abundance of fragrance, garlands, obeisances, incense, lamps, and food, / by outdoor bathing, O king of kings, and likewise by sleeping on the ground,
and at the end of the vow gives a milch cow to a brahmin with devotion— / having performed this vow, a man attains all desires.
He attains [the fruit of] a puṇḍarīka sacrifice, uplifts his own lineage, / and having reached the realm of the Vasus, rejoices like an immortal.
