3.173
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Beginning from the bright fortnight on the eighth lunar day of Soma, O king, / fasting, one should worship the three-eyed god of gods,
either in a liṅga, or in an image, on a lotus, or on the ground, / with an anointing of ghee and milk, and various kinds of bathing,
with an abundance of fragrance, garlands, obeisances, incense, lamps, and food, / with song, dance, and instrumental music, and satisfaction of the fire,
and with worship of brahmins duly, O best of men; / and at the conclusion of the vow, he should also give a milch cow yielding milk.
He attains the fruit of a puṇḍarīka sacrifice and goes to heaven. / Having likewise worshipped Maheśvara on the eighth lunar days of the dark fortnight,
he obtains [the fruit of] an agniṣṭoma sacrifice and goes to heaven. / Having performed the pair of eighth lunar days for a year,

a man should worship these nine kingly mountains on the ninth lunar day. / Holy Uttarakuru, Ramyaka, Hairaṇvata,
Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla, and likewise Ilāvṛta, / Harivarṣa, Kiṃpuruṣa, and the continent of Bhārata:
these are likewise to be worshipped according to their arrangement, O king. / On the ninth lunar day of the bright fortnight, beginning from Caitra, O king,

Attaining human birth, he becomes an emperor, a king delighting the hosts of gods; / and having ruled the earth for a long time, he attains those realms and desires thereafter.
3.175
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Fasting on the ninth lunar day, one should worship Bhadrakālī / in the bright fortnight, O great king, in order beginning from Kārtika,
with an abundance of fragrance, garlands, obeisances, incense, lamps, and food. / Having worshipped for a year, at the end of the vow, to a brahmin
a man gives a pair of garments and obtains his wish at will. / Afflicted with disease, he is freed from disease; bound, he is freed from bondage.
And when accused in royal affairs, he is freed from great fear; / he never has fear from thieves nor from wild beasts.
He obtains sons, wealth at will, excellent women, and various base metals; / having performed worship of Bhavānī according to rule, he attains desired wishes at will.

text_mt:
Bestowing good fortune, enhancing beauty, bestowing charm, and granting the pleasure of love with women, / [this vow] must be performed with effort by a man, O lord of men, and likewise by women, O you of undaunted spirit.
3.194 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Beginning from Mārgaśīrṣa, having worshipped [the deity] in the disc of the moon / while fasting, a man obtains the fruit of a Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice.
Having performed this desired vow for a year, he reaches the world of the moon; / and dwelling there for a very long time, O king, he then attains union with him.
3.195 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Beginning from Proṣṭhapada, on the full moon, / having worshipped the god Varuṇa with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, and food,
and at the end of the vow having given to a twice-born a water-cow / accompanied by an umbrella and shoes, and adorned with a pair of garments,
a man reaches the world of Varuṇa, O king; and dwelling there for a very long time, / upon attaining human birth he becomes free from disease, endowed with beauty, and rich.

3.197 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Fasting on the fourteenth and on the full moon, the best of men / should then drink the five products of the cow and partake of sacrificial food.
Having done so for a year, he is freed from the sins of a month; / therefore, with all effort, one should observe it month by month.
Reaching the world of the lord of men for a year, and dwelling there for a very long time, O king, / upon attaining human birth, honoured by kings, that foremost of the twice-born becomes either a king or an eminent twice-born.
3.198
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Fasting on the fourteenth, / one who worships the god Hari in the form of yoga on the full moon obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Likewise [worshipping him] in the form of brahman on the new moon and on the full moon, / one obtains [the fruit of] a Rājasūya sacrifice and elevates one's own family.

One should worship him in the form of brahman on the new moon and on the full moon; / serving Keśava in the form of yoga, one attains greatness.
At the ends of the months and fortnights, the supreme god Hari / is always exceedingly pleased when worshipped with devotion by one who fasts.
This is known as the Great Observance, which destroys all impurities. / Having performed this for a year, one is exalted in the vault of heaven.
This observance is proclaimed to pacify all sins. / Here, one's own financial capacity alone is the measure in all rituals.
Having observed the vow for twelve years, a man reaches the world of Puruṣottama; / having dwelt there for a very long, auspicious time, O king, he then ultimately attains liberation.
3.199
Vajra said:
O venerable one, by what action is a man not born in an animal womb / or in a barbarian land? Tell that to me as I ask.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
At the Sun's transit into Aries, fasting, the best of men / should worship the god Bhārgava Rāma according to rule and to the best of his ability.

[...] and when the transit into Gemini occurs, one should worship the one who reclines on the serpent hood.
Likewise, at the transit into Cancer, the invincible Boar; / likewise, at the transit into Leo, the lord god Narasiṃha; / at the transit into Virgo, a man should worship the god in female form.
When the transit into Libra has arrived, O king, one should worship Vāmana; / likewise, at the transit into Scorpio, the god of gods, Trivikrama.
At the transit into Sagittarius, O king, [worship] the horse-headed god; / likewise, at the transit into Capricorn, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.
At the transit into Aquarius, O king, [worship] Rāma, the delight of the Yādavas; / and at the transit into Pisces, one should worship the Fish, Vāsudeva.
Either on a painted cloth or in an icon, with an abundance of perfume, garlands, and food, / and in the name of each manifestation, one should make a fire oblation, O ruler of the earth.
At the end of the observance, one should give a water-cow provided with an umbrella and sandals / and accompanied by a pair of garments, and gold every month; / and at night one should worship the god of gods with rows of lamps.

Having performed this desired observance for a year, one is not born among barbarians or animals; / he reaches heaven for a long time and attains desired happiness pleasing to the heart.
3.200
Vajra said:
By which action does a human being obtain the desired birth? / Tell me that, O knower of dharma, for you are said to be all-knowing.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Always on days sacred to Puruṣa, fasting for three nights, a man, / beginning from the month of Caitra, should worship Hari in Kārtika,
with the Puruṣasūkta, with its verses, with flowers, and likewise with fruits, / with incenses, lamps, and food, and with oblations of clarified butter.
A cow should be given at the end of the observance, having performed the observance for a year. / He obtains the birth he desires; no doubt should be entertained here.
This best of observances is not taught to yield [a good] birth alone, O unflagging soul; / it bestows the desired wishes of a man, and gives liberation, O foremost of men.

Vajra said:
O venerable one, by what action does one obtain birth in a [noble] family? / Cut this doubt of mine, for you are said to be all-knowing.

And likewise, O king, he should give the three metals—copper, gold, and silver—to brahmins. / The observance is taught not only to bestow a noble family, but also to bring about the attainment of all desired wishes.
3.202
Vajra said:
O venerable one, by what action is a man born handsome? / Cut this doubt of mine, for you are said to be all-knowing.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When the full moon of Phālguna has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in order, / until the full moon of Caitra, O great king, bathing day by day,
one should worship outside the god Keśava reclining on the serpent hood; / one should eat only one meal, at night, and likewise sleep on the ground.
Fasting for three nights, one should perform the worship on the full moon of Caitra as well; / according to one's means, one should give silver, and likewise a pair of garments.
This best of observances lasting a month has been told by me for one desiring beauty, O unflagging soul. / Having performed it, a man reaches heaven, and on attaining human existence he becomes handsome.

3.203
Vajra said:
O venerable one, by what action does a man attain charm? / Beauty devoid of charm seems fruitless to me.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When the full moon of Kārtika has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in order, / either on a painted cloth or in an icon, one should worship the lord Pradyumna.
He should always bathe outdoors, eat at night with restrained speech, / [eating] once a day, O great king, always dedicated to sacrificial food.
Then, having reached [the month of] Mārgaśīrṣa, pure, having fasted for three nights, / having worshipped the divine Pradyumna and offered oblations of ghee into the fire,
and he should feed brahmins here a meal rich in salt. / Then [he should give] a prastha of powdered salt to a twice-born [brahmin],

text_mt:
For this best of vows is declared to produce beauty of charm and grant ascent to heaven; / not only would the foremost of beings bestow desires upon a man, O hero of the Yādavas.
3.204 / Vajra said: / Blessed one, by what action would a man attain great good fortune? / Beauty and charm are to be known as meaningless without good fortune.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the full moon of Māgha has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in due order, / whether on a cloth or on an image, he should always worship Kṛṣṇa.
He should perform everything mentioned earlier, [subsisting on] sacrificial food, O lord of the earth; / he should constantly perform his bath with fragrant priyaṅgu.
Then, having fasted for three nights, pure, he should make that [gift] on the full moon of Phālguna:
Two garments smeared with saffron are to be given, O king, and likewise a bronze vessel of honey. / And this unequalled vow granting good fortune has been spoken to you by me, O hero among men.
3.205 / Vajra said: / Blessed one, by what action would a man attain health? / Beauty, good fortune, and charm are meaningless for one afflicted with disease.

text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the full moon of Bhādrapada has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in due order, / whether on a cloth or on an image, he should worship Aniruddha.
By the previously stated rite until the full moon of Āśvina arrives, / he should worship the god day after day with lotuses and jasmine flowers.
He should offer oblations into the fire with ghee, give ghee to a twice-born [brahmin], / and feed the brahmins food mostly consisting of dairy products.
Then, on the full moon of Āśvina, having fasted completely for three nights, a man / [should give] a bronze vessel containing ghee and gold to a twice-born [brahmin].
A man should give [this], O tiger among kings, for the increase of health; / this vow is prescribed as granting the world of heaven to men.
It is declared not merely to remove disease, but to produce authority and bestow increase of beauty; / the supreme vow has been told to you, O hero among men, which also brings about the attainment of desired wishes in the world of men.

text_mt:
Having performed this vow for a month as spoken by me, and having attained heaven for a very long time, / upon attaining human birth, a man would indeed become endowed with intellect and endowed with knowledge.
3.207 / Vajra said: / Blessed one, by what action would a man become learned? / A man is to be known as truly a man only when well-educated; otherwise he is a beast.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the full moon of Pauṣa has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in due order, / he should worship the horse-headed god Hari as before.
And he should offer sesamum seeds into the fire, and worship the god with sesamum seeds; / having fasted for three nights on the full moon of Māgha, [he should give] sesamum seeds and gold,
he should give [these] to an eminent brahmin with a fully restrained mind, / as well as an excellent sacred thread and abundant firewood.
Having performed this vow for a month as spoken by me, a man would always be endowed with learning; / having attained the heavenly world and enjoyed pleasures, a man also attains his cherished desires.

3.208 / Vajra said: / Blessed one, by what action would a man become virtuous? / Indeed, good conduct surpasses family, caste, and Vedic learning.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the Āgrāyaṇī full moon has passed, for one month, day after day, / he should worship the invincible divine Boar as before.
He should bathe the god with ghee, offer oblations with ghee, / give ghee to the twice-born, and offer ghee alone [as food].
Having fasted for three nights on the full moon of Pauṣa, he should honor the twice-born / with a vessel of ghee accompanied by gold according to his capacity, O lord of men.
Having performed this vow for a month as spoken by me, and having attained heaven for a very long time, / a man, upon attaining human birth, would be virtuous and attain prosperity and long life.
3.209 / Vajra said: / Blessed one, by what action would [a man] constantly be devoted to dharma, / and a knower of dharma, O great king, on account of the fruitfulness of dharma?
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the full moon of Āṣāḍha has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in due order, / he should worship the god who bears the form of dharma as before.

text_mt:
And at the end of the month, O king, on the full moon day, having observed a three-night fast, he should give gold. / This supreme observance, which brings about dharma and bestows all aims, has been told to you; there is no doubt about this.
3.210 / Vajra said: / By what action, O venerable one, may a man become wealthy? / For only a wealthy man is honored among the worlds.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the Śrāvaṇa full moon day has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in due order, / he should worship, as before, God Viṣṇu, the Lord Saṃkarṣaṇa,
with blue lotuses and leaves of the bhṛṅgarāja plant, O king, / with ghee, with fine milk-rice, and with bilva fruits according to his capacity.
Then, having properly fasted for three nights on the Proṣṭhapadā full moon day, / that best of men should give a cow to an eminent twice-born at the end of the observance.
Having performed this month-long observance as prescribed and reached heaven for a very long time, / a human being, having obtained human birth, becomes endowed with wealth through the observance he performed, O lion among kings.

Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the Jyeṣṭha full moon day has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in due order, / he should worship, as before, the God Hari who bears the universal form.
And having thus observed a three-night fast at the end of the observance and given a well-furnished bed to a twice-born, / he reaches the heavenly world, dwells there for a long time, and, having attained human birth, becomes endowed with enjoyments.
3.213 / Vajra said: / By what action, O venerable one, may one attain victory everywhere— / in legal proceedings, in battle, in gambling, and in debate, O best of the twice-born?
There is no happiness in the worlds higher than the attainment of victory, O best of good men; / the attainment of victory is supreme happiness; tell me the observance for attaining it.

Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the Āśvina full moon day has passed, beginning from the first lunar day in due order, / he should worship, as before, Viṣṇu, the God of gods, Trivikrama.
And at the end of the three-night fast, on the Kārttika full moon day, he should give an excellent bull, / made to bear all kinds of grain and adorned with jewels according to his capacity.
Having performed this month-long observance as prescribed, the heroic king reaches heaven for a very long time; / having dwelt there for a very long time, the man attains victory everywhere in the world of men.
3.214 / Vajra said: / Tell me of other optional observances, O bull among the twice-born, / for women or for men; I consider you all-knowing.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having fasted, one should worship the God Narasiṃha under the Kṛttikās in due order, / beginning from the Kārttika full moon day until the next Kārttika full moon,
always with unguents, flowers, and the like, as prescribed at all times. / And at the end of the observance, having given sandalwood and tagara to a twice-born,
as well as a shield, a principal weapon, and various garments, / he attains victory everywhere, wherever he is born.

व्रतानि त्वं समाचक्ष्व सर्वधर्मभृतां वर .. 3 ..

text_mt:
Thus these vows have been declared to you by me, O king, which constantly remove sin, / bestow heaven, and fulfill desires as wished, granting supreme fullness in this world.
3.215 / Vajra said: / For the sake of worshipping the god Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendour, / tell me other vows, O increaser of the lineage of Bhṛgu.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Seated comfortably at the Gateway to the Gaṅgā, the best of sages, Pulastya, / spoke vows to Dālbhya; listen to those from me.
Dālbhya said: / For the sake of worshipping the god Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendour, / explain the vows [to me], O best of all upholders of dharma.
Pulastya said: / That man who on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight in the month of Phālguna, / chanting the name of the god, 'Kṛṣṇa', again and again with devotion,
and having made one hundred and eight [recitations] in the worship of the god, should chant this, being pure, / bathed, both at the time of setting forth, when rising, slipping, or sneezing;
he should not converse with heretics, fallen people, / or outcasts, and he should worship Kṛṣṇa full of faith.

utkrāntikāle kṛṣṇasya smaraṇaṃ ca tathāśnute .. 11 ..

meaning:
इदं चोदाहरेत्कृष्णे मनः सन्धाय तत्परः ..
कृष्णकृष्ण कृपालुस्त्वमगतीनां गतिर्भव .. 7 ..
संसारार्णवमग्नानां प्रसीद मधुसूदन ..
एवं प्रसाद्योपवसेत्कृत्वा नियतमानसः .. 8 ..
पूर्वेह्नि चान्येद्युश्चापि गव्यं संप्राश्य वै सकृत् ..
स्नातोर्चयित्वा कृष्णेति पुनर्नाम प्रकीर्तयेत् .. 9 ..
वारिधाराव्रते चैव विक्षिपेद्देवपादयोः ..
चैत्रवैशाखयोश्चैव तद्वज्ज्येष्ठे च पूजयेत् .. 3.215.10 ..
मर्त्यलोके गतिं श्रेष्ठां दाल्भ्य प्राप्नोति वै नरः ..
उत्क्रान्तिकाले कृष्णस्य स्मरणं च तथाश्नुते .. 11 ..
आषाढे श्रावणे चैव मासि भाद्रपदे तथा ..
तथैवाश्वयुजे मासि अनेन विधिना नरः .. 12 ..

गोमूत्रप्राशनात्पूतः स्वर्गलोकगतिं व्रजेत् .. 13 ..

उत्क्रान्तिकाले स्मरणं केशवस्य तथाप्नुयात् .. 14 ..
text_mt:
And fixing his mind on Kṛṣṇa, intent on him, he should utter this: / 'O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, you are compassionate; become the refuge of the refuge-less!
Have mercy, O Madhusūdana, on those submerged in the ocean of worldly existence!' / Having thus propitiated him, he should observe a fast, with a controlled mind.
And on the previous day, and on the next day, having partaken of a bovine product once, / bathed, having worshipped, he should recite the name 'Kṛṣṇa' again.
And in the vow, he should pour a stream of water at the feet of the god. / He should worship likewise in Caitra and Vaiśākha, and in Jyeṣṭha.
A man indeed attains an excellent destiny in the mortal world, O Dālbhya, / and likewise at the time of death he attains remembrance of Kṛṣṇa.
In Āṣāḍha, Śrāvaṇa, and in the month of Bhādrapada, / and likewise in the month of Āśvayuja, a man according to this rule,
having fasted, having worshipped, should worship [saying] 'Keśava'. / Purified by consuming cow urine, he goes to the heavenly world.
He attains the worship of the unperishing Lord of the worlds, / and likewise at the time of death he attains remembrance of Keśava.

text_mt:
He who consumes milk and performs this rule as prescribed / properly for the four months beginning with Kārtika,
by that very rule, O brahmin, he should recite the name of Viṣṇu. / He goes to the world of Viṣṇu and remembers imperishable Viṣṇu.
Each month he should give a donation to twice-borns according to rule; / and when the four months are complete, recitation and listening to meritorious [texts] [should be done].
Or else he should cause singing for Vāsudeva to be performed. / Thus he attains an exalted destination through the praising of gods and men.
The fast-breaking which was described to you is to be performed for four months; / by it he attains sovereignty and imperishable pleasures.
By the second [fast-breaking], a man obtains pleasures belonging to Indra; / by the third fast-breaking, he likewise attains the world of Viṣṇu.
Thus this supreme ritual, which brings about a good destiny / and gives satisfaction to Kṛṣṇa, has been declared to men, O tiger among twice-borns.

That man who, possessing faith, fasts on this Sugatidvādaśī, / or likewise a woman, attains various [favourable] destinies.
This lunar day, destroying sin, most auspicious, granting heaven and making heaven, is thus described / for the sake of worshipping the god Viṣṇu, lord of the thirty gods, O one revered by hosts of twice-borns.

At death, one attains mindfulness of the god, and then also reaches a state / agreeable to the mind, O best of the twice-born; then in time one attains union with Janārdana.
Pulastya said: / Listen, O Dālbhya, to this supreme desire-granting observance that bestows offspring upon men, / fasting during which, no interruption of the ancestral rice-ball occurs.
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Caitra, having bathed with a controlled mind, / a man, having worshipped Kṛṣṇa, performs the worship of Devakī.
Fasting, reciting the name of Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the world, / whether seated, walking, or bathed, during sneezing, stumbling, and the like,
and during the worship of Kṛṣṇa, he should proclaim it seven times. / He must not converse with heretics, those living outside prescribed duties, or non-believers.
Then at dawn, having bathed, given a sacrificial fee to a brahmin, / and having performed the worship of Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the world, he should eat.
And likewise in Vaiśākha and Jyeṣṭha: this is indeed a three-month breaking of the fast. / Having fasted, one should bathe Hari, the Lord of the god of gods, with ghee.

In Āṣāḍha and Śrāvaṇa, and likewise in the month of Bhādrapada, / the second is fasted; one should bathe Hari with ghee.
In Āṣāḍha and Śrāvaṇa, and likewise in the month of Bhādrapada, / the second is fasted; the breaking of the fast should be as before.
In Āśvina, Kārtika, and Mārgaśīrṣa is the third breaking of the fast; / in Pauṣa, Māgha, and Phālguna is the fourth, O best of the twice-born.
When each breaking of the fast is complete, one should bathe Hari with ghee; / one should likewise give ghee to brahmins at each breaking of the fast.

Pulastya said: / In the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, the blessed Madhusūdana / observes his own cosmic power and yogic sleep on the body of the serpent.

Pulastya said:
In the month of Proṣṭhapada, during the bright fortnight on the twelfth day, one should bow to him who sleeps upon the waters, / and having worshipped Ananta with flowers, incense, and other offerings, being pure,
not conversing with heretics and the like, self-restrained in vows, / having given a water-cow to a twice-born, one should eat at night, restrained in speech.
Standing, staying, and walking, and during sneezing, stumbling, and the like, / a man should constantly remember and recite the name of Ananta.
By this very rule successively for twelve months indeed, / having fasted, when the breaking of the fast is complete, he should give a sacrificial fee to brahmins.
Having performed this beloved observance for twelve [months], one obtains endless fruits, O brahmin; / and by worshipping Ananta through vows and observances properly performed, there is no doubt in this.

3.220
Pulastya said:
In the month of Pauṣa, on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight, having Śakra as its deity, / one should first worship Viṣṇu in conjunction with the asterism.
From that time forward, O lord of brahmins, month by month he worships Janārdana / fasting, until a year has passed.
Now I shall declare the gift on that charming lunar day, month by month according to the prescribed rule; / learn all of that as it is declared, performed properly and in order according to tradition:
ghee, likewise rice and barley, gold, barley-food, water, gold with a drink, / an umbrella, milk-rice rich in jaggery and molasses, a garland and sandalwood, and a garment in succession;
cow-urine, water, ghee, meat and greens, dūrvā grass, curd, rice, barley, and sesame seeds, / water heated by the sun’s rays, quick darbha grass, and milk: he should consume [these] month by month in order.
One obtains birth in an eminent family, full of wealth and grain, / discerning in all adversity, with unimpaired faculties, and becomes free from illness, intelligent, and happy.
The dialogue between Pulastya and Dālbhya is ended.

स्वल्पवित्तस्य धर्मज्ञ बहिर्वेदि प्रकीर्तितम् .. 3..
text_mt: Sacrifice within the altar-ground is proclaimed for one of abundant wealth; / for one of little wealth, O knower of dharma, [worship] outside the altar-ground is proclaimed.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpānnagandhanaivedyastotrādhyayanakarmaṇā ..
dhūpadīpanamaskārairnityaṃ pūjyā divaukasaḥ ..4..
meaning:
पुष्पान्नगन्धनैवेद्यस्तोत्राध्ययनकर्मणा ..
धूपदीपनमस्कारैर्नित्यं पूज्या दिवौकसः ..4..
text_mt: The gods should always be worshipped with flowers, food, fragrant scents, and food-offerings, / with hymns and acts of recitation, and with incense, lamps, and obeisances.

sanskrit_iast:
tato'pi niyamaiścaiva brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ ..
bahiḥ śuśrūṣayā caiva dānena vividhena ca.. 5 ..
meaning:
ततोऽपि नियमैश्चैव ब्राह्मणानां च तर्पणैः ..
बहिः शुश्रूषया चैव दानेन विविधेन च.. 5 ..
text_mt: Further, by observances, by satisfying the brahmins, / by service outside, and by various forms of giving,

sanskrit_iast:
sadaiva pūjitā devāstuṣṭimāyānti yādava ..
svesve kālaviśeṣeṇa kālaḥ pūrvodito mayā .. 6 ..
meaning:
सदैव पूजिता देवास्तुष्टिमायान्ति यादव ..
स्वेस्वे कालविशेषेण कालः पूर्वोदितो मया .. 6 ..
text_mt: gods worshipped at all times attain satisfaction, O Yādava, / according to their respective particular times; the time has been declared by me previously.

sanskrit_iast:
vajra uvāca ..
devatāḥ kāśca kasminnu kāle saṃpūjayetsadā ..
devatāpūjane kāryaṃ viśeṣānmama kīrtaya .. 7 ..
meaning:
वज्र उवाच ..
देवताः काश्च कस्मिन्नु काले संपूजयेत्सदा ..
देवतापूजने कार्यं विशेषान्मम कीर्तय .. 7 ..
text_mt:
Vajra said:
Which deities should one always worship, and at what time? / Tell me specifically the duty in worshipping the deities.

sanskrit_iast:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
kālaṃ tathāhaṃ vakṣyāmi devatāpūjane pṛthak ..
saṃvatsareṇa dharmajña sopavāsasya sarvadā .. 8 ..
meaning:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ..
कालं तथाहं वक्ष्यामि देवतापूजने पृथक् ..
संवत्सरेण धर्मज्ञ सोपवासस्य सर्वदा .. 8 ..
text_mt:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I shall speak likewise of the specific time in worshipping the deities / over the course of a year, O knower of dharma, for one who constantly fasts.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmāṇaṃ pūjayeddevaṃ satataṃ prathamehani ..
pakṣadvaye mahābhāga pañcadaśyāmupoṣitaḥ .. 9 ..
meaning:
ब्रह्माणं पूजयेद्देवं सततं प्रथमेहनि ..
पक्षद्वये महाभाग पञ्चदश्यामुपोषितः .. 9 ..
text_mt: One should worship the god Brahmā continually on the first day; / fasting on the fifteenth day in both fortnights, O fortunate one,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvatsareṇa dharmajña vidyādbahusuvarṇakam..
haṃsayuktena yānena brahmaloke ca gacchati..3.221.10..
meaning:
संवत्सरेण धर्मज्ञ विद्याद्बहुसुवर्णकम्..
हंसयुक्तेन यानेन ब्रह्मलोके च गच्छति..3.221.10..
text_mt: in the course of a year, O knower of dharma, one acquires much gold; / and he goes to the world of Brahmā in a vehicle harnessed with swans.

sanskrit_iast:
caitramāsasya yā śukle prathamā pratipadbhavet.
tadahni brahmaṇaḥ kṛtvā sopavāsastu pūjanam..11..
meaning:
चैत्रमासस्य या शुक्ले प्रथमा प्रतिपद्भवेत्.
तदह्नि ब्रह्मणः कृत्वा सोपवासस्तु पूजनम्..11..
text_mt: That which is the first lunar day of the bright fortnight in the month of Caitra: / having performed the worship of Brahmā on that day while fasting,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvatsaramavāpnoti saukhyāni bhṛgunandana ..
kālasyāvayavāḥ sarve tasminnahani pūjitāḥ..12.
meaning:
संवत्सरमवाप्नोति सौख्यानि भृगुनन्दन ..
कालस्यावयवाः सर्वे तस्मिन्नहनि पूजिताः..12.
text_mt: one obtains pleasures for a whole year, O son of Bhṛgu; / all the divisions of time are worshipped on that day.

sanskrit_iast:
graharkṣāṇi ca dharmajña saukhyaṃ dadyādanuttamam..
saṃvatsarādhipaṃ nāgaṃ tasminnahani pūjayet..13..
meaning:
ग्रहर्क्षाणि च धर्मज्ञ सौख्यं दद्यादनुत्तमम्..
संवत्सराधिपं नागं तस्मिन्नहनि पूजयेत्..13..
text_mt: The planets and lunar mansions, O knower of dharma, grant unequalled happiness; / one should worship the serpent who is the lord of the year on that day.

sanskrit_iast:
grahebhyaḥ saukhyamāpnoti svāsthyamagryaṃ tathaiva ca..
tatrāhni brahmaṇā sṛṣṭaṃ trailokyaṃ prathamaṃ dvija..14..
meaning:
ग्रहेभ्यः सौख्यमाप्नोति स्वास्थ्यमग्र्यं तथैव च..
तत्राह्नि ब्रह्मणा सृष्टं त्रैलोक्यं प्रथमं द्विज..14..
text_mt: He obtains happiness from the planets and likewise foremost health; / on that day, the three worlds were first created by Brahmā, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣaṃ prajāpatiṃ nityaṃ dvitīyāyāmathārcayet ..
phalamāpnoti dharmajña gosavasya na saṃśayaḥ ..15..
meaning:
दक्षं प्रजापतिं नित्यं द्वितीयायामथार्चयेत् ..
फलमाप्नोति धर्मज्ञ गोसवस्य न संशयः ..15..
text_mt: Then one should always worship Dakṣa Prajāpati on the second [lunar day]; / he obtains the fruit of a Gosava sacrifice, O knower of dharma, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā nāsatyayoḥ kṛtvā tasminnahani pūjanam ..
nityamārogyamāpnoti tathā rūpaṃ ca bhārgava..16..
meaning:
तथा नासत्ययोः कृत्वा तस्मिन्नहनि पूजनम् ..
नित्यमारोग्यमाप्नोति तथा रूपं च भार्गव..16..
text_mt: Likewise, having performed the worship of the two Nāsatyas on that day, / he constantly obtains health and also beauty, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast:
śuklapakṣadvitīyāyāṃ bālacandrasya pūjanam..
kṛtvā dattvā ca lavaṇaṃ prāgrātrau subhago bhavet..17..
meaning:
शुक्लपक्षद्वितीयायां बालचन्द्रस्य पूजनम्..
कृत्वा दत्त्वा च लवणं प्राग्रात्रौ सुभगो भवेत्..17..
text_mt: Having performed the worship of the crescent moon on the second day of the bright fortnight / and having given salt early at night, he becomes fortunate.

sanskrit_iast:
sādhyā dvādaśa ye proktāsteṣāṃ kṛtvā tu pūjanam..
tṛtīyasyāṃ mahābhāga dvādaśāhaphalaṃ labhet..18..
meaning:
साध्या द्वादश ये प्रोक्तास्तेषां कृत्वा तु पूजनम्..
तृतीयस्यां महाभाग द्वादशाहफलं लभेत्..18..
text_mt: Having performed the worship of the Sādhyas who are proclaimed as twelve, / on the third [lunar day], O fortunate one, he obtains the fruit of a twelve-day sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
tṛtīyāyāṃ tathābhyarcya brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān..
pṛthakpṛthaṅmahābhāga trivargaphalabhāgbhaveta .. .. 19..
meaning:
तृतीयायां तथाभ्यर्च्य ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरान्..
पृथक्पृथङ्महाभाग त्रिवर्गफलभाग्भवेत .. .. 19..
text_mt: Likewise, having worshipped Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara on the third [lunar day] / separately, O fortunate one, he partakes of the fruit of the threefold aims of life.

sanskrit_iast:
trīṃllokāṃśca tadā rāma samyaksaṃpūjayennaraḥ ..
aiśvaryaṃ mahadāpnoti gatimagryāṃ ca vindati ..3.221.20..
meaning:
त्रींल्लोकांश्च तदा राम सम्यक्संपूजयेन्नरः ..
ऐश्वर्यं महदाप्नोति गतिमग्र्यां च विन्दति ..3.221.20..
text_mt: Then, O Rāma, if a person properly worships the three worlds, / he obtains great sovereignty and attains the foremost destination.

sanskrit_iast:
tṛtīyā śrāvaṇe kṛṣṇā yā syācchravaṇasaṃyutā ..
tasyāṃ saṃpūjya govindaṃ puṣṭimagryāmavāpnuyāt ..21..
meaning:
तृतीया श्रावणे कृष्णा या स्याच्छ्रवणसंयुता ..
तस्यां संपूज्य गोविन्दं पुष्टिमग्र्यामवाप्नुयात् ..21..
text_mt: The third [lunar day] in the dark [fortnight] of Śrāvaṇa that is conjoined with Śravaṇā— / having worshipped Govinda on that day, one obtains the foremost prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
vaiśākhaśuklapakṣe tu tṛtīyāyāmupoṣitaḥ..
akṣayaṃ phalamāpnoti sarvasya sukṛtasya tu .. 22..
meaning:
वैशाखशुक्लपक्षे तु तृतीयायामुपोषितः..
अक्षयं फलमाप्नोति सर्वस्य सुकृतस्य तु .. 22..
text_mt: Fasting on the third [lunar day] in the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, / one obtains imperishable fruit for all of one's good deeds.

sanskrit_iast:
sā tathā kṛttikopetā viśeṣeṇa ca pūjitā ..
tatra dattaṃ hutaṃ taptaṃ sarvaṃ saphalamucyate .. 23 ..
meaning:
सा तथा कृत्तिकोपेता विशेषेण च पूजिता ..
तत्र दत्तं हुतं तप्तं सर्वं सफलमुच्यते .. 23 ..
text_mt: When it is also joined with Kṛttikā and specially worshipped, / whatever is given, offered into the fire, or performed as austerity there is said to be completely fruitful.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣayā sā tithiryasmāttasmātsukṛtamakṣayam ..
akṣataiḥ pūjyate viṣṇustena sāpyakṣatā smṛtā ..24..
meaning:
अक्षया सा तिथिर्यस्मात्तस्मात्सुकृतमक्षयम् ..
अक्षतैः पूज्यते विष्णुस्तेन साप्यक्षता स्मृता ..24..
text_mt: Because that lunar day is imperishable (akṣayā), the merit is therefore imperishable. / Viṣṇu is worshipped with unbroken grains (akṣata), and therefore it is also known as Akṣatā.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣataistu naraḥ snāto viṣṇordattvā tathākṣatān ..
saktūnsusaṃskṛtām̐ścaiva hutvā caiva tathākṣatān .. 25..
meaning:
अक्षतैस्तु नरः स्नातो विष्णोर्दत्त्वा तथाक्षतान् ..
सक्तून्सुसंस्कृताम्̐श्चैव हुत्वा चैव तथाक्षतान् .. 25..
text_mt: A man bathed with unbroken grains, having offered unbroken grains to Viṣṇu, / and well-prepared barley meal, and having also offered unbroken grains into the fire,

sanskrit_iast:
vipreṣu dattvā tāneva tathā saktuṃ susaṃskṛtam ..
yavānnabhuṅ mahārāja phalamakṣayyamaśnute ..26 ..
meaning:
विप्रेषु दत्त्वा तानेव तथा सक्तुं सुसंस्कृतम् ..
यवान्नभुङ् महाराज फलमक्षय्यमश्नुते ..26 ..
text_mt: and having given those very things to brahmins, as well as well-prepared barley meal, / eating barley food, O great king, enjoys imperishable fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
ekāmapyuktavatkṛtvā tṛtīyāṃ bhṛgunandana ..
eṣāmabdatṛtīyānāṃ sarvāsāṃ tatphalaṃ bhavet ..27..
meaning:
एकामप्युक्तवत्कृत्वा तृतीयां भृगुनन्दन ..
एषामब्दतृतीयानां सर्वासां तत्फलं भवेत् ..27..
text_mt: Having observed even a single third [lunar day] as described, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / that [very] fruit of all these third [lunar days] of the year is obtained.

sanskrit_iast:
proktāstu bhṛgavo nāma devā dvādaśa ye purā ..
caturthyāṃ pūjanaṃ teṣāṃ kṛtvā divamavāpnuyāt .. 28 ..
meaning:
प्रोक्तास्तु भृगवो नाम देवा द्वादश ये पुरा ..
चतुर्थ्यां पूजनं तेषां कृत्वा दिवमवाप्नुयात् .. 28 ..
text_mt: Those twelve gods who were declared of old to be named Bhṛgus— / having worshipped them on the fourth [lunar day], one attains heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
yamasya pūjanaṃ kṛtvā caturthyāmeva dhārmikaḥ ..
nāpnoti nārakaṃ duḥkhaṃ tuṣṭe ravisute naraḥ .. 29 ..
meaning:
यमस्य पूजनं कृत्वा चतुर्थ्यामेव धार्मिकः ..
नाप्नोति नारकं दुःखं तुष्टे रविसुते नरः .. 29 ..
text_mt: Having performed the worship of Yama on the fourth [lunar day], a righteous / man does not incur infernal suffering when the son of Ravi is pleased.

sanskrit_iast:
vināyakamathābhyarcya caturthyāṃ yadunandana ..
sarvavighnavinirmuktaḥ kāryasiddhimavāpnuyāt .. 3.221.30 ..
meaning:
विनायकमथाभ्यर्च्य चतुर्थ्यां यदुनन्दन ..
सर्वविघ्नविनिर्मुक्तः कार्यसिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् .. 3.221.30 ..
text_mt: Then, having worshipped Vināyaka on the fourth [lunar day], O delight of the Yadus, / freed from all obstacles, one attains success in one's undertakings.

sanskrit_iast:
nidrāṃ ratiṃ tathā śraddhāṃ kīrtiṃ medhāṃ sarasvatīm ..
prajñāṃ tuṣṭiṃ tathā kāntiṃ tasminnahani pūjayet .. 31 ..
meaning:
निद्रां रतिं तथा श्रद्धां कीर्तिं मेधां सरस्वतीम् ..
प्रज्ञां तुष्टिं तथा कान्तिं तस्मिन्नहनि पूजयेत् .. 31 ..
text_mt: Nidrā, Rati, and likewise Śraddhā, Kīrti, Medhā, Sarasvatī, / Prajñā, Tuṣṭi, and likewise Kānti one should worship on that day.

sanskrit_iast:
tatprasādamavāpnoti yatheṣṭaṃ manujottama ..
vidyākāmo viśeṣeṇa pūjayettu sarasvatīm .. 32 ..
meaning:
तत्प्रसादमवाप्नोति यथेष्टं मनुजोत्तम ..
विद्याकामो विशेषेण पूजयेत्तु सरस्वतीम् .. 32 ..
text_mt: One attains their grace according to one's desire, O best of men. / One desiring learning, in particular, should worship Sarasvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
devānāṃ mātaraḥ sarvāstathā tatrāhni pūjitāḥ ..
sarvakāmapradā jñeyāḥ puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ .. 33 ..
meaning:
देवानां मातरः सर्वास्तथा तत्राह्नि पूजिताः ..
सर्वकामप्रदा ज्ञेयाः पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः .. 33 ..
text_mt: All the Mothers of the gods worshipped on that day / should be known as granting all desires to a wise man.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcamyāṃ pūjanaṃ kṛtvā tathā candramaso naraḥ ..
saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti yaśaścāgryaṃ ca vindati .. 34 ..
meaning:
पञ्चम्यां पूजनं कृत्वा तथा चन्द्रमसो नरः ..
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति यशश्चाग्र्यं च विन्दति .. 34 ..
text_mt: Having performed worship of the Moon on the fifth [lunar day], a man / attains great good fortune and gains foremost fame.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcamyāṃ pṛthivīṃ devīṃ tathā sampūjayennaraḥ ..
tāmevāpnotyayatnena nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 35 ..
meaning:
पञ्चम्यां पृथिवीं देवीं तथा सम्पूजयेन्नरः ..
तामेवाप्नोत्ययत्नेन नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 35 ..
text_mt: A man should likewise worship the goddess Earth on the fifth [lunar day]; / he gains her without effort—no doubt should be entertained on this point.

sanskrit_iast:
viśvedevāstu ye proktāḥ pūrvameva mayā daśa ..
teṣāṃ sampūjanaṃ kṛtvā pañcamyāṃ divamāpnuyāt .. 36 ..
meaning:
विश्वेदेवास्तु ये प्रोक्ताः पूर्वमेव मया दश ..
तेषां सम्पूजनं कृत्वा पञ्चम्यां दिवमाप्नुयात् .. 36 ..
text_mt: The Viśvedevas who were previously declared by me to be ten— / having worshipped them on the fifth [lunar day], one attains heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭagandharvamabhyarcya pañcamyāṃ subhago bhavet ..
tathā citrarathaṃ teṣāṃ rājānaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 37 ..
meaning:
इष्टगन्धर्वमभ्यर्च्य पञ्चम्यां सुभगो भवेत् ..
तथा चित्ररथं तेषां राजानं च विशेषतः .. 37 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped one's chosen Gandharva on the fifth [lunar day], one becomes fortunate, / and especially their king Citraratha.

sanskrit_iast:
devabhāryāṃ tathā bhāryāṃ sampūjya subhago bhavet ..
iṣṭamapsarasaṃ caiva tathā rūpamavāpnuyāt .. 38 ..
meaning:
देवभार्यां तथा भार्यां सम्पूज्य सुभगो भवेत् ..
इष्टमप्सरसं चैव तथा रूपमवाप्नुयात् .. 38 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped a divine consort and one's wife, one becomes fortunate; / and [worshipping] one's chosen Apsaras, one likewise gains beauty.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭaṃ nāgaṃ tathābhyarcya śriyamāpnotyanuttamām ..
vāruṇaiḥ puṣkarasyārcāṃ pañcamyāṃ yaḥ samācaret .. 39 ..
meaning:
इष्टं नागं तथाभ्यर्च्य श्रियमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ..
वारुणैः पुष्करस्यार्चां पञ्चम्यां यः समाचरेत् .. 39 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped one's chosen Nāga, one attains unexcelled fortune. / Whoever performs the worship of Puṣkara with [mantras] sacred to Varuṇa on the fifth [lunar day]

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya somayajñaphalaṃ bhavet ..
tathā ca pūjayanrājaṃstathā vai nalakūbaram .. 3.221.40 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य सोमयज्ञफलं भवेत् ..
तथा च पूजयन्राजंस्तथा वै नलकूबरम् .. 3.221.40 ..
text_mt: obtains the fruit of a Soma sacrifice, enriched with all desires; / and likewise, O king, worshipping Nalakūbara.

sanskrit_iast:
śriyaḥ sampūjanaṃ kṛtvā pañcamyāṃ prayataḥ sadā ..
śriyamāpnoti vipulāṃ matimagryāṃ ca vindati .. 41..
meaning:
श्रियः सम्पूजनं कृत्वा पञ्चम्यां प्रयतः सदा ..
श्रियमाप्नोति विपुलां मतिमग्र्यां च विन्दति .. 41..
text_mt: Having performed the worship of Śrī on the fifth [lunar day], always restrained, / one attains abundant fortune and gains the foremost intellect.

sanskrit_iast: caitraśuklasya pañcamyāṃ pūjayitvā tathā śriyam..42..
meaning: चैत्रशुक्लस्य पञ्चम्यां पूजयित्वा तथा श्रियम्..42..
text_mt: Having worshipped Śrī on the fifth [lunar day] of the bright [fortnight] of Caitra,

sanskrit_iast:
sakṛdevāpnuyādrājanphalaṃ saṃvatsaroditam ..
sarvasyāṃ nṛpa pañcamyāṃ ratiṃ prītiṃ sarasvatīm..43..
meaning:
सकृदेवाप्नुयाद्राजन्फलं संवत्सरोदितम् ..
सर्वस्यां नृप पञ्चम्यां रतिं प्रीतिं सरस्वतीम्..43..
text_mt: even once, O king, one obtains the fruit proclaimed for a whole year. / On every fifth [lunar day], O king, [worshipping] Rati, Prīti, Sarasvatī,

sanskrit_iast:
umāṃ menāṃ bhadrakālīṃ tathā kātyāyanīmapi ..
dhṛtiṃ svāhāṃ sudhāmṛddhimanusūyāṃ tathā kṣamām..44..
meaning:
उमां मेनां भद्रकालीं तथा कात्यायनीमपि ..
धृतिं स्वाहां सुधामृद्धिमनुसूयां तथा क्षमाम्..44..
text_mt: Umā, Menā, Bhadrakālī, and likewise Kātyāyanī, / Dhṛti, Svāhā, Sudhā, Ṛddhi, Anusūyā, and likewise Kṣamā,

sanskrit_iast:
subhīmāṃ devasenāṃ ca velāṃ jyotsnāṃ tathā śacīm..
gaurīṃ varuṇapatnīṃ ca yamapatnīṃ tathaiva ca .. 45 ..
meaning:
सुभीमां देवसेनां च वेलां ज्योत्स्नां तथा शचीम्..
गौरीं वरुणपत्नीं च यमपत्नीं तथैव च .. 45 ..
text_mt: Subhīmā, Devasenā, Velā, Jyotsnā, and Śacī, / Gaurī, the wife of Varuṇa, and the wife of Yama,

sanskrit_iast: dhūmorṇāṃ sumahābhāgāṃ mṛtyucchāyāṃ tathaiva ca .. 46 ..
meaning: धूमोर्णां सुमहाभागां मृत्युच्छायां तथैव च .. 46 ..
text_mt: the exceedingly fortunate Dhūmorṇā, and likewise Mṛtyucchāyā,

sanskrit_iast:
abhīṣṭāṃ devajananīṃ devapatnīṃ tathaiva ca ..
pūjayankāmamāpnoti tasyā hyekamasaṃśayam ..
airāvataṃ vā garuḍamuccaiḥśravasameva vā..47..
meaning:
अभीष्टां देवजननीं देवपत्नीं तथैव च ..
पूजयन्काममाप्नोति तस्या ह्येकमसंशयम् ..
ऐरावतं वा गरुडमुच्चैःश्रवसमेव वा..47..
text_mt: the beloved mother of the gods, and likewise the wife of a god— / worshipping [her], one undoubtedly attains one desire from her. / Or Airāvata, or Garuḍa, or Uccaiḥśravas,

sanskrit_iast:
harasya vṛṣabhaṃ caiva śastrāṇyastrāṇi yāni ca..
tadā sampūjayanrājā vijayaṃ tamupāśnute ..48..
meaning:
हरस्य वृषभं चैव शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि यानि च..
तदा सम्पूजयन्राजा विजयं तमुपाश्नुते ..48..
text_mt: or the bull of Hara, and whatever weapons and missiles there be— / worshipping them at that time, a king attains that victory.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā bhādrapade māsi śuklapakṣasya pañcamīm ..
nāgasaṃpūjanaṃ kṛtvā dhanabhāgī bhavennaraḥ .. 49 ..
meaning:
तथा भाद्रपदे मासि शुक्लपक्षस्य पञ्चमीम् ..
नागसंपूजनं कृत्वा धनभागी भवेन्नरः .. 49 ..
text_mt: Likewise, having performed the worship of the Nāgas on the fifth [lunar day] of the bright fortnight / in the month of Bhādrapada, a man becomes a possessor of wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
kumāraśca tathā skando viśākhaśca guhastathā ..
caturātmā vinirdiṣṭo bhagavānkrauñcadāraṇaḥ.. 3.221.50 ..
meaning:
कुमारश्च तथा स्कन्दो विशाखश्च गुहस्तथा ..
चतुरात्मा विनिर्दिष्टो भगवान्क्रौञ्चदारणः.. 3.221.50 ..
text_mt: Kumāra, Skanda, Viśākha, and Guha— / the blessed cleaver of Mount Krauñca is declared as fourfold in nature.

sanskrit_iast:
tamabhyarcya naraḥ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ putrānāpnotyabhīpsitān ..
bālakānāṃ gṛhe śreyo naraḥ prāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 51 ..
meaning:
तमभ्यर्च्य नरः षष्ठ्यां पुत्रानाप्नोत्यभीप्सितान् ..
बालकानां गृहे श्रेयो नरः प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् .. 51 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped him on the sixth [lunar day], a man obtains the sons he desires; / a man undoubtedly attains welfare for the children in his house.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛtūnāṃ pūjanaṃ kṛtvā tatra kṣemamavāpnuyāt ..
skandapārśvacarānrājanbhīmapārśvacarāṃstathā .. 52 ..
meaning:
ऋतूनां पूजनं कृत्वा तत्र क्षेममवाप्नुयात् ..
स्कन्दपार्श्वचरान्राजन्भीमपार्श्वचरांस्तथा .. 52 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped the seasons, one obtains security therein. / [Worshipping] the attendants of Skanda, O king, and the attendants of Bhīma,

sanskrit_iast:
yamapārśvacarām̐ścaiva rogamuktimavāpnuyāt ..
kālapāśau tathābhyarcya jvaravyādhīśameva ca .. 53 ..
meaning:
यमपार्श्वचराम्̐श्चैव रोगमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् ..
कालपाशौ तथाभ्यर्च्य ज्वरव्याधीशमेव च .. 53 ..
text_mt: and the attendants of Yama, one obtains release from disease. / Having worshipped the two nooses of Kāla, and the lord of fevers and diseases,

sanskrit_iast:
rogamokṣamavāpnoti vāyuvahnīndavastathā ..
caitraṣaṣṭhyāṃ viśeṣeṇa skandamabhyarcayennaraḥ..54..
meaning:
रोगमोक्षमवाप्नोति वायुवह्नीन्दवस्तथा ..
चैत्रषष्ठ्यां विशेषेण स्कन्दमभ्यर्चयेन्नरः..54..
text_mt: one obtains release from disease; likewise Vāyu, Agni, and the Moon. / On the sixth [lunar day] of Caitra, a man should specially worship Skanda;

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvoktaphalamāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati ..
saptamyāṃ ca samabhyarcya sūryapatnīṃ suvarcalām ..55..
meaning:
पूर्वोक्तफलमाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति ..
सप्तम्यां च समभ्यर्च्य सूर्यपत्नीं सुवर्चलाम् ..55..
text_mt: he obtains the previously stated fruit and goes to the world of heaven. / And having worshipped Suvarcalā, the wife of Sūrya, on the seventh [lunar day],

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭānkāmānavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
devā ekonapañcāśanmaruto nāma kīrtitāḥ .. 56 ..
meaning:
इष्टान्कामानवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
देवा एकोनपञ्चाशन्मरुतो नाम कीर्तिताः .. 56 ..
text_mt: one obtains one's desired wishes—no doubt should be entertained on this point. / The forty-nine gods are celebrated as the Maruts by name;

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāṃ saṃpūjanaṃ kṛtvā saptamyāṃ divamāpnuyāt ..
iṣṭapūjāṃ ca śailasya tadā kṛtvā sukhī bhavet .. 57 ..
meaning:
तेषां संपूजनं कृत्वा सप्तम्यां दिवमाप्नुयात् ..
इष्टपूजां च शैलस्य तदा कृत्वा सुखी भवेत् .. 57 ..
text_mt: having worshipped them on the seventh [lunar day], one attains heaven. / And having performed the desired worship of a mountain at that time, one becomes happy.

sanskrit_iast:
pūjayitvā tathābhīṣṭāṃ saritaṃ puṇyabhāgbhavet ..
vahnisaṃpūjanaṃ kṛtvā vahniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet .. 58 ..
meaning:
पूजयित्वा तथाभीष्टां सरितं पुण्यभाग्भवेत् ..
वह्निसंपूजनं कृत्वा वह्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् .. 58 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped a desired river, one becomes a sharer in merit. / Having performed the worship of Agni, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyoḥ saṃpūjanaṃ kṛtvā prāpnoti paramāṅgatim ..
saṃpūjya ca ṛṣīnsapta somasaṃsthāstu ye smṛtāḥ .. 59 ..
meaning:
वायोः संपूजनं कृत्वा प्राप्नोति परमाङ्गतिम् ..
संपूज्य च ऋषीन्सप्त सोमसंस्थास्तु ये स्मृताः .. 59 ..
text_mt: Having performed the worship of Vāyu, one attains the supreme state. / And having worshipped the seven sages, who are commemorated as abiding in Soma,

sanskrit_iast:
sapta prāpnoti lokānvai gatimagryāṃ ca vindati ..
saptamyāṃ yaduśārdūla iṣṭamabhyarcayanmunim .. 3.221.60 ..
meaning:
सप्त प्राप्नोति लोकान्वै गतिमग्र्यां च विन्दति ..
सप्तम्यां यदुशार्दूल इष्टमभ्यर्चयन्मुनिम् .. 3.221.60 ..
text_mt: one attains the seven worlds and gains the foremost state. / Worshipping one's chosen sage on the seventh [lunar day], O tiger of the Yadus,

sanskrit_iast:
svādhyāyaphalamāpnoti tadvatsāphalyamaśnute ..
pūjayitvā samudrāṃśca drīpānatha tathā naraḥ .. 61 ..
meaning:
स्वाध्यायफलमाप्नोति तद्वत्साफल्यमश्नुते ..
पूजयित्वा समुद्रांश्च द्रीपानथ तथा नरः .. 61 ..
text_mt: one obtains the fruit of recitation of scripture, and likewise enjoys success. / And having worshipped the oceans and the continents, a man,

sanskrit_iast:
pātālānvā mahābhāga bhuvamāpnotyabhīpsitām ..
saptalokāṃstathā tatra pūjayitvā sukhī bhavet .. 62 ..
meaning:
पातालान्वा महाभाग भुवमाप्नोत्यभीप्सिताम् ..
सप्तलोकांस्तथा तत्र पूजयित्वा सुखी भवेत् .. 62 ..
text_mt: or the netherworlds, O fortunate one, attains his desired land. / Having worshipped the seven worlds there, one becomes happy,

sanskrit_iast:
teṣveva ca tathaivāgryāṃ gatimapratimāṃ labhet ..
gaṅgāṃ saptaprakārāṃ ca tathā devīṃ sarasvatīm .. 63 ..
meaning:
तेष्वेव च तथैवाग्र्यां गतिमप्रतिमां लभेत् ..
गङ्गां सप्तप्रकारां च तथा देवीं सरस्वतीम् .. 63 ..
text_mt: and in those very [worlds] one attains the foremost, matchless state. / [Worshipping] the sevenfold Gaṅgā and the goddess Sarasvatī,

sanskrit_iast:
saptayajñānavāpnoti naraḥ saṃpūjayandhruvam ..
ādityaṃ pūjayeddevaṃ śīghraṃ rogairvimucyate .. 64 ..
meaning:
सप्तयज्ञानवाप्नोति नरः संपूजयन्ध्रुवम् ..
आदित्यं पूजयेद्देवं शीघ्रं रोगैर्विमुच्यते .. 64 ..
text_mt: a man worshipping [them] surely attains the seven sacrifices. / One should worship the god Āditya; one is quickly freed from diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
saptamyāṃ yādavaśreṣṭha gatimagryāṃ ca vindati ..
evaṃ supūjanaṃ kṛtvā gatimagryāṃ tathā labhet .. 65 ..
meaning:
सप्तम्यां यादवश्रेष्ठ गतिमग्र्यां च विन्दति ..
एवं सुपूजनं कृत्वा गतिमग्र्यां तथा लभेत् .. 65 ..
text_mt: On the seventh [lunar day], O best of Yādavas, one gains the foremost state. / Having performed proper worship in this way, one likewise attains the foremost state.

sanskrit_iast:
jayantaṃ śakratanayaṃ pūjayitvā sukhī bhavet ..
aṣṭamyāṃ pūjanaṃ kṛtvā vasūnāṃ dharmasattama .. 66 ..
meaning:
जयन्तं शक्रतनयं पूजयित्वा सुखी भवेत् ..
अष्टम्यां पूजनं कृत्वा वसूनां धर्मसत्तम .. 66 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped Jayanta, the son of Śakra, one becomes happy. / Having performed the worship of the Vasus on the eighth [lunar day], O best of the righteous,

sanskrit_iast:
nākalokamavāpnoti gatimagryāṃ ca vindati ..
ekānaṃśāṃ tadā devīṃ tathā saṃpūjayennaraḥ .. 67 ..
meaning:
नाकलोकमवाप्नोति गतिमग्र्यां च विन्दति ..
एकानंशां तदा देवीं तथा संपूजयेन्नरः .. 67 ..
text_mt: he attains the heavenly world and finds the highest path. / If a man then likewise worships the goddess Ekānaṃśā,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute ..
mahādevaṃ samabhyarcya sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 68 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ..
महादेवं समभ्यर्च्य सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् .. 68 ..
text_mt: he enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice rich in all desires. / Having worshipped Mahādeva, he would obtain all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
vīrabhadraṃ sanaṃdīśaṃ laguḍeśaṃ tathaiva ca..
bhadrakālīṃ tathābhyarcya navamyāṃ yadunandana .. 69 ..
meaning:
वीरभद्रं सनंदीशं लगुडेशं तथैव च..
भद्रकालीं तथाभ्यर्च्य नवम्यां यदुनन्दन .. 69 ..
text_mt: Having likewise worshipped Vīrabhadra, together with Nandin and Laguḍeśa, / and Bhadrakālī on the ninth [lunar day], O joy of the Yadus,

sanskrit_iast:
kāmamekamavāpnoti yaṃ kañcinmanasepsitam ..
catuṣpatheṣu ramyeṣu tathaivāṭṭālakeṣu ca .. 3.221.70 ..
meaning:
काममेकमवाप्नोति यं कञ्चिन्मनसेप्सितम् ..
चतुष्पथेषु रम्येषु तथैवाट्टालकेषु च .. 3.221.70 ..
text_mt: he obtains a single desire, whatever is wished for in his mind. / At charming crossroads, and likewise on watchtowers,

sanskrit_iast:
giriśṛṅgeṣu ramyeṣu nadītīreṣu cāpyatha ..
guhāsu caiva ramyāsu piśācānāṃ baliṃ haret .. 71 ..
meaning:
गिरिशृङ्गेषु रम्येषु नदीतीरेषु चाप्यथ ..
गुहासु चैव रम्यासु पिशाचानां बलिं हरेत् .. 71 ..
text_mt: on lovely mountain peaks, and on riverbanks, / and in charming caves, one should offer an oblation for the piśācas.

sanskrit_iast:
śakrādīnāṃ ca devānāṃ ye ca pārśvacarāḥ surāḥ ..
teṣāṃ balimupākurvankṣemamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 72 ..
meaning:
शक्रादीनां च देवानां ये च पार्श्वचराः सुराः ..
तेषां बलिमुपाकुर्वन्क्षेममाप्नोति मानवः .. 72 ..
text_mt: And for the gods who are attendants of deities beginning with Śakra, / offering an oblation to them, a mortal attains security.

sanskrit_iast:
āyudhaṃ pūjayitvā ca tathā vijayamāpnuyāt ..
vidyāmāpnoti vipulāṃ pūjayitvā sarasvatīm .. 73 ..
meaning:
आयुधं पूजयित्वा च तथा विजयमाप्नुयात् ..
विद्यामाप्नोति विपुलां पूजयित्वा सरस्वतीम् .. 73 ..
text_mt: And having worshipped a weapon, he would likewise attain victory. / Having worshipped Sarasvatī, he attains extensive learning.

sanskrit_iast:
vidyākāmastu kurvīta tadā pustakapūjanam ..
tathaivāśvayuje śukle bhadrakālīṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 74 ..
meaning:
विद्याकामस्तु कुर्वीत तदा पुस्तकपूजनम् ..
तथैवाश्वयुजे शुक्ले भद्रकालीं विशेषतः .. 74 ..
text_mt: One who desires learning should then perform the worship of books; / likewise, in the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja, especially to Bhadrakālī.

sanskrit_iast:
navamyāṃ pūjayitvā tu sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..
daśamyāṃ pūjayanrājanviśvedevāṃstathā daśa .. 75 ..
meaning:
नवम्यां पूजयित्वा तु सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ..
दशम्यां पूजयन्राजन्विश्वेदेवांस्तथा दश .. 75 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped [her] on the ninth [lunar day], he would obtain all desires. / Worshipping the ten Viśvedevas on the tenth [lunar day], O king,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute ..
tadā saṃpūjayanrājaṃstathaiva ca diśo daśa .. 76 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ..
तदा संपूजयन्राजंस्तथैव च दिशो दश .. 76 ..
text_mt: he enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice rich in all desires. / Then worshipping, O king, likewise the ten directions,

sanskrit_iast:
kriyāsāphalyamāpnoti yatra yatrābhijāyate ..
dharmaṃ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ sarvasattvasukhāvaham .. 77 ..
meaning:
क्रियासाफल्यमाप्नोति यत्र यत्राभिजायते ..
धर्मं संपूज्य देवेशं सर्वसत्त्वसुखावहम् .. 77 ..
text_mt: he attains success in his actions wherever he is born. / Having worshipped Dharma, lord of gods, bringer of happiness to all beings,

sanskrit_iast:
dharme matimavāpnoti dharmasāphalyameva ca..
ekādaśyāṃ tu saṃpūjya rudrānekādaśaiva ca .. 78 ..
meaning:
धर्मे मतिमवाप्नोति धर्मसाफल्यमेव च..
एकादश्यां तु संपूज्य रुद्रानेकादशैव च .. 78 ..
text_mt: he obtains a mind set on dharma and the success of dharma. / But having worshipped the eleven Rudras on the eleventh [lunar day],

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute..
tathā sarvagatānrudrāṃstadā sarvatra pūjayet .. 79 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते..
तथा सर्वगतान्रुद्रांस्तदा सर्वत्र पूजयेत् .. 79 ..
text_mt: he enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice rich in all desires. / Likewise, he should then worship everywhere the all-pervading Rudras;

sanskrit_iast:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti sarvagānaparājitān ..
tathā ca dvādaśādityāndvādaśyāṃ pūjayennaraḥ .. 3.221.80 ..
meaning:

Vajra said:
O venerable one, I wish to hear, with respect to the lights individually: / what should be done by one who has fasted, and what fruit would thereby arise?
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In this regard, understand this ancient tale as I recite it: / the dialogue between the overseer of wealth and Aṣṭāvakra.
Formerly, Aṣṭāvakra, who knew dharma, asked for the maiden Suprabhā, / [the daughter] of the foremost sage among the Bhārgavas, who was generous.
To the sage who possessed beauty and wealth, the sage said: / "If the nature of women is understood by you, O best among those who know dharma,
then I shall give to you my maiden whose eyes are like those of a young deer."
Aṣṭāvakra said:
"The nature of women has not been understood by me, O best of brahmins.

the one of great austerities reached the abode of the giver of wealth / on Kailāsa, the foremost of mountains, filled with all desires.

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed by the lord of wealth, the great sage replied: / "I wish to hear from you, O protector of wealth, the dharma that bears great fruit."
Vaiśravaṇa said:
"O brahmin, the worship of one's own deity at the light, / a dharma bearing great fruit, O twice-born—hear that from me as I speak.
On all the lights, O twice-born, fasting and with senses subdued, / having performed the worship of the deity, one enjoys the fruit as spoken.
Beginning with the bright [half] of Caitra, [undertaking] the unsurpassed vow on the light, / one should observe it on the light as desired for a year, free from sloth.
On the thirty lights, O foremost of twice-born, concentrated for one month, / eating only at night for a year, one should worship the deity of the light
every day, O greatly fortunate one; through that he attains his desire. / Whoever performs the unsurpassed vow of the light in the month of Āṣāḍha,
eating only at night every day and eating at a single time, O twice-born, / should avoid drinking water at any time other than the time of food.

Beginning from the light of Brahmā up to the light of the Cosmic Person, / when the light of the Cosmic Person is reached, having satisfied the brahmins
and given garments to the twice-born, as well as gold and silver, / he attains the world of heaven for a long time, O best of twice-born.
And attaining human birth, he is born handsome, / ever free from disease, strong, and also victorious over enemies and powerful.
He obtains foremost women, birth in an excellent family, / attains great good fortune, and also supreme charm,
friendship with the virtuous, knowledge, an excellent course in dharma, / foremost vehicles, and whatever else he desires.
The fruitful [vow] for one eating at night on the lights in a month, [worshipping] the best of gods, has been told to you, O twice-born; / hereafter I shall explain to you the distinct fruit for one who properly fasts on a light.

text_mt:
In the Saura, having worshipped the Sun, he would attain freedom from disease;
in the Candra, having worshipped the Moon, he would obtain supreme bliss.
In the Goroca, having worshipped the cow Surabhi, the mother of the world,
O knower of dharma, he obtains cows and her world as well.
Having reached the lunar day of Niyati, worshipping Niyati,
he attains long life wherever he is born.
In the Vaiṣṇava, having worshipped Viṣṇu, he attains the world of Viṣṇu;
in the Raudra, having worshipped Rudra, he attains his world.
A man obtains sons in the Kaumāra, worshipping Kumāra.
Having performed the worship of the ancestors in the Pitṛroca with concentration,
he obtains his desired worship and goes to the world of the ancestors.
In the Vāruṇa, worshipping the god Varuṇa, he obtains horses.
And in the Ananta, having worshipped Ananta, the supporter of the earth,
he attains the endless fruit of his well-performed deed.
In the Vāyavya, having worshipped Vāyu, he would obtain profit in trade;
in the Yāmya, having worshipped Yama, he meets with no fear from hell.

text_mt:
In the Sārasvata, having worshipped the goddess Sarasvatī, O twice-born one,
he obtains learning according to his wish, and through it becomes an eloquent speaker.
In the Śrīroca, having worshipped Śrī, he obtains radiant fortune.
And in my own roca, a man worshipping me
becomes a possessor of wealth wherever he is born.
In the Śailaroca, having worshipped the mountain, he becomes happy.
In the Bhūroca, having worshipped the Earth, he obtains an unsurpassed realm.
Having performed the worship of the Vedas in the Vedaroca with concentration,
a man obtains the Vedas, and a lord of men obtains sacrifices.
And in the Pauruṣa roca, worshipping the Cosmic Person in water,
he obtains all desires and finds the means to liberation.
Worshipping the ancient Cosmic Person who is devoid of form, devoid of touch, devoid of smell, devoid of taste, / and devoid of sound, he attains the path of liberation.

3.224
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having thus heard about the roca observance, having dined in the house of the Giver of Wealth,
having heard singing and instrumental music, and having watched charming dance,
having stayed there for one night, honoured by the Guardian of Wealth,
that righteous twice-born one went north towards the snowy mountain.
In a certain mountainous region he saw a beautiful house,
shining like a mass of moonbeams, endowed with all objects of desire.
In that house he then saw an old, beautiful woman,
adorned with all ornaments, surrounded by many
young, excellent women of charming attire;
and she honoured him in proper sequence with water for the feet and other rites.
And having anointed him with fragrant oil, she bathed him, O Yādava,
and with pleasant-to-the-touch breezes and various fragrances,
she smeared his limbs with fragrant sandalwood paste;
and she also honoured him with garments, ornaments, and garlands.

She fed him with food abundant in all desirable things,
and gave him fragrant, very charming betel.
In that wonderful house, she provided a very charming bed
with a white counterpane, variegated, well-spread, and exceedingly luxurious.
Having dismissed all those fawn-eyed women,
that passionate lady went to sleep there in another such [bed].
Then, late at night, under the pretext of cold, from her own bed
that fair-complexioned lady went to the bed of Aṣṭāvakra.
Seeing her arrived at his bed, he said, 'What is this?
O lady of sweet smiles, this is not appropriate for your age.
My celibacy is unbroken, and I avoid the wives of others.
Disregarding me so freely, what do you wish to do?'
The Direction said:
'O twice-born one, it is not only in youth that we women are fickle;
even at the end of life, impelled by desire, we indulge in fickleness.

text_mt:
I think you have not heard the nature of women, O best of the twice-born!
They are not attracted by age, nor by beauty, nor by lineage, nor by sacred learning.
Only rarely are they attracted by character, dress, wealth, or valour;
they desire any man as he comes to hand—such is the sacred tradition.'
For those women over whom great guard is kept, attach themselves to hunches and dwarfs,
or even to servants here, O descendant of Bhṛgu, [if they are] a man.
Fire is not sated with firewood, nor the great ocean with rivers,
nor Death with all beings, nor the fair-eyed women with men.
Smiling women destroy a family in mere sport;
for [faithfulness] to a woman’s lover by nature is hard to find, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
There is no secrecy, there is no opportunity, and there is no wooer;
by that, O knower of dharma, the chastity of women is maintained.
You were sent to me, O fortunate one, by that great-souled [sage],
to understand here the character of women as seen and heard by us.

Knowing this, however, you must not feel revulsion toward women;
for women are the very root of dharma, wealth, and pleasure.
Fire, food, and water are the causes of men’s sustenance,
and the very same are declared to be destroyers; so too women should be understood.
Just as there is no livelihood in the world without fire, food, and water,
so the householder stage of life cannot exist in any way without women.
Therefore they are to be guarded with wisdom, not harshly and not softly;
women are the root of misfortunes, and [yet] the means to the three aims of life.
One should not place trust in them, but should guard them like a jewel;
making them busy with household duties, they must be guarded by one who desires prosperity.
Having heard this, honored by that woman on the second day,
he went to the abode of Kubera, and from there to his [prospective] father-in-law's house.
Then, having approached his father-in-law, he reported everything to him;
and having heard about the conduct of women, he asked that brahmin:

“Has the desire to marry arisen, or has it not arisen? Tell me that.”
Having heard this, Aṣṭāvakra spoke the reply to the sage:
“This path is not secure, nor is another path to be found;
therefore, O knower of dharma, give me your daughter to be my wife.”
Hearing this, the sage, a descendant of Bhṛgu, gave him his daughter
on an auspicious lunar day, weekday, asterism, and hour.
Having obtained that dark-eyed wife, the root of the three aims of life,
he attained supreme satisfaction and rejoiced with her.
And then that great-souled man guarded her, keeping her constantly engaged in household duties;
and she, established in dharma and an exceedingly virtuous wife, served the foremost of twice-borns.

and having bathed with the Puruṣasūkta, with a restrained mind,
having performed libation with it, and recitation, O best of men,
a man should worship Janārdana as the Haṃsa in the center of an eight-petaled lotus,
honored with the Puruṣasūkta,
copiously with flowers, and likewise with incense, and thereafter with fruits,
and then with a lamp, O king, and after that with food offering.
Then one should worship the fire with the Puruṣasūkta;
and then, at the conclusion of the ritual, a milch cow should be given.
Having performed this supreme purifying observance for a year,
one obtains all desires, both celestial and human.
He attains the [merit of the] horse-sacrifice and obtains [that of the] Rājasūya;
having enjoyed pleasures, he subsequently attains liberation without doubt.
This is auspicious, supremely pure, increasing fortune and expanding dharma;
the supreme observance known as Haṃsavrata should be performed by a man in the world of men.

Vajra said:
What was spoken by that Swan to the self-composed sages? / Cut away this doubt of mine, O enhancer of the Bhṛgu lineage!
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Much was spoken by that Swan to the self-composed sages. / Therefore, I shall speak some of it; listen to it from me as I recite:
The sages said:
Declare the dharma of the castes and stages of life, O foremost of the twice-born, / as well as what may and may not be eaten, and likewise purity and ritual impurity.
The Swan said:
Sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, giving gifts, and acceptance of gifts from the distinguished, / teaching, and study are proclaimed as the duties of a brahmin.
Giving gifts, study, sacrifice, cattle rearing, commerce, / and freedom from malice, O knower of dharma, are considered the common dharma.

text_mt:
In direct order of the castes, the birth is equal to the mother. / All those born in reverse order become despised by the noble.
The Sūta, the Vaidehaka, and the Cāṇḍāla, O foremost twice-born, / are to be known as sons of a brahmin woman from kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra wombs [respectively].
The Māgadha and the Pukkasa are the sons of a kṣatriya woman by vaiśyas and śūdras; / and the Āyogava is proclaimed as the son of a śūdra upon a vaiśya woman.
Others born from intermixture upon intermixture cannot be enumerated. / Their marriage is with equals, not with the higher nor with the lower.
For Sūtas, horsemanship and charioteering; for Māgadhas, the act of praise; / the Vaideha shall subsist by stringed instruments; and for Pukkasas, the profession of a hunter;
for an Āyogava, handicrafts and appearing on stage; / for Caṇḍālas, untouchability and living on execution.
For those slain in battle for the sake of cows and brahmins, or entirely on account of women and children, / or while performing work for the sake of their master, success is ordained; there is no doubt in this.

3.228
The Swan said:
Having initiated the student, the teacher should instruct him in purity first of all, / in conduct, the fire ritual, and the twilight worship.
Rising early in the morning, purified, bathed, having made offerings to the sacred fire, / he should approach the teacher with restraint and perform salutation.
Permitted by the teacher, he should then undertake study. / Then he should perform the round of alms among brahmins according to rule.
He should not beg in the house of the teacher; he may eat with his permission. / He should engage in what is beneficial and dear to the teacher, with devotion, free from egotism.
He should avoid honey, meat, collyrium, ancestral rites, dancing, singing, rashness, / injury, speaking ill of others, and adornment.
He should always, with self-restraint, wear a girdle, an animal skin, and a staff. / Having cast them into the waters when ruined, he should wear others.
The wise student should always sleep on the ground, remain celibate and composed; / having taken such a vow, he should undertake the acquisition of the Veda.

3.229
The Swan said:
Then, living in the householder stage of life, having established the fires, knowing dharma, / having married according to rule, and having acquired wealth through dharma,
he should pursue the threefold aims of life there, and sacrifice with various sacrifices; / he should observe proper conduct, and also study the Veda.
He should perform the suspension of the Vedic verses at the end of the bright fortnight of Śrāvaṇa; / the commencement rite is prescribed on the Rohiṇī day of the month of Pauṣa.
After the suspension, he should never study the Veda [anew]; / even then, the study of the scriptures is prescribed for the twice-born.
Effort must be made in the worship of guests; this must be done by householders at all times. / No other dharma exists for him, O brahmins; this is proclaimed as his highest dharma.

A king is not defiled, nor is wind defiled, O best of the twice-born, nor indeed are flies; / and that which is unseen is declared undefiled, as are the rays of light that are seen.
3.232 / Haṃsa said: / Ritual impurity due to death is prescribed for ten days among sapiṇḍas / for a brahmin, O best of the twice-born; twelve days for a king [kṣatriya];
a fortnight is prescribed for a vaiśya, and a month for a śūdra, / both at birth and at death, for those desiring purity according to rule.
At the end of the first [period], complete purity is attained for an equal, O best of the twice-born; / and at the end of the second, it is always known to be for an unequal.
If within the ten days one hears of a death or a birth, / one remains impure only for whatever is left of the ten nights.
If the ten nights have passed, but within a year, / purification is ordained after three nights; but beyond that, upon merely bathing.
In the case of a miscarriage, purification takes as many nights as the months [of pregnancy]. / Up to the appearance of teeth, it is immediate; up to tonsure, it is one day and night;

three nights until the investiture of vows; beyond that, ten nights. / For girls, marriage is declared to take the place of the vows.
When they are married, no ritual impurity is prescribed on the father’s side. / For a maternal grandfather it is three nights; and for wives who have gone to another,
and for remarried women belonging to oneself, and for sons gone to another [caste or adopted], / and when a teacher has died, or the king of one's dwelling-land,
for the teacher’s wife and sons, for a pupil, and for fellow students, / ritual impurity lasts one night, and likewise when one who provides food has died.
For suicides killed by falling from a cliff, fire, starvation, or water, / and for outcasts, there is no ritual impurity; nor for those struck down by lightning or weapons.
Artisans, vow-keepers, students, the king’s treasury officials, and consecrated sacrificers / are declared not subject to ritual impurity, as are those executing the king’s command.
For an expired śūdra, after one year, purification is held [to take] five days; / purification takes twelve days when three years have elapsed;
when six years have passed, it is declared to take a month. / On following a corpse, bathing and consuming clarified butter bring purification.

Through the ten days of birth and death, there is no rite of purity, nor food to be offered to brahmins; / nor is there any fault in acceptance of gifts when the sacrificial fees consist of bipeds, quadrupeds, or grain.
3.233 / Haṃsa said: / The sacred part for the gods is considered to be at the tips of the fingers; that for the ancestors is at the base of the forefinger; / that for Brahmā is at the base of the thumb; and that for men is at the little finger.
One should sip water using the Brahmā part, gratify the gods with the divine part, / gratify the ancestors with the ancestral part, O knower of dharma, and likewise drink with the human part.
During the unalterable silent prayer, and likewise during sacrificing for oneself and officiating for others, / and during teaching and studying, a man must not be distracted in mind.
In these very duties and in the presence of teachers, / one should uncover the right hand and should not wear sandals.
The fire rite, the rite to the gods, ritual sipping, / dining, and the ancestral rite one should not perform with knees exposed.
One should never pronounce the name of an initiated person here, O sages; / nor should the teacher's name alone ever be uttered.

sanskrit_iast:
yācamānaṃ yathāśaktyā na kuryādvimukhaṃ kvacit ..
daivaṃ pūrvāhṇikaṃ kāryaṃ tvaparāhṇe tu paitṛkam .. 7 ..
atithīnāṃ tathā pūjā sarvakālaṃ vidhīyate ..
yadviśiṣṭatamaṃ loke yaccāsti dayitaṃ gṛhe .. 8 ..
tattadguṇavate deyaṃ tadevākṣayamicchatā ..
priyāṇi labhate loke priyadaḥ priyakṛttathā .. 9 ..
pratiśrutaṃ prayatnena dātavyamṛṣisattamāḥ ..
aprayacchaṃstadāpnoti mūrtīṣṭakṛtasaṃśayam .. 3.233.10 ..
narakaṃ mahadāpnoti śṛgālaścaiva jāyate ..
mātā pitā guruścaiva jyeṣṭho bhrātā tathā svasā .. 11 ..
pitṛvyo mātulaścaiva tathā mātṛṣvasā dvijāḥ ..
pitṛṣvasā tathā śvaśrūrgurubhāryā tathaiva ca.. .. 12 ..
mātāmahaśca śvaśuraḥ pūjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ ..
pratyutthānaśca kartavyaṃ teṣāṃ pūrvābhivādanam .. 13 ..
meaning:
याचमानं यथाशक्त्या न कुर्याद्विमुखं क्वचित् ..
दैवं पूर्वाह्णिकं कार्यं त्वपराह्णे तु पैतृकम् .. 7 ..
अतिथीनां तथा पूजा सर्वकालं विधीयते ..
यद्विशिष्टतमं लोके यच्चास्ति दयितं गृहे .. 8 ..
तत्तद्गुणवते देयं तदेवाक्षयमिच्छता ..
प्रियाणि लभते लोके प्रियदः प्रियकृत्तथा .. 9 ..
प्रतिश्रुतं प्रयत्नेन दातव्यमृषिसत्तमाः ..
अप्रयच्छंस्तदाप्नोति मूर्तीष्टकृतसंशयम् .. 3.233.10 ..
नरकं महदाप्नोति शृगालश्चैव जायते ..
माता पिता गुरुश्चैव ज्येष्ठो भ्राता तथा स्वसा .. 11 ..
पितृव्यो मातुलश्चैव तथा मातृष्वसा द्विजाः ..
पितृष्वसा तथा श्वश्रूर्गुरुभार्या तथैव च.. .. 12 ..
मातामहश्च श्वशुरः पूजनीयाः प्रयत्नतः ..
प्रत्युत्थानश्च कर्तव्यं तेषां पूर्वाभिवादनम् .. 13 ..
text_mt:
One should never turn away a petitioner according to one's capacity; / the rite for gods belongs to the morning, but that for ancestors to the afternoon.
Likewise, the honoring of guests is prescribed at all times; / whatever is most excellent in the world and whatever is cherished in the home,
all that should be given to the virtuous by one desiring it to be inexhaustible; / one who gives pleasant things and does pleasant things obtains pleasant things in this world.
What has been promised must be given with effort, O best of sages; / not giving it, he incurs uncertainty regarding what was offered to the deities;
he goes to a terrible hell and is reborn as a jackal. / Mother, father, teacher, elder brother, and sister,
paternal uncle, maternal uncle, and maternal aunt, O twice-born, / paternal aunt, mother-in-law, and teacher's wife likewise,
maternal grandfather, and father-in-law should be honored with effort; / one must rise up to greet them and offer obeisance first.

sanskrit_iast:
mātulaśca pitṛvyaśca yadā syātāṃ kanī yasau ..
nābhivādyāstu te pūrvaṃ pratyutthānaṃ tu kārayet .. 14 ..
ucchiṣṭo na spṛśecchīrṣaṃ sarve prāṇāstadāśrayāḥ ..
pūrvāṃ sandhyāṃ japaṃstiṣṭhedāsīnaścaiva paścimām .. 15 ..
meaning:
मातुलश्च पितृव्यश्च यदा स्यातां कनी यसौ ..
नाभिवाद्यास्तु ते पूर्वं प्रत्युत्थानं तु कारयेत् .. 14 ..
उच्छिष्टो न स्पृशेच्छीर्षं सर्वे प्राणास्तदाश्रयाः ..
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां जपंस्तिष्ठेदासीनश्चैव पश्चिमाम् .. 15 ..
text_mt:
When a maternal uncle and a paternal uncle are younger, / they should not be saluted first, but one should rise up to greet them.
One who is impure with food residue should not touch his head, for all the vital breaths reside there; / one should remain standing while reciting the morning twilight devotion, and seated during the evening one.

sanskrit_iast:
madhyandine niśākāle tvardharātre viśeṣataḥ ..
catuṣpathaṃ na seveta upasandhye tathaiva ca .. 16 ..
meaning:
मध्यन्दिने निशाकाले त्वर्धरात्रे विशेषतः ..
चतुष्पथं न सेवेत उपसन्ध्ये तथैव च .. 16 ..
text_mt: At midday, at night, and especially at midnight, / and likewise at the two twilights, one should not resort to a crossroads.

sanskrit_iast:
nāstikyaṃ vedanindāñca devatānāñca kutsanam ..
dveṣastambhātimānau ca taikṣṇyaṃ caiva vivarjayeta .. 17 ..
meaning:
नास्तिक्यं वेदनिन्दाञ्च देवतानाञ्च कुत्सनम् ..
द्वेषस्तम्भातिमानौ च तैक्ष्ण्यं चैव विवर्जयेत .. 17 ..
text_mt: Atheism, abuse of the Vedas, reviling the deities, / malice, obstinacy, excessive pride, and harshness one must avoid.

sanskrit_iast:
parasya daṇḍaṃ nodyacchetkruddho nainaṃ nipātayet ..
anyatra putrācchiṣyādvā śiṣṭyarthaṃ tāḍanaṃ smṛtam .. 18 ..
meaning:
परस्य दण्डं नोद्यच्छेत्क्रुद्धो नैनं निपातयेत् ..
अन्यत्र पुत्राच्छिष्याद्वा शिष्ट्यर्थं ताडनं स्मृतम् .. 18 ..
text_mt: One should not raise a staff against another, nor let it fall in anger; / except in the case of a son or a pupil, striking is taught for instruction alone.

sanskrit_iast:
na brāhmaṇaṃ parivadennakṣatrāṇi na nirdiśet ..
tithiṃ pakṣasya na brūyāttathāsyāyurna riṣyate .. 19 ..
meaning:
न ब्राह्मणं परिवदेन्नक्षत्राणि न निर्दिशेत् ..
तिथिं पक्षस्य न ब्रूयात्तथास्यायुर्न रिष्यते .. 19 ..
text_mt: One should not revile a brahmin, nor point out the lunar mansions; / one should not announce the lunar day of a fortnight; thus one's life is not impaired.

sanskrit_iast:
prāgastaśāyī na bhavenna cābhyudayaśāyikaḥ ..
avalokyo na cādarśo malino buddhimattaraiḥ .. 3.233.20 ..
meaning:
प्रागस्तशायी न भवेन्न चाभ्युदयशायिकः ..
अवलोक्यो न चादर्शो मलिनो बुद्धिमत्तरैः .. 3.233.20 ..
text_mt: One should not be asleep before sunset nor asleep at sunrise; / and a dirty mirror should not be looked into by the truly wise.

sanskrit_iast:
akṛtvā devatāpūjāṃ nānyaṃ gacchetkadācana ..
anyatra tu guruṃ vṛddhaṃ dhārmikaṃ vā vicakṣaṇam..21..
meaning:
अकृत्वा देवतापूजां नान्यं गच्छेत्कदाचन ..
अन्यत्र तु गुरुं वृद्धं धार्मिकं वा विचक्षणम्..21..
text_mt: Without having performed worship of the deities, one should never visit another; / except indeed a teacher, an elder, a righteous man, or a sage.

sanskrit_iast:
varjayecca tathā prājñāścāsanākarṣaṇaṃ sadā ..
snātvā tu nāvamājeta gātrāṇi tu vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 22..
meaning:
वर्जयेच्च तथा प्राज्ञाश्चासनाकर्षणं सदा ..
स्नात्वा तु नावमाजेत गात्राणि तु विचक्षणः .. 22..
text_mt: The wise should always avoid dragging a seat; / having bathed, a discerning person should not wipe his limbs.

sanskrit_iast:
viparyayaṃ na kurvīta vāsaso buddhimānnaraḥ ..
tathā nānyadhṛtaṃ dhāryaṃ na cāpadaśameva ca .. 23 ..
meaning:
विपर्ययं न कुर्वीत वाससो बुद्धिमान्नरः ..
तथा नान्यधृतं धार्यं न चापदशमेव च .. 23 ..
text_mt: A wise man should not reverse his garments; / nor should one wear clothes worn by another, nor one without a hem.

sanskrit_iast:
anyadeva bhavedvāsaḥ śayanīye dvijottamāḥ ..
anyadrathyāsu devānāṃ tvarcāyāmanyadeva tu .. 24 ..
meaning:
अन्यदेव भवेद्वासः शयनीये द्विजोत्तमाः ..
अन्यद्रथ्यासु देवानां त्वर्चायामन्यदेव तु .. 24 ..
text_mt: One garment should be worn for sleeping, O best of twice-born, / another on the streets, and yet another during worship of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
upavāsaṃ tu kurvīta snātaḥ śuciralaṃkṛtaḥ ..
parvakāleṣu sarveṣu brahmacārī tathā bhavet .. 25 ..
meaning:
उपवासं तु कुर्वीत स्नातः शुचिरलंकृतः ..
पर्वकालेषु सर्वेषु ब्रह्मचारी तथा भवेत् .. 25 ..
text_mt: Having bathed, being pure and adorned, one should observe a fast; / during all junction times one should likewise remain celibate.

sanskrit_iast:
pippalaṃ ca vaṭañcaiva śaṇaśākaṃ tathaiva ca ..
udumbaraṃ na khādeta bhavyārthī puruṣaḥ sadā ..26 ..
meaning:
पिप्पलं च वटञ्चैव शणशाकं तथैव च ..
उदुम्बरं न खादेत भव्यार्थी पुरुषः सदा ..26 ..
text_mt: A man seeking prosperity should never eat / pippala, vaṭa, hemp-greens, and udumbara.

sanskrit_iast:
putramāṃsopamaṃ māṃsaṃ pṛṣṭhamāṃsaṃ ca varjayet ..
pāṇau ca lavaṇaṃ rātrau dadhisaktūṃstathaiva ca .. 27 ..
meaning:
पुत्रमांसोपमं मांसं पृष्ठमांसं च वर्जयेत् ..
पाणौ च लवणं रात्रौ दधिसक्तूंस्तथैव च .. 27 ..
text_mt: Meat akin to one's son's flesh and meat from the back [of an animal] one should avoid; / and salt held in the hand, and at night, yogurt and roasted barley flour.

sanskrit_iast:
sāyaṃ prātaśca bhuñjīta nāntarāle kadācana ..
sāyaṃ prātarmanuṣyāṇāmaśanaṃ devanirmitam .. 28 ..
meaning:
सायं प्रातश्च भुञ्जीत नान्तराले कदाचन ..
सायं प्रातर्मनुष्याणामशनं देवनिर्मितम् .. 28 ..
text_mt: One should eat in the evening and in the morning, and never in between; / morning and evening meals were established by the gods for men.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmau sadaiva cāśnīyānna cāsīno ca śabdavat ..
toyapūrṇaṃ yadā pānamatithibhyo dvijottamāḥ .. 29 ..
meaning:
भूमौ सदैव चाश्नीयान्न चासीनो च शब्दवत् ..
तोयपूर्णं यदा पानमतिथिभ्यो द्विजोत्तमाः .. 29 ..
text_mt: One should always eat on the ground, not seated [haphazardly], and without making noise; / when drink filled with water [is served] to guests, O best of twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
paścādbhuñjīta medhāvī na cāpyanyamanā naraḥ ..
na dhāvedvarṣamāṇe tu nadīṃ mattāṃ na laṅghayet ..3.233.30..
meaning:
पश्चाद्भुञ्जीत मेधावी न चाप्यन्यमना नरः ..
न धावेद्वर्षमाणे तु नदीं मत्तां न लङ्घयेत् ..3.233.30..
text_mt: the wise man should eat afterwards, without being distracted; / one should not run while it is raining, nor cross a raging river.

sanskrit_iast:
gāṃ carantīṃ pibantañca vatsakaṃ na niṣedhayeta ..
samānamekapaṅktyāṃ tu deyamannaṃ tathā bhavet..31..
meaning:
गां चरन्तीं पिबन्तञ्च वत्सकं न निषेधयेत ..
समानमेकपङ्क्त्यां तु देयमन्नं तथा भवेत्..31..
text_mt: One should not prevent a cow while grazing or a calf while drinking; / in a single row [of diners], equal food should be given.

sanskrit_iast:
