text_mt: Having bathed his head, he should not touch any limb with oil; / he should not carry a burden on his head, nor fire and water together.

sanskrit_iast:
na toyaṃ prakṣipedvahnau vahniṃ toye tathaiva ca ..
varjayedatisauhārdaṃ bhojyānnasya ca kutsanam .. 239 ..
meaning:
न तोयं प्रक्षिपेद्वह्नौ वह्निं तोये तथैव च ..
वर्जयेदतिसौहार्दं भोज्यान्नस्य च कुत्सनम् .. 239 ..
text_mt: He should not throw water into fire, nor likewise fire into water; / he should avoid excessive intimacy, and disparagement of edible food.

sanskrit_iast:
rājadviṣṭaṃ gaṇadviṣṭaṃ lokadviṣṭaṃ vivarjayet ..
sāyaṃ prātaśca viduṣāṃ śṛṇuyātpuṣkalā giraḥ .. 3.233.240 ..
meaning:
राजद्विष्टं गणद्विष्टं लोकद्विष्टं विवर्जयेत् ..
सायं प्रातश्च विदुषां शृणुयात्पुष्कला गिरः .. 3.233.240 ..
text_mt: He should avoid what is hated by the king, hated by the community, and hated by the people. / Evening and morning he should listen to the abundant words of the learned.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃskṛtaṃ pāyasaṃ nityaṃ yavāgvāṃ kṛsaraṃ vadet ..
śmaśrukarmaṇi cāyuṣyaṃ jīvitena tathā kṛtiḥ .. 241 ..
meaning:
संस्कृतं पायसं नित्यं यवाग्वां कृसरं वदेत् ..
श्मश्रुकर्मणि चायुष्यं जीवितेन तथा कृतिः .. 241 ..
text_mt: He should always call rice-milk 'refined', and gruel 'kṛsara'; / in shaving he should say 'life-prolonging', and thus of life, 'successful'.

sanskrit_iast:
vyādhitānāṃ tu sarveṣāmāyuṣaḥ pratinandanam ..
śrāntasya viśramaśceti cāḍhyatāṃ sīriṇastathā .. 242 ..
meaning:
व्याधितानां तु सर्वेषामायुषः प्रतिनन्दनम् ..
श्रान्तस्य विश्रमश्चेति चाढ्यतां सीरिणस्तथा .. 242 ..
text_mt: To all the sick, [he should utter] a greeting of long life, / and to a weary man, 'rest', and likewise 'wealth' to a plowman;

sanskrit_iast:
āsīnasya sukhaṃ cāpi puṇyāhamapi gacchataḥ ..
devakarmapravṛttasya prāsādaṃ parikīrtayet .. 243 ..
meaning:
आसीनस्य सुखं चापि पुण्याहमपि गच्छतः ..
देवकर्मप्रवृत्तस्य प्रासादं परिकीर्तयेत् .. 243 ..
text_mt: and to one seated, 'comfort', and 'auspicious day' to one who is departing; / to one engaged in rites for the gods, he should proclaim 'favor'.

sanskrit_iast:
na jātu tvamiti brūyādāpannopi mahattaram ..
tvaṃkāro vā vadho veti vidvatsu na viśiṣyate .. 244 ..
meaning:
न जातु त्वमिति ब्रूयादापन्नोपि महत्तरम् ..
त्वंकारो वा वधो वेति विद्वत्सु न विशिष्यते .. 244 ..
text_mt: Even when in distress, he should never say 'you' to an elder; / whether addressed with 'you' or struck down, among the wise there is no difference.

sanskrit_iast:
avarāṇāṃ samānānāṃ śiṣyāṇāñcaitadiṣyate ..
eka eva careddharmaṃ na dharmadhvajiko bhavet .. 245 ..
meaning:
अवराणां समानानां शिष्याणाञ्चैतदिष्यते ..
एक एव चरेद्धर्मं न धर्मध्वजिको भवेत् .. 245 ..
text_mt: This is permitted for inferiors, equals, and disciples. / He should practice dharma alone; he should not be an ostentatious displayer of dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
arceddevānna dambhena sevetāmāyayā gurūn ..
nidhiṃ vidadhyātpārakyaṃ yatrārthaḥ śabdavāniti .. 246 ..
meaning:
अर्चेद्देवान्न दम्भेन सेवेतामायया गुरून् ..
निधिं विदध्यात्पारक्यं यत्रार्थः शब्दवानिति .. 246 ..
text_mt: He should not worship the gods with hypocrisy, nor serve teachers with deceit. / He should establish a treasure for the other world, where wealth is fruitful.

sanskrit_iast:
karma vai saphalaṃ kṛtvā gurūṇāṃ pratipādayet ..
vṛddhānnāti vadejjātu na tu sampreṣayetkvacit ..247..
meaning:
कर्म वै सफलं कृत्वा गुरूणां प्रतिपादयेत् ..
वृद्धान्नाति वदेज्जातु न तु सम्प्रेषयेत्क्वचित् ..247..
text_mt: Having made an action fruitful, he should dedicate it to his elders; / he should never talk back to elders, nor send them on errands anywhere.

sanskrit_iast:
na vegito'nyakāryaḥ syānnāditvānnāni kutsayet..
muktakeśo na gacchettu svapnāhārasabhāstriyaḥ..248..
meaning:
न वेगितोऽन्यकार्यः स्यान्नादित्वान्नानि कुत्सयेत्..
मुक्तकेशो न गच्छेत्तु स्वप्नाहारसभास्त्रियः..248..
text_mt: Urged by bodily calls, he should not attend to other business; having eaten food, he should not disparage it. / With disheveled hair he should not go to sleep, food, assemblies, or women.

sanskrit_iast:
pāṇinālabhya niṣkrāmedratnapūjyājyamaṇḍalam ..
pradakṣiṇantu kurvīta maṃgalyaṃ sarvadā yatiḥ..249..
meaning:
पाणिनालभ्य निष्क्रामेद्रत्नपूज्याज्यमण्डलम् ..
प्रदक्षिणन्तु कुर्वीत मंगल्यं सर्वदा यतिः..249..
text_mt: Touching a jewel, a venerable object, or a bowl of ghee with his hand, he should step forth. / An ascetic should always circumambulate an auspicious object clockwise.

sanskrit_iast:
sūnāñca bandhanāgāraṃ nṛpanṛtyagṛhe tathā ..
antaḥ puraṃ ca ṛṣayo dūrataḥ parivarjayet .. 3.233.250 ..
meaning:
सूनाञ्च बन्धनागारं नृपनृत्यगृहे तथा ..
अन्तः पुरं च ऋषयो दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् .. 3.233.250 ..
text_mt: A slaughterhouse, a prison, a king's dance hall, / and an inner chamber: sages should avoid these from afar.

sanskrit_iast:
triḥ pakṣasya kṛtaśmaśrurnakhalomāni kalpayet ..
na pratisphālayedambu pāṇinā caraṇena vā .. 251 ..
meaning:
त्रिः पक्षस्य कृतश्मश्रुर्नखलोमानि कल्पयेत् ..
न प्रतिस्फालयेदम्बु पाणिना चरणेन वा .. 251 ..
text_mt: Having shaved his beard three times in a fortnight, he should trim his nails and hair. / He should not splash water with his hand or foot.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsaṃvṛtamukhaḥ kuryātkṣutamaṃgavijṛmbhaṇam ..
nādvāreṇa suhṛdveśma na dvāreṇa riporviśet .. 252 ..
meaning:
नासंवृतमुखः कुर्यात्क्षुतमंगविजृम्भणम् ..
नाद्वारेण सुहृद्वेश्म न द्वारेण रिपोर्विशेत् .. 252 ..
text_mt: He should not sneeze or stretch his limbs without covering his mouth. / He should not enter a friend's house except by the door, nor an enemy's by the door.

sanskrit_iast:
na sarpaśastraiḥ krīḍettu nadīvegaṃ vivarjayet ..
vidyātpratikṣaṇaṃ mṛtyorayathātathaceṣṭitam .. 253 ..
meaning:
न सर्पशस्त्रैः क्रीडेत्तु नदीवेगं विवर्जयेत् ..
विद्यात्प्रतिक्षणं मृत्योरयथातथचेष्टितम् .. 253 ..
text_mt: He should not play with snakes or weapons; he should avoid the current of a river. / He should know every moment the unpredictable movement of death.

sanskrit_iast:
āharejjñānamarthāṃśca naro hyamaravatsadā ..
keśairiva gṛhītastu mṛtyunā dharmamācaret .. 254 ..
meaning:
आहरेज्ज्ञानमर्थांश्च नरो ह्यमरवत्सदा ..
केशैरिव गृहीतस्तु मृत्युना धर्ममाचरेत् .. 254 ..
text_mt: A man should always acquire knowledge and wealth as if he were immortal, / but he should practice dharma as if seized by the hair by death.

sanskrit_iast:
praviśejjanasaṃbādhaṃ tathātigahanaṃ na ca ..
hema nāsaṃskṛtaṃ dhāryaṃ niśi loṣṭaṃ na ca kṣipet ..255..
meaning:
प्रविशेज्जनसंबाधं तथातिगहनं न च ..
हेम नासंस्कृतं धार्यं निशि लोष्टं न च क्षिपेत् ..255..
text_mt: He should not enter a crowd of people, nor an impenetrable thicket. / Unrefined gold should not be worn, nor should he throw a clod at night.

sanskrit_iast:
ādau paṅktyāṃ na cāśnīyādvarjayedbhūmitāḍanam..
varjayecchātraśabalaṃ divā nidrāṃ tathaiva ca .. 256 ..
meaning:
आदौ पङ्क्त्यां न चाश्नीयाद्वर्जयेद्भूमिताडनम्..
वर्जयेच्छात्रशबलं दिवा निद्रां तथैव च .. 256 ..
text_mt: He should not eat first in a row of diners, and he should avoid striking the ground; / he should avoid what is mixed with students, and sleep by day as well.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmaḥ krodho bhayo harṣaṃ lobho darpastathaiva ca ..
ripavaḥ ṣaḍ vijetavyā puruṣeṇa vipaścitā .. 257 ..
meaning:
कामः क्रोधो भयो हर्षं लोभो दर्पस्तथैव च ..
रिपवः षड् विजेतव्या पुरुषेण विपश्चिता .. 257 ..
text_mt: Desire, anger, fear, exhilaration, greed, and pride: / these six enemies must be conquered by a wise man.

sanskrit_iast:
ariṣaḍvargasaṃnyāsātkuryādindriyanigrahama ..
yogakṣemaṃ sadotthānātprajñāṃ vṛddhopasevanāt .. 258 ..
meaning:
अरिषड्वर्गसंन्यासात्कुर्यादिन्द्रियनिग्रहम ..
योगक्षेमं सदोत्थानात्प्रज्ञां वृद्धोपसेवनात् .. 258 ..
text_mt: Through the renunciation of the group of six enemies he should restrain the senses, / [procure] welfare through constant enterprise, and wisdom through attendance on elders.

sanskrit_iast:
praśrayeṇa jayenmānaṃ dainyaṃ dṛṣṭāṃta saṃśrayāt ..
akrodhena jayetkrodhaṃ vinayena tvanāryatām .. 259 ..
meaning:
प्रश्रयेण जयेन्मानं दैन्यं दृष्टांत संश्रयात् ..
अक्रोधेन जयेत्क्रोधं विनयेन त्वनार्यताम् .. 259 ..
text_mt: He should conquer arrogance with modesty, wretchedness by relying on good examples, / anger with freedom from anger, and ignobility with disciplined conduct.

sanskrit_iast:
śīghratvāddhastapādaṃ ca vācamuccāraṇājjayet ..
ajñānaṃ jñānasaṃyogātkāmaṃ kāmāṃgavarjanāt .. 3.233.260 ..
meaning:
शीघ्रत्वाद्धस्तपादं च वाचमुच्चारणाज्जयेत् ..
अज्ञानं ज्ञानसंयोगात्कामं कामांगवर्जनात् .. 3.233.260 ..
text_mt: He should master hands and feet through slowness of movement, and speech through [deliberate] utterance; / ignorance through union with knowledge, and lust through the avoidance of lust's incitements.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmiṣṭhairāgamairlobhaṃ krodhaṃ maitryādvivarjayet ..
kāruṇyena jayenmānaṃ kālaṃ kāryopapattibhiḥ .. 261 ..
meaning:
धर्मिष्ठैरागमैर्लोभं क्रोधं मैत्र्याद्विवर्जयेत् ..
कारुण्येन जयेन्मानं कालं कार्योपपत्तिभिः .. 261 ..
text_mt: He should avoid greed through righteous scriptures, anger through friendliness, / conquer arrogance with compassion, and time with proper timing of actions.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānaṃ sukhaduḥkhādyaṃ tvanabhijñāya yojayet ..
dhṛtyā śiśnodaraṃ rakṣetpāṇipādaṃ ca cakṣuṣā .. 262 ..
meaning:
आत्मानं सुखदुःखाद्यं त्वनभिज्ञाय योजयेत् ..
धृत्या शिश्नोदरं रक्षेत्पाणिपादं च चक्षुषा .. 262 ..
text_mt: He should engage himself without being overwhelmed by pleasure, pain, and the rest. / With steadfastness he should guard the genitals and belly, and hands and feet with the eyes;

sanskrit_iast:
cakṣuḥśrotre ca manasā mano vācaṃ ca karmaṇā ..
deśa kālānubandhārthaṃ dharmāṇāmavirodhi yat .. 263 ..
meaning:
चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च मनसा मनो वाचं च कर्मणा ..
देश कालानुबन्धार्थं धर्माणामविरोधि यत् .. 263 ..
text_mt: eyes and ears with the mind, and mind and speech with action. / For the sake of conformity with place and time, whatever is unopposed to dharma,

sanskrit_iast:
tattatsukhaṃ niṣeveta nākasmānniḥsukhī bhavet ..
rūpasaṃdarśanaśravyarasagandhānsadā jayet..264..
meaning:
तत्तत्सुखं निषेवेत नाकस्मान्निःसुखी भवेत् ..
रूपसंदर्शनश्रव्यरसगन्धान्सदा जयेत्..264..
text_mt: he should enjoy that pleasure; he should not be devoid of happiness without cause. / He should constantly conquer visible forms, sounds, tastes, and scents.

sanskrit_iast:
vasannapi sadomadhye hyasakto manasā bhavet ..
pareṣāntatra saṃdadhyātpratikūlaṃ yadātmanaḥ .. 265 ..
meaning:
वसन्नपि सदोमध्ये ह्यसक्तो मनसा भवेत् ..
परेषान्तत्र संदध्यात्प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः .. 265 ..
text_mt: Even while dwelling in an assembly, he should be unattached in mind; / he should not inflict upon others what is disagreeable to himself.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛcchreṣvapi na tatkuryātsādhūnāṃ yadasammatam ..
jīrṇāśī ca mitāśī ca hitāśī ca tathā bhavet ..266..
meaning:
कृच्छ्रेष्वपि न तत्कुर्यात्साधूनां यदसम्मतम् ..
जीर्णाशी च मिताशी च हिताशी च तथा भवेत् ..266..
text_mt: Even in distress he should not do what is disapproved by the virtuous; / and he should be an eater of digested food, a moderate eater, and an eater of wholesome food.

sanskrit_iast:
śasyate yairguṇairanyairyeranyairarjitaṃ yaśaḥ ..
uñchavṛttirbhavatyeva viparītamatastyajet .. 267 ..
meaning:
शस्यते यैर्गुणैरन्यैर्येरन्यैरर्जितं यशः ..
उञ्छवृत्तिर्भवत्येव विपरीतमतस्त्यजेत् .. 267 ..
text_mt: By whichever virtues other men are praised, and by which others have acquired fame, / he should live by gleaning them, and abandon the contrary mindset.

sanskrit_iast:
sukāruṇikamātmānaṃ khyāpayennāpi nirghṛṇam ..
deśakālau ca śaktiṃ ca janatāñcāvalokayet .. 268 ..
meaning:
सुकारुणिकमात्मानं ख्यापयेन्नापि निर्घृणम् ..
देशकालौ च शक्तिं च जनताञ्चावलोकयेत् .. 268 ..
text_mt: One should make oneself known as truly compassionate, not cruel; / and one should consider place, time, power, and the people.

sanskrit_iast:
na mṛduḥ syānna ca krūro hyubhāveva samāśrayet ..
mṛdurbhavatyavajñātaḥ tīkṣṇādudvijate janaḥ .. 269 ..
meaning:
न मृदुः स्यान्न च क्रूरो ह्युभावेव समाश्रयेत् ..
मृदुर्भवत्यवज्ञातः तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः .. 269 ..
text_mt: One should neither be gentle nor cruel, but indeed adopt both; / a gentle person is treated with contempt, and people tremble before a severe one.

sanskrit_iast:
anālakṣitacittaḥ syānnaikānte kiñcidācaret ..
vidyātparasya randhrāṇi svaraṃdhraṃ chādayetpunaḥ .. 3.233.270 ..
meaning:
अनालक्षितचित्तः स्यान्नैकान्ते किञ्चिदाचरेत् ..
विद्यात्परस्य रन्ध्राणि स्वरंध्रं छादयेत्पुनः .. 3.233.270 ..
text_mt: One's mind should remain imperceptible; one should perform nothing in solitude. / One should know the weaknesses of another, yet cover one's own weakness.

sanskrit_iast:
gūhetkūrma ivāṅgāni rakṣedātmānamātmanā ..
vāgādīni sahāyāni kṛtvā prajñāṃ ca mantriṇam .. 271 ..
meaning:
गूहेत्कूर्म इवाङ्गानि रक्षेदात्मानमात्मना ..
वागादीनि सहायानि कृत्वा प्रज्ञां च मन्त्रिणम् .. 271 ..
text_mt: One should conceal one's limbs like a tortoise and protect oneself by oneself, / making speech and the [other senses] allies and wisdom the counselor.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmakāmasamṛddhyarthaṃ dāsādyarthaḥ pumānbhavet ..
arthānarthau samāsādya harṣadainye vivarjayet..272..
meaning:

Endowed with proper conduct, one goes to heaven; possessing proper conduct alone, one is free from disease; / possessing proper conduct alone, one lives long; possessing proper conduct alone, one enjoys good fortune.
3.234 / Haṃsa said: / Having incurred the need for expiation through fate or past deeds, / a man should not associate with good people until the expiation is performed.
Killing a brahmin, drinking liquor, theft, and violating the teacher's bed— / these they call the great sins, and association with those [who commit them] as well.
A lie told for self-exaltation, calumny that reaches the king, / and false accusation of a guru are equal to killing a brahmin.
Abandoning the Veda, reviling the Veda, false testimony, slaying a friend, / and eating forbidden food or drink—these six are equal to drinking liquor.
Misappropriating a deposit, and [stealing] a man, a horse, silver, / land, diamonds, or gems, is considered equal to the theft of gold.
Ejaculating seed into uterine [kinswomen], virgins, outcaste women, / and the wives of a friend or a son, they consider equal to violating the guru's bed.

text_mt:
Inflicting pain on a brahmin, smelling things that should not be smelled or liquor, / dishonesty, and intercourse with a man are declared to cause loss of caste.
Slaying a donkey, horse, camel, deer, elephant, goat, or sheep, / and [slaying] a fish, snake, or buffalo is to be known as causing mixture of caste.
Receiving wealth from condemned persons, commerce, serving a śūdra, / and uttering a falsehood are to be known as rendering one unfit to receive gifts.
Killing worms, insects, or birds, eating food tainted by liquor, / stealing fruit, firewood, or flowers, and lack of steadfastness are impurity-producing sins.
All these and others, individually stated, / are removed by vows of steadfastness; listen to them from me:
A killer of a brahmin should dwell in the forest for twelve years, having built a hut, / eating alms food for self-purification, carrying a skull upon a staff as his standard.
Or he may offer himself as a target to weapon-bearers, by his own wish, who are skilled; / or he may cast himself into a kindled fire head downwards three times.

Or he may sacrifice with the horse-sacrifice, the Svarjit, or the Gosava, / or with the Abhijit and Viśvajit, or with the Trivṛt or the Agniṣṭut.
Or muttering any one of the Vedas, he may walk a hundred yojanas / to remove the murder of a brahmin, eating moderately with restrained senses.
Or he should bestow his entire property upon a brahmin who knows the Veda, / or wealth sufficient for a livelihood, or a house with its furnishings.
Or eating sacrificial food, he should follow the Sarasvatī against the current, / or with controlled diet, mutter three times the Saṃhitā of the Veda.
Having shaved his head, he should dwell at the edge of a village, or in a cattle pen, / or in a hermitage, or at the root of a tree, devoted to the welfare of cows and brahmins.
For the sake of a brahmin or for the sake of cows, he may duly abandon his life; / devoted to the welfare of cows and brahmins, he is freed from the murder of a brahmin.
Or having blocked [the enemies of a brahmin] three times, or having recovered all the property / of a brahmin, or on that account losing his life, he is freed.
Thus steadfast in his vow, always celibate and collected, / when the twelfth year is completed, he is freed from the killing of a brahmin.

Or having declared his own sin in an assembly of earthly gods and a king, / he is freed when bathed at the concluding bath (avabhṛtha) of a horse sacrifice.
The brahmin is said to be the root of dharma, and the kṣatriya its top; / therefore, having proclaimed his sin in their assembly, he becomes pure.
A brahmin, merely by his birth, is a deity even to the gods / and an authority for the world; indeed, the Veda is the reason here.
Even three of them who know the Veda might state the expiation for sins; / that would serve for their purification, for the word of the learned is purifying.
Therefore, adopting one or another rule, a collected brahmin, / through self-possession, dispels the sin caused by the killing of a brahmin.
Having killed an unknown embryo, he should perform this very vow; / likewise if [he has killed] a kṣatriya or vaiśya who had studied [the Veda], and a woman who has bathed after her period.
And having spoken an untruth in testimony, having obstructed teachers, / having stolen a deposit, and having committed the murder of a woman or a friend;

this purification is declared for having killed a twice-born unintentionally; / for intentionally slaying a brahmin, no expiation is prescribed.
Having drunk wine out of delusion, a twice-born should drink wine the colour of fire; / when his body is thoroughly burnt by that, he is freed from the sin.
Or he should drink cow’s urine the colour of fire, or water, / or milk, or clarified butter, or the juice of cow dung, until death.
Or he should eat grain-particles for a year, or oil-cake once at night, / to remove the drinking of wine, wearing a garment of hair, with matted locks, bearing a staff.
Wine is indeed the dirt of foods, and sin is called dirt; / therefore, a brahmin, a kṣatriya, and a vaiśya should not drink wine.
Wine should be known as threefold: made from molasses, made from honey, and made from flour; / just as the one is, so is another: they must not be drunk by the twice-born.
Liquor, meat, wine, and spirits are the food of Yakṣas, Rakṣases, and Piśācas; / that should not be consumed by a brahmin eating the oblation of the gods.

Intoxicated, he might fall into what is impure, or he might recite Vedic text, / or, deluded by intoxication, a brahmin might do some other forbidden act.
In whose body the Veda, having entered, is flooded even once with liquor, / his brahminhood departs, and he goes to the state of a śūdra.
This manifold expiation for the drinking of wine has been declared; / hereafter I shall explain the expiation for the theft of gold.
A brahmin possessing stolen gold, approaching the king / and proclaiming his own deed, should say: ‘May your majesty punish me.’
Taking a pestle, the king himself should strike him once; / through death the thief is purified, or a brahmin through asceticism alone.
Desiring to remove through asceticism the dirt born of the theft of gold, / a twice-born, dressed in rags, should perform in the forest the vow of a slayer of a brahmin.
Through these vows a twice-born may dispel the sin caused by theft; / but one who has had intercourse with the wife of an elder should remove it by these vows:

Having proclaimed the sin, he who has violated the bed of an elder should lie down in an iron pot, / or embracing a glowing iron image, he is purified by death;
or having himself cut off his penis and testicles and placed them in his cupped hands, / he should set out towards the southwest direction, walking straight until he collapses.
Or carrying a staff tipped with a skull, clad in rags, with a beard, in a solitary forest, / he should perform the Prājāpatya penance for one year, being collected;
or with restrained senses, he should practice the Cāndrāyaṇa for three months, / with sacrificial food or with barley gruel, for the removal of [the sin of] violating the bed of an elder.
By these vows those guilty of mortal sins should dispel their impurities; / and those guilty of secondary sins [should do so] likewise through various observances.
He who is afflicted with a secondary sin of killing a cow should drink barley gruel for a month; / with shaved head, he should live in a cow-pen, covered with that [cow’s] hide.
He should eat a measured amount without pungent spices or salt at the fourth meal-time; / with restrained senses, he should bathe in cow’s urine for two months.
By day he should follow those cows, and standing upright, inhale their dust; / having served and honoured them, at night he should sit in the vīrāsana posture.

When they stand, he should stand; when they walk, he should follow them; / and when they are seated, he should sit down likewise, self-restrained and free from malice.
If [a cow is] sick, or attacked by dangers such as lions and tigers, / or fallen, or stuck in mud, he should rescue her with all his might.
In heat, in rain, or in cold, or when the wind blows violently, / he should not protect himself without first protecting the cow according to his ability.
Whether in his own or another’s house, field, or threshing floor, / he should not report her eating [crops] or nursing her calf.
The killer of a cow who follows cows according to this rule / dispels in three months the sin caused by the killing of a cow.
Having observed the vow well, he should give [ten] cows with a bull as the eleventh; / if these are not available, he should offer all his possessions to those who know the Veda.
Twice-born guilty of secondary sins should perform this very vow, / or the Cāndrāyaṇa for the purification of one who has broken his vow of celibacy (avakīrṇin).
One who has broken his vow of celibacy, however, should sacrifice to Nirṛti at night / at a crossroads with a one-eyed donkey according to the rite of a pākayajña.

text_mt:
Having offered the oblations into the fire according to rule, and at the end with the Samidh verse, / he should offer oblations of clarified butter to Vāta, Indra, Guru, and Agni.
The intentional emission of semen by a twice-born while bound by a vow / is declared by the knowers of dharma and speakers of the Veda to be a transgression of the vow.
The Maruts, Puruhūta, Guru, and Pāvaka: / to these four goes the Vedic splendour of one who has broken his vow.
When this sin has occurred, having put on the skin of an ass, / he should go begging at seven houses, proclaiming his own deed.
Subsisting on the alms obtained from them, eating once a day, / and bathing at the three junctures of the day, he becomes purified in a year.
Having committed intentionally any act that causes loss of caste, / he should perform the Sāntapana penance; if unintentionally, the Prājāpatya penance.
For deeds causing mixture [of castes] or rendering one unworthy to receive gifts, one [should observe] the lunar fast [subsisting on] cow-products for a month; / for deeds causing defilement, one should take hot barley-gruel for three days.

text_mt:
A fourth of [the penance for] killing a brahmin is prescribed for killing a kṣatriya; / an eighth part for a vaiśya established in good conduct, but a sixteenth is known for a śūdra.
If a foremost twice-born slays a kṣatriya unintentionally, / he should give a thousand cows together with a bull for the purification of himself;
or, restrained, wearing matted hair, he should observe the vow of a brahmin-slayer for three years, / dwelling in a village far away, having his abode at the foot of a tree.
A foremost twice-born should observe this very penance for a year / having killed a vaiśya established in good conduct, or he should give a hundred cows.
A slayer of a śūdra should observe this entire vow for six months, / or he should give to a brahmin white cows with a bull as the eleventh.
Having killed a cat, a mongoose, a blue jay, or a frog, / or a dog, an iguana, an owl, or a crow, he should observe the vow for killing a śūdra;
or he should drink milk for three nights, or walk the path of a yojana, / or bathe in a flowing stream, or recite a hymn addressed to the waters.

text_mt:
Having killed a snake, a foremost twice-born should give a spade made of black iron; / for a eunuch, a load of straw and one māṣaka of lead.
For a boar, a pot of ghee; but a droṇa of sesame for a partridge; / for a parrot, a two-year-old calf; and having killed a curlew, a three-year-old [calf].
Having killed a swan, a crane, a heron, and a peacock, / a monkey, a hawk, or a vulture, he should present a cow to a brahmin.
Having killed a horse, he should give a garment, or five dark-blue bulls; / a goat and a sheep [for killing each other], a draft-ox [for killing an ox], and a one-year-old [calf] having killed a donkey.
Having killed a carnivorous deer, he should give a milch cow; / for a non-carnivorous one, a heifer; but having killed a camel, a kṛṣṇala [of gold].
He should give respectively a deer-skin, a bow, a goat, or a sheep for purification / upon killing a woman of any of the four varnas who is living in the forest.
A twice-born who is unable to effect expiation by giving gifts for [killing] snakes and the like / should perform a kṛcchra penance for each one in order to remove the sin.

text_mt:
Upon slaying a thousand creatures possessing bones, / or a full cart-load of boneless ones, he should observe the vow for killing a śūdra.
He should give something small to a brahmin for the killing of boned [creatures]; / and for boneless creatures, breath-control is the purification.
For cutting down fruit-bearing trees, a hundred Ṛgvedic verses are to be recited, / and [the same for cutting] shrubs, climbing vines, creepers, and flowering plants.
For [killing] creatures born in food and the like, or those born everywhere in liquids, / and those originating in fruits and flowers, the sipping of ghee is the purification.
For needlessly destroying herbs born of cultivation / or those grown of themselves in the forest, he should follow [a cow] or keep a vow of [drinking only] milk for one day.
By these vows, the sin arising from injury is to be dispelled. / Hear completely [about the sin] committed knowingly or unknowingly in eating improper food and the like.
Having drunk spirituous liquor through ignorance, he is purified by the sacrament alone; / [if drunk] intentionally, there is no expiation; it terminates only with life: such is the established rule.

text_mt:
Having drunk water kept in a vessel for liquor or remaining in a jar for spirits, / he should stay for five nights drinking milk boiled with śaṅkhapuṣpī.
Having touched or given wine, or having accepted it in accordance with the rule, / and having drunk water left by a śūdra, he should drink kuśa-water for three days.
A brahmin who drinks soma, having smelled the breath of a liquor-drinker, / is purified by [controlling his] breaths in water, sipping water thrice, and consuming ghee.
Having consumed feces or urine through ignorance, or [food] touched by liquor, / the three twice-born varnas require the sacrament again.
The garment, the girdle, the staff, the begging of alms, and the vows / cease for the twice-born in the rite of the renewed sacrament.
Having eaten the food of those whose food should not be eaten, or the leftovers of a woman or a śūdra, / or having consumed uneatable meat, he should drink milk for seven nights.
Having drunk fermented drinks, astringent brews, and impure [beverages], a twice-born / remains impure only for as long as that [drink] does not pass downward.

text_mt:
Having consumed the urine and feces of a village pig, a donkey, a camel, / a jackal, a monkey, or a crow, he should perform a cāndrāyaṇa twice or thrice.
Having eaten dried meats, or mushrooms grown from the ground, / or [meat] of unknown origin lying in broth, he should perform this very vow.
For eating carnivorous animals, pigs, and cocks, / or men, crows, and donkeys, the taptakṛcchra is the purification.
And a twice-born who, distressed by lack of livelihood, eats food of a monthly ancestral rite, / should fast for three days and dwell in water for one day.
A keeper of vows who should somehow eat honey or meat / should perform an ordinary kṛcchra and then complete the remainder of the vow.
Having eaten the leftovers of a cat, a crow, a mouse, a dog, or a mongoose, / or [food] fallen upon by hair or insects, he should drink [an extract of] brāhmī and suvarcalā.
Food that is unfit to be eaten should not be consumed by one desiring purity for himself; / but if eaten through ignorance, it should be vomited out, or purified quickly by purifying rites.

text_mt:
This various rule of vows has been stated for the eating of improper food. / Let the rule of vows for the removers of the sin of theft be heard.
A foremost twice-born who intentionally commits thefts of grain, cooked food, or wealth / from the house of a member of his own caste, is purified by a year-long kṛcchra.
For the abduction of men, of women, or [the theft] of a field or a house, / and of the waters of wells and tanks, the cāndrāyaṇa is remembered as the purification.
Having committed the theft of articles of small value from another's house, / he should perform the sāntapana kṛcchra after returning that [article], for his own purification.
For stealing solid or liquid food, a vehicle, a bed, or a seat, / and flowers, roots, or fruits, the five cow-products are the purification.
For [stealing] grass, wood, trees, dry food, and jaggery, / and clothes, leather, and meat, there should be fasting for three nights.
For [stealing] gems, pearls, coral, copper, and silver, / iron, bell-metal, and stones, [he should subsist] on broken grains of rice for twelve days.

sanskrit_iast:

ebhirvratairapohyeta pāpaṃ steyakṛtaṃ dvijaḥ ..
agamyagamanīyantu vratairebhirapānudet .. 117 ..

sakhyuḥ putrasya ca strīṣu kumārīṣvantyajāsu ca..118..
paitṛṣvasreyāṃ bhaginīṃ svasrīyāṃ mātureva ca..
mātuśca bhrāturāptasya gatvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret ..119..
etāḥ striyastu bhāryārthe nopayacchettu buddhimān..
jñātitvenānupeyāstāḥ patanti hyupayannadhaḥ ..3.234.120..
amānuṣīṣu puruṣa udakyāyāmayoniṣu ..
retaḥ siktvā jale caiva kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ caret .. 121 ..
maithunaṃ tu samāsevya puṃsi yoṣiti vā dvijaḥ ..
goyānepsu divā caiva savāsā snānamācaret .. 122 ..
meaning:
कार्पासकीटजीर्णानां द्विशफैकशफस्य च ..
पक्षिगन्धौषधीनाञ्च रज्ज्वाश्चैव त्र्यहं पयः .. 116 ..
एभिर्व्रतैरपोह्येत पापं स्तेयकृतं द्विजः ..
अगम्यगमनीयन्तु व्रतैरेभिरपानुदेत् .. 117 ..
गुरुतल्पव्रतं कुर्याद्रेतः सिक्त्वा स्वयोनिषु ..
सख्युः पुत्रस्य च स्त्रीषु कुमारीष्वन्त्यजासु च..118..
पैतृष्वस्रेयां भगिनीं स्वस्रीयां मातुरेव च..
मातुश्च भ्रातुराप्तस्य गत्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ..119..
एताः स्त्रियस्तु भार्यार्थे नोपयच्छेत्तु बुद्धिमान्..
ज्ञातित्वेनानुपेयास्ताः पतन्ति ह्युपयन्नधः ..3.234.120..

गोयानेप्सु दिवा चैव सवासा स्नानमाचरेत् .. 122 ..
text_mt:
For [stealing] cotton, silk, and worn garments, two-hoofed and one-hoofed animals, / birds, perfumes, medicinal herbs, and rope, [he should drink] milk for three days.
By these observances a twice-born would remove the sin committed by theft; / but one who has had intercourse with an forbidden woman should dispel it by these observances:
He should perform the observance for violating the guru's bed after discharging semen into women of his own clan, / into the wives of a friend or a son, into maidens, and into outcaste women.
Having approached the daughter of his father's sister, his sister, his sister's daughter, or [the daughter] of his mother, / or [the daughter] of a close brother of his mother, he should perform the cāndrāyaṇa penance.
A wise man should not marry these women as his wife; / they are not to be approached on account of kinship, for by marrying [them] one falls downward.
After discharging semen into non-human females, into a menstruating woman, into improper orifices, / and into water, a man should perform the santapana-kṛcchra penance.
Having engaged in sexual intercourse with a man or a woman, / in an ox-cart, in water, or by day, a twice-born should bathe with his clothes on.

sanskrit_iast:

yatpuṃsaḥ paradāreṣu taccaināṃ cārayedvratam..124..

meaning:
चाण्डालान्त्य स्त्रियं गत्वा भुक्त्वा च प्रतिगृह्य च ..

विप्रदुष्टां स्त्रियं भर्ता निरुन्ध्यादेकवेश्मनि ...
यत्पुंसः परदारेषु तच्चैनां चारयेद्व्रतम्..124..
सा चेत्पुनः प्रदुष्येत सदृशेनोपयन्त्रिता..
कृच्छ्रं चान्द्रायणं चैव तदस्याः पावनं स्मृतम् ..125..
यत्करोत्यैकरात्रेण वृषलीसेवनं द्विजः ..
तद्भैक्ष्यभुग्जपन्नित्यं त्रिभिर्वषैर्व्यपोहति ..126..
एषा पापकृतामुक्ता चतुर्णामपि निष्कृतिः ..

याजनाध्यापनाद्यौनान्न तु यानासनाशनात् .. 128 ..
यो येन पतितेनैवं संसर्गं याति मानवः ..
स तस्यैव व्रतं कुर्यात्तत्संसर्गस्य शुद्धये .. 129..
text_mt:
Having approached a Caṇḍāla or outcaste woman, eaten [her food], or accepted gifts [from her], / a brahmin falls through ignorance; through intentional action, however, he becomes equal [to her].
A husband should confine an adulterous wife in a single room; / whatever observance is [prescribed] for a man [who approaches] another's wife, he should make her perform that.
If, though restrained, she should again become unchaste with an equal, / a kṛcchra and a cāndrāyaṇa penance are traditionally taught as her purifier.
Whatever [sin] a twice-born incurs by spending a single night serving an outcaste woman, / he removes by eating begged food and reciting [prayers] constantly for three years.
This expiation has been stated for those of all four [castes] who commit sins; / hear now these expiations for those who associate with fallen persons:
Associating with a fallen person, one falls within a year / through sacrificing for him, teaching him, or matrimonial alliance, but not through riding, sitting, or eating [with him].
Whatever person enters into association with whatever fallen one in this manner, / he should perform that very one's observance for the purification of that association.

दायादस्य प्रदानश्च यात्रामेव च लौकिके ..132..
ज्येष्ठता च निवर्त्तेत ज्येष्ठं वापि च यद्वसु ..

वस्त्रान्नपानं देयं तु वसेयुश्च गृहान्तिके .. 136 ..
text_mt:
The sapinda relatives should perform the water-offering for the fallen person outside, / on an inauspicious day at twilight, in the presence of relatives, officiating priests, and the guru.
A female slave should overturn a pot full of water as if he were deceased; / together with the relatives, they should observe ritual impurity for a day and a night.
From then on, they should cease conversation and eating together with him, / the bestowal of inheritance, and social interaction in worldly life.
Seniority ceases, as well as whatever wealth belongs to the eldest; / a younger [brother] superior in virtue should obtain the eldest's share of his [estate].
When the penance has been performed, however, having bathed at an auspicious reservoir of water / together with him, they should drink from a fresh pot full of water.
Throwing that pot into the water and entering his own home, / he may perform all rituals with relatives as before.
One should perform this very rule even for fallen women; / clothing, food, and drink must be given, and they should dwell near the house.

text_mt:
One should not conduct any business with sinners who are unpurified; / but once they have performed purification, one should never despise them.
Even if purified in accordance with dharma, killers of children, the ungrateful, / killers of those seeking refuge, and killers of women—one must not live together with them.
Those twice-born to whom the Sāvitrī has not been taught according to rule, / having caused them to perform three kṛcchra penances, one should initiate according to rule.
Those twice-born who are engaged in improper acts and desire penance, / and those abandoned by the Veda, one should also prescribe this for them.
Whatever wealth brahmins acquire through reprehensible action, / they become pure by relinquishing it, by recitation of prayers, and by ascetic practice.
Having recited three thousand [verses] of the Sāvitrī with concentrated mind / and drinking milk in a cowpen for a month, one is released from improper acceptance of gifts.
When he returns from the cowpen, emaciated from fasting / and bowing down, they should ask him: 'Gentle one, do you desire equality [with us]?'

text_mt:
Having spoken the truth to the brahmins, he should scatter fodder for the cows; / at a watering place made by cows, they should receive him.
Having officiated at sacrifices for the degraded, or performed funeral rites for others, / or performed malevolent sorcery and an ahīna sacrifice, one is purified by three kṛcchra penances.
A twice-born who abandons one who has sought refuge and one who reviles the Veda / dispels that sin by subsisting on barley for a year.
Bitten by dogs, jackals, or donkeys, or by domestic carnivorous animals, / or by donkeys, horses, camels, and boars, one is purified by breath-control.
Eating only at the sixth mealtime for a month, or recitation of the Saṃhitā, / and daily oblations of all kinds are the purification of those unfit to sit in the row.
Mounting a camel cart or a donkey cart intentionally, / a brahmin, having bathed unclothed, is purified by breath-control.
Passing urine or feces without water or into water, / having plunged into water outside with his clothes on and touched a cow, he is purified.

text_mt:
In the neglect of the daily rituals prescribed by the Veda / and in the breach of the observances of a graduate, fasting is the penance.
Having said 'Hum' to a brahmin, or 'Thou' to a superior, / having bathed, not eating for the remainder of the day, and saluting him, one should propitiate him.
Having struck him even with a blade of grass, or tied him by the neck with a cloth, / or defeated him in debate, one should bow down and propitiate him.
Raising [a hand or weapon against a brahmin], one goes to hell for a hundred years; / but striking [him] with the desire to kill, for a thousand [years].
As many dust particles as the blood of a twice-born binds, / for that many thousands of years the perpetrator shall dwell in hell.
Having threatened [a brahmin], he should perform a kṛcchra; an ati-kṛcchra upon striking down; / having caused blood from a brahmin, he should perform a kṛcchrātikṛcchra.
Daily study of the Veda according to ability, performance of the great sacrifices, and forbearance / swiftly destroy even sins born of mortal sins.

3.235
हंस उवाच ..
इत्येतदेनसामुक्तं प्रायश्चित्तं यधाविधि ..
अत ऊर्ध्वं रहस्यानां प्रायश्चित्तं निबोधत .. 1 ..

text_mt:
Just as fire instantly burns what it encounters through its brilliance, / so the knower of the Veda burns all sin through the fire of knowledge.
Having ascertained a man's persistence in sin, his capacity, place, and time, / purification not explicitly taught should be given upon reflection, and this must also be examined when it has been stated.
3.235
The Haṃsa said:
Thus has been spoken the expiation for sins according to rule.
Henceforth, learn the expiation for secret [sins].
Sixteen breath-controls with the vyāhṛtis and the Praṇava,
performed day after day, purify even the slayer of an embryo in a month.
Having recited the Kautsa [hymn], the one beginning with 'aja', the Vāsiṣṭha [hymn], and each triplet,
the Māhitra and the Śuddhavatīs, even a drinker of liquor is purified.
Having recited once the Asyavāmīya hymn and the Śivasaṃkalpa,
one who has stolen gold becomes stainless in an instant.
Having repeated the Haviṣmat hymn and the one beginning 'na tamaṃhaḥ',
and reciting the Puruṣasūkta, a violator of the Guru's bed is freed.

text_mt:
Wishing to dispel sins, gross or subtle,
one should recite for a year the verse 'apa' and that beginning 'yat kiñcedam'.
Having accepted what should not be accepted and having eaten condemned food,
a man reciting the Taratsamandı̄ya is purified in three days.
One of many sins is purified by repeating the Somāraudra hymn for a month,
bathing in a river, and [reciting] the triplet beginning 'aryamṇam'.
A sinner should recite the heptad beginning 'indram' for half a year;
having done what is blameworthy in water, he should subsist on alms for a month.
Having offered ghee for a year with the Śākalahomīya mantras,
or reciting the verse 'namaḥ', a twice-born destroys even very heavy sin.
One tainted by minor sins should follow cows with concentrated mind;
repeating the Pāvamānī hymns for a year while subsisting on alms, he is purified.
Or repeating the Vedic Saṃhitā three times in a forest, restrained,
he is freed from all sins, purified by three Parāka austerities.

One who fasts for three days, going to the waters thrice a day,
is freed from all sins having recited the Aghamarṣaṇa thrice.
Repeating three times the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā or that of the Yajurvedas with concentrated mind,
or of the Sāmans along with the secret teachings, he is freed from all sins.
Which is the verbal form of that Supreme Person in whom the entire world is bound—
reciting that Oṃkāra with unflagging mind, a mortal quickly casts off sins.

We wish to hear of the deeds by which sin is destroyed,

The Haṃsa said:
For three days in the morning, for three days in the evening, for three days he should eat unasked-for food,
and for the next three days he should not eat; [thus] a twice-born performs the Prājāpatya vow.

Cow's urine, cow dung, milk, curd, ghee, and kuśa-grass water,
and fasting for one night: this is known as the Sāntapana penance.

he should practice non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, and uprightness.

Thrice by day and thrice by night he should enter the water with his clothes on;
and he should never speak to women, śūdras, or fallen outcasts.

He should pass the time by standing and sitting, or if unable, he may lie on the ground;
he should be celibate, observing vows, worshipping gurus, gods, and twice-borns.

meaning:
ख्यापनेनानुतापेन तपसाध्ययनेन च ..
पामकृन्मुच्यते पापात्तथा दानेन चापरः..13..
text_mt:
By confession, by repentance, by ascetic austerity, and by sacred study,
a sinner is freed from sin; and another likewise by giving gifts.

sanskrit_iast:
yasminkarmaṇyapi kṛte manasaḥ syādalāghavam ..
tasmim̐stāvattapaḥ kuryādyāvattuṣṭikaraṃ bhavet..14..
meaning:
यस्मिन्कर्मण्यपि कृते मनसः स्यादलाघवम् ..
तस्मिम्̐स्तावत्तपः कुर्याद्यावत्तुष्टिकरं भवेत्..14..
text_mt:
Whatever deed having been done causes unease of mind,
one should perform ascetic austerity for that until satisfaction arises.

sanskrit_iast:
pāpasya nāśastapasā vidheyo dharmasya vṛddhistapasā vidheyā ..
pāpapraṇāśe tvatha dharmavṛddhau kāmāḥ samṛdhyanti narasya viprāḥ .. 15 ..

.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..

जप्येन कामानाप्नोति सत्येन च परां गतिम् ..3 ..

ध्यानेन धारणाभिश्च पदमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ..4 ..

शौचेन देवाः प्रीयन्ते प्रीयन्ते चोपवासतः .. 5..
उपवासप्रतप्तानां कामावाप्तिर्ध्रुवं भवेत् ..
ददाति विपुलान्भोगान्संग्रामेष्वपलायिनाम् .. 6 ..

sanskrit_iast:
madhumāṃsanivṛtto'pi paraṃ saukhyamupāśnute ..
ahiṃsayā tvarogī syāddīrghāyuścāpyahiṃsayā..7..
rūpalāvaṇyasaubhāgyadhanadhānyayutaḥ sadā ..
tīrthānusaraṇādviprāḥ pāpanāśamavāpnuyāt.8..
sarvakalmaṣahīnaśca yām̐llokānmanasecchati ..
pratiśrayapradānena sthānamāpnotyanuttamam ..9..

samaṃ kṛtvā vivardhante kīrtirāryuyaśo balam .. 11 ..

sarvakāmānavāpnoti brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati .. 12 ..

pānīyamapi viprendrā brāhmaṃ lokaṃ prapadyate .. 13 ..

sarvānkāmānavāpnoti gatimāpnotyabhīpsitām .. 14 ..
meaning:
मधुमांसनिवृत्तोऽपि परं सौख्यमुपाश्नुते ..
अहिंसया त्वरोगी स्याद्दीर्घायुश्चाप्यहिंसया..7..
रूपलावण्यसौभाग्यधनधान्ययुतः सदा ..
तीर्थानुसरणाद्विप्राः पापनाशमवाप्नुयात्.8..
सर्वकल्मषहीनश्च याम्̐ल्लोकान्मनसेच्छति ..
प्रतिश्रयप्रदानेन स्थानमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ..9..
पूज्यपूजयिता विप्रा यशसा युज्यते नरः ..
अभिवादनशीलस्य नित्यं वृद्धोपसेविनः..3.237.10..
समं कृत्वा विवर्धन्ते कीर्तिरार्युयशो बलम् .. 11 ..
ऋतुकालादृते भार्या तथैव परिवर्जयेत् ..
सर्वकामानवाप्नोति ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति .. 12 ..
उभौ कालौ तु भुञ्जानस्त्वन्तरा परिवर्जयेत् ..
पानीयमपि विप्रेन्द्रा ब्राह्मं लोकं प्रपद्यते .. 13 ..
अनेनैव विधानेन देशकालाशनो नरः ..
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति गतिमाप्नोत्यभीप्सिताम् .. 14 ..
text_mt:
One who abstains from alcohol and meat also enjoys supreme happiness;
by non-violence one is free from disease, and by non-violence one gains long life.
He is constantly endowed with physical beauty, charm, good fortune, wealth, and grain;
by visiting sacred bathing places, O brahmins, one obtains destruction of sins.
Free from all defilements, whatever worlds he desires in his mind,
by giving shelter he attains the unsurpassed abode.
The man who honours those worthy of honour, O brahmins, is endowed with glory. / For one who is inclined to prostration and constantly attends upon the elders,
all together increase: fame, lifespan, glory, and strength.
Likewise, one who avoids his wife except during the fertile period / obtains all desires and goes to the world of Brahmā.
Eating at both times, but avoiding [food] in between, / even water, O foremost of brahmins, he attains the world of Brahmā.
A man who eats according to place and time by this very rule / obtains all desires and attains his wished-for state.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā bhojanakāle tu maunaṃ yastu samācaret ..
upavāsaphalantasya pratyahaṃ bhojane smṛtam .. 15 ..
meaning:
तथा भोजनकाले तु मौनं यस्तु समाचरेत् ..
उपवासफलन्तस्य प्रत्यहं भोजने स्मृतम् .. 15 ..
text_mt: Moreover, he who observes silence at the time of eating / is regarded as gaining the fruit of fasting each day with his meal.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti maunī naktāśanassakṛt ..
nāpnoti nārakaṃ duḥkhaṃ nityasnāyī naro bahiḥ ..16..
meaning:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति मौनी नक्ताशनस्सकृत् ..
नाप्नोति नारकं दुःखं नित्यस्नायी नरो बहिः ..16..
text_mt: Silent, eating only at night, he obtains all desires; / a man who constantly bathes outdoors does not encounter the suffering of hell.

sanskrit_iast:
yo dadyādaparikliṣṭamannamadhvani vartate ..
śrāntāyādṛṣṭapūrvāya tasya puṇyaphalaṃ mahat .. 17 ..
meaning:
यो दद्यादपरिक्लिष्टमन्नमध्वनि वर्तते ..
श्रान्तायादृष्टपूर्वाय तस्य पुण्यफलं महत् .. 17 ..
text_mt: Whoever gives unwearied food to someone travelling on the road, / tired and never seen before, gains great meritorious fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
pādyamāsanamevātha dīpamannaṃ pratiśrayam ..
dadyādatithipūjārthaṃ yajñāḥ pañca sudakṣiṇāḥ.. 18 ..
meaning:
पाद्यमासनमेवाथ दीपमन्नं प्रतिश्रयम् ..
दद्यादतिथिपूजार्थं यज्ञाः पञ्च सुदक्षिणाः.. 18 ..
text_mt: Water for the feet, a seat, a lamp, food, and shelter: / one should provide these to honour a guest; these are five sacrifices with generous fees.

sanskrit_iast:
cakṣurdadyānmano dadyādvācaṃ dadyācca sūnṛtām ..
anuvrajedupāsīta yajñāḥ pañca sudakṣiṇāḥ ..19..
meaning:
चक्षुर्दद्यान्मनो दद्याद्वाचं दद्याच्च सूनृताम् ..
अनुव्रजेदुपासीत यज्ञाः पञ्च सुदक्षिणाः ..19..
text_mt: One should offer a friendly look, one should offer a kindly mind, and one should speak truthful, pleasant speech; / one should accompany [him when leaving] and attend upon [him]: these are five sacrifices with generous fees.

sanskrit_iast:
sthaṇḍileṣu śayānānāṃ gṛhāṇi śayanāni ca ..
cīra valkalasaṃvīta vāsāṃsyābharaṇāni ca ..3.237.20..
meaning:
स्थण्डिलेषु शयानानां गृहाणि शयनानि च ..
चीर वल्कलसंवीत वासांस्याभरणानि च ..3.237.20..
text_mt: For those who sleep on bare ground, houses and beds [are granted]; / for those clad in rags and bark, garments and ornaments [are granted];

sanskrit_iast:
vāhanāsanayānāni yogātmani tapodhane ..
agnīnupaśayānasya rājapauruṣamucyate .. 21..
meaning:
वाहनासनयानानि योगात्मनि तपोधने ..
अग्नीनुपशयानस्य राजपौरुषमुच्यते .. 21..
text_mt: mounts, seats, and vehicles for one whose self is in yoga and whose wealth is asceticism; / for one who sleeps beside the fires, royal prowess is declared.

sanskrit_iast:
rasānāṃ prati saṃhāre saubhāgyamadhigacchati ..
āmiṣapratisaṃhāre sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..22..
meaning:
रसानां प्रति संहारे सौभाग्यमधिगच्छति ..
आमिषप्रतिसंहारे सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ..22..
text_mt: By giving up relishes, he attains good fortune; / by giving up meat, he would obtain all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
arvākśirāstu yo lambettoyavāsaṃ ca yo vaset ..
satataṃ caikaśāyī ca labhate cepsitāṃ gatim ..23..
meaning:
अर्वाक्शिरास्तु यो लम्बेत्तोयवासं च यो वसेत् ..
सततं चैकशायी च लभते चेप्सितां गतिम् ..23..
text_mt: He who hangs head downwards, he who dwells in water, / and he who constantly sleeps alone, attains his desired destination.

sanskrit_iast:
vīrāsanaṃ vīraśayyāṃ vīrasthānamupāsataḥ ..
akṣayāstasya vai lokāḥ sarvakāmapradāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
वीरासनं वीरशय्यां वीरस्थानमुपासतः ..
अक्षयास्तस्य वै लोकाः सर्वकामप्रदाः स्मृताः .. 24 ..
text_mt: For one who practises the hero's posture, the hero's bed, and the hero's station, / imperishable worlds granting all desires are declared for him.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanaṃ bhavati dānena maunenājñāṃ prayacchati ..
upabhogām̐śca tapasā brahmacaryeṇa jīvitam .. 25 ..
meaning:
धनं भवति दानेन मौनेनाज्ञां प्रयच्छति ..
उपभोगाम्̐श्च तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण जीवितम् .. 25 ..
text_mt: Wealth comes through giving; through silence he imparts authority; / pleasures through ascetic heat, and long life through celibacy.

sanskrit_iast:
rūpamaiśvaryamārogyamahiṃsāphalamaśnute ..
phalaṃ phalāśināṃ rājyaṃ svargaḥ parṇāśināṃ phalam ..26..
meaning:
रूपमैश्वर्यमारोग्यमहिंसाफलमश्नुते ..
फलं फलाशिनां राज्यं स्वर्गः पर्णाशिनां फलम् ..26..
text_mt: Beauty, sovereignty, and health he enjoys as the fruit of non-violence. / Sovereignty is the fruit for those who eat fruit; heaven is the fruit for those who eat leaves.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpāśināṃ tathaiśvaryaṃ dhanaṃ śākāśināṃ mahat ..
payobhakṣyā divaṃ yāṃti abbhakṣyāścāmitāṃ gatim ..27 ..
meaning:
पुष्पाशिनां तथैश्वर्यं धनं शाकाशिनां महत् ..
पयोभक्ष्या दिवं यांति अब्भक्ष्याश्चामितां गतिम् ..27 ..
text_mt: Sovereignty likewise for those who eat flowers; great wealth for those who eat greens. / Those who subsist on milk go to heaven, and those who subsist on water go to an immeasurable destination.

sanskrit_iast:
daṃtolūkhaliko vipro yaścāpyuñchena jīvati ..
kāpotīñcāśrito vṛttiṃ yatheṣṭāṅgatimāpnuyāt .. 28 ..
meaning:
दंतोलूखलिको विप्रो यश्चाप्युञ्छेन जीवति ..
कापोतीञ्चाश्रितो वृत्तिं यथेष्टाङ्गतिमाप्नुयात् .. 28 ..
text_mt: A brahmin using his teeth as a mortar, and he who lives by gleaning, / or undertakes the livelihood of a pigeon, would attain a destination as he desires.

sanskrit_iast:
prāyopaveśanādrājyaṃ sarvatra phalamaśnute..
svargaṃ satyena labhate dīkṣayā kulamuttamam .. 29 ..
meaning:
प्रायोपवेशनाद्राज्यं सर्वत्र फलमश्नुते..
स्वर्गं सत्येन लभते दीक्षया कुलमुत्तमम् .. 29 ..
text_mt: From fasting unto death, he enjoys sovereignty everywhere as the fruit; / he obtains heaven through truthfulness, and a superior lineage through consecration.

sanskrit_iast: gavoḍhāḥ śākadīkṣāyāḥ svargakāmī tṛṇāśanaḥ ..3.237.30..
meaning: गवोढाः शाकदीक्षायाः स्वर्गकामी तृणाशनः ..3.237.30..
text_mt: Desiring heaven, one who bears the yoke of cattle, who is consecrated to eating greens, or who eats grass,

sanskrit_iast:
tryahastriṣavaṇaṃ snātvā vāyuṃ pītvā kratuṃ labhet ..
yajñayājī tathāpnoti yām̐llokānmanasecchati .. 31 ..
meaning:
त्र्यहस्त्रिषवणं स्नात्वा वायुं पीत्वा क्रतुं लभेत् ..
यज्ञयाजी तथाप्नोति याम्̐ल्लोकान्मनसेच्छति .. 31 ..
text_mt: bathing at the three junctures of the day for three days and drinking wind, obtains [the fruit of] a sacrifice; / a performer of sacrifice likewise attains whatever worlds he desires in his mind.

sanskrit_iast:
upavāsaṃ ca dīkṣāṃ cāpyabhiṣekaṃ ca vai dvijāḥ ..
kṛtvā dvādaśavarṣāṇi vīrasthānādviśiṣyate ..32..
meaning:
उपवासं च दीक्षां चाप्यभिषेकं च वै द्विजाः ..
कृत्वा द्वादशवर्षाणि वीरस्थानाद्विशिष्यते ..32..
text_mt: O twice-born, having performed fasting, consecration, and ablutions / for twelve years, he surpasses the hero's station.

sanskrit_iast:
adhītya sarvānvedānvai sarvaduḥkhairvimucyate ..
mānasaṃ hi dhanaṃ dharmaḥ svargalokamavāpnuyāt ..33..
meaning:
अधीत्य सर्वान्वेदान्वै सर्वदुःखैर्विमुच्यते ..
मानसं हि धनं धर्मः स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात् ..33..
text_mt: Having studied all the Vedas, he is indeed freed from all suffering; / dharma is mental wealth; he would attain the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast:
yena prīṇāti pitaraṃ tena prītaḥ prajāpatiḥ..
prīṇāti mātaraṃ yena pṛthivī tena pūjitā.. 34..
meaning:
येन प्रीणाति पितरं तेन प्रीतः प्रजापतिः..
प्रीणाति मातरं येन पृथिवी तेन पूजिता.. 34..
text_mt: By that with which he pleases his father, Prajāpati is pleased; / by that with which he pleases his mother, the Earth is honoured.

sanskrit_iast:
yena prīṇātyupādhyāyantena syādbrahma pūjitam..
sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ..35...
meaning:
येन प्रीणात्युपाध्यायन्तेन स्याद्ब्रह्म पूजितम्..
सर्वे तस्यादृता धर्मा यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः..35...
text_mt: By that with which he pleases his teacher, the Veda would be honoured; / all dharmas are revered for him by whom these three are revered.

sanskrit_iast:
anādṛtāstu yasyaite sarvāstasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ ..
guruśuśrūṣayā vidyā nityaṃ śrāddheṣu santatiḥ..36..
meaning:
अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफलाः क्रियाः ..
गुरुशुश्रूषया विद्या नित्यं श्राद्धेषु सन्ततिः..36..
text_mt: For him by whom these are disregarded, all his rites are fruitless. / Knowledge comes through service to the guru, and constant progeny through ancestral rites.

sanskrit_iast:
nityasnāyī bhaveddakṣaḥ saṃdhye tu dve japansadā..
dvijaśuśrūṣayā rājyaṃ dvijatvaṃ vāpi puṣkalam ..37 ..
meaning:
नित्यस्नायी भवेद्दक्षः संध्ये तु द्वे जपन्सदा..
द्विजशुश्रूषया राज्यं द्विजत्वं वापि पुष्कलम् ..37 ..
text_mt: One who bathes regularly should become capable, constantly reciting [mantras] at the two twilights. / Sovereignty or abundant brahminhood comes through service to the twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
devaśuśrūṣayā kāmānyatheṣṭānprāpnuyānnaraḥ ..
sāntvadaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvaśokaiḥ pramucyate .. 38 ..
meaning:
देवशुश्रूषया कामान्यथेष्टान्प्राप्नुयान्नरः ..
सान्त्वदः सर्वभूतानां सर्वशोकैः प्रमुच्यते .. 38 ..
text_mt: Through service to the gods, a man would obtain desires as he wishes; / one who gives comfort to all beings is freed from all griefs.

sanskrit_iast:
keśaśmaśrūnvārayataḥ tvagryā bhavati santatiḥ ..
gandhamālyānnivṛttyā tu kīrtirbhavati puṣkalā .. 39 ..
meaning:
केशश्मश्रून्वारयतः त्वग्र्या भवति सन्ततिः ..
गन्धमाल्यान्निवृत्त्या तु कीर्तिर्भवति पुष्कला .. 39 ..
text_mt: For one who restrains his hair and beard, foremost progeny arises; / through abstention from perfume and garlands, abundant fame arises.

sanskrit_iast:
paricaryārataḥ samyaṅ na rogaistvabhibhūyate ..
golokamāpnoti tathā gavāñca paricaryayā .. 3.237.40 ..
meaning:
परिचर्यारतः सम्यङ् न रोगैस्त्वभिभूयते ..
गोलोकमाप्नोति तथा गवाञ्च परिचर्यया .. 3.237.40 ..
text_mt: One who is devoted to proper service is not overcome by illnesses; / and through service to cattle he attains the world of cows.

sanskrit_iast:
devamālyāpanayanātpādaśaucāddvijasya tu ..
śrāntasaṃvāhanādviprāḥ sukhamatyantamaśnute .. 41 ..
meaning:
देवमाल्यापनयनात्पादशौचाद्द्विजस्य तु ..
श्रान्तसंवाहनाद्विप्राः सुखमत्यन्तमश्नुते .. 41 ..
text_mt: From clearing away the god’s garlands, from washing the feet of a twice-born, / and from massaging the weary, O brahmins, he enjoys supreme happiness.

sanskrit_iast:
jale saptasahasrāṇi ekādaśa hutāśane ..
bhṛguprapāte ca daśa saṃgrāme viṃśatistathā .. 42 ..
meaning:
जले सप्तसहस्राणि एकादश हुताशने ..
भृगुप्रपाते च दश संग्रामे विंशतिस्तथा .. 42 ..
text_mt: [He rejoices for] seven thousand [years] in water, eleven [thousand] in fire, / and ten [thousand] from falling from a cliff, and twenty [thousand] in battle;

sanskrit_iast:
naro varṣasahasrāṇi tanuṃ tyaktvā tu modate .
anāśake tu dharmajñāḥ parisaṃkhyā na vidyate .. 43 ..
meaning:
नरो वर्षसहस्राणि तनुं त्यक्त्वा तु मोदते .
अनाशके तु धर्मज्ञाः परिसंख्या न विद्यते .. 43 ..
text_mt: having abandoned his body, a man rejoices for thousands of years. / But for death by starvation, O knowers of dharma, no limit is found.

sanskrit_iast:
merau sādhayate rājyaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ bhuvi jāyate ..
mahāprasthānamāviśya yatheṣṭāṃ gatimāpnuyāt .. 44 ..
meaning:
मेरौ साधयते राज्यं यथेष्टं भुवि जायते ..
महाप्रस्थानमाविश्य यथेष्टां गतिमाप्नुयात् .. 44 ..
text_mt: He establishes sovereignty on Meru, or is born on earth as he desires; / having entered upon the great departure, he would obtain his desired destination.

sanskrit_iast:
vahnipraveśaniyatamamīṣṭaṃ lokamaśnute ..
vāruṇaṃ lokamāpnoti tyaktvāmbhasi tanuṃ naraḥ..45..
meaning:
वह्निप्रवेशनियतममीष्टं लोकमश्नुते ..
वारुणं लोकमाप्नोति त्यक्त्वाम्भसि तनुं नरः..45..
text_mt: He who is disciplined in entering fire enjoys his desired world; / a man who casts off his body in water attains the world of Varuṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
anārto vyādhirahito na tyajedātmanastanum ..
asūryā nāma te lokā andhena tamasā vṛtāḥ ..
tām̐ste pretyābhigacchanti ye ke cātmahano janāḥ ..46..
meaning:
अनार्तो व्याधिरहितो न त्यजेदात्मनस्तनुम् ..
असूर्या नाम ते लोका अन्धेन तमसा वृताः ..
ताम्̐स्ते प्रेत्याभिगच्छन्ति ये के चात्महनो जनाः ..46..
text_mt: One who is not afflicted and is free from disease must not cast off his own body. / Sunless indeed are those worlds, enveloped in blind darkness; / to them after death go those people who are slayers of the self.

sanskrit_iast:
aniṣṭairātmano jñātvā mṛtyukālamupasthitam ..
vyādhito bhiṣajā tyaktaḥ pūrṇe cāyuṣi vāsake .. ..47..
meaning:
अनिष्टैरात्मनो ज्ञात्वा मृत्युकालमुपस्थितम् ..
व्याधितो भिषजा त्यक्तः पूर्णे चायुषि वासके .. ..47..
text_mt: Having recognised by inauspicious signs that the time of death has arrived, / sick, given up by the physician, when his lifespan has been completed,

sanskrit_iast:
yathāgamānusāreṇa saṃtyajedātmanastanum ..
tasminkāle tanutyāgādyathoktaṃ phalamāpnuyāt ..48..
meaning:
यथागमानुसारेण संत्यजेदात्मनस्तनुम् ..
तस्मिन्काले तनुत्यागाद्यथोक्तं फलमाप्नुयात् ..48..
text_mt: he should cast off his own body in accordance with the scriptures. / From the abandonment of the body at that time, he would obtain the fruit as stated.

sanskrit_iast:
āyuṣastu paraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ maraṇaṃ brāhmaṇa dvayoḥ ..
kṣatriyasya tu saṅgrāme mṛte bhartari yoṣitaḥ ..49..
meaning:
आयुषस्तु परं दृष्टं मरणं ब्राह्मण द्वयोः ..
क्षत्रियस्य तु सङ्ग्रामे मृते भर्तरि योषितः ..49..
text_mt: Death after the end of lifespan is seen for the two: / for a kṣatriya in battle, and for a woman when her husband has died.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇārthe gavārthe vā yastyajedātmanastanum ..
ātmānaṃ yūpamutsṛjya sa yajño'nantadakṣiṇaḥ .. .. 3.237.50 ..
meaning:
ब्राह्मणार्थे गवार्थे वा यस्त्यजेदात्मनस्तनुम् ..
आत्मानं यूपमुत्सृज्य स यज्ञोऽनन्तदक्षिणः .. .. 3.237.50 ..
text_mt: Whoever casts off his own body for the sake of a brahmin or for the sake of a cow, / abandoning himself as the sacrificial post, that sacrifice has infinite fees.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṣpaṃ mṛgakharotsṛṣṭaṃ yo mṛgaiḥ saha sevate ..
dīkṣito vai mudā yuktaḥ sa gacchatyamarāvatīm .. 51 ..
meaning:
शष्पं मृगखरोत्सृष्टं यो मृगैः सह सेवते ..
दीक्षितो वै मुदा युक्तः स गच्छत्यमरावतीम् .. 51 ..
text_mt: He who partakes of young grass left by deer and wild asses, together with deer, / consecrated and filled with joy, goes to Amarāvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
rovalaṃ śīrṇaparṇaṃ vā tadvrataṃ yo niṣevate ..
śānto yo manasā nityaṃ sa gacchetparamāṅgatim .. 52 ..
meaning:
रोवलं शीर्णपर्णं वा तद्व्रतं यो निषेवते ..
शान्तो यो मनसा नित्यं स गच्छेत्परमाङ्गतिम् .. 52 ..
text_mt: He who observes that vow [living on] roots or fallen leaves, / who is ever calm in mind, would go to the supreme state.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyubhakṣyombubhakṣyo vā phalamūlāśanopi vā ..
yakṣeśaiśvaryamādāya modate'psarasāṅgaṇaiḥ .. 53 ..
meaning:
वायुभक्ष्योम्बुभक्ष्यो वा फलमूलाशनोपि वा ..
यक्षेशैश्वर्यमादाय मोदतेऽप्सरसाङ्गणैः .. 53 ..
text_mt: Subsisting on wind, subsisting on water, or eating fruit and roots, / receiving the sovereignty of the lord of the yakṣas, he rejoices with hosts of apsarases.

sanskrit_iast:
agniyogavaho grīṣme vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā ..
tīrttvā dvādaśavarṣāṇi rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
अग्नियोगवहो ग्रीष्मे विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा ..
तीर्त्त्वा द्वादशवर्षाणि राजा भवति पार्थिवः .. 54 ..
text_mt: Enduring the yoga of the [five] fires in the summer, through rites prescribed by rule, / having crossed twelve years, he becomes an earthly king.

sanskrit_iast:
āhāraniyamaṃ kṛtvā munirdvādaśavārṣikam ..
vrataṃ saṃsādhya kāle tu rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ .. 55 ..
meaning:
आहारनियमं कृत्वा मुनिर्द्वादशवार्षिकम् ..
व्रतं संसाध्य काले तु राजा भवति पार्थिवः .. 55 ..
text_mt: The sage, having observed dietary restriction for twelve years / and having fulfilled the vow in due time, becomes an earthly king.

sanskrit_iast:
sthaṇḍile śuddhamākāśaṃ parigṛhya samantataḥ ..
praviśya ca mudā yukto dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm .. 56 ..
meaning:
स्थण्डिले शुद्धमाकाशं परिगृह्य समन्ततः ..
प्रविश्य च मुदा युक्तो दीक्षां द्वादशवार्षिकीम् .. 56 ..
text_mt: Surrounding himself completely with clear open space on a bare patch of ground, / and entering upon a twelve-year consecration with a joyful mind,

sanskrit_iast:
sthaṇḍilasya phalānyāhuryānāni śayanāni ca ..
gṛhāṇi śayanārhāṇi candraśubhrāṇi brāhmaṇaḥ .. 57 .
meaning:
स्थण्डिलस्य फलान्याहुर्यानानि शयनानि च ..
गृहाणि शयनार्हाणि चन्द्रशुभ्राणि ब्राह्मणः .. 57 .
text_mt: they say the fruits of [lying on] bare ground are vehicles and couches, / and houses worthy of reclining in, bright as the moon, O brahmin.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānamupajīvanyo niyato niyatāśanaḥ ..
dehaṃ cānaśane tyaktvā sa svargaṃ samupāśnute .. 58 ..
meaning:
आत्मानमुपजीवन्यो नियतो नियताशनः ..
देहं चानशने त्यक्त्वा स स्वर्गं समुपाश्नुते .. 58 ..
text_mt: One who relies only on himself, restrained and of measured food, / and gives up his body through fasting, attains heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānamupajīvanyo dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm ..
aśmanā caraṇau hatvā guhyakeṣu ca modate .. 59 ..
meaning:
आत्मानमुपजीवन्यो दीक्षां द्वादशवार्षिकीम् ..
अश्मना चरणौ हत्वा गुह्यकेषु च मोदते .. 59 ..
text_mt: One who relies only on himself through a twelve-year consecration, / having struck his feet with a stone, rejoices among the Guhyakas.

sanskrit_iast:
sādhayitvātmanātmānaṃ nirdvandvo niṣparigrahaḥ ..
tīrtvā dvādaśavarṣāṇi dīkṣāmekāṃmanogatām ..
svargalokamavāpnoti devaiśca saha modate .. 3.237.60 ..
meaning:
साधयित्वात्मनात्मानं निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः ..
तीर्त्वा द्वादशवर्षाणि दीक्षामेकांमनोगताम् ..
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति देवैश्च सह मोदते .. 3.237.60 ..
text_mt: Having perfected the self by means of the self, free from the pairs of opposites, without possessions, / having passed through twelve years of an exclusive consecration fixed in the mind, / he reaches the heavenly world and rejoices with the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānamupajīvanyo dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm ..
hutvāgnau dehamutsṛjya vahniloke mahīyate .. 61 ..
meaning:
आत्मानमुपजीवन्यो दीक्षां द्वादशवार्षिकीम् ..
हुत्वाग्नौ देहमुत्सृज्य वह्निलोके महीयते .. 61 ..
text_mt: One who relies only on himself through a twelve-year consecration, / having offered himself into the fire and cast off his body, is glorified in the world of Agni.

sanskrit_iast:
yastu vipro yathānyāyaṃ dīkṣito niyatendriyaḥ ..
ātmanyātmānamādāya nirdvandvo dharmalālasaḥ .. 62 ..
meaning:
यस्तु विप्रो यथान्यायं दीक्षितो नियतेन्द्रियः ..
आत्मन्यात्मानमादाय निर्द्वन्द्वो धर्मलालसः .. 62 ..
text_mt: A wise brahmin who is consecrated according to rule, with restrained senses, / withdrawing the self into the self, free from the pairs of opposites, eager for dharma,

sanskrit_iast:
cīrtvā dvādaśa varṣāṇi dīkṣāmetāṃ manogatām..
araṇīsahitaḥ skandhe baddhvā gacchatyanāvṛtam .. 63 ..
meaning:
चीर्त्वा द्वादश वर्षाणि दीक्षामेतां मनोगताम्..
अरणीसहितः स्कन्धे बद्ध्वा गच्छत्यनावृतम् .. 63 ..
text_mt: having observed this consecration fixed in the mind for twelve years, / with fire-sticks bound upon his shoulder, goes to the unobstructed realm.

sanskrit_iast:
vīrāddhvānamanānītya vīrāsanaratassadā ..
vīrasthāyī ca satataṃ sa vīragatimāpnuyāt .. 64 ..
meaning:
वीराद्ध्वानमनानीत्य वीरासनरतस्सदा ..
वीरस्थायी च सततं स वीरगतिमाप्नुयात् .. 64 ..
text_mt: Not swerving from the path of heroes, always devoted to the hero's posture, / and ever abiding as a hero, he would attain the destiny of heroes.

sanskrit_iast:
dhīralokagato vīro vīrayogavahaḥ sadā ..
satvasthaḥ sarvamutsṛjya dīkṣito niyataḥ śuciḥ ..
śakralokagataḥ śrīmānmodate divi devavat .. 65 ..
meaning:
धीरलोकगतो वीरो वीरयोगवहः सदा ..
सत्वस्थः सर्वमुत्सृज्य दीक्षितो नियतः शुचिः ..
शक्रलोकगतः श्रीमान्मोदते दिवि देववत् .. 65 ..
text_mt: The hero who has gone to the world of the steadfast, always maintaining heroic discipline, / established in sattva, casting aside everything, consecrated, self-controlled, pure, / having gone to Śakra's world, radiant, rejoices in heaven like a god.

sanskrit_iast:
upavāsavratairdāntā ahiṃsāsatyavādinaḥ ..
saṃsiddhāḥ pretya gandharvaiḥ saha modantyanāmayāḥ .. 66 ..
meaning:
उपवासव्रतैर्दान्ता अहिंसासत्यवादिनः ..
संसिद्धाः प्रेत्य गन्धर्वैः सह मोदन्त्यनामयाः .. 66 ..
text_mt: Subdued through vows of fasting, devoted to non-violence and speaking the truth, / perfected, free from affliction, after death they rejoice with the Gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast:
maṇḍūkayogaśayanā yathāsthānaṃ yathāvidhi ..
dīkṣāṃ carati dharmātmā sa nāgaiḥ saha modate .. 67 ..
meaning:
मण्डूकयोगशयना यथास्थानं यथाविधि ..
दीक्षां चरति धर्मात्मा स नागैः सह मोदते .. 67 ..
text_mt: Lying down in the frog posture according to place and according to rule, / the righteous one who observes this consecration rejoices with the Nāgas.

sanskrit_iast:
ārdravāsāstu śiśire vrataṃ vahati yo naraḥ ..
dvādaśābdāni niyataṃ rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ ..68..
meaning:
आर्द्रवासास्तु शिशिरे व्रतं वहति यो नरः ..
द्वादशाब्दानि नियतं राजा भवति पार्थिवः ..68..
text_mt: The man who, clad in wet clothes during the cold season, bears this vow / with restraint for twelve years, becomes an earthly king.

sanskrit_iast:
varṣarātre tathā yaśca bhavatyākāśasādhakaḥ ..
anapastīrthaśāyī ca rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ..69 ..
meaning:
वर्षरात्रे तथा यश्च भवत्याकाशसाधकः ..
अनपस्तीर्थशायी च राजा भवति पार्थिवः..69 ..
text_mt: And he who, during the rainy season, accomplishes [his vow] under the open sky / and lies down at a sacred ford without [shelter from] water, becomes an earthly king.

sanskrit_iast:
tyaktvā vanagatāḥ prāṇānsaptapūrvāṃstathāparān ..
narāṃstārayitā duḥkhādātmānaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 3.237.70 ..
meaning:
त्यक्त्वा वनगताः प्राणान्सप्तपूर्वांस्तथापरान् ..
नरांस्तारयिता दुःखादात्मानं च विशेषतः .. 3.237.70 ..
text_mt: Having given up their life-breaths in the forest, / they deliver from suffering seven preceding generations and seven succeeding, and especially themselves.

sanskrit_iast:
yenayena śarīreṇa yadyatkarma karoti yaḥ ..
tenatena śarīreṇa tattatphalamupāśnute .. 71 ..
meaning:
येनयेन शरीरेण यद्यत्कर्म करोति यः ..
तेनतेन शरीरेण तत्तत्फलमुपाश्नुते .. 71 ..
text_mt: With whatever body one performs whatever deed, / with that very body he experiences that very fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāṃ yasyāmavasthāyāṃ yatkaroti śubhāśubham ..
tasyāṃ tasyāmavasthāyāṃ tatphalamupāśnute .. 72 ..
meaning:
यस्यां यस्यामवस्थायां यत्करोति शुभाशुभम् ..
तस्यां तस्यामवस्थायां तत्फलमुपाश्नुते .. 72 ..
text_mt: In whatever stage of life one does good or evil, / in that very stage of life he experiences its fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
nareṇa hi kṛtaṃ karma sadā pañcendriyairiha ..
te hyasya sākṣiṇo nityaṃ ṣaṣṭha ātmā tathaiva ca .. 73 ..
meaning:
नरेण हि कृतं कर्म सदा पञ्चेन्द्रियैरिह ..
ते ह्यस्य साक्षिणो नित्यं षष्ठ आत्मा तथैव च .. 73 ..
text_mt: A deed performed here by a man always through his five senses / has those very [senses] as its eternal witnesses, and the sixth is the self likewise.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā dhenusahasreṣu vatso vindati mātaram ..
evametatkṛtaṃ karma karttāramanuvindati..74..
meaning:
यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम् ..
एवमेतत्कृतं कर्म कर्त्तारमनुविन्दति..74..
text_mt: Just as a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows, / so this deed that was performed finds its doer.

sanskrit_iast:
avaśyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ karma bhoktavyaṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ vāpi tasmātsukṛtamācaret ..75..
meaning:
अवश्यं हि कृतं कर्म भोक्तव्यं द्विजपुङ्गवाः ..
सुकृतं दुष्कृतं वापि तस्मात्सुकृतमाचरेत् ..75..
text_mt: For a deed that has been done must inevitably be experienced, O foremost of the twice-born, / whether it be good or evil; therefore one should practice good deeds.

sanskrit_iast:
acodyamānāni yathā puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca ..
svakālaṃ nātivartante tathā karma purā kṛtam .. 76 ..
meaning:
अचोद्यमानानि यथा पुष्पाणि च फलानि च ..
स्वकालं नातिवर्तन्ते तथा कर्म पुरा कृतम् .. 76 ..
text_mt: Just as flowers and fruits, without being urged, / do not pass by their proper season, so it is with deeds done in the past.

sanskrit_iast:
yanmantre bhavati vṛthābhiyujyamāne yatsatye bhavati vṛthābhipūyamāne ..
yaccāgnau bhavati vṛthābhihūyamāne tatsarvaṃ bhavati vṛthābhidhīyamāne .. 77..
3.238
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
dṛṣṭāriṣṭasya bhavatā dehatyāgaḥ prakīrttitaḥ ..
tasmādasmākamācakṣva tvariṣṭāni mahāmate .. 1 ..
haṃsa uvāca ..
pravṛttervikṛtirnṝṇāṃ buddhīndriyaśarīrajā ..
akasmāddṛśyate yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ maraṇamādiśet .. 2..
etatsamāsātkathitaṃ vistaro'yamataḥ param ..
sūkṣmāriṣṭāvabodhārthaṃ tathā spaṣṭārthameva ca ..3..
na tu karmaṇi yo vyabhre prabhākarma niśābhṛtaḥ ..

Whatever [fault] occurs when a mantra is employed in vain, whatever occurs when truth is declared in vain, / and whatever occurs when an oblation is offered into the fire in vain—all that occurs when words are spoken in vain.
3.238 / The sages said: / The abandonment of the body was proclaimed by you for one who has seen portents of death. / Therefore, O high-minded one, declare the portents of death to us.
Haṃsa said: / When a sudden distortion of the natural functioning of men arising in the intellect, senses, or body / is observed, one should predict their death.
This has been told in brief; now follows the detailed explanation, / for the sake of understanding subtle portents of death as well as obvious ones.
He who in a cloudless sky does not see the light-action of the moon, / or the shadow of the moon and the sun, or their movement,
[or who sees] in the path of the gods the brilliance of fire, the Pole Star, the star Arundhatī, / or sees what is unseen by others, his death will occur within a year.
And he who does not see the radiance of other things that possess radiance, / his death is declared to occur in the eleventh month.

text_mt:
He who in a dream at night vomits gold, silver, urine, or feces, / goes to the abode of Yama in the tenth month.
From seeing rākṣasas, the deceased, piśācas, or yakṣas, / or other beings beyond the senses, death is certain in the ninth [month].
He who grows weak though eating rich food in abundance, / or grows fat though not eating, falls into death in the eighth [month].
He whose footprint in dust or mud is seen to be incomplete, / broken, or distorted, falls into death in the seventh month.
He upon whose head carnivorous birds settle, O twice-born— / crows, hawks, and the like—for him one should predict death in the sixth [month].
He from whose body dust resembling cow-dung powder is wiped away, / and whose own shadow is distorted, falls into death in the fifth [month].
Having seen lightning in a cloudless sky, he certainly dies in the fourth [month].
Having seen a rainbow in water, or a sky that is not there, / O foremost of the twice-born, O knowers of dharma, he certainly dies in the third [month].

text_mt:
When there is twitching of an eye without any disease, / or if one [eye] is seen displaced from its socket, [death] is ordained.
A distorted and crooked nose brings death within a month.
Within half a month [when there is] the arising of a foul stench from one's own body. / And he who does not see his own reflection in another's eye, / he sees Yama within twelve days, O fortunate ones.
The man who does not smell the scent of an extinguished lamp, / O knowers of dharma, certainly sees the son of Sūrya within seven days.
When, for one who has just bathed and been anointed, the chest, feet, and head / dry up quickly, one should predict death for him in three days.
When red spots appear on the cheeks and there is discoloration of the skin, / one should predict the death of that man within a day and night.
And he who, when both ears are closed with his fingers, does not hear [the inner sound],
sound, and does not see his face in a spotless mirror, / and sees men who have arrived, one should indicate immediate death.

text_mt:
When the smoke from the head ceases, or if it arises from something wet with water, / [or] upon the sinking of the nose, O knowers of dharma, one should predict death in two days.
An inversion of touch, sight, taste, smell, sound, and movement / is observed in those about to die, whether healthy or afflicted with illness.
When an embodied being suddenly perceives smooth as rough, / or a reversal of cold and heat, his survival is rare.
He sees the earth like water and water like the earth; / he looks upon what is beyond the senses, but does not see what is placed in his hand.
And [he sees] space like the earth, and the earth like space; / and he sees himself like space, and the full moon on the new moon day.
An inversion of white and black, an inversion of gross and subtle, / and an inversion of the real and unreal are seen when life comes to an end.
An inversion of the six tastes, a reversal of the desirable and undesirable, / grasping in every way, seeing restraint, grasping what is beyond the senses—
excessive craving for inedible things leads to death; / and an inversion occurs in the perception of good and bad odors.

Union with the undesirable [as if] desirable, union with the desirable [as if] undesirable, / and an inversion of fear and courage occurs when life comes to an end.
Extremely long or extremely short, accompanied by darkness, and very cold / becomes the exhalation of those whose life is departing, when prāṇa is abandoned.
There is sound from things unstruck, and soundlessness from struck things; / soundlessness from struck things occurs in the house of men about to die.
When the lord of day has turned north, on an auspicious day, free of delusion, / or with Nārāyaṇa abiding in his heart, death comes to a virtuous person, O chiefs of the twice-born.
3.239
The sages said:
Which faults destroy sin, and which destroy men? / And which virtues, O Mahādeva, always bring about prosperity?
Haṃsa said:
Ignorance is considered the greatest of all faults. / The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting soul perishes.
Desire, anger, greed, joyous excitement, and pride / constantly enter a creature shrouded by ignorance, O best of the twice-born.

कृतपुण्योऽपि यः पापं करोति पुरुषः क्वचित् ..
स्वर्गेऽपि न सुखं तस्य तद्भयादुपजायते .. 3 ..
text_mt:
Only through ignorance does the undiscerning person gather sins; / having taken the wrong path through ignorance, he goes to hell.
A creature shrouded by ignorance does not stand on the auspicious path; / therefore, an effort must be made by the discerning person to calm ignorance.
Study of the scriptures, the service of elders, / and likewise devotion to the guru are deemed to pacify ignorance.
In the two worlds, O illustrious ones, there is no enemy of man equal to ignorance; / therefore, one who desires happiness in both worlds should make an effort toward knowledge.
3.240
Haṃsa said:
Through sin, a man becomes a vessel for all miseries; / through sin, he goes to hell, and becomes odious here in this world.
A man of sinful conduct perishes even from sin; / sin alone is the supreme misery of all beings, O bulls among the twice-born.
Even if a man has performed merit, if he commits a sin anywhere, / there is no happiness for him even in heaven, out of fear of that [sin].

दीनान्धकृपणानाथांस्तथा च परमार्भकाः .. 4..

text_mt:
He alone is [fortunate] among men in this world who has no sin. / [Look at] the wretched, the blind, the miserable, the helpless, and exceedingly frail children,
and others born in animal wombs, and others in hells, / and in plant wombs, and also in animal wombs.
Diseases, imprisonment, execution, torment, and beatings many times over / a man incurs, O knower of dharma, through sinful action.
Those foremost men who are free from sin experience no suffering whatsoever here; / therefore, sin should be avoided with effort by the wise, and a store of merit should be made.

text_mt:
3.241
Haṃsa said:
A man who follows desire perishes following desire; / but he whose soul consists purely of desire soon falls from fortune.
title: Mānadoṣavarṇanaḥ

हंस उवाच ..
नात्यर्थहर्षः कार्यस्तु कदाचिदपि पण्डितैः..
अत्यर्थहृष्टः पुरुषः कार्यं वेत्ति न किञ्चन .. 1 ..
सम्पदञ्चञ्चलां प्राप्य हर्षं प्राज्ञो विवर्जयेत् ..

कस्तासां विश्वसेत्प्राज्ञो वेश्यास्स्त्रीणां यथा तथा ..

text_mt:
A man who pursues desire conjoined with dharma and wealth is never separated / from desires; therefore, a wise person should always indulge [desire] conjoined with dharma and wealth.
3.242
Haṃsa said:
Excessive joy should never be indulged in by the wise; / an excessively joyful man knows nothing of what is to be done.
Having attained unsteady fortune, the wise person should avoid excessive joy; / for many have been seen ruined in this world, deluded by fortune.
In prosperity or in adversity, the wise person should not abandon his innate nature; / all fortunes are fickle by their very nature, O twice-born.
What wise man would trust them, just as [he would not trust] courtesans? / A man incurs delusion through contact with them.
All accumulations end in exhaustion; elevations end in falling; / unions end in separation; and indeed, life ends in death.
Wisdom does not lead to wealth, nor does dullness lead to poverty. / A wise man knows the course of worldly alternation; no other does.

हंस उवाच..
मानं विवर्जितं सद्भिर्वर्जनीयं सदा बुधैः..

ब्राह्मण्याच्च परिभ्रष्टा ब्राह्मणा बहवो द्विजाः..

A wise man, understanding that [wealth] to be completely fickle, should avoid rejoicing upon attaining it, / and he should not feel grief at the loss of wealth. Whatever is to be, will be; there is no destruction of that.
3.243
Haṃsa said:
Pride has been avoided by the virtuous; it must always be avoided by the wise. / Through pride, many kings have perished along with their retinues, / and many brahmin twice-born have fallen from their brahminhood. / Pride is the locus of all faults, the destroyer of both worlds.
The basest of men does not distinguish the proper from the improper because of pride. / A man seized by pride disrespects even his elders in this world.
A man certainly performs wrongful acts because of pride. / For one seized by the crocodile of pride, there is no liberation whatsoever.
Desire, anger, and greed are the destroyers of all living beings; / they enter a man seized by pride, O foremost of the twice-born.
And overcome by pride, he goes to hell, / without foundation, O best of men; therefore, one should avoid it.

text_mt:
There is no enemy of man equal to pride; a creature in this world goes to destruction through pride. / Therefore, pride, the path to hell, must always be avoided by the wise.
3.244
Haṃsa said:
Intoxication has been abandoned by the virtuous; it must be avoided with effort. / In intoxication, there are many faults that destroy both worlds.
One who is intoxicated does not know his duty; he even disrespects his elders. / For the intoxicated, O brahmins, the gate to hell is always wide open.
The intoxicated does not know fear, even in a most dreadful death. / One who is intoxicated, overtaken by delusion, understands nothing.
Even among all intoxications, the intoxication from drinking is known to be the lowest. / Overpowered by it, a man is no different from a dead corpse.
There is no fault equal to ignorance, and intoxication is its supreme cause here. / Therefore, drinking, the cause of intoxication, must be avoided with effort by a man.
3.245
Haṃsa said:
The greedy man does not recognize faults; the greedy man does not realize sin. / A man possessed by greed falls under the sway of misfortunes.
