text_mt:
The hairs age as a man ages; the nails age as he ages; / the teeth age as he ages; but craving alone does not age.
This bottomless mine of craving is unprecedented, O bulls among the twice-born: / even while being filled constantly, it is dug out all the more by it.
No one is ever able to fill it. / Only those who have taken refuge in contentment are able to fulfill it.
Whatever rice, barley, gold, cattle, and women exist upon the earth— / thinking that all this is not enough for a single person, one should attain tranquility.
That which is hard to cast off by the evil-minded, which does not age as one ages, / which is a fatal disease—giving up that craving brings happiness.
The greedy man has no kinsman, no son, no elder; the greedy man has no other worlds and no livelihood. / For the greedy man, all faults are declared to cause misery in both worlds, O hosts of gods.

haṃsa uvāca ..

meaning:
3.246
हंस उवाच ..
क्रोध एकः परः शत्रुः क्रोध एको विनाशकृत् ..

text_mt:
3.246
Haṃsa said:
Anger alone is the supreme enemy; anger alone is the destroyer. / A man overcome by anger would even kill himself.
title: Krodhadoṣavarṇanaḥ

sanskrit_iast:

नरः क्रोधसमाविष्टो नान्यं मित्रमपि द्विजान् .. 2 ..
text_mt: He distinguishes neither benefit nor harm, nor proper action from improper action; / a man seized by anger sees no other friend, nor even brahmins, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
gurūnākṣipati krodhānnainaṃ hi namate janaḥ ..

text_mt: Anger is the root of calamities, the gateway to hell, / and the dreadful abode of misfortunes; one should avoid it with effort.

akāryamiti kāryāṇi kṛtvā kāryavaśānnaraḥ ..

क्रोधाभिभूतस्य भवन्ति मिथ्या नरस्य तस्मात्परिवर्जयेत्तम् .. 7 ..
3.247
.. हंस उवाच .. ..
सर्वेषामेव पापानां नास्तिक्यं पातकं परम् ..
नास्तिक्याद्धि परं नास्ति किञ्चिन्पापं द्विजोत्तमाः .. 1 ..
अकार्यमिति कार्याणि कृत्वा कार्यवशान्नरः ..
पश्चात्तापेन संयुक्तः क्षिप्रं पापं व्यपोहति .. 2 ..
कार्यबुद्ध्या त्वकार्याणि यः करोति नराधमः ..
कथं निवर्तनं तेभ्यो जायते तस्य वै द्विजाः .. 3..
नास्तिक्यस्य तथा मूलं त्वसच्छास्त्रावगाहनम् ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन तद्विवर्ज्यं विजानता ..4..
सर्वो हि मानवो लोके परलोकनिबन्धनः ..
तत्रापि निरपेक्षस्य किन्नु लोके निबन्धनम् ..5..
ये तु वै नास्तिका लोके नरा लोकं प्रति द्विजाः ..
नरके ते हि पच्यन्ते बहुकालं न संशयः ..6..
text_mt:
Sacrifice, gifts, purifying austerities, visiting sacred places, and the Vedas / become futile for a man overcome by anger; therefore, one should avoid it.
3.247
Haṃsa said:
Of all sins, disbelief is the supreme degradation; / indeed, there is no sin greater than disbelief, O foremost of the twice-born.
A man who performs actions under the compulsion of necessity, knowing them to be forbidden, / quickly dispels the sin when accompanied by remorse.
But the lowest of men who performs forbidden acts with the notion that they are duties— / how can there be turning away from them for him, O twice-born?
The root of disbelief is immersion in false scriptures; / therefore, with all effort, it must be avoided by one who understands.
For every human in this world is bound to the other world; / and what bond can there be in this world for one who disregards even that?
Moreover, those men who are atheists regarding the world, O twice-born, / they are indeed roasted in hell for a long time, there is no doubt.

meaning:
नास्तिक्यमेकं पुरुषस्य लोके विनाशनं विप्रवराः प्रदिष्टम् ..
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन विवर्जनीयो नास्तिक्यभावः सुखमीप्समानैः..7..
3.248
हंस उवाच ..
अहङ्कारात्परं नास्ति लोके किञ्चिद्विनाशनम् ..
अहङ्कारेण भूपालाः शतशो निधनङ्गताः .. 1 ..
अहंकृतास्तथा नष्टा ब्राह्मणाश्च सहस्रशः ..
मान्यामान्यन्न जानन्ति कार्याकार्यं त्वहंकृताः .. 2 ..
अहंकृतस्तथा लोके न विद्यामधिगच्छति ..
विपन्नकार्यश्च तथा न प्राज्ञान्परिपृच्छति .. 3 ..
न शृणोति तथान्येषां दर्पपूर्णो विचक्षणः ..
पातादन्यन्नभैषज्यं दर्पान्नास्त्येह कीर्तनम् .. 4 ..
बलाधिकैस्तथा वीरैर्गुरुभिश्च तथैव च ..
मरणे संनिकृष्टेपि मरणस्य विचक्षणः .. 5 ..
हेतुभूतानि कर्माणि निन्दितानि निषेवते ..
स्थिते स्थितांस्तथा प्राज्ञान्भाषमाणान्विनिन्दति .. 6 ..
text_mt:
Atheism alone is declared to be the ruin of a man in this world, O best of brahmins; / therefore, the state of atheism must be avoided with exertion by those who desire happiness.
3.248
Haṃsa said:
There is nothing in the world that brings ruin greater than egoism; / through egoism, rulers of the earth have gone to their deaths by the hundreds.
Likewise, brahmins have perished by the thousands when filled with egoism; / egoistic people do not know who is venerable and who is not, nor what is to be done and what is not to be done.
Likewise, the egoistic person does not attain knowledge in the world; / and when his affairs are ruined, he does not consult the wise.
Filled with arrogance, he does not listen to others, [thinking himself] discerning; / other than a fall, there is no medicine here proclaimed for arrogance.
Even when death is near at hand, [caused] by those superior in strength, / by warriors, or likewise by elders, [thinking himself] discerning,
He indulges in blameworthy deeds that become the cause of death; / and he reviles wise men who stand firm [in virtue] as they speak.

meaning:
अहंकृतानां नरके प्रदिष्टा गतिर्ध्रुवं लोकविनिन्दितानाम् ..
प्राज्ञेन तस्मात्परिवर्जनीयो दर्पो विनाशैककरः सदैव ..7..
3.249
हंस उवाच ..
दत्तं यच्छौचहीनेन न तद्गृह्णन्ति देवताः ..
बुभुत्सवश्च धर्मज्ञाः शुचिकामाश्च देवताः .. 1 ..
यक्षैश्च राक्षसैश्चैव पिशाचैश्च निशाचरैः ..
डाकिनीभिश्च धर्मज्ञाः शौचहीनोऽभिभूयते .. 2 ..
शौचहीनमथाभ्येति स्वयं निन्दति कं द्विजाः ..
व्याधिहीनो ह्यशौचश्च सर्वैरेवाभिभूयते .. 3 ..
वर्धते च तथानर्थाः समर्थाश्च व्रजन्ति च ..
शौचहीनस्य रिपवो यान्ति वृद्धिं परां द्विजाः .. 4 ..
स्त्रीशौचमर्थशौचं च वाक्छौचमपि च द्विजाः ..
एतानि यस्य शौचानि स शुचिः परिकीर्तितः .. 5 ..
योर्थे शुचिः स हि शुचिर्न मृद्वारिशुचिः शुचिः ..
ततश्चाप्यधिकं शौचमहिंसा परिकीर्तिता .. 6 ..
text_mt:
The destination prescribed for egoistic men, reviled by the world, is surely in hell; / therefore, arrogance, which brings only ruin, must always be avoided by the wise man.
3.249
Haṃsa said:
The deities do not accept what is given by one devoid of purity; / for the deities wish to know [the heart], O knowers of dharma, and desire purity.
By yakṣas, by rākṣasas, and by piśācas, night-wanderers, / and by ḍākinīs, O knowers of dharma, one devoid of purity is overcome.
Who does he blame when misfortune comes of its own accord to one devoid of purity, O twice-born? / Even if free from disease, one who is ritually impure is overcome by all.
Misfortunes increase, and capable [enemies] advance; / the enemies of one devoid of purity attain supreme growth, O twice-born.
Purity regarding women, purity regarding wealth, and also purity of speech, O twice-born— / he in whom these purities exist is proclaimed pure.
He who is pure in wealth is indeed pure, not he who is purified with earth and water; / and non-violence is proclaimed to be a purity even higher than that.

śaucena hīnāśca bhavanti nindyāstasmādaśaucaṃ parivarjanīyam .. 7 ..
3.250
haṃsa uvāca ..
ācārahīnāḥ puruṣā bhavantyalpāyuṣo dvijāḥ ..
ācārahīnaśca tathā rākṣasairabhibhūyate .. 1 ..
yakṣaiḥ piśācairgandharvaistathā cānyairniśācaraiḥ ..
ḍākinībhiḥ surāṇāṃ ca tathā pārṣagaṇāḥ pṛthaka ..2 ..
dattamācārahīnena na pratīcchanti devatāḥ ..
pitaraśca mahābhāga ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ .. 3 ..
sarvalakṣaṇayukto'pi narastvācāravarjitaḥ ..
na prāpnoti tathā vidyāṃ na ca kiñcidabhīpsitam ..
ācārahīnaḥ puruṣo narakaṃ pratipadyate .. 4 ..
ācārahīnaṃ na punanti vedā yadyapyadhītāḥ saha ṣaḍbhiraṅgaiḥ ..
ācārahīnena tu dharmakāryaṃ kṛtaṃ hi sarvaṃ bhavatīha mithyā .. 5 ..
meaning:
शौचेन हीना नरकं व्रजन्ति शौचेन हीना विभजन्त्यनर्थान् ..
शौचेन हीनाश्च भवन्ति निन्द्यास्तस्मादशौचं परिवर्जनीयम् .. 7 ..
3.250
हंस उवाच ..
आचारहीनाः पुरुषा भवन्त्यल्पायुषो द्विजाः ..
आचारहीनश्च तथा राक्षसैरभिभूयते .. 1 ..
यक्षैः पिशाचैर्गन्धर्वैस्तथा चान्यैर्निशाचरैः ..
डाकिनीभिः सुराणां च तथा पार्षगणाः पृथक ..2 ..
दत्तमाचारहीनेन न प्रतीच्छन्ति देवताः ..
पितरश्च महाभाग ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः .. 3 ..
सर्वलक्षणयुक्तोऽपि नरस्त्वाचारवर्जितः ..
न प्राप्नोति तथा विद्यां न च किञ्चिदभीप्सितम् ..
आचारहीनः पुरुषो नरकं प्रतिपद्यते .. 4 ..
आचारहीनं न पुनन्ति वेदा यद्यप्यधीताः सह षड्भिरङ्गैः ..
आचारहीनेन तु धर्मकार्यं कृतं हि सर्वं भवतीह मिथ्या .. 5 ..
text_mt:
Those devoid of purity go to hell; those devoid of purity share in misfortunes; / those devoid of purity become blameworthy; therefore, ritual impurity must be avoided.
3.250
Haṃsa said:
Men devoid of proper conduct become short-lived, O twice-born; / and one devoid of proper conduct is likewise overcome by rākṣasas,
By yakṣas, piśācas, gandharvas, and by other night-wanderers, / by ḍākinīs, and severally by the attendant retinues of the gods.
The deities do not accept what is given by one devoid of proper conduct, / nor do the ancestors, O fortunate one, nor the sages whose wealth is austerity.
Even a man endowed with all auspicious marks, if devoid of proper conduct, / does not attain knowledge, nor anything he desires; / a man devoid of proper conduct arrives in hell.
The Vedas do not purify one devoid of proper conduct, even if studied together with the six limbs; / for every act of dharma performed by one devoid of proper conduct becomes futile here.

text_mt:
3.251
Haṃsa said:
One should always avoid untruth; untruth is the highest sin; / for there is no door to one's own ruin greater than untruth.

तस्मान्न स्तेनयेद्वाचं य इच्छेद्धितमात्मनः .. 2 ..

text_mt: Untruth must never be spoken anywhere, and especially in testimony; / for speaking untruth in testimony, one sinks [into hell] together with one's ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
hanti jātānajātām̐śca hiraṇyārthe'nṛtaṃ vadan ..
sarvaṃ bhūmyanṛtaṃ hanti māsma bhūmyanṛtaṃ vadet .. 5 ..
meaning:
हन्ति जातानजाताम्̐श्च हिरण्यार्थेऽनृतं वदन् ..
सर्वं भूम्यनृतं हन्ति मास्म भूम्यनृतं वदेत् .. 5 ..
text_mt: One kills both the born and the unborn when speaking untruth for the sake of gold; / one kills everything by untruth concerning land; one should never speak untruth concerning land.

sanskrit_iast:
apsu bhūmivadityāhuḥ strīṇāṃ bhoge ca maithune ..
abjeṣu caiva ratneṣu sarveṣvaśmamayeṣu ca .. 6 ..
meaning:
अप्सु भूमिवदित्याहुः स्त्रीणां भोगे च मैथुने ..
अब्जेषु चैव रत्नेषु सर्वेष्वश्ममयेषु च .. 6 ..
text_mt: They say that concerning water it is like land, and also in the enjoyment of women and sexual intercourse, / and concerning water-born gems and all things made of stone.

sanskrit_iast:
etāndoṣānavekṣyaiva sarvānanṛtabhāṣaṇe ..
yathāśrutaṃ yathādṛṣṭaṃ sarvamevāñjasā vadet .. 7 ..
meaning:
एतान्दोषानवेक्ष्यैव सर्वाननृतभाषणे ..
यथाश्रुतं यथादृष्टं सर्वमेवाञ्जसा वदेत् .. 7 ..
text_mt: Having observed all these faults in speaking untruth, / one should speak everything straightforwardly, just as heard and just as seen.

sanskrit_iast:
nagno muṇḍaḥ kapālī ca bhikṣārthī kṣutpipāsitaḥ ..
andhaḥ śatrugṛhaṃ gacchenna sākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet .. 8 ..
meaning:
नग्नो मुण्डः कपाली च भिक्षार्थी क्षुत्पिपासितः ..
अन्धः शत्रुगृहं गच्छेन्न साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत् .. 8 ..
text_mt: Naked, shaven-headed, carrying a skull-bowl, seeking alms, hungry and thirsty, / blind, he would go to the house of an enemy; [so] let him not speak false testimony.

sanskrit_iast:
sākṣye'nṛtaṃ vadanpāśairbadhyate vāruṇairbhṛśam ..
niviśante tamājātīstasmātsākṣye vadedṛtam .. 9 ..
meaning:
साक्ष्येऽनृतं वदन्पाशैर्बध्यते वारुणैर्भृशम् ..
निविशन्ते तमाजातीस्तस्मात्साक्ष्ये वदेदृतम् .. 9 ..
text_mt: Speaking untruth in testimony, one is bound tightly with the nooses of Varuṇa; / darknesses enter him for births; therefore, one should speak truth in testimony.

sanskrit_iast:
yanmayā gaditaṃ pāpaṃ dvijena kūṭasākṣiṇaḥ ..
tato'dhikamavāpnoni sadyo mithyā'bhiśaṃsane .. 3.251.10 ..
meaning:
यन्मया गदितं पापं द्विजेन कूटसाक्षिणः ..
ततोऽधिकमवाप्नोनि सद्यो मिथ्याऽभिशंसने .. 3.251.10 ..
text_mt: Whatever sin has been spoken of by me for a false witness, O twice-born, / more than that does he attain immediately in making a false accusation.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā krodhādbhayāllobhādajñānādvā dvijottamāḥ ..
yo'nṛtaṃ bhāṣate sadbhyaḥ sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam .. 11 ..
meaning:
यथा क्रोधाद्भयाल्लोभादज्ञानाद्वा द्विजोत्तमाः ..
योऽनृतं भाषते सद्भ्यः स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् .. 11 ..
text_mt: Whoever speaks untruth to the virtuous out of anger, fear, greed, / or ignorance, O best of twice-born, he surely goes to hell.

sanskrit_iast:
avākchirāstamasyandhe kilbiṣī narake patet ..
yaḥ praśnaṃ vitathaṃ brūyātpṛṣṭaḥ saddharmaniścaye .. 12 ..
meaning:
अवाक्छिरास्तमस्यन्धे किल्बिषी नरके पतेत् ..
यः प्रश्नं वितथं ब्रूयात्पृष्टः सद्धर्मनिश्चये .. 12 ..
text_mt: Head downwards into blind darkness the sinner would fall into hell, / who, when questioned in the determination of true dharma, gives a false answer.

sanskrit_iast:
andho matsyānivāśnāti nirapekṣaṃ sakaṇṭakān ..
yo bhāṣate'rtha vaikalyamapratyakṣaṃ sabhāṅgataḥ ..13..
meaning:
अन्धो मत्स्यानिवाश्नाति निरपेक्षं सकण्टकान् ..
यो भाषतेऽर्थ वैकल्यमप्रत्यक्षं सभाङ्गतः ..13..
text_mt: As a blind man heedlessly eats fish along with the bones, / so does he who, having entered the assembly, speaks of an impairment of matter that was not directly perceived.

sanskrit_iast:
kūṭakarmatulāmāne rasānāṃ bhedane tathā ..
viśvāsanyāsaharaṇe rahasyasamabhedane .. 14 ..
meaning:
कूटकर्मतुलामाने रसानां भेदने तथा ..
विश्वासन्यासहरणे रहस्यसमभेदने .. 14 ..
text_mt: In fraudulent deeds with scales and measures, and likewise in the adulteration of liquids, / in the misappropriation of a deposit given in trust, and in the breach of a secret agreement,

sanskrit_iast:
mṛtiṃ kalpayate yaśca madhu māṃsena pātakam ..
dvijasya surayā vāpi lobhena ca viśeṣataḥ .. 15 ..
meaning:
मृतिं कल्पयते यश्च मधु मांसेन पातकम् ..
द्विजस्य सुरया वापि लोभेन च विशेषतः .. 15 ..
text_mt: And who brings about death, the sin [caused] by honey with meat, / or by wine for a twice-born, and especially out of greed;

sanskrit_iast:
gobrāhmaṇavadhe vāpi gurupitṛvadhe tathā ..
vayasyadāragamane gurudārapradarśane .. 16 ..
meaning:
गोब्राह्मणवधे वापि गुरुपितृवधे तथा ..
वयस्यदारगमने गुरुदारप्रदर्शने .. 16 ..
text_mt: or in the killing of a cow or a brahmin, and likewise in the killing of a guru or a father, / in having intercourse with a friend's wife, in exposing the guru's wife;

sanskrit_iast:
vyutpādane ca śastrāṇāṃ śastrotsāde tathaiva ca ..
bhartṛpiṇḍāpaharaṇe saṃgrāmācca palāyane ..17..
meaning:

text_mt: and in the manufacture of weapons, and likewise in destroying weapons, / in embezzling the master's livelihood, and in fleeing from battle;

sanskrit_iast:
śaraṇāgatasaṃtyāge gacchataśca divā striyam ..

meaning:

प्रेष्यां च गच्छतः पापं राजद्रोहे तथैव च .. 18 ..

text_mt: and of one who distributes unevenly in an assembly [of eaters], and in a śrāddha [performed] for a friend, / of one who gives away a maiden for a bride-price, and of a seller of hair;

meaning:
विप्रस्य पातकं यच्च प्राणिनां विक्रये भवेत् ..
आमश्राद्धभुजः पापमयाज्यस्य च याजने .. 3.251.20 ..
text_mt: and the sin of a brahmin that arises in the sale of living beings, / the sin of eating an āmaśrāddha, and in officiating at a sacrifice for one not entitled to sacrifice;

sarvāṇyetāni pāpāni dvijaḥ sabhyaḥ samāpnuyāt .. 21 ..
meaning:
मिथ्या राज्यस्य करणे परद्रव्यापहारिणः ..
सर्वाण्येतानि पापानि द्विजः सभ्यः समाप्नुयात् .. 21 ..
text_mt: in falsely ruling a kingdom, and of one who steals another's property— / all these sins a twice-born assessor in the court incurs

sanskrit_iast:

यद्यन्यथा वदेत्तस्माद्धर्म्यं सभ्यः सदा वदेत् ..

kūṭakarmā tu narakaṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha majjati ..

दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च ..23..

sanskrit_iast:
tato daśaguṇaṃ kālaṃ sabhyo mithyābhibhāṣitā ..
rāgadveṣapravṛttastu vyavahāre'pi pārthivaḥ .. 24 ..

रागद्वेषप्रवृत्तस्तु व्यवहारेऽपि पार्थिवः .. 24 ..
text_mt: An assessor who speaks falsely [dwells there] for ten times that duration; / and an earthly ruler who acts out of passion and malice in judicial proceedings

ukte vacasi dharmye tu sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate .. 25 ..
meaning:

उक्ते वचसि धर्म्ये तु सद्यः पापात्प्रमुच्यते .. 25 ..
text_mt: surely dwells in hell for ten times that duration. / But when righteous speech is uttered, one is instantly freed from sin.

sanskrit_iast:
rājā narakamāpnoti satyavākyaṃ vilaṃghayana ..
śūdraviṭkṣatraviprāṇāṃ yatrokte prāpnuyādvadhaḥ .. 26 ..
meaning:
राजा नरकमाप्नोति सत्यवाक्यं विलंघयन ..
शूद्रविट्क्षत्रविप्राणां यत्रोक्ते प्राप्नुयाद्वधः .. 26 ..
text_mt: A king reaches hell by transgressing truthful speech. / Where the slaughter of a śūdra, a vaiśya, a kṣatriya, or a brahmin would occur if spoken,

meaning:

वाग्दैवतैश्च चरुभिर्यजनैश्च सरस्वतीम् ...27..

meaning:

उदुत्यृचे वा वारुण्ये ऋचा वाग्दैवतेन वा ..28..

बहवः सुखमेधन्ते यस्मिन्विप्रा निपातिते ..
वाच्यं तस्य वधे प्राप्ते यथाभूतमिति श्रुतिः .. 29 ..

haṃsa uvāca ..
sarveṣāmeva pāpānāṃ hiṃsā paramihocyate ..

न नर्मयुक्तं वचनं हिनस्ति न स्त्रीषु विप्रा न विवाहकाले ..
प्राणात्यये सर्वधनापहारे पञ्चानृतान्याहुरपातकानि .. 3.251.30 ..

हंस उवाच ..
सर्वेषामेव पापानां हिंसा परमिहोच्यते ..
हिंसा बलमसाधूनां हिंसा लोकद्वयापहा .. 1 ..

महद्दुःखमवाप्नोति पुरुषः प्राणिनाशनात् .. 2 ..

आततायिनमायान्तं हन्यादेवाविचारयन् .. 4 ..

जिघांसन्तं जिघांसीयात्तेन पापं न विद्यते .. 5 ..

text_mt:
A statement made in jest does not harm, nor among women, O brahmins, nor at the time of marriage, / nor when life is in peril, nor at the loss of all one's wealth: they declare these five untruths to be without sin.
3.252
Haṃsa said:
Violence is declared here to be the foremost of all sins; / violence is the strength of the wicked; violence destroys both worlds.
Not even a worm or a moth should be killed in any way. / A man incurs great suffering from destroying living beings.
When an assailant attacks, whether a man or an animal, / if one devoid of [other] means kills him, he is not afflicted by sin.
Whether a guru, a child, an old man, or a venerable person, / one should slay an approaching assailant without hesitation.
Even if an approaching assailant has mastered the Vedānta, in battle / one seeking to kill should be killed; no sin is found thereby.
When an enemy is struck down by blows in battle, there is no sin at all; / there is sin only when he is killed after having been conquered and captured.

text_mt:
A capable man who strikes down one already conquered in battle / goes to a dreadful hell for many hundreds of years.
And released from infernal suffering for many hundreds of years, / those men who are slayers of men are cast into unformed embryos.
As many hairs as an animal has, that many times does the slayer of an animal for no ritual purpose / suffer killing in this world, in the hereafter, and [attains no] expiation.
Even by killing an insect or cutting grass, / a man goes to hell, O knowers of dharma, through his own action.
Violence toward women, violence toward wealth, and dreadful violence toward living beings: / threefold is violence declared, shunned by wise men.
One devoted to non-violence must diligently shun another's wife, / and likewise, with great effort, another's property left even in an uninhabited place.
Therefore, terrifying violence toward living beings should not be committed at all; / the pitiless person who separates even a single living being from its life,

3.253
The sages said:
Tell us, O best of the twice-born, knower of dharma, king of birds, O high-minded one: / what various [fates] does a man attain by sinful action?
The Swan said:
Having committed sin, O brahmins, a man goes to hell; / and freed from hell, he enters an animal womb.
Through sins of action born of the body, a man becomes an immovable object; / through those of speech, a bird or a beast; through those of the mind, the lowest caste.
The states of mortals arising from action are declared to be threefold— / high, low, and intermediate—characterised by ten marks.
Coveting the property of others, harbouring malicious thoughts in the mind, / and adherence to false doctrines: this is the threefold action of the mind.
Harshness, untruthfulness, slander in every respect, / and incoherent babble: this is the fourfold [sin] of speech.

Taking what is not given, violence outside the ordinance, / and association with another's wife: this is handed down as the threefold [sin] of the body.
Therefore, O brahmins, even when one practices these ten marks in a single [life], / having attained human form through adharma, one becomes miserable.
Here, through evil deeds done in this life, or some through those done previously, / wicked men suffer deformation of form:
A killer of a brahmin becomes consumptive; a violator of the guru's bed has a diseased skin; / a drinker of surā has black teeth; a stealer of gold has deformed nails.
A stealer of clothes suffers from white leprosy; a stealer of horses becomes lame; / so too a stealer of any vehicle should be known as lame.
The lowest of men, having stolen a cow, is born blind in this world; / a stealer of grain has redundant limbs; a thief of speech is mute.
Reviling gurus, masters, and twice-born men, and likewise reviling the Vedas / and listening to it, the evil-minded, lowest of men becomes deaf.
A stealer of food becomes chronically diseased; / and having deprived even a single living being of life, one becomes sick.

virūpa eva bhavati tathāvikreyavikrayāt .. 27 ..

meaning:

जात्यन्धतामवाप्नोति परलोके न संशयः .. 23 ..
वर्णाधिकस्य जीवित्वा वर्णहीनेन कर्मणा ..
तस्यैव योनिमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 24 ..
तथैवाधिकवर्णस्य यदि जीवति कर्मणा ..
हीनवर्णस्तथा लोके भवत्यन्धः स दुर्मतिः .. 25 ..
यस्यान्नेनोदरस्थेन मृत्युमेति द्विजः क्वचित् ..
तस्यैव योनिमाप्नोति स्वकृतेनापि कर्मणा .. 26 ..
आमश्राद्धं तथा भुक्त्वा विरूपो जायते नरः ..
विरूप एव भवति तथाविक्रेयविक्रयात् .. 27 ..
विनापराधेन तथा कृत्वा पत्न्यधिवेदनम् ..

text_mt:
A stealer of lamps becomes blind; an extinguisher of lamps becomes one-eyed; / performing an action with knowledge bestowed by providence, an extremely evil-minded person / is born with bubble-like eyes or afflicted with eye disease.
Having looked at another man's naked wife with an evil eye, / a man attains congenital blindness in the next world, without a doubt.
If a man of higher class lives by the work of a lower class, / he attains the very womb of that [caste]; no doubt need be entertained here.
Likewise, if a man of lower class lives by the work / of a higher class, that evil-minded man becomes blind in this world.
If a twice-born dies anywhere with someone's food in his stomach, / he attains the very womb of that [giver] by his own deed.
Having eaten at an uncooked śrāddha, a man is born deformed; / he also becomes deformed by selling what is not to be sold.
Likewise, having superseded a wife without fault, / he suffers defeat in legal proceedings and in battle.

Likewise, having performed sorcery with roots for the sake of subjugation, / he becomes hated by the world in this realm; there is no doubt of this.
A student who breaks his vow of chastity becomes afflicted with a disease of the penis; / likewise in this world, a younger brother married before the elder is afflicted with all diseases.
A sinful priest for those not eligible to sacrifice is born of mixed caste; / a seller of the Veda is born a fool and a gambler.

text_mt:
Wealth should not be acquired through an action causing distress to others, which creates a multitude of faults; / for a fault born of causing distress to others cannot be destroyed even in the abode of the gods.
3.254 / The Swan said: / Knowledge brings happiness in the world; knowledge is considered the supreme eye. / From knowledge a human being obtains dharma, and from knowledge wealth;
from knowledge one obtains pleasure, and from knowledge one goes to liberation. / Therefore, with every effort, one should make an exertion toward knowledge.
Through knowledge one obtains everything whatever one desires in the mind. / And the sole cause of knowledge is the constant study of the treatises,
attendance upon the teacher and guru, service to the elders, / freedom from laziness, lack of stinginess, and avoiding sleep by day.
Knowledge is the supreme kin, knowledge is the guide along the path; / through knowledge, likewise, one abandons the afflictions of bondage to saṃsāra.
Through knowledge a person knows, through knowledge one attains dispassion; / through knowledge one obtains that having reached which one does not grieve.

3.255

धर्मे यत्नः सदा कार्यो धर्म एकः सुखावहः ..
धर्मेण पाल्यते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् .. 1 ..
धारणाद्धर्ममित्याहुर्धर्मो धारयति प्रजाः ..
धर्मे संसेविते कामान्प्राप्नोति मनसेप्सितान् .. 2 ..
धर्मेणार्थं तथा लोके प्राप्नोति मनसेप्सितम् ..

दस्युभिर्मुषितस्येव युक्तमाक्रन्दितं चिरम् ..

नास्ति धर्मविहीनस्य सुखमण्वपि वै द्विजाः ..
धर्मेण देवैर्देवत्वमृषित्वमृषिभिस्तथा .. 6 ..
text_mt:
Knowing this, a person must always make an effort in knowledge, O ones of undepressed spirit! / Having attained knowledge, those of great spirit, freed from suffering, become happy.
3.255 / The Swan said: / Effort should always be made in dharma; dharma alone brings happiness. / By dharma the entire three worlds, moving and unmoving, are preserved.
They say it is called dharma because of sustaining; dharma sustains the creatures. / When dharma is practiced, one attains the desires longed for in the mind.
By dharma, likewise, one obtains wealth desired in the mind in the world. / Leaving behind the dead body like a piece of wood or a clod of earth on the ground,
the relatives turn their backs and depart, but dharma alone follows after. / If even a single day has passed devoid of dharma,
it is fitting to weep loudly for a long time, like one plundered by robbers. / One should practice dharma with all one's strength, because life is impermanent.
For one devoid of dharma there is not even an atom of happiness, O twice-born! / By dharma the gods attained godhood, and the ṛṣis likewise attained the state of ṛṣis.

text_mt:
The entire world was obtained and created by Brahmā through dharma. / Hari, by whom all this was created, is indeed established in dharma.
There is no destruction of dharma once performed; therefore, dharma must be done by a person. / When dharma is done, there is no fear for men in the other world or here, O best of the twice-born!

text_mt:
A virtuous wife who attentively serves her husband attains supreme merit; / in the world of men, supreme merit is declared for subjects through service to the king.
3.257 / The Swan said: / Practice of svādhyāya should always be performed by the wise person. / Through svādhyāya one attains whatever one desires in the mind.
With milk, honey, curds, and meat, in proper order, / one should recite the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma hymns, and likewise the Atharvan.
One should offer tarpaṇa to the ancestors with clarified butter through the Vedāṅga; / reciting the Upavedas as well, one gratifies them with boiled rice.
Apart from all the places, reciting at will / the Sāṃkhya-Yoga, the Pāñcarātra, and likewise the Pāśupata,
one gratifies the ancestors with milk mixed with honey; / and likewise the theological dialogues, the Purāṇa, praises of heroes, and verses,
and reciting hymns daily, [one gratifies them] with curd and honey. / Therefore, with all effort, a twice-born should practice svādhyāya.

3.258
हंस उवाच ..
ब्रह्मचर्येऽभिसंयुक्तो द्विजः स्वर्गमुपाश्नुते ..

text_mt:
Recitation of the Veda alone is sacred asceticism here; recitation of the Veda alone is likewise sacrifice here. / Only the man who practices recitation of the Veda attains heaven and the desired liberation.
3.258 / The Swan said: / Endowed with celibacy, a twice-born reaches heaven. / Celibacy is the supreme abode; celibacy is the supreme asceticism.
Celibacy is the supreme sacrifice; celibacy is the supreme renown. / Endowed with celibacy, one can attain all desires.
Through celibacy, a man can turn a non-deity into a deity, and a deity into a non-deity; / likewise, he can create other worlds.
Likewise, he can quickly destroy even previously created [worlds]. / Through celibacy, a man attains whatever he desires.
That power of the lords of creatures to create offspring, O best of the twice-born, / and that of the ṛṣis, O twice-born, is to be understood as [arising] through celibacy.
Many thousands of lifelong celibate brahmins / have gone to heaven without producing a lineage of descendants.

text_mt:
He who has not fallen from celibacy goes to heaven even if he lacks a son. / For those who have fallen and are devoid of sons, no destination is ordained in the worlds.
2.259 / The Swan said: / But for a man who has fallen from celibacy and is devoid of offspring, / no destination exists in the world, even if he has performed intense asceticism.
Through a son he conquers worlds; through a grandson he attains immortality; / and through a son's grandson he reaches the domain of the sun.
Through a daughter, O best of the twice-born, he reaches heaven; / likewise, through a daughter's son, a man goes to the worlds of the lord of creatures.
Because a son rescues his father from the hell named Put, / therefore he was called 'putra' by the Self-born himself.
In this world, no difference is found between a son and a daughter's son; / for in the other world, a daughter's son delivers him just like a son's son.
Therefore, one who cuts off the lineage surely goes to hell. / Surrounded by sons and grandsons, he is magnified in the heavenly world.

text_mt:
Only a man possessing offspring, O chiefs of the twice-born, is endowed with supreme fame. / Endowed with fame, the preeminent man who has offspring then ascends to heaven.
3.260 / The Swan said: / A man devoted to fame is magnified in heaven for a long time. / Fame is declared to be the body of an embodied soul even when dead.
A man does not recognize [distinction] here and in the hereafter for one endowed with fame. / Those endowed with fame become the supreme vessel of the highest good in this world.
The sound of a meritorious deed touches heaven and earth. / As long as that sound exists, so long is he called a man.
For just so long does a man eternally enjoy in heaven and here / inexhaustible worlds that grant all desires.
That man who has infamy goes to hell. / As long as his fame is sung in the worlds, O knowers of dharma,

so long does he enjoy unexcelled divine pleasures in heaven. / Holy fame in the holy world yields no sin at all / when a man's [praise] is proclaimed; therefore one should practice merit.
Those preeminent men endowed with fame go to the firmament of heaven for a very long time; / those with infamy go to hell; therefore, fame is preeminent for a man.

text_mt: Renown is the splendor of a man, his supreme ornament. / For one devoid of renown in this world, an ornament is merely a supreme blemish.

text_mt:
Renown is preeminent for a man in the world; those devoted to renown go to heaven; / and in both worlds the cherished desires of the mind are fulfilled for those endowed with renown.
3.262 / The Swan said: / By sacrifice the gods live; by sacrifice likewise the ancestors. / All creatures depend on the gods, and the deities depend on sacrifice.
For sacrifice is Lord Viṣṇu, in whom everything is established. / For the sake of sacrifice, animals, gods, and plants were created.
For the sake of sacrifice, humans were created by the Self-born himself. / And sacrifice is for the prosperity of all; therefore one should be devoted to sacrifice.
The virtuous who eat the remnants of sacrifice are freed from all sins. / Whatever wealth belongs to those devoted to sacrifice, the wise know that as property of the gods.
Sacrifice alone is the supreme refuge of plants and animals. / Together with his company and his kinsmen, he is magnified in the firmament of heaven.
The animal sprinkled in a sacrifice, and likewise plants, O twice-born,
employed in a sacrifice rejoice in heaven; of this there is no doubt.

text_mt:
Honoured by the gods in heaven through sacrifice, the great-souled man
attains happiness, O noble ones; therefore one should zealously worship with sacrifices.
2.263
Haṃsa said:
Good conduct is pre-eminent in this world; everything is established upon it.
Through good conduct one attains everything, whatever one desires in one's mind.
The rites performed by one devoid of good conduct become fruitless.
Therefore, a discerning man should be endowed with good conduct.
Through good conduct Śakra, king of the gods, attained sovereignty over the immortals;
through good conduct even the King of Dharma attained the status of King of Dharma.
Through good conduct the god Varuṇa attained the status of king of kings;
and through good conduct even Kubera attained the overseership of wealth.
Through good conduct one attains happiness and heaven, O best of men;
through good conduct one reaches that place going whereto one does not grieve.
Having acquired good conduct, the pre-eminent man attains all principal desires;
therefore, a man should always zealously cultivate good conduct, which bestows happiness.

Sun and moon, wind and fire, sky, earth, waters, the heart and Yama,
day and night, both auspicious twilights, and Dharma know a man's conduct.

that is not dharma where there is no truth; that is not truth which is shot through with deceit.

text_mt:
In the world of the gods or on earth, O foremost twice-born, there is nothing for that man / for whom there is no attainment through the supreme excellence of asceticism, O noble ones.
The Haṃsa said: / They say this world is under control, hanging upon the arms of warriors; / thus, among all warriors, valor alone is distinguished.
For the sake of a brahmin, or for cows, or for one's lord, or on account of a friend, / those who fall when attacked go to the back of heaven.
When robbery of wealth has arrived, when an assault on one's wife has arrived, / and for one's own protection, one who fights would go to heaven.
For kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and brahmins, battle alone is the ultimate resort. / And for the protection of oneself, when ruin of the country has arrived,
when the loss of one's wife has arrived, and in the confusion of sacrificial fees, / a brahmin should take up a weapon, and also when intermixture [of castes] has presented itself.
A brahmin should arrange his livelihood according to the duty of a kṣatriya or not; / he must not turn back from battle; his beneficial duty lies there then.

text_mt:
One who has an only son, one with grass in his mouth, one saying 'I am yours,' / one protecting women and children, a coward, one intent on flight,
one deprived of weapons, one afflicted by calamity, one engaged with another, / a beast of burden, a carter, and a mere spectator of the battle—
these are not to be killed, O best of the twice-born, by one who knows the dharma of battle. / One standing in a chariot should not fight with a foot soldier.
Wishing for a fight with an equal, or likewise with a superior, / a man who slays an inferior reaches hell, or even if slain by him.
A man who arms himself without arming his mount / goes quickly to hell, despite his good deeds.
This dharma of battle has been declared; now understand the fruit of it: / the gain of dharma, the gain of wealth, and the gain of fame belong indeed to him.
The warrior who fights in battle, crushing the enemy host— / his are dharma, wealth, and pleasure, and sacrifices with fully paid fees.

text_mt:
By sacrificing with sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma with large sacrificial fees, / one does not attain that fruit which is attained in battle.
When blood issues forth from his limbs on the battlefield, / his sin departs from his body along with that very blood.
And he endures supreme distress in the healing of his wounds; / no asceticism is greater than that which a hero attains.
He whose blows are struck in battle, or even if it happens by fate / to one who is fighting, O knowers of dharma, he too is exalted in heaven.
As one enjoys the reward in battle after committing the greater slaughter, / he who, having slain the enemy facing him, mounts that [enemy's] chariot,
conquers Viṣṇu's stride, fighting thus on the battlefield; / but he who, having slain the army commander, mounts his chariot,
attains four horse-sacrifices through that deed. / As many weapons pierce his skin in combat,
so many imperishable worlds yielding all desires he obtains. / Wherever a warrior is killed, struck down by enemies,

3.268
Haṃsa said:
Non-violence is declared here to be the supreme dharma among all dharmas. / Through non-violence one obtains whatever is desired by the mind.
Violence against women, violence against wealth, and likewise violence against living beings— / avoiding threefold violence, one reaches the world of Brahmā.
Courtesy, beauty and charm, and also supreme good fortune, / wealth, grain, and health, dharma, knowledge, and women,
kingship, vast enjoyments, and even desired brahminhood, / and the eight [supernatural] qualities, and long life—
those who practice non-violence attain these and whatever else is rare. / A creature who practices non-violence should likewise be an abstainer from meat.
One who might sacrifice month after month with a horse sacrifice for a hundred years, / and one who does not eat meat—the two may or may not be equal.

He sacrifices always with a sacrificial session; he gives gifts always; / he is always an ascetic by avoiding liquor and meat.
All the Vedas would not achieve that, nor indeed all gifts, / as would he who, having tasted the savor of meat, abandons all meats.
For abandoning meat is difficult for one who knows its taste. / This fourfold vow is the best for living beings who fear death.
Then one becomes in this world to living beings who desire life / trustworthy and approachable, as there is no taste for violence.
Just as one's own life is dear to oneself, so it is to beings. / Great-souled knowers of the self should proceed by comparison with oneself.
Non-violence is the highest dharma; this is truly so, O best of twice-born. / The person who eats meats either out of greed or out of delusion,
he is to be regarded as pitiless, devoid of all dharma. / He who wishes to increase his own flesh with the flesh of another,
he dwells in an anxious abode wherever he is born. / The buyer kills by wealth; the eater [kills] by consumption;

the slayer [kills] by slaying and binding; thus this is threefold killing. / But one who, having eaten meat, desists even afterwards,
his dharma is also very great, who turns back from sin. / By rākṣasas, piśācas, ḍākinīs, or night-wanderers,
he who shuns meat would not be overcome by these or by others. / Sky-wanderers protect him whether living or dead,
from behind, O tiger among twice-born, who shuns meat. / Likewise, he who shuns meat would not be overcome by others.
Even at the smell of his funeral pyre's smoke when dead, night-wanderers / and carnivorous beings perish—for him who shuns meat.
From weapons, fire, kings, and thieves, from water and likewise from poison, / he has no fear, nor of anything else whatsoever.
They do not reach those worlds which are the worlds of those who abstain from meat. / He is [truly] one bearing the staff of renunciation; he is valiant; he is a sacrificer; he practices austerity;

3.269
Haṃsa said:
Forbearance is dharma; forbearance is truth; forbearance is purity; forbearance is strength; / forbearance is sacrifices; forbearance is charity; and forbearance is supreme austerity.
He who endures when reviled or beaten by others, / takes away good deeds from that [abuser] and gives [him] bad deeds.
He who possesses forbearance is righteous; by forbearance alone, O best of twice-born, / he burns the reviler and goes to the heavenly world.
Only one fault of those who have forbearance is found, no second: / that people consider him who is endowed with forbearance to be powerless.

O chiefs of twice-born, even that which is his fault should be known as a great virtue, / because of taking up merit and transferring evil.
Having died, the man possessing forbearance reaches the world of Brahmā / by a shining aerial chariot, sun-colored and yoked with swans.
For millions of years he attains the highest desires in heaven and here, O brahmins. / A man who endures all and is devoted to forbearance—therefore a person should always be forbearing.
3.270 / Haṃsa said: / Compassion is the supreme dharma in this world, O best of twice-born. / Therefore, a person who possesses self-restraint should indeed be grateful.
For the slayer of a brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and likewise for him who has broken his vow, / an expiation is prescribed, O king; for the ungrateful man there is no expiation.
Those vilest of men who are ungrateful are not freed from hell / until the dissolution of all beings, O dreadful ones; there should be no doubt about this.
They are indeed born into the animal womb and dwell in an abode of suffering. / When danger has arrived, such men find protection nowhere.

Only he is truly a man in whom a good deed done is not destroyed. / The grateful man attains heaven; the grateful man attains greatness.
Whether a master or a servant, a brahmin or a guru, / whoever does not abandon [such a one] in distress is honored in heaven.
Having served [a master] while prosperous, he who abandons him when destitute, / that man is the most cruel in the world, a receptacle of hell.
A man should not abandon a servant in his own house whose youth has passed away; / abandoning him who is incapacitated in old age, he will attain hell.
An old elephant or horse, or a milch cow, or a trained ox— / whoever abandons [these] is of very evil mind and enters hell.
Having tethered animals, those who do not care for them with grass or water / properly, O tigers among twice-born, those men go to hell.
An animal seized in one's house with an incurable disease / should be treated; one should not abandon it as long as it lives, O best of twice-born.

From abandoning it, a human being surely attains hell. / Having served a prosperous master, the vile person / who later abandons him when he is impoverished surely goes to hell.
The man who undergoes distress from serving a master deprived of wealth, / that is prescribed as his austerity for the world of Brahmā, O twice-born.
The grateful man is [a true] person in the world, and the grateful man enjoys all things. / The grateful man attains everything, whatever he desires in his mind.
Mother, father, son, patron of a sacrifice, and sacrificial priest, / master, guru, servant, relative, and animal,
or a wife, O best of twice-born, one should never abandon in thought. / For upon abandoning these, one falls; he surely goes to hell.
Likewise, one should not abandon the sacred fire, nor should one extinguish the sacred fire; / similarly, O brahmins, having abandoned the worship of deities, one goes to hell.
In the shade of whichever tree a person has rested, / he should not harm even a leaf from it, remembering the duty of gratitude.

The world of Brahmā which cannot be attained even by great, very difficult austerity, O lords of the twice-born, / that world of Brahmā a grateful man attains swiftly; there is no doubt here.

text_mt:
Endowed with right conduct, one goes to heaven; possessing right conduct alone, one becomes free of disease; / possessing right conduct alone, one lives long; possessing right conduct alone, one enjoys fortune.
3.272 / Haṃsa said: / The gods praise purity, and so do the brahmin-seers. / What is given by one endowed with purity, the heaven-dwellers eat.
Or rather, purity brings the fruition of all dharmas; / only a man endowed with purity attains the realm he desires.
Bodily purity is taught to be by water and earth, but the purity of freedom from greed cleanses the mind. / The man whose mind is purified attains the world of the Grandfather.
3.273 / Haṃsa said: / Visiting sacred places is purity; visiting sacred places is austerity. / Purified by the waters of sacred places, men go to heaven without a doubt.
Visiting sacred places is holy, and a man should attain it by foot-travel; / with sins exhausted through the travel, he attains heaven.
It accomplishes the quelling of the sin of sinners without austerity; / it makes one equal to a sinless person, as has been proclaimed.

Those chiefs of the twice-born who are devoted to visiting sacred fords, freed from sin, attain heaven; / and having dwelt there happily for a very long time, they attain happiness in the mortal world.
3.274
Haṃsa said:
Sacrifices require many implements and vast provisions of various materials; / they cannot be performed by a poor man, O foremost of the upholders of dharma.
Yet the fruit of sacrifice can be obtained even by poor men, O twice-born; / a man should fast by being constantly devoted to fasting.
Fasting up to a month is called asceticism here; / beyond that, fasting unto death is proclaimed for the twice-born.
Eating at the sixth mealtime is declared here to be the highest asceticism for a śūdra; / for those of mixed-caste birth, one day is proclaimed.
If a śūdra should ever perform asceticism beyond the sixth mealtime, / it should be known that there is ruin in the kingdom and great affliction for the king.
A śūdra, eating at the sixth mealtime, may practice asceticism according to his ability; / or up to a month's fast, a twice-born may practice according to his ability.

text_mt:
There is no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā; there is no goal equal to Kṛṣṇa; / there is no recitation equal to the Gāyatrī; [no] oblation equal to [that with] the sacred utterances.
Likewise, [no] achievement in the water destroying sin [is greater] than the Aghamarṣaṇa; / there is no merit equal to non-violence; [no] gift higher than the sacrifice.
Just so, O twice-born, there is no asceticism higher than fasting; / for those heated by fasts, lasting happiness follows immediately.
Disposed to the asceticism of fasting, having reached the heavenly world, / they rejoice together with the gods, just like the hosts of deities.
Fasting is prescribed as pacifying the sin of the sinful and granting the desired wishes of the virtuous, / especially when having a deity as its refuge.
The gods turn gracious faces toward those engaged in fasting, / and even grant their wishes; there should be no doubt about this.
Having taken refuge in Vāsudeva, a man who has properly fasted / obtains endless fruit; for Hari, self-controlled, is endless.
Those brahmins who have fasted after taking refuge in Vāsudeva / do not return even today, like rivers to the oceans.

Those men who have fasted according to rule, reaching heaven and being honored by the gods, / accompanied by celestial nymphs, become free of all sorrow in that world.
3.275
Haṃsa said:
Endowed with concentration of mind, one obtains very great fruit / from visiting a sacred ford, O brahmins, as also from having properly fasted.
For man, it is [the mind] alone that accomplishes all actions; / whatever a man performs with a purified mind,
[even if little,] yields abundant fruit for him here and in the hereafter. / For the mind is the supreme entity; one should always strive for its purity.
A creature endowed with purity of mind does not fall into hell; / he attains the heavenly world or indeed the supreme abode.
Dwelling with virtues when one's faults have departed, O givers of honor, / should be known as true fasting, not the emaciation of the body.
In the spotless, deeply blissful, pure, great lake whose bank is truth, / one should bathe in the mental sacred ford, for that is the unexcelled sacred ford.

Relying on faith and performing meritorious deeds, men attain an auspicious destination.
Haṃsa said:
Obligatory, occasional, optional, forming part of a rite, removing dirt,
and bathing for a rite as the sixth: bathing is proclaimed to be of six kinds.
The obligatory and occasional [baths] may be performed with hot water or with water belonging to another;
and the third bath, which is said to remove dirt, [may be performed in this way as well].
Having lifted out five lumps [of earth], one should bathe in water belonging to another;
otherwise, a man who bathes is tainted with a portion of wrongdoing.
Even when having lifted out five lumps of earth, a man who bathes with water belonging to another
attains purification, but not the fruit of bathing.
One who bathes with water heated by fire does not attain the fruit born of bathing;
having bathed, he attains purification and becomes fit for ritual action.
Therefore, at holy places, in oceans, and in lakes,
in divine rivers, and also in springs,

text_mt:
Having bathed their limbs in the Gaṅgā, having enjoyed divine pleasures in heaven for a long time, and then attaining human existence,
they become happy in this world, prosperous, endowed with fame, dedicated to dharma, and free from sorrow.
Haṃsa said:
Recitation is proclaimed in the world to bring accomplishment to the twice-born;
by recitation, O best of the twice-born, one attains accomplishment especially.
A brahmin would certainly attain accomplishment through recitation alone, there is no doubt of this;
whether he performs other [rites] or not, a brahmin is called friendly [to all].
Comfortably seated on a wooden seat or even on a kuśa-grass seat,
one should concentratedly perform recitation, or even standing upright,
facing the east or north, or even facing the sun,
having darbha-grass in hand, O best of the twice-born, having known the certainty of dharma,
having known the seer of the mantra, its metre, its deity,
and its application, one should perform recitation while meditating on the deity of the mantra.
It should not be done too quickly, nor too slowly;
at the time of recitation, O best of the twice-born, one should pronounce all the syllables.

text_mt:
The wise man, free from sloth, should repeat the mantra according to his ability.
Vedic study is [performed] aloud, while recitation is said to be in a whisper.
Mental recitation is taught to bear much fruit, even more than that.
A rosary should be made of rudrākṣa beads, O best of the twice-born,
or of lotus seeds, O fortunate ones, or else of putrajīvaka seeds,
of pearls, of coral, of gold, or of crystal,
or, O brahmins, of a cord of kuśa grass properly knotted by a virtuous man;
or one may correctly keep count with the joints of the fingers.
Having performed recitation in this manner, O twice-born, worshipping the deity of the mantra,
one surely attains whatever one desires in one's heart.
Having attained success through recitation, one may reach the world of Brahmā;
through recitation one is freed from evil; through recitation one may go to heaven.
Through recitation one attains liberation; therefore one should be devoted to recitation.
A desireless man surely attains liberation through recitation.

All the sages achieved perfection solely through recitation, O best of the twice-born.
Recitation is the supreme purifier of the twice-born; through recitation one abandons all evil;
through recitation one obtains desired worlds; through recitation a twice-born man attains liberation.
3.279
Haṃsa said:
Having performed the recitation of a mantra submerged in water, O best of the twice-born,
one obtains imperishable fruit and is freed from all sins.
A mantra repeated underwater by one meditating on the deity of the mantra
liberates a man from evil, even from that born of heinous sins.
Twice-born whose sins are washed away by the water within surely go to heaven.
Therefore, submerged in water, a man should diligently perform the recitation of the mantra.
3.280
Haṃsa said:
Exhalation, inhalation, and also retention, O twice-born:
breath control is to be understood as single, possessing three states, and bearing great fruit.

Taking in the breath, when one performs the study of the mantra
with the mind, O best of brahmins, that is proclaimed as recaka.
Holding the breath, neither taking it in nor releasing it,
that is declared as pūraka, destroying all blemishes.
One should thus practice breath control while meditating on the deity of the mantra;
there is no austerity for the twice-born higher than breath control.
From retention wind is generated, and from that fire is born;
then water [is generated] in the body; by these three, a man is purified.
One who, free from sloth, performs breath control, O best of the twice-born,
will practice the highest austerity from the tip of his hair to the tip of his nails.
The merit one attains from breath control is not obtained
from visiting holy bathing places, O twice-born, nor through sacrifice, nor through penances.
Brahmins devoted to breath control, all their blemishes washed away,
attain heaven or the liberation desired by their mind.

3.282
The Haṃsa said:
The steady fixation of the mind upon a single external object
is taught as concentration, which causes the binding of the mind.
It should be practiced upon an image of a deity where one's intellect may become steady.
Having obtained a single target for the fickle mind,
one should strive diligently for its restraint for the sake of subduing the mind.
Or, the wise man should make the binding of the target upon the earth.
Having obtained the target in the practice upon earth, he should abandon the practice upon earth.
Having obtained the target, O best of men, a man should practice upon fire.
Having abandoned [that], he should then cause [the mind to focus] on wind, and then on space.
Ascending in this manner step by step, a man, taking target after target,
having practiced concentration on external objects, attains mastery of the mind.
As long as the binding concentration of this fickle mind [is unachieved],

Having attained motionless concentration, one may then attain meditation.
Where concentration has been fixed, when one leaves this body,
one attains identity with that; there should be no doubt here.
Having attained concentration, a best of men, having cast off his body,
attains liberation in time; but through meditation [it comes] quickly: such is the rule.
A man established in concentration, having attained identity with that,
when he goes to the Cosmic Person, then he realizes [Him].
Having attained concentration, a man attains liberation certainly,
but after a long time; through meditation [it comes] quickly: such is the rule.
Likewise, in all the world, external objects are to be known as perishable;
concentration should be practiced upon them for the sake of seizing the mind.
Having attained the motionless binding of the mind, the best of men,
from that practice of concentration, surely attains liberation.

3.283
The Haṃsa said:
Concentration upon an external object is proclaimed as concentration;
that very same [focus] within the mind, O best of men, is designated as meditation.
On the pericarp of the downward-facing heart-lotus, O best of the twice-born,
a wise man should perform meditation on the sun, the mass of splendour.
Within the sun is situated the moon, within the moon the fire;
within the splendour is situated the essence, more intensely luminous even than splendour.
In its midst is Lord Viṣṇu, the eternal Supreme Self,
the infallible Cosmic Person, ever all-pervading, the Great Lord.
One should behold Him, subtler than the subtlest, whose form is splendour, difficult to approach;
having seen Him through the discipline of meditation, a man attains perfection.
Assuming unwearied one of the yogic postures:
the svastika, sarvatobhadra, paryaṅka, or lotus posture,

text_mt:
One should know that Supreme Cosmic Person as devoid of sound, touch, and taste,
and free from smell and form, having gone to whom one does not grieve.
Devoid [of mental activity], intent on meditation, O brahmins, it is proclaimed as samādhi;
having attained it, he is never overcome by other men.
There is no happiness higher than samādhi anywhere in the three worlds;
and established in samādhi, one is not moved even by heavy sorrow.
Even if conches by the hundreds are blown in his ears,
and if kettle-drums are beaten, he does not perceive external sound.
Likewise, struck with blows, or with his body burned by fire,
or standing in intense, dreadful cold, he does not perceive external touch.
What need is there to speak of victory over external smell or taste for such a one?
He who, having seen the Self by the self, again attains samādhi,
neither thirst nor hunger ever assails him;
even as he abandons thirst, not eating, he observes [the Self].

text_mt:
That best of men knows only one distress:
rising from samādhi—by that he is deeply tormented.
That happiness which a man obtains upon attaining motionless samādhi / is not in heaven, nor in the netherworld, nor among human beings.
Upon attaining samādhi and abandoning the bondage of the body, a person / pervades all the worlds, the three worlds with the moving and unmoving.
And that person pervades whatever is even outside the three worlds; / upon attaining samādhi, a human being attains infinity.
Free from birth, death, old age, disease, grief, and suffering, / all-pervading, destroying everything, consisting of the qualities of all senses,
everywhere and at all times, O brahmins, he is in that [state]—there is no doubt about this; / he then attains the nature of the Cosmic Person and attains all power.
Restraining the mind indeed in fixations, ascending then afterwards to meditation, / and abiding in samādhi, the high-minded one attains equality with the Supreme Person.

text_mt:
3.285 / The sages said: / That which is the root of the attainment of the great state, O best of the twice-born, / declare all of that to us, marked by direct perception.
Haṃsa said: / All men who are guided by resolve attain it; / there is nothing in the world exceedingly difficult to obtain for those who have resolve as their second.
Resolve is the highest kinsman; a companion comes next; / endowed with that, a man attains [it] completely; this is certain.
In dharma, in wealth, in pleasure, and in liberation, O best of sages, / a man who possesses resolve is always to be known as a vessel.
For those destitute of resolve, even a slight objective is hard to attain; / for those who lack resolve, being lazy and wicked-minded,
wealth, even when seized in hand, is destroyed suddenly and quickly; / one who is destitute of resolve is no better than a tree-trunk.
Therefore, men who are devoted to diligent effort are declared in the world to be enjoyers of their desires; / theirs is both this world and the other, and likewise the path to liberation is not far for them.

For things first intended by the mind, success accompanied by resolve has been taught; / therefore, the virtuous say that all undertakings in the world have their root in intention.
3.287 / The sages said: / For the attainment of the state of the highest good, withdrawal of the senses has been spoken by you, / as well as the yoga of fixation and meditation, and also excellent samādhi.
Declare again to us, for the benefit of men moving in the cycle of existence, / the supreme path that brings happiness in both worlds.
Haṃsa said: / Fire is the mouth of the deities, the refuge of all beings; / only through serving it does one enjoy all desires.
It is the supreme form of Viṣṇu; what is given to it, the sun receives; / from the sun comes rain, then from that comes food, and from food the world arises.
The gods rain downward, but earthly beings rain upward; / what is given by earthly beings into the fire is principal, raining upward.
Whatever deity a brahmin offers an oblation to, / having first uttered the syllable Oṃ, that [deity] becomes always pleased with him.

text_mt:
By oblation a person abandons sin; by oblation he likewise goes to heaven; / an oblation indeed destroys all misfortune in the world—there is no doubt of this.
3.288 / Haṃsa said: / All creatures are subject to fate; this world is dependent on the gods; / likewise, the happiness and suffering of human beings are dependent on the gods.
Men experience the good and the bad ordained by the gods; / therefore, with all effort, one should be devoted to the worship of the gods.
And the gods are pleased through devotion, as well as through supreme faith; / worshipped by a pure person, the gods are pleased, and not otherwise.
Through service to the gods, heaven [is attained]; through service to the gods, happiness; / through service to the gods, kingdom or even liberation is attained.
The gods always desire a devoted person in this world; / the gods are surely compassionate to devotees, here and hereafter.
The gods surely protect the devotee, O best of the twice-born; / through the satisfaction of the god, one obtains whatever desires one wishes in one's mind.

jātaprabhṛti yaṃ devaṃ bhaktyā nityamathārcayeta ..
antakāle tu saṃprāpte so'pi trātā bhaved dhruvam ..7..
kiṃ vā pāpavihīnasya kṣipraṃ tuṣyanti devatāḥ ..
tasmātpāpaṃ na karttavyaṃ nareṇa tridaśāśrayāt .. 8 ..
devāśritānāṃ pāpānāṃ kṣipraṃ pāpaṃ vinaśyati ..
natveva pātakaṃ karma vṛthā teṣāṃ prajāyate .. 9 ..
tathā bahu phalaṃ loke kathitaṃ tridaśāśrayam ..
sarvānsamarcayeddevānekaṃ vā devamāśrayet .. 3.288.10 ..
devārcāṃ śraddhayā kṛtvā dhruvaṃ tallokamāpnuyāt ..
kṛtvā devagṛhaṃ viprā narastallokamāpnuyāt .. 11 ..
paramāṇūni yāvanti bhavanti suraveśmanaḥ ..
tāvato'bdānavāpnoti tallokānnātra saṃśayaḥ .. 12 ..
yāvadvāraṃ karotīha devaveśma sudhāsitam ..
janmāntarāṇi tāvanti yaśasā sa virājate .. 13 ..
meaning:
जातप्रभृति यं देवं भक्त्या नित्यमथार्चयेत ..
अन्तकाले तु संप्राप्ते सोऽपि त्राता भवेद् ध्रुवम् ..7..
किं वा पापविहीनस्य क्षिप्रं तुष्यन्ति देवताः ..
तस्मात्पापं न कर्त्तव्यं नरेण त्रिदशाश्रयात् .. 8 ..
देवाश्रितानां पापानां क्षिप्रं पापं विनश्यति ..
नत्वेव पातकं कर्म वृथा तेषां प्रजायते .. 9 ..
तथा बहु फलं लोके कथितं त्रिदशाश्रयम् ..
सर्वान्समर्चयेद्देवानेकं वा देवमाश्रयेत् .. 3.288.10 ..
देवार्चां श्रद्धया कृत्वा ध्रुवं तल्लोकमाप्नुयात् ..
कृत्वा देवगृहं विप्रा नरस्तल्लोकमाप्नुयात् .. 11 ..
परमाणूनि यावन्ति भवन्ति सुरवेश्मनः ..
तावतोऽब्दानवाप्नोति तल्लोकान्नात्र संशयः .. 12 ..
यावद्वारं करोतीह देववेश्म सुधासितम् ..
जन्मान्तराणि तावन्ति यशसा स विराजते .. 13 ..
text_mt:
Whatever god one should constantly worship with devotion from birth onward, / when the time of death arrives, that [god] surely becomes one's savior.
Or rather, the deities are swiftly pleased with one free from sin; / therefore a man should not commit sin, taking refuge in the gods.
The sin of sinners who have taken refuge in a god is swiftly destroyed; / indeed, sinful action does not arise in vain for them.
Thus taking refuge in the gods is proclaimed in the world to bear great fruit. / One should worship all the gods, or take refuge in a single god.
Having performed the worship of a god with faith, one surely attains that deity's world; / having built a house for a god, O brahmins, a man attains that deity's world.
As many atoms as there are in the abode of the god, / for so many years he attains that deity's world; of this there is no doubt.
As many times as he makes the house of the god whitewashed with mortar in this world, / for so many future births he shines with fame.

sanskrit_iast:
pratipādya tathā bhaktyā dhvajaṃ tridaśaveśmani ..
nirṇudatyāśu pāpāni mahāpātakajānyapi .. 14 ..
citrakarma tathā kṛtvā gandharvai saha modate ..
devamālyāpanayanādgodānaphalamāpnuyāt. .. 15 ..
meaning:
प्रतिपाद्य तथा भक्त्या ध्वजं त्रिदशवेश्मनि ..
निर्णुदत्याशु पापानि महापातकजान्यपि .. 14 ..
चित्रकर्म तथा कृत्वा गन्धर्वै सह मोदते ..
देवमाल्यापनयनाद्गोदानफलमाप्नुयात्. .. 15 ..
text_mt:
Likewise, dedicating a banner at the house of the gods with devotion, / one quickly dispels sins, even those born of heinous crimes.
Likewise, having made a painting, he rejoices with the gandharvas; / from removing withered garlands from a god, one obtains the fruit of giving a cow.

sanskrit_iast:
pāpairvimucyate sarvaiḥ prokṣaṇāddevaveśmanaḥ ..
sammārjanāttathā pāpaṃ vyapohati na saṃśayaḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
पापैर्विमुच्यते सर्वैः प्रोक्षणाद्देववेश्मनः ..
सम्मार्जनात्तथा पापं व्यपोहति न संशयः .. 16 ..
text_mt: One is freed from all sins by sprinkling the house of a god; / likewise, by sweeping it, one removes sin without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmānabhīṣṭānāpnoti devaveśmopalepanāt ..
sudhārekhānvitaṃ kṛtvā maryādāṃ nātivartate .. 17 ..
meaning:
कामानभीष्टानाप्नोति देववेश्मोपलेपनात् ..
सुधारेखान्वितं कृत्वा मर्यादां नातिवर्तते .. 17 ..
text_mt: One obtains desired wishes by smearing the house of a god; / having made it marked with lines of mortar, one does not exceed proper limits.

sanskrit_iast:
varṇakaiścitritaṃ kṛtvā saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..
gandharvatvamavāpnoti gandhairabhyukṣya mānavāḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
वर्णकैश्चित्रितं कृत्वा सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ..
गन्धर्वत्वमवाप्नोति गन्धैरभ्युक्ष्य मानवाः .. 18 ..
text_mt: Having decorated it with pigments, one obtains great good fortune; / sprinkling it with perfumes, men attain gandharva-hood.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpairvikiraṇaṃ kṛtvā rūpavānabhijāyate ..
abhyajya devapratimāṃ sarvaduḥkhairvimucyate .. 19 ..
meaning:
पुष्पैर्विकिरणं कृत्वा रूपवानभिजायते ..
अभ्यज्य देवप्रतिमां सर्वदुःखैर्विमुच्यते .. 19 ..
text_mt: Scattering [it] with flowers, one is born handsome; / by anointing the image of a god, one is freed from all sufferings.

sanskrit_iast:
virūkṣayitvā tāmeva pāpebhyo vipramucyate ..
oṣadhībhistathā snāpya nāsatyaiḥ saha modate .. 3.288.20 ..
meaning:
विरूक्षयित्वा तामेव पापेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते ..
ओषधीभिस्तथा स्नाप्य नासत्यैः सह मोदते .. 3.288.20 ..
text_mt: Removing the unguents from it, one is completely freed from sins; / bathing [it] with herbs, he rejoices with the Nāsatyas.

sanskrit_iast:
loke prajāpateryāti vedaiḥ saṃsnāpya devatām ...
puṣpodakena snapanātsaubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute .. 21 ..
meaning:
लोके प्रजापतेर्याति वेदैः संस्नाप्य देवताम् ...
पुष्पोदकेन स्नपनात्सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते .. 21 ..
text_mt: Bathing the deity with the Vedas, he goes to the world of Prajāpati; / by bathing [the deity] with flower-scented water, one enjoys great good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
phalodakena saṃsnāpya saphalāṃ vindate kriyām ..
nāgavallījalaiḥ snāpya nāgalokaṃ sa gacchati .. 22 ..
meaning:
फलोदकेन संस्नाप्य सफलां विन्दते क्रियाम् ..
नागवल्लीजलैः स्नाप्य नागलोकं स गच्छति .. 22 ..
text_mt: Bathing [the deity] with fruit-water, one attains fruitful action; / bathing [the deity] with betel-leaf water, he goes to the world of the nāgas.

sanskrit_iast:
ratnodakena snapanāddhānadaṃ lokamāpnuyāt ..
gandhodakena mukhyena gandharvaiḥ saha modate .. 23 ..
meaning:
रत्नोदकेन स्नपनाद्धानदं लोकमाप्नुयात् ..
गन्धोदकेन मुख्येन गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते .. 23 ..
text_mt: By bathing [the deity] with water of gems, one attains the world of the Wealth-Giver; / with the foremost perfumed water, he rejoices with the gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast:
tīrthodakena puṇyena svargalokamavāpnuyāt ..
tathānulipya gandhaiśca śakraloke mahīyate .. 24 ..
meaning:
तीर्थोदकेन पुण्येन स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात् ..
तथानुलिप्य गन्धैश्च शक्रलोके महीयते .. 24 ..
text_mt: With auspicious water from sacred pilgrimage places, one attains the heavenly world; / and having anointed [the deity] with perfumes, he is exalted in Śakra's world.

sanskrit_iast:
vibhūṣaṇapradānena rājā bhavati bhūtale ..
rājaliṅgapradānena rājā bhavati hi kṣitau .. 25 ..
meaning:
विभूषणप्रदानेन राजा भवति भूतले ..
राजलिङ्गप्रदानेन राजा भवति हि क्षितौ .. 25 ..
text_mt: By giving ornaments, one becomes a king on the earth; / by giving the insignia of royalty, one indeed becomes a king on earth.

sanskrit_iast:
vastradānena loke'sminsuveśastvabhijāyate ..
deve mālyapradānena parā lakṣmīṃ samaśnute .. 26 ..
meaning:
वस्त्रदानेन लोकेऽस्मिन्सुवेशस्त्वभिजायते ..
देवे माल्यप्रदानेन परा लक्ष्मीं समश्नुते .. 26 ..
text_mt: By giving cloth, one is born beautifully dressed in this world; / by giving a garland to a god, one enjoys supreme prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpapradānena tathā gatimagryāmavāpnuyāt ..
dīpadānena cakṣuṣmānprakāśaścaiva jāyate .. 27 ..
meaning:
धूपप्रदानेन तथा गतिमग्र्यामवाप्नुयात् ..
दीपदानेन चक्षुष्मान्प्रकाशश्चैव जायते .. 27 ..
text_mt: Likewise, by giving incense, one attains the highest path; / by giving a lamp, one becomes endowed with vision and luminous.

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvāṃ gatimavāpnoti sarvatra ca tathāgryatām ..
devatābhyastathā viprā nivedyānnamatandritaḥ .. 28 ..
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वां गतिमवाप्नोति सर्वत्र च तथाग्र्यताम् ..
देवताभ्यस्तथा विप्रा निवेद्यान्नमतन्द्रितः .. 28 ..
text_mt: He attains an upward path, and supreme status everywhere; / and unweariedly offering food to deities, O brahmins,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute ..
paritoṣamathāyāti devatā balikarmaṇā .. 29 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ..
परितोषमथायाति देवता बलिकर्मणा .. 29 ..
text_mt: he enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice replete with all desires; / and a deity attains satisfaction through the ritual offering of food.

sanskrit_iast:
tāstuṣṭāstarpayanyenaṃ sarvakāmasamṛddhibhiḥ ..
hṛdyapānapradānena tṛptimāpnoti śāśvatīm .. 3.288.30 ..
meaning:
तास्तुष्टास्तर्पयन्येनं सर्वकामसमृद्धिभिः ..
हृद्यपानप्रदानेन तृप्तिमाप्नोति शाश्वतीम् .. 3.288.30 ..
text_mt: Pleased, they satisfy him with the fulfillments of all desires; / by offering delightful drinks, one attains everlasting satisfaction.

sanskrit_iast:
devatānāṃ namaskārātkiñcitpāpaṃ praṇaśyati ..
tathaivābhyadhikaṃ pāpaṃ praṇipātena naśyati .. 31 ..
meaning:
देवतानां नमस्कारात्किञ्चित्पापं प्रणश्यति ..
तथैवाभ्यधिकं पापं प्रणिपातेन नश्यति .. 31 ..
text_mt: From bowing to deities, some sin is destroyed; / likewise, greater sin is destroyed by prostration.

sanskrit_iast:
tato'pyabhyadhikaṃ kiñcitkṛtvā deve pradakṣiṇām ..
stutikriyā devatānāṃ sarvakāmaphalapradā .. 32 ...
meaning:
ततोऽप्यभ्यधिकं किञ्चित्कृत्वा देवे प्रदक्षिणाम् ..
स्तुतिक्रिया देवतानां सर्वकामफलप्रदा .. 32 ...
text_mt: Something still greater than that [is gained] by circumambulating a god; / the act of praising deities bestows the fruit of all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
gītena devatāstoṣamupayānti dvijottamāḥ ..
tathā vādyena nṛtyena puruṣasya viśeṣataḥ ..33 ..
meaning:
गीतेन देवतास्तोषमुपयान्ति द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तथा वाद्येन नृत्येन पुरुषस्य विशेषतः ..33 ..
text_mt: O best of the twice-born, the deities attain satisfaction through song, / and especially through instrumental music and dance offered by a man.

sanskrit_iast:
nṛttaṃ gītaṃ tathā vādyaṃ svayamācarate dvijā ..
devasālokyamāpnoti puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ .. 34 ..
meaning:
नृत्तं गीतं तथा वाद्यं स्वयमाचरते द्विजा ..
देवसालोक्यमाप्नोति पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः .. 34 ..
text_mt: If a wise man himself performs dance, song, / and instrumental music, O twice-born, he attains co-residence with the god.

sanskrit_iast:
vācanāditihāsānāṃ pāpamokṣamavāpnuyāt ..
mūlyena kārayedgītaṃ gandharvatvamathāpnuyāt .. 35 ..
meaning:
वाचनादितिहासानां पापमोक्षमवाप्नुयात् ..
मूल्येन कारयेद्गीतं गन्धर्वत्वमथाप्नुयात् .. 35 ..
text_mt: From the recitation of historical epics, one attains release from sin; / if one arranges song by paying a price, one attains gandharva-hood.

sanskrit_iast:
vādyaṃ dattvātha dharmajñaṃ vasūnāṃ lokamaśnute ..
nṛttena lokamāpnoti śaṅkarasya mahātmanaḥ .. 36 ..
meaning:
वाद्यं दत्त्वाथ धर्मज्ञं वसूनां लोकमश्नुते ..
नृत्तेन लोकमाप्नोति शङ्करस्य महात्मनः .. 36 ..
text_mt: Providing instrumental music, one who knows dharma enjoys the world of the Vasus; / through dance, one attains the world of the great-souled Śaṅkara.

sanskrit_iast:
itihāsapradānena buddhimāñjāyate naraḥ ..
āhutiṃ devamuddiśya yo dadāti hutāśane .. 37 ..
meaning:
इतिहासप्रदानेन बुद्धिमाञ्जायते नरः ..
आहुतिं देवमुद्दिश्य यो ददाति हुताशने .. 37 ..
text_mt: By presenting historical epics, a man becomes intelligent. / Whoever offers an oblation in the sacrificial fire dedicated to a god,

sanskrit_iast:
sa devastarpayatyenaṃ kāmairvā tena tarpitaḥ ..
devamuddiśya viprāṇāṃ yo dadātīha bhojanam .. 38 ..
meaning:
स देवस्तर्पयत्येनं कामैर्वा तेन तर्पितः ..
देवमुद्दिश्य विप्राणां यो ददातीह भोजनम् .. 38 ..
text_mt: that god, satisfied by him, satisfies him with desired things. / Whoever in this world offers food to brahmins dedicated to a god,

sanskrit_iast:
sa devaḥ prītimānasya kāmāniṣṭānprayacchati ..
devamuddiśya yatkiñcidbrāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradīyate ..39..
meaning:
स देवः प्रीतिमानस्य कामानिष्टान्प्रयच्छति ..
देवमुद्दिश्य यत्किञ्चिद्ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदीयते ..39..
text_mt: that god, being pleased with him, bestows his cherished desires. / Whatever is given to brahmins dedicated to a god,

sanskrit_iast:
tadeva prāpyate loke prasanne tridaśe bahu ..
yānaṃ śayyāsanaṃ chatraṃ pāduke cāpyupānahau .. 3.288.40 ..
meaning:
तदेव प्राप्यते लोके प्रसन्ने त्रिदशे बहु ..
यानं शय्यासनं छत्रं पादुके चाप्युपानहौ .. 3.288.40 ..
text_mt: that very thing is obtained abundantly in the world when the god is pleased: / a carriage, a bed, a seat, an umbrella, sandals, and shoes.

sanskrit_iast:
vāhanaṃ gāṃ ca dharmajñāstridaśabhyo dadāti yaḥ ..
ekaikasmādavāpnoti vahniṣṭomaphalaṃ naraḥ .. 41 ..
meaning:
वाहनं गां च धर्मज्ञास्त्रिदशभ्यो ददाति यः ..
एकैकस्मादवाप्नोति वह्निष्टोमफलं नरः .. 41 ..
text_mt: The man who gives a mount or a cow to the gods, O knowers of dharma, / obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice from each one.

sanskrit_iast:
dattvā phalāni devebhyaḥ saphalāṃ vindate kriyām ..
nivedya sasyāni tathā gatimāpnotyanuttamām .. 42 ..
meaning:
दत्त्वा फलानि देवेभ्यः सफलां विन्दते क्रियाम् ..
निवेद्य सस्यानि तथा गतिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् .. 42 ..
text_mt: Having given fruits to the gods, one finds one's work fruitful; / likewise, having offered crops, one attains an unsurpassed state.

sanskrit_iast:
naiti devastathā prītiṃ dānairnṛtyaistathā phalaiḥ ..
prītimeti yathā viprāḥ svāśritānāntu pūjanaiḥ .. 43 ..
meaning:
नैति देवस्तथा प्रीतिं दानैर्नृत्यैस्तथा फलैः ..
प्रीतिमेति यथा विप्राः स्वाश्रितानान्तु पूजनैः .. 43 ..
text_mt: A god does not attain such pleasure through gifts, through dances, or through fruits, / as he attains pleasure, O brahmins, through the worship of those who take refuge in him.

sanskrit_iast:
devatā naiva tuṣyanti dānena bahudhā dvijāḥ ..
yathā bhaktyā tu tuṣyanti tasmādbhaktiṃ samāśrayet .. 44 ..
meaning:
देवता नैव तुष्यन्ति दानेन बहुधा द्विजाः ..
यथा भक्त्या तु तुष्यन्ति तस्माद्भक्तिं समाश्रयेत् .. 44 ..
text_mt: Deities are not so greatly pleased by giving, O twice-born, / as they are pleased through devotion; therefore one should resort to devotion.

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtapūrṇāni pātrāṇi dattvā śrāddhe tathā naraḥ ..
dīrghaṃ jīvitamāpnoti na rogaiścābhibhūyate .. 45 ..
meaning:
घृतपूर्णानि पात्राणि दत्त्वा श्राद्धे तथा नरः ..
दीर्घं जीवितमाप्नोति न रोगैश्चाभिभूयते .. 45 ..
text_mt: Having given vessels full of clarified butter in a ancestral rite, a man / attains a long life and is not overcome by diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
madhupūrṇāni pātrāṇi dattvā saubhāgyamāpnuyāt ..
yathākathañcitpātrāṇāṃ dānādbhavati sattamāḥ ..46..
meaning:
मधुपूर्णानि पात्राणि दत्त्वा सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् ..
यथाकथञ्चित्पात्राणां दानाद्भवति सत्तमाः ..46..
text_mt: Having given vessels full of honey, one obtains good fortune. / From the gift of vessels in any manner whatsoever, O best of men,

sanskrit_iast:
pātraṃ nu sarvakāmānāṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
puṣpavṛkṣapradānena gṛhamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
पात्रं नु सर्वकामानां नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
पुष्पवृक्षप्रदानेन गृहमाप्नोति मानवः .. 47 ..
text_mt: one becomes a vessel indeed for all desired things; no doubt should be entertained here. / By giving flowering trees, a man obtains a home.

sanskrit_iast:
phalavṛkṣapradānena grāmasyādhipatirbhavet ..

3.289
Haṃsa said:
Vaiśyas are the deity of śūdras, and kṣatriyas are [the deity] of vaiśyas; / brahmins are [the deity] of kṣatriyas, and the fire-god is also [the deity] of those [brahmins].
The celibate student has the teacher as deity, and women have the husband as deity; / the householder has the guest as deity; therefore, he should always honour him.
Having performed the vaiśvadeva rite in the home evening and morning with concentrated mind, / having offered the rice balls, and having given alms to an ascetic, / by respectfully giving alms, he obtains the fruit of giving a cow; / and he should scatter food on the ground for dogs, dog-cookers, and birds.
Immobile and mobile creatures depend on the householder for life; / the householder should sustain both the dead and the living.
Because he continually sustains [them] here, he is exalted in heaven; / worms, insects, fallen outcasts, enemies, and foremost of the twice-born—

By standing up and advancing before him, he attains the fruit of giving a cow; / and by offering a seat, that best of men attains a station.
And by inquiring after his well-being, a man becomes intelligent; / then, by washing his feet and massaging his weary [limbs],
by fanning him with a chowrie or by fanning him with a palm leaf, / by offering anointment for his feet, or by offering a lamp,
by providing a bed at night, and likewise by massaging him— / from each single one, he obtains the highest fruit of giving a cow.
By attending upon him with stories, he attains union with fame; / and by reciting historical narratives to him according to his desire,
he attains the heavenly world; with song, dance, festivities, and the like, / having honoured him, he undoubtedly attains the state of a gandharva.
By granting shelter, he enjoys all desired things; / and having offered earth, a tooth-stick, and water for cleansing,

Having unweariedly provided him a bath preceded by an oil-rub, / he enjoys health, beauty, grace, wealth, and grain.
Having provided all kinds of principal baths, O best of the twice-born, / he attains the world of the Nāsatya twins; on this point no doubt should be made.
Likewise, having given fragrant perfumes, he rejoices with the gandharvas; / by the gift of a bracelet, he enjoys great good fortune.
From bathing a guest, the merit produced is equal to the gift of ten cows; / by gratifying him with whatever he desires, one obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice.
And having given him whatever he desires, he enjoys that very thing inexhaustibly; / therefore, with all his strength, a man should always honour the guest.
Whatever that noble [guest], being satisfied, wishes for a man, / he attains all that before long; therefore, the guest must always be worshipped by one devoted to dharma.

3.290
Haṃsa said:
Brahmins are the deity on earth; brahmins are the deity in heaven; / there is no being whatever higher than brahmins in the three worlds.
They can make a non-deity into a deity; they can make a deity into a non-deity; / for brahmins are exalted, twice-born [beings who] are constantly worshipped.
From brahmins the gods were originally born, so says sacred tradition; / from brahmins comes the entire world; therefore, they are always most worthy of worship.
Through their mouth deities eat, and likewise the ancestors / and the exalted sages; what being is greater than that?
Whatever a man gives with devotion to brahmins, / that very thing he obtains in abundance, O knowers of dharma, birth after birth.
Even with wind from a palm-leaf fan, and by massaging weary [limbs], / by wiping limbs clean, and likewise by the act of applying collyrium,
by offering washing for the feet, and by cleansing of both feet, / by personal service as desired—through just a single one, O best of the twice-born,
