sanskrit_iast:
balantuṣṭiśca puṣṭiśca tathā śrāddhakriyā dvijāḥ..
nāsau sampannamaśnāti yasya dhenurna vidyate....
tasmātsarvapradānānāṃ gavāṃ dānamanuttamam ..
hīnāṅgīṃ kṣīrapāṃ vṛddhāṃ dugdhadohāṃ nirindriyām..3..
meaning:
बलन्तुष्टिश्च पुष्टिश्च तथा श्राद्धक्रिया द्विजाः..
नासौ सम्पन्नमश्नाति यस्य धेनुर्न विद्यते....
तस्मात्सर्वप्रदानानां गवां दानमनुत्तमम् ..
हीनाङ्गीं क्षीरपां वृद्धां दुग्धदोहां निरिन्द्रियाम्..3..
text_mt: strength, contentment, nourishment, and likewise śrāddha rites, O twice-born. / He who has no milch cow does not eat what is prosperous. / Therefore, of all gifts, the gift of cows is unsurpassed. / [A cow] defective in limbs, drinking her own milk, old, dry of milk, bereft of sense organs,

sanskrit_iast:
vyādhitāṃ viṣamāṃ vyālāṃ tathaiva prapalāyinīm ..
mūlyaistathāpyasaṃśuddhairhṛtāśca dvijapuṅgavāt..4..
meaning:
व्याधितां विषमां व्यालां तथैव प्रपलायिनीम् ..
मूल्यैस्तथाप्यसंशुद्धैर्हृताश्च द्विजपुङ्गवात्..4..
text_mt: diseased, treacherous, vicious, or likewise given to fleeing, / or obtained from an eminent twice-born by impure purchase-prices,

sanskrit_iast:
na dātavyā smṛtā dhenurdattvā narakamāpnuyāt ..
brāhmaṇo yastu kurute gorasānāṃ tu vikrayam..5..
meaning:
न दातव्या स्मृता धेनुर्दत्त्वा नरकमाप्नुयात् ..
ब्राह्मणो यस्तु कुरुते गोरसानां तु विक्रयम्..5..
text_mt: such a cow is handed down as not to be given; having given her, one would attain hell. / A brahmin who carries out the sale of milk products,

sanskrit_iast:
gavāṃ ca vikrayaṃ viprā viṣamo yastathā gavām..
apātradoṣayuktaśca na deyā tasya cāpyatha..6..
meaning:
गवां च विक्रयं विप्रा विषमो यस्तथा गवाम्..
अपात्रदोषयुक्तश्च न देया तस्य चाप्यथ..6..
text_mt: and the sale of cows, O brahmins, or who is harsh toward cows, / and is contaminated by the fault of being an unworthy recipient, to him also [a cow] must not be given.

sanskrit_iast:
naikā bahūnāṃ dātavyā na dvayordvijapuṅgavāḥ..
sā tu vikrayamāpannā dāturnarakadāyinī..7..
meaning:
नैका बहूनां दातव्या न द्वयोर्द्विजपुङ्गवाः..
सा तु विक्रयमापन्ना दातुर्नरकदायिनी..7..
text_mt: One must not be given to many, nor to two, O eminent twice-born; / for she, being brought to sale, brings hell to the giver.

sanskrit_iast:
ekaṃ pātramathāsādya deyāstu bahavaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
gavāṃ pradāne yatnena parīkṣyo brāhmaṇo bhavet .. 8 ..
meaning:
एकं पात्रमथासाद्य देयास्तु बहवः स्मृताः ..
गवां प्रदाने यत्नेन परीक्ष्यो ब्राह्मणो भवेत् .. 8 ..
text_mt: Having found a single worthy recipient, many may be given, so it is handed down. / In the granting of cows, a brahmin must be examined with diligence.

sanskrit_iast:
yathākathañcid dattvā gāṃ dhenuṃ vā'dhenumeva vā ..
arogāmaparikliṣṭāṃ dātā svarge mahīyate ..9..
meaning:
यथाकथञ्चिद् दत्त्वा गां धेनुं वाऽधेनुमेव वा ..
अरोगामपरिक्लिष्टां दाता स्वर्गे महीयते ..9..
text_mt: Having given a cow in any manner whatsoever, whether a milch cow or a non-milch cow, / free from disease and not distressed, the giver is honored in heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
dattvā vatsatarīṃ viprāḥ svargaloke mahīyate ..
gurviṇīṃ ca tathā dattvā vasūnāṃ lokamaśnute .. 3.306.10 ..
meaning:
दत्त्वा वत्सतरीं विप्राः स्वर्गलोके महीयते ..
गुर्विणीं च तथा दत्त्वा वसूनां लोकमश्नुते .. 3.306.10 ..
text_mt: Having given a heifer, O brahmins, he is honored in the world of heaven. / And having given a pregnant one likewise, he enjoys the world of the Vasus.

sanskrit_iast:
prasūyamānāṃ tāṃ dattvā bhūmidānaphalaṃ labhet ..
sravaṃtyāṃ ca tathā dattvā nandane modate naraḥ ..11..
meaning:
प्रसूयमानां तां दत्त्वा भूमिदानफलं लभेत् ..
स्रवंत्यां च तथा दत्त्वा नन्दने मोदते नरः ..11..
text_mt: Having given her while she is giving birth, he obtains the fruit of the gift of land. / And having given [her] while her milk flows, a man rejoices in the Nandana [grove].

sanskrit_iast:
śvetāṃ dattvā somaloke raktāṃ dattvā vibhāvasoḥ ..
kṛṣṇāṃ dattvā tathā yāmye nīlāṃ dattvā ca vāruṇe .. 12 ..
meaning:
श्वेतां दत्त्वा सोमलोके रक्तां दत्त्वा विभावसोः ..
कृष्णां दत्त्वा तथा याम्ये नीलां दत्त्वा च वारुणे .. 12 ..
text_mt: By giving a white [cow, one is honoured] in the world of Soma; by giving a red one, in that of Agni; / by giving a black one, in Yama's realm; and by giving a blue-black one, in Varuṇa's.

sanskrit_iast:
indraloke tu śabalāmindraloke tu rohiṇīm ..
vātareṇusavarṇāṃ tu vāyuloke mahīyate .. 13 ..
meaning:
इन्द्रलोके तु शबलामिन्द्रलोके तु रोहिणीम् ..
वातरेणुसवर्णां तु वायुलोके महीयते .. 13 ..
text_mt: A dappled one [leads] to the world of Indra, and a tawny one to the world of Indra; / while [by giving one] the colour of wind-blown dust, one is magnified in the world of Vāyu.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūmravarṇāṃ tathā dattvā vasūnāṃ lokamaśnute ..
āṣāḍhena savarṇāntu lokaṃ vāruṇamāpnuyāt .. 14 ..
meaning:
धूम्रवर्णां तथा दत्त्वा वसूनां लोकमश्नुते ..
आषाढेन सवर्णान्तु लोकं वारुणमाप्नुयात् .. 14 ..
text_mt: By giving a smoke-coloured one, he attains the world of the Vasus; / and [by giving one] matching the colour of the Āṣāḍha [cloud], he attains the world of Varuṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
suvarṇavarṇāṃ kauberaṃ tāmrāmāṅgirasaṃ tathā ..
palāladhūmravarṇābhāṃ pitṛlokaṃ tathaiva ca..15..
meaning:
सुवर्णवर्णां कौबेरं ताम्रामाङ्गिरसं तथा ..
पलालधूम्रवर्णाभां पितृलोकं तथैव च..15..
text_mt: A gold-coloured one [brings] the realm of Kubera, a copper-coloured one that of the Āṅgirasas, / and one resembling the colour of straw-smoke [brings] the world of the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
śitikaṇṭhāpradānena vaiśvadevamavāpnuyāt ..
gaurīṃ dattvā bhṛgūṇāñca vairāṭābhāṃ prajāpateḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
शितिकण्ठाप्रदानेन वैश्वदेवमवाप्नुयात् ..
गौरीं दत्त्वा भृगूणाञ्च वैराटाभां प्रजापतेः .. 16 ..
text_mt: By bestowing a dark-necked one, one attains the realm of the Viśvedevas; / by giving a yellowish-white one, that of the Bhṛgus; and one resembling a cat's eye, that of Prajāpati.

sanskrit_iast:
pāṇḍukambalavarṇābhāṃ rudrāṇāṃ lokamāpnuyāt ..
śuklabinducitāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ gandharvaiḥ saha modate .. 17 ..
meaning:
पाण्डुकम्बलवर्णाभां रुद्राणां लोकमाप्नुयात् ..
शुक्लबिन्दुचितां कृष्णां गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते .. 17 ..
text_mt: One resembling the colour of a white woolen blanket brings the world of the Rudras; / [giving] a black one covered with white spots, he rejoices with the gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast:
(kapilāñca tathā dattvā yatheṣṭaṃ lokamāpnuyāt ..)
gāvaḥ prakṛtivarṇāstu kapilāḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
(कपिलाञ्च तथा दत्त्वा यथेष्टं लोकमाप्नुयात् ..)
गावः प्रकृतिवर्णास्तु कपिलाः परिकीर्तिताः .. 18 ..
text_mt: (And by giving a kapilā cow, he attains whatever world he desires.) / Cows of their original, natural colour are declared to be kapilā.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtantu varṇavaicitryaṃ pūrvaṃ tāsāntu śambhunā ..
yathā tu gaṅgā saritāṃ dhenūnāṃ kapilā tathā .. 19 ..
meaning:
कृतन्तु वर्णवैचित्र्यं पूर्वं तासान्तु शम्भुना ..
यथा तु गङ्गा सरितां धेनूनां कपिला तथा .. 19 ..
text_mt: Their diversity of colours was produced of old by Śambhu. / Just as the Gaṅgā is among rivers, so is the kapilā among milch cows.

sanskrit_iast:
sāyaṃ prātaśca satataṃ homakāle dvijottamāḥ ..
gāvo dadati vai haumyamṛṣibhyo nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 3.306.20 ..
meaning:
सायं प्रातश्च सततं होमकाले द्विजोत्तमाः ..
गावो ददति वै हौम्यमृषिभ्यो नात्र संशयः .. 3.306.20 ..
text_mt: Constantly at evening and at morning, at the time of the fire offering, O foremost of the twice-born, / cows indeed provide the sacrificial offering to the sages; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
duṣkṛtāni duriṣṭāni durgāṇi viṣamāṇi ca ..
taranti caiva pāpebhyo dhenudānena mānavāḥ .. 21 ..
meaning:
दुष्कृतानि दुरिष्टानि दुर्गाणि विषमाणि च ..
तरन्ति चैव पापेभ्यो धेनुदानेन मानवाः .. 21 ..
text_mt: Through the gift of a milch cow, men cross over / misdeeds, ill-performed rites, perilous places, and rough paths, and from their sins.

sanskrit_iast:
ekāṃ gāṃ daśagurdadyāddaśa dadyācca gośatī ..
śataṃ sahasragurdadyātsarve tulyaphalā hi te .. 22 ..
meaning:
एकां गां दशगुर्दद्याद्दश दद्याच्च गोशती ..
शतं सहस्रगुर्दद्यात्सर्वे तुल्यफला हि ते .. 22 ..
text_mt: One who owns ten cows should give one; one who owns a hundred cows should give ten; / one who owns a thousand cows should give a hundred; for they all reap equal fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
śatavarṣasahasrāṇi tapastaptaṃ suduścaram ..
gobhiḥ pūrvavisṛṣṭābhirgacchema śreṣṭhatāmiti .. 23 ..
meaning:
शतवर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्तं सुदुश्चरम् ..
गोभिः पूर्वविसृष्टाभिर्गच्छेम श्रेष्ठतामिति .. 23 ..
text_mt: Austerity very hard to practice was performed for a hundred thousand years / by the cows created of old, [praying:] 'May we attain pre-eminence!

sanskrit_iast:
loke'smindakṣiṇānāñca sarvā gā vayasottarāḥ ..
bhave tāni ca liṃpyema doṣeṇātiparantapāḥ .. 24 ..
meaning:
लोकेऽस्मिन्दक्षिणानाञ्च सर्वा गा वयसोत्तराः ..
भवे तानि च लिंप्येम दोषेणातिपरन्तपाः .. 24 ..
text_mt: In this world of sacrificial fees, may all cows be superior by age; / and may we not be stained by any fault in existence, O tormentors of foes!

sanskrit_iast:
śakṛttāsāṃ pavitrārthaṃ kurvīrandevamānuṣāḥ ..
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca .. .. 25 ..
meaning:
शकृत्तासां पवित्रार्थं कुर्वीरन्देवमानुषाः ..
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च .. .. 25 ..
text_mt: May gods and men use their dung for the sake of purification, / and likewise all beings, both stationary and moving!

sanskrit_iast:
pradātāraśca golokāngaccheyuriti mānadāḥ ..
etaddhanaṃ dadau tāsāṃ sarvameva pitāmahaḥ .. 26 ..
meaning:
प्रदातारश्च गोलोकान्गच्छेयुरिति मानदाः ..
एतद्धनं ददौ तासां सर्वमेव पितामहः .. 26 ..
text_mt: And may those who bestow [us] go to the world of cows, O givers of honour!' / The Grandfather gave all this wealth to them.

sanskrit_iast:
surabhirdevadhenuryā tasyāḥ putratvamāgatāḥ ..
dharmo vṛṣabharūpeṇa mahādevadhvajaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27 ..
meaning:
सुरभिर्देवधेनुर्या तस्याः पुत्रत्वमागताः ..
धर्मो वृषभरूपेण महादेवध्वजः स्मृतः .. 27 ..
text_mt: They attained the status of sons of Surabhi, who is the divine cow. / Dharma in the form of a bull is traditionally known as the banner of Mahādeva.

sanskrit_iast:
daśadhenupradānena yatheṣṭāṅgatimāpnuyāt ..
śatañca dattvā dharmajñaḥ śakralokamupāgataḥ .. 28 ..
meaning:
दशधेनुप्रदानेन यथेष्टाङ्गतिमाप्नुयात् ..
शतञ्च दत्त्वा धर्मज्ञः शक्रलोकमुपागतः .. 28 ..
text_mt: By the gift of ten milch cows, one attains whatever destination he desires; / and having given a hundred, one who knows dharma arrives at the world of Śakra.

sanskrit_iast:
kalpāvaśeṣaṃ sa sukhī modatyapsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ ..
dattvā sahasraṃ dhenūnāṃ sarvapāpairvimucyate .. 29 ..
meaning:
कल्पावशेषं स सुखी मोदत्यप्सरसां गणैः ..
दत्त्वा सहस्रं धेनूनां सर्वपापैर्विमुच्यते .. 29 ..
text_mt: For the remainder of the aeon, he rejoices happily with hosts of apsarases; / by giving a thousand milch cows, he is freed from all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
ukṣṇāṃ ca ye prayacchanti śatena saha yūthapam ..
sarvapāpavinirmuktāste prayāntyamarāvatīm .. 3.306.30 ..
meaning:
उक्ष्णां च ये प्रयच्छन्ति शतेन सह यूथपम् ..
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तास्ते प्रयान्त्यमरावतीम् .. 3.306.30 ..
text_mt: And those who give a hundred oxen along with the leader of the herd, / fully freed from all sins, go to Amarāvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
kalpāvaśeṣaṃ tridive sukhamupya narottamāḥ ..
mānuṣye dhanasaṃyuktā bhavanti sukhinastataḥ .. 31 ..
meaning:
कल्पावशेषं त्रिदिवे सुखमुप्य नरोत्तमाः ..
मानुष्ये धनसंयुक्ता भवन्ति सुखिनस्ततः .. 31 ..
text_mt: Having dwelt happily in heaven for the remainder of the aeon, O best of men, / they then become happy on attaining human birth, endowed with wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
sahasreṇa gavāṃ sārdhaṃ ye prayacchanti yūthapam ..
alaṃkṛtaṃ yathāśaktyā golokaṃ yānti te narāḥ .. 32 ..
meaning:
सहस्रेण गवां सार्धं ये प्रयच्छन्ति यूथपम् ..
अलंकृतं यथाशक्त्या गोलोकं यान्ति ते नराः .. 32 ..
text_mt: Those men who give a thousand cows together with the leader of the herd, / adorned according to their ability, go to the world of cows.

sanskrit_iast:
ukṣāṇamindriyopetaṃ yastu dadyāddvijātaye ..
daśadhenuphalaṃ tasya nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 33 ..
meaning:
उक्षाणमिन्द्रियोपेतं यस्तु दद्याद्द्विजातये ..
दशधेनुफलं तस्य नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 33 ..
text_mt: He who gives an ox endowed with virility to a twice-born, / obtains the fruit of ten milch cows; no doubt should be entertained on this point.

sanskrit_iast:
goyugaṃ ye prayacchanti sīrayūpayutaṃ dvijāḥ ..
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya prāpnuvanti phalaṃ narāḥ .. 34 ..
meaning:
गोयुगं ये प्रयच्छन्ति सीरयूपयुतं द्विजाः ..
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य प्राप्नुवन्ति फलं नराः .. 34 ..
text_mt: Those men who give a pair of cattle equipped with a plough and yoke, O twice-born, / obtain the reward of one who is enriched with all desired objects.

sanskrit_iast:
gobhiścaturbhiḥ saṃyuktaṃ rathaṃ dattvā dvijātaye ..
dhānyairvastrairyutaṃ śaktyā śakralokaṃ vrajanti te .. 35 ..
meaning:
गोभिश्चतुर्भिः संयुक्तं रथं दत्त्वा द्विजातये ..
धान्यैर्वस्त्रैर्युतं शक्त्या शक्रलोकं व्रजन्ति ते .. 35 ..
text_mt: Having given to a twice-born a chariot yoked with four cows, / furnished with grain and garments according to their capacity, they go to the world of Śakra.

sanskrit_iast:
mānuṣyamāsādya tathā bhavanti vasudhādhipāḥ ..
śakaṭasya pradānantu vinā gobhirmahāphalam .. .. 36 ..
meaning:
मानुष्यमासाद्य तथा भवन्ति वसुधाधिपाः ..
शकटस्य प्रदानन्तु विना गोभिर्महाफलम् .. .. 36 ..
text_mt: And on attaining human birth, they become rulers of the earth. / The gift of a cart, even without cattle, brings great reward;

sanskrit_iast:
viśeṣeṇa mahābhāgāstasya gobhiryutasya ca ..
sasasyaṃ śakaṭaṃ dattvā nākalokaṃ mahīyate .. 37 ..
meaning:
विशेषेण महाभागास्तस्य गोभिर्युतस्य च ..
ससस्यं शकटं दत्त्वा नाकलोकं महीयते .. 37 ..
text_mt: especially so, O fortunate ones, when it is equipped with cattle. / Having given a cart laden with grain, one is magnified in heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
dattvā tu dhenuṃ homārthe brāhmaṇāyāhitāgnaye ..
godānaphalamāpnoti homadānaphalaṃ tathā .. 38 ..
meaning:
दत्त्वा तु धेनुं होमार्थे ब्राह्मणायाहिताग्नये ..
गोदानफलमाप्नोति होमदानफलं तथा .. 38 ..
text_mt: By giving a milch cow for the purpose of the fire offering to a brahmin who maintains the sacred fires, / he obtains the fruit of the gift of a cow and also the fruit of the gift of a fire offering.

sanskrit_iast:
snapanārthaṃ tathā dattvā dhenuṃ rudrasurālaye ..
rudralokamavāpnoti kulañcaiva samuddharet .. .. 39 ..
meaning:
स्नपनार्थं तथा दत्त्वा धेनुं रुद्रसुरालये ..
रुद्रलोकमवाप्नोति कुलञ्चैव समुद्धरेत् .. .. 39 ..
text_mt: Likewise, by giving a milch cow for the bath [of the deity] in a temple of Rudra, / he attains the world of Rudra and uplifts his family.

sanskrit_iast:
dattvā sacailaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ mahādevālaye naraḥ ..
rudralokamavāpnoti kulamuddharate tathā .. 3.306.40 ..
meaning:
दत्त्वा सचैलं वृषभं महादेवालये नरः ..
रुद्रलोकमवाप्नोति कुलमुद्धरते तथा .. 3.306.40 ..
text_mt: Having given a bull with a cloth in a temple of Mahādeva, a man / attains the world of Rudra and likewise uplifts his family.

sanskrit_iast:
dhenūnāṃ kapilā śreṣṭhā vṛṣabhaḥ śveta ucyate ..
śvetantu vṛṣabhaṃ dattvā phalasyānantyamaśnute .. 43 ..
meaning:
धेनूनां कपिला श्रेष्ठा वृषभः श्वेत उच्यते ..
श्वेतन्तु वृषभं दत्त्वा फलस्यानन्त्यमश्नुते .. 43 ..
text_mt: Among milch cows, the kapilā is the best; a white bull is said [to be foremost]. / By giving a white bull, one enjoys endless reward.

sanskrit_iast:
dadhikṣīrahitārthāya vāsudevasurālaye ..
dattvā gāṃ madhuparkārthaṃ cānantaṃ phalamāpnuyāt .. 42 ...
meaning:
दधिक्षीरहितार्थाय वासुदेवसुरालये ..
दत्त्वा गां मधुपर्कार्थं चानन्तं फलमाप्नुयात् .. 42 ...
text_mt: In a temple of Vāsudeva, for the sake of curd and milk / and for the honey-mixture, having given a cow, he attains endless reward.

sanskrit_iast:
gopradānaratā yānti golokaṃ mānavottamāḥ ..
sahāpsarobhirmuditā vimānavaramāsthitāḥ .. 43 ..
meaning:
गोप्रदानरता यान्ति गोलोकं मानवोत्तमाः ..
सहाप्सरोभिर्मुदिता विमानवरमास्थिताः .. 43 ..
text_mt: Those excellent men who take delight in the gift of cows go to the world of cows, / rejoicing together with apsarases, mounted on a supreme celestial chariot.

sanskrit_iast:
apāmadhastālloko yo tasyopari mahīdharāḥ ..
nāgānāmupariṣṭādbhūḥ pṛthivyupari mānavāḥ .. 44 ..
meaning:
अपामधस्ताल्लोको यो तस्योपरि महीधराः ..
नागानामुपरिष्टाद्भूः पृथिव्युपरि मानवाः .. 44 ..
text_mt: The world that is beneath the waters, above that are the mountains; / above the nāgas is the earth; above the earth are human beings.

sanskrit_iast:
manuṣyalokādūrdhvantu khagānāṃ gatirucyate ..
ākāśasyopari ravirdvāraṃ svargasya tatsmṛtam .. .. 45..
meaning:
मनुष्यलोकादूर्ध्वन्तु खगानां गतिरुच्यते ..
आकाशस्योपरि रविर्द्वारं स्वर्गस्य तत्स्मृतम् .. .. 45..
text_mt: Above the world of men is said to be the course of birds; / above the sky is the sun; that is remembered as the gate of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
devalokaḥ parastasmādbrahmalokastataḥ param..
tatropari gavāṃ loko viṣṇulokastataḥ param ..46..
meaning:
देवलोकः परस्तस्माद्ब्रह्मलोकस्ततः परम्..
तत्रोपरि गवां लोको विष्णुलोकस्ततः परम् ..46..
text_mt: Beyond that is the world of the gods; beyond that is the world of Brahmā; / above that is the world of cows; beyond that is the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
ekastvadho duṣkṛtināṃ karmiṇāṃ pṛthivī matā..
brāhme tapasi yuktānāṃ brahmalokaḥ sanātanaḥ ..47 ..
meaning:
एकस्त्वधो दुष्कृतिनां कर्मिणां पृथिवी मता..
ब्राह्मे तपसि युक्तानां ब्रह्मलोकः सनातनः ..47 ..
text_mt: The earth is regarded as the one [destination] below for evildoers and men of ritual action; / the eternal world of Brahmā is for those engaged in the austerities of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
gavāmeva hi goloko durārohā hi sā gatiḥ ..
ekāntino viṣṇubhaktā viṣṇulokaṃ vrajanti te . 48 ..
meaning:
गवामेव हि गोलोको दुरारोहा हि सा गतिः ..
एकान्तिनो विष्णुभक्ता विष्णुलोकं व्रजन्ति ते . 48 ..
text_mt: The world of cows belongs indeed to cows; that destination is difficult to ascend. / Those single-minded devotees of Viṣṇu go to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
gopradānaratā yāṃti golokaṃ sarvakāmadam ..
tatra kāmaphalā vṛkṣā nadyaḥ pāyasakardamāḥ .. 49 ..
meaning:
गोप्रदानरता यांति गोलोकं सर्वकामदम् ..
तत्र कामफला वृक्षा नद्यः पायसकर्दमाः .. 49 ..
text_mt: Those devoted to the gift of cows go to the world of cows which grants all desires. / There, trees bear desired fruits, and rivers have mud of rice boiled in milk.

sanskrit_iast:
suvarṇasikatāścānyā vimalāmbuyutāḥ śubhāḥ ..
yathākāmepsitāstatra bhavanti śubhakarmiṇām .. 3.306.50 ..
meaning:
सुवर्णसिकताश्चान्या विमलाम्बुयुताः शुभाः ..
यथाकामेप्सितास्तत्र भवन्ति शुभकर्मिणाम् .. 3.306.50 ..
text_mt: And there are other auspicious [rivers] with golden sands, endowed with pure water; / there, they are available as desired to those who performed auspicious deeds.

sanskrit_iast:
deśā manoharāḥ śubhrā devārāmavibhūṣaṇāḥ ..
divyena nṛtyagītena vāditreṇa manoharāḥ .. 51 ..
meaning:
देशा मनोहराः शुभ्रा देवारामविभूषणाः ..
दिव्येन नृत्यगीतेन वादित्रेण मनोहराः .. 51 ..
text_mt: The regions are charming, bright, adorned with divine groves, / captivating with celestial dance, song, and musical instruments.

sanskrit_iast:
tatrepsitānāṃ kāmānāmāptirbhavati nityadā ..
hemaśṛṅgīṃ rūpyakhurāṃ muktālāṃgūlabhūṣaṇām .. 52 ..
meaning:
तत्रेप्सितानां कामानामाप्तिर्भवति नित्यदा ..
हेमशृङ्गीं रूप्यखुरां मुक्तालांगूलभूषणाम् .. 52 ..
text_mt: There, the attainment of desired wishes occurs at all times. / [Bestowing a cow] with golden horns, silver hooves, decorated with pearls on her tail,

sanskrit_iast:
ahatāmbarasaṃvītāṃ tathā kāṃsyopadohinīm ..
trirātraṃ sthaṃḍile suptvā trirātraṃ gorasāśanaḥ .. 53 ..
meaning:
अहताम्बरसंवीतां तथा कांस्योपदोहिनीम् ..
त्रिरात्रं स्थंडिले सुप्त्वा त्रिरात्रं गोरसाशनः .. 53 ..
text_mt: clothed in unworn garments, and with a bronze milking vessel, / having slept for three nights on the bare ground and eating the products of the cow for three nights,

sanskrit_iast:
tṛptāntu tarpite dattvā vāsasā saṃvṛtāṃ dvijāḥ ..
sadakṣiṇāṃ mahābhāgāstrirātraṃ gorasaistataḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
तृप्तान्तु तर्पिते दत्त्वा वाससा संवृतां द्विजाः ..
सदक्षिणां महाभागास्त्रिरात्रं गोरसैस्ततः .. 54 ..
text_mt: having given [her] satisfied to one who is gratified, covered with a garment, O twice-born, / along with a sacrificial fee, O fortunate ones, and thereafter for three nights

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇasaṃdhāraṇaṃ kṛtvā gavāṃ loke mahīyate ..
yāvanti dhenuromāṇi tāvadvarṣāṇi mānavaḥ .. 55 ..
meaning:
प्राणसंधारणं कृत्वा गवां लोके महीयते ..
यावन्ति धेनुरोमाणि तावद्वर्षाणि मानवः .. 55 ..
text_mt: sustaining his vital breaths with the products of the cow, a man is honoured / in the world of cows for as many years as there are hairs on the milch cow.

sanskrit_iast:
dattaivaṃ kapilāṃ viprāḥ prāpnotyabhyadhikaṃ phalam ..
sāyaṃ prātarmanuṣyāṇāmaśanaṃ devanirmitam .. 56 ..
meaning:
दत्तैवं कपिलां विप्राः प्राप्नोत्यभ्यधिकं फलम् ..
सायं प्रातर्मनुष्याणामशनं देवनिर्मितम् .. 56 ..
text_mt: Having thus given a kapilā cow, O brahmins, he obtains an even greater fruit. / Evening and morning meal is established by the gods for men.

sanskrit_iast:
tatraikakālamaśnanto dvitīyādaśanānnaraḥ ..
yathoktavidhinā dadyātkrītvā tu kapilāṃ naraḥ .. 57 ..
meaning:
तत्रैककालमश्नन्तो द्वितीयादशनान्नरः ..
यथोक्तविधिना दद्यात्क्रीत्वा तु कपिलां नरः .. 57 ..
text_mt:
Eating only once [a day] from the second meal, a man,
having purchased a brown cow, should give [her] according to the prescribed rite;

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute ..
gavāṃ lokamavāpnoti kulamuddharati svakam .. 58 ..
meaning:
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ..
गवां लोकमवाप्नोति कुलमुद्धरति स्वकम् .. 58 ..
text_mt:
he obtains the fruit of a sacrifice replete with all desires,
attains the world of cows, and redeems his own lineage.

sanskrit_iast:
alaṃkṛtāṃ tato dattvā godānaphalamāpnuyāt ..
ajāmalaṃkṛtāṃ dattvā vahniloke mahīyate .. 59 ..
meaning:
अलंकृतां ततो दत्त्वा गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ..
अजामलंकृतां दत्त्वा वह्निलोके महीयते .. 59 ..
text_mt:
Then, having given her adorned, he would obtain the fruit of gifting a cow.
Having given a decorated she-goat, he is glorified in the world of Agni.

sanskrit_iast:
tadeva lokamāpnoti dattvājaṃ vidhivannaraḥ ..
vāruṇaṃ lokamāpnoti dattvā ca mahiṣīṃ naraḥ..3.306.60..
meaning:
तदेव लोकमाप्नोति दत्त्वाजं विधिवन्नरः ..
वारुणं लोकमाप्नोति दत्त्वा च महिषीं नरः..3.306.60..
text_mt:
A man attains that very world by giving a he-goat according to rule;
and by giving a female buffalo, a man attains the world of Varuṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
mahiṣasya pradānena yāmye loke mahīyate ..
vāruṇaṃ lokamāpnoti dattvorabhraṃ narottamaḥ .. 61.
meaning:
महिषस्य प्रदानेन याम्ये लोके महीयते ..
वारुणं लोकमाप्नोति दत्त्वोरभ्रं नरोत्तमः .. 61.
text_mt:
Through the gift of a male buffalo, he is glorified in the world of Yama.
Having given a ram, the best among men attains the world of Varuṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
avipradātā śatadhā tadeva phalamaśnute ..
āraṇyapaśudānena vāyuloke mahīyate .. 62 ..
meaning:
अविप्रदाता शतधा तदेव फलमश्नुते ..
आरण्यपशुदानेन वायुलोके महीयते .. 62 ..
text_mt:
The giver of a ewe enjoys that very fruit a hundredfold.
Through the gift of a wild animal, he is glorified in the world of Vāyu.

sanskrit_iast:
etadeva phalaṃ proktaṃ pradānena ca pakṣiṇām ..
śastrapiṇḍaki jālādirudakādānatastathā .. 63 ..
meaning:
एतदेव फलं प्रोक्तं प्रदानेन च पक्षिणाम् ..
शस्त्रपिण्डकि जालादिरुदकादानतस्तथा .. 63 ..
text_mt:
This very fruit is proclaimed through the gift of birds,
and likewise through the gift of water, weapons, balls [of food], and nets.

sanskrit_iast:
gorasānāṃ pradānena tṛptimāpnotyanuttamām ..
tatra vāśvayuje māse yastu dadyāddvijātiṣu .. 64 ..
meaning:
गोरसानां प्रदानेन तृप्तिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ..
तत्र वाश्वयुजे मासे यस्तु दद्याद्द्विजातिषु .. 64 ..
text_mt:
Through the gift of cow-products, he attains unsurpassed satisfaction;
and whoever should give to the twice-born in the month of Āśvayuja,

sanskrit_iast:
ārogyaṃ mahadāpnoti yatrayatrābhijāyate ..
tathā dadhnaḥ pradānena maṅgalānyāpnute sadā .. 65 ..
meaning:
आरोग्यं महदाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते ..
तथा दध्नः प्रदानेन मङ्गलान्याप्नुते सदा .. 65 ..
text_mt:
attains great health wherever he is born.
Likewise, through the gift of curd, he always obtains auspicious things.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīradastṛptimāpnoti sarvaduḥkhairvimucyate ..
kṣīreṇa snapanaṃ kṛtvā harasya prayato naraḥ .. 66 ..
meaning:
क्षीरदस्तृप्तिमाप्नोति सर्वदुःखैर्विमुच्यते ..
क्षीरेण स्नपनं कृत्वा हरस्य प्रयतो नरः .. 66 ..
text_mt:
The giver of milk attains satisfaction and is freed from all sorrows.
A restrained man, having performed the bathing of Hara with milk,

sanskrit_iast:
mano'bhitāpanirmukto rudraloke mahīyate ..
paramānnapradānena kāmānāpnoti śāśvatān.. 67 ..
meaning:
मनोऽभितापनिर्मुक्तो रुद्रलोके महीयते ..
परमान्नप्रदानेन कामानाप्नोति शाश्वतान्.. 67 ..
text_mt:
freed from anguish of mind, is glorified in the world of Rudra.
Through the gift of supreme food [rice-milk], he attains eternal desires.

sanskrit_iast:
māsi māsi tu revatyāṃ brāhmaṇānghṛtapāyasam ..
sadakṣiṇaṃ bhojayitvā rūpamāpnotyanuttamam .. 68 ..
meaning:
मासि मासि तु रेवत्यां ब्राह्मणान्घृतपायसम् ..
सदक्षिणं भोजयित्वा रूपमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् .. 68 ..
text_mt:
Month by month on the Revatī [nakṣatra], having fed brahmins
rice-milk cooked with ghee along with a sacrificial fee, he attains unsurpassed beauty.

sanskrit_iast:
ājyantejaḥ samuddiṣṭaṃ cājyaṃ pāpaharaṃ param .
ājyaṃ surāṇāmāhāraścājye lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ .. 69 ..
meaning:
आज्यन्तेजः समुद्दिष्टं चाज्यं पापहरं परम् .
आज्यं सुराणामाहारश्चाज्ये लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः .. 69 ..
text_mt:
Ghee is declared to be splendor, and ghee is the supreme destroyer of sin.
Ghee is the food of the gods, and the worlds are established in ghee.

sanskrit_iast:
ājyena liṅgasnapanaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā tu śūlinaḥ ..
sarvaduḥkhavinirmukto rudraloke mahīyate .. 3.306.70 ..
meaning:
आज्येन लिङ्गस्नपनं नरः कृत्वा तु शूलिनः ..
सर्वदुःखविनिर्मुक्तो रुद्रलोके महीयते .. 3.306.70 ..
text_mt:
A man having bathed the liṅga of the trident-bearer with ghee,
freed from all sorrow, is glorified in the world of Rudra.

sanskrit_iast:
alakṣmīśamanaṃ proktaṃ ghṛtasnānaṃ tathā dvijāḥ ..
kalyamutthāya yo gavyaghṛte mukhamathātmanaḥ . 71 ..
meaning:
अलक्ष्मीशमनं प्रोक्तं घृतस्नानं तथा द्विजाः ..
कल्यमुत्थाय यो गव्यघृते मुखमथात्मनः . 71 ..
text_mt:
Bathing with ghee is declared to appease misfortune, O twice-born.
Having risen early in the morning, whoever [looks at] his own face in cow's ghee,

sanskrit_iast:
paśyate sa jahātyeva kṛtvā pāpamaharniśam ..
alakṣmīrnaśyate cāsya kṣiprameṣā karīṣiṇī .. 72 ..
meaning:
पश्यते स जहात्येव कृत्वा पापमहर्निशम् ..
अलक्ष्मीर्नश्यते चास्य क्षिप्रमेषा करीषिणी .. 72 ..
text_mt:
and sees it, he surely casts away the sin committed day and night;
and his misfortune, rich in cow dung [foulness], is quickly destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtadānānnaro yāti svargalokamasaṃśayam ..
māse cāśvayuje nityaṃ ghṛtaṃ yastu prayacchati .. 73 ..
meaning:
घृतदानान्नरो याति स्वर्गलोकमसंशयम् ..
मासे चाश्वयुजे नित्यं घृतं यस्तु प्रयच्छति .. 73 ..
text_mt:
From the gift of ghee, a man goes to the heavenly world without doubt.
And whoever always offers ghee in the month of Āśvayuja,

sanskrit_iast:
kalyamutthāya viprebhyaḥ prīṇayecca tathāśvinau ..
sa rūpaṃ mahadāpnoti tathā rogaiśca mucyate ..
evaṃ mahāphalaṃ dānaṃ gorasānāṃ tathā gavām .. 74 ..
meaning:
कल्यमुत्थाय विप्रेभ्यः प्रीणयेच्च तथाश्विनौ ..
स रूपं महदाप्नोति तथा रोगैश्च मुच्यते ..
एवं महाफलं दानं गोरसानां तथा गवाम् .. 74 ..

sanskrit_iast:
prayacchate yaḥ kapilāṃ sacailāṃ kāṃsyopadohāṃ kanakāgraśṛṅgīm ..
taistairguṇaiḥ kāmadughā ca bhūtvā naraṃ pradātāramupaiti sā gauḥ .. 75 ..
meaning:
प्रयच्छते यः कपिलां सचैलां कांस्योपदोहां कनकाग्रशृङ्गीम् ..
तैस्तैर्गुणैः कामदुघा च भूत्वा नरं प्रदातारमुपैति सा गौः .. 75 ..
text_mt:
Whoever gives a brown cow along with cloth, with a bronze milking pail and horns tipped with gold—
becoming a wish-yielding cow by those very qualities, she comes to that man, the giver.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvanti romāṇi bhavanti dhenvāstāvatphalaṃ prāpnute gopradātā ..
putrāṃśca pautrāṃśca kulañca sarvamāsaptamaṃ tārayate paratra..76..
3.307
haṃsa uvāca ..
ghṛtadhenupradānañca nibodhata dvijottamāḥ ..
gavyasya sarpiṣaḥ kumbhaṃ pūrṇantu parikalpayet ..1..
kalaśañca tathā pūrṇantasyā vatsaṃ prakalpayet ..
kāṃsyāpidhānasacchannasitavastrayutantathā .. 2 ..
hiraṇyagarbhau kartavyāvanuliptau ca bāhyataḥ ..
ikṣuyaṣṭimayānpādānkhurānrūpyamayām̐stathā .. 3 ..
sauvarṇe cākṣiṇī kārye śṛṅge cāgurukāṣṭhaje ..
saptadhānyaśca kartavye tasya pārśve pṛthakkṛte .. 4 ..
tasya paṭṭaṃ ca kartavyaṃ kambalaṃ ca dvijottamāḥ ..
kuryātturuṣkaraṃ dūre prāṇe hemamayāṃstanān .. 5 ..
tadvaccharkarayā jihvāṃ guḍakṣīramayaṃ mukham ...
kṣaumasūtreṇa lāṃgūlaṃ romāṇi sitasarṣapaiḥ .. 6 ..
meaning:
यावन्ति रोमाणि भवन्ति धेन्वास्तावत्फलं प्राप्नुते गोप्रदाता ..
पुत्रांश्च पौत्रांश्च कुलञ्च सर्वमासप्तमं तारयते परत्र..76..
3.307

घृतधेनुप्रदानञ्च निबोधत द्विजोत्तमाः ..

one endowed with faith should make the back of copper plate.
Having made this arrangement, with consecrations of ghee and milk,
one should worship the all-pervading lord with the name 'Hari having ghee for his radiance.'
Then a man, with perfumes, flowers, food, incense, cloth, and the like,
should offer a lamp with ghee, and likewise [offer] ghee to the directions.
When [making] the oblation, O brahmins, one should give the cow to a brahmin according to one's ability.
Ghṛtācī is pleased with the brahmin, having imagined him as radiant with ghee.
Having given her, for one night a man should be an eater of ghee;
freed from all sins, he attains an eternal world.
A pure man, fasting and having bathed according to this rule,
enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice replete with all desires;
and in a celestial chariot the color of the sun, he is glorified in the world of cows,
where streams flow with ghee and milk, where the mud is rice-pudding,
where trees yield desired fruits, and where accomplishment comes by mere thought,

where there is the perpetual singing and dancing of Gandharvas and Apsarases;
he dwells in that world for a very long time, as long as the fourteen Indras.
Attaining human birth, he becomes free from disease, endowed with good character, beauty, and wealth,
delightful to the mind, dear to women, possessed of riches, and endowed with all comforts.
Haṃsa said:
I shall proclaim the sesame-cow, which removes the fear of all sins.
The wise man should make it in the shape of a cow upon a woollen blanket,
with sixteen prasthas of sesame seeds, and the calf indeed with four;
he should make the spreading of sesame according to the measurement of the cow.
Then one should fashion the cow with jewels, O twice-born, which I shall explain:
having golden horns, silver hooves, an auspicious nose of fragrance,
one should make her tongue of sweet food, her mouth of molasses, her blanket of thread,
her legs of sugarcane, her back of copper, and eyes of pearls;
her ears of excellent leaves, having auspicious teeth of fruit;
one should make her with garlands and flowers, and endowed with an udder of fresh butter.

text_mt:
Equipped with charming fruits and edible sweets, with gems and pearls, / covered with a pair of white garments, and provided with a beautiful umbrella,
having made a bronze milking vessel, one should worship Vāsudeva / with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, reverent bows, incense, lamps, and food.
And a person should offer sesame seeds into the fire in his name alone; / one should satisfy him alone, and present that cow to a keeper of the sacred fire.
He who, having eaten only sesame seeds for three nights, presents the sesame-cow, / and having given it, eats sesame seeds again for one night, O foremost twice-born,
that consumption of sesame seeds is praised as superior even to a cāndrāyaṇa penance. / Freed from all sins, a person delivers his father and grandfather,
and also his [great-]grandfather from evil deeds; / he delivers himself, his sons and grandsons, and even his great-grandson.
Or a person giving a sesame-cow on behalf of a friend / delivers from evil deeds that very one on whose behalf he offers it.
And he who receives it according to rule, or watches it being given, / even he, freed from sin, is honoured in the world of heaven.

One burdened with major sins, or one burdened with minor sins, / even he attains purification through the gift of a sesame-cow.
Having reached the world of the Vasus, and having enjoyed the pleasures of the king of the gods even there, / when he attains human birth he becomes free from disease, endowed with wealth, and possessed of beauty and happiness.
3.309
Haṃsa said:
I shall explain the water-cow for the gratification of the One Who Lies upon the Waters. / A water-jar, O best of the twice-born, provided with gold and silver,
and containing jewels inside, one should prepare, and place it upon barley; / and one should surround it on all sides with all kinds of cultivated grains.
It should be covered with a pair of white garments and adorned with dūrvā sprouts, / accompanied by costus, jatamansi, murā, vetiver, vālukā, and amalaki;
with leaves of priyaṅgu, wearing a white sacred thread; / and one should furnish it with an umbrella, shoes, and a turban.
Having provided it in the four directions with dishes of sesame seeds accompanied by gold, / it is then covered at the mouth with a vessel filled with curds and boiled rice.

In this very same manner one should prepare a water-pitcher as the calf. / Having fasted and thoroughly worshipped the lord of the gods who lies upon the waters,
with flowers, incense, and offerings according to one's means, / a devoted man should present it to a brahmin dressed in fresh garments,
having uttered: 'May Keśava, who lies upon the waters, the source of the universe, be pleased with me.' / Thus he should give it, and the twice-born should also satisfy him.
Having fasted for a day and night, he should give it according to the rule declared by me; / after this he must remain eating uncooked food for a day and night.
Having given the water-cow according to this rule, O foremost of the twice-born, / he attains every delight and obtains eternal desires.
That man likewise attains liberation from all [burdens of] austerities; / he obtains great good fortune and supreme beauty.
Into whosever sight that man comes, / to each and every one he brings supreme delight, O foremost of the twice-born.
He is perpetually satisfied and likewise free from disease; / rid of blemish, he attains the pacification of all afflictions.

text_mt:
The giver, O foremost twice-born, attains the world of Varuṇa by giving it once; / having given it repeatedly, O brahmins, he reaches the world of Viṣṇu.
This supremely purifying gift for the sake of delight has been proclaimed by me, O lords of the twice-born: / auspicious, bringing fame, destroying misfortunes, granting desires, beneficial to the world, and highly praised.
3.310
Haṃsa said:
Gold is the highest gem, and it is the highest of riches; / it is the highest of metals, and indeed the highest of all things.
It is the first offspring of Agni, purifying and supremely auspicious; / destroying all sins when worn, it bestows the world of the gods upon the giver.
Because of its purity, O foremost twice-born, it is constantly worn by the gods / as crowns, earrings, necklaces, keyūra armlets, and aṅgada bracelets.
That gold from the Jambu river belonging to the gods resembles an indragopaka insect; / that of the ancestors has the lustre of moonbeams; that of the Daityas is like a variegated hue;
that of the Nāgas is like the lustre of a parrot; that of women is said to be yellow. / Having given merely a kṛṣṇala of it, a man is freed from sin.

text_mt:
And having given a māṣaka, he enjoys its holy reward. / Having given a māṣaka of gold at the rising of the sun,
and having offered an oblation into the fire, he attains liberation from all sins without doubt; / this is praised as his perpetual observance of the three sacred fires.
When the sun has reached midday, he who, having offered into the fire, gives it— / a great reward is declared for his perpetual offering into the fire.
At the setting of the sun, having offered into the fire, he indeed gives it; / he attains great merit by this daily gift, O twice-born.
He who offers into the fire and gives gold at the three junctions of the day / is not stained by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not [wetted] by water.
By giving a kṛṣṇala once, he lives happily in heaven for a year; / and having given a māṣaka, he lives in heaven for five years.
He who presents a suvarṇa weight of gold to a brahmin / becomes faultless and rejoices in heaven for a full hundred years.

text_mt:
He who presents [his own] weight in gold, O twice-born, / freed from all sins, attains the destination of his desire.
Whether he is a slayer of a brahmin, a drinker of liquor, a thief, or a violator of the guru's bed, / even if burdened with all sins, he is liberated through that gift.
And this is the highest of faithful acts, the highest among supreme gifts; / having given gold to a brahmin, one becomes happy everywhere.
When after a long time he falls from heaven, endowed with beauty and good fortune, / that man is born in a very prosperous family of theirs, endowed with all virtues.
By giving a gold vessel, a person is blessed with sons, / and attains all desires, renown, and heaven.
The giver of silver attains beauty; the giver of copper attains enjoyment. / From giving iron and brass, one undoubtedly obtains base metal.
From giving tin and lead, one obtains an increase of the digestive fire. / Whoever presents an iron vessel at will to a twice-born,
becomes a vessel of desires, and especially so on account of the iron. / Whoever presents artisans' tools made of iron according to the rule, O twice-born,

text_mt:
to him the fruit of the gift of knowledge is declared—there is no doubt here. / A man who gives leather always attains protection.
By the gift of weapons one achieves the destruction of enemies. / By the gift of royal insignia one becomes a king on earth.
And by the gift of precious gems one is born indeed as a king here [on earth]. / Having enjoyed for a very long time the world that belongs to the gift of gems, O twice-born,
the giver of diamond [goes] to the world of Śakra, the giver of ruby to the Sun's. / Having given an emerald, one is immediately honoured in the world of Viṣṇu.
By giving a pearl one attains the realm of Varuṇa. / By giving cat's eye one rejoices in seven continents.
And having given other gems, [one attains the realm] of the king of kings, O twice-born. / Of all gems, gold is said to be the foremost.
Wearing, praising, and giving gold are commended. / The gift alleviates nightmares and destroys the ill-sacrificed;
it should be known as supremely sin-destroying and pacifying misfortune. / Having given gold, one rejoices in worlds desired at will,

text_mt:
Having gone to the world of Brahmā through those who honour brahmins by giving to brahmins whatever they wish, / honoured by gods and brahmins, he becomes happy; therefore, what is requested should be given to brahmins.
3.312 / Haṃsa said: / A man who duly gives human-drawn vehicles to a twice-born, / for him the fruit of an aśvamedha is declared, O best of the twice-born.
By the gift of a palanquin, likewise, [one obtains] the fruit of an agniṣṭoma; / having given a servant who does work, one obtains the fruit of a gosava.
He goes to dwelling in the same world as Śakra who gives a warrior; / but he who gives a female servant who does work to a brahmin,
his worlds are declared to be charming, belonging to the Vasus. / But he who gives a youthful female servant endowed with beauty,
he sports with apsarases filled with joy in the Nandana forest. / O brahmins, he who gives a camel or a donkey to a twice-born,
having reached Alakā, rejoices together with the lords of yakṣas. / The giving of a horse is declared the highest of gifts.

text_mt:
By the gift of a mare, likewise, abundant fruit is remembered. / Those who give a horse go to the world of the sun.
As many hairs as it has, for so many hundreds of years. / Having given a white horse, one obtains ten times that fruit.
Just as a kapilā cow is foremost, even so is it among horses. / [If] he gives a horse with a saddle and with ornaments,
the fruit of a puṇḍarīka sacrifice is declared; no doubt should be made here. / Yoked with four horses and endowed with all equipment,
having given a chariot to a twice-born, one obtains the fruit of a rājasūya. / Duly giving a female elephant, one obtains this very fruit.
By the gift of an elephant, one is glorified in heaven; / in this world he becomes a king endowed with fame and valour.
Having given an elephant with golden girths to a brahmin, O twice-born, / he attains the fruit of both the rājasūya and aśvamedha, without doubt.

text_mt:
Having given to a twice-born a chariot yoked with four elephants, / he obtains the fruit of the gift of the entire earth, without doubt.
By him in this world, indeed, the earth with its mountains, forests, and waters has been given; / and that great-souled man goes to the desired worlds, worshipped by the gods.
3.313 / Haṃsa said: / The gift of clothing is proclaimed the highest of gifts in the world; / for clothing belongs to all deities and obtains applicability to all.
The giver of clothing becomes well-attired, endowed with beauty and wealth, / endowed with charm and good fortune, and free from disease, O twice-born.
Blue, [impure] red, and worn-out [cloth] must not be given to a brahmin. / An excellent [cloth should be] given, [such as one worthy of] the descendants of Aṅgiras, or having given linen [one attains the world] of Bṛhaspati.
Having given a garment of cotton, one is glorified in heaven; / having given one that is woolen, the fruit becomes tenfold.
Having given sheep's wool clothing, one attains the world of the Bhṛgus; / having given goat's wool, [the world] of the descendants of Aṅgiras; having given linen, [the world] of Bṛhaspati;

he attains the world of the Vasus [by giving] garments of kuśa grass and silk; / and having given that which is born of worms, he is glorified in the world of Soma.

Having given cloth dyed with safflower, one attains great good fortune; / from the gift of cloth dyed with saffron, one attains great charm.
Having given cloth dyed with other colours that are not blue, one becomes happy. / In whatever manner the preciousness of the garment increases in this world,
and in whatever manner its whiteness [increases], thus he obtains the fruit of merit. / For other gifts as well, this very [principle] is proclaimed.

The giver of clothing is declared to be the giver of everything, since everywhere he who has clothes / receives honour, O knowers of dharma; therefore, indeed, it is superior.
The giver of clothing, having enjoyed divine pleasures in heaven for a very long time, / by means of a shining aerial chariot having the colour of the sun and yoked with swans,
attains human birth and becomes free from disease, pure, devoted to happiness, modest, / pleasing to people, well-attired, and always worthy of worship among the wise in the world.
3.314 / Haṃsa said: / The gift of grains is declared the highest, O bulls among the twice-born; / and even above all grains, red rice is proclaimed [supreme].
A man, having given red rice, is glorified in the world of the sun; / and having given fragrant [rice], he rejoices with the gandharvas.
By the gift of kalama rice, he is glorified in the world of Śakra; / by the gift of mahāśāli rice, he attains the world of the Vasus.
Having likewise given kāṣṭhaśāli rice, he is happy in Alakā; / from the gift of vrīhi and other grains, he attains heaven.

text_mt:
By the gift of barley, a man is glorified in the world of Śakra; / likewise, by the gift of wheat, he attains the world of the Vasus.
He who gives priyaṅgu becomes dear to the world; / he who gives śyāmāka, with him the deities are pleased.
A man intent on the gift of other bearded grains / attains the world of heaven; no doubt should be made here.
The giver of mung beans [attains] the world of Śakra, but the giver of black gram [attains] the world of Yama; / likewise, O brahmins, the giver of sesame seeds attains whatever world he desires.
By the gift of sixty-day rice, one obtains the world of Nirṛti; / having given common millet and chickpea, one attains the world of Varuṇa.
By [giving] lentils [one attains] the world of Vāyu, and by black-eyed peas that of the Bestower of Wealth; / from the gift of other pod-bearing grains one attains heaven.
From the gift of sugarcane and grapes one attains supreme good fortune; / the giver of jaggery likewise [gains] health, and the giver of white sugar his desired wish.
By giving boiled sugarcane juice one attains supreme satisfaction; / the giver of candied sugar [attains] good fortune, and the giver of honey all desires.

text_mt:
The giver of ghee [attains] long life, and the giver of oil likewise health; / he who gives salt obtains all desires.
The giver of roasted barley flour obtains satisfaction, and the giver of sand-sugar likewise prosperity; / from the gift of others not mentioned one attains heaven.
In the world of mortals, dry grain is said to bring greater fruit than the gift of cooked food; for having received it, / foremost twice-born continually sacrifice with sacrifices; therefore it is declared most meritorious.
3.315
Haṃsa said:
Among all gifts, the gift of food is pre-eminent; / no gift has ever been superior to the gift of food, nor will there ever be.
Here there should be no examination of the recipient, nor a rule of time, / nor is place to be examined here; food is always to be given.
To dogs, outcasts, and likewise to fallen outcasts, / and to worms, insects, and winged creatures, food is always to be given.
For food is life in this world, and the vital breaths are bound to food; / in this world the giver of food is the giver of life, and thus the giver of food gives all.

text_mt:
And when offspring are born to one who has eaten another's food, O best of the twice-born, / it should be understood, O foremost brahmins, that the offspring belongs to him whose food it was.
It should be given to all classes, and [food] of a brahmin should be eaten; / O twice-born, if a brahmin dies with a man's food inside his belly,
he attains that very womb [of the giver's class]; no doubt should be entertained on this matter. / The giver of solid food attains heaven, and the giver of cooked dishes the world of Śakra.
The giver of lickable food [attains] the world of the Apsarases, and the giver of suckable food that of the Vasus; / likewise, the man who gives drinks attains the world of Varuṇa.
For one who offers fragrant, cool drinks, / there will be abundance in all desires; no doubt should be entertained on this matter.
By giving milk-rice pudding there is eternal satisfaction; / if one dies while wishing to drink, he is glorified in the world of cows.
He who gives unstinted food on the road / to a weary person never seen before—great is the fruit of his merit.
Even if he has served food a thousand times [to sinners], he does not go to hell; / in an aerial chariot shining like the sun, he is glorified in heaven.

text_mt:
Likewise, O brahmins, if one removes the hunger of even a single afflicted person, / by that deed he enjoys a great fruit after death.
Whatever is most desirable in the world, and whatever is dear to him in his house, / that very thing should be given to a virtuous person by one desiring it to become imperishable.
Having observed the manifold gifts and their fruit of many kinds, / a man endowed with faith should bestow them upon brahmins, and, contented in mind, he shall obtain the same repeatedly in the human world.

meaning:
पापशीले न दातव्यं कदाचिदपि किञ्चन ..
पापशीले तु यद्दत्तं तद्दातुदोषमावहेत् .. 3 ..
text_mt: Nothing should ever be given to a person of sinful conduct; / whatever is given to a person of sinful conduct brings demerit to the giver.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanadastena pāpena śīghrameveha yujyate ..
tasmātprāpya dhanaṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyaśīlaṃ samācaret .. 4 ..
meaning:
धनदस्तेन पापेन शीघ्रमेवेह युज्यते ..
तस्मात्प्राप्य धनं पुण्यं पुण्यशीलं समाचरेत् .. 4 ..
text_mt: The giver of wealth is soon joined with that sin here; / therefore, having obtained wealth, he should act virtuously through righteous conduct.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanadastena puṇyena yogamāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
annadānena kartavyaṃ pātrāvekṣaṇamaṇvapi .. 5 ..
meaning:
धनदस्तेन पुण्येन योगमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ..
अन्नदानेन कर्तव्यं पात्रावेक्षणमण्वपि .. 5 ..
text_mt: By that merit the giver of wealth attains union [with the divine] without doubt. / In the gift of food, no scrutiny whatsoever of the recipient should be made.

sanskrit_iast:
annaṃ sarvatra dātavyaṃ dharmakāmena vai dvijāḥ ..
sadoṣepi tu nirdoṣaṃ saguṇetiguṇāvaham .. 6 ..
meaning:
अन्नं सर्वत्र दातव्यं धर्मकामेन वै द्विजाः ..
सदोषेपि तु निर्दोषं सगुणेतिगुणावहम् .. 6 ..
text_mt: Food is to be given everywhere by one desiring dharma, O twice-born; / even if [given] to a flawed person it is faultless, and if to a virtuous one, it brings manifold virtue.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena deyamannaṃ sadaiva tu ..
vidyādhyayanasaktānāmannadānaṃ mahāphalam .. 7 ..
meaning:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन देयमन्नं सदैव तु ..
विद्याध्ययनसक्तानामन्नदानं महाफलम् .. 7 ..
text_mt: Therefore, by every effort, food should always be given; / the gift of food to those intent on the study of sacred knowledge brings great fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
śubhānāmapyathānyeṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
yasyānnamupayuñjāno naraḥ karmāṇi sādhayet .. 8 ..
meaning:
शुभानामप्यथान्येषां कर्मणां द्विजपुङ्गवाः ..
यस्यान्नमुपयुञ्जानो नरः कर्माणि साधयेत् .. 8 ..
text_mt: And likewise for other auspicious deeds, O foremost twice-born; / eating whose food a man accomplishes deeds,

sanskrit_iast:
karma sādhayataḥ puṇyamannadātā tathāśnute ..
dattvā nṛpatibhītānāṃ dhanināñca tathā dhanam .. 9 ..
meaning:
कर्म साधयतः पुण्यमन्नदाता तथाश्नुते ..
दत्त्वा नृपतिभीतानां धनिनाञ्च तथा धनम् .. 9 ..
text_mt: the giver of food partakes in the merit of him who accomplishes the deed. / By giving wealth to those terrified of the king and to wealthy persons,

sanskrit_iast:
taskarebhyaśca bhītānāṃ phalamakṣayamaśnute ..
yiyakṣatā tathā dattaṃ vyasane haṃtumicchatā .. 3.316.10 ..
meaning:
तस्करेभ्यश्च भीतानां फलमक्षयमश्नुते ..
यियक्षता तथा दत्तं व्यसने हंतुमिच्छता .. 3.316.10 ..
text_mt: and to those terrified of thieves, one enjoys imperishable fruit. / Likewise, what is given to one wishing to sacrifice or wishing to avert calamity,

sanskrit_iast:
duḥkhānvitānāṃ dīnānāñcākṣayaṃ tatprakīrtitam ..
vivāhamekhalābandhapratiṣṭhādiṣu karmasu ..11..
meaning:
दुःखान्वितानां दीनानाञ्चाक्षयं तत्प्रकीर्तितम् ..
विवाहमेखलाबन्धप्रतिष्ठादिषु कर्मसु ..11..
text_mt: or to those afflicted with sorrow and wretched, is proclaimed imperishable; / in ceremonies such as marriage, investiture of the girdle, and consecration,

sanskrit_iast:
āpanneṣu ca yaddattaṃ tadakṣayyamudāhṛtam ..
yajñopakaraṇaṃ dravyaṃ kṣattriye dvijapuṅgavāḥ .. 12 ..
meaning:
आपन्नेषु च यद्दत्तं तदक्षय्यमुदाहृतम् ..
यज्ञोपकरणं द्रव्यं क्षत्त्रिये द्विजपुङ्गवाः .. 12 ..
text_mt: and whatever is given to those in distress, that is declared imperishable. / An article serving as sacrificial equipment should be given to a kṣatriya, O foremost twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
puṇyopayogi tadvaiśye śūdre śilpopajīvinam ..
yasyopayogi yaddravyaṃ deyaṃ tasyaiva tadbhavet .. 13 ..
meaning:
पुण्योपयोगि तद्वैश्ये शूद्रे शिल्पोपजीविनम् ..
यस्योपयोगि यद्द्रव्यं देयं तस्यैव तद्भवेत् .. 13 ..
text_mt: what is useful for merit to a vaiśya, and what serves his craft to a śūdra living by craftsmanship; / whatever article is useful to someone should be given to that very person.

sanskrit_iast:
yenayena ca bhāṇḍena yasya vṛttirudāhṛtā ..
tattu tasyaiva dātavyaṃ puṇyakāmena dhīmatā .. 14 ..
meaning:
येनयेन च भाण्डेन यस्य वृत्तिरुदाहृता ..
तत्तु तस्यैव दातव्यं पुण्यकामेन धीमता .. 14 ..
text_mt: Whatever vessel or tool is declared to be the livelihood of someone, / that should be given to him alone by a wise person desiring merit.

sanskrit_iast:
daṇḍaṃ kṛṣṇājinañcaiva tathā viprāḥ kamaṇḍalum ..
cīraṃ puṇyamavāpnoti dattvaitāṃ brahmacāriṇe .. 15 ..
meaning:
दण्डं कृष्णाजिनञ्चैव तथा विप्राः कमण्डलुम् ..
चीरं पुण्यमवाप्नोति दत्त्वैतां ब्रह्मचारिणे .. 15 ..
text_mt: Staff, black antelope skin, and water pot, O brahmins, / and bark garments—by giving these to a celibate student, one attains merit.

sanskrit_iast:
vastraṃ śayyāsanaṃ dhānyaṃ dravyaṃ veśma paricchadam ..
gṛhasthāya tu taddattaṃ jñeyaṃ bahuphalaṃ sadā .. 16 ..
meaning:
वस्त्रं शय्यासनं धान्यं द्रव्यं वेश्म परिच्छदम् ..
गृहस्थाय तु तद्दत्तं ज्ञेयं बहुफलं सदा .. 16 ..
text_mt: Cloth, a bed and seat, grain, goods, a house, and household furnishings— / what is given of these to a householder is to be known as always bringing great fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
nīvāravalkalaṃ śākaṃ phalamūlaṃ ca gorasam ..
vānaprasthāya taddattamanantaṃ parikīrtitam .. 17 ..
meaning:
नीवारवल्कलं शाकं फलमूलं च गोरसम् ..
वानप्रस्थाय तद्दत्तमनन्तं परिकीर्तितम् .. 17 ..
text_mt: Wild rice, bark garments, vegetables, fruit, roots, and cow's milk— / what is given of these to a forest-dweller is proclaimed to be endless.

sanskrit_iast:
bhikṣāpradānaṃ yataye pātradānaṃ tathā hitam ..
saubhāgyadravya tāmbūlaraktavastrādikaṃ striyaḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
भिक्षाप्रदानं यतये पात्रदानं तथा हितम् ..
सौभाग्यद्रव्य ताम्बूलरक्तवस्त्रादिकं स्त्रियः .. 18 ..
text_mt: The giving of alms is beneficial for an ascetic, as is the gift of a begging bowl; / articles of auspiciousness, betel, red garments, and the like for a woman.

sanskrit_iast:
strīṇāṃ pradānaṃ dātavyaṃ bhartṛhaste tu nānyathā ..
proktaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ hyetadguptaṃ bhartuḥ prayacchataḥ .. 19 ..
meaning:
स्त्रीणां प्रदानं दातव्यं भर्तृहस्ते तु नान्यथा ..
प्रोक्तं संग्रहणं ह्येतद्गुप्तं भर्तुः प्रयच्छतः .. 19 ..
text_mt: A gift for women is to be given into the hand of her husband, not otherwise; / for giving it secretly from the husband is declared to be adultery.

sanskrit_iast:
annaṃ pratiśrayaṃ cobhau pānthe dattaṃ mahāphalam ..
vivāhādikriyākāle tatkriyāsiddhikārakam .. 3.316.20 ..
meaning:
अन्नं प्रतिश्रयं चोभौ पान्थे दत्तं महाफलम् ..
विवाहादिक्रियाकाले तत्क्रियासिद्धिकारकम् .. 3.316.20 ..
text_mt: Food and shelter, both given to a traveller, bear great fruit. / At the time of rites such as marriage, it brings about the accomplishment of that rite.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ prayacchati dharmajñāḥ sośvamedhamavāpnuyāt..
āturebhyo dhanaṃ dattvā dānaṃ bahuphalaṃ labhet .. 21 ..
meaning:
यः प्रयच्छति धर्मज्ञाः सोश्वमेधमवाप्नुयात्..
आतुरेभ्यो धनं दत्त्वा दानं बहुफलं लभेत् .. 21 ..
text_mt: He who gives [them], O knowers of dharma, obtains an horse sacrifice. / Giving wealth to the sick, one obtains a gift of manifold fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
bāle krīḍanakaṃ dattvā miṣṭamannaṃ tathaiva ca ..
phalaṃ manoharaṃ vāpi agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet ..22 ..
meaning:
बाले क्रीडनकं दत्त्वा मिष्टमन्नं तथैव च ..
फलं मनोहरं वापि अग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् ..22 ..
text_mt: Giving a toy to a child, and sweet food as well, / or lovely fruit, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
miṣṭānnaṃ mānavo dattvā miṣṭānnāni tu kāṃkṣatām..
akṣayaṃ phalamāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati .. 23 ..
meaning:
मिष्टान्नं मानवो दत्त्वा मिष्टान्नानि तु कांक्षताम्..
अक्षयं फलमाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति .. 23 ..
text_mt: A man, giving sweet food to those who long for sweet foods, / attains inexhaustible fruit and goes to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīvihīne tathā dattvā bhojanaṃ dvijasattamāḥ ..
vastraṃ śubhaṃ vā dharmajñāḥ puṇyaṃ mahadupāśnute .. 24 ..
meaning:
श्रीविहीने तथा दत्त्वा भोजनं द्विजसत्तमाः ..
वस्त्रं शुभं वा धर्मज्ञाः पुण्यं महदुपाश्नुते .. 24 ..
text_mt: Likewise, giving a meal to one bereft of fortune, O best of the twice-born, / or beautiful clothing, O knowers of dharma, he partakes of great merit.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛpāsthānaparo viprā vidyutaḥ puruṣaḥ śriyā ..
tasyānukampā katarvyā satāṃ vartmani tiṣṭhataḥ .. 25 ..
meaning:
कृपास्थानपरो विप्रा विद्युतः पुरुषः श्रिया ..
तस्यानुकम्पा कतर्व्या सतां वर्त्मनि तिष्ठतः .. 25 ..
text_mt: A man who is fallen from fortune, O brahmins, is a supreme object of pity. / Compassion should be shown to him by one who walks the path of the good.

sanskrit_iast:
kārye samudyamaṃ kṛtvā pareṣāṃ samupasthite ..
akṣayaṃ phalamāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..26 ..
meaning:
कार्ये समुद्यमं कृत्वा परेषां समुपस्थिते ..
अक्षयं फलमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..26 ..
text_mt: Exerting oneself in an affair of others that has arisen, / one obtains inexhaustible fruit; here no doubt should be held.

sanskrit_iast:
yavasānāṃ pradānena dhenumatsu dvijātiṣu ..
lavaṇānāñca dharmajñā phalamakṣayamaśnute ..27..
meaning:
यवसानां प्रदानेन धेनुमत्सु द्विजातिषु ..
लवणानाञ्च धर्मज्ञा फलमक्षयमश्नुते ..27..
text_mt: By giving fodder and salt to twice-born men / possessing cattle, O knowers of dharma, one enjoys inexhaustible fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
prasaveṣu tadā dattaṃ vyasanānyubhaye tataḥ ..
taddānamakṣayaṃ proktaṃ puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ ..28..
meaning:
प्रसवेषु तदा दत्तं व्यसनान्युभये ततः ..
तद्दानमक्षयं प्रोक्तं पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ..28..
text_mt: Given during childbirths, and then in both kinds of distress, / that gift of a wise man is declared to be inexhaustible.

sanskrit_iast:
dattvā brāhmaṇaśārdūlā jalamātramathārthine ..
phalamakṣayamāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..29..
meaning:
दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणशार्दूला जलमात्रमथार्थिने ..
फलमक्षयमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..29..
text_mt: Giving merely water to a petitioner, O tigers among brahmins, / one obtains inexhaustible fruit; here no doubt should be held.

sanskrit_iast:
kleśaṃ vinā dattamathārthine tu dānaṃ hi loke phaladaṃ niruktam ..
abhyarthitenātha tato na kāryā vimānanā tvarthijanasya śaktyā..3.316.30..

haṃsa uvāca ..

अभ्यर्थितेनाथ ततो न कार्या विमानना त्वर्थिजनस्य शक्त्या..3.316.30..
3.317

हंस उवाच ..

परिपूर्वे तथा दानं यवानां द्विजसत्तमाः .. 2 ..
इडापूर्वेन्नवस्त्राणां धान्यानां चानुपूर्वके ..

उत्तरे त्वयने प्रोक्तं वस्त्रदानं फलप्रदम् ..
स्नानानुलेपनादीनां वसन्ते द्विजपुङ्गवाः..4..
पानकानां तथा ग्रीष्मे छत्राणां तदनन्तरे ..
शरद्यन्नस्य धर्मज्ञा वस्त्राणामपि हैमने..5..
वह्निदानं नरः कृत्वा सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ..
शिशिरे सततं वह्निं तर्पयित्वा तथा तिलैः ..6 ..
text_mt:
A gift given without distress to a supplicant is indeed declared fruitful in the world; / therefore, when asked, one should not dishonour a supplicant, according to one's capacity.
The ṛṣis said: / What gift is proclaimed as bearing great fruit at what time— / tell us that in truth, for you are called all-knowing.
Haṃsa said: / In a Saṃvatsara, the gift of sesame yields great fruit; / in a Parivatsara, likewise, the gift of barley, O best of the twice-born;
in an Iḍāvatsara, of food and garments, and in an Anuvatsara, of grains; / in an Udāvatsara, the gift of silver yields great fruit.
During the northern course [of the sun], the gift of clothing is declared to bestow fruit; / in the spring, O bulls among the twice-born, [the gift] of bathing, unguents, and the like;
likewise, in the summer, of drinks, and immediately after, of umbrellas; / in autumn, O knowers of dharma, of food, and in winter, of garments.
A man, giving fire towards the rising of the sun / and continually gratifying fire with sesame seeds in the cool season,

jalakumbhoparikṛtānakṣayaṃ phalamaśnute ..8..
madhyāhne prāvṛṣi snātaḥ satataṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
tilapradānānmāghe tu prāpyalokaṃ sa gacchati .. 9..
priyaṅguṃ phālgune dattvā priyo bhavati bhūtale ..

apūpānāṃ pradānena vaiśākhe svargamaśnute ..
chatradānaṃ tathā jyeṣṭhe sarvānkāmānupāśnute ..
dattvā copānahau svargañcāṣāḍhe dhruvamaśnute ..11..
śrāvaṇe vastradānasya kīrtitaṃ sumahatphalam ..
proṣṭhapāde tathā māsi pradānātphāṇitasya ca .. 12 ..
āśvine ghṛtadānena rūpavānabhi jāyate ..
kārtike dīpadānena sarvatraujasyamaśnuyāt .. 13 ..
meaning:
कुल्माषं सघृतं दत्त्वा यथाशक्त्या द्विजातिषु ..
कायाग्निदीप्तिं प्राकाश्यं शत्रुनाशञ्च विन्दति ..7..
सक्तून्सिताखण्डयुतांस्त्रपुसोर्वारुकान्वितान् ..
जलकुम्भोपरिकृतानक्षयं फलमश्नुते ..8..
मध्याह्ने प्रावृषि स्नातः सततं द्विजपुङ्गवाः ..
तिलप्रदानान्माघे तु प्राप्यलोकं स गच्छति .. 9..
प्रियङ्गुं फाल्गुने दत्त्वा प्रियो भवति भूतले ..
चैत्रे चित्राणि वस्त्राणि सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते..3.317.10..
अपूपानां प्रदानेन वैशाखे स्वर्गमश्नुते ..
छत्रदानं तथा ज्येष्ठे सर्वान्कामानुपाश्नुते ..
दत्त्वा चोपानहौ स्वर्गञ्चाषाढे ध्रुवमश्नुते ..11..
श्रावणे वस्त्रदानस्य कीर्तितं सुमहत्फलम् ..

and giving gruel with clarified butter according to his capacity to twice-born men, / gains brightness of the bodily fire, radiance, and the destruction of enemies.
Roasted grain flour mixed with pieces of white sugar, accompanied by cucumbers and gourds, / placed upon a water pot—he enjoys inexhaustible fruit.
Having bathed at midday continually during the rainy season, O bulls among the twice-born, / or by giving sesame seeds in Māgha, he goes having reached [that] world.
Giving panic seed in Phālguna, he becomes beloved on the surface of the earth; / [giving] multicoloured clothes in Caitra, he enjoys great good fortune.
By giving sweet cakes in Vaiśākha, he enjoys heaven; / likewise, by giving an umbrella in Jyeṣṭha, he obtains all desires; / and giving shoes in Āṣāḍha, he surely enjoys heaven.
A very great fruit is celebrated for the gift of clothing in Śrāvaṇa; / likewise, from the gift of treacle in the month of Proṣṭhapada;
by giving clarified butter in Āśvina, he is born handsome; / by giving a lamp in Kārtika, he would attain vigour everywhere.

Giving salt in Mārgaśīrṣa, he enjoys good fortune; / in Pauṣa, by the gift of gold, [he attains] supreme nourishment likewise.
The gift of flowers in the bright fortnight is traditionally held to produce prosperity; / and the gift of fruits in the dark fortnight bears great fruit.
Giving on Sunday a cake provided with salt, clarified butter, and molasses, / along with gold, a man is not overcome by diseases.
Giving the same kind on Monday, he would obtain good fortune; / giving firewood on Tuesday, he would obtain the destruction of enemies.
The gift of toys to children is praised on Wednesday; / on Thursday, by the gift of clothing, he fully enjoys supreme nourishment.
He attains pleasure everywhere by giving an attractive woman on Friday; / giving an oil-bath on Saturday, he would obtain long life.

Thus ends the three hundred and seventeenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Rule of Giving at Auspicious Times', in the Haṃsagītā addressed to the sages, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara.
The sages said: / Tell us the observance called Nakṣatrasattra together with gifts, / O foremost of all upholders of dharma, whose clear vision is manifest.
Haṃsa said: / During Kṛttikā, O fortunate ones, having satisfied virtuous brahmins / with milk-rice and clarified butter, one attains unsurpassed worlds.
On Rohiṇī, cooked black-gram grains with food and clarified butter / should be given, with milk as after-drink, to a twice-born man, in order to become free from debt.
Having given a milch cow with her calf under the asterism ruled by Soma, / one goes to human worlds [and then to] an unsurpassed dwelling in heaven.
Having fasted and given kṛsara mixed with oil during Ārdrā, / a man crosses impassable places and mountains of razor blades.
Having given cakes during Punarvasu and likewise excellent food, / one is born famous, endowed with beauty, possessing abundant food, in a noble family.

Having given gold during Puṣya, whether wrought or unwrought, / he shines like the moon in worlds free from darkness.
And he who gives silver or a bull under Āśleṣā, / being freed from all fear, attains welfare as well.
Under Maghā, having given vessels measured by weight filled with sesame seeds, / a man rejoices here and in the hereafter, possessed of sons and cattle.
Having fasted at the time of Pūrva-phālgunī and given to brahmins / edible food mixed with treacle, he obtains good fortune.
Having given, according to rule, sixty-day rice mixed with clarified butter and milk / under Uttarā, he is honored in the heavenly world.
Whatever gift is given by men under Uttarā, / it becomes of great, extraordinary fruit; such is the certainty.
Having fasted and given an elephant-drawn chariot yoked with four [elephants] under Hasta, / a man crosses impassable places and mountains of razor blades.
Having given a bull and sacred fragrances under Citrā, / a man moves about in the world of the apsarases and sports in the Nandana forest.

Then having given wealth under Svātī, whatever is dearest to himself, / he attains auspicious worlds and great renown right here.
Under Viśākhā, having given a draft bull, a cow yielding milk, / and a cart equipped with a yoke-pole, filled with grain and covered with cloth,
he pleases the ancestors and the gods, and having attained it, he enjoys eternity; / he does not encounter impassable places, and goes to the heavenly world.
Having given as prescribed to the brahmins, he finds a desirable livelihood, / and he does not meet with afflictions such as hell; such is the certainty.
Having fasted and given a mantle with an inner garment under Anurādhā, / a man is honored in heaven for a hundred yugas.
Having given black greens with roots to brahmins under Jyeṣṭhā, / a mortal goes to desired prosperity and to a desired destination.
Having given roots and fruits with a composed mind to brahmins under Mūla, / he indeed pleases the ancestors and goes to a desired destination.

Haṃsa said: / Having reached the bright fifteenth day of the month of Caitra, / a man who fasts, having given a pair of colorful garments to a twice-born man,
and [feeding] brahmins, O brahmins, he will attain great good fortune. / On the full moon of Vaiśākha, however, [he should invite] five or seven brahmins
and have [them] recite with black sesame seeds mixed with honey, or with other [sesame seeds], / saying, "May the King of Dharma be pleased!" or whatever is in his heart.
He is freed that very instant from the sins committed throughout his life. / At that very time, likewise, [presenting] a black antelope-skin complete with hooves,
covered with sesame seeds and garments, and adorned with every [kind of] jewel— / and at the end of winter [such a gift] should be given, [or] the earth together with groves and forests.
He who places sesame seeds upon a black antelope-skin, along with gold, honey, and clarified butter, / and gives it to a brahmin, crosses over all wrongdoing.
Likewise, fasting in Jyeṣṭha when the hare-marked [moon] is full, / and giving shoes and a parasol, he becomes exceedingly happy.

a man who knows dharma obtains a wife endowed with beauty and wealth, / blessed with an excellent family, and attains unsurpassed prosperity.

On the twelfth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, a man who gives multi-colored garments / obtains imperishable reward and goes to the heavenly realm.
In the month of Vaiśākha on the twelfth lunar day, from the gift of gold, / and in the month of Jyeṣṭha from the gift of a parasol and shoes, O best of the twice-born,
[and] by offering a well-spread couch, he pleases the one who reclines on the serpent; / on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, he is exalted in Śvetadvīpa.
In Śrāvaṇa, by the gift of garments, he is exalted in the world of Viṣṇu. / A giver of a cow goes to Goloka in the month of Bhādrapada, O twice-born.

These gifts have thus been proclaimed by me, O chiefs among the twice-born; and having bestowed them at the proper time, / a man attains the desires cherished in his heart; therefore they extol the great offering.
3.320 / The sages said: / Meritorious sacrificial rites have been declared for those men who possess wealth, / as well as various kinds of gifts for those of middling livelihood.
Various kinds of gifts have also been stated for those of meager livelihood. / For those men who are destitute of wealth, declare the practice of dharma.
The Swan said: / The practice of fasting is their supreme cause of dharma; / likewise, for those endowed with wealth, it is praised as having great fruit.
A man who eats only in the evening and morning, not drinking water in between, / attains after six years the world desired by his mind.
And this, best among auspicious deeds, when performed continually becomes fortunate; / it grants any desired world, is meritorious, and yields great fruit even in human birth.
A man who undertakes a fast month after month, O foremost of the twice-born, / after dwelling for a very long time in that world, when he is born in human existence,

he then becomes long-lived, wealthy, and endowed with beauty. / Performing it fortnight by fortnight in the same way, he enjoys double the fruit.
A best of men who observes a three-night fast month after month, / after falling from the heavenly world, attains the status of a leader of a troop.
Having observed a three-night fast fortnight by fortnight, he becomes a king; / after a very long time, fallen from the heavenly world, he becomes exceedingly powerful.
A twice-born may undertake a three-night fast, but never a śūdra; / eating at every sixth mealtime is declared here to be his supreme austerity.
In the realm of whichever king a śūdra undertakes a three-night fast, / his kingdom suffers from disease, famine, and thieves.
A śūdra should perform austerity with an interval of one or two days, / according to his capacity, O best of the twice-born; through that he obtains his desires.
Beyond this, O foremost of the twice-born, hear the supreme fruit / of the classes who eat only once a day month after month.

text_mt:
He who, self-controlled, passes the month of Caitra eating only one meal [a day], / is born in a great family rich in gold, jewels, and pearls.
A best of the twice-born who passes Vaiśākha eating only one meal [a day]— / whether a man or a woman—attains supremacy among his kinsmen.
A man or woman who passes the month of Jyeṣṭhāmūla eating only one meal [a day] / is born with peerless, supreme sovereignty.
Remaining unwearied through Āṣāḍha eating only one meal [a day], / one is born with much grain, much wealth, and many sons.
He who, self-controlled, passes the month of Śrāvaṇa eating only one meal [a day], / increases his kinsmen and is endowed with coronation wherever he may be.
He who takes only one meal [a day] through the month of Proṣṭhapāda, / becomes rich in wealth and acquires thriving, peerless sovereignty.
Likewise, he who passes the month of Āśvayuja eating only one meal [a day] / is born intelligent, rich in vehicles, and with many sons.

text_mt:
A man who takes only one meal [a day] through the month of Kārtika / is born heroic, with many wives, and renowned.
He who passes the month of Mārgaśīrṣa eating only one meal [a day] / is born sharing in agriculture, with much wealth, and with much grain.
He who passes the month of Pauṣa with only one meal [a day], O leaders of brahmins, / is born fortunate, handsome to behold, and sharing in renown.
He who, self-controlled, passes the month of Māgha eating only one meal [a day] / is born sharing in agriculture, with much wealth, and possessing grain.
He who passes the month governed by Bhaga eating only one meal [a day] / attains greatness amidst his kinsmen in an auspicious, noble family.
He becomes beloved among women, and they become obedient to him. / And these [observances] are traditionally held to bestow the stated fruit when performed for twelve years.
He who takes only one meal continuously for an entire year, / that man obtains the fruit of an Atirātra sacrifice.

text_mt:
Likewise, eating on alternate days for an entire year, / O twice-born, he certainly obtains [the fruit of] the sacrifice named Bahusuvarṇa.
And a man eating on the third day for one year, / [the fruit] of the Vājapeya sacrifice is declared [for him], O best of the twice-born.
Eating only once on every fifth [day] for one year, / he rejoices in heaven for twelve padmas of years.
Likewise, eating only on every sixth [day] for a year, a restrained man / rejoices in heaven for eighteen padmas of years.
Eating a single meal on every seventh day for a year, / he rejoices in heaven for thirty-six padmas of years.
Eating on every eighth day for a year, always restrained, / he rejoices in heaven, in paradise, for fifty padmas of years.
He who eats on every tenth day for a year, / O foremost of brahmins, rejoices in heaven like a god for one aeon.

text_mt:
He who takes sacrificial food when the eleventh day arrives, / rejoices in heaven, in paradise, like a god for two hundred aeons.
He who consumes sacrificial food when the twelfth day arrives, / enjoys three aeons in paradise, endowed with divine happiness.
He who takes sacrificial food when the thirteenth day arrives, / his destiny is proclaimed to be four aeons in paradise.
He who takes sacrificial food when the fourteenth day arrives, / his destiny is proclaimed to be seven aeons in paradise.
A man of righteous mind who eats sacrificial food on the fifteenth [day] for a year, / undoubtedly dwells for [many] aeons in the heavenly realm.
He who eats likewise for one year after a fortnight plus a day, / rejoices in heaven like a god for a hundred aeons, O brahmins.
He who eats a single meal when the seventeenth day arrives, / rejoices in heaven, O brahmins, for five hundred aeons.

And a man who performs it, eating a single meal on the eighteenth day, / rejoices in paradise for a thousand aeons.
He who eats a single meal on the nineteenth day, / rejoices in paradise for a thousand and a half aeons.
And eating at one time when the twentieth day arrives, / dwelling in heaven, he is honoured by the gods for two thousand aeons.
He who makes a single meal on the twenty-first day, / his path leads to heaven for three thousand aeons.
When the twenty-second day has arrived, he who eats a single meal / attains heaven for four thousand aeons.
And on the twenty-third day, he who eats a single meal, / dwelling in heaven, rejoices for five thousand aeons.
On the twenty-fourth day, he who eats a single meal, / dwelling in heaven, rejoices for seven thousand aeons.

text_mt:
And on the twenty-fifth day, he who eats a single meal, / dwelling in heaven, rejoices for ten thousand aeons.
And he who eats a single meal on the twenty-sixth day, / that man remains [there] for twenty-four thousand aeons.
On the twenty-seventh day, he who eats a single meal, / dwelling in heaven, rejoices for [thirty] thousand aeons.
On the twenty-eighth day, he who eats a single meal / rejoices for forty thousand aeons.
On the twenty-ninth day, he who eats a single meal / goes to heaven for fifty thousand aeons.
And he who eats a single meal when the thirtieth day arrives, / dwelling in heaven, is honoured for a hundred thousand aeons.
As a rule, he who eats a single meal as each month passes / rejoices eternally like a god in heaven for a day of the Cosmic Person.
All vows indeed bring happiness for the ancestors for one year; / they are declared to bear fruit over a year; herein no doubt should be entertained.

text_mt:
The departure of a person into heavenly realms according to their actions has been spoken by me, O brahmins; / what more shall I tell beyond this? Say that to me, O foremost in asceticism!
The sages said: / Speak, O one of boundless wisdom, on the dharma of women beyond this; / we wish to hear that, for you are called omniscient.
Haṃsa said: / This was established as the primary dharma of a woman by kinsmen at marriage: / in the presence of fire, she should be a partner in dharma with her husband.
Good-natured, well-disposed, well-proportioned, lovely to behold, / singular in mind, pleasant-faced: she is a partner in dharma with her husband.
Ever looking at her husband's face as if at the face of a son, / she who is virtuous and restrained in conduct is a partner in dharma.
Having heard this auspicious duty to the husband that requires great exertion, / a woman who is supremely devoted to dharma observes vows equal to her husband's.
A virtuous woman constantly looks upon her husband like a god, / rendering service and attendance as if to a deity.

text_mt:
Well-disposed through submissiveness, faithful to vows, fully composed, / single-minded, and cheerful, she shares in the husband's dharma.
Even if addressed with harshness or looked at with a cruel eye, / the woman who has a serene face toward her husband is a devoted wife.
And she whose form neither the moon nor the sun beholds with their eye,
except her husband, that fair-hipped woman becomes a sharer in dharma.
Poor, diseased, wretched, or proclaimed to be afflicted by mental sorrow,
her husband she should protect as if he were her son; such a woman is a sharer in dharma.
The woman who is restrained, capable, and who has sons,
devoted to her husband, her husband being her very life, that woman is a sharer in dharma.
She who always renders obedience and service without despondency,
well-satisfied and cheerful of mind, that woman is a sharer in dharma.
Neither in desires, nor in enjoyments, nor in sovereignty, nor in pleasure
does she have longing as she has for her husband; that woman is a sharer in dharma.
Not desiring sensual pleasure, taking vows, constantly devoted to household service,
keeping her dwelling well swept and smeared with cow dung,

Constantly devoted to the ritual of the fire, always offering flowers and oblations,
having provided, together with her husband, for the deities, guests, and servants,
Consuming the remaining food according to rule and according to injunction,
always having satisfied her servants, she is joined with the dharma of women.
Pleasing the feet of her mother-in-law and father-in-law, endowed with virtues,
always devoted to her mother and father, that woman has asceticism as her wealth.

Brahmins, the weak, the helpless, the wretched, the blind, and the miserable—
the woman who sustains these with food is a sharer in the virtue of devotion to her husband.

She who constantly performs a vow difficult to observe, with a clear mind,
her mind on her husband, devoted to her husband, is a sharer in the virtue of devotion to her husband.

This is merit, this is asceticism, and this is eternal heaven,
when an auspicious woman, possessing a husband, holds her husband supreme.

For a husband is the god of women; a husband is their kinsman; a husband is their refuge.
There is no refuge equal to a husband, nor any deity like a husband.

A husband bestows heaven upon a woman when he is disposed toward her bed,
whatever is to be done or not to be done, or even if it causes loss of life.

fallen into misfortune, captive to an enemy, or afflicted by a brahmin's curse,

text_mt:
Having observed the duties of adversity, that must be done without hesitation.
For independence is proclaimed to be the supreme sin for women; therefore, a woman always / must remain ever free from independence, if she desires heaven for a long time hereafter.
Haṃsa said:
Remaining established in their respective dharmas by the castes is for a lord of the earth
always proclaimed to be the highest dharma, wherever a man may be.
Worship of the gods, brahmins, cows, virtuous women, and holy men,
and the suppression of the wicked, is the source of dharma for a king.
Impartiality in legal proceedings and personal investigation—
one should know this as the supreme dharma of kings, as well as viewing through spies.
Protecting his own realm is dharma, as is subduing enemy kingdoms,
performing sacrifices and giving gifts, and not fleeing from battle.
Hunting, dice, and drinking are condemned for kings,
as are harshness of speech and punishment, and likewise corrupting wealth.
