मङ्गलाचारयुक्तानां सिध्यन्ते देवशक्तयः .. 12 ..
text_mt:
Peace, war, marching, and encamping,
and taking recourse to dual policy and alliance are declared.
Knowing the shifting time in determining the sixfold foreign policy,
O bull-like twice-borns, there should always be effort in conquering the senses by the king.
Then the conquest of servants should be made, and then the conquest of everything.
Desire, anger, pride, greed, arrogance, and likewise joy—
These six internal enemies must be conquered by a king.
Then the enemies belonging to one's own family and those that are natural or artificial are to be conquered.
He should be diligent in the acquisition of land, allies, and gold;
and the cultivation of dharma, wealth, and pleasure must always be pursued by a ruler of the earth.
The sovereign, the minister, the people, the fortress, the treasury, the army, and the ally—
these seven constituents in a kingdom must be protected with effort by the king.
He should likewise be endowed with the powers of fate, counsel, lordship, and energy;
for those who possess auspicious conduct, the powers of the gods succeed.

sanskrit_iast:

rājā sahāyasampannaḥ paśavyañjāṅgalaṃ śivam..14..
vaiśyaśūdrajanaprāyamarogaṃ deśamāvaseta..
tatra durgāṇi kurvīta svadurgañca viśeṣavat .. 15 ..
dhanvadurgammahīdurgaṃ giridurgantathaiva ca ..
adurgaṃ vṛkṣadurgañca naradurgantathaiva ca .. 16 ..
eṣāmanyatame durge dhanadhānyasamāyute ..
hastyaśvarathasampanne maṇibhīrūpaśobhite .. 17 ..
pattyāḍhye yodhabahule yuddhopakaraṇairyute ..
susañcite dhanāḍhye ca bahupeye bahūdake .. 18 ..
hastyaśvanaragovaidyasāṃvatsarayute śubhe ..
ghṛtatailauṣadhiyute sarvopakaraṇaistathā .. 19 ..

pāpataskaradurvṛttakruddhalubdhādivarjite..3.323.20..
meaning:
चतुरङ्गबलं कुर्यात्सुभृतञ्च तथा नृपः ..

महच्चावरणं कार्यन्नित्यमेव समृद्धये ..

वैश्यशूद्रजनप्रायमरोगं देशमावसेत..

धन्वदुर्गम्महीदुर्गं गिरिदुर्गन्तथैव च ..
अदुर्गं वृक्षदुर्गञ्च नरदुर्गन्तथैव च .. 16 ..
एषामन्यतमे दुर्गे धनधान्यसमायुते ..
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्ने मणिभीरूपशोभिते .. 17 ..
पत्त्याढ्ये योधबहुले युद्धोपकरणैर्युते ..
सुसञ्चिते धनाढ्ये च बहुपेये बहूदके .. 18 ..
हस्त्यश्वनरगोवैद्यसांवत्सरयुते शुभे ..

text_mt:
The king should establish a fourfold army and keep it well-maintained;
by deed, mind, and speech, he should always gladden the world.
A great enclosure should constantly be made for prosperity.
A king, well-supplied with allies, [should dwell in] an auspicious wilderness suitable for cattle,
He should inhabit a disease-free country consisting mostly of vaiśyas and śūdras.
There he should build fortresses, and especially his own fortress:
A desert fortress, an earthen fortress, and likewise a hill fortress,
a water fortress, a forest fortress, and likewise a human fortress.
In any one of these fortresses, supplied with wealth and grain,
endowed with elephants, horses, and chariots, adorned with gems and fearlessness,
Abundant in infantry, full of warriors, equipped with implements of war,
well-provisioned, rich in wealth, with much to drink and plenty of water,
Endowed with physicians for elephants, horses, men, and cows, and with astrologers, auspicious,
provided with ghee, oil, and medicinal herbs, and likewise with all implements,
Supplied with ramparts, moats, earthworks, gatehouses, and watchtowers,
free from sinners, thieves, the ill-behaved, the angry, the greedy, and the like,

there the king should dwell in person, equipped with all provisions.
Of noble family, endowed with beauty, of the same caste,
well-behaved, modest, and fond of dharma—such a wife the ruler of men should take.
Together with her, the king should constantly cause the domestic priest
to perform the rite of the five great sacrifices prescribed for the householder stage of life.
He should sacrifice with various sacrifices, and likewise worship the deities;
he should cause temples, wells, and tanks to be constructed,

text_mt:
Wonderful gardens, and dwellings for cows and brahmins.
Punishing the wicked, honoring the virtuous, and acquiring wealth through dharma,

are the great sacrifices of kings, destroying all impurities.

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

एकैकं कारयेत्कर्म मासिमासि महीपतिः .. 43 ..

विदेशपण्याच्च तथा देयम्पञ्चशतं समम् .. 44 ..

text_mt:
There is no toll on a fraction of a kārṣāpaṇa, nor on an artisan’s trade, nor on an infant, nor on a messenger, / nor on what is obtained by alms, on what remains of property plundered, nor on a Vedic scholar, an ascetic, or a sacrifice.
3.324
The sages said:
The duty of a king has been proclaimed by you as the investigation of legal disputes; / expound that to us, for you are declared to be all-knowing.
Haṃsa said:
In the past, in the Kṛta age, the subject-folk were bound by dharma; / then, in the Tretā age, their dharma went to ruin.
When dharma was destroyed, legal procedure was set in motion among men, / and the king, holding the rod of punishment, was made the overseer of legal disputes.
Families, guilds, corporations, and the appointed royal officer: / these are overseers of legal disputes, each higher [in authority] than the preceding.
The king should investigate legal disputes together with learned brahmins, / in accordance with the treatises on dharma, free from desire and aversion.
Born of good family, steadfast in dharma, endowed with purity, possessed of learning, / who are impartial toward enemy and friend—such should the king make court assessors.

text_mt:
If unable to examine legal disputes due to pressing business, the king / should appoint a brahmin who knows all dharma together with the court assessors.
Or else a kṣatriya or a vaiśya, but never a śūdra. / In whichever king’s realm a śūdra is an adjudicator of dharma,
his realm perishes from famine, disease, and thieves. / The maker of false witnesses [shall receive] twice the fine of the dispute;
and likewise twice [the fine for] court assessors settled in passion and hatred. / Whatever wealth has been obtained by the king through unjust legal procedure,
thirty times that must be given to brahmins or cast into water. / Oppressed by others through a path departing from traditional law and custom,
if he reports to the king, that is indeed an occasion of legal dispute. / The lord of the earth should likewise summon the defendant.
One who does not come is defeated and must be severely punished by the king; / [except when hindered] in crossing a river, in a forest, in a bad country, in calamities, and the like,

document, witnesses, possession, and the fourth is a Vedic procedure [by ordeal]. / The essence is declared to be the firm foundation of legal disputes.

likewise those carried out by women, at night, in an inner room, or by many enemies; / but those executed by the diseased, the frightened, the distressed, children, and pupils
one should know as not executed, and likewise those carried out by slaves. / But by the word of a teacher for a pupil, and by the word of a father for a son,
and by the word of a master for a slave, a legal transaction is established. / Transactions executed by women are said to be invalid in the absence of an emergency,
especially regarding money and land, or the sale of an heir's property; / yet these very acts are valid if the husband approves.
In the absence of a husband, in the presence of the king, or of a father and son, [a decision is made]. / A child is up to sixteen years of age, and a youth is designated as paugaṇḍa.
Thereafter, he is competent in legal affairs and independent, except with respect to his father; / for one who has not attained legal majority, independence belongs to the mother.
The wise state that transactions executed by dependent persons are invalid. / Nothing whatsoever should be spoken in a legal dispute by one who is not appointed.

text_mt:
The king should fine one who speaks without being appointed a kṛṣṇala of gold; / whether appointed or not appointed, one who knows the law should utter the relevant statement.
A scribe who writes false statements must be stripped of all his property, / as also one who corrupts the scribe, the court assessors, or the witnesses.
In summoning one who was not summoned, and in releasing one who was summoned, / or if one, thinking 'I am not defeated,' should speak, [the king should declare] him defeated.
The king should punish those [guilty] brahmins with a double fine. / Either the assembly should not be entered, or fair speech must be spoken;
speaking nothing, or speaking falsely, a man becomes sinful. / One-fourth of the sin of adharma falls upon the perpetrator, one-fourth upon the witness,
one-fourth falls upon all the assessors, and one-fourth reaches the king. / But the king becomes guiltless where one deserving censure is censured;
the sin goes to the perpetrator, and the assessors are released. / Setting aside trickery, the king should conduct legal proceedings according to the truth.

Even a fact, if not presented, is lost in a lawsuit. / If the dispute involves a stake, the man must be made to pay that sum: / the fine, his own stake, and to the creditor his money.
That is not an assembly where there are no elders; they are not elders who do not speak dharma; / that is not dharma where there is no truth; that is not truth which is tainted with deceit.
3.325 / Haṃsa said: / Where possession is observed, but title is nowhere seen, / title is the determining factor there, not possession.
Through a pure title, possession becomes authoritative; / possession with an impure title never attains authoritativeness.
Only the claimant being accused should establish the basis of the property; / but possession alone is pure in the case of [property] obtained successively from ancestors.
A bailment […], what is clearly begged for, / and what is enjoyed out of sight, does not lapse by possession.
For land being enjoyed by another while [the owner] looks on and says nothing, the loss of title occurs after twenty years; / for movable property, after ten years.

What has been enjoyed according to rule by three generations of men, / the fourth generation should obtain in that case even in the absence of a written document.

text_mt:
Those who are forgers must be severely punished by the lord of the earth who desires [to attain] the gods. / They are thorns to all people, O brahmins; the king should indeed be their restrainer.
Haṃsa said: / A witness has been seen in the treatise by the wise as elevenfold: / made, of five kinds there; unmade is said to be of six kinds.
Written, reminded, one who happened by, / secret, and a secondary witness: [these] are considered the fivefold made [witness].
The village, the chief judge, and the king of litigants; / he who is an insider in transactions, always sent by the plaintiff;
the family in family disputes: [these] are considered the sixfold unmade. / When two [parties] dispute over property and there are witnesses on both sides,
whose prima facie claim it is, his should be the witnesses. / In whatever [matter] the basis of the prima facie claim would be held on account of the object,
in that dispute the witnesses of the defendant must be questioned. / One should not approach a witness cited by another [party];

nor should he cause division between them; he who does so is defeated. / If a witness who has been specified should die or go to another region,
that is proof for both; for when there is proof, intermediate procedure [applies]. / One who, not indicated as a witness, comes and speaks on his own accord,

nor a Vedic scholar, nor an ascetic, nor one detached from all, / nor one who is diseased, nor one under reproach, nor a robber, nor an evildoer,
nor an old man, nor a child, nor a single person, nor a blind man, nor one with impaired senses, / nor one in distress, nor an intoxicated man, nor an insane man, nor one afflicted by hunger and thirst,
nor one afflicted by fatigue, nor one afflicted by lust, nor an angry man, nor a thief, / nor a relative of the two parties, nor those who travel for a year,
nor those whose faults are seen, nor those afflicted by disease, nor the corrupted. / Women should testify for women, like twice-born for twice-born,

and śūdras for worthy śūdras, mortals of mortal birth [for mortals]. / But anyone who is a direct observer may bear witness for disputants
inside a house, in a forest, or at the loss of life. / Even women must be employed if available, or a child or an elder,
or a disciple, or a kinsman, or a slave, or a hired servant. / But when children, elders, and sick persons speak falsely in testimony,
one should know their speech as excessive, as also that of arrogant minds. / Householders who have sons, indigenous, śūdras, born of vaiśya and kṣatriya [lineage],
are eligible for testimony when spoken to, in cases of forgery or financial calamity. / Trustworthy persons among all castes should be made witnesses in legal cases.
In a multiplicity [of witnesses], one should accept the master of the fee; / in equality, the one superior in virtue; and in virtue, the foremost twice-born.
Witness testimony succeeds from seeing with one's own eyes and from hearing. / There, speaking the truth, a witness does not fall away from dharma and wealth.

A witness declaring otherwise than what was seen and heard goes to hell. / Even if bound, when questioned he should speak just as seen and just as heard.
A single greedy man cannot be a witness, nor many [such] anywhere. / What they speak by their very nature, that is acceptable in a legal proceeding.
Never should the chief judge appoint witnesses who have arrived in the presence of the plaintiff and defendant / [without] comforting them by this rule:
'Whatever you know concerning these two in this matter or in their action, / speak all that with truth, for your status here is that of a witness.'
Then, in the presence of deities and brahmins, O twice-born, / facing north or facing east, in the morning, clean himself, he should question the clean [witnesses]:
He should ask a brahmin, saying 'Speak'; a kṣatriya, saying 'Speak the truth'; / a vaiśya, by cows, seeds, and gold; and a śūdra, by all sins.

स्थावरेषु तु दिव्यानि वर्जनीयानि पार्थिवैः ..
लिखितेन तथा भुक्त्या तेषां भवति साधनम् .. 5 ..
text_mt:
Evildoers indeed think: "No one sees us." / Yet the gods see them, and so does one's own inner person. / The sun and moon, fire and wind, heaven, earth, water, the heart and Yama, / day and night, both twilights, and Dharma know the conduct of a mortal.
The Haṃsa said: / The human determination [of disputes] has been declared; hereafter I shall declare divine ordeal, / when two people are mutually disputing in matters that have no witnesses.
In treason against the king, false accusations, and likewise in violent crimes, / in a lawsuit one should obtain the truth in its reality even by means of an oath.
Oaths have been made by the great sages and by the gods for the sake of matters [of law]; / Vasiṣṭha gave an oath when King Javana entered into a covenant.
A wise man should not take a false oath, even in a very small matter; / for one who takes a futile oath perishes in the next world and in this one.
In the case of immoveable property, ordeals are to be avoided by kings; / their proof is established by written documents as well as by possession.

śastramādāya vaktavyaṃ kṣattriyeṇa tathaiva ca .. 11 ..
dhenuṃ saṃspṛśatā satyaṃ vācyaṃ vaiśyena vai dvijāḥ ..

meaning:
कोशं धटं विषं चाग्निमुदकं तप्तमाषकम् ..
फालं च तण्डुलं चैव दिव्यान्यष्टौ विदुर्बुधाः .. 6 ..
कोशवर्जन्तु दिव्यानि सशिरस्कानि दापयेत् ..
अशिरस्कः स्मृतः कोशः कालान्तरविभावनात .. 7 ..
अशिरस्कानि दिव्यानि राज्ञा कण्टकशोधनैः ..
राज्ञा सर्वाणि देयानि स्वयं च परिमार्गिणा .. .. 8 ..
लोभान्मोहाद्भयाद्वापि भिद्यन्ते साक्षिणः परैः ..
अज्ञानाद्बालभावाच्च भेदे धर्मो व्यवस्थितः .. 9 ..
सर्वद्रव्येषु कनकं मूल्यं तु परिकल्पयेत् ..
माषकेण सुवर्णस्य ..........काल्यमसुखे द्विजम् .. 3.328.10 ..
सत्यं वदामीति शपेन्नान्यत्किञ्चन पार्थिव ..
शस्त्रमादाय वक्तव्यं क्षत्त्रियेण तथैव च .. 11 ..
धेनुं संस्पृशता सत्यं वाच्यं वैश्येन वै द्विजाः ..
शूद्रः कुर्वीत शपथं तथा सर्वैस्तु पातकैः .. 12 ..
text_mt:
Sacred water, the balance, poison, fire, water, the heated bean-weight, / the ploughshare, and sacred grain—the wise know these as the eight ordeals.
Except for the sacred water, one should administer ordeals accompanied by a penalty; / the sacred water is taught as being free from penalty, due to its manifestation over a period of time.
Ordeals free from penalty are to be administered by the king when extirpating criminals; / they are all to be administered by the king himself when he investigates [a matter].
Witnesses are divided by opponents out of greed, delusion, or fear, / or out of ignorance or childishness; when there is divergence, dharma remains settled.
Among all commodities one should estimate the value in gold; / by a māṣaka of gold […] a twice-born in difficulty.
O king, he should swear: "I speak the truth," and nothing else; / likewise, [an oath] should be spoken by a kṣatriya after taking up a weapon.
The truth is to be spoken by a vaiśya while touching a cow, O twice-born; / a śūdra should take an oath through all grave sins.

sanskrit_iast:

yathā tathā mahīpālaḥ śṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama .. 16 ..

varṇināṃ na tathā phālaṃ taṇḍulaṃ mukharogiṇām .. 17 ..
śvāsakāsārditānāṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca no viṣam ..
taptamāṣakamarhanti sarve varṇā niratyayam .. 18 ..
na vyādhimarakākrānte deśe kośaṃ tu pātayet ..
mantrairasvaradivyāni sañcayantīha mānavāḥ ..19..
pratimantravidaḥ stambhanānāṃ vināśane ..
niyuñjīta narendropi nibhṛtāṃ dhanavatsalām .. 3.328.20 ..
meaning:
कृष्णलेन सुवर्णस्य तिलवृद्ध्या तु शापयेत् ..
शूद्रान्न शापयेद्राजा कदाचिदपि वै द्विजाः ..13 ..
विप्रवर्जं तथा कोशं वर्णिनां दापयेन्नृपः ..
सुवर्णमाषकादूर्ध्वमर्वागष्टभ्य एव च .. 14 ..
विप्रवर्जं तु विप्रोऽपि वर्णिनां पूरसंयुतम् ..
कोशस्थाने तु शपथं कारयेदविधारयन् .. 15 ..
अतः परं तु दिव्यानां कुर्यादन्यतमं नरः ..
यथा तथा महीपालः शृणुध्वं गदतो मम .. 16 ..
न शीते तु धटं देयमुष्णकाले हुताशनम् ..
वर्णिनां न तथा फालं तण्डुलं मुखरोगिणाम् .. 17 ..
श्वासकासार्दितानां च ब्राह्मणानां च नो विषम् ..
तप्तमाषकमर्हन्ति सर्वे वर्णा निरत्ययम् .. 18 ..
न व्याधिमरकाक्रान्ते देशे कोशं तु पातयेत् ..
मन्त्रैरस्वरदिव्यानि सञ्चयन्तीह मानवाः ..19..
प्रतिमन्त्रविदः स्तम्भनानां विनाशने ..
नियुञ्जीत नरेन्द्रोपि निभृतां धनवत्सलाम् .. 3.328.20 ..
text_mt:
One should administer an oath by a kṛṣṇala of gold, with an increase of a sesame grain; / the king, O twice-born, should never administer an oath to śūdras [by gold].
Except for the brahmin, the king should administer the ordeal of sacred water to members of the classes, / [in cases valued] above a golden māṣaka and up to eight [māṣakas].
Except for a brahmin, even a brahmin [judge], without hesitating, / should have an oath taken in place of sacred water for members of the classes, accompanied by the city [officials].
Beyond this, a man should perform one of the ordeals; / O ruler of the earth, listen as I speak how [it is done].
The balance is not to be administered in cold weather, nor fire in the hot season; / likewise, the ploughshare is not for members of the classes, nor sacred grain for those suffering from mouth disease.
Poison is not [to be given] to those afflicted with asthma and cough, nor to brahmins; / all classes are eligible for the heated bean-weight without transgression.
One should not administer sacred water in a country overwhelmed by disease and plague; / men here hinder divine ordeals by means of mantras.
A ruler of men should also employ those who know counter-mantras to destroy paralyzing spells— / [officials who are] discreet and fond of wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
divyānāṃ stambhakaṃ jñātvā pāpānnityaṃ mahīpatiḥ ..
vivāsayetsvakādrāṣṭrātte hi lokasya kaṇṭakāḥ .. 21 ..
teṣāmanveṣaṇe yatnaṃ rājā nityaṃ samācaret ..
te hi pāpasamācārāstaskarebhyopi taskarāḥ .. 22 ..
dṛgdṛṣṭidoṣātsvalpepi divyeṣu viniyojayet ..
mahatsvapi na cārtheṣu dharmajñāndharmavatsalān .. 23 ..

svalpe vāpyatha vāsvalpe śapathe tānniyojayet .. 24 ..
na mithyāvacanaṃ yeṣāṃ janmaprabhṛti vidyate ..
śraddadhyātpārthivasteṣāṃ vacane dharmadarśinām ..25 ..
atyantopahatāḥ pāpā nāstikā bhinnasetavaḥ ..
divyānyarhaṃti sarvāṇi svalpadoṣā api dvijāḥ .. 26 ..
ādau bhūmiṃ parīkṣeta dhaṭasyārthe vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
indrasthāne sabhāyāṃ vā digbhāge pūrvadakṣiṇe .. 27 ..
meaning:
दिव्यानां स्तम्भकं ज्ञात्वा पापान्नित्यं महीपतिः ..
विवासयेत्स्वकाद्राष्ट्रात्ते हि लोकस्य कण्टकाः .. 21 ..
तेषामन्वेषणे यत्नं राजा नित्यं समाचरेत् ..
ते हि पापसमाचारास्तस्करेभ्योपि तस्कराः .. 22 ..
दृग्दृष्टिदोषात्स्वल्पेपि दिव्येषु विनियोजयेत् ..
महत्स्वपि न चार्थेषु धर्मज्ञान्धर्मवत्सलान् .. 23 ..
ज्ञात्वा धर्मिष्ठतां राजा पुरुषस्स विचक्षणः ..
स्वल्पे वाप्यथ वास्वल्पे शपथे तान्नियोजयेत् .. 24 ..
न मिथ्यावचनं येषां जन्मप्रभृति विद्यते ..
श्रद्दध्यात्पार्थिवस्तेषां वचने धर्मदर्शिनाम् ..25 ..
अत्यन्तोपहताः पापा नास्तिका भिन्नसेतवः ..
दिव्यान्यर्हंति सर्वाणि स्वल्पदोषा अपि द्विजाः .. 26 ..
आदौ भूमिं परीक्षेत धटस्यार्थे विचक्षणः ..
इन्द्रस्थाने सभायां वा दिग्भागे पूर्वदक्षिणे .. 27 ..
text_mt:
Knowing someone to be a delayer of ordeals, the lord of the earth should always banish / the wicked from his own realm, for they are thorns to the people.
The king should always make an effort in searching for them; / for those who behave wickedly are thieves greater than thieves.
He may assign [people] to ordeals even for a small [matter] due to an eye or vision defect; / but he should not assign those who know dharma and are fond of dharma, even in great matters.
Knowing someone to be most righteous, that discerning king / should assign them to an oath, whether the matter is small or not small.
Those in whom no false word has been found since birth— / the king should place faith in the word of those who perceive dharma.
Those who are utterly corrupted, wicked, atheists, and breakers of moral bounds, / even if their offense is small, O twice-born, are fit for all ordeals.
First, the discerning [king] should inspect the ground for the purpose of the balance, / at the place of Indra or in the court of justice, or in the south-eastern direction.

sanskrit_iast:
dhaṭaṃ niveśayettatra susamāyāṃ tathā bhuvi ..

धटं निवेशयेत्तत्र सुसमायां तथा भुवि ..
यज्ञियस्य तु वृक्षस्य कर्तव्यं मण्डपद्वयम् .. 28 ..

द्वौ हस्तौ निखनेत्काष्ठं दृश्यं स्याद्धस्तपञ्चकम् .. 29 ..
अन्तरञ्च तयोः कार्यं तथा हस्तचतुष्टयम् ..
मण्डपोपरि काष्ठं च दृढं कुर्याद्विचक्षणः .. 3.328.30 ..

खदिरार्जुनवृक्षाणां शिंशिपासालजं तथा .. 31 ..
तुलाकाष्ठं तु कर्तव्यं तथा वै शिक्यकद्वयम् ..
प्राङ्मुखो निश्चलः कार्यः शुचौ देशे धटस्तथा .. 32 ..
वणिक्सुवर्णकारौ च कुलालः कांस्यकारकः ..
तुलाधरे धटः कार्यो रिपौ मित्रे तथा समः .. 33 ..
text_mt:
There he should set up the balance on very level ground; / two pavilions are to be made of a sacrificial tree.
The measure of the pavilion is declared to be seven cubits; / one should dig in two cubits of the wooden post, and five cubits should be visible.
The space between the two should be made four cubits; / and above the pavilion the discerning [builder] should make the crossbeam strong.
One should make the beam of the balance four cubits long, free from defects, and stable, / made of khadira, arjuna, śiṃśipā, or sāla trees.
The beam of the balance is to be made thus, and likewise two suspension baskets; / the balance is to be made facing east, motionless, in a pure place.
The balance-holder should be a merchant, goldsmith, potter, or coppersmith; / the balance must be made impartial towards enemy and friend.

sanskrit_iast:

श्रावयेत्प्राड्विवाकोपि तुलाधारं विचक्षणः ..
ब्रह्मघ्नो ये स्मृता लोका ये च स्त्रीबालघातिनाम् .. 34 ..
text_mt: The discerning chief judge should recite to the balance-holder: / "The worlds that are taught for a brahmin-slayer, and those of the slayers of women and children—

एकस्मिम्̐स्तोलयेच्छिक्ये स्नातं सूपोषितं नरम् .. 35 ..

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:

मूर्ध्नि पत्रं ततस्तस्य न्यस्तपत्रं निवेशयेत् .. 37 ..
text_mt: Having weighed him first, he should then take him down from it; / then he should place upon his head a document written with a text.

ब्रह्मणस्त्वं सुता देवि तुलानाम्नीति कथ्यसे .. 38 ..
text_mt: And this mantra was uttered of old by the Self-born himself: / "O goddess, you are the daughter of Brahmā, and you are called by the name Tulā (Balance).

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
तुकारो गौरवो नित्यं लकारो लघुनि स्मृतः ..
गुरुलाघवसंयोगात्तुला तेन निगद्यसे .. 39 ..
text_mt: The syllable 'tu' is always remembered for heaviness (gaurava), and the syllable 'la' for lightness (laghu); / because of the union of heaviness and lightness, therefore you are called Tulā.

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:

भूय आरोपयेत्तं तु नरं तस्यां सपत्रकम् .. 3.328.40 ..

हीयमाने न शुद्धः स्यादिति धर्मविदो विदुः .. 41 ..

meaning:
शिक्यच्छेदे तुलाभङ्गे पुनरारोपयेन्नरम् ..
तथा निःसंशयं ज्ञानं भवतीति विनिश्चयः .. 42 ..

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
अग्नेर्विधिं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुध्वं गदतो मम ..
सप्तमण्डलकान्कुर्याद्देवब्राह्मणसन्निधौ .. 43 ..
text_mt: I shall explain the rite of fire; listen as I speak! / He should make seven small circles in the presence of the gods and brahmins.

sanskrit_iast:
pratyakṣaṃ kārayeddivyaṃ rājño vādhikṛtasya vā ..
brāhmaṇānāṃ śrutavatāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ tathaiva ca .. 44 ..
meaning:
प्रत्यक्षं कारयेद्दिव्यं राज्ञो वाधिकृतस्य वा ..
ब्राह्मणानां श्रुतवतां प्रकृतीनां तथैव च .. 44 ..
text_mt: He should cause the ordeal to take place before the eyes of the king or his appointed officer, / of learned brahmins, and likewise of the subjects.

sanskrit_iast:
paścime maṇḍale tiṣṭhetprāṅmukhaḥ prāñjaliḥ śuciḥ ..
caraturasre yathā asminkṛtvā caiva samau karau .. 45 ..
meaning:
पश्चिमे मण्डले तिष्ठेत्प्राङ्मुखः प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः ..
चरतुरस्रे यथा अस्मिन्कृत्वा चैव समौ करौ .. 45 ..
text_mt: In the western circle, pure, facing east, with joined hands, / having made both hands flat in this square [manner],

sanskrit_iast:
lakṣayeyuḥ kṣatādīni hastayostasya kāriṇaḥ ..
saptāśvatthasya patrāṇi badhnīyuḥ karayostataḥ .. 46 ..
meaning:
लक्षयेयुः क्षतादीनि हस्तयोस्तस्य कारिणः ..
सप्ताश्वत्थस्य पत्राणि बध्नीयुः करयोस्ततः .. 46 ..
text_mt: the officiants should examine the wounds and so forth on the hands of that person; / then they should bind seven leaves of the holy fig tree onto his hands,

sanskrit_iast:
navena sitasūtreṇa kārpāsena dvijottamāḥ ..
tatastu susamaṃ kṛtvā aṅgulaṃ tvekamāyasam ..47..
meaning:
नवेन सितसूत्रेण कार्पासेन द्विजोत्तमाः ..
ततस्तु सुसमं कृत्वा अङ्गुलं त्वेकमायसम् ..47..
text_mt: with a new, white cotton thread, O best of the twice-born. / Then, having made completely even an iron ball of one aṅgula,

sanskrit_iast:
piṇḍaṃ hutāśasantaptaṃ pañcāśatpalikaṃ dṛḍham ..
ādau pūjāṃ hutāśasya kārayedvasudhādhipaḥ ..48..
meaning:
पिण्डं हुताशसन्तप्तं पञ्चाशत्पलिकं दृढम् ..
आदौ पूजां हुताशस्य कारयेद्वसुधाधिपः ..48..
text_mt: weighing fifty palas, solid, heated in fire— / first the lord of the earth should cause worship of the fire to be performed

sanskrit_iast:
raktacandanadhūmābhyāṃ raktapuṣpaistathaiva ca ..
abhiśastasya mantraṃ ca badhnīyāttasya mūrdhani .. 49 ..
meaning:
रक्तचन्दनधूमाभ्यां रक्तपुष्पैस्तथैव च ..
अभिशस्तस्य मन्त्रं च बध्नीयात्तस्य मूर्धनि .. 49 ..
text_mt: with red sandalwood and incense, and likewise with red flowers; / and he should bind the mantra upon the head of the accused,

sanskrit_iast:
mantreṇānena saṃyuktaṃ brāhmaṇābhihitena tu ..
tvamagne vedāścatvārastvaṃ ca yajñeṣu hūyase..3.328.50..
meaning:
मन्त्रेणानेन संयुक्तं ब्राह्मणाभिहितेन तु ..
त्वमग्ने वेदाश्चत्वारस्त्वं च यज्ञेषु हूयसे..3.328.50..
text_mt: equipped with this mantra spoken by a brahmin: / "O Fire, you are the four Vedas, and you are offered in sacrifices;

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ mukhaṃ sarvadevānāṃ tvaṃ mukhaṃ brahmavādinām..
jaṭharasthopi bhūtānāṃ tvaṃ ca vetsi śubhāśubham..
pāpeṣu darśayātmānamarciṣmānbhava pāvaka .. 51 ..
meaning:
त्वं मुखं सर्वदेवानां त्वं मुखं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्..
जठरस्थोपि भूतानां त्वं च वेत्सि शुभाशुभम्..
पापेषु दर्शयात्मानमर्चिष्मान्भव पावक .. 51 ..
text_mt: you are the mouth of all the gods, you are the mouth of the knowers of the Veda; / dwelling even in the belly of living beings, you know good and bad! / Show yourself against sins; be radiant, O Purifier!

sanskrit_iast:
atha vā śuddhabhāveṣu śīto bhava mahābala ..
tatobhiśastaḥ śanakairmaṇḍalāni parikramet .. 52 ..
meaning:
अथ वा शुद्धभावेषु शीतो भव महाबल ..
ततोभिशस्तः शनकैर्मण्डलानि परिक्रमेत् .. 52 ..
text_mt: Or, towards those of pure disposition, be cool, O mighty one!" / Then the accused should slowly pace through the circles.

sanskrit_iast:
parikramya śanairjahyāllohapiṇḍaṃ tathā kṣitau ..
vimuktahastaṃ taṃ paścātkārayedvrīhimarddanam .. 53 ..
meaning:
परिक्रम्य शनैर्जह्याल्लोहपिण्डं तथा क्षितौ ..
विमुक्तहस्तं तं पश्चात्कारयेद्व्रीहिमर्द्दनम् .. 53 ..
text_mt: Having paced through, he should likewise drop the iron ball slowly onto the ground; / once his hands are free, he should afterwards cause him to rub unhusked rice.

sanskrit_iast:
nirvikārau karau dṛṣṭvā śuddho bhavati dharmataḥ ..
bhayādvā pātayedyastu dagdho vā na vibhāvyate ..54..
meaning:
निर्विकारौ करौ दृष्ट्वा शुद्धो भवति धर्मतः ..
भयाद्वा पातयेद्यस्तु दग्धो वा न विभाव्यते ..54..
text_mt: Seeing both hands unblemished, he becomes pure according to dharma; / but if he drops it out of fear, or if it is not clearly discerned whether he is burned,

sanskrit_iast:
punastu cāharellohaṃ vidhireṣa prakīrtitaḥ ..
toyasyātha pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ sanātanam .. 55 ..
meaning:
पुनस्तु चाहरेल्लोहं विधिरेष प्रकीर्तितः ..
तोयस्याथ प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं धर्म्यं सनातनम् .. 55 ..
text_mt: he should take the iron again: such is the rule proclaimed. / Now I shall declare the righteous, eternal rule of water.

sanskrit_iast:
śaivālanakramatsyādyairvarjite sthāvare jale ..
dharmasthūṇā tatra kāryā puruṣaṃ dharmavatsalam .. 56 ..
meaning:
शैवालनक्रमत्स्याद्यैर्वर्जिते स्थावरे जले ..
धर्मस्थूणा तत्र कार्या पुरुषं धर्मवत्सलम् .. 56 ..
text_mt: In still water devoid of moss, crocodiles, fish, and the like, / a post of dharma is to be set up there. A man fond of dharma

sanskrit_iast:
nābhidaghnodakasthasya gṛhītvottaṃ samāviśet ..
madhyamenātha dhanuṣā madhyasthaḥ puruṣo'paraḥ .. 57..
meaning:
नाभिदघ्नोदकस्थस्य गृहीत्वोत्तं समाविशेत् ..
मध्यमेनाथ धनुषा मध्यस्थः पुरुषोऽपरः .. 57..
text_mt: should enter, grasping [the thigh of] one standing in water up to his navel. / Then another impartial man, with an average bow,

sanskrit_iast:
iṣumokṣaṃ tadā kuryāddeśe tṛṇavivarjite ..
śaramokṣe same kāle nimajjetpuruṣopyasau .. 58 ..
meaning:
इषुमोक्षं तदा कुर्याद्देशे तृणविवर्जिते ..
शरमोक्षे समे काले निमज्जेत्पुरुषोप्यसौ .. 58 ..
text_mt: should discharge an arrow in a place devoid of grass; / at the very time the arrow is discharged, that man should also submerge.

sanskrit_iast:
mūrdhni vinyastapatrastu petrai caitānniveśayet ..
ādidevo'si devānāṃ śaucasyāpyāyanaṃ param .. 59 ..
meaning:
मूर्ध्नि विन्यस्तपत्रस्तु पेत्रै चैतान्निवेशयेत् ..
आदिदेवोऽसि देवानां शौचस्याप्यायनं परम् .. 59 ..
text_mt: With a leaf placed upon his head, he should place these [words] upon the leaf: / "You are the primal god of gods, the supreme sustainer of purity;

sanskrit_iast:
pañcānāṃ lokapālānāṃ tvaṃ variṣṭhaṃ jagatpate ..
trāyasvainaṃ naraṃ pāpātpaśyasi tvaṃ śubhāśubhama .. 3.328.60 ..
meaning:
पञ्चानां लोकपालानां त्वं वरिष्ठं जगत्पते ..
त्रायस्वैनं नरं पापात्पश्यसि त्वं शुभाशुभम .. 3.328.60 ..
text_mt: you are the foremost of the five guardians of the world, O Lord of the universe! / Save this man from sin; you perceive good and evil!

sanskrit_iast:
antaścarasi bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ mokṣavatsthitaḥ ..
iṣuprakṣepaṇasthānādyuvā ca balavānnaraḥ ... .. 61 ..
meaning:
अन्तश्चरसि भूतानां सर्वेषां मोक्षवत्स्थितः ..
इषुप्रक्षेपणस्थानाद्युवा च बलवान्नरः ... .. 61 ..
text_mt: You move within all beings, standing as their liberation!" / And a strong young man, from the place where the arrow was shot,

sanskrit_iast:
dhāvansa parayā śaktyā śaraṃ tatsamupātayet ..
āgate tu śaragrāhe toyasthaścenna dṛśyate .. 62 ..
meaning:
धावन्स परया शक्त्या शरं तत्समुपातयेत् ..
आगते तु शरग्राहे तोयस्थश्चेन्न दृश्यते .. 62 ..
text_mt: running with his utmost strength, should bring back that arrow; / and when the arrow-fetcher returns, if the man in the water is not seen,

sanskrit_iast:
śuddho bhavati dharmeṇa yaścāpyaṅgaṃ na darśayet ..
viṣasyātaḥ pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ sanātanam ..63..
meaning:
शुद्धो भवति धर्मेण यश्चाप्यङ्गं न दर्शयेत् ..
विषस्यातः प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं धर्म्यं सनातनम् ..63..
text_mt: he becomes pure by dharma, and also if he does not show a limb. / Next I shall proclaim the righteous, eternal rule of poison.

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṅgiṇo vatsanābhasya himaśailodbhavasya ca..
yavāssapta pradātavyā atha vā yadghṛtāplutāḥ .. 64 ..
meaning:
शृङ्गिणो वत्सनाभस्य हिमशैलोद्भवस्य च..
यवास्सप्त प्रदातव्या अथ वा यद्घृताप्लुताः .. 64 ..
text_mt: Seven barley-grains of horned vatsanābha poison originating from the snowy mountain / should be administered, or else drenched in clarified butter.

sanskrit_iast:
mūrdhni vinyastapatrasya patre caitanniveśayet ..
tvaṃ viṣa brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ satye dharme vyavasthitaḥ . 65 ..
meaning:
मूर्ध्नि विन्यस्तपत्रस्य पत्रे चैतन्निवेशयेत् ..
त्वं विष ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः सत्ये धर्मे व्यवस्थितः . 65 ..
text_mt: Having placed a leaf upon his head, he should place this [formula] upon the leaf: / "You, O Poison, are the son of Brahmā, established in truth and dharma!

sanskrit_iast:
trāyasvainaṃ naraṃ pāpātsatyenāsya bhavāmṛtam ..
yena vegairvinā jīrṇaṃ chardimūrcchāvivarjitam.. 66 ..
meaning:
त्रायस्वैनं नरं पापात्सत्येनास्य भवामृतम् ..
येन वेगैर्विना जीर्णं छर्दिमूर्च्छाविवर्जितम्.. 66 ..
text_mt: Save this man from sin; through his truth, become nectar!" / If it is digested by him without violent fits, free from vomiting and fainting,

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ tu śuddhaṃ vijānīyāditi dharmavido viduḥ ..
taṇḍulānāṃ pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ sanātanam .. 67 ..
meaning:
तं तु शुद्धं विजानीयादिति धर्मविदो विदुः ..
तण्डुलानां प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं धर्म्यं सनातनम् .. 67 ..
text_mt: one should know him to be pure: so know the knowers of dharma. / I shall declare the righteous, eternal rule of the rice-grains.

sanskrit_iast:
caurye tu taṇḍulā deyā na cānyatra kathaṃcana ..
taṇḍulānudake siktvā rātrau tatraiva sthāpayeta .. 68 ...
meaning:
चौर्ये तु तण्डुला देया न चान्यत्र कथंचन ..
तण्डुलानुदके सिक्त्वा रात्रौ तत्रैव स्थापयेत .. 68 ...
text_mt: Rice-grains are to be given in theft, and never in any other case. / Having soaked the rice-grains in water at night, he should leave them right there.

sanskrit_iast:
taṇḍulānkārayecchuddhāñśālīnāṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
mṛnmayaṃ bhājanaṃ kṛtvā savituḥ purataḥ sthitaḥ .. 69 ..
meaning:
तण्डुलान्कारयेच्छुद्धाञ्शालीनां पृथिवीपतिः ..
मृन्मयं भाजनं कृत्वा सवितुः पुरतः स्थितः .. 69 ..
text_mt: The lord of the earth should have pure grains of śāli rice prepared; / placing an earthen vessel, standing before the sun,

sanskrit_iast:
taṇḍulānmaṃtrayecśuddhānmaṃtreṇānena dharmataḥ ..
dīyate sattvadharmajñairmānuṣāṇāṃ viśodhanam ..3.328.70..
meaning:
तण्डुलान्मंत्रयेच्शुद्धान्मंत्रेणानेन धर्मतः ..
दीयते सत्त्वधर्मज्ञैर्मानुषाणां विशोधनम् ..3.328.70..
text_mt: he should consecrate the pure grains according to dharma with this mantra: / "This purifier of human beings is given by those who know the law of truth.

sanskrit_iast:
tatastaṇḍula satyena dharmatastrātumarhasi ..
prabhāte kārayedeva bhakṣaṇāya na saṃśayaḥ ..71..
meaning:
ततस्तण्डुल सत्येन धर्मतस्त्रातुमर्हसि ..
प्रभाते कारयेदेव भक्षणाय न संशयः ..71..
text_mt: Therefore, O rice-grain, through truth you ought to save [him] according to dharma!" / At dawn he should certainly cause him to chew [them], without a doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
trividhaḥ prāṅmukhasyeha patre niṣṭhīvayettataḥ ..
pippalasyātha bhūrjasya na tvanyasya kathaṃcana .. 72 ..
meaning:
त्रिविधः प्राङ्मुखस्येह पत्रे निष्ठीवयेत्ततः ..
पिप्पलस्याथ भूर्जस्य न त्वन्यस्य कथंचन .. 72 ..
text_mt: He facing east should then spit it out three times here onto a leaf— / of the holy fig tree or of the birch tree, but never on any other.

sanskrit_iast:
śoṇitaṃ dṛśyate yasya tamaśuddhaṃ vinirdiśet ..
athātaḥ saṃprakṣyāmi taptamāṣakanirṇayam .. 73 ..
meaning:
शोणितं दृश्यते यस्य तमशुद्धं विनिर्दिशेत् ..
अथातः संप्रक्ष्यामि तप्तमाषकनिर्णयम् .. 73 ..
text_mt: He in whose [spit] blood is seen, one should declare him impure. / Now therefore I shall declare the decision by the heated māṣaka coin.

sanskrit_iast:
kārayedāyasaṃ pātraṃ tāmraṃ vā ṣoḍaśāṅgulam ..
caturaṅgulakhātaṃ tu mṛnmayaṃ vāpi kārayet .. .. 74 ..
meaning:
कारयेदायसं पात्रं ताम्रं वा षोडशाङ्गुलम् ..
चतुरङ्गुलखातं तु मृन्मयं वापि कारयेत् .. .. 74 ..
text_mt: He should have a vessel made of iron, or of copper, sixteen aṅgulas [wide], / with a depth of four aṅgulas, or he may have it made of clay.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrayedghṛtatailābhyāṃ palairviṃśatibhistataḥ ..
sutapte nikṣipettatra suvarṇasya tu māṣakam .. 75 ..
meaning:
पूरयेद्घृततैलाभ्यां पलैर्विंशतिभिस्ततः ..
सुतप्ते निक्षिपेत्तत्र सुवर्णस्य तु माषकम् .. 75 ..
text_mt: He should fill it with twenty palas of clarified butter and oil; / when it is boiling hot, he should cast a golden māṣaka into it.

sanskrit_iast:
vahnyaktaṃ vinyasenmantramabhiśastasya mūrdhani ..
aṅguṣṭhāṅguliyogena taptamāṣaṃ samuddharet .. 76 ..
meaning:
वह्न्यक्तं विन्यसेन्मन्त्रमभिशस्तस्य मूर्धनि ..
अङ्गुष्ठाङ्गुलियोगेन तप्तमाषं समुद्धरेत् .. 76 ..
text_mt: He should place the mantra addressed to fire upon the head of the accused; / with the thumb and fingers joined, he should take out the heated māṣaka.

sanskrit_iast:
śuddhaṃ jñeyamadagdhaṃ tu visphoṭādivivarjitam ..
phālaśuddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ .. 77 ..
meaning:
शुद्धं ज्ञेयमदग्धं तु विस्फोटादिविवर्जितम् ..
फालशुद्धिं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुध्वं द्विजपुङ्गवाः .. 77 ..
text_mt: If unburned and free from blisters and the like, he should be known as pure. / I shall declare the purification by the ploughshare; listen, O bulls among the twice-born!

sanskrit_iast:
āyasaṃ dvādaśapalaṃ ghaṭitaṃ phālamucyate ..
aṣṭāṅgulaṃ samaṃ dīrghaṃ caturaṃgulavistṛtam .. 78 ..
meaning:
आयसं द्वादशपलं घटितं फालमुच्यते ..
अष्टाङ्गुलं समं दीर्घं चतुरंगुलविस्तृतम् .. 78 ..
text_mt: An iron ploughshare is said to be forged weighing twelve palas, / eight aṅgulas long in straight measure, and four aṅgulas wide.

sanskrit_iast:
vahnyaktaṃ vinyasetpatramabhiśastasya mūrdhani ..
triḥ parāvartayejjihvāṃ lihatassārdhamaṅgulam .. 79 ..
meaning:
वह्न्यक्तं विन्यसेत्पत्रमभिशस्तस्य मूर्धनि ..
त्रिः परावर्तयेज्जिह्वां लिहतस्सार्धमङ्गुलम् .. 79 ..
text_mt: One should place a leaf anointed with fire on the head of the accused. / He should pass his tongue three times, licking [the blade] for an inch and a half.

sanskrit_iast:
gavāṃ kṣīraṃ pradātavyaṃ jihvāśodhanamuttamam ..
jihvāparīkṣaṇaṃ kuryāddagdhāṃ cenna vibhāvyate..3.328.80..
meaning:
गवां क्षीरं प्रदातव्यं जिह्वाशोधनमुत्तमम् ..
जिह्वापरीक्षणं कुर्याद्दग्धां चेन्न विभाव्यते..3.328.80..
text_mt: Cow's milk should be given as the best purifier of the tongue. / One should examine the tongue; if it is not perceived to be burned,

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ viśuddhaṃ vijānīyādviśuddhaṃ caiva mokṣayet ..

the Gāndharva and the Rākṣasa are declared to be middling; / and the Āsura, the Paiśāca, and the Ārṣa are the lowest.
They should never be performed with effort by anyone. / There is no difference between the Āsura and the Ārṣa;
it is to be known simply as a bride-price, whether it is small or whether it is large. / All men who sell living beings go to hell; / and especially a man who sells his own son— / they know his dwelling to be in hell for a multitude of years.
When her husband has died, a maiden who was merely touched by the hand / is entitled to the sacrament again, if her virginity is intact.
Thus some desire, but that is not my opinion, O twice-born; / for when the seventh step has been completed, she is not entitled to another husband.
A maiden who has been given by word of mouth, but not consecrated with mantras, / may be given to another if the husband is found to have a defect.
When a husband is missing, dead, has renounced the world, is impotent, or has fallen from caste— / in these five misfortunes another husband is prescribed for women.

text_mt:
The father, paternal grandfather, brother, kinsman, and likewise the mother— / each subsequent one, if in sound mind, is the giver of the maiden upon the absence of the preceding.
He who gives away a maiden without declaring a defect / should pay two hundred [paṇas] to the king and maintain that maiden.
And whichever man calls an unblemished woman blemished through a fault, / the king should impose upon him the first violent penalty.
He who treats a defective wife as properly blameless, / [the king], having punished him according to his capacity, should set him on the right path.
A woman who defies her husband, arrogant with the power of her kinsmen, / the king should have her eaten by dogs in a place where convicts are executed.
Abandonment of an adulterous wife is ordained.
And if she has intercourse with a lower caste, execution is declared by the wise. / Without the permission of the husband, the king may have authority over women in some cases.
He should discipline a woman whose husband is incapable, with his consent. / He who, having given a maiden to one, gives her again to another—

the king should fine that man a fourth part of his wealth. / When a fault arises in the husband, she should not incur punishment.
The vile man who does not approach his wife in her fertile period / should be fined a māṣaka of gold at every fertile period.
A wife who, being called, does not go to her husband during her fertile period / should be banished by the husband, having declared her fault to her mother.
The lowest of men who abandons an unblemished wife / should be fined a suvarṇa and must maintain her once again.
A man who acts unequally among his married wives / of the same caste should be fined a suvarṇa by the ruler of the earth.
A maiden, upon attaining her fertile period, should wait three years. / After the declared time, the maiden may find a suitable husband.
The maiden should not take ornaments from her father's family in a self-choice, / nor those from her mother or given by her brothers; for if she took them, it would be theft.

3.330
Haṃsa said:
The son born of one's own body, the son of an appointed daughter, and next the son born of the wife; / the son of a remarried woman, the son of an unmarried girl, and likewise the son received with a bride;
the secretly born, the adopted son, and next the purchased son; / the cast-off son, the self-given son, and likewise the son of a śūdra woman—
these are indeed the twelve sons; I shall declare their characteristics. / A son born of himself upon a consecrated [wife] is called the son born of one's own body.
"The son born of her shall be my son." / Even when given away by her father, she is declared an appointed daughter.
Even given without [such] an agreement, one who is without brothers is an appointed daughter; / her son, the son of an appointed daughter, is proclaimed as the second.
Beget through appointment by a brother-in-law, a sagotra, or a learned brahmin, / the son is proclaimed as the field-born.

text_mt:
She who, wanton, abandons her husband and resorts to another out of lust— / her son is proclaimed as the son of a remarried woman, the fourth.
Born of an unmarried maiden, the maiden-born son belongs to her husband alone. / She who is married while pregnant—her son is considered brought with the bride.
Born secretly in the house, he is proclaimed the secretly born. / Purchased from her presence, he is called the purchased son. / Abandoned by both of them, he is remembered as the cast-off.
He who is held by someone is spoken of as his son by adoptive taking; / and he who has offered himself for sonship, O best of twice-born!
If first there is the son of an appointed daughter and afterwards an aurasa is born, / the son of the appointed daughter would have an equal share with the aurasa.
Once the son of an appointed daughter is born, the begetting of a field-born son is futile. / Equal sons are to be known as equal sharers, such as they are.
Sons born against the grain do not share in the inheritance. / The heir of the wealth ought to provide maintenance for them according to their work.

text_mt:
Their offspring are proclaimed as entitled to share upon the death of the father; / in the paternal grandfather's wealth they are entitled to ownership in some measure.
The idiot, the blind, the deaf, and the insane must be maintained, having no share; / their sons who inherit the property take their share in the paternal grandfather's wealth.
According to dharma, there is no share for outcasts, nor for their sons. / But those sons who were born before the act that causes degraded status,
the inheritance must be given to them; they are not considered outcasts. / Likewise, when an expiation has been performed, the outcast is entitled to a share.
His son likewise, O brahmins; no doubt should be entertained here. / If the father should divide [the estate among] the sons, his own will prevails over his own wealth.
Over the grandfather's [wealth], however, the father is not independent according to dharma. / In wealth acquired by the grandfather, of both the father and the son
ownership is to be understood as equal, if the son is endowed with virtues. / When they divide after the father, the mother should also receive an equal share.

text_mt:
All sons of the same caste are likewise to be understood as equal sharers. / A little more is to be given to the eldest; there is no doubt about this.
Even of the son of a Brāhma and Daiva [marriage], those two most venerable are equal, / [while] those born of Paiśāca and Asura [marriages] are like the son of a remarried woman.
When a brahmin has four wives, / the king should divide that wealth which is the inheritance among their sons:
The [son of a] brahmin [wife] takes four shares; the son of a kṣatriyā takes three shares; / the son of a vaiśyā takes two shares; the son of a śūdrā takes one share.
If there are two sons of a brāhmaṇī and one son of a śūdrā, / the wealth of the brahmin is to be divided into nine parts; such is the rule.
Eight shares belong to the two sons of the brāhmaṇī; the ninth belongs to the son of the śūdrā. / If there are two [śūdrā] sons, it should be known, and one son of a brāhmaṇī,
the property of the brahmin is to be divided into six parts; such is the rule. / Two shares are to be given to the two sons of the śūdrā, and four shares to the twice-born.

text_mt:
In accordance with this very rule, the allotment of shares in all cases / of those born to women of different castes must be carried out by the ruler of the earth.
The wealth of a kṣatriya is to be divided into six parts; such is the rule. / Then the sons born of a kṣatriyā should take three shares of the wealth;
the son of a vaiśyā takes two shares; the son of a śūdrā takes one share. / The property of a vaiśya is to be divided into three parts; listen to the allotment in that case also:
The son of a vaiśyā takes two shares; the son of a śūdrā takes one share. / For a sonless man, however, the daughter's son is entitled to the inheritance according to dharma.
In the absence even of a daughter's son, the daughter also takes the wealth; / in her absence, then the wife; in her absence, the uterine brother; / in his absence also, the mother; in her absence, the father takes; / in his absence, the brothers; then the brother's son takes.
If a uterine brother's son exists in any way, / a brother born of another mother shall not obtain [the wealth]; such is the rule.

text_mt:
Where a son of a brother born of another mother is present, / the son of a paternal uncle's brother shall not take the wealth at all.
The next sapiṇḍa and so forth shall take the wealth of each of them; / in his absence, a sakulya; in his absence, it belongs to the guru;
in his absence, to the disciple; in his absence, to twice-born men. / Men learned in the three Vedas, self-restrained, and subdued are entitled to share that wealth.
The property of a brahmin must never be seized by kings. / For other castes, however, in the absence of all, the king shall take.
If two sons born to two [different fathers] from one woman should dispute over wealth, / whatever of the two is paternal to either, that one should take it, not the other.
Wealth that belongs to the mother belongs to the unmarried daughters; / in their absence, to the married daughters; in their absence, to the sons.
What is given before the fire, what is given at the bridal procession, and what is given as an act of affection, / and what is obtained from a brother, mother, or father—strīdhana is remembered as sixfold.

सर्वासामेकपत्नीनामेका चेत्पुत्रिणी भवेत् .. 44 ..
पुत्रवत्यस्तु तास्सर्वास्तेन पुत्रेण कीर्तिताः ..
अनुपघ्नं पितृद्रव्यं श्रमेण यदुपार्जितम् .. 45 ..
स्वयमीहितलब्धं तं नाकामो दातुमर्हति ..
येषां ज्येष्ठः कनिष्ठो वा हीयेतांशप्रदानतः .. 46 ..
म्रियेतान्यतरो वाऽपि तस्य भागो न नुलुप्यते ..
सोदर्या विभजेरंस्तं समेत्य सहिताः समम् .. 47 ..
text_mt:
That which is [received] in the Brāhma, Daiva, Ārṣa, Gāndharva, and Prājāpatya [marriages], / if she dies without issue, is desired for the husband alone.
[While that received] in other [forms] goes to the father […] wealth […] should be. / An ornament which has been worn by women while the husband was alive,
the co-heirs must not divide; if they divide it, they become degraded. / If among brothers born of the same father one should have a son,
all of them are made possessed of a son through that son; such is the sacred tradition. / If among all co-wives one should have a son,
all of them are proclaimed possessed of sons through that son. / What has been acquired by one's own effort without detriment to the ancestral property
What was obtained through one's own effort, he is not obliged to give against his will.
If the eldest or youngest among them is deprived of his share through the distribution of portions,
or if another dies, his share is not lost.
Brothers born of the same womb, gathering together, shall divide it equally,

sanskrit_iast:
bhrātaro ye ca saṃsṛṣṭā bhaginyaśca sajātayaḥ ..
vibhakte tu dhane jātāḥ pitryameva dhanaṃ haret .. 48 ..
vibhaktairvāsya dātavyamaṃśamaṃśānurūpataḥ ..
svabhāgasyānusāreṇa dattvā bhāgaṃ yathākramam .. 49 ..
asaṃskṛtāstu saṃskāryā vibhaktaiḥ kanyakāstathā ..
pravibhāge kṛte yatra paścāchiṣyeta vai dhanam .. 3.330.50 ..
pūrvoktenānusāreṇa vibhāgaṃ tatra kārayet ..
vastraṃ patramalaṅkāraṃ kṛtānnamudavakaṃ striyaḥ .. 51 ..
yogakṣemapracāre ca na vibhajyaṃ ca pustakam ..
rikthagrāhī ṛṇaṃ dadyātpiṇḍaṃ dadyātsa eva tu .. 52 ..
bhartavyānbibhṛyāttasya sarvāniti matirmama ..
rikthagrāhī na yaḥ kuryātpretakarma yathāvidhi ..53 ..
taskaraṃ taṃ svakādrāṣṭrātkṣipraṃ rājā vivāsayet ..
rājagāmī bhavedviprā yasya vittaṃ tu karhicit .. 54 ..
meaning:
भ्रातरो ये च संसृष्टा भगिन्यश्च सजातयः ..
विभक्ते तु धने जाताः पित्र्यमेव धनं हरेत् .. 48 ..
विभक्तैर्वास्य दातव्यमंशमंशानुरूपतः ..
स्वभागस्यानुसारेण दत्त्वा भागं यथाक्रमम् .. 49 ..
असंस्कृतास्तु संस्कार्या विभक्तैः कन्यकास्तथा ..
प्रविभागे कृते यत्र पश्चाछिष्येत वै धनम् .. 3.330.50 ..
पूर्वोक्तेनानुसारेण विभागं तत्र कारयेत् ..
वस्त्रं पत्रमलङ्कारं कृतान्नमुदवकं स्त्रियः .. 51 ..
योगक्षेमप्रचारे च न विभज्यं च पुस्तकम् ..
रिक्थग्राही ऋणं दद्यात्पिण्डं दद्यात्स एव तु .. 52 ..
भर्तव्यान्बिभृयात्तस्य सर्वानिति मतिर्मम ..
रिक्थग्राही न यः कुर्यात्प्रेतकर्म यथाविधि ..53 ..
तस्करं तं स्वकाद्राष्ट्रात्क्षिप्रं राजा विवासयेत् ..
राजगामी भवेद्विप्रा यस्य वित्तं तु कर्हिचित् .. 54 ..
text_mt:
as well as the brothers who have reunited and sisters of the same caste.
When the wealth has been divided, those born afterward take the father's property alone.
Or else, a share must be given to him by those who have already divided, in proportion to their shares,
after giving a share in due order according to their own portion.
Unmarried maiden daughters must likewise be given sacraments by those who have divided.
Where wealth is left behind after the division has been made,
a division must be made there according to what was stated earlier.
Clothing, a vehicle, an ornament, cooked food, water, women,
and during the performance of religious and secular tasks, and a book, are not to be divided.
The heir who takes the inheritance shall pay the debt and he alone shall offer the funerary ball.
He should support all those who ought to be supported by him—such is my opinion.
The heir taking the inheritance who does not perform the rites for the deceased according to rule,
the king should swiftly banish that thief from his own realm.
O brahmins, whenever someone's property falls to the king,

sanskrit_iast:
rājāpi dāpayetpiṇḍaṃ tasya bhṛtyairyathāvidhi ..
yasyāṃ narāṇāmiha vittabhāgī ṛṇasya bhāgī sa tathā niruktaḥ ..
ṛṇāvaśiṣṭaṃ puruṣastu nityaṃ bhuktvā dvijendrāḥ sukṛtī sadā syāt .. 55 ..
meaning:
राजापि दापयेत्पिण्डं तस्य भृत्यैर्यथाविधि ..
यस्यां नराणामिह वित्तभागी ऋणस्य भागी स तथा निरुक्तः ..
ऋणावशिष्टं पुरुषस्तु नित्यं भुक्त्वा द्विजेन्द्राः सुकृती सदा स्यात् .. 55 ..

sanskrit_iast:
3.331
.. haṃsa upāca ..
uttamarṇāya dātavyamadhamarṇena yācitam ..
brāhmaṇendrā dhanaṃ sarvaṃ nihnave tacca bhāvitam .. 1 ..
meaning:
3.331
.. हंस उपाच ..
उत्तमर्णाय दातव्यमधमर्णेन याचितम् ..
ब्राह्मणेन्द्रा धनं सर्वं निह्नवे तच्च भावितम् .. 1 ..
text_mt:
3.331
Haṃsa spoke:
What was requested by the creditor must be paid by the debtor,
O foremost of brahmins; and when it is denied, all that wealth must be proved.
title: Ṛṇadānavarṇanaḥ

sanskrit_iast:
sarvopāyairdhanī vittamṛṇikādāpnuyātsvakam ..
na sa rājñābhiyoktavyaḥ svakaṃ saṃsādhayandhanam .. 2 ..
meaning:
सर्वोपायैर्धनी वित्तमृणिकादाप्नुयात्स्वकम् ..
न स राज्ञाभियोक्तव्यः स्वकं संसाधयन्धनम् .. 2 ..
text_mt:
By all means a creditor may recover his own property from the debtor;
he is not to be prosecuted by the king while recovering his own wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
arthanihnavamānaṃ tu bhāvanābhirvibhāvitam ..
dāpayeddhanikasyārthaṃ rājño daṇḍaṃ ca tatsamam .. 3..
meaning:
अर्थनिह्नवमानं तु भावनाभिर्विभावितम् ..
दापयेद्धनिकस्यार्थं राज्ञो दण्डं च तत्समम् .. 3..
text_mt:
When the denial of the property is proved by means of proofs,
he should cause the creditor's property to be paid, and an equal fine to the king.

sanskrit_iast:
mithyābhiyoge dviguṇamiti yogāddhanaṃ haret ..
bhāgaṃ viṃśatimandadyātprāptārtho dhaniko nṛpe .. 4 ..
meaning:
मिथ्याभियोगे द्विगुणमिति योगाद्धनं हरेत् ..
भागं विंशतिमन्दद्यात्प्राप्तार्थो धनिको नृपे .. 4 ..
text_mt:
In a false claim, he should take twice as much wealth by application of the law;
the creditor who has obtained his property should give a twentieth part to the king,

sanskrit_iast:
yadi rājabalenāsau taddhi tasmādavāpnuyāt ..
dvikaṃ trikaṃ catuṣkaṃ ca pañcakaṃ ca tathā śatam .. 5 ..
meaning:
यदि राजबलेनासौ तद्धि तस्मादवाप्नुयात् ..
द्विकं त्रिकं चतुष्कं च पञ्चकं च तथा शतम् .. 5 ..
text_mt:
if he obtained that indeed from him through the king's force.
Two, three, four, and five per cent,

sanskrit_iast:
varṇānukramato vṛddhiḥ pratimāsaṃ prakīrtitā ..
svayaṃ kṛtāṃ tathā vṛddhiṃ sarve sarvāsu yoniṣu .. 6..
meaning:
वर्णानुक्रमतो वृद्धिः प्रतिमासं प्रकीर्तिता ..
स्वयं कृतां तथा वृद्धिं सर्वे सर्वासु योनिषु .. 6..
text_mt:
is declared to be the monthly interest according to the order of castes.
Likewise, an interest agreed upon by oneself, everyone in all castes

sanskrit_iast:
dātumarhati viprendrā iti me niścitā matiḥ ..
na kvacitprītidattānāṃ vṛddhiḥ saṃvatsaraṃ bhavet .. 7 ..
meaning:
दातुमर्हति विप्रेन्द्रा इति मे निश्चिता मतिः ..
न क्वचित्प्रीतिदत्तानां वृद्धिः संवत्सरं भवेत् .. 7 ..
text_mt:
is bound to pay, O foremost of brahmins—such is my settled opinion.
There is nowhere any interest for a year on things given out of friendship.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāmapi bhavedvṛddhirgate saṃvatsare tathā ..
sā ca vṛddhiryathoktā vai varṇānāmanupūrvaśaḥ .. 8 ..
meaning:
तेषामपि भवेद्वृद्धिर्गते संवत्सरे तथा ..
सा च वृद्धिर्यथोक्ता वै वर्णानामनुपूर्वशः .. 8 ..
text_mt:
Even on those, interest will accrue after a year has elapsed;
and that interest is indeed as stated, according to the order of the castes.

sanskrit_iast:
tathāvidhā grahītavyā nānyatheti hi niścayaḥ ..
ādhibhugdīyate vṛddhiṃ naṣṭāmādhiṃ ca dāpayet .. 9 ..
meaning:
तथाविधा ग्रहीतव्या नान्यथेति हि निश्चयः ..
आधिभुग्दीयते वृद्धिं नष्टामाधिं च दापयेत् .. 9 ..
text_mt:
Interest of such a kind should be taken, not otherwise—this is indeed the settled rule.
He who enjoys a pledge pays interest, and if the pledge is ruined, he should be made to pay for it,

sanskrit_iast:
daivarājakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ vinā brāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
antyavṛddhau praviṣṭāyāṃ cārtau tyāgo vidhīyate .. 3.331.10 ..
meaning:
दैवराजकृतं दोषं विना ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ..
अन्त्यवृद्धौ प्रविष्टायां चार्तौ त्यागो विधीयते .. 3.331.10 ..
text_mt:
except in the case of a fault caused by fate or the king, O best of brahmins.
When the ultimate interest has entered, and in distress, relinquishment is ordained.

sanskrit_iast:
bhojyasyādheḥ parityāgaḥ praviṣṭe tu dhane bhavet ..
bhogasya gaṇanā kāryā na tatra vacanādṛte .. 11 ..
meaning:
भोज्यस्याधेः परित्यागः प्रविष्टे तु धने भवेत् ..
भोगस्य गणना कार्या न तत्र वचनादृते .. 11 ..
text_mt:
The release of a usufructuary pledge occurs when the money has entered;
a calculation of the enjoyment must be made, not without an agreement there.

sanskrit_iast:
dhaninorthaṃ na hīyeta ādhau prāṇayute mṛte ..
hetubhūtastu maraṇe na cetsyāduttamarṇikaḥ .. 12 ..
meaning:
धनिनोर्थं न हीयेत आधौ प्राणयुते मृते ..
हेतुभूतस्तु मरणे न चेत्स्यादुत्तमर्णिकः .. 12 ..
text_mt:
The creditor's property is not lost when a living pledge has died,
provided the creditor was not the cause of death.

sanskrit_iast:
ādhau vivadamānānāṃ bhuktā jīvanti cāparāḥ ..
anyasyādhīkṛtāṃ bhūmiṃ yaścānyasya prayacchati .. 13 ..
meaning:
आधौ विवदमानानां भुक्ता जीवन्ति चापराः ..
अन्यस्याधीकृतां भूमिं यश्चान्यस्य प्रयच्छति .. 13 ..
text_mt:
While people are disputing over a pledge, others enjoy it and live upon it.
And he who gives to another land that was pledged to someone else,

sanskrit_iast:
svayameva narendrastaṃ ghātayedavicārayan ..
dravyeṣvevamathānyeṣu daṇḍaḥ syāddviguṇaṃ bhavet .. 14 ..
meaning:
स्वयमेव नरेन्द्रस्तं घातयेदविचारयन् ..
द्रव्येष्वेवमथान्येषु दण्डः स्याद्द्विगुणं भवेत् .. 14 ..
text_mt:
the ruler of men himself should execute him without deliberation.
In the case of other goods, the fine should be double.

sanskrit_iast:
ādhau samudre naṣṭe tu mudrā yatra na dṛśyate ..
na tatra hīyate vittaṃ dhanikasya kathañcana .. 15 ..
meaning:
आधौ समुद्रे नष्टे तु मुद्रा यत्र न दृश्यते ..
न तत्र हीयते वित्तं धनिकस्य कथञ्चन .. 15 ..
text_mt:
When a sealed pledge is lost where the seal is not seen [tampered with],
the creditor's property is in no way lost in that case.

sanskrit_iast:
anyathā tu tathā naṣṭe dhanikasyaiva hīyate ..
antyā vṛddhirhiraṇyasya dviguṇā parikīrtitā .. 16 ..
meaning:
अन्यथा तु तथा नष्टे धनिकस्यैव हीयते ..
अन्त्या वृद्धिर्हिरण्यस्य द्विगुणा परिकीर्तिता .. 16 ..
text_mt:
Otherwise, when it is lost in that manner, the loss belongs only to the creditor.
The ultimate interest on gold is proclaimed to be double;

sanskrit_iast:
vastrasya triguṇā proktā dhānyasya tu caturguṇā ..
rasasyāṣṭaguṇā vṛddhiḥ strīpaśūnāṃ ca santatiḥ .. 17 ..
meaning:
वस्त्रस्य त्रिगुणा प्रोक्ता धान्यस्य तु चतुर्गुणा ..
रसस्याष्टगुणा वृद्धिः स्त्रीपशूनां च सन्ततिः .. 17 ..
text_mt:
on cloth it is declared to be threefold, but on grain fourfold;
on liquids the interest is eightfold, and of female animals, the offspring.

sanskrit_iast:
strīpaśūnāmṛte vṛddhiḥ paśūnāṃ caiva vidyate ..
urabhrāṇāṃ bhavedvṛddhiḥ sati puṃstve hi vai dvijāḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
स्त्रीपशूनामृते वृद्धिः पशूनां चैव विद्यते ..
उरभ्राणां भवेद्वृद्धिः सति पुंस्त्वे हि वै द्विजाः .. 18 ..
text_mt:
Apart from female animals, interest exists on other animals as well;
there is an increase of sheep when masculinity is present, O twice-born;

sanskrit_iast:
ūrṇāvṛddhirbhavetteṣāṃ varṣāṇi dvādaśaiva tu ..
dravyāṇāmapyanuktānāṃ vṛddhirjñeyā caturguṇā .. 19 ..
meaning:
ऊर्णावृद्धिर्भवेत्तेषां वर्षाणि द्वादशैव तु ..
द्रव्याणामप्यनुक्तानां वृद्धिर्ज्ञेया चतुर्गुणा .. 19 ..
text_mt:
their increase of wool lasts for only twelve years.
On goods not mentioned, the interest should be known as fourfold.

sanskrit_iast:
dīyamānaprayuktaṃ tu puruṣasyāpragṛhṇataḥ ..
tataḥ paraṃ na vṛddhiḥ syātkathaṃciddvijasattamāḥ .. 3.331.20 ..
meaning:
दीयमानप्रयुक्तं तु पुरुषस्याप्रगृह्णतः ..
ततः परं न वृद्धिः स्यात्कथंचिद्द्विजसत्तमाः .. 3.331.20 ..
text_mt:
When money is offered and applied, but the man does not accept it,
there is no interest beyond that in any way, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
svamarthaṃ yo na gṛhṇāti dīyamānaṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..
tasmātsa hīyate viprā dātā tatrānṛṇo bhavet .. 21 ..
meaning:
स्वमर्थं यो न गृह्णाति दीयमानं पुनःपुनः ..
तस्मात्स हीयते विप्रा दाता तत्रानृणो भवेत् .. 21 ..
text_mt:
He who does not take his own property when it is offered repeatedly,
loses it because of that, O brahmins; the payer becomes free from debt in that matter.

sanskrit_iast:
pitā pravasito yasya brāhmaṇā dvidaśāḥ samāḥ ..
ṛṇaṃ tasya sutairdeyaṃ mṛtasya yadi vā punaḥ ..22..
meaning:
पिता प्रवसितो यस्य ब्राह्मणा द्विदशाः समाः ..
ऋणं तस्य सुतैर्देयं मृतस्य यदि वा पुनः ..22..
text_mt:
A father who has gone abroad for twenty years, O brahmins,
his debt must be paid by his sons, or likewise if he is dead.

sanskrit_iast:
paitṛkaṃ tu ṛṇaṃ putraḥ pautro vā dātumarhati..
na kāmastaccaturthaṃ tu dātumarhati karhicit.. .. 23 ..
meaning:
पैतृकं तु ऋणं पुत्रः पौत्रो वा दातुमर्हति..
न कामस्तच्चतुर्थं तु दातुमर्हति कर्हिचित्.. .. 23 ..
text_mt:
A son or grandson ought to pay the paternal debt;
[a descendant] in the fourth degree is never obliged to pay it against his will.

sanskrit_iast:
rikthagrāhī tathā putraḥ strīgrāhī dhanadāsikaḥ ..
putre sthitepi dātavyamṛṇaṃ vai dhanahāriṇāma .. 24 ..
meaning:
रिक्थग्राही तथा पुत्रः स्त्रीग्राही धनदासिकः ..
पुत्रे स्थितेपि दातव्यमृणं वै धनहारिणाम .. 24 ..
text_mt:
The heir who takes the inheritance, as well as the son, the one who takes the wife, and the servant of the wealth;
even when a son is present, the debt must be paid by those who take the wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
rikthagrāhī sutābhāve strīgrāhī dātumarhati ..
svayaṃ dātumaśakto yaḥ kartumicchetpunaḥ kriyām .. 25 ..
meaning:
रिक्थग्राही सुताभावे स्त्रीग्राही दातुमर्हति ..
स्वयं दातुमशक्तो यः कर्तुमिच्छेत्पुनः क्रियाम् .. 25 ..
text_mt:
In the absence of a son, the heir who takes the inheritance or the one who takes the wife should pay it.
One who is himself unable to pay and wishes to renew the contract,

sanskrit_iast:
sa dattvā nirjitāṃ vṛddhiṃ kārayetparivarttayet ..
adarśayitvā tatraiva hiraṇyaṃ parivartayan .. 26 ..
meaning:
स दत्त्वा निर्जितां वृद्धिं कारयेत्परिवर्त्तयेत् ..
अदर्शयित्वा तत्रैव हिरण्यं परिवर्तयन् .. 26 ..
text_mt:
having paid the accrued interest, should cause it to be renewed.
Renewing it without showing the gold right there,

sanskrit_iast:
yāvatī saṃbhavedvṛddhistāvatīṃ dātumarhati..
prātibhāvye vṛthā dānaṃ dyūtamadhyayanaṃ ca yat .. 27 ..
meaning:
यावती संभवेद्वृद्धिस्तावतीं दातुमर्हति..

3.332
Haṃsa said:
A wise man, when able, should deposit a deposit with one who is rich in virtue and born of good family; / and when asked, he ought to return it to him just as it was.
Both he who demands [what is not his] after having made a deposit, and he who does not return what was deposited, / are to be punished like thieves by a king who knows dharma.
An open deposit and a sealed deposit are not to be given to an immediate [relative]; / for these two are destroyed in misfortune, but in the absence of misfortune they are not destroyed.
If that which was deposited is lost in the hands of him into whose hands it was deposited, without his [fault], / he should by no means make it good.
One who enjoys a deposit should be punished [with a fine of] six times the value of the enjoyment. / This very rule is laid down in the case of borrowed objects, trust-deposits, / craftsmen, sealed deposits, open deposits, and mutual deposits;

3.333
Haṃsa said:
Where merchants and others perform work jointly, / hear from me as I speak of that joint enterprise.
For those who perform work jointly by an expedient for the sake of profit, / the investment is the foundation, and from that the shares are determined.
Equal, greater, or less, whatever and of whatever kind one's share may be, / loss, expense, and likewise profit belong to him in that same proportion.
The consent of all must be had regarding expenses, capital goods, and the rest; / dividing equally among all, [the manager] is honored in the world for that reason.
When a calamity brought about by fate or the king has arisen, / a tenth share is prescribed for him who [rescues the goods] there according to his ability.

If calamity should befall one [partner], his heir shall obtain [his share]; / and in the absence of an heir, that property indeed belongs to all of them.
Likewise, in calamities among sacrificial priests, one who completes the ritual is to be honored; / from that, he receives the share of the sacrificial fee that was allotted.
If a sacrificial priest and a sacrificer, being corrupt, should abandon one another, / they are to be fined with the first amercement, and they do not deserve to abandon [each other].
A trust-deposit, a borrowed article, a pledge, and what is common property, / an open deposit, a son and a wife, and one's entire property when there is lineage;
these are not to be given, O best of the twice-born, as well as what has been promised to another. / But [a gift] made by men overcome by anger, fear, or grief is [regarded as] ungiven;
likewise by children, the aged, those not independent, the intoxicated, and the insane; / and out of ignorance, or to an unworthy recipient out of rivalry, O best of the twice-born.
He who takes this through delusion, and he who gives what is not to be given, / both are to be punished like thieves by a king who knows dharma.

A man who takes away what was given by himself or given by another, / surely goes to hell, O brahmins, as does he who does not deliver what he himself gave.
3.334
Haṃsa said:
A hired laborer is said to be of three kinds; I shall describe his characteristics: / one is limited by time, another is limited by place,
and the third is limited by work. All of them are considered workers. / If a hired laborer abandons his wage at the beginning of the work in an improper place or time,
the entire wage is taken away, provided it is not the master's fault; / but if it is forfeited through the fault of the master, the laborer must be paid.
And the king should fine [the offender] a hundred paṇas. / A craftsman who has taken the price but does not deliver the article in time
shall pay double the value and must likewise be made to deliver the article; / and he ought to deliver that article without any loss at all.
If a master dismisses a servant halfway along the road without any fault on the servant's part, / he must pay the full equivalent, and a gold māṣaka to the king.

Food is to be given to one who is sick, and when restored to health he must complete that work; / but if, even when restored to health, he does not perform it, he must repay double the food.
What is lost through negligence must be paid in full; if struck down through a defect, a hundredfold. / He should never be made to pay for what is taken forcibly by thieves.
If he acts to the best of his ability during destruction by water or fire, he should not be made to pay; / likewise, he is by no means to be made to pay for property seized by the king.
Where there should be constant guarding, if he is the overseer there, / he must be made to pay for all that property, whatever is lost there.
A man who takes a cart or the like for hire, / if he does not pay the hire, must be made to pay the hire, even if [the cart] was merely loaded.
For one who undertakes work without an explicit agreement, / having considered the place, time, capability, and devotion according to his capacity,
his wage is to be paid, or he must be compelled by the king with force. / One who has apostatized from asceticism is a slave of the king until death.

text_mt:
One who was maintained during a famine is freed from peril to his life [by giving what was consumed]; / and one captured under a banner is freed by giving a substitute person.
Food and clothing must be given to all at all times; / likewise the king [must maintain] the wage of servants, even for a hundred years,
if the worker there is accompanied by sons and grandsons. / For one who is hired for teaching, this very rule is settled.
If at any time servants should win any wealth through their own work,
all of that belongs to the employer; so know those who know dharma.
A wife, a son, and a slave—these three are considered to possess no property;
whatever they acquire belongs to him whose [dependents] they are.
Slavery is in the direct order of the castes, not in the reverse order;
if [a master] should cause slavery in the reverse order, [the king] should destroy him.
A courtesan who, having accepted her fee, is unwilling, shall pay double;
but a man who does not pay the fee should be made to pay eightfold.

3.335
Haṃsa said:
Having found goods sold by a non-owner, the owner may recover them.
There is clearance through open purchase; purchase in secret is theft.
A purchase for too low a price or by force incurs that blame;
no title is accepted from the buyer; his clearance comes from [tracing] that origin.
The owner shall obtain the property, whether [it was purchased] openly or in secret.
He who, having sold merchandise for a price, does not deliver what was bought,
should be made to give the yield of immovable property and the produce of labor of movable property.
If the value has not fallen, he must deliver the merchandise with interest.
This is the rule for local merchants, and the profit of foreign trade for one who has traveled abroad.
If the merchandise is damaged, burned, or stolen,
that misfortune falls upon the seller alone, [unless] the seller has offered it.

the seller does not commit an offense by selling it elsewhere.
He who displays a faultless item but delivers a defective one
must be made to pay double its price and should also be punished.
This rule is proclaimed for merchandise whose price has been paid.
When unpaid, there is no transgression by the seller, except by agreement.
Having purchased merchandise for a price, if the buyer considers it badly bought,
listen, O brahmins, how the sold item is to be returned:
Within two days [a draught animal] must be returned, and a beast of burden within five days;
a jewel within seven days, metal on that very day,
bipeds within half a month, seeds within ten days,
clothing on the third day, and a weapon on the following day.
A garment that has been worn, soiled, and degraded
does not return to the seller, even though purchased with defects.
Even when goods are sold, one's own property or the leader may recover it;
if the buyer has not practiced deception, it is desired that it belongs to the seller here again.

or contracted by a servant, is known to be binding; those who know the truth say this with one voice.
3.337
Haṃsa said:
When a boundary dispute has arisen, the neighbors, elders, groups,
herdsmen, and boundary cultivators—whatever they say, so it shall be.
All wearing red garlands and garments, bearing earth upon their heads,
they should demarcate the boundary in the month of Jyeṣṭha, in open, level grounds.
One should establish boundary trees: silk-cotton, sacred fig, and kiṃśuka,
and also chaff, charcoal, potsherds, bones, and pebbles.
One should declare the fruit and flower of trees that have grown in the middle of a boundary between two fields / to be common to the two field-owners.
When a branch of [trees] grown in another's field extends elsewhere, / one should recognize him to whose field it has reached as its owner.
[When a stream] is spread out with smell, color, and taste, whether unripe or thick, / positioned in a speech-protecting flow, it stands long for great purification.

3.338
Haṃsa said:
The wise declare wealth to be the root of dharma, profit, and pleasure; / and property is proclaimed to be the external life-breaths of men.
Therefore, thieves must be put to death by a king who knows dharma; / for they deserve death, especially [those causing] all manner of harm.
I see no duty for a king apart from the slaying of a thief. / If a king should release a thief out of affection or greed for wealth,
those who know dharma say that he incurs a hundred murders of brahmins. / A king must not slay a brahmin, [even if] standing in all sins.
He should banish a thief from the kingdom with all his wealth intact; / he should banish a brahmin who has committed a mortal sin after he has been branded.
Property stolen on a village boundary must be made good by the villager; / and into whichever village the footprint should lead, that [village] must likewise be made to pay.

Two [villages] are to be fined if [the property] was stolen in the middle of a boundary; / if in a wilderness, the one appointed there; if in a city, the city-prefect.
All [other] perpetrators of mortal sins are to be put to death by the ruler of the earth. / He should brand a brahmin who is a slayer of a brahmin on the forehead with a headless torso;
a drinker of liquor with [the mark of] a tavern or one made as a horse's hoof; / and the king should brand a brahmin who violates the bed of forbidden women with the mark of the female organ.
Likewise, slayers of men, women, and children must be put to death by the king, / as well as incendiaries, poisoners, and false witnesses in matters concerning land.
And those who breach embankments, and those who commit crimes against the king, / and those who play with false dice must be mutilated of limbs by the king.
And he who plays [dice] with deceit here should be deprived of a hand. / And when wealth is being stolen or murder committed, while people are crying out,
a hearer who does not intervene—the king should put them to death as well. / Slayers of elephants and horses must be executed, and likewise those who slay cows.
For slayers of the remaining domestic animals, however, he should cut off a hand. / A fine of a hundred kārṣāpaṇas is prescribed for the slaying of a wild animal;

3.339
The sages said:
Beyond this, O best of the twice-born, unweariedly tell us
the dharma of those living in the forest, and also the dharma of the stages of life.
Haṃsa said:
When a householder sees wrinkles and grey hair on himself,
and also the offspring of his offspring, then he should take refuge in the forest.
Having entrusted his wife to his sons, or accompanied by her in the forest,
always tending the sacred fires, he should gather wild food.
Whatever his food may be, with that he should worship the ancestors and the deities;
with that very food the wise man should honour an arrived guest.
Or bringing it from a village, he may eat eight mouthfuls, collected in mind;
and likewise he should engage in sacred recitation and wear matted locks.
He should constantly dry up his body through austerities:
wearing wet clothes in winter, and surrounded by the five fires in summer;

He who is disgusted with birth and likewise with death,
and with mental anguish and physical illnesses—him the gods know to be a brahmin.
The impurity of the body, the alteration of what is pleasant and unpleasant,
and seeing one's dwelling in the womb—he is liberated, not otherwise.
There is no joy in birth and death, nor is it insubstantial and purposeless.
'This must be experienced'—with this detachment, the utterance is spoken daily.
Adopting such dispassion, constantly devoted to meditation,
transcending the twenty-four principles, he should perceive the twenty-fifth.
Earth, water, fire, wind, and ether—
one should know these five as the great elements everywhere.
Ears, eyes, touch, taste, and breath—
one should know these as the five sensory faculties in this small body.
Sound, form, touch, taste, and smell—
these are the five faculties of action constantly in this small body.
Mind, intellect, the self, and the unmanifest, O twice-born,

text_mt:
are taught here as four that are beyond the sense faculties.
These make twenty-four; the Cosmic Person is the twenty-fifth,
knowing whom, men of tranquil minds are completely liberated.
Smell, taste, wind, touch, and sound, O twice-born—
these five qualities belong to earth; the gross is perceived in elements of earth.
Taste, form, touch, and sound are regarded as the qualities of water.
Form, touch, and sound are remembered as the qualities of fire;
touch and sound are of wind; and sound is of the ether.
From ether arises sound; touch is the quality of wind;
form is declared of fire; and taste is considered the quality of water.
Smell is said to belong to earth: these are declared the objects of the senses.
Higher than the senses are their objects; higher than the objects is the mind;
higher than the mind is the intellect; higher than the intellect is the great self;
higher than the great self is the unmanifest; and higher than the unmanifest is the Cosmic Person.

text_mt:
There is nothing beyond the Cosmic Person; that is the limit, that is the ultimate goal. / This is the higher secret, this is the supreme imperishable.
Expressed indeed by the syllable Oṃ, beyond the qualities, eternal, / soundless, tasteless, touchless, formless, devoid of smell,
free from sorrow, beyond pleasure and pain: that is the supreme step of Viṣṇu. / If the tip of a hair is divided into a hundred parts, and each imagined a thousandfold,
a hundredth part even of that is called the individual soul. / In the heart is the sun and moon; in the midst of the moon is the fire;
in its midst stands sattva; in the midst of sattva stands Acyuta. / Making one's own body the lower fire-drill and the Praṇava the upper fire-drill,
through the practice of the churning of meditation, one should behold Viṣṇu situated in the heart. / Yet this God is ordained for mortals by means of desires,
by senses veiled with a sheet of ignorance and seeking sense-objects. / This indeed is the Cosmic Person Viṣṇu, manifest and unmanifest, eternal.

text_mt:
He is the creator and the ordainer, the measure, partless, auspicious. / Two brahmans are to be known: the sound-brahman and that which is supreme.
One who is proficient in the sound-brahman attains the supreme brahman. / One should constantly meditate on the subtle, and ever on the auspicious, O twice-born.
From meditation on the subtle, one attains the highest radiant state. / Reality indeed carries the intellect, and the intellect carries the supreme state.
The state carries the moon and sun through the ascetic power of Parameṣṭhin. / Sattva carries both of them, and sattva carries the Lord.

प्रतिमां कारयित्वा तु देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ..
न दुर्गतिमवाप्नोति विष्णुलोकं च गच्छति .. 11 ..
text_mt: One obtains an endless fruit in one adorned with gems and charming. / Having had an image made of the discus-bearing God of gods, / one does not meet with misfortune and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
devasya pratimāyāṃ tu yāvaṃtaḥ paramāṇavaḥ ..
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṇuloke mahīyate .. 12 ..
meaning:
देवस्य प्रतिमायां तु यावंतः परमाणवः ..
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि विष्णुलोके महीयते .. 12 ..
text_mt: As many atoms as there are in the image of the God, / for so many thousands of years is one honored in the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: prāsādavattathā tasya phalasaṃpadudāhṛtā .. 13 ..
meaning: प्रासादवत्तथा तस्य फलसंपदुदाहृता .. 13 ..
text_mt: Just as for the temple, so is the abundance of its fruit declared,

sanskrit_iast:
uttarottarato divyairvinā pakveṣṭikī dvijāḥ ..
yathoktavidhinā devaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya janārdanam .. 14 ..
meaning:
उत्तरोत्तरतो दिव्यैर्विना पक्वेष्टिकी द्विजाः ..
यथोक्तविधिना देवं प्रतिष्ठाप्य जनार्दनम् .. 14 ..
text_mt: successively greater, with divine materials, except for baked brick, O twice-born. / Having consecrated God Janārdana according to the prescribed rule,

sanskrit_iast:
