svayamenaṃ tathā lakṣmīrbhajate nātra saṃśayaḥ..
raktapadmaprado viṣṇostasya syāddviguṇaṃ phalam .. 238 ..
meaning:
स्वयमेनं तथा लक्ष्मीर्भजते नात्र संशयः..
रक्तपद्मप्रदो विष्णोस्तस्य स्याद्द्विगुणं फलम् .. 238 ..
text_mt: Lakṣmī herself attends upon him, there is no doubt of this. / For one who offers a red lotus to Viṣṇu, there shall be twice the fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
nīlotpalasamaṃ dānaṃ campakasya prakīrtitam ..
mallikāpuṣpajātīnāṃ yūthikāyāstathaiva ca .. 239 ..
meaning:
नीलोत्पलसमं दानं चम्पकस्य प्रकीर्तितम् ..
मल्लिकापुष्पजातीनां यूथिकायास्तथैव च .. 239 ..
text_mt: The gift of campaka is proclaimed equal to that of the blue lotus; / of the varieties of mallikā flowers and likewise of jasmine,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā kupyakajātīnāṃ phalasyārdhaṃ prakīrtitam ..
jātīpuṣpapradānena gandharvaiḥ saha modate ..3.341.240 ..
meaning:
तथा कुप्यकजातीनां फलस्यार्धं प्रकीर्तितम् ..
जातीपुष्पप्रदानेन गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ..3.341.240 ..
text_mt: and of varieties of kupyaka, half the fruit is proclaimed. / By the gift of a jātī flower, one rejoices with the gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast:
jātīpuṣpāṣṭakaṃ dattvā vahniṣṭomaphalaṃ labheta..
jātīpuṣpasahasreṇa yatheṣṭāṅgatimāpnuyāt .. 241 ..
meaning:
जातीपुष्पाष्टकं दत्त्वा वह्निष्टोमफलं लभेत..
जातीपुष्पसहस्रेण यथेष्टाङ्गतिमाप्नुयात् .. 241 ..
text_mt: Having given eight jātī flowers, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma; / with a thousand jātī flowers, one attains a destination according to one's desire.

sanskrit_iast:
śvetadvīpamavāpnoti lakṣapūjāvidhāyakaḥ ..
jātīpuṣpayutāṃ mālāṃ karpūrapaṭavāsitām ..242..
meaning:
श्वेतद्वीपमवाप्नोति लक्षपूजाविधायकः ..
जातीपुष्पयुतां मालां कर्पूरपटवासिताम् ..242..
text_mt: One who performs worship with a hundred thousand attains Śvetadvīpa. / A garland strung with jātī flowers, scented with camphor and fragrant powder—

sanskrit_iast:
nivedya devadevāya yatphalaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ ..
śvetaiḥ puṣpaiḥ samabhyarcya sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 243 ..
meaning:
निवेद्य देवदेवाय यत्फलं प्राप्नुयान्नरः ..
श्वेतैः पुष्पैः समभ्यर्च्य सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् .. 243 ..
text_mt: the fruit that a man obtains by offering [it] to the God of gods: / having fully worshipped with white flowers, he attains all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
āścaryamāpnuyālloke pītairdevaṃ samarcayan ..
śatrūṇāmabhicāreṣu tathā kṛṣṇa samarcayet .. 244 ..
meaning:
आश्चर्यमाप्नुयाल्लोके पीतैर्देवं समर्चयन् ..
शत्रूणामभिचारेषु तथा कृष्ण समर्चयेत् .. 244 ..
text_mt: By worshipping the god with yellow [flowers], one attains wondrous glory in the world; / and in magical rites against enemies, one should likewise worship with black [flowers].

sanskrit_iast:
suvarṇapuṣpairabhyarcya rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet ..
ratnairdevamathābhyarcya rājā bhavati bhūtale .. 245 ..
meaning:
सुवर्णपुष्पैरभ्यर्च्य राजसूयफलं लभेत् ..
रत्नैर्देवमथाभ्यर्च्य राजा भवति भूतले .. 245 ..
text_mt: By worshipping with golden flowers, one obtains the fruit of a Rājasūya sacrifice; / and by worshipping the god with gems, one becomes a king on the face of the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā puṣpagṛhaṃ viṣṇoḥ puṣpairvātha vitānakam ..
phalena yogamāpnoti rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ .. 246 ..
meaning:
कृत्वा पुष्पगृहं विष्णोः पुष्पैर्वाथ वितानकम् ..
फलेन योगमाप्नोति राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः .. 246 ..
text_mt: Having made a house of flowers for Viṣṇu, or indeed a canopy with flowers, / one attains union with the fruit of both the Rājasūya and the horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṅkiṇījālasaṃyuktaṃ devarāmāgaṇojvalam ..
vīṇāmurajagītāḍhyaṃ vimānamadhirohati .. 247 ..
meaning:
किङ्किणीजालसंयुक्तं देवरामागणोज्वलम् ..
वीणामुरजगीताढ्यं विमानमधिरोहति .. 247 ..
text_mt: Furnished with a network of small bells, resplendent with a host of heavenly maidens, / and filled with lutes, clay drums, and singing, he ascends an aerial chariot.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpapradānaṃ maṅgalyamalakṣmīvipraṇāśanam ..
lakṣmīvṛddhikaraṃ jñeyaṃ saumanasyavivarddhanam .. 248 ..
meaning:
पुष्पप्रदानं मङ्गल्यमलक्ष्मीविप्रणाशनम् ..
लक्ष्मीवृद्धिकरं ज्ञेयं सौमनस्यविवर्द्धनम् .. 248 ..
text_mt: The gift of flowers is auspicious and destructive of misfortune; / it is known to cause increase of prosperity and to promote cheerfulness of mind.

sanskrit_iast:
saubhāgyajananaṃ caiva tejobalavivṛddhidam ..
na ratnairna suvarṇena na ca vittena bhūriṇā .. 249 ..
meaning:
सौभाग्यजननं चैव तेजोबलविवृद्धिदम् ..
न रत्नैर्न सुवर्णेन न च वित्तेन भूरिणा .. 249 ..
text_mt: It produces good fortune and bestows increase of splendour and strength. / Not by gems, not by gold, nor by abundant wealth

sanskrit_iast:
tathā prasādamāyāti yathā puṣpairjanārdanaḥ ..
vāsantīmallikāpuṣpaṃ tathā ca vārṣike ca vā .. 3.341.250 ..
meaning:
तथा प्रसादमायाति यथा पुष्पैर्जनार्दनः ..
वासन्तीमल्लिकापुष्पं तथा च वार्षिके च वा .. 3.341.250 ..
text_mt: does Janārdana become so pleased as with flowers: / the spring jasmine flower, and likewise [flowers] of the rainy season,

sanskrit_iast:
kupyakaṃ yūthikā caiva tathā caivātimuktakam ..
ketakīṃ campakaṃ caiva māṣavṛṇakameva ca .. 251 ..
meaning:
कुप्यकं यूथिका चैव तथा चैवातिमुक्तकम् ..
केतकीं चम्पकं चैव माषवृणकमेव च .. 251 ..
text_mt: the kupyaka and the yūthikā, and likewise the atimuktaka, / the ketakī, the campaka, and also the māṣavṛṇaka,

sanskrit_iast:
purandhramañjarīpuṣpaṃ cūtapuṣpaṃ tathaiva ca ..
bandhujīvakapuṣpaṃ ca kusumaṃ kuṅkumasya ca .. 252 ..
meaning:
पुरन्ध्रमञ्जरीपुष्पं चूतपुष्पं तथैव च ..
बन्धुजीवकपुष्पं च कुसुमं कुङ्कुमस्य च .. 252 ..
text_mt: the blossom of the purandhra-cluster, and likewise the mango blossom, / the bandhujīvaka flower, and the blossom of saffron,

sanskrit_iast:
jātīpuṣpāṇi sarvāṇi kundapuṣpaṃ tathaiva ca ..
pāṭalī ca tathā vṛttānnīlamindīvaraṃ tathā .. 253 ..
meaning:
जातीपुष्पाणि सर्वाणि कुन्दपुष्पं तथैव च ..
पाटली च तथा वृत्तान्नीलमिन्दीवरं तथा .. 253 ..
text_mt: all varieties of jātī flowers, and likewise the kunda flower, / the pāṭalī, and likewise blue water lilies from round [ponds],

sanskrit_iast:
kumudaṃ śvetaraktaṃ ca śvetaraktau tathā śubhau ..
evamādīni puṣpāṇi dātavyāni sadā hareḥ .. 254 ..
meaning:
कुमुदं श्वेतरक्तं च श्वेतरक्तौ तथा शुभौ ..
एवमादीनि पुष्पाणि दातव्यानि सदा हरेः .. 254 ..
text_mt: the white and red kumuda, and the two auspicious [lotuses], white and red. / Such flowers as these should always be given to Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
svayamāhṛtya yo dadyādāraṇyakusumāni ca ..
sa rājyaṃ sphītamāpnoti loke nihatakaṇṭakam .. 255..
meaning:
स्वयमाहृत्य यो दद्यादारण्यकुसुमानि च ..
स राज्यं स्फीतमाप्नोति लोके निहतकण्टकम् .. 255..
text_mt: He who, having gathered them himself, offers wild flowers / attains a prosperous kingdom in the world with its thorns destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
patraṃ ramyaṃ phalaṃ ramyaṃ pallavaṃ vā dvijottamāḥ ..
bhaktyā nivedya devāya phalasyānantyamaśnute .. 356 ..
meaning:
पत्रं रम्यं फलं रम्यं पल्लवं वा द्विजोत्तमाः ..
भक्त्या निवेद्य देवाय फलस्यानन्त्यमश्नुते .. 356 ..
text_mt: A lovely leaf, a lovely fruit, or a sprout, O best of twice-born, / offering [these] with devotion to the god, one enjoys an endless reward.

sanskrit_iast:
karpūrabodhitānīva paṭṭavāsāṃsi yo naraḥ ..
dadāti devadevāya sośvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 257 ..
meaning:
कर्पूरबोधितानीव पट्टवासांसि यो नरः ..
ददाति देवदेवाय सोश्वमेधफलं लभेत् .. 257 ..
text_mt: That man who gives fine silk garments / as if perfumed with camphor to the god of gods obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
paṭṭavāsāṃsi mukhyāni dattvā svargamupāśnute ..
yaśaścāpnoti vipulaṃ nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate .. 258 ..
meaning:
पट्टवासांसि मुख्यानि दत्त्वा स्वर्गमुपाश्नुते ..
यशश्चाप्नोति विपुलं नाकपृष्ठे महीयते .. 258 ..
text_mt: Having given the foremost silk garments, one reaches heaven; / he gains extensive renown and is honoured upon the dome of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā saubhāgyamāpnoti paṭṭavāsaprado naraḥ ..
yūpenābhyarcya deveśaṃ svargaloke mahīyate..259..
meaning:
तथा सौभाग्यमाप्नोति पट्टवासप्रदो नरः ..
यूपेनाभ्यर्च्य देवेशं स्वर्गलोके महीयते..259..
text_mt: Likewise, the man who gives silk garments attains good fortune. / Having worshipped the lord of gods with a sacrificial post, he is honoured in the world of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpānāmuttamaṃ dhūpaṃ guggulaṃ kṣaudrasarpimat..
dattvā guggulujaṃ dhūpaṃ nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate ..3.341.260..
meaning:
धूपानामुत्तमं धूपं गुग्गुलं क्षौद्रसर्पिमत्..
दत्त्वा गुग्गुलुजं धूपं नाकपृष्ठे महीयते ..3.341.260..
text_mt: The best incense among incenses is guggulu mixed with honey and clarified butter. / Having given incense derived from guggulu, one is honoured upon the dome of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
madhusarpiḥsamāyuktaṃ dvādaśāhātphalaṃ labhet ..
dattvā candanasāreṇa saubhāgyaṃ paramāpnuyāt ..261..
meaning:
मधुसर्पिःसमायुक्तं द्वादशाहात्फलं लभेत् ..
दत्त्वा चन्दनसारेण सौभाग्यं परमाप्नुयात् ..261..
text_mt: Combined with honey and clarified butter, one obtains the fruit of a twelve-day sacrifice. / Having given [incense] with the essence of sandalwood, one attains supreme good fortune;

sanskrit_iast:
tathaivāgurusāreṇa parāṃ siddhimavāpnuyāt ..
dhūpānāmuttamaṃ tadvatsarvakāmaphalapradam .. ..262..
meaning:
तथैवागुरुसारेण परां सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ..
धूपानामुत्तमं तद्वत्सर्वकामफलप्रदम् .. ..262..
text_mt: likewise, with the essence of agallochum, one attains supreme perfection. / In the same way, the best among incenses bestows the fruit of all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpaṃ turuṣkakaṃ dattvā vahniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet ..
dattvā ca kṛtrimaṃ mukhyaṃ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..263..
meaning:
धूपं तुरुष्ककं दत्त्वा वह्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् ..
दत्त्वा च कृत्रिमं मुख्यं सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ..263..
text_mt: Having given turuṣkaka incense, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma; / and having given artificial [incense] of the highest quality, one attains all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
gandhayuktikṛtaṃ dattvā yajñaṃ gosavamāpnuyāt ..
dattvā karpūraniryāsaṃ vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 264 ..
meaning:
गन्धयुक्तिकृतं दत्त्वा यज्ञं गोसवमाप्नुयात् ..
दत्त्वा कर्पूरनिर्यासं वाजिमेधफलं लभेत् .. 264 ..
text_mt: Having given [incense] prepared according to the art of perfumery, one attains the Gosava sacrifice. / Having given camphor resin, one obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
vasante gugguluṃ datvā vahniṣṭomamavāpnuyāt ..
grīṣme candanasāreṇa dvādaśāhātphalaṃ labhet ..265..
meaning:
वसन्ते गुग्गुलुं दत्वा वह्निष्टोममवाप्नुयात् ..
ग्रीष्मे चन्दनसारेण द्वादशाहात्फलं लभेत् ..265..
text_mt: Having given guggulu in spring, one attains an Agniṣṭoma. / In summer, with the essence of sandalwood, one obtains the fruit of a twelve-day sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
turuṣkadānena tathā prāvṛṣyamaratāṃ vrajet ..
karpūradānāccharadi rājasūyamavāpnuyāt .. 266 ..
meaning:
तुरुष्कदानेन तथा प्रावृष्यमरतां व्रजेत् ..
कर्पूरदानाच्छरदि राजसूयमवाप्नुयात् .. 266 ..
text_mt: Likewise, by the gift of turuṣka in the rainy season, one attains immortality. / By the gift of camphor in autumn, one attains a Rājasūya.

sanskrit_iast:
hemante mṛgadarpeṇa vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet ..
śiśire'gurusāreṇa sarvamedhamavāpnuyāt .. 267 ..
meaning:
हेमन्ते मृगदर्पेण वाजिमेधफलं लभेत् ..
शिशिरेऽगुरुसारेण सर्वमेधमवाप्नुयात् .. 267 ..
text_mt: In winter, with musk, one obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice. / In the dewy season, with the essence of agallochum, one attains a Sarvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
vinā mṛgamadāddhūpaṃ jīvajātaṃ vivarjayet ..
dhūpadaḥ svargamāpnoti dhūpadaḥ puṣṭimaśnute ...268..
meaning:
विना मृगमदाद्धूपं जीवजातं विवर्जयेत् ..
धूपदः स्वर्गमाप्नोति धूपदः पुष्टिमश्नुते ...268..
text_mt: Except for musk, one should avoid incense of animal origin. / The giver of incense attains heaven; the giver of incense enjoys nourishment.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpalekhā yathaivordhvaṃ nityameva prasarpati ..
tathaivordhvagatiṃ nityaṃ dhūpadātā bhavennaraḥ ..269..
meaning:
धूपलेखा यथैवोर्ध्वं नित्यमेव प्रसर्पति ..
तथैवोर्ध्वगतिं नित्यं धूपदाता भवेन्नरः ..269..
text_mt: Just as the stream of incense always rises upwards, / even so a man who is a giver of incense constantly has an upward course.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūparājiryadordhvaṃ syādekādīnāṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
sannidhānaṃ tathā vidyāddevadevasya cakriṇaḥ..3.341.270..
meaning:
धूपराजिर्यदोर्ध्वं स्यादेकादीनां द्विजोत्तमाः ..
सन्निधानं तथा विद्याद्देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः..3.341.270..
text_mt: When the line of incense rises straight upwards, O best of twice-born, / one should know that to be the presence of the god of gods who bears the discus.

sanskrit_iast:
dīpaṃ cakṣuḥpradaṃ dadyāttathaivordhvagatipradam ..
urdhvaṃ yathā dhūpaśikhā dātā cordhvagatistathā ..271..
meaning:
दीपं चक्षुःप्रदं दद्यात्तथैवोर्ध्वगतिप्रदम् ..
उर्ध्वं यथा धूपशिखा दाता चोर्ध्वगतिस्तथा ..271..
text_mt: One should give a lamp, which bestows sight and likewise bestows an upward course. / As the flame of incense goes upward, so the giver has an upward course;

sanskrit_iast:
khyāto bhavati lokeṣu svargalokaṃ ca gacchati ..
yāvadakṣinimeṣāṇi dīpo devālaye jvalet .. 272 ..
meaning:
ख्यातो भवति लोकेषु स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति ..
यावदक्षिनिमेषाणि दीपो देवालये ज्वलेत् .. 272 ..
text_mt: he becomes celebrated among the worlds and goes to the world of heaven. / For as many twinklings of an eye as the lamp burns in the god's temple,

sanskrit_iast:
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi dharmātmā lokamaśnute ..
mahāvartipradānena kule deśe tathaiva ca .. 273 ..
meaning:
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि धर्मात्मा लोकमश्नुते ..
महावर्तिप्रदानेन कुले देशे तथैव च .. 273 ..
text_mt: for that many thousands of years the righteous soul enjoys the [heavenly] realm. / By the offering of a large wick in his family and in his country,

sanskrit_iast:
śraiṣṭhyamāpnoti sarvatra yathā sarvaṃ virājate ..
madhuparkapradānena paraṃ padamihāśnute ..274..
meaning:
श्रैष्ठ्यमाप्नोति सर्वत्र यथा सर्वं विराजते ..
मधुपर्कप्रदानेन परं पदमिहाश्नुते ..274..
text_mt: he attains pre-eminence everywhere, just as everything shines brightly. / By the offering of madhuparka, one enjoys the supreme state here [and hereafter].

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtaṃ dadhi tathā kṣaudraṃ madhuparkaṃ vijānatā ..
tatastvarhaṇadānena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 275 ..
meaning:
घृतं दधि तथा क्षौद्रं मधुपर्कं विजानता ..
ततस्त्वर्हणदानेन सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 275 ..
text_mt: [Offering] clarified butter, curd, and honey as madhuparka with understanding, / and then by giving worshipful offerings, one is liberated from all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
tathaivācamanīyasya dānādbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
anantatṛptimāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati .. 276 ..
meaning:
तथैवाचमनीयस्य दानाद्ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ..
अनन्ततृप्तिमाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति .. 276 ..
text_mt: Likewise, from the gift of water for sipping, O best of brahmins, / one attains endless satisfaction and goes to the world of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
dattvā cāsaṃvibhāgāya tathaivānnamatandritaḥ ..
trailokyatarpite puṇyaṃ tatkṣaṇātsamavāpnuyāt .. 277 ...
meaning:
दत्त्वा चासंविभागाय तथैवान्नमतन्द्रितः ..
त्रैलोक्यतर्पिते पुण्यं तत्क्षणात्समवाप्नुयात् .. 277 ...
text_mt: And having given food without withholding, unwearied, / one immediately attains the merit of having satisfied the three worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣayyamannadānaṃ ca pitṝṃstasyopatiṣṭhate ..
odanaṃ vyañjanopetaṃ dattvā svargamavāpnuyāt .. 278 ..
meaning:
अक्षय्यमन्नदानं च पितॄंस्तस्योपतिष्ठते ..
ओदनं व्यञ्जनोपेतं दत्त्वा स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् .. 278 ..
text_mt: And an imperishable gift of food accrues to his ancestors. / Having given boiled rice accompanied by condiments, one attains heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
paramānnapradānena tṛptiṃ vindati śāśvatīm ..
viṣṇulokamavāpnoti kulamuddharati svakam .. 279 ..
meaning:
परमान्नप्रदानेन तृप्तिं विन्दति शाश्वतीम् ..
विष्णुलोकमवाप्नोति कुलमुद्धरति स्वकम् .. 279 ..
text_mt: By the offering of milk-rice, one finds everlasting satisfaction; / he attains the world of Viṣṇu and uplifts his own lineage.

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtaudanapradānena dīrghamāyuravāpnuyāt ..
dadhyodanapradānena śriyamāpnotyanuttamām .. 3.341.280..
meaning:
घृतौदनप्रदानेन दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ..
दध्योदनप्रदानेन श्रियमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् .. 3.341.280..
text_mt: By the offering of rice with clarified butter, one attains long life. / By the offering of rice with curd, one attains unsurpassable splendour.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīraudanapradānena dīrghaṃ jīvitamāpnuyāta ..
ikṣūṇāṃ caiva dānena paraṃ saubhāgyamāpnuyāt ..281..
meaning:
क्षीरौदनप्रदानेन दीर्घं जीवितमाप्नुयात ..
इक्षूणां चैव दानेन परं सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् ..281..
text_mt: By the offering of rice with milk, one attains a long life. / And by the gift of sugarcanes, one attains supreme good fortune;

sanskrit_iast:
rasānāṃ caiva bhāgī syātsvargalokaṃ ca gacchati ..
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti kṣaudraṃ yastu prayacchati .. 282 ..
meaning:
रसानां चैव भागी स्यात्स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति ..
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति क्षौद्रं यस्तु प्रयच्छति .. 282 ..
text_mt: he becomes a partaker of delights and goes to the world of heaven. / But he who offers honey attains all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
tadeva tuhinopetaṃ rājasūyamavāpnuyāt ..
phāṇitasya pradānena vahnayādeyaṃ phalaṃ labhet .. 283 ..
meaning:
तदेव तुहिनोपेतं राजसूयमवाप्नुयात् ..
फाणितस्य प्रदानेन वह्नयादेयं फलं लभेत् .. 283 ..
text_mt: If it is mixed with camphor, one attains a Rājasūya. / By the gift of inspissated sugar-juice, one obtains the reward of the Agnyādheya [rite].

sanskrit_iast:
tathā guḍapradānena daśagodo bhavennaraḥ ..
mukhyaṃ daṇḍaṃ tathā dattvā maitrīṃ sarveṇa vindati .. 284 ..
meaning:
तथा गुडप्रदानेन दशगोदो भवेन्नरः ..
मुख्यं दण्डं तथा दत्त्वा मैत्रीं सर्वेण विन्दति .. 284 ..
text_mt: Likewise, by the gift of jaggery, a man becomes an owner of ten cows. / And having given a prime stalk [of sugarcane], he finds friendship with everyone.

sanskrit_iast:
strīṣu vallabhatāmeti dattvā ca guḍikāṃ tathā ..
sitāyāśca pradānena sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 285 ..
meaning:
स्त्रीषु वल्लभतामेति दत्त्वा च गुडिकां तथा ..
सितायाश्च प्रदानेन सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् .. 285 ..
text_mt: And having given a ball of jaggery, he attains love among women. / And by the gift of refined white sugar, one attains all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
nivedyekṣurasaṃ bhaktyā paraṃ saubhāgyamāpnuyāta ..
vahniṣṭomamavāpnoti yāvakasya nivedakaḥ .. 286 ..
meaning:
निवेद्येक्षुरसं भक्त्या परं सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात ..
वह्निष्टोममवाप्नोति यावकस्य निवेदकः .. 286 ..
text_mt: Having offered sugarcane juice with devotion, one attains supreme good fortune. / One who offers barley porridge attains an Agniṣṭoma.

sanskrit_iast:
atirātramavāpnoti tathā dhūpanivedakaḥ ..
vaidalānāṃ ca bhakṣyāṇāṃ dānātkāmamavāpnuyāta .. 287 ..
meaning:
अतिरात्रमवाप्नोति तथा धूपनिवेदकः ..
वैदलानां च भक्ष्याणां दानात्काममवाप्नुयात .. 287 ..
text_mt: Likewise, one who offers incense attains an Atirātra sacrifice. / And from the gift of pastries made of split pulses, one attains one's desire.

sanskrit_iast:
dīrghajīvitamāpnoti ghṛtapūranivedakaḥ ..
modakānāṃ pradānena kāmānāpnotyabhīpsitān .. 288..
meaning:
दीर्घजीवितमाप्नोति घृतपूरनिवेदकः ..
मोदकानां प्रदानेन कामानाप्नोत्यभीप्सितान् .. 288..
text_mt: One who offers sweets fried in clarified butter attains a long life. / By the gift of sweet dumplings, one attains desired wishes.

sanskrit_iast:
nānāvidhānāṃ bhakṣyāṇāṃ dānātsvargamavāpnuyāt ..
rāgaṣāṃḍavadānena pauṇḍarīkamavāpnuyāt .. 289 ..
meaning:
नानाविधानां भक्ष्याणां दानात्स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् ..
रागषांडवदानेन पौण्डरीकमवाप्नुयात् .. 289 ..
text_mt: By giving various kinds of foods, one would attain heaven. / By giving rāga and ṣāḍava drinks, one would attain [the reward of] a Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
bhojanīyapradānena tṛptimāpnotyanuttamām ..
tathā lehyapradānena saubhāgyamadhigacchati .. 3.341.290 ..
meaning:
भोजनीयप्रदानेन तृप्तिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ..
तथा लेह्यप्रदानेन सौभाग्यमधिगच्छति .. 3.341.290 ..
text_mt: By giving edible meals, one attains unsurpassable satisfaction; / likewise, by giving foods to be licked, one obtains good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
balavarṇamavāpnoti coṣyāṇāṃ vinivedakaḥ ..
peyānāṃ ca pradānena tṛptimāpnotyanuttamām ..291..
meaning:
बलवर्णमवाप्नोति चोष्याणां विनिवेदकः ..
पेयानां च प्रदानेन तृप्तिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ..291..
text_mt: One who offers suckable foods attains strength and complexion, / and by giving beverages, one attains unsurpassable satisfaction.

sanskrit_iast:
pānakāni sugandhīni śītalāni viśeṣataḥ ..
nivedya devadevāya vājimedhamavāpnuyāt .. 292 ..
meaning:
पानकानि सुगन्धीनि शीतलानि विशेषतः ..
निवेद्य देवदेवाय वाजिमेधमवाप्नुयात् .. 292 ..
text_mt: Having offered fragrant drinks, especially cooling ones, / to the God of gods, one would attain [the merit of] a horse sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
tvagelānāgakusumakarpūrasitasaṃyutaiḥ ..
sitākṣaudraguḍopetairgandhavarṇasamanvitaiḥ .. 293 ..
meaning:
त्वगेलानागकुसुमकर्पूरसितसंयुतैः ..
सिताक्षौद्रगुडोपेतैर्गन्धवर्णसमन्वितैः .. 293 ..
text_mt: With [drinks] blended with cinnamon, cardamom, nāgapuṣpa flowers, camphor, and refined sugar, / accompanied by white sugar, honey, and molasses, and endowed with fragrance and color—

sanskrit_iast:
rājasūyamavāpnoti pānakairviniveditaiḥ ..
nivedya nālikerāmbu vahniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet .. 294 ..
meaning:
राजसूयमवाप्नोति पानकैर्विनिवेदितैः ..
निवेद्य नालिकेराम्बु वह्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् .. 294 ..
text_mt: through such offered sweet drinks, one attains [the fruit of] a Rājasūya. / Having offered coconut water, one obtains the fruit of a Vahniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
dhānyānāṃ kṣaudrayuktānāṃ lājānāṃ ca nivedakaḥ ..
mukhyānāṃ caiva saktūnāṃ vahniṣṭomamavāpnuyāt .. 295 ..
meaning:
धान्यानां क्षौद्रयुक्तानां लाजानां च निवेदकः ..
मुख्यानां चैव सक्तूनां वह्निष्टोममवाप्नुयात् .. 295 ..
text_mt: One who offers grains combined with honey, parched rice, / and foremost barley meals, would attain [the fruit of] a Vahniṣṭoma.

sanskrit_iast:
vānaprasthāśritaṃ puṇyaṃ labhecchākanivedakaḥ ..
dattvā haritakaṃ caiva tadeva phalamāpnuyāt ... 296 ..
meaning:
वानप्रस्थाश्रितं पुण्यं लभेच्छाकनिवेदकः ..
दत्त्वा हरितकं चैव तदेव फलमाप्नुयात् ... 296 ..
text_mt: One who offers greens obtains the merit associated with forest-dwellers; / and having given fresh vegetables, one obtains that very same fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
sukule prāpnuyājjanma kandamūlanivedakaḥ ..
nīlotpalavidārīṇāṃ tarūṭasya tathā dvijāḥ .. 297 ..
meaning:
सुकुले प्राप्नुयाज्जन्म कन्दमूलनिवेदकः ..
नीलोत्पलविदारीणां तरूटस्य तथा द्विजाः .. 297 ..
text_mt: One who offers bulbous tubers and roots attains birth in a noble family; / [by the offering] of blue water-lilies, vidārī, and likewise tarūṭa, O twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
kaṃdadānādavāpnoti vānaprasthaphalaṃ labhet ..
trapuñca cārukaṃ dattvā puṇḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet .. 298 ..
meaning:
कंददानादवाप्नोति वानप्रस्थफलं लभेत् ..
त्रपुञ्च चारुकं दत्त्वा पुण्डरीकफलं लभेत् .. 298 ..
text_mt: by giving bulbs one attains and obtains the fruit of a forest-dweller. / Having given cucumbers and cāruka, one obtains the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
karkandhubadarau dattvā tathā pālevataṃ dhavam ..
pārūṣakaṃ tathā proktaṃ panasaṃ nārikelakam .. 299 ..
meaning:
कर्कन्धुबदरौ दत्त्वा तथा पालेवतं धवम् ..
पारूषकं तथा प्रोक्तं पनसं नारिकेलकम् .. 299 ..
text_mt: Having given karkandhu and jujube fruits, and likewise pālevata, dhava, / pārūṣaka, as well as jackfruit and coconut,

sanskrit_iast:
bhavyaṃ mocaṃ tathā caucaṃ kharjūramatha dāḍimam ..
āmrakādiṣu cākṣoṭamāranālapriyālujam .. 3.341.300 ..
meaning:
भव्यं मोचं तथा चौचं खर्जूरमथ दाडिमम् ..
आम्रकादिषु चाक्षोटमारनालप्रियालुजम् .. 3.341.300 ..
text_mt: bhavya, plantain, and cauca, dates, and pomegranate, / walnuts among mango and other [trees], and [the fruit] born of the āranāla and priyāla,

sanskrit_iast:
jāmbū bilvāmale caiva jātyaśrīnārukastathā ..
nāraṅgabījapūrau ca rājaphalguphalānyapi .. 301 ..
meaning:
जाम्बू बिल्वामले चैव जात्यश्रीनारुकस्तथा ..
नारङ्गबीजपूरौ च राजफल्गुफलान्यपि .. 301 ..
text_mt: rose-apple, bilva, and myrobalan, and genuine śrīnāruka, / orange and citron, and royal fig fruits,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā phalgūni mukhyāni devadevāya bhaktitaḥ ..
evamādīni cānyāni yaḥ phalāni prayacchati ..302..
meaning:
तथा फल्गूनि मुख्यानि देवदेवाय भक्तितः ..
एवमादीनि चान्यानि यः फलानि प्रयच्छति ..302..
text_mt: likewise excellent figs, to the God of gods with devotion— / he who offers these and other such fruits

sanskrit_iast:
kriyāsāphalyamāpnoti svargalokaṃ tathaiva ca ..
udumbaraṃ kapitthaṃ ca tathā dantaśaṭhaṃ ca yat .. 303 ..
meaning:
क्रियासाफल्यमाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं तथैव च ..
उदुम्बरं कपित्थं च तथा दन्तशठं च यत् .. 303 ..
text_mt: attains success in his rites and likewise the heavenly world. / The cluster fig, the wood-apple, and that which is dantaśaṭha—

sanskrit_iast:
evamādīni devāya na deyāni kadācana ..
prāpnoti balamārogyaṃ mṛdvīkāvinivedakaḥ ..304 ..
meaning:
एवमादीनि देवाय न देयानि कदाचन ..
प्राप्नोति बलमारोग्यं मृद्वीकाविनिवेदकः ..304 ..
text_mt: such as these should never be given to the God. / An offerer of raisins attains strength and health;

sanskrit_iast:
rasānmukhyānavāpnoti saubhāgyamapi cottamam ..
āmrairabhyarcya deveśamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet.. 305 ..
meaning:
रसान्मुख्यानवाप्नोति सौभाग्यमपि चोत्तमम् ..
आम्रैरभ्यर्च्य देवेशमश्वमेधफलं लभेत्.. 305 ..
text_mt: he obtains foremost savors and also supreme good fortune. / Having worshipped the Lord of gods with mangoes, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
pūgajātīphale dattvā jātīpatraṃ tathaiva ca ..
lavaṅgamatha kaṅkolamelāṃ kaṭuphalaṃ tathā .. 306 ..
meaning:
पूगजातीफले दत्त्वा जातीपत्रं तथैव च ..
लवङ्गमथ कङ्कोलमेलां कटुफलं तथा .. 306 ..
text_mt: Having given betel nut and nutmeg, and likewise mace, / clove, cubeb, cardamom, and kaṭuphala,

sanskrit_iast:
tāmbūlīnāṃ kisalayaṃ svargalokamavāpnuyāt ..
saubhāgyamuttamaṃ loke tathā rūpamanuttamam .. 307 ..
meaning:
ताम्बूलीनां किसलयं स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात् ..
सौभाग्यमुत्तमं लोके तथा रूपमनुत्तमम् .. 307 ..
text_mt: and the sprout of betel vines, one would attain the world of heaven, / supreme good fortune in the world, and unsurpassed beauty.

sanskrit_iast:
mukhavāsapradānena strīṇāṃ vallabhatāṃ vrajet ..
mātrāṇāṃ ca pradānena narakaṃ naiva gacchati .. 308 ..
meaning:
मुखवासप्रदानेन स्त्रीणां वल्लभतां व्रजेत् ..
मात्राणां च प्रदानेन नरकं नैव गच्छति .. 308 ..
text_mt: By giving mouth-perfumes, one becomes beloved to women; / and by giving small portions, one does not go to hell at all.

sanskrit_iast:
mātrābhiḥ pūrayedbhojyāṃstathā bhakṣyānasambhave ..
yatkiñcidbhaktisaṃyukto devadeve prayacchati .. 309 ..
meaning:
मात्राभिः पूरयेद्भोज्यांस्तथा भक्ष्यानसम्भवे ..
यत्किञ्चिद्भक्तिसंयुक्तो देवदेवे प्रयच्छति .. 309 ..
text_mt: With small portions one should fill cooked foods and solid foods when [abundance is] absent. / Whatever one, endowed with devotion, offers to the God of gods,

sanskrit_iast:
tadevākṣayyamāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati ..
na devastoṣamāyāti prabhūtairdhanasañcayaiḥ .. 3.341.310 ..
meaning:
तदेवाक्षय्यमाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति ..
न देवस्तोषमायाति प्रभूतैर्धनसञ्चयैः .. 3.341.310 ..
text_mt: that very thing becomes inexhaustible, and he goes to the heavenly world. / The God does not reach contentment through vast accumulations of wealth,

sanskrit_iast:
yathā toṣamavāpnoti bhaktyā bhaktajanapriyaḥ ..
bhaktyā kāmānavāpnoti bhaktyā svargaṃ ca gacchati .. 311 ..
meaning:
यथा तोषमवाप्नोति भक्त्या भक्तजनप्रियः ..
भक्त्या कामानवाप्नोति भक्त्या स्वर्गं च गच्छति .. 311 ..
text_mt: as he, who loves devoted souls, attains contentment through devotion. / Through devotion one attains one's desires, and through devotion one goes to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
bhaktyā tatpadamāpnoti yatra gatvā na śocati ..
sāmānyabhaktyā yaddattaṃ taddhi padbhyāṃ prayacchati .. 312 ..
meaning:
भक्त्या तत्पदमाप्नोति यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ..
सामान्यभक्त्या यद्दत्तं तद्धि पद्भ्यां प्रयच्छति .. 312 ..
text_mt: Through devotion one attains that state, having gone to which one does not grieve. / What is given with ordinary devotion, he accepts with his feet;

sanskrit_iast:
ekāntabhāvopagamairmūrdhnā dvijavarottamāḥ ..
śvetena vastrayugmena tathā muktāphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. .. 313 ..
meaning:
एकान्तभावोपगमैर्मूर्ध्ना द्विजवरोत्तमाः ..
श्वेतेन वस्त्रयुग्मेन तथा मुक्ताफलैः शुभैः .. .. 313 ..
text_mt: [what is given] by those who have attained single-minded devotion, [he accepts] with his head, O foremost among the best of the twice-born. / With a pair of white garments and auspicious pearls,

sanskrit_iast:
mukhyakarpūradhūpena payasā pāyasena ca ..
padmasūtrasya vartyā ca ghṛtadhūpena cāpyatha .. 314 ..
meaning:
मुख्यकर्पूरधूपेन पयसा पायसेन च ..
पद्मसूत्रस्य वर्त्या च घृतधूपेन चाप्यथ .. 314 ..
text_mt: with incense of choice camphor, with milk and milk-rice, / with a wick of lotus-fiber, and also with incense of ghee,

sanskrit_iast:
pūjayansarvaśuklā syātsarvakāmapradā śivā ..
kṛtvemāṃ mucyate rogī rogācchīghramasaṃśayam ..315..
meaning:
पूजयन्सर्वशुक्ला स्यात्सर्वकामप्रदा शिवा ..
कृत्वेमां मुच्यते रोगी रोगाच्छीघ्रमसंशयम् ..315..
text_mt: worshipping [him], [the rite] should be completely white, granting all desires, and auspicious. / Having performed this, a sick person is swiftly freed from disease, without doubt;

sanskrit_iast:
duḥkhārto mucyate duḥkhādbaddho mucyeta bandhanāt ..
rājagrastaśca mucyeta tathā rājabhayānnaraḥ .. ..316..
meaning:
दुःखार्तो मुच्यते दुःखाद्बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात् ..
राजग्रस्तश्च मुच्येत तथा राजभयान्नरः .. ..316..
text_mt: one afflicted with sorrow is freed from sorrow; one bound is freed from bondage; / and a man seized by a king is freed from fear of the king.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣemeṇa gacchedadhvānaṃ tathānarthavivarjitaḥ ..
tailena snāpitaṃ devaṃ kuṅkumenānulepayet .. 317 ..
meaning:
क्षेमेण गच्छेदध्वानं तथानर्थविवर्जितः ..
तैलेन स्नापितं देवं कुङ्कुमेनानुलेपयेत् .. 317 ..
text_mt: He would travel the road safely and be free from misfortune. / Having bathed the God with oil, one should anoint him with saffron.

sanskrit_iast:
raktairvastraiḥ samabhyarcya vidrumaiśca tathā naraḥ ..
bandhujīvakapuṣpaiśca dhūpenāgurujena ca .. 316 ..
meaning:
रक्तैर्वस्त्रैः समभ्यर्च्य विद्रुमैश्च तथा नरः ..
बन्धुजीवकपुष्पैश्च धूपेनागुरुजेन च .. 316 ..
text_mt: Having worshipped him with red garments, and corals as well, a man, / with bandhujīvaka flowers, and incense made from agallochum,

sanskrit_iast:
tailadīpena vartyā ca mahārajataraktayā ..
drākṣāpānakayuktena vaṭakaiḥ kṛsareṇa ca .. 319 ..
meaning:
तैलदीपेन वर्त्या च महारजतरक्तया ..
द्राक्षापानकयुक्तेन वटकैः कृसरेण च .. 319 ..
text_mt: with an oil lamp and a wick dyed with safflower, / with [a drink] mixed with grape-juice, with fried cakes, and with kṛsara,

sanskrit_iast:
pūjayetsarvaraktā syācchatrupakṣakṣayaṅkarī ..
saubhāgyajananī loke dhanadhānyavivarddhanī .. 3.341.320 ..
meaning:
पूजयेत्सर्वरक्ता स्याच्छत्रुपक्षक्षयङ्करी ..
सौभाग्यजननी लोके धनधान्यविवर्द्धनी .. 3.341.320 ..
text_mt: one should worship him; [the rite] should be completely red, bringing destruction to the enemy's faction, / producing good fortune in the world, increasing wealth and grain,

sanskrit_iast:
svargadā phaladā caiva naranārīvaśaṅkarī ..
evaṃ dānaphalaṃ proktaṃ rājasānāṃ mayā dvijāḥ..321..
meaning:
स्वर्गदा फलदा चैव नरनारीवशङ्करी ..
एवं दानफलं प्रोक्तं राजसानां मया द्विजाः..321..
text_mt: granting heaven, granting fruits, and subduing men and women. / Thus the fruit of giving for passionate persons has been proclaimed by me, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
akāmaḥ sāttvike loke yatkiñcidvinivedayet ..
tenaiva sthānamāpnoti yatra gatvā na śocati ..322..
meaning:
अकामः सात्त्विके लोके यत्किञ्चिद्विनिवेदयेत् ..
तेनैव स्थानमाप्नोति यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ..322..
text_mt: Whatever one without desire offers in a pure state of mind, / by that alone he attains the place, having gone to which one does not grieve.

sanskrit_iast:
dharma vācanikā mūḍhāḥ phalakāmā narādhamāḥ ..
yercayanti jagannāthaṃ te kāmānprāpnuvantyatha .. 323 ..
meaning:
धर्म वाचनिका मूढाः फलकामा नराधमाः ..
येर्चयन्ति जगन्नाथं ते कामान्प्राप्नुवन्त्यथ .. 323 ..
text_mt: Fools who profess dharma merely in words, base men desiring rewards, / who worship the Lord of the world—they merely attain their desires.

sanskrit_iast:
antavattu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tadbhavatyalpamedhasām ..
akāmānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ sāttvikānāṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 324 ..
meaning:
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् ..
अकामानां मनुष्याणां सात्त्विकानां द्विजोत्तमाः .. 324 ..
text_mt: Finite indeed is the fruit of those of small intellect. / For men free from desire who are pure, O best of the twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvaduḥkhavimokṣāya bhavantīyamapi dhruvam ..
ananto bhagavānviṣṇustasya kāmavivarjitaiḥ ... ..325..
meaning:
सर्वदुःखविमोक्षाय भवन्तीयमपि ध्रुवम् ..
अनन्तो भगवान्विष्णुस्तस्य कामविवर्जितैः ... ..325..
text_mt: even this [offering] certainly leads to release from all sorrow. / The Lord Viṣṇu is infinite; by those devoid of desires,

sanskrit_iast:
yadeva dīyate kiñcittadevākṣayyamucyate ..
padbhyāṃ pratīcchate devaḥ sakāmena niveditam .. 326 ..
meaning:
यदेव दीयते किञ्चित्तदेवाक्षय्यमुच्यते ..
पद्भ्यां प्रतीच्छते देवः सकामेन निवेदितम् .. 326 ..
text_mt: whatever little is given to him is declared to be inexhaustible. / The God accepts with his feet what is offered with selfish desire;

sanskrit_iast:
mūrdhnā prapadyate dattamakāmena dvijottamāḥ...
naivedyenātha puṣpairvā vividhairdhanasaṃcayaiḥ .. 327 ..
meaning:
मूर्ध्ना प्रपद्यते दत्तमकामेन द्विजोत्तमाः...
नैवेद्येनाथ पुष्पैर्वा विविधैर्धनसंचयैः .. 327 ..
text_mt: what is given without desire he accepts with his head, O best of the twice-born. / With food offerings, or flowers, or various accumulations of wealth,

sanskrit_iast:
nāsti prayojanaṃ tasya sarvagasyāmitātmanaḥ ..
bhaktyā pratīcchate dattaṃ bhaktānugrahakāraṇāt .. .. 328 ..
meaning:
नास्ति प्रयोजनं तस्य सर्वगस्यामितात्मनः ..
भक्त्या प्रतीच्छते दत्तं भक्तानुग्रहकारणात् .. .. 328 ..
text_mt: there is no need for him, the all-pervading, immeasurable Self; / he accepts what is given with devotion for the sake of blessing his devotees.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmātsarvāsvavasthāsu bhaktirevātra kāraṇam ..
ekāntabhāvopagatāḥ sarvakāmavivarjitāḥ ..329..
meaning:
तस्मात्सर्वास्ववस्थासु भक्तिरेवात्र कारणम् ..
एकान्तभावोपगताः सर्वकामविवर्जिताः ..329..
text_mt: Therefore, in all circumstances, devotion alone is the cause here. / Having attained single-minded devotion, completely free from all desires,

sanskrit_iast:
vaiṣṇavaṃ padamāsādya na nivarteta karhicit..
na bhayaṃ nārakaṃ teṣāṃ na ca vyādhikṛtaṃ bhayam..3.341.330..
meaning:
वैष्णवं पदमासाद्य न निवर्तेत कर्हिचित्..
न भयं नारकं तेषां न च व्याधिकृतं भयम्..3.341.330..
text_mt: having reached the state of Viṣṇu, they never return. / There is no hellish fear for them, nor fear caused by disease,

sanskrit_iast: na vṛttiśatrujaṃ vāpi ye prapannā janārdanam..331..
meaning: न वृत्तिशत्रुजं वापि ये प्रपन्ना जनार्दनम्..331..
text_mt: nor that arising from loss of livelihood or enemies, for those who have taken refuge in Janārdana.

sanskrit_iast:
nivedya bhaktyā madhusūdanāya duracchadaṃ vāpyatha tatprasūnam ..
dūrvāṅkuraṃ vā salilaṃ dvijendrāḥ prāpnoti lokānmanasā yatheṣṭān .. 332 ..
3.342
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
namaste devadeveśa vāsudeva janārdana ..
bhaktānukaṃpa varada puṇḍarīkākṣa suvrata .. 1 ..
brahmaṇya puruṣācintya sṛṣṭisaṃhārakāraka ..
trailokyanātha govinda śaraṇāgatavatsala ... .. 2 ..

3.342
The sages said:
Praise be to you, O lord of the gods of gods, O Vāsudeva, O Janārdana! / O compassionate to devotees, giver of boons, lotus-eyed one, of noble vows!
O friend of brahmins, O Cosmic Person, unthinkable one, maker of creation and destruction! / O protector of the three worlds, Govinda, loving toward those who seek refuge!
O lord of all, O ruler present everywhere, O all-pervading one, praise be to you! / Praise be to you, O lord of the world, O supreme lord of the lords of all worlds!
O dispeller of the gods' distress, O lord of gods, praised by the Grandsire and Hara! / O Viṣṇu, victorious one, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, all-pervading lord whose eyes are the sun and the moon!
O you who resemble a thousand suns, intent on protecting the world! / O you who are primarily the Boar and Narasiṃha, O Vāmana of boundless stride!
O Trivikrama, who with your strides stepped across the boundaries of the universe's sphere! / O you who have struck down the lords of the host of the gods' enemies with the edge of your discus!

O cause of the destruction of all sins simply by being remembered! / O destroyer of the darkness residing in our hearts through the teaching of the scriptures!
O Vaikuṇṭha, who has blunted the strength of all the weapons of the Dānavas, O sinless one! / O you within whose belly all three worlds lie merged!
O you who raised up the earth with a tusk resembling the crescent of the moon! / O Great Boar, who destroyed the great Asura Hiraṇyākṣa!
O you whose claw-tips were reddened with the blood from the chest of the lord of Daityas! / O you who bear the form of Narasiṃha surrounded by garlands of flames! // 3.342.10
O you whose body is variegated by the casting of Lakṣmī's sidelong glances! / O you whose chest is illuminated by the Kaustubha gem, who likewise wear golden garments!
O you who sit upon the seat of the serpent's coils, whose pre-eminent emblem is Tārkṣya! / O protector of the Vedas, having seven necks, resembling a hundred moons!
O you who caused the surface of the earth to increase through the fat of the destroyed Madhu and Kaiṭabha! / O you from the lotus of whose navel the Four-faced One was born, praise be to you!
O you with hands and feet reaching everywhere, with eyes, heads, and faces on all sides! / O endowed with all sense-faculties and qualities, present everywhere, O Puruṣottama!

You are the supreme eye of yogins; you are the supreme refuge of yogins. / And having reached you, yogins never return.
Praise be to you in front, O god, and praise be to you from behind! / Praise be to you across, O god, and praise be to you everywhere!
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus praised by those sages, the sinless Blessed One then / gave a divine eye to those sages of cultivated minds.
They then saw the entire three worlds within the body of that / Viṣṇu of boundless splendour, who had assumed the form of a swan.
Having seen the form of the swan bearing the universal form, those rich in asceticism / bowed their heads and touched the whole earth.
Then, with a sweet voice, the god spoke to them all, / roaring like a thundercloud and a kettledrum, destroying the distress of those who bow down: // 3.342.20
“Arise, O best of the twice-born! Choose a boon, O sinless ones! / Having obtained this fruitful vision, attain what you desire in your mind!”

The sages said:
“Delusion has vanished, memory has been regained, knowledge has been obtained, O Janārdana! / You have been seen in your universal form; what use have we for another boon?
Even so, O lord of gods, if a boon is to be given to us by you, / may our devotion to you be uninterrupted always, O Janārdana!
And whoever reads this supreme dialogue of ours with you, / may he likewise obtain liberation from all sins.
May the sick be freed from disease, the terrified from fear, and the bound from bondage! / May he who desires dharma obtain dharma, and may he who desires wealth obtain wealth!
May he who desires pleasures obtain pleasures, and may he who desires liberation obtain liberation! / And whatever wise man retains this, he goes to the supreme state.
And from hearing this scripture, he goes to heaven. / Bringing prosperity, fame, long life, offspring, and granting all desires,
may this scripture be truly sacred, O slayer of Madhu! / Having heard this supreme scripture, which has arisen from the grace of Viṣṇu,

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-second chapter, entitled “The Sages' Vision of the Swan's Universal Form,” in the Haṃsagītā addressed to the sages, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara. The Haṃsagītā is concluded.
Vajra said:
The god Viṣṇu of wide strides, exceedingly easy to propitiate for the well-disposed,
revealed his universal form to the twice-born when praised.
Tell me of his supreme grace toward his devoted people;
O brāhmaṇa, I do not reach satiety while listening to this nectar of stories.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
O great king, Śakra's charioteer Mātali, who knew the proper rules,
had a daughter worthy of him, renowned as Guṇakeśī.
Formerly, Mātali and Nārada,
roaming across the entire [earth] to search [for a groom], saw the grandson of Āryaka,
named Sumukha. Taking both [him and his mother?], they went
to Śakra among the serpents, and then both of them made a request to Śakra.

Śakra granted a boon to the two: safety for Sumukha from Tārkṣya.
Knowing the prowess of Tārkṣya, he [Śakra] went to Keśava's presence.
The slayer of Madhu granted safety to Sumukha from Tārkṣya. / Thereupon, filled with anger, Tārkṣya approached Keśava.
Garuḍa said:
“Why, having disregarded me, O Kṛṣṇa, is a boon given to Sumukha? / Mounted on my back, you slay your enemies, and you are conscious [of it]; / yet you protect the snake, my enemy, who is the food for my family!
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed then by him, Viṣṇu said to Garuḍa:
“You are not able to bear my entire universe, O lord of birds! / It is I alone who support myself through myself in battle after battle.” // 3.343.10
If you have the strength to bear [me], carry just one arm of mine.'
Having spoken thus, Hari placed his left arm upon his back.
Then, with dejected face, due to losing his wings, that best of birds, / exhausted and wretched, praised the lord of gods, the slayer of Madhu:

text_mt:
Garuḍa said:
Salutations to you, O lord of the gods of gods, revered by gods and demons!
O unconquerable one, O Puṇḍarīkākṣa, O affectionate to those who have come for refuge!
“Your power was not known by me, whose mind was proud of myself. / You alone, O god, always uphold the three worlds, O sinless one!
O god, you alone always bear yourself by yourself;
for the entire three worlds reside in your body, O god!
How are thousands like me capable of bearing you?
Therefore, be gracious, O Lord, to me who reside on your banner!
There is no end, O lord of gods, to your deeds in the three worlds.
Who is capable of proclaiming your deeds without remainder?
Or what praise is there in the recitation of your deeds, O supreme Lord?
You are omnipotent everywhere; be gracious to me, O slayer of foes!
O you who dwell in all beings, O Vāsudeva, O Lord of the world!
O you who recline on the ocean at the end of the aeon, O Nārāyaṇa of great splendour!

text_mt:
O you whose body is made yellow by the filaments of the navel-lotus! / Be gracious to me! Praise be to you from the bird who resides on your banner!” // 3.343.20
The Blessed One said:
“Self-conceit must never be harboured by you, O Tārkṣya! / It is I alone who bear myself through myself, and I also support you.
[…] because you have been made wingless;
for your sake the entire three worlds were placed by me on my arm.
For there is no one else in the world as strong as you, / from whose touch of the staff-like arm life has not departed.
Since, having been born from your body, [your feathers] will be strong, O best of birds, / at the end of [their loss] your wings will become distinguished, without doubt.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed, the fair-winged one regained his beautiful wings,
or rather obtained an increase of splendour and strength by the grace of the god.
Thus Tārkṣya, who was praising the wielder of the Śārṅga bow like a man,
was once again restored to being fair-winged and made exceedingly strong.

text_mt:
Merely upon being requested by Śakra, Sumukha too was made immortal.
Therefore, O king, know concerning that enemy of the Dānavas:
there is indeed nothing that cannot be given to devotees, even the kingdom of the gods, surely;
and for those seized by the noose of death, falling into hell,
that lord of gods, as soon as remembered, turns them away from that fear.
May the enemy of Madhu—who destroys all suffering for devoted men, who is worthy of worship by the foremost of twice-born and wise gods, the slayer of foes, who travels upon the king of birds, and whose complexion resembles water—be pleased with you who are bowed in devotion!
Vajra said:
I wish to hear from you that supreme grace
which was bestowed upon his devoted people by that powerful Viṣṇu.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Formerly, O king, when the three worlds of Śakra were seized by Bali,
Śakra then went for refuge to his father Kaśyapa.
Taking Śakra with him, Kaśyapa then went to the Grandfather [Brahmā].
Boon-granting Brahmā said to him: 'Go, Kaśyapa, to Keśava,

and pray to him for sonship: he will become your son.
"Then he will give all the three worlds to the king of the gods." / Thus addressed, Kaśyapa went, accompanied by the foremost of the thirty [gods],
To the Ocean of Milk, and there beheld Hari through ascetic penance. / Having seen him, he praised him with a hymn of praise. Thereupon Hari,
Having become gracious and assumed sonship, the god, bearing the form of Vāmana, / upholding the universe, stepped across all the three worlds with three strides.
Bound Bali, the lord of the Daityas, and gave [the realm] to Śakra, O best of kings. / Thus praised by Kaśyapa, he had become his son.
Vajra said: / Tell me that auspicious hymn of praise, destroying all sins, / with which Kaśyapa praised Madhusūdana.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hear, O king, the sacred hymn of praise proclaimed by Kaśyapa / upon seeing the God of gods arise from his bed on the Kṣīroda ocean.

text_mt:
Kaśyapa said:
Om! Homage be to you, god of gods, single-horned, worshipped with bull-[offerings], tree of the ocean, Vṛṣākapi, protector of the gods, blameless one, auspicious one, Kapila, Viṣvaksena, Dhruva, Dharma, banner of dharma, Vaikuṇṭha, whirlwind of righteousness, without beginning, middle, or end, beloved of the people, born of the Vṛṣṇis, resting upon the nectar, eternal one, of three abodes, threefold abode, Tuṣita, drum, world of the great ones, / navel of the world, Padmanābha, Viriñca, manifold in form, imperishable in an instant, consumer of oblations, wielder of the broken axe, discus, shaven-headed, Haṃsa, richly bountiful, Hṛṣīkeśa, subtle one, multitude of great sages, stainless one, pillar, foundation of all the worlds, Śipiviṣṭa, without heat, first-born, born of dharma, navel of dharma, whose navel is radiance, whose chariot is the moon, free from sin! You alone are the dweller in the ocean, unborn, Aja Ekapāt, supported by thousands, great-headed, thousand-eyed, thousand-footed, iron-faced, Cosmic Person, thousand-armed, of a thousand forms, thousand-eyed, origin of thousands! The knowers of the Veda call you, who know the Veda, in thousands of ways. They declare you to be the universe of all beings, laughing with flowers, supremely active, you alone! Vauṣaṭ, the syllable vaṣaṭ, svāhā! You partake of the portions in sacrifices, flowing in a hundred streams, flowing in a thousand streams, whether earth or atmosphere, you alone! Made of Brahman, devoted to brahmins, Brahmā, you alone are the directions; you are heaven, you are earth, you are Mātariśvan! You are the hotṛ, the potṛ, the thinker, the leader; you alone are the cause of the oblation, the foremost through your universal splendour, you alone! Together with the directions, adorned with garlands, you are the object of sacrifice; you are concentration, you are the kindling stick! You are the goal of the wise; you are yoga, you are liberation, you are the supreme! You are the sacrificial ladle, you are the supporter, you are the sacrifice, you are soma, you are smoke, you are initiation, you are the sacrificial fee, you are the universe, the ancient one, Turāṣāḍ, Hiraṇyagarbha, Nārāyaṇa, Ananta, equal to the clouds, sun-coloured, possessing the radiance of the sun, Cosmic Person, Puruṣottama, primeval god, Padmanābha, lotus-smiling, lotus-lying, lotus-eyed, golden-haired at the tip, white, Soul of the universe, god of the universe, universal-faced, mouth of the universe, origin of the universe! You alone are the consumer of the universe, active on earth, transcendent being, maker of light, Śambhu, Bhava, self-existent, origin of beings, great being, all-pervading! You alone are the universe, you are the protector of the universe, you are the purifier, the offering, the ordainer of the universe, of upward deeds, foremost in immortality, protector of the earth, anointed with ghee, O Agni, Druhiṇa, of infinite deeds, the ruler, the foremost, universal-flanked! Flank [us], you yourself are the universe; protect those seeking boons!
Whoever constantly recites this hymn composed by Kaśyapa to the best of gods, / pure in the morning, with mind focused on him, will go to the worlds of Puruṣottama.

text_mt:
Vajra said: / Declare to me, who am a devoted person, the supreme grace / of that high-souled Keśava, the God of gods, bearer of the discus.
For I am not satiated hearing the nectar for the ears of him / who alone in this world gives a helping hand to falling men.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Formerly, O sinless one, the gods and the sages debated: / "Sacrifice must be performed with seeds stored for a maximum of three years.
Seeds are designated as 'aja'; you ought not to kill a goat." / This, O knower of dharma, was the view of the sages of purified mind.
The view of the gods, however, was [sacrifice by] an animal. Then, passing on the way, / there was the king named Uparicara Vasu, the foremost of the opulent.
Then the gods and the sages questioned Vasu. / "Sacrifice must be performed with what is presented," was formerly said by Vasu.
Because of that false statement promoting violence, the king, / who had always moved in the sky, fell into a fissure in the earth.

text_mt:
When he was dwelling in the fissure of the earth, having argued in favor of the gods, / the Dānavas resolved to destroy him, devoted as he was to the gods.
Hearing their intended action, the gods of swift prowess / reported the entire matter to Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods.
Then Bṛhaspati, going to the king dwelling in the fissure of the earth, / instructed him in the invincible protective spell of Viṣṇu,
By reciting deeds of the past, present, and future, / a sacred lore destroying all obstacles was fashioned by Brahmā. / Having taught it to that king, Bṛhaspati said this:
Bṛhaspati said: / Staying here, O king, you will consume the continuous stream of ghee poured out by the Brahmins, / and, by the grace of the deities, you will always be invigorated by it.
And through this protective spell, O king, you will be invulnerable / to the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, even though situated in the earth's fissure. / Having spoken thus to the king, he vanished right there.

text_mt:
3.346
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Om, homage to the Blessed One, Vāsudeva! Homage to Ananta, the thousand-headed, resting upon the ocean of milk, whose couch is the coils of Śeṣa, whose mount is Garuḍa, unborn, unconquered, yellow-robed! Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Horse-headed, Boar, Narasiṃha, Vāmana, Trivikrama, Rāma, Rāma, Rāma, homage to you, homage to you, homage to you!
Slay, slay! Cook, cook! Churn, churn! Destroy, destroy! Put to flight, put to flight the supreme asuras, daityas, dānavas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, siddhas, yoginīs, ḍākinīs, the seizing spirits led by Skanda, the planetary and astral spirits, and all others! With conch, discus, thunderbolt, mace, pestle, and plough, turn them to ashes! O thousand-armed one, armed with thousands of weapons, conquer, conquer! Triumph, triumph! Unconquered one, of unimpeded vision, blaze, blaze! Flare up, flare up! Universal-formed, manifold-formed, Madhusūdana, Mahāvarāha, Cosmic Person, Vaikuṇṭha, Nārāyaṇa, Padmanābha, Govinda, Dāmodara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Keśava! Eradicator of all asuras, subduer of all beings, destroyer of all bad dreams, shatterer of all magical devices, crusher of all serpents, great lord of all gods, deliverer from all bonds, smiter of all enemies, destroyer of all fevers, averter of all seizing spirits, appeaser of all sins, Janārdana, homage be to you, svāhā!
Whoever mutters, reads, hears, remembers, wears, or recites this unconquered, supreme Vaiṣṇava, perfected great lore, has no fear of fire, wind, thunderbolt, or lightning;
he has no fear of the ocean, nor fear of seizing spirits,
nor fear of thieves;
nor will he have fear of wild beasts;
nowhere will he have fear from darkness of night, women, royal families, hatred, poison, secondary poisons, administration of poison, bewitchment, enmity, causing enmity, driving away, murder, or imprisonment,
through these uttered, perfected mantras worshipped by the accomplished.
Namely:
Om, homage to you, sinless one, unconquered, boundless, deathless, Aparājitā, perfected by recitation, perfected by recollection, Ekānaṃśā, Umā, Dhruvā, Arundhatī, Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, Jātavedasī, Mānastokā, Sarasvatī, Dharaṇī, Dhāraṇī, Saudāmanī, Aditi, Diti, Vinatā, Gaurī, Gāndhārī, Mātaṅgī, Kṛṣṇayaśodā, speaker of truth, proclaimer of the Absolute, Kālī, Kāpālī, sleep, you who bring true attainment! What is on land, what is in water, or what is in the intermediate space—protect, protect from all beings,
from all afflictions, svāhā!
She whose menstrual flow fails, or if her embryo falls, / she whose children die, and she who bears only a single child—

I have approached the lord of birds for refuge, him of great splendor, who traverses the dark clouds, / having approached the mighty Garuḍa, the sky-roamer of great splendor, the boon-giver, unconquerable and untiring.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Praised by the king, Garuḍa, having taken the king upon his back, / presented him to the god Viṣṇu of boundless splendor.
Seeing the lord of the gods of gods, who destroys the distress of those who bow down, / he praised the invincible lord of gods with devotion, O king of kings.
Vasu said: / Homage to you, lotus-eyed Puṇḍarīkākṣa, affectionate toward those who seek refuge, / slayer of the pride of Daityas and Dānavas, destroyer of the distress of those bowed in homage!
Grantor of desires to those who desire, destroyer of desire, origin of the universe, lord of the world, / destroyer of darkness that arises from the night of the Great Form!
Neither the hosts of gods nor the great ṛṣis know your origin; / you are the beginning of all duties and of the ṛṣis, O teacher of the world!
You are subtler than all beings and greater than the great; / you are far away, O fortunate one, and yet present before all.

Although dwelling within all beings, you are not stained by actions; / bodiless, yet dwelling in the body, remaining in all beings.
You are the Puruṣa, you are the Unmanifest, you are the Self and the intellect; / you are the great elements, O Blessed One, and likewise the senses.
You are meditated upon by yogins, O ancient one who are to be known by the knowledge of yoga; / those who worship you, O Blessed One, attain the supreme state.
I have taken refuge in Vāsudeva, the worthy refuge: victorious, sinless, invincible, omnipresent, the God of gods, / whose power is ever ready to destroy the enemies of the thirty [gods], / worshipful by the best of twice-born and gods, the destroyer of sins.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Praised by Vasu, clad in radiant form and eloquent, Viṣṇu / spoke to the king who stood before him, bowed with folded hands:
Vāsudeva said: / An untruth should not be spoken, O king, even when the breaths have reached the throat; / likewise, a question on dharma especially should not be answered by one alone.

even by one who knows much, O knower of dharma, who desires dharma at any time. / For duties are difficult to discern, subtle, O king, and hard to trace.
Therefore, it should never be spoken by one alone who knows. / Having spoken an untruth, a great hardship has been incurred by you, O ruler of men.
A fall from your station was likewise incurred by speaking for the sake of the gods' sacrifice; / you are continually my devotee, and on that account expiation has been made for you.
In a short time, which was not capable [of being attained] by gods and asuras even in an aeon. / Go, protect your kingdom, and remain likewise unwavering.
Disrespect toward brahmins must never be shown by you in any way; / for a brahmin is a great being, to be known as the supreme deity.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus to Vasu, Viṣṇu vanished right there / along with Garuḍa, O king; and Vasu was filled with wonder.
He also regained his kingdom once more, and likewise the ability to move through the sky; / then he was greeted with respect by all the gods assembled together.

text_mt:
Thus ends the three hundred and forty-eighth chapter, named 'The Narrative of Vasu', in the third book of the venerable Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
Vajra said: / Describe the universal form of the God of gods who bears the discus; / to whom was it shown by him, O enhancer of the Bhṛgu lineage?
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / By devotees with exclusive devotion the universal forms of the God, / which are impossible to describe, were seen many times of old.
Without the grace of Vāsudeva, one does not become endowed with divine vision; / until then there is no capacity to see him bearing the universal form.
In that regard, that which was shown of old to Nārada, O sinless one, / by Viṣṇu, the God of all, that I shall declare to you.
Nārada went to Badaryāśrama, very wonderful, / the abode of Nara-Nārāyaṇa, celebrated as exceedingly delightful,
where Hari, fourfold in self, assumed the state of being the sons of Dharma: / Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Nara, and Lord Nārāyaṇa.

At that time, Hari Kṛṣṇa, when he had passed, was indeed in another world; / and the gods Nara and Nārāyaṇa were likewise devoted to severe austerity.
Stationed on an eight-wheeled vehicle, full of splendour and charming, / standing on one foot, without support, both with arms raised aloft.
Nārada saw both of them there, of blazing splendour; / having saluted the two departed gods, he stood before them.
The twice-born, having then been honoured by Nara and Nārāyaṇa / with water for the feet, respectful offering, water for sipping, and the like, resided there in their hermitage.
Dwelling in the hermitage, that best of vipras once saw the two best of gods, / the sinless ones, performing divine rites without obstacle.
Then, having performed his daily rites, Nārada spoke to those two teachers of the world: / “You two are the lords of the worlds, you two are the supreme lords.
For whose propitiation are you both here engaged in austerity? / Who is worshipped by you two and intended in rites to gods and ancestors?"

["The two said:] / Our supreme Prakṛti, from whom is the origin of all, / in order to show the proper norm, we ever worship that new, undefeated [Lord],
O brahman, in rites intended for gods and ancestors. / In the three worlds, vipras, divine gurus, cows, and the ancestors—
those who worship them, worship indeed that God, the supreme Lord; / whoever worships a god, by him Hari is worshipped.
Even if devoid of rules, O fortunate one, because he is all-pervading; / and desiring to make worship of another god, one should worship Hari.
by that, worship of him is performed according to the prescribed rite, O best of the twice-born; / for the gods and all that is contained in the three worlds reside in the God.
Worship of the three worlds is performed by one who performs the worship of Viṣṇu. / There is no such Brahman in the worlds where Janārdana is not present;
nor is there anything in the worlds that is not established in Viṣṇu: / in whom is all, from whom is all, who is all, and who is everywhere,

and who is eternally composed of all—homage to him, the Self of all! / In the middle of the Kṣīroda ocean there is an island extending many yojanas.
There the men are white, of splendour equal to the moon, / and all are endowed with the marks of universal emperors.
Knowing the prescribed rite of the Pañcarātra, they ever worship Hari. / Moreover, assuming an illusory body, the god Madhusūdana too—"
Hari continually receives that worship with his head; / he always delights with them, and is ever worshipped by them.
Those men here who are endowed with exclusive devotion, / and who, devoid of desire, ever worship the lord of the world,
having abandoned the body, they go to that island called Śveta, / free from exudation, taking no food, all-knowing, and seeing everything.
Lords of all, eternally contented, having attained supreme bliss, / they worship Hari there again for a hundred divine years.
Then, piercing the solar orb, they enter Aniruddha, / through austerities, O sage, into Pradyumna, and then into the lord Saṃkarṣaṇa.

Then, having reached Vāsudeva, they become just like him; / thereupon all become omnipotent, everywhere, at all times,
and, freed from all sufferings, they have attained supreme bliss. / So go quickly from here and [look upon] the dwellers of Śvetadvīpa.
Behold those men, O brahmin; that lord, being pleased with you, / will show [you] his wondrous form, a marvel to the three worlds,
[his] universal form, O tiger among brahmins, pleased Madhusūdana. / Ekata, Dvita, and Trita of great austerities,
having gone to that realm, O brahmin, did not see Janārdana, / because [only] those endowed with exclusive devotion [can see] the world-teacher.
They only heard the verse uttered by the dwellers of Śvetadvīpa, / the highly fortunate ones free of all taint:
“Victory to you, O Puṇḍarīkākṣa! Homage to you, creator of the universe! / May homage be to you, O Hṛṣīkeśa, supreme person, first-born!”

Hearing this verse, they also heard a bodiless voice / of Hari, O highly fortunate one, bringing benefit to all beings:
“[Does anyone] meet death ever after reaching Śvetadvīpa? / There is no entry into Śvetadvīpa without being single-minded devotees, O brahmins.
You are devotees of ordinary disposition and rich in austerity; / endowed with severe austerity, you have therefore come to my land.
You whose essence is of ordinary devotion, go back without delay; / by you the persons dwelling in Śvetadvīpa have been seen.
Through these verses Janārdana is likewise seen; / by men devoted to exclusive devotion, this [verse]
It should be continually murmured, O brahmins; then you will come here again; / this verse is purifying, sacred, and the destroyer of all sins.

“He is invisible to all the gods; how do you wish to see him?” / Thus consoled, Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods,
then brought that sacrifice of the king to completion. / Even the ṛṣis endowed with exclusive devotion to Janārdana,
having come from Śvetadvīpa for divine business in ancient times, O brahmin, / reached Śvetadvīpa again, which is hard to attain for one who must return.
Therefore, see that lord of the gods who resides there, O Nārada; / for you too have many divine tasks to perform.
Even though you go to Śvetadvīpa, O brahmin, you will not at present / have in the worlds that state which brings nirvāṇa; / but at the end of the kalpa, O brahmin, you will attain that state.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Addressed thus, having saluted those two gods, Nārada then went quickly / to that island with the speed of mind and wind.
Having gone there, he saw the dwellers of Śvetadvīpa, / and Nārada worshipped them with his head, full of devotion.

Having reached the great white island, Nārada, glad at heart, / saw those very men, white, with the lustre of the moon, and auspicious.
He honoured them with his head, and was mentally honoured by them; / desirous to see [the Lord], devoted to japa, regarded as enduring every hardship,
With a single-pointed mind, the brahmin, whose arms were long, raised his arms / and sang a hymn of praise to the All, the qualityless, whose self is the qualities:
to peaceful Vāsudeva, and the creator of the universe, O brahmin, / to the endless, the immeasurable, the omnipresent, exceedingly swift,
to him of boundless strength and valour, perpetually worshipped by gods and munis, / to Viṣṇu, destroyer of the burden of worldly existence, destroyer of the sins of those who bow to him.

Atharvaśiras; of five great aeons; venerable teacher; Vālakhilya; Vaikhānasa; yoga of fire; unbroken enumeration; beginning of the age, middle of the age, end of the age; Akhaṇḍala; ancient womb; Kauśika; praised by many; invoked by many; invoked by all; offered to by all; universal form; of infinite path; of infinite coils; infinite one; without beginning or middle; whose end is unmanifest; abode of vows; dwelling in the ocean; equal dwelling; abode of renown; abode of Lakṣmī; abode of fame; abode of ancestral offerings; abode of fortune; dwelling-place of Śrī; dwelling-place of all; Vāsudeva; singer of all metres; having bay horses; horse sacrifice; taker of the sacrificial share; giver of boons; yama; niyama; great niyama; kṛcchra, atikṛcchra, mahākṛcchra, and all kṛcchras; holder of observances; whose dharma is cessation; attainment of sacred teaching; performer of active Vedic rites; unborn one; omnipresent; all-seeing; ungraspable; immovable; of great majesty; whose body is greatness; pure one; greatly pure one; golden one; vast one; unthinkable; unknowable; fire of Brahman; maker of the creation of creatures; maker of the destruction of the unborn; bearer of great māyā; of variegated tufts; giver of boons; taker of the portion of sacrificial cake; traveller who has reached his path; whose thirst is severed; tranquil on every side; whose form is Brahman; bearer of Brahman; dear to brahmins; universal-bodied one; great-bodied one; kinsman; affectionate to devotees; god devoted to brahmins! Devoted to you, desiring to see you, for an exclusive vision: Oṃ, reverence!

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
3.351

text_mt:
3.351
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
He then saw Viṣṇu Hari bearing his universal form, / endowed with colors resembling parrots, yellow, red, white, and black,
title: Viśvarūpākhyānam

sanskrit_iast:
kvacinmecakasaṃyuktaiḥ kvacinmecakarañjitaiḥ ..
cicchaśāṃkasaṃkāśaṃ kvaciddhiṅgulasannibham .. .. 2 ..
meaning:
क्वचिन्मेचकसंयुक्तैः क्वचिन्मेचकरञ्जितैः ..
चिच्छशांकसंकाशं क्वचिद्धिङ्गुलसन्निभम् .. .. 2 ..
text_mt: here and there mingled with dark blue, here and there stained with dark blue, / shining like the pure moon, and in some places resembling cinnabar,

sanskrit_iast:
kvacinmarakataprakhyaṃ padmarāganibhaṃ kvacit ..
kvacitkanakasaṃkāśaṃ kvacinnīlotpalaprabham .. 3 ..
meaning:
क्वचिन्मरकतप्रख्यं पद्मरागनिभं क्वचित् ..
क्वचित्कनकसंकाशं क्वचिन्नीलोत्पलप्रभम् .. 3 ..
text_mt: in some places resembling emerald, in some places like ruby; / in some places resembling gold, in some places with the splendor of a blue lotus;

sanskrit_iast:
kvacitpāṭalapuṣpābhaṃ kvacidgaganasannibham ..
kuṃkumakṣodasaṃkāśaṃ haridrakṣodasannibham .. 4 ..
meaning:
क्वचित्पाटलपुष्पाभं क्वचिद्गगनसन्निभम् ..
कुंकुमक्षोदसंकाशं हरिद्रक्षोदसन्निभम् .. 4 ..
text_mt: in some places possessing the luster of the pāṭalā flower, in others resembling the sky, / like saffron powder and like turmeric powder;

sanskrit_iast:
kvacidrajopalaprakhyamindranīlanibhaṃ kvacit ..
anirdeśyāni varṇāni tathā bibhratkvacitkvacit .. 5 ..
meaning:
क्वचिद्रजोपलप्रख्यमिन्द्रनीलनिभं क्वचित् ..
अनिर्देश्यानि वर्णानि तथा बिभ्रत्क्वचित्क्वचित् .. 5 ..
text_mt: in some places resembling a silver-stone, in some places like a sapphire; / and likewise displaying indescribable colors in various places;

sanskrit_iast:
nānāvidhānāṃ sattvānāṃ vadanāni bahūni ca ..
brahmaśaṃkaraśakrāṇāṃ yamasya varuṇasya ca .. 6 ..
meaning:
नानाविधानां सत्त्वानां वदनानि बहूनि च ..
ब्रह्मशंकरशक्राणां यमस्य वरुणस्य च .. 6 ..
text_mt: and [he saw] many faces of various kinds of beings: / of Brahmā, Śaṃkara, and Indra, and of Yama and Varuṇa;

sanskrit_iast:
dhanadasya hutāśasya vāyornirṛtinastathā ..
grahāṇāmatha ṛkṣāṇāṃ rudrāṇāṃ vasubhiḥ saha .. 7 ..
meaning:
धनदस्य हुताशस्य वायोर्निरृतिनस्तथा ..
ग्रहाणामथ ऋक्षाणां रुद्राणां वसुभिः सह .. 7 ..
text_mt: [and the forms] of Dhanada, of Fire, of Wind, and likewise of Nirṛti, / of the planets and constellations, of the Rudras together with the Vasus,

sanskrit_iast:
ādityānāṃ samarutāṃ bhṛgūṇāṃ ca tathā dvija ..
tathaivāṅgiraso rājansādhyānāmaśvibhiḥ saha .. 8 ..
meaning:
आदित्यानां समरुतां भृगूणां च तथा द्विज ..
तथैवाङ्गिरसो राजन्साध्यानामश्विभिः सह .. 8 ..
text_mt: of the Ādityas with the Maruts, and likewise of the Bhṛgus, O twice-born one; / just so of the Aṅgirases, O king, and of the Sādhyas together with the Aśvins;

sanskrit_iast:
daityānāmatha nānānāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām ..
pitṛpannagayakṣāṇāṃ tathā ca piśitāśinām .. 9 ..
meaning:
दैत्यानामथ नानानां गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् ..
पितृपन्नगयक्षाणां तथा च पिशिताशिनाम् .. 9 ..
text_mt: and of various Daityas, Gandharvas, Uragas, and Rakṣases, / of ancestors, serpents, and Yakṣas, and likewise of flesh-eaters,

sanskrit_iast:
manuṣya hayanāgānāṃ gajāśvamṛgapakṣiṇām ..
dvīpiśārdūlasiṃhānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmatha .. 3.351.10 ..
meaning:
मनुष्य हयनागानां गजाश्वमृगपक्षिणाम् ..
द्वीपिशार्दूलसिंहानां सर्वेषां प्राणिनामथ .. 3.351.10 ..
text_mt: of humans, horses, and elephants, of elephants, horses, beasts, and birds, / of leopards, tigers, and lions, and indeed of all living beings.

sanskrit_iast:
kānicittasya saumyāni kānicidbhīṣaṇāni ca ..
dadarśa tasya vaktrāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 11 ..
meaning:
कानिचित्तस्य सौम्यानि कानिचिद्भीषणानि च ..
ददर्श तस्य वक्त्राणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः .. 11 ..
text_mt: Some of his faces were gentle, and some were terrifying; / he beheld his mouths by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit_iast:
vaktreṣu tasya raudrasya prāṇisaṃghānyanekaśaḥ ..
dadarśa sarvataścāgnīngrasyamānām̐śca viṣṇunā ..12..
meaning:
वक्त्रेषु तस्य रौद्रस्य प्राणिसंघान्यनेकशः ..
ददर्श सर्वतश्चाग्नीन्ग्रस्यमानाम्̐श्च विष्णुना ..12..
text_mt: In the mouths of that terrible one he saw multitudes of living beings in great numbers, / and all around he saw fires being swallowed up by Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
saumyebhyastasya vaktrebhyo nirgacchaṃtyastathā prajāḥ ..
vāhāṃśca vividhām̐stasya sa dadarśātha nāradaḥ .. 13..
meaning:
सौम्येभ्यस्तस्य वक्त्रेभ्यो निर्गच्छंत्यस्तथा प्रजाः ..
वाहांश्च विविधाम्̐स्तस्य स ददर्शाथ नारदः .. 13..
text_mt: And likewise Nārada then saw creatures coming forth / from his gentle mouths, and his various mounts,

sanskrit_iast:
hastām̐śca vividhākārānnānāmudrāsamanvitān ..
yuktānnānāvidhairbhāṇḍairāyudhaiśca sahasraśaḥ..14..

हस्ताम्̐श्च विविधाकारान्नानामुद्रासमन्वितान् ..
युक्तान्नानाविधैर्भाण्डैरायुधैश्च सहस्रशः..14..
text_mt: and his hands of diverse shapes, furnished with various gestures, / equipped with diverse vessels and with weapons by the thousands,

sanskrit_iast:
sruksruvāvedicamasakuśakṛṣṇājināgnibhiḥ ..
kecicca kalaśaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ śaṅkhapadmotpalādibhiḥ..15..
meaning:
स्रुक्स्रुवावेदिचमसकुशकृष्णाजिनाग्निभिः ..
केचिच्च कलशं घण्टां शङ्खपद्मोत्पलादिभिः..15..
text_mt: with oblation-ladles, offering-spoons, altars, sacrificial cups, kuśa grass, black antelope skins, and fires; / and some with water-pots, bells, conches, lotuses, blue water-lilies, and the like;

sanskrit_iast:
kecitkhaḍgagadācakracarmaśūlaparaśvadhaiḥ ..
kecitpāśamahādaṇḍakṛpāṇaśarakārmukaiḥ .. 16 ..
meaning:
केचित्खड्गगदाचक्रचर्मशूलपरश्वधैः ..
केचित्पाशमहादण्डकृपाणशरकार्मुकैः .. 16 ..
text_mt: some with swords, clubs, discuses, shields, tridents, and battle-axes; / some with nooses, great rods, daggers, arrows, and bows;

sanskrit_iast:
kecidbhuśuṇḍīlaguḍaśaktivajrāśmapaṭṭiśaiḥ ..
bījapūrṇākṣamālāśca pūrṇapātraistathā paraiḥ .. 17 ..
meaning:
केचिद्भुशुण्डीलगुडशक्तिवज्राश्मपट्टिशैः ..
बीजपूर्णाक्षमालाश्च पूर्णपात्रैस्तथा परैः .. 17 ..
text_mt: some with bhuśuṇḍī-missiles, cudgels, spears, thunderbolts, sling-stones, and barbed darts; / and others with citrons, rosaries, and full vessels.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ nānāvidhairbhāṇḍaiḥ karāṃstasya samanvitān ..
asaṃkhyeyānmahātejā dadarśa munisattamaḥ .. 18 ..
meaning:
एवं नानाविधैर्भाण्डैः करांस्तस्य समन्वितान् ..
असंख्येयान्महातेजा ददर्श मुनिसत्तमः .. 18 ..
text_mt: Thus the most excellent sage of great splendor beheld / his innumerable hands furnished with various kinds of implements.

sanskrit_iast:
nṛttaśāstravinirdiṣṭo nṛttakarmaṇi cāpyatha ..
śirāṃsi dṛṣṭayo hastāṃstasya devasya dṛṣṭavān .. 19 ..
meaning:
नृत्तशास्त्रविनिर्दिष्टो नृत्तकर्मणि चाप्यथ ..
शिरांसि दृष्टयो हस्तांस्तस्य देवस्य दृष्टवान् .. 19 ..
text_mt: And then he saw the heads, glances, and hands of that god, / as prescribed in the treatise on dance and employed in the performance of dance.

sanskrit_iast:
trailokyaṃ ca tathā kāye sakalaṃ munisattamaḥ ..
devadānavagandharvasayakṣoragarakṣasām .. 3.351.20 ..
meaning:
त्रैलोक्यं च तथा काये सकलं मुनिसत्तमः ..
देवदानवगन्धर्वसयक्षोरगरक्षसाम् .. 3.351.20 ..
text_mt: and likewise the best of sages [saw] the entire triple world in his body, / [consisting] of gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, along with Yakṣas, Uragas, and Rakṣases.

sanskrit_iast:
dvīpāmbhonidhilokaiśca pātālaiścaiva saṃyutam ..
jagatsamagraṃ devasya dehasthaṃ dṛṣṭavānmuniḥ .. 21 ..
meaning:
द्वीपाम्भोनिधिलोकैश्च पातालैश्चैव संयुतम् ..
जगत्समग्रं देवस्य देहस्थं दृष्टवान्मुनिः .. 21 ..
text_mt: the sage beheld the whole universe residing in the body of the god, / together with the continents, the oceans, the worlds, and the nether regions.

sanskrit_iast:
sa dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ rūpaṃ bhīto hṛṣṭaśca vismitaḥ ..
papāta pādayostasya śirasā sāśrulocanaḥ .. 22 ..
